translation_verse: Kʋ jɩjɩgɩrʋ tɩm maama laan ma ba tɩ cɔgɩ lɩla, maŋa fɩnfɩɩn má wʋnɩ.» Kʋ nan na yɩ balʋ maama na co nabwǝǝru tɩn dɩ ba yum tiinǝ, dɩ balʋ na tɔgɩ nabwǝǝru tɩm ba pipi tɩn, dɩ balʋ na zʋʋrɩ nabwǝǝru ba ve je tɩn, ba maama wʋ́ ta zɩgɩ yigǝ yigǝ mʋ ba nii tɩʋ kʋm.

english_verse: When they saw the smoke from her fire, they shouted, “This was the greatest city ever!”
translation_verse: Bantʋ na nɛ nyʋa kam na zaŋɩ tɩʋ kʋm baŋa nɩ tɩn, baá ta dɩ kwǝr-dɩa ba wɩ: «Tʋ-kamunu kʋntʋ ya ba jɩgɩ doŋ.»

english_verse: They cried loudly, and in their sorrow they threw dust on their heads, as they said, “Pity the great city of Babylon! Everyone who sailed the seas became rich from her treasures. But in a single hour the city was destroyed.
translation_verse: Ba ma wʋ́ ta pɛ puuri ba lo ba yum nɩ, yɩ ba keeri ba coosi ba wɩ: «Ei. Lɛɛrʋ lɛɛrʋ! Tʋ-kamunu kʋntʋ jɩjɩgɩrʋ tɩm ŋwaanɩ mʋ pɛ balʋ maama na te nabwǝǝru tɩn ji nadunǝ. Kʋ nan cɔgɩ maŋa fɩnfɩɩn má wʋnɩ.»

english_verse: A powerful angel then picked up a huge stone and threw it into the sea. The angel said, “This is how the great city of Babylon will be thrown down, never to rise again.
translation_verse: Wɛ malɛka kadoŋ kalʋ na tiini ka dana tɩn laan ma kwe kandwɛ kamunu nɩ nɔŋ-zɔŋɔ na yɩ te tɩn. Ka ma dʋlɩ-kʋ ka yagɩ na-fara bam wʋnɩ yɩ ka wɩ: «Baá kwe tʋ-kamunu Babilɔnɩ dɩ ba dʋlɩ ba yagɩ kʋntʋ doŋ mʋ, yɩ nɔɔn-nɔɔnʋ daa bá na kʋ je.

english_verse: The music of harps and singers and of flutes and trumpets will no longer be heard. No workers will ever set up shop in that city, and the sound of grinding grain will be silenced forever.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna daa bá ta wʋ kʋ wʋnɩ sɩ ba taa magɩ kwaanʋ naa ba taa leenǝ, naa ba taa wui wi naa nabwaanʋ. Gɔgɔ naa tɩtʋŋɩ dwi maama dɩ daa bá ta wʋ kʋ wʋnɩ, yɩ nɔŋɔ kwǝri dɩ daa bá ta zaŋɩ kʋ wʋnɩ.

english_verse: Lamps will no longer shine anywhere in Babylon, and couples will never again say wedding vows there. Her merchants ruled the earth, and by her witchcraft she fooled all nations.
translation_verse: Min-zoŋo mini dɩ daa bá tarɩgɩ kʋ wʋnɩ. Kadiri sɔɔ dɩ daa bá kɩ kʋ wʋnɩ. Tʋ-kamunu Babilɔnɩ pipimpiinǝ bam dɛɛn mʋ yɩ lʋgʋ baŋa dɩdɛɛra yigǝ tiinǝ. Kʋ maa ma kʋ liri kikiǝ yam kʋ ganɩ lʋgʋ baŋa dwi tiinǝ maama.

english_verse: After this, I heard what sounded like a lot of voices in heaven, and they were shouting, “Praise the Lord! To our God belongs the glorious power to save,
translation_verse: Amʋ laan ma ni kwǝr-dɩa ka na nyɩ dɩ nɔn-kɔgɔ zanzan na ŋɔɔnɩ baŋa baŋa Wɛ-sɔŋɔ nɩ ba wɩ: «Aleluya. Vrɩm dɩ paarɩ-zulǝ dɩ dam yɩ dɩbam Tu Wɛ nyɩm mʋ.

english_verse: because his judgments are honest and fair. That filthy prostitute ruined the earth with shameful deeds. But God has judged her and made her pay the price for murdering his servants.”
translation_verse: DƖ sarɩya yam yɔɔrɩ lanyɩranɩ, yɩ ya tɔgɩ cɩga. Kʋ na yɩ ka-bor-zɔŋɔ kʋm, Wɛ di kʋ sarɩya yɩ kʋ na cam, dɩ kʋ na pɛ kʋ boorim kikiǝ yam jagɩ je maama ya cɔgɩ lʋgʋ baŋa tɩn. Wɛ ma waarɩ-kʋ dɩ kʋ na gʋ DƖ tɩntʋŋna bam tɩn ŋwaanɩ.»

english_verse: Then the crowd shouted, “Praise the Lord! Smoke will never stop rising from her burning body.”
translation_verse: Ba daa ma ta ba wɩ: «Aleluya. Mini na di-kʋ tɩn, kʋ nyʋa kam wʋ́ ta zaŋɩ mʋ taan, sɩ kʋ taa ve maŋa kalʋ na ba ti tɩn.»

english_verse: From the throne a voice said, “If you worship and fear our God, give praise to him, no matter who you are.”
translation_verse: Kwǝrǝ kadoŋ laan ma ŋɔɔnɩ paarɩ jangɔŋɔ kʋm jǝgǝ kam nɩ ka wɩ: «Abam balʋ maama na yɩ Wɛ tɩntʋŋna tɩn, taá zuli-na dɩbam Tu Wɛ. Abam balʋ maama na kwarɩ-DƖ tɩn, kʋ na yɩ nɔn-kamunǝ dɩ nabwǝnǝ, á taá zuli-DƖ.»

english_verse: Then I heard what seemed to be a large crowd that sounded like a roaring flood and loud thunder all mixed together. They were saying, “Praise the Lord! Our Lord God All-Powerful now rules as king.
translation_verse: Amʋ laan ma ni kwǝri sɩ na nyɩ dɩ nɔn-kɔgɔ zanzan na ŋɔɔnɩ baŋa baŋa, yɩ kʋ dwana nɩ na-fara mʋ wuurǝ yɩ dʋa baga te. Kʋ maa ŋɔɔnɩ kʋ wɩ: «Aleluya. Dɩbam Tu, Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Baŋa-Wɛ mʋ te paarɩ.

english_verse: So we will be glad and happy and give him praise. The wedding day of the Lamb is here, and his bride is ready.
translation_verse: Pa-na dɩ́ taá kɩ wʋpolo dɩ́ cakɩ dɩ́ zuli Wɛ, Pǝlbu wʋm kadiri dɩm maŋa laan na yi tɩn ŋwaanɩ. O kaanɩ wʋm ti o yigǝ sɩ o zʋ-o.

english_verse: She will be given a wedding dress made of pure and shining linen. This linen stands for the good things God's people have done.”
translation_verse: Ba kwe gwar-ŋʋnnʋ tɩlʋ na ba jɩgɩ digiru yɩ tɩ tiini tɩ nyɩɩna tɩn ba pa kaanɩ wʋm zʋ.» Gwaarʋ tɩm kʋntʋ nan mʋ brɩ Wɛ nɔɔna bam kǝm-laarʋ tɩm na yɩ te tɩn.

english_verse: Then the angel told me, “Put this in writing. God will bless everyone who is invited to the wedding feast of the Lamb.” The angel also said, “These things God has said are true.”
translation_verse: Malɛka kam laan ma ta dɩ amʋ ka wɩ: «Pʋpʋnɩ tɩntʋ n tiŋi: Kʋ na yɩ balʋ ba na bǝŋi sɩ ba tɔgɩ ba di Pǝlbu wʋm kadiri candiǝ kam tɩn, bantʋ jɩgɩ yu-yoŋo.» Ka daa ma ta ka wɩ: «Nmʋ na ni kʋlʋ maama tɩn yɩ Wɛ kwǝrǝ mʋ, yɩ ka yɩ cɩga mʋ.»

english_verse: I knelt at the feet of the angel and began to worship him. But the angel said, “Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you and everyone else who tells about Jesus. Don't worship anyone but God. Everyone who tells about Jesus does it by the power of the Spirit.” The Rider on the White Horse
translation_verse: Amʋ ma kuni doonǝ ka yigǝ nɩ sɩ a zuli-ka. Ka ma ta ka wɩ: «Yɩ kɩ kʋntʋ. Amʋ dɩ yɩ Wɛ tɩntʋŋnʋ mʋ, nɩ nmʋ dɩ n ko-biǝ balʋ maama na brɩ nɩ ba tɔgɩ Zezi cɩga kam tɩn dɩ na yɩ te tɩn. N maŋɩ sɩ n zuli Wɛ mʋ.» Kʋ yɩ Zezi cɩga kam kʋntʋ mʋ paɩ Wɛ nijoŋnǝ bam tɔɔlɩ DƖ kwǝrǝ kam. Nɔɔnʋ na dɔgɩ sisǝŋ-pwǝŋǝ baŋa nɩ te tɩn

english_verse: I looked and saw heaven was open, and a white horse was there. Its rider was called Faithful and True, and he is always fair when he judges or goes to war.
translation_verse: Amʋ laan ma nii a na Wɛ-sɔŋɔ ni na pʋrɩ. A ma na sisǝŋ-pwǝŋǝ. Wʋlʋ na dɔgɩ ka baŋa nɩ tɩn yɩrɩ mʋ Wʋ-dɩdʋa Tu dɩ Cɩga Tu. O na di nɔɔna sarɩya dɩ o na kwǝri o jaanɩ jara te tɩn yɔɔrɩ kʋ tɔgɩ cɩga mʋ.

english_verse: He had eyes like flames of fire, and he was wearing a lot of crowns. His name was written on him, but he was the only one who knew what the name meant.
translation_verse: O yiǝ maa sɩɩnɩ nɩ min-vʋgʋ te. Sǝbu-sɩŋa yipwi zanzan ma pu o yuu nɩ. Yɩrɩ dɩdoŋ ma pʋpʋnɩ o yɩra nɩ, yɩ nɔɔn-nɔɔnʋ yǝri-dɩ, kʋ na daɩ o tɩtɩ yɩranɩ.

english_verse: The rider wore a robe that was covered with blood, and he was known as “The Word of God.”
translation_verse: Gwar-dɩdɔrɔ kʋlʋ o na zʋ tɩn ma bugi dɩ jana. Ba maa bǝ-o nɩ Wɛ Bɩtara kam.

english_verse: He was followed by armies from heaven that rode on white horses and were dressed in pure white linen.
translation_verse: Wɛ-sɔŋɔ pamaŋ-kɔgɔ kʋm ma pu o kwaga. Ba ma dɔgɩ sise-pwǝǝnu baŋa nɩ, yɩ ba zʋ gwar-pwǝǝnu tɩlʋ na lana yɩ tɩ ba jɩgɩ digiru tɩn.

english_verse: From his mouth a sharp sword went out to attack the nations. He will rule them with an iron rod and will show the fierce anger of God All-Powerful by trampling the grapes in the pit where wine is made.
translation_verse: Sʋ-lɔŋɔ kʋlʋ na tiini kʋ jɩgɩ ni tɩn maa nuŋi o ni nɩ. O nan wʋ́ ma-kʋ o kɩ jara dɩ lʋgʋ baŋa dwi tiinǝ bam maama o wanɩ, yɩ o daarɩ o taa te-ba dɩ dam. O ma wʋ́ pa Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Baŋa-Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ kʋm tiini kʋ ba ba baŋa, nɩnɛɛnɩ o kanɩ tiu-biǝ mʋ sɩ o ma kɩ sana te.

english_verse: On the part of the robe that covered his thigh was written, “KING OF KINGS AND Lord OF LordS.”
translation_verse: Yɩrɩ dɩdoŋ ma pʋpʋnɩ o gwar-dɩdɔrɔ kʋm yɩra nɩ dɩ o cwe nɩ dɩ wɩ: Pwa maama Pɛ, dɩ yum tiinǝ maama Yuutu.

english_verse: I then saw an angel standing on the sun, and he shouted to all the birds flying in the sky, “Come and join in God's great feast!
translation_verse: Amʋ laan ma na malɛka kadoŋ ka na zɩgɩ wɩa kam tɩtarɩ nɩ. Ka ma tɔɔlɩ dɩ kwǝr-dɩa ka ta dɩ duurǝ dɩ kalwǝǝnu dɩ zunǝ balʋ maama na di nwana tɩn ka wɩ: «Ba-na á la daanɩ á di Wɛ candi-fara kam.

english_verse: I also saw the beast and all kings of the earth come together. They fought against the rider on the white horse and against his army.
translation_verse: Amʋ ma daarɩ a na varɩm wʋm dɩ lʋgʋ baŋa pwa bam maama dɩ ba pamaŋ-kɔgɔ kʋm na lagɩ daanɩ, sɩ ba kɩ jara dɩ wʋlʋ na dɔgɩ sisǝŋǝ kam baŋa nɩ tɩn dɩ o pamaŋ-kɔgɔ kʋm.

english_verse: But the beast was captured and so was the false prophet. This is the same prophet who had worked miracles for the beast, so he could fool everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol. The beast and the false prophet were thrown alive into a lake of burning sulfur.
translation_verse: Ba ma ja varɩm wʋm ba vɔ, dɩ wʋlʋ na brɩ nɩ o yɩ Wɛ nijoŋnu yɩ o yagɩ o daɩ tɩn. Wʋntʋ ya mʋ kɩ wo-kɩnkagɩla dayigǝ varɩm wʋm yigǝ nɩ o ma o ganɩ balʋ na jɩgɩ varɩm wʋm nyɩnyʋgʋ yɩ ba zuli o kamɔgɔ kʋm tɩn. Ba ma kwe bantʋ bale ŋʋnnɩ ba ja vu ba dɩ min-nɩnɩʋ wʋnɩ. Kʋ yɩ ciribi mim mʋ.

english_verse: But the rest of their army was killed by the sword that came from the mouth of the rider on the horse. Then birds stuffed themselves on the dead bodies.
translation_verse: Wʋlʋ na dɔgɩ sisǝŋǝ kam yuu nɩ tɩn maa ma sʋ-lɔŋɔ kʋlʋ na nuŋi o ni nɩ tɩn o gʋ pamaŋ-kɔgɔ kʋlʋ maama na daarɩ tɩn. Zunǝ balʋ maama na di nwana tɩn ma ba ba di ba ya-nwana yam ba su.

english_verse: I saw thrones, and sitting on those thrones were the ones who had been given the right to judge. I also saw the souls of the people who had their heads cut off because they had told about Jesus and preached God's message. They were the same ones who had not worshiped the beast or the idol, and they had refused to let its mark be put on their foreheads or hands. They will come to life and rule with Christ for
translation_verse: Amʋ ma daarɩ a na paarɩ jangwaanʋ yɩ nɔɔna je tɩ baŋa nɩ. Wɛ ma pa-ba dam sɩ ba di nɔɔna taanɩ. A ma daarɩ a na ba na goni balʋ yuni Zezi cɩga kam dɩ Wɛ kwǝrǝ kam tɔɔlɩm ŋwaanɩ tɩn jwǝǝru Wɛ tee nɩ. Bantʋ mʋ yɩ balʋ na wʋ sɛ ba zuli varɩm wʋm naa o kamɔgɔ kʋm tɩn. Ba nan wʋ sɛ ba kɩ varɩm wʋm nyɩnyʋgʋ kʋm ba trǝ nɩ naa ba jɩa nɩ. Ba ma joori ba bi ba na ŋwɩa, yɩ ba tɔgɩ ba di paarɩ dɩ Zezi Krisi sɩ kʋ yi bɩna mʋrʋ.

english_verse: These people are the first to be raised to life, and they are especially blessed and holy. The second death has no power over them. They will be priests for God and Christ and will rule with them for
translation_verse: Balʋ maama na tɔgɩ ba wǝli dayigǝ twa biim dɩm wʋnɩ tɩn jɩgɩ yu-yoŋo, yɩ baá ta yɩ Wɛ tɩtɩ nɔɔna. Tʋʋnɩ dɩlʋ na lagɩ dɩ kɩ bɩle tɩn daa bá ja-ba. Bantʋ wʋ́ ta zɩgɩ Wɛ dɩ Zezi Krisi yigǝ nɩ mʋ ba zuli-ba, yɩ baá tɔgɩ dɩ Zezi ba di paarɩ sɩ kʋ yi bɩna mʋrʋ kʋm. Ba cɔgɩ sʋtaanɩ dam maama

english_verse: He will fool the countries of Gog and Magog, which are at the far ends of the earth, and their people will follow him into battle. They will have as many followers as there are grains of sand along the beach,
translation_verse: Dɩ ma wʋ́ vu dɩ ganɩ dwi tiinǝ balʋ na wʋ lʋgʋ baŋa je sɩm maama nɩ tɩn. Tɩɩnɩ dɩm kʋntʋ yɩra mʋ yɩ Gɔgɩ dɩ Magɔgɩ. Sʋtaanɩ ma wʋ́ pa ba la daanɩ sɩ ba kɩ jara, yɩ ba kɔgɔ kʋm nɔn-biǝ wʋ́ ta dagɩ nɩ bugǝ ni kasʋllʋ na yɩ te tɩn.

english_verse: and they will march all the way across the earth. They will surround the camp of God's people and the city God loves. But fire will come down from heaven and destroy the whole army.
translation_verse: Ba ma wʋ́ nuŋi lʋgʋ baŋa je maama nɩ ba vu ba gilimi Wɛ nɔɔna bam kɔgɔ kʋm na lagɩ daanɩ mɛ tɩn. Tɩʋ kʋm kʋntʋ mʋ yɩ kʋlʋ Wɛ na soe zanzan tɩn. Mini laan ma nuŋi wɛyuu nɩ dɩ ba dɩ cɔgɩ Wɛ dʋna bam kɔgɔ kʋm maama.

english_verse: Then the devil who fooled them will be thrown into the lake of fire and burning sulfur. He will be there with the beast and the false prophet, and they will be in pain day and night forever and ever. The Judgment at the Great White Throne
translation_verse: Ba ma daarɩ ba dʋlɩ sʋtaanɩ na ganɩ-ba tɩn ba dɩ min-nɩnɩʋ kʋlʋ na jɩgɩ ciribi tɩn wʋnɩ. Kʋntʋ mʋ yɩ min-nɩnɩʋ kʋlʋ ba na maŋɩ ba dɩ varɩm wʋm dɩ wʋlʋ na brɩ nɩ o yɩ Wɛ nijoŋnu yɩ o yagɩ o daɩ tɩn ba yagɩ kʋ wʋnɩ tɩn. Ba maama wʋ́ ta wʋ mini dɩm wʋnɩ ba yaarɩ wɩa dɩ tɩtɩɩ maama mʋ, sɩ kʋ taa ve maŋa kalʋ na ba ti tɩn. Wɛ na wʋ́ di nɔɔna sarɩya DƖ ma kweeli te tɩn

english_verse: I saw a great white throne with someone sitting on it. Earth and heaven tried to run away, but there was no place for them to go.
translation_verse: Amʋ daa ma na paarɩ jangɔŋ-kamunu kʋlʋ na yɩ napoŋo tɩn dɩ wʋlʋ na je kʋ baŋa nɩ tɩn. Tɩga baŋa dɩ wɛyuu maama ma duri tɩ kɛ o yigǝ nɩ, yɩ tɩ daa tǝrǝ.

english_verse: I also saw all the dead people standing in front of that throne. Every one of them was there, no matter who they had once been. Several books were opened, and then the book of life was opened. The dead were judged by what those books said they had done.
translation_verse: Amʋ ma na balʋ na tɩgɩ tɩn, dɩdɛɛra dɩ nabwǝnǝ maama, ba zɩgɩ paarɩ jangɔŋɔ kʋm yigǝ nɩ. Ba ma puri twaanʋ sɩ ba nii. Ba ma daarɩ ba puri tɔnɔ kʋlʋ na yɩ Wɛ ŋwɩ-dʋŋa kam tɔnɔ kʋm tɩn. Ba ma di twa bam taanɩ sɩ kʋ maŋɩ dɩ ba na kɩ kʋlʋ tɩn, nɩnɛɛnɩ kʋ na pʋpʋnɩ kʋ tiŋi twaanʋ tɩm wʋnɩ te tɩn.

english_verse: The sea gave up the dead people who were in it, and death and its kingdom also gave up their dead. Then everyone was judged by what they had done.
translation_verse: Curu dɩ tʋʋnɩ ma yagɩ balʋ dɩ na jaanɩ tɩn. Na-fara bam dɩ ma pa twa balʋ na maŋɩ ba wʋnɩ tɩn cwǝŋǝ sɩ ba nuŋi. Ba ma di twa bam kʋntʋ maama sarɩya sɩ kʋ maŋɩ dɩ ba na kɩ kʋlʋ tɩn.

english_verse: Afterwards, death and its kingdom were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
translation_verse: Ba laan ma ja Tʋʋnɩ dɩ Curu ba dʋlɩ ba dɩ min-nɩnɩʋ kʋm wʋnɩ. Min-nɩnɩʋ kʋm kʋntʋ yɩ tʋʋnɩ bɩle tu mʋ.

english_verse: Anyone whose name wasn't written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
translation_verse: Nɔɔnʋ wʋlʋ maama yɩrɩ na maŋɩ dɩ wʋ pʋpʋnɩ dɩ kɩ Wɛ ŋwɩ-dʋŋa tɔnɔ kʋm wʋnɩ tɩn, baá dʋlɩ kʋntʋ tu ba dɩ min-nɩnɩʋ kʋm kʋntʋ wʋnɩ mʋ.

english_verse: Three of these gates were on the east, three were on the north, three more were on the south, and the other three were on the west.
translation_verse: Tɩʋ kʋm sɛ sɩm maama jɩgɩ niǝ yatɔ yatɔ mʋ. Yatɔ yɔɔrɩ wa-puli seeni. Yatɔ maa wʋ wa-puli jagwiǝ seeni. Yatɔ maa wʋ wa-puli jazɩm seeni. Yatɔ maa daarɩ ya wʋ wa-zʋʋrɩ seeni.

english_verse: The city was built on twelve foundation stones. On each of the stones was written the name of one of the Lamb's twelve apostles.
translation_verse: Tɩʋ kʋm kǝbrǝ kam kuri ma cwi kandwa-pulwaarʋ fugǝ-tɩle baŋa nɩ. Pǝlbu wʋm tɩntʋŋna fugǝ-bale bam yɩra ma pʋpʋnɩ pulwaarʋ tɩm kʋntʋ yɩra nɩ.

english_verse: The angel who spoke to me had a gold measuring stick to measure the city and its gates and its walls.
translation_verse: Malɛka kalʋ na ŋɔɔnɩ dɩ amʋ tɩn maa ze sǝbu-sɩŋa nacǝgǝ sɩ ka ma maŋɩ tɩʋ kʋm na maɩ te tɩn, dɩ kʋ niǝ yam dɩ kʋ kǝbrǝ kam dɩ na maɩ te tɩn.

english_verse: The city was shaped like a cube, because it was just as high as it was wide. When the angel measured the city, it was about
translation_verse: Tɩʋ kʋm sɛ sɩna sɩm maama mara sɩ mara mʋ. Malɛka kam ma kwe ka nacǝgǝ kam ka ma maŋɩ tɩʋ kʋm. Kʋ saŋa maama dwarɩm maa yɩ kilomɛtra mʋrr-tɩle dɩ biǝ yale (

english_verse: Then the angel measured the wall, and by our measurements it was about
translation_verse: Ka ma daarɩ ka ma ka jɩŋa ka maŋɩ tɩʋ kʋm kǝbrǝ kam. Ka yɩ kantɩa kuni bi dɩ fiinna-bɩna mʋ (

english_verse: the fifth was onyx, the sixth was carnelian, the seventh was chrysolite, the eighth was beryl, the ninth was topaz, the tenth was chrysoprase, the eleventh was jacinth, and the twelfth was amethyst.
translation_verse: Kandwa-pulwaarʋ tɩlʋ tɩʋ kʋm kǝbrǝ kam na cwi tɩ baŋa nɩ tɩn, ba mɛ kandwa-ŋʋna dwi maama mʋ ba ma pʋpʋrɩ tɩ yɩra. Pulɔrɔ maama jɩgɩ kʋ kandwɛ-nyɩnʋ mʋ, yɩ ya yɩra mʋ tɩntʋ:

english_verse: I did not see a temple there. The Lord God All-Powerful and the Lamb were its temple.
translation_verse: Amʋ ma na nɩ Wɛ-digǝ tǝri tɩʋ kʋm wʋnɩ, bɛŋwaanɩ Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Baŋa-Wɛ tɩtɩ dɩ Pǝlbu wʋm mʋ wʋra yɩ nɔɔna zuli-ba.

english_verse: And the city did not need the sun or the moon. The glory of God was shining on it, and the Lamb was its light.
translation_verse: Ba daa ba lagɩ sɩ wɩa dɩ cana daa ta zǝŋi tɩʋ kʋm baŋa nɩ, Wɛ paarɩ-zulǝ yam paɩ tɩʋ kʋm jɩgɩ pooni, yɩ Pǝlbu wʋm dɩ paɩ kʋ jɩgɩ pooni.

english_verse: Nations will walk by the light of that city, and kings will bring their riches there.
translation_verse: Lʋgʋ baŋa dwi tiinǝ maama wʋ́ taa ŋwɩ pooni dɩm kʋntʋ wʋnɩ. Lʋgʋ baŋa pwa bam ma wʋ́ ja ba jɩjɩgɩrʋ ba ba ba kɩ tɩʋ kʋm wʋnɩ.

english_verse: Its gates are always open during the day, and night never comes.
translation_verse: Dɛ maama ba ma daa bá pɩ tɩʋ kʋm niǝ yam, bɛŋwaanɩ tɩga daa bá yi jǝgǝ kam kʋntʋ nɩ.

english_verse: The glorious treasures of nations will be brought into the city.
translation_verse: Ba ma wʋ́ kwe lʋgʋ baŋa dwi tiinǝ zulǝ dɩ ba jɩjɩgɩrʋ maama ba ja ba ba kɩ da.

english_verse: But nothing unworthy will be allowed to enter. No one who is dirty-minded or who tells lies will be there. Only those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will be in the city.
translation_verse: Kʋ daarɩ kʋlʋ maama na jɩgɩ digiru tɩn bá zʋ kʋ wʋ. Nɔɔnʋ wʋlʋ maama na kɩ wo-zɔɔna tɩn dɩ wʋlʋ maama na yɩ vwa-fɔrʋ tɩn bá zʋ kʋ wʋ. Balʋ yɩra na pʋpʋnɩ ya tiŋi Pǝlbu wʋm ŋwɩa tɔnɔ kʋm wʋnɩ tɩn yɩranɩ má mʋ wʋ́ zʋ tɩʋ kʋm kʋntʋ wʋ.

english_verse: The angel showed me a river that was crystal clear, and its waters gave life. The river came from the throne where God and the Lamb were seated.
translation_verse: Malɛka kam ma daarɩ ka brɩ-nɩ bu-tʋla kalʋ na na paɩ ŋwɩa tɩn. Na bam tiini ba lana yɩ ba nyɩɩnɩ nɩ niu te. Bu-tʋla kam na bam maa burǝ ba nuŋi Wɛ dɩ Pǝlbu wʋm paarɩ jangɔŋɔ kʋm tee nɩ ba duri tɩʋ kʋm tɩtarɩ nɩ.

english_verse: Then it flowed down the middle of the city's main street. On each side of the river are trees that grow a different kind of fruit each month of the year. The fruit gives life, and the leaves are used as medicine to heal the nations.
translation_verse: Tiu kʋlʋ biǝ na paɩ ŋwɩa tɩn maa zɩgɩ bu-tʋla kam jazɩm dɩ jagwiǝ nɩ. Tiu kʋm kʋntʋ maa yǝni kʋ lǝri biǝ kuni fugǝ-bɩle bɩm maama wʋnɩ. Cana maama wʋnɩ kʋ lǝri biǝ mʋ. Kʋ vɔɔrʋ tɩm ma maɩ kʋ sooni lʋgʋ baŋa dwi tiinǝ yɩ ba naɩ yazurǝ.

english_verse: God's curse will no longer be on the people of that city. He and the Lamb will be seated there on their thrones, and its people will worship God
translation_verse: Woŋo kʋlʋ maama Wɛ na culi tɩn daa tǝri tɩʋ kʋm kʋntʋ wʋnɩ. Wɛ dɩ Pǝlbu wʋm paarɩ jangɔŋɔ kʋm mʋ wʋ́ ta wʋ tɩʋ kʋm wʋnɩ, yɩ DƖ tɩntʋŋna bam zuli-DƖ.

english_verse: and will see him face to face. God's name will be written on the foreheads of the people.
translation_verse: Baá ta naɩ Wɛ yibiyǝ, yɩ DƖ yɩrɩ dɩm wʋ́ pʋpʋnɩ ba trǝ nɩ.

english_verse: Never again will night appear, and no one who lives there will ever need a lamp or the sun. The Lord God will be their light, and they will rule forever. The Coming of Christ
translation_verse: Tɩga daa bá yi tɩʋ kʋm nɩ. Ba bá ta lagɩ kanɩɩ sɩ sɩ taa zǝŋi pooni, naa wɩa dɩ. Bɛŋwaanɩ Yuutu Baŋa-Wɛ tɩtɩ wʋ́ ta yɩ pooni DƖ pa-ba. Baá ta tɔgɩ ba di paarɩ sɩ kʋ taa ve maŋa kalʋ na ba ti tɩn.

english_verse: Then I was told: These words are true and can be trusted. The Lord God controls the spirits of his prophets, and he is the one who sent his angel to show his servants what must happen very soon.
translation_verse: Malɛka kam daa ma ta dɩ amʋ ka wɩ: «Taanɩ dɩntʋ maama yɩ cɩga mʋ, dɩ maŋɩ sɩ nɔɔna sɛ-dɩ. Yuutu Baŋa-Wɛ mʋ yɩ dɩlʋ na zǝni DƖ nijoŋnǝ bam dɩ DƖ Joro kʋm yɩ ba tɔɔlɩ DƖ kwǝrǝ kam tɩn. Dɩntʋ mʋ tʋŋɩ DƖ malɛka sɩ ka ba ka brɩ DƖ nɔɔna bam, sɩ ba lwarɩ kʋlʋ na lagɩ kʋ kɩ lele tɩn.» Zezi ma bɩɩnɩ lele

english_verse: Remember, I am coming soon! God will bless everyone who pays attention to the message of this book.
translation_verse: Cǝgi-na, Zezi tagɩ o wɩ: «Amʋ ma bɩɩnɩ lele. Balʋ na sɛ Wɛ kwǝrǝ kalʋ na pʋpʋnɩ tɔnɔ kʋntʋ wʋnɩ tɩn jɩgɩ yu-yoŋo.»

english_verse: My name is John, and I am the one who heard and saw these things. Then after I had heard and seen all this, I knelt down and began to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown it to me.
translation_verse: Amʋ Zan mʋ sɩɩnɩ a ni wǝǝnu tɩm kʋntʋ, yɩ a kwǝri a na-tɩ. Kʋ maama na tu kʋ ba kʋ ti tɩn, a laan ma kuni doonǝ malɛka kalʋ na brɩ-nɩ wǝǝnu tɩm kʋntʋ tɩn yigǝ nɩ sɩ a zuli-ka.

english_verse: But the angel said, Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you. I am the same as a follower or a prophet or anyone else who obeys what is written in this book. God is the one you should worship.
translation_verse: Ka ma ta dɩ amʋ ka wɩ: «Yɩ kɩ kʋntʋ. Amʋ yɩ Wɛ tɩntʋŋnʋ mʋ, nɩ nmʋ dɩ n ko-biǝ balʋ na tɔɔlɩ Wɛ kwǝrǝ kam tɩn dɩ balʋ maama na sɛ kʋlʋ na pʋpʋnɩ tɔnɔ kʋntʋ wʋnɩ tɩn dɩ na yɩ te tɩn. N maŋɩ sɩ n zuli Wɛ mʋ.»

english_verse: Then I was told: I am coming soon! And when I come, I will reward everyone for what they have done.
translation_verse: Cǝgi-na, Zezi tagɩ o wɩ: «A ma bɩɩnɩ lele. A na tuǝ, a laan wʋ́ pa nɔɔnʋ maama ŋwɩɩrʋ tɩlʋ na maŋɩ dɩ o tɩtʋŋa tɩn.

english_verse: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
translation_verse: Amʋ mʋ yɩ pulim dɩ gurim. Amʋ ta mʋ yɩ dayigǝ tu dɩ kwaga tu, amʋ mʋ pulǝ yɩ a gurǝ.»

english_verse: God will bless all who have washed their robes. They will each have the right to eat fruit from the tree that gives life, and they can enter the gates of the city.
translation_verse: Balʋ na zarɩ ba gwaarʋ ba pa tɩ pɩɩrɩ parɩ parɩ tɩn jɩgɩ yu-yoŋo. Bantʋ jɩgɩ cwǝŋǝ sɩ ba di tiu kʋlʋ biǝ na paɩ ŋwɩa tɩn, yɩ ba kwǝri ba jɩgɩ cwǝŋǝ sɩ ba zʋ Wɛ tɩtɩ tɩʋ kʋm wʋ.

english_verse: I am Jesus! And I am the one who sent my angel to tell all of you these things for the churches. I am David's Great Descendant, and I am also the bright morning star.
translation_verse: Zezi tagɩ o wɩ: «Amʋ mʋ tʋŋɩ a malɛka sɩ ka ba ka brɩ abam balʋ na yɩ amʋ kɔgɔ kʋm nɔɔna tɩn wǝǝnu tɩntʋ maama. Amʋ yɩ wʋlʋ kuri na nuŋi Pɛ Davidi dwi dɩm wʋnɩ tɩn. Amʋ yɩ tɩtɩɩtɩ calɩcʋa kalʋ yɩrɩ na yɩ naŋɔgɔ yɩ ka nyɩɩnɩ tɩn.»

english_verse: Here is my warning for everyone who hears the prophecies in this book: If you add anything to them, God will make you suffer all the terrible troubles written in this book.
translation_verse: Amʋ Zan nan lagɩ a kaanɩ balʋ maama na cǝgi wǝǝnu tɩlʋ na pʋpʋnɩ tɔnɔ kʋntʋ wʋnɩ yɩ tɩ yɩ Wɛ kwǝrǝ tɩn. Nɔɔnʋ na wǝli woŋo tɔnɔ kʋntʋ taanɩ dɩm wʋnɩ, Wɛ wʋ́ pa o na yaara yalʋ tɔnɔ kʋm na brɩ tɩn.

english_verse: If you take anything away from these prophecies, God will not let you have part in the life-giving tree and in the holy city described in this book.
translation_verse: Nɔɔnʋ wʋlʋ nan na lɩ woŋo tɔnɔ kʋntʋ wʋnɩ dɩ o yagɩ tɩn, Wɛ wʋ́ lɩ o dɩ yigǝ DƖ yagɩ, sɩ o yɩ da o di tiu kʋlʋ biǝ na paɩ ŋwɩa tɩn naa o tɔgɩ o zʋ Wɛ tɩtɩ tɩʋ kʋm wʋ nɩ tɔnɔ kʋntʋ na brɩ te tɩn.

english_verse: The one who has spoken these things says, “I am coming soon!” So, Lord Jesus, please come soon!
translation_verse: Wʋlʋ na zɩgɩ wǝǝnu tɩm kʋntʋ cɩga kam kwaga nɩ tɩn mʋ tɛ o wɩ: «Kʋ yɩ cɩga mʋ. A ma bɩɩnɩ lele.» Amina. Dɩ́ Yuutu Zezi, nan ba.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord Jesus will be kind to all of you.
translation_verse: Dɩbam Yuutu Zezi yu-yoŋo kʋm wʋ́ ta wʋ abam maama tee nɩ.

english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Boboa kam ne to mo Wɛ naane wɛyuu de tega baŋa.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Tega baŋa kam maama déem jage jeiga maama mo. Kolokolo ya ta tera ka baŋa ne. Na-fɔrɔ kom baŋa maama ye lim yerane. Wɛ Siu kom maa kare wɛɛne ko via na bam baŋa ne.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma ta o we, “Pa se pwooni taa wora!” Pwooni ma seene de ba.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Wɛ ma na we pwooni dem lana, ye o wo pwoli. O déem ma pa se pwooni dem de lim dem pɔɔre daane.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Wɛ déem ma bwoŋi pwooni dem we ‘wea’, ye o daare o bwoŋi lim dem we ‘tete’. Tega ma ba ka yi ye ka daare ka poore. Boboa dɛ dem mo konto.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Wɛ déem daa ma ta o we, “Pa se laŋa taa wora na bam tetare ne se ba pɔɔre yera yera kuni belei.”

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Wɛ ma bwoŋi laŋa kam we ‘wɛyuu’. Tega ma ba ka yi ye ka daare ka poore. Da yalei dɛ dem mo konto.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Wɛ daa ma ta o we, “Pa se na balo na wo wɛyuu kom kuri ne to la ba tigisi jeiga dedoa ba daare se te-kora taa wora.” Ko ma seene ko ke konto.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma bwoŋi te-kora kam we ‘tega baŋa’, ye o daare o bwoŋi na-fɔrɔ kom na lage daane to we ‘naneo’. Wɛ ma na we ko lana, ye o wo pwoli.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Tega kam maa puli ga-lɛɛro dwi maama, de teeni dwi maama na leiri bia to, dedaane te wo-dwa dwi dwi. Wɛ ma na we, o na ke kolo to lana, ye o wo pwoli.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Tega ma ba ka yi ye ka daare ka poore. Da yatɔ dɛ dem mo konto.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Wɛ daa ma ta o we, “Pa se wonnu telo na nyeene to dwi dwi taa wo wɛyuu kom ne se te pɔɔre wea de tete daane. Te wó taa ye memaŋa te bere yadɛ dedaane te-pwoŋa. Te ta wó taa bere da yam, de bena yam, dedaane chane sem maŋa maama.

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Te wó taa nyeene wɛyuu ne se te taa pae pwooni tega kam baŋa ne.” Ko ma seene ko ke konto.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem ma ke wo-nyen-kamuna yalei pa se kolo na nyeene ko gaale to yeini ko taa nyeena wea ne, ye kolo na muri to taa nyeena tete ne. O daa ta ma ke chalechwe sem de o woli da.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Wɛ ma ke wo-nyenno tem konto o zege wɛyuu ne se te taa pae pwooni yi tega kam baŋa.

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Te wó taa nii wea de tete baŋa ne ye te ta wó pɔɔre pwooni de lim daane. Wɛ ma na we, o na ke kolo to lana, ye o wo pwoli.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Tega ma ba ka yi ye ka daare ka poore. Da yana dɛ dem mo konto.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Wɛ daa ma ta o we, “Pa se na-fɔrɔ kom wo su de wonnu telo na ŋwe to dwi maama, se zuna de taa jaana ba beera wɛyuu kom jei sem maama ne.”

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem ma naane naneo wo vare-kamuna de wonnu telo na kare te yɛ na wone to dwi maama. O ta ma naane zuna balo na kare ba jaane wɛyuu ne to ba dwi ba dwi. Wɛ ma na we, o na ke kolo to lana, ye o wo pwoli.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma daare o swɛ te maama swolim ye o we, “Ta‑á lore-na á puli á su naneero tem wo maama. Nam ta pa se zuna bam de puli ba taa daga logo baŋa ne.”

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Tega ma ba ka yi ye ka daare ka poore. Da yanu dɛ dem mo konto.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Wɛ daa ta ma ta o we, “Pa se tega kam baŋa taa jege wonnu telo na ŋwe to dwi dwi, sɔŋɔ vara de ga-vara, de tega-veila dwi maama.” Ko ma seene ko ke konto.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem ma ke logo baŋa vara bam konto, ba dwi ba dwi, kago-vara de sɔŋɔ vara, de tega-veila dwi maama. Wɛ ma na we, o na ke kolo to lana, ye o wo pwoli.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Wɛ laam maa we, “Pa-na se dé mɔ nabiina se ba taa nye de debam, ye ba jege debam tete kamɔgɔ. Banto wó taa jege dam ba taa tei naneo wo ywona yam, de wɛyuu zuna bam, dedaane vara de wonnu telo maama na kare te vei tega kam baŋa ne to.”

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem ma seene o naane nabiina se ba taa jege o tete kamɔgɔ. O déem naane-ba baaro de kaane mo.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: O ma swɛ ba swolim, ye o ta de-ba we, “Ta‑á lore-na bia á puli dedɛ se á jage tega baŋa maama ne se á daare á ta‑á tei-ko. Ta‑á di-na dam naneo wo ywona yam, dedaane wɛyuu zuna bam, de wonnu telo maama na kare te vei tega ne to baŋa ne.”

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Ko daare ko ná ye logo baŋa vara bam maama, de wɛyuu zuna bam, de wonnu telo maama na jege ŋwea ye te kare te vei tega baŋa ne to, amo kwei gaaro tem de teeni vɔɔro tem mo a pa-te se te taa di.” Ko ma seene ko ke konto.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma fɔge o nii kolo maama o na ke to, ye o na we ko tiini ko lamma. Tega ma ba ka yi ye ka daare ka poore. Da yaredo dɛ dem mo konto.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Wɛ déem dɛ chwoŋa kanto mo o naane wɛyuu de tega baŋa dedaane kolo maama na wo te wone to o ba o ti maama.

english_verse: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
translation_verse: Taane dento mo bere Wɛ na naane wɛyuu de tega baŋa ye ko ke tetei to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ déem na ke wɛyuu de tega baŋa o ti to,

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: gaaro de teeni ta tera tega kam baŋa ne se te taa pae wodiiru. Kolokolo ya ta wo puli, kolo ŋwaane Wɛ daa ta wo pɛ se doa ne tega baŋa ne. Nabiinu de ya daa ta tera se o va tega kam.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ déem ma fɔ tega kam teero o ma o mɔ nabiinu. O ma daare o fuli o siu kom na pae ŋwea to, o yage baaro wom momwa ne, pa se o laam jege ŋwea.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ke teeni kara Eden ne, wɛ-puli jei sem seeni. O ma daare o kwei o na mɔɔne baaro wolo to o ja vo o yage dáane.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: O ma pa se teeni dwi dwi nwoŋi teeni kara kam ne, de na tiini de lamma yi ne ye de leiri bia na maŋe de dim to. Kara kam tetare ne mo Wɛ déem pɛ se teeni delei nwoŋi de zege da. De dedoa déem ye tio kolo na pae nɔɔna ŋwea to. Kodwoŋi kom maa ye tio kolo na pae nɔɔna lɔre lane de lwarem ba pɔɔre daane to.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Bu-tole sena sem yiga tu yere mo Pison. Kanto mo gugwoli ka kaare Havila laŋa kam maama. Dáane mo sabu-seŋa wora,

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Bu-tola kalo na saŋe to yere maa ye Gihon. Kanto de ma gugwoli ka kaare Kusi laŋa kam maama.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Batɔ tu wom yere mo ye Tigirisi. Kanto duri ka tole Asiria laŋa kam wɛ-puli jei sem seeni mo. Bu-tola kalo na ke sena to maa ye Yuferata buga kam.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ja baaro wom o vo o yage Eden teeni kara kam ne se o taa toŋe da ye o nii ka baŋa ne.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma pa baaro wom ni we, “Nmo jege chwoŋa se n di teeni bia balo maama na leiri kara kam ne to.

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: Se ko daare tio kolo na pae se nɔɔna lɔre lane de lwarem ba pɔɔre daane to, n dae se n di ko bia bam. Ta‑n yei we, dɛ delo nmo na wó di ko bia to, dento dɛ dem ne mo n lage n te.”

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta o we, “Baaro wom na wora o yerane konto to, ko ba lamma. Konto ŋwaane amo wó ke zeinnu wolo na wó maŋe ded‑o to mo a pa‑o.”

english_verse: So the Lord took some soil and made animals and birds. He brought them to the man to see what names he would give each of them. Then the man named the tame animals and the birds and the wild animals. That's how they got their names. None of these was the right kind of partner for the man.
translation_verse: Baaro wom déem ma pa vara bam dwi maama ba yera, sɔŋɔ-vara de kago-vara maama, ye o ta pa wɛyuu zuna bam dwi maama ba de yera. De konto maama wone to, zeinnu déem tera se o maŋe ded‑o.

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa se baaro wom tiini o dɔ dɔɔm o beiri. O na tigi o dɔa konto to, mo Wɛ le o saŋa kwi sem kua dedoa ye o jwoori o suuri jei sem de ya-nɔna.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: O ma kwei baaro wom saŋa kua kam o ma o mɔ kaane. O ma daare o ja‑o o ja ba baaro wom tei.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Baaro wom laam ma ta o we, “Nii mo! Amo tete dwi dem mo tento! Nmo mɛ amo kua mo n ma‑n ke wonto kwi sem, ye n daare n ma a ya-nɔna yam n ma‑n ke wonto yera yam. Ba wó taa bwoi‑o we ‘kaane’ mo, ba na le‑o baaro yera yam ne to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri pa se baaro ná di kaane, o boboŋa daa ba tɔge o kwo de o nu boboŋa. O laam yeini o me de o kaane wom mo se banto balei ji yera dedoa.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Baaro wom de o kaane wom maama déem maa kare ba beeri kalambwolo mo, ye chaveera ba jege-ba.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Ga-vara balo maama Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ déem na mɔɔne to, wolo na jege swa o dwoi ba maama to ye basankwea mo. Dɛ dedwe ka ma zaŋe ka bwei kaane wom ka we, “Wɛ seene o ta de abam we á yé zaŋe á di tio-bia balo maama na wo teeni kara kam wone to na? Ko ye chega na?”

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “Aawo. Dé jege chwoŋa se dé di teeni delo maama bia na wo kara kam wone to.

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: Ko daare ko ná ye tio kolo na zege kara kam tetare ne to yerane, Wɛ tage o we, dé yé zaŋe dé di ko bia naa dé dwei-ko de. Dé ná ke konto, dé wó te mo.”

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Basankwea kam ma leiri ka we, “Aawo, abam bá seene á te!

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: Chega to, Wɛ pɛ abam ni konto dwoŋi kokuri o yei we, abam ná di tio kom konto bia bam dedoa, á wo wó poore dɛ dem konto ne pa se á ta‑á nye de Wɛ tete ye á yei lane de lwarem pɔɔrem daane.”

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma na we tio kom lamma o yi ne, ye o ta na we ko bia wó taa ywomma se nɔɔno di-ba. O fera ma zo tio-bia bam se o wane o ja yi-poro ba ŋwaane. O na boŋe konto to, o ma gwori tio kom bu o di. O ma daare badwonna o pa o baro wom na wo o takeiri ne to ye o de di.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Konto nɛ sem ni ne mo ba yia seene ya poore, ye ba lɔre we ba zege da kalambwolo. Ba ma gwoni kaporo vɔɔro ba pane-te ba liŋi se ba ma kwoli ba chaveera.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Wɛ-zoore maŋa ne, Baŋa Wɛ maa kare teeni kara kam wone o via. Baaro wom de o kaane wom ma ni ko na dɔne to ye ba seigi ba tete teeni dem tetare ne se Wɛ yé zaŋe o na-ba.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ ma bwoŋi baaro wom ye o we, “Nmo wo yei ne mo?”

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: O ma leiri o we, “A nigi nmo dɔnne mo teeni kara kam ne ye foone jege-ne de a na zege da kalambwolo to ŋwaane. Konto mo pɛ se a duri a seigi.”

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo ke tɛ mo n lɔre we n ye kalambwolo mo? Wɔ mo tage konto o bere‑m? Nmo ga n dia tio kolo bia amo na we n ba jege chwoŋa se n di-ba to mo na?”

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Baaro wom ma leiri o we, “Ko ye kaane wolo wom nmo na yage‑o amo tei ne to mo pɛ-ne tio kom bu ye a di.”

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei kaane wom o we, “Bɛ mo ye nmo ke konto?” Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “Basankwea kam mo gane amo pa se a gwori tio kom bia a di.”

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de basankwea kam o we: “Nmo na ke konto to ŋwaane, a le nmo vara maama wone ye a sɔɔle lwarem a yage nmo baŋa ne. Nmo laam wó ta‑n fɛɛle n puga baŋa ne ye teero yerane mo wó taa ye nmo ni-wodiu taa wuu, se n ba n te.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se nmo de kaane wom taa done daane. Wonto dwi dem dedaane nmo dwi dem wó taa chuli daane. Wonto dwi dem wó popoge n yuu ye nmo de wó done o dwi dem de nakila.”

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma daare o ta de kaane wom o we, “Ko ná ye nmo, amo wó pa se n cham dem puli pu-jare baŋa ne. Nmo wó tiini n yaare mo bu-lore wone. De ko de, nmo fera wó taa wo nmo baro wom wone ye wonto nam wó taa tei‑m.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: O ma ta de baaro wom o we, “Nmo na sɛ n kaane wom ni ye n de di tio kolo bia a na we n yé zaŋe n di-ba to ŋwaane, amo wó sɔɔle lwarem a yage tega kam baŋa ne nmo ŋwaane. Nmo ŋwea maama wone, nmo wó yaare ko chɛ de tega kam varem mo, se n laam ba n na n ni-wodiu.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Sabare de ga-cheiŋo dwi dwi wó nwoŋi tega kam baŋa ne te daane‑m. Nmo wó ta‑n kare n beeri gaao wone se n na n ni-wodiu.

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.

english_verse: Seven days later a flood began to cover the earth.

translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta ded‑o we, “Nam ja na-chwɛ, de bo-chwɛ, de pi-bala, te maama na ye bena yatɔ yatɔ to, n ja n ba. Ta ta‑n jege kunkwoŋa de kunkwon-puuri n woli da.”

english_verse: Abram obeyed the Lord. Then he cut the animals in half and laid the two halves of each animal opposite each other on the ground. But he did not cut the doves and pigeons in half.
translation_verse: Abaram ma ja vara bam konto maama o ba Wɛ yiga ne, ye o chɛ te maama yalei yalei, se ko ná ye zuna bam, o déem wo chɛ tento. O laam ma tigisi-te pa se chichworo maama pipiri ko jeeri kodwoŋi kom.

english_verse: And when birds came down to eat the animals, Abram chased them away.
translation_verse: Duura ma ba se ba di nɔna yam konto. Abaram ma zeili-ba o yage.

english_verse: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and everything became dark and frightening.
translation_verse: Wɛ na wora de zoore to mo Abaram dɔ o beiri. Ko ma tiini ko ke biramm ko kaare mɛ o na wora to ye foone jege‑o.

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Abram, you will live to an old age and die in peace. But I solemnly promise that your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that doesn't belong to them. They will be forced into slavery and abused for
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye nmo tete, amo wó pa se n ta‑n ŋwe ŋwea de yazura mo se n laam te n kokweero maŋa ne.

english_verse: Four generations later, your descendants will return here and take this land, because only then will the people who live here be so sinful that they deserve to be punished.
translation_verse: Dwia yana laŋa ne mo nmo dwi dem laam wó jwoori ba ba ba taa zoore ywo. Kanto maŋa kam mo wó taa ye maŋa kalo Amori tiina bam keim-lwanno na daga ye te yi se a waare-ba to. Maŋa kam ta wo yi se a ke konto.”

english_verse: Sometime after sunset, when it was very dark, a smoking cooking pot and a flaming fire passed between the two halves of each animal.
translation_verse: Tega na yi ye jei sem maama ye lim to mo Abaram nɛ kɔlepɔte de de wo mini. O ta ma na daa de ka min-vogo, ye mina yam konto maama laam ma tɔge nɔna yalo Abaram déem na tigisi to chichworo maama tetare ne ya kɛa.

english_verse: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Dento dɛ dem ne Baŋa Wɛ ma ke ni-gwonim dedaane Abaram ye o we, “Ko ye nmo dwi dem mo a na lage a pa-ba tega kanto, ka na zege Ejipti nabara kam laŋa ne, se ka taa vei Yuferata bu-zaŋa kam seeni to.

english_verse: They will possess the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
translation_verse: Ko déem ye Keni tiina tega kam, de Kenizi tiina bam, de Kadimon tiina bam,

english_verse: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaites,
translation_verse: de Hiti tiina bam, de Pɛrizi tiina bam, de Refayi tiina bam,

english_verse: Abram's wife Sarai had not been able to have any children. But she owned a young Egyptian slave woman named Hagar,
translation_verse: Abaram kaane Sarai déem nam ya wo loge bu o pa‑o. O déem nam ya jege ka-nyaane mo, o na ye Ejipti tiina bukɔ. Ka-nyaane wom yere déem mo ye Hagara.

english_verse: and Sarai said to Abram, “The Lord has not given me any children. Sleep with my slave, and if she has a child, it will be mine.” Abram agreed,
translation_verse: O na wo loge to ŋwaane o ma ta de o baro Abaram we, “Baŋa Wɛ chege amo de bu-lore. Nam véi n peini de a ka-nyaane wom, se dɛ delo ko wó tɔge wonto baŋa ne mo se amo na dwi.” Abaram ma sɛ Sarai na tage tei to.

english_verse: and Sarai gave him Hagar to be his wife. This happened after Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years.
translation_verse: Ka maŋa kam ne, Abaram déem zo Kanaan teo kom ne bena fuga mo. Sarai ma kwei o ka-nyaane Hagara o pa‑o se o ma o ji o kaane.

english_verse: Later, when Hagar knew she was going to have a baby, she became proud and treated Sarai hatefully.
translation_verse: O ma peini de Hagara, ye o ja puga. Hagara ma na nɛ we o jege puga to, o daa maa ba nege Sarai.

english_verse: Then Sarai said to Abram, “It's all your fault! I gave you my slave woman, but she has been hateful to me ever since she found out she was pregnant. You have done me wrong, and you will have to answer to the Lord for this.”
translation_verse: Ko ma pa Sarai ta de Abaram we, “Nmo mo pɛ se amo jege yaara yanto maama a di, kokuri to, a kwei a ka-nyaane a ke n jeŋa ne. O laam na nɛ we o jege puga to, o daa ba nege amo. Baŋa Wɛ mo wó di debam balei taane dento, ko ná ye amo yiga naa nmo yiga mo.”

english_verse: Hagar stopped to rest at a spring in the desert on the road to Shur. While she was there, the angel of the Lord came to her
translation_verse: Hagara ma vo o zo kagoa kam wone o vo o yi buli-yi. Ko déem bwola de Sura chwoŋa kam mo. Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam laam ma ba o tei,

english_verse: and asked, “Hagar, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She answered, “I'm running away from Sarai, my owner.”
translation_verse: ye ka we, “Sarai ka-nyaane Hagara, nmo nwoŋi yei ne mo tento, ye n nam ma n vei yei mo?” O ma leiri we, “A maa dura se a lu a tu Sarai jeŋa ne mo.”

english_verse: I will give you a son, who will be called Ishmael, because I have heard your cry for help. And someday I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them all.
translation_verse: Maleka kam ma ta ded‑o ka woli da ka we: “Nmo laam zege de puga mo tento se n lo bakeira. Nmo jege se n pa o yere we ‘Isameli’, kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ nigi n wo-chechɔgɔ kom.

english_verse: But your son will live far from his relatives; he will be like a wild donkey, fighting everyone, and everyone fighting him.”
translation_verse: O wó taa ye nenɛɛne bonaga kalo ba na bá wane ba ja-ka to mo. O bá taa lage nɔn-dwi maama taane, ye nɔɔna maama de bá taa lage o taane. Wonto de o chorro wó taa chuli daane mo.”

english_verse: Hagar thought, “Have I really seen God and lived to tell about it?” So from then on she called him, “The God Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Hagara na nigi maleka kam konto to, o ma boŋe o tete ne we, “Amo yia seene ya na Baŋa Wɛ wolo na nae amo to.” O ma kwei yere dento o pa Baŋa Wɛ we ‘Wɛ wolo na nae amo to.’

english_verse: That's why people call the well between Kadesh and Bered, “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo ba déem pɛ vole dem konto yere we ‘Beeri Lahayi Royi’. Vole dem ta wora tento, de zege Kadese de Bereda tetare laŋa ne mo.

english_verse: I will keep my solemn promise to you and give you more descendants than can be counted.”
translation_verse: Amo maa wó pa se ni-gwonim delo a dedaane nmo na ke daane to zege chekke, ye a pa se nmo dwi puli de kɔgɔ dedɛ.”

english_verse: Abram bowed with his face to the ground, and God said:
translation_verse: Abaram ma vwi o yibia tega ne se o zuli Wɛ, ye Wɛ ta ded‑o we,

english_verse: I promise that you will be the father of many nations. So now I'm changing your name from Abram to Abraham.
translation_verse: Ba daa bá taa bwoi nmo we Abaram, nmo yere laam wó taa ye Abaraham mo, kokuri to, a pɛ se nmo ji dwi tiina dedɛ nabaaro mo.

english_verse: I will give you a lot of descendants, and they will become great nations. Some of them will even be kings.
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se n na dwi dedɛ. A wó pa se teene nwoŋi nmo yera ne. Pwa maa wó taa wora nmo dwi dem wone.

english_verse: I will give you and them the land in which you are now a foreigner. I will give the whole land of Canaan to your family forever, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Kanaan tiina tega kanto mɛ nmo ta na ye veiru tento to, mo amo lage a kwei a pa nmo de n dwi dem se á ta‑á tei se ko taa vei wuu. Amo wó taa ye banto de Wɛ.”

english_verse: As the sign that you are keeping this promise, you must circumcise every man and boy in your family.
translation_verse: Abam jege se á ta‑á ke peina gwonim mo á yera yam ne. Konto mo wó taa ye memaŋe delo na bere we dé ke ni-gwonim daane.

english_verse: Any man who isn't circumcised hasn't kept his part of the promise and cannot be one of my people.
translation_verse: Ba ná wo gwoni baaro wolo maama peini, kotu daa bá tɔge o woli Isarele dwi dem wone, o na chɔge amo ni-gwonim dem to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Abraham, from now on your wife's name will be Sarah instead of Sarai.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta de Abaraham we, “Ko daare nmo kaane Sarai, daa‑n yé ta‑n bwoi‑o we Sarai, o yere laam ye Sarah mo.

english_verse: I will bless her, and you will have a son by her. She will become the mother of nations, and some of her descendants will even be kings.
translation_verse: A lage a ke zaane mo a ke o yuu ne. A nam lage a tɔge wonto baŋa ne mo a pa nmo bakeira. Amo wó swɛ o swolim se o taa ye teene dedɛ nu. Teene dedɛ pwa mo lage ba nwoŋi wonto wone.”

english_verse: However, I have heard what you asked me to do for Ishmael, and so I will also bless him with many descendants. He will be the father of twelve princes, and I will make his family a great nation.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Isameli taane dem, a niga n na tage tei to. Amo wó swɛ wonto de swolim. Amo wó pa se o dwi puli o na kɔgɔ dedɛ. Pwa fuga-balei mo wó taa wo ba wone, ye ba ji te-zɔŋɔ.

english_verse: But your son Isaac will be born about this time next year, and the promise I am making to you and your family will be for him and his descendants forever.
translation_verse: A ni-gwonim dem mo a laam za wó pa se de zege dedaane Izaak, wolo wom Sarah na wó lo o pa‑m bene dento maŋa kanto ne to.”

english_verse: God finished speaking to Abraham and then left.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma na ŋɔɔne dedaane Abaraham o ti to, o ma kɛ dáa o tei ne.

english_verse: On that same day Abraham obeyed God by circumcising Ishmael. Abraham was also circumcised, and so were all the other men and boys in his household, including his servants and slaves. He was
translation_verse: Abaraham sɔŋɔ kom baara maama, ko ná ye balo ba na loge-ba dáane, naa balo ba na yeigi veira tei ne to, ba maama mo déem dɛ ded‑o ba gwoni ba peina.

english_verse: One hot summer afternoon while Abraham was sitting by the entrance to his tent near the sacred trees of Mamre, the Lord appeared to him.
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo Abaraham déem na zoore Mamere tei-kamunnu tem teiŋa ne to, dɛ dedwe o maa jei o vwei dem ni ne. Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ba o tei. Maŋa kalo wea na dɔge yupare ne to mo konto.

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. He quickly ran to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground,
translation_verse: Abaraham ma kwoni o yuu wɛɛne ye o na nɔɔna batɔ na zege ba twɛ ded‑o. O na nɛ-ba to, mo o ke lela o zaŋe o vwei dem ni ne o jeeri-ba ye o tiini o chɔɔle o yibia tega ne o jɔɔne-ba.

english_verse: and said, “Please come to my home where I can serve you.
translation_verse: O maa we, “Amo Teiru, nenɛɛne n yi ná su amo kikia, se n yé galese amo baŋa ne n kɛ.

english_verse: I'll have some water brought, so you can wash your feet, then you can rest under a tree.
translation_verse: Sɛ se a ja na fenfee a ba se á ma á zare á nɛ, se á daare á jeini tio konto kuri ne á sii.

english_verse: Let me get you some food to give you strength before you leave. I would be honored to serve you.” “Thank you very much,” they answered. “We accept your offer.”
translation_verse: Abam zuli amo mo ye á ba amo tei. Yage-na se a lage wodiu a pa abam se á di se á yera jwoori se á laam ta‑á kɛa.” Ba ma leiri we, “Tɔ, ke nenɛɛne nmo na tage tei to.”

english_verse: Abraham went quickly to his tent and said to Sarah, “Hurry! Get a large sack of flour and make some bread.”
translation_verse: Abaraham ma ke lela o yi Sarah tei vwei dem ne ye o we, “Ke lela n kwei mun-bwei bwɛ setɔ n viiri n ma n wɔ bworobworo.”

english_verse: After saying this, he rushed off to his herd of cattle and picked out one of the best calves, which his servant quickly prepared.
translation_verse: O daa ta ma ke lela o zo o naane dem wo o kuri na-chwɛ delo na lamma to, o ja o pa o tontoŋena se ba ma ke wodiu lela.

english_verse: He then served his guests some yogurt and milk together with the meat. While they were eating, he stood near them under the tree,
translation_verse: O ta ma kwei nayel-pepala, dedaane nayele-na, de wodiu kom o zege ba yiga ne o pa-ba. Nɔɔna bam déem ma jei ba di ye o zege ba tei ne tio kom kuri ne.

english_verse: and they asked, “Where's your wife Sarah?” “She is right there in the tent,” Abraham answered.
translation_verse: Ba ma bwei‑o we, “Se n kaane Sarah wo yei ne mo?” O de ma leiri we, “O wo vwei dem wone.”

english_verse: Abraham and Sarah were very old, and Sarah was well past the age for having children.
translation_verse: Abaraham de Sarah déem ya maŋe ba kwe ye ba bena yam de gaale. Sarah déem kɛ bu-lore.

english_verse: So she laughed and said to herself, “Now that I am worn out and my husband is old, will I really know such happiness?”
translation_verse: Sarah ma mɔne o wone ye o boŋe boboŋe dento nenɛɛne, “Amo laam na kwaare maŋa kalo ne ye amo diga tu wom de tiini o kwe to mo amo laam lage a ni ywoni dento na?”

english_verse: The Lord asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh? Does she doubt that she can have a child in her old age?
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei Abaraham we, “Bɛŋwaane mo Sarah mɔne ye o daare o ta we ‘A laam na kwe tento to, amo wó wane a lo bu na?’

english_verse: I am the Lord! There is nothing too difficult for me. I'll come back next year at the time I promised, and Sarah will already have a son.”
translation_verse: Woŋo wora ko na tiini ko chamma se amo Baŋa Wɛ toŋe na? Nenɛɛne ka maŋa kam ná yia bene wɛɛne, amo wó jwoori a ba nmo tei, dedaane Sarah laam jege bakeira o jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: Sarah was so frightened that she lied and said, “I didn't laugh.” “Yes, you did!” he answered. Abraham Prays for Sodom
translation_verse: Foone ma ja Sarah ye o fo o ni o we, “Amo wo mɔne.” O de maa we, “Chega to, n mɔne.” Abaraham lwoori Wɛ Sodom ŋwaane

english_verse: When the three men got ready to leave, they looked down toward Sodom, and Abraham walked part of the way with them.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma zaŋe se ba kɛ, ye ba laam guni ba nii Sodom seeni. Abaraham de ma vo se o yage-ba chwoŋa ne se ba de laam taa kɛa.

english_verse: The Lord said to himself, “I should tell Abraham what I am going to do,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o tete ne we, “Ko wó ke tɛ mo se amo seigi a na boŋe se a ke tei to ye Abaraham yeiri ko ni ne?

english_verse: since his family will become a great and powerful nation that will be a blessing to all the other nations on earth.
translation_verse: Abaraham dwi dem wó ji te-zɔŋɔ kolo na dana to mo. Wɛ wó da wonto baŋa ne mo o swɛ logo kom baŋa teene dem maama swolim.

english_verse: I have chosen him to teach his family to obey me forever and to do what is right and fair. If they do, I will give Abraham many descendants, just as I promised.”
translation_verse: Kokuri to, amo mo kuri‑o, se o bere o bia de o sɔŋɔ kom maama na wó saŋe o kwaga ne to, se ba taa tɔge Baŋa Wɛ chwoŋa kam ba daare ba taa toŋe kolo na maŋe de kolo na ye chega to. Konto mo wó pa se amo Baŋa Wɛ na pwooli se a ke tetei maama a pa‑o to wane ko toŋe chekke.”

english_verse: Now I am going down to see for myself if those people really are that bad. If they aren't, I would like to know.”
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo amo lage a vo se a nii, ba totoŋa yam seene ya lwara nenɛɛne nɔɔna keira kam na bere tei to na. Ko ná dae konto, amo wó lɔre ko ni ne.”

english_verse: The men turned and started toward Sodom. But the Lord stayed with Abraham.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balei bam ma pipiri ba kwei Sodom chwoŋa kam ba maa kɛa. Abaraham de déem ma maŋe dáane o zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: And Abraham asked him, “Lord, when you destroy the evil people, are you also going to destroy those who are good?
translation_verse: Abaraham ma vaŋe o tete o twɛ Baŋa Wɛ ye o we, “Konto, nmo wó saare nɔn-laaro tem maama mo n woli de puseŋ-nyena bam na?

english_verse: Abraham answered, “I am nothing more than the dust of the earth. Please forgive me, Lord, for daring to speak to you like this.
translation_verse: Abaraham daa ma ŋɔɔne we, “Amo Teiru, amo dae kolokolo nmo yiga ne. A nye de teero dedaane tentwarem mo. A laam nam nɛ baare se a ŋɔɔne dede‑m.

english_verse: Then Abraham said, “I don't have any right to ask you, Lord, but what would you do if you find only
translation_verse: Abaraham maa we, “Nmo maŋe n pa se a na baare se a ŋɔɔne de nmo. Yage se a bwei a nii, se n ná nɛ nɔɔna finlei mo da?” O de ma ta we, “Finlei kom ŋwaane, a bá chɔge-ko.”

english_verse: After speaking with Abraham, the Lord left, and Abraham went back home.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na ŋɔɔne dedaane Abaraham o ti konto to, o ma viiri. Abaraham de ma jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: That evening, while Lot was sitting near the city gate, the two angels arrived in Sodom. When Lot saw them, he got up, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Malese selo na jeeri Abaraham to selei déem ma ba ba yi Sodom dedaan-ni ne, ye Lot déem jei teo kom manchwo-peena ni ne. O na nɛ-ba to, o ma zaŋe wɛɛne o vo se o jeeri-ba ye o chɔɔle o yibia tega ne o ware-ba.

english_verse: and said, “Gentlemen, I am your servant. Please come to my home. You can wash your feet, spend the night, and be on your way in the morning.” They told him, “No, we'll spend the night in the city square.”
translation_verse: O maa we, “Jan ja! Amo tiina bam, pa-na se a ja abam a yi sɔŋɔ, se á swɛ á yera á daare á peini se tega poore se á laam gwoni tega á vo á na maa vei mɛ to.” Ba de ma leiri we, “Aawo, debam lage dé peini teo kom pwola kanto ne mo.”

english_verse: But Lot kept insisting, until they finally agreed and went home with him. He quickly baked some bread, cooked a meal, and they ate.
translation_verse: O déem na tiini o fe-ba to ŋwaane, ba ma tɔge ded‑o ba zo o sɔŋɔ kom wo. O ma ke bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to o pa-ba ye ba di.

english_verse: Before Lot and his guests could go to bed, every man in Sodom, young and old, came and stood outside his house
translation_verse: Ba na wora ba ti ba yiga se ba peini to, mo Sodom teo kom baara bam maama nwoŋi teo kom jei maama ba ba ba gilimi sɔŋɔ kom, nɔn-kwe dedaane nɔn-donno maama.

english_verse: Lot went outside and shut the door behind him.
translation_verse: Lot ma nwoŋi pwooni se o jeeri teo kom nɔɔna bam ye o daare o pe bworo kom.

english_verse: Then he said, “Friends, please don't do such a terrible thing!
translation_verse: O maa we, “Amo dwonna bam, a lwoori abam se á yé ke totoŋ-lɔŋɔ konto dwoŋi.

english_verse: I have two daughters who have never had sex. I'll bring them out, and you can do what you want with them. But don't harm these men. They are guests in my home.”
translation_verse: Cheigi-na ywo, amo jege bukwa balei balo ta na yeiri baara to. Yage-na se a ja-ba a ba a pa abam, se á ke á na lage tei to de-ba. Yage-na nɔɔna banto yera, kokuri to ba tu ba zo amo woro kuri ne mo.”

english_verse: “Don't get in our way,” the crowd answered. “You're a foreigner. What right do you have to order us around? We'll do worse things to you than we're going to do to them.” The crowd kept arguing with Lot. Finally, they rushed toward the door to break it down.
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri Lot we, “Lage jei dé yiga ne!” Ba daa ta ma ta daane ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto ye veiru mo dé teo kom ne. Bɛ mo ye o lage se o bere debam dé na wó ke kolo to?” Ba laam ma ta de Lot we, “Dé nam wó ke nmo dé dwoni dé na wó ke banto tetei to.” Ba ma tiini ba peene Lot ye ba laam fɔɔre ba twɛ o sɔŋɔ ni dem se ba bwori bworo kom ba zo diga kam wone.

english_verse: Then they struck blind everyone in the crowd, and none of them could even find the door.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma pa se nɔn-kwe sem dedaane nɔn-donno tem maama na wo sɔŋɔ kom ni ne to yia dwei, pa se ba kare ba taana ba yeiri bworo kom jei.

english_verse: The two angels said to Lot, “The Lord has heard many terrible things about the people of Sodom, and he has sent us here to destroy the city. Take your family and leave. Take every relative you have in the city, as well as the men your daughters are going to marry.”
translation_verse: Bɛŋwaane dé lage dé chɔge teo kom mo. Nɔɔna tiini ba keeri ba jare Baŋa Wɛ se ko gaale, teo kom nɔn-bia bam kikia ŋwaane. O ma toŋe debam se dé ba dé chɔge-ko.”

english_verse: Lot went to the men who were engaged to his daughters and said, “Hurry up and get out of here! The Lord is going to destroy this city.” But they thought he was joking, and they laughed at him.
translation_verse: Lot déem ma nwoŋi o vo se o ŋɔɔne de o tembaara balo na chare o bukwa bam se ba swo ba ma ke ba kaana to. O maa we, “Ke-na lela á nwoŋi dáa jei sento ne, kokuri Baŋa Wɛ lage o chɔge teo konto mo!” O tembaara bam déem boŋe we o ŋɔɔne o kwɛɛre mo.

english_verse: Early the next morning the two angels tried to make Lot hurry and leave. They said, “Take your wife and your two daughters and get away from here as fast as you can! If you don't, every one of you will be killed when the Lord destroys the city.”
translation_verse: Te-pora ni ne, malese sem ma ta de Lot ba we, “Ke lela! Ja n kaane wom de n bukwa balei balo na wo ywo to se á nwoŋi da ywo-seeni! Ko ná dae konto, Baŋa Wɛ ná waare teo kom, abam de wó da á na chɔgem.”

english_verse: At first, Lot just stood there. But the Lord wanted to save him. So the angels took Lot, his wife, and his two daughters by the hand and led them out of the city.
translation_verse: Ba na tage konto ye Lot ta zege o dáana to, mo ba chaale o jeŋa, de o kaane wom dedaane o bukwa balei bam jea ba ja ba nwoŋi teo kom dáa ne se ba wane ba lu, Baŋa Wɛ déem na duri ba ŋwaŋa to ŋwaane.

english_verse: When they were outside, one of the angels said, “Run for your lives! Don't even look back. And don't stop in the valley. Run to the hills, where you'll be safe.”
translation_verse: Malese sem na jaane-ba se nwoŋi se ti to mo se dedoa tage we, “Duri-na se á lu chɔgem! Yé nii á kwaga ne, á nam yé zege-na jei jei ne bwolo kom wone! Duri-na á yi peero tem jei sem se abam de yé da á na chɔgem!”

english_verse: Lot answered, “You have done us a great favor, sir. You have saved our lives, but please don't make us go to the hills. That's too far away. The city will be destroyed before we can get there, and we will be killed when it happens.
translation_verse: Abam maŋe á ke amo lanyerane ye á duri a ŋwaŋa pa se a jwoŋi a ŋwea. A bá wane a duri a yi peero tem jei sem. Amo ta ná wo chwoŋa ne, chɔgem dento wó yi amo, se a te.

english_verse: There's a town near here. It's only a small place, but my family and I will be safe, if you let us go there.”
translation_verse: Nam nii teo kodwoŋi mo tento bwola bwola a na wó wane a duri a yi da. Ko maa ye te-balaŋa mo. Á wo nɛ na? Pa-ne pwola se a duri a vo dáane, se konto mo a wó lu.”

english_verse: “All right, go there,” he answered. “I won't destroy that town.
translation_verse: O ma ta ded‑o we, “Amo sɛ se a ke konto de a pa‑m. A bá chɔge teo kom konto.

english_verse: Hurry! Run! I can't do anything until you are safely there.” The town was later called Zoar because Lot had said it was small. Sodom and Gomorrah Are Destroyed
translation_verse: Nam ke lela n duri n vo n yi da, kokuri to amo bá wane a ke kolokolo ye nmo wo lugi.” Teo kom na ye balaŋa to ŋwaane mo ba bwoi-ko we Zoara.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Lot reached the town of Zoar,
translation_verse: Lot déem ma vo o yi Zoara dedaane wɛ maŋe de puli mo.

english_verse: He destroyed those cities and everyone who lived in them, as well as their land and the trees and grass that grew there.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem tɔge konto mo o ma chɔge teene dem konto dedaane jei sem maama, ko woli de balo maama na zoore teene dem konto ne to dedaane tega kam wonnu telo maama na nwoŋi ka baŋa ne to.

english_verse: On the way, Lot's wife looked back and was turned into a block of salt.
translation_verse: Lot kaane déem ma gwi o nii o kwaga ne. O ma ji yɛ-kuŋa kandwɛ o zege da.

english_verse: That same morning Abraham got up and went to the place where he had stood and spoken with the Lord.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Abaraham ma gwoni tega o jwoori o vo o ya na zege mɛ Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to.

english_verse: When God destroyed the cities of the valley where Lot lived, he remembered his promise to Abraham and saved Lot from the terrible destruction. Moab and Ammon
translation_verse: Wɛ na chɔge teene dem de bwolo kom maama to, o déem guli Abaraham gula ye o vere Lot o ja nwoŋi cham delo na chɔge jei sem konto maama to. Lot de o bukwa bam taane

english_verse: Lot was afraid to stay on in Zoar. So he took his two daughters and moved to a cave in the hill country.
translation_verse: Lot de o bukwa balei bam laam ma nwoŋi Zoara teo kom ne ba vo ba jeini peero tem wone, kokuri o déem kɔre se o zo Zoara ne. Ba maa zoore peo bɔɔne wone.

english_verse: One day his older daughter said to her sister, “Our father is old, and there are no men anywhere for us to marry.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo bukɔ-kwea kam tage de balaŋa kam we, “Debam kwo wom kwe mo, ye baaro nam tera ywo se o peini de debam nenɛɛne logo baŋa nabiina maama na yeini ba ke tei to.

english_verse: Let's get our father drunk! Then we can sleep with him and have children.”
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, yage se dé pa dé kwo wom nyɔ sana o bugi se dé laam peini ded‑o, se dé kwo wom dwi yé kweeli.”

english_verse: That night they got their father drunk, and the older daughter got in bed with him, but he was too drunk even to know she was there.
translation_verse: Dento tete dem ne, ba ma pa ba kwo nyɔ sana o su. Bukɔ-kwea kam ma zo o peini ded‑o. O kwo wom maa wo maane o na zo o peini ded‑o naa o na zaŋe o nwoŋi maŋa kalo to.

english_verse: The next day the older daughter said to her sister, “I slept with my father last night. We'll get him drunk again tonight, so you can sleep with him, and we can each have a child.”
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, bukɔ-kwea kam ma ta de balaŋa kam we, “Amo de dé kwo diim peini daane mo. Yage se zem tete dento dé daa pa se o nyɔ sana o bugi, se nmo de vo n peini ded‑o se ko pa dé tɔge dé kwo baŋa ne dé twoŋi dé dwi dem.”

english_verse: That night they got their father drunk, and this time the younger sister slept with him. But once again he was too drunk even to know she was there.
translation_verse: Ba ma seene ba pa se ba kwo wom nyɔ sana o su dento tete dem ne. Bukɔ-balaŋa kam de ma vo o peini ded‑o, ye o kwo wom ta wo maane o na zo o peini ded‑o naa o na zaŋe o nwoŋi maŋa kalo to.

english_verse: That's how Lot's two daughters had children.
translation_verse: Lot bukwa bam déem ma ja pwi de ba kwo wom.

english_verse: The older daughter named her son Moab, and he is the ancestor of the Moabites.
translation_verse: Bukɔ-kwea kam ma lo bakeira, ye o pa o yere we ‘Moaba’. Wonto mo ye Moaba tiina bam nabaaro zem dɛ dem ne.

english_verse: The younger daughter named her son Benammi, and he is the ancestor of the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Bukɔ-balaŋa kam de ma lo bakeira, ye o pa o yere we ‘Ben-Ammi’. Wonto mo ye Amon tiina bam nabaaro zem dɛ dem ne.

english_verse: he told everyone that his wife Sarah was his sister. So King Abimelech of Gerar had Sarah brought to him.
translation_verse: O na wora to mo Abaraham tage o kaane Sarah taane we, o ye o nakɔ. Gerare teo kom pɛ Abimeleka ma toŋe Sarah kwaga ne ye o jwoŋi‑o se o ma o ke o kaane.

english_verse: But God came to Abimelech in a dream and said, “You have taken a married woman into your home, and for this you will die!”
translation_verse: Tete dedwe ne Baŋa Wɛ ma ba Abimeleka tei dendwɛ wone o ta ded‑o we, “Nmo ye too mo, kaane wom n na kwei to na ye nɔɔno kaane to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Abimelech said to the Lord, “Don't kill me! I haven't slept with Sarah. Didn't they say they were brother and sister? I am completely innocent.”
translation_verse: Abaraham mo tage de amo we ‘Kaane wom ye a nakɔ mo’, ye kaane wom de ta we ‘O ye a nabɔ’. Amo ke tento de a bochare-laao mo. A jea de ba jege digiru.”

english_verse: Her husband is a prophet. Let her go back to him, and his prayers will save you from death. But if you don't return her, you and all your people will die.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ye amo ni-jwoŋinu mo. Konto ŋwaane, jwoori n pa‑o o kaane wom se o daare o lwoori amo o pa‑m se n ta‑n ŋwe. Ko daare n ná wo ke konto, nmo wó seene n te, de n nɔɔna maama.”

english_verse: Early the next morning Abimelech sent for his officials, and when he told them what had happened, they were frightened.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Abimeleka ma gwoni tega o bwoŋi o nɔɔna bam, ye o daare o lwoni kolo maama na ke to o bere-ba. Ba na nigi to, foone ma tiini de ja-ba.

english_verse: Abimelech then called in Abraham and said: Look what you've done to us! What have I ever done to you? Why did you make me and my nation guilty of such a terrible sin?
translation_verse: Abimeleka ma bwoŋi Abaraham pa se o zo ba tei ye o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo nmo ke debam konto? Bɛ lwarem mo a ke‑m ye nmo laam ja chɔgem n ba amo de a teo kom baŋa ne? Nmo na ke n chɔge amo yiga tei to ba lana.”

english_verse: What were you thinking when you did this?
translation_verse: O ta ma bwei Abaraham we, “Bɛ mo pɛ se n ke konto?”

english_verse: Abraham answered: I did it because I didn't think any of you respected God, and I was sure that someone would kill me to get my wife.
translation_verse: Abaraham laam ma leiri we, “Amo ya boŋe we, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba kɔre Wɛ jei sento ne, ye ba wó wane ba go-ne, a kaane wom ŋwaane.

english_verse: Besides, she is my half sister. We have the same father, but different mothers.
translation_verse: O ta ye a nakɔ mo. Dé dae nu daane mo se o ye a kwo wom bukɔ mo, ye o laam ji amo kaane.

english_verse: When God made us leave my father's home and start wandering, I told her, “If you really love me, then tell everyone that I am your brother.”
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo Wɛ na pɛ se a nwoŋi a kwo sɔŋɔ kom ne ye a kare a beeri to, mo a tage ded‑o we ‘Sarah, ke tento se n bere we n swoi amo: Mɛ maama debam ná vei de yi, se nmo ta we, a ye n nabɔ mo.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, God had kept Abimelech's wife and slaves from having children. But Abraham prayed, and God let them start having children again.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem ya cheiŋi nɔɔna maama de bu-lore mo Abimeleka sɔŋɔ kom ne, Abaraham kaane Sarah ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Lord was good to Sarah and kept his promise.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem nii Sarah baŋa ne ye o seene o ke kolo o na tage ded‑o to o pa‑o.

english_verse: Although Abraham was very old, Sarah had a son exactly at the time God had said.
translation_verse: Sarah déem ma ja puga o lo bakeira o pa Abaraham o kokweero maŋa ne. Ko déem ke ko maŋe de maŋa kalo Wɛ na tage to mo.

english_verse: Abraham named his son Isaac,
translation_verse: Abaraham ma pa bu wom yere we ‘Izaak’.

english_verse: and when the boy was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, just as God had commanded.
translation_verse: Izaak na yi da nana to mo Abaraham gwoni o peini, nenɛɛne Wɛ na tage we o ke tei to.

english_verse: Who would have dared to tell Abraham that someday I would have a child? But in his old age, I have given him a son.”
translation_verse: O daa ta ma woli da o we, “Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ya bá wane o ta de Abaraham we Sarah wó wane o ja bia se ba ŋɔge yele. De konto maama de, amo loge bakeira a pa‑o o kokweero maŋa ne.” Ba zeili Hagara dedaane Isameli ba yage

english_verse: The time came when Sarah no longer had to nurse Isaac, and on that day Abraham gave a big feast. Hagar and Ishmael Are Sent Away
translation_verse: Izaak ma ke nɔɔno ye ba kwori‑o yele. Dɛ dem konto ne, Abaraham ma bwoŋi nɔɔna se ba di kuri kamunu.

english_verse: One day, Sarah noticed Hagar's son Ishmael playing, and she said to Abraham, “Get rid of that Egyptian slave woman and her son! I don't want him to inherit anything. It should all go to my son.”
translation_verse: O na nɛ to, o ma ta de Abaraham we, “Zeili kaane wolo na ye kabaa to de o bu-baaro wom se ba viiri, se kaane wonto bu wom bá tɔge de amo tete bu Izaak o pɔɔre nmo jejegero tem o taa tei.”

english_verse: But God said, “Abraham, don't worry about your slave woman and the boy. Just do what Sarah tells you. Isaac will inherit your family name,
translation_verse: Wɛ ma ta ded‑o we, “Yé ta‑n pae se bakeira kam de n kaba-kana kam taane dem daane‑m. Nam cheigi Sarah na tage tei o bere‑m to, kokuri to, ko lage ko tɔge Izaak baŋa ne mo se nmo dwi dem ba de zege.

english_verse: but the son of the slave woman is also your son, and I will make his descendants into a great nation.”
translation_verse: Amo nam ta wó pa se kaba-kana kam bu-baaro wom dwi de puli de ji teo, o de na ye nmo bu to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Early the next morning Abraham gave Hagar an animal skin full of water and some bread. Then he put the boy on her shoulder and sent them away. They wandered around in the desert near Beersheba,
translation_verse: Tega na poore to zezeŋa ne to, Abaraham ma kwei wodiu o pa Hagara ye o daare o lwo na lɔɔ wone o pa‑o se o daŋe o bakala baŋa ne. O laam ma bane‑o de o bakeira kam o yage-ba chwoŋa ne. Hagara de ma to chwoŋa ne o kare Beeriseba kagoa kam yuu ne o beera.

english_verse: and after they had run out of water, Hagar put her son under a bush.
translation_verse: Lɔɔ kom wo na bam ma ti. O ma ja bu wom o vo jeini sabara kadwoŋi woro ne.

english_verse: When God heard the boy crying, the angel of God called out to Hagar from heaven and said, “Hagar, why are you worried? Don't be afraid. I have heard your son crying.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma ni bakeira kam na keeri to. Wɛ maleka kam maa zege Wɛ telaao ne ka bwoŋi Hagara ka we, “Hagara, bɛ mo kea? Yé ta‑n fona. Wɛ niga bu wom na tigi o keeri to.

english_verse: Help him up and hold his hand, because I will make him the father of a great nation.”
translation_verse: Zaŋe n vo n ja bu wom se o zaŋe, se amo wó pa se o dwi dem ji te-zɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: Then God let her see a well. So she went to the well and filled the skin with water, then gave some to her son.
translation_verse: Wɛ laam ma puri o yia pa se o na vole na tigi da. O ma vo o mɔ na o su o lɔɔ kom ni ye o ja vo o pa bu wom se o nyɔ.

english_verse: God blessed Ishmael, and as the boy grew older, he became an expert at hunting with his bow and arrows. He lived in the Paran Desert, and his mother chose an Egyptian woman for him to marry. A Peace Treaty
translation_verse: Kagoa kam o na zoore mɛ to yere mo Paran. O na wora to, mo o nu vei o lage kaane Ejipti ne o swo o ba o pa‑o. Abaraham de Abimeleka ke ni-mɔrɔ daane

english_verse: Now I want you to promise in the name of God that you will always be loyal to me and my descendants, just as I have always been loyal to you in this land where you have lived as a foreigner.”
translation_verse: Konto to, laam du duuri Wɛ yiga ne we nmo bá‑n ke n gane amo kɔtaa, ko ná ye amo naa a bia bam, naa a dwi dem maama. Amo na ke‑m lanyerane to, nmo de wó ke amo lanyerane, ko ná ye amo de teo kolo nmo na ye veiru ko wone to maama.”

english_verse: And so, Abraham promised he would.
translation_verse: Abaraham maa we, “Amo sɛ se a du duuri dem konto.”

english_verse: One day, Abraham told Abimelech, “Some of your servants have taken over one of my wells.”
translation_verse: Abimeleka nɔɔna nam ya vere Abaraham vole dedwoŋi mo. Abaraham ma ŋɔɔne taane dem de Abimeleka.

english_verse: “This is the first I've heard about it,” Abimelech replied. “Why haven't you said something before? I don't have any idea who did it.”
translation_verse: Abimeleka ma ta o we, “Amo wo lɔre wolo na ke konto to. Nmo wo tage ko taane n bere-ne, ye zem yerane mo amo laam lɔre ko ni ne.”

english_verse: Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle, then the two men made a peace treaty.
translation_verse: Abaraham laam ma ja peeni, de bone, de naane o ja o nwoŋi o pa Abimeleka, ye banto balei ke ni-sɛɛm daane.

english_verse: Abraham separated seven female lambs from his flock of sheep,
translation_verse: Abaraham ma daare o le pi-chwa barepɛ o vara bam wone o zege dáa ne.

english_verse: and Abimelech asked, “Why have you done this?”
translation_verse: Abimeleka ma bwei Abaraham we, “Bɛŋwaane mo nmo pɔɔre pi-chwa yam yarepɛ?”

english_verse: Abraham replied, “I want you to accept these seven lambs as proof that I dug this well.”
translation_verse: O ma leiri we, “Jwoŋi pi-chwa yarepɛ yam amo tei ne se ko taa ye maana we amo mo koge vole dento.”

english_verse: So they called the place Beersheba, because they made a treaty there.
translation_verse: Ba déem ma bwoŋi jei sem konto we Beeriseba, kokuri dáane mo nɔɔna banto balei déem dugi duuri.
