english_verse: When the treaty was completed, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol went back to the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ba na ke ni-sɛɛm dem konto Beeriseba ne ba ti to mo Abimeleka dedaane o jar-keira yiga tu Fikola jwoori ba vo Filisi tiina teo kom.

english_verse: Then Abraham lived a long time as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Abaraham déem maa zoore Filisi tiina teo kom wone o dáane da.

english_verse: Some years later God decided to test Abraham, so he spoke to him. Abraham answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
translation_verse: Ko na ke fee to, Wɛ ma ke Abaraham o nii. O ma bwoŋi‑o o ta we, “Abaraham!” O ma leiri we, “Nii-ne.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Go get Isaac, your only son, the one you dearly love! Take him to the land of Moriah, and I will show you a mountain where you must sacrifice him to me on the fires of an altar.”
translation_verse: Wɛ laam maa we, “Ja n bu-doa Izaak wom n na tiini n swoi to, n vo Moria laŋa kam se n ma‑o n kaane dáane n zwɛ‑o n pa-ne, peero tem dedoa yuu ne a na wó bere‑m to.”

english_verse: So Abraham got up early the next morning and chopped wood for the fire. He put a saddle on his donkey and set out with Isaac and two servants for the place where God had told him to go.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Abaraham ma zaŋe zezeŋa ne o ja o bonaga se o kɛ chwoŋa. O ma ja o tontoŋena balei dedaane o bu-baaro Izaak o woli da. O ma gwoni da-kore selo o na wó ma o zwɛ pɛɛra yam to. O laam ma kwei chwoŋa o maa vei jei selo Wɛ na tage we o véi to.

english_verse: Three days later Abraham looked off in the distance and saw the place.
translation_verse: Da yatɔ dɛ dem ne mo Abaraham kwoni o yuu wɛɛne o na jei sem yiga ne.

english_verse: He told his servants, “Stay here with the donkey, while my son and I go over there to worship. We will come back.”
translation_verse: O ma ta de o tontoŋena bam we, “Abam de bonaga kam maŋe-na ywo se amo dedaane bakeira kam vo dáane. Dé wó vo de zuli Wɛ ye dé daa ta jwoori dé ba abam tei ne.”

english_verse: Abraham put the wood on Isaac's shoulder, but he carried the hot coals and the knife. As the two of them walked along,
translation_verse: Abaraham na tage konto to, o ma kwei dɛ sem o zeŋe o bu-baaro Izaak. Wonto tete laam maa zei mini dem de seo kom. Banto balei na vei ba maa kɛ to,

english_verse: Isaac said, “Father, we have the coals and the wood, but where is the lamb for the sacrifice?” “My son,” Abraham answered, “God will provide the lamb.” The two of them walked on, and
translation_verse: Abaraham ma leiri we, “Amo bu, Wɛ tete mo wó na pipeila kalo dé na wó zwɛ dé ma ke kaanem dem to o pa debam.” Banto balei daa ta maa vei yiga.

english_verse: when they reached the place that God had told him about, Abraham built an altar and placed the wood on it. Next, he tied up his son and put him on the wood.
translation_verse: Ba na yi jei selo Wɛ na tage o bere Abaraham to, o ma tigisi kandwa o lɔ bimbini dáane ye o tɛɛse dɛ sem de baŋa ne. O laam ma vɔ o bu-baaro Izaak ye o gɔ‑o o daŋe dɛ sem baŋa ne.

english_verse: He then took the knife and got ready to kill his son.
translation_verse: O laam ma tore o jeŋa o le seo kom se o go o bu wom.

english_verse: But the Lord's angel shouted from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!” “Here I am!” he answered.
translation_verse: Bedwe baŋa ne mo Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam zege Wɛ telaao ne ka bwoŋi‑o we, “Abaraham! Abaraham!” O de ma sɛ o we, “Nii-ne da.”

english_verse: “Don't hurt the boy or harm him in any way!” the angel said. “Now I know that you truly obey God, because you were willing to offer him your only son.”
translation_verse: Maleka kam ma ta ka we, “Yé ke n bu wom zonne. Nam yé chɔge‑o. Amo laam maane we nmo seene n kɔre Wɛ, kokuri to nmo wo ve se n kwei n bu-doa kam n pa Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: Abraham named that place “The Lord Will Provide.” And even now people say, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”
translation_verse: Ko déem ma pa se Abaraham bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we ‘Baŋa Wɛ wó pa’. De zem maama de, nɔɔna ta yeini ba tɛ we, “Baŋa Wɛ peo kom yuu ne, pɛɛra wó taa wora.”

english_verse: The Lord's angel called out from heaven a second time:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam daa ta ma zege Wɛ telaao ne ka bwoŋi Abaraham ka ke kuni belei

english_verse: You were willing to offer your only son to the Lord, and so he makes you this solemn promise,
translation_verse: ye ka we, “Cheigi Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to we, ‘Nmo na ke tento ye n wo ve se n kwei n bu-doa kam n pa amo mo, a dugi a tete ŋwaane mo we,

english_verse: “I will bless you and give you such a large family, that someday your descendants will be more numerous than the stars in the sky or the grains of sand along the seashore. They will defeat their enemies and take over the cities where their enemies live.
translation_verse: amo wó seene a swɛ nmo swolim, ye a pa se nmo dwi dem puli dedɛ de taa daga nenɛɛne wɛyuu chalechwe sem dedaane naneo ni kasol-bia na daga tei to. Nmo dwi dem wó taa jege dam se ba jwoŋi ba dona teene ba taa tei.

english_verse: You have obeyed me, and so you and your descendants will be a blessing to all nations on earth.”
translation_verse: Ko ta lage ko tɔge nmo dwi dem baŋa ne mo se logo baŋa teene maama na zaane ba de baŋa ne, nmo tete na sɛ amo ni to ŋwaane.’ ”

english_verse: Abraham and Isaac went back to the servants who had come with him, and they returned to Abraham's home in Beersheba. The Children of Nahor
translation_verse: Abaraham de o bu Izaak laam ma jwoori o tontoŋena bam tei. Ba maama ma kwei Beeriseba chwoŋa kam ba maa kɛa. Ba na yi da to, Abaraham ma maŋe Beeriseba ne.

english_verse: Nahor also had another wife. Her name was Reumah, and she had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
translation_verse: Nahora déem jege ka-bia, o yere na ye Reuma. Wonto de déem ma lo bakeiri sento o pa‑o: Teba, de Gaham, de Tahasi, dedaane Maaka.

english_verse: “I live as a foreigner in your land, and I don't own any property where I can bury my wife. Please let me buy a piece of land.”
translation_verse: “Amo ye veiru mo a na zoore abam tetare ne. A nam lwoori tega se á pa-ne se ko taa ye mɛ amo na wó suli a too wom da to.”

english_verse: “Sir,” they answered, “you are an important man. Choose the best place to bury your wife. None of us would refuse you a resting place for your dead.”
translation_verse: “Cheigi ywo-seeni. Nmo ye dedɛɛro kamunu mo debam tetare ne. Konto to, kuri debam yibeela yam wone delo na lamma de pa‑m to se n suli n too wom da. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá ve nmo we n yé suli n too wom o yibeeli ne.”

english_verse: and replied, “If you are willing to let me bury my wife here, please ask Zohar's son Ephron
translation_verse: O ma ta-ba o we, “Abam nam ná sɛ se amo suli a kaane wom ywo-seeni, se á sɛ se á lwoori Zohare bu Eforon á pa-ne.

english_verse: “Sir, the whole field, including the cave, is yours. With my own people as witnesses, I freely give it to you as a burial place for your dead.”
translation_verse: O maa we, “Amo tu, cheigi ywo-seeni. Amo wó kwei kara kam mo a pa‑m zɛɛra, ye a ta wó pa‑m peo-bɔɔne delo na wo ka laŋa ne to a woli da. Amo nɔɔna bam yiga ne mo a kwei a pa‑m. Véi n suli n kaane wom da.”

english_verse: and said to Ephron, “In front of these witnesses, I offer you the full price, so I can bury my wife. Please accept my offer.”
translation_verse: O ma ta de Eforon pa se ba maama ni ye o we, “Nam cheigi a na tɛ kolo to. Amo wó ŋwe tega kam sabu a pa‑m. Sɛ se n jwoŋi sabu kom se amo de wane a kwei a kaane wom a suli dáane.”

english_verse: Abraham was now a very old man. The Lord had made him rich, and he was successful in everything he did.
translation_verse: Abaraham déem ma tiini o kwe ye o bena gaale. O chwoŋa maama wone Baŋa Wɛ ma ke zaane o ke o yuu ne.

english_verse: in the name of the Lord, who rules heaven and earth, that you won't choose a wife for my son Isaac from the people here in the land of Canaan.
translation_verse: Nmo jege se n du duuri Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane, o na tei wɛyuu de tega baŋa to. Du duuri n pa-ne we, debam na seene dé zoore Kanaan tiina bam wone to, nmo bá beeri kaane ba bukwa bam wone n pa amo bu Izaak.

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for him from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: Nmo nam wó jwoori n vo amo nabaara teo kom, de a dwi tiina na wo mɛ to mo n beeri kaane n pa‑o.”

english_verse: But the servant asked, “What if the young woman I choose refuses to leave home and come here with me? Should I send Isaac there to look for a wife?”
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom ma bwei‑o we, “Se kaane wom ná wo sɛ se o tɔge de amo o jwoori o ba tega kanto ne, a wó ke tɛ mo? A wó ja n bu wom a jwoori a vo mɛ n na nwoŋi n ba ywo to mo na?”

english_verse: “No!” Abraham answered. “Don't ever do that, no matter what.
translation_verse: Abaraham ma leiri o ta we, “Ta‑n yei se n daa‑n yé ja amo bu wom n jwoori dáane.

english_verse: The Lord who rules heaven brought me here from the land where I was born and promised that he would give this land to my descendants forever. When you go back there, the Lord will send his angel ahead of you to help you find a wife for my son.
translation_verse: Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ wom na tei wɛyuu to mo jaane amo o ja o nwoŋi a kwo sɔŋɔ ne se a yage a dwi tiina tega kam. Wonto mo ŋɔɔne de amo o du duuri we ‘Nmo dwi dem mo a wó seene a pa tega kanto’. Wonto mo lage o toŋe o maleka se ka tɔge nmo yiga ka vo se nmo wane n na kaane dáane n ja n ba n pa amo bu wom.

english_verse: If the woman refuses to come along, you don't have to keep this promise. But don't ever take my son back there.”
translation_verse: Kaane wom nam ná wo sɛ se o tɔge de nmo o ba ywo-seeni, kanto maŋa ne mo duuri dento daa bá taa wo n yuu ne. Nmo yé ja amo bu wom n jwoori n vo dáane.”

english_verse: So the servant gave Abraham his word that he would do everything he had been told to do.
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom ma sɛ o kwei o jeŋa o ke o tu Abaraham chwei kuri ne ye o du duuri, taane dem konto ŋwaane.

english_verse: Soon after that, the servant loaded ten of Abraham's camels with valuable gifts. Then he set out for the city in northern Syria, where Abraham's brother Nahor lived.
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom laam ma le kona fuga Abaraham kona yam wone o ma o zeŋe o tu wom wo-laaro dwi maama o ja o woli da o kɛ. O ma kwei chwoŋa se o vo Mesopotamia seeni. O ma vo o yi teo kolo Nahora déem na zoore to.

english_verse: When he got there, he let the camels rest near the well outside the city. It was late afternoon, the time when the women came out for water.
translation_verse: O na yi teo kom ni to, o ma pa se o kona yam kuni ya nadwoona ya tigi vole ni ne. Ko déem ye dedaan-ni ne mo, maŋa kalo kaana na nwoŋi ba vei ba mɔɔne na to.

english_verse: The servant prayed: You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships. Please keep your promise to him and let me find a wife for Isaac today.
translation_verse: O ma lwoori Wɛ ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ, amo tu Abaraham Wɛ, nam pa se ko ke lanyerane ko pa-ne zem dɛ dem ne, se n daare n duri amo tu Abaraham ŋwaŋa.

english_verse: The young women of the city will soon come to this well for water,
translation_verse: Nii! Amo zege vole dento ni ne mo, ye teo kom bukwa bam wó ba se ba mɔ na.

english_verse: and I'll ask one of them for a drink. If she gives me a drink and then offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen and that you have kept your promise to my master.
translation_verse: Amo ná tage dedaane busankana kalo we ‘Ja! Zoore n kɔɔro wom n zege se n ke na n pa-ne se a nyɔ,’ ye konto tu wom ná taga we ‘Nyɔ, se n daare se a mɔ na a pa n kona yam se ya de nyɔ,’ pa se wonto taa ye wolo nmo na kuri se n pa Izaak to. Ko nam ná ke konto mo, amo wó lɔre we nmo seene n duri amo tu wom ŋwaŋa.”

english_verse: While he was still praying, a beautiful unmarried young woman came by with a water jar on her shoulder. She was Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his wife Milcah. Rebekah walked past Abraham's servant, then went over to the well, and filled her water jar. When she started back,
translation_verse: Busankana kam déem tiini ka lamma. O déem maa ta yeiri baaro. O ma yi vole dem ni, o mɔ na o su o kɔɔro wom ye o jwoori o bɛ.

english_verse: Abraham's servant ran to her and said, “Please let me have a drink of water.”
translation_verse: Abaraham tontoŋeno wom ma ke lela o jeeri‑o ye o we, “Ja! Twei na n kɔɔro wom ne n pa-ne se a nyɔ.”

english_verse: “I'll be glad to,” she answered. Then she quickly took the jar from her shoulder and held it while he drank.
translation_verse: O de maa we, “Amo tu, nam nyɔ”, ye o ke lela o zoore o kɔɔro wom o zeeri o jea ne se o nyɔ.

english_verse: After he had finished, she said, “Now I'll give your camels all the water they want.” She quickly poured out water for them, and she kept going back for more, until his camels had drunk all they wanted.
translation_verse: O laam ma ke lela o lwo na bam o ke vara na nyɔɔm gwoŋo wone, ye o daa jwoori vole dem ne o mɔ na bam o woli da. O ke konto mo taa o mɔ na bam pa se kona yam maama nyɔ ya su.

english_verse: Abraham's servant did not say a word, but he watched everything Rebekah did, because he wanted to know for certain if this was the woman the Lord had chosen.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom de maa wo tage kolokolo, ye o laam fɔge o nii busankana kam lanyerane se o lɔre Baŋa Wɛ seene o pa se o chwoŋa kam veiŋa ke lanyerane naa ko dae konto.

english_verse: The servant had brought along an expensive gold ring and two large gold bracelets. When Rebekah had finished bringing the water, he gave her the ring for her nose and the bracelets for her arms.
translation_verse: Kona yam na nyɔge na bam ya ti to, mo nɔɔno wom le sabu-seŋa jafole delo ba déem na ke momwa ne to dedaane jeŋa bɛ selei se o pa Rebeka. Wonnu tem konto déem tiini te jege sabu.

english_verse: Then he said, “Please tell me who your father is. Does he have room in his house for me and my men to spend the night?”
translation_verse: O laam ma bwei‑o we, “Nmo ye wɔ bukɔ mo? Jei nam wó taa wo abam sɔŋɔ ne se a peini tete dento se tega poore na?”

english_verse: She answered, “My father is Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah.
translation_verse: Rebeka ma leiri o we, “Amo ye Bɛtuweli bukɔ mo. Wonto maa ye Milika de Nahora bu.”

english_verse: We have a place where you and your men can stay, and we also have enough straw and feed for your camels.”
translation_verse: O ta ma woli da we, “Debam jege jei se nmo dedaane balo na tɔge‑m to peini da. Vara wodiu dedɛ de wora se á kona yam de di ya su.”

english_verse: Then the servant bowed his head and prayed,
translation_verse: O na nigi konto to, nɔɔno wom ma chɔɔle tega ne o zuli Baŋa Wɛ,

english_verse: Her brother Laban heard her tell what the servant had said, and he saw the ring and the bracelets she was wearing. So Laban ran out to Abraham's servant, who was standing by his camels at the well.
translation_verse: O ya maŋe o na jafole dem o nakɔ wom momwɛ ne de bɛ sem na wo o je sem ne to, ye o ta ni taane delo maama nɔɔno wom ya na tage de Rebeka to. Laban ma ke lela o nwoŋi o vo o na nɔɔno wom na zege vole dem ni ne de o kona yam.

english_verse: Then Laban said, “The Lord has brought you safely here. Come home with me. There's no need for you to keep on standing outside. I have a room ready for you in our house, and there's also a place for your camels.”
translation_verse: O maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ ke zaane nmo yuu ne mo. Pa se dé vo sɔŋɔ. Bɛŋwaane mo nmo wó ta‑n zege pwola kanto ne? Amo nam maŋe a kwɛ diga nmo ŋwaane, ye kona yam de wó na jei ya taa tiga.”

english_verse: Abraham's servant went home with Laban, where Laban's servants unloaded his camels and gave them straw and feed. Then they brought water into the house, so Abraham's servant and his men could wash their feet.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom laam ma tɔge o vo o zo ba sɔŋɔ kom. Laban ma zoore o kona yam zela yam. O ma beeri vara wodiu o pa kona yam, ye o daare o ke na se Abaraham tontoŋeno wom de balo na tɔge dedaane‑o to zare ba nɛ.

english_verse: After that, they brought in food. But the servant said, “Before I eat, I must tell you why I have come.” “Go ahead and tell us,” Laban answered.
translation_verse: Ba na jaane wodiu kom ba ba to, mo Abaraham tontoŋeno wom we, “Amo ná wo tage kolo na wo a ni ne to, a bá di wodiu.” Laban maa we, “Nam ta n bere debam.”

english_verse: The servant explained: I am Abraham's servant.
translation_verse: O laam ma tole taane dem o we: “Amo ye Abaraham tontoŋeno mo.

english_verse: The Lord has been good to my master and has made him very rich. He has given him many sheep, goats, cattle, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of silver and gold, and many slaves.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam mo tiini o ke zaane o ke amo tu wom yuu ne pa se o laam ji jejegero tu. Wɛ pɛ‑o peeni, de bone, de naane, ko woli de lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa, de tontoŋe-baara de tontoŋe-kana, dedaane kona de bonɛ.

english_verse: Sarah, my master's wife, didn't have any children until she was very old. Then she had a son, and my master has given him everything.
translation_verse: Amo tu kaane Sarah ya loge bakeira o pa‑o mo o kokweero maŋa kam ne. Amo tu wom de kwei woŋo kolo maama o na jege to mo o pa bu wom konto.

english_verse: I solemnly promised my master that I would do what he said. And he told me, “Don't choose a wife for my son from the women in this land of Canaan.
translation_verse: Amo tu wom laam ya ma pa se amo du duuri, ye o ta we ‘N ná wó beeri kaane se n pa a bu wom, yé beeri Kanaan tiina bukwa bam wone, mɛ tento amo na zoore leile to.

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for my son from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: Nam jwoori n vo amo nabaara teo kom n lage kaane amo tete sɔ-yuu kom ne n pa amo bu wom.’

english_verse: I asked my master, “What if the young woman refuses to come with me?”
translation_verse: Amo de ma bwei a tu wom we ‘Se kaane wom ná ve se o tɔge de amo o jwoori o ba, se a ke tɛ mo?’

english_verse: My master answered, “I have always obeyed the Lord, and he will send his angel to help you find my son a wife from among my own relatives.
translation_verse: O de ma leiri we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wolo wom a na sɛ o ni to wó toŋe o maleka se o da nmo yiga se nmo chwoŋa kam veiŋa ke lanyerane. Ko wó pa se n na kaane n pa amo bu wom se o nwoŋi amo tete sɔ-yuu kom ne, amo kwo dwi tiina wone.

english_verse: But if they refuse to let her come back with you, then you are freed from your promise.”
translation_verse: Nmo nam ná lwoori n vo amo sɔ-yuu kom ne, ye ba ve‑m ba bukɔ wom, n laam wó sii duuri delo a na pɛ se n du to wone.’

english_verse: When I came to the well today, I silently prayed, “You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships, so please lead me to a wife for his son
translation_verse: Amo zem ma na tu a yi vole dem ni to, mo a lwoori Wɛ we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ, na ye amo tu Abaraham Wɛ to, nenɛɛne ko ná su nmo yi, sɛ se a chwoŋa kam veiŋa ke lanyerane.

english_verse: while I am here at the well. When a young woman comes out to get water, I'll ask her to give me a drink.
translation_verse: Nii! Amo zege vole dem ni ne mo ywo. Bukɔ wolo ná tu ywo se o mɔ na ye a ta ded‑o we, “Ja! Pa-ne n kɔɔro wom wo na fee se a nyɔ,”

english_verse: If she gives me a drink and offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen.”
translation_verse: ye kotu ná tage de amo we, “Nyɔ, se a ta wó mɔ na se n kona yam de nyɔ,” sɛ se o taa ye kaane wolo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri se o zo amo tu wom bu-baaro to.’

english_verse: Even before I had finished praying, Rebekah came by with a water jar on her shoulder. When she had filled the jar, I asked her for a drink.
translation_verse: Tɔ. Amo bere a maŋe a wo lwoori wɛ-lworo kom a bochare ne a ti dedaane Rebeka na maa beena, de o bakale baŋa kɔɔro. O ma yi vole dem o mɔ na bam, ye amo de ta ded‑o we ‘Ja! Pa-ne na se a nyɔ.’

english_verse: She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said, “Have a drink. Then I'll get water for your camels.” So I drank, and after that she got some water for my camels.
translation_verse: O ma ke lela o zoore o kɔɔro wom ye o we ‘Nyɔ, se a ta wó pa n kona yam de na se ya nyɔ.’ Amo ma nyɔ ye o seene o mɔ na o pa kona yam ye ya nyɔ.

english_verse: I asked her who her father was, and she answered, “My father is Bethuel the son of Nahor and Milcah.” At once I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
translation_verse: Amo de ma bwei‑o we ‘Nmo ye wɔ bukɔ mo?’ O ma leiri we ‘Amo ye Bɛtuweli bukɔ mo. Amo kwo wom mo ye wolo Milika na loga o pa Nahora to.’ A na lɔre konto to, mo a laam kwei jafole dem a ke o momwɛ ne a daare a kwei bɛ sem a ke o je sem ne.

english_verse: Then I bowed my head and gave thanks to the God my master Abraham worships. The Lord had led me straight to my master's relatives, and I had found a wife for his son.
translation_verse: A ma chɔɔle tega ne a tei Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye amo tu Abaraham Wɛ to. Wɛ wom konto mo dɛ amo yiga ye o bere-ne chwo-laao kom se a wane a na amo tu wom choro bukɔ se o taa ye a tu wom bu-kaane.

english_verse: Now please tell me if you are willing to do the right thing for my master. Will you treat him fairly, or do I have to look for another young woman?
translation_verse: Konto to, ko laam wo abam tei ne. Á ná sɛ se á ke amo tu wom lanyerane ye á ke chega á pa‑o, se á ta á bere-ne. Á nam daa ná lage se á lɔ o kwaga ne mo, ta ta-na á bere-ne, se amo laam wó lɔre chwoŋa kalo a na wó tɔge to.”

english_verse: Laban and Bethuel answered, “The Lord has done this. We have no choice in the matter.
translation_verse: Laban de Bɛtuweli ma leiri we, “Tento nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ tei ne mo. Debam bá wane de ta kolokolo dede‑m nenɛɛne dé sɛ naa dé wo sɛ.

english_verse: Take Rebekah with you; she can marry your master's son, just as the Lord has said.”
translation_verse: Nii Rebeka da, ja‑o n viiri n vo n pa n tu bu wom se o taa ye o kaane, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na bere tei to.”

english_verse: Then he gave clothing, as well as silver and gold jewelry, to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.
translation_verse: O laam ma le zela o tampɔgɔ ne o kwei o pa Rebeka. Pɛɛra yam déem ye sabu-seŋa dedaane lu-nyenno wonnu tedwonna ko woli de gwaaro. O ta ma le pɛɛra yalo na tiini ya ke sabu to o pa Rebeka nabɔ wom de o nu.

english_verse: Abraham's servant and the men with him ate and drank, then spent the night there. The next morning they got up, and the servant told Rebekah's mother and brother, “I would like to go back to my master now.”
translation_verse: Konto maama kwaga ne, o de nɔɔna balo na tɔge daane to laam ma di ba daare ba nyɔ ye ba peini sɔŋɔ kom ne pa se tega poore. Tega na poore ye ba zaŋe zezeŋa ne to mo Abaraham tontoŋeno wom tage we, “Yage-na amo chwoŋa ne se a jwoori a vo a tu wom tei ne.”

english_verse: “Let Rebekah stay with us for a week or ten days,” they answered. “Then she may go.”
translation_verse: Bukɔ wom nabɔ de o nu ma leiri we, “Yage se bukɔ wom maŋe debam tei ne se ko yi nenɛɛne da fuga to, se abam laam viiri.”

english_verse: But he said, “Don't make me stay any longer. The Lord has already helped me find a wife for my master's son. Now let us return.”
translation_verse: O de ma leiri we, “Baŋa Wɛ na lwoori o pa se amo chwoŋa kam ke lanyerane to, daa yé cheiŋi-na amo. Pa-na pwola se a jwoori amo tu wom tei.”

english_verse: They answered, “Let's ask Rebekah what she wants to do.”
translation_verse: Ba maa we, “Yage se dé bwoŋi busankana kam dé bwei‑o dé nii.”

english_verse: They called her and asked, “Are you willing to leave with this man at once?” “Yes,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ba ma bwoŋi Rebeka ba bwei‑o we, “Nmo wó sɛ n da dedaane nɔɔno wonto n kɛ na?” O ma leiri we, “Amo wó vo.”

english_verse: So they agreed to let Rebekah and an old family servant woman leave immediately with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Ba ma sɛ ye ba bane ba nakɔ Rebeka de wolo na wó taa nii o baŋa ne to ba yage chwoŋa ne, ko woli de Abaraham tontoŋeno wom de balo na tɔge ded‑o to.

english_verse: They gave Rebekah their blessing and said, “We pray that God will give you many children and grandchildren and that he will help them defeat their enemies.”
translation_verse: Ba ma kwei Wɛ zaane ba ma swɛ Rebeka swolim ye ba ta ded‑o we: “Debam nakɔ, Wɛ wó pa se nmo dwi puli de yi morro morro. Wɛ wó pa se nmo dwi dem taa jege dam se ba jwoŋi ba dona teene ba taa tei.”

english_verse: Afterwards, Rebekah and the young women who were to travel with her prepared to leave. Then they got on camels and left with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Rebeka de o ka-nyaana bam ma ti ba yiga ye ba di kona yam ba tɔge de nɔɔno wom ba kɛ. Mo ko na ke tei ye Abaraham tontoŋeno wom ja Rebeka o ja viiri.

english_verse: At that time Isaac was living in the southern part of Canaan near a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Izaak déem ya zaŋe Beeri Lahayi Royi ne o vo o zoore tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam ne mo.

english_verse: One evening he was walking out in the fields, when suddenly he saw a group of people approaching on camels. So he started toward them. Rebekah saw him coming; she got down from her camel, and asked, “Who is that man?” “He is my master Isaac,” the servant answered. Then Rebekah covered her face with her veil.
translation_verse: Rebeka daa ma bwei Abaraham tontoŋeno wom we, “Wɔ mo tento kara kam ne o na vei o beene se o jeeri debam to?” O ma leiri we, “Amo tu Izaak mo.” O na lɔre konto to, o ma kwei o yu-gare-daŋɔ kom o ma o kwoli o yibia.

english_verse: The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Abaraham tontoŋeno wom laam ma lwoni o bere Izaak o na ke tei maama to.

english_verse: Isaac took Rebekah into the tent where his mother had lived before she died, and Rebekah became his wife. He loved her and was comforted over the loss of his mother.
translation_verse: Izaak ma ja Rebeka o zo o nu Sarah vwei dem wone. O déem ma di o ma o ke kaane. Izaak maa swoi‑o lanyerane. Izaak wo déem ya chɔge de o nu toone dem ye Rebeka laam pa se o wo jwoori ko zuri.

english_verse: and they had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
translation_verse: Wonto de ma lo bia: Zimiran, de Jokisan, de Medan, de Midian, de Isibaka, dedaane Sua.

english_verse: Later, Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan, and when Dedan grew up, he had three sons: Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
translation_verse: Jokisan déem mo ye Seba de Dedan kwo. Dedan dwi dem mo ye Asuri tiina bam, de Letusi tiina bam, de Leyum tiina bam.

english_verse: Midian also had five sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah.
translation_verse: Midian de bu-baara bam mo tento: Efa, de Efere, de Hanoki, de Abida, de Elida. Banto maama déem ye Ketura dwi mo.

english_verse: While Abraham was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of Hagar and Keturah. He also sent their sons to live in the east far from his son Isaac, and when Abraham died, he left everything to Isaac. The Death of Abraham
translation_verse: Ko daare o ka-bi sem bia bam mo o le pɛɛra o pa-ba ye o daa ta ŋwe. O ma daare o pwɛ-ba o pa se ba yɔɔre ba vo wɛ-puli seeni ye ba daare o bu Izaak.

english_verse: God blessed Isaac after this, and Isaac moved to a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.” Ishmael's Descendants
translation_verse: Abaraham toone dem kwaga ne, mo Wɛ swɛ Izaak swolim. Ka maŋa ne o déem zoore Beeri Lahayi Royi jei sem ne mo. Isameli dwi dem taane

english_verse: Ishmael was the son of Abraham and Hagar, the slave woman of Sarah.
translation_verse: Isameli de o dwi dem yera taane mo tento. Sarah ka-nyaane Hagara na ye Ejipti tu to de Abaraham mo loge Isameli.

english_verse: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
translation_verse: de Misima, de Duma, de Massa,

english_verse: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
translation_verse: de Hadad, de Tema, de Jetura, de Nafisi dedaane Kedema.

english_verse: Each of Ishmael's sons was a tribal chief, and a village was named after each of them.
translation_verse: Isameli bia fuga-balei bam mo konto. Ba dedoa dedoa déem ma ji ba dwi tiina nabaaro. Mo ba yera yam mo konto, nɔɔno maama, de o nawuuri, de o teo.

english_verse: Ishmael had settled in the land east of his brothers, and his sons settled everywhere from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt on the way to Asshur. Ishmael was
translation_verse: O dwi dem ma vo ba jeini tega kalo na zege Havila de Sura tetare laŋa ne to. Jei sem konto yɔɔre ko wo Ejipti siseini ni ne se ko taa vei Asiria seeni to mo. Maŋa maama ba déem jege nankɔɔre mo ba ke de ba chorro tem. Jakob dedaane Esawu taane

english_verse: when he died. The Birth of Esau and Jacob
translation_verse: ) ye o laam ba o te.

english_verse: Rebekah still had no children. So Isaac asked the Lord to let her have a child, and the Lord answered his prayer.
translation_verse: Rebeka déem na ye kadega to, Izaak ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o kaane wom lo bu. Baŋa Wɛ ma sɛ o wɛ-lworo kom, ye o kaane Rebeka ja puga.

english_verse: Before Rebekah gave birth, she knew she was going to have twins, because she could feel them inside her, fighting each other. She thought, “Why is this happening to me?” Finally, she asked the Lord why her twins were fighting,
translation_verse: Bia bam ma yigi daane o puga kam ne. O déem maa we, “Bɛŋwaane mo ko ye tento amo yera yam ne?” Ko ma pa se o vo Baŋa Wɛ yiga o bwei‑o se o lɔre ko kuri.

english_verse: and he told her: “Your two sons will become two separate nations. The younger of the two will be stronger, and the older son will be his servant.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ maa we: “Dwia yalei mo wo nmo puga kam wone. Nmo wó lo dwi dwi kuni belei, ye ba wó ba ba pwɛ chwei. Dwi dedoa wó taa damma de dwoi dedwoŋi dem, zembaaro wom mo wó taa toŋe o pa o nyaane wom.”

english_verse: As Jacob and Esau grew older, Esau liked the outdoors and became a good hunter, while Jacob lived the quiet life of a shepherd.
translation_verse: Bia bam déem ma ba ba ke nɔɔna. Esawu ma ji tɔɔno wolo na tiini o wae o tɔɔna. O maa yeini o swoi se o taa wo pwooni ne maŋa maama. Jakob déem maa ye nɔn-cheno. O maa swoi se o taa wo sɔŋɔ ne maŋa maama.

english_verse: Esau would take the meat of wild animals to his father Isaac, so Isaac loved him more, but Jacob was his mother's favorite son.
translation_verse: Izaak déem maa swoi Esawu, Esawu na jaane kago-vara nɔna yam o tui o pa‑o to ŋwaane. Rebeka de déem maa swoi Jakob.

english_verse: One day, when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came home hungry
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Jakob wora o saŋe o wodiu. Esawu ma zege gaao ne o jwoori sɔŋɔ ye kana tiini ka chɛ‑o.

english_verse: and said, “I'm starving to death! Here and now give me some of that red stew!” That's how Esau got the name “Edom.”
translation_verse: O ma ta de Jakob o we, “Ke lela n wɔɔre n dwoa-nasoŋo kom konto n pa-ne se a di! Kokuri, a wora a toa mo de kana!” Dwoa bam na seene to ŋwaane mo ba déem bwoi‑o we ‘Edom’.

english_verse: But Jacob said, “Promise me your birthrights, here and now!” And that's what Esau did.
translation_verse: Jakob ma leiri we, “Nam du amo yiga ne se n daare.” O de ma du duuri o pa‑o, ye o yeigi o nakwe nyɔɔre dem o pa Jakob.

english_verse: Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_verse: Jakob laam ma kwei bworobworo dedaane dwoa o pa Esawu. O ma di ye o daare o nyɔ. O laam ma zaŋe wɛɛne o maa kɛa. Ko déem tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo ye Esawu nii o nakwe nyɔɔre dem o gwooni-de to.

english_verse: Once during Abraham's lifetime, the fields had not produced enough grain, and now the same thing happened. So Isaac went to King Abimelech of the Philistines in the land of Gerar,
translation_verse: Maŋa kadwoŋi ne kana déem daa ma jwoori ka ba tega baŋa, nenɛɛne ka na maŋe ka ke ye Abaraham ta ŋwe to. Izaak ma zaŋe o vo Filisi tiina pɛ Abimeleka tei Gerare ne.

english_verse: because the Lord had appeared to Isaac and said: Isaac, stay away from Egypt! I will show you where I want you to go.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ba Izaak tei o we, “Yé zaŋe n vo Ejipti teo kom. Nam ta‑n zoore jei sem ne mɛ amo na wó bere‑m to.

english_verse: You will live there as a foreigner, but I will be with you and bless you. I will keep my promise to your father Abraham by giving this land to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: Maŋe n jeini teo konto ne. Amo wó taa wo nmo tei ne ye a swɛ nmo swolim. Amo wó kwei tega kanto maama a pa nmo de n dwi dem ye a daare a pa se duuri delo a na pwooli de nmo kwo Abaraham to seene de ji chega.

english_verse: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth,
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se nmo dwi dem puli dedɛ de taa daga nenɛɛne wɛyuu chalechwe sem na daga tei to, ye a pa ba taa tei tega kanto maama. Ko nam ta wó tɔge nmo dwi dem baŋa ne mo se logo baŋa teene dem maama na zaane ba de yuu ne,

english_verse: with his beautiful wife Rebekah. He was afraid that someone might kill him to get her, and so he told everyone that Rebekah was his sister.
translation_verse: Rebeka na tiini o lamma to ŋwaane, Izaak déem kɔre we teo kom nɔɔna wó ja‑o ba go mo o kaane wom ŋwaane. Ba ná bwei o bwia, o maa tɛ we, Rebeka ye o nakɔ mo. O déem kɔre mo se o ta we, o ye o kaane.

english_verse: After Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah.
translation_verse: Izaak na zo da o dáane fee to, mo pɛ Abimeleka tɔge o sɔŋɔ takworo ne o na Izaak na wora o di bwoŋa dedaane o kaane Rebeka.

english_verse: Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?” “Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
translation_verse: Abimeleka na nɛ konto to, o laam ma bwoŋi Izaak ye o we, “O seene o ye nmo kaane mo! Ko laam nam ke tɛ mo ye nmo ta n we, o ye n nakɔ mo?” Izaak ma leiri we, “A kɔre we ba wó go-ne a kaane wom ŋwaane mo.”

english_verse: “Don't you know what you've done?” Abimelech exclaimed. “If someone had slept with her, you would have made our whole nation guilty!”
translation_verse: Abimeleka laam maa we, “Bɛ mo ye nmo ke debam konto? Baara bam dedoa ya wó wane o peini de n kaane wom, ye konto ya wó pa chaveera ja debam.”

english_verse: Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
translation_verse: Abimeleka laam ma pa kwora yi o nɔɔna bam maama we, “Wolo maama na wó bɛɛse nɔɔno wonto naa o kaane wom to, toone mo wó taa ye kotu ŋweero.”

english_verse: Isaac planted grain and had a good harvest that same year. The Lord blessed him,
translation_verse: Izaak déem ma du wo-dwa tega kam baŋa ne. Bene dem konto ne o ma na wodiiru dedɛ, kuni bi, Baŋa Wɛ na swɛ o swolim to ŋwaane.

english_verse: and Isaac was so successful that he became very rich.
translation_verse: O déem ma duni. O duum dem maa tiini de pula, pa se o ji dedɛɛro kamunu.

english_verse: In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned,
translation_verse: O jejegero tem daga te gaale, te maa ye peeni de bone de naane de tontoŋena dedɛ. Filisi tiina bam déem ma zwe kazwe ded‑o.

english_verse: and they stopped up the wells that Abraham's servants had dug before his death.
translation_verse: Ko ma pa se ba kwei teero ba ma suuri vola yalo maama Abaraham tontoŋena bam déem na koga ye o ta ŋwe to.

english_verse: Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
translation_verse: Abimeleka ma ta de Izaak we, “Nwoŋi n viiri, se nmo laam tiini n damma n dwoi debam.”

english_verse: where he cleaned out those wells that the Philistines had stopped up. Isaac also gave each of the wells the same name that Abraham had given to them.
translation_verse: Izaak déem ma jwoori o gwaare vola yam Filisi tiina bam na suuri o kwo Abaraham toone kwaga ne to. O ta ma jwoori o pa-ya yera yalo o kwo déem na mɛ o bwoŋi-ya to.

english_verse: While his servants were digging in the valley, they found a spring-fed well.
translation_verse: Izaak tontoŋena bam déem ma ko vole dedwoŋi bwolo kom ne ba yi na-ŋona.

english_verse: But the shepherds of Gerar Valley quarreled with Isaac's shepherds and claimed the water belonged to them. So this well was named “Quarrel,” because they had quarreled with Isaac.
translation_verse: Gerare tiina nayera laam ma mage ni-kantɔgɔ de Izaak nayera bam ba we, “Vole dem na bam ye debam nyem mo!” Izaak ma pa vole dem yere we ‘Eseke’, ba na mage ni-kantɔgɔ de baŋa ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Isaac's servants dug another well, and the shepherds also quarreled about it. So that well was named “Jealous.”
translation_verse: Ba daa ta ma ko vole dedwoŋi, ye ba ta mage ni-kantɔgɔ dento de baŋa ne. O ma pa vole dem konto yere we ‘Sitina’.

english_verse: Finally, they dug one more well. There was no quarreling this time, and the well was named “Lots of Room,” because the Lord had given them room and would make them very successful.
translation_verse: Izaak ma zaŋe o fɔɔre dáane o vo o ko vole dedem, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa wo ke jara dento baŋa ne. O ma pa de yere we ‘Rehobofa’, ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ laam pɛ debam pwola se dé jeini de yazura, ye debam wó yerege tega kam baŋa ne.”

english_verse: where the Lord appeared to him that night and told him, “Don't be afraid! I am the God who was worshiped by your father Abraham, my servant. I will be with you and bless you, and because of Abraham I will give you many descendants.”
translation_verse: O na yi da to, tete dem konto ne Baŋa Wɛ ma ba o tei ne ye o we, “Amo mo ye nmo kwo Abaraham Wɛ wom. Yé ta‑n kɔre foone, se amo wo nmo tei ne. Amo wó swɛ nmo swolim. A nam ta wó pa se n dwi dem kɔgɔ puli, amo tontoŋeno Abaraham ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the Lord. Then he set up camp, and his servants started digging a well.
translation_verse: Izaak maa tigisi kandwa o lɔ bimbini dáane ye o bwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ yere o zuli‑o. O ma pu o vwei jei sem konto ne, ye o tontoŋena bam de ko vole.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Abimelech had left Gerar and was taking his advisor Ahuzzath and his army commander Phicol to see Isaac.
translation_verse: Ba na wora konto to, Pɛ Abimeleka zege Gerare ne o ba o tei, wonto de o nakwe Ahuzafa dedaane o jar-keira bam yiga tu Fikola.

english_verse: They answered, “We now know for certain that the Lord is with you, and we have decided there needs to be a peace treaty between you and us. So let's make a solemn agreement
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri we, “Debam maane we Baŋa Wɛ seene o wo nmo tei ne. Dé laam maa we, ko jege se dé du duuri mo se dé ke ni-mɔrɔ daane. Sɛ se debam ke ni-sɛɛm de nmo

english_verse: not to harm each other. Remember, we have never hurt you, and when we sent you away, we let you go in peace. The Lord has truly blessed you.”
translation_verse: se nmo yé ke debam lwarem. Debam déem ke nmo lanyerane mo, se ko dae lwarem kɔtaa, ye dé daare dé bane‑m dé pa se n viiri dedaane yazura. Nmo laam maa n ye wolo Baŋa Wɛ na yɔɔre o swɛ nmo swolim to.”

english_verse: Isaac gave a big feast for them, and everyone ate and drank.
translation_verse: Izaak ma sɛ ye o ke kuri o pa-ba. Ba ma di wodi-fɔrɔ ba daare ba nyɔ.

english_verse: Early the next morning Isaac and the others made a solemn agreement, then he let them go in peace.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, zezeŋa ne nɔɔna bam ma du duuri ba ke ni-sɛɛm daane. Izaak ma bane-ba o yage chwoŋa ne, ye ba de viiri de yazura.

english_verse: So Isaac named the well Shibah, and the town is still called Beersheba. Esau's Foreign Wives
translation_verse: O ma bwoŋi vole dem konto we, Siba, ye dedaane zem maama teo kom konto yere mo ye Beeriseba.

english_verse: But these two women brought a lot of grief to Esau's parents Isaac and Rebekah.
translation_verse: Banto déem tiini ba ja wo-chechɔgɔ mo ba ba ba pa Izaak de Rebeka.

english_verse: Isaac was old and almost blind, when he called in his first-born son Esau, who asked him, “Father, what can I do for you?”
translation_verse: Izaak déem ma kwe ye o yia yam dwei. O déem ma bwoŋi o bu-kwea Esawu ye o laam ta ded‑o we, “Amo bu.” O de ma leiri we, “Nii-ne da.”

english_verse: Isaac replied, “I am old and might die at any time.
translation_verse: Izaak maa we, “Amo laam ye nɔn-kwea mo ye a yeiri amo toone dɛ.

english_verse: So go hunting with your bow and arrows and kill a wild animal.
translation_verse: Konto to, kwei n taŋa kam de ka chena, se n vo gaao n tɔɔne n go kago-varem n pa-ne.

english_verse: Cook some of that tasty food that I love so much and bring it to me. I want to eat it once more and give you my blessing before I die.”
translation_verse: Laam kwei varem wom n ma n ke wodiu na ywomma ne a na yeini a lage tetei to, se n daare n ja n ba n pa-ne se a di. Nmo ná ke konto, a laam wó kwei Wɛ zaane a ma swɛ nmo swolim, se a daare a te.”

english_verse: she said to Jacob, “I heard your father tell Esau
translation_verse: Rebeka ma ta de Jakob we, “Nii ywo, amo nigi nmo kwo na tage de n zembaaro we,

english_verse: to kill a wild animal and cook some tasty food for him before he dies. Your father said this because he wants to bless your brother with the Lord as his witness.
translation_verse: ‘Véi n go kago-varem n ja n ba n saŋe wodi-laao n pa-ne se a di, se a laam kwei Baŋa Wɛ zaane a ma swɛ n swolim, se a laam daare a te.’

english_verse: Now, my son, listen carefully to what I want you to do.
translation_verse: A bu, fɔge n cheigi, se n daare n ke kolo maama a na wó bere‑m to.

english_verse: Go and kill two of your best young goats and bring them to me. I'll cook the tasty food that your father loves so much.
translation_verse: Zo vara bam wone n le bebale selei n ja n ba n pa-ne. Amo laam wó ma-te a ma saŋe n kwo wodiu, se ko taa ywomma ne o na swoi-ko tei to.

english_verse: Then you can take it to him, so he can eat it and give you his blessing before he dies.”
translation_verse: Se n laam ja n zo n pa n kwo se o di. Konto wó pa se o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage n yuu ne, ye o laam daare o te.”

english_verse: “My brother Esau is a hairy man,” Jacob reminded her. “And I am not.
translation_verse: Jakob ma ta de o nu Rebeka we, “Nmo yei we amo zembaaro Esawu ye nɔn-kogo mo, ye amo ye nɔn-siswola.

english_verse: If my father touches me and realizes I am trying to trick him, he will put a curse on me instead of giving me a blessing.”
translation_verse: Amo kwo ná taane amo o nii, ko wó taa nye nenɛɛne amo wora a gane‑o mo, ye amo ya na beeri se o sɔɔle lam o yage a yuu ne to, a laam wó jwoori a ja lwarem mo a ba a pa a tete.”

english_verse: Rebekah insisted, “Let his curse fall on me! Just do what I say and bring me the meat.”
translation_verse: O nu wom maa we, “Amo bu, yage se sɔɔlem dwi maama ba amo baŋa ne. Nmo za n ke amo na we n ke tei to. Véi n ja bone dem n ba n pa-ne.”

english_verse: So Jacob brought the meat to his mother, and she cooked the tasty food that his father liked.
translation_verse: O ma seene o vo o ja-de o ba o pa o nu, ye o de saŋe wodiu kolo na ywomma to, nenɛɛne o kwo wom na lage wodiu kom tei to.

english_verse: Then she took Esau's best clothes and put them on Jacob.
translation_verse: Rebeka laam ma kwei o bu-kwea Esawu gare-laaro na wo o tei ne to, o zo o bu-balaŋa Jakob.

english_verse: She also covered the smooth part of his hands and neck with goatskins
translation_verse: O daa ta ma kwei bone dem tankwallo tem o ma o kwoli Jakob je sem dedaane o ba dem mɛ na ye siswolo to.

english_verse: and gave him some bread and the tasty food she had cooked.
translation_verse: O laam ma kwei wodi-ywoŋo kom, de bworobworo kom o na ke to o pa o bu Jakob.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father and said, “Father, here I am.” “Which one of my sons are you?” his father asked.
translation_verse: Jakob ma vo o kwo tei ye o we, “A kwo.” O de ma leiri we, “Amo bu wɔ mo konto?”

english_verse: Jacob replied, “I am Esau, your first-born, and I have done what you told me. Please sit up and eat the meat I have brought. Then you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Jakob ma leiri o kwo we, “Amo ye nmo bu-kwea Esawu mo. Amo nam ke nenɛɛne nmo na tage tei de amo to mo. Konto to, zaŋe n jeini n di amo wodiu kom, se n laam daare n sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n yage amo yuu ne.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “My son, how did you find an animal so quickly?” “The Lord your God was kind to me,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Izaak ma bwei‑o we, “Amo bu, n ke tetɛ mo n na-ko lela tento?” O ma leiri we, “Nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo woli-ne konto.”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac said, “come closer, where I can touch you and find out if you really are Esau.”
translation_verse: Izaak laam ma ta de Jakob we, “Amo bu, nam fɔɔre n yi amo yera, se a taane‑m a nii nmo seene n ye amo bu-kwea Esawu mo naa n dae.”

english_verse: Jacob went closer. His father touched him and said, “You sound like Jacob, but your hands feel hairy like Esau's.”
translation_verse: Jakob ma fɔɔre o yi o kwo Izaak tei. O ma taane‑o o nii ye o we, “Kwora kam ye Jakob kwora mo, ye jea yam laam ye Esawu jea.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” “Yes, I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: O daa ma bwei‑o we, “Konto to, nmo seene n ye amo bu-kwea Esawu mo na?” O ma leiri we, “Ɛɛ.”

english_verse: So Isaac told him, “Serve me the wild meat, and I can give you my blessing.” Jacob gave him some meat, and he ate it. He also gave him some wine, and he drank it.
translation_verse: Izaak laam ma ta we, “Ja n kago-varem nɔna yam n ba n pa-ne se a di, se a laam daare a kwei a swolim dem a pa‑m.” Jakob ma ja o yi o tei o pa‑o ye o di. O ta ma pa‑o sana ye o nyɔ.

english_verse: Then Isaac said, “Son, come over here and kiss me.”
translation_verse: O kwo Izaak laam ma ta ded‑o we, “Amo bu, fɔɔre n yi ywo, se n kukwori-ne.”

english_verse: While Jacob was kissing him, Isaac caught the smell of his clothes and said: “The smell of my son is like a field the Lord has blessed.
translation_verse: O de ma yi o tei o kukwori‑o. Izaak ma ni o gwaaro tem lwom, ye o daare o o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o we, “Nii mo! Amo bu wom lwom dem nye nenɛɛne pwola kalo Baŋa Wɛ na ke zaane o yage ka baŋa ne to lwom mo.

english_verse: God will bless you, my son, with dew from heaven and with fertile fields, rich with grain and grapes.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Wɛ wó pa se nyɔnɔ nwoŋi wɛyuu ko pa se nmo tega kam fɔge ka ke wodiiru dedɛ, se n mena de n sa-doora gaale.

english_verse: Right after Isaac had given Jacob his blessing and Jacob had gone, Esau came back from hunting.
translation_verse: Izaak na yɔɔre o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o pa Jakob o ti ye Jakob nwoŋi pwooni o daare o kwo wom to, mo o zembaaro Esawu yɔɔre o zege gaao ne o yi.

english_verse: He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Wonto de ma ke wodi-ywoŋo o ja o zo o kwo tei ne. Esawu laam ma ta o kwo we, “A kwo, zaŋe n jeini se n di a kago-varem nɔna yam, se n daare n sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n yage amo yuu ne.”

english_verse: “Who are you?” Isaac asked. “I am Esau, your first-born son.”
translation_verse: O kwo Izaak ma bwei‑o we, “Nmo ye wɔ mo?” O ma leiri we, “Amo ye nmo bu-kwea Esawu mo.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
translation_verse: Esawu maa we, “O yere na ye Jakob to seene ko ye chega mo! O gane amo tento o ke kuni belei mo. O maŋe o ŋɔ amo bu-kwea nyɔɔre dem, ye leile konto o daa vere Wɛ swolim delo ya na ye a nyem to o woli da!” O laam daa ma bwei o kwo we, “Konto, n daa ta jege Wɛ swolim se n kwei n pa-ne na?”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
translation_verse: Izaak ma leiri Esawu we, “Amo maŋe a pa se wonto ji nmo yuu tu ye a ta pa se o nu-bia maama taa ye wonto kabɛ. A nam ta kwei wodi-fɔrɔ dedaane sa-doora a pa‑o. Konto to, amo bu, bɛ daa mo wó daare se a kwei a pa‑m?”

english_verse: “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
translation_verse: Esawu ma fɔge o ta de o kwo o we, “Amo kwo, nmo bere n wo daare Wɛ swolim dedwoŋi na? Nam sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n yage amo de yuu ne! A kwo! A kwo!” Esawu ma to keira ne baŋa baŋa.

english_verse: So his father said: “Your home will be far from that fertile land, where dew comes down from the heavens.
translation_verse: O kwo Izaak ma leiri we: “Nmo zoorem jei bá taa ye tega kalo na ke wodiiru dedɛ. Tega kam ta bá na wɛyuu nyɔnɔ kom.

english_verse: You will live by the power of your sword and be your brother's slave. But when you decide to be free, you will break loose.”
translation_verse: Nmo wó ta‑n ke jara mo n zoora. Nmo wó ta‑n toŋe n pae n nyaane wom ne kabaa tei. Ko laam nam ná zo nmo yera, nmo wó vere n tete wonto dam kuri ne.”

english_verse: Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
translation_verse: Esawu na nigi konto to, o ma done Jakob, ba kwo na kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ wonto swolim to ŋwaane. O ma ta o tete ne we, “Debam kwo bá dáane ye o te. O lua kam ni ná ti, amo laam wó go a nyaane Jakob.”

english_verse: When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you.
translation_verse: Rebeka déem ma ni o bu-kwea Esawu na boŋe tei to. O ma toŋe o bwoŋi o bu-balaŋa Jakob ye o ta ded‑o we, “Nmo zembaaro wom boŋe se o go‑m mo se ko pa o bane zuri.

english_verse: Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran
translation_verse: Konto to, ke tetei amo na wó bere‑m to: Duri n vo amo nabɔ Laban tei Haran ne.

english_verse: and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry
translation_verse: Ta‑n zoore wonto sɔŋɔ ne se ko taa nii maŋa kalo nmo zembaaro wom bane dem na wó zuri to.

english_verse: and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
translation_verse: O bane dem ná seene de zuri ye o swei nmo na toŋe kolo o yera ne to, amo laam wó pa ni se nmo zege dáane n jwoori ywo. Bɛŋwaane mo amo wó yɔɔre a ga abam balei dɛ dedwe wone?”

english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Rebeka laam ma ta de Izaak o we, “Amo yera laam chɛ mo de Hiti bukwa banto Esawu na di to. Jakob de nam daa ná lage o di Hiti tiina bukɔ jei sento ne, amo toone bere de wó taa gare a ŋwea.”

english_verse: Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said: Don't marry any of those Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Rebeka déem na tage konto to, Izaak ma toŋe o bwoŋi Jakob. O ma ta ded‑o o we, “Wɛ taa wo nmo tei ne. Yé zaŋe n di Kanaan tiina bukɔ n ma n ke kaane.

english_verse: Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translation_verse: Zaŋe n vo Mesopotamia leile konto, n nu wom kwo Bɛtuweli sɔŋɔ ne, se n di kaane dáane, nmo nu nabɔ Laban bukwa bam wone.

english_verse: I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation.
translation_verse: Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom wó swɛ nmo swolim ye o pa se á ja dwi á daare á puli dedɛ se á ji nɔn-kɔgɔ.

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: Wɛ wó swɛ nmo de n dwi maama swolim, nenɛɛne o na maŋe o ke o pa n nabaaro Abaraham tei to mo, se á wane á jwoŋi tega kanto á na zoore da nenɛɛne veira tei to á ta‑á tei, nenɛɛne o na pɛ Abaraham tei to.”

english_verse: Isaac then sent Jacob to stay with Rebekah's brother Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean. Esau Marries the Daughter of Ishmael
translation_verse: Izaak ma bane Jakob o yage chwoŋa ne, ye o de ma kɛ Mesopotamia. O déem ma vo o zoore Aram tu Bɛtuweli bu Laban tei ne. Wonto déem ye Jakob de Esawu nu Rebeka nabɔ mo. Esawu di kaane wodwoŋi

english_verse: Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria
translation_verse: Esawu ma ni Izaak na ke tei o kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ Jakob swolim ye o toŋe‑o se o vo Mesopotamia o beeri kaane dáane to. O ta ma ni o na pɛ Jakob ni we, o yé di kaane Kanaan tiina bukwa bam wone.

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Esawu laam ma lɔre we Kanaan tiina bukwa bam o na di o ma o ke o kaana to wo su o kwo Izaak yi kɔtaa.

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Jakob déem ma nwoŋi Beeriseba ne o laam maa vei Haran.

english_verse: In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
translation_verse: O ma dwɛ dendwɛ o na nateini de kuri seeni na wo tega ne ye de yuu kom seeni yi Wɛ telaao ne to. Wɛ malese sem laam maa dɔɔle de baŋa ne se diini ye se tu tega ne.

english_verse: The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said: I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ba o zege da ye o we, “Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, nmo kwo Abaraham Wɛ wom, dedaane Izaak Wɛ wom. Ko ná ye tega kalo baŋa ne nmo laam na tigi tento to, amo wó kwei-ka a pa nmo de n dwi dem.

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Jakob laam ma zaŋe dɔɔm wone. O ma boŋe we, “Baŋa Wɛ seene o wo jei sento ne mo ye amo ya wo lɔre ko ni ne.”

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: Foone ma ja‑o ye o we, “Nii jei sento na jege foone tei! Ywo-seeni dae jei yɔɔ yerane, ko ye Wɛ sɔŋɔ kom mo. Mo Wɛ telaao manchwo-peena yam mo tento.”

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Tega na poore zezeŋa ne to, Jakob ma kwei kandwɛ delo o na mɛ o yeiri o yuu kom to, o cheili-de wɛɛne nenɛɛne ywei dwoŋi ye o laam lwo nuga de baŋa ne.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
translation_verse: O ma bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we ‘Bɛtel’, ye ba déem ya bwoi teo kom konto we ‘Luzi’ mo.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Jakob laam ma du duuri de Baŋa Wɛ we, “Nenɛɛne nmo ná wó taa wo amo tei ne ye n nii amo baŋa ne a chwoŋa kanto maama yuu ne, ye n ná wó pa-ne wodiu se a di dedaane gwaaro se a zo,

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: ye amo laam ba a jwoori a kwo sɔŋɔ de yazura, nmo Baŋa Wɛ wó taa ye amo Wɛ.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Dáane mo o nɛ vole na wo pwola kadwoŋi ne. Pei kɔgɔ kuni betɔ laam tigi se bwola de vole dem, kokuri to nayera bam jege se ba mɔ vole dem konto na mo ba nye pei sem. Kandwɛ delo déem na kwoli vole dem ni to maa daga dedɛ.

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: Vara bam maama ná yeini ba jeeri da ba ti, nayera bam laam yeini ba bibili kandwɛ dem ba yage dáa ne mo ye ba mɔ na ba nye pei sem. Ko kwaga ne ba daa yeini ba jwoori ba ma kandwɛ dem ba ma ba pu vole dem ni.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Jakob ma vo o bwei nayera bam we, “Amo chorro, abam nwoŋi yei mo?” Ba ma leiri we, “Debam nwoŋi Haran mo.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: O ma bwei-ba o we, “Se abam yei Nahora naa kam na ye Laban to na?” Ba ma leiri we, “Ɛɛ, dé yei‑o.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Jakob daa ma bwei-ba o we, “O jege yazura na?” Ba ma leiri we, “Ɛɛ, o jege yazura. Nii o bukɔ Racheli na kale pei sem o maa beena.”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: O maa we, “Nii-na ywo, wea kam daa taa dana. Ko ta wo yi maŋa kalo á na wó pa se vara bam jeeri ba sii to. Nam mɔ-na na bam á pa pei sem se se nyɔ se á laam pa se jwoori se vo se di gaao.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Jakob daa ta na zege o lare de nayera bam konto to, mo Racheli yi da de o kwo pei sem. O déem ye nayero mo.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: O laam ma vo Racheli tei o kukwori‑o ye o keeri wɛ-wɛ.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: O ma ta de Racheli o we o nwoŋi wonto kwo wom dwi dem wone mo, ye Rebeka mo loge‑o. Racheli na nigi konto to, o ma duri o vo o ta de o kwo.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: O kwo Laban na yɔɔre o ni o nakɔ bu Jakob ŋwa konto to, o ma ke lela o nwoŋi o vo o jeeri‑o. O ma kukwori‑o lanyerane. O ma daare o ja‑o o vo o zo o sɔŋɔ. Jakob laam ma tole taane dem maama o bere‑o.

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: Laban laam ma ta ded‑o we, “Chega to, nmo seene n ye amo tete yera mo de amo jana.” Jakob ma maŋe o sɔŋɔ ne se ko yi chana. Jakob di Leah de Racheli o ma ke kaana

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Laban déem ma ta de Jakob we, “Ko wo maŋe se nmo ta‑n toŋe n pae amo zɛɛra, n na ye amo choro to ŋwaane. Ta n bere-ne, ŋweero tɔ mo nmo wó ta‑n lage amo tei ne?”

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Leah yibia kam déem maa lamma, se ko dwoi Racheli, wonto ye-daa kam maŋe daane mo ye o tiini o lamma yi ne.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Jakob boboŋa ma zo Racheli wone ye o ta de Laban o we, “Nmo ná sɛ, amo wó toŋe a pa nmo bena yarepɛ se a jwoŋi n bukɔ-balaŋa Racheli a ma ke kaane.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Laban ma leiri o we, “A ná kwei‑o a pa nmo, ko wó taa gare a ná pɛ nɔn-gaa. Ta‑n zoore amo tei ne ywo-seeni.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Jakob ma seene o toŋe bena yarepɛ maama se o wane o jwoŋi Racheli, ye bena yam nye nenɛɛne da fenfee yerane mo o tei ne, o swono kom o na jege o pa‑o to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Jakob laam ma ta de Laban we, “Pa-ne a kaane wom. A maŋa kam n na pɛ-ne to ti, ye amo de laam lage se a peini ded‑o mo.”

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Laban ma ja teo kom nɔɔna bam maama se ba jeeri daane ba di kadiri kuri.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Tega na yi to, o laam ma gane Jakob o ja o bukɔ Leah o ja o zo o pa Jakob, ye Jakob de peini ded‑o.

english_verse: Laban also gave Zilpah to Leah as her servant woman.
translation_verse: Laban daa ta ma kwei o kaba-kana Zilipa o pa o bukɔ Leah se o ma o ji o ka-nyaane.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, mo Jakob maane we ko ye Leah mo! Ko ma pa se o ta de Laban we, “Bɛ mo ye nmo laam ke amo konto? Amo toŋe taa a pa‑m Racheli ŋwaane mo, ko dae konto mo na? Bɛ laam nam mo ke ye nmo gane amo?”

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Zuri n yera se kadiri dem da yarepɛ yam kɛ, se dé daare se a pa‑m o nyaane wom de a woli da, nenɛɛne n daa‑n ná wó toŋe bena yarepɛ daga n pa-ne.”

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Jakob ma peini de Racheli de, ye o laam za swoi Racheli o dwoi Leah. O daa ma toŋe bena yarepɛ o pa Laban. Jakob bia bam taane

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem maane we Jakob ba tiini o jege Leah swono. Konto ŋwaane o ma pa wonto lora pore lanyerane. Ko daare Racheli maa ye kadega.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Leah ma ja puga ye o lo bakeira. O ma pa o yere we ‘Ruben’, kokuri to o we, “Tento maama ye Baŋa Wɛ na nɛ amo wo-chechɔgɔ kom to ŋwaane mo. Amo baro wom laam wó taa swoi-ne.”

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: O daa ma ja puga ye o daa ta lo bakeira. O maa we, “Tento mo Baŋa Wɛ lɔre we amo gɛ nɔɔna swono, mo kokuri o pɛ a lo wonto de.” O ma pa wonto yere we ‘Simeon’.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Leah daa ta ma ja puga o lo bakeira. O laam ma ta we, “Leile konto, amo baro wom laam wó tane de amo, kokuri to a loge bakeiri setɔ a pa‑o.” O ma pa o yere we ‘Levi’.

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Jakob bane ma zaŋe ded‑o ye o we, “Amo ye Wɛ mo na? Ko dae wonto mo chege nmo de bu-lore na?”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Racheli maa we, “Nam nii amo ka-nyaane Biliha da. Peini ded‑o se o lo bia o pa amo, se amo de wane a tɔge wonto baŋa ne a na dwi.”

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: ye o ja puga o lo bakeira o pa‑o.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Racheli maa we, “Wɛ laam bere we amo de jege bora. O sɛ amo wɛ-lworo ye o pa-ne bakeira.” Konto ŋwaane, o ma pa o yere we ‘Dan’.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Racheli laam maa we, “Amo tiini a yiŋi mo de a zembaaro wom, ye a wane‑o.” O ma pa o yere we ‘Nafitali’.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Leah déem na maane we o daa ba lore bia to, o de ma kwei o ka-nyaane Zilipa o pa Jakob se o ma ji o kaane.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Leah ka-nyaane Zilipa ma lo bakeira o pa Jakob.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Leah laam maa we, “Nii a na nɛ yu-ywoŋo tei!” O ma pa bu wom yere we ‘Gad’.

english_verse: When they had another son,
translation_verse: Zilipa daa ma lo bakeira o pa Jakob.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Leah maa we, “Nii amo na nɛ wopwolo tei! Kaana bam laam wó taa tɛ we a jege yu-ywoŋo mo.” O ma pa o yere we ‘Asere’.

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Leah ma leiri o we, “Nmo maŋe n wo vere amo baro wom a tei ne mo na? Konto to, nmo ta lage se n kwei amo bu Ruben mandaraka vɔɔro tem mo n woli da na?” Racheli maa we, “Amo nam sɛ. Ke n bu wom liri sem n pa-ne, se tete dento Jakob wó ba o peini de nmo.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Dedaan-ni ne Jakob déem ma zege kara kam ne o jwoori sɔŋɔ. Leah ma nwoŋi o jeeri‑o ye o we, “Nmo zem ye se n peini de amo mo. Amo mɛ a bu Ruben mandaraka vɔɔro mo a ŋwe nmo ŋwaane se debam zem peini daane.” O ma seene o peini ded‑o dento tete dem ne.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma sɛ Leah wɛ-lworo, pa se o ja puga o lo bakeira o ke senu o pa Jakob.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Leah laam maa we, “Wɛ mo ŋwe amo ŋweero konto dedaane a na kwei a ka-nyaane wom a pa a baro wom to.” O ma pa o yere we ‘Isakara’.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: O laam maa we, “Wɛ kwei pɛɛre delo na jege yuu to mo o pa-ne. Leile konto, amo baro wom laam wó taa nege amo mo, amo na loge bu-baara baredo a pa‑o to ŋwaane.” O ma pa bu wonto yere we ‘Zebulun’.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Leah laam ma daare o lo busankana ye o pa o yere we ‘Dina’.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: O ma ja puga ye o lo bakeira pa se o we, “Wɛ kwei amo chaveera yam o ja o kɛ dáa.”

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: O ma pa bu wom yere we ‘Josɛf’, ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ ta woli bakeira kadwoŋi da o pa-ne.” Jakob pei sem puli dedɛ

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Racheli déem na loge Josɛf to mo Jakob tage de o kaane kwo Laban we, “A lwoori chwoŋa nmo tei ne, se a jwoori a vo a kwo sɔŋɔ na ye a tete teo to.

english_verse: But Laban told him, “If you really are my friend, stay on, and I'll pay whatever you ask. I'm sure the Lord has blessed me because of you.”
translation_verse: Ta n bere-ne, nmo na lage se n ŋweero taa ye tei maama to, se amo wó ŋwe-te a pa‑m.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Jakob ma ta ded‑o we, “Nmo yei amo na toŋe tei ye a yere n vara bam pa se ba ke lanyerane amo jeŋa ne to.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Fenfee kolo nmo déem na jege ye amo ya ta wo tu n tei ne to laam puli mo dedɛ. Mɛ maama amo ná via, Baŋa Wɛ yeini o ke zaane mo o ke nmo yuu ne. Se leile konto, ko maŋe se a ke kolo na wó woli a tete sɔŋɔ tiina bam mo.”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Laban ma bwei‑o we, “Nmo nam we a pa‑m bɛ mo?” Jakob ma leiri we, “Amo nam bá jwoŋi ŋweero nmo tei ne. Za n sɛ se n ke kolo amo na wó lwoori nmo tei ne to, se a ta wó kale n vara bam a nii ba baŋa ne.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Nam pa-ne chwoŋa zem se a zo nmo vara bam wone a le pi-poporro tem de pipeili selo maama na zwora to, ko woli de bom-poporro tem. Sento dwi maama mo wó taa ye amo ŋweero.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Konto to, amo chega kam laam wó bere jaja jwa seeni mo. Nmo ná tua se n nii ŋweero telo n na pɛ amo to, ye n ná nɛ we amo jege boŋo kolo na dae poporro, naa pipeila kalo na ba zwora to, ta‑n yei we a ŋɔge-te nmo tei ne mo.”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Dento dɛ dem ne nɔɔ mo, Laban vei o le bo-bale selo na ye poporro to, de bo-chwa yalo yera na ye nyɔge nyɔge ye ya jege napwoŋo to o ta woli de pipeili selo na zwora to dwi maama, o pɔɔre-se o ke o bu-baara bam jeŋa ne se ba taa nii-se.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: O ma pa ba vo da yatɔ veiŋa mo ba daare Jakob dedaane vara balo na daare ye o jege-ba o yere to.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Jakob ma na ye o gwoni teeni dedwonna nɛ. Teeni dento dɛ sem ye napwonnu, de yera maa ye Popela, de Aamonda, de Pileeni. O laam ma lɔɔre lɔɔre nɛ sem poro tem jei sedwonna o daare bibeiri-pwonnu pa te wo da-lɛɛro tem wone.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Jakob ma pɔɔre pipeili sem o ke dáa ba yerane. O déem ma yeini o pa pei selo na daare to yɔɔre se jeeri Laban vara balo na zwora de balo na ye vare-poporro to. O ke konto mo o ma na vara o tete ŋwaane ye o wo woli-ba Laban vara bam wone.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye vare-nabwona bam, o yeini o ba ke konto. Ko ma pa se vare-nabwona bam woli Laban vara bam wone ye vare-dedɛɛra bam ji Jakob nyem.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Ko dɛ konto baŋa ne mo ye Jakob tiini o duni. O laam ma ba o jege o tete vara dedɛ, dedaane kona de bonɛ, de kabɛ, baara de kaana maama.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Jakob déem ma ni Laban bia bam na tɛ ba we, “Jakob mo jwoŋi debam kwo déem ya na jege kolo maama to. O zege debam kwo jeŋa wonnu baŋa ne mo o duni.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Jakob ta ma maane we Laban yi daa ta ba sui ded‑o, nenɛɛne ko déem na ye tei to.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Jakob we, “Zaŋe n jwoori n vo n kwoa teo kom, nmo chorro tem na zoore mɛ to, se amo wó taa wo nmo tei ne.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Jakob ma toŋe o bwoŋi Racheli de Leah se ba ba ba jeeri‑o pwola kalo ne o na nii o vara bam da to.

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: O ma ta de-ba we, “Amo maane we abam kwo yi laam daa ba sui dedaane amo, nenɛɛne ko déem na ye tei to. De konto de, Wɛ wom amo kwo na zuli‑o to wo amo tei ne.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Abam yei we amo mɛ a dam maama mo a toŋe a pa á kwo wom.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: De konto maama de, abam kwo wom yeini o pini amo mo ye o leiri amo ŋweero tem kuni fuga. Woŋo maama wone, Wɛ wo pɛ‑o chwoŋa se o ke amo wo-lɔŋɔ.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: O ná yeini o we, vara balo na ye nyɔge nyɔge to mo wó taa ye amo ŋweero, vara bam maama wó lo bia balo na ye nyɔge nyɔge to mo. O daa ná we, vare-poporro tem mo wó taa ye a ŋweero, vara bam maama ta wó lo vare-poporro mo.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Ko ye Wɛ mo dɛ chwoŋa kam konto o jwoŋi abam kwo vara bam o kwei o pa amo.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Amo mo ye Wɛ wolo déem na jeeri‑m Bɛtel ne to. Dáane mo nmo de déem chwi kandwɛ nenɛɛne ywei dwoŋi ye n lwo nuga de baŋa ne n daare n pwooli amo yiga ne. Konto to, zaŋe da teo konto ne leile se n daare n jwoori n vo teo kolo ba na loge‑m to.’ ”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Dé kwo laam maŋe o ke debam nenɛɛne dé ye veira mo tei. O kwei debam mo o yeigi o pa‑m, ye o ta daare o di nyɔɔre delo o na jwoŋi debam ŋwaane to o ti.

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Chega wone to, jejegero telo maama Wɛ na jwoŋi debam kwo wom tei ne o pa nmo to seene te ye debam dedaane dé bia bam nyem mo. Konto to, ke kolo maama Wɛ na we n ke to.”

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Ba na tage konto to, Jakob laam ma kwei o bia de o kaana bam o jeini kona baŋa ne,

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: ye o kale o vara bam maama o ke yiga ne, ko woli de wonnu telo maama o na nɛ Mesopotamia ne to, se o jwoori o vo o kwo Izaak tei Kanaan teo kom ne.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Laban déem ma nwoŋi o vo se o pa ba fane o pei sem koro. Racheli ma zo o ŋɔ o kwo jwona yam.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: O déem ma zaŋe Laban tei ne o kwei o jejegero maama o ke lela o viiri. O ma vo o bɛ Yuferata bu-nia kam o vo o yi Gilead zwonnu laŋa kam. Laban duri o pu Jakob kwaga

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Da yatɔ na kɛ to mo ba tage ba bere Laban we Jakob duri mo o maa viira.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: O ma la o fara o ke daane, ye o laam duri o pare Jakob da yarepɛ. O ma pare o ja‑o Gilead zwonnu laŋa kam ne.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Tete ne Wɛ ma ba Aram tu Laban tei dendwɛ wone ye o ta ded‑o we, “Ta‑n yei se n yé ta kolokolo dedaane Jakob se ko taa ye botare-laao naa botare-balɔrɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Laban na yi Jakob tei konto to, Jakob déem ya tei o vwoa Gilead zwonnu laŋa kam ne mo. Laban de o fara bam de ma tei ba vwoa dáane.

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Nmo na gane-ne tei to, n seigi amo yiga ne n duri mo. Nmo nam ya ná tage n bere-ne se a bane‑m, a ya wó yage‑m chwoŋa ne dedaane wopwolo, ye ba leeni lei ye ba mage kwanno dedaane senyɛ ba pa‑m.

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: N maŋe n wo pɛ-ne pwola se a kukwori a naaro tem dedaane a bukwa bam se a bane-ba a yage chwoŋa ne. Nmo na ke tei to, n tiini n toŋe totoŋ-jworo dedɛ.

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: Amo nam yei nmo na duri kolo ŋwaane to, n kwo sɔŋɔ kom fera mo jaane‑m. Se bɛŋwaane mo nmo nam ŋɔge amo jwona yam n woli da n jege n ma‑n viira?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
