translation_verse: Jakob ma leiri Laban we, “Foone mo jaane amo, kokuri to amo ya boŋe we nmo wó ma dam mo n vere n bukwa bam amo tei ne.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Se ko daare, nmo ná nɛ n jwona yam nɔɔno wolo tei ne, konto tu maŋe se o te mo. Debam maama fara bam yiga ne ywo, fɔge n nii n ná wó na n woŋo amo wonnu tem wone. N nam ná nɛ kolo, se n kwei.” Jakob déem na tage konto to, o wo lɔre we Racheli mo ŋɔge o kwo jwona yam.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Laban laam ma zo Jakob vwei dem wone, de Leah vwei dem wone, de ka-nyaana balei bam vwei dem wone ye o wo nɛ kolokolo. O na nwoŋi Leah vwei dem ne to mo o vei o zo Racheli vwei dem.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Racheli déem ya kwei o kwo jwona yam o ke o kone dem pɔlɔ ne mo ye o laam jei pɔlɔ kom baŋa ne. Laban ma beeri o taane vwei dem jei maama ne ye o wo nɛ kolokolo.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Racheli ma ta de o kwo we, “Amo tu, yé pa se n bane zaŋe, se amo bá wane a zaŋe wɛɛne, kokuri to, amo wo a zarem wone mo.” Ko ma pa se o beeri wuu ye o wo nɛ o sɔŋɔ jwona yam.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Jakob bane ma zaŋe ye o bwɛ Laban. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Amo ke bɛ mo a ja a chɔge? Amo ke lwarem dɔ mo ye nmo laam tɔge amo nɛ tento?

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Kago-vara mo ná maŋe ba ja nmo vara bam wone ba tore tore de, a ba jaane-ba a tui n tei ne se n nii. Amo nam yeini a jwoori a yiri varem wom konto mo a pa‑m. Ŋweena ná vere woŋo, wea ne de tete ne maama, nmo wó pa se a jwoori a yiri-ko mo a pa‑m.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Amo na toŋe a pa‑m tei to, fonyogo déem mage-ne wea ne, ye tete ne waaro zoore-ne dedɛ. Dɔɔm de maa ba tui a yia ne.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Ko nam ye Wɛ mo woli-ne, o na ye a kwo Abaraham Wɛ wom ye Izaak dé kɔre‑o to. Ko nam ya ná dae Wɛ na wo amo tei ne to ŋwaane, nmo ya lage n bane amo n yage chwoŋa ne de je-kore mo. Wɛ nam nɛ ko na tiini ko zo amo yera ye n bɛɛse-ne totoŋa yam baŋa ne tei to. Konto ŋwaane mo pa se o ba nmo tei diim tete ne o bwei nmo.”

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Laban ma leiri Jakob ye o we, “Kaana bam ye amo bukwa mo, bia bam ye amo bia mo, ye vara bam de ye amo vara mo. Chega to, woŋo kolo maama n yia na nae to ye amo nyem. De konto maama de, a jeŋa daa tera de a bukwa banto de bia balo ba na loge to.

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Konto to, pa se dé gwoni ni dé pa daane, se ko taa ye maana debam balei laŋa ne.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Jakob na nigi konto to, o ma kwei kandwɛ o chwi-de nenɛɛne ywei dwoŋi.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: O ma ta de o fara bam we, “Twɛ twɛ-na kandwa á ja á ba-na ywo.” Nɔɔna bam ma la kandwa yam ye ba dogele-ya pa se ya di wɛɛne. Jakob de Laban laam ma jeini kandwa-pwoa yam teiŋa ne ba di wodiu.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban ma bwoŋi jei sem yere we ‘Jegare-Sahadufa’, ye Jakob de bwoŋi jei sem we ‘Galeede’.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban maa we, “Zem dɛ dem ne kandwa-pwoa yanto na dogele to ye maana mo debam balei laŋa ne.” Mo kokuri jei sem yere ye Galeede.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Ba déem ta bwoi jei sem we ‘Mizipa’ mo, kokuri to Laban tage we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó taa yere debam maama, nenɛɛne dé ná maŋe dé wo yiga yiga da-tei ne.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Nenɛɛne nmo ná yaare amo bukwa bam naa n ná n daa‑n ná vei n di kaana badwonna n woli amo bukwa bam wone, nam guli we nɔɔn-nɔɔno ná seene o tere debam tei ne, ko ye Wɛ mo ye maana debam balei laŋa ne.”

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Kandwa-pwoa yanto dedaane ywei dento maa ye maana ya pae debam. Amo bá gaale kandwa yanto a kɛ a ba a yi nmo laŋa kam ne a ke‑m zonne, ye nmo de nam bá gaale-ya se n kɛ n ba amo de laŋa kam ne n ke amo zonne.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Debam kwoa bam Wɛ, Abaraham Wɛ wom, de Nahora Wɛ wom mo wó taa bore bora debam balei laŋa ne.” Jakob laam ma sɛ ye o du duuri Baŋa Wɛ wom o kwo Izaak na kɔre to yere ŋwaane.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: O laam ma go varem o ma kaane o pa Wɛ zwonnu laŋa kam ne ye o daare o bwoŋi o fara bam maama se ba ba ba di ded‑o. Ba na di ba ti to, ba ma maŋe da ba peini se tega poore.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Tega na poore zezeŋa ne to, Laban ma kukwori o bukwa bam de ba bia bam ye o kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ ba swolim. O laam ma kɛ o jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Jakob de ma kwei o chwoŋa o maa kɛa. Wɛ malese ma ba se jeeri‑o.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: O de na nɛ-se to, o maa we, “Wɛ na tei o vwoa de o kwaga tɔgena bam mɛ to mo tento!” O déem bwoŋi jei sem yere we ‘Mahanayim’.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Jakob ma pa nɔɔna ni se ba da yiga ba vo o zembaaro Esawu tei Seyira ne. Edom teo kom mo konto.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: A jege naane de bonɛ de peeni de bone, dedaane kabɛ, baara de kaana maama mo. Konto ŋwaane mo a toŋe kwora kanto a pa‑m se ko pa amo totoŋa yam su nmo yi.’ ”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na via ye ba jwoori Jakob tei ne to, ba ma ta we, “Dé vei dé yi nmo zembaaro Esawu tei. O de nam maa beene nmo tei mo se o jeeri‑m, ye baara bia yana wo o tei ne.”

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: Kokuri to, o boŋe mo we, “Esawu ná tu o yi kɔgɔ popɔra dedoa o chiŋi-ka, popɔra kadwoŋi kam wó duri ka lu.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: O laam ma lwoori Wɛ ye o we, “Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, wom na ye a kwoa Abaraham de Izaak Wɛ to, nmo ya tage de amo n we ‘Jwoori n teo de n chorro tem tei ne, se amo wó ke‑m lanyerane.’

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: Jwoŋi-ne n yage amo zembaaro Esawu jeŋa ne, se amo jege foone we o wó ba o chiŋi amo, de kaana bam dedaane bia bam maama.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Nmo nam maŋe n ta we ‘A wó seene a ke‑m lanyerane. A ta wó pa se n dwi dem taa puli dedɛ nenɛɛne naneo ni kasolo na daga tei to mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam bá wane o nii o ga o ti.’ ”

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne Jakob ma maŋe da o peini. Tega na poore to, o ma twori pɛɛra o jejegero tem wone, se o pa o zembaaro Esawu.

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: Ta‑á yei-na se á za ta we ‘N nyaane Jakob wo kwaga ne o beene.’ ” Kokuri to, o déem boŋe o yuu ne mo we, “Esawu ná nɛ pɛɛra yam a na pɛ se ya tɔge a yiga ya kɛ to, ko wó wane ko pa se o bochare zuri, se amo laam ná yi o tei, dɛ delo o wó jeeri-ne lanyerane.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Jakob ma bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we ‘Peneli’, ye o we, “Amo nɛ Wɛ yibia dedaane yibia ye o duri amo yibwona pa se a wo tege.”

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: O ma daare o ta o bere wolo wom na tɔge ba maama yiga to we, “Amo zembaaro Esawu ná jeeri‑m ye o bwei we ‘Nmo ye wɔ nɔɔno mo? N nam maa n vei yei ne mo, ye wɔ mo tei vara banto maama nmo na jege-ba n kale to?’,

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Konto to, Jakob pɛɛra yam ma lwoori yiga ya kɛ, ye o tete maŋe jei sem ne o peini se tega ba ka poore. Jakob jaŋe dedaane Baŋa Wɛ

english_verse: Jacob got up in the middle of the night and took his wives, his eleven children, and everything he owned across to the other side of the Jabbok River for safety.
translation_verse: O déem na jaane-ba o pa ba bɛ konto to, o ma daare o pa se o jejegero tem maama de tɔge te bɛ.

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: Jakob tete ma maŋe dáane o yerane. Nɔɔno wodwoŋi ma ba o zo jaŋa ded‑o taa, se tega laam ba ka poore.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom laam ma ta we, “Yage-ne se a viiri, se tega lage ka poore mo.” Jakob de ma leiri we, “Nmo ná wo sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n yage amo yuu ne, amo bá sɛ a yage‑m se n viiri!”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma bwei‑o we, “Nmo yere mo bɛ?” O ma leiri we, “A yere mo Jakob.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom laam maa we, “Nmo yere daa bá taa ye Jakob, n yere laam wó taa ye Isarele mo, kokuri to nmo jaŋe jaŋa de Wɛ, ye n ta jaŋe dedaane nabiina. Nmo nam wane.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Jakob laam ma ta we, “Jan ja, ta nmo yere n bere-ne.” O ma leiri we, “Bɛŋwaane mo ye n bwei amo yere bwia?” O laam ma zege da o kwei Wɛ zaane o ma swɛ Jakob swolim.

translation_verse: Wɛ puli mo de maa diini wɛyuu ye Jakob zege Peneli ne o maa kɛa. O ma via ye o dua, o takeiri dem na ywori to ŋwaane.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Esawu laam ma kwoni o yuu wɛɛne o na kaana bam de bia bam maama. O ma bwei‑o we, “Se banto ye bera mo ba wo nmo tei ne to?” Jakob ma leiri we, “Amo tu, mo bia balo Wɛ na dɛ o zaane baŋa ne o pa amo to.”

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Ka-nyaana bam laam ma fɔɔre ba yi, ba de ba bia, ba chɔɔle tega ne.

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.

translation_verse: Esawu ma bwei we, “Se vara balo maama amo na jeeri chwoŋa ne to bere bɛ mo?” O ma leiri we, “Amo tu, ko maama ye se ko pa a totoŋa yam su nmo yi mo.”

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Esawu ma ta o we, “A nyaane, amo maŋe a jege dedɛ mo. Nmo de ta‑n jege n wonnu.”

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Jakob maa we, “Jan ja, nmo yi ná su amo, se n sɛ n jwoŋi pɛɛre dento amo tei ne. A na nɛ nmo yibia to, ko nye de a nɛ Wɛ yibia mo, ko fɔge ko woli de nmo na jeeri amo de wopwolo tei to.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: Nam kwaane se n jwoŋi pɛɛra yalo ba na jaane ba ba pa‑m to, kokuri to Wɛ tiini o ke zaane a baŋa ne ye a jege kolo maama a na lage to.” Jakob na tiini o fe to, Esawu ma sɛ o jwoŋi pɛɛra yam.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Esawu laam ma ta we, “Nam véi se dé kɛ. Amo wó kwogili‑m chwoŋa kam yuu ne.”

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Jakob ma ta ded‑o we, “Amo tu, nmo yei we bia bam tiini ba muri, ye a ta jege se a taa nii pei sem de naane dem baŋa ne mo, ba na jege vare-mɔra to ŋwaane. A ná lage se a tiini a kale vara bam konto dɛ dedwe wone, ba maama wó te mo.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: Konto to, amo tu, nmo da yiga n ta‑n via, se amo wó kale vara bam a ke yiga ne a taa vei mɛ mɛ, ye bia bam de tɔga. Amo laam wó ba a jeeri‑m Seyira ne.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Esawu ma leiri o we, “Ko nam ná ye konto, yage se a pa se a baara bam badwonna maŋe nmo tei ne ba taa tɔge ba via.” Jakob ma leiri we, “Amo tu, bɛ mo ye n jege n tete n daana? Nmo yi na su amo totoŋa yam to, ko maŋe.”

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Jakob de déem ma vo Sukofa. O déem ma lɔ sɔŋɔ da, ye o daare o tei pwei se o vara bam taa tigi da. Mo kokuri pa se jei sem konto yere ye Sukofa.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Jakob déem ya zege Mesopotamia ne ye o laam vo o yi Sɛkɛm. Teo kom konto déem wo Kanaan ne mo. O ma yi da de yazura ye o jeini teo kom pwooni yiga ne.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: O déem na chwi o vwoa yam mɛ to, o ma yeigi tega kam Hamora bia bam tei ne. Sɛkɛm kwo mo konto. Tega kam jene déem ye lu-nyenno sabu-dala bi mo.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: O déem ta ma lɔ bimbini jei sem konto ne se o ma zuli Wɛ, ye o bwoŋi de yere we ‘Isarele tiina Wɛ wom mo ye Wɛ chekke dem’.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Dina déem ye bukɔ wolo Leah na loge o pa Jakob to mo. Dɛ dedwe mo o zaŋe o vo se o jeeri Kanaan teo kom bukwa bam.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Hamora déem ye Hivi tu mo na ye pɛ jei sem konto ne. O maa jege bu-baaro, o yere na ye Sɛkɛm. Sɛkɛm na nɛ Dina to, o ma ja‑o o zi o chɔge.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: O boboŋa déem ma tiini ya zo Dina wone. O na swoi‑o to ŋwaane, o ma ŋɔɔne o kwoori‑o.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Sɛkɛm ma ta de o kwo Hamora o we, “Tɔge bukɔ wonto nɛ n pa-ne se a ma a ke a kaane.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Jakob déem ma ni Sɛkɛm na chɔge o bukɔ Dina tei to, ye o ta maane we o bu-baara bam ta wo gaao ne mo ba nii o vara bam. O maa wo tage kolokolo, ye o cheigi-ba se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Jakob bia bam ma nwoŋi gaao wo ba jwoori sɔŋɔ ye ba ni kolo na ke Dina to. Ba wo ma tiini ko chɔge ye ba bane de zaŋe ko ja gaale. Kokuri to, Sɛkɛm na zi Jakob bukɔ wom to, o yaale Isarele dwi dem mo. Keim dem konto nam ya wo maŋe se nɔɔno toŋe kɔtaa.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Hamora ma ta de-ba o we, “Amo bu Sɛkɛm bochare maama wo abam bukɔ wom wone mo. Jan ja, sɛ-na se o di‑o o ma ke kaane.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Pa-na se dé bia taa di daane. Yei-na á bukwa á pa debam, se á de swo debam de bukwa.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Abam wó wane á ta‑á zoore dedaane debam. Nii-na tega kam maama mo tento abam yiga ne. Ta‑á zoore-na ka wone, se á ta‑á beeri á pipia ye á daare á yeigi tega á ta‑á tei.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Taane dem Sɛkɛm de o kwo Hamora déem na jege ba ŋɔɔne to, Jakob bia bam seigi ba wo mo ba leiri-ba. Ba ke konto kolo ŋwaane Sɛkɛm maŋe o chɔge ba nakɔ Dina.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Ba ma ta de-ba we, “Debam bá wane de ke konto. Debam bá kwei dé nakɔ dé yei dé pa baaro wolo na wo gwoni o peini to. Konto ye chaveera mo debam tei ne.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Ko nam ye se abam mo sɛ se á ke woŋo dedoo á pa debam. Abam dedaane debam maŋe se dé taa ye bedwe mo peina gwonim baŋa ne. Abam jege se á gwoni á baara bam maama peina mo.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Abam nam ná wo sɛ se á gwoni á baara peina, debam wó ja dé nakɔ mo dé viiri abam teo kom ne.”

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Ba taane dem maa lamma de pae Hamora de o bu Sɛkɛm.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Nɔn-doŋo kom daa wo jaane taane dem o jeini. O bochare maama nam na wo Jakob bukɔ wom wone to, ko pɛ se o ke kolo maama ba na bere‑o se o ke to. O kwo sɔŋɔ kom nɔɔna maama déem maa nege‑o dedɛ.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Hamora de o bu Sɛkɛm laam ma nwoŋi ba vo teo kom manchwo-peena ni ne, se ba ŋɔɔne de ba teo kom baara bam.

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: Ba ma ta de-ba we, “Nɔɔna banto yeini ba ke debam lanyerane. Nam sɛ-na se dé pa-ba pwola se ba taa zoore debam teo kom ne. Ba ta wó wane ba taa beera ba ke pipiu ywo-seeni. Debam tega kam daga se ka yi banto de jeiŋa. Dé maa wó wane dé swo ba bukwa ye dé kwei debam de bukwa dé yei-ba.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Woŋo kodoo mo daare se dé ke dé pa nɔɔna bam, se ba laam sɛ ba taa zoore dedaane debam se dé taa ye dwi dedoa. Ba lage se debam baara maama de gwoni dé peina nenɛɛne banto tete na ke tei to.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ke konto, ba naane, de ba jejegero, dedaane ba vara maama laam bá taa ye debam nyem mo na? Konto, pa-na se dé sɛ ba boboŋe dem, se ba taa zoore dedaane debam.”

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Ba na gwoni ba peina yam ye da yatɔ yi to, mo Jakob bu-baara balei, Simeon dedaane Levi, zaŋe ba nwoŋi ba vo Sɛkɛm teo kom. Teo kom baara bam ta wo ba peina gwonim zonne dem wone mo. Dina nabwa balei bam ma kwei ba se-zɔɔro ba zaŋe teo kom baara bam baŋa ne ba go ba maama.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Jakob bu-baara badaara de ma zo teo kom wo ba tɔge twa bam baŋa ne ba ŋɔ teo kom zela yam maama, se ba ma ŋwe ba nakɔ wom chaveera yam jene.

english_verse: God told Jacob, “Return to Bethel, where I appeared to you when you were running from your brother Esau. Make your home there and build an altar for me.”
translation_verse: Wɛ déem laam ma ta Jakob o we, “Zaŋe n vo Bɛtel n ta‑n zoore da. Nmo ná yi da, se n tigisi kandwa n lɔ bimbini, se n zuli amo, Baŋa Wɛ, kokuri to, amo mo tua nmo tei maŋa kalo n déem na duri se n lu n zembaaro Esawu jeŋa ne to.”

english_verse: Jacob said to his family and to everyone else who was traveling with him: Get rid of your foreign gods! Then make yourselves acceptable to worship God and put on clean clothes.
translation_verse: Jakob ma sɛ ye o ta de o diga tiina, de balo maama na wo o tei ne to o we, “Dole-na dwi-gɛ tiina jwona yalo na wo abam tei ne to á yage. Ta‑á kwɛ-na á tete, se á daare á leiri-na á gwaaro tem.

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Pa-na dé zaŋe dé vo Bɛtel. Dáane mo amo lage a lɔ bimbini a ma a zuli Wɛ, wolo wom na zeini-ne maŋa kam a déem na wo yaara wone to, ye o da amo yiga a veiŋa maama ne to.”

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma kwei chwoŋa ba maa kɛa. Wɛ ma pa se foone tiini de ja teo kom konto de ko nawuura yam nɔɔna maama. Konto ma pa se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa ware se o zeili o da Jakob de o nɔɔna bam kwaga.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: O na yi da to mo o lɔge bimbini se o ma o zuli Wɛ. O ma bwoŋi jei sem yere we ‘El-Bɛtel’, kolo ŋwaane ko ye dáane mo Wɛ bere o tete ded‑o maŋa kalo o déem na maa dura se o lu o zembaaro Esawu jeŋa ne to.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Kaane wolo déem ya na nii Rebeka baŋa ne to ma ba o te jei sem konto ne. O yere mo Debora. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli tei-zɔŋɔ kom kuri ne, ko na wo Bɛtel kuri seeni to. Ba ma bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we ‘Wo-chechɔgɔ keira tio’.

english_verse: After Jacob came back to the land of Canaan, God appeared to him again. This time he gave Jacob a new name and blessed him by saying: I am God All-Powerful, and from now on your name will be Israel instead of Jacob. You will have many children. Your descendants will become nations, and some of the men in your family will even be kings.
translation_verse: Wɛ laam ma ta‑o we, “Amo mo ye Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom. Ja dwi se n daare n puli de kɔgɔ. Teene dedɛ wó nwoŋi nmo yera ne, ye pwa de wó taa wora n dwi dem wone.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: A pɛ‑m tega kalo a déem na kwei a pa Abaraham de Izaak to mo se n ta‑n tei-ka. Amo nam ta wó pa nmo dwi dem na wó saŋe nmo kwaga to.”

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Jeiga kalo Wɛ na zege o ŋɔɔne ded‑o to mo Jakob déem kwei kandwɛ o chwi da. O ta ma kwei wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛre de nuga o lwo de baŋa ne o pa Wɛ.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Jakob déem bwoŋi mɛ Wɛ na zege o ŋɔɔne ded‑o to we ‘Bɛtel’. Racheli toone

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Ba déem ma zaŋe Bɛtel ne ba kwei chwoŋa ba maa kɛa. Ba na gɛ fee se ba yi Eferata to mo Racheli virigi puga se o lo, ye ko chɛ o yera ne.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Lora kam na tiini ko chamma ka pa‑o konto to, mo ka-lworinu wolo na jaane‑o se o lo to tage ded‑o we, “Yé ta‑n lwia, se n daa‑n nɛ bakeira kadwoŋi mo.”

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Racheli déem maa wora o toa. O siu kom na lage ko kwori to, mo o pɛ o bakeira kam yere we ‘Benoni’. Bu wom kwo de déem ma pa o yere we ‘Benjamin’.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Racheli ma te ye ba suli‑o Eferata chwoŋa kam yuu ne .

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Jakob ma kwei kandwɛ o chwi Racheli yibeeli dem baŋa ne. De zem maama, kandwɛ dem konto mo bere mɛ yibeeli dem na zege to.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Jakob daa ma kwei chwoŋa o kɛ, ye o vo o chwi o vwei Migadal Edera kwaga ne.

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Jakob ta na zoore laŋa kam konto ne to mo Ruben zoa o peini de o kwo ka-bia dedoa, o yere na ye Biliha to. Jakob ma ni ko ŋwa. Jakob déem jege bu-baara fuga-balei mo.

english_verse: Jacob had twelve sons while living in northern Syria. His first-born Reuben was the son of Leah, who later gave birth to Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun. Leah's servant Zilpah had two sons: Gad and Asher. Jacob and his wife Rachel had Joseph and Benjamin. Rachel's servant woman Bilhah had two more sons: Dan and Naphtali. Isaac Dies
translation_verse: Leah ka-nyaane Zilipa de bu-baara bam mo tento: Gad dedaane Asere. Mo Jakob bu-baara bam mo konto, o kaana bam na loge ba pa‑o ye o déem ta wo Mesopotamia ne to. Izaak toone

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Jakob ma zaŋe o jwoori o vo o kwo Izaak tei, Mamere ne. Jei sem konto déem bwola dedaane Kiriaf-Araba mo . Abaraham de Izaak déem nam zoore dáane mo.

english_verse: Esau, also known as Edom, had many descendants.
translation_verse: Esawu dwi dem mo tento. Wonto yere dedwoŋi maa ye Edom.

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Esawu déem di Kanaan tiina bukwa bam wone mo o ma o ke o kaana. Ba dedoa déem ye Hiti tu Elon bukɔ mo, o yere mo Ada. Balei tu wom maa ye Ana bukɔ Oholibama. Ana déem ye Hivi tu Zibeon bu mo.

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: O déem ta di Isameli bukɔ Basemafa o woli da. Wonto maa ye Nebayofa nakɔ.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Oholibama de déem ma lo Jewusi, de Jalam, dedaane Kora. Esawu kaana bam déem loge bia bam konto maama maŋa kalo o ta na wo Kanaan teo kom ne to mo.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Konto to, Esawu déem vei o zoore Seyira zwonnu laŋa kam ne.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Balo na ye nakwa ye ba nwoŋi Esawu dwi dem ne to mo tento: O bu-kwea Elifaza mo ye dwia yanto nabaaro: Teman, de Omara, de Zefo, de Kenazi,

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: de Kora, de Gatam dedaane Amaleki. Banto maama ye Elifaza bia mo, ye ba kwori ba ye Ada naaro.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
translation_verse: Esawu bu Reweli de maa ye dwia yanto nabaaro: Nahafi, de Zera, Samma dedaane Miza. Banto maama déem ye Reweli bia mo ye ba ye Esawu kaane Basemafa naaro.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Esawu bia balo Ana bukɔ Oholibama na loge o pa‑o to mo banto: Jewusi, de Jalam dedaane Kora. Dwia yam konto maama mo nwoŋi Esawu kaane Ohilibama ne to.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Banto maama déem mo ye Esawu dwi nabaara bam.

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lotan dwi dem nabaara mo tento: Hori dedaane Homam. Timina de déem maa ye Lotan nakɔ.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Sobal dwi dem nabaara mo tento: Alivan, de Manahafa, de Ebal, de Sefo, dedaane Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Zibeon dwi dem nabaara mo tento: Aya dedaane Ana. Ana wonto wom déem mo wo kagoa kam ne o tɔge o kwo bonɛ ye o beeri beeri o vo o na buli-yi delo na na lomma to.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Ezere de dwi dem nabaara mo tento: Bilihan, de Zaavan dedaane Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Disan de dwi dem nabaara mo tento: Yuzi dedaane Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Banto maama déem mo ye Hori dwi dem nabaara bam: Lotan, de Sobal, de Zibeon, de Ana,

english_verse: Before there were kings in Israel, the following kings ruled Edom one after another: Bela son of Beor from Dinhabah; Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah; Husham from the land of Teman; Hadad son of Bedad from Avith ; Samlah from Masrekah; Shaul from the city of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River; Baalhanan son of Achbor; Hadar from the city of Pau .
translation_verse: Baal-Hanan déem na tege to, mo Hadad leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ. Wonto teo kom yere déem mo ye Pawu. O kaane de yere déem mo ye Mehetabeli. Mehetabeli kwo mo déem ye Matiredi ye o kwo-nakwe yere déem ye Mezahabi.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Esawu dwi dem déem na seere tei maama to mo tento, ba de ba nabaara bam, dedaane ba sɔ-yuni tem maama: Timina, de Aliva, de Jefeti,

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: de Oholibama, de Ela, de Pinon,

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: de Kenazi, de Teman, de Mibizare,

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: de Magadeli dedaane Yiram. Edom dwi dem yera mo konto, de jei selo maama ba na jeini to yera yam. Esawu déem mo ye Edom tiina nabaaro.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Jakob déem ta zoore Kanaan teo kom ne mo, jei selo o kwo de déem na maŋe o zoore da to.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma leiri we, “Ba daa tere ywo-seeni. Amo nigi ba na ŋɔɔne ba bere daane we ‘Pa-na se dé vo Dotan.’ ” Josɛf na nigi konto to, o ma da o zembaara bam nɛ o vo o na-ba Dotan laŋa kam ne.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Jakob déem nam swoi Josɛf mo o dwoi o bia babam bam, kokuri to, o loge wonto o kokweero maŋa ne mo. O déem ma sɔ gare-bwora na tiini ka jege nenɔŋa to o pa‑o.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: Josɛf zembaara bam na nɛ we ba kwo swoi wonto mo o dwoi ba maama to, ba ma tiini ba chuli‑o ye ba yaale‑o.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe Josɛf ma dwɛ dendwɛ ye o daare o ta o bere o zembaara bam. Ko ma fɔge ko pa ba chuli‑o dedɛ ba woli da.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: O déem maa we, “Cheigi-na a dendwɛ dento:

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Amo dwɛ we debam maama wo kara ne mo dé vɔ mena. Amo tete men-pwoa yam laam ma zaŋe ya zege wɛɛne cheppe. Abam maama men-pwoa yam laam ma gilimi amo nyem dem ye ya chɔɔle ya tiiri tega ne ya zuli-de.”

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: O zembaara bam ma ta ded‑o we, “Konto nmo boŋe se n ba n di paare mo debam baŋa ne na? Nmo lage se n ba n ta‑n dwoi debam mo na?” O dendwea yam de o bebare taana yam ŋwaane mo ba déem tiini ba chuli‑o dedɛ.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Josɛf déem ta ma dwɛ dendwɛ dedwoŋi, ye o ta de o zembaara bam we, “Cheigi-na! Amo daa dwɛ dendwɛ dedwoŋi mo we, wea kam de chana kam dedaane chalechwe fuga-dedoa mo chɔɔle tega ne amo yiga ne.”

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: O déem na tage-de o bere o kwo de o woli da to, mo o kwo bwɛ‑o ye o we, “Dendwɛ dwi dɔ mo konto nmo dwɛ? Ko ná ye nmo nu, de amo tete, de n zembaara bam maama, dé wó seene dé ba dé chɔɔle tega ne nmo yiga ne na?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: O zembaara bam maama déem ma zwe kazwe ded‑o. Ko daare ye o kwo wom kwei taane dem o ke o boboŋa ne. Josɛf zembaara bam kwei‑o ba yeigi

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Josɛf zembaara bam déem ma kale ba kwo vara bam ba vo ba yi jeiga kadwoŋi na twɛ de Sɛkɛm to se ba di gaao.

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Jakob ma ta de o bu Josɛf we, “Nmo zembaara bam na jege vara bam ba wo mɛ to bwola de Sɛkɛm. Konto to, a lage a toŋe‑m ba tei ne mo.” Josɛf ma sɛ o kwo taane dem.

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: O kwo déem ma ta ded‑o we, “Véi n nii n zembaara bam jege yazura na, n daare n nii vara bam de na ye tei to, se n jwoori n ba n ta n bere-ne.” O ma toŋe‑o pa se o zege Heboron bwolo kom ne o vo Sɛkɛm. Josɛf na yi Sɛkɛm seeni to,

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: baaro wodwoŋi ma jeeri‑o gaao ne o na kare o beeri jei maama to, ye baaro wom bwei‑o we, “Bɛ mo nmo kare n beera?”

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: O ma leiri we, “A beeri a chorro mo. Nmo yei ba na wo mɛ ba tɔge ba vara bam to na?”

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Ba déem na tole ba na‑o, o maa beene to, ba ma ke ni daane se ba go‑o.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Ba ma ta daane ba we, “Dendwea dwɛɛno wom mo tento o maa beena.

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Ruben na nigi konto to, o ma kwaane se o jwoŋi Josɛf ba jeŋa ne o yage. O maa we, “Yé pa-na se dé ti o ŋwea.”

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: O ta maa we, “Yé pa-na o jana lu tega ne. Yé kwei-na á jea á dwei‑o. Za á dole-o-na á de vole-kore dento ne, kagoa kam ne ywo.” Ruben tage konto ye o boŋe se o jwoŋi‑o ba jeŋa ne o daare o jwoori o ja‑o o vo o pa o kwo mo.

english_verse: and threw him into a dry well.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma kwei‑o ba dole ba de vole dem na koge to wone.

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba jeini se ba di wodiu. Ba na wora ba di to mo ba déem kwoni ba yuni wɛɛne ba na Isameli tiina badwonna na nwoŋi Gilead ba via. Ba kona yam maa zeŋe talwoŋ-ywoŋa dwi dwi de terale nuga, ba jege ba maa vei Ejipti se ba ke pipiu.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Judah ma ta de o chorro tem we, “Bɛ nyɔɔre mo debam wó na nenɛɛne dé ná go dé nyaane wom, ye dé daare dé kwoli o jana bam?

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ruben déem na jwoori o ba vole dem ne ye o na we Josɛf tera to, o ma kaare o tete gwaaro de wo-chechɔgɔ.

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: O ma daare o jwoori o chorro tem tei o ta we, “Bu wom daa tera! Amo lage a vo yeini mo tento?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Ba ma ja boŋo ba go, ba daare ba kwei Josɛf gɔrɔ kom ba de varem wom jana bam wone.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: Ba déem ma ja gare-laao kom ba vo ba kwo tei ye ba we, “Dé nɛ tento mo. Fɔge n nii ko na zege ko ye nmo bu Josɛf gɔrɔ kom naa ko dae o nyem.”

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Ba kwo Jakob ma lɔre-ko ye o we, “Ko ye amo bu Josɛf gɔrɔ mo! Kago-varem mo jaane‑o de go de tore tore!”

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane Jakob ma vaŋe o tete gwaaro o kaare, ye o daare o lɛ gare-nyenyaaro. O laam ma keeri o bu wom da dedɛ wone.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: O bu-baara de o bukwa bam maama déem ma ba se ba kwoori‑o se o yage keira. O ma ve ba gana yam ye o we, “Aawo! Amo wó keeri mo taa, se a vo a yi churu ye a na a bu wom dáane.” Josɛf kwo wom déem keeri konto mo o ŋwaane.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Konto maama na jege ko ke to, dedaane Isameli pipim-piina bam jaane Josɛf mo ba vo ba yi Ejipti. Ba ma kwei‑o ba yeigi ba pa Potifare. Wonto déem ye Ejipti Pa-faro che-tara bam maama yiga tu mo.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa kam ne, mo Judah déem zaŋe o chorro tem tei ne ye o vo o zoore de Adulam tu wodwoŋi, o yere na ye Hira to tei ne.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Dáane mo o nɛ Kanaan tiina bukɔ dedoa, o kwo yere na ye Sua to. O ma di‑o o ma ke o kaane.

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma ja puga ye o lo bakeira. Ba déem ma bwoŋi bu wom yere we ‘Era’.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: O daa ta ma lo bakeira kadwoŋi ye ba bwoŋi wonto we ‘Sela’. Chezibi teo ne mo ba loge‑o.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: O ke puseŋa totoŋe Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Wɛ ma go wonto de.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Judah déem ma ta de o bu Era kaane Tamara o we, “Jwoori n vo n kwo sɔŋɔ n ta‑n jei da kadeini. Amo bu-baaro Sela ná ke nɔɔno o ti, se n laam ba.” O déem tage konto kolo ŋwaane o déem boŋe mo we, “Ko ná dae konto, Sela de wó zege o te nenɛɛne o chorro tem na tege tei to.” Tamara ma seene o vo o zoore o kwo sɔŋɔ ne.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Ko maa wora ko wora, Judah kaane wolo na ye Sua bukɔ to déem ma ba o te. Judah na keeri o kaane wom ye lua kam ni kɛ to mo o zaŋe o vo Timina, o de o badwoŋi Hira, Adulam tu wom. O tontoŋena déem maa wora ba fane o pei sem koro.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Tamara déem ma lɔre we, o baro kwo wom wo chwoŋa ne o maa vei Timina se o fane o pei koro.

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: O ma lɔɔre o kadeini gwaaro tem, ye o daare o vɔ gɔrɔ kodwoŋi se o ma kwoli o yibia pa se ba ware‑o ba lɔre. O déem ta ma daare o vo Enayim teo kom o jei manchwo-peena ni ne, kokuri to o maane we Sela déem bege baaro ye ba ta wo sɛ se wom ji o kaane. Enayim déem wo Timina chwoŋa kam ni ne mo.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Judah déem na maa kɛa ye o na‑o to, o pɛ se o ye ka-bworo mo, kaane wom na kwoli o yibia to ŋwaane.

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: O maa we, “Nmo ya lage se a pa‑m bɛ mo a tiŋi daare?” O maa we, “Pa-ne n jafole dem de ŋona kalo na leigi da to, n ta woli n jeŋa nacheiga kam.” O ma sɛ o kwei-te o pa‑o ye ba daare ba peini daane. Konto to, Tamara déem jaane puga de o baro kwo wom.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Judah déem ma toŋe o badwoŋi Adulam tu wom dedaane bebala kam se o ja o vo o pa kaane wom, se o daare o jwoŋi wonnu telo o na mɛ o tiŋi daare to. Hira ma beeri beeri kaane wom o ga.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: O ma bwei Enayim nɔɔna badwonna o we, “Ka-bworo kolo déem na jei á teo kom chwoŋa ni ne to vei yei mo?” Ba ma leiri we, “Ka-bworo konto dwoŋi maŋe ko wo lɛɛne ywo-seeni.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: O ma jwoori o vo Judah tei o ta we, “Amo beeri wuu, ye a ga o ŋwa! Teo kom nɔɔna ma ta we, ka-bworo maŋe ko wo gare ywo.”

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Judah ma ta o we, “Pa dé yage wonnu tem dé na mɛ dé tiŋi daare o tei ne to. Ko ná dae konto, nɔɔna laam wó taa jege debam ba mɔna. A lwoori a toŋe bebala kam se a ya pa‑o, nmo nam wo nɛ‑o mo.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Chane setɔ na kɛ to mo ba tage de Judah we, “N bu-kaane Tamara ke ka-bworo totoŋe mo, ko ŋwaane o laam jege puga mo.” Judah ma ta o we, “Ja-o-na á nwoŋi dáa á zwɛ á go-na.”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Ba déem na jege‑o ba maa nwoŋi to mo o toŋe kwora o pa o baro kwo wom we, “Amo jaane puga kam de baaro wolo na tei wonnu tento to mo. Fɔge n nii lanyerane se n nii n wó wane n lɔre ko na ye wolo jafole de de ŋona, de ko na ye wolo nacheiga to na?”

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Judah ma nii wonnu tem, ye o we, “Te ye amo mo nyem! Kaane wonto jege chega o dwoi amo. Kokuri to, a wo sɛ se a kwei‑o a pa a bu Sela.” O nam daa wo jwoori o peini ded‑o.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: O na wora o lore to mo bakeiri sem dedoa twe o jeŋa pa se ka nwoŋi pwooni. Ka-lworinu wom ma ja jeŋa kam o vɔ gare-ŋon-seŋa o ke da, ye o we, “Wonto mo dɛ yiga o nwoŋi pwooni.”

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: De ko de, bu wom daa ma jwoori o kɔɔre o jeŋa kam o daare ye o choro kom kɛ o nwoŋi pwooni. Ka-lworinu wom maa we, “Nii nmo na pi n nwoŋi pwooni tei!” Konto ŋwaane ba ma bwoŋi o yere we ‘Pɛreza’.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Bakeira kadwoŋi kam laam ma nwoŋi pwooni de o gare-ŋon-seŋa kam o jeŋa ne. Ba ma pa wonto yere we, Zera.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Isameli tiina bam déem ya jaane Josɛf ba vo ba yi Ejipti. Ba ma yeigi‑o ba pa Ejipti tu wodwoŋi, o yere mo Potifare. Wonto maa ye ba teo kom Pa-faro che-tara bam maama yiga tu.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: O tu wom déem maane we Baŋa Wɛ mo wo Josɛf tei ne. O ta ma lɔre we ko ye Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane mo pae se Josɛf jeŋa wonnu maama tɔge chwoŋa.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: O déem yage o jeŋa woŋo maama o pa Josɛf se o taa nii-te o pa‑o. O yiga déem daa tera kolokolo wone, ko ná dae o tete ni-wodiu kom yerane se o ba o di. Josɛf ye-daa kam déem maŋe daane mo ye o tiini o lamma yi ne.

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Josɛf ma ve ye o we, “A bá sɛ! Amo tu wom kwei o sɔŋɔ wonnu maama mo o ke amo jeŋa ne, ye o yiga daa tere kolokolo wone, amo na nii te baŋa ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba dwoi amo sɔŋɔ konto ne. Amo tu wom nam wo cheiŋi kolokolo ywo amo tei ne, ko ná dae nmo yerane, nmo na ye o kaane to ŋwaane. A nam bá wane a toŋe puseŋa totoŋe dento. Ko wó taa ye wɛleere mo Wɛ yiga ne.”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Dɛ maama mo kaane wom yɔɔre o daane Josɛf de taane dem konto dwoŋi. O de maa ba sɛa, ye o jege‑o o liisa, se ba yé twɛ daane.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe, Josɛf ma zo sɔŋɔ kom wone se o toŋe o totoŋa. O dwonna tontoŋena bam wolowolo déem maa tere ko wone.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Potifare kaane wom ma vo o ja‑o o gɔrɔ seeni ye o we, “Ba se dé peini daane!” Josɛf ma vere o tete o daare o gɔrɔ kom o yage kaane wom jeŋa ne, ye o duri o nwoŋi pwooni.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: o ma bwoŋi sɔŋɔ kom wo tontoŋena bam o ta-ba we, “Nii-na a baro na jaane Hiburu tu wonto o ba ywo se o mɔne debam tei! O zo ywo mo se o zi-ne, ye a de tiini a kaase.

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: O nam na nigi we a kaase se ba jwoŋi-ne ba yage to, mo o yage o gɔrɔ a tei ne o daare o duri o nwoŋi.”

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Kaane wom déem ma tiŋi Josɛf gɔrɔ kom o tei ne, ye o cheigi se o baro jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: A na kaase se ba jwoŋi-ne ba yage to, mo o yage o gɔrɔ a tei ne ye o daare o duri o nwoŋi pwooni.”

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: O déem ma pa se ba ja Josɛf ba pe peena diga ne. Dáane mo ba déem yeini ba pe Ejipti Pɛ wom peena. Josɛf déem na wo peena diga kam ne konto to,

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wo o tei ne mo. O ma ke Josɛf lanyerane ye o pa peena diga kam dedɛɛro wom swoi Josɛf.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom déem ma pa Josɛf chwoŋa se wonto taa nii peena badwonna bam o pa‑o. O ma kwei kolo maama na wó ke peena diga kam ne to o ke Josɛf jeŋa ne.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Peena diga kam dedɛɛro wom yiga déem tera de kolo maama o na ke Josɛf jeŋa ne to. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem wo Josɛf tei ne mo ye o keim maama tɔge chwoŋa.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: O déem ma pa ba pe-ba ba yage peena diga ne, Pɛ che-tara yiga tu wom tei ne. Dáane mo ba déem ya lwoori yiga ba pe Josɛf.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Ba na pe-ba ye ba zo jei sem ne to, mo peena diga dedɛɛro wom ma kwei Josɛf o yage ba tei ne ye o zeini-ba de kolo ba na lage to. Ba maa wora konto taa.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Josɛf ma vo se o daane ba peiga. O déem ma maane we woŋo tiini ko daane-ba dedɛ.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri‑o we, “Debam maama dwɛ dé dendwea mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno laam tera se o ta ya kuri o bere debam.” Josɛf ma ta de-ba we, “Wɛ mo ye wolo na bere nɔɔna dendwea kuri to. Ta-na á dendwea yam á bere-ne.”

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Amo ma na we a zei Pa-faro wom na-zoŋa kam mo. A ma gwori tio-bia bam ye a ŋoke-ba a ke nyoa na-zoŋa kam ne. A laam ma kwei a pa Pɛ wom.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Josɛf déem ma ta‑o we, “Dendwɛ dem kuri mo tento: Tio kom nɛ setɔ sem ye da yatɔ mo.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Da yatɔ wɛɛne Pa-faro wom wó le‑m pa se n yuu jwoori ko zeiŋi. O maa wó pa se n jwoori n ta‑n toŋa n faŋa totoŋa yam mo. Nmo wó ta‑n ke Pa-faro wom sana bam o jeŋa ne, ne nmo ya na yeini ne ke tei boboa ne to mo.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Wonnu nam ná kwei chwoŋa te pa‑m, se n guli amo gula. Duri amo yibwona se n ta a taane n bere Pa-faro wom. Konto wó pa se ba pore-ne se a nwoŋi peena diga kanto ne.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, ba jaane-ne mo ba vere Hiburu tiina teo kom ne ba ja ba ba ywo-seeni. Amo nam na yi ywo-seeni to, a wo ke kolokolo a chɔge se ba pe amo jeiga kanto wone.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wolo na nii Pɛ wom bworobworo fɔgem baŋa ne to ma maane we o dwoŋi wom dendwɛ dem kuri lamma de pa‑o. O déem ma ta de Josɛf o we, “Amo de dwɛ we: A zeŋe bworobworo kayɛ setɔ mo a yuu ne, se nam teini da-baŋa ne mo.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Kayaa kalo na wo se maama baŋa ne to ma su de wo-laaro dwi dwi se Pa-faro wom ya di. Zuna laam maa tui ba di wodiiru tem, ye te ta wo amo yuu ne.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Josɛf maa we, “Nmo dendwɛ dem de kuri mo tento: Kayɛ setɔ sem ye da yatɔ mo.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Da yatɔ wɛɛne Pa-faro wom wó le‑m o pa se n yuu zeiŋi. Ba ta wó kuuni n ba ba yage tio yuu ne pa se n te mo, se zuna laam taa tui ba di n ya-nɔna yam.”

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Da yatɔ yam déem ma seene ya yi, ye ko ye Ejipti Pa-faro wom lora dɛ mo. O ma ke kuri o pa o nakwa maama. O déem ma pa se ba pore o tontoŋena balei bam, se ba ba ba jeeri o nakwa bam tei ne.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Pɛ wom sana tu wom, o yɔɔre o swei Josɛf swia mo.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Bena yalei na kɛ to, Ejipti Pa-faro wom ma dwɛ dendwɛ. O dendwɛ dem ne, o déem zege Ejipti bu-tola kam ni ne mo, ba na bwoi-ka we ‘Naili’ to.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: O ma nii o na naane derepɛ ye de nwoŋi buga kam wone. Naane dem nugi bigila bigila, ye de zege bubɛ dem ni ne de di gaao.

english_verse: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
translation_verse: Na-kokware sem laam ma ja naane delo na nugi to se di. Pa-faro wom laam ma puri o yia.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: O déem daa na guni o peini se o dɔ to, mo o dwɛ dendwɛ dedwoŋi: O déem nɛ men-zwaro terepɛ mo te na leigi kaso-fera dedoa baŋa ne. Te maama bega wagela wagela lanyerane.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: O ma daare o na men-zwaro terepɛ tedwonna na nwoŋi te woli da. Tento maa ye memene mo ye te kwaare, kagoa vo-loŋo na nwoŋi wɛ-puli seeni ye ko jege-te ko zwɛa to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Men-memene sem ma ja mena yalo na bega wagela wagela to ya li nyɔ! Pa-faro wom ma puri yia, ye o maane we ko maama ye dendwɛ mo.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Tega na poore zezeŋa ne to, Pa-faro wom boboŋa maa vugimi dedɛ. O ma toŋe o bwoŋi Ejipti teo liri-keira de ba swa tiina maama. O déem ma tole o dendwea yam o bere-ba. Ba wolowolo maa ware ya kuri o ta o bere Pɛ wom.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Dáane mo Pɛ sana tu wom tage ded‑o o we, “Amo laam guli a ya na jege se a ke tei to.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Pɛ, nmo bane déem zaŋe amo de a dwoŋi tontoŋeno wolo na nii bworobworo fɔgem to baŋa ne mo, ye n pa se ba ja debam balei ba pe peena diga ne, n che-tara yiga tu wom tei ne.

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe debam dedoa dedoa déem dwɛ de dendwea mo tete ne, dendwɛ maama dedaane de kuri mo.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Hiburu tiina nɔn-doŋo wodwoŋi de déem maa tɔge o wo jeiga kam ne. Wonto déem mo toŋe o pae nmo che-tara bam yiga tu wom. Dé déem ma tole dé dendwea yam dé bere‑o, ye o daare o maŋe ya dedoa dedoa kuri o bere debam.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom na bere dé dendwea yam kuri tei to mo seene ko ke. Nmo pɛ se a jwoori a na a totoŋa yam mo, ye n daare n pa ba kuuri nɔɔno wodwoŋi wom ba go.”

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom déem ma ta de Josɛf we, “Amo mo dwɛ a dendwɛ ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware se o ta de kuri. Amo nam nigi we nmo yei dendwea kuri n tɛ n bere nɔɔna.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Josɛf ma leiri we, “Pɛ, amo ware a ta. Ko nam ná ye Wɛ, wonto wó pa nmo leira yalo na ye chekke to.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom laam ma ta de Josɛf o we: “A na dwɛ dendwea yam to, a nɛ we a zege Naili buga kam bubɛ baŋa ne mo.

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: Naane derepɛ ma zege buga kam wone de nwoŋi. De nugi bigila bigila, ye de zege de di gaao.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Dento kwaga ne mo naane derepɛ de daa nwoŋi, de na ye na-kokware, ye de tiini de lwara. Amo ta wo fɔge a na na-balɔre sem konto dwoŋi Ejipti teo kom maama ne.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: De na di na-kamuna yam de ti to, de ba nii de nae we de di woŋo. Kokuri to, de ta ye na-kokware mo, nenɛɛne de na maŋe de ye tei to. A laam ma puri a yia.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Amo daa ma dwɛ a na men-zwaro terepɛ, te na leigi kaso-fera dedoa baŋa ne ye te maama be wagela wagela lanyerane to.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Tento kwaga ne mo men-zwaro terepɛ tedwonna de nwoŋi da, te na ye memene ye te kwaare, kagoa vo-loŋo na nwoŋi wɛ-puli seeni ye ko jege-te ko zwɛa to ŋwaane.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Men-zwaaro telo na ye memene to laam ma ja mena yalo na bega wagela wagela to ya li. A ma maŋe dendwea yam a bere a liri-keira bam, ye ba wolowolo wo wane ya kuri o ta o bere-ne.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Josɛf ma ta de Pa-faro wom o we: “Pɛ, nmo dendwea yam maama ye woŋo dedoo mo. Wɛ mo veere o bere‑m o na ti o yiga se o ke tei to.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Na-laaro terepɛ tem ye bena yarepɛ mo. Men-wagela yarepɛ yam de maa ye bena yarepɛ. N dendwea yam maama tɛ woŋo dedoo mo.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye na-balɔre serepɛ sem na ye kokware ye se da kwaga se ba to, de men-zwaro terepɛ tem na ye memene vo-loŋo kom ŋwaane to, tento maama de ye bena yarepɛ mo. Bena yanto wone kana mo wó taa wora.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Bena yarepɛ wone, wodiu wó taa wora kɛɛla kɛɛla Ejipti logo kom maama ne.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bá taa guli we wodiu ya gaale logo kom ne, kolo ŋwaane, kana kalo na wó saŋe wodiiru bena yam to wó tiini ka zo nɔɔna yera mo.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Dendwea yam nam na ye yalei ye ya ta ye woŋo dedoo to, bere we Wɛ mo chwi keim dem se de ke. Ko nam bá dáane se Wɛ pa se keim dem maama toŋe.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Pɛ, ko maŋe se n beeri nɔɔno wolo na jege yi-poro ye o ta ye swa tu to, se n daare n kwei Ejipti logo kom maama n ke kotu jeŋa ne.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Ta kuri nɔɔna balo na wó taa nii logo kom teene maama baŋa ne to n woli da. Bena yarepɛ yalo wodiu na wó gaale to wone, banto jege se ba la wodiiru popɔre senu maama wone popɔra dedoa ba tiŋi.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Ba jege se ba tiŋi wodiiru tento jwa dim ŋwaane mo. Kana ná tu logo baŋa, teo kom nɔn-bia wó na wodiu bena yarepɛ yam konto wone. Nmo ná ke konto, kana kam daa bá wane ka chɔge teo kom.”

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom déem ma bwei o nakwa bam we, “Dé daa wó wane dé na nɔɔno se o taa nye de wonto na? O ye wolo Wɛ jworo na wo o baŋa ne to mo.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: O laam ma ta de Josɛf we, “Wɛ na lwoori o pa se n lɔre wonnu tento maama to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa tera ye o jege yi-poro dedaane swa o yi nmo.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se n ta‑n nii amo sɔŋɔ kom maama baŋa ne. A teo kom nɔn-bia bam maama jege se ba sɛ nmo ni mo. Paare dem yerane ŋwaane mo pa amo dwoi nmo.” Josɛf tu o tei Ejipti teo maama

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma le o dam jafole o kwei o tore Josɛf noa ne. O ta ma zo‑o gare-nyenno na lamma to, ye o daare o kwei sabu-seŋa zambili o lɛ o ba ne.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom déem ma ta de Josɛf we, “Amo mo seene a ye Ejipti Pa-faro wom. Nmo nam ná wo pɛ nɔɔna chwoŋa, ba bá gɔ naga se ba toŋe kolokolo Ejipti maama wone.”

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom ma pa Josɛf yere we ‘Zafenaf-Panea’. O ma daare o kwei bukɔ wodwoŋi o pa‑o se o di o ma ke o kaane. Wonto yere mo Asenaf. O maa ye Ona kaanem tu Potifera bukɔ. Josɛf déem nɛ chwoŋa se o taa nii logo kom maama baŋa ne.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Josɛf ma tiini o la mena o tiŋi pa se ya daga ko gaale, nenɛɛne naneo ni kasol-bia na daga tei to. Ko déem na yi yiga to, Josɛf déem daa ware o jeeli ko ni na mae tei to.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Kana bena yam déem ta wo yi ye Josɛf kaane Asenaf lo bu-baara balei o pa‑o.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Josɛf ma pa o bu-kwea kam yere we ‘Manasɛ’ ye o we, “Wɛ seene o pa se a swei a yaara yam maama de kolo maama na ke a kwo sɔŋɔ ne to.”

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: O ma pa wolo na saŋe to yere we ‘Efrayim’ ye o we, “Wɛ pɛ se a na dwi teo kolo wone a ya na yaare to.”

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Ejipti logo kom na neene de wodiiru to bena yarepɛ yam maama déem tu ya kɛ.

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: Kana bena yarepɛ yam de laam ma bobo. Ko déem seene ko ke nenɛɛne Josɛf na wuuri o ta tei to mo. Kana ma tiini ka di logo baŋa teene maama. Ko déem nam ná ye Ejipti teene dem maama wone, wodiu déem wora mo.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Kana na tu ka ja Ejipti tiina bam to, ba ma vo ba kaase ba jare Pa-faro wom se o pa-ba wodiu. O de ma ta ba maama o we, “Véi-na Josɛf tei, se á ke kolo maama o na wó bere abam se á ke to.”

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna déem zege tega baŋa teene maama ne ba tui Ejipti se ba yeigi wodiu Josɛf tei ne, kokuri to, kana kam déem tiini ka chɛ logo baŋa maama ne mo.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Jakob déem ma lɔre we wodiu wo Ejipti ne. O ma ta o bu-baara bam we, “Wodiu tera ye á jei sɔŋɔ ne se bɛ?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Amo nigi we wodiu wo Ejipti ne. Nam véi-na dáane á yeigi mena á ja á ba, se dé yé pu de kana.”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Josɛf zembaara bam fuga ma zaŋe ba vo Ejipti se ba yeigi mena.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Jakob déem nam ya chege Josɛf nyaane Benjamin mo se o yé tɔge o chorro tedwonna tem o vo. Kokuri to, o kɔre we cham mo wó zege de yi‑o chwoŋa ne.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Jakob bu-baara bam déem to nɔn-kɔgɔ wone mo ba tɔge ba vo Ejipti se ba yeigi wodiu. Kokuri to, kana kam déem chɛ Kanaan logo kom maama de mo.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Josɛf déem nam mo ye dedɛɛro Ejipti ne ye o jege mena o yeigi o pae ko nɔn-bia maama. Josɛf zembaara bam ma vo ba yi o tei, ye ba chɔɔle ba yibia tega ne ba jɔɔne‑o.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: O ma guli o na dwɛ o zembaara bam dendwea yam to, ye o ta-ba o we, “Abam tu se á ŋɔ á yere debam teo kom wonnu mo, se á nii teo kom mɛ na wo chege to.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri‑o we, “Debam tu, ko nam dae konto! Dé ye nmo kabɛ. Dé tu ywo-seeni se dé yeigi wodiu mo.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Debam maama ye baaro dedoa bia mo. Debam vei de chega mo, se dé wo tu se dé ŋɔ dé yere á teo kom.”

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: O daa ta ma ta de-ba o we, “Vwa! Abam tu ywo se á nii debam teo kom jei selo na wo chege to mo.”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Debam tu, dé déem ye fuga-balei mo de kwo dedoa ye dé zoore Kanaan ne. Dé nyaane wom ta wo debam kwo tei ne tento. Ko daare, dedoa kam daa tera.”

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: A lage a faŋe abam mo a nii: A dugi Pa-faro wom yere ŋwaane, abam nyaane wom ná wo tu se a na‑o, a bá sɛ a yage abam se á viiri.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Toŋe-na á wone dedoa se kotu vo o ja á nyaane wom o ba. Abam balo na daare to, a lage a pe á maama mo se a lɔre á taane dem ná ye chega naa vwa. A dugi dedaane Pa-faro wom yere, á nyaane wom ná wo tu, ko wó bere we abam seene á ŋɔne á nii teo kom mo!”

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: O ma pa se ba ja ba maama ba pe da yatɔ.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Da yatɔ dɛ dem na yi to, Josɛf ma ta de-ba we, “Ke-na tento se a pa á jwoŋi á ŋwea, amo na kɔre Wɛ to ŋwaane.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Abam ná seene á vei de chega, se á pa abam dedoa maŋe peena diga kam ne ywo. Abam balo na daare to wó wane á ja wodiiru á vo á pa á sɔŋɔ tiina bam se ba yé pu de kana.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Ko nam jege se á ja á nyaane wom mo á ja á ba se a na‑o. Konto wó bere we abam taane dem ye chega pa se á daa yé ga ŋwea.” Ba ma sɛ,

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: ye ba bwɛ daane ba we, “Dé na nɛ waarem dento maama to, ko ye dé na ke dé nyaane Josɛf tei to ŋwaane mo. Ko déem na ni‑o, ye o lwoori wolim debam tei ne to, dé nɛ ye dé ve se dé duri o yibwona. Konto cham laam nam mo jwoori dé baŋa ne.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Ruben ma leiri o we, “Amo déem tage de abam se á yé ke zonne á pa bu wom. Abam ma ve se á cheigi-ne! Dé laam jege se dé jwoŋi o toone dem ŋweero mo.”

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
