translation_verse: Josɛf déem ma pipiri o vo dáa ye o ka yi-na. O yera na jwoori to, o ma jwoori ba tei o ŋɔɔne de-ba. O déem ma le Simeon ba wone ye o pa se nɔɔna vɔ‑o ba ja viiri ba maama yibia ne.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Josɛf ma pa ni o we, ba kwei mena ba su o zembaara bam ywollu tem maama. O déem ta pɛ se ba jwoori ba ke nɔɔno maama sabu mo o ywolo ne, se ba daare ba pa-ba wodiu ba na wó di chwoŋa ne to.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Ba déem ma vo ba yi mɛ ba na wó peini ba sii se tega poore to. Ba dedoa ma bwoli o ywolo se o le wodiu o pa o bonaga. O ma na o sabu kom na tigi da o ywolo kom ni ne.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: O ma ta de o chorro tem o we, “Amo sabu kom mo ba jwoori ba pa-ne. Nii-ko da a ywolo kom ne.” Ba na lɔre konto to, ba bochara ma di. Foone ma ja-ba ye ba ŋɔɔne ba bere daane ba we, “Bɛ mo Wɛ ke debam tento?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Ba déem ma vo ba yi ba kwo Jakob tei Kanaan ne. Ba ma lwoni kolo maama na yi-ba to ba bere‑o. Ba ma ta ba we,

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Dé ma pa o maane we, dé déem ye chorro fuga-balei mo de kwo dedoa. Dé bere‑o debam dedoa daa na tera tei, dedaane dé nyaan-balaŋa mo laam na wo dé kwo wom tei ne ywo-seeni tei to.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom ma ta dedaane debam o we ‘Ke-na tento se a lɔre we á tage chega. Abam choro dedoa wó maŋe amo tei ne ywo, se á daare á kwei mena á ja á vo á pa á sɔŋɔ tiina se ba yé pu de kana.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Ko nam jege se á ja á nyaane wom mo á ba se a na‑o. Konto mo wó pa se a lɔre we á ye chega tiina ye á wo tu se á ŋɔ á nii dé teo kom. Amo laam maa wó yage á choro kom a ya na pe to, se á de ta‑á beeri á pipia debam teo kom ne.’ ”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Ba na tage konto ba ti to, mo ba maama déem bwoli ba ywollu tem. Ba dedoa dedoa ma na o sabu-ganlɔgere dem na tigi da dedaane sabia bam maama! Ba maama de ba kwo wom na nɛ konto to, foone ma ja-ba.

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Ruben ma ta de o kwo o we, “Kwei bu wom n ke amo jeŋa ne se dé kɛ. A ná wo jaane‑o a jwoori a ke n jeŋa ne, se n go a bu-baara balei bam.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: De konto de, Jakob tage we, “Amo bá sɛ. Amo bu Benjamin bá da dedaane abam o vo. O zembaaro Josɛf maŋe o te ye wonto yerane mo daare o nu-bia wone. Cham ná yi‑o chwoŋa ne, abam wó pa se a te wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane, ye a ja a yu-pwei sento a vo churu.”

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Kana kam déem tiini ka chɛ Kanaan teo maama ne mo.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Jakob sɔŋɔ tiina bam ma di mena yalo maama ba na nɛ Ejipti ne ba ja ba to ba ti. Jakob laam ma ta-ba o we, “Jwoori-na á vo á yeigi wodiu fee á ja á ba ywo-seeni.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Se n nam ná wo sɛ se o tɔge o vo, dé bá wane dé vo, dedɛɛro wom na tage kolo to ŋwaane, de o na we, dé ná wo jaane dé nyaane wom dé ba, o daa bá pa debam chwoŋa se dé zo o tei.”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Jakob ma bwei-ba o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo á tage de nɔɔno wom we á ta jege nyaane wodwoŋi sɔŋɔ ne, ye á ke-ne cham wone tento?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri ba we, “Nɔɔno wom tiini o bwei debam mo o legese dedaane dé dwi maama. O bere o bwei we ‘Abam kwo ta ŋwe na? Á daa ta jege choro kodwoŋi na?’ Debam de ma leiri o bwia yam maama. Dé ya bá wane dé lɔre we o wó ta nenɛɛne, dé vei dé ja dé nyaane wom dé ja ba o tei.”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Judah laam ma ta de o kwo wom o we, “Kwei bu wom n ke amo jeŋa ne se dé ke lela dé kɛ da. Ko ná dae konto, debam de dé bia bam maama wó pu mo de kana.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Chega to, ko ná dae dé na zege dé dáane, tento wɛɛne dé ya vei ye dé daa jwoori se ko yi kuni belei.”

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Ba kwo Jakob ma leiri o we, “Ko nam ná seene ko ye konto, ke-na tento dwoŋi: twori-na dé tega kam wo-laaro dwi dwi á ke á ywollu tem ne se á ja á vo á ma ke pɛɛre á pa dedɛɛro wom. Ko maa wó taa ye terale nuga fenfee, de tooro fee, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa dwi dwi, dedaane teeni bia dwi dwi.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Nam ta ta‑á jege-na mena yam sabu kuni belei á woli da. Kokuri to, á jege se á jwoori á ja kolo ba ya na ke á ywollu tem ne to mo á vo á pa-ba. Dɛ delo ba tusi mo ba ke konto.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom wó pa se nɔɔno wom duri á yibwona ye o pa chwoŋa se á ja á chorro tem, Simeon dedaane Benjamin, á jwoori á ba ywo. Ko ná tu se a ga a bia bam tento, a nam wó ga-ba mo.”

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Ba déem ma ti ba pɛɛra yam yiga, ye ba jege ba sabu kuni belei. Benjamin déem ma da o vo. Ba ma ke lela ba vo Ejipti. Ba na yi da to, ba ma zo Josɛf tei.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Josɛf na nɛ we Benjamin tɔge o wo ba wone to, o ma ta o sɔŋɔ tontoŋena yiga tu wom o we, “Ja nɔɔna banto n vo sɔŋɔ. N ná yia, se n go varem n ma n ke wodiu, se banto wó di wodiu de amo mo wea ne.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Tontoŋena yiga tu wom ma ke o na bere‑o se o ke tei to, ye o jege nɔɔna bam o maa vei o tu wom sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Foone déem maa jege chorro tem dedaane ba na jege-ba ba maa vei Josɛf sɔŋɔ kom to. Ba boboŋa yam déem ye we, “Ko ye sabu kom ba ya na jwoori ba ke dé ywollu tem wone to ŋwaane mo ba jege debam ba vei dáane. Dedɛɛro wom lage o pa ba pɔpɔ ba zi debam mo ba ja ba ma ke wonto kabɛ, ye ba vere debam bonɛ sem de ba woli da.”

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Ba na vei ba yi sɔŋɔ kom manchwoŋo ni to, mo ba ŋɔɔne de Josɛf tontoŋena yiga tu wom,

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: ye ba we, “Jan ja, debam daama maŋe dé ba ywo dé yeigi wodiu.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Dé nam ta jaane sabu dé woli da dé ba se dé daa ma yeigi wodiu. Debam wo lɔre wolo daama na kwei dé sabu kom o jwoori o ke dé ywollu tem ne to.”

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom ma ta o we, “Ko wo chɔge, yé ta‑á fona. Abam Wɛ wom, wolo wom á kwo na tɔge to mo kwei pɛɛra o ke á ywollu tem ne. Amo daama jwoŋi abam sabu kom.” O na tage konto to, o laam ma pore Simeon o ja ba ba tei.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom déem ma pa chorro tem zo Josɛf sɔŋɔ kom. O ta ma mɔ na o pa-ba se ba ma zare ba nɛ, ye o daare o ja wodiiru o ba o pa ba bonɛ sem.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Ba ma ni we ba wó di wodiu dedaane Josɛf mo o sɔŋɔ ne. Ba ma le ba pɛɛra yam ba tiŋi ye ba cheigi Josɛf se o ba wea ne.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Josɛf na tu sɔŋɔ to, ba ma kwei pɛɛra yalo ba na jaane ba jeeri o sɔŋɔ kom ne to ba ja zo diga ba pa‑o. Ba ma chɔɔle ba yibia tega ne ba jɔɔne‑o.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: O ma bwei ba kwaga ye o daare o we, “Á nɔn-kwea kam á ya na tage ka taane á bere-ne to jege yazura na? O daa ta ŋwe na?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri ba we, “Debam kwo ye nmo tontoŋeno mo, o nam ta ŋwe. O jege yazura de ya-dɛɛra.” Ba ma chɔɔle tega ne ba zuli‑o.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Josɛf ma dole o yi o na o nyaane Benjamin na ye o nu-puga bu to. O ma bwei-ba o we, “Abam nyaane wom á na tage o taane á bere-ne to mo tento na?” O ma daare o ta de Benjamin o we, “Amo bu tete, Wɛ zaane wó taa wo nmo yuu ne.”

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Josɛf laam ma su o yia, ye o jwoori o nwoŋi ba tei. O ma fɔge o ja o tete ye o we, “Pɔɔre pɔɔre-na wodiu kom se dé di.”

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Ba déem ke wonto wodiu ko yera mo, chorro tem de nyem ko yera. Ba ma daare ba ke Ejipti tiina balo na wora to de nyem ko yera, kokuri to, ko chula ko pae Ejipti tiina pa se ba ware ba di dedaane Hiburu tiina.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Josɛf ma pa ba pɔɔre pɔɔre o wodiu kom wone ba pa o chorro tem. Benjamin na jwoŋi wodiu kolo to daga ko dwoi o zembaara bam nyem kuni benu. Ba maama maa jei Josɛf tei ne ba di ye ba nyɔ ba su ye lwia tera.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Ta daare n kwei amo lu-nyenno na-zoŋa kam n ke ba nyaan-balaŋa kam ywolo kom ni ne n woli de o de sabu kom.” Tontoŋeno wom ma ke kolo maama Josɛf na bere‑o to.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Tega na jege ka poore to, ba ma pa nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri de ba bonɛ sem maama.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Ba na nwoŋi teo kom wone ye ba maŋe ba wo yi yiga to, dedaane Josɛf na tage o sɔŋɔ tontoŋeno wom o we, “Ke lela n pare nɔɔna bam n ja-ba. N ná yi-ba se n ta de-ba we ‘Bɛŋwaane mo abam mɛ lwarem á ma á ŋwe lanyerane delo a tu wom na ke o pa abam to?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Bɛ mo ye á ŋɔ amo tu na-zoŋa kam? Mo kalo amo tu wom na jege o nyɔ na, ye o ta mae-ka o beeri o nii o yiga. Abam tiini á toŋe puseŋa á pa‑o.’ ”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Josɛf tontoŋeno wom ma seene o pare-ba o ja, ye o lwoni taane dem o bere-ba.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri ba we, “Bɛ mo ye dé tu wom laam tɛ konto? Debam ware dé toŋe konto dwoŋi dé pa‑o kɔtaa!

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Dé daama na maane we sabu kolo dé mɛ dé yeigi wodiu kom tɔge debam ko vo Kanaan teo kom to, dé jwoori dé ja-ko dé ba dé pa abam. Ko dae chega na? Bɛ mo laam nam wó pa se dé ŋɔ sabu-seŋa naa lu-nyenno nmo tu wom sɔŋɔ ne?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Nmo ná nɛ na-zoŋa kam n tontoŋena bam wolo tei ne, konto tu wó te mo. Debam maama balo na daare to maa wó ji dé tu wom kabɛ.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Josɛf tontoŋeno wom ma leiri o we, “Tɔ. A sɛ se ko taa ye ne abam na tage tei to mo. Amo ná nɛ na-zoŋa kam nɔɔno wolo tei ne, konto tu mo wó ji amo kabaa. Ko daare se abam maama viiri á ta‑á tei á tete.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Ba maama ma ke lela ba zoore ba ywollu tem ba tiŋi tega ne ye ba bwoli-te.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Josɛf tontoŋeno wom ma bobo o beira kam. O déem zege nakwe wom baŋa ne mo o vo o yi nyaan-balaŋa kam baŋa. O laam ma vo o na na-zoŋa kam Benjamin ywolo kom ne.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Chorro tem maama na nɛ konto to, ba ma kaare ba tete gwaaro de wo-chechɔgɔ. Ba déem ma jwoori ba kwei ba zela yam ba daŋe ba bonɛ sem baŋa ne, ye ba jwoori teo kom wo.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Josɛf déem ya ta wo sɔŋɔ ne ye Judah de o chorro tem jwoori ba ba ba zo. Ba ma vwi ba yibia tega ne se ba ja o naga.

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Judah déem ma leiri we, “Debam tu, debam ba jege kolokolo se dé ta. Debam ni laam mɔɔre mo. Dé bá wane dé ta kolo dé na wó ma dé jwoŋi dé tete to. Wɛ mo peere debam zem dé chaveera wone. Konto to, debam maama mo laam ye nmo kabɛ, dé maama, ko woli de wolo ba na nɛ na-zoŋa kam o zela wone to.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Josɛf ma leiri o we, “Amo bá wane a pa se ko ke konto dwoŋi! Ba na nɛ na-zoŋa kam wolo zela ne to yerane mo wó ji amo kabaa. Abam maama wó wane á jwoori á kwo wom tei ne de yazura.”

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Judah déem ma tutwoni o yi Josɛf tei o ta o we: “Jan ja, amo tu, pa-ne chwoŋa se dé ŋɔɔne daane jaja. Nam yé pa se n bane zaŋe amo baŋa ne, se nmo de Pa-faro wom tete mae daane mo.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Amo tu, nmo daama bwei debam we, dé ta jege kwo de choro kodwoŋi na?

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Dé ma leiri we, dé jege nɔn-kwea sɔŋɔ ne. Dé nyaan-balaŋa dedoa de ta wora, dé kwo na loge‑o o kokweero maŋa ne mo. Dé ta pɛ se n lɔre we dé nyaane wom konto zembaaro maŋe o te. Wonto yerane laam mo daare o nu-puga bia wone. O kwo wom ma tiini o swoi‑o dedɛ.

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Nmo daa ta ma‑n ta we, dé ja‑o dé ba ywo se nmo de wane n na‑o.

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Dé tu, dé na tage konto to, nmo ta ma n leiri we, dé ná wo jaane dé nyaane wom dé ba, n daa‑n bá‑n pa debam chwoŋa se dé zo n tei.

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Dé na jwoori sɔŋɔ to, dé ma ta dé bere debam kwo kolo maama nmo na tage to.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Ko na ke fee to, dé kwo wom maa we ‘Jwoori-na á vo á yeigi wodiu fee á ja á ba.’

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Dé ma ta‑o we ‘Dé bá wane dé vo, ko ná dae se dé nyaane wom ná dɛ debam kwaga se dé vo. Dé nyaane wom ná tere dé tei ne, dé bá na chwoŋa se dé daa zo dedɛɛro wom tei.’

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Debam kwo wom ma ta o we ‘Abam yei we a kaane Racheli loge bakeiri selei yerane mo o pa-ne.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Dedoa maŋe o jei o daare-ne. Amo na boŋe tei to, kago-varem mo jaane‑o de tore tore. Dedaane zem maama a daa wo nɛ‑o.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Abam nam ná jaane wonto de á viiri ye cham ná yi‑o, abam wó pa se a te wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane, ye a ja a yu-pwei sento a vo churu.’

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: Amo tu, jeeli se n lɔre we nɔn-kwea kam ŋwea de bu wom ŋwea me daane mo. Dé nam ná yi sɔŋɔ ye bu wom tere dé tei ne, amo kwo wó te mo.

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Ko woli da, a kwei a tete a zege daare bu wom ŋwaane ye a ta de a kwo we, a ná wo jwoori a ja‑o a ke o jeŋa ne, se o kwei ko maama o zeŋe amo yuu ne taa wuu.

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Konto to, amo tu, sɛ se amo maŋe ywo a ji n kabaa se a leiri bu wom yuu ne. Pa se bu wom tɔge dedaane o zembaara bam se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Amo bá wane a jwoori a kwo wom tei nenɛɛne bu wom ná tere a tei ne. Amo bá taa lage se a na lwia yalo na wó yi a kwo wom, ne ko ná ke‑o konto.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Josɛf déem daa wo wane o tete o ja o tontoŋena bam yiga ne. O ma bage-ba o we, “Nɔɔno maama nwoŋi da á daare-ne na!” Tontoŋena bam na nwoŋi ba daare Josɛf de o chorro tem yerane, o laam ma ta o na ye wolo to o bere-ba.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: O ma kaase de kwor-dɛa ye o keeri pa se Ejipti tiina bam ni sɔɔ kom. Pa-faro wom sɔŋɔ tiina de déem ni ko ŋwa.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Josɛf déem ta ma ta de o chorro tem we, “Fɔɔre-na á yi a yera.” Ba na yi o tei to, mo o tage o we: “Amo mo ye á choro Josɛf, wolo abam déem na yeigi á pa nɔɔna se ba ja-ne ba vo Ejipti to!

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Kana kam bena yalei mo kɛ tento, ye bena yanu ta daare se ka tiini ka chɛ. Bena yanto wone nɔɔna bá va se ba zage wodiiru.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Ko maa ye Wɛ mo toŋe-ne se a da abam yiga a ba ywo se a che se á dwi yé saare logo kom ne. O mɛ o dam mo o ke konto se a jwoŋi abam a yage chekke.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Ta‑á yei-na we ko dae abam mo pɛ se a ba ywo. Wɛ mo kea. Wonto mo pɛ se amo ji dedɛɛro Pɛ wom yiga ne, se a taa nii o sɔŋɔ kom maama baŋa ne, ye a daare a tei Ejipti teo kom maama.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Nam ke-na lela á jwoori á vo a kwo tei se á ta ded‑o we ‘Nmo bu Josɛf kwora mo tento: Wɛ mo pɛ a tei Ejipti teo kom maama. Kwaane se n daa‑n yé dáane se n ba a tei lela.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Nmo wó ta‑n zoore Gosen laŋa kam seeni mo se n ta‑n twɛ amo ywo-seeni. Nmo de n bia, de n naaro, de n peeni, de n bone, de n naane, dedaane woŋo kolo maama n na jege to wó taa wo dáane mo.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Abam ná wo dáane, amo wó taa nii á baŋa ne se á na wodiu á di. Ta‑n yei we bena yanu mo ta daare se kana kam taa wora. A nam ba lage se kana yaare nmo de n sɔŋɔ tiina bam, ko woli dedaane n vara maama.’

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Abam tete nɛa ye a nyaane Benjamin de nɛa we amo mo seene a ye Josɛf.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Pa-na se a kwo lɔre we Ejipti tiina bam tiini ba zuli-ne mo ywo-seeni, se á daare á ta ded‑o kolo maama á yi na nɛ to. Á laam maa wó ja‑o á ba ywo lela.”

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne Josɛf laam ma kukwori o zembaara bam dedoa dedoa ye o ka ka yi-na ba maama baŋa ne. O chorro tem laam ma na pwola ba ŋɔɔne ded‑o.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom de o sɔŋɔ tiina ma ni we Josɛf chorro mo tu o tei. O de o nakwa bam maama wo ma pwoli ko ŋwaane.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma ta de Josɛf o we, “Ta de n chorro tem se ba vɔ ba bonɛ sem ba jwoori Kanaan teo kom.

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: Ba jege se ba ja á kwo wom dedaane o sɔŋɔ tiina maama mo se ba jwoori ba ba a tei ywo. Amo wó pa-ba Ejipti tega kam mɛ na tiini ka lamma to se ba jeini da. Konto wó pa se ba ni logo kom ywoni lanyerane.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Ta ta de-ba se ba lage sisei-torokooro Ejipti ywo ba ja ba vo Kanaan ba ke ba kaana de ba bia te wone ba ja ba ba. Ba ná beene, se ba ja á kwo ba woli da ba ba ywo-seeni.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Yé pa-na se ko daane abam á zela yam ŋwaane, se Ejipti logo kom wo-laaro maama mo wó taa ye abam nyem.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Jakob bu-baara bam ma ke kolo maama ba déem na bere-ba se ba ke to. Josɛf déem pɛ-ba sisei-torokooro mo, nenɛɛne Pɛ wom na pɛ ni tei to. O déem ta ma pa-ba wodiu se ko woli-ba chwoŋa ne.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: O ma daare o pa ba maama gare-donno se ba zo. Se ko ná ye Benjamin, o déem pɛ wonto lu-nyenno sabu-dala bia yatɔ mo o woli de gare-donno kuni benu.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Wonnu telo Josɛf na toŋe se ba pa o kwo mo tento: wo-laaro dwi dwi mo na nwoŋi Ejipti ne to, bonɛ fuga déem mo maa zeŋe-te. O daa ta ma pa se bona-chwa fuga zeŋe mena de wodiu dedɛ dedaane wo-laaro telo na wó woli o kwo chwoŋa ne to.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Josɛf déem ma bane o chorro tem o yage chwoŋa ne. Ba na maa kɛ to, o ma ta-ba we, “Yé ke-na jara chwoŋa ne!”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ba ma nwoŋi Ejipti ne ye ba vo ba yi ba kwo Jakob tei Kanaan teo kom ne.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Josɛf daa ta ŋwe! Wonto mo laam tei Ejipti teo kom maama o nii ko baŋa ne.” Jakob ma ko o zega, ye o wo sɛ ba taane dem.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Jakob ma ta o we, “Amo laam sɛ! Amo bu Josɛf seene o ta ŋwe mo! Amo wó vo a na‑o mo se a laam daare a te.”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Jakob déem ma lu o woŋo maama o ja o nwoŋi o vo Beeriseba. O na yi da to mo o ke kaanem o pa o kwo Izaak Wɛ wom.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem ma ba Jakob tei tete ne o ŋɔɔne ded‑o o we, “Jakob! Jakob!” O de ma leiri we, “Nii-ne.”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma leiri we, “Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, nmo kwo Wɛ wom. Nam yé kɔre foone se n vo Ejipti, se dáane mo amo lage a pa se n dwi dem puli de ji te-zɔŋɔ.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Amo tete wó tɔge de nmo se dé vo Ejipti. A nam ta wó jwoori a ja n dwi a ba ywo-seeni se ba jeini tega kanto baŋa ne. Nmo nam ná lage n te, nmo bu Josɛf tete mo wó ja nmo pa n te.”

translation_verse: Abam déem ya boŋe se á ke amo mo lwarem. Wɛ ma pipiri á boboŋe dem pa se de ke lam. Kolo na seene ko ke to ya ná wo ke, nɔɔna dedɛ ŋwea zem ya jei mo.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. Amo wó taa nii abam de á bia baŋa ne se á na wodiu á di.” O déem ta ŋɔɔne wo-laaro de o chorro tem mo pa se ba jwoori ba na baare. Josɛf toone

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Josɛf de o kwo sɔŋɔ tiina bam ma lɛɛre ba maŋe Ejipti ne. O bena maama déem maa ye bena bi de fuga (

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: O déem nɛ Efrayim bia se ko yi dwia yatɔ laŋa ne. Manasɛ bu Makira de bia déem ta jeini Josɛf nɛ baŋa ne ba lora maŋa ne.

english_verse: So Joseph died in Egypt at the age of
translation_verse: Josɛf déem jege bena bi de fuga (

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Josɛf de o chorro tem maama dedaane banto yuudwoŋo kom maama ma ba ba te.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Isarele dwi tiina bam déem nam ta puli mo dedɛ ye ba kɔgɔ daga ko gaale. Ba ma tiini ba ke dam ye teo kom maama su de ba dwi dem yerane.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Pa-dooro de déem ma jwoŋi Ejipti o tei. Wonto maa yeiri Josɛf ni ne.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Nii-na Isarele tiina banto na puli dedɛ tei ye ba jege dam ba dwoi debam.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Pa-na se dé ke swa dé che ba pulim dem, se ko ná dae konto, jara ná to debam dedaane teo kodwoŋi tetare ne, ba wó woli debam dona bam wone ba ke jara dedaane debam ye ba laam duri ba lu debam teo kom ne.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane Ejipti tiina ma kuri totoŋa yuu tiina se ba taa bɛɛse-ba de totoŋ-dɛɛra. Ba ma pa se Isarele tiina bam lɔ Pitom teo dedaane Ramesesa teo se Ejipti Pɛ wom taa zege o wodiiru da.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Ba nam na yeini ba tiini ba bɛɛse-ba tei to mo Isarele tiina bam laam fɔge ba pula dedɛ ye ba jage jei maama. Ko ma pa se Ejipti tiina bam tiini ba kɔre foone de Isarele tiina bam.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Ba ma pa se ba ŋwea ke cham dedaane bira magem de teero totoŋ-dɛɛra. Ba déem ta fe-ba se ba taa toŋa ba kare de ba kadwi ne. Konto to Ejipti tiina bam déem bɛɛse Isarele tiina bam ye ba ba jege ba ŋwaŋa.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Kaana balei déem maa wora balo na yeini ba zeini Hiburu kapwi se ba lo bia to. Ba dedoa yere mo Sifira. Wodwoŋi wom de yere maa ye Pua. Ejipti Pɛ wom ma ta de-ba o we,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Á ná yeini á woli Hiburu kaana bam se ba lo, ye ba ná loga, se á fɔge á nii. Bu wom ná ye bakeira, se á go‑o. O daa ná ye busankana, se á yage‑o.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Kaana balei bam maa kɔre Wɛ, ye ba wo sɛ Ejipti Pɛ wom ni. Ba maa pae se bakeiri sem wora.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma bwoŋi kaana bam ye o bwei-ba o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo á ke konto ye á pae se bakeiri sem ta ŋwe?”

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri ba we, “Pɛ. Hiburu kaana bam dae nenɛɛne Ejipti kaana bam tei. Banto wara mo. Ba ma yeini ba gare ba lo ba ti mo ye debam laam yi ba tei.”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Kaana balei bam na kɔre Wɛ to ŋwaane, o ma pa ba de lo bia.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom laam ma pa o nɔɔna bam maama ni dento we, “Hiburu tiina ná loge bakeira maama, á jege se á dole‑o mo á de Naili buga kam ne. Ko daare ko ná ye busankana, se á yage‑o se o ta ŋwe.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Levi dwi tu dedoa déem ma di o tete dwi tiina bukɔ wodwoŋi o ma ke o kaane.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma ja puga o lo bakeira. O ma na we bu wom lamma. O ma da ko ŋwaane o seigi‑o chane setɔ.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: O laam ma maane we o daa bá wane o seigi‑o. O ma kwei tetɔgɔ ba na mɛ sangɛ ba sɔ-ko to, ye o daare o kwei kɔtaale o ma turi-ko se na yé wane ba zo. O déem ma kwei bu wom o ke ko wone ye o daare o ja‑o o vo Naili buga kam ni o seigi‑o nanchan-gullu wone.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Bu wom nakɔ déem maa zege da ye o tole o nii kolo na wó ke‑o to.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Ko na ke fee to, Ejipti Pɛ bukɔ déem ma tu buga kam se o swɛ o yera. O ka-nyaana maa vei ba kaare buga kam ni dem ne. O laam ma tole o na tetɔgɔ kom nanchan-gullu tem wone ye o toŋe o kaba-kana se o vo o ja-ko o ja ba.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: O ma puri ko ni ye o na bu-seseŋa na tigi da ye o keera. Bu wom ŋwaŋa ma zo‑o. O ma ta o we, “Hiburu tiina bu-balwa bam dedoa mo tento.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Bu wom nakɔ wom ma vo Pɛ bukɔ wom tei o bwei‑o o we, “A véi a beeri Hiburu tiina kaana bam wone a pa‑m se ba dedoa taa pae bu wom ŋɔge yele na?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: O ma sɛ ye o we, o véi! Busankana kam ma vo o bwoŋi bu wom nu se o ba.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Pɛ bukɔ wom ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ja bu wonto n vo sɔŋɔ n ta‑n nii o baŋa ne n pa-ne. Amo wó ŋwe‑m ko ŋwaane.” Kaane wom ma seene o ja bu wom o vo sɔŋɔ, o maa jege‑o o kɔna.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Bu wom déem na bege fee to, o nu wom ma ja‑o o vo o pa Pɛ bukɔ wom se o kwei‑o o ma ji o tete bu. O déem ma pa bu wom yere we ‘Moses’, ye o we ‘A na liiri‑o na wone to ŋwaane.’ Moses duri o vo Midian

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: O ma dole o yi o nii jei maama ye o wo nɛ nɔɔn-nɔɔno. O ma mage Ejipti tu wom o go, ye o daare o kwei‑o o seigi kasolo wone.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, o daa ma nwoŋi ye o na Hiburu tiina balei na jege daane. O ma bwei wolo na tusi to o we, “Bɛ mo ye nmo jege n dwoŋi Hiburu tu n maga?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Wɔ mo pɛ nmo ni se n ta‑n ye dedɛɛro debam baŋa ne, se n bore debam bora? Nmo wó go amo n woli Ejipti tu wom n na go to wone mo na?” Moses na nigi konto to, foone ma zo‑o ye o boŋe o tete ne we, “Chega ŋwaane to, a na ke tei to lɔre jaja mo.”

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Ejipti Pɛ wom déem ma ni kolo na ke to. O ma kwaane se o go Moses. Moses ma duri o lu Pɛ wom jeŋa ne ye o vo o zoore Midian teo ne. O déem ma vo o jei vole dedwoŋi teiŋa ne.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Nayera badwonna déem ma ba ba zeili bukwa bam. Moses ma zaŋe o jwoŋi-ba o yage, ye o daare o nye ba vara bam.

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri ba we, “Ejipti tu wodwoŋi mo jwoŋi debam o yage nayera bam jeŋa ne. Wonto mo lɛɛre o mɔ na o ma nye vara bam o pa debam.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: O ma bwei o bukwa bam we, “Nɔɔno wom nam wo yeim mo? Abam yage‑o da se bɛ mo? Bwoŋi-o-na se o ba o di wodiu.”

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Zipora ma lo bakeira ye Moses pa o yere we ‘Geresom’. Kokuri to, o déem boŋe o tete ne mo we, “Amo ye veiru mo sa-teo ne.”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Ko na wora ko wora to, Ejipti Pɛ wom déem ma te. Isarele tiina bam maa ŋwaana ba kabɛɛne ŋwaane. Ba déem tiini ba keeri mo ba lwoori wolim. Ba keira kam ma to Wɛ zwa ne,

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: ye o sɛ ba ŋwana yam. O ma guli ni delo o déem na gwoni o pa Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob to gula.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma nii o na Isarele tiina bam na yaare tei to ye o ke o yiga ba wone.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Moses déem lɛɛre o jege o tembaaro Jetero bone dem de o pei sem o nii te baŋa ne mo. Jetero déem maa ye Midian tiina kaanem tu. Dɛ dedwe, Moses ma ja vara bam o kɛ kagoa kam kwaga ne, o vo o yi Sinayi peo. Peo kom konto mo ye Wɛ tete jeiga kam.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Moses na wora to mo Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam veere ka tete ded‑o ne min-vogo tei to. Moses ma na we mini dem jaane sabara kadwoŋi ye de laam ba di sabara kam de zwɛa.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Moses ma ta o tete ne we, “Amo wó fɔɔre mo a yi a nii wo-kenkagele dento, se a lɔre bɛ mo ke ye sabara kam ba zwɛa to.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma maane we o fɔɔre o yi se o nii. Wɛ ma zege sabara kam wone o bwoŋi‑o o we, “Moses! Moses!” Moses ma leiri we, “Nii-ne da.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma ta o we, “Yé tiini n twɛ ywo. Le n natera yam, se mɛ n na zege to ye amo tete nyem mo.”

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we, “Chega to, amo maane cham delo na yi a nɔɔna bam Ejipti ne to. Ba totoŋa yiga tiina bam na tiini ba bɛɛse-ba pa se ba keeri tei maama to zo amo zwa. A yiga nam wo ba yaara yam wone.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, amo laam tu ba tei se a jwoŋi-ba mo a yage Ejipti tiina bam jeŋa ne. Amo ta wó pa se ba zaŋe ba nwoŋi ba vo ba jeini tega kalo na lamma ye ka daga to baŋa ne. Tega kam konto ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ. Ko nam ye tega kalo Kanaan tiina bam, de Hiti tiina bam, de Amori tiina bam, de Pɛrizi tiina bam, de Hivi tiina bam, dedaane Jebusi tiina bam maama na zoore to mo.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam keira kam yi-ne, ye a ta kwori a na Ejipti tiina bam na jege-ba ba bɛɛse tei maama to.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, a laam nam lage a toŋe nmo mo se n vo Ejipti Pɛ wom tei n ja amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam n nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Moses ma ta de Wɛ o we, “Amo ye wɔ mo? A muri se a vo Pa-faro wom tei a ja Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne.”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Wɛ daa ta ma ta o we, “Amo wó taa wora nmo tei ne. Memaŋe dento mo wó bere we amo mo seene a toŋe‑m: Nmo ná jaane a nɔɔna bam n nwoŋi Ejipti ne, abam laam wó ba peo konto yuu ne mo á zuli-ne.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri o we, “Amo nam ná vei Isarele tiina bam tei ye a ta-ba we ‘Abam nabaara Wɛ wom mo toŋe-ne á tei ne,’ ba wó wane ba bwei amo we ‘Wɛ wom konto yere mo bɛ?’ Tetɛ mo amo wó leiri-ba?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Wɛ ma daare o ta de Moses o we: “Ta de Isarele tiina bam we, ‘Taa wuu Tu Baŋa Wɛ na ye á nabaara Wɛ wom to, Abaraham Wɛ wom, de Izaak Wɛ wom, de Jakob Wɛ wom mo toŋe-ne á tei ne.’ Amo yere dem mo konto se ko taa vei wuu. Ko ná zege dwi dedwe ne se ko vo ko yi dwi dedwoŋi ne, yere dem konto mo ba wó taa mae ba guli a gula.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Nam véi n la Isarele nakwa bam n ke daane se n ta-ba we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye abam nabaara Wɛ wom to, Abaraham Wɛ wom, de Izaak Wɛ wom, de Jakob Wɛ wom mo tu amo tei. O nam tage o we: Amo seene a nii á baŋa ne mo, ye a na kolo maama na yi abam Ejipti ne to.

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: Nmo ná tage konto dwoŋi, Isarele nakwa bam wó sɛ n taane dem. Nmo laam jege se n ja-ba se á vo Ejipti pɛ wom tei, ye á ta ded‑o we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Hiburu tiina bam Wɛ to mo tu debam tei. Konto, pa debam pwola se dé ma da yatɔ dé kwei chwoŋa dé vo kagoa kam wone dé ke kaanem dáane dé pa dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Amo nam yei we Pɛ wom bá sɛ o pa abam pwola se á vo, ko ná dae we a mɛ dam mo a fe‑o.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Amo laam wó ma a dam a waare Ejipti tiina bam dedaane wo-kenkagela yalo a na wó ke ba tetare ne to. Ko kwaga ne mo Pɛ wom laam wó pa abam chwoŋa se á viiri.

english_verse: After I punish the Egyptians, they will be so afraid of you that they will give you anything you want. You are my people, and I will let you take many things with you when you leave the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Amo nam ta wó pa se á kikia su Ejipti tiina bam yi. Konto wó pa se á bá gwɛ de je-yaara á viiri.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Abam kaana maama jege se ba vo ba fara balo na ye Ejipti tiina kaana to tei mo, dedaane kaane wolo maama na zoore ba sɔŋɔ ne to tei. Ba laam maa wó lwoori ba na lu-nyenno wonnu, de sabu-seŋa wonnu, dedaane gwaaro telo á bia na wó taa jege ba zoore to. Abam ná ke konto mo, á wó ma swa á ja Ejipti tiina bam jejegero tem á woli da á viiri.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Moses déem ma leiri Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Dɛ dedwoŋi ne, Isarele tiina bam bá sɛ a taane dem, ba nam bá pa-ne chega. Ba wó wane ba ta nenɛɛne, nmo seene n wo veere n tete de amo.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo n zei de n jeŋa?” O ma leiri o we, “Nacheiga mo a zia.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we, “Dole-ka n de tega ne.” Moses ma dole-ka o de tega ne. Ka ma ji basankwea, ye o duri o daare-ka.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we, “Twe n jeŋa n ja-ka ka nabili seeni.” Moses na twe o jeŋa o ja basankwea kam to, ka ma jwoori ka ji nacheiga o jeŋa ne.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam maa we, “Keim dento wó pa se ba sɛ we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo seene a veere a tete de nmo, amo wolo na ye ba nabaara Wɛ wom to: Abaraham Wɛ wom, de Izaak Wɛ wom, de Jakob Wɛ wom to.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta‑o o we, “Tore n jeŋa n gɔrɔ kom ne se n dwei n nyɔɔne.” O ma ke konto. Moses na jwoori o le o jeŋa kam to, ka pɔpɔ ka peere mo de naywaane jaweo kom.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta o we, “Daa‑n jwoori n tore n jeŋa kam n gɔrɔ kom ne.” Moses ma kwei o jeŋa o tore o gɔrɔ kom ne. O na jwoori o le-ka to, ka pɔpɔ ka ke lanyerane mo, nenɛɛne o yera yam maama na ye tei to.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: De konto de, ba ná nɛ wo-memaŋa yalei yanto ye ba ta ve se ba sɛ n taane dem, se n mɔ na Naili buga kam ne n daare n lwo-ba te-kora kam baŋa ne. Na bam konto wó ji jana tega kam baŋa ne.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Moses déem ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Amo Teiru, amo ware a ŋɔɔne chekke. Ko zege nmo de amo na ŋɔɔne daane to, a maŋe a ware mo. A nam maŋe a bá lɔre ŋɔŋa. A ni ware se de pipiri lanyerane.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Wɔ mo pɛ nabiinu o ni dem? Wɔ mo ke zwa-kwarro de memaaro? Wɔ mo pae nabiinu yia se o taa nae, naa se o taa ye lilwei? Ko dae amo Baŋa Wɛ mo na?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Laam nam véi, se amo wó woli‑m de ŋɔŋa, ye a daare a bere‑m n na wó ta kolo maama to.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Moses maa we, “Amo Teiru, jan ja! Toŋe nɔn-gaa se konto tu vo o toŋe totoŋe dem.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Moses taane dem déem ma zaŋe Baŋa Wɛ bane. Wɛ ma ta‑o o we, “Se nmo zembaaro Aron wolo de na ye Levi tu to, wonto wae o ŋɔɔne lanyerane. Nii ywo! O wo chwoŋa ne o beene se o jeeri‑m. O nam ná nɛ‑m, ko wó pa o wo pwoli dedɛ.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: Aron mo wó lwoni n taane dem o ŋɔɔne de nɔɔna bam, nenɛɛne o ye nmo ni mo tei. Nmo tete wó leiri amo yuu ne n ŋɔɔne ded‑o.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Nam kwei nacheiga kanto nmo na zei n jeŋa ne to n woli da n vo, se n lage n ma-ka n toŋe wo-kenkagela mo.” Moses jwoori o vo Ejipti

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Moses déem ma jwoori o tembaaro Jetero tei o ta‑o o we, “Amo boŋe se a jwoori a chorro tem tei mo Ejipti ne, se a nii ba ta ŋwe de yazura na.” Jetero ma sɛ ye o we, “Véi, se Wɛ wó pa se n yi lanyerane.”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Moses déem ta na wo Midian ne to, mo Baŋa Wɛ ya tage‑o o we, “Jwoori n vo Ejipti, se balo maama na beeri‑m se ba go to laam tega.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Moses ma ja o kaane de o bu-baara bam o jeini-ba bonaga baŋa ne, ye o laam kwei chwoŋa o tɔge de-ba o maa jwoori Ejipti. O déem maa zei Wɛ nacheiga kam o jeŋa ne.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Nmo ná yi Ejipti teo kom, wo-kenkagela yalo maama amo na pɛ‑m dam se n ke to, se n fɔge n ke-ya Ejipti Pɛ wom yiga ne. Amo nam wó pa se o bochare taa dana mo, ye o bá sɛ se amo nɔɔna bam viiri.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Ko ná tu konto, se n ta de Pɛ wom we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo tento: Isarele ye amo bakeiri-kwea mo.

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: Amo nam mo tage de nmo se n pa a bakeiri-kwea kam chwoŋa se o viiri o vo o zuli-ne. Nmo nam ve amo ni. Konto ŋwaane, amo de nam wó go nmo bakeiri-kwea kam mo.’ ”

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Moses kaane Zipora ma zaŋe o kwei kandwɛ-fole na jege ni to o ma o gwoni o bu-baaro wom peini. O ta ma dwei o baro wom napera de tɔnɔ kom ye o ta o we, “Nmo yɔɔre n ye amo baro jana bam ŋwaane mo.”

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: O na ŋɔɔne tei to tɔge de pein-gwoŋa kam ŋwaane mo. Baŋa Wɛ daa maa wo go Moses.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Aron o we, “Zaŋe n vo kagoa kam yuu se n jeeri Moses.” O ma vo o jeeri‑o Wɛ peo kom ne ye o kukwori‑o.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Moses déem laam ma lwoni o bere Aron kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe‑o se o ta to. O ma daare o ta wo-kenkagela yam Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑o ni se o ke to taane o bere Aron.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Aron ma ta kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ déem na tage de Moses to o bere-ba. O de ma ke wo-kenkagela yam maama pa se nɔɔna bam na.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Nakwa bam déem ma sɛ. Ba ta ma ni Baŋa Wɛ na nɛ ba yaara yam ye o chu o ba se o jwoŋi-ba ya wone tei to. Ba ma chɔɔle tega ne ba zuli Wɛ.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Ko na ke fee to, Moses de Aron déem ma vo Ejipti Pɛ wom tei ba ta ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina bam Wɛ to ni mo tento: ‘Pa chwoŋa se a nɔɔna bam viiri. Ba jege se ba vo kagoa wone ba ke kuri mo ba zuli amo.’ ”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom maa we, “Wɔ mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, pa ko maŋe se a sɛ o ni se Isarele tiina bam viiri? Amo yeiri Baŋa Wɛ wom konto, a nam bá pa chwoŋa se Isarele tiina bam viiri.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Ba laam ma leiri‑o ba we, “Hiburu tiina Wɛ wom mo tu debam tei. Konto ŋwaane, dé lwoori nmo tei ne se dé na pwola dé kwei da yatɔ chwoŋa dé vo kagoa kam wone dé ke kaanem dáane dé pa dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Kokuri to, dé ná wo ke konto, o wó waare debam dedaane jawe-chɛɛro dwi dwi mo, naa o pa se dé to jara-keim wone ye dé te.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: O ta maa we, “Nii-na ywo! Nɔɔna bam laam tiini ba daga Ejipti tega kam ne, ye á dáa lage se á cheiŋi-ba se ba yé toŋe ba totoŋa yam.”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Dento dɛ ne, Ejipti Pɛ wom ma bwoŋi dedɛɛra balo na fe tontoŋena bam de totoŋ-chɛɛra to de balo na nii totoŋa yam baŋa ne to, ye o pa-ba ni. O déem maa we:

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Abam daa yé kwei-na ga-korro á pa nɔɔna bam se ba taa mae ba mage bira. Banto tete laam mo jege se ba beeri ga-korro ba ma ba toŋe totoŋa yam.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Ba bira yam ba na wó mage to ba jege se ya muri, de fenfee de. Ba ye jawɔre-nyena mo! Konto ŋwaane mo ba beeri chwoŋa se ba vo ba ke kaanem ba pa ba Wɛ wom.

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Pa-na se totoŋa yam tiini ya chɛ ba yera. Konto wó pa se ba yé na yiga se ba daa cheigi vwa yam konto.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Balo na fe kabɛ sem de totoŋ-chɛɛra to de totoŋa yiga tiina bam déem ma nwoŋi ba vo ba ta de nɔɔna bam ba we, “Pɛ wom tage tento mo: ‘Amo daa bá pa abam ga-korro.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Balo na fe kabɛ sem de totoŋa to, de déem laam tiini ba fe-ba, ye ba tɛ-ba ba we, “Dɛ maama abam totoŋa yam jege se ya yi ko daama na ye tei ye á jwoŋi ga-korro debam tei ne to mo.”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Isarele totoŋa yiga tiina bam laam ma vo ba lwoori Pa-faro wom ba we, “Dé Tu, bɛ laam mo kea ye nmo jege debam n ke tento?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Dedɛɛra bam daa ba pae debam ga-korro se dé taa ma dé toŋa, ye ba ta fe debam se dé mage bira yam se ya yé muri. Ba ta maa jege debam ba maga, ye ko ye banto yiga mo.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma leiri-ba o we, “Nii jawɔre-nyena banto! Abam na vae totoŋa to ŋwaane mo á kare á beeri chwoŋa amo tei ne se á vo á ke kaanem á pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Lela! Se á jwoori á totoŋa ni ne! Ba bá pa abam ga-korro. Á nam ta jege se á mage bira yam mo se ya ja ya ni.”

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam déem na nwoŋi Pɛ wom tei ne to, mo ba jeeri Moses de Aron. Ba de déem nam maŋe ba zege ba cheigi nɔɔna bam mo se ba ba.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Ba na nɛ-ba to, mo ba poone de Moses de Aron ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó waare abam á na ke kolo to ŋwaane. Abam laam pɛ se debam totoŋa tiini ya lwoi mo Ejipti Pɛ de o dedɛɛra bam momwa ne. Á ta ma á pa-ba pwola se ba go debam.”

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Moses ma pipiri o vo o bwei Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Amo Teiru, bɛ mo ye n tiini n ja cham dento n ba n pa n nɔɔna bam? Nmo boŋe se n ke tento mo ye n toŋe-ne ywo to na?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Ko zege dɛ delo amo na vei a ŋɔɔne dedaane Pɛ wom nmo yere ŋwaane to, mo o yɔɔre o pae nmo nɔɔna bam cham se ba taa di. Nmo tete nam ba ke kolokolo se n jwoŋi-ba n yage.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we, “Amo laam lage a pa se n lɔre amo na wó ke Pa-faro wom tei to mo. Amo wó ma dam mo a fe‑o se o yage a nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri. Amo wó pa se o zeili-ba mo se ba nwoŋi ba daare o teo kom.”

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Amo déem ma gwoni ni de-ba, ye a pwooli se a pa-ba Kanaan tega kam. Ba déem nam ta ye veira mo ba zoore jei sem konto ne.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Amo laam nam nigi Isarele tiina bam na ŋwaana tei maama to kolo ŋwaane Ejipti tiina bam tiini ba de-ba kabɛɛne wone. Amo nam wó ke a tɔge de a ni-gwonim dem.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Nam ta de Isarele tiina bam we ‘Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ! A nam wó ma a dam-fɔrɔ de a totoŋ-kamunnu a ma a waare Ejipti tiina bam, se a daare a jwoŋi abam á totoŋ-dɛɛra wone a yage se á daa yé ta‑á ye kabɛ.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: A maa wó pa se á ta‑á ye amo tete nɔɔna. Amo maa wó taa ye abam Wɛ. Konto to, á wó wane á lɔre we amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ, a na jwoŋi abam a yage Ejipti tiina bam jeŋa ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: A maa wó ja abam a zo tega kalo a déem na gwoni ni se a pa Abaraham, de Izaak, dedaane Jakob to. Amo wó seene a pa abam tega kam konto se ka taa ye abam tete nyem. Amo nam mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri o we, “Nmo yei we amo ni ware de pipiri lanyerane. Nii amo tete nɔɔna bam na wo cheigi amo taane dem to, Pɛ wom laam mo wó sɛ o cheigi-de na?”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa Moses de Aron ni ye o we, “Véi-na Isarele tiina bam de Ejipti Pɛ tei, á ta de-ba we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ abam ni se á ja Isarele tiina bam á nwoŋi da Ejipti teo kom ne.” Moses de Aron dwi dem taane

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna banto déem mo wo Isarele sɔ-yuni tem maama yiga ne: Jakob bu-kwea kam mo ye Ruben. Ruben bu-baara bam mo tento: Hanoki, de Pallu, de Hezeron, de Karimi. Sɔ-yuni tento mo ke daane te ye Ruben dwi dem nabaara.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simeon de bu-baara bam mo tento: Jemweli, de Jamin, de Ohadi, de Jakin, de Zohare, dedaane Sawuli. Sɔ-yuni tento mo ke daane te ye Simeon dwi dem nabaara.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gereson bia de ba sɔ-yuni tem déem maa ye Libini de Simeyi.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Merari bia déem mo ye Mahili de Musi. Sɔ-yuni tento mo ke daane te ye Levi dwi dem nabaara.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Izehara bia de déem maa ye Kora, de Nefega, dedaane Zikiri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Yuzeli bia de déem maa ye Misayeli, de Elizafan, de Sitiri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aron déem ma di Eliseba o ma o ke kaane. Wonto maa ye Aminadabi bukɔ mo, ye o ta ye Naason nakɔ. Ba déem loge bia bana mo: Nadab, de Abihu, de Eleaza, de Itamara.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Aron bu Eleaza déem ma di Puteli bukɔ o ma o ke o kaane, ye ba lo Finehase. Levi dwi dem taane mo konto. Sɔ-yuni tem konto maama déem ye Levi dwi dem mo.

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Banto déem ma seene ba vo Ejipti Pa-faro wom tei ba ta ded‑o se o pa Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba viiri. Baŋa Wɛ pɛ Moses de Aron ni

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem na ŋɔɔne de Moses Ejipti teo kom ne to,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: o déem tage o we, “Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. Amo ná tage a bere‑m kolo maama, se n lwoni n ta tento de Ejipti Pɛ wom.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Moses déem ma ve ye o we, “Nmo yei we a ni ware se de pipiri lanyerane. Konto to, Pɛ wom bá sɛ o cheigi amo taane dem.”

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Nmo jege se n ta kolo maama a na wó ŋɔɔne dede‑m to n bere n zembaaro Aron. Wonto laam maa wó ta de Pɛ wom se o yage chwoŋa se Isarele tiina bam viiri ba daare o teo kom.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: De konto de, o ta bá sɛ o cheigi abam taane dem. Amo laam wó ma a dam-fɔrɔ a waare Ejipti tiina bam. Ko kwaga ne, amo wó pa se a nɔɔna bam nwoŋi da teo kom konto ne. Isarele tiina bam maama wó nwoŋi kɔgɔ de kɔgɔ.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord
translation_verse: Moses de Aron ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na bere-ba to.

english_verse: and spoke to the king. At the time, Moses was
translation_verse: Ba déem na vei se ba ŋɔɔne dedaane Pa-faro wom to, de Moses ye bena funɔnɔ (

english_verse: years old, and Aaron was
translation_verse: ) mo. Aron maa ye bena funɔnɔ-yatɔ (

english_verse: . A Stick Turns into a Snake
translation_verse: ). Aron nacheiga kam jigi basankwea

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Ejipti Pɛ wom ná tage o we ‘Ke-na wo-kenkagele se a nii’, se n laam ta de Aron se o kwei o nacheiga kam o dole o de tega ne, Pɛ wom yiga ne. O ná kea, ka wó ji basankwea.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Moses de Aron déem ma vo ba zo Pa-faro wom tei. Ba ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na bere-ba to. Aron déem kwei o nacheiga kam mo o dole o de tega ne, Pɛ wom dedaane o nakwa yiga ne. Ka ma seene ka ji basankwea.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom ma toŋe o bwoŋi o teo kom yi-nara de ko liri-mwa tiina se ba la daane. Liri keira bam na tu to, ba de ma kwei ba liri kikia ba lwoni ba ke wo-kenkagela yanto dwoŋi.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Ejipti Pɛ wom déem nɛ tento maama, ye o bochare ta dana. O déem wo sɛ se o cheigi ba taane dem. Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o ta we ko wó taa ye konto mo. Cham kuni fuga

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Ejipti Pɛ bochare yɔɔre de dana mo, ye o ve se o pa amo nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: O ná tua, se n ta ded‑o we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ wolo Hiburu tiina bam na zuli‑o to mo toŋe-ne se a ta de nmo se n pa o nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba vo kagoa kam wone ba zuli‑o. Nmo nam ta wo sɛ se n pa ba viiri.

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo tento: Wɛ wó ke keim se nmo wane n lɔre we wonto mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. Nii ywo! Amo lage a kwei nacheiga kanto a na zei to a mage Naili na bam se ba pipiri ba ji jana.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Ywona yalo na wo Naili buga kam wone to maama wó te. Na bam de maa wó taa lwoi, pa se Ejipti tiina bam de daa bá wane ba nyɔ buga kam na.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta de Moses o we, “Ta de Aron se o kwei o nacheiga kam o twe-ka o jeeri Ejipti bwi sem, de nabare sem, de bu-nwaro tem, de chwaro tem. O ná ke konto, na bam maama wó pipiri ba ji jana. Ko ná maŋe ko ye kambi sem de kɔɔra bam wone, Ejipti teo kom jei maama wó su de jana.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Moses de Aron ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na bere-ba to. Ejipti Pɛ wom de o nakwa déem zege ba nii mo, ye Aron zeiŋi o nacheiga kam o ma mage na bam baŋa. Naili buga kam na bam maama ma pipiri ba ji jana.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Buga kam wo ywona yam maama ma te pa se ka na bam de tiini ba lwoi. Ejipti tiina bam daa ware na bam se ba nyɔ. Jana déem maa yɔɔre ba su Ejipti teo kom maama.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ejipti liri-keira bam de ma kwei ba liri kikia ba lwoni ba ke konto dwoŋi. Pa-faro wom bochare daa ta maa dana ye o ve se o cheigi Moses de Aron taane dem. Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o ta we ko wó taa ye konto mo.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom laam ma pipiri o jwoori o sɔŋɔ. O bere o wo sɛ se o kwei keim dento o ke o yuu ne.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Ejipti tiina bam maama ma gwaare buli Naili buga kam ni ne se ba wane ba na na ba nyɔ, ba na ware ba nyɔ buga kam tete na bam to ŋwaane.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Moses o we, “Véi n ta Ejipti Pɛ wom we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo tento: Pa a nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri se ba taa wae ba zuli-ne.

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we, “Ta de Aron se o twe o nacheiga kam na wo o jeŋa ne to se ko jeeri bwi sem, de nabare sem, de chwaro tem maama. Konto ná kea, nanchane wó nwoŋi bwi sem wone se faare Ejipti tega kam maama.”

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Ejipti Pa-faro wom ma toŋe o bwoŋi Moses de Aron ye o ta de-ba o we, “Lwoori-na Baŋa Wɛ se o pa se nanchane sem lage jei se daare amo de a nɔɔna bam. Ke-na konto se amo de pa abam nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba vo ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri Pɛ wom o we, “Tɔ, nam da yiga n ta n bere-ne maŋa kalo n na lage se a lwoori Wɛ a pa nmo de n nakwa bam de n nɔn-bia bam maama to. Amo laam wó lwoori Wɛ se o pa nanchane sem jei nmo de n nɔɔna bam sam ne. Se laam wó taa wo Naili buga kam wone yerane mo.”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Jwa ne se n ke konto.” Moses ma ta o we, “Nmo nam na tage tei to mo wó toŋe, se nmo ma n lɔre we debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ ba jege dwoŋi.

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Moses de Aron ma nwoŋi da Pɛ wom tei ne. Moses déem ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ nanchane sem ŋwaane, de o na pɛ se zaŋe se daane Pɛ wom to.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Ejipti tiina bam ma chwooli-se ba tiŋi pwoa dedɛ. Teo kom maama déem chɛ mo de nanchane sem lwom.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye Pa-faro wom, o déem na maane we nanchane sem daa ba daane-ba to, mo o daa ta pɛ se o bochare dana. O daa ta wo sɛ se o cheigi Moses de Aron taane dem, ne Baŋa Wɛ na maŋe o ta we ko wó taa ye tei to.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Moses o we, “Ta n bere Aron se o twe o nacheiga kam o ma mage tega kam, se Ejipti tega kasolo kom maama ji yeena.”

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
