translation_verse: Ba ma sɛ. Aron ma twe o jeŋa o mage tega kam de o nacheiga kam. Yeena ma zaŋe ba meeli nabiina de vara maama. Ejipti teo kom ni maama kasolo déem ma ji yeena.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Ejipti liri-keira bam de ma kwei ba liri kikia ba kwaane se ba lwoni ba pa se yeena ba, ye ba ga ko ŋwa. Yeena yam déem faare teo kom maama mo.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Liri keira bam ma ta de Pa-faro wom ba we, “Wɛ keim mo tento.” De konto maama de, Pɛ wom bochare daa taa dana mo, ye o wo sɛ se o cheigi-ba. Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o ta we ko wó taa ye konto mo.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ta ma ta Moses o we, “Zaŋe zezeŋa ne n vo n che Pɛ wom chwoŋa maŋa kalo o na maa vei buga kam ni to. Laam ta ded‑o we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo tento: Pa amo nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri, se ba vo ba zuli-ne.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Nmo nam ná wo pɛ-ba chwoŋa, amo wó toŋe zɔɔro dedɛ se te daane nmo, de n nakwa bam de n nɔn-bia bam maama. Zɔɔro wó su á sam, ye te faare Ejipti tega kam maama.

english_verse: “The Lord's people in Goshen won't be bothered by flies, but your people in the rest of the country will be tormented by them. That's how you will know that the Lord is here in Egypt. This miracle will happen tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Amo wó pa popɔra kam peini amo nɔɔna bam de abam nɔɔna bam tetare ne. Jwa ne mo amo wó ke wo-kenkagele dem konto.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma seene o toŋe zɔɔro dedɛ o yage Pɛ wom sɔŋɔ ne, de o nakwa bam sam ne. Te déem tiini te chɔge Ejipti teo kom maama.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom ma bwoŋi Moses de Aron ye o ta-ba o we, “Véi-na á kaane á pa á Wɛ wom debam teo konto ne ywo.”

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Debam wó kwei da yatɔ mo dé maa zo kagoa kam wone dé ke kaanem dáane dé pa dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ. O ni dem konto mo o pɛ debam.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom de laam ma ta o we, “Tɔ. Amo wó pa abam chwoŋa se á zo kagoa kam wone á kaane á pa abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Se á yé véi-na yiga yiga. Nam lwoori-na Wɛ á pa amo.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo ná yɔɔre a nwoŋi ywo-seeni, a lage a lwoori Baŋa Wɛ mo. Jwa ne zɔɔro tem wó yage abam yera, Pɛ wom de o nakwa bam de o nɔɔna bam maama. Pɛ, nam ta‑n yei se n daa‑n yé gane debam. Nam yé che nɔɔna bam se ba vo ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma sɛ Moses kwora kam. O déem ma pa se zɔɔro tem yage Ejipti Pɛ wom, de o nakwa bam, dedaane o nɔn-bia bam maama. Zɔɔ dedoa tete déem daa wo daare da.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom daa ta ma pa se o bochare dana. O ma ve se o pa nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem daa ma ta de Moses o we, “Véi Pa-faro wom tei n ta we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na ye Hiburu tiina bam Wɛ wom to ni dem mo tento: Pa amo nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri, se ba vo ba zuli-ne.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam wó pa se popɔra mo taa wora Ejipti tiina vara bam dedaane Isarele tiina vara bam tetare ne. Ko ná ye Isarele tiina vara bam mo, ba dedoa tete ba lage o te.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta de Moses de Aron o we, “Zwɛ-na tentwarem, se á ja á vo Pɛ wom tei. Abam ná yi da, se Moses zege pɛ wom yiga ne o dole tentwarem dem o yage wɛɛne.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Tentwarem dem wó ji fwogo mo wɛyuu ne ye te jage te yi Ejipti teo kom maama. Ko ta wó pa se ŋɔn-pwoni jeini nabiina dedaane vara yera ne se daane-ba logo kom jei maama ne.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Ba ma seene ba kwei tentwarem dem ba ja vo Pɛ wom tei. Moses laam ma kwei-te o ta o yage wɛɛne, ye te pa se ŋɔn-pwoni jeini nabiina dedaane vara yera ne se daane-ba.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Liri keira bam déem wo wane ba vo ba zege Moses yiga ne, ŋɔn-pwoni sem na leigi ba yera ne, de Ejipti tiina bam maama yera ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa se Pɛ wom bochare taa dana, ye o wo sɛ se o cheigi Moses de Aron taane. Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o ta de Moses we ko wó taa ye konto mo.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Moses o we, “Jwa zezeŋa ne se n vo n jeeri Pɛ wom n che o chwoŋa n ta‑o we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na ye Hiburu tiina bam Wɛ wom to ni dem mo tento: Pa a nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri se ba vo ba zuli-ne.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Nmo ná wo sɛ, amo laam wó pa se cham tiini de yi nmo tete yera, ko woli de n nakwa bam de n nɔn-bia bam maama. Ko maa wó pa se nmo lɔre we nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera logo baŋa ne o na maŋe de amo.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Amo yi se a kwei a jeŋa a fere nmo de n nɔn-bia bam maama pa se jawe-chɛɛro tiini te ja abam. Amo ya ná ke konto, abam dwi dem ya wó saare logo kom baŋa ne.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Nmo nam ta pae n tete kamunni mo ye n cheiŋi amo nɔɔna bam se ba yé viiri.

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom nakwa badaara déem ma fone de Baŋa Wɛ taane dem. Banto ma ke lela ba vo ba pa se ba kabɛ sem dedaane ba vara maama ba ba zo sam dem wone.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Ba badwonna yiga déem tera de Baŋa Wɛ taane dem ye ba yage ba kabɛ sem de ba vara bam pwola ne.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Twe n jeŋa n yɔɔre wɛyuu ne, se do-kandwa laam to Ejipti teo kom maama ne. Ya lage ya to ya mage nabiina, de vara, dedaane wodiiru telo na wo Ejipti tiina kare sem ne to mo.”

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka ma tiini ka wuuri jei maama, ye ka ta pepele taa. Ko na zege Ejipti teo kom boboa ne to, do-fɔrɔ konto dwi ta wo fɔge ko ke logo kom ne.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Ko daare Gosen laŋa kam yerane mo, do-kandwa yam déem wo yi da. Dáane mo Isarele tiina bam déem nam zoore to.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Ejipti Pɛ déem ma toŋe o bwoŋi Moses de Aron ye o ta-ba o we, “Amo laam lɔre we a tusi mo, ye Baŋa Wɛ jege chega. Ko ná ye amo de a nɔɔna bam, debam ba jege bora.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Nam lwoori-na Baŋa Wɛ á pa debam-na, se dé yera laam mo chɛ de do-kandwa yam dedaane do-napana kam. Amo de laam wó pa abam pwola se á viiri. Abam daa dae se á maŋe ywo-seeni.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri o we, “Amo ná nwoŋi teo kom wone, a laam wó zeiŋi a je sem wɛɛne a lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se do-napana kam yage bagem. Do-kandwa yam de daa bá taa nena. Konto mo wó pa se nmo lɔre we logo baŋa maama ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Amo nam yei lanyerane we nmo de n nakwa bam ta ba kɔre Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Ko déem na ke tei to, kanzɛ sem de chaara yam chɔge mo, kokuri kanzɛ sem jege se punnu mo. Chaara yam de ma be te maŋe de do-kandwa yam.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Moses ma nwoŋi Pɛ wom tei ne o vo o nwoŋi teo kom wone. O ma vo o zeiŋi o je sem Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne o lwoori‑o. Do-napana kam dedaane do-kandwa yam ma kwori. Doa kam déem daa wo nege tega kam baŋa ne.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom na nɛ we doa kam de do-kandwa yam daa ba nena, ye do-napana kam de daa ba bage to, o ma jwoori o tusi. O de o nakwa bam maama ma pa se ba bochara dana.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: O bochare na dana to, o ve se o pa Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba viiri. Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o pa se Moses lɔre we ko wó taa ye konto mo.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta Moses o we, “Jwoori n vo Ejipti Pɛ wom tei. A nam pɛ se o de o nakwa bam bochara dana mo, se a wane a da ko baŋa ne a ke wo-kenkagela yanto se ba na.

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ko ta wó pa se abam jwa lwoni á bere á bia dedaane ba de bia, se ba lɔre amo na ke tei a waare Ejipti tiina bam de wo-kenkagela yalo a na ke ba tetare ne to. Abam maama laam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Moses de Aron déem ma vo Ejipti Pɛ wom tei ba ta ded‑o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na ye Hiburu tiina bam Wɛ wom to ni dem mo tento: Nmo wó ve se n gwooni n tete amo yiga ne taa se n vo n maŋe yei ne mo? Pa a nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri se ba taa wae ba zuli-ne.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Nmo nam ta ná ve se n pa-ba pwola, amo wó pa se kayere jwa ba se daane n teo kom.

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: Kayere sem lage se meeli jei maama mo, pa se abam daa bá taa nae tega kam. Se maa wó deilimi woŋo kolo maama ta na daare ye do-kandwa yam wo chɔge-ko to, ko woli de teeni delo maama ta na nwoŋi á tega kam ne to.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Se lage se meeli á sam maama mo, nmo tete sɔŋɔ kom, de n nakwa bam sam dem, de n nɔn-bia bam sam dem maama. Ko na zege á nabaara maŋa ne se ko yi zem to, kayere dwi dem konto ta wo fɔge se yo á teo kom ne.” Moses laam ma pipiri o nwoŋi o daare Pa-faro wom.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom nakwa bam ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Dɛ dɔ mo nɔɔno wonto wó sɛ o yage yi-gigilu kolo o na jege o ke dé yera ne to? Nam pa nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba vo ba zuli ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Nmo ta wo maane we dé teo kom maama chɔge nɔɔno wonto ŋwaane mo na?”

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Ba ma bwoŋi Moses de Aron se ba jwoori ba ba Pɛ wom tei. O ma ta-ba o we, “Tɔ, chwoŋa laam wora se á vo á zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Se abam bera mo wó tɔge ba vo?”

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ seene o wó taa wo á tei ne mo nenɛɛne amo ná sɛ se abam kaana de á bia bam tɔge ba vo! Tento yɔɔre ko bere we á boŋe se á ke lwarem mo.

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Ko bá ke! Abam na lwoori chwoŋa se á vo á zuli Baŋa Wɛ to, á baara bam yerane mo wó vo.” Ba déem ma zeili Moses de Aron se ba nwoŋi da Pɛ wom yiga ne.

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Moses ma zeiŋi o nacheiga kam o jeeri Ejipti teo kom baŋa. Dɛ dem konto ne mo Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ se vio nwoŋi wɛ-puli seeni ko ba ko jeeri logo kom. Ko déem dole wea de tete maama mo. Tega déem na jege ka poore to, de vio kom jaane kayere sem ko ba.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Se kɔgɔ déem tiini se gaale dedɛ, ye se meeli teo kom tega kam maama. Ejipti tiina ta wo fɔge ba na kayere sem konto dwi. Se dwi dem konto de daa bá ba kɔtaa.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Kayere sem déem ma kwoli tega kam maama pa se ka zwori ligi-ligi. Se ma di kolo maama do-kandwa yam na daare to. Ko maa ye teeni-bia maama, de ga-zuru, de ba kare wodiiru maama mo. Ejipti wone kolokolo déem daa wo daare ye ko jege zurim.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Pa-faro wom ma ke lela o toŋe o bwoŋi Moses de Aron ye o we, “Amo tusi abam yiga ne de á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Nam yage-na a tusim dento á ma á chɛ-ne, se á daare á lwoori á Tu Baŋa Wɛ se o pa se cham dento kɛ dáa se a sii.”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se vo-dɛɔ kom pipiri ko nwoŋi Wɛ-zoore seeni. Ko ma dole ko kale kayere sem maama ko ja ko vo ko yage Nane-soŋo kom ne. Kayera dedoa tete déem daa wo daare Ejipti teo kom ne.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem daa ta ma pa se Pa-faro wom bochare dana mo. O ma ve se o pa Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba viiri.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ta ma ta de Moses o we, “Twe n jeŋa n yɔɔre wɛyuu ne se lim ba de kwoli Ejipti tega kam baŋa maama. Lim dem wó tiini de zo nɔɔna bam yera.”

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Moses ma twe o jeŋa o yɔɔre wɛyuu ne. Ejipti tega kam baŋa maama ma tiini ka ke lim, se ko maŋe de da yatɔ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Ejipti Pɛ wom déem ma bwoŋi Moses ye o we, “Chwoŋa laam wora se á vo á zuli á Baŋa Wɛ wom. Abam bia de á kaana wó wane ba tɔge ba vo. Nam yage-na á vara bam ywo se á vo.”

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Moses de ma leiri o we, “Dé nam zege n kwora kam kwaga ne. Nmo seene n daa‑n bá‑n na amo.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta Moses o we, “Amo laam lage a pa se cham dedwe mo yi Ejipti Pɛ wom de o nɔɔna bam se ko kweeli. A ná ke konto, o wó pa abam chwoŋa se á viiri. O nam lage o zeili abam mo se á nwoŋi á daare o teo kom.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Nam ta de Isarele tiina bam se ba vo ba fara bam tei ba bwei ba jwoŋi sabu-seŋa dedaane lu-nyenno wonnu. Ba baara de ba kaana maama wó ke konto mo.”

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem nam ke se Ejipti tiina bam mo taa nege Isarele tiina bam. Ko ta ná ye Moses, Ejipti teo nakwa bam dedaane ko nɔn-bia bam kwoni ba nii‑o we o ye nɔn-kamunu mo.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Moses déem ma ta de Pɛ wom o we, “Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo tento: Tete-koro ne, amo Baŋa Wɛ wó tɔge Ejipti teo kom baŋa ne a kɛ.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: Ejipti teo bakeiri-kwea dwi maama wó te. Pɛ wolo na sage paare yituŋu kom ne to bu-kwea wó te, ye kaba-kana kam na choe muni to de bakeiri-kwea de te. Vara balo ba na loge da-yiga to de maa wó te.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Ejipti teo ni maama lage ko taa ye mo ŋɔɔ de keira. Ba ta wo fɔge ba na keira kalo dwi na wó to teo kom ne to, ye ka dwi nam daa bá ba.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Isarele tiina bam na zoore mɛ to, kukura tete bá wei ka fugi nabiina naa vara. Konto mo wó pa se abam lɔre we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ se popɔra wora Ejipti tiina de Isarele tiina tetare ne.”

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem tage dedaane Moses o we, “Pa-faro wom bá sɛ o cheigi nmo taane dem. Ko wó pa se amo na pwola se a tiini a toŋe wo-kenkagela dedɛ Ejipti tiina tei ne.”

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Ejipti teo ne mo Baŋa Wɛ déem ŋɔɔne de Moses dedaane Aron ye o we,

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: “Chana kanto mo wó taa ye boboa chana ka pae abam bene maama wone.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Ta n bere Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama we chana kanto, ka da fuga dɛ dem ne, sɔŋɔ maama ko ni twoo, sɔŋɔ tu wom jege se o beeri pipeila mo naa bebala se o sɔŋɔ tiina bam di kuri.

english_verse: If any family is too small to eat the whole animal, they must share it with their next-door neighbors. Choose either a sheep or a goat, but it must be a one-year-old male that has nothing wrong with it. And it must be large enough for everyone to have some of the meat.
translation_verse: Abam wó wane á kwei pia naa boŋo á ma á toŋe. Varem wom nam jege se o taa ye bene varem mo ye o ta ba jege gɛɛ o yera ne. Varem wom wó taa ye wo-bɛa mo.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Ta‑á nii-na vara bam baŋa ne se ko vo ko yi chana kam da fuga-yana dɛ dem ne. Tega ná lage ka yi, Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama wó go ba vara bam mo.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Ba nam na wó jeini sam delo wone ba di varem wom nɔna yam to, ko jege se ba kwei o jana mo ba taare manchwo-nia sɛ sem de ya yuu ne.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne, ba ta jege se ba wɔ nɔna yam mo, se ba laam di-ya. Ba maa jege se ba ma dwoa vɔɔ-chɛɛro mo dedaane bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to ba di varem wom.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Ko dae se abam di ko nɔn-gwei. Á nam yé saŋe-ko. Varem maama ye se á wɔ mo: yuu, de nɛ, dedaane o wo-zela yam maama.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Abam ná lage á di wodiu kom, se á ta‑á ti á yiga nenɛɛne balo na lage ba vo chwoŋa to. Vɔ-na á gwaaro ye á zo á natera, se á daare á ta‑á zei á nachei sem. Á laam wó di wodiu kom lela. Kokuri to, ko ye Atɔgebabaŋa kuri mo abam lage á di se á ma á zuli amo Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne mo amo wó beeri Ejipti teo kom maama ne, ye a go bakeiri-kwea dwi dem maama, vara dedaane nabiina maama. Amo wó ke konto a ma waare Ejipti tiina bam tangwana de ba jwona yam. Kokuri to, amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Ko daare, jana bam mo wó taa ye memaŋe se ko bere abam na wo sam delo wone to. Amo ná boŋe se a waare Ejipti tiina bam ye a na jana bam, a laam wó tɔge á baŋa a kɛ, se abam yé na chɔgem.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Kwei-na da yarepɛ á di bworobworo-memene selo na ba jege sabɔle se wone to. Yanto da yam boboa dɛ dem ne, á nam jege se á kwei sabɔle delo maama na wo á sam ne to mo á dole á yage. Da yarepɛ yam wone, wolo maama ná di bworobworo kolo na jege sabɔle to, amo wó le konto tu mo a nɔɔna bam tetare ne.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Da yam boboa dɛ dem ne, dedaane da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, á wó jeeri daane á zuli Baŋa Wɛ mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege se o toŋe totoŋa da yalei yam konto ne. Abam nam wó wane á saŋe á wodiiru.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Bene maama wone abam jege se á di Bworobworo-memene kuri dem mo. Kokuri to, ko ye dɛ dem amo na le abam kɔgɔ de kɔgɔ a ja a nwoŋi Ejipti ne to mo. De ye chulu dɛ mo se ko taa vei wuu.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Ko zege boboa chana kam da fuga-yana dɛ dem dedaan-ni ne, se ko vo ko yi ka da finlei-dedwe dɛ dem dedaan-ni ne, se á di bworobworo kolo sabɔle na tere ko wone to.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Da yarepɛ yam wone, sabɔle dae se de taa wo nɔɔn-nɔɔno sɔŋɔ ne. Wolo ná di bworobworo kolo na jege sabɔle ko wone to, amo wó le konto tu a nɔɔna bam tetare ne, konto tu ze ye Isarele tu naa veiru de.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Abam na zoore jei selo maama ne to, se á yé di woŋo kolo na jege sabɔle ko wone to.” Moses berem dem

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Moses déem ma bwoŋi Isarele nakwa bam ye o ta-ba o we, “Nɔɔno maama véi o kuri varem wolo o na wó go Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem ŋwaane to, se o de o diga tiina wane ba di.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Abam ta wó beeri Husopa vɔ-lɛɛro, se á de te nia yam zoŋa de ka wo jana wone. Á laam wó kwei jana bam á taare á sam dem manchwo-nia yam sɛ selei sem dedaane baŋa kam mo. Maŋe-na á sam dem ne se tega poore. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé nwoŋi pwooni ne.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wó ba o beeri Ejipti logo kom ne se o go Ejipti tiina bam. O nam ná nɛ jana bam abam manchwo-nia ne, de ya baŋa kam, de ya sɛ sem ne, o bá pa se toone maleka kam zo á sam wone se o chɔge abam. O wó tɔge abam baŋa mo o kɛ.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Abam nam ná tu á zo teo kom Baŋa Wɛ na gwoni ni se o pa abam to, se á guli á ta‑á ke chullu tem konto.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Abam bia ná tu ba bwei abam we ‘Keim dento kuri mo bɛ?’,

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: se abam de wane á ta de-ba we ‘Ko ye Atɔgebabaŋa kaanem mo debam wora de ke se de ma de zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Kokuri to, dé déem na wo Ejipti ne to, Baŋa Wɛ duri dé ŋwaŋa mo o tɔge debam sam dem baŋa o kɛ, ye o vo o chɔge Ejipti tiina bam.’ ” Moses na tage konto o ti to, Isarele tiina bam ma chɔɔle ba yibia tega ne ba zuli Wɛ.

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na tage o bere Moses dedaane Aron to.

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Tete-koro ne, Baŋa Wɛ déem ma go Ejipti teo kom bakeiri-kwe sem dwi dem maama. Ko zege Ejipti Pɛ na jei paare yituŋu kom baŋa ne to bu-kwea kam, se ko yi ŋweeno wolo na wo peena diga ne to bu-kwea kam, ko ta woli de vara dwi maama de bu-kwe sem.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne mo Pɛ wom de o nakwa bam, dedaane Ejipti tiina bam maama zaŋe ba yɔɔre ba keeri ŋɔɔ! Ejipti tiina maama déem chɛ mo dedaane keira, kolo ŋwaane sɔŋɔ déem tera teo kom wone ye nɔɔno wo tege ko wone. Isarele tiina bam nwoŋi Ejipti ne

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Dento tete ne Pa-faro wom ma toŋe o bwoŋi Moses de Aron. O ma ta de-ba o we, “Nwoŋi-na á viiri á daare a teo! Ja-na Isarele tiina bam maama se á vo á zuli Baŋa Wɛ nenɛɛne á na beeri chwoŋa se á ke tei to.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Kwei-na á pei sem, de á bone dem, dedaane á naane dem maama á woli da á viiri. Á ná via, se á lwoori á Wɛ wom se o zaane taa wo amo de baŋa ne.”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Ejipti tiina bam déem ma bobo se ba taa lwoori Isarele tiina bam se ba ke lela ba viiri. Ba ma ta ba we, “Abam ná wo viiri lela, debam maama wó ji twa mo.”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma kwei ba muni delo sabɔle ta na wo ke de wone to, ba ke zwe selo ba na mae ba viiri muni dem to wone. Ba ma vɔ te maama ba ke ba gwaaro wone, ye ba daare ba kwei tento maama ba daŋe ba bakale baŋa ne ba ja ba kɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ke kolo maama Moses ya na bere-ba to. Ba ya vei Ejipti tiina bam tei ba bwei se ba jwoŋi sabu-seŋa wonnu, de lu-nyenno wonnu, ko woli de gwaaro mo ba tei ne.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ se Isarele tiina bam kikia su Ejipti tiina bam yi mo. Ba déem yɔɔre ba pa-ba kolo maama ba na wó bwei ba tei ne to mo. Ko déem ke konto mo, ye Isarele tiina bam wane ba vere Ejipti tiina jejegero tem ba ja ba viiri.

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma zege Ramesesa ne ba kwei chwoŋa ba maa vei Sukofa. Ba déem ye baara morro kuni bia yaredo (

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna badwonna dedɛ de déem tɔge-ba se ba kɛ. Ba déem ta jege vara na ye pei, de bone, dedaane naane dedɛ.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Ba ma kwei bworobworo muni delo ba na jaane ba nwoŋi Ejipti ne ye sabɔle tere de wone to ba ma fɔge bworobworo se ba di. Nɔɔna bam déem na ke lela ba zaŋe ba nwoŋi Ejipti ne to ŋwaane, ba wo nɛ pwola se ba ti wodiu kom yiga, naa se ba ke sabɔle da se ko fole.

english_verse: The Lord's people left Egypt exactly
translation_verse: Bena bia yana de fintɔ kom (

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem daa ma ta de Moses dedaane Aron o we, “Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem chullu mo tento: Dwi-gɛ tu ba jege se o tɔge o di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye kabɛ selo abam na yeigi-se, ye ba gwoni se peina to, sento wó wane se tɔge se di.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Sɔŋɔ kolo wone abam na wó go varem wom to, mo á wó maŋe ko wone á di nɔna yam maama. Yé ja-ya á nwoŋi pwooni, nam yé bwori-na o kwi de dedoa de.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama nam mo wó da daane ba di kuri dem konto.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Dwi-gɛ tu ná zoore abam wone ye o ná boŋe se o tɔge o di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem o ma zuli Baŋa Wɛ, konto tu jege se o wuuri o gwoni o sɔŋɔ baara bam de bakeiri sem peina mo. O ná ke konto, o jege chwoŋa se o tɔge o di kuri dem, ne o na ye Isarele tu chekke to ŋwaane. Baaro wolo nam na wo gwoni o peini to bá tɔge o di kuri dem.

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma sɛ, ye ba ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na tage o bere Moses de Aron se ba ke to.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ko déem maa ye dɛ dem konto ne mo Baŋa Wɛ jaane Isarele tiina bam o nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne, ba kɔgɔ de ba kɔgɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem laam ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Isarele tiina wone wo-bɛ dwi maama ná ye bu-kwe, se á pɔɔre-se á pa amo. Ko ná ye nabiina wone, naa vara wone wo-kwe selo na ye baara to maama ye amo nyem mo.” Moses berem dem

english_verse: Moses said to the people: Remember this day in the month of Abib. It is the day when the Lord's mighty power rescued you from Egypt, where you were slaves. Do not eat anything made with yeast.
translation_verse: Zem mo abam lage á nwoŋi Ejipti ne. Ko ye boboa chana kam mo, ko yere maa ye Abibi chana kam.

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o gwoni ni de á nabaara bam we o wó pa abam zo tega kadwoŋi mo se á ta‑á tei-ka. Ko nam ye tega kalo Kanaan tiina bam na zoore da to, de Hiti tiina bam, de Amori tiina bam, de Hivi tiina bam, dedaane Jebusi tiina bam mo. Tega kam konto ywomma mo de varem de kɔnɔ. Abam ná yi da, bene maama ne, se á di kuri dento Abibi chana kam ne.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Abam ná yeini á di kuri dem, á wó kwei da yarepɛ mo á ma á di bworobworo kolo sabɔle na tera ko wone to. Ya kweelim dɛ dem ne, á wó di kuri dem á ma á zuli Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Da yam konto ne, se á ta‑á tɛ á bere á bia we ‘Dé wora dé ke tento se dé guli Baŋa Wɛ na ke o pa debam maŋa kalo o na pɛ se dé nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne to mo.’

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kuri dem konto wó taa ye memaŋe mo de pae abam, nenɛɛne á na vɔge woŋo á je ne naa á tira ne se á yé swei tei to. Konto to, Baŋa Wɛ taane wó taa wo á boboŋa ne dedaane á nia ne, se á yé swei-de. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ mo mɛ o dam-fɔrɔ o ma o vere abam o ja nwoŋi Ejipti ne.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Bene maama wone, abam wó ta‑á di kuri dento mo ka maŋa ne.

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: Á ná zo da, á jege se á le wo-bɛ dwi maama na dɛ yiga se nwoŋi se niina puga ne to á pɔɔre-se á pa Baŋa Wɛ. Abam vara bam wone wo-kwe selo na ye baara to ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Jwa seeni, abam bia ná bwei abam se ba lɔre chullu tem kuri na ye tei to, se á ta de-ba we ‘Dé déem ye kabɛ mo Ejipti teo kom ne. Baŋa Wɛ ma kwei o dam-fɔrɔ o vere debam o ja o nwoŋi dé kabɛɛne dem wone.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ejipti Pa-faro wom bochare déem dana mo ye o ve se o pa debam chwoŋa se dé viiri. Konto ŋwaane, Baŋa Wɛ déem go bu-kwe sem dwi maama Ejipti ne, vara dedaane nabiina maama. Konto ŋwaane mo debam yeini dé kwei vare-kwe sem dé ma ke kaanem dé pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ko daare ko ná ye debam tete bakeiri-kwe sem, dé yeini dé ma wonnu dé leiri ba yuu ne dé pa Baŋa Wɛ.’

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Chullu tento wó taa ye memaŋe mo te pae abam nenɛɛne á na vɔge woŋo á je ne naa á tira ne se á yé swei we Baŋa Wɛ mo mɛ o dam-fɔrɔ o ja debam o ja o nwoŋi Ejipti ne to.” Isarele tiina bam kwei chwoŋa ba nwoŋi Ejipti ne

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ejipti Pa-faro wom na pɛ nɔɔna bam chwoŋa se ba viiri to, Wɛ déem wo pɛ se ba kwei chwoŋa kalo na tɔge Filisi tiina laŋa kam to, de ka na maŋe ka ye chwo-kukua to de. Wɛ déem boŋe o tete ne we, “Nɔɔna ná jeeri Isarele tiina bam de jara, ba wó wane ba leiri ba boboŋa ye ba pipiri ba jwoori Ejipti ne.”

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Moses déem kwei Josɛf kwi sem mo o woli da se ba ja ba viiri. Kokuri to, Josɛf déem pɛ se Isarele bia bam du duuri mo, ye o ta-ba we, “Wɛ wó ba o vere abam o yage. Ko nam ná ke konto, se á ja amo kwi sem á nwoŋi da jei sento ne.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma zege Sukofa ne ba vo ba yi Etam. Jei sem konto wo kagoa kam ni ne mo. Ba ma chwi ba vwoa dáane.

english_verse: During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
translation_verse: Wea maama wone, kunkwoŋo kom déem wo nɔɔna bam yiga ne mo. Mini dem de maa wo ba yiga ne tete maama ne.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Ta n bere Isarele tiina bam se ba pipiri ba vo Pi-Hahirofa seeni se ba chwi ba vwoa yam da. Ko maa wo Migidola dedaane naneo kom tetare laŋa ne, ye ko jeeri Baal-Zefon mo.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Ejipti Pɛ wom nam wó boŋe we Isarele tiina bam kare ba beeri mo jei maama ba yeiri chwoŋa. O maa wó ta we, kagoa kam mo chege ba chwoŋa.

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Amo nam daa ta wó pa se o bochare taa dana. O wó pare abam se o ja o jwoori. Tento mo amo wó na chwoŋa a wane Pa-faro wom de o jar-keira bam pa se a laam jwoŋi a zula. Ejipti tiina bam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.” Nɔɔna bam déem ma sɛ ba ke Wɛ na bere-ba kolo to.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna ma ta ba bere Ejipti Pɛ we Isarele tiina bam duri mo ba viiri. O de o nakwa bam ma leiri ba boboŋa ye ba we, “Bɛŋwaane mo dé wó pa Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba lu dé jeŋa ne? Debam gɛ de kabɛ sem mo konto!”

english_verse: best chariots and all his other chariots to start after the Israelites.
translation_verse: ) mo tiini te lamma dedɛ. Toroko maama jege ko dedɛɛro mo.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ya pɛ se Ejipti Pa-faro wom bochare tiini ko dana mo, pa se o pare Isarele tiina bam se o ja. Ko nam ná ye Isarele tiina bam, banto déem vei dedaane baare mo.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma nii ba na Pa-faro wom de o nɔɔna bam na vei ba maa zaŋe ba baŋa ne. Foone ma tiini de ja-ba. Ba ma kaase ba jare Baŋa Wɛ se o zeini-ba.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Ba ma bwɛ Moses ba we, “Nmo jaane debam n ba ywo-seeni se dé te kagoa kanto ne mo na? Yibeela mo tera Ejipti ne se ba ke debam ya wone na? Bɛ mo ye n ja debam n nwoŋi Ejipti ne?

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ mo lage o ja jara o pa abam. Abam wó ta‑á zege da chemm mo ye á nia.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo ye nmo zege n kaase n jare-ne? Ta de nɔɔna bam se ba taa tutwoni ba vei yiga!

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Se nmo zeiŋi n nacheiga kam! Twe-ka naneo kom baŋa ne, se na bam pɔɔre belei. Chwoŋa wó peini na bam tetare ne se Isarele tiina bam nɔne te-kora baŋa ne ba bɛ bubɛ dedem dem ne.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Amo laam wó pa se Ejipti tiina bam bochara taa dana. Ba wó tɔge abam kwaga ba zo naneo kom wone. Dáane mo amo wó wane Pa-faro wom de o jar-keira bam, de ba torokooro, de ba sisein-dira maama pa se a laam jwoŋi a zula.

english_verse: The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Amo ná wane Pɛ wom de o jar-keira bam konto, Ejipti tiina bam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Wɛ maleka kam déem na yeini ka tɔge Isarele tiina jar-keira bam yiga to laam ma tutwoni ka vo ka zege ba kwaga ne. Kunkwoŋo kom de ma kɛ ko vo ko zege deiki ba kwaga ne.

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: Ko déem zege Ejipti tiina kɔgɔ kom dedaane Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom tetare laŋa ne mo. Kunkwoŋo kom ma pa se ko ye lim Ejipti tiina bam tei ne tete dem konto maama ne. Se ko ná ye Isarele tiina bam, banto déem jege pwooni mo. Tete dem konto ne ba kɔgɔ kom déem ware se ba yi da-tei.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Moses déem ma twe o jeŋa naneo kom baŋa ne. Tete dem maama ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se vo-dɛɔ nwoŋi wɛ-puli seeni ko ba ko dole buga kam baŋa ne. Na bam déem ma pɔɔre belei ye te-kora peini ba tetare ne.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem vei te-kora baŋa ne mo ba bɛ naneo kom. Na bam déem nye de kabira mo na chege ba jazem dedaane jagwia maama.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Te-pora ni ne mo Baŋa Wɛ zege kunkwoŋo kom na jege mini to wone o guni o nii Ejipti jar-keira bam ye o pa se vuvuga to ba tetare ne.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: O déem ma pa se ba torokooro tem nɛ sem moore pa se ko chamma se ba wane ba vo ba bɛ. Ejipti tiina bam laam ma ta ba we, “Pa-na se dé duri dé jwoori-na se dé lu Isarele tiina jeŋa ne! Kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ mo wora o jaane jara o woli-ba se ba wane debam.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Twe n jeŋa naneo kom baŋa ne se na bam jwoori ba pu Ejipti tiina bam, de ba torokooro tem, de ba sisein-dira bam maama.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Moses ma twe o jeŋa naneo kom baŋa ne. Tega na jege ka poore to, na bam ma jwoori ba ke daane nenɛɛne ko ya na maŋe ko ye tei to. Ejipti tiina bam nam ya kwaane mo se ba lu, ye Baŋa Wɛ kale banto o de naneo kom wone.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Na bam na jwoori ba ke daane to, ba ma pu Ejipti tiina kɔgɔ kom maama, de ba torokooro tem, de ba sisein-dira bam. Nɔɔno de dedoa tete de wo wane se o lu.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Se ko daare Isarele tiina bam, banto ya vei te-kora baŋa ne mo ba vo ba bɛ naneo kom. Na bam déem nye de kabira mo na chege ba jazem dedaane jagwia maama.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne mo Baŋa Wɛ vere Isarele tiina bam Ejipti tiina bam jeŋa ne o yage. Isarele tiina bam déem ma tole ba na Ejipti tiina bam na tege ba tiga bubɛ dem baŋa ne.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Moses dedaane Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom ma leeni leiŋa kanto se ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ: Amo wó leeni a zuli Baŋa Wɛ, o na pɛ o yere zaŋe wɛɛne to ŋwaane. O jaane siseiŋa dedaane wolo na diini-ka to o dole o de naneo kom wone.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ mo ye wolo na pa-ne dam to, ye wonto ŋwaane mo a leena. O ma bere o tete we o ye amo vereno wom. O ye amo Tu Wɛ mo ye amo wó taa tei‑o. Amo kwo Wɛ mo konto. Amo wó zeiŋi o yere wɛɛne.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ye babea mo. O yere mo ye ‘Taa-wuu Baŋa Wɛ’.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: O vuvugi Ejipti Pɛ wom jar-keira bam de ba torokooro tem o de Nane-soŋo kom wone. Na bam ma pu Pɛ wom jar-keira dedɛɛra bam pa se ba te.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: Debam Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo jeŋa jege dam-fɔrɔ chekke! Nmo jazem dem mage dé dona pa se n wane-ba. Debam Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo jeŋa jege dam!

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Nmo ma‑n wane n dona pa se n yere tiini de zaŋe. Nmo bane tiini de zaŋe ba baŋa ne, nenɛɛne n na tɔrege mini n zwɛ ga-korro tei to.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Nmo momwa vio yerane mo pɛ se naneo kom na bam daŋe da-baŋa ne. Ba zege mo cheppe nenɛɛne kabira dwoŋi mo to. Na-luŋa kam ma leiri ka ji te-dɛa.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Debam dona bam ya boŋe ba we, “Pa-na dé duri dé pu ba kwaga se dé ja-ba. Dé wó kwei se-zɔɔro dé chɔge-ba, ye dé vere ba wonnu dé pɔɔre dé pa daane. Dé wó na kolo maama dé na lage to.”

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ! Wa yam maama wone nmo dwoŋi tera! Nmo zula yam gaale! Nmo yere zaŋe wɛɛne! Nmo ma‑n mae n dam-fɔrɔ n ke wo-kenkagela ye n dwoŋi tera!

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: Nmo twe n jazem dem yerane mo, ye tega kam puri ka li dé dona bam.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Edom tiina pwa bam laam fom mo. Moaba dedɛɛra bam yera maa sae. Kanaan tiina bam baare maama ma jei.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Foone de lwia mo laam jege-ba, ba na nɛ nmo dam-fɔrɔ kom to ŋwaane. Ba zege ba nii mo de foone ye n nɔɔna bam da ba yiga ne ba kɛ. Baŋa Wɛ! Nmo vere n nɔɔna bam n ja nwoŋi ba kabɛɛne wone, ye ba dona bam zege ba nia!

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ paare dem wó taa wora wuu mo.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Aron nakɔ Miriam déem ye Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu mo. O ma kwei senyaga se o ma o leeni leiŋa. Kaana bam maama de tɔge ded‑o ba maa jege senyɛ ba wɔe ye ba sae.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Miriam déem leeni leiŋa kanto mo o bere-ba: “Leeni-na á zuli Baŋa Wɛ, o na pɛ o yere zaŋe wɛɛne to ŋwaane. O jaane siseiŋa dedaane wolo na diini-ka to o dole o de naneo kom wone.” Na-chɛɛra

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba yi Mara jei sem. Na maa wora, ba na ye na-chɛɛra ye nɔɔna bam ware ba nyɔ to. .

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Moses ma lwoori o jare Baŋa Wɛ. Wɛ ma bere‑o tio kodwoŋi naga. O ma kaare-ka o de na bam wone. Na bam ma leiri ba ji na-ywona. Dáane mo Baŋa Wɛ kwei o ni dem o tiŋi o pa nɔɔna bam se ba taa tɔga, ye o daare o faŋe nɔɔna bam o nii.

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: O ma ta de-ba o we, “Nenɛɛne abam na wó sɛ á cheigi amo kwora lanyerane, ye á tɔge chwo-laao amo yiga ne, ye á daare á ke á tɔge amo nia yalo maama a na bere abam to, amo bá sɛ se jaweero telo dwi na daane Ejipti tiina bam to ja abam. Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, wolo wom na zuri á jaweero to.”

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama déem zege Elim ne mo ba vo ba yi kagoa, ka yere mo Sin. Jei sem konto nam wo Elim dedaane Sinayi Peo kom tetare laŋa ne mo. Ba na nwoŋi Ejipti to, chane selei sem da fuga-yanu dɛ ne mo ba vei ba yi da.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Ba na wo kagoa kam ne to, mo nɔɔna bam maama bobo se ba taa poona ye ba bwɛ Moses de Aron.

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: Ba maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ ya ná maŋe o pa se dé te Ejipti ne ko gare tento! Dáane, dé nae wodiu dé di, ye dé done nɔna dé sui. Abam ma ja debam á pa dé nwoŋi da dé ba kagoa kanto ne, se kana go dé kɔgɔ kom maama.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Amo wó pa se bworobworo nwoŋi wɛyuu ne, nenɛɛne doa na nena tei to. Dɛ maama nɔɔna bam jege se ba nwoŋi pwooni mo ba pɛ wodiu kolo na wó maŋe de ba dɛ wone dim to. Amo lage a faŋe-ba mo a nii, ba wó sɛ a ni dem naa ba bá sɛ-de.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Nam ta de-ba se, da yaredo dɛ dem ne se ba pɛ ba dɛ wone wodiu kuni belei, se ba ja ba zo ba sam dem wone.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Moses de Aron ma ta de Isarele tiina bam maama we, “Zem dedaan-ni ne mo abam wó lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ mo jaane abam o ja o nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne o ba ywo-seeni.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Tega ná poore, á lage á na Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom na tiini ko nyeene to mo. Kokuri to, o nigi abam na poona ye á bwɛ‑o tei maama to. Abam na poona konto to, ko ye Wɛ mo á jege á bwɛa. Debam dae kolokolo se á bwɛ debam.”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Moses laam ma ta o we, “Tega ná lage ka yi, Baŋa Wɛ wó pa abam nɔna se á done. Tega ná poore, o ta wó pa abam bworobworo se á di á su. Abam na poone tei to, ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo á jege á bwɛa, ye ko dae debam. Baŋa Wɛ nam mo nigi á pompona kam.”

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Moses déem ma ta de Aron o we, “Ŋɔɔne dedaane Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ nigi á pompona kam. Á ba á la daane o yiga ne.’ ”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Aron déem ta na ŋɔɔne dedaane nɔɔna bam to, ba kwoni ba yum ba nii kagoa kam seeni mo. Ba ma na Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ na tiini ka nyeene kunkwoŋo kom wone tei to.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “Amo nigi Isarele tiina bam pompona kam maama. Nam ta de-ba we ‘Tega ná lage ka yi, abam wó done nɔna, se te-pora ne á di bworobworo á su. Konto mo wó pa se á lɔre we amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ.’ ”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Dedaan-ni dem konto ne, lwi dedɛ ma zaŋe se ba se faare mɛ nɔɔna bam na zoore to. Tega daa na poore to, nyɔnɔ ma to ko gilimi ba vwoa yam maama.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Nyɔnɔ kom ma we, ko daare wo-meena yalo na ye fefala ye ya bwona to maa faare tega kam maama kagoa kam ne.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam na nɛ-ya to, ba wo lɔre ya na ye woŋo kolo. Ba maa bwei daane ba we, “Bɛ mo tento?” Moses ma leiri-ba o we, “Bworobworo kolo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ abam se á ta‑á di to mo konto.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam we á ta‑á ke tento mo: ‘Nɔɔno maama jege se o pɛ tei na wó maŋe o dim de o diga tiina dim to mo. Nɔɔno maama wó wane o na bɔŋa dedoa.’ ”

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma vo ba ke konto. Badwonna déem pɛ dedɛ mo ye babam pɛ fenfee.

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna badwonna ma ve se ba sɛ Moses taane dem. Ba déem ma di ba daare pa se ko poore tega. Wodiu kom ma ji kanzwa ye ko laam lwoi. Moses bane ma zaŋe de nɔɔna bam konto.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Dɛ maama tetete, ba maa yeini ba pɛ tetei na wó maŋe de ba dim to. Wea ná yeini ka di wɛɛne, kolo maama na daare tega ne to wó nyeene mo.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Da yaredo dɛ dem ne, ba déem pɛ wodiu kom kuni belei mo, bwɛ selei nɔɔno maama ŋwaane. Ba nakwa tiina bam ma vo Moses tei ba ta ba bere‑o ko na ke tei to.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Moses ma ta o we, “Di-na wodiu kom konto zem, se zem dɛ dem ye siu dɛ mo se á ma á zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Abam zem bá na wodiu jei de jei tega kam baŋa ne.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Da yaredo mo abam wó ta‑á pɛ wodiu kom. Ko daare da yarepɛ dɛ dem wó taa ye siu dɛ mo ko pae abam. Wodiu bá taa wora se á pɛ-ko.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Ko nam na ke tei to, nɔɔna badwonna mo nwoŋi da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne ba beeri wodiu se ba pɛ, ye ba wo nɛ kolokolo.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Abam wó ve se á sɛ amo nia yam de a bera yam taa se á vo á maŋe yei ne mo?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Á wo nɛ? Baŋa Wɛ tiŋi siu dɛ dem o pa abam. Konto ŋwaane mo da yaredo dɛ dem ne Wɛ wó pa da yalei wodiu se á pɛ. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege se o nwoŋi pwooni da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne. O wó maŋe sɔŋɔ ne mo.”

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma bwoŋi wodiu kom yere we ‘Manna.’ Ko déem nye dedaane nyansaŋa bia mo. Ko maa ye napwoŋo, ye ko ywomma nenɛɛne ba mɛ tooro mo ba fɔge maasa tei to.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Moses ta ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ pɛ o ni dem mo se á kwei Manna yam bɔŋa dedoa á tiŋi jwa ŋwaane. Abam bia jwa wó lɔre wodiu kolo Wɛ na pɛ abam kagoa kam yuu ne, maŋa kalo o na jaane abam o nwoŋi Ejipti ne to.”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Moses laam ma ta de Aron o we, “Kwei zoŋa n daare n zwɛ Manna n ke ka wone se ka maŋe de bɔŋa dedoa. Laam ja-ka n vo n zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Á bia jwa wó taa nae Manna yam dáane maŋa maama.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Aron déem ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na bere Moses to. O kwei Manna yam mo o zege Wɛ ni-gwonim kandwa yalei yam yiga ne se ya taa wo dáane.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom déem ma zege Sin kagoa kam ne, ye ba laam kare ba beeri, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na yeini o bere-ba se ba vo mɛ to. Ba ma vo ba yi jei sedwoŋi ba na bwoi we Refidim to ye ba chwi ba vwoa dáane. Jei sem konto ne, na déem tera se nɔɔna bam nyɔ.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Ba ma bobo se ba taa bwɛ Moses ye ba we, “Pa debam na se dé nyɔ!” Moses ma leiri o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye á bwɛ amo konto? Bɛ mo ye abam lage se á maŋe Baŋa Wɛ á nii?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Na-nyɔm dem nam na jege nɔɔna bam to, ba déem ta poone ye ba bwɛ Moses ba we, “Bɛ mo maŋe ko ba n yuu ne ye n ja debam n nwoŋi Ejipti ne n ba ywo-seeni? Nmo lage se na-nyɔm mo go debam dedaane dé bia dedaane dé vara maama na?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Moses ma kaase o jare Baŋa Wɛ ye o we, “Amo bere a lage a ke nɔɔna banto tetɛ mo? Ba laam boŋe se ba dole-ne de kandwa mo ba go.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri Moses o we, “Kuri Isarele nakwa bam badwonna se á da nɔɔna bam yiga á kɛ. Kwei n nacheiga kalo n na mɛ n mage Naili buga kam to n woli da n vo.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Amo wó zege Sinayi peo kom yuu ne se a jeeri abam. Á ná yi da, nmo laam wó ma n nacheiga kam n mage peo kom. Nmo ná ke konto, na wó nwoŋi ko yera ne se nɔɔna bam nyɔ.” Moses ma ke konto Isarele nakwa bam yiga ne.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Moses déem pɛ jei sem konto yere we ‘Meriba’, de ‘Massa’. Kokuri to, dáane mo Isarele tiina bam poone ye ba maŋe Baŋa Wɛ se ba nii. Ba déem we, “Baŋa Wɛ wo dé tei ne naa o tera mo?” Amaleki tiina ke jara de Isarele tiina bam

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam na wo Refidim ne to, Amaleki tiina bam ma pɔpɔ ba zaŋe ba baŋa ne se ba ke jara de-ba.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Moses ma ta de Josua o we, “Kuri nɔɔna bam badwonna se á vo á jeeri Amaleki tiina bam de jara. Jwa ne, amo de wó taa zege peo kom yuu ne, ye a zei Wɛ nacheiga kam.”

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Moses je sem déem ma bugi. Aron de Hura ma tiŋi kandwɛ, ye ba pa se o jeini de baŋa ne. Ba déem ma teili o je sem pa se lɛɛre se wo wɛɛne. Dedoa zei jazem dem, ye wodwoŋi wom de zei jagwia kam. Ba zei Moses je sem wɛɛne konto mo taa se ko yi wɛ-zoore maŋa.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we, “Popone keim dento n tiŋi tɔnɔ ne se nɔɔna guli ko gula. Ta popone we, Amo wó ba a pa se Amaleki tiina yere saare logo baŋa ne, se n daare n pa se Josua taa yei ko ni ne.”

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Moses ma lɔ kaanem bimbini jei sem konto ne ye o bwoŋi-de we ‘Baŋa Wɛ mo ye amo Tuta.’

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: O maa we, “Ba zeiŋi je mo wɛɛne se se jeeri Baŋa Wɛ. Baŋa Wɛ wó ja jara dedaane Amaleki tiina bam mo de ba kwaga kam taa wuu.”

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Jetero ya toŋe ni mo o pa Moses o we, “Amo maa beene nmo tei. N kaane wom de n bia balei bam de maa tɔga.”

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Ba na yi to, Moses ma nwoŋi se o jeeri-ba. O déem ma tiiri o tembaaro wom yiga ne, ye o daare o kukwori‑o. Ba ma bwei da-kwaga, ye ba laam daare ba zo Moses vwei dem wone se ba lare.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Moses ma lwoni kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe Ejipti Pɛ wom de o nɔɔna bam yerane pa se o vere Isarele tiina bam to o bere Jetero. O ta ma ta ded‑o ba na jeeri cham delo maama chwoŋa kam yuu ne to, de Baŋa Wɛ na ke tei o vere-ba to.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: Amo laam lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ mo daga o dwoi wa yam maama. Kokuri to, o pɛ se o nɔɔna bam lu Ejipti tiina bam dam kuri ne, de ba na bɛɛse-ba tei maama to.”

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Nmo ná lage n ta‑n ke konto, ko bá dáane de n yera na chɛ. Nɔɔna bam yera de maa wó chɛ. Totoŋe dento daga de dwoi nmo yerane jaanem.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Moses ma jeini se o cheigi nɔɔna balo na tu o tei ba saŋe daane to taane. Nɔɔna bam na daga to ŋwaane, ba zege Moses yiga ne mo taa, zezeŋa ne se ko vo ko yi dedaan-ni ne.

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: Moses tembaaro Jetero na nɛ konto to mo o bwei‑o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo ye nmo toŋe totoŋe dento n pae nɔɔna bam n yerane? Nii nɔɔna bam na zege ywo-seeni tetete wɛɛne se ko yi dedaan-ni ne, ye nmo yerane mo bore ba taane.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri‑o o we, “Kokuri to, nɔɔna bam yeini ba tui amo tei se ba lɔre Wɛ boboŋa na ye tei ya pa-ba to mo.

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Jetero ma leiri o we, “Nmo na ke tei to ba tɔge chwoŋa.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Cheigi amo kwea yanto a na lage a pa‑m to, se Wɛ wó taa wora nmo tei ne. Nɔɔna bam ná yeini ba jege kantɔgɔ, ko lana se n kwei ba taane dem n ja n vo Wɛ yiga ne mo.

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: Nmo ta jege se n bere-ba Wɛ nia yam, dedaane o bera yam na bere kolo to, se ba lɔre ba na wó tɔge chwoŋa kalo to.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Nmo ná ke konto dwoŋi nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na bere‑m to, ko daa bá ni‑m. Nɔɔna bam de nam wó jwoori ba sam ne dedaane bochare-zuru.”

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne mo Moses bane o tembaaro Jetero o yage chwoŋa ne pa se o jwoori o vo o tete teo.

english_verse: The Israelites left Rephidim and arrived at the desert. Then two months after leaving Egypt, they arrived at the desert near Mount Sinai, where they set up camp at the foot of the mountain. This was two months after they had left Egypt.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem zege Refidim ne ba vo ba yi Sinayi kagoa kam. Ba na nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne to, ko ye chane setɔ boboa dɛ ne mo ba yi da. Ba ma chwi ba vwoa yam Sinayi Peo kom teiŋa ne.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Moses ma di peo kom yuu se o vo Wɛ tei. Baŋa Wɛ ma zege peo kom yuu ne o bwoŋi‑o ye o we, “Ta tento n bere Isarele tiina bam na ye Jakob dwi dem to:

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Abam nam wó ta‑á ye amo kaanem tiina, ye á toŋe amo paare yerane ŋwaane mo. Abam dwi dem wó taa ye á yera amo ŋwaane.’ Ta konto maama n bere Isarele tiina bam.”

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Moses ma zege peo kom yuu ne o tu. O ma bwoŋi Isarele nakwa bam ye o daare o tole Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam maama o bere-ba.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma sɛ ye ba leiri ba we, “Dé wó ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na tage to.” Moses daa ma ja nɔɔna bam kwora kam o vo o tole o bere Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Moses o we, “Amo lage a ba nmo tei, ye kunkwon-lilirru mo wó kwoli-ne. Ko wó pa se, amo ná tu a ŋɔɔne de nmo, nɔɔna bam wó ni amo kwora ye ba daare ba ke ba wo-dedoa de nmo maŋa maama.” Moses daa ma ta nɔɔna bam taane dem maama o bere Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, “Jwoori n tu nɔɔna bam tei n daare n pa ba kwei zem de jwa dɛ dem ba ma kwɛ ba bochara ba pa amo. Ba jege se ba zare ba gwaaro

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: se ba ti ba yiga se, da yatɔ dɛ ná yia, se a laam ba ba tei. Amo Baŋa Wɛ wó tu a ba Sinayi Peo kom yuu ne se nɔɔna bam maama taa nii ba na-ne.

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Ba ná lage ba go‑o, ba jeŋa yé dwei‑o. Ba nam wó dole‑o mo de kandwa naa ba ta‑o de chena se o te. Ko ná ye nabiinu naa varem mo ye o naga ná nɔne peo kom, o jege se o te mo. Tɔ. Ba nam ná wugi nabɔna kam, nɔɔna bam laam jege chwoŋa se ba fɔɔre ba yi peo kom.”

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Moses ma zege peo kom yuu ne o tu o vo nɔɔna bam tei. O ma pa ba kwɛ ba bochara ba pa Wɛ ye ba daare ba zare ba gwaaro.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Moses ma ta de-ba o we, “Ti-na á yiga da yatɔ dɛ dem ŋwaane. Da yam konto ne, nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé peini de kaane.”

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Da yatɔ dɛ dem tetete mo doa tiini ka pepele ye ka bage pina-pina. Kunkwon-liliru ma tu ko ba ko kwoli peo kom yuu. Nabɔna laam ma tiini ka wuuri sɔɔ dedɛ. Nɔɔna bam na nigi sɔɔ kom to, ba yera maa tiini ya sae ye foone zo-ba.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Moses ma tɔge nɔɔna bam yiga o ja-ba o nwoŋi ba vwoa yam wone se ba vo ba jeeri Wɛ. Ba ma vo ba zege peo kom teiŋa ne.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Nyoa déem maa kwoli Sinayi peo kom yuu maama. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem chugi ko baŋa ne ye mini gilimi‑o. Nyoa kam ma zaŋe toge-toge ka di wɛyuu, nenɛɛne min-vo-fɔrɔ tei. Peo kom maama ma tiini ko ziziŋi.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Nabɔna kam kwori laam maa tiini de dana. Moses déem maa ŋɔɔne de Wɛ, ye Wɛ de leiri o taane dem ne doa na bage tei to.

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma tu o ba Sinayi Peo kom yuu ne. O ma bwoŋi Moses se o di o ba peo kom yuu. Moses ma di Wɛ tei.
