english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, “Jwoori n tu tega n kaane nɔɔna bam se ba yé lɛɛne siseini dem. Ba ba jege se ba fe ba di se ba na amo Baŋa Wɛ. Ba ná fe ba ke konto, ba dedɛ lage ba te mo.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Ko ná maŋe ko ye amo kaanem tiina balo na yeini ba tui amo tei to, ba jege se ba kwɛ ba bochara mo amo ŋwaane. Ko ná dae konto, amo wó chɔge-ba mo.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Nam tu tega n ja Aron se á tɔge daane á di ywo-seeni. Se ko ná ye kaanem tiina bam dedaane nɔɔna bam maama, ba ná fe ba lɛɛne se ba twɛ ywo-seeni, amo bane wó zaŋe de-ba mo, ye a chɔge-ba.”

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Moses ma tu o vo nɔɔna bam tei ye o ta de-ba kolo Baŋa Wɛ na tage to.

english_verse: God said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Wɛ déem mo ŋɔɔne taane dento maama:

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam déem zege yiga yiga mo, ye Moses fɔɔre o twɛ kunkwon-liliru kom mɛ Wɛ na wora to. Chullu tedwonna

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
translation_verse: “Amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Amo maa ye wolo na jaane abam a ja nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne pa se a vere abam á kabɛɛne dem ne a yage to.

english_verse: Do not worship any god except me.
translation_verse: Daa á yé zuli-na wɛ dedwoŋi á woli amo wone.

english_verse: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
translation_verse: Yé zaŋe-na á mɔ kamɔgɔ se ko taa ye jwoni ko pa abam. Á yé mɔ woŋo se ko lwoni wɛyuu wonnu, naa tega baŋa wonnu, naa tega kuri na bam wo wonnu.

english_verse: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye balo na swoi-ne ye ba sɛ a nia yam to, a maa yeini a jege ba swono taa, se ko yi ba dwi dem kuni moro laŋa ne.

english_verse: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
translation_verse: Yé zaŋe-na á bwoŋi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere kafɛ yerane, se Baŋa Wɛ wó waare wolo maama na ke konto to.

english_verse: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ta‑á guli-na Wɛ siu dɛ dem se á pɔɔre-de da yam maama wone á pa Wɛ.

english_verse: You have six days when you can do your work,
translation_verse: Da yarepɛ maama wone, abam jege da yaredo mo se á ma á toŋe totoŋa dwi maama.

english_verse: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem kwei da yaredo mo o naane wɛyuu de tega baŋa, de naneero tem, dedaane wonnu telo na wo tento maama wone to. O laam ma sii da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne. Baŋa Wɛ ma ke zaane o ke siu dɛ dem baŋa ne o pa de ye de yera.

english_verse: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
translation_verse: Ta‑á nege-na á kwoa de á niina, se ko pa á ta‑á jege momwɛ-dɛɛre maŋa kalo á na wó ta‑á zoore tega kalo abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ na lage o pa abam to wone.

english_verse: Do not murder.
translation_verse: Yé zaŋe-na á go nɔɔno.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: Yé ke-na kabwoŋa de nɔɔno wodwoŋi kaane.

english_verse: Do not steal.
translation_verse: Yé ŋɔ-na kolokolo.

english_verse: Do not tell lies about others.
translation_verse: Yé zaŋe-na á bore vwa bora á ma á vane á dwonna.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Yé kwei-na á boboŋa á daŋe á dwonna sam baŋa ne. Nam yé pa-na se á boboŋa taa wo ba kaana baŋa ne. Yé pa-na se á fera zo ba kabɛ naa ba ka-nyaana wone. Yé pa-na se á yi su á dwonna nabɛ, naa ba bonɛ, naa woŋo kolo maama na ye ba nyem to.”

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Abam nam ba jege se á zuli wo-gaa á woli amo ne. Á yé zaŋe á kwei sabu-seŋa naa lu-nyenno á ma á ke jwoni.’ ”

english_verse: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam maama déem ma na doa kam na tiini ka bage ye ka ta pepele tei maama to. Ba ta ma ni nabɔna kam kwori, ye ba daare ba na peo kom maama na kwoli dedaane nyoa tei maama to. Ba yera maa sae ye foone tiini de jege-ba. Ba déem ma fɔɔre ba kɛ dáa.

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: Ba ma ta de Moses ba we, “Jan ja! Nmo ná ŋɔɔne taane n bere debam, dé wó cheigi. Nam yé pa se Wɛ tete ŋɔɔne dedaane debam, se dé wó te.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri nɔɔna bam o we, “Yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. Kokuri to, Wɛ tu abam tei se o faŋe abam mo o nii, se á ta‑á kɔre‑o ye á yé tusi o chwoŋa kam ne.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Ta tento de Isarele tiina bam: ‘Abam tete yia nɛ we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo zege wɛyuu ne a ŋɔɔne de abam.

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Nmo nam ná boŋe se n kwei kandwa se n seene bimbini n pa-ne, se n yé ma kolokolo n ma‑n sare kandwa yam naa n lɔ-ya. Nmo ná ke konto dwoŋi, ko wó pa se bimbini dem ji kafɛ mo amo yiga ne.

english_verse: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_verse: Yé kwei nateini n yeiri bimbini dem yera ne, se n dɔɔle-de n di. Ko dae se nɔɔn-nɔɔno na nmo yera yam bwori, nenɛɛne n ná lage n ke kaanem n pa-ne.”

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
translation_verse: Wolo maama ná mage o kwo naa o nu, se ba go konto tu.

english_verse: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
translation_verse: Ni-kantɔgɔ ná tu nɔɔna balei tetare ne, ye ba dedoa ma kwei kandwɛ naa o jaguli o ma o ke wodwoŋi wom zonne ye o wo tege.

english_verse: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
translation_verse: Wolo ná yeigi Hiburu tu se o ma o ji o kabaa, kabaa kam wó toŋe ka pa‑o bena yaredo mo. Bena yarepɛ bene dem wone, se kotu yage‑o se o viiri zɛɛra, ye kabaa kam bá ŋwe kolokolo.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ná ye badeim ye o ba o toŋe o pa‑m, ye o ná lage o viiri, ko ye wonto yerane mo wó viiri. O ya nam ná maŋe o jege kaane mo ye o ba n tei, o jege se o ja o kaane wom mo o woli da o viiri.

english_verse: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
translation_verse: O na toŋe o pae wolo to ná pɛ‑o kaane, ye o de kaane wom lo bia daane, nɔɔno wom yerane mo wó viiri. Kaane wom de o bia ye o tu wom nyem mo.

english_verse: But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them.
translation_verse: Kabaa kam nam wó wane o ta we, “Amo swoi a tu wom, ko woli de a kaane de a bia bam. A nam bá viiri a daare-ba.”

english_verse: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
translation_verse: O tu wom maa wó ja‑o o vo Wɛ wara-jei sem ni dem seeni o pa o sale bworo kom. Dáane mo o wó kwei se-lwei o puri kabaa kam zwɛ dedoa. Konto bere we kabaa kam ŋwea maama wone, o ye o tu wom nyem mo.

english_verse: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná kwei o bukɔ o yeigi o pa se o ji kabaa, ko dae se ka maŋa ná yia, se ba yage‑o se o viiri nenɛɛne ba na ke baara bam tei to.

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Kaba-kana kam ná chɔge wolo na yeigi‑o to yiga, o tu wom wó wane o jwoori o yeigi‑o o pa. O nam ba jege chwoŋa se o yeigi‑o o pa dwi-gɛ tiina. O tu wom ná ke konto, ko bere we o lɔge ba ni-sɛɛm dem kwaga ne mo.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom nam ya ná yeigi‑o se o bu mo di o ma o ke kaane, ko jege se o taa nii kabaa kam baŋa ne nenɛɛne ko ye o tete bukɔ mo.

english_verse: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ná tu o swo kaane wodwoŋi o woli o wone, ko dae se o ve boboa kaane wom o ni-wodiu, naa gwaaro. O nam dae se o ve‑o sare-peiga.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ná ve se o ke wonnu tento maama o pa kaane wom, kaane wom wó wane o viiri zɛɛra, ye o bá ŋwe kolokolo. Keim-lwanno telo na maŋe de toone to

english_verse: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
translation_verse: Kotu nam ná wo paale o go nɔɔno wom, ye ko ye Wɛ mo jaane o ba, nɔɔno wom konto nam jege se o duri mo o vo jei selo amo na wó kuri to, se o seigi da.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Ko daare, nɔɔno ná paale o dwoŋi mo o tiŋi, ye o seene o go‑o, ko dae se o lu kɔtaa! O ná maŋe o vo o ja amo kaanem bimbini dem, se á vaŋe‑o á ja á nwoŋi pwooni á go.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
translation_verse: Wolo ná zi nabiinu o ja se o yeigi, ye kotu ná maŋe o yeigi‑o mo de, naa nɔɔno wom ta ná wo o tei ne ye ba ja‑o, se ba go kotu.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: Wolo maama ná sɔɔle lwarem o yage o kwo naa o nu yuu ne, se ba go kotu de.

english_verse: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
translation_verse: Wolo ba na ke‑o zonne dem to ná wori ye o daare o zaŋe wɛɛne o zi nacheiga o via, ba daa ba jege se ba ke wolo na ke‑o zonne dem to kolokolo. Kotu wó ŋwe nɔɔno wom de o na chɔge o totoŋa to. O ta wó taa nii o baŋa ne mo se o na yazura lanyerane.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná jege kaba-baaro naa kaba-kana, ye o mage‑o pa se o te ko nɛ sem ni ne, se ba waare kotu.

english_verse: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
translation_verse: Kabaa kam nam ná zaŋe ye ka yi da yalei naa yatɔ wɛɛne, ba daa bá ke ka tu wom kolokolo, kabaa kam na ye o nyem to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: Baara balei jara baŋa ne, ba ná mage kapua pa se o puga kam chɔge, wo-gaa ná wo daane kapua kam, o baro wó gwoni jene mo o pa wolo na pɛ o kaane wom puga kam chɔge to, nenɛɛne nakwa bam na sɛ we ko maŋe tei to.

english_verse: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
translation_verse: Ko nam ná tiini ko chamma ko pa kaane wom, waarem dem de wó taa chamma: ŋwea mo ba wó chɔge ba ma ba leiri ŋwea,

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: Wolo ná mage o kabaa kam yi pa se de chɔge, se kotu pa kabaa kam chwoŋa se ka viiri zɛɛra ka yi dem chɔgem ŋwaane.

english_verse: The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
translation_verse: O nam ná mage kabaa kam yeili mo o guri, se o pa ka viiri zɛɛra, ka yeili dem na guri to ŋwaane.

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: Nabea ná chugi nɔɔno ka go, ba jege se ba dole-ka de kandwa ba go mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá done ka nɔna yam. Ka tu wom de nam bá na waarem.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Nabea kam nam ná maŋe ka kare ka chu nɔɔna mo, se ba kaane ka tu wom se o lei-ka. O ná ve ye ka chu nɔɔno ka go, se ba dole nabea kam de ka tu wom maama ba go.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Too wom yera nɔɔna nam ná sɛ, nabea kam tu wom wó wane o kwei sabu o leiri o ŋwea kam se ko maŋe de ba na lage tei to.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Ko nam ta ye bedwe mo de nabea ná chugi nɔɔno wodwoŋi bu-baaro naa o bukɔ de.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno maa ná gwaare gwoŋo naa o koge bɔɔne ye o wo jwoori o seere-ko, pa se o dwoŋi nabea naa o bonaga to ko wone ka te,

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nabea nam ná chugi o dwoŋi nabea ka go, se ba kwei nabea kalo ta na ŋwe to ba yeigi ba daare ba pɔɔre ka sabu kom ba pa daane. Ba ta wó maŋe kalo na tege to nɔna yam mo ba pa daane, se sabu kom de nɔna yam taa mae daane.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Ko daare nabea kam ná maŋe ka kare ka chu mo ye ka tu wo leigi-ka, ka ná go nɔɔno nabea, ka tu wom jege se o ŋwe nabea kam jene maama mo o pa nɔɔno wom. Nabe-teka kam laam wó taa ye o nyem.

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná ŋɔge nabea ye o go-ka naa o kwei-ka o yeigi, ba ná jaane kotu, o wó kwei nabɛ senu mo o jwoori o ŋwe nabea kalo o na ŋɔge to. Ko nam ná ye pia mo o ŋɔga, se o kwei pei sena o ma o ŋwe pia kalo o na ŋɔge to yuu ne.

english_verse: But if you cannot afford to replace the animals, you must be sold as a slave to pay for what you have stolen. If you steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and are caught with it still alive, you must pay the owner double. If you happen to kill a burglar who breaks into your home after dark, you are not guilty. But if you kill someone who breaks in during the day, you are guilty of murder.
translation_verse: Ŋweeno jege se o jwoori o ŋwe kolo o na ŋɔge to mo. O daa ná ware o ŋwe, se ba ja‑o ba yeigi se o taa ye kabaa jene dem ŋwaane. Ko daare, ba ná jaane ŋweeno wom ye o ta jege varem wolo o na ŋɔge to, se o ŋwe-ko kuni belei o pa kotu, nenɛɛne ko ná ye nabea naa bonaga naa pia mo de. Ŋweeno ná bwori nɔɔno sɔŋɔ tete ne ye ba ja‑o ba mage ba go, wolo na go‑o to bá te ko ŋwaane. Se ko ná ye wea ne mo ba jaane ŋweeno wom, wolo na go‑o to maŋe se o de te mo.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná pɛ se o vara vere ba zo nɔɔno wodwoŋi kara naa o kaduga wone ba ja o wodiiru tem ba chɔge, vara bam tu wó kwei o tete wodiiru tem o ma o ŋwe wodwoŋi wom wonnu tem na chɔge to mo, nenɛɛne ko ná ye mena naa tio-bia mo de.

english_verse: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná puli mini kuri pa se de di de vo de to o dwoŋi kara wone de chɔge o mena yalo ba na maŋe ba zage naa yalo ba na wo zage to de, o jege se o ŋwe wolo kara na chɔge to mo.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná kwei o sabu naa o jejegero o pa o dwoŋi se o taa nii-te o diga wone o pa‑o, ye ŋweeno ná tu o ŋɔ sɔŋɔ kom, ba ná jaane ŋweeno wom, o jege se o ŋwe kolo o na ŋɔge to kuni belei mo.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balei ná mage ni-kantɔgɔ woŋo dedoa ŋwaane, ko ná ye nabea, naa bonaga, naa pia, naa gɔrɔ, naa woŋo kolo maama, se ba vo ba jeeri Wɛ wara-jei sem ne. Nakwa bam laam wó bere wolo na gɛ bora to, se konto tu ŋwe o na to kolo baŋa ne to o pa wodwoŋi wom kuni belei.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná kwei o bonaga, naa o nabea, naa o pia, naa o varem dwi delo maama o pa o dwoŋi se o taa nii o pa‑o, ye varem wom ná tega, naa o ná nɛ zonne, naa o ná jei, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ná tera se o na kolo na ke to,

english_verse: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
translation_verse: wolo ba na kwei varem wom ba ke o jeŋa ne to mo wó vo wara-jei sem o pwooli Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne we wonto wo pɛ se varem wom chɔge. Varem wom tu de nam jege se o sɛ konto mo, se o dwoŋi wom yé ŋwe kolokolo.

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Ko daare, nɔɔna ná ŋɔge varem wom wolo na nii-ko to tei ne, wolo na nii-ko to jege se o ŋwe ko jene dem mo.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: Kago-varem nam ná jaane varem wom o tore tore, se wolo na nii varem wom baŋa ne to ja ko yera yam na tore to o ba o bere varem wom tu. Konto mo ye maana se o yé ŋwe kolokolo.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná jene varem o dwoŋi tei ne, ye varem wom ná tega, naa o ná nɛ zonne, varem wom tu ná tera se o na, wolo na jene varem wom to mo wó jwoori o ŋwe varem wom tu.

english_verse: But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it. Laws for Everyday Life The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ko daare varem wom tu ná nɛ kolo na ke to, nɔɔno wolo na jene varem wom to daa bá ŋwe kolokolo. Kokuri to, o na jene varem wom to, o jene dem ti. Kɔgɔ wo zoorem

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: Bukɔ ná yeiri baaro ye nɔɔno ná gane‑o o lage, kotu nam wó yɔɔre o ke bukɔ wom kadiri mo se o daare o taa tei‑o.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
translation_verse: Kaane ná ye yi-naro, á jege se á go‑o mo.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
translation_verse: Wolo ná peini de varem, se á go‑o.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
translation_verse: Wolo ná zuli wɛ-gaa ye ko dae Baŋa Wɛ yerane, se á yɔɔre á chɔge kotu.

english_verse: Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
translation_verse: Yé daane-na veira, á nam yé bɛɛse-ba. Guli-na we abam de déem ye veira mo Ejipti tega baŋa ne.

english_verse: Do not mistreat widows or orphans.
translation_verse: Yé pa-na se ko zo kadeim yera, naa botaro yera.

english_verse: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
translation_verse: Abam ná yaare-ba pa se ba keeri ba jare-ne, amo wó cheigi ba keira kam.

english_verse: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
translation_verse: A bane maa wó zaŋe abam baŋa ne, ye a daare a go abam de se-zɔɔ mo. Konto maa wó pa se á kaana bam ji kadeina, ye á bia bam de ji botara.

english_verse: Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need.
translation_verse: Amo nɔɔna bam wone, nmo ná jene sabu n pa wolo na ye nabwom to, se n yé ke sabu-leinna kikia de kotu. Yé pa se o ŋwe sabu-daŋɔ o pa‑m.

english_verse: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ná kwei o gɔrɔ o ma tiŋi daare n tei ne, se n yeini n kwei-ko n pa‑o dɛ maama dedaan-ni maŋa ne.

english_verse: because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
translation_verse: O ná lage o peini tete ne, gɔrɔ kom konto yerane mo o yeini o jega se o taa mae o kwoli o tete. O nam ná keeri o jare-ne, amo wó cheigi o keira kam. Kokuri to, amo tiini a duri nɔɔna yibwona mo.

english_verse: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
translation_verse: Yé ŋɔɔne Wɛ n ja n chɔge. Nam yé sɔɔle lwarem n yage wolo na ye nakwe tu to yuu ne.

english_verse: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
translation_verse: Kolo na maŋe se n pɔɔre n wodiiru tem wone n pa amo to, ko ná ye mena, naa wo-nyɔɔro tem, se n yé ve se n ke konto. Nam kwei-na á bakeiri-kwe sem á pa amo.

english_verse: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
translation_verse: Ko ta woli da, wo-kwe selo na nwoŋi á naane dem wone, de á pei sem wone to ye se á pa-ne mo. Vare-kwe selo na ye wo-bɛ to wó maŋe se niina tei ne mo da yarepɛ. Da nana kam dɛ ne, á maa wó pɔɔre-se á pa-ne.

english_verse: You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
translation_verse: Abam maŋe se á ji nɔɔna balo na pwɛ ba tete ba pa amo to mo. Mo kokuri, á ba jege se á di nɔna yalo ga-vara na jaane ba tore tore to. Kwei-na nɔna yam konto á pa kukuri.

english_verse: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
translation_verse: Yé tɔge kɔgɔ kom se n sɛ keim-lwanno totoŋa. Taane ná wora ye n jege maana, se n yé kweele chega kam, nɔɔna dedɛ ná maŋe ba fɔ vwa tei maama de.

english_verse: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
translation_verse: Yé pa nɔɔno di bora o na ye yiniga tu to ŋwaane.

english_verse: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
translation_verse: Nmo ná beeri n yi n dono nabea, naa o bonaga, se n ja-ka n jwoori n vo n pa ka tu.

english_verse: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
translation_verse: Nmo ná nɛ we n dono bonaga zela dum pane-ka tega ne, yé gaale n kɛ. Woli-ka se ka zaŋe wɛɛne.

english_verse: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
translation_verse: Yiniga tu ná jege taane, se n yé kweele o chega kam.

english_verse: Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like. Laws for the Sabbath The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ko dae se á yaare veira, kolo ŋwaane abam de déem ye veira mo Ejipti teo ne, ye á yei ŋwea kam konto na ye tei to. Ka-toŋe-ka-daare chullu Chullu

english_verse: Plant and harvest your crops for six years,
translation_verse: Kwei-na bena yaredo maama á du wodiiru á kare ne se á ta‑á zage-te.

english_verse: but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
translation_verse: Bene delo maama na wó ke yarepɛ to, se á yage á kare se se taa tigi da kafɛ. Bene dem konto ne, yiniga tiina balo na zoore á tetare ne to laam wó zo se wo ba lare wodiiru tem ba di. Ba ma ná daare kolo, se á yage-na se kago-vara de zo ba di. Ta ke-na konto dwoŋi de kare selo á na jeiri Vini teeni de Olivi teeni se wone to de.

english_verse: Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
translation_verse: Abam jege da yaredo mo se á ma á toŋe. Da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, yé toŋe-na kɔtaa! Konto wó pa á na siu, de á nabɛ, de á bonɛ, de á kabɛ, dedaane veira balo na zoore á tetare ne to. Konto wó taa pae á jege dam.

english_verse: Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names. Three Annual Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Yɔɔre á ta‑á ke á tɔge a na bere abam tei maama to. Yé zuli-na wɛ dedwoŋi, ye ko dae amo. Yé bwoŋi-na wɛ dedwoŋi naa jwoni dedwoŋi yere. Bene maama wo kura yatɔ

english_verse: Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
translation_verse: Abam ná lage á go varem se á ma o jana bam á ke kaanem á pa amo, se á yé woli bworobworo kolo na jege sabɔle ko wone to. Nam lɔre-na se á zwɛ varem wom lara kam maama dɛ dem konto ne.

english_verse: Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
translation_verse: Abam kaana bam de wone, ba wolowolo bá ja puga se ka chɔge. Kadega maa bá taa wora. Á maama ŋwea maa wó tiini ka dáane lanyerane.

english_verse: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
translation_verse: Mena zagem maŋa nam ná yia, se á di Ga-kwea kuri dem. Kwei-na mena yalo á na dɛ yiga á zage to, á ba á pa-ne. Ko woli da, abam ná yeini á toŋe á kare totoŋa maama á ti, se á laam di Faao kuri dem.

english_verse: Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
translation_verse: Kuni betɔ bene maama wone á baara bam jege se ba jeeri amo wolo na ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom to yiga ne mo konto dwoŋi.

english_verse: Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
translation_verse: Bene maama Abibi chana kam da yadwonna wone, se á di Bworobworo-memene kuri dem. Kwei-na da yarepɛ á di bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to. Kanto chana kam ne mo á déem nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne. Á na yeini á zuli amo konto to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé ba amo yiga ne ye o ba zei kaanem pɛɛre.

english_verse: Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. A Promise and a Warning The Lord said:
translation_verse: Bene maama wone se á ja á kare wodiiru telo na lwoori yiga te ke ye te lamma to á ja á jeeri abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé kwei bebala de ka nu nayela o saŋe mini wone. Baŋa Wɛ bera

english_verse: I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you.
translation_verse: Nii-na! Amo lage a toŋe amo maleka mo se ka che abam ka ja ka yi jei selo amo na kwɛ se a pa abam to.

english_verse: Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion.
translation_verse: Ta‑á nege-na maleka kam se á daare á sɛ ka taane dem maama. Amo pɛ-ka dam se ka taa toŋe amo totoŋa. Abam wolo ná ve-ka, ka bá yage ka ma chɛ kotu.

english_verse: Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong.
translation_verse: Ta‑á zuli-na amo na ye á Teiru Baŋa Wɛ to yerane. Abam ná ke konto, amo wó ke zaane a yage á wodiu dedaane á na baŋa ne. Amo wó taa cho se jaweero yé ja abam.

english_verse: But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere.
translation_verse: A nam bá zeili ba maama abam yiga ne bene dedoa wone. Amo ná ke konto, tega kam wó ji kagoa yerane mo. Ko wó pa kago-vara tiini ba gaale se ba daane abam.

english_verse: Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
translation_verse: A lage a taa zeili-ba fenfee mo se ba nwoŋi abam yiga ne, se ko yi maŋa kalo abam na wó puli á su logo kom maama to.

english_verse: I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land.
translation_verse: Abam tega kam laŋa wó zege Nane-soŋo kom ni ne mo se ka taa vei Mediterania naneo kom seeni. Ka ta maa wó zege kagoa kam seeni ka vo ka yi Yuferata buga kam ne. Ko ná ye balo na zoore jei sem konto ne leile to, amo wó ke-ba abam dam kuri ne. Abam maa wó zeili-ba se ba nwoŋi á yiga ne.

english_verse: But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods.
translation_verse: Yé ke-na ni-sɛɛm de-ba. Nam yé sɛ-na ba jwona yam.

english_verse: Don't let them stay in your land. They will trap you into sinning against me and worshiping their gods.
translation_verse: Bere á yé sɛ se banto taa zoore abam tega kam baŋa ne. Kolo ŋwaane, ba wó soge abam mo se á tusi amo yiga ne, ye ba ja abam se á zuli ba jwona yam.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we: “Diini peo kom yuu se n ba amo tei. Nam ja Aron, de Nadab, de Abihu dedaane Isarele nakwa fuserepɛ n woli da. Abam ta ná wo yiga yiga, se á tiiri á zuli-ne.

english_verse: Moses gave the Lord's instructions to the people, and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded!”
translation_verse: Moses déem ma tu o maŋe Baŋa Wɛ nia yam de o chullu tem maama o bere nɔɔna bam. Ba maama ma leiri de kwora dedoa ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ na we debam ke kolo maama to, dé wó ke.”

english_verse: Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said. The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Moses ma popone Baŋa Wɛ taane dem maama o tiŋi. Tega na poore to, o ma lɔ kaanem bimbini peo kom teiŋa ne. O déem ta ma kwei kandwa fuga-yalei o chwi, se kandwɛ maama taa zege de pae Isarele dwia fuga-yalei yam.

english_verse: He also sent some young men to burn offerings and to sacrifice bulls as special offerings to the Lord.
translation_verse: O ma toŋe Isarele tiina nɔn-donno tedwonna mo se ba kwei vara ba ma ke kaanem ba zwɛ ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ba ma daare ba kwei nabɛ-pɔle ba ma ke yazura kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar.
translation_verse: Moses déem ma pwori vara bam jana o ke zwe wone. O laam ma kwei jana balo na daare to o miisi o yage kaanem bimbini dem yera ne.

english_verse: Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
translation_verse: O ma daare o kwei Wɛ Ni-gwonim tɔnɔ kom o ga o bere nɔɔna bam. Ba maama daa maa leiri ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ na we debam ke kolo maama to, dé wó ke. Dé wó sɛ o ni dem.”

english_verse: Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
translation_verse: Moses laam ma kwei jana balo na wo zwe sem wone to, o miisi-ba o yage nɔɔna bam yera ne ye o we, “Jana banto mo bere we, ni-gwonim delo Baŋa Wɛ na ke de abam bera yanto baŋa ne to jege bu.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron, together with Nadab and Abihu and the
translation_verse: Moses ma ja Aron, de Nadab de Abihu dedaane Isarele nakwa fuserepɛ ye ba di peo kom yuu.

english_verse: and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something that looked like a pavement made out of sapphire, and it was as bright as the sky.
translation_verse: Dáane mo ba déem nɛ Isarele tiina Wɛ wom. O nɛ sem kuri ne ko nye de pwola mo tiini ka peere ne Safira to, ka ta ye napwon-pwoŋo mo nenɛɛne wɛyuu kom.

english_verse: Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank. Moses on Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Isarele yiga tiina bam déem nɛ Baŋa Wɛ konto, ye o wo chɔge-ba. Ba ma di ye ba daare ba nyɔ dáane.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up on the mountain and stay here for a while. I will give you the two flat stones on which I have written the laws that my people must obey.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Diini n ba amo tei peo kom yuu ne. Nmo wó maŋe ywo-seeni mo se a kwei kandwa-pelɛ selo baŋa ne a na popone a bera yam de a nia yam se a nɔɔna bam taa tɔge to a pa‑m.”

english_verse: Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
translation_verse: Moses ma zaŋe dedaane o zeinnu Josua se ba ti ba yiga ba nwoŋi. Moses laam ma di peo kom yuu se o jeeri Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Moses had told the leaders, “Wait here until we come back. Aaron and Hur will be with you, and they can settle any arguments while we are away.”
translation_verse: O nam ya wuuri o ta de nakwa bam mo o we, “Abam maŋe-na ywo-seeni á ta‑á cheigi debam se dé jwoori dé ba. Aron de Hura wó maŋe á tei ne se wolo maama ná jege ni-kantɔgɔ de o dwoŋi, se ba kwɛ-ko ba pa abam.”

english_verse: When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it,
translation_verse: Moses déem na diini Sinayi peo kom yuu to, kunkwoŋo ma kwoli-ko.

english_verse: blue, purple, and red wool; fine linen; goat hair;
translation_verse: de gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to, de gare-fefale, dedaane boŋo koro,

english_verse: Here is a list of what you are to collect: Gold, silver, and bronze;
translation_verse: Nam jwoŋi pɛɛra yanto dwi ba tei ne: Sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de channa,

english_verse: tanned ram skins; fine leather; acacia wood;
translation_verse: de pi-bea twanno telo ba na seini to, de twan-nyenno, de golesaa dɛ,

english_verse: olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices to mix with the incense and with the oil for dedicating the tent and ordaining the priests;
translation_verse: de min-zwonnu nuga, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa kalo ba na wó ma ba ke Wɛ swolim nuga kam to, de kalo ba na wó zwɛ wara-vwei dem totoŋa ŋwaane to,

english_verse: I also want them to build a special place where I can live among my people.
translation_verse: Amo lage se a nɔɔna bam chwi wara-diga mo ba pa-ne, se a taa zoore ba tetare ne.

english_verse: The lamp on the top and those at the end of each of its six branches must be made so as to shine toward the front of the lampstand.
translation_verse: Nam pa se ba ke min-zwonnu terepɛ se te taa zege nɛ seredo sem yuni ne de daa kam yuu ne. Kwei-na-te á zege se te taa di te pae pwooni min-zwon-zego kom yiga seeni.

english_verse: Cover it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the lid.
translation_verse: Pa ba kwei sabu-seŋa na tiini ka ye chekke to ba ma kwoli ka yiga de ka kwaga maama, se sabu-seŋa tɔge ka nia yam maama.

english_verse: Make two poles of acacia wood. Cover them with gold
translation_verse: Ba ta wó gwoni golesaa dɛ selei ba daare ba kwei sabu-seŋa ba kwoli dɛ sem konto maama.

english_verse: and put them through the rings, so the chest can be carried by the poles.
translation_verse: Laam pa se ba kwei dɛ sem ba tore dakaa kam kwana yam wone, se ba daare ba ja dɛ sem ba ma zeŋe dakaa kam.

english_verse: Inside it place the two flat stones with the Ten Commandments on them and put the gold lid on top of the chest.
translation_verse: Laam kwei-na amo ni-gwonim kandwa yalei yam á ke dakaa kam wone, se á daare á kwei ni-pugu kom á pu ka ni.

english_verse: I will meet you there between the two creatures and tell you what my people must do and what they must not do. The Table for the Sacred Bread (Exodus
translation_verse: Amo wó taa tui ni-gwonim dakaa kam baŋa seeni a jeeri‑m cherubi selei sem tetare laŋa ne. Dáane mo amo wó bere‑m a nia yam maama se Isarele tiina bam taa tɔge-ya. Tabolo Kom

english_verse: Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border
translation_verse: Sabu-seŋa kam na wó tɔge tabolo kom nia yam to wó taa ye da-yiga noa maŋem mo.

english_verse: Make four gold rings and attach one to each of the legs
translation_verse: Nam mɔ-na sabu-seŋa kwana yana á meeli tabolo kom nɛ sena sem na wo mɛ to.

english_verse: near the edging. The poles for carrying the table are to be placed through these rings and are to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Ko nam wó taa ye golesaa dɛ mo nmo wó kwoli de sabu-seŋa, se ba taa maa zeŋe-ko.

english_verse: The table is to be kept in the holy place, and the sacred loaves of bread must always be on it. All bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings are to be made of pure gold and set on this table. The Lampstand (Exodus
translation_verse: Tabolo kom wó taa wo amo wara-jei di-yuu kom ne mo maŋa maama, ye bworobworo kolo na ye ko yera ko tigi amo yiga ne to taa wo ko baŋa ne. Min-zwon-zego kom

english_verse: The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold.
translation_verse: Pun-kogela yam, de nɛ seredo sem, de daa kam tete maama ye se ba mage sabu-seŋa kandwɛ-dale dedwe mo ba ma ke-te.

english_verse: and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
translation_verse: Nam pa se ba ke woŋo maama se ko maŋe de tetei amo na bere‑m peo kom yuu ne to.”

english_verse: The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.
translation_verse: “Nam pa se ba kwei gare-jale-laaro fuga na nwoŋi gare-fefale delo na ye chekke to ba ma ke wara-vwei dem. Kwei-na gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to á ma‑á sɔ-ya. Á maa wó daare á gɔgere cherubi nyenyero á ke gare-jala yam yera ne.

english_verse: and sew them together into two panels with five sections each.
translation_verse: Laam twoŋi-na gare-jala yanu á ke daane, se ya ji gare-pum dedoa. Ta ke-na konto de gare-jala yanu yadwonna yam.

english_verse: The panel of goat hair will be a meter longer than the tent itself, so fold
translation_verse: Boŋo koro gare-jale dem maa wó li wara-vwei dem dedɔrem seeni se ko dwoni gare-jale dedwoŋi dem se ko maŋe de jatwogo de noa ni maŋem bedwe mo.

english_verse: Sew five of the sections together to make one panel. Then sew the other six together to make a second panel, and fold the sixth section double over the front of the tent.
translation_verse: Laam kwei-na gare-jala yanu á twoŋi daane se ya ji gare-pum. Á ta wó kwei gare-jala yaredo yam na daare to mo á twoŋi daane se ya de ji gare-pum. Abam maa wó piri gare-jala yaredo tu wom belei á jeeri wɛɛne se ko maŋe de wara-vwei dem ni seeni.

english_verse: Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Daa‑n ta pa se ba pwoni pi-bɛ tankwallo ba daare ba seini-te nasoŋo se ba maa kwoli wara-vwei dem. Kwei-na twan-nyenno á daŋe boboa twanno tem baŋa ne.

english_verse: Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid.
translation_verse: Nam ta kwei-na wɛleera saarem ni-pugu kom á ma pu ni-gwonim dakaa kam na zege Wɛ di-yun-gala kam ne to.

english_verse: Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Pa se ba beeri golesaa ywoa yalo na zege cheppe to, se ba kwei-se ba ke wara-vwei dem.

english_verse: Place two silver stands under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so the frames can be joined together. Put
translation_verse: Lu-nyenno wonnu finna mo á wó ke se ywoa yam taa zege te baŋa ne. Wonnu telei maa wó taa wora ywei maama ŋwaane.

english_verse: For the back wall along the west side use six frames
translation_verse: Ko ná ye saŋa kalo na wo bira-kwaga ne ye ka jeeri wɛ-zoore seeni to, se á chwi ywoa yaredo dáane.

english_verse: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom.
translation_verse: Abam maa wó twoŋi gugworru ywoa yam konto se ya meeli daane. Ko wó zege tega kam ne mo ko meeli se ko taa diini baŋa kam mɛ sabu-seŋa kwane dem na leigi da to.

english_verse: Altogether, this back wall will have eight frames with two silver stands under each one.
translation_verse: Bira-kwaga kam seeni ywoa yam laam maa wó taa ye nana mo, ye ya laam jege lu-nyenno wonnu fuga-teredo telo na wó teili-ya to.

english_verse: Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold and attach gold rings to the frames to run the crossbars through.
translation_verse: Laam kwei-na sabu-seŋa á kwoli ywoa yam, se á daare á ma á ke kwana á meeli ywoa yam yera ne se dagare sem taa tore ya wone. Dagare sem de ye se á taare-se de sabu-seŋa mo.

english_verse: Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain. The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Laam pa se ba chwi wara-vwei dem se de zege ne amo na bere‑m tetei peo kom yuu ne to. Wɛ di-yun-gala gare-jale dem

english_verse: Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
translation_verse: Yiga diga kam na ye Wɛ di-yuu kom to mo á wó zege tabolo kom se ko taa wo vwei dem jagwia saŋa kam seeni. Min-zwon-zego kom maa wó taa wo vwei dem jazem saŋa kam seeni.

english_verse: Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_verse: Abam ná sɔge gare-jale dem konto, á laam wó kwei golesaa dɛ senu á taare-se de sabu-seŋa ye á daare á ke sabu-seŋa gwoli á meeli se yera ne. Laam mɔ-na channa wonnu tenu se á chwi dɛ sem te baŋa ne, ye á daare á lei gare-jale dem da.”

english_verse: Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Abam nam wó tore dɛ sem konto mo kwana yana yam na wo dakaa kam sɛ sem ne to, se á ta‑á wae-ka á zeŋa.

english_verse: All the equipment for the altar must also be made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans.
translation_verse: Nam ta kwei-na channa á ke kaanem dakaa kam yera totoŋa zela maama. Mɔ-na zwe selo ba na wó taa mae ba pɛ tentwarem to, de sɛbullu, de na-zwe, de mini zon-tanlɛ, dedaane wonnu telo na wó taa mae te chu nɔna to.

english_verse: Halfway up the altar build a ledge around it, and cover the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. Then attach a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners of the altar.
translation_verse: Maŋe-na dakaa kam tetare ne á ke wo-daŋɔ á meeli ka yera ne. Ta kwei-na channa luuru á sɔ á lɛɛne daane se á kwei-ko á de wo-daŋɔ kom baŋa ne. Laam ke-na channa kwana yana á meeli-ya dakaa kam sɛ sem ne se ya maŋe de channa lɛɛna yam.

english_verse: Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain. The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Á wó twoŋi dɛ sem daane mo á ma á ke dakaa kam se ka taa ye wo-wogo. Nam pa se ko maŋe de amo na bere‑m tei peo kom yuu ne to.” Konkɔlɔ kolo na kaare wara-vwei dem to

english_verse: Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning
translation_verse: “Nam ta de Isarele tiina bam se ba ja Olivi nuga kalo na ye chekke to ba ba ba pa‑m min-zwonnu tem ŋwaane. Konto mo wó pa se te mini taa di taa, ye de ba dwia.

english_verse: Surround the sacred tent with a courtyard
translation_verse: Ni dem jagwia seeni de wó taa ye konto mo.

english_verse: for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain
translation_verse: Daa á ta kwei-na gwaaro tem á daŋe dɛ finlei baŋa ne. Dɛ sem nam wó taa zege channa luuru finlei baŋa ne mo. Á ta maa wó kwei lu-nyenno á mɔ gwoli á meeli dɛ sem yera ne de te lu-vɔɔro tem.

english_verse: Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard. The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place (Leviticus
translation_verse: Á ta wó kwei channa mo á ma á ke zela yalo maama na maŋe de wara-vwei dem totoŋa to. Paara yalo á na wó ke se ya taa jaane vwei dem de konkɔlɔ kom gare-jala yam to de wó taa ye channa mo á wó ma á ke-ya.” Min-zwonnu tem nuga

english_verse: in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye min-zwon-zego kom, se á zege-ko Wɛ wara-vwei di-yuu kom ne mɛ gare-jale dem na kwoli ni-gwonim dakaa kam to mo. Aron de o bia bam nam wó nii mo se min-zwonnu tem taa di Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne taa, se te yé dwei wɛ-zoore maŋa ne se ko yi te-pora dɛ maama wone. Isarele tiina bam de ba dwi dem nam wó taa tɔge ni dento mo taa wuu.”

english_verse: Send for your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They are the ones I have chosen from Israel to serve as my priests.
translation_verse: “Pa se n zembaaro Aron de o bia, Nadab, de Abihu, de Eleaza, de Itamara ba nmo tei se n pɔɔre-ba se ba taa ye ba yera de nɔɔna bam maama. Banto mo wó taa ye amo kaanem tiina se ba taa toŋe ba pa-ne.

english_verse: Aaron is to be dedicated as my high priest, and his clothes must be made only by persons who possess skills that I have given them.
translation_verse: Abam na wó pɔɔre Aron se o taa ye amo kaanem tu to ŋwaane, nam kuri-na gwaro se amo pa-ba swa se ba sɔ o gwaaro tem.

english_verse: Here are the items that need to be made: a breastpiece, a priestly vest, a robe, an embroidered shirt, a turban, and a sash. These sacred clothes are to be made for your brother Aaron and his sons who will be my priests.
translation_verse: Nam pa se ba sɔ zula gwaaro tento dwi: Nyɔɔne gare-pale, de gare-wogo, de gare-bwora, de gare-dedɔrɔ kolo ba na mɛ nyenyero dedɛ ba ma gɔgere-ko to, de teiŋa vovoa, dedaane yuu gare-yi. Ba maa wó ke gwaaro tento dwoŋi, se ba pa n zembaaro Aron de o bia bam se ba yeini ba zo-te ba taa toŋe kaanem totoŋa ba pa-ne.

english_verse: Use only gold and fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool, for making these clothes. The Vest for the High Priest (Exodus
translation_verse: Pa se gwaro tem kwei gare-fefale selo na ye chekke to, ye ba laam woli de gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye sabu-seŋa, de nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to ba ma sɔ-te. Gare-wogo kom

english_verse: Put two onyx stones in gold settings, then attach one to each of the shoulder straps. On one of these stones engrave the names of Israel's first six sons in the order of their birth. And do the same with his remaining six sons on the other stone. In this way Aaron will always carry the names of the tribes of Israel when he enters the holy place, and I will never forget my people.
translation_verse: Laam meeli-na kandwa yalei yam á lei gare-wogo kom vɔna vovwe sem yera ne. Ya ye kandwa-gula mo se ya guli Isarele tiina bam ba dwia yam yera. Aron ná yeini o tui amo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, o wó taa yeini o zeŋe ba yera yam konto mo, se o yé swei ba swia maŋa de maŋa.

english_verse: Attach two gold settings to the shoulder straps and fasten them with two braided chains of pure gold. The Breastpiece for the High Priest (Exodus
translation_verse: Nam ta kwei-na sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to á ke chaponno telei nenɛɛne ŋone dwoŋi to. Vɔ-na chaponno tem kuna yalei yam yera ne se te ja gare-wogo kom yiga de kwaga. Nyɔɔne gare-pale dem

english_verse: and engrave on each of them the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Nam ta sare-na Isarele dwi maama yera fuga-yalei yam kandwa yam baŋa ne. Kandwɛ maama wó bere yere dedwe se de taa ye maana.

english_verse: with four rows of three precious stones: In the first row put a carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald;
translation_verse: Abam laam wó tigisi kandwa-nyenno dwi dwi se ya peini gene sena de kandwa-nyenno tetɔ. Boboa gena kam kandwa-nyenno tem wó taa ye Rubi, de Topazi, dedaane Berili.

english_verse: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
translation_verse: Gena belei tu kandwa-nyenno tem maa wó taa ye Tukwazi, de Safira, dedaane Emeraleda.

english_verse: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
translation_verse: Gena betɔ tu wom maa wó taa jege kandwa-nyenno tento: Jakinfa, de Agate, dedaane Ametisita.

english_verse: and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount the stones in delicate gold settings
translation_verse: Se gena bena tu wom kandwa-nyenno tem taa ye Berili, de Onika dedaane Jasipa. Abam maa wó kwei sabu-seŋa á tɔge kandwa yam konto maama nia yam.

english_verse: Attach two gold rings to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fasten them with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps.
translation_verse: se á ta ja chaponno tem nia yadwonna yam á vo á kuni dedaane kuna yalei yam se te ja gare-wogo kom vɔna vovwe sem.

english_verse: Then take a blue cord and tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. This will keep the breastpiece in place.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne, se á kwei gare-ŋona kalo nyenyego na ye nazwon-pupwia to á ma‑á vɔ kwana yalei yam na wo gare-pale dem kuri ne to, de yalo na wo gare-wogo kom vɔna yam seeni to á ke daane. Konto wó pa se gare-pale dem yé taa bibiga.

english_verse: with an opening in the center for his head. Be sure to bind the material around the collar to keep it from wearing out.
translation_verse: Nam bɔɔre-na ko tetare dem, se nɔɔno yuu wane ko tɔge da ko zo. Bɛɛre-na ba dem seeni maama se ko yé kaare.

english_verse: If Aaron wears these clothes when he enters the holy place as my high priest, the sound of the bells will be heard, and his life will not be in danger.
translation_verse: Aron ná yeini o lage o toŋe kaanem totoŋa, se o zo gare-bwora kam konto. O ná lage o zo amo di-yuu kom naa o ná nwoŋi da, lwoŋina yam sɔɔ kwori wó taa ni, se o yé te.

english_verse: On a narrow strip of pure gold engrave the words: “Dedicated to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Nam kwei-na sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to á ke wo-pelɔgɔ. Laam sare-na ko baŋa ne we, ‘Wose mo Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane’.

english_verse: Fasten it to the front of Aaron's turban with a blue cord,
translation_verse: Á ta wó kwei gare-ŋona kalo nyenyego na ye nazwon-pupwia to á ma‑á meeli wo-pelɔgɔ kom o yuu gare-yi dem yiga seeni.

english_verse: so he can wear it on his forehead. This will show that he will take on himself the guilt for any sins the people of Israel commit in offering their gifts to me, and I will forgive them.
translation_verse: Ko wó maŋe Aron tiri ne mo maŋa maama. Isarele tiina bam ná yeini ba ja pɛɛra ba jeeri se ba pa-ne, ye tusim ná wora ba totoŋa yam ne, amo wó da Aron ŋwaane a yage a ma chɛ-ba, pa se a sɛ a jwoŋi ba pɛɛra yam konto.

english_verse: Since Aaron's sons are priests, they should also look dignified. So make robes, sashes, and special caps for them.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye Aron bia bam, sɔ-na nenɔŋa gwaaro, de yipwi, dedaane teiŋa vovwe á pa-ba. Konto mo wó zuli ba kaanem totoŋe dem.

english_verse: Then dress Aaron and his sons in these clothes, pour olive oil on their heads, and ordain them as my priests.
translation_verse: Pa se Aron de o bia bam zo ba gwaaro tem, se n daare n kwei swolim nuga n lwo ba yuni ne amo ŋwaane n ma n pwɛ-ba se ba taa ye a kaanem tiina.

english_verse: Make linen shorts for them that reach from the waist down to the thigh, so they won't expose themselves.
translation_verse: Ta kwei-na gare-fefale á sɔ gare-kuri-kukwi á pa-ba se ba yeini ba zo. Se maa wó zege ba teiŋa ne se yi ba chwoa mo. Konto wó pa se ba yé taa ye bwori.

english_verse: Whenever they enter the sacred tent or serve at the altar or enter the holy place, they must wear these shorts, or else they will be guilty and die. This same rule applies to any of their descendants who serve as priests.
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo maama Aron de o bia bam ná yeini ba zo amo wara-jei sem, naa ba ná lage ba yi amo kaanem dakaa kam ba toŋe ba pa-ne, ba jege se ba zo gare-kuri-kukwi sem konto mo. Ko ná dae konto, ba wó na ba chaveera ye ba te ko ŋwaane. Aron de o dwi dem maama jege se ba taa tɔge a ni dem konto mo se ko taa vei wuu.”

english_verse: Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy.
translation_verse: Dɛ maama wone se n go nabea n ma n kaane n pa-ne wɛleera saarem ŋwaane. Ko ta wó pa se kaanem dakaa kam fɔge ka kwɛ. Nmo nam ta wó kwei swolim nuga mo n ma n turi dakaa kam yera ne se ko pa se ka taa ye wose.

english_verse: Then from your finest flour make three batches of dough without yeast. Shape some of it into larger loaves, some into smaller loaves mixed with olive oil, and the rest into thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: Nam ta lage-na mun-bwei se á ma á ke bworobworo kolo sabɔle na wo woli ko wone to. Pwori-na muni dem se á viiri dedwoŋi de nuga á bibili á ma á ke bworobworo kamuna, se á daare á fɔge bworobworo balwa de. Muni delo na daare to se á bibili-de memene ye á laam ma nuga á taare-te.

english_verse: Put all of this bread in a basket and bring it when you come to sacrifice the three animals to me.
translation_verse: Nmo laam ma‑n wó kwei te maama n ke tetɔgɔ wone, n ja-te n woli de nabea kam, de pi-bɛ sem n jeeri amo tei ne.

english_verse: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and tell them to wash themselves.
translation_verse: Pa se Aron de o bia bam maama ba ba zege wara-vwei dem ni ne, ye n pa ba swɛ ba yera ba kwɛ ba tete amo ŋwaane.

english_verse: Dress Aaron in the priestly shirt, the robe that goes under the sacred vest, the vest itself, the breastpiece, and the sash.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne se n pa Aron zo kaanem tiina gwaaro tem: gare-dedɔrɔ kom, de gare-bwora kam, de gare-wogo kom, dedaane nyɔɔne gare-pale dem. Ta kwei vovoa kam n vɔ o teiŋa ne.

english_verse: and then ordain him by pouring olive oil on his head.
translation_verse: Lwo Wɛ swolim nuga o yuu ne se n ma n tiŋi‑o o totoŋa ŋwaane n pa amo.

english_verse: Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Ja nabea kam n vo n zege wara-jei sem manchwo-peena ne. Pa se Aron de o bia bam kwei ba je ba daŋe ka yuu ne.

english_verse: Kill the bull near my altar in front of the tent.
translation_verse: Laam go nabea kam wara-jei sem manchwo-peena ni dem ne se ko taa bwola de amo kaanem dakaa kam.

english_verse: Use a finger to smear some of its blood on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest of the blood on the ground next to the altar.
translation_verse: Le n noa n laŋe jana bam badwonna n taare dakaa kam nyea yam ne. Jana balo na daare to, se n lwo-ba n yage tega ne, dakaa kam teiŋa ne.

english_verse: But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye nabea kam nɔna yam, de ka tankɔlɔ kom, de ka puga wodiu kom maama, ja-na-te á nwoŋi dáa dáa á zwɛ-te. Ko ye wɛleera saarem kaanem mo ko pa-ba.

english_verse: Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Daa‑n ja pi-bea dedoa n nwoŋi, se Aron de o bia bam kwei ba je ba daŋe ka yuu ne,

english_verse: Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: se n laam go-ka n daare n kwei ka jana bam n zezage kaanem dakaa kam sɛ sena sem maama ne.

english_verse: Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head.
translation_verse: Nam gwoni pia kam nɔna yam yera yera, se n daare n zare ka wo-zela yam de ka nɛ sem. Laam kwei wonnu tem konto maama de ka yuu kom n daŋe dakaa kam baŋa ne.

english_verse: Then make sure that the whole animal goes up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Nmo ma‑n wó zwɛ te maama se te taa ye zwɛɛm kaanem te pa-ne. Te nyoa kam lwom wó taa ywona de pa amo, ye de pwoli amo wo.

english_verse: Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Nam ja pi-bea kadwoŋi kam n nwoŋi, se Aron de o bia bam laam kwei ba je ba daŋe ka yuu ne.

english_verse: Kill the ram and place some of its blood on Aaron's right ear lobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot. Do the same for each of his sons and splatter the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne se n go-ka. Laam ke ka jana bam n taŋe Aron de o bia bam jazem zwa ne, de ba jazem no-kweero tem, dedaane ba jazem namimbi-kweero tem maama. Jana balo na daare to, se n zezage-ba dakaa kam sɛ sena sem ne.

english_verse: Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Kwei jana balo na wo dakaa kam baŋa ne to badwonna, de Wɛ swolim nuga kam, n viiri-te daane n laam ma n zezage Aron yera ne, se n ta zezage-te o gwaaro tem ne. Ta zezage-te n ke o bia bam yera ne, se n daare n zezage-te ba gwaaro tem ne. Keim dento wó pa se Aron de o bia bam de ba gwaaro tem maama mo pwɛ ba yera amo ŋwaane.

english_verse: This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: Pi-bea kam konto tɔge ka toŋe pwɛɛm totoŋe dem mo. Konto ŋwaane, le ka jazem chwei dem, de ka nabili-bwogo kom mɛ na jege lara to, de ka wo-zela yam lara kam, de chwɛ dem kuri seeni, dedaane tapwale-bia yalei yam, de ya lara kam maama.

english_verse: and put this bread, together with the meat, into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then they will lift it all up to show that it is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: se n kwei-te n pa Aron de o bia bam, ko woli de pi-bea kam nɔna yam. Banto wó zeiŋi-te wɛɛne ba yaare-te amo yiga ne se ko bere we ba kwei-te ba pa amo mo.

english_verse: After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne, se n jwoŋi nɔna yam de bworobworo kom maama n daŋe zwɛɛm kaanem dem baŋa ne se n zwɛ-te kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne. Te nyoa kam lwom wó taa ywona de pa amo, ye de pwoli amo wo.

english_verse: You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye pwɛɛm totoŋe pi-bea kam, kwei ka nyɔɔne seeni nɔna yam, se n zeiŋi-ya wɛɛne n yaare amo yiga ne, se n laam daare n wane-ya n di.

english_verse: After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
translation_verse: Wolo na wó leiri Aron yuu ne to, ye se ba kwei da yarepɛ mo ba pwɛ‑o ba zege o totoŋe dem ŋwaane. O wó zo gwaaro tem mo da yarepɛ yam maama wone ye o zo amo di-yuu kom wone o toŋe o pa-ne.

english_verse: Boil the meat of the ordination ram in a sacred place,
translation_verse: Kwei pwɛɛm totoŋe pi-bea kam nɔna yam n vo wara-jei selo na ye se yera to ne, n saŋe-ya.

english_verse: then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Aron de o bia bam yerane mo wó kwei nɔna yam konto de bworobworo kolo na wo tetɔgɔ kom wone to ba di wara-jei sem manchwo-peena ni ne.

english_verse: At their ordination, a ceremony of forgiveness was performed for them with this sacred food, and only they have the right to eat it.
translation_verse: Wodiu kom konto ye kolo amo na tɔge ko ŋwaane a ma saare ba wɛleera pa se ba ji amo kaanem tiina to mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege chwoŋa se o di-ko, ko ná dae kaanem tiina bam yerane, ko na ye a nyem to ŋwaane.

english_verse: If any of the sacred food is left until morning, it must be completely burned.
translation_verse: Nɔna yam de bworobworo kom ná zege te poore tega, se á zwɛ-te. Á daa yé di-te, te na ye a nyem to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you.
translation_verse: Kwei da yarepɛ se n ma n tiŋi Aron de o bia bam amo kaanem totoŋa yam ŋwaane. Yɔɔre n ke se ko maŋe de a na bere‑m tei to.

english_verse: Do this for seven days, and the altar will become so holy that anyone who touches it will become holy. Daily Sacrifices (Leviticus
translation_verse: Nmo ná ke konto dakaa kam baŋa ne se ko yi da yarepɛ, ka wó yɔɔre ka taa ye wose mo amo ŋwaane. Nɔɔno wolo de woŋo kolo maama na dwei-ka to de nam pwɛ mo amo ŋwaane. Dɛ maama pɛɛra yam

english_verse: one in the morning and one in the evening.
translation_verse: Dedoa wó kwei ka kaane zezeŋa ne mo, se kadwoŋi kam kaane dedaan-ni maŋa ne.

english_verse: With each lamb offer one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of pure olive oil, and also pour out a liter of wine as an offering. The smell of this sacrifice on the fires of the altar will be pleasing to me.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye dedaan-ni pi-bala kam, ta kwei-na muni, de nuga, de sa-sona konto dwoŋi á woli da á ke kaanem á pa-ne. Ko wó taa ye wodiu pɛɛre ko pa-ne. Ko nyoa kam lwom wó taa ywona ko pa-ne ye ko pwoli amo wo.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always offer this sacrifice on the altar at the entrance to the sacred tent. People of Israel, I will meet and speak with you there, and my shining glory will make the place holy.
translation_verse: Chega to, amo wó ba a jeeri Isarele tiina bam dáane, ye a nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom mo wó tiini ko nyeene jei sem konto ne se se taa ye wose.

english_verse: Because of who I am, the tent will become sacred, and Aaron and his sons will become worthy to serve as my priests.
translation_verse: A maa wó pwɛ wara-vwei dem de de kaanem dakaa kam maama se te taa ye wose. A nam ta wó pɔɔre Aron de o bu-baara bam se ba ji amo kaanem tiina.

english_verse: I will live among you as your God,
translation_verse: A maa wó taa zoore de Isarele tiina bam, se a taa ye ba Wɛ.

english_verse: and you will know that I am the Lord your God, the one who rescued you from Egypt, so that I could live among you.
translation_verse: Banto de maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. A nam jaane-ba mo a nwoŋi Ejipti ne a ba ywo-seeni se a taa zoore de-ba. Chega to, amo mo ye ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: It is truly holy because it is dedicated to me, so don't ever make any for yourselves.
translation_verse: Yé ke-na ka dwi se á ma á toŋe totoŋe dedwoŋi á pa á tete. Ba na kwei talwoŋ-ywoŋa kam konto ba pa amo to ŋwaane mo ka ye wose.

english_verse: Mix four liters of olive oil with the following costly spices: six kilograms of myrrh, three kilograms of cinnamon, three kilograms of cane, and six kilograms of cassia. Measure these according to the official standards. Then use this sacred mixture
translation_verse: Laam pa se wolo na tiini o yei terale nuga keim to viiri te maama daane o ke-ka. Amo swolim nuga kam konto wó taa ye ka yera mo amo ŋwaane.

english_verse: Build an altar of acacia wood where you can burn incense.
translation_verse: “Pa se ba kwei golesaa dɛ ba ma ke dakaa kalo talwoŋ-ywoŋa na wó taa zwɛ de baŋa ne to.

english_verse: Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it.
translation_verse: Kwei-na sabu-seŋa kalo na ye chekke to á kwoli dakaa kam maama, ye á daare á ma sabu-seŋa kam á tɔge ka nia yam.

english_verse: Then below the edging on opposite sides attach two gold rings through which you can put the poles for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Ta ke-na sabu-seŋa kwana yalei á meeli-ya dakaa kam sɛ selei sem ne, se ya maŋe de ka nia yam kuri seeni. Laam tore-na dɛ ya wone se nɔɔna taa mae ba zeŋe-ka.

english_verse: These poles are also to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Dɛ sem konto wó taa ye golesaa dɛ mo á wó ma á ke ye á daare á kwei sabu-seŋa á kwoli se maama.

english_verse: Put the altar in front of the inside curtain of the sacred tent. The chest with the place of mercy is kept behind that curtain, and I will talk with you there.
translation_verse: Á maa wó zege dakaa kam konto se ka taa wo gare-jale delo na chege amo di-yun-gala kam to yiga ne. Ni-gwonim dakaa kam de ka ni-pugu kom wó taa wo gare-jale dem kwaga ne. Ko maa ye wɛleera saarem ni-pugu kom seeni mo amo wó jeeri‑m se dé ŋɔɔne.

english_verse: Burn only the proper incense on the altar and never use it for grain sacrifices or animal sacrifices or drink offerings.
translation_verse: Yé zwɛ-na talwoŋ-yɔɔ dakaa kam konto baŋa ne. Nam yé ke-na zwɛɛm kaanem, naa muni pɛɛre kaanem, naa wo-nyɔɔro kaanem ka baŋa ne.

translation_verse: Banto de ba dwi dem jege se ba taa se ba je de ba nɛ mo, se ba yé te. Amo ni dem mo konto se ko taa vei wuu.” Wɛ swolim nuga kam

english_verse: Moses told the Israelites that the Lord had said: The Sabbath belongs to me. Now I command you and your descendants to always obey the laws of the Sabbath. By doing this, you will know that I have chosen you as my own.
translation_verse: “Ta Isarele tiina bam se ba taa yei da yarepɛ dɛ dem ni ne. Abam ná ke á tɔge amo ni dem da yarepɛ dɛ dem ŋwaane, ko wó taa ye maana abam de á dwi maama tei ne, se á lɔre we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo kuri abam se á ta‑á ye amo nyem.

english_verse: Keep the Sabbath holy. You have six days to do your work, but the Sabbath is mine, and it must remain a day of rest. If you work on the Sabbath, you will no longer be part of my people, and you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Kwei-na da yaredo á toŋe á totoŋa. Ko daare se da yarepɛ dɛ dem taa ye de yera de pae amo Baŋa Wɛ. Ko maa ye siu dɛ mo. Wolo ná toŋe de dɛ dem ne, se á go kotu.

english_verse: This day will always serve as a reminder, both to me and to the Israelites, that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, then on the seventh day I rested and relaxed.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ye maana dɛ mo de pa amo de Isarele tiina bam se ko taa vei wuu, se á guli we amo kwei da yaredo mo a ma a naane wɛyuu de tega baŋa. A laam ma sii da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, a naanem totoŋe dem na ti to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: When God had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two flat stones on which he had written all his laws with his own hand.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na ŋɔɔne de Moses Sinayi Peo kom yuu ne o ti to, mo o kwei kandwa-pelɛ selei sem o pa‑o. Wɛ nam ya mo mɛ o tete jeŋa o popone o ni-gwonim dem botara ya baŋa ne.

english_verse: Moses, I have seen how stubborn these people are,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we, “Moses, amo nɛ we nɔɔna banto zwabania tiini ka gaale.

english_verse: The people got up early the next morning and killed some animals to be used for sacrifices and others to be eaten. Then everyone ate and drank so much that they began to carry on like wild people.
translation_verse: Tega na poore tetete to, nɔɔna bam ma ba ba go vara se ba ma ke zwɛɛm kaanem, ye ba kwei badaara ba ke yazura kaanem se ba di nɔna yam. Ba déem lɛɛre ba di wodi-fɔrɔ mo ye ba nyɔa, ba daare ba zaŋe ba kwɛɛre yɔɔ yɔɔ.

english_verse: Moses said to them, “You obeyed the Lord and did what was right, and so you will serve as his priests for the people of Israel. It was hard for you to kill your own sons and brothers, but the Lord has blessed you and made you his priests today.”
translation_verse: Moses ta ma ta-ba o we, “Abam na sɛ Wɛ ni dem ye á go á bia de á chorro to ŋwaane, á laam wó ta‑á ye Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina mo se á ta‑á toŋe á pa o nɔɔna bam. Baŋa Wɛ swolim dem laam nam wo á baŋa ne.”

english_verse: After the people saw that Moses had been on the mountain for a long time, they went to Aaron and said, “Make us an image of a god who will lead and protect us. Moses brought us out of Egypt, but nobody knows what has happened to him.”
translation_verse: Moses déem nam ya maŋe peo kom yuu ne mo o dáane. Nɔɔna bam ma vo ba jeeri Aron tei ne ba we, “Moses mo seene o ja debam o nwoŋi Ejipti ne o ba ywo-seeni. Dé nam yeiri kolo na yi‑o to. Nam ke woŋo se ko lwoni wɛ n pa debam se ko taa tɔge debam yiga.”

english_verse: Aaron told them, “Bring me the gold earrings that your wives and sons and daughters are wearing.”
translation_verse: Aron ma leiri-ba o we, “Le-na sabu-seŋa zwa-kwana yam abam kaana de á bia de á bukwa bam na ke ba zwa ne to á ja á ba á pa-ne.”

english_verse: then he melted them and made an idol in the shape of a young bull. All the people said to one another, “This is the god who brought us out of Egypt!”
translation_verse: Aron na jwoŋi sabu-seŋa kam to, o ma nyeene-ka ye o laam mɔ kamɔgɔ nenɛɛne na-mɔra o pa-ba. Nɔɔna bam na nɛ-ka to, mo ba bage de kwor-dɛa ba bere daane ba we, “Isarele tiina bam, á wɛ dem mo tento, de na jaane debam de ja nwoŋi Ejipti ne de ba ywo-seeni.”

english_verse: When Aaron saw what was happening, he built an altar in front of the idol and said, “Tomorrow we will celebrate in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Aron ma na kolo na ke to ye o lɔ bimbini na-mɔra kam yiga ne. O ma ta o we, “Jwa ne, se dé maama jeeri dé di kuri dé ma zuli Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Hurry back down! Those people you led out of Egypt are acting like fools.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Ke lela n tu n nɔɔna bam tei ne. N na jaane balo n nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom ne to bobo se ba toŋe jworim mo.

english_verse: They have already stopped obeying me and have made themselves an idol in the shape of a young bull. They have bowed down to it, offered sacrifices, and said that it is the god who brought them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ba gare ba ve chwoŋa kalo amo na bere-ba se ba tɔge to mo, ye ba ke jwoni na nye de na-mɔra. Ba maa tɛ daane ba we, ‘Isarele tiina bam, á wɛ dem mo tento, de na jaane abam de nwoŋi Ejipti ne de ba ywo-seeni.’ ”

english_verse: and I'm angry enough to destroy them, so don't try to stop me. But I will make your descendants into a great nation.
translation_verse: Amo bane nam zaŋe de-ba mo ye ko maŋe se a chɔge-ba. Yé che a yiga de a boboŋe dem. Amo nam ta wó zege nmo baŋa ne se a pa n dwi dem puli de ji te-zɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: Moses tried to get the Lord God to change his mind: Our Lord, you used your mighty power to bring these people out of Egypt. Now don't become angry and destroy them.
translation_verse: Moses ma kwaane o lwoori o Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom se o leiri o boboŋe dem. O ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo mɛ n dam-fɔrɔ n ja nɔɔna banto n zege Ejipti ne n ba ywo-seeni. Kɔ ŋwaane mo nmo bane wó zaŋe de-ba se n chɔge-ba?

english_verse: If you do, the Egyptians will say that you brought your people out here into the mountains just to get rid of them. Please don't be angry with your people. Don't destroy them!
translation_verse: Nmo ná chɔge-ba, Ejipti tiina bam wó taa tɛ we, ‘Wɛ gane o nɔɔna bam mo o ja o vo peero tem jei ne se o go-ba. Ba yere maa wó saare logo baŋa ne!’ Ja! Yage n ban-zɔŋɔ kom, se n leiri n boboŋa se n yé chɔge-ba, ba na ye nmo tete nɔɔna bam to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Remember the solemn promise you made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You promised that someday they would have as many descendants as there are stars in the sky and that you would give them land.
translation_verse: Guli n ni-gwonim dem n déem na ke de Abaraham, de Izaak dedaane Jakob to gula. Nmo tete ne mo n dugi de-ba we ba dwi dem wó ba de puli nenɛɛne wɛyuu chalechwe na ye tei to, se ba daare ba taa tei tega kanto.”

english_verse: So even though the Lord had threatened to destroy the people, he changed his mind and let them live.
translation_verse: Moses na tage konto to, Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o boboŋe dem o ya na jega se o chɔge nɔɔna bam to, ye o daa wo chɔge-ba.

english_verse: Moses went back down the mountain with the two flat stones on which God had written all of his laws with his own hand, using both sides of the stones.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ tete ni taane mo o déem nam popone de o jeŋa. O ma sare-ya o tiŋi kandwa-pelɛ sem baŋa ne.

english_verse: When Joshua heard the noisy shouts of the people, he said to Moses, “A battle must be going on down in the camp.”
translation_verse: Moses zeinnu Josua déem ma ni nɔɔna bam na jege sɔɔ kolo ba ke to ŋwa. O ma ta de Moses o we, “Sɔɔ konto nye nenɛɛne tiguri-kaasa mo to nɔɔna bam na gilimi mɛ to wone.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “It doesn't sound like they are shouting because they have won or lost a battle. It sounds more like a wild party!”
translation_verse: Moses de ma leiri‑o o we, “Sɔɔ konto wo bere we ba wane ba dona, ko nam wo bere we ba dona di-ba. Ko ye kwɛɛra sɔɔ mo.”

english_verse: As Moses got closer to the camp, he saw the idol, and he also saw the people dancing around. This made him so angry that he threw down the stones and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Moses na fɔɔre o yi peo kom kuri ne to, mo o nɛ ba jwoni dem. O ta ma na nɔɔna bam na sae tei to. O bane ma tiini de zaŋe. O ban-zɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne, mo o dole kandwa-pelɛ sem de dam peo kom teiŋa ne ye ya lɔ.

english_verse: He melted the idol the people had made, and he ground it into powder. He scattered it in their water and made them drink it.
translation_verse: O ta ma kwei na-mɔra jwoni dem o de mini ne pa se de nyeene. O laam ma cho-de pa se de ji muni, ye o daare o viiri de muni dem de na o kwei o pa nɔɔna bam se ba nyɔ.

english_verse: Moses asked Aaron, “What did these people do to harm you? Why did you make them sin in this terrible way?”

translation_verse: Aron ma leiri‑o o we, “Ja! Yé pa se n bane zaŋe de amo, se n maŋe n yei we, ba ná boŋe se ba ke kolo, nɔɔno ware-ba o gwi.

english_verse: They even told me, “That man Moses led us out of Egypt, but now we don't know what has happened to him. Make us a god to lead us.”
translation_verse: Ba tu amo tei ne mo ba we, ‘Moses na jaane debam o nwoŋi Ejipti ne o ba ywo-seeni to, dé yeiri kolo na yi‑o to. Nam ke woŋo se ko lwoni wɛ n pa debam se ko taa tɔge debam yiga.’

english_verse: Then I asked them to bring me their gold earrings. They took them off and gave them to me. I threw the gold into a fire, and out came this bull.
translation_verse: Amo de ma ta de-ba se ba ja ba sabu-seŋa zwa-kwana ba ja ba ba ba pa-ne. Ba na le-ya ba pa-ne to, mo a dole-ya a de mini wone ye ya ji na-mɔra kanto!”

english_verse: Moses knew that the people were out of control and that it was Aaron's fault. And now they had made fools of themselves in front of their enemies.
translation_verse: Moses ma maane we nɔɔna bam daa ware ba ja. O ta lɔre we ko zege Aron yera ne mo ye ba ke konto, kolo ŋwaane nɔɔna bam déem ya toŋe jworim mo pa se ba dona mɔne-ba.

english_verse: So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and shouted, “Everyone who is on the Lord's side come over here!” Then the men of the Levi tribe gathered around Moses,

translation_verse: O ma ta de-ba o we, “Isarele Baŋa Wɛ wom mo pɛ abam ni se á maama kwei á se-zɔɔro á zo nɔɔna bam wone á ta‑á goe yɔɔ. Yé kuri-na á chorro, de á badwonna, de á fara á yage.”

english_verse: The next day Moses told the people, “This is a terrible thing you have done. But I will go back to the Lord to see if I can do something to keep this sin from being held against you.”
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Moses ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam ya tiini á ke wɛleere. Amo nam wó jwoori a di Baŋa Wɛ tei se a kwaane a ke abam de Baŋa Wɛ daane se o ma o chɛ abam.”

english_verse: Moses returned to the Lord and said, “The people have committed a terrible sin. They have made a gold idol to be their god.
