english_verse: The Lord replied, “I will wipe out of my book the name of everyone who has sinned against me.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Aawo! Wolo ná ke o tusi amo yiga ne, mo amo wó saare kotu yere a yage se de daa yé taa wo amo tɔnɔ kom wone.

english_verse: Now take my people to the place I told you about, and my angel will lead you. But when the time comes, I will punish them for this sin.”
translation_verse: Nam jwoori n vo n tɔge nɔɔna bam yiga se á vo mɛ amo na tage dede‑m se á vo to. Amo maleka kam wó taa wo á yiga ne. Maŋa nam ná yia, amo laam wó waare-ba ba wɛleere dento ŋwaane.”

english_verse: So the Lord punished the people of Israel with a terrible disease for talking Aaron into making the gold idol.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se jawe-chɛɛro to Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne de ba na pɛ se Aron ke sabu-seŋa na-mɔra jwoni dem o pa-ba to.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: You led the people of Israel out of Egypt. Now get ready to lead them to the land I promised their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta de Moses o we, “Zaŋe-na se á kɛ! Nam ja Isarele tiina bam n na jaane n nwoŋi Ejipti ne n ba ywo-seeni to, se á vo tega kalo amo na gwoni ni dedaane á nabaara Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob se a pa banto de ba dwi dem to.

english_verse: It is a land rich with milk and honey, and I will send an angel to force out those people who live there—the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. But I will not go with my people. They are so rebellious that I would destroy them before they get there.
translation_verse: Ba tega kam á na maa vei to tiini ka ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ. Amo nam za bá tɔge de abam se dé vo, á na ye zwabani-nyena to ŋwaane. Amo ná tɔge de abam, a wae a chɔge abam chwoŋa ne.”

english_verse: Even before the Lord said these harsh things, he had told Moses, “These people really are rebellious, and I would kill them at once, if I went with them. But tell them to take off their fancy jewelry, then I'll decide what to do with them.” So the people started mourning,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam ya wuuri o ta Moses mo se o ta de Isarele tiina bam we, “Baŋa Wɛ ná maŋe o tɔge de abam fenfee de, o wó chɔge abam mo, á zwa na ba ni to ŋwaane. Nam lɔɔre-na á yera wo-nyenno se Wɛ laam lɔre o na wó ke abam tei to.”

english_verse: and after leaving Mount Sinai, they stopped wearing fancy jewelry. The Lord Is with His People
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Isarele tiina bam na zege Sinayi peo kom jei sem ne ba maa kɛ to, ba daa wo kwei wo-nyenno ba ke ba yera ne. Jeerim vwei dem

english_verse: Each time Moses went out to this tent, everyone would stand at the entrance to their own tents and watch him enter.
translation_verse: Moses ná yeini o maa vei se o zo jeerim vwei dem wone, nɔɔna bam maama wó nwoŋi ba zege ba vwoa yam nia ne mo. Ba laam maa nii‑o se o vo o yi vwei dem o zo de wone.

english_verse: Then they would bow down because a thick cloud would come down in front of the tent, and the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, just like a friend. Afterwards, Moses would return to camp, but his young assistant Joshua would stay at the tent. The Lord Promises To Be with His People
translation_verse: Moses ná yeini o zo vwei dem wone, Baŋa Wɛ ŋɔɔne ded‑o jaja nenɛɛne nɔɔno na ŋɔɔne de o dwoŋi tei to mo. Ko kwaga ne Moses maa yeini o jwoori nɔɔna bam tei, mɛ ba na zoore to. Nɔn-doŋo wolo na ye Moses zeinnu to maa yeini o maŋe jeerim vwei dem wone. Wonto maa ye Nun bu Josua. Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom

english_verse: Moses said to the Lord, “I know that you have told me to lead these people to the land you promised them. But you have not said who will go along to help me. You have said that you are my friend and that you are pleased with me.
translation_verse: Moses déem tage de Baŋa Wɛ mo o we, “Nmo seene n bere-ne we a tɔge nɔɔna banto yiga se a ja-ba a vo tega kam baŋa. Nmo nam ta wo pɛ se a lɔre a zeinnu wom mo. Nmo ta ma‑n tɛ we nmo yei amo wo ye a kikia su n yi.

english_verse: If this is true, let me know what your plans are, then I can obey and continue to please you. And don't forget that you have chosen this nation to be your own.”
translation_verse: Tento maama nam ná seene ko ye chega, se n bere-ne n chwei sem chekke. Konto wó pa se a fɔge a sɛ nmo ni lanyerane, ye a ta ke nmo boboŋa yam na lage tei to. Nam yé swei we n tete mo kuri dwi dem konto nɔɔna bam se ba taa ye nmo nyem.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “I will go with you and give you peace.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri Moses o we, “Amo tete mo wó taa wo nmo tei ne, ye a pa se n bochare zuri.”

english_verse: Then Moses replied, “If you aren't going with us, please don't make us leave this place.
translation_verse: Moses ma ta o we, “Nmo nam ná ba lage n tɔge debam se dé vo, se n yé pa se dé gɔ naga.

english_verse: But if you do go with us, everyone will know that you are pleased with your people and with me. That way, we will be different from the rest of the people on earth.”
translation_verse: Nmo nam ná tɔge n wo dé tei ne ye dé via, nɔɔna maama wó lɔre we nɔɔna banto kikia su nmo yi. Ba ta wó lɔre we debam ye dé yera mo logo baŋa nɔɔna maama wone.”

english_verse: So the Lord told him, “I will do what you have asked, because I am your friend and I am pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we, “Amo wó ke kolo maama nmo na lage to, a na yei nmo wo ye n kikia su amo yi to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Then Moses said, “I pray that you will let me see you in all of your glory.”
translation_verse: Moses daa ma ta de Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A lwoori‑m mo se n pa-ne pwola se a na nmo nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom chekke.”

english_verse: The Lord answered: All right. I am the Lord, and I show mercy and kindness to anyone I choose. I will let you see my glory and hear my holy name,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom. Amo wó duri wolo maama a na kuri to yibwona ye a ke zaane kotu yuu ne. Amo nam wó bere‑m a lanyerane dem se n yia na-de, ye a daare a pa se n ni a yere dem chekke.

english_verse: but I won't let you see my face, because anyone who sees my face will die.
translation_verse: Nmo nam ba jege se n na a yibia mo, kolo ŋwaane wolo maama ná nɛ amo yibia, konto tu wó te mo.

english_verse: There is a rock not far from me. Stand beside it,
translation_verse: Nii ywo! Peo kodwoŋi zege ywo-seeni bwola bwola. Véi n ta‑n zege ko baŋa ne.

english_verse: and before I pass by in all of my shining glory, I will put you in a large crack in the rock. I will cover your eyes with my hand until I have passed by.
translation_verse: Amo nam ná lage a tɔge n tei ne se a kɛ de a nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom, a wó ja‑m se n seigi peo gugworo ne, ye a kwoli n yibia de a jeŋa, se a wane a gaale‑m a kɛ.

english_verse: Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. You will not see my face.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne a laam wó dɔne a jeŋa se n wane n na amo kwaga kam. Se ko ná ye amo yibia, n ba jege se n na-ka.”

english_verse: The Lord said: I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta o we: “Nii mo! Amo ta lage a gwoni ni de abam mo. Nmo nɔɔna bam yiga ne mo amo wó ke wo-kenkagela yalo dwoŋi ta na wo fɔge ya ke logo baŋa ne to. Teene delo na bwola de abam to wó taa zege ba nia ye foone ja-ba mo, wo-kenkagela yalo amo Baŋa Wɛ na wó ke abam tetare ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Be ready tomorrow morning to come up Mount Sinai and meet me at the top.
translation_verse: Nam ti n yiga se jwa tetete n di Sinayi peo kom yuu n ba amo tei se dé jeeri daane.

english_verse: No one is to come with you or to be on the mountain at all. Don't even let the sheep and cattle graze at the foot of the mountain.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam ba jege se o tɔge dede‑m o di peo kom yuu. Nɔɔna bam maama jege se ba maŋe peo kom dáa ne mo. Yé pa-na se á pei, de á bone, de á naane taa bwola peo kom teiŋa ne se de di gaao.”

english_verse: So Moses cut two flat stones like the first ones, and early the next morning he carried them to the top of Mount Sinai, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Moses ma sare kandwa-pelɛ selei ne boboa nyena yam na ye tei to. Tega na poore tetete to, o ma ja-ya o di Sinayi peo kom yuu, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to.

english_verse: Then he passed in front of Moses and called out, “I am the Lord God. I am merciful and very patient with my people. I show great love, and I can be trusted.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma tɔge Moses yiga ne o kɛ ye o we: “Amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom, Taa Wuu Tu Baŋa Wɛ! A jege nɔɔna ŋwaŋa, ye a ke zaane a ke ba yuu ne. A maa yeini a peene a bane de-ba. A swono kom gaale, ye a chega kam de bá fɔge ka ti.

english_verse: Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Moses ma ke lela o chɔɔle o yuu tega ne se o zuli Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: He prayed, “Lord, if you really are pleased with me, I pray that you will go with us. It is true that these people are sinful and rebellious, but forgive our sin and let us be your people.” A Promise and Its Demands (Exodus
translation_verse: O ma lwoori‑o o we, “Amo Teiru, a kikia nam ná seene ya su nmo yi, se n tɔge debam se dé vo. Chega ŋwaane to, nɔɔna bam seene ba ye zwabani-nyena mo. Nam kwei ba wɛleera de ba tusim kikia n ma‑n chɛ-ba. Ta pa se dé taa ye nmo tete nyɔn-mage nɔɔna, se n ta‑n tei debam.”

english_verse: Your men must come to worship me three times a year, because I am the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Bene maama wone se abam baara bam jeeri amo yiga ne kuni betɔ, se ba zuli-ne. Kolo ŋwaane, amo mo ye Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: The first-born males of your families and of your flocks and herds belong to me.
translation_verse: Abam dwi dem wone, bu-kwe sem de á vara maama wone cheeri-bia bam ye amo nyem mo.

english_verse: Your men will even marry their women and be influenced to worship their gods.
translation_verse: Abam baara bam ná di jei sem konto bukwa ba maa ke kaana, kaana bam konto nam mo wó gane-ba se ba zuli ba jwona yam.

english_verse: Don't make treaties with any of those people. If you do, it will be like falling into a trap.
translation_verse: Ta‑á yei-na se á yé ke ni-sɛɛm de nɔɔna balo na zoore tega kam konto ne to. Se á ná me de-ba, ba wó soge abam se á tusi amo yiga ne.

english_verse: Instead, you must destroy their altars and tear down the sacred poles they use in the worship of the goddess Asherah.
translation_verse: Nam ke-na tento de-ba: Chɔge-na ba bimbina yam, de ba kandwa-siswollu tem na ye ba jwona to. Gwoni-na ba Asera nyenyego dɛ sem á de tega ne.

english_verse: Don't make treaties with the people there, or you will soon find yourselves worshiping their gods and taking part in their sacrificial meals.
translation_verse: Nam yé ke-na ni-sɛɛm dedaane nɔɔna balo na zoore tega kam konto ne to. Abam ná me de-ba, ba wó soge abam se á ta‑á zuli ba jwona yam, ye á daare á woli ba wone se á tɔge á di ba jwona wodiiru tem mo.

english_verse: Don't fail to observe the Festival of Thin Bread in the month of Abib. Obey me and eat bread without yeast for seven days during Abib, because that is the month you left Egypt.
translation_verse: Abam wó ta‑á di Bworobworo-memene kuri dem mo. Bene maama wone, se á kwei da yarepɛ á ma á di bworobworo kolo sabɔle na wo woli ko wone to, Abibi chana kam ne. Ko déem ye chana kam konto ne mo abam nwoŋi Ejipti teo kom wone.

english_verse: You can save the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must save every first-born son. Bring an offering every time you come to worship.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye bonaga cheeri-bu, se á kwei pipeila á leiri ka yuu ne. Konto ná ware, se á bwori ka ba á go. Abam wó kwei wonnu mo á leiri á bu-kwe sem yuu ne á pa-ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé vei de je-kore o ba amo yiga ye o ba zei pɛɛre.

english_verse: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
translation_verse: Abam wodiiru tem ná dɛ yiga se te ke kwea maŋa ne, se á di Ga-kwea kuri. Chaara zagem maŋa de nam ná yi se á taa di Faao kuri dem.

english_verse: As you advance, I will force the nations out of your land and enlarge your borders. Then no one will try to take your property when you come to worship me these three times each year.
translation_verse: Amo lage a zeili dwia yalo na wo dáane ye abam ta wo zo da to mo, se á ná yeini á jeeri kuni betɔ se á di kura yanto, nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé kwaane se o jwoŋi á tega kam. A nam ta wó pa se á tega kam yale ka pa abam.

english_verse: When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
translation_verse: Abam ná kwei varem se á ke kaanem, yé woli-na bworobworo kolo sabɔle na wo ko wone to da se á ke pɛɛre á pa-ne. Nam yé pa-na se Atɔgebabaŋa wodiu maŋe á tei ne ko poore tega.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
translation_verse: Bene maama wone se á ja á kare sem wodiiru telo na lwoori yiga te ke ye te lamma to á ja á jeeri abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé kwei bebala de ka nu nayela o saŋe mini wone.”

english_verse: Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining.
translation_verse: Moses ma zege peo kom yuu ne o tu nɔɔna bam tei, ye o zei kandwa-pelɛ sem Wɛ ni-gwonim dem botara na popone da to. Moses de Baŋa Wɛ nam ya na ŋɔɔne daane to, mo o yibia tiini ka nyeena ye o yeiri ko ni ne.

english_verse: When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him.
translation_verse: Aron de Isarele tiina bam maama na nɛ we Moses yibia kam nyeene to, ba ma kɔre se ba fɔɔre ba yi o yera.

english_verse: Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them.
translation_verse: Moses na maane konto to, mo o bwoŋi Aron de Isarele nakwa bam se ba ba o tei. Ba na yi da to, o ma ŋɔɔne de-ba.

english_verse: Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam maama laam ma fɔɔre ba yi ba gilimi Moses. O de ma kwei Baŋa Wɛ nia yam o ya na pɛ‑o Sinayi peo kom yuu ne to o pa-ba.

english_verse: The face of Moses kept shining, and after he had spoken with the people, he covered his face with a veil.
translation_verse: Moses yibia nam ta nyeene mo. O na ŋɔɔne de nɔɔna bam o ti to, mo o kwei gare-fefala o ma o kwoli o yibia.

english_verse: Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say.
translation_verse: Moses déem ná lage se o zo wara-vwei dem ne se o de Baŋa Wɛ ŋɔɔne daane, o yeini o le gare-fefala kam mo. O laam maa ná nwoŋi pwooni se o daa yeini o lwoni Baŋa Wɛ na bere tei maama to o bere nɔɔna bam,

english_verse: They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_verse: ba daa ta ma na we o yibia tiini ka nyeene mo. Moses ma ná yeini o ŋɔɔne de-ba o ti, o wó jwoori o kwei o gare-fefala kam mo o kwoli o yibia. O déem ma yɔɔre o ke konto mo taa se ko taa nii o daa ná boŋe se o vo o ŋɔɔne de Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: You have six days in which to do your work. But the seventh day must be dedicated to me, your Lord, as a day of rest. Whoever works on the Sabbath will be put to death.
translation_verse: Kwei-na da yaredo á ma‑á toŋe á totoŋa. Ko daare se da yarepɛ dɛ dem taa ye de yera de pa abam. Ko maa ye siu dɛ, amo Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane. Wolo ná toŋe de dɛ dem konto ne, se á go kotu.

english_verse: Don't even build a cooking fire at home on the Sabbath. Offerings for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Yé tɔre-na mini á sam wone se á saŋe wodiiru da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne.” Wara-jei sem yera zela yam

english_verse: The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made.
translation_verse: Kaana balo de na yei gare-ŋone ŋom to de ma ja gare-fefale de gare-ŋone selo ba na ŋoge to ba ja ba ba. Gare-ŋone sem nyenyero maa ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ.

english_verse: I will welcome an offering from anyone who wants to give something. You may bring gold, silver, or bronze;
translation_verse: Ja-na pɛɛra á ba á pa Baŋa Wɛ. Wolo wo nam ná dɛa, se kotu ja pɛɛra yanto dwi: sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, dedaane channa,

english_verse: blue, purple, or red wool; fine linen; goat hair;
translation_verse: de gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to, de gare-fefale, dedaane boŋo koro,

english_verse: tanned ram skin or fine leather; acacia wood;
translation_verse: de pi-bea twanno telo ba na seini to, de twan-nyenno, de golesaa dɛ,

english_verse: olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices for the oil of dedication and for the incense; or
translation_verse: de min-zwonnu nuga, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa kalo ba na wó ma ba ke Wɛ swolim nuga kam, de kalo ba na wó zwɛ wara-vwei dem totoŋa ŋwaane to,

english_verse: the sacred chest with its carrying poles, its place of mercy, and the curtain in front of it;
translation_verse: ko woli de Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam, de dɛ selo ba na wó taa ma zeŋe-ka to, de wɛleera saarem ni-pugu kom, de gare-jale delo na chege Wɛ di-yun-gala kam to,

english_verse: the table with its carrying poles and all that goes on it, including the sacred bread;
translation_verse: de tabolo kom, de ko dɛ selo ba na wó taa maa zeŋe-ko to, de ko yera zela yam maama, de bworobworo kolo na tigi da Wɛ ŋwaane to,

english_verse: the incense altar with its carrying poles and sweet-smelling incense; the ordination oil; the curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent;
translation_verse: de talwoŋ-ywoŋa zwɛɛm dakaa kam, de dɛ selo ba na wó taa ma zeŋe-ka to, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa kam tete, de Wɛ swolim nuga kam, dedaane gare-jale delo na wó pale wara-vwei dem ni ne to,

english_verse: the curtains with the posts and stands that go around the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance;
translation_verse: de konkɔlɔ kom gare-jala yam, de dɛ selo ya na wó pale se baŋa ne to, de se luuru tem, de gare-jale delo na wó che konkɔlɔ kom manchwo-peena ni dem to,

english_verse: the pegs and ropes for the tent and the courtyard;
translation_verse: de paara yalo na wó chwi ya ja vwei dem de konkɔlɔ kom zela yam to, de ya ŋone sem,

english_verse: Then those who wanted to bring gifts to the Lord, brought them to be used for the sacred tent, the worship services, and the priestly clothes.
translation_verse: Balo maama na boŋe keim ye ba jege wopwolo ko ŋwaane to ma ja pɛɛra ba ba ba pa Baŋa Wɛ se ya woli wara-jei sem totoŋa yam, de kaanem totoŋa yam, dedaane kaanem tiina bam gwaaro tem sɔɔm.

english_verse: Everyone brought their blue, purple, and red wool, their fine linen, and their cloth made of goat hair, as well as their ram skins dyed red and their fine leather.
translation_verse: Badwonna déem ma ja gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to, de gare-fefale, dedaane boŋo koro, de pi-bea twanno telo ba na seini to, de twan-nyenno ba ba.

english_verse: Anyone who had silver or bronze or acacia wood brought it as a gift to the Lord.
translation_verse: Balo maa ná jege lu-nyenno, naa channa, naa golesaa dɛ selo na wó woli totoŋa yam to, ba de ma ja-te ba ba ba zeiŋi Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: And the women who knew how to make cloth from goat hair were glad to do so.
translation_verse: Kaana bam badwonna de ma kwei boŋo koro ba ma ŋo gare-ŋone.

english_verse: The leaders brought different kinds of jewels to be sewn on the special clothes and the breastpiece for the high priest.
translation_verse: Yiga tiina bam ma ja Onika kandwa de kandwa-nyenno dwi dwi ba ba se ba kwei-ya ba meeli kaanem yiga tu gare-wogo kom dedaane o gare-pale dem yera ne.

english_verse: They also brought sweet-smelling spices to be mixed with the incense and olive oil that were for the lamps and for ordaining the priests.
translation_verse: Ba ta ma ja min-zwonnu nuga kam, de wo-talwooru telo ba na wó woli talwoŋ-ywoŋa kam wone dedaane Wɛ swolim nuga kam wone to ba ja ba ba.

english_verse: Moses had told the people what the Lord wanted them to do, and many of them decided to bring their gifts. Bezalel and Oholiab (Exodus
translation_verse: Moses nam ya tage Baŋa Wɛ na lage se Isarele tiina bam ke totoŋa yalo to o bere-ba, pa se nɔɔna bam dedɛ boboŋa ja se ba ja wo-ywoŋo pɛɛra ba ba ba ke Wɛ jeŋa ne. Bezaleli dedaane Oholiaba taane

english_verse: Moses said to the people of Israel: The Lord has chosen Bezalel of the Judah tribe.
translation_verse: Moses laam ma ta de Isarele tiina bam o we, “Nii-na. Baŋa Wɛ mo kuri Yuri bu Bezaleli. Wonto kwo-nakwe maa ye Hura ye o nwoŋi Judah dwi dem wone.

english_verse: Not only has the Lord filled him with his Spirit, but he has given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood.
translation_verse: O ta wae o kwei kandwa-nyenno de dɛ o sara o maa gɔgere wonnu dwi dwi. O yɔɔre o ye gɔgɔ mo chekke.

english_verse: and he gave them the gifts that the people of Israel had donated for building the place of worship. In fact, so much was being given each morning,
translation_verse: Ba de maa jwoŋi pɛɛra yalo maama nɔɔna bam na pɛ se ba maa ke wara-jei sem to Moses jeŋa ne. Se ko ná ye nɔɔna bam, ba ta yɔɔre ba jaane wo-ywoŋo pɛɛra mo ba tui Moses tei dɛ maama zezeŋa ne, ye ya laam tiini ya gaale.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, there is already more than we need for what the Lord has assigned us to do.”
translation_verse: “Pɛɛra yalo nɔɔna bam na jaane ba ba totoŋa yam ŋwaane to daga ya dwoi totoŋe delo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ debam ni se dé toŋe to.”

english_verse: But there was already more than enough to do what needed to be done. The Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Kokuri to, ba na maŋe ba pa tei to yi se ko toŋe totoŋa yam se ya ti. Wara-jei sem

english_verse: The skilled workers got together to make the sacred tent and its linen curtains that were woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Each of the ten panels was twelve meters long and two meters wide,
translation_verse: Gare-jala fuga kam maama déem mae daane mo. Gare-jale dedwe dedɔrem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finlei-nana. De kayɔlɔ baŋa maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni bena.

english_verse: and they were sewn together to make two curtains with five panels each.
translation_verse: Ba ma nyaane gare-jala yanu ba twoŋi daane, ba ta daare ba nyaane yanu yadwonna yam de ba twoŋi daane. Te laam ma ji gare-puna yalei.

english_verse: These eleven sections were joined to make two panels, one with five and the other with six sections.
translation_verse: Ba ma kwei gare-jala yanu ba twoŋi daane se ya ji gare-pum, ye ba daare ba kwei gare-jala yaredo yam na daare to mo ba twoŋi daane se ya de ji gare-pum.

english_verse: Fifty loops were put along one of the wider sides of each panel,
translation_verse: Ba ma ke kuna finnu ba lei gare-pum ni-dedɔrɔ kom seeni, ye ba daare ba ke konto gare-pum dedwoŋi dem ne.

english_verse: Two other coverings were made—one with fine leather and the other with ram skins dyed red. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Ba ta ma pwoni pi-bɛ tankwallo ba daare ba seini-te nasoŋo se ba maa kwoli wara-vwei dem, ye ba kwei twan-nyenno ba daŋe boboa twanno tem baŋa ne.

english_verse: Altogether, along the back wall there were eight frames with two silver stands under each of them.
translation_verse: Bira-kwaga kam seeni ywoa yam déem ye nana mo, ye ya jege luuru fuga-teredo telo na teili-ya to.

english_verse: Six frames were used for the back wall along the west side
translation_verse: Ko ná ye saŋa kalo na wo bira-kwaga ne ye ka jeeri wɛ-zoore seeni to, ba ma ke ywoa yaredo se ba chwi-ya dáane.

english_verse: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. These corner frames were joined from top to bottom.
translation_verse: Ba ma twoŋi gugworru ywoa yam konto se ya meeli daane. Ko zege tega kam ne mo ko meeli se ko taa diini baŋa kam mɛ sabu-seŋa kwane dem na leigi da to.

english_verse: Five crossbars were made for each of the wooden frames, with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall.
translation_verse: Tetare dagara kam ma tole ka zege saŋa kam daa dedoa ne ka vo ka yi daa kadwoŋi kam, ka twoŋi ywoa yam maama ka ke daane.

english_verse: The frames and crossbars were covered with gold, and gold rings were attached to the frames to run the crossbars through. The Inside Curtain for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Ba déem ta kwei sabu-seŋa ba kwoli ywoa yam, ye ba daare ba maa ke kwana ba meeli ywoa yam yera ne se dagare sem taa tore ya wone. Ba ta ma kwoli dagare sem de sabu-seŋa.

english_verse: For the entrance to the tent, they used a curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye wara-vwei ni dem, ba ma kwei gare-fefale selo na ye chekke to de gare-ŋone selo nyenyero na ye nazwon-pupwia, de nasoŋ-pupwia, de nasoŋo chwɛ-chwɛ to ba ma sɔ gare-jale delo na wó lei ni dem ne to. Ba ma daare ba gɔgere nyenyero gare-jale dem yera ne.

english_verse: They made the inside curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.

english_verse: Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
translation_verse: Kotu ta wó kwei o jeŋa mo o daŋe nabea kam yuu ne se ko bere we varem wom leiri o yuu ne mo, se Wɛ wane o saare o wɛleera yam o yage.

english_verse: After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: O laam maa wó gwoni nabea kam ba Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, se Aron dwi dem na ye kaanem tiina to de laam kwei ka jana bam ba ja vo ba dole dole kaanem dakaa kam na wo wara-vwei ni dem ne to sɛ sena sem yera ne.

english_verse: while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing.
translation_verse: Kaanem tiina bam de maa wó tɔre mini kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba tigisi dɛ ba daŋe mini dem baŋa ne.

english_verse: Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye varem wom nɛ sem, de o loro tem, se kotu zare tento yiga se kaanem tu wom laam zwɛ te maama kula kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne. Pɛɛre dem konto ye zwɛɛm kaanem mo. De lwom maa ywomma de pae Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: O laam maa wó ja varem wom o vo kaanem dakaa kam saŋa kalo na jeeri baŋa seeni to o go‑o Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Kaanem tiina bam de maa wó kwei varem wom jana bam ba dole dole kaanem dakaa kam sɛ sena sem yera ne.

english_verse: Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye varem wom nɛ sem, de o loro tem, se kotu zare tento yiga se kaanem tu wom laam zwɛ te maama kula kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne. Pɛɛre dem konto ye zwɛɛm kaanem mo. De lwom maa ywomma de pae Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye zuna dwi dem mo kotu kuri se o ma ke zwɛɛm kaanem o pa Baŋa Wɛ, se o kwei kunkwoŋa, naa kunkwon-puuri o ma o toŋe.

english_verse: A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar,
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom mo wó ja-ka o yi kaanem dakaa kam jei sem se o jujugi ka yuu o gwori ye o daare o zwɛ ka yuu kom kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne. O laam maa wó zulimi zuŋa kam se ka jana lwoori ba ke kaanem dakaa kam saŋa ne.

english_verse: remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar.
translation_verse: O ta wó le ka fonfɔlɔ kom de kolo maama na wo ko wone to, ye o daare o dole-te o yage kaanem dakaa kam saŋa kalo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to ne, tentwarem na dogele mɛ to.

english_verse: When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour,
translation_verse: Abam wolo ná boŋe se o ja muni pɛɛre o ba se o kaane o pa Baŋa Wɛ, kotu jege se o beeri mun-bwei delo na lamma chekke to. O wó lwo Olivi nuga de baŋa ne, se o daare o woli Faraniki talwoŋ-ywoŋa da.

english_verse: and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: O laam maa wó ja o pɛɛre dem o vo Aron dwi dem kaanem tiina bam tei. Ba dedoa mo wó zwɛ muni dem na gwaane de nuga to, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa kam maama o ke o ja-bɔŋɔ ne. O laam wó zwɛ pɛɛre dem popɔra kanto mo kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne se ka taa ye gulim pɛɛre ka pa Wɛ. Pɛɛre dem konto lwom maa ywomma de pae Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
translation_verse: Muni pɛɛre delo ta na daare to wó taa ye Aron de o bia bam nyem mo. De maa tiini de ye wose mo, de na nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ wodiu pɛɛra yam wone to ŋwaane.

english_verse: If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
translation_verse: Abam wolo nam ná boŋe se o wɔ bworobworo kura wone se o kwei o ma ke kaanem dento dwoŋi, kotu jege se o kwei mun-bwei delo na tiini de lamma chekke, ye sabɔle wo woli da to. O wae o gwaane muni dem de nuga o ma ke bworobworo kom, naa se o kwei muni dem o ma wɔ bworobworo-memene o daare o ma nuga o taare taare de maama.

english_verse: If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast.
translation_verse: Kotu nam ná lage se o wɔ bworobworo kom luu baŋa ne, se o kwei mun-bwei delo na tiini de lamma chekke to o ma ke wodiu pɛɛre dem konto. O wó woli nuga da, se o yé pa se sabɔle woli de wone.

english_verse: Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne, o wó fɔ-ko mena-mena mo, ye o daare o lwo nuga ko baŋa ne, se ko taa ye wodiu pɛɛre.

english_verse: If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
translation_verse: Kotu nam ná saŋe o wodiu pɛɛre dem kambia wone, se o kwei mun-bwei delo na tiini de lamma chekke to, ye o woli nuga de wone.

english_verse: You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Nmo ná mɛ wonnu tem konto n ke wodiu pɛɛre dem se n kaane n pa Baŋa Wɛ, n laam wó ja-de n vo n pa Wɛ kaanem tu wom. Wonto de laam wó ja-de o vo kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa.

english_verse: Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: O wó kwei pɛɛre dem o pɔɔre popɔra kadwoŋi se ka taa ye gulim pɛɛre ka pa Wɛ, ye o zwɛ-ka kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne. Pɛɛre dem konto lwom maa ywomma de pae Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
translation_verse: Wodiu pɛɛre delo ta na daare to wó taa ye Aron de o bia bam nyem mo. De maa tiini de ye wose mo, de na nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ wodiu pɛɛra yam wone to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Yeast and honey must never be burned on the altar, so don't ever mix either of these in a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: Abam wolo ná lage se o kwei wodiu pɛɛre o kaane o pa Baŋa Wɛ, se o yé woli sabɔle de wone. Kokuri to, sabɔle dedaane tooro dae se abam ma-te á zwɛ á ke pɛɛre á pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Kotu nam ná lage se o kwei wodiiru telo na lwoori yiga te ke to o pa Baŋa Wɛ, o jege chwoŋa se o woli sabɔle de tooro te wone. Ko nam dae se á kwei wonnu tem konto á zwɛ kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne se te lwom taa ywomma.

english_verse: Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest.
translation_verse: Abam wolo nam ná boŋe se o kwei o kara wodiu kolo na dɛ yiga ko ke to o pa Baŋa Wɛ, se kotu kwei ko bia o nɔ ko wodi-doŋo maŋa ne ye o daare o wɔ de mini.

english_verse: You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: O ta wó gwaane nuga ko wone o daare o kwei talwoŋ-ywoŋa o woli da, se ko taa ye wodiu pɛɛre mo.

english_verse: A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu laam maa wó pɔɔre gulim pɛɛre popɔra ko wone se o kwei o zwɛ o pa Wɛ. Men-bia bam chichworo de nuga kam chichworo dedaane talwoŋ-ywoŋa kam maama mo o jege se o kwei o zwɛ konto, ko na ye wodiu pɛɛre mo ko pae Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane.

english_verse: When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal.
translation_verse: Abam wolo ná boŋe se o ke yazura pɛɛre o kaane o pa Baŋa Wɛ, ye kotu ná kuri na-bala, naa na-choa o vara bam wone, ko wó taa ye kalo na ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to mo.

english_verse: Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Kotu laam maa wó kwei o jeŋa o daŋe varem wom yuu ne ye o daare o gwoni varem wom ba wara-vwei dem ni dem ne. Aron dwi dem kaanem tiina bam maa wó kwei varem wom jana bam ba dole dole kaanem dakaa kam sɛ sena sem yera ne.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: dedaane o tapwale-bia balei bam de lara kalo na meeli da to mo. O ta wó le chwɛ dem kuri seeni mo o woli da.

english_verse: Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
translation_verse: Kaanem tiina bam laam maa wó kwei wonnu tem konto maama ba ja vo ba tiŋi kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne ba zwɛ-te ba woli de zwɛɛm pɛɛre delo na maŋe de wora mini ne to. Pɛɛre dem konto lwom maa ywomma ko pae Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ta wó wane o ma pia, naa boŋo se o ma o ke yazura pɛɛre o pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ko wae ko ye wo-bala naa wo-kana kalo na ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to.

english_verse: If you offer a sheep, you must present it to me at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye pia mo nɔɔno wom jaane o ba, se o ja-ka o jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: O laam maa wó kwei o jeŋa o daŋe ka yuu ne ye o daare o gwoni varem wom ba wara-vwei dem yiga ne. Aron bia bam laam maa wó kwei varem wom jana bam ba dole dole kaanem dakaa kam sɛ sena sem yera ne.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: Ba ta wó le varem wom tapwale-bia balei bam de lara kalo na meeli da to, de chwɛ dem kuri seeni ba woli da.

english_verse: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom laam wó kwei-te o ja o vo o zwɛ kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne, se ko taa ye nɔna mo na ye pɛɛra ya pae Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye boŋo mo nɔɔno jaane o ba se o ma o ke pɛɛre dem konto o pa Baŋa Wɛ,

english_verse: at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: kotu wó kwei o jeŋa mo o daŋe ko yuu ne, ye o daare o gwoni ko ba wara-vwei dem yiga ne. Aron bia bam maa wó kwei boŋo kom jana bam ba dole dole kaanem dakaa kam sɛ sena sem maama yera ne.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: dedaane ko tapwale-bia balei bam de lara kalo na meeli da to. O ta wó le chwɛ dem kuri seeni mo o woli da.

english_verse: One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me. All fat belongs to me.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom laam maa wó kwei-te o ja o vo o zwɛ kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne, se ko taa ye wodiu na ye pɛɛre ko pae Baŋa Wɛ to. Pɛɛre dem konto lwom maa ywomma ko pae Baŋa Wɛ. Varem wom lara kam maama ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo.

english_verse: So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
translation_verse: Abam ná vei á wo jei selo maama ne, á ba jege se á fɔge á di lara naa jana. Abam de á kwaga kam maama jege se á ta‑á tɔge Wɛ ni dem konto se ko taa vei wuu.”

english_verse: This is a sacrifice for sin. So he will lay his hand on the animal's head, before having it killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: O jege se o kwei o jeŋa mo o daŋe ka yuu ne, se o laam gwoni ka ba o go. O wó ke konto ko maŋe de jeiga kalo ba na yeini ba goe zwɛɛm kaanem vara bam Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to mo. Nɔɔno wom kaanem dem konto ye wɛleere saarem kaanem mo.

english_verse: Then a priest will dip a finger in the blood; he will smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom laam maa wó de o noa boŋo kom jana ne, se o ma jana bam o taare zwɛɛm kaanem dakaa kam nyea yana yam. Jana balo na daare to ye se o lwo-ba zwɛɛm kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa ne mo.

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: Offer a sacrifice to ask forgiveness when you sin by accidentally doing something I have told you not to do. When the High Priest Sins The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Ta de Isarele tiina bam we: Abam wolo ná ke woŋo kolo Baŋa Wɛ nia yam na bere we ko chuli to, ye kotu ná wo paale o ke o tusi mo, pa-na se o ke tento:

english_verse: When the high priest sins, he makes everyone else guilty too. And so, he must sacrifice a young bull that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Wɛ kaanem tiina yiga tu wom mo ná ke o tusi konto dwoŋi, pa se o wɛleere jene ba nɔɔna bam maama yuu ne, o wó ja na-bala kalo na ba jege gɛɛ to mo o ba se o ma o ke wɛleere saarem kaanem o pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: The priest will lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay his hand on its head, and kill it there.
translation_verse: O jege se o ja na-bala kam mo o ja o ba wara-vwei dem ni ne se o jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. O laam wó kwei o jeŋa o daŋe ka yuu ne, se o daare o gwoni ka ba dáane.

english_verse: Then, in my presence, he will smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: O ta wó ma jana bam o taare talwoŋa zwɛɛm bimbini na wo wara-vwei dem ne ye de zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to, de nyea yana yam seeni. Jana balo laam na daare to mo, o wó ja-ba o vo o zege wara-vwei ni dem ne ye o daare o lwo-ba zwɛɛm kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa ne.

english_verse: The priest will remove the fat from the bull, just as he does when he sacrifices a bull to ask my blessing. This includes the fat on the insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. He will then send it all up in smoke.
translation_verse: O na wó le wonnu tem konto to ye bedwe de o na yeini o ke tetei de na-bala kalo nɔɔno na jaane o ba se o ma ke yazura pɛɛre o pa Wɛ to. O laam maa wó zwɛ te maama zwɛɛm kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne.

english_verse: The skin and flesh of the bull, together with its legs, insides, and the food still in its stomach, are to be taken outside the camp and burned on a wood fire near the ash heap. When the Whole Nation Sins The Lord said:
translation_verse: kaanem tiina yiga tu wom jege se o kwei te maama na daare to o ja nwoŋi ba tigisim jeiga kam o yi dáa dáa. Jei sem konto wó taa ye pwola kalo ba na kwɛ Wɛ chullu tem ŋwaane ye ba dole zwɛɛm kaanem tentwarem da to. O wó kwei tento maama o ja o vo dáane o zwɛ dɛ selo na jege mini to baŋa ne, ba na dogele tentwarem mɛ to.

english_verse: Once you realize what has happened, you must sacrifice a young bull to ask my forgiveness. Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Ba ná tu ba maane ba tusim dem ni ne, ko jege se ba ja na-bala mo ba ba se ba ma ke wɛleere saarem kaanem ba pa Wɛ. Ba wó kwei-ka ba ja ba vo wara-vwei dem yiga ne.

english_verse: where your tribal leaders will lay their hands on its head, before having it killed in my presence.
translation_verse: Isarele nakwa bam maa wó vo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne ba kwei ba je ba daŋe na-bala kam yuu ne, ye ba dedoa gwoni ka ba o go.

english_verse: The priest will take a bowl of the animal's blood inside the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Kaanem tiina yiga tu wom maa wó lwo na-bala kam jana badwonna o ke zoŋa ne o ja o zo wara-vwei dem wone.

english_verse: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
translation_verse: O laam maa wó kwei o noa o laŋe jana bam, ye o miisi jana bam se ko jeeri Wɛ di-yuu kom gare-jale dem. O jege se o ke konto Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne kuni berepɛ mo.

english_verse: Then, in my presence, he must smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: O ta wó ma jana bam o taare talwoŋa zwɛɛm bimbini delo na wo wara-vwei dem ne ye de zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to, de nyea yana yam seeni. Jana balo laam na daare to mo, o wó ja-ba o vo o zege wara-vwei ni dem ne ye o daare o lwo-ba zwɛɛm kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa ne.

english_verse: After this, the priest will remove the fat from the bull and send it up in smoke on the altar. Finally, he will burn its remains outside the camp, just as he did with the other bull. By this sacrifice the sin of the whole nation will be forgiven. When a Tribal Leader Sins The Lord God said:
translation_verse: O ta jege se o kwei na-bala kam o ja o nwoŋi ba tigisim jeiga kam o vo dáa dáa, ye o daare o zwɛ-ka, nenɛɛne o na ke tei de na-bala kakam kam to. Ko maa ye wɛleere saarem kaanem mo ko pae Isarele nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama.

english_verse: As soon as the leader realizes what has happened, he must sacrifice a goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Ba ná pɛ o maane we o sage chwoŋa, se o ja bo-bala kalo na ba jege gɛɛ to o ba o ke kaanem.

english_verse: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom laam maa wó de o noa boŋo kom jana ne, se o ma jana bam o taare zwɛɛm kaanem dakaa kam nyea yana yam. Jana balo na daare to ye se o lwo-ba zwɛɛm kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa ne mo.

english_verse: Then he must send all of the fat up in smoke, just as he does when a sacrifice is offered to ask my blessing. By this sacrifice the leader's sin will be forgiven. When Ordinary People Sin The Lord said:
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye varem wom lara kam maama, o jege se o zwɛ ka maama mo kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne, nenɛɛne o na zwɛ lara o ma ke yazura pɛɛre dem tei to. Kaanem tu wom wó da chwoŋa kam konto mo o ma le nɔɔno wom lwarem, se Wɛ de kwei o tusim dem o ma chɛ‑o.

english_verse: As soon as you realize what you have done, you must sacrifice a female goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Ba ná pɛ o maane o tusim dem ni ne, se o ja bo-choa kalo na ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to o ba o ke kaanem o wɛleere dem ŋwaane.

english_verse: Lead the goat to the north side of the bronze altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
translation_verse: O jege se o kwei o jeŋa mo o daŋe ka yuu ne, se o laam gwoni ka ba, jeiga kalo ba na yeini ba goe zwɛɛm kaanem vara bam da to.

english_verse: After this, the priest will remove all of the fat, just as he does when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. The priest will then send the fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. This animal is sacrificed so that I will forgive you ordinary people when you sin.
translation_verse: O ta jege se o lɔɔne ko lara kam mo, nenɛɛne o na ke tei dedaane yazura pɛɛre varem lara kam to. O ta wó zwɛ lara kam kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne se ka lwom taa ywomma ko pae Baŋa Wɛ. Kaanem tu wom wó da chwoŋa kam konto o ma le nɔɔno wom lwarem, se Wɛ de kwei o tusim dem o ma chɛ‑o.

english_verse: If you offer a lamb instead of a goat as a sacrifice for sin, it must be a female that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ná kuri pia o ma o ke wɛleere kaanem, kotu wó ja pi-choa mo na ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to o ja o ba.

english_verse: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom laam maa wó de o noa boŋo kom jana ne, se o ma jana bam o taare zwɛɛm kaanem dakaa kam nyea yana yam. Jana balo na daare to ye se o lwo-ba zwɛɛm kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa ne mo.

english_verse: After this, all of the fat must be removed, just as when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. Then the priest will send it up in smoke to me, together with a food offering, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: O ta jege se o lɔɔne pia kam lara kam mo, nenɛɛne o na ke tei dedaane yazura pɛɛre pia lara kam to. O ta wó kwei lara kam o daŋe Baŋa Wɛ pɛɛra yadwonna yam baŋa ne o daare o zwɛ-ka kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne. Kaanem tu wom wó da chwoŋa kam konto o ma le lwarem delo nɔɔno wom na ke to, se Wɛ de kwei o tusim dem o ma chɛ‑o.

english_verse: As soon as you discover that you have committed any of these sins, you must confess what you have done.
translation_verse: Chwei sento maama wone mo, abam wolo ná tu o maane we o sage chwoŋa, se o ta o wɛleera jaja Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: Then you must bring a female sheep or goat to me as the price for your sin. A priest will sacrifice the animal, and you will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Kotu nam wó ja pi-choa naa bo-choa mo o ja o ba o ke wɛleere saarem kaanem o pa Baŋa Wɛ se o ma o ŋwe o wɛleere jene. Kaanem tu wom maa wó kwei varem wom o ma o le kotu lwarem dem Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: Give both birds to the priest, who will offer one as a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness. He will wring its neck without tearing off its head,
translation_verse: Kotu wó ja kunkwona bam o vo o ke kaanem tu wom jeŋa ne. Kaanem tu wom maa wó bobo o kwei dedoa o ma o ke wɛleere saarem kaanem dem. O jege se o bwori ka ba mo se o yé gwori ka yuu.

english_verse: splatter some of its blood on one side of the bronze altar, and drain out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: O ta wó ma ka jana bam badwonna o miisi kaanem dakaa kam saŋa dedoa ne. Jana balo na daare to, se o lwo ba maama o yage kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa ne. Konto ye wɛleere saarem kaanem dem mo.

english_verse: If you are so poor that you cannot afford doves or pigeons, you may bring one kilogram of your finest flour. This is a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, so don't sprinkle olive oil or sweet-smelling incense on it.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ná ba jege kunkwona balei, naa kunkwon-puura balei se o ja o ba, kotu nam wó ja mun-bwei bwɛ selei o ja o ba o ma o ke wɛleere saarem kaanem mo. O nam yé woli nuga naa talwoŋ-ywoŋa de wone, kokuri to, ko ye wɛleere saarem kaanem mo.

english_verse: Give the flour to a priest, who will scoop up a handful and send it up in smoke together with the other offerings. This is a reminder that all of the flour belongs to me.
translation_verse: Kotu wó ja muni dem o vo o ke kaanem tu wom jeŋa ne. Kaanem tu wom wó zwɛ jaguli-yi se de taa ye gulim pɛɛre de pa Wɛ mo. O wó zwɛ-de kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne o woli de wodiu pɛɛra yadwonna na zwɛ ya pae Baŋa Wɛ to. Konto ye wɛleere saarem kaanem dem mo.

english_verse: By offering this sacrifice, the priest pays the price for any of these sins you may have committed. The priest gets to keep the rest of the flour, just as he does with grain sacrifices. Sacrifices To Make Things Right (Leviticus
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom wó tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo, se o le nɔɔno wom lwarem dem Wɛ yiga ne, se Wɛ de yage o tusim dem o ma chɛ‑o. Muni delo maama ná daare, de ye kaanem tu wom nyem mo, nenɛɛne wodiu pɛɛre ná daare, ko de na ye o nyem tei to.” Wɛleere jene kaanem

english_verse: The Lord told Moses what the people must do to make things right when they find out they have cheated the Lord without meaning to: If this happens, you must either sacrifice a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay the price of a ram with the official money used by the priests.
translation_verse: “Abam wolo maama ná sage chwoŋa ye o ná pini Baŋa Wɛ wonnu telo na ye wose to baŋa ne, ye o wo paale o ke o tusi konto, kotu wó ja pi-bala kalo na ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to mo o ja o ba o pa Baŋa Wɛ se o ŋwe o wɛleere dem jene. Pi-bala kam sabu wó maŋe de lu-nyenno telo dunni na tɔge wara-jei sem maŋem chekke to. Konto ye wɛleere jene kaanem dem mo.

english_verse: The next morning you will dress in your priestly clothes, including your linen underwear. Then clean away the ashes left by the sacrifices and pile them beside the altar.
translation_verse: Tega ná poore, kaanem tu wom wó zo o gare-bwora kam de o gare-kuri-kukua kam, ba na mɛ gare-fefale ba sɔ-te to mo. O laam maa wó pɛ tentwarem delo varem wom na zwɛ o daare kaanem dakaa kam ne to, se o ta la-de o tiŋi kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa ne.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses what the people must do when they commit other sins against the Lord: You have sinned if you rob or cheat someone, if you keep back money or valuables left in your care, or if you find something and claim not to have it.
translation_verse: naa o ná nɛ woŋo kolo na jei to ye o fɔ vwa we o wo nɛ-ko, naa o ná fɔge vwa wonnu tedwonna ŋwaane pa se o tusi ne nabiina na yeini ba tusi tei maama to.

english_verse: In addition, you must either bring to the priest a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay him for one. The priest will then offer it as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven for what you did wrong. Daily Sacrifices (Exodus
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom wó tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo se o le nɔɔno wom lwarem dem Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Wɛ ta wó yage wɛleera yalo maama o na ke konto dwoŋi to o ma chɛ‑o.” Wɛ kaanem tiina bam totoŋa Vara zwɛɛm kaanem

english_verse: This sacrifice is very holy, and only the priests may have any part of it.
translation_verse: Baaro wolo maama na nwoŋi kaanem tiina dwi dem wone to jege chwoŋa se o di wɛleere saarem varem nɔna yam mo. Ya nam tiini ya ye wose mo.

english_verse: If the meat was cooked in a clay pot, the pot must be destroyed, but if it was cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
translation_verse: Ba ná kwei dɔgɔ kambia ba ma saŋe nɔna yam, se ba laam lɔ-ka. Ko nam ná ye channa kambia mo ba mɛ ba saŋe, se ba fɔge ba titigi-ka se ka gɔ lanyerane, ye ba daare ba seeri.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons how to offer the daily sacrifices that are sent up in smoke to please the Lord: You must put the animal for the sacrifice on the altar in the evening and let it stay there all night. But make sure the fire keeps burning.
translation_verse: “Ta n bere Aron de o bu-baara bam amo nia yanto we: Zwɛɛm kaanem dem jege se de ke tento mo. Ba na zwɛ varem wolo ba kaane ba pa Wɛ to jege se o maŋe kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne mo, se o zwɛ tete dem maama wone se tega laam ba ka poore. Abam nam wó pa se kaanem dakaa kam mini dem taa di taa mo.

english_verse: The fire must never go out, so put wood on it each morning. After this, you are to lay an animal on the altar next to the fat that you sacrifice to ask my blessing. Then send it all up in smoke to me.
translation_verse: Kaanem dakaa kam baŋa mini dem dae se de dwei. Zezeŋa maama ne kaanem tu wom jege se o woli dɛ mo mini dem ne se de taa di. O laam maa wó tigisi zwɛɛm kaanem varem wom mini dem baŋa ne, se o daare o zwɛ varem lara kalo na ye yazura pɛɛre ka pa Wɛ to.

english_verse: The altar fire must always be kept burning—it must never go out. Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord The Lord said:
translation_verse: Mini dem jege se de taa di mo taa, se de yé dwei kɔtaa! Wodiu pɛɛre kaanem

english_verse: When someone offers a sacrifice to give thanks to me, the priests from Aaron's family must bring it to the front of the bronze altar,
translation_verse: Wodiu pɛɛre kaanem dem jege se de ke tento mo. Aron bu-baara bam mo wó ja pɛɛre dem konto ba vo kaanem dakaa kam yiga ne se ba kwei-de ba pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: where one of them will scoop up a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense on it. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, he will lay all of this on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Ba wolo na zege se o toŋe kaanem totoŋa to maa wó zwɛ pɛɛre dem muni de nuga o ja-bɔŋɔ ne, o woli de talwoŋ-ywoŋa kam maama. O wó kwei pɛɛre dem popɔra kanto mo o zwɛ kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne se ka taa ye gulim pɛɛre ka pa Wɛ. Pɛɛre dem konto lwom maa ywomma de pae Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: The rest of it is to be baked without yeast and eaten by the priests in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent. This bread is very holy, just like the sacrifices for sin or the sacrifices for making things right, and I have given this part to the priests from what is offered to me on the altar.
translation_verse: Ba jege se ba kwei muni dem ba ma ba wɔ bworobworo, ye sabɔle tere ko wone. Kokuri to, pɛɛre dem de ye wose mo, ne wɛleere saarem kaanem dem de wɛleere jene kaanem dem de na ye tei to. Baŋa Wɛ pɔɔre wodiu kom konto o wodiu pɛɛra yam wone mo o pa kaanem tiina bam.

english_verse: Only the men in Aaron's family are allowed to eat this bread, and they must go through a ceremony to be made holy before touching it. This law will never change. When Priests Are Ordained
translation_verse: Aron diga kam baara maama mo jege chwoŋa se ba di-ko. Ni dem konto wó taa wora taa ko pae Aron de o kwaga kam, se ba wane ba jwoŋi ba nyem Baŋa Wɛ wodiu pɛɛra yam wone. Wolo maama nam ná dwei wodiu kom konto, kotu de pwɛ mo amo ŋwaane.”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to Moses
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta Moses o we:

english_verse: mixed with olive oil and cooked in a shallow pan. The bread must then be crumbled into small pieces and sent up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: O ta wó woli nuga mo muni dem ne, ye o daare o kware-de luu baŋa ne. O laam wó mumugi wodiu kom o ma ke wodiu pɛɛre o pa Baŋa Wɛ se de lwom taa ywomma de pa‑o.

english_verse: Each of Aaron's descendants who is ordained as a priest must perform this ceremony and make sure that the bread is completely burned on the altar. None of it may be eaten! Sacrifices for Sin (Leviticus
translation_verse: Muni pɛɛre delo Wɛ kaanem tu na yeini o ke to, ko dae se o di wodiu kom de fenfee de. Ko fe se o zwɛ ko maama mo kula.” Wɛleere saarem kaanem

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta Moses o we:

english_verse: how the priests from Aaron's family were to offer the sacrifice for sin: This sacrifice is very sacred, and the animal must be killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: “Ta de Aron de o bia bam we: Wɛleere saarem kaanem dem jege se de ke tento mo. Ba wó go wɛleere saarem varem wom ba pa Baŋa Wɛ jeiga kalo ne ba na yeini ba go zwɛɛm kaanem varem wom da to mo. Kokuri, kaanem dem konto tiini de ye wose mo.

english_verse: The priest who offers this sacrifice must eat it in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wolo nam ná ke kaanem dem konto, o wó di varem wom wara-vwei dem konkɔlɔ kom ne mɛ na ye wose to mo.

english_verse: and anyone or anything that touches the meat will be holy. If any of the animal's blood is splattered on the clothes of the priest, they must be washed in a holy place.
translation_verse: Kolo maama ná dwei varem wom konto, ko de pwɛ mo amo ŋwaane. Varem wom jana ná taŋe gɔrɔ kolo, se á maŋe jei selo na ye wose to wone á zare-ko.

english_verse: None of the meat may be eaten from the sacrifices for sin that require blood to be brought into the sacred tent. These sacrifices must be completely burned.
translation_verse: Ko daare ko ná ye wɛleere saarem varem wolo jana ba na jaane ba zo wara-vwei dem wone se ba le lwarem Wɛ yiga ne to, á ba jege chwoŋa se á di varem wom konto. Ko ye se á zwɛ o maama á pa Baŋa Wɛ mo.”

english_verse: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke to me.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom maa wó zwɛ wonnu tem konto maama kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne, se te taa ye pɛɛre te pae Baŋa Wɛ. Konto ye wɛleere jene kaanem mo.

english_verse: Give me one loaf or wafer from each of these four kinds of bread, after which they will belong to the priest who splattered the blood against the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Kotu laam wó le bworobworo dwia yam konto maama wone dedoa dedoa o ba o ma ke kaanem o pa Baŋa Wɛ. Bworobwooru tem konto wó taa ye kaanem tu wolo na kwei yazura kaanem varem wom jana bam o dole dole kaanem dakaa kam yera ne to nyem mo.

english_verse: Don't eat any of the meat that has touched something unclean. Instead, burn it. The rest of the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean and acceptable to me.
translation_verse: Nɔna yam ná dwei woŋo kolo maama na jege digiru Wɛ chullu tem seeni to, ko dae se á di-ya. Á jege se á zwɛ nɔna yam konto mo. Ko daare ko ná ye nɔna yadwonna yam, wolo maama na kwɛ o tete Wɛ ŋwaane to jege chwoŋa se o di-ya.

english_verse: The sacrifice to make things right is very sacred.
translation_verse: “Wɛleere jene kaanem dem jege se de ke tento mo. Kaanem dem konto tiini de ye wose mo.

english_verse: The animal must be killed in the same place where the sacrifice to please me is killed, and the animal's blood must be splattered against the four sides of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Ba wó go wɛleere jene kaanem varem wom jeiga kalo ba na yeini ba go zwɛɛm kaanem varem wom da to mo. Kaanem tu wom laam wó kwei varem wom jana mo o dole dole kaanem dakaa kam sɛ sena sem ne.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: dedaane o tapwale-bia balei bam de lara kalo na meeli da to mo, ko ta woli de o chwɛ dem kuri dem seeni.

english_verse: This sacrifice for making things right is very holy. Only the priests may eat it, and they must eat it in a holy place.
translation_verse: Baaro wolo maama na nwoŋi kaanem tiina dwi dem wone to jege chwoŋa se o di varem wom nɔna yam. Ba nam jege se ba di-ya jeiga kalo na ye wose to ne mo, ya na tiini ya ye wose to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The ceremony for this sacrifice and the one for sin are the same, and the meat may be eaten only by the priest who performs this ceremony of forgiveness.
translation_verse: Wɛleere jene kaanem dem dedaane wɛleere saarem kaanem dem maama jege chulu dedoa mo. Kaanem tu wolo na ke-ya o ma le nɔɔno lwarem Wɛ yiga ne to mo jege chwoŋa se o di ya nɔna yam.

english_verse: In fact, the priest who offers a sacrifice to please me may keep the skin of the animal,
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem dem, Kaanem tu wolo na kaane-de o pa Wɛ to mo tei varem wom tankɔlɔ kom.

english_verse: All other grain sacrifices—with or without olive oil in them—are to be divided equally among the priests of Aaron's family. Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ko daare muni pɛɛra yadwonna yam yalo na ye wodi-gwei to, Aron bu-baara bam maama wó chɛ-te mo ba pa daane se ko taa mae daane, nenɛɛne nuga ná woli muni dem wone, naa ka ná wo woli da de. Yazura pɛɛre kaanem

english_verse: Here are the instructions for offering a sacrifice to ask my blessing:
translation_verse: Yazura pɛɛre kaanem delo nɔɔno na wó ke o pa Baŋa Wɛ to jege se de ke tento mo.

english_verse: If you offer it to give thanks, you must offer some bread together with it. Use the finest flour to make three kinds of bread without yeast—two in the form of loaves mixed with olive oil and one in the form of thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná ke pɛɛre konto dwoŋi se o ma ke Wɛ lei, kotu jege se o kwei bworobworo o ja o ba o woli de kaanem dem varem wom. O wó gwaane muni de nuga mo o ma ke bworobworo kolo sabɔle na tere ko wone to. O ta wó kwei muni dem o ma wɔ bworobworo-memene o daare o ma nuga o taare taare de maama. O daa ta wó kwei mun-bwei mo o gwaane de nuga o ma wɔ bworobworo dwi dedwoŋi.

english_verse: When you offer an animal to ask a blessing from me or to thank me, the meat belongs to you, but it must be eaten the same day.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye varem wom tete nɔna yam, ba jege se ba di ya maama dɛ delo wone ba na ke kaanem dem to mo. Ba yé pa se tega poore ye ya ta wora.

english_verse: It is different with the sacrifices you offer when you make me a promise or voluntarily give me something. The meat from those sacrifices may be kept and eaten the next day,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ná ke yazura pɛɛre kaanem ni-gwonim ŋwaane, naa ko ye o wo-ywoŋo pɛɛre mo, ba wó di varem wom nɔna yam dɛ dem ba na ke kaanem dem to wone, ba jege chwoŋa se ba tiŋi nɔna yalo ba na di ba daare to se tega ná poore, se ba di-ya.

english_verse: but any that is left over must be destroyed. If you eat any of it after the second day, your sacrifice will be useless and unacceptable, and you will be both disgusting and guilty.
translation_verse: Da yatɔ dɛ dem ne, yazura kaanem dem nɔna yam ná daare ye nɔɔno ná di-ya, Baŋa Wɛ bá sɛ o jwoŋi kotu pɛɛre dem. Kaanem dem bá taa jege nyɔɔre de pa wolo na ke-de to. De jigi wo-zɔɔne mo Wɛ tei ne, ye kotu maŋe se o na waarem.

english_verse: But don't eat any of this meat if you have become unclean by touching something unclean from a human or an animal or from any other creature. If you do, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Ko ta woli da, nɔɔno wolo ná dwei woŋo kolo na jege digiru Wɛ chullu tem seeni to, ko ná maŋe ko ye nabiinu wo-digiru, naa varem wo-digiru, naa wo-zɔɔne delo Wɛ na chuli to, ye o ná tɔge o di kaanem dem nɔna yam, ba jege se ba le kotu de se o daa yé tɔge o woli Isarele dwi dem wone mo.” Wɛ chuli se Isarele tiina bam di jana dedaane lara

english_verse: to say to the people: Don't eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats.
translation_verse: “Ta n bere Isarele tiina bam we: Yé di-na lara kalo na wo naane yera ne to, naa pei yera ne to, naa bone yera ne to.

english_verse: If one of your animals dies or is killed by some wild animal, you may do anything with its fat except eat it.
translation_verse: Á vara bam dedoa ná tege o tete toone, naa kago-vara ná tore‑o, á jege chwoŋa se á kwei o lara kam á ke kolo maama á na lage to, se á nam yé di-ka.

english_verse: If you eat the fat of an animal that can be used as a sacrifice to me, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Wolo ná di vara balo dwi na maŋe se ba ma ba ke wodiu pɛɛre ba pa Baŋa Wɛ to lara, ba jege se ba le kotu se o daa yé tɔge o woli Isarele dwi dem wone mo.

english_verse: And no matter where you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal,
translation_verse: Abam ná vei á zoore jei selo maama ne, yé fɔge á di-na varem jana, naa zuna jana.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de Moses o we:

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: If you want to offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, you must bring the part to be burned and lay it on the bronze altar. But you must first lift up the choice ribs with their fat to show that the offering is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Kotu nam wó ja-de de o tete je mo o ba o ke wodiu pɛɛre o pa Baŋa Wɛ. O wó kwei varem wom lara kam de o nyɔɔne seeni nɔna yam, o zeiŋi-te wɛɛne se te taa ye pɛɛre te pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: A priest from Aaron's family will then send the fat up in smoke, but the ribs belong to the priests.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom maa wó zwɛ varem wom lara kam kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne o pa Wɛ, se ko ná ye varem wom nyɔɔne dem, de ye Aron de o bia bam nyem mo.

english_verse: The upper joint of the right hind leg is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the animal.
translation_verse: Ko ye kaanem tu wolo na kwei varem wom lara de o jana bam o ma o ke yazura kaanem dem to mo wó jwoŋi-de.

english_verse: These are the ceremonies for sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessing or his forgiveness, as well as the ceremonies for those sacrifices that demand a payment and for the sacrifices that are offered when priests are ordained.
translation_verse: Chullu tem konto mo wora kaanem dwi dwi ŋwaane. Ko maa ye zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem dem, de wodiu pɛɛre kaanem dem, de wɛleere saarem kaanem dem, de wɛleere jene kaanem dem, de kaanem tiina tiŋim kaanem dem, dedaane yazura pɛɛre kaanem dem.

english_verse: While Moses and the people of Israel were in the desert at Mount Sinai, the Lord commanded them to start offering these sacrifices.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem na kwei nia yanto o pa Moses se Isarele tiina bam taa tɔge-ya ba ma kwei ba pɛɛra yam ba ke kaanem ba pa‑o to, de ba déem wo Sinayi Peo kom teiŋa ne mo kagoa kam yuu ne.

english_verse: Moses lifted up the choice ribs of the ram to show that they were dedicated to the Lord. This was the part that the Lord had said Moses could have.
translation_verse: Moses laam ma kwei pi-bea kam nyɔɔne dem o zeiŋi wɛɛne se de taa ye pɛɛre de pae Baŋa Wɛ. Wonto tete popɔra mo konto o na jege chwoŋa se o le-ka kaanem tiina kwɛɛm pi-bea kam wone, ne Baŋa Wɛ ya na pɛ‑o ni se o ke tei to.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta Moses o we:

english_verse: he said, “We are here to follow the Lord's instructions.”
translation_verse: O ma ta de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ ni delo se de ke to mo tento.”

english_verse: After Moses told Aaron and his sons to step forward, he told them to wash themselves.
translation_verse: Moses ma pa se Aron de o bia bam nwoŋi ba zege, ye o daare o pa ba swɛ ba yera ba kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: He put the priestly shirt and robe on Aaron and wrapped the sash around his waist. Then he put the sacred vest on Aaron and fastened it with the finely woven belt.
translation_verse: O laam ma kwei kaanem gare-dedɔrɔ kom o zo Aron. O ma kwei vovoa kam o vɔ Aron teiŋa ne, ye o daare o pa o zo gare-bwora kam. O ma kwei gare-wogo kom o zo‑o ye o ta kwei ko teiŋa vovoa kam o vɔ o ke da.

english_verse: Next, he put on Aaron the sacred breastpiece that was used in finding out what the Lord wanted his people to do.
translation_verse: O ta ma kwei nyɔɔne gare-pale dem o zo‑o ye o daare o ke Yurim de Tumim kandwa yam de gare-fɛɛla wone.

english_verse: He placed the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban was the narrow strip of thin gold as a sign of his dedication to the Lord.
translation_verse: O déem ta kwei yuu gare-yi dem mo o ba o yuu ne. O ma daare o kwei sabu-seŋa wo-pelɔgɔ kolo na bere we kaanem tu wom ye Wɛ nyem to o lei vovoa kam o tiri dem seeni, se ko tɔge ni delo Baŋa Wɛ ya na pɛ Moses se o ke to.

english_verse: Moses then dedicated the sacred tent and everything in it to the Lord by sprinkling them with some of the oil for ordination.
translation_verse: Moses déem ma kwei Wɛ swolim nuga kam o lwo o yage Wɛ wara-vwei dem maama de wonnu telo maama na wo de wone to yera ne, se te taa ye te yera Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: He also poured some of the oil on Aaron's head to dedicate him to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye Aron, Moses déem lwogi Wɛ swolim nuga kam wonto yuu ne mo o tiŋi‑o Wɛ kaanem totoŋa ŋwaane, se o de taa ye Wɛ nyem.

english_verse: Moses led out the bull that was to be sacrificed for sin, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Moses ma ja nabea kam ba na wó kwei ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem dem to o ja o nwoŋi. Aron de o bia bam de ma daŋe ba je ka yuu ne.

english_verse: After it was killed, Moses dipped a finger in the blood and smeared some of it on each of the four corners of the bronze altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the altar. This purified the altar and made it a fit place for offering the sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Moses ma gwoni ka ba. O ma lwoori ka jana bam badwonna o daare o ma o noa o laŋe-ba o ma o taare kaanem dakaa kam ka nyea yana yam seeni se o kwɛ-ka Wɛ ŋwaane. O laam ma lwo jana balo na daare to kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa ne. O na ke tei maama to pɛ se kaanem dakaa kam ye wose mo, pa se ka maŋe de wɛleere saarem totoŋa.

english_verse: Moses then took the fat on the bull's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and sent them up in smoke on the altar fire.
translation_verse: Moses ta ma lɔɔne nabea kam lara kalo na meeli ka wo-zela yam yera ne to, o woli de ka chwɛ dem kuri seeni dem, de ka tapwale-bia bam de lara kalo na meeli da to maama. O déem ma zwɛ te maama kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne.

english_verse: Finally, he took the skin and the flesh of the bull, together with the food still in its stomach, and burned them outside the camp, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye nabea kam tankɔlɔ kom, de ka nɔna yam, de ka wo-zela yalo na daare to, o jaane-te o nwoŋi dáa ne mo, ye o zwɛ-te se ko tɔge ni delo Baŋa Wɛ ya na pɛ‑o se o ke to.

english_verse: Moses led out the ram for the sacrifice to please the Lord. After Aaron and his sons had laid their hands on its head,
translation_verse: Moses ta ma ja pi-bea kalo ba na wó ma ba ke zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem dem to o nwoŋi o zege. Aron de o bu-baara bam de ma kwei ba je ba daŋe ka yuu ne.

english_verse: Moses killed the ram and splattered its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: O laam ma gwoni ka ba. Moses ma lwoori ka jana bam o dole dole kaanem dakaa kam sɛ sena sem maama ne.

english_verse: Moses had the animal cut up, and he washed its insides and hind legs. Then he laid the head, the fat, and the rest of the ram on the altar and sent them up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. All this was done just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: O ma zare ka wo-zela yam de ka nɛ sem yiga se o laam zwɛ te maama kula kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne se ko tɔge ni delo Baŋa Wɛ ya na pɛ‑o se o ke tei to. Zwɛɛm kaanem dem konto maa ye wodiu pɛɛre de pa Baŋa Wɛ. De lwom maa ywomma de pa‑o.

english_verse: Moses led out the ram for the ceremony of ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head,
translation_verse: Moses daa ma ja pi-bea kadwoŋi kam na wora kaanem tiina kwɛɛm ŋwaane to o ja o nwoŋi. Aron de o bia bam de ma kwei ba je ba daŋe ka yuu ne.

english_verse: and it was killed. Moses smeared some of its blood on Aaron's right earlobe, some on his right thumb, and some on the big toe of his right foot.
translation_verse: O ma gwoni ka ba. Moses ma daare o lwoori ka jana bam badwonna o taŋe Aron jazem zwɛ dem ne, de o jazem no-kweo kom, dedaane o jazem namimbu-kweo kom.

english_verse: He took the animal's fat tail, the fat on its insides, and the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right hind leg.
translation_verse: Moses ma lɔɔne pia kam lara kam maama, de ka nabili-bwogo kom, de lara kalo na meeli o wo-zela yam yera ne to, o ta woli chwɛ dem kuri seeni dedaane tapwale-bia balei bam de lara kalo na meeli da to. O déem ta kwei ka jazem chwei dem mo o woli da.

english_verse: Then he took from a basket some of each of the three kinds of bread that had been made without yeast and had been dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: O laam ma kwei tetɔgɔ kom de ko bworobworo-memene selo na ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem to o le bworobworo dwia yatɔ yam wone dedoa dedoa, ye sabɔle tere te wone. O laam ma kwei te maama o daŋe lara kam de pia kam jazem chwei dem baŋa ne.

english_verse: Moses placed the bread on top of the meat and gave it all to Aaron and his sons, who lifted it up to show that it was dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: O ma kwei wonnu tem konto maama o ke Aron de o bia bam je sem ne se ba zeiŋi-te wɛɛne se te taa ye pɛɛre te pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: After this, Moses placed it on the fires of the altar and sent it up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. This was part of the ordination ceremony.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne mo Moses jwoŋi-te ba jeŋa ne o daare o daŋe-te zwɛɛm kaanem varem wolo na wo kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne to o zwɛ, se ko taa ye kaanem tiina kwɛɛm kaanem. Kaanem dem konto ye wodiu pɛɛre mo ko pae Baŋa Wɛ. De lwom maa ywomma de pa‑o.

english_verse: Finally, Moses sprinkled the priestly clothes of Aaron and his sons with some of the oil for ordination and with some of the blood from the altar. So Aaron and his sons, together with their priestly clothes, were dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Konto na ti to, mo Moses kwei Wɛ swolim nuga kam dedaane jana balo na wo kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne to badwonna o miisi Aron de o gwaaro tem yera ne. O ta ma miisi-te Aron bia bam de ba de gwaaro tem yera ne. Keim dem konto déem pɛ se Aron de o bia bam dedaane ba gwaaro tem maama ye te yera mo Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: Moses said to Aaron and his sons: The Lord told me that you must boil this meat at the entrance to the sacred tent and eat it there with the bread.
translation_verse: Moses laam ma ta Aron de o bu-baara bam o we, “Kwei-na kaanem dem nɔna yalo na daare to á vo á saŋe wara-vwei dem ni ne, se á maŋe dáane á di-ya de bworobworo kolo amo na le tetɔgɔ kom wone to, nenɛɛne Wɛ na pɛ ni we, Aron de o bia bam jege chwoŋa se ba di-ya tei to.

english_verse: and stay near the entrance to the sacred tent until the ordination ceremony ends seven days from now.
translation_verse: Nam maŋe-na wara-vwei dem ni ne da yarepɛ, se chulu kolo na ye abam kwɛɛm ŋwaane to ná ti, se á nwoŋi pwooni.

english_verse: We have obeyed the Lord in everything that has been done today, so that your sins may be forgiven.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ ni we dé ke tento mo se dé wane dé le abam lwarem dem o yiga ne.

english_verse: The Lord has told me that you must stay near the entrance to the tent for seven days and nights, or else you will die.
translation_verse: Abam jege se á maŋe wara-vwei dem ni ne da yarepɛ, wea de tete maama, ko na ye Wɛ ni dem to ŋwaane. Wolo nam ná ve ye o nwoŋi pwooni, kotu jege se o te mo. Mo ni delo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ amo to.”

english_verse: Aaron and his sons obeyed everything that the Lord had told Moses they must do.
translation_verse: Aron de o bu-baara bam de déem ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Moses ni se ba ke to.

english_verse: Then he said to Aaron: Find a young bull and a ram that have nothing wrong with them. Offer the bull to the Lord as a sacrifice for sin and the ram as a sacrifice to please him.
translation_verse: O ma ta Aron o we, “Beeri na-bala na ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to se n ma‑n ke wɛleere saarem kaanem n pa Baŋa Wɛ, se n daare n beeri pi-bala na ba jege gɛɛ to de se n ma n ke zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem n pa‑o.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that they must offer sacrifices as well. They must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to please the Lord. The bull and the ram must be a year old and have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Nam ta de Isarele tiina bam se ba beeri bo-bala wɛleere saarem kaanem ŋwaane. Ba ta maa wó beeri na-bala na ye bene, de pi-bala na ye bene to mo se ba ma ba ke zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem. Te nam ba jege se gɛɛ taa wo te yera ne.

english_verse: Then the people must offer a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing and also a grain sacrifice mixed with oil. Do this, because the Lord will appear to you today.
translation_verse: Ba ta wó beeri nabea, de pi-bea mo se ba ma ba ke yazura pɛɛre kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ba ta wó ja muni pɛɛre delo nuga na viiri de wone to se ba ma ba ke kaanem. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ zem wó ba o veere o tete ba tetare ne.”

english_verse: After the animals and the grain had been brought to the front of the sacred tent, and the people were standing there in the presence of the Lord,
translation_verse: Ba ma seene ba ja kolo maama Moses na pɛ-ba ni se ba ja ba ba to ba jeeri Wɛ wara-jei sem manchwo-peena yam ne. Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama de ma fɔɔre ba yi jei sem se ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Moses said: The Lord has ordered you to do this, so that he may appear to you in all of his glory.
translation_verse: Moses déem ma ta de-ba o we, “Tento maama tɔge ni delo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ abam se á ke to, se o laam ba o veere o tete de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom abam yiga ne.”

english_verse: Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the bull that was to be the sacrifice for his sins.
translation_verse: Aron ma seene o yi kaanem dakaa kam ye o kwei na-bala kalo na wora o tete wɛleere saarem ŋwaane to o gwoni ka ba.

english_verse: His sons brought him the blood. He dipped a finger in it, smeared some on the four corners of the bronze altar, and poured out the rest at its foot.
translation_verse: O bia bam ma ja ka jana ba yi o tei ba pa‑o, ye o kwei o noa o laŋe jana bam. O laam ma kwei-ba o taare kaanem dakaa kam nyea yam, ye o daare o lwo balo na daare to kaanem dakaa kam teiŋa ne.

english_verse: But he sent up in smoke the fat, the kidneys, and the lower part of the liver, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
