translation_verse: Kohafe tiina bam tete nam ba jege chwoŋa se ba zo wara-vwei dem wone ba taa kare ba nii de yera zela yam, se ko yé pa ba te.” Gereson tiina bam taane

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem tage de Moses o we:

english_verse: for carrying the curtains of the sacred tent, its two outer coverings, the curtain for the entrance to the tent,
translation_verse: Ba wó taa zeŋe wara-vwei dem tete, dedaane gare-jala yalo na kwoli-de to, de twan-nyenno telo na daŋe da to, de gare-jale delo na leigi vwei dem ni ne to,

english_verse: the curtains hanging around the courtyard of the tent, and the curtain and ropes for the entrance to the courtyard. The Gershonites are to do whatever needs to be done to take care of these things,
translation_verse: de gare-jala yalo na kwoli wara-jei sem konkɔlɔ kom mɛ vwei dem tete de kaanem dakaa kam na wora to maama, de konkɔlɔ kom ni gare-jale dem, dedaane gwaaro tem konto ŋone de te yera zela maama. Gereson tiina bam mo wó taa toŋe wonnu tem konto maama totoŋa yam.

english_verse: These are the duties of the Gershonites at the sacred tent, and Ithamar son of Aaron will make sure they do their work. The Duties of the Merarite Clans
translation_verse: Mo totoŋa yalo Gereson dwi tiina bam na jege se ba taa toŋa wara-vwei dem ŋwaane to. Kaanem tu Aron bu Itamara nam mo wó taa nii-ba se ba taa toŋe ba totoŋa yam.” Merari tiina bam taane

english_verse: as well as the posts that support the courtyard, together with their stands, tent pegs, and ropes. The Merarites are to be told exactly what objects they are to carry,
translation_verse: de da-dɛɛra yalo na kaare wara-jei konkɔlɔ kom to, de ya zegem wonnu tem, de paara yam maama, de ŋone sem, de zela yalo maama na wora totoŋa yam konto ŋwaane to. Á wó pa nɔɔno maama ni se o lɔre woŋo de woŋo kolo o na wó zeŋe to.

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelite leaders obeyed the Lord and counted the Levi tribe by families and clans, to find out how many men there were between the ages of
translation_verse: Ba déem jeeli-ba se ko tɔge de Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo. Moses ma pa se nɔɔno maama lɔre o totoŋe dem de woŋo kolo o na wó zeŋe to. Konto to, ba déem jeeli Levi tiina bam maama ni nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Moses ni se o ke tei to mo.

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel, “Put out of the camp everyone who has leprosy or a bodily discharge or who has touched a dead body. Now that I live among my people, their camp must be kept clean.”

translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem konto ye ba pa ba maama nwoŋi ba vo dáa. Tusim jene taane

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you commit a crime against someone, you have sinned against me.

english_verse: If the victim has no relative who can accept this money, it belongs to me and will be paid to the priest. In addition to that payment, you must take a ram for the priest to sacrifice so your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom nam ná tega ye o wo daare o yera nɔɔno se kotu jwoŋi tusim jene dem sabu kom konto, se á pa ko taa ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem. Wolo na tusi to wó ŋwe-ko o pa kaanem tu wom mo. O ta wó ja pi-bea o woli da o vo, se kaanem tu wom kwei-ka o ke kaanem se o le konto tu tusim dem Wɛ yiga ne o yage.

english_verse: When you make a donation to the sacred tent, that money belongs only to the priest, and each priest will keep what is given to him. A Suspicious Husband
translation_verse: Nɔɔno maama wae o kuri pɛɛra yalo o na wó pa Wɛ to. Kaanem tu maama nam wó taa tei pɛɛra yalo ba na kwei ba pa‑o to mo.” Baara de kaana tetare laŋa taane

english_verse: The priest will lead the woman to my altar and make her stand there.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom maa wó pa se kaane wom ba o zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: He will then pour sacred water into a clay jar and stir in some dust from the floor of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: O ta maa wó mɔ na balo na ye wose to o lwo o ke kasantana wone. O ta wó pɛ wara-jei sem tega kasolo ye o daare o yuŋi o viiri na bam wone.

english_verse: Next, he will remove her veil, then hand her the barley offering, and say, “If you have been faithful to your husband, this water won't harm you. translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se sensɔle-balɔrɔ taa tɔge‑m n dwi tiina bam wone, se n dwi tiina de sɔɔle lwarem ba yage n yera ne. english_verse: The priest will write these curses on special paper and wash them off into the bitter water,
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom laam wó popone sensɔle-balɔrɔ kom konto o ke tɔnɔ wone. O maa wó seeri poponem dem o yage na-chɛɛra bam wone,

english_verse: He will take the barley offering from her and lift it up in dedication to me, the Lord. Then he will place it on my altar
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom ta wó jwoŋi muni pɛɛre delo na wora kazwe ŋwaane to kaane wom jeŋa ne, se o zeiŋi-de wɛɛne o pa Baŋa Wɛ. O laam maa wó kwei-de o ja vo o twɛ kaanem dakaa kam.

english_verse: But if she is innocent, her body will not be harmed, and she will still be able to have children.
translation_verse: O nam ná wo ke o chɔge ye o ba jege digiru Wɛ chullu tem seeni, kolokolo bá ke‑o. Chwoŋa ta wó taa wora se o lo bia.

english_verse: This is the ceremony that must take place at my altar when a husband suspects that his wife has been unfaithful. The priest must tell the woman to stand in my presence and carefully follow these instructions.
translation_verse: naa o baro wom boboŋa ná jege‑o ya daana konto dwoŋi, ye o yeiri chega kam o tia, á wó ke konto mo. Kaanem tu wom wó pa se kaane wom ba o zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se o daare o ke chullu tem konto maama o yera ne.

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: If any of you want to dedicate yourself to me by vowing to become a Nazirite,
translation_verse: “Ta de Isarele tiina bam we: Abam baaro wolo maama naa kaane ná gwoni ni se o taa ye Naziri tu ye o pɔɔre o tete o ke Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ne,

english_verse: you must no longer drink any wine or beer or use any kind of vinegar. Don't drink grape juice or eat grapes or raisins—
translation_verse: kotu nam taa yei ko ni ne se o daa yé nyɔ sana dwi dwi. Ko ná ye sa-dɛɛra, naa sa-nyɔna, naa Vini tio nyoa, se o yé zaŋe o nyɔ! O ta yé di Vini tio-bia, ba ná maŋe ba ko de.

english_verse: During the time that you are a Nazirite, you must never go close to a dead body,
translation_verse: Da yam konto ne o ta ba jege se o yi too yera, o na kwei o tete o ke Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: not even that of your father, mother, brother, or sister. That would make you unclean. Your hair is the sign that you are dedicated to me, so remain holy.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam maama wone o na pɔɔre o tete konto to, o ye wose mo Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: If someone suddenly dies near you, your hair is no longer sacred, and you must shave it seven days later during the ceremony to make you clean.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ná pɔpɔ o te Naziri tu jeŋa ne mo, ko bere we o ni-gwonim dem mo chɔge, pa se o yu-ywei sem daa ba jege kuri. Kotu jege se o cheigi da yarepɛ wɛɛne mo, se o kwɛ o tete de chullu tem, ye o fane o yu-ywei sem.

english_verse: Then on the next day, bring two doves or two pigeons to the priest at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Tega na wó poore se ko taa ye da nana dɛ to, se o ja kunkwona balei, naa kunkwon-puura balei o vo wara-jei sem ne o pa kaanem tu wom.

english_verse: He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. You will then be forgiven for being too near a dead body, and your hair will again become sacred.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom wó kwei kunkwona bam dedoa o ma o ke wɛleera saarem kaanem nɔɔno wom ŋwaane, ye o daare o kwei kadwoŋi kam o ma o ke zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem. Naziri tu wom na tusi de o na yi too yera to ŋwaane, kaanem dem wó le o tusim dem Wɛ yiga ne. Dɛ dem konto ne mo ba wó jwoori ba kwɛ o yu-ywei sem Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: But the dead body made you unacceptable, so you must make another vow to become a Nazirite and be dedicated once more. Finally, a year-old ram must be offered as the sacrifice to make things right.
translation_verse: Naziri tu wom nam jege se o daa jwoori o pɔɔre o tete mo o ke Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ne. O na maŋe o pɔɔre o tete da yalo wone to daa ba jege kuri, too wom na pɛ se o chɔge o tete de chullu tem to ŋwaane. O maa wó kwei pi-bala na ye bene to, se ba ma ba ke wɛleera jene kaanem ba pa‑o.

english_verse: and offer three animals that have nothing wrong with them: a year-old ram as a sacrifice to please me, a year-old female lamb as a sacrifice for sin, and a full-grown ram as a sacrifice to ask my blessing.
translation_verse: O laam wó ja vara batɔ na ba jege gɛɛ ba yera ne to mo o ba o ke kaanem o pa Baŋa Wɛ. O wó taa jege pi-bala na ye bene to, se o ma o ke zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem. O ta wó taa jege pi-chwɛ na ye bene to, se o ma o ke wɛleera saarem kaanem, ye o daare o taa jege pi-bɛa se o ma-ka o ke yazura pɛɛre kaanem.

english_verse: Wine offerings and grain sacrifices must also be brought with these animals. Finally, you are to bring a basket of bread made with your finest flour and olive oil, but without yeast. Also bring some thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: O nam ta wó taa jege tetɔgɔ de bworobwooru dwi dwi telo sabɔle na wo woli te wone to. Ba wó kwei mun-bwei ba viiri de nuga ba ma ke bworobwooru tedwonna, ye ba daare ba ke bworobworo-memena yalo na taare de nuga to. Kotu ta wó kwei wodiu pɛɛra de wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛra o woli da.

english_verse: The priest will take these gifts to my altar and offer them, so that I will be pleased and will forgive you.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom laam maa wó jwoŋi wonnu tem konto maama o ba o ke kaanem o pa Baŋa Wɛ. O wó ke wɛleera saarem kaanem se o daare o ke zwɛɛm kaanem dem.

english_verse: After that, you will stand at the entrance to the sacred tent, shave your head, and put the hair in the fire where the priest has offered the sacrifice to ask my blessing.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne Naziri tu wom wó zege wara-jei sem ni ne mo o fane o yuu. O maa wó kwei o yu-ywei sem na bere we o pɔɔre o tete Wɛ ŋwaane to o dole o de mini delo na wora de zwɛ yazura pɛɛre dem ŋwaane to wone.

english_verse: Once the meat from the ram's shoulder has been boiled, the priest will take it, along with one loaf of bread and one wafer brushed with oil, and give them to you.
translation_verse: O na fane o yuu o ti to, kaanem tu wom wó kwei pi-bɛa kam vɔŋɔ kolo na saŋe ko be to, dedaane bworobwooru dwia yalei na wo tetɔgɔ kom wone to dedoa dedoa o ke kotu jeŋa ne.

english_verse: You will hand them back to the priest, who will lift them up in dedication to me. Then he can eat the meat from the ram's shoulder, its choice ribs, and its hind leg, because this is his share of the sacrifice. After this, you will no longer be a Nazirite, and you will be free to drink wine.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom maa wó jwoori o jwoŋi-te, ye o zeiŋi-te wɛɛne o pa Baŋa Wɛ. Wonnu tem konto ye Wɛ kaanem tu wom nyem mo se te woli de varem wom nyɔɔne delo o na zeiŋi wɛɛne to de chwei delo o na ke Wɛ jeŋa ne to. Konto ná ke ko ti, nɔɔno wom laam jege chwoŋa se o nyɔ sana.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will bless and protect you,
translation_verse: ‘Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ abam swolim, se o daare o taa kwoli abam.

english_verse: and that he will show you mercy and kindness.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ yibia wó jeeri abam seeni, se o daare o ke zaane abam yuu ne.

english_verse: May the Lord be good to you and give you peace.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se o yiga taa wo á wone, se á ta‑á jege yazura.’

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If Aaron and his sons ask me to bless the Israelites, I will give them my blessing.”
translation_verse: Konto to, ba wó ma amo yere ba ma sɔɔle swolim ba ke Isarele tiina bam yuu ne. Amo maa wó seene a swɛ ba swolim.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ruben Sedura bu Elizura

english_verse: Whenever Moses needed to talk with the Lord, he went into the sacred tent, where he heard the Lord's voice coming from between the two winged creatures above the lid of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Moses déem ná yeini o zo wara-vwei dem wone se o ŋɔɔne de Baŋa Wɛ, o yeini o ni Wɛ kwora kam mo na ŋɔɔne ka nwoŋi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam baŋa seeni. Ko déem ye cherubi selei sem na zege dakaa kam ni-pugu kom baŋa ne to tetare ne mo Baŋa Wɛ yeini o ŋɔɔne de Moses.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: “Tell Aaron to put the seven lamps on the lampstand so they shine toward the front.”
translation_verse: “Ta de Aron se o zege min-zwonnu terepɛ tem min-zwon-zego kom baŋa ne, se te taa nyeene te pwooni te jeeri ko yiga kam seeni.”

english_verse: The lampstand was made of hammered gold from its base to the decorative flowers on top, exactly like the pattern the Lord had described to Moses. Instructions for Ordaining the Levites
translation_verse: Ba déem ya kwei sabu-seŋa mo ba mage ba gɔgere min-zwon-zego kom maama, se ko zege ko kuri dem ne ko yi pun-kogela yam na wo ko baŋa seeni to. Ko maa ye Baŋa Wɛ déem na pɛ Moses ni se ba ke-ko tei to mo chekke. Ba na pɔɔre Levi tiina bam ba totoŋa ŋwaane tei to

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de Moses o we:

english_verse: The Levites must be acceptable to me before they begin working at the sacred tent. So separate them from the rest of the Israelites
translation_verse: “Nmo jege se n pɔɔre Levi tiina bam mo se ba taa ye ba yera de Isarele tiina bam maama, se n daare n kwɛ-ba de chullu tem.

english_verse: and sprinkle them with the water that washes away their sins. Then have them shave their entire bodies and wash their clothes.
translation_verse: Nmo nam na wó kwɛ-ba tei to ye se n misi na mo ba yera ne wɛleera saarem ŋwaane. Ta pa se ba fane ba yera yam jei maama koro ba yage, se ba daare ba zare ba gwaaro. Keim dem konto wó kwɛ-ba.

english_verse: They are to bring a bull and its proper grain sacrifice of flour mixed with olive oil. And they must bring a second bull as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Ba laam maa wó ja na-bala, dedaane wodiu pɛɛre delo na maŋe to ba ba. Wodiu pɛɛre dem maa ye mun-bwei na viiri de nuga to mo. Nmo de maa wó ja na-bala kadwoŋi n ba se n ma‑n ke wɛleera saarem kaanem.

english_verse: Then you, Moses, will call together all the people of Israel and send the Levites to my sacred tent,
translation_verse: Pa se Levi tiina bam ba ba zege wara-jei sem ni ne, se Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama de ba ba jeeri da.

english_verse: Aaron will present the Levites to me as a gift from the people, so that the Levites will do my work.
translation_verse: Aron maa wó kwei Levi tiina bam o ke amo jeŋa ne, ne o zeiŋi-ba amo yiga ne mo tei to. Ba ye Isarele tiina bam maama pɛɛre mo ba na kwei se ba taa toŋe ba pa-ne.

english_verse: After this, the Levites are to place their hands on the heads of the bulls. Sacrifice one of the bulls for the forgiveness of sin, and the other to make sure that I am pleased. Then the Levites will be acceptable to me.
translation_verse: Levi tiina bam laam wó daŋe ba je nabɛ selei sem yuni ne. Nabea dedoa ye se ba kwei-ka ba ke wɛleera saarem kaanem, se ba kwei kadwoŋi kam ba ke zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem delo na wó le Levi tiina bam wɛleera amo yiga ne to.

english_verse: They will stand at my altar in front of Aaron and his sons, who will dedicate the Levites to me.
translation_verse: Ta daare n pa se Levi tiina bam zege Aron de o bia bam yiga ne, ye n ke se ko taa nye de n zeiŋi-ba mo amo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: This ceremony will show that the Levites are different from the other Israelites and belong to me in a special way.
translation_verse: Nam ke konto se n ma‑n pɔɔre Levi tiina bam, se ba taa ye ba yera Isarele tiina bam maama wone. Levi tiina bam wó taa ye amo nyem.

english_verse: After they have been made acceptable and have been dedicated, they will be allowed to work at my sacred tent.
translation_verse: Nmo ná pɛ se ba kwɛ ba tete de chullu tem konto, ye n daare n kwei-ba n ke amo jeŋa ne, ba laam jege chwoŋa se ba taa toŋe wara-jei sem totoŋa.

english_verse: When I killed the oldest sons of the Egyptians, I decided that the first-born sons in each Israelite family would be mine, as well as every first-born male from their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Isarele tiina bam wone, de ba vara wone wo-kwe selo na ye baara to maama ye amo nyem mo. Amo déem na go Ejipti tiina bakeiri-kwe sem to, mo a kuri se Isarele tiina bakeiri-kwe sem taa ye a nyem.

english_verse: But now I have chosen these Levites as substitutes for the first-born sons,
translation_verse: A laam nam kwei Levi tiina bam mo se ba leiri Isarele tiina bakeiri-kwe sem yuu ne.

english_verse: and I have given them as gifts to Aaron and his sons to serve at the sacred tent. I will hold them responsible for what happens to anyone who gets too close to the sacred tent. The Levites Are Dedicated to the Lord
translation_verse: A ma yɔɔre a kuri-ba Isarele tiina bam maama wone a pa Aron de o bia bam, se ba taa toŋe wara-jei sem totoŋa. Ba jege se ba fɔge ba kwɛ Isarele tiina bam tusim mo amo yiga ne, se ba yé na chɔgem de ba na tiini ba fɔɔre ba yi amo wara-vwei dem seeni to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelites made sure that the Levites did everything the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Moses, de Aron, de Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama ma nii ko baŋa ne pa se Levi tiina bam ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ ni se ba ke to.

english_verse: The Levites sprinkled themselves with the water of forgiveness and washed their clothes. Then Aaron brought them to the altar and offered sacrifices to forgive their sins and make them acceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Levi tiina bam ma kwɛ ba tete de chullu tem, ye ba daare ba zare ba gwaaro. Aron de ma ke se ko bere we o zeiŋi-ba o ke Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ne. O ta ma ke chullu telo na le ba wɛleera Wɛ yiga ne to, pa se ba fɔge ba kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: They may help the other Levites in their duties, but they must no longer be responsible for any work themselves. Remember this when you assign their duties.”
translation_verse: Ba nam jege chwoŋa se ba woli ba dwonna Levi tiina se ba toŋe ba totoŋa wara-jei sem ne, se banto daa bá taa jege ba tete totoŋe. Nmo wó tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo n pa se Levi tiina bam taa toŋe ba totoŋa.”

english_verse: to say to the people, “Celebrate Passover
translation_verse: “Pa se Isarele tiina bam di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem ka maŋa kam ne.

english_verse: in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month and do it by following all the regulations.”
translation_verse: Chana kanto da fuga-yana dɛ dem ná yia, se ba di kuri dem wɛ-zoore maŋa ne se ko taa via. Ba nam jege se ba di-de se ko maŋe de de dim chwoŋa kam mo.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
translation_verse: Moses ma ta de nɔɔna bam ye ba de seene ba di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem Sinayi kagoa kam ne konto. Ko déem ye boboa chana kam da fuga-yana dɛ dem wɛ-zoore maŋa ne mo ba di-de. Isarele tiina bam déem ke nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Moses ni se ba ke tei to mo.

english_verse: Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Nɔɔna badwonna déem wo maŋe de chullu tem, pa se chwoŋa wo peini ka pa-ba se ba tɔge ba di kuri dem de dɛ dem ne. Ko maa ye ba déem na dwei too ŋwaane to mo. Dɛ dem konto ne ba ma vo Moses de Aron tei,

english_verse: “Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
translation_verse: ye ba ta ba we, “Debam seene dé dwei too pa se dé wo maŋe de chullu tem. Konto nam wó che se dé yé tɔge de Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom dé kwei dé pɛɛra dé pa Baŋa Wɛ ka maŋa kam ne na?”

english_verse: Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri-ba o we, “Zuri-na á yera se a bwei Baŋa Wɛ se dé lɔre dé na wó ke tei abam ŋwaane to.”

english_verse: The Lord then told Moses
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ de ma ta de Moses o we:

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover.
translation_verse: “Ta n bere Isarele tiina bam we: Abam de á kwaga kam balo maama ná dwei too pa se ba wo maŋe de chullu tem, naa ba ná vei chwoŋa mo yiga yiga, ba de wó taa jege chwoŋa se ba di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem.

english_verse: But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs,
translation_verse: Ba nam jege se ba cheigi se chane selei chana kam da fuga-yana dɛ dem ná yia se ba di-ko wɛ-zoore maŋa ne se ko taa via. Ba wó di pipeila kam nɔna mo, ye ba di bworobworo-memene selo sabɔle na tere ko wone to, dedaane dwoa vɔɔ-chɛɛro ba woli da.

english_verse: and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
translation_verse: Ba yé pa se wodiu kom konto zege ko poore tega, naa se ba bwori varem wom kwi de dedoa de. Ba ná lage ba di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem, ba jege se ba ke ba tɔge de dim chwoŋa kam maama mo.

english_verse: But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
translation_verse: Wolo nam ná maŋe de chullu tem, ye o ná wo vei chwo-dɔrɔ, kotu ná ve se o di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem, o nam daa bá tɔge o woli Isarele dwi dem wone, o na wo jaane o pɛɛra o ba amo yiga ne ka maŋa kam ne to ŋwaane. O tusim dem konto wó taa wo o yuu ne ye o maŋe se o na waarem mo.

english_verse: As soon as the sacred tent was set up, a thick cloud appeared and covered it. The cloud was there each day, and during the night, a fire could be seen in it.
translation_verse: Ko nam yeini ko ke konto mo dɛ maama wone. Kunkwoŋo mo yeini ko kwoli wara-vwei dem, ye tete ne ko nye de mini.

english_verse: The Lord used this cloud to tell the Israelites when to move their camp and where to set it up again. As long as the cloud covered the tent, the Israelites did not break camp. But when the cloud moved, they followed it, and wherever it stopped, they camped and stayed there,
translation_verse: Ko ná maŋe da taa, ye ko ba zaŋa, Isarele tiina bam de wó maŋe jei sem konto ne mo, ne Baŋa Wɛ na bere-ba se ba ke tei to.

english_verse: whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites.
translation_verse: Kunkwoŋo kom déem ná ke da yalei, naa chana, naa bene, ye ko ná yɔɔre ko maŋe wara-vwei dem baŋa ne, Isarele tiina bam de wó maŋe jei sem konto ne mo. Ko ná zaŋe ko vei maŋa kalo ne, ba de wó zaŋe ba tɔge ko kwaga mo ba via.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we:

english_verse: Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp.
translation_verse: “Nam pa se ba kwei lu-nyenno ba mage-te se ba ma ba ke nabwanno telei. Nmo laam ma‑n wó yeini n pa se ba kwei-te ba ma ba bwoŋi nɔɔna bam ba ke daane, naa se ba gɔ ba vwoa ba vo jei sedwoŋi.

english_verse: If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ba ná yeini ba wu nabwanno telei tem titwon-twono, se nɔɔna bam maama da ba jeeri‑m wara-jei sem ni ne.

english_verse: But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
translation_verse: Se ba ná wugi nabɔnɔ dedoa yerane, ko ye sɔ-yuni yiga tiina bam mo wó ba ba jeeri‑m.

english_verse: Give a signal on a trumpet when it is time to break camp. The first blast will be the signal for the tribes camped on the east side, and the second blast will be the signal for those on the south.
translation_verse: Ba daa ná wugi-te ba ke belei tu, se dwia yalo na jei vwei dem tega-kuri seeni to de gɔ ba vwoa. Ba ná wugi nabwanno tem ba kɔ, ko wó bere nɔɔna bam we maŋa kam yia se ba nwoŋi ba kɛ.

english_verse: But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná yeini ko ye se nɔɔna bam maama jeeri daane, se ba wu nabwanno tem ba leiri te kwori.

english_verse: The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
translation_verse: Aron bia bam na ye kaanem tiina to mo jege se ba taa wui nabwanno tem. Amo ni dem konto wó taa wora taa wuu mo ko pa abam de á kwaga kam maama.

english_verse: Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you.
translation_verse: Á ná nwoŋi se á kwaare jara de á dona balo na tu se ba chɔge á tega kam to, se á pa se ba wu nabwanno tem ba kɔ tigura ŋwaane. Ko ná ke konto, abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó ni ko ŋwa, se o jwoŋi abam o yage á dona bam jeŋa ne.

english_verse: On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on.
translation_verse: Dento bene dem chane selei chana kam da finlei dɛ dem ne mo kunkwoŋo kom ya na dɔge wara-vwei dem baŋa ne to zaŋe.

english_verse: So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: Ko ma pa se Isarele tiina bam de gɔ ba vwoa ba yage Sinayi kagoa kam ye ba tole ba via. Kunkwoŋo kom déem ma vo ko yi Paran kagoa kam ko maŋe dáane ko zege.

english_verse: This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
translation_verse: Ba na bobo ba zaŋe se ba vo jeiga kadwoŋi konto to, ko ye Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge Moses baŋa o pa-ba ni se ba ke tei to mo.

english_verse: Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe,
translation_verse: Judah dwi dem de ba kwaga kam déem ma bobo se ba nwoŋi ba kɛ, ye ba zei ba gwɛɛm yere dem. Aminadabi bu Naason déem nam mo wo ba kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne.

english_verse: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe,
translation_verse: Zuwara bu Netaneli maa wo Isakara dwi dem yiga ne.

english_verse: and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
translation_verse: Helon bu Eliabi maa wo Zebulun dwi dem yiga ne.

english_verse: The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma kore wara-vwei dem, se Gereson tiina de Merari tiina bam zeŋe de zela yam ba taa vei ba tɔge Judah kɔgɔ kom kwaga.

english_verse: Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe,
translation_verse: Ruben dwi dem de ba kwaga kam déem ma saŋe se ba nwoŋi ba kɛ, ye ba zei ba gwɛɛm yere dem. Sedura bu Elizura déem nam mo wo ba kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne.

english_verse: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe,
translation_verse: Zurisadayi bu Selumeli maa wo Simeon dwi dem yiga ne.

english_verse: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Deweli bu Eliasafe maa wo Isakara dwi dem yiga ne.

english_verse: Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
translation_verse: Kohafe tiina de ma zeŋe wara-jei wo-zela yalo na tiini ya ye wose to ba vei ba tɔge-ba. Ba ná yeini ba yi mɛ ba daa na wó jeini to, dedaane nɔɔna badwonna maŋe ba chwi wara-jei sem ko jei ne.

english_verse: Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe,
translation_verse: Efrayim dwi dem de ba kwaga kam déem ma saŋe se ba nwoŋi ba kɛ, ye ba zei ba gwɛɛm yere dem. Amihuda bu Elisama déem nam mo wo ba kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne.

english_verse: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe,
translation_verse: Pedazura bu Gamaleli maa wo Manasɛ dwi dem yiga ne.

english_verse: and Abidan son of Gideoni was the leader of the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Gideoni bu Abidan maa wo Benjamin dwi dem yiga ne.

english_verse: Dan and the tribes that camped alongside it were to protect the Israelites against an attack from behind, and so they marched last, carrying their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Dan,
translation_verse: Dan dwi dem de ba kwaga kam déem ma kweeli se ba nwoŋi ba kɛ, ye ba zei ba gwɛɛm yere dem. Amisadayi bu Ahiyezera déem nam mo wo ba kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne.

english_verse: Pagiel son of Ochran was the leader of the Asher tribe,
translation_verse: Ocharan bu Pageli maa wo Asere dwi dem yiga ne.

english_verse: and Ahira son of Enan was the leader of the Naphtali tribe.
translation_verse: Enan bu Ahira maa wo Nafitali dwi dem yiga ne.

english_verse: Hobab the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, was there. And Moses said to him, “We're leaving for the place the Lord has promised us. He has said that all will go well for us. So come along, and we will make sure that all goes well for you.”
translation_verse: Midian tu Reweli bu Hobabi de déem tɔge o wo ba tei ne. Reweli maa ye Moses tembaaro. Moses ma ta de Hobabi o we, “Ko laam yi se debam zaŋe dé vo jei selo Baŋa Wɛ na gwoni ni se o kwei o pa debam to. O nam pɛ se dé lɔre we dé ná yi da, ko wó taa lana ko pae debam. Nmo de nam ba se dé maama kɛ, se dé wó nii nmo baŋa ne ye n tɔge n na wo-laaro.”

english_verse: “No, I won't go,” Hobab answered. “I'm returning home to be with my own people.”
translation_verse: Hobabi ma leiri‑o o we, “Aawo! Amo de lage se a jwoori a tete teo mo, se a taa zoore a nɔɔna tei ne.”

english_verse: “Please go with us!” Moses said. “You can be our guide because you know the places to camp in the desert.
translation_verse: Moses daa ma ta o we, “Ja! Pa se dé maama kɛ, se nmo wó ta‑n bere debam chwoŋa kam, nmo na yei kagoa kam jei sem lanyerane to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Besides that, if you go, we will give you a share of the good things the Lord gives us.”
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne, n ná dɛ dé kwaga se dé yi da, dé wó chɛ wo-laaro telo maama Baŋa Wɛ na wó pa debam to, se nmo de da n na te wone.”

english_verse: The people of Israel began their journey from Mount Sinai. They traveled three days, and the Levites who carried the sacred chest led the way, so the Lord could show them where to camp.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam maama déem ma yage Sinayi peo kom jei sem ye ba vei taa, da yatɔ. Ba na maa vei to, Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam maa wo ba yiga ne, se ka bere-ba jei se ba jeini da.

english_verse: One day the Israelites started complaining about their troubles. The Lord heard them and became so angry that he destroyed the outer edges of their camp with fire.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam déem na nɛ cham dwi dwi to, mo ba yɔɔre ba poone ye Baŋa Wɛ ni ba pompona kam. O na nigi to, o bane ma zaŋe de-ba ye o pa se mini di ba na chwi ba vwoa yam mɛ daa dedoa to nia yam.

english_verse: When the people begged Moses to help, he prayed, and the fire went out.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma lwoori Moses se o woli-ba. O de ma lwoori Wɛ, ye mini dem dwei.

english_verse: They named the place “Burning,” because in his anger the Lord had set their camp on fire. The People Grumble about Being Hungry
translation_verse: Ba ma bwoŋi jei sem yere we ‘Tabera’. Ko maa ye Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ se mini zwɛ ba vwoa yam to ŋwaane mo.

english_verse: One day some foreigners among the Israelites became greedy for food, and even the Israelites themselves began moaning, “We don't have any meat!
translation_verse: Nɔn-wo-korro déem tɔge ba wo Isarele tiina bam wone pa ba via. Banto fera ma tiini ya zo wodiiru tedwonna. Isarele tiina bam de ma bobo se ba ŋwaana ba we, “Dé ya ná nɛ nɔna se dé done, ko ba gare tento na?

english_verse: In Egypt we could eat all the fish we wanted, and there were cucumbers, melons, all kinds of onions, and garlic.
translation_verse: Dé déem na wo Ejipti wone to, dé nae ywona dé di zɛɛra. Dé ta di nyambɔla, de gaana, de gaburu dwi dwi, de gaaliki, ne dé boboŋa na lage tei to mo.

english_verse: But we're starving out here, and the only food we have is this manna.”
translation_verse: Nam nii! Dé yera chɛ mo. Wodiu kolo yerane dé na yɔɔre dé nae to ye Manna kanto mo!”

english_verse: and tasted like something baked with sweet olive oil. It appeared at night with the dew. In the morning the people would collect the manna, grind or crush it into flour, then boil it and make it into thin wafers.
translation_verse: Manna yam déem yeini ya tɔge de nyɔnɔ mo ya toe tete ne. Nɔɔna bam maa yeini ba nwoŋi ba pɛ-ya ba cho, naa ba zɔ-ya, ye ba laam saŋe muni dem ba ke nenɛɛne pɛɛla dwoŋi tei. Ba déem ná di-ya, ya nye de bworobworo mo ba na wɔge de nuga.

english_verse: He prayed: I am your servant, Lord, so why are you doing this to me? What have I done to deserve this? You've made me responsible for all these people,
translation_verse: O ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ ye o we, “Amo Tu Wɛ, bɛ mo ke ye n kwei cham dento n pa-ne? Bɛ mo a ke a chɔge n yiga, ye n pa se nɔɔna banto jege-ne ba daana?

english_verse: but they're not my children. You told me to nurse them along and to carry them to the land you promised their ancestors.
translation_verse: Ko dae amo mo naane-ba, a nam wo loge-ba. Nmo ta wó pa se a ke-ba a ja-kukworo ne, a daare a ja-ba se dé vo dé yi tega kalo nmo na gwoni ni de dé nabaara se n kwei n pa-ba to na?

english_verse: They keep whining for meat, but where can I get meat for them?
translation_verse: Ba nam na tiini ba poone nɔna ŋwaane konto to, amo lage a na-ya yein-seeni mo a pa-ba?

english_verse: This job is too much for me. How can I take care of all these people by myself?
translation_verse: Totoŋe dem n na kwei n pa-ne to tiini de dwoi a jaanem. Amo yerane ware nɔɔna bam a ja.

english_verse: If this is the way you're going to treat me, just kill me now and end my miserable life! Seventy Leaders Are Chosen To Help Moses
translation_verse: Ko ná ye tento mo n kuri se ko taa ye amo yera ne, se n duri amo yibwona n daare n le a ŋwea lela se a sii de yaara yanto!” Nakwa fuserepɛ

english_verse: As for the Israelites, I have heard them complaining about not having meat and about being better off in Egypt. So tell them to make themselves acceptable to me, because tomorrow they will have meat.
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye nɔɔna bam, se n ta de-ba we: ‘Kwɛ-na á tete se á jwa wó na nɔna se á done. Baŋa Wɛ seene o ni á pompona kam de á na tage á we, á fera zo nɔna donem, ye á Ejipti ŋwea kam ya gare á leile ŋwea kam to. Tɔ. Baŋa Wɛ wó pa abam nɔna ye á jege se á done-ya mo.

english_verse: grown men are here with me. How can you say there will be enough meat to feed them and their families for a whole month?
translation_verse: ) mo. Nmo laam nam tage we n wó pa ba maama nɔna se ba taa done dɛ dɛ se ko yi chana mo na?

english_verse: Even if we butchered all our sheep and cattle, or caught every fish in the sea, we wouldn't have enough to feed them.”
translation_verse: Dé ná lage dé go dé naane dem maama, de dé vare-balwa bam maama, ko ta bá yi ba dim. Dé ná gɔɔne naneo wo ywona yam maama dé pa-ba, ko bere ko bá yi-ba!”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “I can do anything! Watch and you'll see my words come true.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei‑o we, “Amo dam dem muri mo na? Cheigi fee se n ma‑n lɔre we kolo a na tage to lage ko ke mo.”

english_verse: Eldad and Medad were two leaders who had not gone to the tent. But when the Spirit took control of them, they began shouting like prophets right there in camp.
translation_verse: Eledadi de Medadi de déem wo nakwa fuserepɛ bam wone mo. Ba ma maŋe ba vwoa yam seeni, ye ba wo tɔge ba zo wara-jei sem ne. Ba na wora konto to, mo jworo kom tu ba baŋa. Ba de ma bobo se ba taa pworisa.

english_verse: Joshua was there helping Moses, as he had done since he was young. And he said to Moses, “Sir, you must stop them!”
translation_verse: Nun bu Josua nam déem maŋe o zege o nɔn-donne maŋa ne mo o toŋe o woli Moses. O ma ta de Moses o we, “Dé kwo, che-ba de ba keim dem konto!”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “Are you concerned what this might do to me? I wish the Lord would give his Spirit to all his people so everyone could be a prophet.”
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri‑o o we, “Ko ye amo ŋwaane mo n jege boboŋa konto dwoŋi na? Nam yage! Amo tei ne, Baŋa Wɛ ya ná pɛ se o nɔɔna bam maama su de o jworo pa se ba pworisi nenɛɛne Wɛ ni-jwoŋina bam na yeini ba ke tei to, ko ya gara.”

english_verse: But before the meat could be eaten, the Lord became angry and sent a deadly disease through the camp.
translation_verse: Lwi sem nɔna yam ta na wo nɔɔna bam nia ne ye ba ta wo di ba ti to, mo Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe de-ba. O ma pa se jawe-chɛɛro to ba tetare ne.

english_verse: After they had buried the people who had been so greedy for meat, they called the place “Graves for the Greedy.”
translation_verse: Ba déem ma kwei nɔɔna bam dedɛ ba suli, jaweero tem na go-ba to ŋwaane. Ba ma bwoŋi jei sem konto we ‘Kiberof-Hataava’, kokuri to ba suli balo fera na zo nɔna wone to jei sem konto ne mo.

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Aaron and Miriam. And after the Lord left
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ bane ma tiini de zaŋe de Aron de Miriam ye o zaŋe o kɛ o daare-ba.

english_verse: and the cloud disappeared from over the sacred tent, Miriam's skin turned white with leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her,
translation_verse: Kunkwoŋo kom ma gɔ ko tete wara-vwei dem baŋa ne. Sento nɛ sem ni ne mo Miriam yera tiini ya peere dedaane naywaane jaweo kom. Aron ma pipiri o nii o na kolo na ke Miriam yera ne to.

english_verse: he said to Moses, “Sir, please don't punish us for doing such a foolish thing.
translation_verse: O ma tiini o lwoori Moses o we, “Dé kwo, jan ja! Dé lwoori‑m se n yé waare debam dé tusim dento ŋwaane. Debam tiini dé toŋe jworim mo.

english_verse: Don't let Miriam's flesh rot away like a child born dead!”
translation_verse: Nii ko baŋa ne se Miriam yé taa nye de bu-too wolo yera na moore to!”

english_verse: But the Lord replied, “Miriam would be disgraced for seven days if her father had punished her by spitting in her face. So make her stay outside the camp for seven days, before coming back.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri Moses o we, “Miriam kwo ya ná twe lileeru o ke o yibia ne, ko ya wó pa se o di chaveera se ko yi da yarepɛ mo. Konto ŋwaane, pa-na se o nwoŋi dáa Isarele tiina bam wone, se á daare á pe‑o da yarepɛ. Ko kwaga ne se á pa‑o chwoŋa se o jwoori o taa zoore ba wone.”

english_verse: Then they left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne mo ba zaŋe Hazerofa ne ye ba laam vo ba yi Paran kagoa kam. Ba ma chwi ba vwoa dáane.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: “Choose a leader from each tribe and send them into Canaan to explore the land I am giving you.”
translation_verse: “Le nɔɔna se ba vo ba ŋɔ ba nii Kanaan tega kam, ko na ye tega kalo a na lage a pa Isarele tiina bam to ŋwaane. Kuri yiga tu dedoa dedoa Isarele dwi maama wone.”

english_verse: Before Moses sent them into Canaan, he said: After you go through the Southern Desert of Canaan, continue north into the hill country
translation_verse: Moses déem na lage o toŋe-ba se ba vo ba zo Kanaan tega kam wone to, mo o tage de-ba o we, “Tɔge-na tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam, se á laam ta‑á tole á diini baŋa seeni se á vo á yi zwonnu laŋa kam.

english_verse: and find out what those regions are like. Be sure to remember how many people live there, how strong they are,
translation_verse: Kwaane-na se á lɔre tega kam konto na ye tei to. Fɔge-na á nii nɔɔna balo na zoore da to kɔgɔ na mae tei, dedaane ba dam na mae tei to.

english_verse: and if they live in open towns or walled cities. See if the land is good for growing crops and find out what kinds of trees grow there. It's time for grapes to ripen, so try to bring back some of the fruit that grows there.
translation_verse: Ba tega kam ke wodiiru lanyerane na? Teeni wora na? Vɔ-na á wo ye á kwaane-na se á gwori teeni bia badwonna á ja á ba se dé nii.” Ko déem nam ye maŋa kalo Vini tio-bia na bobo ba bera se nɔɔna gwori-ba to mo.

english_verse: The twelve men left to explore Canaan from the Zin Desert in the south all the way to the town of Rehob near Lebo-Hamath in the north.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma seene ba di baŋa seeni ba tole ye ba nii tega kam na ye tei to. Ba zege Zin kagoa kam ne mo ba vo ba yi Rehobi. Jei sem konto bwola de Lebo-Hamafa mo.

english_verse: As they went through the Southern Desert, they came to the town of Hebron, which was seven years older than the Egyptian town of Zoan. In Hebron, they saw the three Anakim clans of Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai.
translation_verse: Ba daa ma tɔge tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam ba kɛ ba yi Heboron. Ba déem chwi teo kom konto bena yarepɛ mo ye ba daare ba chwi Zoan teo na wo Ejipti wone to. Ba déem na yi Heboron teo kom to, mo ba nɛ nɔn-sawaara balo na zoore da to. Banto maa ye Anaki bia batɔ sɔ-yuu tiina, ba yera na ye Ahiman, de Sesayi, de Talimayi to.

english_verse: But the people who live there are strong, and their cities are large and walled. We even saw the three Anakim clans.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo na zoore da to nam mo tiini ba dana. Ba teene dem de maa yala, ye de lɔ de pe. Dé ta nɛ we Anaki dwi tiina de zoore dáane mo.

english_verse: Besides that, the Amalekites live in the Southern Desert; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites are in the hill country; and the Canaanites live along the Mediterranean Sea and the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Amaleki tiina bam de zoore tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam ne mo. Hiti tiina bam, de Jebusi tiina, de Amori tiina bam de maa wo zwonnu laŋa kam ne. Ko daare ye Kanaan tiina bam de zoore Mediterania naneo kom ni ne, de Jɔdan buga kam ni ne.”

english_verse: Then they started spreading rumors and saying, “We won't be able to grow anything in that soil. And the people are like giants.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma ŋɔɔne ta-balɔrɔ tega kam seeni ba bere Isarele tiina bam. Ba maa we, “Tega kalo dé na vei dé nii to wó chɔge balo na zoore ka wone to. Ka nɔn-bia bam maama ye nɔn-wagela mo.

english_verse: and complained to Moses and Aaron, “We wish we had died in Egypt or somewhere out here in the desert!
translation_verse: Ba maa jege Moses de Aron ba poona ye ba we, “Dé ya ná tege Ejipti wone, naa kagoa kanto wone, ko ya wó taa gara.

english_verse: Is the Lord leading us into Canaan, just to have us killed and our women and children captured? We'd be better off in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ jege debam o zoore Kanaan tega kam wone se bɛ mo? Ko ye se ba go debam mo, se ba daare ba vere dé kaana de dé bia ba taa tei. Dé ná jwoori Ejipti teo, ko gara!”

english_verse: Then they said to one another, “Let's choose our own leader and go back.”
translation_verse: Ba ma ŋɔɔne ba bere daane ba we, “Pa-na se dé kuri yiga tu se konto tu ja debam o jwoori Ejipti.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron bowed down to pray in front of the crowd.
translation_verse: Moses de Aron maa vwi ba yibi sem tega ne ye nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama déem jeeri ba yiga ne.

english_verse: and said: We saw the land ourselves, and it's very good.
translation_verse: Ba ma ta de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama ba we, “Tega kalo dé na vei dé kaare dé nii to lana lanyerane.

english_verse: If we obey the Lord, he will surely give us that land rich with milk and honey.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ yi nam ná su dé kikia, o wó ja debam o zo te-ywoŋa kam konto wone, ye o daare o kwei-ka o pa debam. Ka ywomma mo de varem de kɔnɔ.

english_verse: So don't rebel. We have no reason to be afraid of the people who live there. The Lord is on our side, and they won't stand a chance against us!
translation_verse: Nam yé pa-na se dé lɔ Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne. Yé kɔre-na foone de nɔɔna balo na zoore tega kam wone to, dé na wó wane-ba dé di to ŋwaane. Woro daa tera se ba duri ba seigi ko wone. Baŋa Wɛ nam wo dé tei ne. Yé pa-na se dé taa kɔre foone!”

english_verse: The crowd threatened to stone Moses and Aaron to death. But just then, the Lord appeared in a cloud at the sacred tent. Moses Prays for the People
translation_verse: Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom boboŋa ma ja se ba dole Moses de Aron de kandwa ba go. Baŋa Wɛ ma pɔpɔ o chu o zege wara-vwei dem baŋa ne o veere o tete de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom o bere Isarele tiina bam maama. Moses lwoori Wɛ o pa nɔɔna bam

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I have done great things for these people, and they still reject me by refusing to believe in my power.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Tetɛ mo amo wó peene a tete de nɔɔna banto? Ba wó taa jege-ne ba gwoona taa se ba vo ba maŋe yei ne mo? A ke wo-kamuna dedɛ ba tetare ne, ye ba ta ve-ne.

english_verse: So they will no longer be my people. I will destroy them, but I will make you the ancestor of a nation even stronger than theirs.”
translation_verse: Amo laam nam lage a chɔge-ba de jawe-chɛɛro mo. A wó pa se ba dwi dem ti se a daare a pa nmo ji dwi-doore kwo. Dwi delo na wó zege nmo yera ne to wó taa daga, ye de ta dana de dwoi banto na ye tei to.”

english_verse: that you love to show mercy and kindness. And you said that you are very patient, but that you will punish everyone guilty of doing wrong—not only them but their children and grandchildren as well.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ yeini o peene o bane. O swono kom nam ba tia. O maa kwei nɔɔna wɛleera de ba tusim o yage o maa chɛ-ba. Se ko ná ye balo na gɛ bora to, o yeini o waare-ba de ba bia maama mo se ko yi ba naaro, de ba na-jwooru dwia yatɔ naa yana laŋa ne.

english_verse: You are merciful, and you treat people better than they deserve. So please forgive these people, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Nmo swono kom na seene ko gaale to ŋwaane, a lwoori‑m se n kwei nɔɔna banto wɛleera n ma n chɛ-ba. Ta ke n pa-ba nenɛɛne n na maŋe n yeini n ke tei de-ba ko zege ba na nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne to.”

english_verse: I swear that not one of these Israelites will enter the land I promised to give their ancestors. These people have seen my power in Egypt and in the desert, but they will never see Canaan. They have disobeyed and tested me too many times.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri ba wolowolo bá zo tega kalo a na gwoni ni de ba nabaara bam se a pa-ba to wone. Balo maama na gwooni amo to bá na tega kam konto.

english_verse: But my servant Caleb isn't like the others. So because he has faith in me, I will allow him to cross into Canaan, and his descendants will settle there.
translation_verse: Amo tontoŋeno Kaleb boboŋa nam ye ya yera mo de o dwonna bam boboŋ-balwaaro tem. O kwei o bochare maama mo o ma o tɔge-ne. Konto ŋwaane amo wó pa se o zo tega kalo o na vei o nii to se o de o kwaga kam taa tei-ka.

english_verse: Now listen, Moses! The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valleys of Canaan. And tomorrow, you'll need to turn around and head back into the desert toward the Red Sea. The Israelites Are Punished for Complaining
translation_verse: Tɔ. Amaleki tiina de Kanaan tiina bam na zoore bwollu laŋa kam ne ye ba che á chwoŋa to ŋwaane, jwa tetete se á maama jwoori á pipiri á mage á yuni kagoa kam seeni se á kwei Nane-soŋo chwoŋa kam á ta‑á via.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta de Moses de Aron o we:

english_verse: to give this message to the people of Israel: You sinful people have complained against me too many times! Now I swear by my own life that I will give you exactly what you wanted.
translation_verse: Konto to, ta-na á bere-ba we: ‘Ne amo Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a seene a lage a ke abam ne á na tage tei ye a ni to mo.

english_verse: You will die right here in the desert, and your dead bodies will cover the ground. You have insulted me, and none of you men who are over
translation_verse: Abam wó te kagoa kanto wone mo se á yera yam faare tega kam jei maama ne. Á baara balo maama na yi bena finlei ba daŋe ye ba tɔge ba wo jeelim dem wone to wó te mo, ba na poone amo to ŋwaane.

english_verse: will enter the land that I solemnly promised to give you as your own—only Caleb and Joshua will go in.
translation_verse: Abam wolowolo bá zo tega kalo amo déem na dugi duuri se a pa abam se á jeini da to. Jefunɛ bu Kaleb de Nun bu Josua yerane mo wó zo da.

english_verse: You were worried that your own children would be captured. But I, the Lord, will let them enter the land you have rejected.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye á bia balo á na jege ba lwia we tega kam tiina wó vere-ba ba taa tei to, a lage a pa se ba zo tega kalo abam na ve se á jwoŋi to mo ba taa tei.

english_verse: You will die here in the desert!
translation_verse: Se ko daare abam tete, á wó te kagoa kanto wone mo

english_verse: So they got up early the next morning and got ready to head toward the hill country of Canaan. They said, “We were wrong to complain about the Lord. Let's go into the land that he promised us.”
translation_verse: Tega na poore tetete to, mo ba zaŋe se ba vo Kanaan zwonnu laŋa kam. Ba maa we, “Dé tiini dé tusi dedaane dé na ve Baŋa Wɛ ni dem to. Dé laam ti yiga se dé vo dé kwei tega kam Baŋa Wɛ na gwoni ni se o pa debam to.”

english_verse: Ten of the men sent to explore the land had brought back bad news and had made the people complain against the Lord.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye Moses déem na toŋe nɔɔna balo se ba vo ba ŋɔ ba nii tega kam ye ba jwoori ba ŋɔɔne ta-balwaaro ka ŋwaane pa se nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama poone‑o to,

english_verse: So he sent a deadly disease that killed those men,

english_verse: If you sacrifice a young ram or goat, you must also offer a kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil as a grain sacrifice. A liter of wine must also be poured on the altar.

english_verse: And if the animal is a full-grown ram, you must offer two kilograms of flour mixed with one and a half liters of olive oil. One and a half liters of wine must also be poured on the altar. The smell of this smoke is pleasing to me.
translation_verse: O ta wó ja sa-sona bɔŋa dedoa de chichworo o woli da se ka taa ye wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛre. Kaanem dem konto lwom wó taa ywomma de pae Baŋa Wɛ.

translation_verse: Nmo ta wó woli sa-sona bwɛ selei se ko taa ye wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛre. Kaanem dem konto wó taa ye zwɛɛm pɛɛre mo. De nyoa kam wó taa ywomma ka pae Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: If you are a native Israelite, you must obey these rules each time you offer a bull, a ram, or a goat as a sacrifice.

english_verse: This law will never change. I am the Lord, and I consider all people the same, whether they are Israelites or foreigners living among you.
translation_verse: Abam balo na ye tembia to dedaane veira balo na zoore abam wone to jege se á ta‑á tɔge Wɛ nia yam bedwe mo ye popɔra tera.”

english_verse: When you eat food in the land that I am giving you, remember to set aside some of it as an offering to me.
translation_verse: ye á ná lage á di wodiu kolo tega kam na ke ka pa abam to, se á le ko wone á ma‑á ke pɛɛre se á zeiŋi-de wɛɛne á pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: From the first batch of bread dough that you make after each new grain harvest, make a loaf of bread and offer it to me, just as you offer grain.
translation_verse: Abam ná bobo á zage mena ye á kwei-ya á cho muni, se á ma-de á fɔge bworobworo se ko taa ye pɛɛre ko pae Baŋa Wɛ. Pɔɔre-na konto á pa Wɛ ne á na yeini á ke tei de mena yalo á na fere to.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses to tell the people what must be done if they ever disobey his laws:
translation_verse: Á ná maŋe á chɔge ni delo maama Baŋa Wɛ na bobo o tɔge Moses baŋa o pa abam to, naa ni delo maama na zege de pa á kwaga kam to,

english_verse: If all of you disobey one of my laws without knowing it, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice, a wine offering, and a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: ye á wo paale á chɔge-de, ye abam maama ya ná yeiri ko ni ne, se á kɔgɔ kom ja na-bala á ma‑á ke zwɛɛm kaanem se de lwom dem taa ywomma de pae Baŋa Wɛ. Á ta wó ja wodiu pɛɛre de wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛre na maŋe to á woli da, ye á daare á ja bo-bala á ba á ma‑á ke wɛleera saarem kaanem.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong without knowing it, you must sacrifice a year-old female goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye abam wone nɔɔno dedoa ná tusi ye o wo paale o ke, kotu wó ja bo-choa kalo na ye bene dedoa to o ba o ma o ke wɛleera saarem kaanem.

english_verse: The priest will then ask me to forgive you, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom maa wó tɔge ko chwoŋa se o le konto tu tusim dem Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Konto ná kea, Wɛ wó yage o wɛleera o ma chɛ‑o.

english_verse: The law will be the same for anyone who does wrong without meaning to, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
translation_verse: Ni dento zege de pae wolo maama na tusi ye o wo paale o ke to mo, kotu ná ye Isarele tu naa veiru de.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong on purpose, whether Israelite or foreigner, you have sinned against me by disobeying my laws. You will no longer belong to my people. A Man Put to Death for Gathering Firewood on the Sabbath
translation_verse: O na ke tei to bere we o gwooni Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam ye o ta daare o chɔge o nia yam. O wɛleera yam wó taa wo o yuu ne. Á jege se á yɔɔre á le‑o se o daa yé tɔge o woli a nɔɔna bam wone.” Siu dɛ chullu tem chɔgem taane

english_verse: Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ta na wo kagoa kam wone ba kare ba vei to, mo dɛ dedwe ba jaane nɔɔno na wora o puuri dɛ Wɛ siu dɛ dem ne.

english_verse: He was taken to Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community.
translation_verse: Ba ma ja‑o ba vo ba yi Moses de Aron de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama tei.

english_verse: But no one knew what to do with him, so he was not allowed to leave.
translation_verse: Ba ma pe‑o se ba cheigi ba nii, ba na yeiri ko na wó maŋe se ba ke‑o tei to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the people to take that man outside the camp and stone him to death!”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “O jege se o te mo. Ja-na nɔɔno wom á nwoŋi á vo dáa se Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom dole‑o de kandwa ba go.”

english_verse: So he was killed, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Tassels on the People's Clothes
translation_verse: Ba ma seene ba ja‑o ba vo ba dole‑o ba go, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Moses ni se ba ke tei to. Ba gwaaro nia yam kuna taane

english_verse: These will remind you that you must obey my laws and teachings. And when you do, you will be dedicated to me and won't follow your own sinful desires.
translation_verse: Konto to, á wó toŋe á tɔge amo nia yam maama. Á ta wó pɔɔre á tete á pa á Tu Wɛ wom.

english_verse: Korah son of Izhar was a Levite from the Kohathite clan. One day he called together Dathan, Abiram, and On from the Reuben tribe, and the four of them decided to rebel against Moses. So they asked
translation_verse: Ba déem dwoni de Moses, ye Isarele kɔgɔ kom yiga tiina bia yalei de finnu balo nɔɔna na nege to maa zege ba kwaga ne.

english_verse: and Aaron and said, “Why do you think you're so much better than everyone else? We're part of the Lord's holy people, and he's with all of us. What makes you think you're the only ones in charge?”
translation_verse: Ba laam ma vo ba jeeri Moses de Aron, ye ba ta de-ba ba we, “Abam zeiŋi á tete á gaale ko na maŋe se á ke tei to. Á boŋe we á gare Isarele tiina bam maama mo na? Dé kɔgɔ kom wone nɔɔno maama ye Wɛ nyem mo. Baŋa Wɛ maa wo nɔɔno maama tei ne. Bɛ nam mo ye á zeiŋi á tete Baŋa Wɛ kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne?”

english_verse: When Moses heard this, he knelt down to pray.
translation_verse: Moses na nigi ba taane dem to, mo o vwi o yibia tega ne.

english_verse: Then he said to Korah and his followers: Tomorrow morning the Lord will show us the person he has chosen to be his priest, and that man will faithfully serve him.
translation_verse: O laam ma ta o bere Kora de o kwaga kɔgɔ kom o we, “Jwa tetete Baŋa Wɛ tete wó bere debam wolo o na seene o pɔɔre se o taa ye o nyem to. O ta wó pa kotu chwoŋa se o fɔɔre o twɛ o tei. Nɔɔno wolo o na seene o kuri to mo wó zege o yiga ne.

english_verse: Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
translation_verse: se á jwa ke min-chala se wone. Á ta wó kwei talwoŋ-ywoŋa á ke á woli da se á daare á vo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Baŋa Wɛ wó kuri wolo o na pɔɔre se o taa ye o nyem to. Abam Levi dwi tiina mo zeiŋi á tete á gaale!”

english_verse: You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want?
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ pɔɔre abam Isarele dwi tiina bam maama wone se á ta‑á toŋe á pa‑o o wara-jei sem ne, se á daare á ta‑á zege Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom yiga ne á woli-ba Wɛ zula seeni. O na kwei totoŋe dem konto o pa abam to dae kolokolo abam tei ne na?

english_verse: The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest.
translation_verse: O pɛ chwoŋa se nmo, Kora, de n dwonna Levi tiina badaara bam taa tui o yiga ne. Nmo nam boŋe se n ji Wɛ kaanem tu mo n woli da na?

english_verse: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come!
translation_verse: Moses ma toŋe o bwoŋi Eliabi bia, Datan de Abiram. Ba ma toŋe kwora o tei ne ba we, “Dé bá ba nmo tei!

english_verse: It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around!
translation_verse: Nmo jaane debam n nwoŋi Ejipti te-ywoŋa kalo na lana de varem de kɔnɔ to wone n ba ywo-seeni se dé te kagoa kanto wone. Ko nam dae kolokolo nmo tei ne ye n ta boŋe se n di dam dé baŋa ne!

english_verse: Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
translation_verse: Moses bane ma tiini de zaŋe ye o ta de Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Yé pa n yiga taa wo nɔɔna banto pɛɛra yam wone. A wo chɔge ba yiga, a nam wo jwoŋi ba bonaga dedoa tete de.”

english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Moses laam ma ta de Kora o we, “Jwa ne se nmo de n kwaga kɔgɔ kom ba á zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Abam maama de Aron wó ba á jeeri da.

english_verse: The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, nɔɔna bam maama ma seene ba kwei ba zwe de se wo min-chala, ye ba laam daŋe talwoŋ-ywoŋa se wone. Ba ma vo ba jeeri Moses de Aron ye ba maama zege wara-jei sem ni ne.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Kora déem ya pɛ se Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama ba ba jeeri wara-jei sem ni ne ba zege Moses de Aron yiga ne. Ba maama na tu ba zege da konto to, Baŋa Wɛ ma veere o tete de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom o bere ba maama,

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: ye o ta de Moses de Aron o we,

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: “Abam balei kɛ-na dáa á daare Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom, se a yɔɔre a lage a ti-ba mo leile konto.”

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Moses de Aron ma vwi ba yibia tega ne ba lwoori Wɛ ba we, “Dé Tu Wɛ, nmo ŋwaane mo nabiina maama ŋwe. Nɔɔno dedoa nam ná ke o tusi, nmo wó da ko ŋwaane n ke bane de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama mo na?”

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: “Nam ta de kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama se ba ja ba tete ba vo dáa ba daare Kora, de Datan, de Abiram vwoa yam.”

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Moses ma zaŋe o vo Datan de Abiram tei ye Isarele nakwa bam de tɔge o kwaga.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: Moses maa jege nɔn-kɔgɔ kom o kaane ye o we, “Lage-na jei á vo, se á daare puseŋ-nyena banto. Nam yé zaŋe-na á dwei ba kolokolo, se á de tɔge de-ba á te ba wɛleera yam ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Moses laam ma ta o we, “Keim dento baŋa ne mo abam wó ma á sɛ we Baŋa Wɛ mo toŋe-ne, se ko dae a tete boboŋa ŋwaane mo a ke totoŋa yalo a na jege a ke to.

english_verse: If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna banto ná tege ba tete toone, ko bere we Baŋa Wɛ wo toŋe-ne, se a tete mo ke a boboŋa.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam ná ke wo-kenkagele delo ta na wo maŋe de ke to, pa se tega kam bɔke belei ka jwoŋi-ba ka li, ye banto de ba wonnu maama ná zo tega kuri ne ye ba ŋwe, ko wó pa se á lɔre we ba na gwooni Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane mo o ke konto.”

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Moses na yɔɔre o ta konto o ti to, mo tega kam mɛ seeni nɔɔna bam na zege to bɔke belei.

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Ba de ba wonnu maama na sirimi ba zo gwoŋo kom wone konto to, mo tega kam jwoori ka kwoni ka tete. Nɔɔna bam konto laam jei, ye ba daa tera Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom wone.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem nigi nɔɔna bam na laare bɔge-bɔge tei to. Ba de ma duri se ba lu ye ba laare ba we, “Dé vae se tega kam li debam de!”

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
translation_verse: ba na kwei-se ba ma ke pɛɛra ba pa Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane. Nɔɔna balo na ke konto to laam tege mo ba wɛleera ŋwaane. english_verse: just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers. The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
translation_verse: Ko maa ye maana ko pa Isarele tiina bam se ba taa yei we nɔɔn-nɔɔno dae se o zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa o pa Baŋa Wɛ ye o wo nwoŋi Aron dwi dem wone. english_verse: The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
translation_verse: Tega na poore to mo Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama vei Moses de Aron tei ye ba poone ba we, “Abam balei mo go Wɛ nɔɔna bam badaara.”

english_verse: As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na yɔɔre ba jeeri ba gilimi-ba to, mo Moses de Aron pipiri se ba nii wara-jei sem seeni, dedaane kunkwoŋo kom tu ko kwoli wara-vwei dem ye Baŋa Wɛ pɔpɔ o veere o tete de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom o bere ba maama.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent,
translation_verse: Moses de Aron ma vo ba zege wara-vwei dem yiga ne.

english_verse: where the Lord said to them,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: “Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.” They immediately bowed down and prayed.
translation_verse: “Fɔɔre á zege-na dáa ne de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom se a laam yɔɔre a ti ba maama bedwe baŋa ne.” Ba de ma vwi ba yibia tega ne.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
translation_verse: Moses ma ta de Aron o we, “Zaŋe n kwei n min-chala zoŋa kam n daare n le min-chala kaanem dakaa kam mini wone n ke zoŋa kam wone. english_verse: Israelites were dead, not counting those who had died with Korah and his followers.
translation_verse: ). Twa bam konto déem mo woli de balo na maŋe ba te Kora keim-balɔrɔ kom ŋwaane to.
