english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: Call together the twelve tribes of Israel and tell the leader of each tribe to write his name on the walking stick he carries as a symbol of his authority. Make sure Aaron's name is written on the one from the Levi tribe, then collect all the sticks.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye Levi dwi dem nacheiga kam, se n popone Aron yere n ke ka yera ne. Konto to, ba sɔ-yuni tem maama yiga tu nacheiga kam wó taa wora.

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Nam kwei nachei sem konto n ja n zo wara-vwei dem wone n tiŋi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne, mɛ seeni a na yeini a jeeri‑m to.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye nɔɔno wolo amo na kuri se o taa ye a kaanem yiga tu wom to, kotu nacheiga kam wó kwi de vɔɔro. A maa wó tɔge ko baŋa ne se Isarele tiina bam na yɔɔre ba jege‑m ba poona tei to yage.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Moses ma ta Wɛ ni dem o bere Isarele tiina bam. Ba yiga tiina bam ma seene ba pa‑o ba nachei fuga-selei, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nacheiga. Aron nacheiga kam de ma woli da Levi dwi dem ŋwaane.

english_verse: Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Moses ma ja se maama o zo wara-vwei dem wone o tiŋi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Moses ma ja nachei sem maama ya na tigi Baŋa Wɛ dakaa kam yiga ne to o nwoŋi pwooni, se Isarele tiina bam maama na. Yiga tiina bam maama ma lɔre ba nachei ye ba kwei-se.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Moses o we, “Ja Aron nacheiga kam n jwoori n zo n tiŋi ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne. Ka ye maana mo ka pa zwabani-nyena bam we, ba ná wo yage ba pompona kam amo ŋwaane, a wó chɔge-ba.”

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Nmo dé n bia ná yeini á toŋe wara-vwei dem totoŋa, se á pa se á chorro Levi dwi tiina bam taa tui ba woli abam wone ba taa toŋa.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Ta‑á nii ba baŋa ne se ba taa toŋe wara-jei sem maama totoŋa yam. Nam yé pa-na se ba yi ba dwei wara-vwei dem wo-zela yam, naa kaanem dakaa kam. Á ná pɛ-ba chwoŋa pa se ba ke konto, abam de banto maama wó te mo.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Banto mo wó woli abam wone se á ta‑á toŋe wara-jei sem totoŋa yam maama. Ko ná dae banto yerane, nɔn-gaa ba jege chwoŋa se o twɛ abam totoŋa jei sem.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Nmo de n bia bam wó nii wara-vwei dem tete, de kaanem dakaa kam totoŋa baŋa ne, se amo bane daa yé zaŋe de Isarele tiina bam.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Amo tete mo kuri Levi dwi dem Isarele dwia yam maama wone se ba taa ye a nyem. A laam ma kwei-ba a pa abam kaanem tiina bam se ba taa zeini abam.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Nmo de n bia bam yerane mo wó taa toŋe kaanem tiina totoŋa yam. Abam mo jege chwoŋa se á ta‑á ke kaanem á pa-ne dakaa kam baŋa ne, ye á ta daare á gaale á zo wara-vwei gare-jale dem yiga ne. Kaanem totoŋe dem á na wó toŋe to ye pɛɛre mo amo na kwei a pa abam. Nɔn-gaa ná kwaane se o twɛ á totoŋa jei sem, kotu jege se o te mo.” Wɛ kaanem tiina bam pɛɛra taane

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Vara bam konto nɔna nam ye abam nyem mo se á di, nenɛɛne á na jege chwoŋa se á di vara nyɔɔna yalo á na zeiŋi wɛɛne amo ŋwaane to, de ba jazem chwoa yam tei to.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye pɛɛra yalo na tiini ya ye wose ye nɔɔna jaane ba tui ba pa-ne to, á wó pɔɔre á nyem pɛɛra yalo ba na wo zwɛ kaanem dakaa kam baŋa ne to wone mo. Ko ná ye ba wodiu pɛɛra yam, de ba wɛleera saarem pɛɛra yam, de ba wɛleere jene pɛɛra yam, nmo de n bia wó jwoŋi á nyem ya maama wone.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye pɛɛra yalo nɔɔna na yeini ba pɔɔre ba nuga wone, de ba Vini sa-sona wone, de ba wodiiru telo maama na yeini te lwoori yiga te ke to wone ba ja ba ba ba pa-ne to, amo kwei tento a pa abam mo.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Wodiiru telo maama tega kam na yeini te ke ye nɔɔna ja-te ba ba ba pa-ne to wó taa ye abam nyem. N diga tiina bam wolo maama ná maŋe de chullu tem, kotu jege chwoŋa se o jwoŋi te wone o di.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: Woŋo kolo maama Isarele tiina bam na yɔɔre ba kwei ba ke amo jeŋa ne to de wó taa ye abam nyem.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam bakeiri-kwe sem, de ba vare-kwe sem ba na yeini ba ja ba ba se ba pa-ne to maama ye abam nyem mo. Á nam wó pa se ba ŋwe sabu mo se ko leiri ba bakeiri-kwe sem yuu ne. Ko ta ná ye vare-kwe selo na wo maŋe de chullu tem to, ba wó ŋwe sabu se ŋwaane.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Ba ná lage ba ŋwe sabu ba bakeiri-kwe sem ŋwaane, abam wó jwoŋi sɛkɛle sabu-dala yanu mo bu wolo na yi chana to ŋwaane. Sabu kom konto dunni jege se ko tɔge de wara-jei sem maŋem chekke na ye tei to mo. Sɛkɛle dedoa maa ye gɛra kuni finlei.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye vare-kwea kalo na ye naao, naa pia, naa boŋo, ko dae se á jwoŋi sabu ko ŋwaane. Vara bam konto dwoŋi yɔɔre ba ye amo nyem mo. Á jege se á kwei ba jana á miisi kaanem dakaa kam yera ne mo, ye á daare á zwɛ ba lara kam á ma‑á ke zwɛɛm kaanem á pa-ne, se ka lwom dem taa ywomma de pa-ne.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Pɛɛra yalo maama Isarele tiina bam na pɔɔre se ba kwei ba pa-ne to mo amo kwei-ya se ya taa ye nmo de n bia bam nyem, bakeiri de busankane maama. Ya wó taa ye abam nyem taa wuu. Amo ni dem konto wó yɔɔre de taa wora ko pae nmo de n kwaga kam se ko taa vei wuu.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Aron o we: “Ba ná lage ba pɔɔre tega kam ba pa Isarele tiina bam, nmo bá‑n tɔge n jwoŋi n popɔra ka wone. Nmo daa bá‑n na n nyɔn-mage nyem, ko ná dae amo yerane. Amo tete nam mo yɔɔre a maŋe a pa‑m.

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye Levi dwi tiina bam, amo wó pa ba jwoŋi ba ŋweero totoŋa yalo ba na jege ba toŋe wara-vwei dem wone to baŋa ne. Isarele tiina bam ná yeini ba le popɔra dedoa ba wonnu tem popɔre fuga maama wone se ba pa-ne, amo wó kwei amo popɔra kam konto a pa Levi dwi tiina bam.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Banto yerane mo jege se ba taa nii wara-vwei dem baŋa ne, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé chɔge de chullu tem. Nɔn-gaa daa ba jege chwoŋa se o fɔɔre o yi wara-vwei dem. Wolo ná ke konto, kotu tusim dem wó taa wo o yuu ne ye o jege se o te mo. Levi tiina bam de jege se ba na waarem ko ŋwaane. Ni dento a na pɛ abam to wó taa wora mo taa wuu ko pae abam de á kwaga kam. Levi tiina bam nam bá tɔge ba jwoŋi ba popɔra tega kam pɔɔrem baŋa ne, ne ba chorro Isarele tiina bam na wó na tei to.

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: “Ta n bere Levi tiina bam we: Abam ná jwoŋi Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yalo na ye abam nyem to Isarele tiina bam tei ne, se á de le popɔra dedoa fuga maama wone á pa Baŋa Wɛ. Ya wó taa ye abam tete Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra á na le banto Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yam wone to mo.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wó jeeli á Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra yam konto, nenɛɛne á ya ná kwei á tete mena naa sa-doora á pa‑o to mo.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Ta ta de Levi tiina bam we: Abam ná pɔɔre wonnu telo na tiini te lana to á pa Wɛ, o wó jeeli á pɛɛra yam konto, nenɛɛne á ya ná kwei á tete mena naa sa-doora á pa‑o to mo.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Á ná yɔɔre á le wonnu telo na tiini te lana to se te taa ye á Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra á pa‑o, á bá na chɔgem chullu tem seeni. Pɛɛra yalo Isarele tiina bam na jaane ba tui ba pa-ne to ye wose mo. Ko dae se á kwei-ya á di yɔɔ yɔɔ. Á ná tɔge chwei sem konto, á bá te chullu tem chɔgem ŋwaane.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: “Amo Baŋa Wɛ tiŋi a ni dento mo se á ta‑á tɔge-de. Ta-na á bere Isarele tiina bam we: Ba jege se ba ja na-chwɛ-soŋo kolo na ba jege gɛɛ ko yera ne ye ba ta wo kwei-ko ba ma toŋe to mo ba ba ba pa abam.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Á wó kwei-ko á pa kaanem tu Eleaza. O de maa wó ja-ko o nwoŋi o vo dáa, pa se ba go-ko ye o zege o nia.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Eleaza ta wó de o noa na-chwɛ dem jana wone, ye o laam pipiri o jeeri wara-jei sem yiga seeni o miisi jana bam kuni berepɛ.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Na-chwɛ dem na jege de zwɛ konto to, kaanem tu wom laam wó kwei Sedare daa dedoa, de Husopa tio vɔɔro, de gare-ŋon-seŋa, o dole-te o de mini dem wone.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne se kaanem tu wom swɛ o yera o daare o zare o gwaaro. O laam jege chwoŋa se o jwoori o taa zoore Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom wone. O laam maa wó digiri chullu tem seeni se ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wolo de na zwɛ na-chwɛ dem to de wó zare o gwaaro mo ye o daare o swɛ o yera. Wonto de wó digiri chullu tem seeni mo se ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Wolo na maŋe de chullu tem to maa wó pɛ na-chwɛ dem tentwarem dem, ye o ke-de pwola kalo ba na kwɛ Wɛ ŋwaane to ne. Jeiga kam konto nam wó taa ye dáa dáa mo de á na zoore mɛ to. Ba ta wó yeini ba viiri tentwarem dem na wone se Isarele tiina bam ma ba kwɛ ba tete de chullu tem wɛleera saarem ŋwaane.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Wolo na pɛ tentwarem dem to de wó zare o gwaaro mo. O de wó digiri chullu tem seeni se ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa mo. Abam Isarele tiina bam de veira balo na zoore á wone to jege se á tɔge ni dento mo se ko taa vei wuu.

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Wolo ná dwei too, konto tu digiri chullu tem seeni mo se ko taa vei da yarepɛ.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: O jege se o kwei chullu kwɛɛm na bam mo o ma o kwɛ o tete de chullu tem. O wó ke konto da yatɔ dɛ dem ne, dedaane da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne mo, se o laam maŋe de chullu tem. O ná wo kwɛ o tete da yam konto ne, o yɔɔre o ta wo maŋe de chullu tem mo.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ná dwei too, ye o ve se o kwɛ o tete chullu tem ŋwaane, kotu chɔge Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem mo. Ba le‑o se o daa yé woli Isarele tiina bam wone. O ta digiri chullu tem seeni mo, ba na wo kwei chullu kwɛɛm na bam ba miisi o yera ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná wo vwei ne ye o te, chullu tem bere we wolo maama na wora ye kotu te, de wolo na zo da o maŋe de o toone dem to maama digiri mo chullu tem seeni se ko taa vei da yarepɛ.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno na maŋe de chullu tem to laam wó kwei Husopa tio vɔɔro o de na bam wone o daare o miisi vwei dem, de de wo-zela yam, de nɔɔna balo na wo de wone ye nɔɔno wom te to. Ko ta ye bedwe mo de wolo ná dwei too, naa too kua, naa yibeeli. Ba jege se ba miisi kotu de chullu kwɛɛm na bam mo.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Á wó miisi wolo na digiri to da yatɔ dɛ dem ne, dedaane da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, se o laam maŋe de chullu tem. Nɔɔno wom wó zare o gwaaro mo o daare o swɛ o yera. Dedaan-ni maŋa ná yia, o wó maŋe de chullu tem.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná digiri chullu tem seeni, ye o ve se o kwɛ o tete de chullu tem, ba jege se ba le kotu se o daa yé woli Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom wone mo, o na chɔge Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem to ŋwaane. O ta digiri mo chullu tem seeni, ba na wo kwei chullu kwɛɛm na bam ba miisi o yera ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Nia yanto nam wó taa wora taa wuu ya pa abam. Wolo na kwei chullu kwɛɛm na bam o miisi nɔɔna to de jege se o zare o gwaaro mo. Wolo maama de ná dwei na bam konto, kotu wó digiri chullu tem seeni, se ko taa nii dedaan-ni maŋa.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Wolo na digiri chullu tem seeni to ná dwei woŋo kolo maama, woŋo kom konto de digiri mo. Wolo de nam ná dwei woŋo kom, o de wó digiri o tete se ko taa nii dedaan-ni maŋa mo.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom déem ma beeri ba vo ba yi Zin kagoa kam boboa chana kam ne. Ba ma vo ba chwi ba vwoa Kadese ne ba zoore da. Ba na wora to, Miriam déem ma te ye ba suli‑o da.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ba ma bwɛ Moses ye ba we, “Debam de déem ya ná tɔge dedaane dé chorro tem dé te Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem yiga ne, ko ya gare tento.

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Nmo nam yɔɔre n ja debam na ye Baŋa Wɛ kɔgɔ kom to mo n ba n dole n yage kagoa kanto ne, se debam dedaane dé vara maama te.

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Bɛ mo ye n ja debam n nwoŋi Ejipti teo wone se dé ba dé zege kasol-gwiu konto ne? Wodiiru ware se te ke ywo-seeni, kaporro nam tera, Vini teeni de tera, Pomegara teeni de maa tera. Na de nam tera se dé nyɔ!”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Moses de Aron ma tutwoni ba kɛ ba daare nɔn-kɔgɔ kom ba vo ba zege wara-vwei dem ni ne. Ba ma vwi ba yibia tega ne, ye Baŋa Wɛ pɔpɔ o chu o veere o tete ko tɔge de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom o bere-ba.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Zaŋe n kwei n nacheiga kam se nmo de n zembaaro Aron vo á la kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama á ke daane. Laam zege ba yiga ne n ŋɔɔne de peo kolo na zege tento to. Na wó ta ba nwoŋi ko yera ne. Chega to, nmo wó pa na taa nwoŋi peo kom wone ba pae nɔn-kɔgɔ kom de ba vara bam se ba taa nyɔa.”

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: O de Aron ma ja nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama ba vo ba zege peo kom yiga ne. Moses laam ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam zwabani-nyena banto, cheigi-na! Debam mo jege se dé pa se na ta ba nwoŋi peo konto ne se á nyɔ na?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: O laam ma zeiŋi o jeŋa wɛɛne ye o kwei o nacheiga kam o ma mage peo kom kuni belei. Na-fɔrɔ ma pɔpɔ ba wuura ye ba chuura, pa se nɔɔna bam de ba vara nyɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Ko daare Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses de Aron o we, “Abam nam wo ke á wo-dedoa de amo se ko pa Isarele tiina bam lɔre we, amo yɔɔre a ye wose. Á wo-dedoa kam na muri to ŋwaane, a daa bá pa abam chwoŋa se á ja amo nɔn-kɔgɔ kom á vo á zo tega kalo a na lage a pa-ba to wone.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Ba déem jege jei sem konto ba bwoi we ‘Meriba’ mo. Dáane mo Isarele tiina bam mage kantɔgɔ dedaane Baŋa Wɛ. O de ma bere-ba o wo-pwoŋo kom na ye tei to. Edom teo pɛ ve se o pa Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba kɛ

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Moses déem ma zege Kadese ne o toŋe kwora o pa Edom teo pɛ o we: “Debam ye nmo tete chorro Isarele dwi tiina bam mo. Nmo maŋe n yei yaara yalo maama na yi debam to ni ne.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: Dé nabaara déem vei ba zo Ejipti teo wone ba maŋe da bena dedɛ. Ko kwaga ne mo Ejipti tiina bam bɛɛse dé kwoa bam de debam de.

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: Dé na keeri dé jare Baŋa Wɛ to, mo o nigi dé wɛ-lworo kom. O ma tɔge o maleka baŋa ne o ja debam o nwoŋi teo kom konto ne. Dé laam nam tu dé jei Kadese ne mo, ko na wo abam teo kom siseini ni ne to.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Dé maa lwoori nmo mo se n pa debam chwoŋa se dé tɔge n tega kam baŋa dé kɛ. Dé bá tɔge á kare de á kadwi seeni. Dé maŋe dé bá mɔ na á vola yam ne dé nyɔ. Dé nam wó yɔɔre dé tole chwo-fara kam yerane mo taa se dé vo dé bɛ abam laŋa kam. Dé bere dé bá ywori chwoŋa kam ne.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Edom pɛ wom ma leiri o we, “Aawo! Debam bá pa abam chwoŋa se á tɔge dé laŋa kam á kɛ. Abam nam ná fe se á tɔge da á kɛ, dé wó nwoŋi dé jeeri abam de jara.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma jwoori ba leiri ba we, “Dé nam wó maŋe chwo-fara kam ni ne mo dé taa via. Debam de dé vara ná nyɔge á na, dé wó ŋwe dé pa abam. Dé na lwoori kolo yerane to mo ye se dé tɔge á laŋa kam ne dé kɛ.”

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Konto to, Edom tiina bam wo pɛ Isarele tiina bam chwoŋa se ba tɔge ba laŋa kam ba kɛ. Ko déem pɛ se Isarele tiina bam pipiri mo ba jwoori kwaga se ba kwei chwo-gaa. Aron toone

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama déem ma zege Kadese ne ba vo ba yi Hora peo kom

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Aron lage o maŋe ywo-seeni mo o te. O bá zo tega kalo a na lage a pa Isarele tiina bam to wone, abam balei na nwoŋi amo ni dem kwaga ne Meriba jei sem ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Moses, nam ja Aron de o bu Eleaza se á maama di Hora peo kom yuu.

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: Pa se Aron lɔɔre o kaanem gare-laaro tem, se n kwei-te n zo o bu Eleaza. Kokuri to, Aron lage o te peo kom yuu ne mo.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Moses maa seene o ke tei Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ ni se o ke to. Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama déem zege ba nia mo ye wonto, de Aron, dedaane Eleaza di Hora peo kom yuu.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Moses ma lɔɔre Aron kaanem gwaaro tem, ye o daare o kwei-te o zo Eleaza. Aron ma maŋe peo kom yuu ne o te. Moses de Eleaza ma zege peo kom yuu ne ba maa tu tega.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na yɔɔre ba lɔre we Aron tege to, mo ba maama keeri o lua kam da fintɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem na zaŋe Hora peo kom ne to, ko jege se ba kaare ba yage Edom laŋa kam dáa ne mo. Ba ma kwei Nane-soŋo chwoŋa kam ba kɛ. Ba nam na wo chwoŋa ne ba vei to, mo nɔɔna bam daa wo wane ba ja ba tete.

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: Ba maa ŋwaane Wɛ de daane Moses ye ba we, “Moses, bɛ mo ye nmo yɔɔre n ja debam n nwoŋi Ejipti wone, se dé ba dé te kagoa kanto wone? Wodi-laao tera ywo-seeni. Na de maa tera se dé nyɔ. Dé yera de laam chɛ de wodi-yɔɔ konto.”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se basankwe selo ni na chana to to Isarele tiina bam wone, ye se done ba dedɛ se go.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam badwonna ma vo Moses tei ba ta ba we, “Dé na ŋɔɔne dé chɔge Baŋa Wɛ de nmo to, ko ye wɛleere mo dé kea. Nam lwoori Baŋa Wɛ n pa debam, se o pa se basankwe sento viiri se daare debam.” Moses de ma lwoori Wɛ o pa nɔɔna bam.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Moses o we, “Nam yɔɔre n mɔ basankwea, se n daare n kwei-ka n lei daa yera ne. Basankwe sem ná done wolo maama, kotu wó kwoni o nii-ka se o ma jwoŋi o ŋwea.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Moses ma kwei channa o ma o mɔ basankwea o daare o lei-ka daa yera ne o zege-ka deiki. Wolo maama basankwe sem na done ye o kwoni o nii channa basankwea kam to mo jwoŋi o ŋwea o yage. Ba kwei chwoŋa ba maa vei Moaba

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam daa ma zaŋe ba vo ba yi Obofe teo ba jeini da.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma zaŋe ba vo ba bɛ Aranon buga kam, ye ba vo ba jeini kagoa kalo na wo Amori tiina laŋa kam siseini ni ne to. Aranon buga kam déem mo ye siseini na tigi Moaba tiina bam de Amori tiina bam tetare ne to.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane nam mo tei Baŋa Wɛ Jara-keim Tɔnɔ kom tage jei sem konto taane we: “Waheba teo na wo Sufa laŋa ne, de ko nabare sem, de Aranon buga kam,

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: de nabare sem siswooru tem konto na tigi Moaba siseini ni ne, ye te kɛ te yi Ara teo to.”

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Ba ma zege jei sem konto ne ba vo ba yi Beeri teo. Vole maa wo teo kom konto ne, ye dáane mo Baŋa Wɛ déem tage de Moses o we, “La nɔɔna bam n ke daane se a lage a pa-ba na mo se ba nyɔ.”

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa ne mo Isarele tiina bam leeni leiŋa kanto ba we: “Vole dem na buri na de pa debam to, debam de wó ke wopwolo ye dé leeni lei!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Pwa mo koge vole dem! Naduna de ma fɔge-de! Ba kwei ba paare nachei sem mo ba ko-de!” Isarele tiina bam déem ma zaŋe kagoa kam ne ba vo ba jeini Matana ne.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ba ma zege Bamofe ne ba vo ba yi bwolo kodwoŋi na wo Moaba laŋa kam ne to. Ba ma jeini mɛ na twɛ de Pisiga peo kom to. Peo kom yuu maa yɔɔre ko jeeri kagoa kam seeni. Ba na di Pɛ Sihon de Pɛ Oga tei to

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma toŋe kwora ba pa Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon, ye ba we:

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Dé lwoori nmo mo se n pa debam chwoŋa se dé tɔge n tega kam baŋa dé kɛ. Dé bá ywori chwoŋa kam ne dé tɔge á kare de á kadwi seeni. Dé maŋe dé bá mɔ na á vola yam ne dé nyɔ. Dé nam wó yɔɔre dé tole chwo-fara kam yerane mo taa se dé vo dé bɛ abam laŋa kam.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Pɛ Sihon ma ve se Isarele tiina bam tɔge o laŋa kam ne ba kɛ. O ma bwoŋi o jar-keira bam maama o ke daane, ye ba nwoŋi ba vo kagoa kam wone se ba jeeri Isarele tiina bam. Ba na yi Jahaza seeni to, mo ba déem kwaare jara de-ba.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma di-ba. Ba ma vere ba tega kam ba tei, ko zege Aranon buga kam ni ne, se ko yi Jaboke buga kam. Ba nam wo bɛ Jaboke buga kam ba kɛ, ko na ye Amon tiina bam siseini dem ye de fɔge de che de dam to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem vere Amori tiina teene dem maama, de ba te-fɔrɔ Hesebon de ko nawuura yam mo. Ba maa lɛɛre ba zoore de wone.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Min-fɔrɔ déem nwoŋi Pɛ Sihon teo Hesebon wone ko jage ko di Moaba teo Ara, de naduna balo na zoore Aranon peero tem wone to.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Debam laam nam yɔɔre dé wane-ba dé di mo, ko zege Hesebon ne se ko yi Dibon seeni. Dé chɔge-ba mo se ko vo ko yi Nofa, se ko ta yi Medeba seeni.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem na jeini Amori tiina tega kam ne to,

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: mo Moses toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba ŋɔ ba nii Jazera teo kom. Ba na nii-ko to, Isarele tiina bam ma vo ba di teo kom konto de ko nawuura yam. Ba ma zeili Amori tiina bam na zoore jei sem konto ne to.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne mo Isarele tiina bam pipiri ba kwei Basan chwoŋa kam ba via. Basan teo Pɛ Oga ma nwoŋi de o jar-keira bam maama o vo o jeeri-ba Ederi ne se ba kwaare jara.

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma yɔɔre ba ti Pɛ Oga, de o bia, de o jar-keira bam maama pa se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa wo daare. Ba maa lɛɛre ba zoore o tega kam ne.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma gɔ ba vwoa yam ba vo ba yi Moaba laŋa kam te-kampare ba jeini da. Jei sem konto wo Jɔdan buga kam ni ne mo ye Jeriko de wo bubɛ dedwoŋi dem seeni.

english_verse: When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked.
translation_verse: Foone ma tiini de zo o de o nɔɔna bam, Isarele tiina bam kɔgɔ kom na daga to ŋwaane. Moaba tiina bam nagwola ma te Isarele tiina bam ŋwaane.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Ba ma ta de Midian tiina nakwa bam ba we, “Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom lage ko ba ko chɔge debam de dé wonnu tem maama, ne nabea na yɔɔre ka gaane gaao pwola ne tei to mo.”

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: Moaba Pɛ Balaki déem toŋe kwora o pa Beora bu Balaam se o ba o tei. Balaam déem zoore Amawa teo kodwoŋi ne, ko yere mo Petora. Ko déem wo Yuferata buga kam ni ne mo. Pɛ Balaki maa we: “Nɔn-dwi dedwoŋi mo zege Ejipti ne ba ba ywo-seeni. Ba yɔɔre ba jage jei maama mo, ye ba laam ba ba jeini amo tega kam ni ne.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam konto dana ba dwoi debam. Nam ba n sɔɔle lwarem n yage ba yera ne, se ko pa dé wane-ba dé zeili se ba viiri ba daare debam. Amo yei lanyerane we nmo ná yeini n sɔɔle Wɛ swolim n yage wolo yera ne, konto tu wó seene o jwoŋi Wɛ swolim mo. N ma‑n ná sɔɔle lwarem n daŋe wolo yuu ne, kotu wó seene o na lɛɛro mo.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Moaba de Midian tiina nakwa bam ma zaŋe se ba vo Balaam tei. Ba ma kwei kwora se ba ŋwe‑o o yi-nɛɛre totoŋe dem ŋwaane. Ba na yi da to mo ba pɛ‑o Balaki ni dem.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Balaam ma leiri-ba o we, “Maŋe-na ywo-seeni á peini, se tega ná poore, se a laam leiri á taane dem, ne Baŋa Wɛ na veere o boboŋa o bere-ne tei to.” Moaba dedɛɛra bam ma maŋe o sɔŋɔ ne ba peini.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Tete ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma ba Balaam tei ye o we, “Nɔɔna banto ye bera mo ye ba ba nmo sɔŋɔ?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Balaam ma leiri o we, “Moaba teo Pɛ Balaki mo toŋe-ba se ba ba ba ta de amo we,

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: nɔn-dwi dedwoŋi mo nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba ba ba jage tega kam baŋa maama. O laam maa lage se a vo o tei, se a sɔɔle lwarem a daŋe ba baŋa ne, se o wane-ba o zeili se ba viiri ba daare‑o.”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Wɛ ma ta ded‑o o we, “Yé sɛ n tɔge Balaki tontoŋena bam kwaga se á vo o tei. Nam yé sɔɔle lwarem n daŋe nɔn-kɔgɔ kom konto baŋa ne, se amo maŋe a swɛ ba swolim mo.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Balaam ma yi Balaki tontoŋena bam tei ye o ta de-ba o we, “Jwoori-na á tete teo, se Baŋa Wɛ ve se a da de abam a vo.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Balaki daa ma toŋe o dedɛɛra badwonna se ba vo Balaam tei. Banto tiini ba ye naduna, ye ba daga ba dwoi boboa nɔɔna bam.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Ba na yi Balaam tei to, mo ba we, “Zipore bu Balaki toŋe ni o we, n yé pa kolokolo che‑m se n ba omo tei.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Nam maŋe-na ywo-seeni á peini, nenɛɛne á dwonna bam daama na ke tei to. Amo ta wó nii Baŋa Wɛ jege boboŋe dedwoŋi se o daa veere o bere-ne na?”

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Balaam ma zaŋe o vɔ o bonaga de zela. O na diini-ka to, o ma tɔge de Moaba dedɛɛra bam pa se ba kɛ. Balaam de o bonaga kam

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ bane nam ya zaŋe de Balaam mo o na tɔge de-ba o maa vei to ŋwaane. Balaam déem diini o bonaga mo ye ba via. O tontoŋena balei de maa tɔge ba via. Ba na maa vei to, Baŋa Wɛ maleka ma zege ka che Balaam chwoŋa se o yé kɛ.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Bonaga kam na nɛ we Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam chege ba chwoŋa ye se-zɔɔ wo ka jeŋa ne to, mo ka yage chwoŋa kam ye ka lɔ ka zo gaaro wone. Balaam maa mage-ka ye o ja-ka o jwoori o de chwoŋa kam ne.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Bonaga kam daa ma na Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam. Ka ma peene ka tete de kabira kam pa se kabiri kam kweere Balaam napere. O daa ma mage o bonaga kam.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ta ma fɔɔre ka yi ka zege chwoŋa kam mɛ na tiini ka peene to ne. Laŋa daa tera se bonaga kam tɔge jazem naa jagwia seeni ka kɛ.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Ka de na nɛ konto to, mo ka to tega ne ka tiga. Balaam daa maa ware o bane o ja. O ma kwei o nacheiga o jege bonaga kam o maga.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Se nɛ sem ni ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ bonaga kam chwoŋa se ka ŋɔɔne. Ka ma bwei Balaam ka we, “Bɛ mo a ke a chɔge pa se n yɔɔre n mage-ne kuni betɔ tento dwoŋi?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Balaam ma leiri-ka o we, “Ko ye nmo na pɛ se a nye de jworo to ŋwaane mo. A ya ná maŋe a jege se-zɔɔ ywo-seeni, a ya wó go‑m lela.”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Bonaga kam laam maa we, “Amo dae nmo tete bonaga mo ye n jege-ne n diini maŋa maama na? A nam yeini a ke tento dwoŋi nmo yera ne na?” Balaam ma leiri we, “Aawo! N ta wo ke tento dwoŋi.”

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Maleka kam ma bwei‑o ka we, “Bɛŋwaane mo nmo mage n bonaga kam kuni betɔ konto? Amo nwoŋi se a ba a dwoni de nmo, kokuri to, a nɛ we chwoŋa kalo n na kwei to ba jege kuri.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Ko ná dae n bonaga kam ŋwaane, tento a ya go‑m. Ka nɛ-ne mo pa se ka ywori chwoŋa kam ne kuni betɔ. Ko ya ná dae konto, a ya wó go‑m ye a daare a yage n bonaga kam pa se ka viiri.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Balaam ma leiri maleka kam o we, “Amo ke a tusi. A ya yeiri we nmo chege chwoŋa mo se n dwoni de amo. De ko de, nmo yi ná wo su a veiŋa kam, amo wó jwoori sɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ma ta ded‑o ka we, “Ta tɔge de nɔɔna bam n kɛ. Nam lɔre se n ta kolo yerane amo na wó bere‑m se n ta to.” Balaam laam ma da de Balaki dedɛɛra bam o kɛ.

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Balaki na nigi we Balaam wo chwoŋa ne o beene o tei to, mo o nwoŋi o vo se o jeeri‑o Moaba teo kodwoŋi ne. Ko déem wo Aranon buga kam ni ne mo, se ko maŋe de o laŋa kam siseini.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: O na yi da to, o ma bwei Balaam o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n wo sɛ a kwora kam a na toŋe to? Bɛ mo ye n wo tu lela? Nmo boŋe se a jeŋa muri se a ŋwe‑m mo na?”

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Ba ma tɔge daane ba vo Kiriaf-Huzofa.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Ba na yi da to, Balaki ma kwei naane de pei o ke kaanem. O ma fɔ nɔna yam wone o kwei o pa Balaam de o teo dedɛɛra balo na tɔge ded‑o to.

english_verse: and listed everything that had been taken from the Midianites. The list included
translation_verse: dedaane bukwa balo na yeiri baara to morro fintɔ-telei (

english_verse: and said, “Sir, we have counted our troops, and not one soldier is missing.
translation_verse: ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Dé kwo, debam na jeeli dé nɔɔna bam ni, kɔgɔ de kɔgɔ to, dé maane we nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo jei.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar accepted the jewelry from the commanders,
translation_verse: Moses de Wɛ kaanem tu Eleaza ma jwoŋi sabu-seŋa jejegero tem jar-keira dedɛɛra bam tei ne.

english_verse: This did not include the things that the soldiers had kept for themselves.
translation_verse: Ko daare jar-keira bam maama de déem jwoŋi ba nyem wonnu telo ba na vere Midian tiina bam tei ne to wone mo.

english_verse: So Moses and Eleazar placed the gold in the Lord's sacred tent to remind Israel of what had happened.
translation_verse: Moses de Eleaza déem ma jwoŋi sabu-seŋa wonnu tem dedɛɛra bam tei ne ba ja ba vo ba tiŋi wara-jei sem wone, se ko taa ye gula ko pae Isarele tiina bam Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben and Gad owned a lot of cattle and sheep, and they saw that the regions of Jazer and Gilead had good pastureland.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye Ruben de Gad dwia yam, ba vara kɔgɔ déem daga dedɛ. Ba ma na we Jazera tega kam de Gilead tega kam lana se vara bam taa di ba sui.

english_verse: So they went to Moses, Eleazar, and the other leaders of Israel and said,
translation_verse: Ba ma vo Moses, de Wɛ kaanem tu Eleaza, dedaane Isarele kɔgɔ kom yiga tiina badwonna bam tei, ye ba we,

english_verse: “The Lord has helped us capture the land around the towns of Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon. That's good pastureland, and since we own cattle and sheep,
translation_verse: “Baŋa Wɛ seene o woli debam pa se dé di Atarofa, de Dibon, de Jazera, de Nimira, de Hesebon, de Elealɛ, de Sebam, de Nebo, de Beon. Dé nam maane we tega kalo na gilimi teene dento to tiini ka lana de vara kɔnɔ. Chega to, dé vara kɔgɔ kom daga dedɛ.

english_verse: would you let us stay here east of the Jordan River and have this land as our own?”
translation_verse: Dé kwo, nmo yi ná su dé kikia yam, sɛ se dé yé bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. Kwei ywo-seeni tega kam n pa debam se dé taa tei.”

english_verse: If you did that, it would discourage the others from crossing over into the land the Lord promised them.
translation_verse: Abam ná ke konto, á chorro tem vɔna wó pare mo pa se ba ga chwoŋa se ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ba vo ba zo tega kalo Baŋa Wɛ na kwei o pa-ba to wone.

english_verse: This is exactly what happened when I sent your ancestors from Kadesh-Barnea to explore the land.
translation_verse: Amo déem na zege Kadese-Baranea ne, ye a toŋe á kwoa bam se ba vo ba nii tega kam to, ba déem ke abam kikia yam dwoŋi mo.

english_verse: Moses said: You promised that you would be ready to fight for the Lord.
translation_verse: Moses ma leiri-ba o we: “Abam ná seene yia mo se á ke konto, ti-na yiga se á nwoŋi á vo á ke jara yam Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: So Moses gave the Machirites the region of Gilead, and they settled there.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane Moses ma kwei Gilead laŋa kam o pa Makira sɔ-yuu tiina bam se ba taa zoore da.

english_verse: Now you people of Reuben and Gad are doing the same thing and making the Lord even angrier.
translation_verse: Nii-na! Abam nam daa zege se á tɔge á kwoa totoŋ-naga kam mo, se Baŋa Wɛ bane daa tiini de zaŋe Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne de woli da. Á ye puseŋ-nyena mo!

english_verse: If you reject the Lord, he will once again abandon his people and leave them here in the desert. And you will be to blame!
translation_verse: Abam zem ná ywori Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne, á wó pa se o de ve nɔɔna bam maama mo o yage kagoa kanto wone. Abam wó pa se ba na ba chɔgem.”

english_verse: We will stay with them until they have settled in their own tribal lands.
translation_verse: Dé nam bá jwoori ywo-seeni, ko ná dae we Isarele dwi tiina maama nɛ ba jeiŋa jei se ba jeini.

english_verse: The land on this side of the Jordan River will be ours, so we won't expect to receive any on the other side.
translation_verse: Debam tete bá tɔge dé jwoŋi tega kalo na tigi Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ dedwoŋi dem seeni to, dé na nɛ dé tega kam ywo-seeni to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: You also agreed to cross the Jordan and stay with the rest of the Israelites, until the Lord forces our enemies out of the land. If you do these things,
translation_verse: Nam pa-na se á baara bam maama kwei ba jara zela yam ba tɔge ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ba vo ba jeeri dé dona bam de jara, se ko taa nii Baŋa Wɛ ná zeili-ba dé yiga ne

english_verse: Go ahead and build towns for your wives and children, and places for your sheep and goats. Just be sure to do what you have promised.
translation_verse: Tɔ. Lɔ-na teene se á kaana de á bia taa zoore de wone. Ta fɔge-na jei se á pe á pei sem, de á bone dem se wone. Nam ta ke-na á na gwoni ni se á ke tei to.”

english_verse: The men from Reuben and Gad answered: Sir, we will do just what you have said.
translation_verse: Gad dwi tiina de Ruben dwi tiina bam ma leiri Moses ba we: “Dé kwo. Dé wó ke tei nmo na pɛ debam ni se dé ke to.

english_verse: Our wives and children and sheep and cattle will stay here in the towns in Gilead.
translation_verse: Dé kaana, de dé bia, de dé vara mo wó maŋe Gilead teene dem laŋa ne.

english_verse: “Make sure that the tribes of Gad and Reuben prepare for battle and cross the Jordan River with you. If they do, then after the land is in your control, give them the region of Gilead as their tribal land.
translation_verse: “Ruben dwi tiina de Gad dwi tiina baara bam maama jege se ba kwei ba jara zela ba tɔge de abam ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam, se ba vo ba ke jara Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane ba woli abam se á de jwoŋi á tega. Konto ná ke pa se á na á jeiŋa jei, se á laam kwei Gilead laŋa kam á pa-ba se ba taa tei.

english_verse: But if they break their promise, they will receive land on the other side of the Jordan, like the rest of the tribes.”
translation_verse: Ba nam ná wo sɛ se ba bɛ ba vo ba ke jara yam, se á pa ba de tɔge ba jwoŋi ba tega Kanaan laŋa kam ne, mɛ á maama na wó jwoŋi á nyem to.”

english_verse: The tribes of Gad and Reuben replied, “We are your servants and will do whatever the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Gad dwi tiina bam, de Ruben dwi tiina bam ma leiri ba we, “Dé kwo, dé wó ke se ko tɔge de Baŋa Wɛ ni dem.

english_verse: We will cross the Jordan River, ready to fight for the Lord in Canaan. But the land we will inherit as our own will be on this side of the river.”
translation_verse: Dé wó kwei dé jara zela dé tɔge dé bɛ Jɔdan buga kam dé zo Kanaan laŋa kam wone se dé ke jara Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane. Ko kwaga ne dé laam wó jwoori dé jeini ywo-seeni se dé taa tei tega kanto na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to.”

english_verse: So Moses gave the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh the territory and towns that King Sihon the Amorite had ruled, as well as the territory and towns that King Og of Bashan had ruled.
translation_verse: Moses déem ma kwei tega o pa Gad dwi tiina bam, de Ruben dwi tiina bam, de Josɛf bu Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom se ba taa tei. O na pɛ-ba tega kalo to maa ye: Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon paare dim laŋa kam, dedaane Basan teo Pɛ Oga paare dim laŋa kam mo, ko ná ye ba tega kam maama, de ba teene dem de de nawuura yam.

english_verse: The tribe of Gad rebuilt the towns of Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
translation_verse: Gad tiina bam déem ma fɔge ba lɔ Dibon, de Atarofa, de Arowa,

english_verse: Atroth-Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
translation_verse: de Aterofa-Sofan, de Jazera, de Jogebeha,

english_verse: Beth-Nimrah, and Beth-Haran. They built walls around them and also built places to keep their sheep and goats.
translation_verse: de Bɛte-Nimira, dedaane Bɛte-Haran. Ba ma lɔ teene dem konto ba pe, ye ba daare ba fɔge jei se ba pe ba pei se wone.

english_verse: The tribe of Reuben rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
translation_verse: Ruben tiina bam de ma jwoori ba lɔ Hesebon, de Elealɛ, de Kiriafayim,

english_verse: Sibmah, as well as the towns that used to be known as Nebo and Baal-Meon. They renamed all those places.
translation_verse: de Nebo, de Baal-Meon, ko woli de Sibima. Ba déem pɛ teene dem konto de yera mo. De yera badwonna de déem leiri mo.

english_verse: The clan of Machir from the tribe of East Manasseh went to the region of Gilead, captured its towns, and forced out the Amorites.
translation_verse: Manasɛ bu Makira sɔ-yuu tiina bam déem vei Gilead teo kom ba ke jara ba di-ko, ye ba zeili Amori tiina bam ya na zoore da to.

english_verse: Moses kept a list of the places they camped, just as the Lord had instructed. Here is the record of their journey:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma pa Moses ni se o taa popone mɛ de mɛ maama ba na yeini ba yi se ba chwi ba vwoa yam to. Isarele tiina bam na tɔge jei selo ye Moses popone se yera o tiŋi to mo tento:

english_verse: Israel left the Egyptian city of Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month. This was the day after the Lord had punished Egypt's gods by killing the first-born sons in every Egyptian family. So while the Egyptians were burying the bodies, they watched the Israelites proudly leave their country.
translation_verse: Banto maa wora ba suli ba twa, Baŋa Wɛ na mage ba bakeiri-kwe sem maama o go to ŋwaane. Baŋa Wɛ dɛ keim dem konto baŋa ne mo o chɔge Ejipti tiina jwona yam dam.

english_verse: and from there, they moved their camp to Etham on the edge of the desert.
translation_verse: Ba ma zege dáane ba vo Etam. Ko maa wo kagoa kam ni ne.

english_verse: Then they turned back toward Pi-Hahiroth, east of Baal-Zephon, and camped near Migdol.
translation_verse: Ba daa ma pipiri ba vo Pi Hahirofa. Jei sem konto wo Baal-Zefon wɛ-puli seeni mo. Ba ma chwi ba vwoa Migidola seeni.

english_verse: They left Elim and camped near the Red Sea,
translation_verse: Ba daa na yage Elim to, ba ma jwoori Nane-soŋo kom ni ne ba jeini da.

english_verse: then turned east and camped along the western edge of the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: Ba na yage Nane-soŋo kom seeni to, ba ma vo ba chwi ba vwoa Sin kagoa kam wone.

english_verse: From there they went to Dophkah, Alush, and Rephidim, where they had no water.
translation_verse: Ba ma zaŋe Alusi ne ba vo ba chwi ba vwoa Refidim ne. Jei sem konto ne na déem tera se nɔɔna bam taa nyɔa.

english_verse: They left Rephidim and finally reached the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: Ba na yage Refidim to, ba laam ma zo Sinayi kagoa kam ne.

english_verse: That's where the Lord commanded Aaron the priest to go to the top of the mountain. Aaron died there on the first day of the fifth month,
translation_verse: Ba na wora to, mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ Aron ni se o di peo kom yuu. Aron ma di ye o daare o te. Isarele tiina bam na nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne to bena finna bene dem, chane senu chana kam boboa dɛ ne mo o tega.

english_verse: It was then that the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Southern Desert of Canaan, heard that Israel was headed that way.
translation_verse: Arada teo pɛ na zoore Kanaan kagoa kam na wo tega-kuri seeni to ma ni we Isarele tiina bam beene o jei sem seeni.

english_verse: The Israelites left Mount Hor and headed toward Moab. Along the way, they camped at Zalmonah, Punon, Oboth, Iye-Abarim in the territory of Moab, Dibon-Gad, Almon-Diblathaim, at a place near Mount Nebo in the Abarim Mountains,
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem na yage Hora peo kom ba daare ba beeri ba zege jei selo ne ye ba chwi ba vwoa to mo tento: Zalemona, de Punon, de Obofe, de Ye-Abarim na wo Moaba laŋa kam siseini ni ne to, de Dibon-Gad, de Alemon-Dibilafayim, de Abarim peero jei selo na bwola de Nebo peo kom to.

english_verse: Their camp stretched from Beth-Jeshimoth to Acacia. The Lord's Command To Conquer Canaan
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma chwi ba vwoa Jɔdan buga kam ni ne, ko zege Bɛte-Jesimofa ne se ko taa vei Abel-Sitim.

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ba na wo Moaba laŋa kam te-kampare ne konto to, mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Moses o we:

english_verse: to give the people of Israel this message: When you cross the Jordan River and enter Canaan,
translation_verse: “Nam ta de Isarele tiina bam we: Abam ná bɛ Jɔdan buga kam se á zo Kanaan tega kam wone,

english_verse: Then settle in the land—I have given it to you as your own.
translation_verse: Laam daare á jeini-na ba tega kam wone, se amo mo kwei-ka a pa abam se á ta‑á tei.

english_verse: I will show you how to divide the land among the tribes, according to the number of clans in each one, so that the larger tribes will have more land than the smaller ones.
translation_verse: Nam pɔɔre-na tega kam se á dwia yam maama jwoŋi ba nyem, sɔ-yuu de sɔ-yuu. Abam wó ta jɔrɔ mo, se á ma‑á pɔɔre-ka á pa-ba. Sɔ-yuu maama wó jwoŋi tega se ko maŋe de ba ni na mae tei to mo, ne ba ná maŋe ba ye kɔ-kamunu naa kɔ-balaŋa de.

english_verse: If you don't force out all the people there, they will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your back. They will always be trouble for you,
translation_verse: Abam nam ná ve se á zeili balo na zoore tega kam ne to, ba balo na daare to wó pa á yera chɛ, nenɛɛne da-chɔrɔ mo chugi á yia, naa sabare mo zɔ á yera yam. Á ná tu á jeini tega kam ne, ba lage ba taa daane abam mo taa.

english_verse: and I will treat you as severely as I planned on treating them.
translation_verse: Amo Baŋa Wɛ laam maa wó chɔge abam de, nenɛɛne a na boŋe se a ke-ba tei to.”

english_verse: The southern border will be the Zin Desert and the northwest part of Edom. This border will begin at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Tega-kuri seeni siseini dem wó tɔge Zin kagoa kam, Edom laŋa kam siseini na wo mɛ to. Wɛ-puli daa kam seeni, siseini dem wó bobo Yɛ naneo kom ne mo.

english_verse: It will go west from there, but will turn southward to include Scorpion Pass, the village of Zin, and the town of Kadesh-Barnea. From there, the border will continue to Hazar-Addar and on to Azmon.
translation_verse: Ka ta ma vo ka lɛɛne Nɔŋɔ zwonnu chwoŋa kam tega-kuri seeni ka kɛ ka yi Zin se ka daare ka tɔge Kadese-Baranea kuri seeni ka vo ka yi Hazare-Adara de Azemon.

english_verse: It will run along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ka laam wó pipiri ka taa tɔge Ejipti bu-nɔgɔ kom se ka vo ka kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ni ne.

english_verse: The western border will be the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye á tega kam wɛ-zoore seeni siseini dem, de ye Mediterania naneo kom mo.

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean, then continue eastward to Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Á baŋa seeni siseini dem wó zege Mediterania naneo kom ni ne mo de tole de yi Hora peo kom.

english_verse: After that, it will run to Lebo-Hamath and across to Zedad, which is the northern edge of your land.
translation_verse: Ka wó zege dáane ka vo ka yi Lebo-Hamafa, de Zedadi,

english_verse: From Zedad, the border will continue east to Ziphron and end at Hazar-Enan.
translation_verse: de Ziforon, se ka laam kweeli Hazara-Enan ne.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin at Hazar-Enan in the north, then run south to Shepham,
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye á wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem, ka wó zege Hazara-Enan ne mo ka tole ka yi Sefam.

english_verse: and on down to Riblah on the east side of Ain. From there, it will go south to the eastern hills of Lake Galilee,
translation_verse: Ka ta wó tu kuri ka vo Ribila na wo Ayin wɛ-puli seeni to. Ka ná zege dáane ka wó vo ka yi zwonnu telo na wo Galili naneo kom bubɛ delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to mo,

english_verse: then follow the Jordan River down to the north end of the Dead Sea. The land within those four borders will belong to you.
translation_verse: se ka laam tu ka tɔge Jɔdan buga kam ka vo ka kweeli Yɛ naneo kom ne. Abam tega kam siseina yana yam mo konto.”

english_verse: Then Moses told the people, “You will receive the land inside these borders. It will be yours, but the Lord has commanded you to divide it among the nine and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Moses déem ma ta de Isarele tiina bam o we, “Tega kanto mo abam jege se á ta jɔrɔ se á pɔɔre-ka á ta‑á tei. Baŋa Wɛ pɛ ni se á kwei-ka á pɔɔre á pa á dwia nogo de chichworo kom mo.

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh have already been given their land
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Ruben dwi dem, de Gad dwi dem, dedaane Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom maŋe ba na ba tega kam.

english_verse: across from Jericho, east of the Jordan River.” The Leaders Who Will Divide the Land
translation_verse: Tega kalo ba na lage ba jwoŋi ba taa tei to wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni, mɛ na jeeri Jeriko bubɛ dedwoŋi dem seeni to mo.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta de Moses o we,

english_verse: “Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun will divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Nɔɔna balo na wó pɔɔre tega kam ba pa abam to yera mo tento: Wɛ kaanem tu Eleaza, de Nun bu Josua.

english_verse: and here is the list of their names: Caleb son of Jephunneh from Judah, Shemuel son of Ammihud from Simeon, Elidad son of Chislon from Benjamin, Bukki son of Jogli from Dan, Hanniel son of Ephod from Manasseh, Kemuel son of Shiphtan from Ephraim, Elizaphan son of Parnach from Zebulun, Paltiel son of Azzan from Issachar, Ahihud son of Shelomi from Asher, and Pedahel son of Ammihud from Naphtali.”
translation_verse: Baara bam yera mo tento: Dwi dem Yiga tu wom Judah Jefunɛ bu Kaleb Simeon Amihuda bu Semuwel Benjamin Chisilon bu Elidad Dan Jogili bu Buki Manasɛ Efodi bu Hanneli Efrayim Sifitan bu Kemweli Zebulun Paranaki bu Elizafan Isakara Azan bu Paliteli Asere Selomi bu Ahihuda Nafitali Amihuda bu Pedaheli

english_verse: These are the men the Lord commanded to help Eleazar and Joshua divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam konto déem ye balo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ba ni se ba tɔge ba pɔɔre Kanaan tega kam ba pa Isarele tiina bam se ba taa tei to mo.

english_verse: That way, the Levites will have towns to live in and pastures for their animals.
translation_verse: Konto mo wó pa se ba de taa jege teene ba zoore da, ye ba jege pwoli se ba taa kɔne ba vara dwi maama.

english_verse: Six of the towns you give them will be Safe Towns where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection. But you will also give the Levites
translation_verse: Nam le-na teene deredo Levi tiina teene dem wone se de taa wora ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane. Nɔɔno ná go o dwoŋi ye o wo paale o ke, se konto tu duri o zo teene dem konto dedoa wone o seigi. Abam ta jege se á kwei teene finna-delei á pa Levi dwi tiina bam á woli da,

english_verse: Since the towns for the Levites must come from Israel's own tribal lands, the larger tribes will give more towns than the smaller ones. The Safe Towns (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Á wó kuri teene dem konto á le Isarele dwi maama tega kam wone se Levi dwi tiina taa zoore de wone. Konto ŋwaane á jege se á le teene se ko maŋe de dwi maama tega kam na mae tei to, ne ba ná ye kɔ-kamunu naa kɔ-balaŋa mo de.”

english_verse: by one of the victim's relatives. He will take revengefor his relative's death as soon as he finds you.
translation_verse: Ba na go wolo to yera nɔɔno mo jege se o beeri nɔn-goro wom. O maa ná nɛ‑o, se o yɔɔre o go‑o.

english_verse: There are to be six of these Safe Towns,
translation_verse: Le-na teene deredo ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Lord then told Moses
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de Moses o we:

english_verse: to tell the people of Israel: After you have crossed the Jordan River and are settled in Canaan,
translation_verse: “Nam ta de Isarele tiina bam we: Abam ná bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ye á zo Kanaan tega kam wone,

english_verse: If the victim's relatives think it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of these Safe Towns for protection and not be killed before a trial is held.
translation_verse: Konto mo wó pa se o wane o duri o vo o lu wolo na beeri o gom to jeŋa ne. Ba bá na chwoŋa se ba go kotu ye teo kom nakwa bam wo nigi o ni taane se ba lɔre kolo na ke to.

english_verse: They will be places of protection for anyone who lives in Israel and accidentally kills someone. Laws about Murder and Accidental Killing The Lord said:
translation_verse: Teene deredo dem konto wó taa wora Isarele tiina, de veira, de balo maama na zoore de-ba to ŋwaane mo, se wolo maama ná go o dwoŋi ye o wo paale o ke, se konto tu duri o zo de dedoa wone o jwoŋi o tete.

english_verse: Suppose you hit someone with a piece of iron or a large stone or a dangerous wooden tool. If that person dies, then you are a murderer and must be put to death
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ta ná zei kandwɛ-kamunu, naa da-lɔŋɔ o jeŋa ne, ye o ná kwei-ko o mage o dwoŋi pa se kotu te, ko bere we o paale o ke mo. O ye nɔn-goro mo ye ba jege se ba go o de mo.

english_verse: Or suppose you get angry and kill someone by pushing or hitting or by throwing something. You are a murderer and must be put to death by one of the victim's relatives.
translation_verse: naa o ná mage‑o de o jagula, pa se o dwoŋi wom te, o ye nɔn-goro mo ye o maŋe se ba go o de mo. Ba na go wolo to yera nɔɔno jege se o beeri nɔn-goro wom jei mo se o go‑o.

english_verse: But if you are not angry and accidentally kill someone in any of these ways, the townspeople must hold a trial and decide if you are guilty.
translation_verse: se teo kom nakwa di nɔɔno wom de wolo o na go to yera nɔɔno taane dem se ba tɔge bera yam konto ba bore chega kam.

english_verse: But if you ever leave the Safe Town
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom nam ná nwoŋi ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi teo kom wone,

english_verse: and are killed by the victim's relative, he cannot be punished for killing you.
translation_verse: ye too wom yera nɔɔno ná nɛ‑o o ja o go, o toone dem bá taa wo kotu yuu ne. Kotu jege chwoŋa se o go‑o.

english_verse: Death is the penalty for murder. But no one accused of murder can be put to death unless there are at least two witnesses to the crime.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná zaŋe o go o dwoŋi, á ba jege chwoŋa se á go kotu, ko ná dae we nɔɔna mo pɛ maana we o seene o ye nɔn-goro. Nɔn-doa yerane ni taane nam bá wane de pa nɔɔno te.

english_verse: You cannot give someone money to escape the death penalty; you must pay with your own life!
translation_verse: Nɔn-goro ye se ba go‑o mo. Konto tu bá wane o ŋwe sabu se o ma jwoŋi o ŋwea.

english_verse: And if you have been proven innocent of murder and are living in a Safe Town, you cannot pay to go back home; you must stay there until the high priest dies.
translation_verse: Ko ta woli da, wolo ná zo ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi teo kodwoŋi wone o na wo paale o go nɔɔno to ŋwaane, konto tu bá wane o ŋwe sabu se o ma o jwoori o tete sɔŋɔ lela, ye kaanem yiga tu wom ta wo tege.

english_verse: I, the Lord, live among you people of Israel, so your land must be kept pure. But when a murder takes place, blood pollutes the land, and it becomes unclean. If that happens, the murderer must be put to death, so the land will be clean again. Keep murder out of Israel!
translation_verse: Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo zoore Isarele tiina bam tetare ne. Konto ŋwaane, yé pa-na se tega kalo amo de abam na jei ka wone to chɔge.”

english_verse: One day the family leaders from the Gilead clan of the Manasseh tribe went to Moses and the other family leaders of Israel
translation_verse: Gilead sɔ-yuu kom yiga tiina déem ma zaŋe dɛ dedwe ba fɔɔre ba yi Moses dedaane Isarele sɔ-yuni tedaara yiga tiina bam tei. Gilead kwo maa ye Makira. Wonto kwo de maa ye Josɛf bu Manasɛ.

english_verse: and said, “Sir, the Lord has said that he will show what land each tribe will receive as their own. And the Lord has commanded you to give the daughters of our relative Zelophehad the land that he would have received.
translation_verse: Ba ma ta de Moses ba we, “Dé kwo, Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ nmo mo ni se n ta jɔrɔ n ma‑n pɔɔre tega kam n pa Isarele dwia yam maama. O ta ma pa ni se n kwei tega kalo ya na wó taa ye debam choro Zelofehada nyem to n pa o bukwa bam.

english_verse: But if they marry men from other tribes of Israel, the land they receive will become part of that tribe's inheritance and will no longer belong to us.
translation_verse: Banto nam ná zo banna na nwoŋi Isarele sɔ-yuu kodwoŋi wone to, ba tega kam laam wó ji sɔ-yuu kom konto nyem mo se ba woli-ka ba tete tega kam wone. Ko maa wó pa se debam tega kam muri.

english_verse: Even when land is returned to its original owner in the Year of Celebration, we will not get back Zelophehad's land—it will belong to the tribe into which his daughters married.”
translation_verse: Ko nam ná yi ywoni dim bene dem pa se Isarele tiina kwei ba wonnu ba jwoori ba pae te tiina, Zelofehada bukɔ wolo maama ná zo baro sɔ-yuu-gaa wone, kotu tega laam wó lɛɛre ka ji sɔ-yuu kom konto nyem, pa se dé nabaara bam sɔ-yuu kom ga-ka.”

english_verse: So Moses told the people that the Lord had said: These men from the Manasseh tribe are right.
translation_verse: Moses déem na lɔre Baŋa Wɛ ni na ye tei de taane dem to, o ma pa Isarele tiina bam ni we, “Josɛf dwi dem nɔɔna na tage kolo to ye chega mo.

english_verse: I will allow Zelophehad's daughters to marry anyone, as long as those men belong to one of the clans of the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ ni delo Zelofehada bukwa bam ŋwaane to mo tento: Ba jege chwoŋa se ba kuri banna balo ba na wó zo to. Ko nam jege se ba banna nwoŋi ba kwo sɔ-yuu kom wone mo.

english_verse: Tribal land must not be given to another tribe—it will remain the property of the tribe that received it.
translation_verse: Tega kalo Isarele sɔ-yuu maama na wó jwoŋi to jege se ka maŋe ba tete sɔ-yuu kom de ba kwaga kam tei ne mo. Ka bá lɛɛre ka ji sɔ-yuu kodwoŋi nyem.

english_verse: In the future, any daughter who inherits land must marry someone from her own tribe. Israel's tribal land is never to be passed from one tribe to another.
translation_verse: Sɔ-yuu maama tega bá lɛɛre ka ji sɔ-yuu kodwoŋi nyem. Isarele sɔ-yuni tem maama tega kam jege se ka maŋe sɔ-yuu kom konto tei ne, se ba taa tei-ka.”

english_verse: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah the daughters of Zelophehad obeyed the Lord and married their uncles' sons
translation_verse: Maala, de Tiraza, de Hogela, de Milika, dedaane Noah mo konto. Ba ma zo ba kwo chorro tedwonna.

english_verse: and remained part of the Manasseh tribe. So their land stayed in their father's clan.
translation_verse: Ba banna déem nwoŋi Josɛf bu Manasɛ sɔ-yuni tem wone mo. Konto ŋwaane ba tega kam maŋe ba kwo sɔ-yuu kom tei ne ye ba tei-ka.

english_verse: These are the laws that the Lord gave to Moses and the Israelites while they were camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge Moses baŋa ne o pa Isarele tiina bam nia de chullu telo to mo konto. Ka maŋa ne, de ba ta wo Moaba laŋa kam te-kampare ne mo. Jei sem konto wo Jɔdan buga kam ni ne ye Jeriko wo bubɛ dedwoŋi dem seeni.

english_verse: Now, turn around and go back into the desert by way of Red Sea Road.
translation_verse: Ko daare ko ná ye abam, jwoori-na á pipiri á kwei chwoŋa kalo na maa vei Nane-soŋo kom seeni to se á zo kagoa kam wone á ta‑á via.’

english_verse: People of Israel, when we were in our camp at Mount Sinai, the Lord our God told us: You have stayed here long enough.
translation_verse: “Debam ya ta na wo Sinayi Peo kom teiŋa ne to, mo debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ tage debam o we: ‘Abam tiini á jeini ywo-seeni á dáane.

english_verse: Leave this place and go into the land that belongs to the Amorites and their neighbors the Canaanites. This land includes the Jordan River valley, the hill country, the western foothills, the Southern Desert, the Mediterranean seacoast, the Lebanon Mountains, and all the territory as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Zaŋe-na á gɔ á vwoa yam se á ta‑á vei Amori tiina zwonnu laŋa kam ne, dedaane teene delo maama na gilimi jei sem konto to. Ko nam ye maama se ko taa vei peero tem laŋa kam maama mo. Ta véi-na á yi wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem, dedaane tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam, ko ta woli de teene delo na wo Mediterania naneo kom ni ne to. Véi-na jei selo maama Kanaan tiina na zoore to dedaane Lebanon laŋa kam, se á kɛ á yi Yuferata buga kam seeni.

english_verse: After I gave these instructions to the judges, I taught you the Lord's commands. Men Were Sent To Explore the Hill Country (Numbers
translation_verse: Ko maama wone a maŋe a ta a bere abam kolo maama á na jege se á ke to mo.” Nɔɔna vei ba nii Kanaan tega kam Jeelim

english_verse: You stayed in your tents and grumbled, “The Lord must hate us—he brought us out of Egypt, just so he could hand us over to the Amorites and get rid of us.
translation_verse: Abam maa wo á vwoa yam ne ye á nyenyɔna da-tei ne á we, ‘Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ na chuli debam to ŋwaane mo o jaane debam o ja o ba o ke Amori tiina bam jeŋa ne se ba go debam.

english_verse: Right after the Lord commanded us to leave Mount Sinai, I told you: Israel, being your leader is too big a job for one person.
translation_verse: “Dé ya ta na wo Sinayi Peo kom ne to, mo amo tage de abam a we, ‘Ko tiini ko chamma ko gaale se amo yerane taa nii abam baŋa ne.

english_verse: God has even promised to bless us a thousand times more, and I pray that he will.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam gwoni ni dedaane dé nabaara bam we o wó pa se dé puli dedɛ. Wɛ wó swɛ abam swolim se o pa á dwi dem puli kuni moro mo.

english_verse: But I cannot take care of all your problems and settle all your arguments alone.
translation_verse: Abam na jege á taana de á ni-kantɔgɔ á daane-ne tei to, amo yerane laam nam wó ke tetɛ mo se a taa nii á baŋa ne?

english_verse: and others became judges. I gave these judges the following instructions: When you settle legal cases, your decisions must be fair. It doesn't matter if the case is between two Israelites, or between an Israelite and a foreigner living in your community.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye balo na wó taa kwɛ á taana to, amo déem pɛ-ba ni a we, ‘Zuri-na á yera se á cheigi nɔɔna bam taane dwi maama se á daare á ma á bore bora á pa-ba. Ko ná ye Isarele dwi tu de o dwoŋi mo jege taane, naa ko ná ye Isarele dwi tu de veiru wodwoŋi, se á yé kuri-ba daane.

english_verse: And it doesn't matter if one is helpless and the other is powerful. Don't be afraid of anyone! No matter who shows up in your court, God will help you make a fair decision. If any case is too hard for you, bring the people to me, and I will make the decision.
translation_verse: Ko ná maŋe ko ye naduna naa nabwona de, se á yé kuri-ba daane de á na bore ba bora tei to. Ko dae se abam taa kɔre nɔɔna yia de taane dim. Ko ye Wɛ mo wó pa se á na boboŋa se á bore chega bora. Taane delo nam ná dana de dwoi abam jaanem, se á ja-de á ba á pa amo se a nii de baŋa ne.’

english_verse: even though he had always been with us in the desert. During the daytime, the Lord was in the cloud, leading us in the right direction and showing us where to camp. And at night, he was there in the fire.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ya yeini o da abam yiga mo o kwɛ á chwoŋa kam, ye o beeri jei selo á na wó pu á vwoa to. Tete maama ne o wo mini wone o tɔge á yiga, se ko daare wea ne o yeini o wo kunkwoŋo wone mo o ma o bere abam chwoŋa se á ta‑á tɔge ka wone á via.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded us to leave Mount Sinai and go to the hill country that belonged to the Amorites, so we started out into the huge desert. You remember how frightening it was, but soon we were at Kadesh-Barnea,
translation_verse: “Dé déem ke kolo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ debam ni se dé ke to. Dé ma zege Sinayi peo kom seeni dé vo dé tɔge kagoa kam wone ka na yala ye ka jege foone dedɛ ka pa debam to. Dé ma tole konto taa dé vo dé twɛ Amori tiina zwonnu laŋa kam, ye dé yi Kadese-Baranea ne.

english_verse: and I told you, “We have reached the hill country. It belongs to the Amorites now, but the Lord our God is giving it to us. He is the same God our ancestors worshiped, and he has told us to go in and take this land, so don't hesitate and be afraid.”
translation_verse: Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o kwei tega kam o ke á jeŋa ne. Nam zaŋe-na á vo á zo ka wone á jwoŋi-ka á ta‑á tei. Baŋa Wɛ wom á nabaara bam na tɔge to maŋe o ta abam se á ke konto mo. Yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. Yé pa-na se á vɔna pare.’

english_verse: Then all of you came to me and said, “Before we go into the land, let's send some men to explore it. When they come back, they can tell us about the towns we will find and what roads we should take to get there.”
translation_verse: Abam maama déem ma ba amo tei ye á we, ‘Nam pa se dé toŋe nɔɔna badwonna se banto da yiga ba vo ba ŋɔ ba nii logo kom. Ba laam maa wó wane ba jwoori debam tei ba pa dé lɔre chwoŋa kalo chekke dé na wó tɔge to, dedaane teene delo dwi na wo jei sem ne to.’

english_verse: It seemed like a good idea, so I chose twelve men, one from each tribe.
translation_verse: Abam boboŋe dem déem maa lamma amo tei ne. A ma seene a kuri nɔɔna fuga-balei se ba nwoŋi abam dwia yam maama wone, dwi maama nɔɔno dedoa.

english_verse: and even brought back some of the fruit. They said, “The Lord our God is giving us good land.” Israel Refused To Obey the Lord (Numbers
translation_verse: Ba ma ja tega kam wodiiru tedwonna ba ba debam tei ye ba we, ‘Tega kalo debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ na lage o pa debam to tiini ka lamma dedɛ.’ ” Nɔɔna bam ya lɔge Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne

english_verse: Then you came back to the place of worship at Kadesh-Barnea and wept, but the Lord would not listen to your prayers. Israel Spent Years in the Desert Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Abam déem ma jwoori ye á daare á vo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne á keeri á lwoori wolim o tei ne. O nam wo sɛ se o cheigi á wɛ-lworo kom.
