english_verse: It is the same as eating the meat from a deer or a gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And in this way, anyone who is unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat.
translation_verse: Ko maa nye de á na lage á di woŋa naa feira ye nɔɔna maama jege chwoŋa se ba di, ba ná maŋe ba kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane naa ba wo kwɛ ba tete de.

english_verse: But don't eat the blood. It is the life of the animal, so let it drain out on the ground before you eat the meat.
translation_verse: Yé kwei-na jana bam á ma á ji wodiu. Nam kwei-na-ba á lwo tega ne, ne á na wó lwo na á yage tei to.

english_verse: Do you want the Lord to make you successful? Do you want your children to be successful even after you are gone? Then do what pleases the Lord and don't eat blood.
translation_verse: Á ná seene á ve jana bam dim, ko wó pa se Baŋa Wɛ wo pwoli lanyerane. Á ŋwea maa wó ke lanyerane ka pa abam de á kwaga kam maama.

english_verse: All sacrifices and offerings to the Lord must be taken to the place where he chooses to be worshiped. If you offer a sacrifice to please the Lord, all of its meat must be burned on the altar. You can eat the meat from certain kinds of sacrifices, but you must always pour out the animal's blood on the altar.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye zwɛɛm kaanem, se á zwɛ varem wom Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem baŋa ne, nɔna yam de jana bam maama. Ko nam ná ye kaanem delo á na wó di de nɔna yam to, á jege se á lwo jana bam bimbini dem baŋa ne á yage mo.

english_verse: If you obey these laws, you will be doing what the Lord your God says is right and good. Then he will help you and your descendants be successful. Worship the Lord in the Right Way Moses said:
translation_verse: Ta‑á yei-na se á ta‑á sɛ Wɛ nia yalo maama amo na bere abam to, se ko pa á ŋwea ke lanyerane ka pa abam de á kwaga kam maama taa wuu, á kikia na wó taa tɔge chwoŋa ye ya pwoli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wo to ŋwaane. Ba yé taa zuli jwona

english_verse: Israel, as you go into the land and attack the nations that are there, the Lord will get rid of them, and you can have their land.
translation_verse: Abam ná lage á zo dwi-gɛ tiina logo kom, á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó zeili-ba á yiga ne pa se ba daare ba tega kam se á jwoŋi-ka á ta‑á tei.

english_verse: But that's when you must be especially careful not to ask, “How did those nations worship their gods? Shouldn't we worship the Lord in the same way?”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ná tu o ba o chɔge dwi-gɛ tiina bam konto, yé pa-na se ba soge abam se á tɔge ba jwona yam. Yé bwei-na nenɛɛne: ‘Nɔɔna banto yeini ba tɔge chwoŋa kɔ mo ba zuli ba jwona yam? Debam de lage dé ke konto dwoŋi mo.’

english_verse: Obey all the laws and teachings I am giving you. Don't add any, and don't take any away.
translation_verse: Ta‑á yei-na se á ta‑á tɔge Wɛ nia yalo maama amo na bere abam to. Yé zaŋe-na á woli kolokolo ya wone, nam yé le-na kolokolo ya wone á yage.

english_verse: Someday a prophet may come along who is able to perform miracles or tell what will happen in the future. Then the prophet may say, “Let's start worshiping some new gods—some gods that we know nothing about.”
translation_verse: ye wo-kenkagela yam ná seene ya ke ne o na tage tei to, o wó wane o soge abam se á zuli dwi-gɛ tiina wa-yɔɔro, ye o ta nenɛɛne: ‘Pa-na dé zaŋe dé tɔge wa yadwonna se dé zuli-ya.’

english_verse: If the prophet says this, don't listen! The Lord your God will be watching to find out whether or not you love him with all your heart and soul.
translation_verse: Sampwora naa yi-naro ná tage konto dwoŋi, yé cheigi-na o taane. Ko nam ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo maane abam se o nii, á seene á swoi‑o de á bochare maama de á boboŋa maama naa á ba swoi.

english_verse: You must be completely faithful to the Lord. Worship and obey only the Lord and do this with fear and trembling,
translation_verse: Ta‑á tɔge-na abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom se á ta‑á kɔre‑o. Sɛ-na o nia yam ye á cheigi o kwora kam, se á ta‑á toŋe á pa‑o ye á sale‑o.

english_verse: And when the rest of Israel hears about it, they will be afraid, and no one else will ever do such an evil thing again.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam maama ná nigi kolo na ke to, foone wó ja-ba, pa se abam wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá toŋe keim-lɔŋɔ konto dwoŋi.

english_verse: After the Lord your God gives you towns to live in, you may hear a rumor about one of the towns.
translation_verse: Ko daa ta ná ye teene delo abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á zoore de wone to, á wae á ni we,

english_verse: You may hear that some worthless people have talked everyone there into worshiping other gods, even though these gods had never done anything for them.
translation_verse: nɔn-wo-korro tedwonna zaŋe teo kodwoŋi ne ye ba soge ba teo kom nɔɔna pa se ba ywori Baŋa Wɛ chwoŋa wone se ba daare ba zuli wa yayam. Abam nam ya yeiri wa yam konto zula.

english_verse: You must carefully find out if the rumor is true. Then if the people of that town have actually done such a disgusting thing in your own country,
translation_verse: Á ná nigi kanto sawea kam dwoŋi, kwaane-na á tɔge ka nɛ se á lɔre chega kam. Ko ná ye chega mo we totoŋ-lɔŋɔ kom seene ko ke abam tetare ne,

english_verse: Gather all the possessions of the people who lived there, and pile them up in the marketplace, without keeping anything for yourself. Set the pile and the whole town on fire, and don't ever rebuild the town. The whole town will be a sacrifice to the Lord your God. Then he won't be angry anymore, and he will have mercy on you and make your nation stronger, just as he promised your ancestors.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye teo kom wonnu telo maama na maŋe de chɔgem Wɛ ŋwaane to, yé pa se á fera zo kolokolo se á kwei. Á ná sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem konto, o bane wó zuri ye o daare o duri abam ŋwaŋa, pa se á kɔgɔ kom puli dedɛ, ne o na pwooli de á nabaara bam se o ke tei to.

english_verse: That's why you must do what the Lord your God says is right. I am giving you his laws and teachings today, and you must obey them.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane abam jege se á cheigi abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam ye á sɛ o nia yam maama, ne amo zem na bere abam tei to. Ta‑á ke-na kolo na jege chega o yiga ne to.”

english_verse: Out of all the nations on this earth, the Lord your God chose you to be his own. You belong to the Lord, so don't behave like those who worship other gods. Animals That Can Be Eaten (Leviticus
translation_verse: Abam seene á ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo. Logo baŋa nɔɔna maama wone mo o kuri abam se á ta‑á ye o tete nɔɔna o yi na su to. Wonnu telo na maŋe de dim to Chullu

english_verse: You can eat any clean bird.
translation_verse: Á wae á di zuna balo maama na maŋe de dim to.

english_verse: You may eat the meat of cattle, sheep, and goats; wild sheep and goats; and gazelles, antelopes, and all kinds of deer.
translation_verse: naa woŋa, naa feira, naa siga, naa kagoa wo boŋo, naa nambworo, naa kagoa wo pia.

english_verse: It is all right to eat meat from any animals that have divided hoofs and also chew the cud.
translation_verse: Á ta wae á di varem wolo maama napɔɔna na lɔge belei ye ba yeini ba done gaao ba guli ba jwoori ba done to.

english_verse: But don't eat camels, rabbits, and rock badgers. These animals chew the cud but do not have divided hoofs. You must treat them as unclean.
translation_verse: Ko nam dae se á di kone, naa zwoni, naa pe-ware, se vara bam konto done gaao ba guli ye ba napɔɔna laam wo lɔge belei. Konto ŋwaane banto wo maŋe se á di-ba.

english_verse: And don't eat pork, since pigs have divided hoofs, but they do not chew their cud. Don't even touch a dead pig!
translation_verse: Teira de nam wo maŋe se á di-ya. Ya napɔɔna lɔge belei ye ya laam ba done gaao ya gula ya jwoori ya dona. Konto ŋwaane ko chula se á di ya nɔna. Ya ná tega, bere á yé dwei-ya.

english_verse: You can eat any fish that has fins and scales. But there are other creatures that live in the water,
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye wonnu telo na zoore na wone to, á wae á di ywona yalo na jege nabili-pelwaro ye ya ta jege poro pa te kwoli ya yera to.

english_verse: and if they do not have fins and scales, you must not eat them. Treat them as unclean.
translation_verse: Ko daare ko ná ye woŋo maama na wo na wone ye ko ba jege nabili-pelwaro dedaane poro na kwoli-ko to, ko chula se á di-ko. Ko wo maŋe de dim.

english_verse: However, you are allowed to eat certain kinds of winged insects.
translation_verse: Á za wae á di wo-korro telo na maŋe de dim to.

english_verse: You belong to the Lord your God, so if you happen to find a dead animal, don't eat its meat. You may give it to foreigners who live in your town or sell it to foreigners who are visiting your town. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. Give the Lord Ten Percent of Your Harvest Moses said:
translation_verse: Yé zaŋe-na á di varem wolo na tega o tete ne to. Á wae á kwei á pa veira balo na zoore abam teo kom ne to se ba di, naa á kwei á yeigi á pa sa-teena. Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kuri abam se á ta‑á ye o tete nɔɔna mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé kwei bebala de ka nu nayela o saŋe mini wone. Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra

english_verse: People of Israel, every year you must set aside ten percent of your grain harvest.
translation_verse: Bene maama wone ta‑á yei-na se á le á kare sem wodiiru popɔra dedoa fuga maama wone á pa Wɛ.

english_verse: Also set aside ten percent of your wine and olive oil, and the first-born of every cow, sheep, and goat. Take these to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, and eat them there. This will teach you to always respect the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Laam ja-na Wɛ-teiri wodiiru tem konto á ja vo jeiga kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli o yere da to. Ko ná ye á mena yam, de á sa-doora bam, de á nuga kam, de á vara bam na dɛ yiga ba lo bia balo to, se á vo á di Wɛ-teiri dem á Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, se á ta‑á kɔre‑o taa wuu.

english_verse: But suppose you can't carry that ten percent of your harvest to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. If you live too far away, or if the Lord gives you a big harvest,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam ná yɔɔre o ke zaane abam yuu ne pa se á na wodiiru dedɛ, ye o wara-jei sem ná ye yiga yiga ka pa abam se á ja á wodiiru tem á yi da, se á ke tento:

english_verse: When you and your family arrive, spend the money on food for a big celebration. Buy cattle, sheep, goats, wine, beer, and if there are any other kinds of food that you want, buy those too.
translation_verse: Á ná yi da, se á laam ma á yeigi kolo maama á na lage to se á di. Ko ná ye naane, naa pei, naa sana, abam de á sɔŋɔ tiina bam wó di-te á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne de wopwolo.

english_verse: And since people of the Levi tribe won't own any land for growing crops, remember to ask the Levites to celebrate with you.
translation_verse: Za ta‑á yei-na se á yé swei-na Levi dwi tiina balo na zoore abam tei ne to ni ne, banto na ba jege ba tete tega se ba taa tei to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Every third year, instead of using the ten percent of your harvest for a big celebration, bring it into town and put it in a community storehouse.
translation_verse: Bena yatɔ bene dem maama ná yeini de yi, se á kwei-na Wɛ-teiri wodiiru tem maama á la-te jeiga dedoa á teo maama wone.

english_verse: The Levites have no land of their own, so you must give them food from the storehouse. You must also give food to the poor who live in your town, including orphans, widows, and foreigners. If they have enough to eat, then the Lord your God will be pleased and make you successful in everything you do.
translation_verse: Wodiiru tem konto wó taa ye Levi dwi tiina bam nyem mo, banto na ba jege ba tete tega to ŋwaane. Abam ta jege se á kwei-te á pa veira, de botara, de kadeina balo na zoore abam wone to mo. Ba maama wó wane ba ba ba jwoŋi wodiu ba di ba su. Ke-na konto se ko pa á Tu Baŋa Wɛ zaane taa wo á baŋa ne de kolo maama á na lage á toŋe to.”

english_verse: After the Lord your God gives land to each of you, there may be poor Israelites in the town where you live. If there are, then don't be mean and selfish with your money.
translation_verse: Á ná zo tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam to, ye yiniga ná jaane á dwoŋi Isarele tu wolo na zoore á teo wone to, yé ve-na se á woli‑o, á na jege wo-chɛɔ to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Every seven years you must announce, “The Lord says loans do not need to be paid back.” Then if you have loaned money to another Israelite, you can no longer ask for payment.
translation_verse: Á na wó ke tei to mo tento: Wolo maama na kwei sabu o jene o pa o dwoŋi Isarele tu to jege se o yage jene dem o ma chɛ‑o mo. Kotu daa yé boŋe se o jwoŋi o sabu kom o choro kom tei ne, Baŋa Wɛ na bere we ko ye jena saarem bene to ŋwaane.

english_verse: This law applies only to loans you have made to other Israelites. Foreigners will still have to pay back what you have loaned them.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye veiru, n wae n jwoŋi n jene dem o tei ne. Ko daare ko ná ye n tete nɔɔna bam jena yam mo, se n yage n chɛ-ba.

english_verse: No one in Israel should ever be poor. The Lord your God is giving you this land, and he has promised to make you very successful, if you obey his laws and teachings that I'm giving you today. You will lend money to many nations, but you won't have to borrow. You will rule many nations, but they won't rule you.
translation_verse: Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ abam swolim ne o na pwooli se o ke tei to. Konto to, á wo ta‑á jena á pae dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ ye á ba jege se á di jena ba tei ne. Á wó ta‑á jege dam dwi-gɛ tiina baŋa ne. Teo kodwoŋi nam bá di dam abam baŋa ne.

english_verse: Be careful! Don't say to yourself, “Soon it will be the seventh year, and then I won't be able to get my money back.” It would be horrible for you to think that way and to be so selfish that you refuse to help the poor. They are your relatives, and if you don't help them, they may ask the Lord to decide whether you have done wrong. And he will say that you are guilty.
translation_verse: Ta‑n yei se n yé pa se boboŋ-lɔŋɔ ba n kana ne ye n ta nenɛɛne: ‘Bena yarepɛ bene dem na ye jena saarem bene to bwola.’ Nmo ná boŋe konto dwoŋi ye n ve se n jene n pa n dwoŋi Isarele tu wolo yiniga na jaane‑o to, ko ye puseŋa keim mo n kea. Nɔɔno wom wó wane o keeri o jare Baŋa Wɛ nmo ŋwaane, ye Wɛ wó pa n to de n bora.

english_verse: You should be happy to give the poor what they need, because then the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
translation_verse: N jege se n pa yiniga tu zɛɛra mo se n yé ke wo-chɛɔ ded‑o. N Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom laam wó swɛ nmo swolim pa se kolo maama n na jege n toŋe to ke lanyerane ko pa‑m.

english_verse: But if the animal is lame or blind or has something else wrong with it, you must not sacrifice it to the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Varem wolo nam ná jege gɛɛ o yera ne, ne o ná ye vare-gwana, naa vare-lilwei, naa o jege tusim dwi delo, ko wo maŋe se á kwei wonto dwi á ma‑á ke kaanem á pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: And don't just tell them they are free to leave—
translation_verse: N nam ná yage‑o, yé pa o viiri de je-yaara.

english_verse: But one of your slaves may say, “I love you and your family, and I would be better off staying with you, so please don't make me leave.”
translation_verse: N kabaa kam nam wó wane o ta de nmo we o ba lage se o viiri, o na swoi nmo de n sɔŋɔ tiina bam ye n ke‑o lanyerane to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Take the slave to the door of your house and push a sharp metal rod through one earlobe and into the door. Such slaves will belong to you for life, whether they are men or women.
translation_verse: O ná tage konto dwoŋi, ko jege se n ja‑o mo n vo n pa se o sale manchwo-peena bworo kom, se n daare n kwei silwei n puri o zwɛ dedoa. Konto bere we o wó taa ye nmo kabaa se ko taa nii o toone. N kabaa kam ná ye kaane, se n ke‑o de konto dwoŋi.

english_verse: If the first-born animal of a cow or sheep or goat is a male, it must be given to the Lord. Don't put first-born cattle to work or cut wool from first-born sheep.
translation_verse: Le-na wo-bale selo á vara bam na dɛ yiga ba lo to se á kwei á pa á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Yé ma-na naane dem konto á toŋe totoŋe, nam yé fane á pei sem konto koro.

english_verse: Instead, each year you must take the first-born of these animals to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped. You and your family will sacrifice them to the Lord and then eat them as part of a sacred meal.
translation_verse: Bene maama wone abam de á sɔŋɔ tiina tiina bam jege se á vo jeiga kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kuri to ye á di wonnu tem konto o yiga ne.

english_verse: You can butcher it where you live, and eat it just like the meat of a deer or gazelle that you kill while hunting. Even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some.
translation_verse: Á nam jege se á kwei vara bam konto dwoŋi á di á sam ne mo. Ko nye de á na lage á di woŋa naa feira ye nɔɔna maama jege chwoŋa se ba di, ba ná maŋe ba kwɛ ba tete Wɛ ŋwaane naa ba wo kwɛ ba tete mo de.

english_verse: But you must never eat the blood of an animal—let it drain out on the ground.
translation_verse: Ko nam chula se á di vara bam jana. Pa-na se jana bam lwo tega ne, ne á na wó lwo na á yage tei to.”

english_verse: People of Israel, you must celebrate Passover in the month of Abib, because one night in that month years ago, the Lord your God rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: “Bene maama Abibi chana kam ne, á jege se á di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem á ma á zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, kokuri kanto chana kam dɛ dedoa ne mo o jaane abam tete ne o ja nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne.

english_verse: People of Israel, if you want to enjoy a long and successful life, make sure that everyone is treated with justice in the land the Lord is giving you. Don't Set Up Sacred Poles or Stones Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Yɔɔre-na á tɔge chega borem lanyerane se ko pa á wane á zo tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam to wone á dáane.

english_verse: Eat all of the meat of the Passover sacrifice that same night. But don't serve bread made with yeast at the Passover meal. Serve the same kind of thin bread that you ate when you were slaves suffering in Egypt and when you had to leave Egypt quickly. As long as you live, this thin bread will remind you of the day you left Egypt. For seven days following Passover, don't make any bread with yeast. In fact, there should be no yeast anywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Da yarepɛ yam maama wone, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege se sabɔle ta wo o sɔŋɔ ne. Varem wolo á na wó go kuri dem boboa dɛ dem dedaan-ni ne to, á jege se á di o nɔna yam maama mo se tega laam poore.

english_verse: Eat thin bread for the next six days. Then on the seventh day, don't do any work. Instead, come together and worship the Lord. The Harvest Festival (Exodus
translation_verse: Da yaredo yalo na saŋe to wone, á wó di bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to mo, se da yarepɛ dɛ dem ná yia, á la daane se á kɔgɔ kom maama zuli á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Á ba jege se á toŋe dɛ dem konto ne. Ga-kwea kuri dem Nwoŋim

english_verse: Don't offer the Passover sacrifice in just any town where you happen to live.
translation_verse: Abam ná wo teo kolo maama ne á Tu Baŋa Wɛ na lage o pa abam to, se á yé go Atɔgebabaŋa vara bam jei de jei,

english_verse: It must be offered at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Kill the sacrifice at sunset, the time of day when you left Egypt.
translation_verse: ko ná dae jeiga kalo o na wó kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli o yere da to yerane. Wɛ-zoore maŋa ne mo á wó go vara bam se ko maŋe de maŋa kalo á na yage Ejipti to.

english_verse: Then cook it and eat it there at the place of worship, returning to your tents the next morning.
translation_verse: Saŋe-na nɔna yam á di Wɛ jeiga kam ne, se tega ná poore, á laam zaŋe á jwoori á vwoa ne.

english_verse: And don't set up a sacred stone! The Lord hates these things.
translation_verse: Nam ta yé chwi-na kandwɛ se de taa ye jwoni de pa abam. Baŋa Wɛ chuli wonnu tem konto maama.

english_verse: After you have finished the grain harvest and the grape harvest, take your sons and daughters and all your servants to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. The Lord will give you big harvests and make you successful in everything you do. You will be completely happy, so celebrate this festival in honor of the Lord your God. Three Festivals at the Place of Worship (Exodus
translation_verse: Á wó vo jeiga kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wó kuri to á ke da yarepɛ á di kuri dem á ma‑á zuli‑o. Á wó ta‑á jege wopwolo lanyerane, Baŋa Wɛ na ke zaane á baŋa ne de á wodiiru de kolo maama á na toŋe to ŋwaane.

english_verse: When you build the altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God, don't set up a sacred pole for the worship of the goddess Asherah.
translation_verse: Á ná lage á lɔ bimbini á pa á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, ta‑á yei-na se á yé kwei daa á ma‑á sare Asera nyenyego á zege da se á zuli-ko.

english_verse: Seven weeks after you start your grain harvest,
translation_verse: Á ná bobo se á zage á wodiiru tem, jeeli-na da yarepɛ yarepɛ kuni berepɛ,

english_verse: go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped and celebrate the Harvest Festival in honor of the Lord your God. Bring him an offering as large as you can afford, depending on how big a harvest he has given you. Be sure to take along your sons and daughters and all your servants. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
translation_verse: Á jege se á vo jeiga kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wó kuri se nɔɔna taa zuli o yere da to á di kuri dem de wopwolo o yiga ne. Ko wó taa ye abam, de á bia, de á kabɛ, ko woli de Levi tiina, de veira, de botara, de kadeina balo maama na zoore á tetare ne to mo.

english_verse: The bigger the harvest the Lord gives you, the bigger your gift should be. Treat Everyone with Justice Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Nɔɔno maama wó kwei pɛɛre se ko maŋe de Baŋa Wɛ na ke zaane o baŋa ne o woli‑o tei to mo o ja jeeri. Bora borem

english_verse: Each year there are three festivals when all Israelite men must go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. These are the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters. And don't forget to take along a gift for the Lord.
translation_verse: Bene maama wone kuni betɔ mo á baara bam jege se ba vo jeiga kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wó kuri to ba jeeri o yiga ne ba zuli‑o. Ko wó taa ye Bworobworo-memene kuri dem, de Ga-kwea kuri dem, de Vwoa chwiim kuri dem mo. Nɔɔno maama nam jege se o taa zei pɛɛre mo o ja vo o ma zuli Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: After you are settled in the towns that you will receive from the Lord your God, the people in each town must appoint judges and other officers. Those of you that become judges must be completely fair when you make legal decisions, even if someone important is involved. Don't take bribes to give unfair decisions. Bribes keep people who are wise from seeing the truth and turn honest people into liars.
translation_verse: Nmo nam ná di nɔɔno taane, n dae se n zege vwa wone, naa n pu nɔɔn-nɔɔno kwaga n bora borem ne. Ko dae se n jwoŋi dim, bɛŋwaane pɛɛra wae ya dwei nɔn-ŋona tete yia ye ya kweele chega taane ya pa se de ji vwa.

english_verse: If an ox or a sheep has something wrong with it, don't offer it as a sacrifice to the Lord your God—he will be disgusted! Put To Death People Who Worship Idols Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Yé kwei-na varem wolo na jege gɛɛ naa tusim o yera ne to á ma‑á kaane á pa á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, se o chuli konto.

english_verse: So when you hear that someone in your town is committing this disgusting sin, you must carefully find out if that person really is guilty.
translation_verse: Sawea kanto dwoŋi ná to á zwa ne, á jege se á tɔge ka nɛ se á lɔre chega kam. Nɔɔno wom nam ná seene o toŋe wo-lɔŋɔ kom konto Isarele teo kom ne,

english_verse: But you will need two or three witnesses—one witness isn't enough to prove a person guilty. Get rid of those who are guilty of such evil. Take them outside your town gates and everyone must stone them to death. But the witnesses must be the first to throw stones. Difficult Cases Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Maana-para bam mo jege se ba da yiga ba dole kandwa se nɔɔna bam maama pu ba kwaga ba dole kotu. Kanto chwoŋa kam mo á wó tɔge á ma‑á saare lwarem dem konto abam tetare ne. Taana yalo na dana ya dwoi to taane

english_verse: When other Israelites hear about it, they will be afraid and obey the decisions of the court. The King Moses said:
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne Isarele tiina bam maama ná nigi kolo na ke to, foone wó ja-ba, pa se ba daa yé zeiŋi ba tete ba ve bora borem. Isarele tiina bam Pɛ

english_verse: People of Israel, after you capture the land the Lord your God is giving you, and after you settle on it, you will say, “We want a king, just like the nations around us.”
translation_verse: Abam ná tu á zo tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam to, á laam wó boŋe se á tiŋi pɛ se o taa tei abam, nenɛɛne teene delo na gilimi abam to na jege pwa tei to.

english_verse: Go ahead and appoint a king, but make sure that he is an Israelite and that he is the one the Lord has chosen.
translation_verse: Nam tiŋi-na wolo yerane á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wó kuri to se o ji á pɛ. O jege se o taa ye abam tete dwi tu mo. Yé zaŋe á tiŋi-na veiru se o ji á pɛ.

english_verse: And the king must not have a lot of wives—they might tempt him to be unfaithful to the Lord. Finally, the king must not try to get huge amounts of silver and gold.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ba jege se o taa jege kaana dedɛ, banto na wae ba pae se o lɔ Wɛ kwaga ne to ŋwaane. O nam ba jege se o tiini o beeri dunni o pa o tete.

english_verse: The official copy of God's laws will be kept by the priests of the Levi tribe. So, as soon as anyone becomes king, he must go to the priests and write out a copy of these laws while they watch.
translation_verse: O ná bobo se o di paare, ko jege se o vo Wɛ kaanem tiina bam tei mo o beeri Wɛ nia yam se ba lwoni ya dwonna ba tiŋi tɔnɔ wone ba pa‑o.

english_verse: So when I want to speak to them, I will choose one of them to be a prophet like you. I will give my message to that prophet, who will tell the people exactly what I have said.
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se amo ni-jwoŋinu nwoŋi ba dwi wone, ne nmo de na ye tei to, ye a toŋe‑o ba tei ne. Amo wó bere‑o a taane dem, se o lwoni o bere nɔɔna bam.

english_verse: Some Levites may have money from selling family possessions, and others may not. But all Levites serving at the place of worship will receive the same amount of food from the sacrifices and gifts brought by the people. Don't Do Disgusting Things Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Wonto de jege chwoŋa se o taa jwoŋi o wodiu se ko taa mae de babam bam na jwoŋi tei to mo, de o ná maŋe o jwoŋi kolo o kwo jejegero tem baŋa ne de. Wo-zɔɔna kikia

english_verse: When you sacrifice a bull or sheep, the priests will be given the shoulder, the jaws, and the stomach.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná tu o kaane naao naa pia o pa Wɛ, kaanem tiina bam jege chwoŋa se ba le vɔŋɔ, de peyaa, de puga ba pa ba tete.

english_verse: In addition, they will receive the first part of your grain harvest and part of your first batches of wine and olive oil. You must also give them the first wool that is cut from your sheep each year.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye Wɛ pɛɛra yalo na ye mena, de sa-doora, de nuga, de pei-koro, ye te lwoori yiga te ke to, wonnu tento de wó taa ye Wɛ kaanem tiina nyem mo.

english_verse: Give these gifts to the priests, because the Lord has chosen them and their descendants out of all the tribes of Israel to be his special servants at the place of worship.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom pɔɔre Levi dwi dem Isarele dwia yam maama wone se banto de ba bia taa toŋe ba pa‑o o wara-jei sem ne, se ko taa vei wuu.

english_verse: Any Levite can leave his hometown, and go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped,
translation_verse: Levi tu ná boŋe se o nwoŋi á teo kolo maama o na zoore to ne se o vo jeiga kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kuri to, o jege chwoŋa se o ke konto,

english_verse: and then be a special servant of the Lord there, just like all the other Levites.
translation_verse: se o vo o toŋe o pa o Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ne o dwonna Levi tiina bam de na toŋe ba pa‑o tei to.

english_verse: Soon you will go into the land that the Lord your God is giving you. The nations that live there do things that are disgusting to the Lord, and you must not follow their example.
translation_verse: Á ná tu á zo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam tega kalo to wone, se á yé lwoni totoŋ-zɔɔna yalo dwi-gɛ tiina balo na zoore da ye ba toŋe to.

english_verse: Don't sacrifice your son or daughter. And don't try to use any kind of magic or witchcraft to tell fortunes or to cast spells or to talk with spirits of the dead.
translation_verse: Ko chula se abam wolo zwɛ o bu mini wone o ma ke kaanem. Ko ta chula se yi-nara, de vora, de chera, de liri-mwa tiina taa wo abam tetare ne ba toŋe ba totoŋa. Baŋa Wɛ chuli balo na dole sabu-pwona ba ma beeri ba nii ba yiga to de, dedaane chichiri vora maama.

english_verse: The Lord is disgusted with anyone who does these things, and that's why he will help you destroy the nations that are in the land.
translation_verse: O chuli balo maama na toŋe totoŋ-vɛɛsa yam konto dwoŋi to. Ko maa ye konto ŋwaane mo o lage o da á yiga o zeili dwi-gɛ tiina bam se abam wane á zo da.

english_verse: Never be guilty of doing any of these disgusting things! A Prophet like Moses Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Abam nam jege se á yɔɔre á tɔge á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom chwei sem, se á yé tusi de fenfee de. Baŋa Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu

english_verse: You will go in and take the land from nations that practice magic and witchcraft. But the Lord your God won't allow you to do those things.
translation_verse: Dwi-gɛ tiina balo á na wó zeili to yeini ba cheigi vora de yi-nara veera yam mo. Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom nam wo pɛ abam pwola se á ke konto.

english_verse: Instead, he will choose one of your own people to be a prophet just like me, and you must do what that prophet says.
translation_verse: O za wó toŋe o ni-jwoŋinu á tei ne, ne amo na ye tei to. Wonto wó nwoŋi abam tete dwi dem wone mo. Nam cheigi-na o taane dem.

english_verse: You were asking for a prophet the day you were gathered at Mount Sinai and said to the Lord, “Please don't let us hear your voice or see this terrible fire again—if we do, we will die!”
translation_verse: Abam déem na gilimi daane Sinayi peo kom teiŋa ne dɛ delo to, á lwoori á we, á daa ba lage se á ni Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam vekke, á nam ba lage se á na Wɛ min-vo-fɔrɔ kom, á na fona we á wó te to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me: Moses, they have said the right thing.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we: ‘Nɔɔna bam na lwoori kolo to maama jege chega.

english_verse: Since the message comes from me, anyone who doesn't obey the message will have to answer to me.
translation_verse: O na wó taa ŋɔɔne amo yere ŋwaane to, wolo maama ná ve se o sɛ o ni, amo tete wó seene yia mo a bwei kotu.

english_verse: But if I haven't spoken, and a prophet claims to have a message from me, you must kill that prophet, and you must also kill any prophet who claims to have a message from another god. Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Sampwora kalo maama nam ná mɛ amo yere o ŋɔɔne taane ye ko dae amo mo pɛ‑o taane dem, konto tu jege se o te mo. Ko ta ye bedwe mo de sampwora kalo na wó ma wa yadwonna yere o pworisi to, wonto de jege se o te mo.’

english_verse: You may be asking yourselves, “How can we tell if a prophet's message really comes from the Lord?”
translation_verse: Á nam wae á bwei nenɛɛne, á wó ke tɛ mo á lɔre we sampwora kanto na ŋɔɔne kolo to seene ko ye Baŋa Wɛ taane naa ko dae.

english_verse: You will know, because if the Lord says something will happen, it will happen. And if it doesn't, you will know that the prophet was falsely claiming to speak for the Lord. Don't be afraid of any prophet whose message doesn't come from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ne sampwora ná mɛ Baŋa Wɛ yere o ŋɔɔne taane ye kolo o na tage to wo ke, ko bere we ko dae Baŋa Wɛ kwora mo o ŋɔɔne. Sampwora kam konto zeiŋi o tete mo o ŋɔɔna. Á ba jege se á ta‑á kɔre‑o.”

english_verse: Israel, the Lord your God has promised that if you obey his laws and teachings I'm giving you, and if you always love him, then he will give you the land he promised your ancestors. When that happens, you must name three more Safe Towns in the new territory.
translation_verse: ko jege se á ta kuri teene detɔ mo á woli da. Á nam wó ta‑á tɔge Wɛ nia yalo maama amo na pɛ abam zem tento to, se á ta‑á swoi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ye á tɔge o chwei sem, se o laam woli tega kam maama o pa abam se á ta‑á tei.

english_verse: Soon you will go into the land and attack the nations. The Lord your God will destroy them and give you their lands, towns, and homes. Then after you are settled,
translation_verse: “Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom laam wó chɔge dwia yalo á na lage á kwei ya tega á ta‑á tei to. Á wó vo á zeili-ba ye á daare á ta‑á zoore ba teene de ba sam wone.

english_verse: you must choose three of your towns to be Safe Towns. Divide the land into three regions with one Safe Town near the middle of each, so that a Safe Town can be easily reached from anywhere in your land. Then, if one of you accidentally kills someone, you can run to a Safe Town and find protection from being put to death. But you must not have been angry with the person you killed.
translation_verse: Mo ko na wó ke tei ko pa nɔɔno wolo na go o dwoŋi ye o wo paale o ke to. Ko ná dae we ba ya maŋe ba done daane, nɔɔno wom konto wó wane o duri o zo teo kom o jwoŋi o tete o yage.

english_verse: For example, suppose you and a friend go into the forest to cut wood. You are chopping down a tree with an ax, when the ax head slips off the handle, hits your friend, and kills him. You can run to one of the Safe Towns and save your life.
translation_verse: Ko maŋe de nɔɔna balei ná dɛ daane ba zo kagoa se ba gwoni dɛ. Ba dedoa ná wora o zage tio pa se o dwooru yuu le ko mage wodwoŋi wom ko go, o wó wane o duri o vo o zo teene dem konto dedoa o seigi se o jwoŋi o tete.

english_verse: You don't deserve to die, since you did not mean to harm your friend. But he did get killed, and his relatives might be very angry. They might even choose one of the men from their family to track you down and kill you. If it is too far to one of the Safe Towns, the victim's relative might be able to catch you and kill you.
translation_verse: Ko ná dae konto, ye chwoŋa kam ná tiini ka dɔra, wolo na tege to yera nɔɔno wó wane o pare nɔn-goro wom o yi ye o tɔge o ban-zɔŋɔ kom baŋa o ja‑o o go. Kotu nam wo maŋe se o te, o na wo paale o go o dwoŋi wom to ŋwaane.

english_verse: That's why I said there must be three Safe Towns.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri a pɛ abam ni we á kuri teene detɔ ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane.

english_verse: You will need them, so innocent people won't be killed on your land while they are trying to reach a Safe Town that is too far away. You will be guilty of murder, if innocent people lose their lives because you didn't name enough Safe Towns in the land the Lord your God will give you.
translation_verse: Á jege se á kuri teene detɔ á woli da, se nɔɔna balo na wo maŋe se ba te to yé te. Abam ná wo ke konto, ye nɔɔno ná tega konto dwoŋi tega kalo Baŋa Wɛ na lage o pa abam to wone, o jana wó ta wo á yuu ne.

english_verse: But what if you really do commit murder? Suppose one of you hates a neighbor. So you wait in a deserted place, kill the neighbor, and run to a Safe Town.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ná maŋe o chuli o dwoŋi ye o beeri pwola se o go‑o, ko ye o paale mo. Konto tu laam ná duri o vo o zo teene dento dedoa wone se o seigi,

english_verse: If that happens, the leaders of your town must send messengers to bring you back from the Safe Town. They will hand you over to one of the victim's relatives, who will put you to death.
translation_verse: o tete teo kom nakwa mo jege se ba toŋe ba ja‑o ba jwoori ba teo kom, se ba daare ba ke‑o wolo o na go to yera nɔɔno jeŋa ne. O jege se o te mo.

english_verse: Israel, for the good of the whole country, you must kill anyone who murders an innocent person. Never show mercy to a murderer! Property Lines Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Yé duri-na nɔn-goro ŋwaŋa. Saare-na keim-lɔŋɔ konto dwoŋi Isarele laŋa kam ne se á ŋwea wane ka ke lanyerane ka pa abam. Faŋa faŋa siseina yam

english_verse: In the land the Lord is giving you, there are already stones set up to mark the property lines between fields. So don't move those stones. Witnesses Must Tell the Truth Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Abam ná tu á zo tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á tei to wone, nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé zaŋe o di o zo o dwoŋi siseini delo na maŋe de lɔ de tiga faŋa faŋa to. Maana para taane

english_verse: If you accuse someone of a crime, but seem to be lying,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná kwaane se o pa ko zo o dwoŋi yera ye o bwɛ‑o Wɛ nia chɔgem baŋa ne,

english_verse: then both you and the accused must be taken to the court at the place where the Lord is worshiped. There the priests and judges will find out if you are lying or telling the truth. If you are lying and the accused is innocent,
translation_verse: Banto mo wó nii ba taane dem wone zii ba kwaane ba lɔre ko ye chega naa vwa. Ba ná nɛ we nɔɔno wom bwɛ o dwoŋi Isarele tu vwa wone,

english_verse: then you will be punished without mercy. You will receive the same punishment the accused would have received if found guilty, whether it means losing an eye, a tooth, a hand, a foot, or even your life. Israel, the crime of telling lies in court must be punished. And when people hear what happens to witnesses that lie, everyone else who testifies in court will tell the truth.
translation_verse: Yé duri-na vwa-nyem ŋwaŋa. Ŋwea mo ba wó chɔge ba ma ba leiri ŋwea, yi mo ba wó le ba ma leiri yi, yeili mo ba wó guri ba ma leiri yeili, jeŋa mo ba wó le ba ma leiri jeŋa, naa naga mo ba wó ma leiri naga.”

english_verse: If you have to go to war, you may find yourselves facing an enemy army that is bigger than yours and that has horses and chariots. But don't be afraid! The Lord your God rescued you from Egypt, and he will help you fight.
translation_verse: “Á ná nwoŋi se á kwaare jara de á dona, ye á ná nɛ we ba jar-keira, de ba torokooro, de ba sisein-nɔɔna daga te dwoi abam, yé kɔre-na foone. Á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na vere abam Ejipti tiina jeŋa ne to wó taa wo á tei ne.

english_verse: Before you march into battle, a priest will go to the front of the army
translation_verse: Á ná nwoŋi se á ke jara yam, Wɛ kaanem tu mo wó nwoŋi o zege á yiga ne o ta de jar-keira bam o we:

english_verse: and say, “Soldiers of Israel, listen to me! Today when you go into battle, don't be afraid of the enemy, and when you see them, don't panic.
translation_verse: ‘Cheigi-na, Isarele tiina bam, á zem na lage á kwaare jara de á dona to, yé kɔre-na foone. Nam yé pa-na se á yera ta sae, naa se á vɔna pare.

english_verse: The Lord your God will fight alongside you and help you win the battle.”
translation_verse: Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo lage o da á yiga o ja jara yam o pa abam, se á wane á dona á di.’

english_verse: Then the tribal officials will say to the troops: If any of you have built a new house, but haven't yet moved in, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to live in your new house.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne jar-keira dedɛɛra bam wó zaŋe ba ta de nɔɔna bam maama ba we: ‘Abam wolo maama ná lɔge diga ye o ta wo lwoori Wɛ swolim o yage ka baŋa ne, se kotu jwoori sɔŋɔ! Kotu ná zo jara wone ye o te, nɔn-gaa mo wó jwoŋi-ka o taa tei.

english_verse: If any of you have planted a vineyard but haven't had your first grape harvest, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to enjoy your grapes.
translation_verse: Abam wolo nam ná puli o Vini teeni gaare ye o ta wo nɛ chwoŋa se o di tio-bia bam ywoni, se kotu de jwoori sɔŋɔ! Kotu ná zo jara wone ye o te, nɔn-gaa mo wó vo o di tio-bia bam.

english_verse: If any of you are engaged to be married, you may go back home and get married. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to marry the woman you are engaged to.
translation_verse: Abam wolo de ná jei se o wuli kaane leile ye o ta wo di‑o, se kotu jwoori sɔŋɔ! Kotu de ná zo jara wone ye o te, nɔn-gaa mo wó di kaane wom.’ Dedɛɛra bam ta wó ta ba woli da ba we:

english_verse: Finally, if any of you are afraid, you may go home. We don't want you to discourage the other soldiers.
translation_verse: ‘Abam wolo baare ná jei ye foone jege‑o, kotu jwoori sɔŋɔ, se o yé pa se nɔɔna badwonna bam wo leere.’

english_verse: When the officials are finished giving these orders, they will appoint officers to be in command of the army.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛra bam ná ŋɔɔne tento ba ti, ba laam wó kuri yiga tiina se ba taa nii jar-keira bam popɔra maama baŋa ne.

english_verse: Whenever you capture towns in the land the Lord your God is giving you, be sure to kill all the people and animals.
translation_verse: Ko daare ko ná ye teene delo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á tei to, á jege se á go nɔɔna balo maama de vara balo maama na wo de wone to mo.

english_verse: If you allow them to live, they will persuade you to worship their disgusting gods, and you will be unfaithful to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ko ná dae konto, ba wó pa se á ke wɛleere á chɔge á Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga ye á lwoni totoŋ-zɔɔna yalo ba na toŋe ba ma zuli ba jwona yam to mo.

english_verse: When you are attacking a town, don't chop down its fruit trees, not even if you have had the town surrounded for a long time. Fruit trees aren't your enemies, and they produce food that you can eat, so don't cut them down.
translation_verse: Abam ná vei á kwaare jara de teo kodwoŋi, ye á ná kaare-ko á pu á dáane, yé zage-na teeni delo na wo teo kom ni ne to á de tega ne. Á jege chwoŋa se á di de tio-bia bam, se á yé chɔge teeni dem. Teeni dem dae á dona se á kwaare jara de dento.

english_verse: You may need wood to make ladders and towers to help you get over the walls and capture the town. But use only trees that you know are not fruit trees.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye teeni delo á na yei we de ba leiri bia to, á jege chwoŋa se á zage-de ye á daare á kwei dɛ sem á ma‑á ke jara zela yalo na wó woli abam se á kaare teo kom á pu se á laam wane ko nɔn-bia bam to.”

english_verse: Suppose the body of a murder victim is found in a field in the land the Lord your God is giving you, and no one knows who the murderer is.
translation_verse: “Abam ná tu á zoore tega kalo wone á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á tei to, á ná nɛ ba na go nɔɔno pwola ne ye á yeiri wolo na go‑o to,

english_verse: The judges and other leaders from the towns around there must find out what town is the closest to where the body was found.
translation_verse: á nakwa de balo na nii taana baŋa ne to mo wo nwoŋi ba vo ba maŋe too wom na tigi mɛ to se ko vo yi teene delo na bwola de ka jeiga kam to.

english_verse: The leaders from that town will go to their cattle herds and choose a young cow that has never been put to work.
translation_verse: Teo kolo na ye bwola bwola de jeiga kam to nakwa bam laam maa wó lage na-chwɛ delo ba ta na wo mɛ ba toŋe to.

english_verse: They and some of the priests will take this cow to a nearby valley where there is a stream, but no crops. Once they reach the valley, the leaders will break the cow's neck. The priests must be there, because the Lord your God has chosen them to be his special servants at the place of worship. The Lord has chosen them to bless the people in his name and to be judges in all legal cases, whether property or injury is involved.
translation_verse: Levi dwi kaanem tiina de jege se ba taa wora mo se ba nii totoŋe dem. Kokuri to á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kuri banto mo se ba taa toŋe ba pa‑o ba daare ba taa sɔɔle Wɛ swolim ba ke o nɔɔna yuu ne. Baŋa Wɛ pɛ-ba dam se ba kwɛ taane delo maama na jege ni-kantɔgɔ naa zonne keim to.

english_verse: The town leaders will wash their hands over the body of the dead cow
translation_verse: Teo kolo na bwola de jeiga kam to nakwa bam laam maa wó sane ba je na-teko kom baŋa ne,

english_verse: and say, “We had no part in this murder, and we don't know who did it.
translation_verse: ye ba ta jaja ba we, ‘Ko dae debam mo go nɔɔno wom. Dé yia nam wo nɛ wolo na toŋe dento totoŋe dem to.

english_verse: But since an innocent person was murdered, we beg you, our Lord, to accept this sacrifice and forgive Israel. We are your people, and you rescued us. Please don't hold this crime against us.” If you obey the Lord and do these things, he will forgive Israel. Marrying a Woman Taken Prisoner in War Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Á ná tɔge ni delo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ abam to, á wó saare lwarem dem á tetare ne, ye o toone dem bá taa wo á yuu ne. Kaana balo ba na vere jara baŋa ne to taane

english_verse: From time to time, you men will serve as soldiers and go off to war. The Lord your God will help you defeat your enemies, and you will take many prisoners.
translation_verse: Abam ná kwaare jara de á dona ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwei-ba o ke á jeŋa ne pa se á wane-ba ye á ja ba badwonna á ja viiri,

english_verse: One of these prisoners may be a beautiful woman, and you may want to marry her. But first you must bring her into your home, and have her shave her head, cut her nails, get rid of her foreign clothes, and start wearing Israelite clothes. She will mourn a month for her father and mother, then you can marry her.
translation_verse: O jege se o lɔɔre gwaaro telo o ya na zo o tete teo ne to ye o leiri o zo tedwonna. O maa wó maŋe nmo sɔŋɔ ne chana dedoa o keeri o kwo de o nu. Chana dedoa kam kwaga ne n laam jege chwoŋa se n peini ded‑o, n na pɛ se o ji n kaane to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Later on, if you are not happy with the woman, you can divorce her, and she can go free. But you have slept with her as your wife, so you cannot sell her as a slave or make her into your own slave. Rights of a First-Born Son Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ko ná wora ko wora ye n daa‑n ba lage‑o, se n yage‑o se o viiri zɛɛra. O jege chwoŋa se o vo mɛ o na lage to. N na fe‑o pa se o peini dede‑m to ŋwaane, n bá‑n wane n yeigi‑o n jwoŋi sabu naa n bɛɛse‑o ne n kabaa tei. Bu-kwea taane

english_verse: Suppose a man has two wives and loves one more than the other. The first son of either wife is the man's first-born son, even if the boy's mother is the wife the man doesn't love. Later, when the man is near death and is dividing up his property, he must give a double share to his first-born son, simply because he was the first to be born. A Son Who Rebels Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: O nam jege se o zege wolo na ye o bu-kwea kam chekke to kwaga ne, ye o pa‑o o jejegero tem maama wone popɔra kuni belei, ne ko na maŋe se bu-kwea jwoŋi tei to, ko ná maŋe ko dae o ka-swono kom bu de. Zwabani-nyem taane

english_verse: A father and a mother may have a stubborn and rebellious son who refuses to obey them even after he has been punished.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wolo ná jege bu na ye yi-dɛɛre de zwabani-nyem ye o ba sɛ o kwo de o nu, ne ba na maŋe ba waare‑o tei maama de,

english_verse: If a son is like that, his parents must drag him to the town gate, where the leaders of the town hold their meetings.
translation_verse: o tiina bam jege se ba ja‑o mo ba vo o teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni ne ba jeeri teo kom nakwa bam se ba di o taane.

english_verse: The parents will tell the leaders, “This son of ours is stubborn and never obeys. He spends all his time drinking and partying.”
translation_verse: Ba wó ta de nakwa bam ba we, ‘Dé bu ye yi-dɛɛre de zwabani-nyem mo. O yeini o ba sɛ debam ni taane. O ta kwori o ye nɔn-kwolo de sa-nyɔro.’

english_verse: The men of the town will stone that son to death, because they must get rid of the evil he brought into the community. Everyone in Israel will be afraid when they hear how he was punished. The Body of a Criminal Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Teo kom baara bam maama laam jege se ba la mo ba dole‑o de kandwa ba go. Á ná ke konto, á wó saare lwarem dem á tetare ne. Isarele tiina bam maama ná nigi kolo na ke to, foone wó ja-ba. Chullu tedwonna

english_verse: If a criminal is put to death, and you hang the dead body on a tree,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná ke keim-lɔŋɔ kolo na maŋe de toone to, ye ba ná go‑o ba daare ba lei o yera daa baŋa ne,

english_verse: you must not leave it there overnight. Bury it the same day, because the dead body of a criminal hanging on a tree will bring God's curse on the land. The Lord your God is giving this land to you, so don't make it unclean by leaving the bodies of executed criminals on display.
translation_verse: ko dae se á pa se too wom taa page daa kam baŋa ne se tega ba ka poore. Á jege se á ke too wom dɛ dem konto ne mo. Wolo ba ná leigi daa yuu ne ba go, Wɛ sɔɔlem mo wo kotu yuu ne. Á nam jege se á suli‑o mo tega ne se ko yé chɔge tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á tei to.”

english_verse: If you see a cow or sheep wandering around lost, take the animal back to its owner.
translation_verse: “N ná nɛ n dwoŋi naao naa o pia na maa jia, yé pu n yia n yage se varem wom jei. Nam ja-ko n jwoori n vo n pa kotu.

english_verse: If the owner lives too far away, or if you don't know who the owner is, take the animal home with you and take care of it. The owner will come looking for the animal, and then you can give it back.
translation_verse: Kotu nam ná wo yiga yiga naa n ná yeiri wolo na tei varem wom, ja-ko n vo n sɔŋɔ se n ta‑n nii-ko. Kotu laam ná tu o beeri o varem wom, se n kwei n pa‑o.

english_verse: That's what you should do if you find anything that belongs to someone else. Do whatever you can to help, whether you find a cow or sheep or donkey or some clothing.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye n dwoŋi bonaga, naa o gɔrɔ, naa o woŋo kolo maama mo ná jei, se n ke konto dwoŋi. Yé pu n yia n yage se ko jei.

english_verse: Oxen and donkeys that carry heavy loads can stumble and fall, and be unable to get up by themselves. So as you walk along the road, help anyone who is trying to get an ox or donkey back on its feet. Don't Pretend To Be the Opposite Sex Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: N ná wo chwoŋa ne, ye n ná nɛ n dwoŋi bonaga naa o naao ná toa, yé gaale n kɛ. Woli‑o se o ja-ko o zege.

english_verse: Women must not pretend to be men, and men must not pretend to be women. The Lord your God is disgusted with people who do that. Don't Take a Mother Bird Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Kaana dae se ba zo baara gwaaro. Baara de nam ba jege se ba zo kaana gwaaro. Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom chuli balo na toŋe yanto totoŋa to.

english_verse: As you walk along the road, you might see a bird's nest in a tree or on the ground. If the mother bird is in the nest with either her eggs or her baby birds, you are allowed to take the baby birds or the eggs, but not the mother bird. Let her go free, and the Lord will bless you with a long and successful life. Put a Wall around Your Flat Roof
translation_verse: N jege chwoŋa se n ja ka bia bam, naa chechara yam n viiri se n daare nu wom se o kɛ. Ke konto se n ŋwea ke lanyerane ye n wane n dáane tega kam baŋa ne.

english_verse: If you build a house, make sure to put a low wall around the edge of the flat roof. Then if someone falls off the roof and is killed, it won't be your fault. Laws against Mixing Different Things Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Abam wolo ná lage o lɔ diga, kotu jege se o lɔ naware mo o kaare ka nayuu kom o che. N ná ke konto, ye nɔɔno ná zege ko yuu ne o to tega ne, kotu jana bá taa wo n yuu ne.

english_verse: If you plant a vineyard, don't plant any other fruit tree or crop in it. If you do plant something else there, you must bring to the place of worship everything you harvest from the vineyard.
translation_verse: Abam wolo ná dugi Vini teeni o gaare ne, kotu yé du wo-gaa o woli o gaare dem konto ne. N ná ke konto, wodiiru dwi dwi dem konto bá taa ye nmo nyem. N jege se n pɔɔre-te mo n pa Wɛ.

english_verse: Don't hitch an ox and a donkey to your plow at the same time.
translation_verse: Yé pa se nabea de bonaga sale daane se vaŋe vɔrɔ.

english_verse: When you weave cloth for clothing, you can use thread made of flax or wool, but not both together.
translation_verse: Nam yé zo gɔrɔ kolo ba na mɛ gare-ŋone yera yera ba ma sɔ-ko to, ne ko ná ye lɔŋɔ dedaane pei koro gare-ŋone.

english_verse: And when you make a coat, sew a tassel on each of the four corners. When a Husband Accuses His Wife Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ko ná ye gare-daŋɔ kolo n na wó zo to, se n seere-ko se kuna taa wo ko nia yana yam ne. Baro de o kaane taane

english_verse: Suppose a man starts hating his wife soon after they are married.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná swo kaane o peini ded‑o ye ko kwaga ne o daa ba lage‑o,

english_verse: He might tell ugly lies about her, and say, “I married this woman, but when we slept together, I found out she wasn't a virgin.”
translation_verse: o wó wane o fɔ vwa o daŋe o baŋa ne we, o na tu o peini de kaane wom to, o lɔre we o maŋe o lɔre baara ye o laam swoi‑o. O ná pɛ se kaane wom tiini o na chaveera konto dwoŋi,

english_verse: If this happens, the bride's father and mother must go to the town gate to show the town leaders the proof that the woman was a virgin.
translation_verse: bukɔ wom kwo de o nu mo jege se ba kwei gɔrɔ kolo na bere we bukɔ wom lɔre baara o baro wom tei ne to mo ba ja vo teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni ba bere teo kom nakwa.

english_verse: Her father will say, “I let my daughter marry this man, but he started hating her
translation_verse: Bukɔ wom kwo wó ta we, ‘A kwei a bukɔ a pa nɔɔno wonto se o di o ma ke o kaane, ye leile o daa ba lage‑o.

english_verse: and accusing her of not being a virgin. But he is wrong, because here is proof that she was a virgin!” Then the bride's parents will show them the bed sheet from the woman's wedding night.
translation_verse: O nam fɔge vwa o pa‑o we, o lɔre baara ye o laam zo‑o. Nii-na ba boboa sare-peiga gɔrɔ na taŋe de jana to mo tento. Konto nam bere we a bukɔ wom lɔre baara wonto tei ne mo.’

english_verse: The town leaders will beat the man with a whip
translation_verse: Teo kom nakwa bam laam wó ja nɔɔno wom mo ba waare‑o lanyerane.

english_verse: But if the man was right and there is no proof that his bride was a virgin,
translation_verse: Baaro wom nam na tage tei to ná ye chega mo ye kolokolo tera se ko bere we bukɔ wom maŋe o wo lɔre baara,

english_verse: the men of the town will take the woman to the door of her father's house and stone her to death. This woman brought evil into your community by sleeping with someone before she got married, and you must get rid of that evil by killing her. Laws about Illegal Sex Moses said:
translation_verse: ba jege se ba ja bukɔ wom mo ba nwoŋi o kwo sɔŋɔ ne, ye ba zege‑o pwooni yiga ne se teo kom baara bam dole‑o de kandwa ba go. O ta na zoore o kwo sɔŋɔ ne to o ke ka-bworo totoŋ-zɔɔna pa se chaveera di Isarele tiina bam. Konto ŋwaane, á jege se á saare lwarem dem konto mo á tetare ne.

english_verse: People of Israel, if a man is caught having sex with someone else's wife, you must put them both to death. That way, you will get rid of the evil they have done in Israel.
translation_verse: Baaro ná peini de nɔɔno wodwoŋi kaane ye á peere-ba, á jege se á go ba maama balei mo, se á wane á saare lwarem dem konto Isarele laŋa kam ne.

english_verse: If a man is caught in town having sex with an engaged woman who isn't screaming for help, they both must be put to death. The man is guilty of having sex with a married woman. And the woman is guilty because she didn't call for help, even though she was inside a town and people were nearby. Take them both to the town gate and stone them to death. You must get rid of the evil they brought into your community.
translation_verse: á wó ja-ba á nwoŋi teo kom dáa mo á dole de kandwa á go. Bukɔ wom jege se o te, o na wo teo wone ye o wo kaase se ba jwoŋi‑o ba yage to ŋwaane. Ko daare baaro wom jege se o te de o na chɔge bukɔ wolo na ye nɔɔno wodwoŋi kaane to mo. Konto ŋwaane, á jege se á saare lwarem dem konto mo á tetare ne.

english_verse: If an engaged woman is raped out in the country, only the man will be put to death.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ná wo pwola ne mo ye o zi bukɔ wolo na lage o zo baro to, baaro wom yerane mo jege se o te.

english_verse: Do not punish the woman at all; she has done nothing wrong, and certainly nothing deserving death. This crime is like murder,
translation_verse: Á ba jege se á ke busankana kam kolokolo. O wo ke o tusi se ko maŋe de o toone. Keim konto dwoŋi nye de nɔɔno na li o dwoŋi o go to mo,

english_verse: because the woman was alone out in the country when the man attacked her. She screamed, but there was no one to help her.
translation_verse: se baaro wom zi bukɔ wom pwola ne mo ywoo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se o jwoŋi bukɔ wom o yage, de o na maŋe o kaase tei to de.

english_verse: Suppose a woman isn't engaged to be married, and a man forces her to have sex with him. If he is caught,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná jeeri bukɔ wolo ta na yeiri baara to o zi‑o, ye ba ná peere-ba,

english_verse: A man must not marry a woman who was married to his father. This would be a disgrace to his father.
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé fɔge o ke o kwo chaveera se o peini de o kwo kaane wodwoŋi.”

english_verse: If a man's private parts have been crushed or cut off, he cannot fully belong to the Lord's people.
translation_verse: “Nɔɔno wolo ba na lwe to de wolo ba na gwoni o peini ba yage to ba jege chwoŋa se o tɔge o taa wo Baŋa Wɛ nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wone.

english_verse: No one born outside of a legal marriage, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can fully belong to the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Bia balo de ba na wo loge kadiri wone to de ba naaro se ko taa vei kuni fuga laŋa ne to de bá tɔge ba taa wo Baŋa Wɛ nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wone.

english_verse: No Ammonites or Moabites, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can become part of Israel, the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye Amon de Moaba tiina bam, banto de ba jege chwoŋa se ba tɔge ba taa wo Baŋa Wɛ nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wone, ko woli de ba naaro se ko taa vei kuni fuga laŋa ne.

english_verse: This is because when you came out of Egypt, they refused to provide you with food and water. And besides, they hired Balaam to put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Kokuri á déem na nwoŋi Ejipti ne á maa kɛa to, ba ve se ba woli abam de na de wodiu, ye ba kwori ba yeigi Beora bu Balaam de sabu se o sɔɔle lwarem o yage á baŋa ne. Beora déem zoore Mesopotamia teo Petora ne mo.

english_verse: But the Lord your God loves you, so he refused to listen to Balaam and turned Balaam's curse into a blessing.
translation_verse: Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom déem maa wo sɛ Balaam sɔɔlem dem, o na tiini o swoi abam to ŋwaane. O ma pipiri sɔɔlem dem o pa de ji swolim de pa abam.

english_verse: But Edomites are your relatives, and you lived as foreigners in the country of Egypt. Now you must be kind to Edomites and Egyptians
translation_verse: Nam yé gwooni-na Edom tiina, se ba ye á chorro mo. Á ta yé gwooni Ejipti tiina bam, se á déem ye veira mo ba teo kom ne.

english_verse: and let their great-grandchildren become part of Israel, the Lord's people. Keep the Army Camp Acceptable Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Banto naaro tem ko zege dwi kuni betɔ laŋa ne se ko taa tua jege chwoŋa se ba tɔge ba taa wo Baŋa Wɛ nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wone. Jar-keira bam tigisim jeiga kwɛɛm

english_verse: When you men go off to fight your enemies, make sure your camp is acceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Á ná tigisi daane se á kwaare jara de á dona, se á ta‑á cho-na á tete de kolo maama na jege digiru Wɛ chullu tem seeni to.

english_verse: For example, if something happens at night that makes a man unclean and unfit for worship, he must go outside the camp and stay there
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wolo nywanno tem ná lwogi tete ne, kotu jege se o nwoŋi dáa mo se o daa yé jwoori nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wone dɛ dem konto ne, o na chɔge o tete de Wɛ chullu tem to ŋwaane.

english_verse: until late afternoon. Then he must take a bath, and at sunset he can go back into camp.
translation_verse: Dedaan-ni ne mo o wó swɛ o yera, ye wɛ ná zoa, o laam jege chwoŋa se o jwoori o peini jar-keira bam tigisim jeiga kam ne.

english_verse: Set up a place outside the camp to be used as a toilet area.
translation_verse: Lage-na jei na ye dáa dáa de á tigisim jeiga kam to se á ta‑á vei á zege nɛ da.

english_verse: And make sure that you have a small shovel in your equipment. When you go out to the toilet area, use the shovel to dig a hole. Then, after you relieve yourself, bury the waste in the hole.
translation_verse: Á ná lage á vo á zege nɛ sem, le-na vɔrɔ á zela yam ne á ja vo se á ko gwoŋo. Á ná zege á ti, se á daare á suli beinnu tem.

english_verse: You must keep your camp clean of filthy and disgusting things. The Lord is always present in your camp, ready to rescue you and give you victory over your enemies. But if he sees something disgusting in your camp, he may turn around and leave. Runaway Slaves from Other Countries Moses said:
translation_verse: Pa-na se á tigisim jeiga kam taa ye wose, á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na kare o choa abam se o pa á wane á dona á di to ŋwaane. Ko dae se o na wo-zɔɔne á tetare ne se o viiri o daare abam. Wɛ nia dwi dwi

english_verse: When runaway slaves from other countries come to Israel and ask for protection, you must not hand them back to their owners.
translation_verse: Dwi-gɛ tu kabaa ná duri ka yi á teo kom se ka dale á tei ne, yé zeili‑o á pa o jwoori o tu tei.

english_verse: Instead, you must let them choose which one of your towns they want to live in. Don't be cruel to runaway slaves. Temple Prostitutes Moses said:
translation_verse: Pa‑o chwoŋa se o kuri á teene dem wone mɛ o na wó taa zoore to. Á ba jege se á bɛɛse‑o.

english_verse: People of Israel, don't any of you ever be temple prostitutes.
translation_verse: Isarele tu, baaro naa kaane, ba jege se o bwoori jwona zulim ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Lord your God is disgusted with men and women who are prostitutes of any kind, and he will not accept a gift from them, even if it had been promised to him. Interest on Loans Moses said:
translation_verse: Á nam ba jege se á kwei kabworim kikia sabu á ja á vo Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem se á ŋwe kampwola jene. Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom chuli kabworim dwi maama.

english_verse: When you lend money, food, or anything else to another Israelite, you are not allowed to charge interest.
translation_verse: N ná mɛ wodiu mo naa sabu naa woŋo kolo maama mo n jene n pa n dwoŋi Isarele tu, yé ta‑n lage nyɔɔre ko baŋa ne.

english_verse: You can charge a foreigner interest. But if you charge other Israelites interest, the Lord your God will not let you be successful in the land you are about to take. Sacred Promises to the Lord Moses said:
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye veira, n jege chwoŋa se n na nyɔɔre ba jena baŋa ne, se n yé ta‑n lage nyɔɔre n dwoŋi Isarele tu tei ne. Á ná tu á zo tega kam á tei, tɔge-na ni dem konto se á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó swɛ abam swolim se kolo maama á na jege á toŋe to ke lanyerane ko pa abam.

english_verse: People of Israel, if you make a sacred promise to give a gift to the Lord, then do it as soon as you can. If the Lord has to come looking for the gift you promised, you will be guilty of breaking that promise.
translation_verse: N ná gwoni ni n pa Baŋa Wɛ, yé dáane se n kwei n ni dem. Á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wó bwei‑m n wɛleere dem konto ŋwaane.

english_verse: On the other hand, if you never make a sacred promise, you can't be guilty of breaking it.
translation_verse: N nam ná wo gwoni ni n pa Wɛ, wɛleere de bá taa wora.

english_verse: You must keep whatever promises you make to the Lord. After all, you are the one who chose to make the promises. Eating Someone Else's Produce
translation_verse: N ná gwoni ni, ko ye n tete boboŋa ŋwaane mo pɛ se n pwooli. Konto to, nii ko baŋa ne se n kwei n ni dem lela.

english_verse: If you go into a vineyard that belongs to someone else, you are allowed to eat as many grapes as you want while you are there. But don't take any with you when you leave.
translation_verse: N ná tɔge n dwoŋi gaare o na dugi Vini teeni de wone to n via, n jege chwoŋa se n di de tio-bia bam ne n na wae tei to. Za n yé gwori n ke n tampɔgɔ ne n ja n viiri.

english_verse: In the same way, if you are in a grain field that belongs to someone else, you can pick heads of grain and eat the kernels. But don't cut down the stalks of grain and take them with you.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye n dwoŋi kara mo n tɔge da n via, n jege chwoŋa se n bwori mena n yu n done. Za n yé ma sekwara n ma‑n gaane-ya.”

english_verse: Suppose a woman was divorced by her first husband because he found something disgraceful about her. He wrote out divorce papers, gave them to her, and sent her away.
translation_verse: “Abam wolo ná swo o kaane ye o laam ba o ba lage kaane wom, o na ke kolo na jege chaveera to ŋwaane, kotu wó wane o popone kaane yagem tɔnɔ o pa‑o ye o zeili‑o se o viiri.

english_verse: Since she has slept with her second husband, she cannot marry her first husband again. Their marriage would pollute the land that the Lord your God is giving you, and he would be disgusted. Newlyweds Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: o boboa baro wom ba jege chwoŋa se o jwoori o swoi‑o maŋa de maŋa, kaane wom na chɔge o tete de baaro wodwoŋi wom to ŋwaane. O ná jwoori o swoi‑o, o chugi Baŋa Wɛ yi mo. Yé ja-na wɛleere dem konto dwoŋi á vo á chɔge tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á tei to.

english_verse: If a man and a woman have been married less than one year, he must not be sent off to war or sent away to do forced labor. He must be allowed to stay home for a year and be happy with his wife. Loans Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná swo ka-dooro ye ba ta wo ke bene dedoa daane, o dae se ba woli‑o jar-keira wone, naa se ba pa o toŋe kɔgɔ wo totoŋa. Pa-na se o kwɛ totoŋa bene dedwe se o wane o maŋe sɔŋɔ ne o pa se o kaane wom wo pwoli. Wɛ nia yadwonna

english_verse: When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that they will pay back the loan. But don't take one or both of their millstones, or else they may starve. They need these stones for grinding grain into flour to make bread. Kidnapping Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: N ná kwei woŋo n jene n pa nɔɔno ye o lage se o tiŋi daare, nam yé kwei o diga kam namim n ja n viiri, ko na ye kolo o de o diga tiina na mae ba ke ba ni-wodiu to ŋwaane.

english_verse: If you are guilty of kidnapping Israelites and forcing them into slavery, you will be put to death to remove this evil from the community. Skin Diseases Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wolo maama ná zi o ja o dwoŋi Isarele tu se o fe‑o se o ji o kabaa naa o yeigi‑o mo o pa kabɛɛne ne, kotu jege se o te mo. Ke-na konto se á saare lwarem dem konto á tetare ne.

english_verse: I have told the priests what to do if any of you have leprosy, so do exactly what they say.
translation_verse: Naywaane jaweo kom ná jege‑m, fɔge n ta‑n yei se n ke ne Wɛ kaanem tiina bam na wó bere‑m tei maama to. Tɔge-na bera yalo amo na maŋe a pa-ba to chekke.

english_verse: And remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam after you left Egypt. Loans Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Guli-na á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na toŋe tei de Miriam maŋa kalo á na nwoŋi Ejipti ne á maa kɛ to.

english_verse: When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that the money will be paid back. But you must not go into their house to get it.
translation_verse: N ná kwei woŋo n jene n pa nɔɔno, ye tɔge n zo o diga se n jwoŋi gɔrɔ kolo o na lage o ma tiŋi daare to.

english_verse: Wait outside, and they will bring out the item you have agreed on.
translation_verse: Ta‑n pɔe pwooni ne se o tete ja o nwoŋi o pa‑m.

english_verse: Suppose someone is so poor that a coat is the only thing that can be offered as a guarantee on a loan. Don't keep the coat overnight.
translation_verse: O ná ye yiniga tu, yé pa se o gɔrɔ kom peini n sɔŋɔ ne.

english_verse: Instead, give it back before sunset, so the owner can keep warm and sleep and ask the Lord to bless you. Then the Lord your God will notice that you have done the right thing. Poor People's Wages Moses said:
translation_verse: Wɛ ná lage de zo, se n jwoori n kwei o gɔrɔ kom n pa‑o se o ma o kwoli o tete. Keim dem konto wó pa se o ke nmo lei ko ŋwaane. N Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom de wó pa ko taa ye totoŋ-laao mo n kea.

english_verse: If you hire poor people to work for you, don't hold back their pay, whether they are Israelites or foreigners who live in your town.
translation_verse: Nabwom ná toŋe o pa‑m sabu ŋwaane, se n yé zaŋe n peene‑o, o ya ze ye n choro Isarele tu, naa veiru mo na zoore n teo kom wone to.

english_verse: Pay them their wages at the end of each day, because they live in poverty and need the money to survive. If you don't pay them on time, they will complain about you to the Lord, and he will punish you. The Death Penalty Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Dɛ maama ŋwe o sabu n pa‑o se wɛ laam zo. O na ye yiniga tu to, o teena wo sabu kom baŋa ne mo. N ná wo ŋwe‑o, o wó kaase o jare Baŋa Wɛ mo n ŋwaane, pa se ko ji wɛleere n yuu ne.

english_verse: Parents must not be put to death for crimes committed by their children, and children must not be put to death for crimes committed by their parents. Don't put anyone to death for someone else's crime. Don't Mistreat the Powerless Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Kwoa ba jege se ba te ba bia kikia ŋwaane. Bia de nam ba jege se ba te ba kwoa kikia ŋwaane. Nɔɔno ná maŋe se o te, ko wó taa ye o tete yuu lwarem ŋwaane mo.

english_verse: Make sure that orphans and foreigners are treated fairly. And if you lend money to a widow and want to keep something of hers to guarantee that she will pay you back, don't take any of her clothes.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye botara de veira balo na zoore á wone to, yé vane-na ba chega se ba yé na bora. Nam yé kwei kadeim gare-jale n ma n tiŋi daare.

english_verse: You were slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws. Leave Some of Your Harvest for the Poor Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Guli-na we abam déem ye kabɛ mo Ejipti ne, ye á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom laam ba o jwoŋi abam o yage. Mo kokuri a tage Wɛ ni dem konto a pa abam se á ta‑á tɔga.

english_verse: If you forget to bring in a stack of harvested grain, don't go back in the field to get it. Leave it for the poor, including foreigners, orphans, and widows, and the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
translation_verse: Abam ná wora á gwei á wodiiru tem ye á ná pɛ á daare men-pwoa yadwonna á yage kara ne, daa yé jwoori-na á vo á pɛ-ya. Yage-na-ya á pa veira, de botara, de kadeina se á Tu Baŋa Wɛ zaane taa wo á baŋa ne de kolo maama á na lage á toŋe to.

english_verse: When you harvest your olives, don't try to get them all for yourself, but leave some for the poor.
translation_verse: Á ná sugi á Olivi teeni dem se de tio-bia bam to ye á pɛ-ba, su-na bedwe yerane. Balo laam na daare to wó taa ye veira, de botara, de kadeina nyem mo se ba vo ba lare.

english_verse: And when you pick your grapes, go over the vines only once, then let the poor have what is left.
translation_verse: Á ná gwori á Vini tio-bia bam, se á ta vo á gwori-ba bedwe yerane. Balo na daare to ye veira, de botara, de kadeina nyem mo se ba laam vo ba lare.

english_verse: You lived in poverty as slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws.
translation_verse: Yé fɔge á swei we abam de déem ye kabɛ mo Ejipti ne. Mo kokuri a tage Wɛ ni dem konto a pa abam se á ta‑á tɔga.”

english_verse: Suppose you and someone else each accuse the other of doing something wrong, and you go to court, where the judges decide you are guilty. If your punishment is to be beaten with a whip, one of the judges will order you to lie down, and you will receive the number of lashes you deserve.
translation_verse: Wolo na to to ná maŋe se ba mage‑o, dedɛɛro wom wó pa se o peini o puga baŋa ne mo se ba laam fere‑o. Ferem dem na wó taa mae tei to nam jege se de maŋe de lwarem delo o na ke to mo.

english_verse: Forty lashes is the most that you can be given, because more than that might make other Israelites think you are worthless. Don't Muzzle an Ox Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ba jege chwoŋa se ba fere‑o se ko yi kuni finna mo. Ko ba jege se ko dwoni konto. Ko ná dwoni konto, á wó tiini á gwooni kotu mo.

english_verse: Don't muzzle an ox while it is threshing grain. A Son for a Dead Brother Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: N ná jege nabea n ma n toŋe n faao, yé vɔ ka ni se ka yé wane men-bia bam ka di.

english_verse: But suppose the brother refuses to marry the widow. She must go to a meeting of the town leaders at the town gate and say, “My husband died without having a son to carry on his name. And my husband's brother refuses to marry me so I can have a son.”
translation_verse: Too wom choro kom nam ná ba lage se o swoi‑o, kadeim wom wó vo teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni ne o jeeri nakwa bam mo ye o ta de-ba we, ‘Amo baro choro kom ba lage se o toŋe kolo na wó pa se o choro kom na dwi Isarele dwia yam wone to.’

english_verse: The leaders will call the living brother to the town gate and try to persuade him to marry the widow. But if he doesn't change his mind and marry her,
translation_verse: Teo kom nakwa bam laam maa wó bwoŋi‑o se o ba ye ba ŋɔɔne ded‑o. O ta ná ve se o swo kadeim wom,

english_verse: she must go over to him while the town leaders watch. She will pull off one of his sandals and spit in his face, while saying, “That's what happens to a man who won't help provide descendants for his dead brother.”
translation_verse: kaane wom laam wó fɔɔre o yi o tei mo nakwa bam yiga ne, ye o le nɔɔno wom natere dedwe o daare o twe lileeru o ke o yibia ne, ye o ta o we, ‘Tento mo ba jege se ba ke de wolo na ve se o pa o choro kom lo dwi to.’

english_verse: From then on, that man's family will be known as “the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off.” When Two Men Fight Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Isarele dwi tiina bam laam wó taa bwoi nɔɔno dwi dem konto we, ‘Ba na le nɔɔno wolo natere dedwe to sɔŋɔ tiina’.

english_verse: If two men are fighting, and the wife of one man tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the other man's private parts,
translation_verse: Baara balei ná jege daane ye ba dedoa kaane yi se o zeini o baro wom, o ná jaane baaro wowom wom manchala seeni mo o vaŋe,

english_verse: you must cut off her hand. Don't have any mercy. Be Honest in Business Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: yé duri-na kaane wom ŋwaŋa. Nam gwoni-na o jeŋa.

english_verse: Don't try to cheat people by having two sets of weights or measures, one to get more when you are buying, and the other to give less when you are selling.
translation_verse: Yé zaŋe n pini nɔɔna de n na maŋe wonnu tei n yeigi to. Ko dae se n ta‑n jege luuru telei n tampɔgɔ wone n ma n maŋe wonnu dum, naa n jege bwɛ selei na dae bedwe to.

english_verse: If you weigh and measure things honestly, the Lord your God will let you enjoy a long life in the land he is giving you.
translation_verse: Nam ma luuru de bwɛ selo na ye chekke to yerane n ta‑n ma n maŋe wonnu n yeiga. Ke konto se n wane n dáane tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam to wone de momwɛ-dɛɛre.

english_verse: But the Lord is disgusted with anyone who cheats or is dishonest. Wipe Out Amalek Moses said:
translation_verse: Kokuri to, abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom chuli balo na toŋe yanto totoŋa ye ba pini ba dwonna to. Amaleki tiina bam chɔgem

english_verse: People of Israel, do you remember what the Amalekites did to you after you came out of Egypt?
translation_verse: Guli-na Amaleki tiina bam déem na ke abam tei maŋa kalo á na nwoŋi Ejipti ne á maa kɛ to.

english_verse: You were tired, and they followed along behind, attacking those who could not keep up with the others. This showed that the Amalekites have no respect for God.
translation_verse: Á déem na bugi ye á bwona maŋa kalo to, ba jeeri abam chwoŋa ne ye ba go abam balo na wo kwaga ne ba waleme ba vei to maama. Konto mo ba mɛ ba bere we ba ba kɔre Wɛ.

english_verse: The Lord your God will help you capture the land, and he will give you peace. But when that day comes, you must wipe out Amalek so completely that no one will remember they ever lived.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri, á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ná tu o pa se á dona maama daa yé daane abam ye á sii de wo-zuru tega kalo o na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á tei to wone, se á laam saare Amaleki tiina bam logo baŋa maama ne se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa yé guli ba gula. Yé swei-na se á ke konto!”

english_verse: The Lord is giving you the land, and soon you will conquer it, settle down,
translation_verse: “Abam ná tu á zo tega kalo á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na lage o pa abam se á ta‑á tei to ye á ná jeini da,

english_verse: and plant crops. And when you begin harvesting each of your crops, the very first things you pick must be put in a basket. Take them to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped,
translation_verse: nɔɔno maama jege se o le wodiiru telo na lwoori yiga te ke o tega kam ne to o ke kayaa wone, se o ja o vo jeiga kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó kuri se nɔɔna zuli o yere da to mo.

english_verse: and tell the priest, “Long ago the Lord our God promised our ancestors that he would give us this land. And today, I thank him for keeping his promise and giving me a share of the land.”
translation_verse: Nmo wó vo n ta de Wɛ kaanem tu wolo na wora o nii jei sem da yam konto ne to n we: ‘A tɛ chega Baŋa Wɛ wolo nmo na toŋe n pa‑o to yiga ne we amo seene a zo tega kalo Baŋa Wɛ na gwoni ni de dé nabaara bam we o wó pa debam to wone.’

english_verse: The priest will take the basket and set it in front of the Lord's altar.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom wó jwoŋi n kayaa kam o zege Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem yiga ne.

english_verse: Then, standing there in front of the place of worship, you must pray: My ancestor was homeless, an Aramean who went to live in Egypt. There were only a few in his family then, but they became great and powerful, a nation of many people.
translation_verse: Nmo laam wó ta taane dento nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne we: ‘Amo nabaaro déem ye Aram tu na yeini o beeri to mo. O déem ma ja o diga tiina o vo Ejipti o zoore dáane. Ba déem na vei da to, ba ye fenfee yerane mo, ye ba laam ba ba puli ba ji dwi delo na dana lanyerane.

english_verse: The Egyptians were cruel and had no pity on us. They mistreated our people and forced us into slavery.
translation_verse: Ejipti tiina bam ma bɛɛse debam de je-dɛa ye ba fe debam pa se dé toŋe totoŋ-dɛɛra dé pa-ba.

english_verse: We called out for help to you, the Lord God of our ancestors. You heard our cries; you knew we were in trouble and abused.
translation_verse: Dé laam ma kaase dé jare dé nabaara Baŋa Wɛ wom se o zeini debam dé chanɛɛre dem wone. O déem ma maane dé yaara yam dedaane dé wo-chechɔgɔ kom, ye o daare o sɛ dé wɛ-lworo kom.
