translation_verse: O ma daare o ta de-ba o we, “Zo-na buga kam tetare se á gaale jei selo ba na zeŋe Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba zege to. Abam dedoa dedoa maa wó kwei kandwɛ-kamunu o dwi dem ŋwaane, o daŋe o bakale baŋa ne o ja o ba mɛ dé na wó peini zem to.

english_verse: Someday your children will ask, “Why are these rocks here?” Then you can tell them how the water stopped flowing when the chest was being carried across the river. These rocks will always remind our people of what happened here today.
translation_verse: se á ta de-ba we, ‘Ya guli debam maŋa kalo Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam na wora ka bɛ Jɔdan buga kam, ye buga kam na kɔ to mo. Ya ye gula mo ya pae Isarele kɔgɔ kom se ko taa vei wuu.’ ”

english_verse: The men followed the instructions that the Lord had given Joshua. They picked up twelve rocks, one for each tribe, and carried them to the camp, where they put them down.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma sɛ ba ke Baŋa Wɛ na bere Josua se ba ke tei maama to. Ba fuga-balei bam dedoa maama ma kwei kandwɛ dedwe se ko maŋe de ba dwia yam ni na mae tei to. Ba ma ja kandwa yam ba vo jei selo nɔɔna bam na lage ba peini tete dem konto ne to, ye ba tigisi-ya da.

english_verse: Joshua set up a monument next to the place where the priests were standing. This monument was also made of twelve large rocks, and it is still there in the middle of the river. The People of Israel Set Up Camp at Gilgal
translation_verse: Josua ma pa se nɔɔna badwonna maŋe Jɔdan buga kam tetare ne ba tigisi kandwa fuga-yalei. Ba tigisi-ya mɛ seeni kaanem tiina bam na zeŋe ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba zege to mo. Kandwa yam konto ta wora de zem maama.

english_verse: It was the tenth day of the first month of the year when Israel crossed the Jordan River. They set up camp at Gilgal, which was east of the land controlled by Jericho.
translation_verse: Boboa chana kam da fuga dɛ dem ne mo Isarele tiina bam déem bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. Ba ma yi Giligal ye ba chwi ba vwoa da. Teo kom konto wo Jeriko teo wɛ-puli seeni mo.

english_verse: The men who had carried the twelve rocks from the Jordan brought them to Joshua, and they made them into a monument.
translation_verse: Ko nam ya ye Giligal ne mo Josua pɛ se ba tigisi gula kandwa fuga-yalei yam ba na jaane ba nwoŋi Jɔdan buga kam ne to.

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Years from now your children will ask you why these rocks are here.
translation_verse: Josua ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Maŋa beena se á bia bwei abam we, ‘Kandwa yanto tigisi ywo-seeni bɛŋwaane mo?’

english_verse: Tell them, “The Lord our God dried up the Jordan River so we could walk across. He did the same thing here for us that he did for our people at the Red Sea,
translation_verse: Abam ta maa wó pa se ba lɔre we, dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se buga kam we á yibia ne nenɛɛne o déem na ke tei Nane-soŋo kom ni ne ye dé nɔɔna bam maama bɛ to.

english_verse: because he wants everyone on earth to know how powerful he is. And he wants us to worship only him.”
translation_verse: O nam ke konto mo se logo baŋa teene dem maama lɔre we, Baŋa Wɛ ye Wɛ-kamunu ye o jege dam. Konto maa wó pa se abam ta‑á zuli‑o se ko taa vei wuu.”

english_verse: The Amorite kings west of the Jordan River and the Canaanite kings along the Mediterranean Sea lost their courage and their will to fight, when they heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan River to let Israel go across. Israel Gets Ready To Celebrate Passover
translation_verse: Amori tiina pwa bam déem wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-zoore seeni mo, ye Kanaan tiina pwa bam de zoore Mediterania naneo kom nia yam ne. Banto maama ma ni we Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se Jɔdan buga kam we mo pa se Isarele tiina bam bɛ. Ba na nigi konto to, ba vɔna maama ma pare, ye ba nagwola te. Ba daa ba lage se ba jeeri Isarele tiina bam de jara.

english_verse: While Israel was camped at Gilgal, the Lord said, “Joshua, make some flint knives and circumcise the rest of the Israelite men and boys.”
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa ne mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Josua o we, “Ke fane se n ma n gwoni Isarele tiina balo na daare to peina.”

english_verse: Joshua made the knives, then circumcised those men and boys at Haaraloth Hill.
translation_verse: Josua ma seene o ke fane ye o gwoni nɔɔna bam peina zwoŋo kodwoŋi yuu ne, ko yere mo Gibeaf-Haaralof.

english_verse: Everyone who had been circumcised needed time to heal, and they stayed in camp.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na gwoni ba peina yam konto to, Isarele kɔgɔ kom ma maŋe dáane pa ba ŋɔna yam jei.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua, “It was a disgrace for my people to be slaves in Egypt, but now I have taken away that disgrace.” So the Israelites named the place Gilgal, and it still has that name.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Josua o we, “Amo zem lɔɔre Ejipti teo chaveera yalo maama ya na wo abam baŋa ne to a yage dáa ne.” Isarele tiina bam ma bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we Giligal. Dedaane zem maama, ba ta bwoi yere dem konto mo.

english_verse: The next day, God stopped sending the Israelites manna to eat each morning, and they started eating food grown in the land of Canaan. They ate roasted grain and thin bread made of the barley they had gathered from nearby fields. Israel Captures Jericho
translation_verse: Dento dɛ dem ne, ba na di tega kam baŋa wodiu to, mo Baŋa Wɛ chege se Manna yam daa yé zege wɛɛne ya to se Isarele tiina bam pɛ. Ko na zege kanto maŋa ne to, Isarele tiina bam laam lɛɛre ba di Kanaan tega kam wodiiru mo. Isarele tiina bam di Jeriko

english_verse: One day, Joshua was near Jericho when he saw a man standing some distance in front of him. The man was holding a sword, so Joshua walked up to him and asked, “Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe Josua na twɛ Jeriko to, mo o tole o na nɔɔno na zege o yiga ne. Kotu zei se-zɔɔ mo o jeŋa ne. Josua ma fɔɔre o yi nɔɔno wom tei ye o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo tɔge n woli debam kɔgɔ kom wone mo naa n woli dé dona bam wone mo?”

english_verse: “Neither,” he answered. “I am here because I am the commander of the Lord's army.” Joshua fell to his knees and bowed down to the ground. “I am your servant,” he said. “Tell me what to do.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo ba tɔge á wolowolo! Chega ŋwaane to, amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ jar-keira bam yiga tu. Konto ŋwaane mo a nam tu ywo-seeni.” Josua na nigi konto to, mo o to o vwi o yibia tega ne ye o jɔɔne‑o. Josua ta ma ta ded‑o o we, “Amo tu, a ye nmo tontoŋeno mo. Ta n bere-ne kolo a na jege se a ke to.”

english_verse: “Take off your sandals,” the commander answered. “This is a holy place.” So Joshua took off his sandals.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ jar-keira yiga tu wom laam ma ta ded‑o o we, “Le n natera yam, se nmo na zege mɛ to ye wose mo.” O ma seene o ke konto.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Jericho had been locking the gates in their town wall because they were afraid of the Israelites. No one could go out or come in.
translation_verse: Jeriko teo kom maama déem pe mo ko zega Isarele tiina bam ŋwaane. Nɔɔna daa ba jege chwoŋa se ba zo teo kom wone naa ba nwoŋi pwooni.

english_verse: The Lord said to Joshua: With my help, you and your army will defeat the king of Jericho and his army, and you will capture the town. Here is how to do it: March slowly around Jericho once a day for six days.
translation_verse: Abam maama de á jar-keira bam jege se á vo mo á kaare teo kom bedwe dɛ maama, se ko yi da yaredo.

english_verse: Take along the sacred chest and tell seven priests to walk in front of it, carrying trumpets. But on the seventh day, march slowly around the town seven times while the priests blow their trumpets.
translation_verse: Kaanem tiina barepɛ mo wó taa jege nabwanno ba tɔge Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne ba kɛa. Da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, á wó vo á kaare teo kom kuni berepɛ mo, ye kaanem tiina balo na zei nabwanno tem to de maa wó taa wui-te.

english_verse: Then the priests will blast on their trumpets, and everyone else will shout. The wall will fall down, and your soldiers can go straight in from every side.
translation_verse: Kaanem tiina bam wó ba ba tiini ba wu nabwanno tem ba dáane. Ko ná ke konto, se n pa nɔn-kɔgɔ kom laare de tiguri-kaasa, se teo kom kabiri-dɛɛro tem wó to tega ne buri-buri. Nɔɔna bam maama laam wó duri ba yɔɔre ba zo teo kom ba jage jei maama.”

english_verse: Joshua called the priests together and said, “Take the chest and tell seven priests to carry trumpets and march ahead of it.”
translation_verse: Nun bu Josua ma bwoŋi kaanem tiina bam ye o ta-ba o we, “Kwei-na Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam á zeŋe. Ta kuri-na kaanem tiina barepɛ se ba taa wo ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne ba taa zei nabwanno.”

english_verse: Early the next morning, Joshua and everyone else started marching around Jericho in the same order as the day before. One group of soldiers was in front, followed by the seven priests with trumpets and the priests who carried the chest. The rest of the army came next. The seven priests blew their trumpets while everyone marched slowly around Jericho and back to camp. They did this once a day for six days.
translation_verse: Da yalei dɛ dem ne nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama de ma saŋe ba kwaga ba vo ba kaare teo kom ni bedwe, ye ba laam jwoori ba vwoa yam ne. Ba ke konto mo taa, se ko yi da yaredo.

english_verse: On the seventh day, the army got up at daybreak. They marched slowly around Jericho the same as they had done for the past six days, except on this day they went around seven times.
translation_verse: Da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, Isarele tiina bam gwoni tega mo ba zaŋe. Ba ma tɔge naga kalo ba na yeini ba tɔga ba kaare teo kom to. Dento dɛ dem ne ba za kaare kuni berepɛ mo.

english_verse: Then the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua yelled: Get ready to shout! The Lord will let you capture this town.
translation_verse: Kaarem berepɛ tu wom baŋa ne, mo kaanem tiina bam wugi nabwanno tem ba dáane. Josua de ma pa ni o we, “Laare-na de tiguri-kaasa, kokuri Baŋa Wɛ mo kwei teo kom o ke á jeŋa ne!

english_verse: But you must destroy it and everything in it, to show that it now belongs to the Lord. The woman Rahab helped the spies we sent, so protect her and the others who are inside her house. But kill everyone else in the town.
translation_verse: Teo kom de kolo maama na wo ko wone to ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo. Zwɛ-na te maama á pa‑o. Ka-bworo Rahaba, de balo na wo o sɔŋɔ kom ne to yerane mo wó lu. Kokuri wonto mo ye wolo na seigi dé na toŋe balo se ba ŋɔ ba nii tega kam to.

english_verse: The silver and gold and everything made of bronze and iron belong to the Lord and must be put in his treasury. Be careful to follow these instructions, because if you see something you want and take it, the Lord will destroy Israel. And it will be all your fault.
translation_verse: Teo kom sabu-seŋa dedaane lu-nyenno de ko channa de ko luuru tem maama ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo. Tento maama ye se á la-te mo á pa Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: The priests blew their trumpets again, and the soldiers shouted as loud as they could. The walls of Jericho fell flat. Then the soldiers rushed up the hill, went straight into the town, and captured it.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na yɔɔre ba ni nabwanno tem kwori to, mo ba tiini ba laare tiguri-kaasa. Jeriko kabiri-lilirru tem ma to tega ne maama vim! Nɔɔna bam maama ma duri ba zo teo kom wone ba jwoŋi-ko ba tei.

english_verse: After Jericho was destroyed, Joshua warned the people, “Someday a man will rebuild Jericho, but the Lord will put a curse on him, and the man's oldest son will die when he starts to build the town wall. And by the time he finishes the wall and puts gates in it, all his children will be dead.”
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa kam ne Josua ma zege o du duuri dento o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se wolo maama na boŋe se o jwoori o lɔ Jeriko teo kom to na o lɛɛro. Kotu bu-kwea mo wó te se teo kom biri-beira laam zege. Se wolo maama na wó ke ko bworru-kamuna yam da to de ga o jeŋa bu.”

english_verse: The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem maa wo Josua tei ne maŋa maama. O yere ma zaŋe jei sem maama ne.

english_verse: The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem toŋe vwa mo wonnu telo Baŋa Wɛ na we te maŋe de chɔgem to baŋa ne. Akane déem mo ŋɔge wonnu tem tedwonna. O déem ye Karimi bu mo, ba maa ye Zabidi diga tiina. Ba ta ye Judah dwi dem nɔɔna mo na ye Zera sɔ-yuu tiina. Akane kikia yam ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ bane zaŋe de Isarele tiina maama.

english_verse: Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset.
translation_verse: Josua wo ma pɛ. O déem ma kaare o gwaaro, ye o daare o to o vwi o yibia tega ne. O déem ta bibili Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne taa, se ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa. Isarele nakwa bam de déem ke konto mo ye ba pɛ kasolo ba taare ba yuni maama.

english_verse: Then Joshua said: Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
translation_verse: Josua laam maa we, “Tento maama ye bɛ? Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, bɛŋwaane mo nmo jaane debam n bɛ buga kam n ba ywo-seeni? N lage n kwei debam mo n ke Amori tiina bam jeŋa ne na? Nmo we ba chɔge debam mo na? Debam ya ná maŋe Jɔdan buga daa kakam kam ne, ko ba gare tento na?

english_verse: I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy.
translation_verse: Amo Teiru, kɔ mo amo daa jege se a ta, ye dé dona pa se dé pipiri dé duri tento?

english_verse: Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
translation_verse: Kanaan tiina bam dedaane dwia yalo maama na zoore ywo-seeni to laam ná nigi tento, ba wó na baare se ba ba ba gilimi debam ba ke tetare ne. Ba laam maa wó pa se dé yere jei tega baŋa ne. Konto ná kea, nmo yere-kamunu nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom nam daa bɛ?”

english_verse: The Lord answered: Stop lying there on the ground! Get up!
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta Josua o we: “Zaŋe wɛɛne! Ko ke tetɛ mo ye n vwi n yibia tega ne konto?

english_verse: I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam mo tusi, ye ba ve ni-sɛɛm delo na wo amo de banto tetare ne to. Ba ma ŋɔ wonnu telo a na we te ye amo nyem to. Ba ŋweene dem kwaga ne, ba ta fɔge vwa. Ba ta daare ba kwei wonnu tem konto ba woli ba tete wonnu wone.

english_verse: What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane nam pa se á duri á dona bam yiga ne. Lɛɛro nam wo Isarele yuu ne ye ba maŋe de chɔgem. Abam nam ná wo chɔge wonnu telo ya na ye se te chɔge ye á kwei-te to, amo daa bá taa wo á tetare ne.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
translation_verse: Zaŋe n vo n ta se nɔɔna bam kwɛ ba tete se ba jwa jeeri-ne! Kokuri Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom tage tento mo: ‘Abam kwei wonnu telo na jege se te taa ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem to mo á woli á wonnu wone. Abam nam ná wo le-te á wonnu tem wone, á bá wane á dona bam á di.’

english_verse: “Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come,
translation_verse: Abam kɔgɔ kom maama jwa wó jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Baŋa Wɛ maa wó le Isarele dwi delo na tusi to. Dwi dem laam maa wó nwoŋi sɔ-yuu de sɔ-yuu se Baŋa Wɛ le sɔ-yuu kolo na tusi to. Sɔ-yuu kom de wó nwoŋi mo diga maama wone, se Baŋa Wɛ le diga kalo na tusi to, ye diga kam konto de laam ma nwoŋi nɔɔno dedoa dedoa, se Baŋa Wɛ le wolo na tusi to.

english_verse: and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
translation_verse: Ba ná nɛ nɔɔno wolo na ŋɔge wonnu telo á na jege se á chɔge to, ba laam wó zwɛ kotu mo. Ba ta jege se ba ja o yera woŋo maama mo ba woli da ba nwoŋi ba zwɛ. Kokuri, o tiini o ke wo-balɔrɔ mo na dae se ko ke Isarele ne. O chɔge ni-sɛɛm delo Wɛ de o nɔɔna bam na ke daane to mo.”

english_verse: Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Josua ma pa se Isarele tiina bam nwoŋi se Wɛ le dwi delo na tusi to. Judah dwi dem mo ba déem le.

english_verse: Then Joshua brought the clans of Judah to the Lord, and the Lord showed that the Zerah clan was guilty. One by one he brought the leader of each family in the Zerah clan to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Zabdi's family was guilty.
translation_verse: Judah dwi dem ma nwoŋi sɔ-yuu de sɔ-yuu. Ba ma le Zera sɔ-yuu kom. Zera di sem na bobo se te nwoŋi to, Zabidi diga kam mo ba le.

english_verse: Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
translation_verse: Zabidi diga kam nɔɔna bam ma nwoŋi nɔɔno dedoa dedoa ye ba le Karimi bu Akane.

english_verse: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
translation_verse: Josua laam ma ta de Akane we, “Amo bu, nmo zege Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to yiga ne mo. Konto to, pa‑o zula se n daare n ta chega. Ta n keim dem maama jaja n bere-ne, se n yé seigi kolokolo amo yiga ne.”

english_verse: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Akane ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo seene a tusi a chɔge Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to yiga. Amo nam ke tento mo:

english_verse: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma kwei wonnu tem vwei dem ne ba ja nwoŋi ba ba Josua dedaane Isarele tiina bam tei ne. Ba ma jale te maama Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
translation_verse: Josua laam ma ta ded‑o o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo ye n ja cham dento n ba n pa debam? Baŋa Wɛ de nam wó pa cham yi‑m zem.” Isarele tiina bam maama laam ma dole‑o de kandwa ba go. Ba déem ta dole o woŋo maama mo ba go. Ko kwaga ne, ba déem ma zwɛ wonto de o diga tiina bam de o wonnu maama.

english_verse: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma tigisi kandwa o baŋa ne. Kandwa-dogela yam ta wora dedaane zem maama. Ko nam na zege kanto maŋa ne se ko yi zem to, ba jege jei sem konto ba bwoi we, Cham bwolo mo. Ko ma pa se Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom dem to.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't be afraid, and don't be discouraged by what happened at the town of Ai. Take the army and attack again. But first, order part of the army to set up an ambush on the other side of the town. I will help you defeat the king of Ai and his army, and you will capture the town and the land around it. Destroy Ai and kill its king as you did at Jericho. But you may keep the livestock and everything else you want.
translation_verse: Ke-na Ayi teo kom de ko Pɛ nenɛɛne á na ke Jeriko de ko Pɛ wom tei to. Tento mo za wó leiri: Wonnu telo maama á na wó di Ayi teo kom wone to ye á nyem mo se á ta‑á jega. Ko maa ye ba naane dem de ba jejegero mo konto. Nam véi-na á vwɛ se ko taa bwola de teo kom.”

english_verse: The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away,
translation_verse: Dé lage dé pa ba pare debam mo, ye dé wora dé gane-ba mo konto se ba maama nwoŋi ba daare ba teo kom. Kokuri, ba wó boŋe ba tete ne we, ‘Dé daa pɛ se Isarele tiina bam duri debam yiga ne nenɛɛne boboa kam to.’

english_verse: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
translation_verse: Á maa ná nɛ we á vere teo kom maama, se á zwɛ-ko. Baŋa Wɛ we á ke konto mo, amo de nam pɛ abam ni se á ke konto.”

english_verse: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
translation_verse: Tega na jege ka poore to, Josua ma la Isarele jar-keira bam o ke daane. O de Isarele nakwa bam ma to ba yiga ne ye ba laam kwei Ayi chwoŋa ba maa kɛa.

english_verse: They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north.
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba maŋe Ayi teo kom baŋa seeni daa kam ne ba chwi ba vwoa. Bwolo mo déem tigi ba dedaane Ayi teo kom tetare ne.

english_verse: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
translation_verse: Ba na ke tei to mo tento: Ba nɔn-kɔgɔ kom ma zege ba maŋe dedaane teo kom baŋa seeni daa kam, ye balo na seigi ba vwɛ to zege ba maŋe de teo kom wɛ-zoore seeni. Josua tete laam ma vo bwolo kom ne tete dem konto.

english_verse: So he called out every man in Ai to go after Joshua's troops. They all rushed out to chase the Israelite army, and they left the town gates wide open. Not one man was left in Ai or in Bethel. Joshua let the men of Ai chase him and his army farther and farther away from Ai.
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno déem daa wo daare Ayi ne naa Bɛtel teo ne. Ba maama déem nwoŋi mo se ba pare ba ja Isarele tiina bam. Ba teo kom manchwo-peena yam ma daare ya tiga woo.

english_verse: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Josua o we, “Twe n chichwei dem n jeeri Ayi teo kom, se a lage a kwei teo kom mo a ke n jeŋa ne.” Josua ma ke Baŋa Wɛ na bere se o ke tei to.

english_verse: When Joshua and his troops saw smoke rising from the town, they knew that the other part of their army had captured it. So they turned and attacked. The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from their town. But they could not escape, because the soldiers they had been chasing had suddenly turned and started fighting.
translation_verse: Josua de nɔɔna balo na wo o tei ne to maane we, balo na vwɛ teo kom ni ne to wane-ko. Ba ma pipiri ba jeeri Ayi tiina bam ba di-ba jara wone.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them. The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma pare Ayi teo kom nɔɔna balo maama na nwoŋi ko wone to ye ba go ba maama nyɔ pwola kam ne! Konto kwaga ne mo ba duri ba zo teo kom wone ba go balo maama na wo ko wone to.

english_verse: Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. Those rocks are still there, and the town itself has never been rebuilt. Joshua Reads the Blessings and Curses (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye Ayi teo Pɛ wom, Josua kuuni‑o mo o yage tio yera ne pa se o leiga da konto taa, se ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa. Wɛ-zoore maŋa ne, Isarele tiina bam ma fwoli‑o ba ja ba vo ba dole ba yage teo kom manchwoŋo ni ne. Ba déem ma la kandwa ba pane o maama. Kandwa yam déem diini mo vili vili ye ya ta wora se ko ba yi zem. Ba guli Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dem gula

english_verse: Moses had said that everyone in Israel was to go to the valley between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, where they were to be blessed. So everyone went there, including the foreigners, the leaders, officials, and judges. Half of the people stood on one side of the valley, and half on the other side, with the priests from the Levi tribe standing in the middle with the sacred chest. Then in a loud voice, Joshua read the blessings and curses from The Book of the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Taane tera Moses na popone o tiŋi Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom wone ye Josua wo gage se Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama ni. O déem gage ko maama mo nyɔ pa se ba cheigi. Kaana bam de bia bam maama déem woli da mo ba cheigi ye veira bam de déem wo maŋe kwaga ne.

english_verse: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
translation_verse: Ko daare Gibeon tiina bam na nigi Josua de o kwaga kam na ke tei Jeriko dedaane Ayi teene dem baŋa ne to,

english_verse: So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country. The men put worn-out bags on their donkeys and found some old wineskins that had cracked and had been sewn back together.
translation_verse: mo ba ke swa se ba wane ba jwoŋi ba tete ba yage. Ba ma ke wodiu, ye ba kwei-ko ba ke ywollu-dwonnu wone ba daŋe ba bonɛ baŋa ne. Ba lɔɔro tem de déem maa dwoori lanyerane ye te kaare kaare.

english_verse: Their sandals were old and patched, and their clothes were worn out. They even took along some dry and crumbly bread.
translation_verse: Gwaaro telo nɔɔna bam na lɛ to déem maa ye gare-zenzwara, ye ba kwei natere-gorro ba zo. Ba wodiiru de déem ma kuuni, ye kodwoŋi de ko.

english_verse: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
translation_verse: Josua de o nɔɔna bam déem maŋe Giligal ne mo ba chwi ba vwoa. Gibeon tiina bam ma vo ba yi da, ye ba ta de Josua dedaane Isarele tiina bam ba we, “Debam teo ba ŋwae. Dé nam tu abam tei se dé ke ni-sɛɛm mo de abam.”

english_verse: The Israelites replied, “But maybe you really live near us. We can't make a peace treaty with you if you live nearby.” The Gibeonites said, “If you make a peace treaty with us, we will be your servants.” “Who are you?” Joshua asked. “Where do you come from?” They answered:
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma leiri Josua we, “Debam tu se dé sɛ dé pa abam.” Josua ta ma jwoori o bwei-ba o we, “Abam ye bera mo, ye á nwoŋi yei mo?”

english_verse: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri‑o ba we: “Debam nwoŋi teo yiga yiga mo dé ba ywo. Ko nam ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yere-kamunu kom ŋwaane mo dé tua. Dé nigi o na ke tei maama Ejipti ne to.

english_verse: and what he did to those two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan: King Og of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, and King Sihon of Heshbon.
translation_verse: Dé ta nigi Baŋa Wɛ na toŋe tei dedaane Amori tiina pwa balei bam na zoore Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to. Ko maa ye Hesebon teo Pɛ Sihon mo dedaane Basan teo Pɛ Oga paare dem na di Asetarof ne to.

english_verse: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
translation_verse: Debam teo nakwa dedaane dé nɔn-bia bam maama ma ta debam ba we, ‘Kwei-na wodiiru chwo-dɔrɔ kom ŋwaane se á vo á jeeri Isarele tiina bam. Nam ta-na de-ba we: Debam lage se dé sɛ dé pa abam. Abam de nam sɛ se dé ke-na ni-sɛɛm daane.’

english_verse: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
translation_verse: Nii-na debam bworobworo konto! Dé yɔɔre de wɔ-ko dé ti mo ye dé kwei chwoŋa se dé ba ywo. Leile konto ko nam kuuni mo ye ko ko.

english_verse: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
translation_verse: Lɔɔro tento dé na ke na te wone to ya ye lɔ-donno mo. Te laam nam dwoori mo, ye te bage bage. Dé natera dedaane dé gwaaro maama ma chɔge chwo-dɔrɔ kom baŋa ne mo.”

english_verse: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
translation_verse: Isarele nakwa bam ma jwoŋi Gibeon tiina wodiu kom ba laŋe ba nii, ye ba wo bwei se ba lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa.

english_verse: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
translation_verse: Josua ma ke ni-sɛɛm de nɔɔna bam se Isarele tiina bam yé go-ba. Isarele nakwa bam de déem ma du duuri se ko seene ko taa ye konto.

english_verse: A couple of days later, the Israelites found out that these people actually lived in the nearby towns of Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim. So the Israelites left the place where they had camped and arrived at the four towns two days later.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma kaare laŋa kam se ba nii Gibeon tiina teene dem na wo mɛ to. Ba ma kwei da yatɔ ba yi ba teene dem. Teene dem yera déem mo ye Gibeon, de Chefira, de Beerofa, dedaane Kiriaf-Jeerim.

english_verse: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam maa wo jeeri Gibeon nɔɔna bam de jara, ba yiga tiina bam na lwoori yiga ba ke ni-sɛɛm de-ba ye ba ma Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom yere mo ba du duuri ba pa-ba to ŋwaane. Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama ma bobo se ba poone ba yiga tiina bam, ni-sɛɛm dem ŋwaane.

english_verse: but the leaders reminded them, “We promised these people in the name of the Lord God of Israel that we would let them live, so we must not harm them. If we break our promise, God will punish us. We'll let them live, but we'll make them cut wood and carry water for our people.”
translation_verse: Ba daa maa we, “Ba ná ŋwe, dé wó pa se ba taa gwoni dɛ ye ba daare ba mɔɔne na ba pae Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama.” Isarele nakwa bam déem na bwɛ se ba ke kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
translation_verse: Josua ma bwoŋi Gibeon tiina bam ye o bwei-ba o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo á gane debam konto? Abam tage we á teo ba ŋwae, ye á laam zoore ywo-seeni bwola bwola.

english_verse: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
translation_verse: Lɛɛro laam nam mo wo á yuu ne. Ko zege zem dɛ dem se ko taa vei wuu, á wó ta‑á ye balo na gwoni dɛ mo, ye á daare á mɔɔne na debam Wɛ sɔŋɔ kom totoŋa ŋwaane.”

english_verse: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri Josua ba we, “Dé ye n tontoŋena mo. Dé maŋe dé ni abam Baŋa Wɛ wom na pɛ o tontoŋeno Moses kwora we, o di wɔnɔ tega kanto maama baŋa ne o pa abam, se á daare á chɔge ka nabiina bam maama tei to. Ko ma tiini ko pa se foone zo debam ye dé ke dé na ke tei maama to.

english_verse: and you are strong enough to do anything to us that you want. We just ask you to do what seems right.”
translation_verse: Dé laam nam to nmo pwoa ne. Ke debam tei maama n na nɛ we ko tɔge chwoŋa to.”

english_verse: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
translation_verse: Josua ma sɛ. O maa wo pɛ pwola se Isarele tiina bam go-ba.

english_verse: but he did tell the Gibeonites that they would have to be servants of the nation of Israel. They would have to cut firewood and bring it for the priests to use for burning sacrifices on the Lord's altar, wherever the Lord decided the altar would be. The Gibeonites would also have to carry water for the priests. And that is still the work of the Gibeonites.
translation_verse: Ko na zege dento dɛ dem ne se ko yi zem to, Josua pɛ se Gibeon nɔɔna bam taa gwoni dɛ mo ye ba daare ba mɔɔne na ba pae Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama. Ba déem ta ke konto mo Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem totoŋa ŋwaane. Ko nam ye jei selo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to ne mo ba ke konto.

english_verse: King Adonizedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured and destroyed the town of Ai, and then killed its king as he had done at Jericho. He also learned that the Gibeonites had signed a peace treaty with Israel.
translation_verse: Adoni-Zɛdeka na ye Jerusalem teo Pɛ to déem nigi we Josua di Ayi teo kom. O ta nigi we Josua yɔɔre o chɔge teo kom maama de ko Pɛ, nenɛɛne o na maŋe o lwoori yiga o ke tei de Jeriko teo de ko Pɛ tei to. O ta nigi Gibeon tiina bam na ke ni-sɛɛm dedaane Isarele tiina bam pa se ba zoore de-ba tei to.

english_verse: This frightened Adonizedek and his people. They knew that Gibeon was a large town, as big as the towns that had kings, and even bigger than the town of Ai had been. And all of the men of Gibeon were warriors.
translation_verse: Ko ma pa se foone tiini de zo wonto de o teo nɔɔna bam, kolo ŋwaane Gibeon déem ye te-fɔrɔ mo ko dwoi Ayi teo kom. Ko nɔn-bia bam de déem nam ya ye jar-keira mo chekke.

english_verse: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
translation_verse: Mo kokuri Pɛ Adoni-Zɛdeka toŋe se pwa banto jeeri ba woli‑o: Heboron teo pɛ Hoham, de Jaremuf teo pɛ Piram, ko woli de Lakisi teo pɛ Jafia, dedaane Egilon teo pɛ Debiri.

english_verse: “The Gibeonites have signed a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. Come and help me attack Gibeon!”
translation_verse: O ma pa-ba kwora kanto we, “Ba-na á woli-ne se dé ke jara dedaane Gibeon tiina bam. Kokuri to, ba ke ni-sɛɛm mo dedaane Josua de o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam.”

english_verse: the Gibeonites sent a message to the Israelite camp at Gilgal: “Joshua, please come and rescue us! The Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together and are attacking us. We are your servants, so don't let us down. Please hurry!”
translation_verse: Gibeon tiina bam ma toŋe kwora lela se ka yi Josua, ye Isarele tiina bam ta wo Giligal ne. Ba maa we, “Debam ye nmo tontoŋena mo. Nam yé swei-na debam swia. Ke-na lela á ba á jwoŋi debam á yage. Kokuri Amori tiina bam maama na zoore zwonnu tem laŋa ne to mo gilimi daane se ba chɔge debam.”

english_verse: “Joshua,” the Lord said, “don't be afraid of the Amorites. They will run away when you attack, and I will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta dedaane Josua o we, “Yé ta‑n kɔre foone. A lage a pa se nmo mo di-ba. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na wó wane o dwoni de nmo.”

english_verse: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se Amori tiina bam boboŋa jei, ye Isarele tiina bam déem go ba dedɛ Gibeon ne. Amori tiina bam badwonna ma kwei zwonnu laŋa chwoŋa kam na wo Bɛte-Horon seeni to. Ba na duri se ba lu to, mo Isarele tiina bam pare-ba ba goe ba vo ba kwaare Azeka dedaane Makeda na wo tega-kuri seeni to.

english_verse: And while these troops were going down through Beth-Horon Pass, the Lord made huge hailstones fall on them all the way to Azekah. More of the enemy soldiers died from the hail than from the Israelite weapons.
translation_verse: Amori tiina bam maa na zege Bɛte-Horon ne ba duri ba vei Azeka seeni konto to, mo Baŋa Wɛ tɔge ba kwaga o dole-ba dedaane do-kandwa taa, se ba vo ba yi Azeka. Do-kandwa yam déem ma go ba dedɛ se ko dwoni balo Isarele tiina bam na go to.

english_verse: The Lord was helping the Israelites defeat the Amorites that day. So about noon, Joshua prayed to the Lord loud enough for the Israelites to hear: “Our Lord, make the sun stop in the sky over Gibeon, and the moon stand still over Aijalon Valley.” So the sun and the moon stopped and stood still until Israel defeated its enemies. This poem can be found in The Book of Jashar. The sun stood still and didn't go down for about a whole day.
translation_verse: Wea kam ma maŋe da, ka zege cheppe. Chana kam de daa maa wo fofɔ ka vo yiga, se ko taa nii Isarele tiina bam na di ba dona bam ba ti to. Keim dento maama nam popone mo de tigi Jasare tɔnɔ kom wone. Wea kam déem ma maŋe wɛyuu kom tetare ne ka zege cheppe. Ka maa wo vei ka to, se ko maŋe de dɛ-puni.

english_verse: Never before and never since has the Lord done anything like that for someone who prayed. The Lord was really fighting for Israel.
translation_verse: Dé ta wo fɔge dé na dɛ nenɛɛne dɛ dem konto, pa se Baŋa Wɛ cheigi nabiinu kwora konto dwoŋi. Baŋa Wɛ ma woli de Isarele tiina bam ye ba ke jara yam.

english_verse: After the battle, Joshua and the Israelites went back to their camp at Gilgal. Joshua Kills the Five Enemy Kings
translation_verse: Josua dedaane Isarele tiina bam maama daa ma jwoori Giligal ne, mɛ ba ya na maŋe ba zoore to. Ba go Amori tiina pwa banu

english_verse: While the enemy soldiers were running from the Israelites, the five enemy kings ran away and hid in a cave near Makkedah.
translation_verse: Jara yam ta na wora ya ke konto to, Amori pwa banu bam ma duri ba vo ba seigi peo kodwoŋi bɔɔne wone. Jei sem wo Makeda laŋa ne mo.

english_verse: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ma na-ba ye o chɔ o bere Josua ba na wo mɛ to.

english_verse: Joshua answered, “Roll some big stones over the mouth of the cave and leave a few soldiers to guard it.
translation_verse: Josua de ma pa ni we, “Lage-na kandwa kamuna á ma á pe peo bɔɔne delo ba na seigi da to ni, se á ta daare á beeri nɔɔna se ba yere bɔɔne dem.

english_verse: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
translation_verse: Ko daare abam wolowolo yé maŋe kwaga ne! Pare-na á dona bam, se á che ba yiga se ba yé zo ba teene dem wone. Kolo ŋwaane, abam Baŋa Wɛ wom pɛ abam dam se á di-ba mo.”

english_verse: So Joshua and the Israelites almost wiped out the enemy soldiers. Only a few safely reached their walled towns.
translation_verse: Josua dedaane o jar-keira bam ma wane Amori tiina jar-keira bam maama ba ti. Ba fenfee yerane mo duri ba lu ba vo ba zo ba teene delo na lɔge de pe to wone.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp at Makkedah, where Joshua was waiting for them. No one around there dared say anything bad about the Israelites.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne, Isarele jar-keira bam maama ma jwoori Makeda dedaane yazura. Dáane mo Josua ya wora o cheigi-ba. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa maa ware se o ta Isarele tiina bam yera wo-lɔŋɔ.

english_verse: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
translation_verse: Josua ma ta o we, “Dɔne-na kandwa yam peo bɔɔne dem ni ne, se á ja pwa banu bam á ba amo tei.”

english_verse: The soldiers opened the entrance to the cave and brought out the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma ja Jerusalem pɛ, de Heboron pɛ, de Jaremuf pɛ, de Lakisi pɛ, ko woli dedaane Egilon pɛ ba ba o tei.

english_verse: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
translation_verse: Josua laam ma bwoŋi Isarele jar-keira bam maama ye o ta dedaane bembɛ selo na tɔge ded‑o ba vo ba ke jara yam to o we, “Fɔɔre-na á yi ywo, se á kwei á nɛ á daŋe pwa banto dedoa dedoa ba ne.” Ba de ma seene ba ke konto.

english_verse: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
translation_verse: Josua laam ma go pwa banu bam, ye o kwei ba yera yam o lei teeni denu yera ne. Pwa bam ma maŋe teeni dem yera ne se ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa.

english_verse: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
translation_verse: Wɛ-zoore maŋa ne, Josua ma pa ni se ba bwoli twa bam teeni dem yera ne, ye ba laam dole-ba ba de peo bɔɔne delo wone ba ya na seigi to. Ba ma jwoori ba kwei kandwa kamuna ba ma ba pe de ni. Dáane mo ya ta wora se ko yi zem maama. Josua di teene dedwonna tega-kuri seeni

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
translation_verse: Josua dedaane Isarele jar-keira bam maama zege dáane mo ba vo Libina. Ba déem ma ke jara dedaane teo kom konto tiina.

english_verse: The Lord let them capture the town and its king, and they killed the king and everyone else, just as they had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ta ma pa se ba di Libina tiina bam. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo lugi da. Josua ma toŋe dedaane Libina teo pɛ wom de o nɔɔna bam ne o na ke tei Jeriko ne to.

english_verse: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Josua dedaane o kɔgɔ kom ma zege Libina ne ba kɛ ba yi Lakisi. Ba ma gilimi teo kom ba pu, ye ba ke jara de ko.

english_verse: and the next day the Lord let them capture the town. They killed everyone, as they had done at Libnah.
translation_verse: Jara yam keim da yalei dɛ dem ne mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ ba di teo kom konto. Isarele tiina bam ma go teo kom nɔɔna maama, ne ba déem na ke tei Libina ne to.

english_verse: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa kam ne, Gezere teo Pɛ Horam de ma ba se o da o woli Lakisi tiina bam. Josua ma ti wonto de o jar-keira bam maama, nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo daare.

english_verse: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Josua laam ma ja o nɔɔna bam maama o vo Egilon. Ba ma gilimi teo kom ba pu, ye ba ke jara de-ba.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Eglon and attacked Hebron.
translation_verse: Josua de o nɔɔna bam ma zege Egilon ne ba vo se ba ke jara dedaane Heboron tiina.

english_verse: They captured the town and the nearby villages, then killed everyone, including the king. They destroyed Hebron in the same way they had destroyed Eglon.
translation_verse: Ba déem ma wane teo kom konto dedaane ko nawuura yam maama. Ba déem go ko pɛ wom de ko nɔn-bia bam maama. Ba maa wo daare nɔɔn-nɔɔno teo kom wone. Ba déem toŋe de-ba nenɛɛne ba na ke tei maama Egilon baŋa ne to mo.

english_verse: Joshua and the Israelite army turned and attacked Debir.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam daa ma pipiri ba vo ba ke jara dedaane Debiri teo.

english_verse: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
translation_verse: Ba déem ma wane teo kom de ko pɛ maama. Ba di teo kom nɔɔna maama, dedaane ko nawuura yam mo, ye ba go ko nɔɔna maama. Josua déem na toŋe tei Heboron dedaane Libina yera ne to, mo o ta ke konto Debiri teo pɛ de o nɔɔna bam yera ne.

english_verse: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
translation_verse: Josua déem ma di laŋa kam konto maama. O déem wane pwa bam de ba nɔɔna bam maama: balo na zoore zwonnu laŋa kam ne, dedaane wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne, de tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam wone, ko woli de wɛ-puli seeni peero laŋa kam ne. Josua nɔɔna bam ma yɔɔre ba chɔge ba maama, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo daare. Isarele Baŋa Wɛ wom nam ya maŋe o pa-ba ni se ba ke konto mo.

english_verse: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
translation_verse: Josua wane nɔɔna bam mo se ko zege Kadese-Baranea na wo kuri seeni to ko taa vei Gaza. O ta ma di-ba se ko zege Gosen laŋa kam ne, se ko yi Gibeon na wo baŋa seeni to.

english_verse: King Jabin of Hazor heard about Joshua's victories, so he sent messages to many nearby kings and asked them to join him in fighting Israel. He sent these messages to King Jobab of Madon, the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
translation_verse: Hazora teo pɛ Jabin déem ma ni Isarele tiina bam na di wɔnɔ laŋa kam maama baŋa ne tei to. O ma toŋe kwora o pa Pɛ Jobaba. Wonto déem ye Madon teo pɛ mo. O kwora kam ta ma yi Simiron teo pɛ, dedaane Akasaf teo pɛ wom de.

english_verse: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
translation_verse: O déem ta ma guli dedaane pwa balo maama na wo baŋa seeni peero tem laŋa ne to, de pwa balo na wo Galili kuri seeni se ko maŋe dedaane Jɔdan buga kam to, ko woli de balo na wo wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne se ko taa vei Dora na wo naneo kom ni ne to.

english_verse: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: Pɛ Jabin ta ma pa kwora yi Kanaan tiina bam. Banto zoore Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni de ka wɛ-zoore seeni maama ne mo. O ta ma toŋe kwora Amori tiina bam, de Hiti tiina bam, de Pɛrizi tiina bam, dedaane Jebusi tiina bam tei ne. Banto nam zoore zwonnu laŋa ne mo. O kwora kam ta ma yi Hivi tiina bam de. Banto déem zoore Mizipa laŋa ne mo, Heremon Peo kom teiŋa ne.

english_verse: The kings and their armies went to Merom Pond, where they set up camp, and got ready to fight Israel. It seemed as though there were more soldiers and horses and chariots than there are grains of sand on a beach.
translation_verse: Pwa bam de ba jar-keira bam laam ma la daane Merom bu-nɔgɔ kom ni ne, se ba ke jara dedaane Isarele tiina bam.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Josua o we, “Yé kɔre foone de-ba. Jwa kanto maŋa ne, ba maama wó ji twa mo á yibia ne. Abam maa wó pa se ba sisein-nɔɔna bam gwarege, se á daare á zwɛ ba sisei-torokooro tem maama.”

english_verse: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
translation_verse: Josua dedaane Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama ma pɔpɔ ba zaŋe pwa bam de ba nɔɔna bam baŋa ne. Ba ma ke jara de-ba Merom bu-nɔgɔ kom jei sem ne.

english_verse: and crippled the enemies' horses. Joshua followed the Lord's instructions, and the Lord helped Israel defeat the enemy. The Israelite army even chased enemy soldiers as far as Misrephoth-Maim to the northwest, the city of Sidon to the north, and Mizpeh Valley to the northeast. None of the enemy soldiers escaped alive. The Israelites came back after the battle and burned the enemy's chariots.
translation_verse: Josua déem ma ke kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑o ni se o ke to. O déem pɛ se ba sisein-nɔɔna bam maama ji wo-gwane mo, ye o daare o zwɛ ba sisei-torokooro tem maama.

english_verse: Up to this time, the king of Hazor had controlled the kingdoms that had joined together to attack Israel, so Joshua led his army back and captured Hazor. They killed its king
translation_verse: Josua laam ma jwoori o pipiri o vo o ke jara de Hazora teo kom. O ma wane teo kom nɔɔna de ba pɛ wom maama, ye o go-ba. Kanto maŋa ne, Hazora déem mo ye teene dem konto maama te-fɔrɔ.

english_verse: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Josua déem ma di wɔnɔ laŋa kam maama wuu baŋa ne, ko zege zwonnu laŋa kam ne, se ko taa tu tega-kuri kagoa kam seeni. Ko daa ta vei Gosen seeni, de wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem, de Jɔdan bwolo kom, ko woli dedaane peero laŋa kam maama.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he wanted the towns in this region destroyed and their people killed without mercy. That's why the Lord made the people in the towns stubborn and determined to fight Israel. The only town that signed a peace treaty with Israel was the Hivite town of Gibeon. The Israelite army captured the rest of the towns in battle.
translation_verse: Ko déem nam ye Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ se ba bochara ke dam, se ba ke jara de Isarele tiina bam. O dɛ ko baŋa ne se o pa ba yɔɔre ba na chɔgem, ye yibwona tera ko wone. Konto maama nam ke ko maŋe de Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ Moses ni tei to mo.

english_verse: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa kam ne mo Josua déem chɔge nɔn-sawaara balo na ye Anaki tiina to. Ba déem zoore Isarele de Judah zwonnu laŋa kam ne mo. Ba teene dem maa ye Heboron de Debiri de Anaba. Josua déem yɔɔre o chɔge ba maama mo dedaane ba teene dem.

english_verse: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
translation_verse: Anaki tiina bam déem daa maa wo daare Isarele tega kam baŋa ne, se ba badwonna déem za ta daare ba zoore Gaza ne, de Gafa ne, dedaane Asedodi wone.

english_verse: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Ko dɛ chwoŋa kam konto mo ye Josua jwoŋi tega kam maama, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ déem na maŋe o pa Moses ni tei to. Josua de ma pɔɔre pɔɔre tega kam o pa Isarele tiina bam, se ko tɔge dwi dedaane dwi se ba taa tei. Nɔɔna bam laam ma sii de jara-keim.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Moses ya ta na wo tege to, Isarele tiina bam maŋe ba di pwa balei balo na zoore Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to. Ba déem go-ba mo ye ba daare ba jwoŋi ba tega kam ba tei. Ba tega kam zege Aranon bwolo kom ne mo, ka laam tɔge Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni ka di baŋa seeni ka yi Heremon Peo kom.

english_verse: The first king that Moses and the Israelites defeated was an Amorite, King Sihon of Heshbon. The southern border of his kingdom ran down the middle of the Arnon River gorge, taking in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the gorge. The Jabbok River separated Sihon's kingdom from the Ammonites on the east. Then the Jabbok turned west and became his northern border, so his kingdom included the southern half of the region of Gilead.
translation_verse: Da-yiga pɛ wom ye Amori tiina pɛ Sihon, o déem na zoore Hesebon wone to mo. O paare laŋa kam zege Arowa na wo Aranon bwolo kom ni ne to mo ka yi Jaboke buga kam. Buga kam konto déem mo ye Amon tiina bam siseini. Teo kolo na wo Aranon bwolo kom tetare ne to, ko woli de Gilead tega kam chichworo tɔge te wo laŋa kam wone.

english_verse: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
translation_verse: Pɛ Sihon laŋa kam ya ta ma zege Galili naneo kom kuri seeni ka tɔge Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni, ka vo ka yi Araba naneo kom. Yɛ naneo kom mo konto. O tega kam ta ma yi Bɛte-Jesimofa, se ka laam ta tu tega-kuri seeni ka yi Pisiga peo kom teiŋa.

english_verse: Next, Moses and the Israelites defeated King Og of Bashan, who lived in the town of Ashtaroth part of each year and in Edrei the rest of the year. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: Moses de o nɔɔna bam déem ta ma di Basan teo Pɛ Oga. Wonto déem mo kweeli Refayi tiina bam jeŋa ne. O déem jege o paare dem o di Asetarof dedaane Ederi teene dem ne mo.

english_verse: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
translation_verse: Jei sento maama déem mo ye o paare dim laŋa kam: Heremon Peo kom, de Saleka, dedaane Basan laŋa kam maama na vei ka yi Gesura tiina de Maaka tiina laŋa siseini dem na wo wɛ-zoore seeni to. O déem ta ma tei Gilead chichworo kolo na wo baŋa seeni to. O paare laŋa kam déem kɛ ka yi Hesebon Pɛ Sihon laŋa siseini dem.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses dedaane Isarele tiina bam déem mo wane pwa balei bam konto. O ma kwei ba tega kam o pɔɔre pɔɔre o pa Ruben dwi dem, de Gad dwi dem, ko woli dedaane Manasɛ dwi dem chichworo, se ba taa tei.

english_verse: Later, Joshua and the Israelites defeated many kings west of the Jordan River, from Baal-Gad in Lebanon Valley in the north to Mount Halak near the country of Edom in the south. This region included the hill country and the foothills, the Jordan River valley and its western slopes, and the Southern Desert. Joshua and the Israelites took this land from the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. Joshua divided up the land among the tribes of Israel. The Israelites defeated the kings of the following towns west of the Jordan River:
translation_verse: Mɛ o na pɔɔre o pa-ba to woli de zwonnu tem laŋa kam, dedaane wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem. Ka daa maa kwei Jɔdan bwolo kom dedaane laŋa kam konto maama, se ko taa vei kagoa kam na wo tega-kuri seeni to. Nɔɔna balo déem na zoore teene dem konto maama wone to ye Hiti tiina, de Amori tiina, de Kanaan tiina, de Pɛrizi tiina, de Hivi tiina, dedaane Jebusi tiina bam mo.

english_verse: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
translation_verse: Josua déem na tiini o kwe maŋa kalo to, mo Baŋa Wɛ tage ded‑o o we: “Nmo laam kwe dedɛ, ye tega kam jei dedɛ ta wora se á vo á jwoŋi á ta‑á tei.

english_verse: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye Manasɛ dwi dem chichworo kodwoŋi kom, ko woli dedaane Ruben dwi dem, de Gad dwi dem, Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses déem maŋe o pa banto ba tega kam popɔra Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni mo.

english_verse: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
translation_verse: Ba laŋa kam yale konto mo ka yi Arowa na wo Aranon bwolo kom ni ne to, de teo kolo na wo bwolo kom tetare ne to, ko woli de te-kampare jei selo maama na zege Medeba ne se ko yi Dibon to.

english_verse: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
translation_verse: Ka ta yi teene delo maama na ye Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon nyem to. Wonto déem nam di paare Hesebon wone mo. Ka ta ma vo ka yi Amon teo siseini dem.

english_verse: Geshur and Maacah were part of this region, and so was the whole territory that King Og had ruled, that is, Gilead, Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far east as Salecah. Og had lived in Ashtaroth part of each year, and he had lived in Edrei the rest of the year. Og had been one of the last of the Rephaim, but Moses had defeated Sihon and Og and their people and had forced them to leave their land.
translation_verse: Basan teo Pɛ Oga laŋa kam maama de ye ba nyem mo. Wonto déem di o paare Asetarof dedaane Ederi ne mo. Wonto déem mo kweeli Refayi tiina bam jeŋa ne. Moses déem maa di-ba, ye o zeili-ba o daare tega kam konto.

english_verse: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem maa wo zeili Gesura tiina bam de Maaka tiina bam. Nɔɔna bam konto de déem maa tɔge ba zoore de Isarele tiina bam se ko yi zem maama.

english_verse: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
translation_verse: Moses déem na pɔɔre tega kam o pa Isarele tiina bam to, Levi dwi dem yerane mo wo tɔge ba jwoŋi tega kam popɔra. Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o pa Moses ni we, banto popɔra wó nwoŋi pɛɛra yalo Isarele tiina bam na jaane ba tui ba zwɛ Wɛ bimbini dem baŋa ne ba pa ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom to mo. Ruben dwi dem tega kam

english_verse: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Moses déem kwei tega kanto mo o pa Ruben dwi dem. O ma pa sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem se ba taa tei.

english_verse: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
translation_verse: Banto laŋa kam yale konto mo ka yi Arowa na wo Aranon bwolo kom ni ne to, de teo kolo na na wo bwolo kom tetare ne to, ko woli de te-kampare jei selo maama na bwola de Medeba to.

english_verse: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: dedaane teene delo maama na wo te-kampare jei sem ne to. Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon déem na di paare Hesebon wone ye o tei laŋa kalo maama to de maa ye Ruben dwi dem nyem. Moses déem ma di pɛ wom konto de Midian pwa bam maama mo: Evi, de Rekem, de Zura, de Hura, dedaane Reba. Banto déem mo tei tega kam ba pa Pɛ Sihon.

english_verse: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma go Beora bu Balaam wolo na ye voro to ba woli de nɔɔna babam bam.

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: Ruben dwi dem tega kam déem vei ka kweeli Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ baŋa ne mo. Ba déem kwei teene dem konto de de nawuura yam maama ba tei, diga maama de ka nyem. Gad dwi dem tega kam

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Moses déem ta ma kwei tega kadwoŋi o pa Gad dwi dem. O ma pa sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem se ba taa tei.

english_verse: It included the town of Jazer, and in the Gilead region their territory took in the land and towns as far east as the town of Aroer just west of Rabbah. This was about half of the land that had once belonged to the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Banto laŋa kam ma kwei Jazera de teene delo maama na wo Gilead laŋa kam ne, ko ta woli de Amon tiina tega kam chichworo, se ko taa vei Arowa na wo Raba wɛ-puli seeni to.

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: Ba laŋa kam zege Hesebon ne, se ka vo ka yi Ramaf-Mizipa dedaane Betonim. Ka ta zege Mahanayim ne, se ka yi Debiri laŋa kam.

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: Jɔdan bwolo kom seeni to, ba tega kam ma kwei Bɛte-Haram, de Bɛte-Nimira, de Sukofa, dedaane Zafon. Hesebon teo Pɛ Sihon laŋa kalo ya ta na daare to de maa ye ba nyem. Gad dwi dem tega kam déem vei ka kweeli Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ baŋa ne mo, ka ta tɔge buga kam wɛ-puli seeni ka yi Galili naneo kom ni.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Ba déem kwei teene dem konto de de nawuura yam maama ba tei, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. Manasɛ dwi dem chichworo tega kam

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Moses déem ta ma kwei tega kadwoŋi o pa Manasɛ sɔ-yuu kom chichworo. O ma pa diga maama de ka nyem se ba taa tei.

english_verse: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
translation_verse: Gilead laŋa kam chichworo de maa woli da, dedaane Pɛ Oga déem na di o paare dem teene delo ne to, Asetarof dedaane Ederi mo konto. Jei sem konto maama déem laam jigi Manasɛ bu Makira sɔ-yuu kom chichworo nyem mo.

english_verse: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
translation_verse: Mo ko na ke tei ye Moses déem wo Moaba bwollu tem laŋa kam ne o pɔɔre tega kalo na wo Jeriko teo de Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Se ko na daare Levi dwi tiina bam to, Moses déem wo pɔɔre tega kadwoŋi o pa banto ba nyem se ba taa tei. Kokuri to, Isarele Baŋa Wɛ wom mo maŋe o pwooli o pa-ba we, wonto wó taa ye ba jejaano paro.

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ta maa wo Giligal ne. Ba na wora to mo Judah dwi tiina toŋe nɔɔna Josua tei ne. Ba dedoa déem ye Jefunɛ bu Kaleb, o na nwoŋi Kenizi sɔ-yuu kom ne to. Kaleb ma ta de Josua o we, “Yé swei Baŋa Wɛ déem na tage debam balei taane tetei maama o bere o tontoŋeno Moses, ye dé déem ta wo Kadese-Baranea ne to.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Dento dɛ dem ne mo Moses déem tage o pwooli de amo o we, ‘Nmo na nɔne n naga Kanaan tega kalo ne konto to wó taa ye nmo nyem. Nmo de n bia mo wó taa tei-ka se ko taa vei wuu, n na tɔge Baŋa Wɛ de n wo maama to ŋwaane.’

english_verse: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Konto to, kwei zwonnu laŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ déem na pwooli se ka taa ye amo nyem to n pa-ne. Nmo wó guli we Anaki tiina bam mo wo daane. Ba teene dem ma lɔ de di vili vili. De ko de, Baŋa Wɛ na wo amo tei ne to ŋwaane, a wó wane-ba a zeili, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ na tage se a ke tei to.”

english_verse: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa ya ta na wo yi to, ba déem jege teo kom mo ba bwoi we Kiriaf-Araba, Araba déem na ye Anaki tiina bam nɔn-sawɔrɔ to ŋwaane. Tega kam laam ma sii ye jara daa tera.

english_verse: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ba tega kam tega-kuri seeni bobo Yɛ naneo kom kuri nabili seeni mo.

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: Ka ma vo ka lɛɛne Nɔŋɔ zwonnu chwoŋa kam tega-kuri seeni ka kɛ ka yi Zin kagoa kam ne. Ka ta maa vei Kadese-Baranea kuri seeni konto, ka daare ka yi Hezeron ne. Ka laam ma di Adara ne ka pipiri ka yɔɔre Karaka seeni.

english_verse: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
translation_verse: Ka ma zege dáane ka tɔge Azemon ne, ka tole taa ka yi Ejipti bu-nɔgɔ kom, ye ka laam vo ka kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ni ne mo. Judah dwi dem tega kam tega-kuri seeni siseini mo konto.

english_verse: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: ye ka laam vo ka yi Bɛte-Hogala. Ka ta ma tɔge Bɛte-Araba baŋa seeni ka kɛ ka yi Bohan Kandwɛ dem. Bohan déem ye Ruben bu mo.

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: Ka na zege dáane to, ka laam ma kwei Akore bwolo kom, ka yi Debiri ne, ka daare ka pipiri baŋa seeni ka di Giligal ne. Giligal déem yɔɔre Adumim sisworo kom na wo bwolo kom tega-kuri seeni to. Ko na zege dáane to, siseini dem laam ma kɛ de yi En-Semesa buli-yia yam ne mo, se ka yi En-Rogele.

english_verse: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Siseini dem ta tole de tɔge Ben-Hinom bwolo kom ne mo, se ko taa vei Jebusi tiina teo kom zwoŋo kom tega-kuri seeni. Jerusalem mo konto. De daa ta ma kɛ de di baŋa seeni se ko maŋe de Hinom bwolo kom wɛ-zoore dem seeni, Refayim bwolo kom baŋa seeni na kweeli mɛ to mo.

english_verse: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: Ka zege zwoŋo kom baŋa ne ka vo ka yi Nefatoa buli-yia yam ne mo, se ka yi teene delo na wo Eforon Peo kom teiŋa ne to. Ka daa ma gugwoli ka yɔɔre Baala seeni.

english_verse: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
translation_verse: Ba tega kam na kwei Baala wɛ-zoore seeni to, ka vo ka tɔge Seyira Peo kom mo, ka vo ka yi Jeerim peo sisworo kom. Ka laam ma tu ka vo Bɛte-Semesa teo kom, ka daare ka tɔge Timina seeni ka kɛ.

english_verse: It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea,
translation_verse: Siseini dem ta kɛ de vo zwoŋo kolo na wo Ekoron baŋa seeni to mo, de pipiri de yɔɔre Sikeron de daare de kɛ de gaale Baala peo kom. De ma yi Jaminia teo kom ne, ye de vo de kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ne.

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne to, o vei o ke jara mo dedaane Debiri teo kom tiina.

english_verse: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ya pɛ Josua ni mo se o fɔ Judah laŋa kam wone o pa Jefunɛ bu Kaleb. Josua de ma seene o ke konto. Ba déem kwei Heboron mo ba pa‑o. Teo kom konto ya ye Araba nyem mo. Wonto maa ye Anaki tiina nabaaro.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
translation_verse: Kaleb déem ma zeili Anaki dwia yatɔ yam na wo Heboron ne to, o daare jei sem konto. Banto déem mo ye: Sesayi, Ahiman, dedaane Talimayi.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Kaleb déem ma ta o we, “Amo wó kwei a bukɔ Akisa a pa nɔɔno wolo maama na wó wane o vo o ke jara dedaane Kiriaf-Sefera tiina bam ye o wane-ba to.”

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Kadiri dem maŋa kam ne mo, o tage de o baro wom se ba beeri tega ba jwoŋi o kwo wom tei ne. O déem ma di bonaga o vo o tu o kwo yiga ne, ye o kwo bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo nmo lage se a ke a pa‑m?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
translation_verse: Akisa ma leiri‑o o we, “A lwoori se n ke-ne zaane mo. Nmo na pɛ-ne tega kalo to ye kagoa yerane mo. Konto to, a lage mɛ na na buri to mo se n kwei n pa-ne.” Kaleb ma beeri buli-yia jei o pa‑o, baŋa seeni de tega-kuri seeni maama.

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Tega kanto mo ba déem pɛ Judah dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: de Lebaof, de Silihim, de Ayin, dedaane Rimon. De déem ye teene finlei-nogo mo de de nawuura yam maama.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: de Saarayim, de Aditayim, de Gedera, dedaane Gederotayim. De ye teene fuga-dena mo, dedaane de nawuura yam.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: de Gederofa, de Bɛte-Dagon, de Naama, de Makeda. Teene fuga-deredo mo konto, de de nawuura yam.

english_verse: The twelfth region was located in the desert along the Dead Sea, and it had the following six towns with their surrounding villages: Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, Salt Town, and En-Gedi. The Jebusites
translation_verse: de Nibisan , ko woli de En-Gedi. Dento de maa ye teene deredo, de de nawuura yam.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Jebusi tiina bam déem zoore Jerusalem ne mo. Judah tiina bam nam wo wane-ba ba zeili. Jebusi tiina bam dedaane Judah tiina bam maa zoore daane de zem maama.

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Laŋa kanto mo ba déem pɔɔre ba pa Efrayim dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem: Ba tega kam na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to zege Atarof-Adara ne mo. Ka laam ma tole konto, ka di Bɛte-Horon baŋa seeni,

english_verse: Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
translation_verse: Efrayim tiina bam déem ta jwoŋi teene dedwonna na wo Manasɛ dwi dem laŋa kam wone mo.

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Kanaan tiina déem ya zoore Gezere teo wone ye Efrayim tiina bam wo zeili-ba. Banto de Efrayim tiina bam maa zoore daane de zem maama. Efrayim tiina bam déem za fe-ba mo, se ba taa toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛra.

english_verse: The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring.
translation_verse: Manasɛ dwi dem laŋa kam ma zege Asere dwi dem siseini ne, se ko taa vei Mikimefa na wo Sɛkɛm wɛ-puli seeni to mo. Siseini dem ta zege Mikimefa ne mo de tu kuri seeni, de yi Tapua tiina na zoore mɛ to.

english_verse: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
translation_verse: Tega kalo na gilimi Tapua teo to nam ye Manasɛ dwi dem nyem mo, ye Tapua teo kom tete ye Efrayim nyem. Ko déem jei Manasɛ siseini baŋa ne mo.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Teene dedwonna déem ye Manasɛ dwi dem nyem mo, ye de wo Isakara dedaane Asere dwia yam tega baŋa ne. De maa ye: Bɛte-San, de Ibeleyam, de Dora tiina , de Endora, de Taanaka dedaane Megido, ko ta woli de dento nawuura yam de.

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: Manasɛ dwi tiina nam wo wane ba zeili balo na zoore teene dem konto ne to. Ko ma pa se Kanaan tiina bam de yɔɔre ba zoore de wone.

english_verse: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam maa na tu ba dana maŋa kalo to, ba ta wo zeili Kanaan tiina bam. Ba déem jege-ba ba pa se ba toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛra mo ba pa-ba. Josɛf dwi tiina lwoori Josua ba tega kam ŋwaane

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Ko na wora ko wora to, Josɛf dwi tiina ma vo ba lwoori Josua ba we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n pa debam tega kam pɔɔrem dedoa yerane se dé taa tei? Nii Baŋa Wɛ na tiini o ke zaane debam yuu ne pa se dé kɔgɔ kom daga tei!”

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Josua de ma leiri-ba o we, “Abam na daga konto ye á maane we Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam muri se á pɔɔre-ka á pa daane to, nam zo-na Pɛrizi tiina dedaane Refayi tiina kagoa kam wone. Dáane mo abam wó wane á de teeni ye á daare á chɛ gula se tega taa wora ka pa abam.”

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Ba daa ma leiri‑o ba we, “Zwonnu laŋa kam seene ka muri debam dedɛ. Dé ta maa bá wane dé jeeri Kanaan tiina balo na zoore bwollu tem ne to dé zeili. Banto mae luuru mo ba ma ke torokooro ba jege ba ke ba jara, ko ná ye balo na zoore Bɛte-San seeni de balo na wo Jezerele bwollu tem ne to maama de.”

english_verse: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
translation_verse: Josua ma ta de Efrayim dwi dem de Manasɛ dwi dem o we, “Abam seene á ye nɔn-kɔgɔ mo ye á jege dam. Abam nam wó wane á na tega a woli a tega kam ne.

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: Zwonnu seeni laŋa kam na ye goa to ye se á kwei á pɔɔre á pa daane mo. Véi-na dáane á zage gula á na lage tei maama to. Ko nam ná ye Kanaan tiina balo na zoore jei sem konto ne ye ba jege dam, pa ba taa jege jara-keim torokooro to maama de, á wó wane-ba á zeili á daare ba tega kam á ta‑á tei.”

english_verse: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
