translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na kwei chwoŋa se ba vo ba maŋe tega kam to, Josua ma ta-ba o we, “Véi-na á maane tega kam lanyerane se á popone ka memaŋa na ye tei to. Abam laam maa wó jwoori Siloo ywo-seeni. Amo de wó ta jɔrɔ Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne a pa abam.”

english_verse: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma seene ba ke konto. Ba nɔne tega kam ni maama mo ba ja, ye ba ta pɔɔre-ka laŋa de laŋa kuni berepɛ. Ba ma popone ba bere laŋa maama na ye tei to de ka teene. Ba na ti to, mo ba jwoori Josua de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama tei Siloo ne.

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: Josua ma ta jɔrɔ se o lɔre Baŋa Wɛ na lage se tega kam pɔɔre ka pa-ba tei to. O laam ma pɔɔre pɔɔre tega kam o pa Isarele dwia yalo na daare to maama. Benjamin dwi dem tega kam

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Ba na tage jɔrɔ to, Benjamin dwi dem mo bobo se ba na ba tega kam popɔra, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. Ba tega kam déem wo Judah dwi dem de Josɛf dwi dem tega tetare ne mo.

english_verse: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
translation_verse: Ka baŋa seeni siseini dem zege Jɔdan buga kam ne mo de di Jeriko baŋa. Ba tega kam daa ma tɔge wɛ-zoore seeni ka kwei zwonnu laŋa kam ka vo ka yi Bɛte-Aven kagoa kam.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ka ma pipiri ka kwei peo kom wɛ-zoore seeni daa kam ka duri ka vo kuri seeni, ka maa vei Kiriaf-Baal. Kiriaf-Jeerim mo konto. Ko maa ye Judah dwi tiina nyem. Benjamin wɛ-zoore seeni siseini dem mo konto.

english_verse: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye ba tega-kuri seeni siseini dem, de déem bobo Kiriaf-Jeerim ni ne mo de vo de yi Nefatoa buli-yia yam seeni.

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: Ka ta vo ka yi peo kolo na wo Refayim bwolo kom baŋa seeni ye ko tole ko nii Hinom bwolo kom teiŋa to. Siseini dem ta siseiri de tɔge bwolo kom de tu kuri de kɛ Jebusi tiina teo kom kuri seeni, de yi En-Rogele.

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Ba tega kam zege dáane ka diini baŋa seeni mo ye siseini dem gugwoli de yi En-Semesa, de Gelilofa. Jei sem konto lɛɛne Adumim sisworo kom mo. Siseini dem daa ta ma kɛ de yi Bohan Kandwɛ dem. Bohan déem ye Ruben bu mo.

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Siseini dem ma kɛ Bɛte-Araba sisworo kom baŋa seeni de tu de zo Jɔdan bwolo kom wone.

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Tega kam laam ma tole ka gaale Bɛte-Hogala baŋa seeni sisworo kom, ka vo ka kweeli Yɛ naneo kom baŋa seeni bubɛ dem ne, Jɔdan buga kam na vei ka guri mɛ to mo. Dento nam mo ye Benjamin kuri seeni siseini dem.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Jɔdan buga kam tete mo ye Benjamin tega kam wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem. Siseina yalo ba déem na pɔɔre se Benjamin dwi dem taa jege to mo konto.

english_verse: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
translation_verse: Simeon dwi dem déem mo saŋe se ba jwoŋi ba popɔra kam. Ba tega kam déem tole ka vo ka gaale Judah tega siseini dem mo.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: de Bɛte-Lebayofa, de Saruhen. Dento ye teene fuga-detɔ mo, dedaane de nawuura yam.

english_verse: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
translation_verse: Ka ta tole wɛ-puli seeni mo ka yi Gafa-Hefera dedaane Efakazina, ye ka laam pipiri ka da Nea seeni ka vo ka yi Rimon.

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Ko ta woli de Ayin, de Rimon, de Efera, de Asan. Ba teene dem konto ye dena mo de de nawuura yam maama.

english_verse: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
translation_verse: Te-balwa na gilimi teene dem konto to déem tole kuri seeni mo de yi Baalafe-Beya mo. Rama mo konto. Tega kam konto mo ba déem pɛ Simeon dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem.

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Judah popɔra kam déem daga ka dwoi ba nɔn-bia bam. Konto ŋwaane mo Simeon dwi tiina déem jwoŋi Judah tega kam kadwoŋi ba jega. Zebulun dwi dem tega kam

english_verse: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
translation_verse: Ka siseini dem baŋa seeni pipiri mo de jeeri Hanafona, se de vo de kweeli Ifitah-Eli bwolo kom ne.

english_verse: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Zebulun teene déem ye fuga-delei mo dedaane de nawuura yam maama. Ba teene dem dedwonna mo tento: Katafa, de Nahalali, de Simiron, de Idala, de Bɛtelehem.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Teene dem konto de de nawuura yam mo ba déem pɛ Zebulun dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. Isakara dwi dem tega kam

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Teene dem konto de de nawuura yam mo ba déem pɛ Isakara dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. Asere dwi dem tega kam

english_verse: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
translation_verse: Ka ta ma gugwoli ka vo wɛ-puli seeni ka yi Bɛte-Dagon se ka laam vo ka dwei Zebulun dwi dem laŋa kam ka daare ka yi Ifitah-Eli bwolo kom. Ba tega kam ta vei baŋa seeni ka yi Bɛte-Emeke, de Neyeli. Ka ma kɛ ka vo Kabuli,

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: de Eboron, de Rehobi, de Hamon, dedaane Kana, se ka kɛ ka vo ka yi Sidon teo kamunu.

english_verse: Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. Asher had a total of
translation_verse: Teene dem konto de de nawuura yam mo ba déem pɛ Asere dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. Nafitali dwi dem tega kam

english_verse: The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included
translation_verse: Teene dem konto de de nawuura yam mo ba déem pɛ Nafitali dwi dem, sɔ-yuu maama de ko nyem. Dan dwi dem tega kam

english_verse: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_verse: Ko déem na ke tei Wɛ jeerim vwei dem na wo Siloo ne konto to, ko nam ye Wɛ kaanem tu Eleaza, de Josua, de Isarele sɔ-yuni yiga tiina bam mo zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne ba pɔɔre pɔɔre tega kam ba pa daane. Ba ma pɔɔre-ka ba ti, pa se Isarele dwi maama jwoŋi ba tega.

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma kuri teene dem konto ba tiŋi ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane. Ko maa ye se nɔɔno ná wo paale o go nɔɔno, o ná ye Isarele tu naa veiru, se konto tu duri o zo de wone o seigi se wolo o na go to yera nɔɔna yé yi‑o ba go. Ko ta ye se teo kom nakwa bam wane o taane dem mo ba di de chega.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Maŋa kadwoŋi ne mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Josua o we,

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: “Laam ta de Isarele tiina bam se ba le teene dedwonna, ka-duri-ka-zo-ka-seigi ŋwaane, nenɛɛne a na maŋe a ta de Moses se o bere‑m tei to.

english_verse: If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
translation_verse: O maa ná duri o vo o yi teene dem konto dedoa, o wó vo ko manchwoŋo ni ne o lwoni o taane dem de teo kom nakwa bam mo. Banto maa wó beeri jei ba pa‑o se o zo ba teo kom o taa zoore de-ba.

english_verse: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
translation_verse: Wolo na beeri o gom to nam ná pare‑o o yi da, ko dae se teo kom tiina le‑o ba pa konto tu, kolo ŋwaane o wo paale o go nɔɔno wom. O nam ya ba chuli‑o.

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: Teo kom nakwa bam wó di o taane se ba lɔre ko ke ko maŋe mo naa o paale o go o dwoŋi wom mo. O ná wo paale o ke, ba maa wó yage se o taa zoore de-ba se ko yi kaanem yiga tu wom ná tega. Konto mo o laam wó wane o jwoori o tete teo kom.”

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: Ko ma pa se ba le Galili teo Kedesa na wo Nafitali zwonnu laŋa kam ne to ba zege ko ŋwaane. Ba ta le Sɛkɛm na wo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne to mo, de Kiriaf-Araba na wo Judah zwonnu laŋa kam ne to. Teo kom konto laam mo ye Heboron.

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ko daare teene delo na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to mo ba kuri Bezere na wo Ruben dwi dem laŋa kam ne to. Jei sem konto ye te-kampare mo ka yi kagoa kam na wo Jeriko wɛ-puli seeni to. Ba ta ma le Gad dwi dem teo Ramofa na wo Gilead ne to, dedaane Manasɛ dwi dem teo Golan na wo Basan ne to.

english_verse: While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
translation_verse: Maŋa kam kam konto ne de ba ta zoore Kanaan teo Siloo wone mo. Levi yiga tiina bam ma yi ba tei ba ta ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ nam ya maŋe o pa Moses ni mo we, debam jege se dé jwoŋi teene mo dé taa zoore da se dé daare dé taa kɔna.”

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam tete déem ma da Baŋa Wɛ ni dem ŋwaane ba le ba dwia yam dedoa dedoa teene dedwonna ba pa-ba se ba taa zoora. Ba ta ma pa-ba vara pwoli se ba taa maa kɔne vara. Kohafe sɔ-yuu tiina teene dem

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Ba ma ta jɔrɔ se ba lɔre Baŋa Wɛ na lage se teene dem pɔɔre de pa Levi dwi tiina bam tei to. Kohafe tiina bam nam mo dɛ yiga ba na ba teene dem popɔra, diga maama de ka nyem. Banto balo na ye Wɛ kaanem tu Aron diga kam to ma jwoŋi teene fuga-detɔ, ye de maama wo Judah de Simeon dedaane Benjamin dwia yam laŋa wone.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem na pɛ Moses ni se ba pɔɔre teene dem ba pa Levi tiina bam tei to mo Isarele tiina bam de kea, ko woli dedaane vara pwoli se ba taa kɔne ba vara.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Konto to, teene fuga-detɔ dedaane de vara pwoli sem mo ba déem kwei ba pa Aron diga tiina bam na ye kaanem tiina to.

english_verse: The people of the Levi tribe had a total of
translation_verse: Teo maama maa jege vara pwoli selo na kaare-ko to.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa Isarele tiina bam tega kalo maama o ya na gwoni ni de ba nabaara se o pa-ba to. Ba de ma jaŋe ba di-ka ye ba jeini ka wone.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa ba sii de jara keim, ne o na gwoni ni de ba nabaara bam se o ke tei to. Isarele tiina dona bam wolowolo wo wane-ba ba chɔge, Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ba dam se ba di-ba to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem na gwoni ni se o ke wo-laaro telo maama o pa Isarele tiina bam to mo o seene o ke o pa-ba. Dedoa tete wo maŋe kwaga ne.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Josua laam ma toŋe ni se Ruben dwi tiina bam de Gad dwi tiina bam dedaane Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom na wo wɛ-puli seeni to ba se o na-ba.

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Abam peene mo ye á sɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ nia yam, á daare á woli á chorro tem taa se ko yi leile. Á maa wo nwoŋi ba kwaga ne.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ko nam yi se á jwoori á sam dem na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni, ye Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno Moses kwei o pa abam to. Kolo ŋwaane, Baŋa Wɛ na gwoni ni se o pa á chorro tem sii de jara keim to, o seene o ke konto mo.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Nam kwaane-na se á ta‑á ke kolo maama Moses na bere se á ke to. O maŋe o bere abam se á ta‑á swoi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, ye á daare á ta‑á jege chega á pa‑o. Abam ta jege se á zuli‑o mo ye á sɛ o ni dedaane á bochara de á dam maama.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Ko na wora ko wora to mo Isarele dwia yadwonna nigi we Ruben tiina bam, de Gad tiina bam de Manasɛ dwi chichworo kodwoŋi kom mo lɔge kaanem bimbini ba zege Gelilofa ne, ko na maŋe de banto bubɛ dem na wo Jɔdan buga kam ne to.

english_verse: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama ma jeeri Siloo ne, se ba vo ba kwaare jara de ba chorro tem na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to.

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Ba ma toŋe Wɛ kaanem tu Eleaza bu Finehase se o vo o ŋɔɔne de-ba se ko laam daare se ba jeeri-ba de jara.

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: Ba ta ma le yiga tiina fuga se ba nwoŋi ba dwia fuga kam maama wone ba tɔge de Finehase ba vo ba tei. Banto maama jege sam mo ba nii de baŋa ne.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Finehase de nɔɔna fuga bam ma vo Gilead ba jeeri de Ruben tiina bam, de Gad tiina de Manasɛ dwi chichworo kodwoŋi kom, ye ba ta de-ba ba we,

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: “Baŋa Wɛ kɔ-fɔrɔ kom mo toŋe debam á tei ne se dé bwei abam dé nii kolo ŋwaane á daa na ba jege chega dedaane Baŋa Wɛ to. Bɛ mo kea ye abam lɔ Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne, ye á daare á lɔ bimbini se á ta‑á ke kaanem de baŋa ne? Abam daa ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Abam swei wɛleere delo dé déem na ke Peora ne ye Baŋa Wɛ waare debam to mo na? O pɛ se jawe-chɛɔ to dé wone ye ko go dé kɔgɔ kom dedɛ. Wɛleere dem konto nam ta wo nwoŋi dé tetare ne.

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Abam daa boŋe se á nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne mo na? Abam zem ná ve‑o, o bane jwa wó zaŋe mo dedaane Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama.

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Abam tega kam nam ná chɔge mo pa se á ware Baŋa Wɛ se á zuli‑o ka wone, se á bɛ Jɔdan buga kam á ba á ta‑á zoore debam tei ne Baŋa Wɛ vwei dem na wo mɛ to. Yé ywori-na Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne, dedaane debam maama kwaga ne, se á ke bimbini á woli debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ kaanem bimbini dem wone.

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Nam ta guli-na maŋa kam Zera bu Akane na chɔge Wɛ yiga ye o kwei wonnu telo Baŋa Wɛ na we te ye o nyem to. Ko déem dae Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama mo nɛ waarem ko ŋwaane na? Nɔɔna dedɛ mo dɛ ba te Akane wɛleere dem ŋwaane se ko déem dae o yerane mo tega.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh answered:
translation_verse: Ruben tiina bam, de Gad tiina bam, de Manasɛ dwi chichworo kom ma leiri-ba ba we:

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: “Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo dwoi maama! Wonto mo wó ta o pa debam! O yei kolo ŋwaane dé na ke bimbini dem to. Ta‑á yei-na we dé bere dé wo baare Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne. Ko nam ná dae konto, se dé yé lu zem dɛ dento.

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Dé taane dem ná ye vwa se Baŋa Wɛ waare debam. Dé wo ke bimbini dem se dé ma nwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ kwaga ne. Dé nam wo boŋe se dé kwei-de dé ma dé ke vara zwɛɛm kaanem, naa wodiu-kaanem, naa yazura kaanem se dé jwoŋi swolim Baŋa Wɛ tei ne.

english_verse: We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.” Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwei Jɔdan buga kam o ma o ji siseini mo se ka pɔɔre debam Isarele tiina bam dedaane abam Ruben tiina de Gad tiina bam daane. Abam dae Baŋa Wɛ nyem!’ Tɔ. Ko ná ke konto, abam bia wó che debam bia se ba yé tɔge ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Konto nam mo pɛ se dé ke bimbini dem. Ko dae se dé ma dé ke vara zwɛɛm kaanem de kaanem dwi maama.

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Eleaza bu Finehase ma ta de-ba o we, “Debam laam lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ seene o wo dé tei ne. Kokuri to, abam wo chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. Ko ta bere we abam wo pɛ chwoŋa se Baŋa Wɛ waare debam Isarele tiina bam.”

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Finehase de Isarele kɔ-fɔrɔ yiga tiina bam ma zaŋe Gilead ne ba jwoori ba vo Kanaan. Ba ma lwoni ba bere Isarele tiina bam maama ba dedaane Ruben de Gad tiina bam jeiŋa kam na tu tei to.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam wo ma to ye ba bobo se ba taa tei Wɛ. Ba ya boŋe se ba ke jara de Ruben de Gad tiina bam mo se ba ti ba dwi dem. Ba laam ma dole boboŋe dem konto ba yage.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Ruben de Gad tiina bam ma ta ba we, “Bimbini dento ye maana mo de pae debam maama we, Baŋa Wɛ mo seene o ye debam Tu Wɛ.” Ba maa jege-de ba bwoi we ‘Maana Bimbini’.

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Ko na wora ko wora to, Baŋa Wɛ déem laam ma pa se Isarele tiina bam dona maama daa ba daane-ba. Josua de nam ya tiini o kwe mo ka maŋa ne.

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo o bwoŋi Isarele tiina nakwa bam, de ba yiga tiina bam, dedaane dedɛɛra balo na nii ba baŋa ne to. O ma ta de-ba o we, “Amo tiini a kwe dedɛ.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Abam nam nɛ á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na dɛ abam ŋwaane o ke tei maama de teene delo ya na wo ywo to. Wonto mo jaŋe o di-de o pa abam.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Abam ná vei se á jeeri-ba de jara, Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se ba duri abam yiga ne. O ni-gwonim dem ŋwaane mo o lage o zeili-ba se abam wane ba tega kam á jwoŋi.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, ke-na dam á tete kuri ne se á daare á ke á tɔge Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom Moses na popone to chekke. Yé kuri-na yadwonna á yage.

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: Abam ba jege se á ta‑á ye de teene delo na gilimi abam to. Yé zuli-na ba jwona. Ta lɔre-na se á yé kwei ya yera á ma á ke ni-gwonim kolokolo baŋa ne.

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: Kokuri, abam na jeeri teene delo na daga ye de ta tiini de dana to, Baŋa Wɛ zeili-ba mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware se o dwoni de abam.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na jaŋe o pa abam to ŋwaane mo pa se á wone dedoa tete wó zeili á dona moro, nenɛɛne o na gwoni ni de abam we o wó ke tei to.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Nam kwaane-na á ta‑á swoi á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: nam lɔre-na se Baŋa Wɛ wom daa bá zeili-ba se abam zo. Teene dem konto maa wó jwoori de ji da-bunnu á yiga ne. De wó taa nye de fena kalo na fere ka zoore á yera to mo, ye de ta ji sabare se zɔa á yia. Ba wó yaare abam taa se ko yi maŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó saare abam yere te-ywoŋa kalo o na kwei o pa abam to baŋa ne.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: Ko daa bá dáane se amo te. Abam tete nam yei we Baŋa Wɛ seene o ke o ya na gwoni ni se o ke tei maama to, kolokolo wo maŋe kwaga ne.

english_verse: Yes, when the Lord makes a promise, he does what he has promised. But when he makes a threat, he will also do what he has threatened. The Lord is our God. He gave us this wonderful land and made an agreement with us that we would worship only him. But if you worship other gods, it will make the Lord furious. He will start getting rid of you, and soon not one of you will be left in this good land that he has given you.
translation_verse: Abam ná ve se á tɔge Baŋa Wɛ ni-sɛɛm dem, ye á bobo se á ta‑á zuli wa yadwonna, lɔre-na we o bane wó zaŋe de abam mo se o chɔge abam lela. Abam wolowolo daa ma bá daare te-ywoŋa kanto o na kwei o pa abam to baŋa ne.”

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Josua laam ma bwoŋi Isarele tiina bam maama se ba jeeri Sɛkɛm ne, banto de ba nakwa bam, de ba yiga tiina dedaane dedɛɛra balo na nii ba baŋa ne to. Ba maama ma ja ba tete ba yi Wɛ yiga.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Josua ma ta de nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Isarele Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora mo tento: Boboa kam ne abam kwoa nabaara bam ya ta wo Yuferata buga kam bubɛ dedwoŋi dem ne mo. Ba dwi dem maama déem maa zuli jwona. Abaraham de Nahora kwo Tera de déem tɔge ba zuli-ya mo.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: Amo déem ma kuri abam nabaaro Abaraham. Amo ma pa se o nwoŋi da tega kalo na kɛ ka bɛ Yuferata buga kam to, ye a tiini a pa‑o dwi na daga. Da-yiga to a déem kwei Izaak mo a pa‑o.

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ko na yi se Izaak lo bia to, a ma kwei Jakob de Esawu a pa‑o. Amo ma pa Esawu tei Seyira zwonnu laŋa kam, ye a kuri se Jakob de o bia bam tu ba vo Ejipti teo ba zoore da.

english_verse: Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Amo na jaane á nabaara bam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne to, ba ma yi Nane-soŋo kom ni. Ejipti tiina bam déem ya kwei sisein-nɔɔna de se torokooro mo ba ma pare á nabaara bam ba vo ba yi Nane-soŋo kom ni ne.

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: Ba déem ma keeri ba jare-ne se a woli-ba. Amo Baŋa Wɛ ma tiŋi lim banto de Ejipti tiina bam tetare ne ye a ta pa se naneo kom di Ejipti tiina bam. Ba yibia ne mo a ke konto Ejipti tiina bam baŋa ne. Ko kwaga ne, á nabaara bam laam ma zo kagoa ne ba daane ka wone.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: Amo ma ja abam teo nɔɔna bam a yi Amori tiina bam tega kam. Banto déem zoore Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni mo. Nɔɔna bam konto na nwoŋi se ba ke jara de abam to, a ma pa se á di-ba. Abam ma yɔɔre á chɔge-ba, ye á jwoŋi ba tega á laam tei.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Moaba teo pɛ Balaki na ye Zipore bu to déem ma boŋe se o ke jara de abam. O déem ma beeri Beora bu Balaam jei, se o ba o sɔɔle lwarem o yage abam yuu ne.

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: Amo ma jwoŋi abam a yage Balaki jeŋa ne de a na ve se a cheigi Balaam taane dem to. A ma pa se o jwoori o sɔɔle swolim dedɛ o pa abam.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: Abam déem na bɛ Jɔdan buga kam á vo á yi Jeriko to, ba teo kom tiina nwoŋi mo se ba ke jara de abam. Amori tiina bam, de Pɛrizi tiina, de Kanaan tiina, de Hiti tiina, de Giragasi tiina, de Hivi tiina, dedaane Jebusi tiina de ta jeeri abam mo de jara ye amo pa se abam di ba maama.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Abam déem na gwɛ tega kam ne á ma‑á vei to, amo ma vugimi á dona boboŋa ye ba duri ba daare abam. Ko dae á se-zɔɔro de á tɛ mo á kwei á ma á zeili-ba. Ko nye de amo ya na ke Amori tiina pwa balei bam tei to mo.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: Abam wo yaare tega kanto ŋwaane, amo mo kwei-ka a pa abam. Abam laam zoore teene delo á na wo lɔge to wone mo, á nam wo de kare ye á jege-se á di. Abam ta jege teeni-bia á di ye á wo jeiri-de.”

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: Josua laam ma ta de-ba o we, “Ko nam ye se abam ta‑á zuli Baŋa Wɛ de á chega maama mo. Dole-na jwona yalo á kwoa bam déem na jege ba zuli Yuferata buga bubɛ dedwoŋi dem ne to, de yalo ba déem na jege ba zuli Ejipti ne to á yage, se á zuli Baŋa Wɛ yerane.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Abam wo nam ná wo dɛ se á ta‑á zuli Baŋa Wɛ, se á kuri wɛ delo á na wó zuli to. Abam wó zuli wa yalo á kwoa bam déem na jege ba zuli Yuferata buga bubɛ dedwoŋi dem ne to mo, naa á laam na zoore Amori tiina tega ne to, á wó zuli ba jwona yam mo? Ko nam ta wo á tei ne. Se ko ná ye amo de a diga tiina maama, debam wó taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ mo.”

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam maama ma leiri‑o ba we, “Debam bá yage Baŋa Wɛ wom se dé daare dé zuli wa yadwonna.

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ mo ye debam Wɛ. Debam dedaane dé kwoa ya ye kabɛ mo Ejipti wone, ye dé yi na o na toŋe wo-kenkagela se o ma o vere debam o ja o nwoŋi Ejipti ne tei to. Dwi-gɛ tiina déem seene ba gilimi debam jei maama ne. De ko de, dé ná vei mɛ maama, Baŋa Wɛ yeini o kwoli debam mo.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Debam déem na gwɛ tega kam ne dé maa beene to, mo Baŋa Wɛ zeili Amori tiina bam dedaane teene dedɛ, se debam na pwola dé zo tega kanto wone. Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo ye debam Wɛ, ye debam de wó taa zuli wonto mo.”

english_verse: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
translation_verse: Josua daa ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Baŋa Wɛ ye wose mo. Abam bá wane‑o á zuli. O yi nam page abam baŋa ne mo. Abam maa ná lɔge o kwaga ne naa á ná ke wɛleera, o bá kwei o chɛ abam.

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: Abam ná yage‑o se á daare á zuli wa-yɔɔro, wonto de wó pipiri o yage abam mo. O maa na boŋe se o ke abam lanyerane to, o laam wó waare abam mo, ye o daare o chɔge abam.”

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: De konto maama de, nɔɔna bam ta leiri Josua ba we, “Debam boboŋa tiini ya ja se dé taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ mo.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Josua laam ma ta-ba o we, “Abam tete mo pɛ maana we á kuri se á ta‑á zuli Baŋa Wɛ mo.” Ba maama ma leiri we, “Ɛɛ! Debam tete mo pɛ maana.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Josua ma ta o we, “Ko nam ná ye konto, chɔge-na wa-gɛ sem ta na wo á tetare ne to, se á daare á kwei á bochare maama á pa Isarele Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam de ma ta we, “Debam wó zuli dé Baŋa Wɛ wom mo, se dé daare dé sɛ wonto yerane ni.”

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne mo Josua zege Sɛkɛm ne o woli Isarele tiina bam se ba ke ni-sɛɛm de Baŋa Wɛ. O ta ma pa-ba nia se ba taa tɔga.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: O déem ta popone wonnu tem konto maama o ke Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom wone mo. O ma daare o kwei kandwɛ-kamunu o chwi tei-zɔŋɔ kom kuri ne se ko maŋe dedaane Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem.

english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: Josua ma ta nɔɔna bam o we, “Kandwɛ dento nigi Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei maama de debam to. Ko bere we de ye maana mo dé maama tei ne, se abam yé lɔ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem kwaga ne.” Ba suli Josua te-ywoŋa kam ne

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Josua déem ma pa se nɔɔna bam maama jage se ba vo ba jeini mɛ ba na pɔɔre tega kam ba pa-ba to ne.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Josua nam ya jege o tete tega Timinaf-Sera ne. Ka wo Gaasa Peo kom baŋa seeni mo, Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli ka wone.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Josua ŋwea maŋa kam maama ne, Isarele tiina bam yɔɔre ba sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni mo chekke. Ba nakwa badaara de déem nɛ kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na ke o pa Isarele tiina bam to. Banto ta na ŋwe to, ba kɔ-fɔrɔ kom ta zuli Baŋa Wɛ mo, ye ba wo ywori o ni dem kwaga ne.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ya zeŋe Josɛf kwi sem mo ba ja ba nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba yi dáane. Ba ma suli-se Sɛkɛm ne, tega kalo Jakob déem na yeigi Hamora bia bam tei ne to. Hamora nam ya ye Sɛkɛm kwo mo. Jakob déem ma ŋwe sabu-dala bi ba tega kam ŋwaane. Josɛf dwi dem laam ma jwoŋi tega kam konto ba tei.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Aron bu Eleaza de déem ma te. Ba ma suli‑o Gibea ne, teo kolo ba na pɔɔre ba pa o bu Finehase Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne to.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Josua toone dem kwaga ne, Isarele tiina bam ma bwei se ba lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa ye ba we, “Isarele dwia yam wone dwi dɔ mo wó lwoori yiga se ba kwaare jara de Kanaan tiina bam?”

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Judah tiina bam ma vo Simeon tiina bam tei, ba na ye chorro to ŋwaane, ye ba ta we, “Kanaan tiina mo zoore tega kalo Baŋa Wɛ na kwei o pa debam to baŋa ne. Nam ba-na á zeini debam se dé di-ba, se á de ná lage á ke jara á tega kam ŋwaane se debam de woli abam.”

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Ba ma pa se jara yam yi Kanaan tiina balo na wo Heboron teo wone to. Boboa kam ne, jei sem konto yere déem ye Kiriaf-Araba mo. Dáane mo ba di Sesayi, de Ahiman dedaane Talimayi de ba dwi dem maama.

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: ye Adoni-Bezeki kwaane se o duri o lu ba jeŋa ne, ye o wo wane. Ba na jaane‑o to, mo ba gwoni o nu-kweero tem dedaane o namimbi-kweero tem ba yage.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Judah tiina bam ma jeeri Jerusalem teo kom de jara. Ba ma di-ko, ye ba go ko nɔn-bia bam ba daare ba zwɛ-ko.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: Kanaan tiina badwonna nam ya zoore zwonnu laŋa kam ne mo, de tega-kuri kagoa kam seeni, dedaane wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne. Judah tiina bam déem ta ma zege Jerusalem ne ba vo ba kwaare jara de ba maama.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Judah tiina bam daa ma zege dáane ba vo se ba jeeri Debiri tiina de jara. Boboa ne to, teo kom konto yere déem mo ye Kiriaf-Sefera.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Kadiri dem maŋa kam ne mo, Akisa tage de o baro wom se ba beeri tega ba jwoŋi o kwo wom tei ne. O déem ma di bonaga o vo o tu o kwo yiga ne, ye o kwo bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo nmo lage se a ke a pa‑m?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: Akisa ma leiri‑o o we, “A lwoori se n ke-ne zaane mo. Nmo na pɛ-ne tega kalo to ye kagoa yerane mo. Konto to, a lage se n beeri buli-yia jei mo n pa-ne.” Kaleb ma beeri buli-yia jei o pa‑o, baŋa seeni de tega-kuri seeni maama.

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Moses tembaaro dwi dem mo ye Keni tiina bam. Ba ma zege Jeriko ne ba woli dedaane Judah tiina bam ye ba vo Judah kagoa kam kuri seeni. Ba maa zoore Arada ne dedaane jei sem konto nɔɔna bam.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem mo woli Judah tiina bam ye ba di teene delo maama na wo zwonnu laŋa kam ne to. Se ko ná ye Kanaan tiina balo na zoore bwollu tem seeni to, ba déem wo wane banto ba di, nɔn-dwoa bam konto na mae luuru mo ba ke jara-keim torokooro to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Moses na pɛ ni se ba ke tei to mo ba de kea. Ba kwei Heboron mo ba pa Kaleb. Wonto de déem ya zeili Anaki bia batɔ bam mo o daare jei sem konto o jwoŋi o tei.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Benjamin dwi tiina bam déem wo wane se ba zeili Jebusi tiina bam. Nɔn-dwoa bam konto zoore Jerusalem ne mo, ye de zem maama, Jebusi tiina bam gwaane de Benjamin tiina bam mo ba zoore teo kom konto ne.

english_verse: The Ephraim and Manasseh tribes were getting ready to attack Bethel, which at that time was called Luz. And the Lord helped them when they sent spies to find out as much as they could about Bethel.
translation_verse: Josɛf dwi tiina bam de ma vo ba jeeri Bɛtel de jara. Boboa ne to teo kom yere ye Luzi mo. Baŋa Wɛ déem ma woli-ba. Ba ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba ŋɔ ba nii teo kom na ye tei to.

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Balo na vei se ba ŋɔ ba nii to ma na nɔɔno na zege teo kom wone o maa nwoŋa. Ba déem ma ta‑o ba we, “Nmo ná bere debam chwoŋa se dé wane dé zo abam teo kom wone, dé bá ke‑m kolokolo dé chɔge.”

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma seene o bere-ba chwoŋa kam, ye ba de vo ba zo teo kom wone ba go ko nɔn-bia maama ye ba yage nɔɔno wom de o diga tiina se ba taa ŋwe.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom laam ma vo o zoore Hiti tiina bam laŋa ne. O déem lɔge teo mo ye o bwoŋi-ko yere we Luzi. Teo kom ta jege yere dem konto de zem maama.

english_verse: Canaanites lived in the towns of Beth-Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and all the villages nearby. The Canaanites were determined to stay, and the Manasseh tribe never did get rid of them. But later on, when the Israelites grew more powerful, they made slaves of the Canaanites.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam maa na tu ba dana maŋa kalo to, ba fe Kanaan tiina bam se ba taa toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛra mo ba pa-ba. Ba nam ya wo zeili ba maama ba ti.

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Kanaan tiina badwonna de déem zoore Gezere ne, ye Efrayim dwi dem wo zeili-ba. Kanaan tiina bam déem ma lɛɛre ba zoore de-ba.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Zebulun tiina bam de maa wo zeili Kanaan tiina balo na zoore Kitiron ne dedaane Nahalali ne to. Ba yage-ba mo pa ba tɔge ba zoore de-ba ye ba laam fe-ba se ba taa toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛra ba pa-ba.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Nafitali dwi tiina de maa wo zeili balo na zoore Bɛte-Semesa de Bɛte-Anafa ne to. Ko ma pa se Nafitali tiina bam dedaane tega kam konto nɔɔna bam lɛɛre ba zoore daane. Nafitali tiina bam déem za fe teene dem konto tiina bam mo se ba taa toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛra ba pa-ba.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amori tiina bam dam déem dwoi Dan dwi dem dam. Ba ma che-ba ba yage zwonnu laŋa kam ne pa se ba daa wo wane se ba tu ba ba bwollu tem seeni.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Amori tiina bam déem ma yɔɔre ba maŋe Ayijalon ne, de Saalibim ne, dedaane Heresi Peo kom seeni ba zoora. Ko daare maŋa kalo Josɛf dwi dem na tu ba na dam to, mo ba fe Amori tiina se ba taa toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛra ba pa-ba.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Amori tiina bam tega kam siseini déem zege zwonnu chwoŋa kalo ba na bwoi we ‘Nɔŋɔ chwoŋa’ to mo, ka vo ka tɔge Sela seeni ka kɛ yiga.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Maŋa dedoa mo Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam zege Giligal ne ka jeeri Bokim ne. Ka déem ma kwei Wɛ kwora kanto ka pa Isarele tiina bam: “Amo mo jaane abam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne a ba ywo-seeni, pa se á zo tega kalo a na gwoni ni dedaane á nabaara bam se a pa-ba to, ye a we, ‘A bere a bá nwoŋi ni-sɛɛm delo a na ke de abam to kwaga ne.

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: Ko nam dae se abam dedaane tega kam konto nɔɔna ke ni-sɛɛm daane. Abam jege se á ja ba jwona kaanem bimbina yam á chɔge á yage mo.’ Abam nam ve ni dem konto a na pɛ abam to. Bɛŋwaane mo ye á ke konto?

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Ba ma bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we Bokim. Ba déem ma ke kaanem dáane ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Josua toone

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Ba déem ma kwei‑o ba suli o tete tega kam ba na pɔɔre ba pa‑o to ne. Ka wo Timinaf-Heresa ne mo, Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne. Ka déem maŋe dedaane Gaasa Peo kom baŋa seeni mo.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Banto dwi dem maama ma te ba ti. Dwi dedwoŋi déem daa ma zaŋe Isarele wone. Banto yeiri Baŋa Wɛ wom ye ba wo lɔre kolo de kolo maama o na ke o pa Isarele dwi tiina bam to.

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ná yeini ba nwoŋi se ba ke jara, Baŋa Wɛ wó che-ba mo, nenɛɛne o na maŋe o lwoori yiga o kaane-ba we, o wó ke tei to. Isarele tiina bam maa tiini ba wo cham wone.

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne Baŋa Wɛ déem ta yeini o le jwoŋina mo o pa-ba. Jwoŋina bam laam mo daa yeini ba jwoŋi-ba ba yage venverena bam jeŋa ne.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Konto maama wó ke, ye Isarele tiina bam ta lage jwona mo se ba taa kaana. Ba ba nege ba jwoŋina balo na tei-ba to. Ba maa yage chwei selo ba kwoa déem na tɔge to. Ba maa yeini ba yage Wɛ chwoŋa lela ye ba daa ba sɛ Baŋa Wɛ nia yam.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam dona ná yeini ba pa se ko zo ba yera, Baŋa Wɛ déem yeini o ŋwane o pa-ba mo ye o toŋe jwoŋinu ba ŋwaane. Wɛ ma yeini o woli kotu pa se o jwoŋi-ba ba dona jeŋa ne o yage. Jwoŋinu wom ná wo tege, ko yeini ko zura mo ko pa Isarele tiina bam.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Ko daare, jwoŋinu wom ná yɔɔre o te, ba daa yeini ba ywori mo ba to ba chwo-dwoi sem wone. Ba daa yeini ba ke lwarem mo ba dwoni ba kwoa bam kikia yam. Ba maa yeini ba jwoori ba zo jwo-kaanem wone, ye ba pa se ba wo dana de lwarem keim.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ bane laam ma tiini de zaŋe de Isarele tiina bam ye o we: “Nɔɔna banto yɔɔre ba chɔge ni-sɛɛm delo amo dedaane ba nabaara na ke daane to mo. Ba ta ma ve se ba sɛ amo ni dem.

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane amo daa bá zeili teene delo Josua na tege o daare ye ba wo di-de to.

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Amo wó yage se teene dem konto taa wora mo se a taa ma a faŋe Isarele tiina bam a nia, ba wó sɛ ba tɔge Baŋa Wɛ nenɛɛne ba kwoa bam na tɔge tei to, naa ba bá tɔge.”

english_verse: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem lage se Isarele tiina bam maama mo me dedaane jara-keim, se ba kwaga kam na yeiri jara-keim to de taa yei ya laŋa.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Balo na daare tega kam ne to maa ye: Filisi tiina de ba pwa banu bam, de Kanaan tiina bam maama, ko ta woli de Sidon tiina bam dedaane Hivi tiina balo na zoore Lebanon peero tem seeni, ko na zege Baal-Heremon Peo kom ne se ko yi Lebo-Hamafa seeni to.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Teene dem konto ta daare se Baŋa Wɛ tɔge de baŋa ne o faŋe Isarele tiina bam o nii, ba wó tɔge o nia yam nenɛɛne Moses na maŋe o bere ba nabaara bam se ba taa ke tei to, naa ba bá tɔge.

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: Ba na gwaane daane konto to, Isarele tiina bam déem ma sɛ se ba de teene dem konto tiina di da-bukwa. Ko déem dɛ chwoŋa kam konto mo ye ba bobo se ba taa kaane teene dem jwona yam. Ofineli yera taane

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem tiini ba toŋe lwarem ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. Ba swei ba Baŋa Wɛ wom swia, ye ba daare ba zuli Baal dedaane Asera jwona yam.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ bane déem ma tiini de zaŋe dedaane-ba. O ma pa pwola pa se Mesopotamia teo Pɛ Kusan Risatayim di-ba. Isarele tiina bam déem ma toŋe ba pa‑o bena nana.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Ba ma kaase ba jare Baŋa Wɛ, pa se o le jwoŋinu o pa-ba. Ko nam ye Kenazi bu Ofineli mo. Kenazi de déem maa ye Kaleb nyaane. O ma seene o jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage.

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem daa ma tiini ba toŋe lwarem ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. O ma pa pwola pa se Moaba teo Pɛ Egolon di-ba.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Egolon ma sɔ ni dedaane Amon tiina bam de Amaleki tiina bam, ye ba vo ba kwaare jara de Isarele tiina bam. O déem ma vere Jeriko teo kom o tei.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: O na pɛ pɛ wom o pɛɛra yam o ti to, mo o toŋe nɔɔna balo na dɛ ded‑o ba zeŋe-ya to se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and the Lord chose Ehud from the Benjamin tribe to rescue them. They put Ehud in charge of taking the taxes to King Eglon, but before Ehud went, he made a double-edged dagger. Ehud was left-handed, so he strapped the dagger to his right thigh, where it was hidden under his robes.
translation_verse: Ehuda déem ma pa ba ke se-zɔɔ na jege nia yalei ba pa‑o. Ko dedɔrem maŋe dedaane jatwogo maŋem mo. O ma kuni-ko o yage o jazem chwei seeni, ye o daare o ma o gwaaro tem o kwoli-ko.

english_verse: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom déem nam ya jei o yerane mo di-balaŋa na wo o sɔŋɔ kom nayuu ne to, ko na zura to ŋwaane. Ehuda ma yi o yera ye o ta o we, “Wɛ mo pɛ-ne kwora se a ta a bere‑m.” Pɛ wom ma zaŋe o zege wɛɛne.

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Ehuda ma kwei o jagwia kam o le se-zɔɔ kom na wo o jazem chwei ne to. O laam ma moore ko maama Egolon puga ne.

english_verse: that even the handle was buried in his fat. Ehud left the dagger there. Then after closing and locking the doors to the room, he climbed through a window onto the porch
translation_verse: O ma pe nayuu diga kam ni o yage‑o da, ye o daare o nwoŋi o maa kɛa.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: O déem na kɛ o daare to, Pɛ wom tontoŋena ma di nayuu kom ye ba na we diga kam nia pe mo. Ba déem ma boŋe we o ga wora o zege nɛ mo ka wone.

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Ba na cheigi taa ko ba ko kɛ maŋa ye o ta wo pore diga kam to, mo ba beeri bwor-bu ba ma pore. Ba ma na we ba tu wom tege mo o tigi tega ne.

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Ba déem na cheigi taa se Pɛ wom pore to, dedaane Ehuda maŋe o duri o lu o gaale ba na sare kandwa yam mɛ to, o kɛ o yi Seyira teo kom.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: O ma pa-ba ni we, “Ta‑á tɔge-na amo. Kokuri, Baŋa Wɛ mo kwei á dona Moaba tiina bam o ke á jeŋa ne, se á di-ba.” Nɔɔna bam maama ma tɔge Ehuda kwaga. Ba ma vo ba yi jei selo Moaba tiina na yeini ba tɔge-da ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam to. Ba ma cheiŋi chwoŋa kam se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé tɔge-da o kɛ.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma di Moaba tiina bam pa se ba toŋe ba pa-ba. Ba déem ma sii de jara se ko yi bena funɔnɔ. Samgare yera taane

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Jwoŋinu wolo déem na saŋe o jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage to mo ye Samgare. O déem ye Anafa bu mo. O ma kwei zaangwoli o ma go Filisi tiina bia yaredo.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ehuda toone kwaga ne, mo Isarele tiina bam daa tiini ba toŋe lwarem ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Sisera ta ma ta‑o o we, “Ta‑n zege vwei dem ni ne n nia, se nɔɔno wolo ná tu o bwei we, nɔɔno wo ywo-seeni na, se n ta we, ‘Aawo’ ”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Wɛ sampwora kadwoŋi déem wora o yere mo Debora. O maa ye Lapidofa kaane. Wonto mo nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne da yam konto ne.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: O déem yeini o jei konkwara kadwoŋi kuri ne mo. Isarele tiina bam maama maa yeini ba tui o tei se o nii ba taane baŋa ne o pa-ba. Jei sem déem wo Efrayim zwonnu tem laŋa ne mo, ko maŋe de Rama de Bɛtel tetare ne.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo o déem toŋe o bwoŋi Abinowam bu Baraki. Wonto nwoŋi Kedesa ne mo, Nafitali dwi dem wone. O ma ta‑o o we, “Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom pɛ nmo ni dento mo: ‘Véi n kuri nɔɔna morro fuga se ba nwoŋi Nafitali dedaane Zebulun dwia yam wone. Nmo laam ma‑n wó da ba yiga se á vo á jeeri Tabora Peo kom ne.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Amo wó soge Jabin jar-keira bam yiga tu Sisera se o nwoŋi o vo o yi Kison buga kam o jeeri abam de jara. O wó taa jege o jara-keim torokooro tem dedaane o jar-keira bam maama. Amo nam wó ke-ba n jeŋa ne pa se n di-ba.’ ”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: O ma leiri Baraki o we, “Amo wó tɔge‑m se dé vo. Nmo nam na jaane boboŋe delo to, n bá‑n na yere de ŋwaane, kokuri Baŋa Wɛ lage o kwei Sisera o ke kaane jeŋa ne mo se o go‑o.” Debora déem ma zaŋe o tɔge Baraki ye ba vo Kedesa.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Keni tu dedoa déem wora o yere mo Hebera. Wonto déem pwɛ o tete mo Keni tiina badwonna bam wone. Banto ye Hobabi dwi dem mo. Hobabi maa ye Moses dɔ. Hebera ya vei o chwi o vwei se ko maŋe dedaane tei-zɔŋɔ kom na wo Zaananim ne to. Ko déem bwola de Kedesa mo.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Sisera déem ma ni we Abinowam bu Baraki vei Tabora Peo kom ne.

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Debora déem laam ma ta Baraki o we, “Zaŋe se dé kɛ! Baŋa Wɛ zem kwei Sisera mo o ke n jeŋa ne. Nam véi n jeeri‑o de jara, se Baŋa Wɛ mo lage o da n yiga.” Baraki déem ma seene o ja o nɔɔna morro fuga pa se ba zege Tabora Peo kom yuu ne ba tu tega.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Baraki na nwoŋi se o jeeri-ba to, mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se vuvuga to Sisera de o jar-keira bam tetare ne, dedaane ba torokooro tem maama. Sisera déem ma zege o toroko kom wone o faŋe o chu tega ne, ye o laam duri se o lu.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Baraki ma pare ba jar-keira bam dedaane ba torokooro tem taa se ko vo ko yi Harosɛf-Hagoyim. O de o nɔɔna bam ma go Sisera jar-keira bam maama. Dedoa tete déem wo daare.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Sisera déem ma duri de o napera o vo se o zo Keni tu Hebera kaane Jayeli vwei wone. O vei da kolo ŋwaane, Jabin de Hebera diga kam ni ywona daane mo.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Jayeli déem ma nwoŋi se o jeeri Sisera, ye o ta‑o o we, “Amo tu, duri n ba n zo amo vwei dem ne. Yé ta‑n kɔre foone.” O déem ma duri o zo da, ye kaane wom de seigi‑o, o daare o kwei gwaaro o ma o kwoli‑o.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Sisera ma ta de Jayeli o we, “Ja! Pa-ne na fee se a nyɔ, kokuri, na-nyɔm mo lage de go-ne.” O déem ma kwei loa de ka wo nayela o pa‑o se o nyɔ, ye o jwoori o kwoli‑o.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Baraki déem ma pare Sisera o yi vwei dem. Jayeli na nɛ‑o to, o ma jeeri‑o, ye o ta o we, “Ba n nii nɔɔno wolo n na kare n beeri to.” Baraki ma zo de Sisera tigi da, ye paare dem tɔge o zwa-kwaale ne de ja tega.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se Kanaan teo Pɛ Jabin daa ba jege dam Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma tiini ba na dam, ye ba jege Jabin ba fe taa, se ko yi maŋa kalo ba na chɔge‑o ba ti to.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne mo Debora dedaane Abinowam bu-baaro Baraki déem leeni leiŋa kanto we:

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Abam pwa de dedɛɛra maama, cheigi-na, se a leeni leiŋa a tei Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom. Amo wó leeni a zuli Baŋa Wɛ mo!

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: Peero tem de dɔne mo Sinayi Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Te ma ziziŋi Isarele Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo Anafa bu Samgare na nii tega kam baŋa ne to ko woli dedaane Jayeli maŋa ne, chwo-veila déem daa ba tɔge pempala ba via, se ba tɔge chwo-balɛ yerane mo.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna déem daa ba zoore Isarele teene nawuura yam ne ya, se ko taa nii maŋa kalo Debora na nwoŋi se o nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne, ye o ye ba maama nu to.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem na kuri se ba taa zuli wa-gɛ to, jara mo to ba teene dem ne. Ba jar-keira morro finna bam wone, wɔ déem mo zei jara nantana naa chichwei?

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: A wo mo dɛ Isarele bembɛ sem de nɔɔna balo na sɛ ba tɔge ba ke jara to kikia yam. Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de tia mo!

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: Cheigi-na á nii, abam balo na dɔge bonɛ-pwonnu baŋa ne ye á jei pwal-laaro baŋa ne to, ko woli de abam balo na vei tega ne to.

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Cheigi-na se á wó ni lei-mɔra na leeni ba ke sɔɔ tei to. Ba kare ba tɛ Baŋa Wɛ na ke wo-kamunnu telo to. Ba ta maa tɛ Isarele tiina bam na di ba dona tei to. Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam ma zaŋe ba teene dem wone se ba jeeri manchwo-peena yam ne.

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Balo na daare ye ba jege chega to ma vo ba dedɛɛra bam tei. Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam ma da o ŋwaane ba woli-ne se dé ke jara.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Isakara bembɛ sem ma tɔge Debora kwaga. Chega to, Isakara nɔɔna bam de ma tɔge Baraki kwaga ba yɔɔre ba tu bwolo kom ne mo se ba kwaare jara yam. Ko nam ná ye Ruben dwi dem tiina, banto ya ta jei boboŋa wone mo.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Bɛŋwaane mo á maŋe kwaga ne ye á yere pei sem? Á boŋe se á cheigi nayera na jege wi ba wui tei to mo na? Chega ŋwaane to, Ruben dwi dem ya ta jei boboŋa wone mo.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gilead tiina bam de ma maŋe Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni. Dan dwi tiina de ma maŋe kwaga ne de ba nabwooru tem. Asere dwi dem déem ma maŋe naneo kom ni ne. Banto wo nwoŋi ba teene dem ne.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Ko daare Zebulun tiina bam dedaane Nafitali tiina bam déem sɛ se ba ga ba ŋwea jara wone mo.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: Kanaan teene pwa bam nwoŋi se ba ke jara. Ba ma kwaare jara Taanaka ne, se ko maŋe dedaane Megido bwi sem. Ba nam gɛ lu-nyenno wonnu se ba ja ba viiri.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kison na-ŋone sem ma chwooli-ba se ja viiri; Kison bu-tola kam na wora taa wuu to mo konto. Amo wó da konto ŋwaane a vo yiga mo de dam.

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Sisein-nɔɔna bam wurigi mo se maa kɛa. Se napɔɔna yam maa guri tega.

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Jayeli mo tiini o jege yu-ywoŋo kaana maama wone! O maa ye Keni tu Hebera kaane ye o jege yu-ywoŋo o dwoi kaana balo maama na zoore vwoa wone to.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Sisera déem lwoori na mo se o nyɔ. Jayeli ma kwei nayela o pa‑o. O déem ma beeri veira zoŋa, o ke nayel-pepala da o pa‑o.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: O déem zei vwei paare mo o jagwia ne, ye o jazem dem jege bagwori. O ma pa paare dem o lɔ Sisera yuu kom o chochoge. Paare dem ma tɔge o zwa-kwaale ne de nwoŋi de ja tega.

english_verse: Sisera sank to his knees and fell dead at her feet.
translation_verse: Sisera sesare mo o to tega ne o tiga. O maŋe Jayeli nɛ seeni mo o te o tiga yiri-titi.

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ, sɛ se nmo dona maama te toone dem konto dwoŋi. Ko daare balo na swoi nmo to, pa se ba taa nyeena de dam ne wea na nye de dam ka pulim maŋa ne tei to. Isarele tiina bam déem ma sii de jara se ko yi bena finna.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem daa ma toŋe lwarem ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. O ma kwei-ba o ke Midian tiina jeŋa ne, ye ba pa se ko zo Isarele tiina bam yera bena yarepɛ.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ná yeini ba du ba wo-dwa, Midian tiina bam wó tɔge de Amaleki tiina dedaane dwia yalo maama na zoore wɛ-puli seeni to mo ba ba ba jeeri-ba de jara.

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Midian tiina bam yeini ba ja ba vara mo ba ba ye ba daare ba chwi ba vwoa dáane. Banto de ba kona yam ni déem ware ko ga ko ti. Ba maa wó yeini ba meeli tega kam maama nenɛɛne kayere tei to, ye ba deilimi-ka nywa!

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem na dɛ Midian tiina bam kikia ŋwaane ba keeri ba jare Baŋa Wɛ konto to,

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a prophet to them with this message: I am the Lord God of Israel, so listen to what I say. You were slaves in Egypt, but I set you free and led you out of Egypt into this land. And when nations here made life miserable for you, I rescued you and helped you get rid of them and take their land.
translation_verse: A ma jwoŋi abam Ejipti tiina bam jeŋa ne a yage. A ta ma jwoŋi abam a yage nɔn-dwoa balo maama na bɛɛse abam to jeŋa ne. Amo ma zeili á dona bam pa se ba nwoŋi ba daare ba tega kam ye abam laam tei.

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: A ma ta de abam we, ‘Amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Konto to, á ba jege se á zuli jwona yalo Amori tiina bam na zula ye á laam wo ba tega kam ne to.’ Abam nam wo sɛ amo kwora kam.”

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
