translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ma vo ka jei tei-zɔŋɔ kom na wo Ofera ne to kuri ne. Ko ye Abizeri tu Joasa nyem mo. O bu Gideon maa zege da o fere banina peo gwoŋo wone. Ba déem yeini ba nɔne Vini tio-bia mo gwoŋo kom konto wone. Gideon déem nam ke konto se o seigi mena yam Midian tiina bam yiga ne mo.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam déem ma yi Gideon tei ne ka we, “Nmo tiini n ye bembea mo, ye Baŋa Wɛ de wo n tei ne.”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Gideon ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, Baŋa Wɛ ná seene o wo dé tei ne, bɛ mo ye kikia yanto maama jege ya ke dé yera ne? Wo-kenkagela yalo dwi dé kwoa bam na maŋe ba bere debam we o toŋe ba tetare ne to daa wo yein-seeni mo? Ba déem ta bere debam we, Baŋa Wɛ mo jaane-ba o ja o nwoŋi Ejipti ne. Leile nam, Baŋa Wɛ dole debam mo o yage, o daare o ke debam Midian tiina bam jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ tete déem laam ma pa Gideon ni o we, “Véi n ma n dam dento n na jege to n toŋe, se n jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam n yage Midian tiina jeŋa ne, se amo tete mo toŋe‑m.”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Gideon ma leiri o we, “Amo Teiru, amo lage a ke tetɛ mo a jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam a yage? Debam diga kam mo tiini ka bwona Manasɛ dwi dem wone. Amo ta ma tiini a ye balaŋa dé diga kam nɔɔna maama wone.”

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo wó taa wo n tei ne, ye nmo wó chochoge Midian tiina bam maama nenɛɛne ba ye nɔɔno dedoa mo tei.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Gideon ma ta o we, “N yi ná seene de su amo kikia, se n ke wo-memaŋe n bere-ne. Konto wó pa se a lɔre we nmo Baŋa Wɛ mo ŋɔɔne de amo.

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Gideon ma vo sɔŋɔ o saŋe bo-choa, ye o ta kwei muni kuriwaa bu dedoa o ma ke bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle to. O ta ma ke nɔna yam tetɔgɔ wone ye o daare o lwo ya nyoa bam o ke kambia wone, o laam ja o vo o pa‑o tei-zɔŋɔ kom kuri ne.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Wɛ maleka kam ma ta ded‑o ka we, “Kwei nɔna yam dedaane bworobworo kom n daŋe peo konto yuu ne, se n daare n lwo nyoa bam te baŋa ne.” Gideon ma seene o ke konto.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam nam ya zei nacheiga mo o jeŋa ne. O ma kwei nacheiga kam ye o ma ka ni dem seeni o dwei nɔna yam dedaane bworobworo kom. Peo kom déem ma ja mini, ye de zwɛ te maama. Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam déem ma jei.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Gideon déem ma maane we, ko ye Baŋa Wɛ maleka mo o nɛa. Foone ma tiini de zo‑o ye o laare we, “Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo nɛ nmo tete maleka kam jaja.”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta‑o o we, “Pa n bochare zuri! Yé ta‑n fona, se n bá‑n te.”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Gideon déem ma lɔ bimbini se o ma zuli Wɛ jei sem konto ne, ye o bwoŋi-de we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ ye Bochare-zuru Tu mo.’ Bimbini dem konto ta wo Ofera ne, mɛ na ye Abizeri sɔ-yuu tiina nyem to mo.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne mo Baŋa Wɛ déem tage Gideon o we, “Véi n ja n kwo nabea kam, dedaane kadwoŋi na ye bena yarepɛ to, se n laam ma n gwɛɛne bimbini delo n kwo na kaane Baal de baŋa ne to n de tega ne. N ta wó gwoni Asera nyenyego daa kam na sale de yera ne to mo n de tega ne.

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: Nmo ta jege se n zege zwoŋo konto yuu ne mo n lɔ bimbini delo na yɔɔre to n pa n Tu Baŋa Wɛ. Ta kwei Asera nyenyego daa kam n na gwoni to n ma n tɔre mini se n zwɛ nabea belei tu wom n kaane n pa Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Gideon déem ma le nɔɔna fuga o tontoŋena bam wone ye ba vo ba ke kolo Baŋa Wɛ na bere‑o se o ke to. O nam ya kɔre o chorro dedaane teo kom nɔɔna bam mo. Mo kokuri, o wo wane se o ke konto wea ne, ye o ke tete ne.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Tega na poore tetete to, mo teo kom tiina zaŋe ba na we, Baal bimbini dem bwori mo de to tega ne. Ba ta nɛ we Asera nyenyego daa kam de gwoni mo ya ka daa tera. Ba ta nɛ we nɔɔna kwei nabea balei tu wom ba ma ke kaanem ba yage bimbini delo ba na lɔge ba zege to baŋa ne.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Ba ma bwɛ daane ba we, “Wɔ mo ke tento?” Ba na yɛ ko wone to mo ba maane we, ko ye Joasa bu Gideon mo ke keim dem.

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔɔna bam ma vo Joasa tei ba ta ba we, “Pa se n bu wom nwoŋi o ba ywo-seeni se dé go‑o, kolo ŋwaane, o vaare Baal bimbini dem mo o de tega ne, ye o daare o gwoni Asera nyenyego daa kam na yeiri de yera ne to o woli da.”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Joasa déem ma ta de balo maama na tu ba ta taane ba bere‑o to o we, “Abam wó wane Baal jaŋa á jwoŋi á jaŋe á pa‑o na? Wolo maama na wó jaŋe o pa Baal to wó te mo se tega laam poore. Baal ná seene o ye wɛ, yage-o-na se o tete jaŋe o jaŋa, kokuri to, wonto bimbini mo ba vaare ba de tega ne.”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Ko na zege dɛ dem konto ne to, mo ba lɛɛre ba jege Gideon ba bwoi we ‘Jerubi-Baal’. Kokuri to o kwo Joasa ya tage o we, “Yage-na se Baal tete jaŋe o jaŋa, ko na ye wonto bimbini dem mo ba vaare ba de tega ne to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Midian tiina bam, de Amaleki tiina bam dedaane dwia yalo maama na zoore wɛ-puli seeni to déem ma woli daane, ye ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ba vo ba chwi ba vwoa Jezerele bwolo kom wone.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ jworo ma chu Gideon baŋa ne dedaane dam. O ma wu nabɔnɔ o bwoŋi Abizeri sɔ-yuu kom o ke daane se ba tɔge o kwaga.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: O ta ma toŋe kwora o bwoŋi Manasɛ tiina bam maama se ba nwoŋi jara ŋwaane. O kwora kam déem ta yi Asere tiina bam, de Zebulun dedaane Nafitali tiina bam. Ba maama ma nwoŋi ba pɛ o kwaga ba pu.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: Tankɔlɔ mo tento a lage a tiŋi mɛ dé na fere mena to. Tega ná poore, ye nyɔnɔ ná bugi tankɔlɔ kom yerane, ye tega kam ná koga, mo a wó lɔre we nmo wó seene n da amo baŋa ne n jwoŋi Isarele tiina n yage nenɛɛne n na tage tei to.”

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Ko déem seene ko ke konto mo. Tega na poore to, Gideon ŋoke na mo tankɔlɔ kom yera ne o su zoŋa.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Gideon daa ma lwoori Wɛ o we, “Yé pa se n bane zaŋe de amo. Sɛ se a ta faŋe‑m a nii de woŋo dedoa. Pa se tankɔlɔ kom yera ne ko, se nyɔnɔ bugi tega kam maama.”

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne Wɛ ta ke konto mo. Tega na poore to, tankɔlɔ kom yerane mo koga, ye tega kam maama bugi de nyɔnɔ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Gideon dedaane o jar-keira bam ma zaŋe zezeŋa ne ba vo ba chwi ba vwoa Haroda buli-yi dem seeni. Midian tiina bam déem wo baŋa seeni mo. Ba de ma chwi ba vwoa bwolo kolo na wo Morɛ zwoŋo kom teiŋa ne to wone.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma ta Gideon o we, “Nɔɔna balo na tɔge nmo kwaga to tiini ba daga. A ná di Midian tiina bam a pa‑m, nɔɔna bam wó taa jege kamunim ba pae ba tete we banto mo di-ba. Ba bá pa a na a zula.

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: Konto to, ta n bere nɔɔna bam maama we, wolo ná fona, se kotu jwoori o viiri o daare debam.” Nɔɔna morro finlei-telei (

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Nmo nam ná fona se n jeeri-ba de jara mo, se n zaŋe n tɔge dedaane n tontoŋeno Pura se á vo da á nii.

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta Gideon o we, “N nɔɔna bam ta tiini ba daga dedɛ. Ja-ba n vo buga kam seeni se a pɔɔre balo na wó tɔge nmo to a pa‑m. Amo na wó ta wolo we, o da dede‑m se á vo á kwaare jara yam to mo wó vo, se a ná we wolo bá vo, kotu dae se o tɔge.”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Gideon ma ja nɔɔna bam maama o vo buga kam. Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta‑o o we, “Maane balo na wó lagese na bam nenɛɛne kukura na ke tei to, dedaane balo de na wó kuni ba nadwoona tega ne ye ba nyɔ na bam to, se n pɔɔre-ba daane.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta Gideon o we, “Amo lage a tɔge nɔɔna bia yatɔ yanto baŋa ne mo a jwoŋi n nɔɔna bam maama a yage, se a daare a kwei Midian tiina bam a ke n jeŋa ne se n di-ba. Ta balo maama na daare to se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: men stay here. The rest of you may go home, but leave your food and trumpets with us.” Gideon's army camp was on top of a hill overlooking the Midianite camp in the valley.
translation_verse: ) déem mo mɛ ba je ba kase na bam ba nyɔ. Balo maama na daare to kuni dwoona mo tega ne ye ba nyɔ na bam.

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne, Baŋa Wɛ ma ta Gideon o we, “Zaŋe n vo Midian tiina bam na tigi mɛ to n kwaare jara de-ba, se a lage a kwei-ba a ke n jeŋa ne mo.

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: Nmo ná yi ba tei ye n ni ba lara yam, nmo wó na baare se n jeeri-ba.” Gideon dedaane o tontoŋeno Pura ma da daane ba vo ba dona bam vwoa yam ni seeni.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Midian tiina bam, dedaane Amaleki tiina bam, de wɛ-puli seeni nɔɔna bam maama ya jare ba tete mo bwolo kom tega ne, nenɛɛne kayere na tiini se yo tei to. Ba kona yam kɔgɔ de maa tiini ya gaale nenɛɛne naneo ni kasolo na daga tei to.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Gideon déem yi da o maŋe, dedaane nɔɔno mo wora o tɛ o dendwɛ o bere o dwoŋi. Kotu maa we, “Amo dwɛ we bworobworo mo bibili ko zo debam na tigi mɛ tento to, ye ko laam mage vwei dedaane dam pa se de pipiri de pu tega ne.”

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: O dwoŋi wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Konto maama tɛ Joasa bu Gideon se-zɔɔ kom taane mo. O ye Isarele tu mo, ye Wɛ pa‑o dam se o di Midian tiina dedaane debam jar-keira bam maama!”

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Gideon na nigi dendwɛ dem dedaane de kuri o ti to, mo o kuni nadwoona o zuli Baŋa Wɛ. O laam ma jwoori Isarele jar-keira bam na wo mɛ to, ye o ta-ba o we, “Zaŋe-na wɛɛne, se Baŋa Wɛ lage o pa se á di Midian tiina bam mo.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: Amo dedaane balo na wo a tei ne to wó wu dé nabwanno tem. Abam ná nɛ konto, se á de wu á nabwanno tem á kaare dé dona bam tiga jei sem maama ne. Á laam maa wó laare wɛɛne we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane, dedaane Gideon ŋwaane!’ ”

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Ko déem na yi tete-koro maŋa kalo Midian tiina yerena bam na leiri daane to, mo Gideon dedaane nɔɔna bi delo na wo o tei ne to vei ba yi ba dona bam vwoa yam ni. Ba ma wu ba nabwanno tem, ye ba daare ba lɔ ba kamwaro tem ba na zei to.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Gideon nɔɔna bam popɔra kuni betɔ kom maama déem mo wugi ba nabwanno, ye ba daare ba lɔ ba kamwaro tem. Ba déem ma zei mini ba jagwia seeni, ye ba nabwanno tem wo ba jazem seeni. Ba laam ma laare wɛɛne we, “Se-zɔɔ kom ye Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane dedaane Gideon ŋwaane mo!”

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam maama maŋe mɛ ba na zege konto to mo ba kaare ba dona bam ba ke tetare ne. Ba dona bam maa kare ba chwoosi ye ba duri se ba lu.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo Gideon nɔɔna bam na jege ba nabwanno tem ba wui konto to, dedaane Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se ba dona bam mo kwei ba se-zɔɔro ba beeri da-jei se ba go. Midian tiina jar-keira bam déem kwei Zerera chwoŋa kam mo ba duri ba vo ba yi Bɛte-Sita. Ba ta ma yi Abel-Mehola na bwola dedaane Tabafa to.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina balo na nwoŋi Nafitali dwi wone, de Asere dwi wone, de Manasɛ dwi dem maama wone to ma nwoŋi ba pare Midian tiina bam, ne ba na jwoŋi ni se ba ke tei to.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Gideon déem ta toŋe nɔɔna mo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam maama ne se ba ta-ba we, “Nwoŋi-na á ke jara dedaane Midian tiina bam. Che-na Jɔdan buga kam dedaane bu-tole sem se ko yi Bɛte-Bara seeni. Yé pa-na se Midian tiina bam na pwola ba bɛ bwi sem.” Efrayim tiina bam déem ma seene ba nwoŋi ba che Jɔdan buga kam de bu-tole sem nia maama, se ko yi Bɛte-Bara.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Ba déem na zeili Midian tiina bam to, mo ba jaane ba yiga tiina balei. Oreba dedaane Zeebi mo konto. Oreba peo kom ne mo ba déem go Oreba, ye ba daare ba go Zeebi mɛ ba na nɔne Vini tio-bia to ye ba bwoi-ko we ‘Zeebi nɔnem jeiga’. Ba déem ma gwoni Oreba dedaane Zeebi yuni tem ba le ye ba ja-te ba vo ba pa Gideon. Maŋa kam konto ne, dedaane Gideon zoore Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni mo.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Efrayim tiina bam déem ma yi Gideon tei ye ba ŋwaana ba we, “Bɛŋwaane mo n ya wo bwoŋi debam se dé de nwoŋi dé tɔge dé ke jara de Midian tiina bam? Bɛ mo dé ke‑m ye n ke debam konto?” Ba déem ma tiini ba bwɛ‑o.

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: O ma leiri-ba o we, “Amo na ke tei to wo yi kolo abam na ke to. Abam Efrayim tiina na toŋe fenfee kolo to daga ko dwoi amo diga kam maama na ke tei to.

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Kolo ŋwaane, Wɛ woli abam pa se á go Midian dedɛɛra balei bam, Oreba dedaane Zeebi. Amo na ke tei maama to yi konto na?” O taane dem konto ma pa se ba bane dem zuri. Zeba dedaane Zalemuna taane

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: O ma ta Sukofa tiina bam o we, “Ja! Pa-na a kwaga tɔgena bam bworobworo se ba di, kolo ŋwaane ba tiini ba bugi mo. Dé wora dé pare Midian pwa Zeba dedaane Zalemuna mo se dé ja.”

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Sukofa teo nakwa bam ma leiri ba we, “Abam ta wo jaane Zeba dedaane Zalemuna á ke á jeŋa ne, ye n lage se dé pa n jar-keira bam bworobworo. Dé bá sɛ.”

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Gideon daa ma ta-ba o we, “Á na tage konto dwoŋi to, Baŋa Wɛ nam ná pɛ se dé ja Zeba dedaane Zalemuna, amo wó kwei kagoa yuu sabare mo a ma a fere abam!”

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: O na zege dáane to, o vei Peneli mo. O ta ma lwoori-ba nenɛɛne o ya na ke tei Sukofa ne to. Peneli tiina bam de déem ta leiri‑o Sukofa tiina bam leira yam dwoŋi mo.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: O ma ta ba de o we, “Amo ná di pwa bam ye a jwoori de yazura, a lage a vaare á di-dedɔrɔ konto mo a de tega ne!”

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Gideon ma vo Sukofa tiina bam tei o ta-ba o we, “Nam nii-na Zeba de Zalemuna mo tento! Abam ya ve se á woli-ne ye á ta we, ‘Nmo ta wo jaane Zeba de Zalemuna, ye n lage se dé woli n nɔɔna bam na bugi to de bworobworo.’ ”

english_verse: Gideon reached the enemy camp by going east along Nomad Road past Nobah and Jogbehah. He made a surprise attack,
translation_verse: Gideon déem ma kwei pipiu tiina chwoŋa kalo na tigi Noba dedaane Jogebeha wɛ-puli seeni to, o vo o dare o dona bam de jara.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Gideon ma zege jara jei sem ne o maa jwoori sɔŋɔ. O nam ya tɔge Heresa zwonnu tem sisworo chwoŋa kam mo.

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: Ba na maa kɛ to mo ba nɛ Sukofa tiina nɔn-doŋo dedoa. Gideon ma ja‑o se o bwei‑o teo kom yiga tiina bam bwia. Nɔn-doŋo kom ma popone ba nakwa fuserepɛ barepɛ bam yera o pa‑o.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: O ma pa se teo kom nakwa bam nwoŋi pwooni, ye o kwei kagoa yuu sabare o ma fere-ba.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: O ta ma vo o vaare Peneli di-dedɔrɔ kom o de tega ne, ye o daare o go teo kom konto nɔɔna bam.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Gideon laam ma bwei Zeba de Zalemuna o we, “Nɔɔna bera dwi mo abam déem goa Tabora ne?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ba ye nenɛɛne nmo na ye tei to mo. Ba maama nye de pa-bia mo.”

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: O daa ma ta-ba o we, “Nɔɔna balo á na go konto to ye amo chorro mo, amo tete nu-bia. Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó zege amo chega kam kwaga ne we, abam ya ná wo go-ba, amo de ya wó yage abam.”

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Gideon ma ta o bu-kwea Jefere o we, “Véi n go-ba!” Bu wom maa wo sɛ se o le o se-zɔɔ kom, o ta na ye bu ye foone jege‑o to ŋwaane.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Zeba dedaane Zalemuna déem ma ta Gideon ba we, “Nmo tete yi n go debam, kokuri to, nabiinu na ye tei to, o dam de mae konto mo.” Gideon ma seene o vo o go-ba. O ma daare o le lu-nyenno telo na wo ba kona yam ba ne to o ja o viiri. Gideon na ke jwoni delo to

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Ko na ke fee to, mo Isarele tiina bam vei ba ta de Gideon ba we, “Debam lage se nmo mo di paare dé baŋa ne, se n bu dedaane n naa de jwa di paare dé baŋa ne. Kokuri, nmo mo jwoŋi debam n yage Midian tiina bam jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Gideon déem ma leiri-ba o we, “Amo bá sɛ se a di paare á baŋa ne. A bu de nam bá di abam paare. Baŋa Wɛ mo wó taa ye abam Pɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam déem ma leiri ba we, “Dé sɛ de wopwolo.” Ba ma lware gare-jale tega ne pa se nɔɔno maama kwei zwa-kwane dedoa o na jwoŋi ba dona bam jeŋa ne to o de da.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: O ta jege ka-bia kadwoŋi Sɛkɛm ne. Kaane wom ma lo bakeira o pa‑o, ye o de pa bu wom yere we Abimeleka.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Gideon kwe lanyerane mo ye o laam te. Ba ma suli‑o o kwo Joasa yibeeli dem wone. De déem wo Abizeri dwi tiina teo Ofera ne mo.

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Gideon na yɔɔre o te to, mo Isarele tiina bam daa dole ba chega de Wɛ ba yage, ye ba jwoori ba kaane Baal jwona yam. Ba vei ba kwei Baal-Berifa mo se jwoni dem konto taa ye ba wɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma yɔɔre ba swei Baŋa Wɛ swia. Wonto nam ya mo jwoŋi-ba o yage ba dona balo maama na gilimi-ba to jeŋa ne.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Ba maa wo ke lanyerane de Gideon sɔŋɔ tiina bam, de wo-laaro telo maama o na ke o pa-ba to de.

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: O nabanna bam déem ma vo ba jeeri Sɛkɛm nakwa bam dedaane taane dem konto. Ba maama ma boŋe ba ja se ba tɔge o kwaga, kokuri to Abimeleka ye ba choro mo.

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: O déem ma vo Ofera teo kom o zo o kwo sɔŋɔ. O ma ja o chorro tem fuserepɛ na ye Gideon bia to o daŋe pelɔrɔ baŋa ne, ye o go ba maama. Gideon jeŋa-bu Jotam ma duri o seigi pa se wonto yerane lu o jeŋa ne.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Sɛkɛm tiina bam maama dedaane Bɛte-Millo tiina bam laam ma jeeri daane tei-zɔŋɔ kom na wo Sɛkɛm ne to kuri ne ba tiŋi Abimeleka paare.

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Jotam déem ma ni kolo maama na ke to. O ma vo o zege Gerizim peo kom yuu ne, ye o tiini o laare o we: “Sɛkɛm tiina bam, cheigi-na a taane dento, se Wɛ de wane o cheigi abam taane.

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: A sensɔla kampwo! Teeni déem mo beeri wolo na wó di paare de baŋa ne to. De ma ta Olivi tio kom de we, ‘Ta‑n di paare dé baŋa ne.’

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Olivi tio kom ma leiri-de ko we, ‘Amo nuga kam yeini ka pa se wa dedaane nabiina maama mo na zula lanyerane. A bá yage a nuga kam totoŋa se a ja a nɛ a ba a taa zuula teeni dedwonna dem baŋa ne.’

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Teeni dem daa ma vo kaporo tei ne de we, ‘Ba n ta‑n nii dé baŋa ne.’

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Kaporo kom de ma leiri-de ko we, ‘Amo bia bam na jege sonno dedaane ywoni tei to, a bá yage-ba se a ja a nɛ a ba a taa zuula teeni dedwonna dem baŋa ne.’

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Teeni dem daa ma vo Vini tio kom tei de ta we, ‘Ba n ta‑n di paare dé baŋa ne.’

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Vini tio kom ma ta ko we, ‘Amo bia bam na ke sana balo to yeini ba jaane wopwolo mo ba tui wa dedaane nabiina tetare ne. A bá yage konto totoŋa se a daare a ja a nɛ a ba a taa zuula teeni dedwonna dem baŋa ne.’

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Teeni dem maama laam ma ga ga de ta sabare-mangwola de we, ‘Ba n ta‑n di paare dé baŋa ne.’

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Sabare-mangwola kam déem ma ta teeni dem ka we, ‘Á boboŋa ná seene ya ja se á kuri-ne se a ji á pɛ, nam ba-na á dale amo woro kom ne. Ko nam ná dae konto, amo wó pa se mini nwoŋi sabare-mangwola kam ne ka zwɛ Lebanon Sedare teeni dem maama!’

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: Abam nam ke bɛ mo á pa amo kwo sɔŋɔ kom zem dɛ dento ne? Á zaŋe á go o bia fuserepɛ mo pelɔrɔ baŋa ne, ye á laam kuri o kaba-kana kam bu Abimeleka se o taa ye Sɛkɛm maama Pɛ, o na ye á choro to ŋwaane.

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye boboŋ-laaro de chega baŋa ne mo á tɔge á ke tento á pa Gideon dedaane o sɔŋɔ tiina bam zem dɛ dem dento ne, Wɛ wó pa se á ni ywoni Abimeleka ŋwaane. O de nam wó na wopwolo abam ŋwaane.

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: Ko nam daa ná dae konto, se mini nwoŋi Abimeleka yera ne de zwɛ Sɛkɛm tiina nakwa bam dedaane Bɛte-Millo tiina bam kula! Mini ta maa wó nwoŋi Sɛkɛm dedaane Bɛte-Millo tiina bam de yera ne de zwɛ Abimeleka kula!”

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Jotam déem na tage konto o ti to, o ma duri o kɛ. O ma vo o yi Beeri teo ye o zoore dáane, o na kɔre foone de o choro Abimeleka to ŋwaane. Abimeleka paare dim

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Abimeleka déem ma di paare Isarele ne bena yatɔ.

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Sɛkɛm tiina bam na lage se ba chɔge Abimeleka to, ba yeini ba pa se nɔɔna mo vo ba vwɛ peero tem seeni. Wolo maama laam maa ná yeini o tɔge dáane se o kɛ, venverena ma nwoŋi ba vere-ba. Abimeleka déem ma ni kolo maama na jege ko ke to.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Ebedi bu Gaale déem ma tɔge dedaane o chorro tem o vo o wo Sɛkɛm ne. Sɛkɛm tiina nakwa bam maa jege o chega.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe ba maama ma vo ba kare se ba gwori Vini tio-bia. Ba laam ma kwei-ba ba ma ke sana ba jege ba nyɔa, ye ba daare ba di ywoni. Ba déem ta zo ba jwoni dem diga mo ba ke kuri se ba zuli-de. Ba na wora ba di to, mo ba jege Abimeleka ba ke ba mɔna.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Ebedi bu Gaale déem ma ta kɔgɔ kom o we, “Wɔ mo ye Abimeleka, se debam Sɛkɛm tiina taa toŋe dé pa‑o? Wonto dae Gideon bu mo na? O kwaga saŋeno dae Zebula mo na? Bɛ mo ye debam Sɛkɛm bia wó taa kɔre Abimeleka? Dé nam jege se dé toŋe dé pa dé kwo Hamora mo.

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Nɔn-kɔgɔ konto maama ya ná zege amo kwaga ne, a ya wó zeili Abimeleka. Amo ya wó ta‑o we, ‘N ná ye baaro, ke n jar-keira bam n ke daane se dé jeeri!’ ”

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Teo kom yuu tu Zebula déem na nigi Gaale taane dem konto to, mo o bane tiini de zaŋe.

english_verse: And so he sent some messengers to Abimelech. But they had to pretend to be doing something else, or they would not have been allowed to leave Shechem. Zebul told the messengers to say: Gaal the son of Ebed has come to Shechem along with his brothers, and they have persuaded the people to let Gaal rule Shechem instead of you.
translation_verse: O ma seigi o toŋe nɔɔna Abimeleka tei ne se ba ta we, “Ebedi bu Gaale dedaane o chorro mo tu ba zoore ywo-seeni. Ba nam soge teo kom maama mo pa se ba lɔ nmo kwaga ne.

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Konto to, nmo dedaane n nɔɔna bam maama kwaane-na á ba tete ne á seigi teo kom pwola kam ne.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Tega maa ná jege ka poora, se á zaŋe á pɔpɔ á zo teo kom wone. Gaale dedaane o kɔgɔ kom laam maa ná nwoŋi se ba jeeri abam, á wó wane á ke-ba á na lage tei to.”

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Abimeleka dedaane o jar-keira bam maama déem ma nwoŋi ba vo ba vwɛ Sɛkɛm pwola kam ne. Ba nam ya pɔɔre ba tete kuni bena mo.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Tega na poore ye ba zaŋe mɛ ba ya na vwɛ to, dedaane Gaale nwoŋi o zege teo kom manchwo-peena ni ne mo.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Gaale déem ma na-ba ye o ta Zebula o we, “Nii nɔɔna na zege peero tem seeni ba siseiri ba maa tu ywo-seeni!” Zebula de ma leiri‑o o we, “Peero tem lunlunnu mo nye de nabiina nmo yibia ne.”

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Gaale daa ma ta o we, “Ba seene ba ye nɔɔna mo, ye ba zege tega kam tetare seeni ba beena! Ba kɔgɔ dedoa de ma nwoŋi vora bam tei-zɔŋɔ kom seeni ba beena.”

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Zebula ma leiri o we, “Nmo ni-wɛɛle dem vei yeim mo? Nmo ya taga n su n ni mo we, Abimeleka ye wɔ mo se debam taa toŋe dé pa‑o? Nɔɔna banto mo n ya‑n gwooni to, laam nam nwoŋi n jeeri-ba de jara se dé nii!”

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Gaale ma da Sɛkɛm tiina bam yiga pa se ba nwoŋi ba kwaare Abimeleka dedaane jara.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Abimeleka déem ma pare Gaale de o nɔɔna bam pa se ba duri. Nɔɔna dedɛ déem mo nɛ zonne se ko vo ko kwaare ba teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni ne.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Abimeleka déem ma maŋe Aruma ne o zoora. Zebula de ma zeili Gaale dedaane o chorro tem pa se ba nwoŋi ba daare Sɛkɛm teo kom.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Sɛkɛm tiina bam nwoŋi ba vo pwola kam ne mo. Abimeleka ma lɔre ko ni ne.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: O de déem ma ke o jar-keira bam daane, ye o pɔɔre-ba kuni betɔ. O ta ma vo o pa ba vwɛ pwola kam ne ye o cheigi Sɛkɛm tiina bam. Ba na nwoŋi teo kom ni ne ye o na-ba to, mo o zaŋe o jeeri-ba de jara.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Abimeleka dedaane o kɔgɔ kom popɔra dedoa mo vei ba che teo kom manchwo-peene dem ba zega. Popɔre selei na daare o jar-keira bam wone to de laam ma duri ba vo pwola kam ne ba jeeri Sɛkɛm tiina bam, ye ba go-ba.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Jara yam ke dɛ dem konto maama ne mo. Abimeleka ma kwaane o di teo kom. O ma vaare-ko o de tega ne, ye o daare o go ko nɔn-bia bam maama. O laam ma kwei yɛ o zezage teo kom tega kam baŋa jei maama ne.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Teo kom nakwa balo na wo Sɛkɛm di-dedɔrɔ kom wone to déem ma ni ko na ke tei to. Ba ma duri ba zo El-Berifa di-yuu kom wone se ba seigi.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Abimeleka ma lɔre ba na seigi mɛ to.

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: O ma tɔge dedaane o nɔɔna bam maama o vo Zalemon peo kom yuu ne. O ma kwei dwooru o gwoni dɛ o daŋe o bakale baŋa ne, ye o ta o nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Kolo maama á na nɛ amo na ke to, se á de ke konto.”

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Ba maama ma gwoni tio nɛ ba zeŋe ba tɔge Abimeleka kwaga. Ba ma ja-te ba vo di-yuu kom teiŋa ne ba tigisi te maama ba yeiri ko yera ne. Ba laam ma zwɛ diga kam, pa se nɔɔna balo maama na wo Sɛkɛm di-dedɔrɔ kom wone to te nyɔ! Ba yi nɔɔna moro, baara dedaane kaana maama.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Abimeleka déem ma vo o kaare Tebeza maama o pu, se o wane teo kom konto o di.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Teo kom nam ya jege di-dedɔrɔ kolo na dana to. Nɔɔna bam maama, baara dedaane kaana, ko woli de teo kom nakwa bam maama ma duri ba vo ba zo diga kam. Ba ma fɔge ba pe ka ni dem ye ba daare ba di nayuu kom baŋa.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Abimeleka ma vo o yi di-dedɔrɔ kom se o chɔge-ko. O na yi ko ni dem seeni se o zwɛ-ko to,

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: kaane wodwoŋi ma zege nayuu kom ne o dole namin-kamunu o de o yuu ne o lɔ o yu-kwoli-champoa kam.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Abimeleka ma bwoŋi nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara-keim zela yam to o ta‑o o we, “Le n se-zɔɔ kom n ma n go-ne, se a ba lage se ba taa tɛ amo taane we, Kaane mo go-ne.” Nɔɔno wom de ma seene o zɔ‑o o go.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam na nɛ we ba Pɛ Abimeleka tege to, ba maama ma jwoori ba vo ba sam.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem nam tɔge chwoŋa kanto mo o ŋwe jene Abimeleka yera ne dedaane lwarem delo o na ke o kwo wom to. Kokuri to, o go o chorro fuserepɛ mo.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Wɛ ta ma pa se Sɛkɛm tiina bam na ba totoŋ-lwanno tem ŋweero. Ko déem ke ko tɔge sɔɔlem delo maama Gideon bu Jotam na tage o pa-ba to mo.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Abimeleka toone kwaga ne mo Pua bu Tola déem tu o jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage. O nwoŋi Isakara dwi dem ne mo, ye o kwo-nakwe yere ye Dodo. O maa zoore Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam teo kodwoŋi ne, ko yere na ye Samira to.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Wonto de toone kwaga ne mo Jayira tua o wora. O ye Gilead tu mo, ye o nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne bena finlei-yalei.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Jayira ma te, ye ba suli‑o Kamon ne. Amon tiina bam na pɛ ko zo Isarele tiina bam yera tei to

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ bane ma tiini de zaŋe dedaane Isarele tiina bam, ye o pa chwoŋa se Filisi tiina bam dedaane Amon tiina bam di-ba.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Gilead nɔn-yum tem ma bwɛ daane we, “Wolo maama na sɛ se o da yiga o ja jara yam o jeeri Amon tiina bam to mo wó taa ye Gilead tiina bam maama yuu tu.”

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Amon tiina bam ma bɛ Jɔdan buga kam, ye ba ba ba ke jara dedaane Judah tiina bam, de Benjamin tiina bam, dedaane Efrayim tiina bam maama. Isarele tiina wo ma tiini ko pɛ.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma kaase ba jare Baŋa Wɛ ye ba we, “Chega ŋwaane to, debam tusi mo n yiga ne, kokuri to dé yage nmo na ye debam Wɛ wom to mo ye dé laam vo dé zuli Baal jwona yam.”

english_verse: The Lord answered: In the past when you came crying to me for help, I rescued you. At one time or another I've rescued you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines, the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites.
translation_verse: Ko ta ke konto mo ye Sidon tiina bam de Amaleki tiina bam de Midian tiina bam yaare abam. Á ma á keeri á jare-ne, ye a jwoŋi abam a yage ba maama jeŋa ne.

english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Véi-na á keeri á jare wa yalo á laam na kuri á pa á tete to, se ya jwoŋi abam ya yage á cham dem wone.”

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma ta Baŋa Wɛ ba we, “Debam ke wɛleere dedɛ. Ke n na lage tei to debam yera ne, se n jwoŋi debam n yage zem dɛ dento.”

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Ba laam ma dole ba wa-yɔɔro telo na wo ba tetare ne to ba yage, ye ba daare ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Baŋa Wɛ daa maa ware se o taa chem ye o nii Isarele tiina bam de ba cham dem. Jefeta yera taane

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Amon tiina bam déem ma bwoŋi daane se ba kwaare jara de Isarele tiina bam. Ba ma vo ba chwi ba vwoa Gilead ne. Isarele tiina bam de ma ke ba tete daane ba jeeri Mizipa ne ba chwi ba vwoa da.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Ba ma ta‑o ba we, “Ba n to dé yiga ne, se dé vo dé ke jara dedaane Amon tiina bam.”

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Jefeta ma ta-ba o we, “Abam déem chuli-ne mo, ye á fe-ne á zeili se a nwoŋi a daare a kwo sɔŋɔ kom. Bɛŋwaane mo á cham maŋa ne á daa beeri amo jei?”

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Gilead nakwa bam ma leiri‑o ba we, “De konto maama de, dé pipiri dé beene nmo tei mo, se n tɔge dé yiga se dé ke jara dedaane Amon tiina bam. Konto kwaga ne, nmo laam wó ta‑n ye Gilead tiina bam maama yuu tu mo.”

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Jefeta ta ma bwei-ba o we, “Chega to, abam ná jaane-ne á jwoori se dé ke jara dedaane Amon tiina bam, ye Baŋa Wɛ ná kwei-ba o ke dé jeŋa ne pa se dé di-ba, á wó sɛ se a taa ye á yuu tu na?”

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Gilead nakwa bam ma leiri‑o ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ ye maana tu dé tetare ne we, debam sɛ se dé ke nmo na tage tei to.”

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Jefeta ma tɔge-ba o jwoori o vo Mizipa. Nakwa bam ma sɛ se o taa tei-ba, ye o daare o ye ba jara yiga tu. Jefeta na wo Mizipa ne to, o ma jwoori o ta o taane dem maama Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Jefeta déem ma toŋe kwora Amon tiina Pɛ wom tei ne o bwei o we, “Bɛ mo tigi debam laŋa ne pa se n ba se n ke jara dedaane debam?”

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Amon tiina Pɛ wom ma leiri Jefeta nɔɔna bam o we, “Maŋa kalo Isarele tiina bam déem na zege Ejipti ne ba beene to, ba vere a tega kalo na zege Aranon buga kam ne ka tole Jaboke buga kam, se ko taa vei Jɔdan buga kam maama to mo. Abam nam jege se á jwoori á pa-ne a tega mo de bochare-zuru.”

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Jefeta daa ma toŋe nɔɔna Amon tiina Pɛ wom tei ne dedaane kwora kanto:

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: “Jefeta we, ko dae we Isarele tiina bam déem jwoŋi Moaba tiina dedaane Amon tiina tega mo.

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: Kolo na wora to mo ye we, Isarele tiina bam na nwoŋi Ejipti ne to, ba kwei kagoa chwoŋa kam mo ba vo ba yi Nane-soŋo kom, ba zege dáane ba vo ba yi Kadese.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Ba ma toŋe nɔɔna Edom Pɛ tei ne we, ‘Pa debam pwola se dé tɔge n tega kam baŋa ne dé kɛ.’ Edom Pɛ ma ve. Ba ta ma lwoori chwoŋa Moaba tiina Pɛ tei ne, ye o de wo sɛ se ba kɛ. Konto ma pa se Isarele tiina bam maŋe Kadese ne.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: Ba déem ma kare kagoa kam ne ba via, ye ba bebare Edom tega kam dedaane Moaba tega kam. Ba vei konto mo taa ba tɔge Moaba tega kam wɛ-puli seeni. Ba ma vo ba chwi ba vwoa Aranon buga kam bubɛ dedwoŋi dem ne. Ba wo zo Moaba laŋa kam, kokuri to Aranon buga kam mo ye Moaba laŋa kam siseini.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ma toŋe kwora Amori tiina Pɛ Sihon tei ne. Wonto ya jege o paare o di Hesebon ne mo. Ba maa we, ‘Pa debam chwoŋa se dé tɔge n tega kam baŋa dé vo dé teo.’

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Sihon maa wo pɛ Isarele tiina bam chega se ba tɔge o tega kam baŋa ne ba kɛ. O ma ke o jar-keira bam o ke daane pa se ba jeeri Jahaza ne, ye ba laam ke jara dedaane Isarele tiina bam.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom ma pa se Sihon dedaane o nɔɔna bam maama zo Isarele jeŋa pa se ba di-ba. Ko laam ma pa se Isarele dwi tiina jwoŋi Amori tiina na zoore tega kam konto ne to ba tei.

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: Ba ma jwoŋi Amori tiina tega kam maama, ko na zege Aranon buga kam ne se ko tole ko yi Jaboke buga kam to. Ko daa ta zege kagoa kam ne se ko yi Jɔdan buga kam to.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: Chega ŋwaane to, Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom mo zeili Amori tiina bam ye o kwei ba tega o pa debam Isarele tiina bam. Chwoŋa kɔ mo á jega se á ma á jwoŋi-ka?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Abam wɛ dem yere na ye Chemosi to na pɛ abam kolo se á ta‑á tei to, pa-na se á yi su-ko, se debam de wó taa jege kolo maama debam Tu Baŋa Wɛ na kwei o pa debam to mo.

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Nmo boŋe we n gare Zipore bu Balaki na ye Moaba tiina Pɛ to mo na? O wo sɛ se o dwoni dedaane Isarele tiina bam, naa se o jeeri-ba de jara. Ko dae chega na?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Amo wo ke kolokolo a chɔge n yiga. Nmo nam na kwaane n beeri jara dedaane amo to, n wo ke lanyerane. Baŋa Wɛ nam ye wolo na bore chega bora to mo. Wonto zem mo wó di bora Isarele tiina bam dedaane Amon tiina bam tetare ne.”

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Amon tiina Pɛ wom déem maa wo cheigi kwora kalo Jefeta na toŋe o pa‑o to.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ jworo déem ma chu Jefeta baŋa ne de dam. O ma zaŋe o tɔge Gilead de Manasɛ laŋa kam maama o kɛ o yi Gilead teo Mizipa. O ma zege dáane o vo Amon tiina bam na gilimi mɛ to.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Jefeta ma gwoni ni dedaane Baŋa Wɛ we, “Nmo ná kwei Amon tiina bam n ke amo jeŋa ne pa se a di-ba,

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Jefeta déem ma jwoori Mizipa. Maŋa kalo o na yɔɔre o maa yi sɔŋɔ to, mo o bukɔ nwoŋi se o jeeri‑o. O jege senyɛ mo o wɔe ye o sae o jeeri o kwo wom. Bukɔ wom konto yerane mo Jefeta loga, bakeira naa busankana daa wo woli da.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: O maa na nɛ‑o to, mo o wo chɔge dedɛ. O ma kaare o gwaaro ye o laare o we, “A bukɔ, n go-ne! N tiini n ja cham n ba n pa-ne! Amo wuuri a gwoni ni dedaane Baŋa Wɛ ye a daa bá jwoori a ni dem kwaga ne.”

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Bukɔ wom de ma leiri o we, “A kwo, nmo na gwoni ni dedaane Baŋa Wɛ tei to, nam ma-ne n ke kolo n na tage de Wɛ we n wó ke to. Kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ pɛ se n ŋwe jene n dona Amon tiina bam baŋa ne.”

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: O laam ma lwoori o kwo o we, “Amo nam lwoori‑m se n ke woŋo dedoa n pa-ne. Pa-ne pwola se a kwei chane selei a vo peero tem seeni, se a tɔge dedaane a yuudwonna a taa beera, se a keeri a na yeiri baaro ye a lage a te to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Jefeta ma sɛ ye o we, “Tɔ. Nam véi!” O ma pa se o lage jei o vo o ke chane selei, wonto dedaane o yuudwonna maama. Ba ma maŋe peero tem laŋa ne ba keeri o na yeiri baaro ye o lage o te to ŋwaane.

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: bene maama wone ba bukwa wó ma da yana mo ba nwoŋi ba keeri se ba guli Gilead tu Jefeta bukɔ wom gula.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Efrayim dwi tiina bam déem ma ke ba tete daane jara-keim ŋwaane. Ba ma bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ba vo Zafon. Ba ma yi Jefeta tei, ye ba ta‑o ba we, “Nmo na vei se n ke jara dedaane Amon tiina bam to, bɛ mo ye n wo bwoŋi debam se dé tɔge dé ke jara yam? Dé lage dé zwɛ n sɔŋɔ kom de n tete maama mo.”

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Jefeta ma leiri-ba o we, “Amo de a diga kam ya mo jege ta-kamunu dedaane Amon tiina bam. Amo ma toŋe a ta abam, ye á wo sɛ se á ba á jwoŋi-ne á yage ba jeŋa ne.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: A na maane we abam wo ti á yiga se á woli-ne to, mo a dole a ŋwea a yage ye a lɛɛne siseini dem a vo a jeeri Amon tiina bam. Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se a di-ba. Chwoŋa kɔ mo abam zem jega se á ba á jeeri amo de jara?”

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Jefeta déem ma ja Gilead jar-keira bam maama o ke daane se ba kwaare Efrayim tiina bam de jara. Efrayim tiina bam ma ta Gilead tiina bam taane ba we, “Abam Gilead tiina bam ye nɔn-yɔɔro mo ye á nwoŋi Efrayim dedaane Manasɛ dwia yam wone á ba ywo-seeni.” Konto ŋwaane, Gilead tiina bam ma kwaane ba di Efrayim tiina bam.

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Gilead tiina bam ma vo ba cheiŋi jei selo Efrayim tiina bam na yeini ba tɔge da ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam to. Efrayim tu laam ná boŋe se o bɛ buga kam o jwoori sɔŋɔ, ye o ná lwoori chwoŋa ba tei ne se o kɛ, Gilead tiina bam wó bwei‑o mo we, “Nmo ye Efrayim tu mo na?” O ná we, ‘Aawo!’,

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: ba wó bwei kotu mo we, ‘Ta we, Chibolɛf!’ Kotu ma yeini o we, ‘Sibolɛf’, kokuri o ware yere dem konto o bwoŋi lanyerane. Gilead tiina bam ma yeini ba ja‑o ba go Jɔdan bubɛ dem konto ne. Da yam konto ne, Efrayim tiina bam morro finna-telei (

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Gilead tu Jefeta déem nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne bena yaredo mo ye o laam te. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o tete teo Gilead wone. Ibazan de Elon de Abedon taane

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: ye o laam te. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli Bɛtelehem ne.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Ibazan de toone kwaga ne, Elon na ye Zebulun tu to mo nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne bena fuga,

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: ye o laam te. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli Zebulun tiina teo Ayijalon ne.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem daa ma toŋe lwarem ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. Baŋa Wɛ ma pa chwoŋa pa se Filisi tiina bam di-ba, ye ba pa ko zo ba yera bena finna.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Manoa. O maa ye Dan dwi tu ye o zoore Zora teo ne. O ya jege kaane o na ye kadega to mo.

english_verse: but one day an angel from the Lord appeared to her and said: You have never been able to have any children, but very soon you will be pregnant and have a son. He will belong to God from the day he is born, so his hair must never be cut. And even before he is born, you must not drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Your son will begin to set Israel free from the Philistines.
translation_verse: Nmo wó ja puga n lo n bu wom konto. O lora kam kwaga ne ko ba jege se fana gwoni o yu-ywei sem. Kokuri to o biini maŋa ne se ko taa via, bu wom ye se n pɔɔre‑o mo n ke Wɛ jeŋa ne se o taa ye Naziri tu. Wonto mo lage o bobo se o jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage Filisi tiina bam jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma vo o ta o baro o we, “Wɛ nɔɔno dedoa mo tu amo tei. O nyenyego kom ya tiini ko jege foone, nenɛɛne Baŋa Wɛ maleka nyenyego na ye tei to. Amo wo bwei‑o se a lɔre o na nwoŋi mɛ to, o de nam wo tage o yere o bere-ne.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma ta o bere-ne we, a lage a ja puga a lo bakeira mo. Konto ŋwaane a ba jege se a nyɔ sa-dɛɛra naa a di wodi-yɔɔro telo na chuli to. Kokuri to bu wom wó taa ye Naziri tu na ye o yera mo Wɛ ŋwaane, ko zege o biini ne se ko taa nii o toone maŋa.”

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Manoa déem ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Amo Teiru, ja! Pa se Wɛ tontoŋeno wolo n na toŋe debam tei ne to jwoori o ba, se o bere debam dé na wó ke tei dé nii bu wonto baŋa ne lanyerane to.”

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Wɛ ma sɛ Manoa wɛ-lworo kom. O kaane wom jei pwola ne mo ye Wɛ maleka kam jwoori ka ba o tei ye Manoa ya tera.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma duri lela o vo o ta o baro wom o we, “Nɔɔno wolo ya na tu a tei ne to daa jwoori o ba!”

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Manoa ma zaŋe o da o kaane wom kwaga. Ba na yi nɔɔno wom tei to, mo Manoa bwei‑o o we, “Nmo mo ye nɔɔno wolo ya na ŋɔɔne dedaane amo kaane to na?” O de ma leiri we, “Ɛɛ!”

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Manoa laam ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo taane dem nam ná jigi chega, bu wom konto ŋwea dedaane o totoŋa wó taa ye tɛ mo?”

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Maleka kam ma leiri ka we, “Ko jege se n kaane wom kwei kolo maama a na tage a bere‑o to mo o ke o bochare ne.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: Wonto tete ba jege se o di woŋo kolo maama na nwoŋi Vini tio yera ne to. O ta ba jege se o nyɔ sa-dɛɛra, naa o di wo-yɔɔro telo na chuli to. O yɔɔre o ye se o ke o tɔge kolo maama a na bere‑o to mo.”

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Manoa déem wo lɔre we nɔɔno wom ye Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam mo. O ma ta maleka kam o we, “Zuri n yera konto se dé beeri boŋo dé ma dé ke na dé pa‑m.” Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ma leiri‑o ka we, “Abam ná maŋe á wo pɛ-ne chwoŋa se a viiri, a ta bá di á wodiu kom. Á nam ná jege boŋo, se á ja-ko á zwɛ á ke kaanem á pa Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Manoa daa ma ta Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam o we, “Nmo yere nam mo ye bɛ? Se n taane dem ná jigi chega se debam de wane dé ke‑m zula.”

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam ma leiri‑o ka we, “Bɛŋwaane mo ye n bwei a yere dem bwia? De tiini de ye yere-kenkagele mo.”

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Manoa ma ja boŋo o woli de wodiu pɛɛre. O laam ma kwei-te o tiŋi peo baŋa ne o kaane o pa Baŋa Wɛ. Baŋa Wɛ ma ke wo-kenkagele ye Manoa dedaane o kaane wom zege ba nia.

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Min-vogo kom na zege peo bimbini dem ne de jaane de diini wɛ to, mo Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam tɔge de mini dem ka di. Manoa de o kaane wom na nɛ konto to, mo ba vwi ba yibia tega ne.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ maleka kam daa maa wo jwoori Manoa dedaane o kaane wom tei ne. Ko ma pa se Manoa lɔre we nɔɔno wolo na tu ba tei to ye Baŋa Wɛ maleka mo.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Manoa ma ta o kaane wom o we, “Ko zege ko nii mo we debam lage dé te mo, kokuri dé nɛ Wɛ yibia!”

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: O kaane wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa ya ná ye se o go debam, o ya bá jwoŋi zwɛɛm pɛɛre dedaane wodiu pɛɛre dé tei ne. O nam ya ta bá bere debam wo-kenkagela yanto, naa o ŋɔɔne wonnu tento dedaane debam.”

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Kaane wom déem ma lo bakeira. Ba ma pa o yere we, ‘Samson’. Bu wom ma ke nɔɔno ye Baŋa Wɛ swolim wo o yuu ne.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Samson déem zoore teo kodwoŋi ne, ko na wo Zora dedaane Esatola tetare ne ye ko yere ye Mahanɛ-Dan to. O na wora to mo Baŋa Wɛ jworo yeini ko chu o baŋa ne ko zeini‑o de dam.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Samson vei Timina. O ma na Filisi tiina bukɔ dedoa.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: O déem ma jwoori o ta de o kwo dedaane o nu o we, “Amo nɛ bukɔ mo Timina ne, o na ye Filisi tiina bam bukɔ. Véi-na á swo‑o á pa-ne se a di a ma ke a kaane.”

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: O kwo dedaane o nu ma leiri‑o ba we, “Bukwa mo ti nmo tete dwi tiina wone na? Debam dwi dem wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno mo tera o na su nmo yi pa se n ma n vei Filisi tiina banto na ye dwi-gɛ to tetare ne se n beeri n kaane na?” Samson ta ma fe o kwo ye o we, “Kaane wom konto mo amo boboŋa tɔga. Véi n swoi‑o n pa-ne.”

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: O kwo dedaane o nu maa yeiri we Baŋa Wɛ tɔge chwoŋa kanto mo se o na pwola o ma o chiŋi jara de Filisi tiina bam. Ka maŋa ne, Filisi tiina bam déem di dam Isarele tiina baŋa ne mo.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ jworo ma chu o baŋa ne dedaane dam, ye o kwei o je-bwori yerane o ma o kaare nywoŋo kom nenɛɛne ko ye bobona mo to. O nam wo tage kolo o na ke to o bere o kwo dedaane o nu.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: O ma vo teo wo pa se o de kaane wom lare daane. Samson wo ma da kaane wom dedɛ.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Ko na ke da fenfee to, Samson ma jwoori o vo se o laam swo o kaane wom. O na yi mɛ o ya na go nywoŋo kom to, o ma ywori se o nii ko ye tetɛ mo. O ma maane we twe mo zo nywoŋ-teko kom wone, ye se ke tooro.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: O ma lɔɔne tooro tem, ye o di-te o maa kɛa. O na yi o kwo de o nu tei to, mo o pɛ-ba tooro tem ye ba de di. O maa wo tage o bere-ba we te nwoŋi nywoŋ-teko yera ne mo.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Samson kwo ma vo Timina se ba ke kadiri dem. Samson ma ke kuri, ne nɔn-donno déem na yeini ba ke kadiri ŋwaane tei to.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam na nɛ‑o to, mo ba pɛ‑o ba nɔn-donno fintɔ se ba taa wo o tei ne.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Abam nam ná wo lɔre dendea kam kuri, abam mo wó pa-ne gare-fefale fintɔ dedaane gare-laaro fintɔ tem.” Ba ma leiri o taane dem ba we, “Dé sɛ. Ta n dendea kam se dé cheigi.”

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: O ma ta-ba o we: “Wodiu mo nwoŋi diru yera ne pa se a di, Wo-sonno de ma nwoŋi dedɛɛro wom yera ne.” Da yatɔ maama mo nɔɔna bam jaŋe dedaane dendea kam, ye ba wo lɔre ka kuri.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Da yana dɛ dem ne mo ba tage Samson kaane wom ba we, “Soge n baro wom se o ta dendea kam kuri o bere debam. Ko ná dae konto, dé lage dé zwɛ nmo dedaane n kwo sɔŋɔ tiina maama mo dé go. Abam na bwoŋi debam se dé ba ywo-seeni to, ko ye se á vere debam mo na?”

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Samson kaane wom ma ka yi-na o yiga ne ye o we, “A maane we n ba lage amo lanyerane. N de dendea mo n pa a kwo sɔŋɔ tiina bam ye n laam wo tage ka kuri n bere-ne.” O de ma leiri kaane wom o we, “Ta‑n yei we amo maŋe a wo tage taane dento a bere a kwo dedaane a nu. Bɛ mo wó taa tei se a ta de kuri a bere‑m?”

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Da yarepɛ maama wone mo kaane wom yɔɔre o nyenyɔne Samson yiga ne. Kuri dem da yarepɛ yam maama wone kaane wom kane yi-na konto mo ye o nyenyɔne Samson yiga ne. O na bilisi‑o konto ye da yarepɛ dɛ dem yi to, Samson ma ta dendea kam kuri o bere‑o. O de ma vo o maŋe-de o bere nɔn-donno tem.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Wea na lage ka zo da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne to, mo teo kom nɔɔna bam tage Samson ba we: “Bɛ daa mo sona ko dwoi tooro? Bɛ nam daa mo dana ko dwoi nywoŋo?” Samson ma leiri-ba o we: “Abam ya ná wo jaane amo na-chwɛ dem á ma á va, abam ya bá lɔre a dendea kam kuri.”

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Ba déem ma kwei Samson kaane wom ba pa nɔn-doŋo kom na jigi o badwoŋi kadiri maŋa kam ne to.
