english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: “Amo ya boŋe we n daa‑n ba lage‑o mo, pa se a kwei‑o a pa n yuudwoŋi wom. Kaane wom nyaane mo tento, ye o maŋe o lamma o dwoi zembaaro wom. N ná lage‑o, se a kwei a pa‑m.”

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Samson ma ta ba maama o we, “Amo laam nɛ chwoŋa se a toŋe kolo a na lage to Filisi tiina bam yera ne, ye ko bá taa ye a yiga!”

english_verse: Samson went out and caught
translation_verse: Samson ma vo o ja nywoŋ-kuri bia yatɔ (

english_verse: foxes and tied them together in pairs with oil-soaked rags around their tails.
translation_verse: ). O vɔge-se mo selei selei se nabila yam seeni, ye o daare o beeri gaao o vɔ-ko o meeli se nabila yam ne.

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: O ma tɔrege mini gaaro tem wone, ye o yage nywoŋ-kuri sem se se duri se zo Filisi tiina bam kare sem wone pa se mini dem zwɛ ba wodiiru tem maama. Mena yalo na bege ya ti ye ba ta wo zage-ya to, de men-pwoa yam, de Vini teeni, de Olivi teeni dem maama mo chɔge.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam ma bwei daane ba we, “Wɔ mo ke tento?” Ba ma leiri ba we, “Samson mo toŋe konto. Ko nam ye Timina tu wom na kwei Samson kaane wom o pa o yuudwoŋi wom to ŋwaane mo o ke konto.” Filisi tiina bam ma vo ba zwɛ kaane wom de o kwo ba go.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Samson ma du duuri o we, “Abam na toŋe totoŋ-lɔŋɔ konto to, amo ná wo yiri a jene á yera ne, a bá yage.”

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: O ma tiini o seene yia o jeeri-ba de jara, ye o go ba dedɛ. Ko kwaga ne mo o vei Etam, o vo o zoore peo bɔɔne wone.

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam déem ma vo ba chwi ba vwoa Judah laŋa ne, ye ba kwaare jara dedaane Lehi tiina bam.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Judah dwi tiina bam ma bwei-ba ba we, “Bɛŋwaane mo abam tu se á kwaare jara dedaane debam?” Ba de ma leiri ba we, “Debam tu se dé ja Samson mo se dé vo dé ke‑o nenɛɛne o na ke debam tei to.”

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Judah tiina bam nɔɔna morro tetɔ ma vo peo bɔɔne dem na wo Etam ne to, ye ba laam ta Samson ba we, “Nmo yei we Filisi tiina bam mo tei debam. Bɛ mo ye n ke debam konto?” O ma leiri o we, “Ba na ke-ne tei to ŋwaane mo amo de ke-ba konto.”

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma ta‑o ba we, “Dé nam tu se dé ja nmo dé ke Filisi tiina bam jeŋa ne mo.” Samson ma leiri-ba o we, “Du-na duuri á pa-ne we abam tete bá go-ne.”

english_verse: “We promise,” the men said. “We will only tie you up and turn you over to the Philistines. We won't kill you.” Then they tied up his hands and arms with two brand-new ropes and led him away from Etam Rock. When the Philistines saw that Samson was being brought to their camp at Jawbone, they started shouting and ran toward him. But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and Samson broke the ropes, as though they were pieces of burnt cloth.
translation_verse: Ba na jaane‑o ba yi Lehi to, mo Filisi tiina bam chwoosi ba yaga ye ba duri ba jeeri se ba jwoŋi‑o. Baŋa Wɛ jworo kom ma chu o baŋa ne de dam. Ŋone sem ma kɔ lela nenɛɛne mini na to bobɔɔro wone ye ko ye tei to.

english_verse: Samson glanced around and spotted the jawbone of a donkey. The jawbone had not yet dried out, so it was still hard and heavy. Samson grabbed it and started hitting Philistines—he killed
translation_verse: Samson ma dole o yi o na bonaga peyaa-ku-doŋa na tigi dáane. O ma twe o jeŋa o kwei-ka o ma o go nɔɔna moro.

english_verse: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
translation_verse: Samson ma ta o we: “A kwei bonaga peyaa kua mo, a ma a go-ba a tigisi pwei de pwei a tiŋi. Amo mɛ bonaga peyaa kua mo, a ma a go nɔɔna moro.”

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: O na ŋɔɔne konto o ti to, mo o dole peyaa kua kam o yage. Ba déem ma pa jei sem yere we ‘Ramafa-Lehi’.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Samson keim dento maama kwaga ne mo na-nyɔm tiini de chɛ‑o. O ma keeri o jare Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Nmo mo tɔge n tontoŋeno baŋa ne n di jara yanto. N laam nam lage se a te leile mo dedaane na-nyɔm, se dwi-gɛ tiina banto ja-ne mɔle yerane na?”

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se bɔɔne puri tega ne, ye na ta ba nwoŋi pa se o nyɔ. O ma jwoori o na dam. Lehi ne mo konto kea. Ba maa bwoi jei sem yere we, ‘En-Hakore.’ Buli-yi dem ta wo Lehi ne dedaane zem maama.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Ba ma ta Gaza tiina bam ba we, “Samson wo ywo-seeni mo!” Ba de ma vo o na wo mɛ to, ye ba kaare-ko ba pu. Tete dem konto ne ba ma cheigi teo kom manchwo-peena yam ne. Ba maa tigi ba sia ye ba we, “Dé wó gwoni tega zezenzeŋa mo dé vo dé li‑o dé go.”

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Konto na ke ko kɛ to, mo Samson daa nɛ kaane wodwoŋi, o na zoore Sorɛki bwolo ne. Kaane wom yere mo ye Delila. Samson boboŋa ma zo o wone.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Filisi teene yuu tiina bam ma vo kaane wom tei ba ta‑o ba we, “Kwaane n soge‑o se n lɔre o dam-fɔrɔ kom na nwoŋi mɛ to, se dé lɔre dé na wó ke tei dé ja‑o dé vɔ mɔle mɔle to. Se debam dedoa dedoa wó ŋwe‑m lu-nyenno sabu-dala bia fuga-dedoa (

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Delila ma da ko ŋwaane o bwei Samson we, “Ja! Ta n bere-ne nmo dam-fɔrɔ kom na nwoŋi mɛ to. Ba nam wó ke tɛ mo ba wane‑m ba ja se n yé wane lege-lege n ke?”

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Samson ma leiri‑o o we, “Ba ná kwei taŋa ŋon-donno terepɛ telo ta na wo koge to ba ma vɔ-ne, amo wó taa bwona mo ywale-ywale nenɛɛne nɔɔna maama na ye tei to.”

english_verse: The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him. Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
translation_verse: Delila nam ya pɛ se nɔɔna badwonna mo dale diga kadwoŋi ne ye ba cheiga. O ma laare o bwoŋi Samson o we, “Samson! Filisi tiina bam beene se ba ja‑m ywoo!” Samson ma pɛ o zaŋe o vaŋe taŋa ŋone sem o kɔ lela nenɛɛne gare-ŋona na dwei mini ye ka di tei to. Ba maa wo wane ba lɔre o dam-fɔrɔ kom na zege mɛ to.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Delila daa ma ta‑o o we, “Nmo na gane-ne konto to, a maane we n jege-ne mo n mɔna. Ja! Ta n bere-ne nɔɔna na wó ke tei ba ja‑m to.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Samson ma ta‑o o we, “Ba ná mɛ ŋon-dwe selo ba ta na wo mɛ ba ke kolokolo to ba ma ba vɔ-ne, a laam wó taa bwona mo nenɛɛne nɔɔna maama na ye tei to.”

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Delila ma beeri ŋon-dwe o ma o vɔ‑o. O daa ta ma pa se nɔɔna bam dale diga kam ne ba cheiga. O laam ma laare o we, “Samson! Filisi tiina bam beene se ba ja‑m ywoo!” Samson déem ma zaŋe o vaŋe tento o kɔ nenɛɛne gare-ŋona dwoŋi to.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Delila daa ma ta‑o o we, “Nmo ta jege-ne mo n gana, ye n daare n mɔne-ne. N bá‑n ta ba na wó ke tei ba ja‑m to n bere-ne na?” O ma leiri‑o o we, “Nii a yu-ywei sem na pane kuni berepɛ tei to, se n laam ja-se n ke daane n vɔ n ke paare yera ne, nenɛɛne ba na dole gare-yi tei to. N ná ke konto, amo wó taa bwona mo nenɛɛne nɔɔna maama na ye tei to.”

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: Delila ma gane‑o pa se o dɔ. O ma ja o yu-ywei sem na pane kuni berepɛ to o vɔ o meeli gare-yi ba na wora ba dole to yera ne, ye o daare o pa-se de paare. O laam ma laare o we, “Samson! Filisi tiina bam beene se ba ja‑m ywoo!” O ma pɛ o zaŋe dɔɔm wone, ye o vaŋe paare dem o guri. Gare-yi-dolo kom dedaane gare-yi dem maama maa wo o yera ne.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma ta‑o o we, “Nmo na tɛ we n swoi-ne to, bɛ mo ye n wo ke n wo dedaane amo? N gane-ne tento n ke kuni betɔ, ye n ta wo sɛ se n ta n dam-fɔrɔ kom na zege mɛ to.”

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Dɛ maama o ma tiini o jege Samson yia o gigila de taane dem konto. Samson yera ma ba ya chɛ, ye o kare o beeri toone jei.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: O ma ga ko ŋwa ye o ta o chega kam o bere kaane wom o we, “Fana ta wo gwoni amo yu-ywei sento. Ko zege maŋa kalo a na wo a nu puga ne to mo Wɛ pɔɔre-ne se a taa ye Naziri tu a pa‑o. Ba ná fane a yu-ywei sem, amo wó ga a dam dem mo, pa se a taa bwona ywale-ywale nenɛɛne nɔɔna maama na ye tei to.”

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Delila ma lɔre we o tage o chega maama mo o bere‑o. O ma toŋe o bwoŋi Filisi yuu tiina bam ye o ta de-ba o we, “Jwoori á ba-na, se o laam tage chega kam jei o bere-ne.” Nɔɔna bam ma ja o sabu kom ba woli da ba ba ba pa‑o.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: O ma gane Samson pa se o peini o nɛ baŋa ne o dɔ. O laam ma bwoŋi nɔɔno pa se kotu ba o fane Samson yu-ywei sem na pane kuni berepɛ to. Delila ma gane Samson pa se o ba o ga o dam dem.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam ma ja‑o, ye ba daare ba chochɔrege o yi-chele-bia ba le. Ba ma ja‑o ba vo Gaza teo wone, ye ba kwei channa chegero ba ma lei‑o ba zege. O déem na wo peena diga ne konto to, ba maa jege‑o ba choe ba muni.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Samson yu-ywei sem daa ma bobo se se taa nwoŋa. Samson toone

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Filisi yuu tiina bam ma jeeri daane se ba kaane ba jwoni Dagon, se ba daare ba di kuri dedaane wopwolo. Ba maa we, “Dé wɛ dem pɛ se dé jeŋa zo dé dono Samson.”

english_verse: Everyone there was having a good time, and they shouted, “Bring out Samson—he's still good for a few more laughs!” The rulers had Samson brought from the prison, and when the people saw him, this is how they praised their god: Samson ruined our crops and killed our people. He was our enemy, but our god helped us capture him. They made fun of Samson for a while, then they told him to stand near the columns that supported the roof.
translation_verse: Ba na wora ba di ywoni konto to, mo ba bwɛ daane ba we, “Ja-na Samson á ba ywo-seeni se o taa ke mola se dé taa mɔna.” Ba ma ja Samson ba nwoŋi peena diga kam ne ba ba ba tei ne. O ma seene o ke pa se ba mɔna. Ba ma pa o zege sɔŋɔ kom ywoa yalei tetare ne.

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Samson ma ta bu wolo na jege‑o o vaŋe to o we, “Pa se a dwei ywoa yalo na jege sɔŋɔ konto ya zege to, se a lage se a sale ya yera ne mo.”

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Samson ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o we, “Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, guli amo gula, se n jwoori n pa-ne dam bedwe yerane. Amo Tu Wɛ, pa se a daa ke keim dedwe a ma yiri jene Filisi tiina bam baŋa ne, de ba na le a yi-chele-bia bam to.”

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Samson ma to o gorege ywoa yalei yalo na jege sɔŋɔ kom ya zege ko tetare ne to. O jazem maa jege ywei dedwe, ye jagwia kam de jege dedem dem. O laam ma yigi-ya.

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: O ta ma laare o we, “Yage se amo dedaane Filisi tiina bam tɔge daane dé te.” O ma tiini o yigi sɔŋɔ kom ywoa yam dedaane o dam maama, pa se ko to ko li Filisi yuu tiina bam dedaane nɔɔna balo maama na wo ko wone to. Ko ma pa se Samson toone dɛ ne, o na go nɔɔna balo to daga ba dwoi balo o na ŋwe ye o go to.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: O chorro tem dedaane ba sɔŋɔ tiina maama ma ba ba kwei o yera yam ba jwoori sɔŋɔ. Ba ma suli‑o o kwo Manoa yibeeli dem ne. Zora dedaane Esatola tetare laŋa ne mo konto. O déem nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne bena finlei mo.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: Mika na kwei-ko o pa o nu to, o nu wom ma le sabu-dala bia yalei o pa gɔgɔ, pa se o ma o ke jwoni, ye o daare o ma lu-nyenno o taare-de o pa‑o. Ba ma pa se de zege Mika sɔŋɔ ne.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Mika déem ya kwɛ diga mo o sɔŋɔ kom ne se ka taa ye wara-jei. O ma ke o jwona de kaanem gare-wogo o zege da, ye o daare o kuri o bia bam dedoa se o taa ye kaanem tu o pa‑o.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa ne, Pɛ ta tere Isarele logo kom wone, nɔɔno maama maa ke o boboŋa na lage tei to.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma nwoŋi da Bɛtelehem ne se o beeri jei-gaa o zo o taa toŋe o totoŋa. O ma beeri o yi Mika sɔŋɔ na wo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne to.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Mika ma bwei nɔɔno wom o we, “Nmo nwoŋi yein-seeni mo?” O de ma leiri o we, “Amo ye Levi tu mo, ye a laam zoore Bɛtelehem na wo Judah ne to. A nam kare a beeri mɛ a na wó taa zoore ye a na totoŋa to mo.”

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Mika laam ma ta o we, “Nam ta‑n zoore ywo-seeni. Nmo laam wó ta‑n bere-ne chwei ye n daare n kaane n pa-ne. Bene maama wone, amo wó pa‑m lu-nyenno sabu-dala fuga, dedaane gwaaro, ye a ta pa‑m n ni-wodiu.”

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: O ma le‑o o zege pa se o ye kaanem tu o pa‑o. Nɔɔno wom de ma lɛɛre o maŋe Mika sɔŋɔ ne.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Mika ma ta o we, “Amo yei we Baŋa Wɛ laam wó ke-ne lanyerane, a na jege Levi dwi tu a sɔŋɔ ne pa se o ye a kaanem tu to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Wonnu tento maama déem na jege te ke to, Isarele tiina bam ya ta ba jege pɛ. Ka maŋa ne, Dan dwi tiina bam ma kare ba beeri tega se ba taa zoore ka wone. Kokuri, tega kalo Isarele tiina bam na pɔɔre ba pa daane to, Dan tiina bam ya ta wo nɛ ba tete laŋa ka wone.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Dan tiina bam ma le ba dwi dem wo babɛ senu ba na nwoŋi sɔ-yuu maama wone to. Ba ma zege Zora dedaane Esatola ne ba toŋe-ba ba we, “Véi-na á kaare tega kam, se á daare á ŋɔ á nii ka maama na ye tei to.” Ba déem ma kaare taa ba vo ba yi Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam. Ba ma vo Mika sɔŋɔ ba zo ba peini dáane.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Ba na wo Mika sɔŋɔ ne to, mo ba maane Levi dwi tu wolo na zoore da to kwor-taŋa ba lɔre. Ba ma yi o tei ba bwei‑o ba we, “Wɔ mo jaane‑m o ba ywo-seeni? Nmo wo ywo n ke bɛ mo?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: O de ma leiri-ba o we, “Amo dedaane Mika mo maŋe daane, o nam ke-ne lanyerane, ye o ta ŋwe-ne pa se a lɛɛre a ye o kaanem tu.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Ba ma ta‑o ba we, “Nam lwoori Wɛ n pa debam se dé lɔre dé chwoŋa kam wó ja ywoni ka ba ka pa debam, naa ka bá ja ka ba.”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom ma leiri-ba o we, “Yé pa-na se á bochara taa maga, se Baŋa Wɛ yiga wora á chwoŋa kam wone.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Babɛ senu sem ma nwoŋi dáane ba to chwoŋa ne ba maa kɛa. Ba ma vo ba yi Layisi. Teo kom nɔɔna bam zoore yalem mo daane, ye foone ba jege-ba nenɛɛne Sidon tiina bam tei to. Woŋo maama tiini ko yi-ba, ye ba jejegero gaale. Ba ya zoore da de ywoni mo de wo-zuru. Ba teo kom maa ye yiga yiga dedaane Sidon tiina bam. Ba maa ba toŋa dedaane nɔɔna badwonna.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Babɛ senu sem ma jwoori Zora dedaane Esatola ne. Ba dwi tiina bam ma bwei ba kwaga.

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Abam ná yi ba teo kom, á wó na we jei sem daga dedɛ. Nɔɔna bam maa zoore da yalem, ye woŋo maama tiini ko yi-ba. Baŋa Wɛ de ma kwei tega kam o ke á jeŋa ne se á ta‑á tei.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Dan dwi tiina bam nɔɔna bia yaredo ma zege Zora dedaane Esatola ne ba nwoŋi de ba jara-keim zela se ba vo ba jeeri-ba.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba twɛ Kiriaf-Jeerim na wo Judah laŋa kam ne to ba chwi ba vwoa da. Jei sem wo Kiriaf-Jeerim wɛ-puli seeni mo. De zem maama ba ta bwoi jei sem yere we, ‘Mahanɛ-Dan’.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Ba ma zege dáane ba vo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne ba vo ba yi Mika sɔŋɔ kom.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Babɛ senu sem ya na vei ba ŋɔ ba nii Layisi to ma ta de ba dwonna bam ba we, “Abam yei we sam dento dedoa wone jwoni wora ba na gɔgere de lu-nyenno na? Kaanem gare-wogo, de jwona yadwonna de maa wora. Jeeli-na á nii á na wó ke tei dedaane tento maama to.”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Daa‑n yé jwoori n puri n ni. Ta‑n tɔge debam, se n ji dé kwo dedaane debam kaanem tu. Nmo ná tu n ji kaanem tu n pa Isarele dwi dem sɔ-yuu kodwoŋi ba gare n ná ye nɔɔno dedoa dedaane o sɔŋɔ tiina yerane kaanem tu na?”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom ma sɛ ba taane dem. O ma kwei kaanem gɔrɔ kom dedaane jwona yam maama, ye o laam pɛ ba kwaga o pu se ba kɛ.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Ba maama ma to chwoŋa ne ba maa kɛa, ye ba bia bam, de ba vara, dedaane ba zela wo yiga ne.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Dan nɔɔna bam na kɛ ba yi yiga fee to, mo Mika bwoŋi o dedaane balo na zoore daane to o ke daane. Ba ma pare Dan tiina bam ba ja.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Ba ma chwoosi ba bwoŋi Dan tiina bam, ye ba de leiri ba bwei Mika ba we, “Bɛ mo ke ye nmo pɛ nɔn-kɔgɔ konto n ke n kwaga ne?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Mika maa we, “Abam kwei amo jwona yalo a na ke to, dedaane a kaanem tu wom mo á ja á viiri. Bɛ mo ye á daa ta jege ni se á bwei-ne we, ‘Bɛ mo kea?’ Bɛ mo abam daa daare á pa-ne?”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Dan tiina bam ma leiri Mika taane dem ba we, “Yé ta‑n ŋwaana! Nmo ná lage n tete, daa‑n yé jwoori n puri n ni. Ko ná dae konto, ban-lom tiina na wo dé tetare ne to wó yi‑m, se n dedaane n sɔŋɔ tiina bam maama ga á ŋwea.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Dan tiina bam ma kwei chwoŋa ba maa kɛa. Mika ma na we ba tiini ba damma ba dwoi‑o. O de ma jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: The tribe of Dan took Micah's priest and the things Micah had made, and headed for Laish, which was located in a valley controlled by the town of Beth-Rehob. Laish was defenseless, because it had no walls and was too far from Sidon for the Sidonians to help defend it. The leaders of Laish had not even asked nearby towns to help them in case of an attack. The warriors from Dan made a surprise attack on Laish, killing everyone and burning it down. Then they rebuilt the town and settled there themselves.
translation_verse: Jwoŋinu maa tera se o woli-ba, kokuri jei sem konto dɔra mo dedaane Sidon teo kom. Ba maa ba toŋe dedaane nɔɔna badwonna. Teo kom konto wo bwolo ne mo, ye ko bwola de Bɛte-Rehoba. Dan tiina bam déem ma jwoori ba lɔ teo kom konto ba zege, ye ba lɛɛre ba zoore ko wone.

translation_verse: Kan-baro wom ma ja boboŋa se o vo o ŋɔɔne de o kaane wom se o ja‑o o jwoori o tei. O ma ja o tontoŋeno dedaane o bonɛ selei o woli da o vo. Kaane wom ma pa o zo o kwo tei ye o kwo de jeeri‑o de wopwolo.

translation_verse: Kaan-kwo wom ma fe‑o pa se o maŋe da o peini da yatɔ. Ba maama ma di ye ba nyɔa daane.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Da yana dɛ dem ne, Levi tu wom ma zaŋe zezeŋa ne se o viiri. Kaan-kwo wom ma ta‑o o we, “Saare n ni, se n na dam n viiri.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Baara bam konto balei ma maŋe da ba di ye ba nyɔ daane. Kaane wom kwo ma ta Levi tu wom o we, “Ta maŋe ywo-seeni n peini, se n di ywoni.”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Levi tu wom ta ma kwaane se o viiri. Kaan-kwo wom daa ta ma fe‑o pa se o maŋe da o peini.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Da yanu dɛ dem ne, baaro wom ma zaŋe zezeŋa ne o bwoli chwoŋa se o kɛ. Kaan-kwo wom daa ma ta o we, “Cheigi se n saare n ni, se wea maŋa ne nmo laam wó wane n viiri.” Banto balei daa ma di daane.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom dedaane o ka-bia kam de o tontoŋeno wom daa ma zaŋe se ba viiri. O tembaaro wom daa ma jwoori o ta o we, “Ko gɛ fee mo se tega yi. Daa‑n ta peini ywo se n di ywoni, se wɛ dem to mo konto. Te-pora maŋa ne abam wó wane á gwoni tega á zaŋe á kɛ.”

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Baaro wom daa maa wo sɛ se o peini tete dem konto ne. O ma ja o ka-bia kam dedaane bonɛ selei sem, ye o kwei chwoŋa o laam vo o yi Jebusi tiina teo kom na ye Jerusalem to.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Ba na twɛ Jebusi to, dedaane tega kam wora ka yi mo. Levi tu wom tontoŋeno ma ta o we, “Pa se dé ywori Jebusi tiina bam tei ne dé peini se tega ná poore, se dé laam viiri.”

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Levi tu wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Debam bá vo dé zo veira teo mɛ na dae Isarele dwi tiina na zoore to. Dé wó fɔɔre dé kɛ dé yi teo kodwoŋi mo.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Ba ma gaale Jebusi ba kɛ. Ba ma vo ba yi Gibea, de wɛ zo mo. Jei sem konto wo Benjamin laŋa kam ne mo.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Ba ma ywori dáane se ba peini. Ba ma vo ba jei teo kom lara jei sem ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa wo tu ba tei se o ja-ba o ja o vo o sɔŋɔ se ba peini.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ba na wora to mo nɔn-kwea kadwoŋi déem nwoŋi o kara o tɔge da o maa jwoori sɔŋɔ. Wonto déem zoore Gibea ne ye o ya nwoŋi Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne mo. O dae Benjamin dwi tu nenɛɛne teo kom tiina na ye tei to.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Nɔn-kwea kam ma maane we, chwo-veilu mo jei teo kom lara jei sem ne. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo nwoŋi yei ne mo n ba n jei ywo-seeni, ye n nam ma‑n vei yei mo?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Levi tu wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Debam zege Judah teo Bɛtelehem ne mo dé maa jwoori sɔŋɔ. A sɔŋɔ kom wo Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam na ye yiga yiga de sam to mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam wo tu o ja debam o vo o sɔŋɔ se dé peini dé poore tega.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Debam nam jege dé vara bam wodiu. Wodiu de sana maa wora se amo de a kaane wom dedaane a tontoŋeno wom di. Dé jege kolo maama dé na lage to.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Nɔn-kwea kam ma leiri o we, “Wɛ wó pa abam yazura. Á ba amo tei, se a nii á baŋa ne. Yé maŋe-na pwola kanto ne á peini.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: O ma ja-ba o vo sɔŋɔ, ye o pa ba bonɛ sem wodiu. O veira bam ma zare ba nɛ, ye ba jeini se ba di wodiu.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Ba na wora ba di ywoni konto to, mo teo kom nɔn-wo-korro tedwonna tua ba kaare sɔŋɔ kom ba pu ye ba dɔne ko bworo kom. Ba ma ta nɔn-kwea kam ba we, “Pa se veiru wom na tu o wo n tei ne to nwoŋi o ba ywo-seeni, se debam lage se dé lage‑o mo!”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Nɔn-kwea kam ma nwoŋi o vo ba tei, ye o ta-ba o we, “A badwonna bam, yé ke-na lwarem dem konto, se ko wo maŋe! Yé swei-na we nɔɔno wom ye amo veiru mo.

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Nii-na amo bukɔ mo tento! O ta yeiri baara. Veiru wom de maa vei de o ka-bia mo. A wó ja banto a ba a pa abam se á ke-ba á na lage tei to. Se ko ná ye nɔɔno wonto, yé ke-na totoŋ-lɔŋɔ kom konto o yuu ne, se ko tiini ko jege chaveera mo.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔɔna bam maa wo sɛ. Levi tu wom ma fe o yigi o ka-bia kam o pa o nwoŋi o vo ba tei. Ba ma zi‑o ba lage tete dem konto maama taa se ko taa nii te-pora. Tega na poore to mo ba yage‑o.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Tega na jege ka poore to, mo kaane wom kwaane o vo o to o tigi nɔn-kwea kam diga ni ne, mɛ o baro wom déem na tigi da to. Wɛ puli mo ye o ta maŋe da o tiga.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Tega kam na poore pa se Levi tu wom pore diga kam ni se o nwoŋi to, mo o nɛ we o ka-bia kam tigi diga kam ni ne, ye o kwaane se o ja ka ni dem.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma ta o ka-bia kam o we, “Zaŋe se dé viiri.” Kaane wom maa wo leiri. O ma kwei‑o o daŋe o bonaga baŋa ne, ye o kwei chwoŋa o maa viira.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: O na yi sɔŋɔ to, mo o zo diga o lage seo o ma o gwoni o ka-bia yera yam kuni fuga-belei. O ma pɔɔre pɔɔre kaane wom yera yam o toŋe o pa Isarele dwia fuga-yalei yam maama.

translation_verse: Wolo maama déem na nɛ keim dem konto to maa we, “Keim dento dwoŋi ta wo fɔge de ke se dé na. Ko na zege maŋa kalo Isarele tiina bam na nwoŋi Ejipti ne to, se ko yi zem maama, dé ta wo nigi tento! Bwɛ-na se dé nii dé wó ke tetɛ mo!”

translation_verse: Levi dwi tu wolo kaane ba na go to ma tole o we: “Amo dedaane a ka-bia kam mo beeri de vo de yi Benjamin teo Gibea, ye dé boŋe se dé maŋe da dé peini se tega poore.

translation_verse: A na maane we nɔɔna banto tiini ba toŋe chave-totoŋe Isarele teo kom ne to ŋwaane mo a gwoni a ka-bia kam yera yam, ye a laam pɔɔre-ya yera yera a toŋe a pa Isarele dwi maama.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Konto to, abam maama na ye Isarele dwi tiina to, laam ja-na taane dem se dé lɔre kolo dé na wó ke to.”

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam maama ma ta dedaane kwora dedoa ba we, “Debam bá jwoori dé sam. Debam wone dedoa tete bá jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Isarele dwi tiina bam maama ma toŋe kwora ba pa Benjamin dwi tiina na wo mɛ maama to we, “Bɛŋwaane mo ye lɛɛro tento ke abam tetare ne?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Ko dae se dé sɛ lwarem totoŋe dento dwoŋi Isarele ne. Konto to, pa-na se Gibea teo nɔn-wo-korro tem na ke totoŋe dem konto to nwoŋi pwooni se dé go-ba.” Benjamin tiina bam maa wo sɛ ba cheigi ba dwonna Isarele tiina bam kwora kam.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Ba ma zege ba teene dem maama wone ba nwoŋi. Ba ta ma vo ba jeeri Gibea ne se ba kwaare jara dedaane Isarele tiina badaara bam maama.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Isarele tiina bam ma gɔ ba vwoa yam ba vo Gibea ba chwi pa se ya bwola dedaane teo kom.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Ba ta ma nwoŋi ba vwoa yam ne ba vo ba zege teo kom yiga ne se ba jeeri Benjamin tiina bam dedaane jara.

translation_verse: Kanto maŋa ne, dedaane Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam wo Bɛtel ne mo. Finehase na ye Eleaza bu, ye o kwo-nakwe ye Aron to mo toŋe dakaa kam totoŋa o ma zuli Wɛ. english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma jwoori Gibea teo, ye ba pa se nɔɔna badwonna vwɛ ba kaare teo kom maama.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Ba ma kwaane se ba duri ba lu Isarele tiina bam, ye ba kwei kagoa chwoŋa kam ba dura. Isarele tiina bam maa wo pɛ-ba chwoŋa se ba lu. Ba badwonna ma nwoŋi ba teene dem ne ba ke Benjamin tiina bam ba tetare ne, ye ba laam go-ba.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Ko kweelim ne to Benjamin jar-keira bam morro finlei-tenu na ye jara bembɛ to maama mo tega dɛ dem konto ne.

translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem ya jeeri Mizipa ne ba du duuri we, “Debam wolowolo bá pa Benjamin dwi tu di debam bukɔ kɔtaa!”

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Ba jara yam na ti to, Isarele tiina bam ma la daane ba gilimi Bɛtel ne. Ba ma tiini ba kaase ye ba keera se ko taa vei dedaan-ni ne, ba wo na pɛ to ŋwaane.

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Tega na poore tetete to, nɔɔna bam ma zaŋe ba lɔ kaanem bimbini ye ba kwei zwɛɛm pɛɛra de yazura pɛɛra ba kaane ba pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam maama ma bwei daane we, “Debam na tu dé jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne konto to, Isarele sɔ-yuu kɔ mo wo dɛ ba jeeri?” Ba bwei konto kolo ŋwaane ba ya dugi duuri mo we, wolo maama ná wo tɔge o jeeri Mizipa ne, se ba go kotu.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam maama wo ma pɛ, ba chorro Benjamin dwi tiina bam ŋwaane. Ba ta maa we, “Zem dɛ dento, Benjamin sɔ-yuu kom wora ko jei mo Isarele ne.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Debam nam ya na dɛ yiga dé du duuri we dé bá pa ba di dé wolowolo bukɔ to, dé laam wó na kaana yei ne mo, se dé pa Benjamin tiina baara balo fenfee na daare to?”

english_verse: Again the Israelites asked, “Did any of the tribes stay away from the meeting at Mizpah?” After asking around, they discovered that no one had come from Jabesh in Gilead.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, ba ya jeeli nɔɔna bam ni mo, ye ba wo nɛ Jabese Gilead nɔɔna bam wolowolo da.

translation_verse: Babɛ sem na yi Jabese Gilead to, mo ba maane we bukɔ-pwoli bia yana (

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam wo ma tiini ko chɔge Benjamin tiina bam ŋwaane, kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ sɛ se gwoŋo mo peini Isarele dwia yam tetare ne.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Ba kɔgɔ kom nakwa bam ma ta ba we, “Benjamin kaana bam maama tege ba ti. Dé laam nam wó na kaana yei ne mo se dé pa balo na daare Benjamin dwi dem wone to?

english_verse: If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out.
translation_verse: Benjamin dwi tiina balo na daare to jege se ba puli mo. Isarele sɔ-yuu dedoa tete ba jege se ko jei.

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Debam nam dɛ yiga dé du duuri dento mo we, ‘Sensɔle-balɔrɔ wó taa wo wolo maama na wó pa Benjamin tiina bam o bukɔ to yuu ne.’ Konto ŋwaane, dé bá wane dé pa-ba dé bukwa se ba ji ba kaana.”

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Ba ma boŋe ba ja we, “Baŋa Wɛ kuri dem dé na yeini dé di bene maama Siloo ne to bá daane de yi.” Siloo wo Bɛtel teo kom baŋa seeni mo. Ko ta maa wo chwoŋa kalo na nwoŋi Bɛtel ne ka vei Sɛkɛm to wɛ-puli seeni. Lebona kuri seeni mo konto.

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Ba ma pa Benjamin tiina bam ni dento we, “Véi-na á seigi Vini teeni kare sem wone,

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: se á ta‑á yera chwoŋa kam. Siloo tiina bukwa bam ná nwoŋi teo kom se ba tɔge ba sa kwɛɛra yam, se á zaŋe á na seigi mɛ to á nwoŋi á yi á ja-ba, baaro maama de o kaane, se á ja-ba á vo Benjamin laŋa kam á ta‑á jega.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Bukwa bam kwoa naa ba nabwa ná wo sɛ se á ta‑á di-ba, debam laam wó lwoori-ba we, ‘Popo, yage-na chwoŋa se nɔɔna bam taa jege á bukwa bam ba di. Kokuri jara yam na ke to, debam wo wane dé lage kaana dé pa-ba. Abam de nam wo yiri á ni dem, kolo ŋwaane abam tete wo kwei á bukwa á pa-ba.’ ”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Benjamin tiina bam déem ma seene ba ke konto. Ba vei Siloo seeni mo, ye ba kuri bukɔ-pwoli selo na sae to wone ba ja ba viiri, baaro maama de o kaane. Ba ma jwoori ba zoorem jei. Ba ma lɔ ba teene dem ba zoore de wone.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne mo Isarele tiina bam maama laam jwoori ba sam. Sɔ-yuu maama de diga maama jwoori ba jeiŋa jei mo.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto, pɛ déem ta tera Isarele ne. Nɔɔno maama maa ke o boboŋa na lage tei to.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom yere mo Elimeleka. O kaane yere maa ye Nawomi. O bakeiri sem yera maa ye Maalon de Kilion. Ba déem ye Eferata dwi dem tiina mo ba na nwoŋi Judah teo, Bɛtelehem. Ba ma seene ba vo ba zoore Moaba teo kom ne.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Ba na wora to, Elimeleka ma te ye o daare Nawomi de o bakeiri selei sem.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Banto ma swo Moaba bukwa ba ma ke ba kaana. Dedoa yere mo Orepa, wodwoŋi wom yere maa ye Ruf. Ba déem ma zo Moaba ne ba yi bena fuga.

english_verse: Mahlon and Chilion also died. Now Naomi had no husband or sons.
translation_verse: Maalon de Kilion de déem ma te. Ko laam ma daare Nawomi, ye o daa ba jege baro naa bu-baara.

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Ba maama ma zaŋe ba yage ba déem na zoore mɛ to ye ba tɔge chwoŋa ba maa vei Judah teo kom.

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Nawomi ma ta de o bu-kaana balei bam o we, “Abam maama jwoori-na á niina tei. Baŋa Wɛ wó ke abam lanyerane, nenɛɛne abam ya na ke amo de á banna bam lanyerane tei to.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Wɛ wó pa abam chwoŋa se á zo banna badwonna ye á na yazura ba sam ne.” O ma kukwori-ba ye ba keeri bɔge-bɔge.

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Dé bá yage‑m! Dé wó tɔge nmo mo dé vo n nɔɔna bam tei.”

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Nawomi maa we, “A bukwa bam, jwoori-na á daare-ne. Bɛŋwaane mo á boŋe se á tɔge-ne á vo? Amo daa lage a lo bakeiri se ba ji abam banna mo na?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Jwoori-na á sam, se a tiini a kwe a kɛ ban-zore. A ya ná maŋe a boŋe we a wó wane a lo bia, ye a ná nɛ baro zem se a daare a lo bakeiri mo de,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: abam ta wó jeini á cheigi se á zo-ba na? Abam bá zo banna badwonna na? A bukwa bam, ko bá ke konto. Ko tiini ko chamma amo yerane ko dwoi abam, kolo ŋwaane Baŋa Wɛ mo chɔge a yiga.”

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Nawomi na nɛ konto to, o ma ta de Ruf o we, “N wo nɛ na? Nmo yuudwoŋi wom maa jwoori o nɔɔna bam tei se o daare o taa zuli ba dwi jwona yam mo. Nmo de kwaane se n ke konto.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Ruf ma leiri‑o o we, “Yé fe-ne se a ke kolo a na vae to, se a bá ywori n kwaga ne. Nmo na lage n vo jei selo maama to, amo de wó tɔge a vo. Nmo na wó ta‑n zoore mɛ to, amo de wó zo dáane. Nmo nɔɔna bam wó taa ye amo de nɔɔna. Wɛ wolo nmo na zuli to mo, amo de wó zuli.

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: Nmo na wó ba n te mɛ to, dáane mo amo de wó te se ba suli-ne da. Wɛ wó waare-ne lanyerane nenɛɛne a ná sɛ se woŋo pɔɔre debam daane ye ko dae toone yerane.”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Nawomi na maane we Ruf seene o yia se o tɔge‑o to, o daa wo tage kolokolo.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Ba ma vo taa ba vo ba yi Bɛtelehem. Ba na yi da to, ko ma ke teo kom nɔɔna bam yaau. Kaana bam ma bwei daane ba we, “Nawomi mo tento na?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Nawomi ma ta o we, “Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom pɛ se a ŋwea ke cham mo. Konto ŋwaane, daa á yé bwoŋi-na a yere we Nawomi. Nam ta‑á bwoi a yere we Mara.

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: A na nwoŋi ywo-seeni to, a jeŋa wonnu déem daga dedɛ. Baŋa Wɛ laam ma pa se a jwoori de je-kore. Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom mo lɔge a kwaga ne ye o daare o ja cham dedɛ o ba a baŋa ne. Konto to, bɛŋwaane mo á daa wó ta‑á bwoi a yere we Nawomi? Ko ba jege kuri.”

english_verse: One day, Ruth said to Naomi, “Let me see if I can find someone who will let me pick up the grain left in the fields by the harvest workers.” Naomi answered, “Go ahead, my daughter.” So immediately Ruth went out to pick up grain in a field. She didn't know it was owned by Boaz, a relative of Naomi's husband Elimelech, as well as a rich and important man.
translation_verse: Ruf ma nwoŋi o vo o beeri kare sem wone. O ma tɔge tontoŋena bam kwaga o lare mena yam. Ko na lage ko wonnu to, o ma vo o yi kara kalo na ye Bowaza nyem to. Wonto nwoŋi Elimeleka sɔ-yuu kom mo.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Ko na ke fee to, Bowaza ma nwoŋi Bɛtelehem teo wo o yi kara kam. O ma ware o tontoŋena bam o we, “Baŋa Wɛ taa wo á tei ne!” Ba ma sɛ ye ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ nmo swolim!”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Bowaza ma bwei o tontoŋena yiga tu wom o we, “Bukɔ wom ye wɔ bu mo?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Yiga tu wom ma leiri o we, “O ye Moaba tiina bukɔ mo ye o tɔge de Nawomi o ba ywo.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: O nam lwoori-ne mo se a pa‑o chwoŋa se o taa tɔge tontoŋena bam kwaga o lare mena yam. O tu zezeŋa ne mo o toŋe ywo ye o laam zaŋe o vo se o jeini vwei dem ne.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Bowaza ma vo o ta de Ruf o we, “A bukɔ, cheigi-ne. Daa‑n yé véi nɔn-gaa kara n lare mena, ko ná dae kara kanto ne. Maŋe ywo-seeni n tɔge de kaana bam se á ta‑á toŋa.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Maane se n nii ba na wó gwei mena yam mɛ de mɛ to, se n ta‑n wo kaana bam tei ne. Amo kaane baara bam se ba yé daane‑m. Na-nyɔm ná jege‑m, se n twei na kɔɔra balo nɔn-donno tem na mɔɔne na ba ke da to wone n nyɔ.”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Bowaza ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo lɔre woŋo kolo maama n na ke n pa Nawomi, ko zege n baro wom na tega se ko ba ko yi zem to. A nigi we n yage n kwo, de n nu, de n teo kom kwaga ne mo, ye n daare n ba n zoore ywo, de nɔɔna balo n na maŋe n yeiri to.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wó jwoori o ŋwe nmo keim-laaro tem jene, pa se n na wo-laaro dedɛ o tei ne. N tu Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom tei mo se o yarege o vɔna o kwoli‑m, ye wonto wó seene o woli‑m.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Ruf ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, a ke n lei. N tiini n ke-ne lanyerane pa se a bochare zuri de n taane dem, ye a maŋe a wo yi n tontoŋena bam dedoa de.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Ba na jeini se ba di wodiu to, Bowaza ma ta de Ruf o we, “Ba n woli debam wone se dé di wodiu.” O ma jeini tontoŋena bam tei ne se o di. Bowaza ma daare o pa‑o men-wɔa. O ma di o su ye o daare kodwoŋi.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Ruf laam ma zaŋe o maa vei se o lare mena yam. Bowaza ma pa o nɔn-donno tem ni o we, “Pa-o-na chwoŋa se o taa lare mena yam, de ko ná maŋe ko ye men-zwaro tem na wo mɛ to de. Á yé che-na o yiga.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Á ná wora á pɛ mena yam, le-na men-ŋona yadwonna á paale á de tega ne se o wane o lare-ya. Yé bwɛ-o-na.”

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Ruf ma vo kara kam o wora o lare mena yam se ko taa vei dedaan-ni ne. O ma fere-ya ye o na se ko maŋe de kuriwaa bu dedoa.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: O ma kwei mena yam o zeŋe o jwoori teo kom wone ye o vo o bere o baro-nu Nawomi o na nɛ ko ma tei to. O ma daare o pa‑o wodiu kolo o ya na di o daare to.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Nawomi ma bwei‑o o we, “N vei n toŋe wɔ kara ne mo ye n na tento maama? Ko ná ye wolo na nii n baŋa ne to, Wɛ wó swɛ o swolim.” Ruf ma ta o bere‑o o na vei o toŋe nɔɔno wolo kara ne to, ye o we, “Nɔɔno wom yere mo Bowaza.”

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Nawomi ma fɔge o ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ Bowaza swolim! Wɛ ta yeini o ke lanyerane o pae nɔn-ŋwena de balo na tege to.” O ta ma ta o we, “Bowaza ye debam yera nɔɔno wolo na maŋe se o nii debam baŋa ne to.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Ruf daa ta ma ta o we, “Kolo na woli da to mo ye o pɛ chwoŋa se a tɔge de o tontoŋena bam a lare mena yam se ko taa nii ba kara kam totoŋa maama ná ti.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Nawomi ma leiri o we, “A bukɔ, n ná tɔge de Bowaza tontoŋ-kana bam n toŋa, ko gara. N ná vei nɔn-gaa kara, ba wae ba daane‑m.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ruf ma seene o ke konto. O ma sale Bowaza tontoŋena bam yera ne o lare mena yam se ba ba ba ti mena yam zagem maama. O déem maa zoore o baro-nu Nawomi tei ne.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe, Nawomi ma ta de Ruf o we, “A bukɔ, ko maŋe se a kwaane a lage jeiŋa jei a pa‑m, se n ta‑n zoore da dedaane yazura.

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Chega to, Bowaza wolo n na toŋe o tontoŋ-kana bam tei ne to ye debam yera nɔɔno mo. Zem dedaan-ni ne o wó taa wo mena ferem jeiga kam ne se ba chaare o mena yam.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Véi n swɛ n yera n daare n kwɛ n tete lanyerane de terale nuga dedaane gwaaro telo na lana to. Laam zaŋe n vo mena ferem jeiga kam se n jeeri‑o. Nam yé pa se o lɔre nmo ko taa nii o na di wodiu o ti to.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: O ná vei se o peini, maane o na tigi o dɔa mɛ to, se n laam vo n zeiŋi o gare-jale dem o nɛ sem seeni ye n daare n peini dáane. O wó ta de nmo n na wó ke woŋo kolo to.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Ruf ma leiri o we, “N na tage kolo maama to, amo wó ke.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Ruf déem ma vo mena ferem jeiga kam o ke kolo o baro-nu wom na tage o bere‑o to.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Bowaza na di wodiu o ti to, o wo ma pwoli lanyerane. O ma vo men-pwoa yam teiŋa ne o tigi da o dɔa. Ruf ma lɔɔre o vo mɛmɛ o yi o tei. O ma puri o gare-jale dem o nɛ sem seeni ye o peini dáane.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Tete-koro ne Bowaza yera maa sae ye o pipiri. O ma pɔpɔ o na kaane na tigi o nɛ sem seeni.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: O ma bwei o we, “Nmo ye wɔ mo?” O ma leiri o we, “N bukɔ Ruf mo. Amo tu, nmo ye debam yera nɔɔno wolo na maŋe se n nii amo baŋa ne to mo. Nam kwei n gare-jale n ma n pu amo se a zo n woro kom wone.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Bowaza ma leiri o we, “A bukɔ, Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ nmo swolim. Nmo lanyerane keim dento dwoni faŋa keim dem. N wo sɛ n tɔge teo kom nɔn-donno tem kwaga, ba ya ze jege wonnu naa ba ná ye zora de.

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: A bukɔ, nam yé ta‑n fona. N na lage woŋo kolo to, a wó ke a pa‑m. Teo kom nɔɔna bam maama maane we n ye ka-yero mo.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Ko ye chega mo we amo ye n yera nɔɔno, se nɔɔno wodwoŋi wora o na wo yiga ne o dwoi amo se o nii n baŋa ne.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Ta‑n tigi ywo-seeni tete dento maama, se tega ná poore, dé wó bwei dé nii o boboŋa tɔge keim dento naa ya ba tɔga. O ná sɛ se o ke konto, ko lamma. A dugi de Baŋa Wɛ wolo na ŋwe to yere we, o daa ná wo sɛ, amo wó taa nii n baŋa ne. Peini ywo-seeni se ko taa vei te-pora.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Ruf ma peini Bowaza nɛ sem seeni. O ma daare o gwoni tega o zaŋe lela se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé na‑o. Kokuri to, Bowaza ba lage se nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre we Ruf tu o tei.

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Bowaza ma ta o we, “Dɔne n gare-vɔɔ kom n lware tega ne.” O ma lware-ko. Bowaza ma lwo chaara bwɛ seredo o ke da o daare o ja o zeŋe‑o. O laam ma jwoori o vo teo kom wo.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: ye o we, “O we a yé jwoori de je-kore. O ma pa-ne mena yanto maama.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Nawomi laam ma ta de Ruf o we, “Nam zuri n yera se dé nii tento maama na lage ko ke tei to. Bowaza ná wo nɛ taane dem kuri, o bá sii.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Bowaza ma vo teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni o jeini mɛ nakwa bam déem na jei ba di taane to. Ko na ke fee to, o yera nɔɔno wolo de daa na tiini o bwola ye o ta o taane to ma tɔge da o maa kɛa. Bowaza ma bwoŋi‑o o we, “A choro, ba n jeini ywo.” O ma vo o jeini da.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Bowaza ma bwoŋi teo kom nakwa fuga o pa ba de jeini ba tei ne. Ba na jeini to,

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: o ma ta de o choro kom o we, “Nawomi laam nwoŋi Moaba o jwoori o ba. O maa lage se o kwei debam choro Elimeleka tega kam o yeigi.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Amo na boŋe tei to, ko maŋe se n ta‑n yei ko ni ne. Nmo ná laga se n yeigi tega kam, se n yeigi-ka nakwa bam de nɔɔna balo maama na jei ywo to yiga ne. N ná lage n jwoŋi-ka, nam jwoŋi! N daa‑n ná ba laga, se n ta se a lɔre. Nmo mo wó da yiga se n yeigi-ka. Nmo nam ná wo yeigi-ka, amo wó wane a yeigi.” Nɔɔno wom ma leiri o we, o wó yeigi-ka.

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Bowaza maa we, “Tɔ. N nam ná yeigi tega kam Nawomi tei ne, ta‑n yei we, nmo wó lɛɛre n swo Ruf na ye kadeim ye o nwoŋi Moaba to n woli da. Konto mo wó pa se tega kam maŋe o bar-dwooru wom dwi jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom na nigi konto to, o ma ta o we, “Ko nam ná ye konto, amo daa bá yeigi tega kam. A ná yeigi-ka, a bia jwa bá taa tei-ka. Nmo nam ná wó leiri a yuu ne n yeigi-ka, se n ke konto.”

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Bowaza choro kom na tage o we, Bowaza mo wó yeigi tega kam to, o ma le o natere o pa‑o.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Bowaza laam ma ta de nakwa bam, de balo maama na wora to o we, “Abam maama zem nɛ we amo yeigi woŋo kolo maama ya na ye Elimeleka nyem to, ko woli de o bia Kilion, de Maalon de wonnu maama Nawomi tei ne.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye Moaba tiina bukɔ Ruf wolo na ye Maalon kadeim to, amo jwoŋi‑o a woli da pa se o ye a kaane. Konto wó pa se too wom yere taa wo o jejegero baŋa ne, ye o dwi taa twoŋi taa dé teo kom ne. Abam zem maane we ko ye chega.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Nakwa bam de balo maama na wo teo kom manchwo-peena yam ni ne to ma sɛ ye ba we, “Debam seene dé na kolo na ke to. Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se kaane wolo n zem na swo to lo bia, nenɛɛne Racheli de Leah déem na loge bia pa se Isarele dwi dem daga to. Wɛ wó pa se nmo tiini n ji nadum Eferata teo ne ye n ta‑n jege yere Bɛtelehem teo ne.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wó pa kaane wonto lo bia dedɛ o pa‑m, pa se n dwi dem yere zaŋe nenɛɛne Judah de Tamara déem na loge Pɛreza ye o pa Judah sɔŋɔ kom yale tei to.” Bowaza dwi dem se ko yi David

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Teo kom kaana bam laam ma ta de Nawomi ba we, “Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de tia! Kokuri to, o zem pɛ‑m naa se o taa nii n baŋa ne. Wɛ wó pa se bu wom yere zaŋe Isarele tiina maama tei ne!

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Wonto wó pa se n ŋwea daa taa jege ywoni ye o fɔge o nii nmo baŋa ne n kokweero maŋa ne. N bu-kaane Ruf mo loga. Wonto nam tiini o swoi‑m lanyerane ye o dwoi bu-baara barepɛ n tei ne.”

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Kaana balo na zoore ba bwola de-ba to maa we, “Nawomi bu mo tento.” Ba ma pa bu wom yere we Obeda. Wonto déem mo loge Jesse. Jesse de ma ba o lo Pɛ David.

english_verse: Here is a list of the ancestors of David: Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, and Perez.
translation_verse: Obeda déem ma lo Jesse. Jesse de ma lo Pɛ David.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Elikana. O déem nwoŋi Eferata dwi dem wone mo, de Zufa sɔ-yuu kom ne. O kwo yere maa ye Jeroham, ye o nabaara ye Elihu, de Tohu, de Zufa. O déem zoore Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam teo kodwoŋi ne, ko yere mo Rama.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Elikana kaana déem ye balei mo. Ba dedoa yere mo Hanna, wodwoŋi wom yere maa ye Penina. Penina déem maa jege bia ye Hanna ba jege bu.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Bene maama ne, Elikana yeini o zege Rama ne o ja o diga kam maama mo o vo wara-jei sem na wo Siloo ne to se o zuli Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ, ye o daare o ke kaanem o pa‑o. Eli bia balei bam, Hofini dedaane Finehase déem mo ye Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam Siloo ne.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Elikana ná yeini o ke kaanem konto, o yeini o maŋe nɔna yam mo o pa Penina, ye o daare o kwei yadwonna o pa o bia bam de.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye Hanna, Elikana yeini o maŋe nɔna yam kuni belei o pa‑o, o na tiini o swoi‑o to ŋwaane mo. Baŋa Wɛ nam wo pɛ pwola se wonto lo bia.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Hanna ka-dwoŋi Penina maa yeini o ke‑o o mɔna, ye o daare o pae ko zoore o yera lanyerane.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Ko maa ye konto mo bene de bene. Ba ná vei Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem ne, Penina wó tiini o pa ko chɛ Hanna yera mo. O de déem maa yeini o ve se o di wodiu, ye o lɛɛre o da keira yerane taa.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: O baro Elikana laam ma yeini o bwei we, “Hanna, bɛŋwaane mo ye n ve wodiu. Bɛ mo ye n wo tiini ko chɔge konto? Yé ta‑n keera. Amo ba dwoi bia fuga n tei ne na?”

english_verse: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Maŋa dedoa ne, ba na vei Siloo ye ba di ba ti to, mo Hanna zaŋe o zo wara-jei sem ne, se o ware Baŋa Wɛ. Konto de Wɛ kaanem tu Eli déem ya jei diga kam ni ne, o na yeini o jei mɛ to.

english_verse: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
translation_verse: Hanna yiga ma tiini ka nyɔne, ye o keera. O ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ,

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: ye o pwooli o we, “Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo ye nmo tontoŋeno mo. Nii lɛɛro tento a na wo te wone to, se n guli amo gula. Nmo ná wo swei amo swia, ye n ná pɛ-ne bakeira, amo nam lage a jwoori a kwei‑o mo a pa nmo, se o ŋwea maama wone o taa ye nmo nyem. Fan-choa de nam bá fɔge ka tɔge o yuu ka kɛ.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Hanna wɛ-lworo kom maama déem ke o bochare ne mo. O ni-vɔɔro tem déem mage daane mo, ye o kwora ba zaŋa. Eli na nɛ konto to, o déem boŋe we kaane wom nyɔge sana mo o su.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: O ma ta de Hanna o we, “Nmo zo ywo se n bere n sa-nyɔre totoŋa mo na? Yage n sa-nyɔre kikia yam konto!”

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Yé ta‑n boŋe we amo ga ye ka-yɔɔ mo, se ko ye a wo mo chɔge dedɛ ko ja kɛ jeŋa. Konto mo tei a tiini a lwoori Wɛ.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Eli laam ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ko nam ná ye konto, zaŋe n vo de yazura, se Isarele tiina Wɛ wom wó pa‑m n na beeri kolo to.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Hanna ma leiri o we, “Amo tu. A ke n lei. Wɛ wó pa a kikia su n yi.” O ma zaŋe o viiri, o vo o di wodiu. O yiga daa maa wo nyɔne.

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Tega na poore tetete to, Elikana diga tiina bam maama daa ma zo wara-jei sem ne ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ, ye ba daare ba jwoori sɔŋɔ Rama ne. Elikana déem ma peini de o kaane Hanna. Baŋa Wɛ ma sɛ Hanna na lwoori kolo o tei ne to.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Hanna ma ba o ja puga ye o lo bakeira. O ma pa bu wom yere we ‘Samuwel’. Kokuri to, o déem tage mo o we, “Amo lwoori Baŋa Wɛ mo ye a jwoŋi‑o.” Hanna ke Samuwel Wɛ jeŋa ne

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Bene dedwoŋi déem daa ma yi se Elikana de o diga tiina bam jwoori ba vo Siloo ba ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ, se Elikana de kwei ni delo o ya na tiŋi o pa Wɛ to.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Hanna maa wo tɔge de-ba o vo. O déem tage de o baro wom mo o we, “Yage se a ná tu a kwori bu wom yele, a tete wó ja‑o a vo wara-jei sem se a ke‑o Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ne. O maa wó maŋe da se ko vo ko yi o toone.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Elikana ma leiri o we, “Nam ke kolo maama na maŋe ko pa‑m to. Maŋe ywo se bu wom waare. Baŋa Wɛ nam wó pa se o ni dem ji chega ko pa‑m.” Hanna ma maŋe sɔŋɔ ne ye o kɔne o bu wom.
