english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Hanna ma ta de Eli o we, “Amo tu. Ko na ye chega to, amo mo ye kaane wolo déem na zege n tei ne ye a lwoori Baŋa Wɛ to.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Ko ye bu wonto ŋwaane mo a ya lwoori Baŋa Wɛ, ye o pa-ne a na lage kolo to.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Konto to, a lage o jwoori a kwei‑o mo a pa Baŋa Wɛ. Bu wom ŋwea kam maama wone, o ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo.” O na tage konto to, ba ma kuni nadwoona ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ dáane.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ, nmo ye Wo-pwoŋo Tu ye n dwoŋi tera! Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa tera o na mae dede‑m. Peo kodwoŋi daa tera, ko na jege dam ne debam Wɛ wom!

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ye Wɛ wolo na yei totoŋe maama ni ne to mo. O maa bore nɔɔna bora ba totoŋa ŋwaane. Konto ŋwaane, yage-na ni-wɛɛle taane! Kweele-na á kamunni ŋwɛ selo á na jege to á yage tega ne.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛra tɛ sem bwori ye ba dam maama ti. Nabwona dam laam za fɔge de puli mo taa.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Balo ya na yeini ba di ba sui to laam wora ba beeri totoŋa se ba ma na ba ni-wodiu. Balo kana ya na wɔe to de laam maa di lanyerane ba sui. Kadega kam loge bia barepɛ mo. Wolo bia ya na daga to laam tu o ga o bu-kɔgɔ kom.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ mo jaane toone de ŋwea o tui. O maa pae se nɔɔna tu churu, ye o ta pae se badwonna zaŋa.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Wonto mo pae se nɔɔna ye nabwona, ye o ta pae se badaara ye jejegero tiina. O wae o pa se dedoa wo tega ne, ye o daare o zeiŋi wodwoŋi.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: O yeini o liiri yiniga tu mo bworu wone. O maa le nabwom o lɛɛro wone. O laam maa pa ba taa tɔge ba jei pa-bia tetare ne, se nɔɔna taa pa-ba zula lanyerane. Kokuri, tega kam baŋa maama ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem mo, ye wonto mo chwi woŋo maama ko jeiga ne.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: O nii balo na zege de chega ba pa‑o to baŋa ne mo. Nɔn-balwaaro nam wó tɔge lim wone mo ba jei. Dam yerane ware de jwoŋi nɔɔno de yage.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ mo wó chɔge o dona bam maama. O lage o zege wɛyuu ne mo o bage o yage ba baŋa ne! Baŋa Wɛ maa wó di nabiina maama taane. Ko nam ná ye pɛ wolo o na tiŋi to, o wó pa‑o dam se nɔɔna maama taa pa‑o zula.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Elikana de Hanna ma jwoori ba sɔŋɔ Rama ne. Samuwel ma maŋe Siloo ne. O déem toŋe o pa Baŋa Wɛ mo, ye kaanem tu Eli nii o baŋa ne. Eli bia bam taane

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: Ba ta maa yeini ba chɔge Wɛ kaanem totoŋa chullu tem. Kokuri, nɔɔna ná tu se ba ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ, ye nɔna yam ta na wora ya saŋa maŋa kalo to, mo Wɛ kaanem tu tontoŋeno wom wó da o ba ye o zei da-chɔrɔ na jege nyea yatɔ to.

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom laam wó chu o le nɔna yalo na wora ya saŋe to wone. Ko ná maŋe ko ye kambia ne, naa nakeina ne, naa woŋo kolo maama ne, nɔna yalo maama da-chɔrɔ kom na wó tore ko zɔ to mo wó taa ye Wɛ kaanem tu wom nyem. Ba déem jege kikia yam konto mo ba ke de Isarele tiina balo maama na tu Siloo se ba ke kaanem to.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Se ko woli da to, ba déem ná yeini ba go varem ye ba ta wo lɔɔne varem wom lara ba zwɛ bimbini dem baŋa ne se ba daare, Wɛ kaanem tu tontoŋeno wom wae o tui o tɛ we, “Pa-ne nɔn-gwei delo kaanem tu wom na wó wɔ to, se o ba lage o jwoŋi nɔn-saŋa n tei ne se o di.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ná zege se o ta we, “Yage se dé ná zwɛ lara kam dé daare, se n laam le nɔna yalo n na lage to,” tontoŋeno wom wó leiri mo o we, “Aawo! Pa-ne lela! Ko ná dae konto, a laam wó vere-ya de dam mo.”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Eli bia bam wɛleere dem déem tiini de gaale mo ye de chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. Kokuri, ba déem pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ kaanem pɛɛra yam ba jege kuri.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Bene maama, o nu wom yeini o sɔ gare-bwora balaŋa mo se o pa‑o. O ná tɔge de o baro o ba wara-jei sem se ba ke bene dem kaanem, o yeini o ja gare-bwora kam mo o ja o ba o pa‑o.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Eli de maa yeini o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o ke Elikana de o kaane Hanna yuu ne o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó pa kaane wonto lo bia o pa‑m, se ba leiri bu wonto yuu ne, o na kwei bu wom o pa Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane.” Ba de laam maa yeini ba jwoori ba sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma seene o ke zaane o ke Hanna yuu ne. O ma lo bakeiri setɔ dedaane busankane selei. Se ko ná ye Samuwel, wonto déem ke nɔɔno mo, ye o toŋe o pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Amo bia bam, Baŋa Wɛ nɔɔna bam na jege á taane ba tɛ tei to ba lamma. Nam yage-na kikia yam konto.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wolo ná ke o chɔge o dwoŋi nabiinu yiga, Baŋa Wɛ ta wó wane o zege kotu kwaga ne. Nɔɔno nam ná ke o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ tete yiga mo, o lage o ke tɛ mo?” De konto maama de, Eli bia bam ta wo sɛ o taane dem. Kokuri, Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa maŋe ya ja mo se o go-ba.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Ko daare, Samuwel déem fɔge o ke nɔɔno mo. Baŋa Wɛ dedaane nabiina maama maa lage o taane. Waarem delo na wó ba Eli sɔŋɔ baŋa ne to

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Wɛ tontoŋeno wodwoŋi déem ma ba Eli tei ye o we: “Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo tento: Isarele tiina bam déem ta na ye kabɛ Ejipti pa-faro wom jeŋa ne to, amo déem veere a tete dedaane nmo nabaaro Aron.

english_verse: Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar. But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
translation_verse: Bɛ nam mo tei ye abam gwooni pɛɛra yalo amo na pɛ ni se á jwoŋi-ya á ma á ke kaanem á pa-ne a diga kam wone to? Nmo nam na ke tei to bere we n tiini n kɔre n bia bam se ko dwoni n na kɔre amo tei to. Kokuri, abam jege amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam wodi-laaro tem mo á di á nu bigila bigila.

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Amo wolo na ye Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom to ni dem mo tento: Amo déem ya pwooli mo we, á sɔ-yuu kom dedaane á dwi dem wó taa ye a kaanem tiina se ko taa vei wuu. Amo laam nam tɛ a we, ko daa bá taa ye konto. Kokuri, amo wó zuli balo dwi maama na zuli-ne to mo, se a daare a nii balo yiga na tere a wone to a chweese.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Ta‑n yei we maŋa lage ka yi se a pa se n dwi dem ti. Nɔn-kweo daa bá taa wora n kwo dwi dem wone. Nmo diga tiina bam maama wó te ba nɔn-donne maŋa ne mo.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Nmo wó na lɛɛro na tu amo wara-jei sem baŋa ne tei to. Nmo ta wó na amo na wó ke Isarele tiina bam lanyerane tei to, se ko daare abam dwi dem ne, nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá kwe se o laam te.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Amo nam za wó pa se n bia bam wo dedoa daare se o taa toŋe a kaanem bimbini dem totoŋa. Wonto yia nam wó dwei pa se wo-chechɔgɔ yerane taa wora. Abam dwi dem na daare to maa wó te ba nɔn-donne maŋa ne.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Nmo bia bam balei Hofini dedaane Finehase wó da daane mo ba te dɛ dedwe wone. Ko na wó ke-ba tei to ye se n wane n lɔre we kolo maama a na tage to wó ji chega.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Amo laam wó kuri kaanem tu wodwoŋi na jege chega lanyerane to. Kotu wó taa toŋe ye o ke a boboŋa na lage kolo maama to o pa-ne. A maa wó pa se o dwi tiina fɔge ba puli lanyerane, se ba taa toŋe ba pae pɛ wolo a na wó kuri to.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Abam dwi dem wone balo na wó daare to laam wó vo kaanem tu wom konto tei ba lwoori sabu dedaane wodiu. Ba wó ta ba we, ‘Popo, pa se debam de da dé toŋe kaanem tiina totoŋa yam, se debam de da dé laŋe wodiu.’ ”

english_verse: Samuel served the Lord by helping Eli the priest, who was by that time almost blind. In those days, the Lord hardly ever spoke directly to people, and he did not appear to them in dreams very often. But one night, Eli was asleep in his room,
translation_verse: Eli yia yam déem lage ya dwei mo ye o ba nae lanyerane. Tete dedoa, o maa tigi o tiga jei ne o dɔa.

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: Samuwel de maa tigi wara-jei sem ne se ko maŋe dedaane Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam o dɔa. Ko déem ye tete-koro mo, ye Wɛ min-zwoŋo kom ya ta wo dwei.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma bwoŋi Samuwel. O de ma leiri o we, “Nii-ne da.”

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: O ma zaŋe o duri o zo Eli tei ye o we, “A kwo, nmo na bwoŋi-ne to, nii-ne da.” Eli ma ta ded‑o o we, “Amo wo bwoŋi‑m. Jwoori n vo n peini.” Bu wom ma jwoori o vo o peiga jei o peini.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma bwoŋi o yere o we, “Samuwel!” Samuwel ma pɛ o zaŋe wɛɛne. O ma duri o vo Eli tei ye o ta ded‑o o we, “A kwo, nii-ne da, n na bwoŋi-ne to.” Eli ta ma leiri o we, “A bu, amo wo bwoŋi‑m. Jwoori n vo n peini.”

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Samuwel déem ya ta wo me de Baŋa Wɛ. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ ya ta wo veere o kwora o bere‑o.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma bwoŋi Samuwel o ke kuni betɔ. Bu wom daa ma duri o vo Eli tei o we, “Amo kwo, n na bwoŋi-ne to, nii-ne da.” Ko laam ma ba Eli yuu ne we, ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo bwoi bu wom.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: O laam ma ta Samuwel o we, “Jwoori n vo n ta‑n tiga, se o daa ná bwoŋi‑m, se n ta we, ‘Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, ta‑n ŋɔɔna, se a ye n tontoŋeno ye a cheigi n taane dem mo.’ ” Samuwel ma seene o vo o peini o peiga jei ne.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma jwoori o ba o zege da. O ma bwoŋi‑o ne o ya na maŋe o bwoŋi tei to o we, “Samuwel! Samuwel!” Samuwel ma leiri o we, “Amo Tu, ta‑n ŋɔɔna, se a ye n tontoŋeno ye a cheigi n taane dem mo.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta o we, “Amo ti a yiga mo se a ke wo-kenkagele Isarele tiina bam wone. Balo maama na wó ni ko ŋwa to yera maa wó sɔɔre.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, a maŋe a wuuri a kaane‑o we, a lage a waare o diga kam taa wuu, o bia bam keim-lwanno tem ŋwaane. Kolo ŋwaane, Eli ya yei o bia bam na tiini ba lwɛ amo dedɛ tei to ni ne, ye o wo de-ba chwoŋa ne.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo, amo tage a du de Eli diga tiina bam a we, ‘Kaanem dwi de pɛɛra dwi daa bá taa wora, se ya wane ya saare ba tusim dem maŋa de maŋa.’ ”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Samuwel na nigi konto to, o ma lɛɛre o tigi da se tega vo ka poore. O laam ma pore Wɛ wara-jei sem manchwo-peena yam. Foone déem maa tiini de jege‑o. O ma ware se o ta kolo Wɛ na veere o bere‑o to de Eli.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Eli ma bwoŋi‑o we, “Amo bu Samuwel!” Samuwel ma leiri o we, “Nii-ne da.”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Eli laam ma bwei‑o o we, “O tage bɛ mo de nmo? Yé zaŋe n seigi kolokolo amo yiga ne, se Wɛ wó pa n tiini n na lɛɛro, nenɛɛne n ná wo tage kolo maama o na ŋɔɔne dede‑m to n bere ne.”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Samuwel ma tole Wɛ kwora kam maama nyɔ o bere‑o, o wo kweele kolokolo tega ne. Eli ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam mo konto. Yage se o ke kolo na wo o boboŋa ne to.”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Samuwel déem maa wora o ke nɔɔno, ye Baŋa Wɛ wo o tei ne. Ko ma pa se kolo maama Samuwel na tɛ to yeini ko ji chega.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam maama, ko na zege Dan ne se ko yi Beeriseba to, ba maama déem pɛ chega mo we Samuwel seene o ye Baŋa Wɛ sampwora mo chekke.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ta yeini o veere o tete mo Siloo ne. O maa wó yeini o ba Samuwel tei o ŋɔɔne ded‑o.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Samuwel de déem ma lwoni Baŋa Wɛ kwora pa ka yi Isarele tiina bam maama. Filisi tiina vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam Isarele tiina bam déem ma nwoŋi se ba vo ba kwaare jara de Filisi tiina bam. Ba ma vo ba tei ba vwoa Ebeneza seeni, ye Filisi tiina bam vo ba tei ba vwoa Afeka seeni.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Ba ma toŋe nɔɔna Siloo ne, se ba vo ba ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba ba ba tei ne. Ka maa ye jeiga kalo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na di paare cherubi sem tetare laŋa ne to mo. Eli bia balei, Hofini dedaane Finehase mo déem dɛ ba zeŋe dakaa kam ba ja ba ba.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina jar-keira balo na daare to ma zege jara kapworo ne ba jwoori ba ya na tigisi daane mɛ seeni to. Ba nakwa bam ma bwei daane ba we, “Bɛ mo ke ye Baŋa Wɛ pa se Filisi tiina bam wane debam zem konto?” Ba ta maa we, “Pa-na se dé toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo Siloo ba ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ba ywo-seeni. Konto wó pa se Baŋa Wɛ taa wo dé tei ne, ye o jwoŋi debam o yage dé dona bam jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam ma ni sɔɔ kom. Ba ma bwei daane ba we, “Sɔɔ konto na zaŋe Hiburu tiina bam vwoa yam ne to kuri mo bɛ?” Ba ma maane we ko ye Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam mo tu ka yi Isarele tiina bam na tigisi daane mɛ to.

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: Ko ma pa se foone tiini de zo Filisi tiina bam. Ba maa tɛ ba we, “Cham nam yi debam na! Ba wa yam mo tu ya zo ba tetare ne konto! Dé ta wo nɛ konto woŋo dwoŋi!

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Lɛɛro yi debam! Wɔ mo wó wane o jwoŋi debam o yage wa-dɛɛra yanto jeŋa ne? Ko ye wa yam konto mo déem pɛ se chanɛɛre dwi dwi ja Ejipti tiina bam kagoa kam ne ya go.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam, á pa-na dé di baare! Ke-na jara yam ne babɛ tei! Ko ná dae konto, dé lage dé ji Hiburu tiina bam kabɛ mo, nenɛɛne banto de déem na ye debam kabɛ tei to. Konto to, jaŋe-na de baare!”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam ma vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam, ye ba daare ba go Eli bia balei bam, Hofini dedaane Finehase. Eli toone

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Dento dɛ dem ne mo Benjamin dwi tu dedoa zege jara kapworo kom ne o duri o vo o yi Siloo. Nɔɔno wom ya kaare o gwaaro, ye kasolo taare o yuu maama, o wo na chɔge to ŋwaane.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Eli boboŋa maama déem nam ya duri ya da Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam kwaga mo, se o lɔre kolo na kea ka baŋa ne to. O ma vo o jei chwoŋa ni ne, se o cheigi o ni jara-keim dem taane. Nɔɔno wom ma ba o zo teo kom wo o ta jara yam laŋa ya na vei tei to. Ba na nigi to, teo kom tiina bam maama maa chwoosa ba yaga bɔge-bɔge.

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma leiri o we, “Ko ye lɛɛro mo dé nɛa. Isarele jar-keira bam duri Filisi tiina bam yiga ne se ba lu. Ba kɔgɔ dedɛ mo tega. Nmo de bia bam Hofini dedaane Finehase de tɔge ba te mo. Filisi tiina bam ta ma vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba viiri!”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom na yɔɔre o ta kolo na ke Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yera ne to, mo Eli yale o to o kwaga ne. O déem jei teo kom manchwo-peena ni ne mo, ye o to tega ne konto. O na yale o to o kolɔ-bea baŋa ne to, mo o ba bwori pa se o te. Kokuri to, o déem kwe mo dedɛ, ye o ta tiini o nu o gaale. Eli déem ya nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne bena finna mo.

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Eli bu Finehase kaane wom déem jege puga mo, ye ka be ka ti se o lo. O de ma ni we ba vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba viiri, ye o baro wom dedaane o baro kwo wom maama tega. O na nigi to, mo o puga dɛ ka virigi ka lage lora. O maa wo wane o wori.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: O na lage o te o lora kam baŋa ne to, kaana balo na lwori‑o se o lo to ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Nam vɔ wo, se n loge bakeira mo.” O maa wo leiri kolokolo.

english_verse: Instead she kept thinking about losing her husband and her father-in-law. So she said, “My son will be named Ichabod, because the glory of Israel left our country when the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: O ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom nwoŋi ko daare Isarele teo kom, ba na vere Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba ja ba viiri to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Ba ma ja-ka ba zo ba jwo-dɛɛre diga kam ye ba daare ba zege-ka jwoni dem kamɔgɔ kom teiŋa ne. Jwoni dem yere mo ye Dagon.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Asedodi tiina bam ma zaŋe ba vo ba zo diga kam. Ba ma na we Dagon to o yibia baŋa ne Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne. Ba déem ma jwoori ba gɔ-de ba chwi de zega jei sem ne.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Tega daa na poore to, mo ba nɛ we jwoni dem daa ta to Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam yiga ne. Jwoni dem yuu dedaane de jataala maama bwori mo te tigi diga kam ni ne dáa dáa. De yera yam yerane mo daare.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Konto mo pɛ se, dedaane zem maama, balo maama na yeini ba zo Dagon diga kam ne to ba sɛ se ba nɔne diga kam ni dem jei sem ba kɛ, ko ná maŋe ko ye balo na tu se ba kaane Dagon to de.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma pa ko tiini ko zo Asedodi tiina bam yera. Ko ma ni balo na zoore jei sem konto maama ne to ye foone zo-ba. O ma pa se kasili-nabiina ŋone ba yera ne.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Asedodi tiina bam na maane kolo na jege ko ke to, ba ma laare ba we, “Ko ye Isarele tiina Wɛ dem mo wora o waare debam, dedaane dé wɛ Dagon. Dé yé pa se wonto ni-gwonim dakaa kam maŋe debam tei ne ywo.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Ba ma la Filisi tiina dedɛɛra bam ba ke daane se ba jeini ba bane. Ba ma bwei-ba ba we, “Dé laam nam wó ke tɛ mo dedaane Isarele tiina wɛ dem dakaa kam?” Ba ma bwɛ ba ja ye ba we, “Pa-na se nɔɔna kwei-ka ba ja vo Gafa.” Ba ma seene ba ja-ka ba vo ba yi da.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Ba daa ma pa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam vo Ekoron. Ba na jaane-ka ba yi teo kom wo to, mo Ekoron tiina bam chwoosi ba yage ba we, “Ba jege Isarele tiina wɛ dem dakaa kam mo ba beene ywo! Nii ba na lage ba go debam de dé dwi dem maama tei!”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Ba ma toŋe ba la Filisi dedɛɛra bam ba ke daane, ye ba ta ba we, “Toŋe-na Isarele tiina wɛ dem dakaa kam se ka jwoori ka na nwoŋi mɛ to. Se ko ná dae konto, ka wó wane ka go debam dedaane dé dwi dem maama ka ti.” Vuvuga ma to teo kom maama ne, ba na kɔre toone to ŋwaane. Baŋa Wɛ ma pa se ko tiini ko zo ba yera.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Balo na wo tege to, kasili-nabiina mo ŋone ba yera ne. Nɔɔna bam déem maa kaase bɔge-bɔge.

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Ba ma bwoŋi ba kaanem tiina de ba yi-nara, ye ba bwei-ba ba we, “Dé wó ke Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam tetɛ mo? Dé wó tɔge chwoŋa kɔ mo dé toŋe-ka se ka jwoori ka vo ka jeiga?”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri ba we, “Abam ná lage á toŋe Isarele tiina Wɛ dem dakaa kam se ka jwoori ka na nwoŋi mɛ to, ko nam ye se á toŋe-ka dedaane pɛɛre mo. Ko dae se dakaa kam jwoori ka vo bwori. Pɛɛre dem konto mo á lage á ma‑á ywoori ba wɛ dem, se de yage á wɛleere dem jene de ma chɛ abam. Konto mo wó pa se á jwoori á na yazura ye á daare á lɔre kolo ŋwaane o na tiini o pa ko zo á yera to.”

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: se te taa nye nenɛɛne telo na jege á teene dem te chɔge to. Konto mo á wó pa Isarele tiina Wɛ dem jwoŋi zula. Dɛ delo, abam ná ke konto, o wó jwoori o dɔne o je-dɛa abam baŋa ne, de á jwona yam, dedaane á tega kam maama baŋa ne, se á daa yé na cham.

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Konto to, kwei-na dɛ á ke toroko-doŋo. Laam beeri-na naane delei na loga, ye ba ta wo kwei-de se ba ma toŋe to. Ja-na naane dem á lei de toroko kom se de taa vaŋe-ko, se á daare á pwɛ nwa balo naane dem na loge to á pe.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: ye á fɔge á nii. Naane dem ná lɛɛne debam siseini dem ye de kwei Bɛte-Semesa chwoŋa kam de maa kɛa, dé wó lɔre we ko ye Isarele tiina Wɛ dem mo seene o toŋe chanɛɛre dento o yage debam yera ne. Se naane dem ná tɔge chwo-gaa, dé wó lɔre we ko ke ko maŋe daane mo, se ko dae wo-lɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam ma seene ba ke konto. Ba déem beeri naane delei delo na loge to mo ba lei toroko yera ne. Ko daare ye ba pe de nwa bam sɔŋɔ ne.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Ba ma kwei Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba daŋe toroko kom baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba zege dakaa kalo sabu-seŋa baywoa de kasili-nabiina kamwaro tem na wo ka wone to ba ke da.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Bɛte-Semesa tiina bam déem ya wo ba bwollu tem ne mo ba gwei banina. Ba ma kwoni ba yuni ba nii, ye ba na Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam. Ko ma pa se ba wo tiini ko pwoli dedɛ.

english_verse: The cows left the road and pulled the cart into a field that belonged to Joshua from Beth-Shemesh, and they stopped beside a huge rock. Some men from the tribe of Levi were there. So they took the chest off the cart and placed it on the rock, and then they did the same thing with the bag of gold rats and sores. A few other people chopped up the cart and made a fire. They killed the cows and burned them as sacrifices to the Lord. After that, they offered more sacrifices.
translation_verse: Levi dwi tiina bam déem ya gɔge Baŋa Wɛ dakaa kam toroko kom baŋa ne ba ja tu tega. Ba ta ma kwei dakaa kalo sabu-seŋa kamwaro tem na wo ka wone to ba woli da. Ba ma zege tento maama peo kamunu kom baŋa ne. Dɛ dem konto ne Bɛte-Semesa tiina bam ma ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra de pɛɛra yadwonna ba kaane ba pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina dedɛɛra banu bam déem zege mo ba nii totoŋa yam konto maama. Ba laam ma jwoori ba vo Ekoron dɛ dem konto ne.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Sabu-seŋa kasili-nabiina kamwaro tenu tem déem zege te pae teene dento mo: Asedodi, de Gaza, de Asekelon, de Gafa, dedaane Ekoron. Filisi tiina bam déem kwei tento mo se ba ma ba ywoori Baŋa Wɛ ba wɛleere dem ŋwaane.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Ba sabu-seŋa baywoa yanu yam de maa zege ya pae teene denu delo dedɛɛra bam na nii de baŋa ne to. De maa ye te-fwaaro delo na lɔge de pe de dam to, ko woli de te-balwa bam na wo chege to. Peo kamunu kolo baŋa ne ba na zege Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam to daa ta wo Bɛte-Semesa tu Josua bwolo kom ne de zem maama mo, se ko taa ye maana de kolo na ke da to.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Bɛte-Semesa tiina bam ma bwei daane ba we, “Debam wone wɔ mo wó wane Baŋa Wɛ wom yiga ne o zege? O tiini o ye wose mo. Dé wó pa se o dakaa kam zege ywo ka vo nɔɔno wɔ tei ne mo?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Ba ma toŋe kwora Kiriaf-Jeerim tiina tei ne ba we, “Filisi tiina bam jaane Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba jwoori ba ba ba yage ywo-seeni mo. Konto to, ba-na á kwei-ka á ja á vo á tei.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Kiriaf-Jeerim tiina bam ma seene ba ba ba kwei Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam. Ba ma ja-ka ba vo ba zege nɔɔno wodwoŋi sɔŋɔ ne, o yere na ye Abinadaba. O déem zoore peo yuu ne mo. Ba ma kuri wonto bu Eleaza ye ba pwɛ‑o se o taa nii dakaa kam baŋa ne. Samuwel nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Samuwel déem ma zaŋe o ta de Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama o we, “Abam ná seene á seene yia mo se á jwoori Baŋa Wɛ tei ne, ko nam ye se á le Asetare jwona yam de jwo-yɔɔro tem maama á tetare ne á dole á yage, se á daare á lwei á wo maama á pa Baŋa Wɛ. Abam ná zuli wonto yerane, o wó jwoŋi abam Filisi tiina bam jeŋa ne o yage.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma seene ba dole Baal dedaane Asetare jwona yalo na wo ba tetare ne to ba yage. Ba laam ma sɛ se ba taa zuli Baŋa Wɛ yerane.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Samuwel ma toŋe ni o pa Isarele tiina bam se ba maama la ba jeeri Mizipa ne, se o de lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o pa-ba.

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma seene ba vo ba jeeri Mizipa ne. Ba na gilimi ba ti to, ba ma mɔ na ba lwo tega ne ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Dɛ dem konto maama ne, ba ya vɔge ba nia mo ye ba we, “Dé seene dé ke lwarem dé chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga.” Isarele tiina bam déem na wo Mizipa ne konto to, Samuwel mo tu o ji ba yiga tu.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam déem ma ni we Isarele tiina bam jeeri daane Mizipa ne. Ba dedɛɛra banu bam ma la ba jar-keira bam ba ke daane se ba vo ba kwaare jara de Isarele tiina bam. Isarele tiina bam na nigi ko ŋwa to, mo foone tiini de zo-ba.

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Samuwel ta na wora o ke kaanem dem o pa Baŋa Wɛ to, mo Filisi tiina bam fɔɔre ba twɛ se ba ja jara yam ba yi Isarele tiina bam. Ba ma yi da de Baŋa Wɛ zege wɛyuu ne o pa se doa tiini ka bage-ba pina-pina! Foone ma tiini de ja Filisi tiina bam, pa se ba duri Isarele tiina bam yiga ne ba jage jei maama ne!

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma da ko ŋwaane ba zege Mizipa ne, ba pare Filisi tiina bam taa, ba vo ba yi Bɛte-Kara kuri seeni. Ba maa jege-ba ba goe konto ye ba via.

english_verse: The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them. For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ko dɛ konto baŋa ne mo, ye Isarele tiina bam wane Filisi tiina bam. Baŋa Wɛ déem ma che-ba, pa se ba daa wo lɛɛne Isarele laŋa kam ne. Samuwel ta na ŋwe to, Baŋa Wɛ déem lɔge Filisi tiina bam kwaga ne mo.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma jwoori ba jwoŋi teene delo maama na wo Ekoron dedaane Gafa laŋa ne ye Filisi tiina bam ya vere-de ba tei ne to. Isarele tiina bam déem jwoori ba na ba tega kam ni maama mo. Yazura déem maa wora Isarele tiina bam dedaane Amori tiina bam laŋa ne.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samuwel déem nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne taa, ko vo ko yi o toone mo.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Bene maama ne, o déem yeini o vei o kare teene dento mo: Bɛtel, de Giligal, dedaane Mizipa. Jei sento maama ne mo o yeini o kwɛ nɔɔna bam taana o pa-ba.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: O nam ná yeini o ti, o daa yeini o jwoori Rama mo o vo o jeini o tete sɔŋɔ ne. O na wora to, o ta ma nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. O déem ma lɔ kaanem bimbini Rama ne o pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: O bu-kwea kam yere mo ye Joweli. Wolo na saŋe wonto kwaga to yere maa ye Abija. Ba déem yeini ba jeeri Beeriseba ne mo, ye ba nii Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Isarele nakwa bam laam ma la ba jeeri daane, ye ba vo Samuwel tei Rama ne.

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Leile konto, nmo tiini n kwe mo. N bia bam nam ba tɔge nmo nɛ-bwora. Konto to, tiŋi pɛ n pa debam, se kotu taa nii dé baŋa ne, nenɛɛne teene dedwonna dem na jege pwa tei to.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Nakwa bam na tage we ba lage pɛ to déem tiini ko daane Samuwel dedɛ. O ma lwoori Wɛ ko ŋwaane.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Konto to, za n sɛ ba kwora kam, se n daare n kaane-ba dedɛ se ba lɔre ba pɛ wom na wó toŋe tei ba yera ne to.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Samuwel laam ma tole Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to maama o bere nɔɔna balo na tu o tei se ba beeri pɛ to,

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: ye o we, “Wolo abam na beeri se o di paare á baŋa ne to na wó toŋe kolo á yera ne to mo tento: o lage o fe á bakeiri mo se ba ji o jar-keira. O wó pa ba badwonna taa chwo o jara-keim torokooro, se badaara taa diini sisein-nɔɔna, ye badaara duri torokooro tem yiga ne ba kwɛ chwoŋa kam ba pa‑o.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom lage o vere á kare selo na tiini se lamma to mo, de jei selo á na dugi Vini de Olivi teeni se wone to, se o daare o kwei-se o pa o tontoŋena.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: O ta maa wó jwoŋi á mena de á tio-bia fuga maama wone popɔra dedoa, se o kwei o pa o kwaga nɔɔna de o tontoŋena.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye abam tete tontoŋena, baara de kaana, de á naane, de á bonɛ, o lage o jwoŋi balo maama na lana to mo o taa tei se ba taa toŋe ba pa‑o.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: O ta lage o jwoŋi á vare-mumugu fuga maama wone popɔra dedoa mo. Abam tete de nam wó ji o kabɛ.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem ná tua ye á jege pɛ, á wó tiini á chwoosi á lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o woli abam, pɛ wom na bɛɛse abam tei to ŋwaane. Dɛ dem konto ne Baŋa Wɛ nam ba lage o cheigi á taane dem.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: Dé lage se dé taa nye nenɛɛne teene dedwonna dem na ye tei to mo. Dé pɛ wom wó taa nii dé baŋa ne, ye o ta wó tɔge dé yiga se dé yeini dé kwaare jara dwi maama!”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Samuwel ma cheigi nɔɔna bam ni taane dem maama, ye o de vo o lwoni woŋo maama o bere Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Nam sɛ ba taane dem n daare n tiŋi pɛ n pa-ba.” Samuwel ma sɛ, ye o yage ni o pa Isarele tiina bam se ba maama jwoori ba sam.

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Benjamin dwi tu wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Kisi. O maa ye nadum. O déem ye Abiyeli bu mo. O kwo-nakwe yere maa ye Zerora ye wonto de kwo yere ye Bekorafa. Banto déem nwoŋi Benjamin dwi tu Afiya sɔ-yuu kom ne mo.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Kisi bu dedoa déem wora, o yere mo ye Sɔɔl. O maa ye nenɔm ye o dwoŋi tera Isarele tiina bam maama wone. O déem ye nɔn-wagele mo chekke. O maa ye nɔn-doŋo ye o tiini o dɔra o dwoi o yuudwonna bam maama.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Kisi bonɛ sedwonna ywori se jei. O ma ta o bu Sɔɔl o we, “Ja dé tontoŋena bam wone dedoa se á vo á beeri bonɛ sem.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma seene o ke konto. Wonto de o tontoŋeno wom ma tole Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam maama, de Salisa jei sem maama, ba beeri bonɛ sem ba ga. Ba ma kɛ ba vo ba yi Saalim, ye ba wo nɛ-se dáane de. Ba ma daare ba tɔge Benjamin laŋa kam maama. Ba ta maa wo nɛ bonɛ sem jei sem konto mɛ mɛ.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Ba laam ma beeri ba vo ba yi Zufa. Sɔɔl ma ta de o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Pa se dé jwoori sɔŋɔ. Tento wɛɛne, amo kwo daa ba nii bonɛ sem, o laam jei o boŋe debam boboŋa mo, dé na daane to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Nii, Wɛ tontoŋeno dedoa wo teo konto ne. Nɔɔna tiini ba nege‑o, kokuri, kolo maama o na tɛ to yeini ko ke konto mo. Pa se dé beeri o jei dé vo, se dɛ delo wonto wó bere debam chwoŋa kalo de na wó tɔge to.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl laam ma bwei‑o o we, “Dé nam ná lage dé vo nɔɔno wom tei, bɛ mo dé wó ja dé vo dé pa‑o ye dé wodiu maama ti tento to? Kolokolo daa tera dé tampɔro tem wone, naa woŋo wora?”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Nii mo! Amo jege sabu-dale balaŋa. Amo wó kwei dento mo a pa‑o, se o bere debam chwoŋa kalo dé na wó da to.”

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl laam ma ta o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Ko nam lamma, dé kɛ.” Ba ma kwei chwoŋa ba maa vei teo kolo Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na zoore da to.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Ba na wora ba diini zwoŋo se ba vo ba yi teo kom to, mo ba jeeri bukwa na nwoŋi teo kom wone ba maa vei buga se ba mɔ na. Ba ma bwei-ba ba we, “Yi-naro wom zem wo ywo na?”

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Bukwa bam ma leiri ba we, “Ɛɛ! Nam ke-na lela, se o yɔɔre o wo abam yiga ne mo. Zem mo o daa ta tu debam teo. Kokuri, o lage o woli dé nɔɔna bam wone se ba ke kaanem zwoŋo yuu wara-jei bimbini dem baŋa ne.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Á ná zo teo kom wo, á wó wane á yi‑o ye o ta wo diini o yi mɛ kaanem dem na wó ke to. Nɔɔna bam wó taa jei ba cheigi wonto mo se o ba o lwoori Wɛ swolim o ke kaanem dem baŋa ne, se wonto de nɔɔna bam maama laam wane ba di wodiu. Nam véi-na, se á wó na‑o.”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba zo teo kom wone. Ba na maa zoore to, mo Samuwel de maa beene se o jeeri-ba. O déem wo chwoŋa ne mo, o diini o maa vei kaanem jei sem.

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Jwa kanto maŋa ne, amo wó toŋe Benjamin dwi tu dedoa se o ba n tei. Ko ye se n lwo swolim nuga mo o yuu ne, se n ma n tiŋi‑o se o taa ye amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam yiga tu. Se wonto mo wó jwoŋi a nɔɔna bam o yage Filisi tiina jeŋa ne. Kokuri, a nii a na a nɔɔna bam cham dem, ye ba keira kam de yi-ne.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Samuwel yi na tu de peere Sɔɔl to, mo Baŋa Wɛ tage ded‑o o we, “Nɔɔno wonto mo a tage o taane a bere‑m to. Wonto mo wó taa nii amo nɔɔna bam baŋa ne.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Samuwel na wo teo kom manchwo-peena ni ne to mo Sɔɔl fɔɔre o vo o yi o tei. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Ja! Bere debam Yi-naro wom na zoore mɛ to.”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Samuwel ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo mo ye Yi-naro wom. Nam da-na amo yiga se dé di zwoŋo kom baŋa dé vo kaanem jei sem. Zem mo dé wó tɔge daane dé di kaanem dem wodiu. Jwa zezeŋa ne, a ta wó ta kolo maama na wora to a bere‑m, se a daare a yage‑m chwoŋa ne se n viiri.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Pa se n boboŋa taa tiga, se ko ná ye bonɛ selo na jei da yatɔ zem tento to, ba jwoori ba na-se. Nam lɔre we, Isarele tiina bam maama yi page nmo de n kwo sɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne mo.”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Amo nam nwoŋi Benjamin dwi dem wone mo. Isarele dwia yam maama wone, Benjamin dwi dem mo tiini de muri. Amo ta na nwoŋi diga kalo ne to mo ye kalo nɔɔn-nɔɔno na yeiri ka ni ne to. Tetɛ mo ye nmo ŋɔɔne taane dento n pa-ne?”

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Wodi-saŋeno wom ma kwei chwei dem de de nɔna yam maama o ja o vo o zege Sɔɔl yiga ne. Samuwel laam ma ta de Sɔɔl o we, “Ko ye nmo nyem mo. Di n na lage tei to, se a maŋe a tiŋi nɔne dento n ŋwaane mo, ye a laam bwoŋi nɔɔna banto maama se dé di daane.” Dento dɛ dem ne, Sɔɔl dedaane Samuwel ma di wodiu daane.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Ba na di ba ti to, ba ma zege da ba tu ba jwoori teo kom wone. Samuwel ma ja Sɔɔl o di sɔŋɔ kom nayuu baŋa ye ba lara.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Tega na jege ka poore to, mo ba gwoni tega ba zaŋe. Samuwel ma ta de Sɔɔl ya na wo nayuu kom ne to o we, “Nam zaŋe n ti n yiga, se a bane‑m a yage chwoŋa ne se n viiri.” Sɔɔl na zaŋe o tu nayuu kom ne to, o de Samuwel ma nwoŋi pwooni ba kwei chwoŋa ba maa kɛa.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Ba na vei ba yi teo kom ni dem to, Samuwel ma ta de Sɔɔl o we, “Ta de n tontoŋeno wom se o tɔge yiga o taa via.” Sɔɔl tontoŋeno wom na kɛ o ti to, mo Samuwel daa tage o we, “Zege konto, se a ta Wɛ kwora kam a bere‑m.”

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Zem, nmo ná nwoŋi amo tei ne, ye n ná kɛ n yi Benjamin laŋa siseini dem, Racheli yibeeli dem na wo Zeliza ne to, n wó jeeri baara balei. Banto maa wó ta ba bere‑m we, ba jwoori ba na bonɛ selo n ya na kare n beeri to. Ba ta wó pa n maane we n kwo wom daa ba jege se lwia, se o laam jege lwia mo nmo tete ŋwaane ye o bwei o we, ‘Amo wó ke tɛ mo se a jwoori a na a bu wom?’

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Nmo ná zege dáane ye n vo n yi Tabora tei-zɔŋɔ kom, n ta wó jeeri baara batɔ na maa vei Bɛtel se ba ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ. Ba dedoa wó taa jege bebale setɔ, dedoa maa zei bworobwooru tetɔ, ye batɔ tu wom de jege lɔɔ de ko wo sa-doora bam.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: N laam ná zege dáane, n wó vo n yi Wɛ zwoŋo kom na wo Gibea seeni to. Dáane mo Filisi tiina jar-keira bam jege tigisim jei. Nmo ná yi teo kom ni, n wó jeeri Wɛ sampwori sedwonna kɔgɔ na zege zwoŋo kom wara-jei sem ne ba maa tua. Ba maa wó taa tae kwanno dwi dwi, ye ba wɔe senyɛ, ba daare ba taa wu wui. Ba maa wó taa via ye ba pworisa.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ jworo laam wó ba nmo baŋa dedaane dam pa se n de woli ba wone n tɔge n ta‑n pworisa. Konto baŋa ne n lage n leiri mo n ji nɔn-gaa.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: Nmo laam ma‑n wó da yiga n vo Giligal, se a laam ba. Amo nam ná tu a jeeri‑m, a laam wó ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra dedaane yazura pɛɛra a ma kaane a pa Wɛ. Nmo jege se n cheigi-ne da yarepɛ mo, se a laam ba a yi‑m Giligal ne. A ná tua, a laam wó bere‑m kolo daa na wora se n ke to.” Sɔɔl jigi Isarele tiina pɛ

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl déem na pipiri se o kɛ o daare Samuwel to, mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ o bochare leiri de ji bochare-doore. Dɛ dem konto ne woŋo maama seene ko ke ko maŋe dedaane Samuwel na tage tei to mo.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl dedaane o tontoŋeno wom na dɛ ba yi Gibea to, mo ba nɛ Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ na beene se ba jeeri-ba. Wɛ jworo ma ba Sɔɔl baŋa dedaane dam. O ma to ba wone o tɔge o pworisa.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo déem na yei Sɔɔl faŋa to ma na o na ke tei ye o pworisi to, ye ba bwei daane ba we, “Keitaa! Bɛ mo yi Kisi bu wom tento? Sɔɔl de ga tɔge o wo sampwori sem wone mo na?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Jei sem konto nɔɔno dedoa ma ta o we, “Se sampwori sento sem, á yei ba kwoa na?” Ko maama na ke tei to déem ma lɛɛre ko ji sinseira we, “Sɔɔl de laam tɔge o wo sampwori sem wone mo na?”

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl na pworisi o ti to, o laam ma bɛ o di zwoŋo baŋa wara-jei sem.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl kwo choro wodwoŋi déem ma na Sɔɔl de o tontoŋeno wom ye o bwei-ba o we “Abam ya vei yei ne mo?” Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Dé ya kare dé beeri bonɛ sem mo. Dé nam na wo nɛ-se to, mo dé vei Samuwel tei.”

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: O kwo choro kom ma ta o we, “Nam ta n bere-ne Samuwel na tage kolo dede‑m to.”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ta ma leiri o we, “O yɔɔre o ta debam mo we dé kɔ jworo, se ba nɛ bonɛ sem.” Ko daare, Sɔɔl wo sɛ se o ta kolo Samuwel na ŋɔɔne ded‑o paare dim ŋwaane to.

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Samuwel déem ma bwoŋi Isarele tiina bam maama se ba ba Mizipa ba jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: Ba na lage daane to, o ma ta de-ba o we, “Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora mo tento: Isarele tiina bam, amo mo jaane abam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne a ba ywo-seeni. Amo ta ma vere abam Ejipti tiina jeŋa ne, ye a jwoŋi abam a yage teene delo maama déem na bɛɛse abam to jeŋa ne.

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Abam Tu Wɛ ye wolo na yeini o vere abam á cham de á yaara maama wone to mo. De konto de, abam ta lɔge Wɛ kwaga ne mo ye á we, á lage pɛ se o taa wo á yiga ne. Konto ŋwaane nam ba-na á tigisi á tete Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, dwi de dwi, sɔ-yuu de sɔ-yuu.”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Samuwel laam ma bwoŋi Isarele dwia yam maama se ba nwoŋi dwi de dwi ba zege o yiga ne. Wɛ ma kuri Benjamin dwi dem ba maama wone.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Samuwel daa ma pa Benjamin dwi dem tutwoni de yi, sɔ-yuu de sɔ-yuu. Wɛ ma kuri Matiri sɔ-yuu kom ba wone. Se ko kweeli to, Kisi bu Sɔɔl mo Wɛ kuri Matiri sɔ-yuu kom wone. Nɔɔna déem ma vo ba beeri‑o ba ga.

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna déem ma duri ba vo ba vaŋe‑o ba ja ba nwoŋi pwola. Sɔɔl na tu o zege nɔɔna bam tetare ne to, ba ma na we o zege wagele wagele mo, ye o dedɔrem dwoi nɔɔna bam maama.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Samuwel laam ma ta de nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Nii-na, nɔɔno wonto mo Baŋa Wɛ kuri o pa abam. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera debam maama wone se kotu dwoni de wonto.” Nɔɔna bam maama ma kaase de kwor-dɛa ba we, “Wɛ wó pa dé pɛ wom momwɛ-dɛɛre.”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Samuwel laam ma lwoni o bere nɔɔna bam se ba lɔre paare dim totoŋ-naga na wó taa ye tei maama to. O ta ma popone tento o ke tɔnɔ wone, ye o kwei-ko o tiŋi Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Konto kwaga ne mo o bane nɔɔna bam o pa ba jwoori ba sam.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl de ma jwoori o vo o sɔŋɔ Gibea ne. Nɔɔna badwonna na ye babɛ to déem ma kwogili‑o ye ba tɔge‑o ba vo. Wɛ déem ya pɛ se banto boboŋa tɔge Sɔɔl mo.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Nɔn-wo-korro tedwonna ba wo na ba ŋwae to de maa wora, ye ba ŋwaane ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto yi se o jwoŋi debam o yage na?” Ba na gwooni‑o konto to, ba wo sɛ se ba ja pɛɛra ba ba ba pa‑o. Sɔɔl ma chem.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Amon tiina pɛ Nahasi déem lage o jar-keira o vo Jabese Gilead, se o li teo kom konto o jwoŋi o taa tei. Teo kom baara bam ma ta de Nahasi ba we, “Nam pa dé gwoni ni daane, se dé wó sɛ se n ta‑n tei debam.”

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: O ma leiri-ba o we, “Amo beeri chaveera mo se a ke Isarele tiina bam yera ne. Konto to, á na lage se dé gwoni ni daane, ko nam jege se a chochɔrege a le nɔɔno maama jazem yi mo ywo-seeni, se a daare a gwoni ni de abam.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Teo kom nakwa bam ma ta‑o ba we, “Nam pa debam pwola se dé kwei da yarepɛ dé toŋe kwora Isarele tega kam maama ne dé beeri wolim. Dé ná beeri dé pwoli ye jwoŋinu ná wo tu se o vere debam n jeŋa ne o yage, dé laam wó ba dé sɛ‑m.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna badwonna ma ja kwora kam konto ba vo ba yi Gibea. Sɔɔl teo kom mo konto. Ba ma ta taane dem ba de Gibea tiina bam zwa ne. Ba de na nigi to, ba ma kaase bɔge-bɔge.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Konto de Sɔɔl ya zege o kara ne mo o kale o nabɛ o maa jwoori sɔŋɔ. O na nigi sɔɔ kom to, mo o bwei o we, “Bɛ mo ke nɔɔna bam yera ne ye ba kaase konto ŋɔɔ?” Ba ma lwoni kwora kalo na nwoŋi Jabese ka ba to ba bere‑o.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl na nigi to, Baŋa Wɛ jworo ma chu o baŋa de dam. O wo ma pɛ.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: O ma ja o nabɛ sem selei o go. O ta ma tore tore se nɔna yam mura-mura, ye o pa nɔɔna ja-ya ba jage se ya yi Isarele tiina maama. Nɔɔna bam ná yi jei selo maama, ba wó ta tento mo ba we, “Sɔɔl de Samuwel mo wora ba lae jar-keira ba ke daane. Wolo ná wo sɛ se o nwoŋi o tɔge ba kwaga, ba lage ba ke kotu ne ba na ke tei de nabɛ sento to mo.” Foone ma tiini de zo Isarele tiina bam Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane. Ba maama jilli ma nwoŋi se ba vo ba kwaare jara.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Sɔɔl de o kwaga nɔɔna bam ma toŋe Jabese teo nɔɔna se ba jwoori ba teo kom de kwora kanto: “Jwa we-bere maŋa ne, dé wó ba dé jwoŋi abam dé yage.” Nɔɔna bam na jaane kwora kam ba yi Jabese Gilead ye ba ta to, teo kom tiina wo ma pwoli dedɛ.

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: De ko de, ba ta toŋe kwora Amon tiina bam tei ne mo we, “Ko ta wo á tei ne. Dé jwa wo á jeŋa ne, se á ke debam á na boŋe tei to.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Tega na lage ka poore to, mo Sɔɔl pɔɔre o jar-keira bam kuni betɔ. O laam ma pa ba nwoŋi ye ba pɔpɔ ba zaŋe Amon tiina kɔgɔ kom baŋa ne. Ba ma wane-ba, ye ba go ba dedɛ se ko vo ko yi wea berem maŋa. Balo fee na lugi to ma duri ba jage jei maama ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa wo tɔge de o dwoŋi.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma yi Samuwel tei ba we, “Nɔɔna balo na gwooni Sɔɔl ye ba we, ko ya wo maŋe se o di paare debam baŋa ne to, ba wo yei ne mo? Nam pa debam chwoŋa se dé go-ba!”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Sɔɔl maa wo sɛ ye o we, “Zem dɛ dento, yé go-na nɔɔn-nɔɔno! Kolo ŋwaane to, ko ye zem dɛ dem mo Baŋa Wɛ jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Samuwel laam ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we, “Pa se dé jwoori-na Giligal se dé kwɛ Sɔɔl paare dem se de da chwoŋa nɔɔna maama yia ne.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Ba maama ma seene ba vo Giligal. Ba ma fɔge ba tiŋi Sɔɔl paare dem wara-jei sem ne, ye ba daare ba ke yazura pɛɛra ba ma ke kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Jei sem konto ne mo Sɔɔl de Isarele tiina bam maama déem chake de wopwolo.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Ko zege a nɔn-donne maŋa ne mo a wo abam yiga ne se ko ba ko yi zem. Leile konto a tiini a kwe ye a yuu peere. Amo bia laam ye baara mo, ye ba wo á wone. Pɛ wom laam leiri amo yuu ne mo, se o taa nii á baŋa ne.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Nii-na ne da, a jale a tete mo Baŋa Wɛ dedaane o pɛ wom yiga ne. Ta-na chega: abam wɔ mo amo vere o nabea naa o bonaga? Wɔ mo a nam ke‑o swa a pini? A bɛɛse wɔ mo abam wone? Wɔ mo sugi amo yia de pɛɛre se ko kwoli o keim-balɔrɔ? Amo ná tusi tei kolo maama wone, se á ta á bere-ne, se a jwoori a yiri-te a pa abam.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Samuwel daa ma ta de nɔɔna bam o we: “Baŋa Wɛ déem mo kuri Moses dedaane Aron ye o tɔge banto baŋa ne o ja abam kwoa bam o nwoŋi Ejipti ne.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Ta‑á zege konto, se a lage a bwɛ abam mo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, se ko tɔge dedaane Baŋa Wɛ na ke wo-kamunnu telo maama o ma jwoŋi abam de á kwoa bam o yage to.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Jakob de o dwi tiina déem na jeini Ejipti ne to, mo abam nabaara bam déem keeri ba jare Baŋa Wɛ. Wɛ ma pa Moses de Aron vere-ba ba ja nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba ba ba zoore tega kanto á laam na tei to ne.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Á kwoa bam déem daa ma keeri ba jare Baŋa Wɛ ye ba we, ‘Debam tusi mo. Dé pipiri dé yage Baŋa Wɛ zula ye dé daare dé zuli Baal dedaane Asetare jwona yam. Nam jwoŋi debam n yage dé dona jeŋa ne, se dé laam wó jwoori dé taa zuli‑m.’

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma kuri Gideon, de Baraki, de Jefeta, dedaane amo, Samuwel o pa abam. Wɛ ma tɔge nɔɔna bam konto baŋa ne o jwoŋi abam o yage á dona bam maama jeŋa ne, se á ta‑á wae á zoore de yazura.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Abam nam na yɔɔre á na Amon tiina pɛ Nahasi na lage o kwaare jara de abam to, mo á tage de amo á we, ‘Lage pɛ n pa debam, se o taa nii dé baŋa ne.’ Á tage konto ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ya mo maŋe o ye abam pɛ.

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: Á nam nii-na á pɛ wom mo tento. O maa ye pɛ wolo á na lwoori Wɛ o ŋwaane ye Baŋa Wɛ kuri‑o o pa abam to.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Ko daare á na pɛ se á zwa se, ye á ve se á sɛ o nia yam, Baŋa Wɛ de wó lɔ abam de á pɛ wom kwaga ne mo.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Nam ta‑á zege á na zege mɛ konto to, se Baŋa Wɛ wó ke wo-kamunu á yibia ne leile konto.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Maŋa kanto dae te-pwoŋa mo na? Amo nam wó lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o pa doa ba ka taa baga ka wuura ye ka nena. Abam ná nɛ do-fɔrɔ kom, á wó maane we á tiini á sa chwoŋa ye á chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga mo, de á na tage we á lage pɛ to.”

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Samuwel na seene o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ to, Wɛ ma pa do-fɔrɔ ba ka baga ye ka nena dɛ dem konto ne. Ko ma pa nɔɔna bam maama tiini ba kɔre Baŋa Wɛ dedaane Samuwel.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Ba ma ta de Samuwel ba we, “Pwopwo, ja n Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom teiŋa n pa debam se dé yé te. Debam laam seene dé lɔre we dé wɛleera yam daga, ye dé ta woli ya wone mo dedaane dé na we dé lage pɛ to.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Samuwel laam ma leiri-ba o we, “Chega to, abam seene á ke wo-balɔrɔ. Nam yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone. Ko laam nam jege se á ta‑á tɔge Baŋa Wɛ de á wo maama mo, se á daa yé lɔ o kwaga ne.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Yé zuli-na jwona. Yanto ba jege dam, ya nam bá wane abam ya jwoŋi ya yage cham wone. Ya ye wo-yɔɔro yerane mo.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ bá sɛ o ve abam balo na ye o nɔɔna bam to, o tete yere-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane. Kokuri to, wonto mo kuri abam se o pa á ta‑á ye o tete nɔɔna.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye amo, a ta wó taa lwoori Baŋa Wɛ a pa abam. Ko ya ná dae konto, a ya wó ke wɛleere mo. Amo za wó taa bere abam chwo-laaro telo na maŋe se á tɔge to.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Ta‑á kɔre-na Baŋa Wɛ se á daare á ta‑á zuli‑o de á bochare maama. Guli-na wo-kamunnu telo maama o na ke o pa abam to.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Nam ta‑á yei-na we, abam de á pɛ wom ná misi á yuni keim-balwaaro wone, Wɛ wó pa á yera maama saare tega baŋa ne mo.”

english_verse: cavalry, and as many foot soldiers as there are grains of sand on the beach. They went to Michmash and set up camp there east of Beth-Aven.
translation_verse: ). Ba jar-keira maama ni déem ware de ga de ti. Ba daga dedɛ nenɛɛne naneo ni kasolo mo tei. Ba ma tɔge daane ba vo Mikimasa ba chwi ba vwoa da. Jei sem konto jeeri Bɛte-Aven wɛ-puli seeni mo.

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma ni we Sɔɔl mo wane Filisi tiina jar-keira kɔgɔ kolo na wo Gibea ne to o zeili. Konto nam mo pɛ Isarele tiina bam kikia maama lwoi Filisi tiina bam momwa ne. Isarele tiina jar-keira bam maama ma sɛ Sɔɔl kwora kam ye ba vo ba jeeri‑o Giligal ne.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam ma na we ko tiini ko zo ba yera, Filisi tiina bam na jege-ba ba peene to ŋwaane. Ba ma duri ba vo ba seigi peero bɔɔna wone, de punnu wone, de gugworru wone, de gwonnu wone, de vola wone se ba wane ba lu.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Ba badwonna bere ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ye ba zo Gad dedaane Gilead laŋa kam ne mo. Sɔɔl ma maŋe Giligal ne. Foone ma ja nɔɔna balo na wo o tei ne to pa se ba yera sae pɔm-pɔm.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: O déem peene mo se o cheigi Samuwel na wó ba maŋa kalo to. O ma cheigi da yarepɛ ne Samuwel na tage tei to. Samuwel yuu na ba nae to, Sɔɔl nɔɔna bam laam ma bobo se ba jage ba daare‑o.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma ga ga o we, “Ja-na zwɛɛm pɛɛra yam dedaane yazura pɛɛra yam á ba á pa-ne.” O na jwoŋi-te nɔɔna bam tei ne to, mo o kwei varem wom o wora o zwɛ o ma o ke kaanem.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
