translation_verse: O na yɔɔre o ti kaanem dem to dedaane Samuwel dɛ o yi da. Sɔɔl ma vo se o jeeri‑o o daare o zaane‑o.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Samuwel ma bwei Sɔɔl o we, “Bɛ mo konto n kea?” Sɔɔl ma leiri‑o o we, “Maŋa kalo nmo na pɛ se n ba to na yia ye n ta wo tu to, amo nɔɔna bam ya wora ba jage ba daare-ne. Filisi tiina jar-keira bam de ma jeeri daane Mikimasa ne se ba kwaare jara dedaane debam.

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: Amo ya ta maa jege lwia we ba wó ba Giligal ywo-seeni ba zaŋe a baŋa ne, ye a ta wo lwoori Baŋa Wɛ zeinim jara yam ŋwaane. Konto to amo boŋe we ko fee mo se a ke lela a ke kaanem dem.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuwel ma ta o we, “Nmo tiini n toŋe jworim dedɛ. Nmo wo tɔge ni delo nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑m se n da to. N ya ná dɛ-de chekke, Baŋa Wɛ ya wó pa nmo de n dwi dem di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne, se ko taa vei wuu.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Nam nii! N paare dem daa bá taa wora taa. Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o beeri o na nɔɔno wolo kikia na dɛ o wo to, ye o laam wó pa wonto mo taa nii o nɔɔna bam baŋa ne, nmo na wo dɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Samuwel ma zege Giligal ne o kwei o chwoŋa o maa kɛa. Nɔɔna balo ta na wo Sɔɔl tei ne to ma tɔge ded‑o ba vo Gibea na wo Benjamin laŋa kam ne to. Sɔɔl ma jeeli ba ni daane, o na we ba ta yi nɔɔna bia yaredo (

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl de o bu Jonatan dedaane ba kɔgɔ kom maama maa maŋe Benjamin teo Gibea ne ba tiga. Filisi tiina bam de maa maŋe Mikimasa ne ba tiga.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina jar-keira badwonna ma zege ba na gilimi mɛ to ne ba pɔɔre ba tete kuni betɔ. Ba maa yeini ba nwoŋi se ba taa mage ba dona ye ba vere ba wonnu. Popɔra dedoa déem kwei Ofera chwoŋa kam na wo Suwali laŋa kam seeni to mo.

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: Ba popɔra kadwoŋi de ma kwei Bɛte-Horon chwoŋa kam, ko daare ye popɔra kalo na daare to de kwei chwoŋa kalo na vei siseini dem laŋa ne, mɛ na maŋe de Zeboyim bwolo kom de kagoa kam to.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa kam ne, luru tera Isarele tiina teene dem maama wone. Kokuri to, Filisi tiina bam mo déem ya tage ba we, “Dé yé pa Hiburu tiina bam pwola se ba ke se-zɔɔro dedaane chichwoa ba ma daane debam.”

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye vaane, Filisi tiina bam maa yeini ba pa ba ŋwe sabu-dala yalei se ba dwori-de ba pa-ba. Ko daare ko ná ye dwoora, de pengasa, de chichwoa, ba wó ŋwe sabu-dale dedoa mo.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam déem ma pa ba jar-keira kɔgɔ kodwoŋi vo ba che Mikimasa zwonnu chwoŋa kam.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Peo dedoa déem jeeri baŋa seeni daa kam mo, ye ko yɔɔre Mikimasa. Kodwoŋi kom de maa wo tega-kuri seeni daa kam ne, ye ko yɔɔre Geba.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Jonatan ma ta de nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara zela yam to o we, “Nam pa dé bɛ dé yi nɔn-kafɛ tento na wo mɛ to! Dɛ delo Baŋa Wɛ wó woli debam se dé wane-ba. Baŋa Wɛ ná lage o jwoŋi o nɔɔna bam o yage, kolokolo bá cheiŋi‑o. Dé ná daga naa dé ná muri de, ko maama ye bedwe mo Wɛ tei ne.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Jonatan maa we, “Nam pa dé fɔɔre dé vo dé bere dé tete Filisi tiina bam.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Ba ná tage ba bere debam we, ‘Ta‑á zege-na á cheigi debam se dé beene á tei’, de wó maŋe da mo, de bá di dé yi ba tei.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Ko daare ba ná tage we, ‘Titwoni-na á di peo kom á ba-na ywo-seeni’, dé wó di dé yi-ba mo. Konto wó bere we Baŋa Wɛ mo seene o kwei-ba o ke debam jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Ba laam ma tɔɔle ba ta Jonatan dedaane nɔn-doŋo wom ba we, “Tutwoni á yi-na ywo-seeni, se dé wane dé bere abam woŋo.” Jonatan ma ta o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Ta‑n tɔge a kwaga n diini, se Baŋa Wɛ mo ke nɔɔna bam konto Isarele tiina bam jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Jonatan laam ma gwane o di peo kom, ye o tontoŋeno wom tɔge o kwaga. O ma jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara o mage o de tega ne. O ná mage wolo o de tega ne, nɔn-doŋo wom wó tɔge o kwaga o go kotu.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Dé nɔɔna bam ya ná nɛ chwoŋa se ba di wodiu kolo maama ba na vere Filisi tiina bam tei ne to, ko ya bá taa gare na? Tento ba ya wó na dam se ba go Filisi tiina bam dedɛ ba dwoni ba zem na go tei to.”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl dedaane o jar-keira bam maama ma ke daane ba yɔɔre Filisi tiina bam jei sem se ba kwaare jara de-ba. Ba ma vo ba na we vuvuga tiini ka to Filisi tiina bam wone ye ba kwaare jara da-baŋa ne.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Foone ma tiini de ja Filisi tiina jar-keira balo maama déem na wo pwola ne to, de balo na nwoŋi vero ŋwaane to, de balo na yere ba tigisim jei to, de ba teo kom nɔn-bia bam maama. Tega kam ma ziziŋi, kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ mo ke se foone dem konto taa wora.

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl nɔɔna balo na zege Gibea ne ba tole ba nii kolo na wora ko ke to ma na we, Filisi tiina bam jage mo ye ba duri jei maama ne.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl laam ma ta o nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Jeeli-na dé nɔɔna bam maama ni, se dé lɔre balo na tere ywo-seeni to.” Ba na jeeli ba ti to, mo ba maane we Jonatan de nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara-keim zela yam to mo tera.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Wɛ kaanem tu Ahija déem na jege kaanem zela yam o tei ne to, Sɔɔl ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ja gare-wogo kom n fɔɔre n yi ywo-seeni se dé bwei Baŋa Wɛ dé nii dé wó ke tɛ mo.”

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: O ta na wora o ŋɔɔne de kaanem tu wom konto to, ba ma ni vuvuga sɔɔ na tiini ko zaŋe Filisi tiina bam tigisim jei sem ne. Sɔɔl ma ta‑o we, “Le n jeŋa gare-wogo kom ne. Maŋa daa tera se dé bwei Baŋa Wɛ dé nii.”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Hiburu tiina balo ya na tɔge de Filisi tiina bam ba ke jara yam ba woli-ba to laam ma jwoori ba lɛɛne ba pu Isarele tiina balo na wo Sɔɔl de Jonatan tei ne to.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ko daare Isarele tiina balo ya na seigi Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne to de ma ba ba ni we, Filisi tiina bam kwaane ba duri se ba lu Isarele tiina jeŋa ne mo. Ba de ma nwoŋi ba tɔge ba pare-ba de fora.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne mo Isarele tiina bam yera tiini ya bwona, kana na jege-ba to ŋwaane. Kokuri to, Sɔɔl déem ya dugi duuri mo ye o daare o pa ni dento o nɔɔna bam o we, “Wolo maama ná di wodiu zem ko lwoori wɛ-zoore maŋa ye a ta wo yiri a jene a dona bam baŋa ne, se sɔɔlem taa wo kotu yuu ne.” Ko ma pa se dɛ dem konto, o nɔɔna bam wolowolo wo laŋe wodiu o ni ne.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Ba na dɛ da ba kɛ ye ba na tooro tem konto to, ba wolowolo wo laŋe-te. Sensɔla kam mo ba déem kɔre.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Ko daare Jonatan déem wo nigi we o kwo dugi mo o pa nɔɔna bam. O ma kwei o nacheiga kam o twe o ma laŋe to-nuga. O laam ma weeri de o jeŋa o di. O yera ma daŋe, ye o ta wara.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam dedoa ma ta de Jonatan o we, “Nmo kwo nam dugi mo o yage dé jar-keira bam baŋa ne we, ‘Lɛɛro taa wo wolo maama na wó di wodiu zem to baŋa ne.’ Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo dé maama bwona tento ye kana jege debam.”

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Jonatan ma ta o we, “Chega to, a kwo pɛ ko zo á maama yera chekke. Nii a na di tooro tem fenfee ye a jwoori a na dam tei!

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Ba ma ke lela ba pɛ wonnu telo ba na vere Filisi tiina bam tei ne to se ba na wodiu ba di. Ba ma go pei, de naane, de na-mɔre, ba daare ba jege nɔna yam ba buri ba di gweeni, ye vara bam jana wo lwoori ba lu tega ne.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna ma ta Sɔɔl ba we, “Nii debam nɔɔna bam na ke wɛleere delo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Ba jege nɔna mo ba done de ya yera jana.” Sɔɔl ma ta o we, “Abam chɔge á chega de Baŋa Wɛ. Bibili-na kandwɛ-kamunu á ja á ba ywo-seeni á pa-ne.”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: O daa ma ta o we, “Véi-na á da nɔɔna bam wone á ta se ba maama ja ba naane dedaane ba pei sem ba ba ywo-seeni. Ba jege se ba go vara bam maama kandwɛ dem baŋa ne ba daare ba di ywo mo. Ko dae se ba done nɔna yam de ya yera jana ba ma ke wɛleere Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.” Tete dem konto ne, nɔɔna bam maama ma ja ba vara ba ba ba go dáane.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Sɔɔl de ma lɔ kaanem bimbini se o ma o zuli Baŋa Wɛ. Mo bimbini delo o na dɛ yiga o lɔ o pa Baŋa Wɛ to.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Nam pa-na se dé vo dé pare Filisi tiina bam tete dento wone se ko taa nii te-pora maŋa ne. Dé wó go-ba ye dé daare dé vere ba zela. Dé yé daare nɔɔno dedoa de.” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ke kolo maama n na boŋe n ja se n ke to.” Kaanem yiga tu wom ma ta o we, “Yage-na se dé bwei Baŋa Wɛ se dé lɔre o boboŋa.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma bwei Wɛ o we, “A ja jara a jeeri Filisi tiina bam se n pa dé di-ba na?” Baŋa Wɛ maa wo leiri‑o dento dɛ dem ne.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Ko ma pa Sɔɔl ta de Isarele jar-keira yiga tiina bam o we, “Á ba-na ywo se dé lɔre wɛleere dwi dɔ mo dé ke zem.

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: A dugi dedaane Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na pae Isarele tiina di ba jara to a we, wolo maama na ke wɛleere dem to wó te mo. Ko ná maŋe ko ye amo bu Jonatan de, o bá lu.” O na tage konto to, ba maama wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo leiri taane.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl laam ma ta de Isarele jar-keira bam o we, “Abam maama véi-na dáa á zege kɔgɔ dedoa, se amo de a bu Jonatan de zege ywo-seeni.” Nɔɔna bam ma sɛ ye ba we, “Ke kolo nmo na boŋe n ja se n ke to.”

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma lwoori Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom o we, “Popo, bere-ne woŋo kolo ŋwaane n na wo leiri debam lworo kom zem to. Ko ná ye amo, naa a bu Jonatan yiga mo, pa se Yurim kandwɛ dem bere. Ko nam ná ye Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom yiga mo, se n pa Tumim kandwɛ dem bere.” Jɔrɔ kom ma ja Jonatan de Sɔɔl, ye ko yage Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl daa ma ta o we, “Laam pa Wɛ kuri amo de a bu Jonatan tetare ne.” Jɔrɔ kom ma le Jonatan.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl laam ma bwei o bu wom o we, “Nmo ke bɛ mo n sa chwoŋa?” Jonatan ma ta o we, “Amo mɛ a nacheiga ni mo a laŋe tooro fenfee a di. Konto to, a nam jege se a te mo na?”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma ta o we, “Jonatan, lɛɛro taa wo amo yuu ne nenɛɛne a ná wo pɛ se n te!”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Isarele jar-keira bam ma ta de Sɔɔl ba we, “Konto bá ke! Ko dae Jonatan mo jaane wɔnɔ-kamunu konto o ba o pa debam Isarele tiina bam na? Debam dugi de ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere dem we Jonatan yu-yua dedoa tete bá gɔ o yuu ne. Ko ye Wɛ mo woli‑o pa o ke kolo maama o na ke zem to!” Ko déem ke konto mo ye Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom jwoŋi Jonatan momwɛ ba yage, ye o daa wo tege.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Sɔɔl laam ma yage Filisi tiina bam zeilim. Filisi tiina bam ma jwoori ba tete teo. Sɔɔl na di paare ye o ke kolo to

english_verse: When Saul became king, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, the Philistines, and the Amalekites had all been robbing the Israelites. Saul fought back against these enemies and stopped them from robbing Israel. He was a brave commander and always won his battles. Saul's Family
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye Amaleki tiina bam, o tiini o ke baare o wane-ba. Ko ma pa se o jwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o yage balo maama déem na jege-ba ba vere to jeŋa ne.

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo maama Sɔɔl na ŋwe to, tigura dedɛ ma ke Isarele tiina bam dedaane Filisi tiina bam laŋa ne. Sɔɔl déem ná maane we nɔɔno wolo dana ye o ta jege baare, o wó pa kotu da o zo o jar-keira kɔgɔ kom wone mo.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Samuwel déem tage de Sɔɔl o we, “Ko ye amo mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ ni se a tiŋi nmo se n di paare o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. Konto to, cheigi kwora kalo Baŋa Wɛ na jege se o pa‑m to.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ we: ‘A lage a waare Amaleki tiina mo ba déem na toŋe tei de Isarele tiina bam to ŋwaane. Maŋa kalo Isarele tiina bam na nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba maa beene to, Amaleki tiina bam chege ba chwoŋa ye ba jeeri-ba de jara mo.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Konto to, vei n kwaare jara dedaane Amaleki tiina bam. Yɔɔre n chɔge-ba de ba woŋo maama. Yé ja ba ŋwaŋa. Go-na ba baara, de ba kaana, de ba bia, de ba bu-sese, ko woli de ba naane, de ba pei, de ba kona, de ba bonɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma bwoŋi o jar-keira bam o ke daane pa ba jeeri Telayim ne. Jar-keira morro fuga (

english_verse: of these were from Judah. Saul organized them,
translation_verse: ) de maa nwoŋi Isarele dwia yadaara yam ne.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Samuwel o we,

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl laam ma da o kɔgɔ kom yiga ye ba vo Amaleki tiina teo kom. Ba ma vwɛ nabara kadwoŋi ne, ye ba cheigi se ba nwoŋi da ba zaŋe Amaleki tiina bam baŋa ne.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Keni dwi tiina de déem zoore jei sem konto ne. Sɔɔl ma pa-ba kwora o we, “Maŋa kalo Isarele tiina bam na nwoŋi Ejipti ne ba maa kɛ to, abam kwoa déem ke-ba lanyerane. Konto to, zaŋe-na á vo yiga á daare Amaleki tiina bam, se a lage a chɔge ba maama mo. Ko nam dae se abam de da á te.” Keni tiina bam ma seene ba vo dáa ba daare Amaleki tiina bam.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Ko daare, Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam déem wo go pɛ Agagi. Ba ma yage teo kom vare-ŋona bam, naane de pei maama. Ba wo sɛ se ba go-te. Ko daare ko ná ye wo-kokware sem de telo na ba jege kuri to, ba yɔɔre ba chɔge tento maama mo nyɔ!

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: “A wo chɔge mo, de a na pɛ Sɔɔl ji pɛ to. O lɔge amo kwaga ne mo, ye o ba sɛ se o ke a ni dem ne.” Samuwel wo ma pɛ, ye o tiini o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ tete dem maama ne o poore tega.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Samuwel ma gwoni tega o zaŋe se o vo o beeri Sɔɔl jei. Ba ma ta ba bere‑o we, Sɔɔl vei Kamele mo, o nam chwi kandwɛ-kamunu mo o zege da se ko pa o na yere. Ba ta we, o na zege dáane to, o laam vei Giligal mo.

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Samuwel ma vo o yi Sɔɔl tei. Sɔɔl ma ware‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ swolim taa wo n yuu ne. Amo ke a tɔge Baŋa Wɛ ni dem chekke.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Samuwel ma bwei‑o we, “Chega? Bɛ nam daa mo ke ye a ni naane dem dedaane pei sem keira konto?”

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma leiri‑o o we, “Jar-keira bam mo vere vare-ŋona banto Amaleki tiina jeŋa ne ba ja ba se ba ma ke kaanem ba pa nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Ko daare kolo maama laam na daare to, dé yɔɔre dé chɔge-te mo kula!”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Samuwel ma bage‑o o we, “Pu n ni konto, se a ta kwora kalo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ne diim tete ne to a bere‑m.” Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “A nam cheiga.”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuwel laam maa we, “Nmo ya maŋe n nii n tete we, n dae kolokolo yiga da. De ko de, Baŋa Wɛ nam mo pɛ n ji Isarele dwi tiina bam maama yiga tu. O ma tiŋi‑m se n ta‑n ye ba pɛ.

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Ko ná ye chega, amo ke Baŋa Wɛ ni dem mo chekke. A dɛ chwoŋa kalo o na toŋe-ne se a da to. A ma yɔɔre a chɔge Amaleki tiina bam, ye a daare a ja ba pɛ Agagi a ba ywo-seeni.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Dé nam na di-ba to, mo a nɔɔna bam kuri pei selo na lamma to, dedaane naane delo na lamma to, ba le wonnu telo na maŋe de chɔgem to wone. Ba nam jaane-te ba ba Giligal ywo-seeni mo, se ba ma ba ke kaanem mo ba pa nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: N ná lɔge Wɛ kwaga ne, konto de yi-nɛɛre ye bedwe mo. Yi-dɛɛre-nyem dedaane jwo-kaano de maa ba gare daane. Nmo na ve Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam to, o de ve‑m we n daa‑n bá‑n taa ye pɛ.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma leiri Samuwel o we, “Chega to, amo ke wɛleere. A ve Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam. A wo sɛ nmo na bere-ne se a ke tei to. A nam ya kɔre a nɔɔna bam mo, pa a ke banto na lage tei to.

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Samuwel ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo bá tɔge‑m a jwoori. Kokuri to, nmo ve Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam pa o de ve‑m we, n daa‑n bá‑n taa ye Isarele tiina pɛ.”

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Samuwel laam ma pipiri se o viiri. Sɔɔl ma ja o gɔrɔ kom ni dem seeni ye ko kaare.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Samuwel ma ta‑o o we, “Nii! Baŋa Wɛ zem jwoori o jwoŋi Isarele tiina paare dem na wo n jeŋa ne to mo o daare‑m. O ma kwei-de o pa n dwoŋi wolo na gare‑m to.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina Nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ba fɔe vwa, o taane de maa ba gɔe de yaga. Kokuri to, o dae nabiin-zwona, se o taa zae o ni.”

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Amo seene a ke wɛleere. De konto maama de, yé pa a na a chaveera Isarele nakwa bam dedaane ba kɔgɔ kom maama yiga ne. Nam jwoori n da de amo se a vo a zuli n Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Samuwel ma sɛ. O ma da de Sɔɔl o jwoori pa Sɔɔl vo o zuli Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Samuwel laam ma ta o we, “Ja-na Amaleki tiina pɛ Agagi á ja á ba ywo-seeni.” Agagi ma zaŋe o vo o yi o tei de baare ye o boŋe o wone we, “Cham de toone daa bá yi-ne.”

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Samuwel maa we, “Nmo mɛ n se-zɔɔ mo n pa kaana dedɛ ga ba bia. Konto chwoŋa kam ne mo nmo de nu wó ga o bia.” O ma zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne o kwei o se-zɔɔ kom o cha Agagi mura-mura Giligal ne.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Samuwel ma jwoori o vo Rama. Sɔɔl de ma jwoori sɔŋɔ o tete teo Gibea ne.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samuwel daa wo jwoori o vo o na Sɔɔl se ko yi o toone. Sɔɔl totoŋ-naga déem za pɛ Samuwel yiga nyɔne dedɛ. Baŋa Wɛ de wo déem chɔge mo de o na pɛ Sɔɔl di paare Isarele tiina baŋa ne to.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Baŋa Wɛ tage de Samuwel o we, “Amo maŋe a ve Sɔɔl we, o daa bá taa ye Isarele tiina pɛ. N nam wó keeri o ŋwaane taa se n vo n maŋe yei ne mo? Zaŋe n kwei n kwara kam n su-ka de nuga, se n daare n vo Jesse sɔŋɔ Bɛtelehem ne. Kokuri to, amo kuri o bia bam dedoa mo se o ji pɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Samuwel maa we, “Amo wó ke tetɛ mo a vo a ke konto? Sɔɔl ná niga, o wó go-ne mo.” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Ja na-chwɛ n woli da, se n laam ta we n tu se n ke kaanem mo n pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samuwel ma ke kolo Baŋa Wɛ na bere to, ye o vo Bɛtelehem. O na yi da to, teo kom nakwa ma nwoŋi ba jeeri‑o ye ba yera sae. Ba ma bwei‑o ba we, “Ko ye ywoni mo ye n vei n beene na?”

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Samuwel ma leiri-ba o we, “Ɛɛ, a tu de ywoni mo. Amo tu ywo se a ke kaanem mo a pa Baŋa Wɛ. Kwɛ-na á tete, se á ba á gwaane de amo se dé ke kaanem dem.” O ma vo o le Jesse de o bia bam pa ba kwɛ ba tete ye o daare o bwoŋi-ba se ba vo kaanem dem jeiga.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Jesse dedaane o bia bam na yi da to, Samuwel ma na o bu-kwea Eliabi. O ma ta o wone we, “N nɛ naa n wo nɛ, baaro wonto na zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to mo ye wolo o na kuri se o tiŋi pɛ to.”

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Samuwel o we, “Yé jeeli n daŋe baaro wom yibia pwooni na ye tei to baŋa ne, naa o na ye nɔn-wagele to ne. Amo ve wonto mo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ ba nii wonnu o nae-te nenɛɛne nabiina na nae tei to. Nabiina nii ba nae pwooni yiga kam mo, Baŋa Wɛ nam nii o nae bochare-yi dem ne mo.”

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Jesse laam ma bwoŋi o bu Abinadaba o pa o vo Samuwel tei se o na‑o. Samuwel ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wo kuri wonto de.”

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Jesse daa ma toŋe Samma o tei ne. Samuwel ta maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ wo kuri wonto de.”

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Jesse bere o pa o bia barepɛ maama mo vo Samuwel tei ba da o yiga ne ba kɛ, ye Samuwel we, “Baŋa Wɛ wo kuri banto wolowolo.”

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: O laam ma ga ga o bwei Jesse o we, “Nmo bia bam maama mo konto na?” Jesse ma ta o we, “Jeŋa-bu wom mo daare. Wonto nam wo pei sem kwaga ne mo o yere-se.” Samuwel maa we, “Toŋe n bwoŋi‑o se o ba. Wonto ná wo tu ywo-seeni, dé bá wane dé ke kaanem dem se dé di.”

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Jesse ma pa ba bwoŋi o jeŋa-bu David ye o ba. O maa ye lanno ye yazura yi‑o lanyerane. O yibia ta maa pwomma. Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Samuwel o we, “Zaŋe n lwo nuga o yuu ne, se wonto mo a kuri.”

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Samuwel ma kwei kwara kam de ka wo nuga o lwo David yuu ne, o chorro tem yibia ne. Sento nɛ sem ni ne mo Baŋa Wɛ Jworo chugi David baŋa ne de dam. Ko maa wo o tei ne taa, ko zege dɛ dem konto ne se ko taa via. Samuwel laam ma jwoori o vo Rama. David toŋa o pae Pɛ Sɔɔl

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ Jworo ma nwoŋi ko daare Sɔɔl. Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri o kwei jwori-lɔŋɔ o pa ko yeini ko daane‑o.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl tontoŋena bam ma ta‑o ba we, “Dé maane we Wɛ mo pɛ se jwori-lɔŋɔ ba ko jege‑m ko daana.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Pɛ, dé ye nmo tontoŋena mo. Konto, yage se dé beeri jei sem maama ne dé nii wolo na wae o tae kɔnɔ chekke to. Baŋa Wɛ ná pɛ se jwori-lɔŋɔ kom ba n baŋa ne ye kotu ná tage o kɔnɔ kom, nmo wo wó to.”

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma pa-ba ni o we, “Kwaane-na á beeri nɔɔno wolo na tae kɔnɔ lanyerane to á ja á ba á pa-ne.”

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl tontoŋena bam dedoa ma leiri o we, “Amo nɛ nɔɔno wodwoŋi, o ye Bɛtelehem tu Jesse bu mo. O yei kɔnɔ tam lanyerane. Nɔɔno wom ye babea ye o yei jara keim. O ni taane de ywomma, ye o yibia pwomma. Baŋa Wɛ maa wo o tei ne.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma toŋe kwora Jesse tei ne ye o we, “Nmo bu David wolo na yere n pei sem to mo a laga. Pa o ba a tei.”

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Jesse ma ja bonaga o daare o kwei bworobworo, dedaane lɔɔ de ko wo sana, de bo-chwɛ o daŋe ka baŋa ne. O ma toŋe o bu David se o ja o vo o pa Sɔɔl.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Ko ke konto mo ye David da o zo Sɔɔl tontoŋena bam wone. Sɔɔl déem maa tiini o swoi David. O ma le‑o se o taa ye wolo na wó taa zei o jara zela yam to.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma toŋe kwora o pa Jesse o we, “Amo wo tiini ko pwoli de n bu David. Konto to, yage se o maŋe a tei ne o taa toŋa o pa-ne.”

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo maama Wɛ ná yeini o pa jwori-lɔŋɔ kom zo Sɔɔl, David wó ta o kɔnɔ kom mo. Konto ná yeini ko ke, Sɔɔl wo wó to mo, ye ko gara ko pa‑o. Jwori-lɔŋɔ kom maa yeini ko viiri ko daare‑o.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam déem ma la ba jar-keira bam ba ke daane. Ba ma vo Judah teo kolo yere na ye Sokoo to se ba kwaare jara da. Ba déem chwi ba vwoa Efese-Damima ne mo. Jei sem konto wo Sokoo dedaane Azeka tetare laŋa ne mo.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam déem tigisi daane mo, ba zege zwoŋo dedoa yuu ne. Isarele tiina bam de maa zege zwoŋo kodwoŋi yuu ne, ye bwolo laam tigi ba maama tetare ne ko pɔɔre-ba daane.

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: Channa kam mo o mɛ o kwoli o nachere sem seeni. O ta jege channa se-zɔɔ mo o na peili o kwaga ne.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: David na go Goliafe ye o zege jara pwola ne o jwoori o ba to, mo Abenera jaane‑o o ja o zo Sɔɔl tei ne. David ta jege Goliafe yuu kom mo o jeŋa ne.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: ). Nɔn-doŋo maa tɔge o yiga o zei o jara-keim nantana kam o via.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Goliafe ma zaŋe o zege o bage Isarele tiina jar-keira bam o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo á maama wora á tigisi se á ke jara? Amo ye Filisi tiina bam babea mo. Abam de ye Sɔɔl jar-keira mo naa á dae? Le-na á wone nɔɔno dedoa, se kotu jeeri amo de jara.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom konto ná wane amo o go, debam Filisi tiina maama wó ji abam kabɛ. Amo de daa ná wane kotu a go, abam de mo wó taa ye debam kabɛ ye á toŋe á pae debam.

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
translation_verse: Amo nii Isarele jar-keira bam mo a gwooni. Le-na nɔɔno á pa-ne se dé jeeri daane de jara.”

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Sɔɔl dedaane o nɔɔna bam na nigi Filisi tu wom taane dem to, ba bochare ma di ye foone tiini de zo-ba. David vei jara jei sem

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: David kwo déem maa ye Eferata tu Jesse. Jesse déem nwoŋi Judah teo Bɛtelehem ne mo. O maa jege bakeiri nana. Sɔɔl paare dem maŋa kam ne to de Jesse kwe dedɛ mo.

english_verse: the oldest was Eliab, the next was Abinadab, and Shammah was the third. The three of them had gone off to fight in Saul's army. David was Jesse's youngest son.
translation_verse: David déem nam mo ye ba maama nyaane. O zembaara batɔ na vei ba wora ba woli Sɔɔl to,

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: mo David yeini o vei sɔŋɔ Bɛtelehem ne ye o jwoora, se o taa nii o kwo pei sem baŋa ne.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Goliafe lɛɛre o dole kandwona konto mo taa Isarele tiina bam yiga ne da finna, zezeŋa ne de dedaan-ni ne maama.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: O ma kwei o nayera da-lɔŋɔ kom, o daare o vo nabara ni ne o kuri kandwa-siswollu tenu. O ma de kandwa yam konto o nayera tampɔgɔ ne, ye o daare o kwei o napana, o laam maa vei se o jeeri Filisi tu wom.

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Yanto da yam ne, mo Jesse tage de o bu David o we, “Kwei men-wɔa ywolo konto na maŋe de kuriwaa bu dedoa to, de bworobwooru fuga kanto, se n ke lela n ja n vo n pa n chorro tem na wo jara kapworo ne to.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Nam ta kwei nayel-pepala banto fuga n woli da n vo n pa ba jar-keira yiga tu wom. Nmo laam ma‑n wó lɔre ko na ye tei n chorro tem yera ne, se n daare n ja taane n nwoŋi ba tei ne n ba se ko pa a kɔ jworo.

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: David ma gwoni tega o zaŋe te-pora ni ne. O ma lage nɔɔno wodwoŋi o kwei pei sem o ke o jeŋa ne. O ta ma vɔ o zela yam o ke daane. O ma kwei chwoŋa o maa kɛa, nenɛɛne o kwo Jesse na maŋe tei o bere‑o to. O na dɛ dɛ o yi jara jei sem to, dedaane jar-keira bam de nwoŋi mo ba maa vei se ba chichei ba zege jara ŋwaane. Ba déem maa mage tiguri-kaasa.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Isarele jar-keira bam dedaane Filisi jar-keira bam ma tigisi tigisi, ye ba yibia laam jeeri daane.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: David ma yage o wodiiru tem o pa wolo na nii jar-keira bam zela yam baŋa ne to. O laam ma duri o vo o yi jara yam yiga kam ne, ye o bwei o chorro tem kwaga.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam na nɛ Goliafe konto to, ba duri mo o yiga ne, foone na tiini de ja-ba to ŋwaane.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam déem maa ŋɔɔne da-tei ne ba we, “Nii-na nɔɔno wonto na yɔɔre o nwoŋi dɛ dɛ o gwooni debam tei! Pɛ Sɔɔl gwoni ni mo we, wolo maama ná go nɔɔno wonto, o wó pa kotu ŋweero dedɛ. O ta wó pa kotu mo o bukɔ se o ma o ke o kaane. Kotu sɔŋɔ tiina de daa bá taa ŋwe lampwoo.”

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: David ma bwei balo na zege o tei ne konto to o we, “Nɔɔno ná zaŋe o go Filisi tu wonto, se chaveera yalo o na jege o ke de Isarele tiina bam to ti, bɛ nyɔɔre mo kotu wó na? Filisi tu wonto ye nɔn-kafɛ mo. O za ye wɔ mo se o taa zege o dwoni de Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ jar-keira bam?”

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Jar-keira bam ma tole taane dem ye ba ta kolo maama pɛ wom na wó ke o pa wolo na wó go Goliafe to ba bere David.

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: David zemba-kwea Eliabi ma ni o na zege de nɔɔna bam o lare tei maama to. O bane ma tiini de zaŋe de David ye o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo tu ywo-seeni se n ke bɛ mo? Pei sem fenfee n na yage kagoa ne to, n pɛ wɔ mo nii-se? A lɔre n kamunni dem ni ne. Nmo paale n ba se n nii jara yam keim dem mo!”

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: David ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo amo ke a ja a chɔge? Konto a yé bwei bwia de na?”

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: O ma tutwoni o vo o jwoori o bwei nɔn-gɛ taane dem konto. Ba de ta ma pa‑o boboa nɔɔna bam leira yam.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna badwonna ma ni David na ŋɔɔne tei to, ye ba vo ba lwoni ba bere Sɔɔl. Sɔɔl ma pa ba bwoŋi David.

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo bá‑n wane n jeeri nɔɔno wom se á ke jara. Ta‑n yei we n ye bu mo. Filisi tu wonto nam maŋe o seŋe o nɔn-donne maŋa ne mo, o lɔre jara keim.”

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Ko ma pa David leiri o we, “A kwo, amo yeini a jege a kwo pei mo a nia. Nywoŋo naa kago-vara dwi maama ná yeini ko ba ko ja a vara bam dedoa,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: a yeini a duri a vo a yi-ko, a daare a mage-ko mo se a vere a varem wom ko ni ne. Nywoŋo kom konto laam ná yeini ko pipiri se ko ja amo, a yeini a to a gorege ko ba ne mo, ye a laam daare a go-ko.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: Amo go nywonnu dedaane kago-vara badwonna konto dwoŋi a na. Filisi tu wom de dae kolokolo. A wó go‑o de. Ko ya wo maŋe se o gwooni Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ jar-keira bam.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na jwoŋi amo o yage nywonnu dedaane kago-vara babam jeŋa ne to mo. O ta wora se o jwoŋi-ne o yage Filisi tu wom jeŋa ne.” Sɔɔl laam ma ta de David o we, “Tɔ! Nam véi se Baŋa Wɛ wó taa wo n tei ne.”

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl déem kwei wonto tete jara gwaaro tem o zo David mo. O ma kwei channa yu-gwoŋo o ma pu o yuu kom, ye o ta kwei luu jara-keim gɔrɔ o ma kwoli o nyɔɔne dem.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: David ma kwei Sɔɔl se-zɔɔ kom o vɔ jara-keim gwaaro tem yera ne, ye o laam kwaane se o vo o nii. O na wo zo gwaaro tento dwoŋi o me to, veiŋa maa chamma ka pa‑o. O ma ta de Sɔɔl o we, “Jara zela yanto bá jwoŋi-ne, kokuri to amo wo toŋe de-te a na.” O ma lɔɔre te maama o tiŋi.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Filisi tu wom maa fofɔ o vei mɛmɛ o twɛ David. Nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara-keim nantana kam maa wo o yiga ne o via.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Goliafe na yɔɔre o nii o na David to, o maane we o ye bu mo. O ma gwooni‑o de o na ye bu-pwola na ye lanno to ŋwaane.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: O ma bwei David o we, “N boŋe we a ye kukura mo na, ye n jege da-lɔŋɔ n beene amo baŋa ne konto?” O ma kwei o teo kom jwo-dɛɛra yam yera o ma o sɔɔle lwarem o yage David yuu ne.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: O ta ma ta o we, “Fɔɔre n yi ywo-seeni, se a ná wo kwei n ya-nɔna yam a pa zuna dedaane kago-vara se ba di.”

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: David ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo jege se-zɔɔ de chichwei de kalaŋa mo n beene se n ma n jeeri amo de jara. Amo nam jege Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yere mo a beene n baŋa ne. O maa ye wolo na tei Isarele jar-keira bam maama to. Ko nam ye wonto yere mo n jege n gwoona.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Zem dɛ dento, Baŋa Wɛ wó ke‑m a jeŋa ne. A wó mage‑m a de tega ne, ye a gwoni n yuu. Zem, a ta lage a kwei Filisi jar-keira ya-nɔna yam mo a pa wɛyuu zuna de kago-vara se ba di. Tega baŋa nɔɔna maama laam wó sɛ de chega we, Wɛ wora o na tei Isarele tiina bam.

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: Nɔn-kɔgɔ kolo maama na jeeri ywo-seeni to wó lɔre we, Baŋa Wɛ ná lage o jwoŋi nɔɔna o yage, ko dae se-zɔɔ naa chichwei mo o mae o jwoŋi-ba o yaga. Jara yam ye Baŋa Wɛ mo tei-ya. Wonto nam wó wane abam maama o ke debam jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: O laam ma tore o le kandwɛ o tampɔgɔ kom wone. O ma kwei kandwɛ dem o ke o napana kam ne, ye o vuvugi-ka o dole o yage. Kandwɛ dem ma yɔɔre de vo de lɔ Goliafe tiri, de moore de zo da. Goliafe ma to tega ne, ye o yibia vwi tega ne.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Mo ko na tu tei, David déem mɛ napana dedaane kandwɛ mo o ma o di Goliafe. O ma mage‑o o go ye ko dae se-zɔɔ mo o mɛ o go‑o.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: David ma duri o yi o zege Goliafe baŋa ne. O ta ma le Goliafe tete se-zɔɔ ko pwolo ne, o ma go‑o o daare o gwoni o yuu. Filisi tiina bam na maane we ba babea kam tege to, mo ba maama pipiri ba duri se ba lu.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Isarele jar-keira bam dedaane Judah jar-keira bam ma laare de tiguri-kaasa, ye ba daare ba pɛ Filisi tiina bam kwaga ba pu. Ba ma pare-ba konto taa ba vo ba kwaare Gafa ni ne dedaane Ekoron manchwo-peena ne. Filisi tiina dedɛ twa maa maŋe Saarayim chwoŋa kam yuu ne ba tigi tigi konto, se ko vo ko yi Gafa dedaane Ekoron ne.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Isarele jar-keira bam na zeili Filisi tiina bam ba ti ye ba jwoori to, ba ma lu kolo maama na wo ba tiga jei sem ne to ba ja ba viiri.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: David ma ja Goliafe yuu kom o ja o vo Jerusalem, se ko daare Goliafe jara-keim zela yam mo o jaane yanto o zo o tiŋi o tete vwei wone.

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo David ya na maa vei se o jeeri Goliafe to, mo Sɔɔl ŋɔɔne o taane de o jar-keira yiga tu wom, Abenera mo konto. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Nɔn-doŋo kom ye wɔ bu mo?” Abenera ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, ko na ye chega to, amo yeiri o kwo na ye wolo to.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma bwei‑o o we, “A bu, n kwo ye wɔ mo?” David ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, amo ye Bɛtelehem tu Jesse bu mo.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Ko déem zege dɛ dem konto ne, Sɔɔl lɛɛre o cheiŋi David mo pa o toŋe o pa‑o. David daa wo jwoori o kwo wom sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Jonatan na swoi David ne o na swoi o tete tei to ŋwaane, o pɛ se ba gwoni ni mo daane.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Jonatan ma lɔɔre o gare-bwora kam, ye o kwei-ka o pa David. O ta ma le o jara gwaaro tem o kwei o pa‑o, ko woli de o se-zɔɔ kom, de o taŋa kam, dedaane o tankila kam de.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Sɔɔl déem ná toŋe David jei selo maama ne, ko yeini ko vei yiga lanyerane mo. Konto ŋwaane Sɔɔl ma pa‑o dam o jar-keira bam tetare ne. Sɔɔl keim dem konto ma pwoli nɔɔna bam maama wo, ye ko ta pwoli o nakwa bam de wo.

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: David déem na go Filisi tu wom ye jar-keira bam maa jwoori sɔŋɔ to, mo kaana nwoŋi Isarele teene dem maama wone ba ba se ba jeeri Pɛ Sɔɔl. Ba maa leeni de wopwolo, ya ba sae. Ba maa jege senyɛ ba wɔe ye ba tae kwanno.

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl na nigi ba leiŋa kam to, o wo déem wo dɛ ka taane dem. O bane ma zaŋe. O ma jeeli o wone o we, “Ta‑n nii tei! Ba pɛ se David go nɔɔna morro fuga fuga mo, ye ko daare amo, a go moro moro yerane mo. Ko laam nam daare paare dem mo se ba jwoŋi ba pa wonto.”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Tega déem na poore to, Wɛ ma pa jwori-lɔŋɔ ba ko jwoŋi Sɔɔl de dam. O maa wo o tete diga kam ne o kare o yirisa. David maa jege o kɔnɔ kom o tae ne o na yeini o ke tei to. Sɔɔl de maa zei chichwei o jeŋa ne.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: O ma boŋe o ja we, “A lage a dole‑o mo a tane de kabira kam.” O ma dole‑o kuni belei, ye David de liisi kuni belei wom maama.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl déem ma kɔre David, kolo ŋwaane Baŋa Wɛ wo David tei ne mo ye o lɔ wonto kwaga ne.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: O ná ke woŋo kolo maama, ko vei yiga mo lanyerane, Baŋa Wɛ na wo o tei ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Sɔɔl tage de David o we, “Nii a bukɔ-kwea kam Meraba. Nmo ná jaŋe Baŋa Wɛ jara yam dedaane baare, ye n jege chega n pa-ne, amo de wó pa‑m Meraba, se n ma n ke n kaane.” Sɔɔl déem tage konto ye o boŋe o tete ne o we, “Amo bá ma a tete jeŋa a ma a go David. A nam wó pa Filisi tiina bam chwoŋa se ba go‑o.”

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: David ma leiri Sɔɔl o we, “Amo ye wɔ mo ye a kwo dwi dem de ye bɛ mo Isarele dwia yam wone se a wane a ji pɛ bukɔ baro?”

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam ma ba ka yi se ba kwei Sɔɔl bukɔ Meraba ba pa David. Ba ma jwoori ba kwei‑o ba pa Mehola tu wodwoŋi, o yere na ye Adireli.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl déem ta jege bukɔ wodwoŋi, o yere na ye Mikaale. O maa lage David ni taane. Sɔɔl na lɔre ko ni ne to, o wo ma pwoli.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl daa ma boŋe o tete yera ne o we, “A ná kwei Mikaale a pa David se o ma o ke o kaane, a wó wane a tɔge o ŋwaane a gane David, se Filisi tiina bam na chwoŋa se ba go‑o.” O ma ta de David o we, “Pwola ta wora se n di amo bukɔ wodwoŋi.”

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Ba ma seene ba ta botare sem konto ba bere David, ye o leiri o we, “Abam ná wo lɔre! Á boŋe we ko ye mɔle mo se nɔɔno wane o ji pɛ bukɔ baro na? Amo dae kolokolo yiga da, ye a ta ye yiniga tu.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl nakwa bam ma lwoni kolo maama David na tage to ba bere‑o.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma jwoori o ta-ba o we, “Ta-na á bere David we, ‘Filisi tiina bam na yaare pɛ dedɛ to, o ma lage se o ŋwe jene ba baŋa ne. Konto, pɛɛre delo yerane pɛ na lage se n pa‑o o bukɔ wom ŋwaane to mo ye Filisi tiina bi fwoli-twanno.’ ” Sɔɔl déem tage konto ye o boŋe se o ja Filisi tiina bam je mo o ma o go David.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Pɛ nakwa bam ma jwoori ba ja pɛ kwora kam ba vo David tei. David na nigi to, o wo ma pwoli de taane dem, o na wó ji pɛ wom bukɔ baro to ŋwaane. Kadiri dɛ dem na lage de yi to,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma lɔre jaja we Baŋa Wɛ mo wo David tei ne. O ta ma maane we o bukɔ Mikaale seene o swoi David.

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: Ko laam ma fɔge ko pa o tiini o kɔre‑o. Sɔɔl ma lɛɛre o done David taa, se ko yi o toone.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Filisi jar-keira bam déem yeini ba tui ba ke jara mo de Isarele tiina bam ba ba yaga. Sɔɔl jar-keira yiga tiina bam maama wone David mo di Filisi tiina bam se ko dwoni ba maama. Ko ma pa David yere jage jei maama ne.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl déem zaŋe dɛ dedwe mo o ta Jonatan dedaane o nakwa bam maama we, ba kwaane ba go David. Jonatan yiga déem nam maa tiini ka wo David wone.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: Amo wó da de a kwo se dé ba nmo na seigi mɛ to dé taa zega. A laam wó taa tɛ nmo taane ded‑o, se a nii o na wó leiri kolo to se a laam ba a ta a bere‑m.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Yé swei we o déem na vei se o go Goliafe to, ko ye o tete ŋwea mo o dole o yage. Baŋa Wɛ ma da wonto baŋa ne o di wɔnɔ o pa Isarele tiina bam maama. Nmo na nɛ konto to, n wo pwoli mo. Bɛ nam daa mo kea ye nmo lage se n ja nɔɔno wolo na wo ke kolokolo to n chɔge? Nmo ná go David, ko bá taa jege kuri.”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Jonatan taane dem tiini de dwei Sɔɔl bochare. O ma du duuri o we, “Amo tɛ chega de ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere we, David daa bá te.”

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Jonatan laam ma bwoŋi David ye o ta kolo maama na ke o de o kwo laŋa ne to, o bere‑o. O déem ta jaane‑o mo o vo Sɔɔl tei, pa o toŋe o pa Sɔɔl nenɛɛne boboa kam ne o ya na maŋe o toŋe o pa‑o tei to.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne, jara daa jwoori ya chu Isarele tiina de Filisi tiina tetare ne. David déem ma di-ba ye o fe-ba pa se ba duri o yiga ne.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: O ma kwaane se o dole David de o chichwei dem o tane kabira yera ne. David ma liisi pa se chichwei dem moore de maŋe kabira kam yera ne. Tete dem konto ne David ma duri o lu.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba gilimi David sɔŋɔ ba yere-ko tete dem konto, se tega ná poore, se ba go‑o. David kaane Mikaale ma kaane‑o o we, “Nmo ná wo ke lela n lage jei n vo, jwa ne n lage n te mo.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: O ma ja David o pa o tɔge takworo ne o chu, ye o duri o lu.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Mikaale ma daare o kwei jwoni o tiŋi David sara ne. O ma kwei boŋo koro o kwɛ kwɛ o ke yuu kom seeni, ye o laam kwei gare-jale o ma kwoli ko maama.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl tontoŋena bam na zo sɔŋɔ kom se ba ja David to, Mikaale ma ta de-ba o we, David weele mo.

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: De konto maama de, Sɔɔl toŋe-ba mo se ba jwoori ba vo ba na David yera. O maa we, “Ja-o-na á ba ywo-seeni de o sara kam maama, se a go‑o.”

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na jwoori ba vo ba na to, ba maane we jwoni yerane mo tigi sara kam ne, ye boŋo koro mo wo jwoni dem yuu seeni.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Sɔɔl na lɔre kolo na ke to mo o bwei Mikaale o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n gane-ne, ye n pa a dono wom chwoŋa se o duri o lu?” Mikaale ma leiri‑o o we, “David tage o we, a ná wo yage chwoŋa a pa‑o se o lu, o wó go-ne mo.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: David déem na duri o lu konto to, o ma vo Samuwel tei Rama ne. O ma tole kolo maama Sɔɔl na ke‑o to o bere Samuwel. Ba laam ma da daane ba vo Nayofi ba zoore da.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna ma vo ba ta de Sɔɔl ba we, “David wo Rama teo kodwoŋi ne mo, ko yere ye Nayofi.”

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl na nigi konto to, o ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba ja David. Ba na yi da to, ba ma na Wɛ sampwori sedwonna na zege ba pworisa, ye Samuwel wo ba yiga ne. Baŋa Wɛ jworo ma chu Sɔɔl nɔɔna bam maama baŋa ne. Ba de ma da ba to pworisim ne.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Ba ma ta ba bere Sɔɔl kolo na ke to. O daa ma toŋe nɔɔna badwonna. Ba na yi da to, ba de bobo se ba taa pworisa mo. O daa ta ma toŋe nɔɔna o ke kuni betɔ, ye ba de to pworisim ne.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl tete laam ma zaŋe o kwei Rama chwoŋa, se o da ba kwaga. O na vei o yi vole-kamunu kom na wo Seku ne to, mo o bwei nɔɔna o we, “Samuwel dedaane David wo yein-seeni mo?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ba wo Rama teo Nayofi ne mo.”

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ta na wo chwoŋa ne o maa vei Nayofi to, Wɛ jworo ma chu o de baŋa ne. O maa pworisi o via konto taa o vo o yi Nayofi.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: O na yi Samuwel tei to, mo o lɔɔre o gwaaro, ye o ta wora o pworisa dɛ dem maama wone. O ma tigi da tete dem konto maama ne, se tega ba ka poore. Ko déem ke konto mo ye ba seeri sinseira kam ba we, “Sɔɔl de tɔge o wo sampwori sem wone mo na?”

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: David déem ma zege Rama teo Nayofi ne o duri se o lu Sɔɔl, ye o daare o vo Jonatan tei. O ma bwei Jonatan o we, “Amo bere a ke bɛ mo a chɔge ye n kwo kwaane se o go-ne? Bɛ lwarem mo a ke‑o?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Jonatan ma leiri‑o o we, “Wɛ bá sɛ se ko ke konto. Nmo bá‑n te. Amo kwo bá ke woŋo ye o wo tage o pa a maane ko ni ne. Ko ná maŋe ko ye wo-balaŋa naa wo-kamunu, o yeini o ba seigi-ne. Ko bá wane ko ke konto!”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: David ma ta o du ye o we, “Jonatan, ko seene ko ye chega mo we n kwo beeri se o go-ne mo. O nam yei we nmo yiga tiini ka wo amo wone. Mo kokuri o wo pɛ se n lɔre o boboŋa, o na ba lage se o chɔge nmo wo to ŋwaane. Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane, de nmo tete yere ŋwaane we, amo tiini a bwola de toone.”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Jonatan maa we, “Nmo na lage se a ke kolo maama to, a wó ke a pa‑m.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: David ma leiri o we, “Nmo yei we jwa ne mo chan-doŋa kuri dem di. Ko maa jege se a taa tɔge a wo balo na jeini dedaane pɛ ba di wodiu to mo. Nam sɛ se a vo pwola a seigi da se ko vo ko yi jwa yiga dedaan-ni ne.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Nmo kwo ná maane we a tera ye o bwei a bwia, se n ta we, ‘David ya lwoori chwoŋa mo a tei ne se o ke lela o vo Bɛtelehem o woli de o diga tiina se ba tɔge daane ba ke kaanem, nenɛɛne ba na yeini ba ke bene maama wone o sɔ-yuu kom maama ŋwaane to.’

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Tɔ. Nmo ná tage konto, ye n kwo ná we, ‘Ko lamma’, ta‑n yei we kolokolo bá yi-ne. Se n taane dem baŋa ne, o bane ná zaŋe, lɔre se o boboŋa jaane se o go-ne mo.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Ja! Nam ke woŋo konto n pa-ne, debam na ke ni-sɛɛm daane Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to ŋwaane. Nmo nam daa‑n ná maane we a seene a ke lwarem mo, se nmo tete go-ne. Yé ja-ne n vo n pa n kwo.”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Jonatan ma leiri o we, “Wɛ bá sɛ se ko ke konto. Amo ya ná maane we a kwo boboŋa jaane se o go‑m mo, a ya bá ta a bere‑m na?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Jonatan maa we, “Pa se dé nwoŋi dé vo pwola kam wone.” Ba ma tɔge daane ba kɛ.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Ba na zege da konto to, Jonatan ma ta de David o we, “Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom taa ye maana tu debam balei laŋa ne we, ko ná ke da yalei, amo wó bwei a kwo a lɔre o boboŋa na ye tei de nmo to. O boboŋa yam ná lamma, a wó pa n maane.

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: O boboŋa nam ná jaane se o chɔge‑m, a ta wó pa‑m kwora, ye a daare a yage chwoŋa a pa‑m se n duri n lu. Baŋa Wɛ nam wó pa se ko tiini ko ni amo, nenɛɛne a ná wo ke kolo a na we a wó ke to. Amo ta lwoori Baŋa Wɛ mo a pa‑m, se o taa wora dede‑m nenɛɛne o déem na wo amo kwo tei ne tei to.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: se n ta ta‑n jege amo bia bam swono se ko taa vei wuu. Baŋa Wɛ ná tu o ba o chɔge nmo dona bam maama pa se ba yera saare logo baŋa ne, se n yé yage swono kom konto de a dwi dem.”

english_verse: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
translation_verse: Jonatan déem tɔge konto mo o ma o fɔge o ke ni-sɛɛm dedaane David de o dwi dem. O ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se David dona bam maama bere‑o chega.”

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Jonatan ta ma pa David tɔge o swono kom baŋa ne o du duuri ba ni-sɛɛm dem ŋwaane. Kokuri to, o déem tiini o swoi David mo nenɛɛne o na swoi o tete tei to.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne, Jonatan ma ta de David o we, “Jwa dɛ dem mo ye chan-doŋa kuri dem. Nɔɔna bam wó lɔre we nmo tera, nmo jeiŋa jei sem na wó taa zege kafɛ to ŋwaane.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Tega daa na wó poore to, se n zaŋe n kɛ yiga yiga n vo mɛ n na seigi boboa kam ne to, se ko maŋe dedaane Ezeli kandwɛ dem teiŋa ne. Laam ta‑n cheigi-ne dáane.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: A maa wó pa bu wolo na wo a tei ne to vo o beeri che-tɛɛra yam. Amo ná tage de bu wom a we, ‘Nii mo! Chena yam wo n saŋa kanto ne mo ya twɛ ywo-seeni. Kwei-ya n ja n ba.’ Se n ta‑n yei we ko ye yazura mo. Konto, n wó wane n nwoŋi n na seigi mɛ to n ba. Kokuri to, ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane kolokolo bá ke‑m.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: A nam daa ná tage de bu wom a we, ‘Chena yam wo nmo yiga ne mo ya kɛ ya gaale‑m,’ se n lage jei n duri n viiri. Konto ye se n lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ‑m chwoŋa se n viiri.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Nam yé swei debam balei ni-sɛɛm dem swia! Baŋa Wɛ mo ye maana tu debam laŋa ne taa wuu, se dé wane dé ke dé su ni-sɛɛm dem.”

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: David déem ma vo o seigi pwola kam ne. Chan-doŋa kuri dɛ dem na yi to, pɛ Sɔɔl ma jeini de o dedɛɛra bam se o di kuri dem wodiu.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: O ma jeini o na maŋe o yeini o jei mɛ to ye o sale kabira. Jonatan ma jeini o jeeri‑o. Abenera de ma jeini Sɔɔl takeiri ne. Ko daare ye David jeiŋa jei sem mo tigi kafɛ.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma na, ye o wo tage kolokolo dɛ dem konto ne. Kokuri to o ya boŋe we, “Dɛ delo woŋo mo chege David yiga pa se o wo tu. Tento o lage o kwɛ o tete se ko maŋe de chullu tem mo, se o laam ba o di kuri dem.”

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Tega daa na poore chan-doŋa da yalei dɛ dem ne to, Sɔɔl ma maane we David daa ta tera. O ma ga ga o bwei o bu Jonatan o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye Jesse bu wom wo tu se o di kuri dem wodiu diim dedaane zem maama?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: O tage de amo we, ‘Ja! Debam diga kam mo jege kaanem se dé ke dé ma di kuri dé teo kom ne. Amo zembaaro ma toŋe o bwoŋi-ne. Nam sɛ dé badwoŋo kom ŋwaane, se n pa a vo se a jwoori.’ Konto ŋwaane nam mo pɛ se David zem tere ywo-seeni se o di wodiu nmo tei ne.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
