translation_verse: Sɔɔl na nigi Jonatan na tage kolo to, o bane ma zaŋe o baŋa ne ye o we, “Nmo dae amo bu chekke! N jege yi-dɛɛre ne n nu mo tei! A maane we n lɔge amo kwaga ne, ye n daare n tɔge Jesse bu David kwaga mo. Nmo na ke tei to ye n tete de n nu wom chaveera mo.

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Ta‑n yei we Jesse bu wom ta ná ŋwe, nmo bá wane n di ywoni. N bá‑n na chwoŋa se n di paare dem. Ke lela n toŋe nɔɔna se ba ja‑o ba ba ywo-seeni, se o jege se o te mo!”

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Jonatan ma leiri o kwo o bwei o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo o jege se o te? O ke kɔ mo o ja o chɔge?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Konto baŋa ne mo Sɔɔl kwei o chichwei o dole Jonatan se o kwaane o go. Jonatan laam ma maane we Sɔɔl seene yia mo se o go David.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Jonatan ma pɛ o zaŋe wodiu kom baŋa ne de ban-zɔŋɔ, ye o daa wo di kolokolo chan-doŋa da yalei dɛ dem ne. O wo déem ma tiini ko chɔge de o kwo na jege kolo o toŋe David yera ne to.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Jonatan ma zaŋe o da dedaane bu o vo pwola kalo David na seigi to, ne ba na maŋe ba bane ba tiŋi tei to.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: O ma ta de bu wom o we, “Duri n vo n twɛ che-tɛɛra yalo a na wó ta tento to n ja n ba n pa-ne.” Bu wom na bobo se o duri to, mo Jonatan vaŋe taŋa o ta chene o pa de gaale‑o de kɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Bu wom na yi chene dem na to jei selo ne to, Jonatan ma tɔɔle o ta‑o o we, “Ta‑n via! Chene dem kɛ de wo n yiga ne mo.”

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: O ta ma tɔɔle o we, “Ke lela! Yé ta‑n zega! Ta‑n via!” Bu wom ma twɛ chene dem ye o jwoori o pa o tu wom.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Bu wom nam wo lɔre keim dem konto kuri. Jonatan dedaane David yerane mo yei kolo na wora to.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Jonatan laam ma kwei taŋa kam de ka chena yam o pa bu wom. O ma ta‑o se o ja-ya o jwoori teo kom wone.

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Bu wom na kɛ o daare to, David ma zaŋe kandwa yalo kwaga ne o ya na seigi to, o nwoŋi o vo o yi Jonatan tei ye o daare o vwi o yibia tega ne kuni betɔ. O de Jonatan ma kukwori daane ye ba keera. David nam mo tiini o keeri o dwoni Jonatan.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Jonatan laam ma ta de David o we, “Wɛ taa wo n tei ne! Za n yé swei we dé ke ni-sɛɛm mo daane Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane we, Baŋa Wɛ ye maana tu debam balei laŋa ne, dedaane dé dwia yam laŋa ne se ko taa vei wuu.” Ba na ŋɔɔne ba ti to, David ma zaŋe o kɛ. Jonatan de ma jwoori o vo teo kom wo.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: David déem ma vo Nobi. Wɛ kaanem tu maa wora, o yere mo Ahimeleka. David na tu o tei to, Ahimeleka ma nwoŋi se o jeeri‑o ye o yera sae. O ma bwei David o we, “Bɛ mo ye n vei n yerane ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba tɔge dede‑m?”

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: David ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ mo toŋe-ne. O nam we a yé pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre ni delo o na pɛ-ne to. Ko ná ye a nɔɔna bam, a tage de-ba se ba taa cheigi-ne jei sedwoŋi ne mo.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: N jege wodiu n tei ne na? Lage bworobwooru tenu naa woŋo kolo maama dwi n na jege to n pa-ne.”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Bworobworo kolo yerane na wo amo tei ne to ye kolo na yeini ko tigi da Baŋa Wɛ ŋwaane to mo. Nmo de n nɔɔna bam nam ná wo peini de kaana da yanto ne, á wó wane á kwei-ko á di.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: David maa we, “Chega to, debam de kaana wo yi daane. Amo nɔɔna bam ná maŋe ba yeini ba beeri yɔɔ yerane mo de, ba wó taa cho ba tete de kaana Wɛ ŋwaane. Konto laam na ye wo-chɛɔ to, ko tiini ko ke dwono mo!”

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl tontoŋeno dedoa déem maa wora, o yere na ye Doegi. O maa ye Edom tu ye o kwori o ye Sɔɔl nayera bam yiga tu. Dɛ dem konto ne wonto déem wo Ahimeleka tei ne, o na jege se o kwɛ o tete Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: David ta ma bwei Ahimeleka o we, “Nmo wó ta‑n jege chichwei naa se-zɔɔ n tei ne na? Pɛ wom tontoŋa kam tiini ka lomma mo pa se a wo nɛ pwola se a kwei a se-zɔɔ kom. A maa ba jege jara zele de zele.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Ahimeleka ma leiri o we, “Se-zɔɔ kodwoŋi wora. Ko ye Filisi tu Goliafe wolo nmo déem na go Ela bwolo kom ne to nyem mo. Ko nam kukuli de gɔrɔ ko tigi a gare-wogo kom kwaga ne. N ná lage-ko se n kwei. Se-zɔɔ kodwoŋi daa tera.” David ma leiri o we, “Se-zɔɔ tera ko na dwoi-ko. Amo wó jwoŋi-ko.”

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne David déem ma zaŋe o duri se o lu Sɔɔl yiga ne. O ma vo o yi Gafa teo pɛ Akisi tei.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Pɛ Akisi dedɛɛra bam na nɛ David to, ba ma ta de Akisi ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto ye David mo, ba teo pɛ wom. Ko dae konto na? O teo kom nɔɔna bam yeini ba sae ye ba leeni ba seini‑o mo ba we: ‘Sɔɔl go o dona bam moro de moro. Se ko ná ye David, wonto ma go o dona bam morro fuga de fuga.’ ”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: David na nigi konto to, o ma jeeli nɔɔna bam taane dem maama, ye ko pa foone tiini de ja‑o de Gafa teo pɛ Akisi.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, David na yeini o wo ba tei ne to, o maa ke nenɛɛne o yirisi mo. O déem kare o ke yuu-vuvuga kikia mo, ye o jege ba teo kom manchwoŋo ni bworru o kwɛɛra yɔɔ yɔɔ ye o beiri te yera ne. O ta maa yage o twana yam pa se o lileeru nwoŋi te bɔɔre ya maama.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Pɛ Akisi ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam wo nɛ we nɔɔno wonto ye chichwoo mo na? Bɛŋwaane mo á nam jaane‑o á ba amo tei?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: Amo gɛ chichwooru mo ye á ja‑o á ba amo tei na? A ba lage se wonto taa wo a sɔŋɔ ne o jege-ne o daana!”

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: David déem ma zege Gafa teo kom ne, o duri o vo o seigi peo kodwoŋi bɔɔne wone. Jei sem konto bwola dedaane Adulam teo mo. O chorro de o sɔŋɔ tiina bam maama na nigi we o wo dáane to, ba ma vo o tei.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: David déem ma zege dáane o vo Moaba teo Mizipa. O ma ta de Moaba pɛ wom o we, “A lwoori‑m mo se n pa a kwo dedaane a nu taa wo nmo tei ne, se ko taa nii a na tu a lɔre Wɛ na jege kolo se o ke o pa-ne to.”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: David ma ja-ba o vo o yage Moaba pɛ wom sɔŋɔ ne. Ba maa wo pɛ wom tei ne maŋa kalo maama David déem na kare o seigi o tete jei sem konto ne to.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe Wɛ sampwora Gaadi ma ba o ta de David o we, “Daa‑n yé maŋe gugworo kom ne ywo-seeni! Zaŋe n nwoŋi n vo Judah.” David ma pɛ o zaŋe o vo o zoore Herefa kagoa kam wone. Sɔɔl pɛ ba go Nobi teo kaanem tiina

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl déem maa wo Gibea teo zwoŋo kodwoŋi yuu ne. O maa jei sana kuri ne, ye o zei chichwei o jeŋa ne. O dedɛɛra bam maama maa kaare‑o ba zega. Sɔɔl laam ma ba o lɔre we ba nigi David ŋwa mo.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: O ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam, Benjamin tiina bam, á boŋe we Jesse bu David ná di paare, o ta wó taa yei á ni ne, se o pa abam kare de kadwi ye o daare o pa á taa wo o jar-keira bam yiga ne na?

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo á ke ni daane se á lɔ amo kwaga ne na? Amo tete bu Jonatan mo ke ni dedaane Jesse bu wom se ba chɔge-ne, ye abam wolowolo wo pɛ se a lɔre ko ni ne. Abam bere we á yiga tere amo wone. Amo bu wom maŋe o soge a tontoŋeno pa se o kwaane o na pwola o go-ne, ye á wo tage á bere-ne!”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Edom tu Doegi de déem tɔge o wo Sɔɔl nɔɔna bam tei ne. O na nigi Sɔɔl na tage kolo to, o maa we, “Maŋa kam a na wo Nobi ne to, mo a nɛ Jesse bu wom na tu Ahituba bu Ahimeleka tei.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Ahimeleka ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ se o lɔre David yiga na ye tei to. O ta pɛ David wodiiru, ye o daare o kwei Filisi tu Goliafe se-zɔɔ kom o woli da o pa‑o.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl na nigi konto to, o ma toŋe o bwoŋi Ahimeleka dedaane o sɔŋɔ tiina maama se ba ba o tei. Banto déem ye Wɛ kaanem tiina mo Nobi teo ne. Ba maama na yi Sɔɔl tei to,

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: o ma ta o we, “Ahituba bu, cheigi ywo!” O de ma leiri o we, “Pɛ, a cheiga.”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye nmo sɔ ni dedaane Jesse bu wom, se á ke á chɔge-ne? Nmo pɛ‑o wodiu, de se-zɔɔ, ye n ta ma‑n sɔɔle Wɛ n kwɛ o chwoŋa. Konto ma pa se o lɔ amo kwaga ne, ye o zem tɔge amo nɛ tento se o go-ne!”

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Chega to, ko dae dento dɛ ne mo a bobo se a sɔɔle Wɛ a pa‑o. A nam ke a chɔge mo na? Yé ja taane dento n jeeri amo de a sɔŋɔ tiina bam, se amo yeiri taane dem kolokolo ni ne.”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ta maa we, “Ahimeleka, nmo dedaane n dwi dem maama jege se á te mo.”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: O ma ta de balo na zege ba yere‑o to o we, “Zaŋe-na á go Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam! Kokuri to, ba sɔge ni dedaane David se ba chɔge-ne. Ba maane we David maa duri se o lu amo mo, ye ba wo tage ba bere-ne.” Pɛ dedɛɛra bam maa wo sɛ se ba ma ba je ba dwei Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma vo Nobi teo kom, mɛ kaanem tiina bam na zoore da to. O ma go teo kom nɔɔna bam maama. O pɛ ba go baara, de kaana, de ba bia, ko bere ko woli bu-sese de mo. Ba ta ma go ba naane, de ba bonɛ, ko woli de ba pei maama.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: O ma lwoni o bere‑o Sɔɔl na go Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina bam tei to.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, ta‑n wo amo tei ne. Yé ta‑n kɔre foone. A yei we Sɔɔl beeri debam balei mo se o go. Nmo nam ná wo amo tei ne, cham bá yi‑m.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo ba tage ba bere David ba we, “Filisi tiina bam mo vei se ba ke jara de Keila tiina. Ba nam vere ba mena ye ba ta wora ba fere-ya mo.”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: David nɔɔna bam ma ta‑o ba we, “Nii dé na maŋe dé wo Judah laŋa kam ne mo ywo-seeni, ye dé fona de Filisi tiina bam. Se dé laam nam ná lage dé jeeri-ba Keila ne, ko bá taa ye lɛɛro ko pa debam na?”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: David daa ma vo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se o bwei o lɔre o na wó ke tei to. Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Nam véi Keila leile konto, se amo wó ke Filisi tiina bam nmo jeŋa ne se n di-ba.”

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: David de o nɔɔna bam ma zaŋe ba vo Keila ba jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara. Ba ma wane-ba ye ba vere ba vara ba ja ba viiri. Ba ma go Filisi tiina bam dedɛ, ye ba daare ba jwoŋi Keila tiina bam ba yage.

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: David laam ma lwoori Wɛ o we, “Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom, amo nigi we Sɔɔl lage o ba ywo-seeni mo o chɔge teo kom amo ŋwaane.

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: David daa ma bwei o we, “Se Keila tiina bam, ba wó kwei amo de a nɔɔna bam ba ke Sɔɔl jeŋa ne na?” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Ɛɛ, ba wó kwei abam ba pa‑o.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: David déem maa wo Zifi kagoa kam ne o seigi zwonnu laŋa kam gugworru tem wone. Sɔɔl de ma yɔɔre o beeri‑o mo se o wane‑o o ja. Wɛ maa wo pɛ se Sɔɔl na o jei.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: David déem wo Zifi kagoa kam jei sedwoŋi ne, Horesi ne mo. O na wora to, o ma maane we Sɔɔl nwoŋi o ba se o go‑o.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl bu Jonatan de nam ya vei Horesi. O ma vo David tei, o daare o pa o na baare Baŋa Wɛ dam ŋwaane.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: Jonatan ma ta‑o o we, “Yé ta‑n fona, se a kwo Sɔɔl bá yi‑m o ja. O maŋe o yei we, nmo mo lage n ta‑n ye Isarele tiina Pɛ, se amo laam saŋe n kwaga a taa wo n takeiri ne.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Banto balei daa ma ke ni-sɛɛm Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se ba taa jege chega ba pa daane. Konto kwaga ne mo Jonatan jwoori o vo sɔŋɔ. David maa maŋe Horesi ne.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Zifi tiina badwonna ma zaŋe ba vo Sɔɔl tei Gibea ne. Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Pɛ, David tu o seigi debam laŋa kam Horesi zwonnu tem ne. O wo Hakila peo kom na wo Jesimon tega-kuri seeni to yuu ne mo.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Á ke chega. Baŋa Wɛ swolim taa wo á yuu ne, de á na lage a lanyerane to!

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Nam ta kwaane-na á woli-ne fee. Jwoori-na á vo á lɔre o na wo mɛ chekke to, dedaane nɔɔna balo na nɛ‑o dáane to. Amo nigi we o tiini o wae o peperega.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Véi-na á fɔge á beeri á lɔre o seigim jei sem maama, se á laam ba á ta á bere-ne jaja. Ko kwaga ne, a laam wó da de abam a vo. O ta ná wo laŋa kam konto ne, a wó beeri a na o jeiga. Ko ná maŋe ko ye se a beeri Judah sɔ-yuni tem maama wone mo de, a ta wó ja‑o.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma ke lela ba lwoori Sɔɔl ba vo Zifi, ye Sɔɔl laam saŋe kwaga o yi da. David de o nɔɔna bam déem ya seigi Maon kagoa kam ne mo. Ba maa wo Araba bwolo kom na wo Jesimon tega-kuri seeni to ne mo.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam ma nwoŋi se ba beeri David jei. David de ma ni Sɔɔl ŋwa. O de o nɔɔna bam ma vo peo-kamunu kodwoŋi na wo Maon kagoa kam ne to ba seigi da. Sɔɔl ma lɔre David na wo mɛ to. O ma vo Maon kagoa kam ne o pu o kwaga vira-vira.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam maa wo peo kom daa dedoa ne mo ba via. David de o nɔɔna bam de maa wo ko daa kadwoŋi ne ba kwaane se ba lu Sɔɔl jeŋa ne. Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam ma daare fee se ba yi David de o nɔɔna bam tei se ba li-ba.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Ko nɛ ni ne mo nɔɔno duri o vo o yi Sɔɔl tei ye o we, “Ke-na lela á ba! Filisi tiina bam mo chugi ba puri debam teo kom baŋa ne!”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma ga ga o yage David zeilim. O ma jwoori o pipiri se o vo o jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara. Konto ŋwaane mo ba jege jei sem konto yere ba bwoi we ‘Popɔra Peo’.

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: David déem ma zege dáane o vo En-Gedi o seigi jei sem konto ne.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Jara yalo déem na wo Sɔɔl dedaane Filisi tiina bam tetare ne to ma ti. Sɔɔl na jwoori sɔŋɔ to mo o nigi we David wo En-Gedi kagoa kam seeni.

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Ba na wo chwoŋa ne to, mo ba yi jei selo nayera na yeini ba pe ba pei da to. Peo bɔɔne maa wora de na bwola de chwoŋa kam ni. Sɔɔl ma ywori o zo bɔɔne dem wone se o fo fea. Peo bɔɔne dem konto ne mo David de o nɔɔna bam de déem seigi. Banto nam jwoori ba wo yiga ne mo dáa dáa.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: David nɔɔna bam na nɛ Sɔɔl to ba ma ta de David ba we, “Nii pwola na tigi jaja ka pa‑m tei! Zem dɛ dento mo ye dɛ delo Baŋa Wɛ na tage de taane, de o na taga we, o wó kwei n dono wom o ke n jeŋa ne se nmo ke‑o n na lage tei to.” David ma vwɛ konto mɛmɛ o vo o ja Sɔɔl gɔrɔ kom kuri seeni o gwoni, ye Sɔɔl yeiri ko ni ne.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne mo David boboŋa daane‑o dedɛ de kolo o na ke to.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Taane dem konto mo David mɛ o kuni o nɔɔna teiŋa, ye ko che pa se ba wo ke Sɔɔl kolokolo. Sɔɔl ma zaŋe peo bɔɔne dem wone o nwoŋi se o kɛ.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: David de laam ma pi o nwoŋi peo bɔɔne dem wone ye o zege dáa ne o bwoŋi Sɔɔl o we, “Pɛ! Amo tu, denlei!” Sɔɔl ma pipiri se o nii. David ma vwi o yibia tega ne o pa‑o zula,

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: ye o ta o we: “Amo kwo, bɛŋwaane mo n kare n cheigi balo na tɛ ba we amo kwaane se a chɔge‑m to taane?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Nmo zem nɛ we, n na zo peo bɔɔne dem wone to, Baŋa Wɛ kwei nmo o ke amo jeŋa ne mo. A nɔɔna bam badwonna ya we dé go‑m mo, ye amo wo pɛ-ba chwoŋa. Amo ma ta-ba a we, ‘A bá sɛ a ke a tu wom zonne, o na ye wolo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to ŋwaane.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: A kwo, fɔge n nii gare-zenzware dento a zei a jeŋa ne to! De nwoŋi nmo gɔrɔ kom kuri seeni mo. Amo na yi n yera to, a ya wó wane‑m a go. A na gwoni n gɔrɔ kom, ye a daare n tete a yage to, laam nam lɔre we a ba jege nmo lwarem puga a jei. A bere a wo lɔge nmo kwaga ne. Nmo laam ma‑n pu amo kwaga se n le a momwɛ, ye a wo ke‑m kolokolo a chɔge.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam mo wó bere debam balei wone wolo na jege bora to. Baŋa Wɛ mo wó ŋwe amo jene nmo yuu ne, dedaane n na jege amo n ke tei maama to. Se ko ná ye amo, a bá kwei a jeŋa a ma a dwei‑m de fee de.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Faŋa tiina maa we, ‘Keim tɔge de tu mo.’ Konto to, amo bá ke nmo lwarem.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Amo nam ye wɔ mo ye Isarele tiina pɛ pare-ne se o go? Amo ye kukuri-teka, naa yeenu mo nmo jege n zeila? Ko ba jege kuri.

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: O ta ma ta o we, “Yage, se n jege chega, amo mo toŋe vwa. Nmo nam ke amo lanyerane, ye amo lage nmo chɔgem.

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Nmo zem pɛ se a lɔre we n lage a ni taane. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ ya pɛ‑m pwola se n go-ne, ye n wo sɛ se n go-ne.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná jeeri o dono ye o ja‑o, o daa wó yage‑o se o kɛ mɔle mɔle mo na? Nmo zem na ke-ne lanyerane to, Baŋa Wɛ mo wó ke zaane n yuu ne.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Amo laam lɔre we nmo mo wó seene n ji Isarele tiina Pɛ, ye n paare dem wó zege chekke.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: A nam lwoori‑m mo se n ta n du de Baŋa Wɛ yere we, n ná tu n di paare, n bá‑n chɔge a dwi dem se de ti maama. Yé pa se a yere dem jei a kwo sɔŋɔ kom wone.”

english_verse: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
translation_verse: David déem na wo kagoa kam ne konto to, mo o nigi we Nabale tu se o fane o vara bam koro.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Ta-na ded‑o we: ‘Wɛ wó pa nmo de n sɔŋɔ tiina maama yazura de momwɛ-dɛɛre! Wɛ wó pa se n jeŋa wonnu maama ke lanyerane!

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Amo nam nigi we nmo wora n pa ba fane n vara bam koro mo. A maa lage se n maane we, nmo nayera bam ya na wo debam tei ne to, dé wo daane-ba. Maŋa kalo maama ba na wo Kamele seeni to, ba kolokolo wo jei.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Nam bwei n tontoŋena bam n nii, se ba wó ta konto mo. Zem na ye kuri dim dɛ to mo a lwoori‑m se n ke a nɔn-donno tem lanyerane, dé badwoŋo kom ŋwaane. Pa debam zeina yalo maama n na jege n jeŋa ne to.’ ”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: David nɔɔna bam ma ja o kwora kam ba vo ba pa Nabale. Ba laam ma zege se ba jwoŋi leira.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Nabale ma leiri-ba o we, “David mo ye wɔ? Amo yeiri‑o. Jesse bu wonto nɛ o tete na? Leile konto, tontoŋeno wolo maama ná jeini o boŋe ga, o wó zaŋe mo o lɔ o tu kwaga ne se o taa tei o tete.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Amo bá sɛ se a kwei a wodiu dedaane a na a pa nɔn-yɔɔro telo a na yeiri mɛ ba na nwoŋi to. A bá kwei vara balo a na go se a tontoŋena di to a pa abam.”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: David nɔɔna bam ma jwoori ba vo David tei, ye ba ta kolo maama Nabale na tage to ba bere‑o.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Konto to, fɔge n jeeli se n nii n na wó ke kolo n woli dé maama to. Kokuri lɛɛro mo lage te yi dé tu wom de o sɔŋɔ kom maama, de o na tiini o ye puseŋ-nyeno, ye o ba sɛ o jwoŋi bera to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: handfuls of dried figs. She loaded all the food on donkeys
translation_verse: ). O ma kwei wonnu tem konto maama o vɔ bonɛ baŋa ne.

english_verse: handfuls of raisins, and
translation_verse: ), de kapere-kora maasa bia yalei (

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: O ma ta de o tontoŋena bam o we, “Ja-na wonnu tento á ta‑á wo yiga ne se amo de wó saŋe á kwaga a ba.” Konto maama to, o wo pɛ o baro wom maane ko ni ne.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Abigali ma di o bonaga baŋa ne o kwei chwoŋa o maa via. O wo chwoŋa kam ne mo, se ko maŋe dedaane mɛ na gugwoli ko kaare peo kom to. David de o nɔɔna bam maa tu peo kom yuu ne ba beena. Ba ma jeeri daane.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: David ya boŋe o ja we, “A yɔɔre a yaare a tete mo kafɛ ye a déem wora a yere Nabale jea wonnu kagoa kam wone. Amo ke‑o lanyerane pa se o kolokolo wo jei. Laam nam nii o na mɛ balɔrɔ mo o jwoori o leini lanyerane delo a na ke‑o to.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Amo nam dugi de Wɛ se o pa lɛɛro yi amo, nenɛɛne tega daa ná poore ye a wo go baara balo maama na ye o dwi tiina to pa se ba wolowolo wo daare de dedoa de.”

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Amo tu, a nam lwoori‑m mo se n ma n chɛ-ne de a ná ke kolo a ja a chɔge. Amo yei we Baŋa Wɛ wó pa n paare dem fɔge de zege taa, nmo na ye wolo na jaŋe Baŋa Wɛ jara n pa‑o to ŋwaane. Wɛ bá sɛ se n ke lwarem n ŋwea maama wone.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná pare nmo se o go‑m, n Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo wó taa kwoli‑m se cham yé yi n ŋwea. Ko nam ná ye n dona bam, o ta maa wó pa se ba ŋwea yɔɔre ka jei, nenɛɛne nɔɔno na kwei kandwɛ o ke napana wone, ye o laam dole-ka pa kandwɛ dem jei tei to.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: A yei we Baŋa Wɛ wó seene o ke wo-laaro telo maama o na gwoni ni se o ke o pa‑m to. O ta wó pa se n ji Isarele tiina pɛ.

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: Ko maama ná kea, nmo boboŋa daa bá chɔge, nenɛɛne n ya ná go nɔɔna kafɛ yerane. Nmo boboŋa bá daane‑m de n na mɛ n tete jeŋa n ŋwe n jene nɔn-gwia baŋa ne to. Amo tu, Baŋa Wɛ ná tu o ke‑m lanyerane konto, se n guli amo de gula.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: David ma ta Abigali o we: “Amo wó seini Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom mo, kokuri to, wonto mo toŋe‑m se n ba n jeeri-ne zem dɛ dento.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ mo chege amo chwoŋa se a yé chɔge abam. Nmo ya ná wo ke lela n ba n jeeri debam, tento n baro wom de o nɔɔna maama na ye baara naa bakeiri to ya tega. Dé ya wó go baaro dwi maama na wo o sɔŋɔ kom ne to, se tega daa ba ka poore. Amo dugi de Isarele tiina Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom mo we a tɛ chega mo konto.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: David ma jwoŋi Abigali pɛɛra yam ye o daare o ta‑o o we, “Jwoori n vo sɔŋɔ, se n daare n pa n wo taa tiga. Amo wó ke n na tage tei n bere-ne to.”

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Tega laam na poore ye sana bam nwoŋi Nabale yia ne to, mo o kaane wom tole kolo maama na ke to o bere‑o. Nabale na nigi to, o bochare ma tiini de baane, ye o yera yam maama bobo se ya taa toa.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Da fuga na ke ya woli da to mo Baŋa Wɛ fere Nabale pa o te.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: O ma chɔɔle o yibia tega ne ye o leiri-ba o we, “Amo ye David tontoŋ-kana mo. A maa wó sɛ se a zare o tontoŋena bam nɛ.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Abigali ma ke lela o zaŋe o di bonaga, ye o pa o ka-nyaana banu tɔge‑o ba vo. Ba ma pɛ David nɔɔna bam kwaga ba pu ba vo ba yi David tei, pa se o ji o kaane.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: David nam ya maŋe o di Jezerele teo bukɔ Ahinoam mo o ma o ke o kaane. Abigali laam ma woli da o ye o kaane.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye o ka-kwea kam na ye Sɔɔl bukɔ Mikaale to, Sɔɔl déem ya kwei‑o mo o pa o zo Layisi bu Paliteli. Nɔɔno wom konto déem nwoŋi Galim mo.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Ziifi tiina badwonna déem ma zaŋe ba vo Gibea ye ba ta de Sɔɔl ba we, “David tu o seigi Hakila peo kom yuu ne, jei selo na jeeri Jesimon kagoa kam ne to mo.”

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Ba na yi chwoŋa kalo na wo Hakila peo kom teiŋa ne to ba ma zege ba chwi ba vwoa jei selo na jeeri Jesimon to ne. David ma maŋe kagoa kam wone. O ma ba o ni we Sɔɔl tu se o beeri o jei.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: David na lɔre to, o laam ma zaŋe o vo o yi mɛ Sɔɔl de o nɔɔna bam na tigi to. O ma maane Sɔɔl de o jar-keira yiga tu Abenera na tigi mɛ chekke to. Abenera maa ye Nera bu. Sɔɔl maa tigi o dɔa ye jar-keira bam maama laam maa gilimi‑o ba ke tetare ne.

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto tete ne David dedaane Abisayi ma lɔɔre ba vo Sɔɔl de o jar-keira bam tiga jei sem. Ba na yi da to, dedaane Sɔɔl tigi o jar-keira bam tetare ne mo o dɔa. O chichwei ma moore tega ne de maŋe de o yuu kom seeni. Abenera dedaane jar-keira bam maama maa gilimi‑o ba ke tetare ne, ye ba de dɔa.

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: David ma leiri‑o o we, “Yé ke zonne o yera ne! Nɔɔno ná mage pɛ wolo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to, kotu tusim wó taa wo o yuu ne.

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane, wonto mo wó mage Sɔɔl o go. Wɛ wae o pae se o toa o tete toone, naa o te jara-keim baŋa ne.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam wó che amo se a ma a jeŋa a go wolo Baŋa Wɛ swolim nuga na wo o yuu ne to. Nam pa se dé kwei o chichwei dem, de na moore o yuu seeni to, dedaane o na-kunkwolo kom dé ja dé viiri.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: David ma gɔ Sɔɔl chichwei dem ye o daare o kwei o na-kunkwolo kom te na zege te maŋe o yuu seeni to, ye ba kɛ. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam wo nɛ-ba. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno de wo lɔre kolo na ke to. Ba maama maa tigi ba dɔa ye ba wo zaŋe, Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ ba tiini ba dɔ ba lusi to ŋwaane.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: David dedaane Abisayi ma jwoori ba tɔge bwolo kom ba bɛ daa kadwoŋi kam ne. Ba ma vo ba di peo kodwoŋi yuu ba zege da, ye pwola daga banto de Sɔɔl nɔɔna bam tetare laŋa ne.

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: David ma jwoori o leiri‑o o we, “Abenera, nmo dae babea n dwoi Isarele jar-keira bam maama mo na? Bɛ mo ke ye n ware n pɛ wom se n ta‑n yera? Ba ya tu mo se ba go n tu wom.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Nmo na ke tei tento to ba lana. Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane, nmo dedaane n kwaga nɔɔna bam maama maŋe se á te mo, kolo ŋwaane á wo fɔge á yere a tu wom Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to. Laam nam fɔge-na á nii! Pɛ wom chichwei dem ya na wo o yuu seeni to wo yei ne mo? Se o na-kunkwolo kom de bɛ?”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma lɔre David kwora kam ye o bwei‑o o we, “Amo bu David, nmo mo konto na?” David ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, amo mo konto.”

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Amo tu, a lwoori‑m mo se n cheigi a taane dento. Ko ya ná ye Baŋa Wɛ mo na pɛ se n pare amo tento, a teene we o wó jwoŋi pɛɛre a jeŋa ne ye o leiri o boboŋa yam. Se ko ná ye nabiina mo kwei amo yuu ba mage de nmo nyem, Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se ba na lɛɛro. Kokuri to, ba fe-ne ba le a nabaara tega kam ne, Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ se ka taa ye amo nyem to, ye ba daare ba pa se a kare a zoore jwo-kaana teene ne. Ba laam maa we, a taa kaane jwona.

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Nam yé pa se a jana lu ka ke sa-teena tega ne, yiga yiga dedaane tega kalo na ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem to. Amo bere a ye wɔ mo? Yeenu dento, mo Isarele tiina pɛ tɔge-ne o para? Naa a ye luga mo ye n jege-ne n choa peero tem ne?”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma ta David o we, “Amo bu David, jwoori n ba amo tei! Amo mo ke lwarem. Amo nam daa ba boŋe se a ke‑m zonne. Kokuri to, n zem bere we a jege lonne nmo yibia ne, ye n wo go-ne. Chega to, amo toŋe jworim. A tiini a tusi mo.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: David daa ta maa we, “Pɛ, nii n chichwei dem mo tento. Toŋe n nɔn-donno tem dedoa se o ba o jwoŋi o ja o ba o pa‑m.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ mo yeini o bore o pa nɔɔno maama de o na jege chega de wo-dedoa tei to. Baŋa Wɛ ya pɛ-ne pwola se a go‑m zem, ye a wo ke konto, nmo na ye pɛ wolo o na kuri to ŋwaane.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Amo zem na pɛ se n ŋwea kam jege kuri amo yibia ne to, a lwoori Wɛ mo se amo de ŋwea kam taa jege kuri o yibia ne se o taa cho-ne cham dwi maama wone.”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl laam ma ta David o we, “Amo bu, Baŋa Wɛ swolim taa wo n tei ne. Nmo ná ke kolo maama, ko wó ke lam ko pa‑m.” David ma kwei o chwoŋa o maa kɛa. Sɔɔl de ma jwoori o vo sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo David déem jeini o boŋe o tete ne o we, “Ko laam bwola se Sɔɔl ja-ne o go. A ná duri a vo a seigi Filisi tiina bam tetare ne, ko wó taa gara. A daa ná tera Isarele tiina teo kom maama ne, Sɔɔl wó beeri-ne o ga. Konto maa wó pa se a lu o jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma ni we David duri o vo o wo Gafa ne. O ma yage David beira kam.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe David ma ta de Akisi o we, “Pɛ, nmo yi ná seene de su de amo totoŋa yam, se n le n teene dem wone te-balaŋa dedoa se amo de a nɔɔna bam taa zoore da. Ko dae se amo de taa tɔge a zoore n tei ne te-fɔrɔ konto wone.”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Akisi ma sɛ ye o kwei Zikalag dento dɛ dem ne o pa David. Ko na zege kanto maŋa ne se ko yi zem maama to, Zikalag lɛɛre ko ye Judah pwa bam mo tei-ko.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: David déem ma zo Filisi tiina bam tetare ne bene dedaane chane sena.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne, David de o nɔɔna bam ma yeini ba kwaare jara de Gesura tiina, de Girizi tiina, ko woli de Amaleki tiina bam. Ko zege faŋa faŋa to, teene dem konto tiina déem zoore jei sem konto ne se ko vo ko yi Sura seeni de Ejipti seeni maama mo.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: David de o nɔɔna bam ná jeeri teo kolo maama, ba yeini ba chɔge ko maama mo. Ba ma go ko nɔɔna bam, baara de kaana maama, ye ba daare ba vere ba pei sem, de ba naane dem, de ba bonɛ, dedaane ba kona yam, ko woli de ba gwaaro maama. O laam ma yeini o jwoori o vo Akisi tei.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Akisi de ma yeini o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo zem vei teo kɔ mo n chɔge-ko ye n daare n vere ba wonnu?” David de ma yeini o leiri o we, “Dé vei Judah teo kodwoŋi kagoa kam wone mo dé vere nɔɔna bam,” naa o wae o tɛ we, “Dé vei kagoa kam seeni mɛ Jerameeli tiina na wora to mo dé vere-ba,” naa o we, “Dé vei kagoa kam seeni mɛ Keni tiina na wora to mo dé vere-ba.”

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo David ná jeeri teo kolo de jara, o wó kwaane o go ko nɔɔna bam maama, baara de kaana. O ma yeini o we, “A ná wo go-ba, ba wó wane ba vo Gafa ba ta ba bere Akisi amo na yeini a ke kolo maama to mo.” Maŋa kalo maama David na tu o wo Filisi tiina tetare ne to, o déem yeini o ke konto mo.

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Filisi jar-keira bam ma vo Sunem ba gilimi daane. Sɔɔl ma bwoŋi Isarele tiina bam o ke daane pa se ba jeeri Giliboa ne.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl na yɔɔre o dole o yi o na Filisi jar-keira bam to, mo foone zo‑o, o bochare de ma di kwaa.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: O ma kwaane o bwei Baŋa Wɛ se o nii o na wó ke kolo to. Baŋa Wɛ nam wo sɛ o leiri‑o. Ko ná ye dendwea, naa Yurim de Tumim kandwa yam, naa sampwori, Baŋa Wɛ wo tɔge se baŋa ne o pa‑o leira de fenfee de.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl laam ma ta de o nakwa bam o we, “Véi-na á beeri kaane wolo na wae o bwei chira se o lɔre kolo na wora to á pa-ne. Ko jege se a vo kotu tei ne mo a nii a yiga.” O nakwa bam ma ta‑o ba we, “Kaane wodwoŋi mo wo Endora ne, o na nae chekke.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “Nmo nam yei Sɔɔl na ke kolo ye o zeili chichiri vora de yi-nara maama pa se ba nwoŋi Isarele tega ne to. Bɛ mo ye n lage n kwei kalanchogo n ma n ja amo? Nmo laam ma n lage se ba go amo de!”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma ta o du o we, “Amo dugi de Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere we, n ná toŋe a totoŋe dem n pa-ne, n bá‑n na waarem ko ŋwaane.”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma bwei‑o o we, “Wɔ mo n lage se a bwoŋi se o nwoŋi o ba?” Sɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Bwoŋi Samuwel chiru n pa-ne.”

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Kaane wom na yɔɔre o na Samuwel to, mo o laare cheppe! O ma pipiri o ta de Sɔɔl o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n gane-ne konto? Nmo mo ye Pɛ Sɔɔl!”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma leiri‑o o we, “Yé ta‑n fona, za n ta kolo n na nɛ to n bere-ne.” Kaane wom ma ta o we, “A nɛ chiru mo na nwoŋi tega ne, ye o zaŋe o beene.”

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma bwei o we, “O nyenyego ye tetɛ mo?” Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “O ye nɔn-kwea mo na beene ye o zo gare-dedɔrɔ.” Sɔɔl ma maane we ko seene ko ye Samuwel mo. O ma vwi o yibia tega ne se o pa‑o zula.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Samuwel ma bwei Sɔɔl o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n daane-ne konto? N jaane-ne n jwoori n ba ywo-seeni se a ke bɛ mo?” Sɔɔl ma ta o we, “A wo mo dia, ye a yeiri a na wó ke kolo to. Kokuri to, Filisi tiina bam jeeri-ne mo de jara. Baŋa Wɛ nam lɔge amo kwaga ne mo. O daa ba tɔge sampwori baŋa ne, naa dendwea baŋa ne se o leiri-ne. Konto ŋwaane nam mo tei a bwoŋi‑m se a lɔre a na wó ke tei to.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Samuwel ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ nam na lɔge nmo kwaga ne pa se o ji n dono to, bɛ mo ye n daa‑n bwoŋi-ne se n bwei n nii n na wó ke tei?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na ke kolo de nmo to ye kolo a na wuuri a ta a bere‑m to mo. O jwoŋi paare dem nmo jeŋa ne mo, ye o kwei-de o pa n dwoŋi. David mo konto!

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ déem pɛ‑m ni se n chɔge Amaleki tiina bam de ba wonnu tem maama, o bane na zaŋe de-ba to ŋwaane. Nmo nam wo sɛ n ke o ni dem konto chekke. Konto nam mo pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ zem ke‑m tento.

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl na nigi taane dem konto maama to, mo o to tega ne o tigi da konto yirr. Samuwel taane dem ma tiini de pa foone zo‑o. O yera maa bwomma, o na wo di wodiu dɛ dem konto ne wea de tete maama to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma fɔɔre o yi Sɔɔl yera, ye o maane we o bochare tiini de fwei. O ma ta‑o o we, “Ja, amo tu! Amo na sɛ nmo ni to, a yɔɔre a ve a ŋwea mo, ye a ke nmo na lage tei to a pa‑m.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Konto to, a lwoori‑m mo se n sɛ amo na wó ta kolo to. Yage se a ke wodiu fee se n di. Konto wó pa n na dam se n wane n jwoori n viiri.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma ve ye o we, “Amo bá di wodiu.” O nɔɔna bam ma tɔge de kaane wom ba lwoori‑o. O laam ma sɛ. O ma kwaane o zaŋe wɛɛne, ye o daare o jeini gadwogo baŋa ne.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Kaane wom ya jege na-paale o sɔŋɔ ne o na jege-de o kɔne to. Sento nɛ sem ni ne o ma ja-de o go. O ta ma kwei muni o ma fɔge bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: O na ti wodiu kom yiga to, o ma kwei-ko o pa Sɔɔl dedaane o nɔɔna bam. Ba ma di ye ba daare ba gwoni tega ba zaŋe ba viiri.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Filisi dedɛɛra bam bane ma zaŋe dedaane Akisi ye ba we, “Pa se nɔɔno wom jwoori o viiri! Pa o jwoori o vo teo kolo nmo na pɛ‑o se o taa zoore da to. Yé pa o tɔge debam se dé kwaare jara yam. Ta‑n yei we o wó wane o lɔ debam kwaga ne, ye o pipiri o go dé jar-keira badwonna. Konto wó pa se o de Sɔɔl jwoori ba ke daane.

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Akisi ma bwoŋi David ye o ta‑o o we, “Amo dugi de ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ we a seene a jege n chega mo. Ko zege nmo na tu n me dedaane amo to se ko yi zem maama, amo wo nɛ n wo-lɔŋɔ. Ko ya ná ye amo tei ne, a ya lage se n da dedaane amo mo se dé vo dé ke jara yam. Pwa babam bam nam wo pɛ‑m chega.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Konto to, jwoori n vo sɔŋɔ chemm. Yé zaŋe n ke kolo na wó daane pwa bam to.”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Akisi ma jwoori o leiri o we, “Chega to, n totoŋa yam su amo yi. Amo maa nii nmo nenɛɛne a na nii Wɛ maleka tei to mo. De konto de, Filisi pwa badwonna bam nam mo ve, ye ba tɛ ba we, nmo bá‑n tɔge n vo n ke jara yanto.

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Konto to, jwa zezeŋa ne se á gwoni tega á zaŋe, nmo de nɔɔna balo maama na dɛ dede‑m ba ba amo tei to. Tega ná poore, pa se á kɔgɔ kom zaŋe á jwoori á viiri.”

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Tega na seene ka poore to, David de o nɔɔna bam ma gwoni tega ba zaŋe ba kwei Filisi teo chwoŋa ba maa jwoora. Filisi tiina bam de ma kɛ ba vo Jezerele.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: David de o nɔɔna bam na zege jara kapworo ne to, da yatɔ dɛ ne mo ba vei ba yi Zikalag. Ba ma maane we Amaleki tiina bam mo tu ba di Judah tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam maama. Ba ya tu ba ja jara dedaane Zikalag teo kom, ye ba daare ba zwɛ-ko.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: David de o kwaga kɔgɔ kom ma tiini ba kaase ŋɔɔ! Ba ma keeri taa ye dam daa tere ba tei ne se ba keeri.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: David boboŋa maama ma jei. Kokuri to, nɔɔna bam maama wo déem pɛ mo de ba na gɛ ba bia bam to. Ba ma ke bana se ba dole David de kandwa ba go. David ma sale Baŋa Wɛ yera ne pa se o na baare.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: David laam ma ta dedaane Wɛ kaanem tu Abiatara o we, “Kwei kaanem gare-wogo kom n ja n ba, se dé ma dé bwei Wɛ dé nii dé wó ke tetɛ mo.” Abiatara ma ja gare-wogo kom o ba o pa‑o.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: David ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A zaŋe a pare dé dona banto na? A ná pɛ ba kwaga a pu, a wó yi-ba a ja na?” Wɛ ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, véi-na á zeili-ba, se á wó yi-ba. Abam nam ta wó jwoŋi á nɔɔna bam á yage.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Ba na maa vei to, David nɔɔna bam badwonna ma vo ba na Ejipti tu wodwoŋi na beeri gaao kom wone. Ba ma ja‑o ba vo David tei, ye ba daare ba pa‑o wodiu se o di dedaane na se o nyɔ.

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: Kapere-kora dedaane kekan-wogila bwɛ selei mo ba pɛ‑o ye o di. O na di o ti to mo o dam jwoori, kokuri to, da yatɔ maama mo o wo di wodiu ye o wo nyɔge na, wea dedaane tete maama.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: David ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo ye wɔ nɔɔno mo? N nam nwoŋi yei mo?” Nɔn-doŋo kom ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo nwoŋi Ejipti mo, ye a laam ye Amaleki tu kabaa. Da yatɔ na kɛ to, mo a tu wom dole-ne o yage, a na weele to ŋwaane.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Dé ya vei dé ja jara de teene delo na wo kagoa kam seeni ye Cherete tiina bam zoore da to mo, de Judah laŋa kam tega-kuri seeni, ye dé ta yi kagoa kalo Kaleb dwi tiina na wora to. Dé ma zwɛ Zikalag teo kom dé woli da.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: David ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nmo wó wane n ja-ne n yi mɛ venverena banto na wora to na?” O ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, a wó sɛ a ja‑m se dé vo ba na wo mɛ to. Nam du de Wɛ yere we, n bá‑n go-ne, n nam bá‑n jwoori n kwei-ne n ke a tu wom jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Tega na lage ka yi to, David ma zaŋe ba baŋa ne. O ma lɛɛre o jeeri-ba de jara taa se ko vo ko yi tega na poore to wɛ-zoore maŋa ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo lugi, ko ná dae nɔn-donno bia yana yerane. Banto déem kwei kona mo ba di ye ba duri ba viiri.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: David ma ja vara bam maama pa se o nɔɔna bam kale-ba ba ke ba kɔgɔ kom yiga ne. Ba maa via ye ba we, “Wonnu tento maama ye David nyem mo jara yam ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Puseŋ-nyena de nɔn-yɔɔro déem maa wo David kwaga nɔɔna bam wone. Ba ma ta ba we, “Nɔɔna banto wo wane ba tɔge de debam ba vo ba ke jara yam. Konto ŋwaane, dé bá sɛ se dé pɔɔre wonnu telo dé na vere dé dona bam tei ne to dé pa-ba. Dé wó pa nɔɔno maama kwei o kaane de o bia bam yerane mo o ja o viiri!”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: David ma ta o we, “Amo nɔɔna bam, yé ke-na wo-loŋo dedaane woŋo kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ debam to. Wonto mo kwoli debam, ye o daare o pa dé di dé dona balo ya na tu ba vere debam to.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Abam taane dem tera. Nɔɔna bam maama wó chɛ kolo Wɛ na pɛ debam to, se ko taa mae daane. Balo na vei jara jei to, de balo na maŋe kwaga ne ba nii zela yam baŋa ne to maama wó jwoŋi ko mae daane mo.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Ko na zege dɛ dem konto ne to se ko ba ko yi zem, David lɛɛre o pa Isarele tiina bam tɔge ni dem konto mo.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: David ma ja kolo maama o na vere Amaleki tiina bam tei ne to, o ja o jwoori Zikalag. O ma pa ba le wonnu tem tedwonna ba ja ba vo ba pa Judah nakwa bam na ye o yuudwonna to, ye ba ta-ba ba we, “Nii-na, dé vere wonnu tento Baŋa Wɛ dona bam jeŋa ne mo. Abam de jwoŋi-na pɛɛre á ta‑á jega.”

english_verse: This is a list of the towns where David sent gifts: Bethel, Ramoth in the Southern Desert, Jattir, Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa, Racal, the towns belonging to the Jerahmeelites and the Kenites, Hormah, Bor-Ashan, Athach, and Hebron. He also sent gifts to the other towns where he and his men had traveled.
translation_verse: ko ta woli de Heboron tiina bam. David déem toŋe pɛɛra yam se ya yi teene delo maama o de o nɔɔna bam na kare da ba kɛa ba beira kam wone to mo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Konto maama na jege ko ke to, dedaane Filisi tiina bam kwaare jara mo dedaane Isarele tiina bam. Isarele jar-keira bam ma jage sae ye Filisi tiina bam pare-ba. Ba ma go Isarele tiina bam dedɛ Giliboa peo kom yuu ne.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl de o bia bam ma duri, ye Filisi tiina bam pɛ ba kwaga ba pu. Ba ma go Sɔɔl bia Jonatan, de Abinadaba, de Maliki-Sua.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Jara yam ma tiini ya peene Sɔɔl dedɛ. O dona bam ma na‑o ye ba ta ba chena ba tɔ‑o pa ko tiini ko ke‑o zonne.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ma ta de nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara zela yam to o we, “Le n se-zɔɔ kom n ma n zɔ-ne n go. Amo ba lage se Filisi nɔn-yɔɔro tento yi amo yera ba de zɔ-ne se ba mɔne-ne ba ke chaveera” Nɔn-doŋo kom maa wo sɛ se o go‑o, foone na tiini de jege‑o to ŋwaane. Konto baŋa ne to, Sɔɔl ma vaŋe o tete se-zɔɔ o le. O ma kwei-ko o moore o puga ne, ye o daare o to ko baŋa ne o te.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Ko déem ke konto mo ye Sɔɔl de o bia batɔ bam maama tɔge daane ba te, ko woli de nɔn-doŋo wolo na zei o jara zela yam to, de o kwaga nɔɔna bam maama. Ba maama déem tega dɛ dem konto ne mo.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina balo déem na zoore Jezerele bwolo kom seeni to, de balo na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to ma lɔre we Sɔɔl de o bia bam tege mo, ye Isarele jar-keira bam maama duri ba jage. Ba na nigi konto to mo ba duri ba lage jei ba daare ba teene dem. Filisi tiina bam ma vo ba zoore de wone.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Filisi tiina bam ma jwoori jara kapworo kom ne se ba zane ba le jejegero twa bam yera ne. Ba ma na we Sɔɔl de o bia batɔ bam tege mo ba tigi Giliboa peo kom yuu ne.

english_verse: The Philistines cut off Saul's head and pulled off his armor. Then they put his armor in the temple of the goddess Astarte, and they nailed his body to the city wall of Beth-Shan. They also sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the good news in the temples of their idols and among their people.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye Sɔɔl jara zela yam, ba kwei-ya ba ja zo ba tiŋi ba jwoni Asetare diga kam ne mo. Ba ma daare ba kwei o yera yam ba vo ba pale Bɛte-San teo kabira kam yera ne.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo déem na zoore Jabese Gilead ne to ma ni Filisi tiina bam na ke Sɔɔl tei maama to.

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: Balo na tiini ba ye bembɛ ba wone to ma zaŋe tete ne ba vo ba yi Bɛte-San se tega laam poore. Ba ma pare Sɔɔl de o bia bam yera yam teo kom kabira yera ne. Ba laam ma ja-ya ba jwoori Jabese, ye ba daare ba zwɛ-ya.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne mo ba lage ba kwi sem ba ke daane, ye ba kwei-se ba suli sana kadwoŋi kuri ne, Jabese teo wone. Ba ta ma di ba lwi ye ba vɔ ba nia da yarepɛ.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: David déem di Amaleki tiina bam mo ye o daare o jwoori Zikalag. O maa maŋe da o ke da yalei dedaane Sɔɔl maŋe o te.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: David na jwoori ye ko ke da yatɔ to nɔɔno ma nwoŋi Sɔɔl jar-keira bam wone o ba o tei. Nɔɔno wom déem ya kaare o gwaaro mo, ye o daare o kwei kasolo o ma o taare o yuu o wo-chechɔgɔ kom ŋwaane. O ma yi David tei, ye o vwi o yibia tega ne o zuli‑o.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: David ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo nwoŋi yei ne mo?” O de ma leiri o we, “Amo ya tɔge a wo Isarele jar-keira bam wone mo, ye a duri a lu jara yam wone a ba ywo-seeni.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: David daa ma ta‑o o we, “Ta kolo maama na ke to n bere-ne.” Nɔɔno wom ma leiri o we, “Isarele jar-keira bam duri mo ba jage se ba lu. Ba dedɛ nɛ zonne mo, ba badwonna de ma te. Sɔɔl de o bu Jonatan de ma tɔge ba te.”

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: David daa ma bwei nɔɔno wom o we, “N ke tɛ mo n lɔre we Sɔɔl de Jonatan seene ba te?”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Nɔn-doŋo kom ma leiri o we, “Amo yɔɔre a zege Giliboa peo kom yuu ne mo ye a na Sɔɔl na sale o chichwei dem yera ne o zega. Ko ma maŋe dedaane dé dona bam diini ba sisein-nɔɔna de ba torokooro tem ba duri ba ma yi o tei.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: O ma pipiri o na amo ye o bwoŋi-ne se a vo a woli‑o. A ma sɛ ye a we, ‘Pɛ, nii-ne da!’

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: O ma bwei amo o we, ‘N ye wɔ mo?’. Amo ma leiri‑o a we ‘A ye Amaleki tu mo.’

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: O na tage konto to, a ma lɛɛre a go‑o, bɛŋwaane a lɔre we ko tiini ko ni‑o ye o daa bá wori. A laam ma dɔne paare yipuga kam na wo o yuu ne to, ye a daare a le o jeŋa baŋa kam, se a ja a ba a pa‑m. Amo tu, nii-te da.”

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Ba ma lɛɛre ba keeri taa ye ba vɔ ni se ko vo ko yi dedaan-ni maŋa. Ba wo déem chɔge dedɛ Sɔɔl de o bu Jonatan toone dem ŋwaane, dedaane Baŋa Wɛ tete nɔɔna bam maama ŋwaane, de Isarele tiina bam dedɛ na tege jara yam wone to ŋwaane.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: David daa ma bwei nɔn-doŋo kolo na jaane kwora kam o ba o pa‑o to o we, “Nmo nwoŋi yei ne mo?” O de ma leiri o we, “A ye Amaleki tu mo, ye a laam zoore Isarele tega kam ne.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: David nam ya tage de Amaleki tu wom mo o we, “Nmo toone dem ye n tete yiga mo. N mɛ n ni mo n ŋɔɔne n ve n tete bora, de n na we, nmo mo go Pɛ wolo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to.” David keeri Sɔɔl de Jonatan toone

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: David déem laam ma leeni luseim leiŋa se o ma o guli Sɔɔl de Jonatan gula.

english_verse: and he ordered his men to teach the song to everyone in Judah. He called it “The Song of the Bow,” and it can be found in The Book of Jashar. This is the song:
translation_verse: O ta ma pa ni se ba kwei-ka ba bere Judah tiina maama. O ma bwoŋi leiŋa kam we ‘Taŋa Baŋa Leiŋa.’ Leiŋa kam konto popone ka tiŋi Jasare tɔnɔ kom wone mo. O maa we:

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: “Isarele tiina bam, dé bembɛ sem to dé peero tem yuu ne ba te. Nii-na dé jar-keira dedɛɛra bam na tiini ba to tei!

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Yé ta-na taane dento se Gafa tiina ni. Yé tɔɔle-na-de Asekelon teo kom pwooni ne. Filisi tiina kaana ná nigi-de, ba wó taa chake mo de wopwolo. Balo na yeiri Wɛ to wó taa mɔna.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: Giliboa peero tem, Wɛ bá sɛ se nyɔnɔ daa to á yuu ne. Doa de nam daa bá ne. Abam kare sem daa bá ke wodiiru. Kokuri to, dáane mo babɛ sem jara zela yam maŋe teero wone. Ba daa ba lage ba lwo nuga ba ma taare Sɔɔl jara-keim nantana kam.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl de Jonatan, nɔɔna déem jege ba swono dedɛ! Ba ŋwea wone, ba ye daane mo, ba ta ma tɔge daane ba te. Ba tiini ba wara ba dwoi maaro, ye ba ta dana ba dwoi nywonnu.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Nii-na jar-keira bembɛ sem na to jara tetare ne tei! Jonatan ma te o tigi peero tem yuu ne.

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: Amo choro Jonatan, a wo tiini ko chɔge nmo ŋwaane. Nmo tiini n jege lonne n pa-ne! Swono kolo nmo na jege n pa amo to dwoi nɔɔno de o kaane swono na ye tei to.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Nii-na jar-keira bembɛ sem na to jara wone tei! Ba jara zela yam daa ba jege kuri!”

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne, David ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A jwoori Judah laŋa kam se a vo a taa zoore ba teene dem dedoa ne na?” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we “Ɛɛ, véi.” David daa ma bwei‑o o we, “Teo kɔ mo a nam wó vo?” Baŋa Wɛ maa we, “Véi Heboron.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: David ma zaŋe o vo Heboron se o taa zoore da, o de o kaana balei bam, Ahinoam dedaane Abigali. Ahinoam nam ya nwoŋi Jezerele ne mo, Abigali maa ye Kamele tu Nabale kadeim wom.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: David nɔɔna bam de ba sɔŋɔ tiina maama de déem ma tɔge ded‑o ba vo ba zoore Heboron teo kom de ko nawuura yam wone.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Judah tiina nakwa bam ma vo Heboron ne, ye ba lwo nuga David yuu ne ba tiŋi‑o se o taa ye Judah tiina pɛ. David ma ni we Jabese Gilead tiina mo kwei Sɔɔl ba suli.

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: David ma toŋe nɔɔna ba tei ne de kwora kanto ye o we: “Baŋa Wɛ wó swɛ abam swolim, de á na bere á pɛ wom chega á kwei‑o á suli to.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Amo nam sɔɔle Baŋa Wɛ mo a pa abam se o de bere abam chega, o daare o ke abam lanyerane. Á keim-laao konto ŋwaane amo de wó ke abam lanyerane.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Sɔɔl na tege to, nam ta jege-na baare, se á daare á ta‑á dana! Lɔre-na we Judah tiina bam tiŋi-ne mo se a taa ye ba pɛ.” David sɔŋɔ kom dedaane Sɔɔl sɔŋɔ kom tetare jara yam taane

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Nera bu Abenera déem mo ye Sɔɔl jar-keira bam yiga tu. Sɔɔl na tege to, Abenera ma ja Sɔɔl bu Isi-Bosefa o bɛ Jɔdan buga kam o lu o vo Mahanayim.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: David ma maŋe Heboron ne o di paare Judah tiina bam baŋa ne bena yarepɛ de chichworo.

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe Abenera de Isi-Bosefa dedɛɛra bam ma zege Mahanayim ne ba vo Gibeon.
