english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Zeruya bu Joaba de déem ma ja David dedɛɛra bam o vo o jeeri Abenera de o nɔɔna bam Gibeon bula kam ne. Nɔɔno maama de o jar-keira maa wo bula kam bubɛ ne, kɔgɔ dedoa wo bula kam daa kadwoŋi ne ye kɔgɔ kodwoŋi wo ka daa kakam kam ne pa se ba jeini ba jeeri daane.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Abenera ma ta de Joaba o we, “Le n jar-keira bam wone nɔɔno dedoa dedoa se amo de le dedoa dedoa. Banto maa wó jeeri daane ba jaŋe balei balei se dé nii.” Joaba ma sɛ.

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Ba ma le Benjamin dwi dem nɔɔna fuga-balei na ye Isi-Bosefa kwaga nɔɔna to se ba nwoŋi ba jeeri David nɔɔna fuga-balei dedaane jara.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Ba balei balei na wo jara yam wone to, ba maama ma ja da yu-ywei. Ba laam ma kwei se-zɔɔro ba moore da sɛ ne, ye ba go daane. Ko dɛ konto mo ye nɔɔna finlei-bana bam maama te. Ba ma pa jei sem konto yere we, ‘Se-zɔɔro Kapworo’.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Ko na tu ko chɛ to, nɔɔna bam maama ma lɛɛre ba zo jara wone. David jar-keira bam ma di Abenera de Isarele jar-keira bam.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Zeruya bia batɔ bam, Joaba, de Abisayi, de Asaheli déem tɔge ba wo jara yam wone. Ko ná ye Asaheli, wonto déem wara o dwoi feira.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Abenera ma pipiri o na‑o ye o we, “Asaheli, nmo mo pare-ne konto na?” O de ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ! Amo mo pare‑m.”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Abenera daa ma ta‑o o we, “Nam yage amo se n vo n beeri nɔn-doŋo kodwoŋi n pare. N ná jaane kotu, se n jwoŋi o jara zela yam n ta‑n tei.” Asaheli ma ve se o yage Abenera zeilim.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Abenera daa ta ma kaane‑o ye o we, “Yé ta‑n pare-ne se n ja! Amo ba lage se a fere‑m a de tega ne a go. Nmo ná fe-ne se a go‑m, a daa bá wane n zembaaro Joaba yibia a nii.”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Asaheli nam wo sɛ se o jwoori kwaga. Abenera ma kwei o chichwei dem nabili seeni o tɔ Asaheli puga ne de dam pa se de moore da ye de kɛ de nwoŋi o kwaga ne. Asaheli ma to tega ne o te. Wolo maama na tu o yi mɛ Asaheli na tege o tigi to, kotu wó maŋe dáane mo o zege.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Joaba de Abisayi laam ma zeili Abenera se ba ja. Wɛ-zoore maŋa ne mo ba yi Amma zwoŋo kom seeni. Jei sem konto wo Gibeon kagoa kam chwoŋa ne mo, mɛ na bwola de Gia to.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Abenera ma la Benjamin jar-keira bam o ke daane zwoŋo kodwoŋi yuu ne. Ba ti ba yiga mo se ba ke jara.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Abenera ma tɔɔle o bwoŋi Joaba o we, “Dé lage dé ja jara taa dé go daane dé vo dé yi yei ne mo? N bá‑n pa dé yage konto na? N wo maane we ko kweelim jei wó taa ye wo-chechɔgɔ yerane mo na? Debam maama na ye chorro daane to, nmo bá‑n ke lela n ta de n nɔɔna bam se ba daa yé zeili debam na?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Joaba ma sɛ ye o we, “Amo dugi Ŋwea Tu Wɛ wom yere ŋwaane, nmo ya ná wo tage tento, a nɔɔna bam ya wó kwei tete dem maama ba ma zeili abam ba ja mo.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Joaba ma le o nabɔnɔ kom o wu pa se o nɔɔna bam maama zege. Ba ma yage Isarele tiina bam parem. Ba daa wo mage jara dedaane-ba.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Tete dem konto maama Abenera de o jar-keira bam ma vo ba tɔge Jɔdan bwolo kom ne ba kɛ. Ba ma vo ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. Tega na poore to, ba ta maa vei taa, ba vo ba yi Mahanayim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Joaba na yage Abenera zeilim to, o ma zaŋe se o jwoori sɔŋɔ. O ma jeeli o nɔɔna bam ni ye o maane we ba fuga-nogo mo woli Asaheli wone ye ba tera.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Joaba de o nɔɔna bam ma ja Asaheli yera yam ba vo Bɛtelehem. Ba ma suli‑o o kwo yibeeli dem wone. Konto kwaga ne, mo ba vei konto taa tete dem maama wone. Te-pora ni ne ba ma yi Heboron.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo tigura kam na tigi Sɔɔl diga kam de David diga kam tetare ne to, Abenera ma ba o jege dam dedɛ Sɔɔl kwaga nɔɔna bam maama wone.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl nam ya jege o ka-bia wodwoŋi, o yere na ye Rizapa. Wonto maa ye Aya bukɔ. Dɛ dedwe Sɔɔl bu Isi-Bosefa ma ta de Abenera o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n vo n peini de a kwo ka-bia kam?”

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Isi-Bosefa taane dem ma fuli Abenera wo dedɛ. O ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo pɛ chega we amo ye bebare nyem mo na? Amo wó yeigi Sɔɔl kwaga nɔɔna bam a ke Judah tiina jeŋa ne na? De zem maama, a tiini a kwei a chega maama mo a pa n kwo Sɔɔl, de o diga tiina dedaane o badwonna maama. Amo nam mo chege David pa se o ta wo di nmo, ye n laam kwei kaane wonto taane n ja n jeeri-ne.

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem gwoni ni o tiŋi de David o we, o wó jwoŋi paare dem Sɔɔl dwi dem tei ne o pa David. Wɛ nam wó pa se a na a lɛɛro, nenɛɛne a ná wo pɛ se ni-gwonim dem konto ji chega. Amo laam wó woli David se o di paare Judah tiina de Isarele tiina bam maama baŋa ne, ko na zege Dan laŋa kam seeni se ko yi Beeriseba to.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Isi-Bosefa ma ga ni se o puri de Abenera, o na tiini o kɔre‑o to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Abenera ma toŋe nɔɔna David tei ne o we, “Teo kom maama ye wɔ nyem mo, ye ko dae nmo? Nam sɛ se nmo de amo ke ni-sɛɛm daane, se a ja Isarele tiina bam maama a ba a ke n kwaga ne.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: David ma jwoori o leiri‑o o we, “Nmo taane dem lamma. N nam ná lage se dé fɔge dé ke ni-sɛɛm daane, se n ná beene, se n ja Sɔɔl bukɔ Mikaale n jwoori n ja n ba n pa-ne.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: David ma daare o toŋe nɔɔna Isi-Bosefa tei ne o we, “Jwoori n pa-ne a kaane Mikaale. A déem go Filisi tiina bi mo se a wane‑o a di a ma ke a kaane.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Mikaale déem nam ya zo Layisi bu Paliteli mo. Isi-Bosefa ma pa ba vo ba jwoŋi Mikaale o tei ne.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Ba na maa kɛ to, Paliteli ma tɔge Mikaale kwaga ye o keeri taa o vo o yi Bahurim teo kom. Abenera ma bage‑o o we, o jwoori sɔŋɔ! O ma pipiri o jwoori.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Abenera ma vo Isarele nakwa bam tei o ta de-ba o we, “Maŋa kalo abam na boŋe se David taa ye á pɛ to, ko dae zem.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Chwoŋa laam tiga se á ke á boboŋa na lage tei to. Nam yé swei-na we Baŋa Wɛ ya maŋe o gwoni ni se o tɔge o tontoŋeno David baŋa ne o jwoŋi o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam o yage Filisi tiina bam de dé dona maama jeŋa ne mo.”

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Abenera tete ma vo o ŋɔɔne de Benjamin dwi tiina bam. O laam ma daare o vo Heboron se o lwoni kolo na ke to o bere David, se o taa yei Isarele tiina de Benjamin tiina bam maama na boŋe se ba ke tei to.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Abenera ma ja nɔɔna finlei o ke o kwaga ne ye ba vo Heboron. Ba na yi da to, mo David pɛ se ba ke kuri kamunu ba pa-ba.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne mo Abenera déem tage de David o we, “Pɛ, pa-ne chwoŋa se a vo a la Isarele tiina bam a ke daane se ba jeeri‑m. Ba laam maa wó ke ni-sɛɛm dede‑m se n ta‑n ye ba pɛ, n di paare tega kam maama ne, ne n boboŋa na lage tei to.” David ma bane Abenera o yage chwoŋa ne, pa o jwoori o viiri de o yazura.

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Joaba de David jar-keira bam déem ya vei jara keim ne mo. Ba ma vere jejegero dedɛ ba dona tei ne ba ja jwoori sɔŋɔ. Ba na yi Heboron to dedaane Abenera daa tera. O de David ŋɔɔne ba ti mo, ye pɛ wom pa se o viiri de o yazura.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Joaba dedaane o kwaga kam na yɔɔre ba yi to, mo nɔɔno tage‑o o we, “Nera bu Abenera ya tu ywo-seeni o na Pɛ, ye o pa o jwoori o viiri de o yazura.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Joaba ma vo o zo David tei ye o we, “Abenera na tu nmo tei to, bɛ mo ye n yage‑o pa se o jwoori o viiri mɔle mɔle?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Nmo maŋe n yei Abenera na ye wolo. O tu se o ŋɔ n swa mo o nii, se o lɔre n na-veili dedaane kolo maama n na jege n ke to.”

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Joaba ma nwoŋi da David tei ne, ye o vo o toŋe nɔɔna Abenera kwaga ne se ba ja‑o ba jwoori. Ba ma beeri‑o ba na Sira vole dem seeni. Ba ma ja‑o ba jwoori, ye David yeiri ko ni ne.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Abenera na jwoori o vo o yi Heboron to, mo Joaba jaane‑o o fɔɔre o vo gugworo kodwoŋi ne, teo kom manchwo-peo ni ne. O ma ke nenɛɛne o lage se ba bwɛ woŋo mo daane. Dáane mo o zɔge‑o o puga ne o go, se ko ŋwe Abenera na go wonto choro Asaheli to jene.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: David déem na tu o lɔre we Joaba go Abenera to, o maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ wó zege amo kwaga ne we amo de a nɔn-bia bam maama yiga tera Abenera toone dem wone.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Abenera toone dem jene wo Joaba de o sɔŋɔ tiina baŋa ne. Wɛ wó pa se Joaba dwi dem maama wone, jaweero dwi dwi yé fɔge te ti se ko taa vei wuu. Ŋɔn-pwoni wó le ba badwonna yera ne. Ba badwonna wó taa ye naywanno, de gwaaro. Ba badwonna wó te jara keim wone. Ba badaara wó ga wodiu se ba di.”

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Ko déem dɛ konto mo ye Joaba de o nyaane Abisayi paale ba go Abenera. Ko nam ye o de déem na go ba choro Asaheli Gibeon jara yam ne to ŋwaane mo ba ke konto.

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: David ma ta de Joaba de o nɔɔna bam maama o we, “Á maama kaare-na á gwaaro, se á daare á zo gare-nyenyaaro wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. Dé jege se dé di Abenera lua mo.” David tete ma pɛ Abenera na wo gandwa yalo baŋa ne to kwaga o pu.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Ba ma kwei Abenera ba suli Heboron wone. David ma maŋe o yibeeli dem ne o keeri dedɛ. Nɔɔna bam maama de ma tiini ba keeri.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: David déem dɛ ko ŋwaane o leeni luseim leiŋa kanto Abenera baŋa ne o we: “Abenera ye nɔn-jworo mo, pa se o te toone dento dwi na?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Abenera, ba wo vɔge n je sem. Ba nam wo mɛ chaponno ba vɔ n nɛ de. Nmo yɔɔre n te nɔn-gora jeŋa ne mo!” David na leeni leiŋa kam konto to, nɔɔna bam maama daa ma to keira ne.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Ba ma kwaane se ba kwoori David se o jwoori o di wodiu dɛ dem konto ne. O ma ve ye o du duuri o we, “Amo ná di wodiu ye wɛ wo zo, se Wɛ pa lɛɛro yi-ne!”

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na maane David na ke tei konto to, ba ma sɛ de wopwolo. Ba wo yeini ko da kolo maama pɛ wom na ke to mo.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Dento dɛ dem ne, Judah tiina bam de Isarele tiina bam maama ma lɔre we, Abenera na tege to, ko dae David yiga.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: David déem ma ta de o nɔɔna bam o we, “Abam wo maane we Isarele tiina nɔn-kamunu zem mo tege na?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Amo zem ye Pɛ wolo Wɛ na kuri to mo. De konto de, a nam tiini a bwona mo lage-lage. Zeruya bia balei bam konto tiini ba dana se a wane-ba a che. Baŋa Wɛ nam mo wó waare-ba se ko maŋe de ba totoŋ-lwanno tem!”

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl bu Isi-Bosefa déem ma ni we ba go Abenera Heboron wone. O vɔna ma pare, ye foone de zo Isarele tiina bam maama ko ŋwaane.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Isi-Bosefa déem jege jar-keira yiga tiina balei na ye Beerofa tu Rimon bia. Ba yera maa ye Baana de Rekabi. Ba ye Benjamin dwi tiina mo. Ba déem jeeli Beerofa teo kom ba ke Benjamin laŋa kam wone mo.

english_verse: The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, balo déem ya na zoore Beerofa ne to duri mo ba vo ba zoore Gitayim teo ne. Ba nam ye veira mo teo kom konto ne de zem maama.

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl bu Jonatan déem jege bu o yere na ye Mefibosɛfi. O maa ye gɔrɔ. Maŋa kalo o na jege bena yanu to, mo ba jaane Sɔɔl de Jonatan lua taane ba nwoŋi Jezerele teo wone ba ba. Ba na nigi to mo kaane wolo na jege Mefibosɛfi o nii to kwei‑o se o ja o duri o lu. O na tiini o lage lela to, bu wom ma vere o jeŋa ne o kwori o to tega ne pa se o ji gɔrɔ.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe wea kam na tiini ka dana to, mo Isi-Bosefa tigi o diga ne o sia. Rimon bia Rekabi de Baana ma vo ba yi o sɔŋɔ kom.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Ba ma zo sɔŋɔ kom wone ba ke nenɛɛne ba lage ba beeri muni mo. Ba ma zo o diga kam wo de o tigi o dɔ mo o gadwogo baŋa ne. Ba ma kwei seo ba zɔ o puga ne ba go. Ba ma gwoni o yuu, ye ba ja-ko ba jwoori ba liisi ba viiri. Tete dem konto ne, ba ma yɔɔre ba kwei Jɔdan bwolo chwoŋa kam ba vo taa ba poore tega.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Ba ma ja Isi-Bosefa yuu kom ba vo Heboron. Ba ma zo Pɛ David tei ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Nii, nmo dono Sɔɔl bu Isi-Bosefa yuu mo tento. Sɔɔl déem kwaane se o go nmo mo, ye zem dɛ dento Baŋa Wɛ ŋwe n jene Sɔɔl de o dwi dem maama baŋa ne o pa‑m.”

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem tu o ta de amo we Sɔɔl tega. Kotu ya boŋe we ta-laao mo o tage o bere-ne se o jwoŋi ŋweero de ŋwaane. A ma pa se ba ja‑o ba go Zikalag ne se ko taa ye o ŋweero!

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Abam nam zo nɔn-ŋom diga á go‑o o peiga jei ne ye o dɔa. Á na toŋe puseŋa kikia yalo to, ko wó taa ye tɛ mo á yera ne? Amo dugi we amo de wó go abam mo se ko leiri nɔɔno wom toone dem yuu ne, pa se á yera jei logo baŋa ne.”

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: David ma pa o nɔɔna bam ni se ba go-ba. Ba ma go-ba ye ba daare ba gwoni ba je de ba nɛ. Ba ma kwei ba yera yam ba vo ba pale ba yage Heboron buga kam ni ne. Ba ma daare ba kwei Isi-Bosefa yuu kom ba ja ba vo ba suli Abenera yibeeli dem na wo Heboron ne to wone.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Tura teo Pɛ Hiram déem ma toŋe nɔɔna David tei ne se ba ke pipiu daane. O ma pa se ba ja Sedare da-kwollu ba vo ba pa‑o. O ta ma pa se gwaro, de kandwa-cherena tɔge ba vo, pa se ba lɔ pɛ sɔŋɔ ba pa David.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: O ya jeini Heboron ne o di paare Judah dwi tiina baŋa ne bena yarepɛ de chichworo mo, ye o daare o vo o jeini Jerusalem ne o di Isarele tiina dedaane Judah tiina maama paare bena fintɔ-yatɔ. David na di Jerusalem tei to

english_verse: David told his troops, “You will have to go up through the water tunnel to get those Jebusites. I hate people like them who can't walk or see.” That's why there is still a rule that says, “Only people who can walk and see are allowed in the temple.” David captured the fortress on Mount Zion, then he moved there and named it David's City. He had the city rebuilt, starting with the landfill to the east.
translation_verse: David na di teo kom dam jeiga kam to, mo o lɛɛre o maŋe da o zoore ko wone. O ma bwoŋi ko yere we ‘David teo’. O ma zege mɛ tega kam na suuri ka maŋe daane to o jwoori o lɔ teo kom o zege o kaage jeiga kam maama.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Jebusi tiina déem mo zoore Jerusalem teo kom ne. David dedaane o jar-keira bam ma zaŋe ba vo Jerusalem se ba ke jara de Jebusi tiina bam. Nɔɔna bam konto maa wo jeeli we David wó wane o di ba teo kom. Mo kokuri ba déem mɔne‑o ye ba ta ba we, “Lilwoa de gwane tete wó wane ba che abam se á yé zo ywo-seeni.”

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: David dam dem déem ma fɔge de puli de ke da, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na wo o tei ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: David ma lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ mo seene o pa se o di Isarele teo paare, ye o ta daare o pa se o paare dem fɔge de puli lanyerane Wɛ tete nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam ŋwaane.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: David na zege Heboron ne o vo o zoore Jerusalem ne to, mo o daa ta swo ka-bi dedɛ o woli o kaana bam wone. Ba ma lo bia dedɛ, bakeiri de busankane, ba pa‑o.

english_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
translation_verse: de Ibihara, de Elisua, de Nefega, de Jafia,

english_verse: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. David Fights the Philistines (
translation_verse: de Elisama, de Eliada, dedaane Elifeleti. David di Filisi tiina bam

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bam déem ma ni we ba tiŋi David se o taa ye Isarele tiina pɛ. Ba ma la ba jar-keira bam maama ba ke daane ba vo ba beeri o jeiga se ba ja. David ma lɔre ko ni ne ye o nwoŋi teo kom ne o vo o seigi dalem jei sem ne.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: David ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A véi a jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara, se nmo wó ke-ba a jeŋa ne na?” Baŋa Wɛ ma leiri‑o o we, “Ɛɛ, zaŋe n vo n jeeri-ba, se amo wó seene a ke-ba n jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: David ma vo o yi Baal Perazim o jeeri Filisi tiina bam. O ma wane-ba o di. O laam ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ mage o pore a dona bam baŋa ne mo o zeili-ba, nenɛɛne na na mage ba pore tei to.” Ba ma lɛɛre ba jege jei sem konto ba bwoi we ‘Baal Perazim’.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Dáane mo Filisi tiina bam duri ba daare ba jwona yam ba yage. David de o nɔɔna bam ma pɛ-ya ba ja ba viiri.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Ko na ke da fenfee to, Filisi jar-keira bam daa ta ma jwoori ba ba ba faare Refayim bwolo kom maama.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: David daa ma bwei Baŋa Wɛ se o lɔre o na wo ke tei to. Wɛ ma ta o we, “Nmo ná jeeri-ba, se n yé yɔɔre ba yiga vekke. Nam kaare n tɔge Balesam teeni dem n kekare dáa kadwoŋi kam ne n yi ba kwaga seeni.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Ta‑n nii teeni dem yuu ne. Nmo ná tu n ni ko dɔna de baŋa ne, se n laam zaŋe n jeeri-ba. Ko bere we amo Baŋa Wɛ tete mo dɛ á yiga se a jeeri Filisi tiina bam de jara se a di-ba.”

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: David ma seene o ke kolo Baŋa Wɛ na bere‑o se o ke to. Ko ma pa se o wane Filisi tiina bam o di. O ma zege Gibeon ne o pare-ba o vo o yi Gezere.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo na zeŋe dakaa kam to na gɔge naba-laara yaredo to, David ma pa ba zege. O ma go nabea dedaane na-paale o ke kaanem o zuli Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: David nam ya zo gare-wogo kolo ba na mɛ gare-fefale ba sɔ to mo. O maa tiini o sae de o dam maama se o zuli Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Wonto de Isarele tiina bam maama ma ja Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba jege ba zoore Jerusalem wone. Ba na tiini ba jege wopwolo to, ba maama ma ke sɔɔ ye ba wui nabwanno.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Ba na yɔɔre ba jege Baŋa Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba zoore Jerusalem teo wone tei to mo, Sɔɔl bukɔ Mikaale tɔge o takworo seeni o nii o na kɔgɔ kom. O maa na nɛ Pɛ David na faŋe ye o sae o zuli Baŋa Wɛ tei to, o ma chweese‑o o bochare ne.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Dakaa kam nam ya wo Abinadaba sɔŋɔ ne mo. O sɔŋɔ kom de déem maa wo zwoŋo yuu ne. Ba ma vo ba kwei-ka ba daŋe nabɛ toroko-doŋo baŋa ne. Ba laam ma siseiri ba tu zwoŋo kom kuri ne. Abinadaba bia balei Yuza de Ahio maa tɔge toroko kom ye ba yere-ko.

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: O ma da ba yiga se ba vo Judah teo Baala, se ba daare ba ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba jwoori Jerusalem. Dakaa kam konto nam wora Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane mo. Wonto di paare cherubi sem tetare laŋa ne, se na zege dakaa kam baŋa ne to.

english_verse: with Ahio walking in front of it.
translation_verse: Ahio maa wo ko yiga ne o via.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: David de Isarele dwi tiina bam maama ma leeni lei ba seini Baŋa Wɛ de ba dam maama. Ba ta maa jege kwanno, de senyɛ, de gungwei, dedaane kwɛɛra zela dwi dwi ba kwɛɛre ye ba daare ba sae ba tɔge kwaga.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba yi Nakon na yeini o fere o mena mɛ to. Nabɛ sem ma gare se tete se lage se to. Yuza ma zi Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam se o pa ka fɔge ka zege.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ bane ma tiini de zaŋe Yuza baŋa ne, o na wo sɛ se o tɔge dakaa kam chullu tem to ŋwaane. Nɛ sem konto ni ne, o ma mage Yuza dakaa kam teiŋa ne o go.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: David wo ma fuli dedɛ de Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge o ban-zɔŋɔ kom baŋa o go Yuza to ŋwaane. Konto ma pa o bwoŋi jei sem konto yere we, ‘Pɛrezi Yuza.’ Mo jei sem yere de zem maama.

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: O daa maa wo sɛ se o ja-ka o ja o vo o zo Jerusalem teo wone. O ma lɛɛre o pa se ba ywori ba ja-ka ba vo Gafa tu Obed-Edom sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna ma ta ba bere Pɛ David ba we, “Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam na wo Obed-Edom sɔŋɔ ne to, Baŋa Wɛ swɛ o swolim lanyerane. O wonnu maama de ma vo yiga.” David laam ma vo Obed-Edom sɔŋɔ o vo o ja dakaa kam o ja o ba Jerusalem teo wone de wopwolo dedɛ.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: David déem ya maŋe o chwi vwei dedwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ dakaa kam ŋwaane. Ba laam ma kwei dakaa kam ba zege vwei dem wone. David ma go vara o ke kaanem o zwɛ o pa Baŋa Wɛ, ye o daare o ja yazura pɛɛra o ba se o ma o zuli‑o.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: O ta ma pa se ba chɛ wodiiru tem ba pa Isarele tiina kɔgɔ kom maama, baara de kaana. Nɔɔno maama ma jwoŋi bworobworo dedoa, de nɔn-wɔa, de kekan-wogila bɔŋa dedoa. Ba laam ma jage ba vo ba sam.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Konto maama na ti to, David ma jwoori o tete sɔŋɔ se o sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o yage o sɔŋɔ tiina bam yuu ne. Sɔɔl bukɔ Mikaale ma jeeri‑o chwoŋa ne ye o we, “Nmo wolo na ye Isarele tiina Pɛ wom to zem yage n tete chekke! Nmo tiini n toŋe jworim dedɛ, de n na jale n tete pa se n tontoŋena bam busankan-bia na n chaveera to!”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: David ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo zem sage se a zuli Baŋa Wɛ mo. Wonto mo yage nmo kwo de n kwo sɔŋɔ tiina o daare o kuri amo se a taa nii o nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne. A nam ta wó fɔge a bere a wopwolo de do.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: Amo nam ta lage a yaale a tete a dwoni a na ke tei to mo. Amo nii a tete se a ta dae kolokolo mo, se ko ná ye busankan-bia balo n na tɛ ba taane to, banto wó yɔɔre ba tiini ba zuli-ne mo.”

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Amo nam bá fɔge a dɔne a swono kom o baŋa ne, nenɛɛne a déem na ke tei dedaane Sɔɔl ye a le‑o paare dem wone se nmo laam ji pɛ to.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe David ma ta de Wɛ sampwora Natan o we, “Nii amo mo tento! A zoore sɔ-fɔrɔ kolo ba na kwei Sedare da-ŋonno ba ma lɔ-ko to, ko daare ye Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam laam wo vwei kuri ne.”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Natan ma leiri o we, “Ke n boboŋa na jaane tei maama to, se Baŋa Wɛ wo n tei ne.”

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Véi n ta de amo tontoŋeno David we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: N boŋe we nmo mo wó lɔ sɔŋɔ n pa-ne se a taa zoore da na?

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Ko nam na ye tei to, ko na zege maŋa kalo a na jaane Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne to, se ko ba ko yi zem, amo ta wo fɔge a zo sɔŋɔ wone. Mɛ maama a ná jaane-ba a ja a vo, a yeini a zoore vwei wone mo.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Jei selo maama amo dedaane Isarele tiina bam na beeri dé vo to, amo ta wo fɔge a ta de yiga tiina balo a na kuri se ba taa nii a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam to we, “Bɛ mo ke ye á wo kwei Sedare da-ŋonno á ma á lɔ sɔŋɔ á pa-ne?” ’

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Konto to, ta de a tontoŋeno David we, ‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo na le nmo to, dedaane n déem ye nayero mo gaao ne n nii pei baŋa ne. A ma daare a pa se n di paare amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Mɛ maama nmo na yeini n vei to, a déem tɔge n kwaga konto mo, ye a pa se n dona dwi maama saare tega baŋa ne. Leile konto, amo wó pa n yere tiini de zaŋe, se n ta‑n tɔge n ye logo baŋa nɔn-kamuna bam wone dedoa.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Amo laam nam kwei tega kalo a nɔɔna bam na wó taa zoore ka wone to mo a pa-ba. Ko lage ko taa ye ba tete kugu jei nɔɔn-nɔɔno na bá wane o daane-ba ka wone to mo. Nankɔ-nyena daa bá bɛɛse-ba nenɛɛne ko déem na ke tei,

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Nmo ŋwea kam ná ba ka ti ye ba kwei‑m ba suli mɛ ba déem na suli nmo kwoa bam to, a ta wó pa n dwi dem wone nɔɔno dedoa zaŋe se wonto leiri nmo yuu ne o ji pɛ. A maa wó pa se o paare dem jeini de dam.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Ko ye wonto mo wó lɔ sɔŋɔ amo yere dem zulim ŋwaane. Amo ta wó pa se wonto dwi dem taa di paare dem taa wuu.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Amo wó taa ye o kwo, se o de taa ye amo bu. O ná ke o sa chwoŋa, a lage a ma da-lɔŋɔ mo a ma a de‑o chwoŋa ne, ye a korese‑o nenɛɛne nabiina na ke ba bia tei to.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo ye Isarele dwi tiina Wɛ wom. Nmo nam le wonnu tento maama n bere-ne we a dwi dem wó puli pa se a sɔŋɔ kom jeini de dam. Konto ŋwaane mo pɛ se a na baare a lwoori‑m konto dwoŋi.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: David ma vo o zo Baŋa Wɛ wara-vwei dem o jeini da, ye o ware Wɛ o we: “Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo ye wɔ mo, amo dwi dem de ye bɛ mo, ye n zeini amo tento se ko yi zem?

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people?
translation_verse: De konto maama de, n ta boŋe se n ke-ne lanyerane n woli da! Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo laam nam tiŋi ni mo a jwa dwi dem ŋwaane. Ko maa ye wo-kenkagele ko pa-ne!

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Amo nam daa jege bɛ mo se a ta? Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, amo ye n tontoŋeno mo ye n yei a maama n tia.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Ko ye nmo tete ni-gwonim dem ŋwaane de n boboŋa yam ŋwaane mo n ke wo-kamunnu tento maama, ye n daare n le-te n bere-ne.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, konto ŋwaane mo nmo tiini n ye kamunu! Nmo dwoŋi tera! Nmo yerane mo ye Wɛ. Dé yɔɔre dé yei konto mo chekke.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Debam Isarele tiina bam mo ye dwi dedwe logo baŋa ne. Dwi dedwoŋi tera de na ma de Isarele tiina bam. Nmo déem jwoŋi-ba kabɛɛne wone mo pa se ba ji nmo tete nɔɔna, se n daare n pa n yere zaŋe wɛɛne. Nmo na vere-ba Ejipti tiina jeŋa ne to, n déem ke wo-kenkagela na jege foone to mo ba tetare ne. Ko ta ná ye dwi tiina balo na kwaane se ba che-ba to, n zeili banto mo de ba wa maama.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Nmo ma‑n kuri Isarele dwi tiina bam se ba taa ye nmo tete nɔɔna se ko taa vei wuu. Ko daare nmo Baŋa Wɛ de ma ji banto Wɛ wom.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo seene n ye Baŋa Wɛ chekke mo! Nmo ni taane dem ye chega mo. Nmo nam pwooli wo-laaro tento n pa amo wolo na ye n tontoŋeno to mo.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Amo lwoori‑m se n swɛ a kwaga kam swolim mo, se n ta‑n ke-ba zaane taa wuu. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo na gwoni n ni konto to, n swolim wó yɔɔre de taa tɔge a dwi dem mo se ko taa vei wuu!”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Jehoyada bu Benaya mo nii Cherete tiina bam dedaane Peleti tiina bam. David bia bam ma toŋe kaanem tiina totoŋa ba pa‑o.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: David déem ma kwaare jara o di Moaba tiina bam de. O ma pa se ba peini tega ne ba twoŋi daane, ye o laam kwei ŋona o maŋe-ba kuni betɔ betɔ o vo o ti. Ŋona kam dedɔrem kuni belei ná yi mɛ, ba wó go nɔɔna bam konto mo. Ka dedɔrem yi dedoa ná daare ka yi mɛ, ba wó yage se banto taa ŋwe mo. Moaba tiina bam déem ma lɛɛre ba zo David dam kuri ne, ye ba tui ba ŋwe lampwoo ba pa‑o.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Rehobi bu Hadadezere déem ye Zoba teo pɛ mo. O nam ya maa vei se o jwoori o jwoŋi Yuferata buga laŋa kam teene dem mo o taa tei. David ma jeeri Hadadezere de jara o di.

english_verse: of their soldiers. When he returned, he built a monument.
translation_verse: ). O na jwoori jara yam wone to, o yere déem ma tiini de zaŋe.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: David ma daare o ja o jar-keira badwonna o vo che Aram tiina bam laŋa kam maama. Damasika ne mo konto. Aram tiina bam déem ma zo David dam kuri ne, ye ba ŋwe lampwoo ba pa‑o. Mɛ maama David ná via, Baŋa Wɛ yeini o pa se o di o dona mo jara wone.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: David ma vere sabu-seŋa jara zela yalo Hadadezere dedɛɛra bam ya na jege to o ja o jwoori o vo Jerusalem.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye Teba dedaane Berotayi teene dem Hadadezere na tei to, Pɛ David ma zo de wone o vere channa wonnu dedɛ o ja o viiri.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: Toyi tete déem ya ke jara kuni dedɛ mo de Hadadezere. O ma toŋe o bu Joram se o vo o jɔɔne David o ke‑o yu-ywoŋo lei de o na wane Hadadezere o di to ŋwaane. Joram ma ja lu-nyenno pɛɛra, de sabu-seŋa pɛɛra, de channa pɛɛra o vo o pa David.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: David ma kwei pɛɛra yam konto o pa se ba taa mae ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ. O déem ya maŋe o ke konto dwoŋi de lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa wonnu telo o na vere o dona bam tei ne to mo.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Ahituba bu Zadoki dedaane Abiatara bu Ahimeleka déem ye Wɛ kaanem tiina mo. Seraya maa ye David tɔn-poponno.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Zeruya bu Joaba mo ye David jar-keira bam yiga tu. Ahiluda bu Jehosafate de ma nii woŋo maama se o popone-te o tiŋi.

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo David bwei o we, “Sɔɔl dwi dem nɔɔno wo daare se amo da Jonatan ŋwaane a ke kotu lanyerane na?”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Pɛ David ma bwei‑o o we, “Sɔɔl dwi dem nɔɔno daa wo daare se a ke kotu lanyerane Wɛ zaane dem ŋwaane na?” Ziba ma leiri o we, “Jonatan ta daare bu dedoa. O nam gwarege mo o nɛ sem maama ne o jei.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Pɛ David daa ma bwei o we, “O nam wo yei ne mo?” Ziba ma leiri o we, “O wo Lo-Debara ne mo, Ameli bu Makira sɔŋɔ ne.”

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Jonatan bu wom konto yere mo ye Mefibosɛfi. O kwo-nakwe maa ye Sɔɔl. O na tu o yi David tei to, o ma vwi o yibia tega ne o jɔɔne‑o. David ma bwoŋi‑o o we, “Mefibosɛfi!” O de ma leiri o we, “Amo wolo na ye n tontoŋeno to mo tento.”

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: David ma ta‑o o we, “Yé ta‑n fona. Amo boboŋa maŋe ya ja se a ke‑m lanyerane mo n kwo Jonatan ŋwaane. A wó kwei tega kalo maama ya na ye n kwo-nakwe Sɔɔl nyem to a jwoori a pa‑m. A ta pɛ‑m chwoŋa se n ta‑n zoore amo sɔŋɔ kom ne n di wodiu kolo amo na wó di to.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Mefibosɛfi daa ma vwi o yibia tega ne ye o we, “Amo ye n tontoŋeno mo, a de kukuri-teka ba gare daane. Bɛŋwaane mo ye n boŋe se n ke-ne lanyerane konto?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Pɛ David ma bwoŋi Sɔɔl tontoŋeno Ziba o ta ded‑o o we, “Amo kwei woŋo kolo maama ya na ye nmo tu Sɔɔl de o diga kam nyem to mo a jwoori a pa o naa Mefibosɛfi.

english_verse: Ziba replied, “Your Majesty, I will do exactly what you tell me to do.” So Ziba's family and servants worked for Mephibosheth. Mephibosheth was lame, but he lived in Jerusalem and ate at David's table, just like one of David's own sons. And he had a young son of his own, named Mica.
translation_verse: Mefibosɛfi na gwarege o nɛ sem maama ne to laam ma ba o zoore Jerusalem ne. Maŋa maama o maa tɔge o di kolo maama Pɛ wom na yeini o di to.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Hadadezere kwaga pwa bam maama ma maane we Isarele tiina bam yɔɔre ba di-ba mo jara wone. Ba ma lwoori yibwona Isarele tiina bam tei ne ye ba daare ba sɛ ba pa-ba. Aram tiina bam laam ma kɔre se ba daa woli Amori tiina bam jara keim baŋa ne.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: David ma ta o we, “Amo lage a ke Nahasi bu Hanun lanyerane mo nenɛɛne o kwo de déem na ke amo lanyerane tei to.” O ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba ke Hanun lei de o kwo lua kam. David nɔɔna bam na yi Amon tiina laŋa kam to,

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: Amon tiina dedɛɛra bam ma ta de ba pɛ Hanun ba we, “Nmo pɛ chega we David boŋe lanyerane mo ye o toŋe nɔɔna se ba ba ba ke n kwo lua kam lei na? Lɔre we o toŋe-ba se ba ŋɔ ba nii dé teo kom mo, se o wane o ba o di debam.”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Hanun ma pa se ba ja David tontoŋena bam ba cheeri ba twana yam ba daare chichwo-chwooru. Ba ta ma ja ba gwaaro tem tetare ne ba gwoni ba yage se ko yi ba takeira seeni. Ba laam ma yage-ba se ba viiri de kuri-nɔrɔ.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: David tontoŋena bam ma kɔre se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ, chaveera na jege-ba to ŋwaane. David na nigi ko na ke-ba tei to, o ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba jeeri-ba chwoŋa ne. O ma pa-ba kwora o we, “Maŋe-na Jeriko ne se á twana yam ná nwoŋi maama se á laam jwoori sɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Amon tiina bam ma maane we ba kikia maama laam lwoi David momwa ne. Ba ma vo ba sɔ ni de Aram tiina balo na wo Bɛte-Rehoba ne, de Zoba ne to, ba jwoŋi ba jar-keira morro finlei (

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Ke dam n tete kuri ne se n ta ta‑n jege baare! Pa-na dé jaŋe dé pa dé nɔɔna bam dedaane dé Tu Wɛ wom teene dem ŋwaane. Baŋa Wɛ wó ke kolo na su o yi to!”

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: David na lɔre ko ni ne to, o ma toŋe Joaba se o ja o babɛ sem kɔgɔ kom maama o vo o jeeri-ba de jara.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Amon tiina bam ma gwɛ ba nwoŋi ba chichei ba zege ba te-fɔrɔ kom manchwoŋo ni ne se ba ke jara yam. Ko daare Aram tiina balo na nwoŋi Zoba de Rehobi to, de Toba tiina bam, dedaane Maaka tiina bam de laam ma chichei ba zege teo kom pwola ne ye ba cheiga.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Joaba ma lɔre we ba dona bam lage ba jeeri-ba yiga de kwaga maama mo. O ma kuri Isarele jar-keira bam wone balo na tiini ba yei jara laŋa chekke to, se banto yɔɔre ba jeeri Aram tiina bam.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Jar-keira balo na daare to, o ma ke-ba o nyaane Abisayi jeŋa ne se banto maama vo ba jeeri Amon tiina bam.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Joaba laam ma ta Abisayi o we, “Nmo ná nɛ we Aram tiina bam tiini ba dana ba dwoi amo, se n ba n woli-ne. Amon tiina bam de nam ná dana ba dwoi nmo, amo de wó ba a woli‑m.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Joaba de o jar-keira bam ma ja jara yam ba jeeri Aram tiina bam, ye ba duri ba jage.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amon tiina bam na nɛ we Aram tiina bam duri ba jage to, mo ba de duri ba jwoori ba zo ba teo kom wone, ye ba daare Abisayi de o jar-keira kɔgɔ kom. Jara yam ma ti pa se Joaba jwoori o vo Jerusalem.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Aram tiina bam na maane we Isarele tiina bam wane-ba ba di to, mo ba jwoori ba la ba jar-keira bam ba ke daane.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Zoba teo Pɛ Hadadezere ma bwoŋi Aram tiina balo na wo Yuferata buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to se ba vo ba jeeri Helam ne. Hadadezere jar-keira yiga tu Sobaka déem wo ba yiga ne mo.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
translation_verse: David ma maane ba na ke tei to. O de ma la Isarele jar-keira bam maama o ke daane. Ba ma vo ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam ba lɛɛne ba vo ba yi Helam. Aram tiina bam ma chichei ba fɔge ba zege ye ba jeeri David de jara.

english_verse: It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ko déem ma yi teeni punnu keim maŋa. Ko maa ye maŋa kalo pwa na yeini ba nwoŋi se ba ke jara to mo. David ma toŋe Joaba de o dedɛɛra badwonna, dedaane Isarele jar-keira bam maama, se ba vo ba kwaare jara de Amon tiina bam. Ba ma chɔge-ba ye ba daare ba li Raba teo kom se ba ja. Ko daare David tete ma maŋe Jerusalem ne.

english_verse: he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?
translation_verse: o bane wó wane de zaŋe ye o ta we, ‘Bɛ mo ye á tiini á yi teo kom se á ke jara de-ba? Abam ya yeiri we nɔɔna bam wó dale ba teo kabiri sem ne ba ta che-tɛɛra na?

english_verse: Late one afternoon, David got up from a nap and was walking around on the flat roof of his palace. A beautiful young woman was down below in her courtyard, bathing as her religion required. David happened to see her, and he sent one of his servants to find out who she was. The servant came back and told David, “Her name is Bathsheba. She is the daughter of Eliam, and she is the wife of Uriah the Hittite.” David sent some messengers to bring her to his palace. She came to him, and he slept with her. Then she returned home.
translation_verse: David ma toŋe nɔɔna pa se ba vo ba ja kaane wom ba ba. Kaane wom na tu to, o ma peini ded‑o. Yanto da yam ne kaane wom ya ke o wo zarem mo, ye o daare o kwɛ o tete se ko maŋe de chullu tem. O ma zaŋe o jwoori o sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
translation_verse: Bafeseba ma ja puga, ye o toŋe o ta de David o we, “Amo jege puga mo.”

english_verse: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
translation_verse: Yuria na yi David tei to, mo David bwei o kwaga se o lɔre Joaba, de jar-keira bam laŋa na ye tei to. O ta ma bwei se o lɔre jara yam na vei tei to.

english_verse: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
translation_verse: O laam ma ta de Yuria o we, “Nam véi sɔŋɔ n sii fee.” Yuria na nwoŋi Pɛ sɔŋɔ ne to, mo David toŋe nɔɔna se ba ja pɛɛre ba saŋe o kwaga ba vo ba pa‑o sɔŋɔ ne.

english_verse: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
translation_verse: Yuria nam wo vei o tete sɔŋɔ. O ma maŋe de pɛ tontoŋena bam, o peini pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo kom ni ne.

english_verse: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
translation_verse: David ma maane we Yuria wo vei sɔŋɔ, ye o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo nwoŋi chwo-dɔrɔ n ba n yi ywo-seeni. Bɛ mo tei ye n wo vei sɔŋɔ?”

english_verse: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
translation_verse: Yuria ma leiri‑o o we, “Isarele tiina de Judah tiina bam maama nwoŋi mo se ba ke jara. Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam de wo ba tei ne. Amo yiga tu Joaba de o dedɛɛra bam maama de tigi pwola ne. Ko laam nam wó ke tɛ mo se a vo sɔŋɔ a taa di ye a nyɔa, se a daare a peini de a kaane? Pɛ, a dugi n ŋwea kam ŋwaane de n tete yere dem ŋwaane we, a bá fɔge a ke konto!”

english_verse: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
translation_verse: David ma ta‑o o we, “Nam peini ywo zem, se jwa ne a laam wó yage‑m se n jwoori jara jei sem ne.” Dɛ dem konto ne, Yuria ma maŋe Jerusalem ne o peini o poore tega.

english_verse: David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards.
translation_verse: David ma bwoŋi‑o pa se ba di daane. O ma pa se ba nye Yuria dedaane sana, ye o tiini o bugi. De konto maama de, Yuria wo vei sɔŋɔ se o peini. O maŋe pɛ sɔŋɔ ni ne de pɛ tontoŋena bam mo o peini o sara kam ne.

english_verse: Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab.
translation_verse: Tega na poore tetete to, David ma popone tɔnɔ o toŋe Yuria se o ja o vo o pa Joaba.

english_verse: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
translation_verse: Tɔnɔ kom popone ko we, “Kwei Yuria n zege jar-keira bam yiga ne, mɛ jara yam na tiini ya chana to, se á daare á tutwoni á jwoori kwaga á daare‑o o yerane se dé dona bam go‑o.”

english_verse: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Joaba déem li Raba teo kom mo ye o nii ko maama. O ma kwei Yuria o zege jei selo ba dona bam babɛ sem na daga to.

english_verse: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔɔna ma nwoŋi ba jeeri Joaba jar-keira bam de jara. Ba ma go David nɔɔna bam badwonna ko woli de Yuria tete.

english_verse: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
translation_verse: Joaba ma toŋe kwora David tei ne se o bere‑o jara yam na ke tei to.

english_verse: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
translation_verse: O ma ta tontoŋeno wom o we, “Nmo ná tole jara yam na ke tei maama to n pa pɛ wom n ti,

english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Á swei Gideon bu Abimeleka swia na? Ko déem ye kaane mo zege Tebeza teo kom kabira yuu ne o dole nɔŋɔ namim o de o yuu ne o go. Abam tiini á yi ba kabira kam teiŋa wo bɛ mo?’ Tɔ. Pɛ wom ná bwei‑m konto, se n ta ded‑o we, ‘Nmo tontoŋeno Yuria de tɔge o te mo.’ ”

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom ma seene o vo o yi David tei, ye o tole kolo maama Joaba na bere‑o se o ta to.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: O ma woli da o we, “Dé dona bam ya tiini ba dana ba dwoi debam mo. Ba ma nwoŋi ba teo kom ba jeeri debam de jara pwola kam ne. Dé ma kwaane dé zeili-ba dé jwoori ba teo kom ni ne.

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Dáane mo ba che-tara bam zege ba teo kabiri sem yuu ne ba ta debam. Nmo nɔɔna bam badwonna tega, ye n tontoŋeno Yuria na ye Hiti tu to de tɔge o te mo.”

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: David ma ta de tontoŋeno wom o we, “Nmo ná jwoori, se n ta de Joaba we, ‘Yé pa n wo chɔge de kolo na ke to. Wolo maama na lwoori o vo jara wone to wae o toa. Fɔge n ja baare. Tiini á kwaare-na jara yam de-ba se á di teo kom.’ ”

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Bafeseba na nigi we o baro wom tega jara yam ne to, o ma keeri dedɛ o ŋwaane.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: Lua kam ni na kɛ to, mo David toŋe o pa ba vo ba ja‑o ba ba pɛ sɔŋɔ pa se o ji o kaane. O déem ma lo bakeira o pa David. Kolo David nam na ke to déem chɔge Baŋa Wɛ wo mo.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Nadum wom vara bam gaale dedɛ, naane de pei de bone.

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo veiru tu nadum wom sɔŋɔ. Nadum wom maa wo sɛ se o le o vara bam wone se ba ma ba ke na ba pa o veiru wom. O ma vo o vere yiniga tu wom pia kam se ba ma ba ke o veiru wom na bam.”

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: David na nigi sensɔla kam to, o bane ma tiini de zaŋe dedaane nadum wom ye o ta de Natan o we, “Amo dugi de Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ we nɔɔno wom konto jege se o te mo!

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: O ta wó ŋwe kolo o na vere yiniga tu wom tei ne to kuni bena mo o pa‑o, o na ba jege o ŋwaŋa to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Natan laam ma ta de David o we, “Nmo mo ye nɔɔno wom konto! Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora mo tento: Amo mo kuri‑m se n ta‑n ye Isarele tiina pɛ, ye a jwoŋi‑m a yage Sɔɔl jeŋa ne.

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: A ma kwei Sɔɔl paare dem a pa‑m, ye a ta pa se o kaana bam ji nmo nyem. A ma pa se n di paare Isarele de Judah tiina bam maama baŋa ne. Konto ya ná ba daga mo de, a ya ta wó wane a woli ko wone kuni belei a pa‑m.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Bɛŋwaane mo nmo nam tiini n gwooni amo Baŋa Wɛ taane dem, ye n daare n ke wo-balɔrɔ konto? Nmo pɛ se Amon tiina go Hiti tu Yuria jara ne. Nmo na go‑o to, n laam ma‑n daare n di o kaane!

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Nam lɔre we n diga tiina laam wó taa tɔge jara baŋa ne mo ba toa. Kokuri to, n ve amo mo ye n vere Yuria kaane se o ji nmo nyem.

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: Chega ŋwaane to, a lage a pa se n tete yera nɔɔno mo ke‑m se ko yi. Nmo wó ta‑n nia se a kwei n kaana a pa nɔn-gaa se kotu peini de-ba pwooni yiga ne.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Nmo na ke wɛleere to, n seigi mo n ke. Amo nam wó pa se keim dento ke pwooni yiga ne se Isarele tiina bam maama na.”

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Ko nam na ye tei to, n na tiini n nii Baŋa Wɛ n gwooni de n keim dem to ŋwaane, n bu wom mo wó te.”

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne, Natan laam ma viiri. David bu wom toone Baŋa Wɛ déem ma pa se bu wolo Yuria kaane Bafeseba de David na loge daane to weele ye ko tiini ko chɛ.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: David ma lwoori Wɛ o pa bu wom se o na yazura, ye o vɔ ni. Tete maama ne, o ná yeini o zo diga se o peini, o ta tigi tega ne mo.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: O sɔŋɔ kom nakwa bam ma vo o tei ba kwaane ba lwoori‑o se o zaŋe tega kam ne ye ba ga. O ma ve se o da de-ba o di wodiu.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Bu wom weele da yarepɛ mo ye o te. David dedɛɛra bam ma kɔre se ba pa o lɔre ko ni ne. Ba déem bwɛ ba tete ne mo ba we, “Bu wom ya ta na ŋwe ye dé ŋɔɔne taane de David to, o ve se o leiri dé taane dem. Bu wom laam nam na tege tento to, de wó ke tɛ mo dé ta dé bere‑o? Dé ná wo lɔre, o wó wane o ke zonne o tete yera ne!”

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: David na tole o na we o tontoŋena bam jege woŋo mo ba waase ba bere daane to, o ma maane we bu wom mo tega. O ma bwei-ba o we, “Bu wom tege mo na?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Ɛɛ, Wɛ jwoŋi‑o mo o daare debam.”

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: O dedɛɛra bam ma bwei‑o ba we, “Nmo keim dem ke debam yaau dedɛ. Bu wom ta na ŋwe to, nmo keeri mo o ŋwaane, ye n vɔ ni. O laam nam na tege to, n zaŋe mo n wora n di wodiu. Bɛ mo konto?”

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: David ma leiri-ba o we, “Bu wom ya ta na ŋwe to, amo ya vɔ ni mo ye a keera. A ya boŋe we Baŋa Wɛ wó wane o duri amo yibwona mo ye o pa bu wom wori.

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Amo nam gɛ‑o. Bɛŋwaane mo a daa wó taa vɔ ni? Amo wó wane a pa bu wom jwoori o taa ŋwe na? Dɛ wora amo na wó vo bu wom tei, se wonto daa ba lage o jwoori o ba amo tei.”

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: David déem ma gane o kaane Bafeseba se o pa o bochare peini tega ne. Ba daa ma peini daane ye o ja puga o lo bakeira. Ba ma pa bu wom konto yere we ‘Solomon’. Baŋa Wɛ ma swoi bu wom.

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (
translation_verse: Ko ma pa se o toŋe o ni-jwoŋinu Natan se o vo o pa bu wom yere we ‘Jedidia’, Baŋa Wɛ na swoi‑o to ŋwaane. David di Raba teo kom

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Ko daare Joaba déem daa ta jeeri Amon tiina balo na zoore Raba teo wone to de jara. O ma di teo kom paare jei sem.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: O laam ma toŋe kwora o pa David ye o we, “Amo ke jara de Raba teo kom ye a wane mɛ ba teo kom na bam na zege da ba tui to a ja.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Nam kwaane n la dé jar-keira balo na daare to n ke daane, se n ba n jeeri teo kom de jara n daare n di-ba. Nmo ná wo ke konto, ye amo tete ná di teo kom, amo laam wó jwoŋi yere nmo yiga ne.”

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: David ma seene o la o jar-keira bam o ke daane o vo o jeeri Raba tiina bam de jara. O ma wane teo kom o jwoŋi o tei.

english_verse: and took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about
translation_verse: David ma dɔne sabu-seŋa paare yipuga kam ba pɛ wom yuu ne. Ka dunni daga dedɛ, nenɛɛne kilo fintɔ-tenu (

english_verse: kilograms of gold, and there was a valuable jewel on it. David put the jewel on his own crown. He also carried off everything else of value.
translation_verse: ), ye kandwɛ-nyeno mo meeli ka yera ne. Ba ma kwei kandwɛ dem ba ke David yipuga kam ne. O de o nɔɔna bam déem ta ma pɛ teo kom jejegero dedɛ ba ja ba viiri.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye teo kom nɔn-bia bam, o déem kwei-ba mo o de totoŋ-dɛɛra wone. O ma pa se ba yeini ba taa mae pengasa, de dwoora, de seene ba toŋa, se ba badaara de taa mage wara. David déem ke Amon tiina teene dem maama konto dwoŋi mo. Konto kwaga ne, David dedaane o jar-keira bam maama ma jwoori ba vo Jerusalem.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: David bu Abisalom déem jege nakɔ, o yere mo Tamara. O maa ye ka-laao. David bu wodwoŋi de maa wora, o yere na ye Aminon. Wonto fera maa tiini ya wo o nakɔ Tamara wone.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Tamara ya ta yeiri baaro. Konto to, Aminon ma lɔre we ko wó taa chamma se o yi o nakɔ wom yuu. O ma da ko ŋwaane o weele, boboŋe dem na tiini de daane‑o to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Aminon déem jege yuudwoŋi, o yere mo Jonadabi. O maa ye David zembaaro Simea bu. Jonadabi déem jege swa-goa mo ko ja gaale.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe o ma bwei Aminon o we, “Bɛ mo daane‑m? Nmo ye pa-bu mo ye ko dae se dɛ maama n ta‑n jei de wo-chechɔgɔ. Nam ta n bere-ne kolo na jege‑m to.” Aminon ma ta o we, “A fera mo tiini ya zo a nyaane Abisalom nakɔ Tamara.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Jonadabi ma leiri‑o o we, “Zo n ta‑n tigi n sara baŋa ne, n paale n ke nenɛɛne n weele mo tei. Nmo kwo ná tu se o daane n jaweo kom, se n ta ded‑o we, ‘A kwo, pa a nakɔ Tamara ba amo tei ywo-seeni o ke wodiu o pa-ne. Amo lage se o saŋe wodiu kom a yiga ne se a taa nae, se a taa di-ko o jeŋa ne.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Aminon ma seene o zo o tigi sara wone o ke nenɛɛne o weele mo tei. Pɛ David na tu se o daane o jaweo kom to, mo o tage‑o o we, “Popo, amo lage se a nakɔ Tamara mo ba ywo-seeni o fɔge maasa fenfee o pa-ne, se a di o jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Tamara na yi da to, dedaane Aminon tigi sara baŋa ne mo. O ma zwɛ muni o viiri Aminon yibia ne. O ta ma fɔge maasa ye o tigi o nia.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: Bukɔ wom laam ma le wodiu kom o ke zoŋa ne o pa‑o se o di. Aminon ma ve ye o we, “Nɔɔno maama nwoŋi pwooni ne se á daare-ne na!” Nɔɔna bam maama ma seene ba nwoŋi.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Aminon laam ma ta de Tamara o we, “Nam kwei wodiu kom n ja n zo diga kam wone amo na tigi mɛ to, se a jwoŋi wodiu kom n jeŋa ne a di.” Tamara ma seene o ja wodiu kom o zo o na tigi diga kalo wone to.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: O na jege wodiu kom o ma yi o yera to mo Aminon zi‑o ye o we, “Amo nakɔ, sɛ se dé peini daane!”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: O de ma leiri‑o o we, “A nabɔ, yé fe-ne se dé toŋe totoŋ-zɔɔne dento! Keim-balɔrɔ konto dae se ko ke Isarele tega baŋa ne.

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Aminon maa wo sɛ se o cheigi o taane dem. O na dana o dwoi bukɔ wom to o ma wane o zi‑o o lage.

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Tamara ma leiri o we, “Chwoŋa tera se n zeili-ne! Nmo ná ke konto, ko maŋe ko wó taa ye lɛɛro ko dwoi n na chɔge-ne tento to.” Aminon maa wo sɛ o taane dem.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: O ma bwoŋi o tontoŋeno ye o ta‑o o we, “Vaŋe kaane wonto n ja n nwoŋi n yage pwooni ne, se n daare n pe a bworo kom.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: O tontoŋeno wom ma seene o vaŋe Tamara o ja o nwoŋi ye o daare o fɔge o pe bworo kom. Tamara nam ya zo gare-dedɔrɔ na tiini ko jege nenɔŋa to mo. Tento mo ye gwaaro telo dwi pɛ bukɔ-pwoli na yeini ba zoora to.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Tamara laam ma pɛ tentwarem o chaare o yage o yuu maama, ye o daare o ja o gare-dedɔrɔ kom o kaare kaare. O ta ma kwei o je o daŋe o yuu ne, ye o chwoosa o maa vei sɔŋɔ.
