english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: O nabɔ Abisalom ma na‑o ye o bwei‑o o we, “N nabɔ Aminon mo ke lɛɛro tento nmo yera ne na? O nam na ye n nabɔ to, yé ke sɔɔ se nɔɔna maane ko ni ne. A nakɔ, nam ta yé pa se ko taa wɔe‑m.” Tamara ma vo Abisalom sɔŋɔ ne o zoore da. O maa yɔɔre o jei de wo-chechɔgɔ yerane.

english_verse: When David heard what had happened to Tamar, he was very angry. But Amnon was his oldest son and also his favorite, and David would not do anything to make Amnon unhappy.
translation_verse: David déem ma ni kolo maama Aminon na ke to. O bane ma tiini de zaŋe.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye Abisalom, o wo sɛ se o ŋɔɔne de Aminon, ko ná maŋe ko ye ta-laao naa ta-balɔrɔ de. O déem nam tiini o chuli‑o mo, o na chɔge o nakɔ to ŋwaane. Abisalom go Aminon

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne bena yalei maa kɛ. Abisalom tontoŋena maa wo Baal-Hazora ne se ba fane o pei sem koro. Jei sem konto wo Efrayim teo kom seeni mo. Abisalom ma bwoŋi pɛ bia bam maama se ba da ba jeeri da.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: O ma vo o ta de Pɛ David o we, “Pɛ, amo tontoŋena bam mo wora ba fane a pei sem koro. Nmo dedaane n nakwa ya ná sɛ se á ba da, ko wó taa lamma.”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: David ma leiri‑o o we, “A bu, ko bá wane ko ke konto. Dé maama ná lage dé ba, nmo wó chɔge n jeŋa mo.” Abisalom ta ma kwaane se o nii David wó sɛ o vo na, ye o wo sɛ. David ma sɔɔle Wɛ swolim o pa Abisalom.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Abisalom laam ma ta o we, “Nmo nam ná bá wane n vo, yage se a zembaaro Aminon tɔge de debam o vo.” Pɛ David ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo ye n lage se wonto tɔge o vo?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Abisalom ma tiini o gigili David yia pa se o ga ga o yage o pa Aminon tɔge dedaane pa-bia badwonna bam se ba vo Abisalom pei sem koro fanem ne.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Ba na ti kuri dem yiga to, Abisalom ma pa o tontoŋena bam ni o we, “Fɔge á ta‑á yere-na Aminon. O ná nyɔge sana o bugi, amo wó ke woŋo se ko bere we chwoŋa tiga se á go‑o. Konto ná kea, se á zaŋe o baŋa ne á go‑o. Yé ta‑á fona, se ko ye amo mo pɛ abam ni dem konto. Ke-na dam á tete kuri ne, se á daare á ta‑á jege baare.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Abisalom tontoŋena bam ma seene ba ke kolo o na bere-ba se ba ke to. Ba go Aminon mo. Pɛ wom bia badaara bam maama na nɛ konto to, ba ma di ba bona-sisei ba duri ba viiri.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Ba ta na wo chwoŋa ne ba maa kɛ to, kwora ya maŋe ka yi David ka we, “Abisalom zaŋe o go n bia bam maama. Dedoa daa wo daare.”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Pɛ David na nigi konto to, o ma kaare o gwaaro o wo-chechɔgɔ kom ŋwaane, ye o daare o dole o tete tega ne o tiga. O tontoŋena bam maama de maa zege o tei ne ye ba kaare ba gwaaro.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: David zembaaro Simea bu Jonadabi ma yi o tei o ta o we, “Pɛ, ko dae we ba go n bia bam maama. Aminon yerane mo tega. Abisalom nam maŋe o ja boboŋa se o go‑o ko zege maŋa kam Aminon na chɔge o nakɔ Tamara to mo.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Nam yé sɛ we n bia bam maama tega, se Aminon yerane mo ba goa.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Ko daare Abisalom, wonto déem duri mo o jei. Nɔn-doŋo wolo ba na le se o taa zege o yere teo kom to laam ma tole o na nɔn-kɔgɔ na wo Horon chwoŋa ne ba tɔge zwoŋo yuu ne ba siseiri ba beena. O ma vo o ta pɛ wom o we, “Amo nɛ nɔɔna na zege Horon seeni ba beena.”

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Jonadabi ma ta de David o we, “Nmo bia bam mo konto ba maa beene, nenɛɛne a na maŋe a ta tei to.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: O ni dem maŋe de wo to tega ne, dedaane David bia bam na yi da. Ba maama ma to keira ne ye ba chwoosa baŋa baŋa. David dedaane o nakwa bam de ma tiini ba keeri dedɛ.

english_verse: David was sad for a long time because Amnon was dead. David Lets Absalom Come Home Absalom had run away to Geshur, where he stayed for three years with King Talmai the son of Ammihud.
translation_verse: Abisalom déem nam ya duri o vo o seigi o nu nakwe Talimayi tei ne mo o wora. Wonto maa ye Amihuda bu ye o ta ye Gesura teo pɛ. Abisalom déem maŋe Gesura ne o ke bena yatɔ mo. Ko daare David ma keeri o bu Aminon lua kam o dáane.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: O wo laam ma ba ko to de Aminon toone dem. O boboŋa ma jwoori ya vo Abisalom wone se ba ke daane.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Zeruya bu Joaba déem ma maane we David boboŋa tigi Abisalom wone mo dɛ maama.

english_verse: and he sent someone to bring in the wise woman who lived in Tekoa. Joab told her, “Put on funeral clothes and don't use any makeup. Go to the king and pretend you have spent a long time mourning the death of a loved one.” Then he told her what to say.
translation_verse: Nmo laam ma‑n wó vo pɛ wom tei n ta kolo amo na wó bere‑m to.” Joaba laam ma bere kaane wom kolo maama o na wó ta de pɛ to.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Tekoa tiina kaane wom ma vo o yi pɛ wom yiga o vwi o yibia tega ne o zuli‑o, ye o ta o we, “Pɛ, jan ja! Woli-ne!”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo n laga?” O de ma leiri o we, “Dé kwo, amo baro tega o daare-ne kadeim mo.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: A nam ya jege bakeiri selei mo. Dɛ dedwe mo ba vei kara ye jara to ba tetare ne dáane. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno na tera se o lwɛ-ba to, mo ba dedoa mage wodwoŋi wom o go.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Dé sɔ-yuu kom maama laam nam zege amo baŋa ne se a ja a bu wom a ja a ba a pa-ba se ba go, o na go o choro kom to ŋwaane. Ba maa lage se ba pa a dwi dem ti mo. Wonto yerane laam mo ye a yi na daare. Ba ná go‑o, amo gɛ mo konto, a baro de daa maa ba taa jege bu se ko jwa bwoŋi o yere.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma ta de kaane wom o we, “Jwoori n vo sɔŋɔ, se a wó nii n taane dem baŋa ne se de kwɛ.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Tekoa tiina kaane wom ta maa we, “Pɛ, keim dem konto wo amo de a dwi dem yuu ne mo. Se ko ná ye nmo dedaane paare dem n na jege n di to, daanem dae se de yi‑m.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom laam ma ta o we, “Wolo maama ná ŋɔɔne taane dedaane‑m, se n ja kotu n ba amo yiga ne, se o daa bá na chwoŋa o daane‑m.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Kaane wom ta ma ta o we, “Konto to, nam kwei n Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere dem n du we, wolo na lage se o jwoori o jwoŋi a bu wolo na tege to jene dem to daa yé na chwoŋa se o go a bu wonto de o woli da.” Pɛ David maa we, “Amo dugi dedaane Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere we, n bu wom yu-yua dedoa tete bá gɔ ka to tega ne.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: O laam ma ta Pɛ wom o we: “Dé kwo, lɔre we n wo tɔge chwoŋa de n na jege Wɛ nɔɔna bam n ke keim delo to. Nmo tete bu wo sa-teo ne mo ye n wo pɛ‑o chwoŋa se o jwoori sɔŋɔ. Nmo nam na ŋɔɔne tei de amo to, n de n tete mo konto.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno maama jege se o te mo. Toone nye de na balo na lwogi tega ne to mo, ba daa ware-ba se ba jwoori ba pɛ ba ke jeiga dedoa ne. Wɛ nam ba beeri nɔɔna toone, se ko ná ye balo na ba ŋwae to, o yeini o pore chwoŋa se ba wane ba jwoori o tei.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Pɛ, amo na jaane taane dem a ba nmo tei to, ko ye nɔɔna bam na pɛ foone di amo to ŋwaane mo. A ye nmo tontoŋ-kana mo. A ma boŋe a tete ne we, a ná tu a ta de nmo, n wó wane-ne n woli.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Pɛ, a nam jege chega we nmo wó seene n jwoŋi amo de a bu wom se wolo na kwaane se o chɔge debam to yé yi dé yuu. Wonto lage se dé ga dé tega kam popɔra Wɛ na pɛ debam to mo.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Amo laam nam tɛ a tete ne mo we, ‘Amo wo laam tiga mo de kolo pɛ na gwoni ni se o ke to. Kokuri to, dé kwo, nmo nye nenɛɛne Wɛ maleka mo, n wae n kuri lanyerane dedaane balɔrɔ n pɔɔre daane. N Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó taa wora dede‑m.’ ”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma ta de kaane wom o we, “Amo de lage a bwei‑m woŋo mo, nam yé seigi kolokolo de amo.” Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “A kwo, bwei n bwia yam.”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Pɛ David ma bwei‑o o we, “Joaba yiga tɔge ka wo keim dento wone na?” Kaane wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, amo dugi nmo ŋwea kam ŋwaane we nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane se o fo chega kam nmo yiga ne. Nmo dedɛɛro Joaba mo seene o bere-ne kolo maama a na wó ke to, dedaane kolo maama a na jege se a ta to.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: O nam ke konto maama se ko pa keim dem mo pipiri de kwɛ. Dé kwo, nmo nam maŋe n jege swa mo, ne Wɛ maleka tei, n ma‑n yei kolo maama na ke dé tega kam baŋa ne to.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: David laam ma bwoŋi Joaba ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Tɔ. A lage a ke n boboŋa yam mo. Zaŋe n vo n ja a bu Abisalom n jwoori n ba ywo-seeni.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Joaba déem ma zaŋe o vo Gesura o ja Abisalom o jwoori o ba Jerusalem.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: David nam ya maŋe o pa ni mo o we, “Abisalom maŋe se o vo o tete sɔŋɔ kom mo o taa wora. A bá sɛ se o ba amo tei.” Abisalom ma seene o vo o zoore o tete sɔŋɔ kom ne ye o wo nɛ pɛ wom yibia.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: O déem yeini o pa se ba fa o yuu bedwe mo bene maama wone, o yu-ywei sem na tiini se dɔra ye se duna to ŋwaane. Ba ná yeini ba gwoni-se, se dunni wó taa maŋe de kilo telei mo.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: O déem jege bakeiri setɔ de busankana dedoa mo. Busankana kam yere maa ye Tamara. O na tu o ke nɔɔno to, o tiini o lana dedɛ.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Abisalom déem zo Jerusalem ne bena yalei mo, ye o wo wane pɛ wom yibia o na.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: O ma toŋe o ta se Joaba ba o tei se o daare o ja taane dem o vo Pɛ David tei o pa‑o. Joaba ma ve se o vo Abisalom tei. Abisalom ta ma toŋe Joaba kwaga ne kuni balei maama ye o daa ta wo sɛ se o ba.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Joaba laam ma zaŋe o vo Abisalom sɔŋɔ o bwei‑o o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n pa n tontoŋena vo ba zwɛ a kara kam?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Abisalom ma leiri o we, “Amo toŋe n kwaga ne se n ba amo tei ye n wo sɛ. A ya lage se n vo pɛ wom tei n bwei‑o mo we, ‘Bɛŋwaane mo amo bere a zege Gesura ne a ba ywo-seeni? Ko nye de a ya ná maŋe dáane mo a zoora, ko ya wó taa gara ko pa-ne.’ Tɔ. Amo nam ta lage se a na pɛ wom mo. O nam ná yei we a keim wo maŋe, se o go-ne.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Joaba ma vo Pɛ David tei o tole kolo maama Abisalom na tage to o bere‑o. David ma pa ba bwoŋi Abisalom se o ba. O na yi da to, mo o vwi o yibia tega ne o ware‑o. Pɛ wom ma sɛ o peiga ye o ja‑o o kukwori.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: O ma yeini o gwoni tega o vo teo kom manchwoŋo ni chwoŋa kam o zega. O ná yeini o na nɔɔno na jege taane o maa vei pɛ tei se o di-de o pa kotu, Abisalom wó fɔɔre o yi kotu tei mo o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo nwoŋi yei ne mo?” Nɔɔno wom laam maa wó ta o na nwoŋi Isarele teo kolo ne to.

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Abisalom wó yeini o ta‑o mo o we, “Ɛhɛɛ. Nmo taane dem wora, n nam jege bora de. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam mo tere pɛ nakwa bam wone se o nii de baŋa ne o pa‑m.

english_verse: I wish someone would make me the judge around here! I would be fair to everyone.”
translation_verse: Amo de ya ná jege chwoŋa se a tɔge a nii taana baŋa ne mo tento, nɔɔna ya wó wane ba ba amo tei, se a bore chega bora a pa-ba.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Ko ta woli da to, nɔɔna ná yeini ba yi Abisalom tei se ba tiiri ba jɔɔne‑o, o wó tei o jeŋa mo o vaŋe-ba o yi o yera, o kukwori-ba.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Abisalom déem yeini o jeeri balo maama na jege taane ba tui pɛ tei to o ke konto mo. O ma tɔge chwoŋa kam konto o soge Isarele tiina bam dedɛ o ke o kwaga ne.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne, bena yana ma kɛ. Abisalom ma zaŋe dɛ dedwe o vo o ta de pɛ wom o we, “Jan ja! Pa-ne chwoŋa se a vo Heboron a kwei ni-gwonim delo a déem na tiŋi dedaane Baŋa Wɛ to.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Amo déem na wo Gesura ne ye a zoore de Aram tiina bam to, mo a gwoni ni a we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ ná jwoori o ja-ne o ba Jerusalem, amo wó vo Heboron a ke kaanem a zuli‑o.’ ”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma pa‑o chwoŋa. Abisalom ma seene o zaŋe o vo Heboron.

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: David ma ta de o nakwa balo na wo o tei ne Jerusalem wone to o we, “Pa-na se dé zaŋe dé duri dé nwoŋi da teo kom wone. Dé ná wo ke lela dé lu Abisalom jeŋa ne, o bá dáane o ba o yi debam, ye o go debam de dé teo kom nɔɔna maama.”

english_verse: David left behind ten of his wives to take care of the palace, but the rest of his family and his officials and soldiers went with him. They stopped at the last house at the edge of the city.
translation_verse: Pɛ David na nwoŋi konto to, mo nɔɔna bam maama tɔge o kwaga ba via. Ba ma vo ba yi teo kom ni. Ba ma maŋe da ba zege fee.

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: David jar-keira bam maama ma tɔge da ba kɛ yiga ba maa via. Banto maa ye Cherete tiina bam, de Peleti tiina bam, ko woli de Giti tiina bia yaredo (

english_verse: soldiers who had followed him from Gath. Their commander was Ittai.
translation_verse: ) balo na nwoŋi Gafa ba ba ba tɔge David kwaga to.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: David ma ta de Giti tu Itayi o we, “Nmo tɔge debam kwaga se bɛ mo? N nwoŋi sa-teo mo n ba n ji veiru dé tetare ne. Nam jwoori Jerusalem se n ta‑n wo pa-dooro wom tei ne.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Nmo na tu n me de amo to jege da yalei yerane mo. Kɔ nam mo wó pa se n ta‑n tɔge debam? Amo ta kare a beeri mo, a yeiri a na maa vei mɛ. Konto to, ja n jar-keira bam se á jwoori teo kom wo. Baŋa Wɛ wó taa ke‑m lanyerane de chega.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Itayi ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, nmo na ŋwe to, amo dugi de Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere we, a lage a taa tɔge n kwaga mo se a vo mɛ maama n na wó vo to, ko ná maŋe ko ye toone de ŋwea wone mo de.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: David ma ta‑o we, “Ko nam lana, kɛ yiga se dé taa via.” Itayi de o diga tiina dedaane o jar-keira bam maama ma tɔge de David kɔgɔ kom ba via.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: David dedaane o kwaga kam na maa nwoŋi Jerusalem teo wone to, balo na zoore jei sem maama ne to maa keeri ye ba chwoosa. O ma tɔge de-ba o vo o yi Kidoron nabara kam. Ba maama ma bɛ, ba vo ba kwei kagoa chwoŋa kam ba ma kɛa.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Wɛ kaanem tiina Zadoki de Abiatara déem tɔge ba wora. Levi dwi tiina badwonna ma zeŋe Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba tɔge-ba. Ba laam ma zoore-ka ba zege tega ne ye ba daa wo kwei-ka se ko taa nii maŋa kam nɔɔna bam maama na nwoŋi teo kom wone ba kɛ ba ti to.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: David ma ta de Zadoki o we, “Nam ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam n jwoori Jerusalem wone. Baŋa Wɛ yi ná su amo totoŋa, o wó jwoori o ja-ne o ba se a ma a yi a na-ka, se a ta na Wɛ wara-vwei dem.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: O wo nam daa ná wo pwoli de amo, se o ke-ne o boboŋa yam na lage tei to.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: O ta ma ta de Zadoki o woli da o we, “N wo nɛ na? Ja n bu Ahimaazi se á jwoori teo kom wone de yazura. Abiatara dedaane o bu Jonatan de wó tɔge‑m ba vo.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Zadoki dedaane Abiatara ma ja Wɛ ni-gwonim dakaa kam ba jwoori Jerusalem wone. Ba ma maŋe da ba zoora.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: David déem ma diini Olivi peo kom yuu ye o chwoosa o via. O déem wo zo natera, ye o kwei gɔrɔ o ma kwoli o yibia o wo-chechɔgɔ kom ŋwaane. O nɔɔna bam de ma kwoli ba yibia, ye ba chwoosa ba via.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Ba ma ta de David ba we, “Ahitofeli de nwoŋi nmo kwaga ne, ye o vo o woli kɔgɔ kolo na tɔge Abisalom kwaga to wone mo.” David na nigi konto to, o ma lwoori Wɛ o we, “Baŋa Wɛ! Nam pipiri Ahitofeli bera maama se ya ji jworim ya pa Abisalom.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: David ma yɔɔre o di peo kom yuu o vo o yi mɛ nɔɔna na yeini ba zuli Wɛ to. Dáane mo o maŋe de Husayi. Wonto déem ye Ariki tu mo. O gwaaro tem ma kaare kaare, ye kasolo de taare o yuu kom.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: David déem ma ta‑o o we, “Nmo ná lage n ta‑n tɔge de debam, ko bá jwoŋi-ne.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Nam sɛ se n jwoori teo kom wone. N ná yi da, se n ta de Abisalom we, ‘A beene se a ji n tontoŋeno mo. A nam wó taa toŋe a woli‑m, nenɛɛne a ya n na woli nmo kwo David tei to.’ Konto ná kea, nmo wó na chwoŋa se n vugimi Ahitofeli bera yam se ya yé zege.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Wɛ kaanem tiina Zadoki dedaane Abiatara de wó taa wora. Soswea kalo maama nmo na wó ni pɛ sɔŋɔ ne to, se n lwoni n bere-ba.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Ba bia Ahimaazi dedaane Jonatan de tɔge ba wora. Á ná tu á lɔre woŋo kolo maama, se á pa banto ba ba ta ba bere-ne kolo na wora to.”

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: David badwoŋi Husayi ma jwoori o vo Jerusalem teo kom wo. O na yi da to, dedaane Abisalom de o kɔgɔ kom de yɔɔre ba maa zoore teo kom ne mo.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: David ma bwei Ziba o we, “Nmo jege tento maama se n ma n ke bɛ mo?” Ziba ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo diga tiina wó wane ba di bonɛ sem ba taa via. Ko ná ye wodiiru tem dedaane teeni bia bam, te ye n nɔɔna bam nyem mo se ba di. Sana bam maa ye se balo na wó ba ba bugi kagoa chwoŋa kam ne to nyɔ se ba yera jwoori ya na dam.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: David daa ma bwei‑o o we, “Se Mefibosɛfi na ye n tu Sɔɔl naa to, o wo yei ne mo?” Ziba ma leiri‑o o we, “O maŋe Jerusalem ne mo ye o boŋe o we, ‘Isarele tiina bam laam wó kwei a kwo-nakwe paare dem ba jwoori ba pa-ne.’ ”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: David ma ta‑o o we, “Ko na ye konto to, wonnu telo maama Mefibosɛfi ya na tei to mo, amo laam kwei-te a pa nmo se te ji nmo nyem.” Ziba ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo tu, a ke nmo lei. Amo ye nmo tontoŋeno mo. Wɛ wó pa se a kikia taa sui nmo yi maŋa maama.” Simeyi sɔɔle lwarem o yage David yuu ne

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Pɛ David déem ma o vo o twɛ Bahurim teo kom. Nɔɔno wodwoŋi ma nwoŋi o jeeri‑o ye o sɔɔle lwarem o daŋe o yuu ne. O yere mo Simeyi. O kwo yere maa ye Gera, ye o nwoŋi Sɔɔl dwi dem wone.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Simeyi maa jege kandwa o dole David dedaane o dedɛɛra bam, de David babɛ sem maŋe ba gilimi‑o mo ba ke tetare ne.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Simeyi maa jege David o twea ye o we, “Vei daa, vei daa! Nmo ye nɔn-goro! Nmo tiini n ye nɔn-wo-koro mo de!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: Nmo vere Sɔɔl paare dem n jwoŋi, ye n daare n go o diga tiina bam dedɛ. Konto nam mo pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ wora o ŋwe jene dem konto n yuu ne. O jwoŋi paare dem mo o pa n bu Abisalom. Ko wó ni‑m, nɔn-goro!”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Zeruya bu Abisayi ma ta de David o we, “Pɛ, kukuri-teka kanto wo maŋe se o taa jege‑m o yaala. Pa-ne chwoŋa se a yi a gwoni o yuu kom a de tega ne.”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: David ma leiri o we, “Abam Zeruya bia bam, á yiga mo ka kɔ? Baŋa Wɛ mo ná tage de Simeyi se o sɔɔle lwarem o yage amo yuu ne, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege chwoŋa se o che‑o.”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: David laam ma ta de Abisayi de o dedɛɛra bam maama o we, “Amo tete bu-lora mo beeri-ne se o go. Benjamin tu wonto laam mo wó yage-ne na? Yage-o-na se o sɔɔle lwarem dwi delo maama o na lage to. Baŋa Wɛ ga mo we o ke konto.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam daa ná nɛ a cham dem, o wó wane o pipiri sɔɔlem dento zem se de ji swolim de pa-ne.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: David de o kwaga kam maa lɛɛre ba vei chwoŋa kam yuu ne. Ba na maa vei to, Simeyi maa dale zwoŋo kom teiŋa o tɔge-ba, ye o sɔɔle o yage ba yuu ne, o daare o dole-ba de kandwa. O ta maa tae fwogo o ke ba yera ne.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Pɛ David dedaane o nɔɔna bam déem ma vo ba yi Jɔdan buga kam. Ba maama ma tiini ba bugi. Ba ma maŋe da ye ba yera zuri. Husayi dedaane Ahitofeli bera yam

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Abisalom dedaane Isarele tiina bam maama ma vo ba zo Jerusalem teo kom wo, ye Ahitofeli tɔge o wo ba wone.

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Abisalom ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo de David badwoŋo kom chɔge lela mo na? Bɛ mo ke ye n wo dɛ ded‑o n viiri?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Husayi ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo jege se a tɔge pɛ wolo Baŋa Wɛ na kuri to mo, wolo kɔgɔ konto dedaane Isarele tiina bam maama na kuri se o taa ye pɛ to. A nam wó kwei a chega maama mo a pa‑m.

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Abisalom laam ma bwei Ahitofeli o we, “Dé na tu dé wora to, bɛ mo dé laam wó ke? Nmo boboŋa yam ye tɛ mo?”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Ahitofeli ma leiri‑o o we, “Zaŋe n vo n peini de n kwo ka-bi selo o na duri o daare se ba leeni ba taa nii o sɔŋɔ kom to. Nmo ná ke konto, Isarele tiina bam maama wó lɔre we n kikia maama lwoi n kwo momwa ne mo, de n na chɔge o yiga tei to ŋwaane. Ko maa wó pa se balo maama na tɔge‑m to fɔge ba na baare.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Ba ma di pɛ sɔŋɔ kom nayuu ba chwi vwei ba pa Abisalom. Abisalom ma zo de wone o lage o kwo ka-bi sem maama ye Isarele tiina bam maama zege ba nia.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: David ze ná wo mɛ de mɛ maama, dé wó beeri o jei dé yi‑o. De wó to o baŋa ne dé li‑o mo nenɛɛne nyɔnɔ na toe tega ne tei to. Konto mo David de o jar-keira bam wolowolo daa bá daare, de dedoa de.

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: se a daare a ja o nɔɔna bam maama a jwoori a ba a ke nmo kwaga ne. Nɔɔno wolo nmo na beeri to yerane ná tega, ba maama wó jwoori n tei ne de ba yazura.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Ahitofeli kwea yam konto déem maa lana ya pae Abisalom dedaane Isarele nakwa bam maama.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Abisalom ma ta o we, “Dé nam daa wó cheigi Ariki tu Husayi de kwora mo se dé lɔre wonto boboŋa na ye tei to.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Husayi ma zo o tei ye Abisalom ta o we, “Ahitofeli bere we dé ke tento mo. Dé wó sɛ o ni dem naa, nmo de wó bere debam dé na wó ke tei? Nam ta se dé nii.”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Husayi ma leiri Abisalom o we, “Amo tei ne, Ahitofeli na pɛ kwea yalo tento to ba lana.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Nmo maŋe n yei we n kwo de o nɔɔna bam ye babɛ mo chekke. Leile konto ba laam jei de ban-zɔŋɔ mo nenɛɛne ba na vere nywoŋ-kura bia ba daare-ka tei to. Ko woli da, nmo kwo na ye jara-keim bembea to ŋwaane, tete dento o bá peini o nɔɔna bam na tigi mɛ to.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Tento wɛɛne o beeri peo bɔɔne, naa gugworo kodwoŋi mo o seigi da. Wonto wae o lwoori yiga o nwoŋi o jeeri debam de jara. Nɔɔna laam ná niga, ba wó ta ba we, ‘Hei! Ba wane Abisalom kɔgɔ kom, ye ba dedɛ te.’

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Konto wó pa se nmo jar-keira babɛ sem tete vɔna pare, ye foone zo-ba. Isarele tiina maama nam maŋe ba yei n kwo na tiini o yei jara laŋa tei, dedaane o jar-keira bam na ye bembɛ chekke tei to.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Kwea yalo amo na jege to mo tento: la Isarele tiina bam maama n ke daane, ko na zege Dan laŋa kam seeni se ko yi Beeriseba to. Nmo jar-keira bam kɔgɔ laam maa wó taa daga ne naneo ni kasolo tei. Nmo tete laam wó da ba yiga se á vo á ke jara yam.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: O ta ná maŋe o duri se o zo teo kamunu kolo wone de, dé kɔgɔ kom maama wó beeri ŋone mo ba kwei ba vɔ teo kom konto kandwa yam ba tuuri ba ja ba tu bwolo tega. Teo kom konto kandwɛ dedwe tete daa bá daare de taa zege da.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Abisalom dedaane Isarele nakwa bam maama ma ta ba we, “Husayi bera yam jege kuri ya dwoi Ahitofeli nyena yam.” Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ na lage se lɛɛro ba Abisalom baŋa ne to ŋwaane, o déem tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo se o pa Ahitofeli bera yam yé zege, de ya na maŋe ya lana to de.

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Husayi ma zaŋe o vo Wɛ kaanem tiina Zadoki de Abiatara tei o tole kolo na ke to o bere-ba ye o we, “Ahitofeli ya bere Abisalom dedaane Isarele nakwa bam se ba ke tento de tento mo, amo de ma bere-ba se ba ke tento de tento.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Konto nam ke-na lela á toŋe kwora David tei ne we, zem tete ne o yé maŋe kagoa kam ne o peini buga kam ni ne. O nam jege se o bɛ Jɔdan buga kam lela o kɛ o vo yiga, se ba yé ba ba di o dedaane o nɔɔna bam maama.”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Jonatan de Ahimaazi déem kɔre se ba zo Jerusalem teo kom wo, se nɔɔna wó na-ba mo. Konto ŋwaane ba ma yeini ba seigi En-Rogele ne se bukɔ bu ja kwora kalo maama na wora o ba o pa-ba se ba de laam vo ba ta de David.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe nɔn-doŋo kodwoŋi ma na-ba ye o vo o ta o bere Abisalom. Jonatan de Ahimaazi ma ke lela ba duri ba vo Bahurim ba seigi nɔɔno wodwoŋi sɔŋɔ ne. Vole déem wo o konkɔlɔ wone. Nɔɔna balei bam ma tu de wone.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom kaane ma kwei woŋo o ma o pu vole dem ni, ye o daare o jare mena de baŋa ne. Ko ma pa se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yeiri kolo na wora to.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Abisalom dedɛɛra bam ma vo ba yi kaane wom tei ye ba bwei‑o ba we, “Ahimaazi dedaane Jonatan wo yei ne mo?” Kaane wom ma leiri-ba o we, “Ba bɛ buga kam mo ba kɛ.” Nɔɔna bam ma beeri-ba ba ga, ye ba jwoori Jerusalem wone.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Abisalom dedɛɛra bam na kɛ ba daare to, mo Ahimaazi dedaane Jonatan nwoŋi vole dem wone ba duri ba vo ba yi David tei. Ba ma tole kolo maama Ahitofeli na ŋɔɔne ko vo David seeni to, ye ba daare ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Ke lela n zaŋe n bɛ buga kam!”

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Sento nɛ sem ni ne mo David dedaane o kwaga kam maama zaŋe se ba taa bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. Tega na jege ka poore to, dedaane ba maama déem bɛ buga kam mo, ba dedoa daa wo daare.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Ahitofeli na maane we Abisalom de Isarele nakwa bam ve se ba sɛ o bera yam to, mo o diini o bonaga o jwoori o tete sɔŋɔ Giloo ne. O na yi da to, mo o bere o sɔŋɔ tiina ba na wó ke tei ne o ná tera. O laam ma kwei ŋona o vo o kuuni o tete o te. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli o kwoa di-dwoŋo ne.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Abisalom dedaane Isarele kɔgɔ kom maama déem ma vo ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam, dedaane David duri o vo o yi Mahanayim teo kom.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Abisalom nam ya pɛ se Amasa mo leiri Joaba yuu ne o ji o jar-keira bam yiga tu. Amasa kwo yere mo ye Jefere. O maa ye Isameli tu. Amasa nu déem ye Nahasi bukɔ Abigali, Abigali maa ye Joaba nu Zeruya choro.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Abisalom dedaane Isarele tiina bam ma vo ba chwi ba vwoa Gilead laŋa kam ne.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: David na yi Mahanayim to, mo nɔɔna batɔ déem jeeri‑o. Banto wo dedoa ye Nahasi bu Sobi na nwoŋi Amon tiina teo Raba to mo. Wodwoŋi maa ye Ameli bu Makira na nwoŋi Lo-Debara to. Batɔ tu wom maa ye Gilead tu Bazilayi na nwoŋi Rogelim to.

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: de tooro, de nayela, ko woli de pei, dedaane nayel-pepala. Ba ma kwei tento maama ba pa David dedaane o nɔɔna bam se ba di. Kokuri to, ba déem tage mo ba we, “Kana dedaane na-nyɔm mo tiini ko chɛ nɔɔna bam, ba na wo kagoa kam ne ba vei taa ye ba tiini ba bugi to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: O ma pɔɔre o jar-keira bam kuni betɔ. O ma kwei kɔgɔ dedoa o ke Joaba jeŋa ne. O nyaane Abisayi na ye Zeruya bu to de maa wo ba kɔgɔ dedoa yiga ne. Balo maama na daare to, o ma ke-ba Giti tu Itayi jeŋa ne. David laam ma ta o jar-keira bam maama o we, “Amo tete wó tɔge abam se dé vo dé kwaare jara yam.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: David nɔɔno wodwoŋi ma na‑o ye o duri o vo o ta o bere Joaba o we, “Amo nɛ Abisalom na sagele tio nɛ ne!”

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Jara yam ma jage ya zo jei sem goa kam maama wone. Kagoa kam tete déem pɛ se nɔɔna dedɛ te, se ko dwoni jar-keira bam se-zɔɔro na go balo to.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Joaba ma ta de nɔɔno wom o we, “Bɛ? Nmo nɛ Abisalom mo ye n wo go‑o ka jeiga da? Nmo ya ná mage‑o n go, a ya wó pa‑m lu-nyenno sabu-dala fuga, ye a daare a pa‑m bembea tankila a woli da.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Amo ya ná ve pɛ wom ni ye a paale a go Abisalom, pɛ daa ta wó ni ko ŋwa. Kokuri to, kolokolo ba seigi pɛ yiga ne. Nmo nam ya bá‑n zege a kwaga ne.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Joaba ma ta o we, “Amo bá wane a zuri a yera se a taa cheigi lara yanto!” O ma zaŋe o kwei chichwoa yatɔ o vo o yi tei-zɔŋɔ kom dedaane Abisalom ta ŋwe mo o sagele tio kom nɛ sem ne. Joaba ma le chichwoa yatɔ yam o zɔ Abisalom bochare ne.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Joaba nɔn-donno fuga na zei o jara zela yam to laam ma yi ba gilimi Abisalom ba mage‑o ba go.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Joaba laam ma pa ba wu nabɔnɔ se ko bere we jara yam ti. O jar-keira bam ma yage Isarele tiina bam zeilim ye ba jwoori o tei.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Ba ma kwei Abisalom yera yam ba dole ba yage gwoŋ-chanluŋu wone, kagoa kam ne. Ba ma pɛ kandwa-kamuna ba ma li-ko pa se ya dogele baŋa baŋa. Konto maama to, dedaane Isarele nɔɔna bam maama duri ba jwoori ba sam mo.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Abisalom déem ta na ŋwe to, o ya chwi kandwɛ-kamunu mo o zege Pɛ bwolo kom ne se ko taa bwoi o yere. O déem ya boŋe o tete ne mo o we, “Amo ba jege bakeira se o jwa bwoŋi a yere.” O ma kwei o tete yere o pa kandwɛ dem. De zem maama, ba ta bwoi-ko we, ‘Abisalom Kandwɛ’ mo. David keeri Abisalom ŋwaane

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Zadoki bu Ahimaazi ma ta de Joaba o we, “Pa-ne chwoŋa se a duri a vo ta Pɛ David we Baŋa Wɛ jwoŋi‑o o yage o dona jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Joaba ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo zem ba jege kwor-ywoŋa se n ja n vo n pa pɛ. Ko wó taa ye dɛ dedwoŋi ne mo se ko dae zem. Kokuri to, pɛ wom bu mo tega.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Joaba ma daare o ta de Kusi tu na zege o tei ne to o we, “Véi n ta nmo yi na nɛ kolo maama to n bere pɛ wom.” Kusi tu wom ma tiiri tega ne o jɔɔne‑o ye o zaŋe o duri o maa kɛa.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Zadoki bu Ahimaazi daa ta ma ta de Joaba o we, “Ko ná ye tei maama de, nam sɛ se amo de duri a saŋe Kusi tu wom kwaga a vo Pɛ David tei.” Joaba ma bwei‑o o we, “A bu, bɛŋwaane mo n yɔɔre n lage se n kwei kwora kam n ja n vo? Ka ba lage ka ja nyɔɔre ka pa nmo.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: David déem nam ya jei teo kom manchwoŋo ni bworru telei tem tetare laŋa ne mo. Teo kom yereno ma vo o di o dɔge teo kom manchwoŋo kabira kam yuu ne. O ma nii o tole o na nɔɔno na duri o yerane o beene.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Yereno wom ma tɔɔle o ta de Pɛ David. David ma leiri o we, “Kotu ná duri o yerane, ko bere we ko ye kwor-ywoŋa mo o jege o beene.” Wolo na duri to ma tiini o vaŋe o twɛ-ba.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Yereno wom daa ma tole o na nɔɔno wodwoŋi de na duri o beene. O ma tɔɔle o ta de manchwoŋo yereno wom o we, “Nii nɔɔno wodwoŋi de na duri o yerane o maa beena.” Pɛ wom maa we, “O de wó taa jege kwor-ywoŋa mo o beene.”

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Yereno wom ma zege kabira kam yuu ne o tɔɔle o we, “Amo na nɛ to, boboa nɔɔno wom duri nenɛɛne Zadoki bu Ahimaazi na yeini o duri tei to mo.” David ma leiri o we, “Wonto ye nɔn-ŋom mo. Tento wɛɛne o jege ta-ŋom mo o beene.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ahimaazi na yi to, mo o tɔɔle o ta de pɛ wom o we, “Woŋo maama ke lam!” O ma vwi o yibia tega ne o jɔɔne pɛ wom ye o we, “Pɛ, n Tu Baŋa Wɛ maŋe de tia, o na pɛ se n di n dona balo na lɔge n kwaga ne to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma bwei‑o o we, “A bu Abisalom jege yazura na?” Ahimaazi ma leiri o we, “Maŋa kalo Joaba na lage o toŋe amo dedaane n nɔn-doŋo wom se dé ba to, mo a nɛ kɔgɔ na gilimi ye ko maama ye vugima yerane. Amo nam yeiri kolo ŋwaane ba na ke sɔɔ kom to.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom maa we, “Kɛ n zege dáa ne!” Ahimaazi ma fɔɔre o zege dáa ne.

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Pɛ David ma bwei Kusi tu wom o we, “A bu Abisalom jege yazura na?” Kusi tu wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Amo tu, Wɛ wó pa se n dona bam de balo maama na lage ba lɔ n kwaga ne to ŋwea guri nenɛɛne nɔn-doŋo wonto zem na guri tei to.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom na nigi konto to, o wo ma tiini ko chɔge dedɛ. O ma vo o di o zo wɛyuu diga kalo na yeeri de teo kom manchwoŋo kom to o to keira ne. O na maa vei to, o tiini o kaase mo ye o we, “Amo bu Abisalom! Aaa! Abisalom, a bu ywoo! Amo ya mo ná tega ye nmo ŋwe, ko ya ba gara na? Aaa! Abisalom, a bu ywoo!”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba ta ba bere Joaba ba we, “Pɛ David tiini o keeri o bu Abisalom toone dem ŋwaane mo.”

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: David jar-keira bam ma ni we o yɔɔre o keeri o bu lua kam mo. Ko ma pa se ba ware ba di ywoni dento dɛ dem ne, ye dɛ dem konto lɛɛre de ji wo-chechɔgɔ dɛ.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Dento dɛ dem ne, nɔɔna bam lɔɔre mo ba jwoori ba zo teo kom wone, nenɛɛne nɔɔna na di-ba jara baŋa ne ye chaveera jege-ba tei to.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: David ma kwei o je o kwoli o yibia ye o kaase baŋa baŋa o we, “Aaa! A bu Abisalom! A bu ywoo!”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Joaba ma zaŋe o vo o zo pɛ tei ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Nmo zem tiini n ke n jar-keira bam chaveera. Yé swei we banto mo jwoŋi nmo tete ŋwea, de n kaana ŋwea, de n bakeiri de n bukwa ŋwea, dedaane n ka-bi sem maama ŋwea ba yage!

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: Nmo na ke tei to, ko nye de nmo swoi balo na chuli‑m to mo, ye n daare n chuli balo na swoi‑m to. Nmo zem bere jaja we n yiga tera de n jar-keira bam de n dedɛɛra bam maama. Amo maane we Abisalom ya ná ŋwe, ye debam maama te, konto ya wó pwoli nmo wo.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Nmo nam ná lage chega, se n zaŋe n nwoŋi n vo n nɔɔna bam tei n pa se ba jwoori ba na baare. A dugi de Baŋa Wɛ yere we, nmo nam ná ve se n ke konto, se tega daa ta ná jege ka poora, nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá daare se kotu taa zege n kwaga ne. Konto, ko laam wó tiini ko ji lɛɛro mo ko pa‑m, se ko dwoni cham delo maama na tu n baŋa ne, ko zege n biini ne ko ba ko yi zem to!”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Pɛ David na nigi konto to, o ma zaŋe o vo o jeini teo kom manchwoŋo kom ni ne. O nɔɔna bam ma ni we pɛ wom nwoŋi pwooni o jei da. Ba ma vo o tei ba gilimi daane o yiga ne. David jwoori o zo Jerusalem teo wone Isarele tiina balo na tɔge Abisalom kwaga to déem nam ya jwoori ba sam mo.

english_verse: everyone in Israel started arguing. They were saying to each other, “King David rescued us from the Philistines and from our other enemies. But then we chose Absalom to be our new leader, and David had to leave the country to get away. Absalom died in battle, so why hasn't something been done to bring David back?”
translation_verse: Dé nam ya kuri Abisalom mo se o taa ye dé pɛ. O de ma te jara yam wone. Dé daa zege dé dáane se bɛ mo? Pa-na se dé vo dé ja Pɛ David dé jwoori dé ba ywo-seeni.”

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: David ma toŋe kwora Wɛ kaanem tiina Zadoki de Abiatara tei ne o we: “Véi-na Judah nakwa bam tei á ta de-ba we, ‘Isarele dwi tiina bam maama taane dem maŋe de to amo zwɛ ne. Bɛ mo pɛ se á ye balo na kweeli se á bwoŋi á pɛ wom se o jwoori sɔŋɔ?

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Abam ye amo chorro mo, á ye amo tete yera dedaane a jana. Bɛŋwaane mo abam nam maŋe kwaga ne, ye nɔɔna badwonna lwoori yiga ba bwoŋi-ne se a jwoori?’

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Nam ta véi-na Amasa tei á ta ded‑o we, ‘Nmo dae amo choro mo na? Wɛ wó pa se lɛɛro yi-ne nenɛɛne a na wo pɛ se nmo laam leiri Joaba yuu ne n ji a jar-keira bam yiga tu.’ ”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: David taane dem ma dwei Judah dwi tiina bam maama bochara. Ba ma ke ba ni daane ne nɔɔno dedoa tei, pa se ba toŋe kwora ba pa David ba we, “Ja n nɔɔna bam maama se á jwoori sɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Gera bu Simeyi na ye Benjamin tu ye o nwoŋi Bahurim to de ma ke lela o tɔge o woli Judah tiina kɔgɔ kom wone se o da o jeeri Pɛ David.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: Amo tu, amo lɔre lanyerane we a ke lwarem mo. Konto ŋwaane mo amo dɛ yiga Josɛf dwi tiina maama wone se a ba a jeeri‑m.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: David na yi to, ba ma bɛ buga kam ba ja o diga tiina bam de ba zela yam ba jwoori ba bɛ. Ba déem ta ma ke kolo maama na tɔge pɛ wom boboŋa to. Simeyi yera taane Simeyi de ma bɛ o vo o yi Pɛ David tei. O ma to o vwi o yibia David yiga ne.

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: O ma ta o we, “Pɛ, a lwoori‑m se n yage a keim-balɔrɔ kom n ma n chɛ-ne. Ko ná ye kolo amo ya na ke nmo yera ne, maŋa kam nmo na duri n daare Jerusalem to, yé kwei-ko n ke n yuu ne.

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: David ma leiri Abisayi o we, “Abam Zeruya bia bam! Á yiga mo ka kɔ? Abam zem mo jigi amo sebanyena na? Zem dɛ dento mo Isarale tiina bam jwoori ba pa-ne chwoŋa se a taa ye ba pɛ. Konto ŋwaane, ba bá go nɔɔn-nɔɔno zem.”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Pɛ wom laam ma pipiri o ta de Simeyi o we, “Amo gwoni ni a pa‑m we, n bá‑n te.” Mefibosɛfi yera taane

english_verse: Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
translation_verse: O na nwoŋi Jerusalem o ba o yi David tei konto to, o ma daane pɛ wom peiga. David ma bwei‑o o we, “Mefibosɛfi, bɛ mo ke ye n wo dɛ amo kwaga se dé kɛ?”

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: O ma leiri o we, “Pɛ, nmo yei a na maŋe a ye gɔrɔ tei to. Konto mo tei a pɛ ni we ba ti a bonaga kam yiga ba pa-ne se a di a ma tɔge dede‑m. Amo tontoŋeno Ziba mo nwoŋi a kwaga ne.

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: O ma chwo amo n yiga ne. Nmo nam yei woŋo maama kuri, nenɛɛne n ye Wɛ maleka mo tei. Ke kolo maama na wo n boboŋa ne se n ke to.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Kokuri, amo kwo-nakwe dwi tiina bam yɔɔre ba maŋe se n ya go debam maama mo, ye n ta sɛ se amo taa tɔge a di nmo sɔŋɔ ne. Amo daa wó taa jege chwoŋa se a lwoori woŋo kodwoŋi nmo tei ne a woli da na?”

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Daa‑n yé chɔge n ni. Amo pɛ ni se nmo dedaane Ziba pɔɔre tega kalo maama na ye Sɔɔl nyem to á pa daane.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Mefibosɛfi ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, o ná lage te maama, se o kwei o taa jega. Nmo na jwoori sɔŋɔ de n yazura to maŋe ko pa amo.” Bazilayi yera taane

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Gilead tu Bazilayi de ma zege Rogelim ne o ba se o jeeri Pɛ David se ba bɛ Jɔdan buga kam, se o daare o yage‑o chwoŋa ne se o kɛ.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: David ma ta ded‑o o we, “Da n bɛ Jɔdan buga kam n tɔge debam se dé vo Jerusalem, se a taa nii n baŋa ne.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Bazilayi ma leiri pɛ wom o we, “A lage a da de nmo a vo Jerusalem a ke bɛ mo? Amo ŋwea daa bá daga.

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Pɛ, nam yage se a da dede‑m a bɛ Jɔdan buga kam, ye a kwogili‑m se dé yi yiga fee. Amo na ye n tontoŋeno to, konto wó taa ye zula yalo na maŋe de amo to.

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Pa-ne chwoŋa se a laam jwoori sɔŋɔ, se a vo a te a teo ne ye ba kwei-ne ba ke a kwo de a nu yibeela tei ne. Nam nii a bu Chimam mo tento. Wonto wó tɔge‑m se á vo Jerusalem. O wó taa toŋe o pa‑m, ye n de ná lage se n ke tei maama n pa‑o, n wae n ke.”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Pɛ David maa we, “Tɔ. Chimam wó da amo o vo Jerusalem, se a ke kolo maama na wó pwoli n wo to a pa‑o. Ko daare, woŋo kolo maama nmo na wó ta‑n lage amo tei ne to, amo wó ke-ko a pa‑m.”

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: David jar-keira bam maama laam ma bɛ Jɔdan buga kam. Pɛ wom tete de ma bɛ. O ma kukwori Bazilayi o bane‑o o yage chwoŋa ne pa se o jwoori o vo sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Judah nɔɔna bam maama, dedaane Isarele nɔɔna bam chichworo mo déem kwogili David ba bɛ buga kam ba maa kɛa. Chimam de ma tɔge Pɛ David, ye ba kɛ ba vo ba yi Giligal.

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Judah tiina bam de déem ma leiri ba we, “Pɛ wom nwoŋi debam Judah dwi tiina bam wone mo. Bɛ mo ye keim dento daane abam pa se á bane zaŋe? Dé wo di pɛ wodiu, dé nam wo jwoŋi o kolokolo dé totoŋe dem ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam daa ma leiri-ba ba we, “Abam na tage á we á dwi dem nɔɔno ye Pɛ to, nam lɔre-na we debam ye Isarele dwia fuga nɔɔna mo, pa se debam tei‑o kuni fuga. Bɛ mo ye á tiini á gwooni debam konto? Yé swei-na we debam mo lwoori abam yiga dé ja boboŋe se dé vo dé ja pɛ wom dé jwoori dé ba sɔŋɔ.” De ko de, Judah tiina bam déem ta ŋɔɔne wo-zɔŋɔ taane mo se ko dwoni Isarele tiina bam taane dem na ye tei to.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Bichiri bu Seba déem maa wo Giligal ne. O ye Benjamin dwi tu mo, ye o ta ye nɔn-wo-koro. O ma wu nabɔnɔ ye o tɔɔle o ta o we, “Isarele tiina bam, debam dedaane Jesse bu David dae daane. Dé yiga tera o paare dem wone! Pa-na dé jwoori-na sam.”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam maama ma da ko ŋwaane ba nwoŋi David kwaga ne ye ba daare ba pɛ Seba kwaga ba pu. Ko daare Judah tiina bam déem tiini ba meeli Pɛ David yera ne mo. Ba ma zege Jɔdan buga bam seeni ba kwogili‑o ba vo ba yi Jerusalem.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: David na jwoori Jerusalem o vo o zo o sɔŋɔ kom wone to, mo o jaane o ka-bi fuga selo o ya na yage se ba taa nii o sɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne to o ja o vo o seigi sɔŋɔ kodwoŋi ne. O ma pa se nɔɔna yere-ba, ye ba daare ba pa-ba ba ni-wodiu. Pɛ wom daa maa wo peini de-ba, ye ba lɛɛre ba maŋe dáane ba di kadeini taa se ba vo ba te.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Pɛ David ma ta de Amasa o we, “Toŋe n bwoŋi Judah tiina bam, se n pa ba la daane. Pa se á maama da daane á ba ywo-seeni da yatɔ dɛ ne.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Amasa ma zaŋe o vo se o bwoŋi Judah tiina bam o ke daane. O ma dáane o kɛ dɛ dem pɛ wom na pɛ‑o to.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: David ma ta de Abisayi o we, “Dé ná wo ke lela, Bichiri bu Seba wó daane debam o dwoni Abisalom na ke tei to. Konto to, ja amo jar-keira bam n ke n kwaga ne se á vo á jeeri‑o de jara. Ko ná dae konto, o wó wane o vo o zo teene delo na lɔge de pe to wone, ye dé daa bá yi‑o.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Abisayi ma zaŋe o nwoŋi Jerusalem ne, ye Joaba de o nɔɔna bam, de Cherete tiina bam, de Peleti tiina bam, ko woli de jar-keira babɛ sem maama wo o kwaga ne. Ba ma nwoŋi ba vo se ba pare Seba ba ja.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba maŋe de kandwɛ-kamunu kom na wo Gibeon ne to, dedaane Amasa tu o ba o jeeri-ba. Joaba déem ya zo o jara-keim gwaaro tem mo ye se-zɔɔ laam vɔ o teiŋa seeni. O ma fɔɔre se o vo o yi Amasa tei ye seo kom wo ko pwolo wone.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Joaba ma jɔɔne Amasa ye o we, “Amo choro, n jege yazura na?” O ma daare o ma o jazem o ja Amasa o tɔne seeni o yi o yera nenɛɛne o lage se ba kukwori daane mo tei.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Amasa nam wo jeeli we Joaba zei seo mo o jagwia ne se o ga ke‑o woŋo. Joaba ma kwei seo kom o zɔ Amasa puga ne pa se o loro ta te nwoŋi te to tega ne. Joaba daa wo zɔge‑o o ke belei, Amasa na maŋe o te lela to ŋwaane. Joaba de o nyaane Abisayi daa ta ma to chwoŋa ne se ba pare Seba ba ja.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Joaba nɔn-doŋo wodwoŋi ma vo o zege Amasa yera yam baŋa ne o tɔɔle o we, “Abam wolo maama yiga ná wo Joaba de David wone, se kotu zaŋe o taa tɔge Joaba kwaga.”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Amasa déem ma te o tigi pempale dem tetare ne. O ma bibili o jana bam wone. Joaba nɔɔno wom ma maane we wolo maama ná yeini o yi too wom na wo mɛ to, kotu yeini o zege da o nii mo. O ma tuuri Amasa o ja o kɛ pempale dem dáa ne. O ma tiŋi‑o gaao ne, ye o daare o kwei gɔrɔ o ma o kwoli‑o.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: O na pɛ se Amasa yera yam daa ba tigi pempale dem tetare ne to, jar-keira bam maama ma tɔge Joaba kwaga se ba beeri Seba ba ja.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Seba déem nam ya kaare Isarele dwi maama laŋa ne mo ye o laam vo o yi Abel Bɛte-Maaka. Bichiri dwi tiina bam maama ma tɔge ded‑o ba zo teo kom wone.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Joaba de o nɔɔna bam ma vo ba pu teo kom maama se ba ja Seba. Ba ma pɛ kasolo ba lɔ taara ba sale teo kom kabiri sem teiŋa ne. Ba maa kwori ba jege da-kwollu kamuna ba kuusi teo kom kabiri sem se se bwori se to tega ne.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Kaane wodwoŋi déem nam ya wo teo kom ne ye o swa gaale. O ma zege ko kabira yera ne o tɔɔle o ta nɔɔna bam o we, “Cheigi-na! Cheigi-na! Bwoŋi-na Joaba se o fofɔ o twɛ ywo-seeni, se a lage a ŋɔɔne ded‑o mo.”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Joaba ma vo o twɛ‑o. Kaane wom ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo mo ye Joaba to na?” O ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ.” Kaane wom ma ta o we, “A kwo, nam fɔge n cheigi kolo amo na jege se a ta to.” Joaba ma leiri‑o o we, “Ta‑n tɛa, se a de cheiga.”

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: O laam ma ta o we, “Faŋa tu mo we, ‘Wolo ná lage se o taane kwɛ, kotu wó vo Abel teo mo, se de kwɛ.’

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Tɔ. Debam teo kom tiini ko jege kuri ka pa Isarele dwi tiina maama mo. Dé ye balo na lage chega de yazura tɔgem mo dé gaale. Bɛ mo ke ye á kwaane se á chɔge teo kolo na ye Baŋa Wɛ nyem to?”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Joaba ma leiri‑o o we, “Ko fɔge ko dae konto! A bere a maŋe a wo ke a boboŋa ne se a chɔge abam.

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Ko dae we dé boŋe se dé chɔge á teo kom. Ko ye nɔɔno dedoa yerane ŋwaane mo dé tua. Nam ja Bichiri bu Seba na nwoŋi Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne to n pa debam, se dé wó kɛ de daare á teo kom. Kokuri to, wonto mo vaŋe kɔgɔ o ke o kwaga ne se ba ve Pɛ David.” Kaane wom maa we, “Ta‑n cheiga, se dé wó da kabira kam baŋa dé dole o yuu dé de tega ne dé pa‑m.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma ja o boboŋ-laao kom o vo teo kom tiina tei. Ba ma gwoni Seba yuu, ba daare ba dole-ko ba de Joaba yiga ne. O de ma wu nabɔnɔ se o ma o gwɛɛne jara yam. O de o nɔɔna bam ma viiri ba daare teo kom, ye ba maama jwoori ba sam. Joaba de ma jwoori pɛ wom tei Jerusalem ne. Pɛ David dedɛɛra bam

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Joaba déem mo wo Isarele jar-keira bam maama yiga ne. Jehoyada bu Benaya de maa wo Cherete tiina bam dedaane Peleti tiina bam yiga ne.

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Adoniram déem mo ye fefeo totoŋa yam yiga tu. Ahiluda bu Jehosafate maa nii woŋo maama se o popone-te o tiŋi.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Seeva déem mo ye pɛ wom tɔn-poponno. Zadoki de Abiatara maa ye Wɛ kaanem tiina.

english_verse: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_verse: Jayiri tu Yira de déem wo David kaanem tiina bam wone mo.

english_verse: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
translation_verse: Banto déem dae Isarele dwi tiina. Ba maa ye Amori tiina balo na daare ba dwi dem wone to. Isarele tiina bam déem ya dugi we ba bá chɔge-ba. De ko de, Sɔɔl déem tiini o kwaane se o ti ba dwi dem mo, o na jege boboŋ-dɛɛra se o woli Isarele tiina de Judah tiina to ŋwaane. David ma bwoŋi Gibeon tiina bam,

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: ), ye o vɔ se-zɔɔ-doŋo o yera ne. O boboŋa ma ja se o go David.

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Sɔɔl déem yɔɔre o boŋe se o ti dé dwi dem mo, se dé yé daare Isarele tega kam baŋa ne. Konto mo pɛ se o kwaane o go debam dedɛ.

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: Nam le baara barepɛ o dwi dem wone n ja n ba n pa debam. Debam de maa wó ja-ba dé vo Sɔɔl tete teo Gibea, o na ye pɛ wolo Baŋa Wɛ déem na kuri to. Teo kom konto ne mo dé wó go-ba dé yage Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne.” Pɛ wom ma ta-ba o we, “Amo wó ja-ba a ba a pa abam.”

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Ko daare, Pɛ David guli ni-gwonim delo o de Sɔɔl bu Jonatan déem na ke ba pa daane Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to. O ma yage Jonatan bu Mefibosɛfi se ba yé go‑o.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: David ma kwei baara barepɛ bam konto o ke Gibeon tiina bam jeŋa ne. Ba de ma jwoŋi-ba ba ja ba vo peo yuu ne ye ba go-ba ba yage Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. Ba maama barepɛ bam tɔge daane ba te mo. Ko déem ke ko maŋe de chaara zagem maŋa mo.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Aya bukɔ Rizipa déem ma kwei gare-nyenyaaro o ja o di peo kolo yuu twa bam na tigi to. O ma lware gɔrɔ kom o jei pelɔrɔ kom baŋa ne. O ma maŋe da o jeini, ko na zege faao ni ne se ko jwoori ko vo ko yi doa nenem maŋa to. Wea maama, o maa yeini o zeili zuna, se ba yé jeini twa bam baŋa ne. Tete ne de, o ta zeili kago-vara mo se ba yé di-ba.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: o ma zaŋe o vo Jabese Gilead se o jwoŋi Sɔɔl dedaane o bu Jonatan kwi sem nɔɔna bam konto tei ne. Maŋa kalo Filisi tiina bam ya na go Sɔɔl de Jonatan Giliboa peo kom yuu ne ye ba daare ba pale ba yera yam Bɛte-San teo kom pwooni ne to, ko ye Jabese Gilead tiina bam mo déem vei ba ŋɔ kwi sem ba ja jwoori ba teo kom.
