english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Ba ma kwei Sɔɔl de Jonatan kwi sem maama ba ja ba vo ba suli Sɔɔl kwo Kisi yibeeli dem wone. Benjamin laŋa kam teo Zela ne mo konto. Ba ta ma ke kolo maama Pɛ David na pɛ ni se ba ke to. Ba na ke konto maama ba ti to, Baŋa Wɛ laam ma sɛ ba teo kom wɛ-lworo. David kwaare jara de Filisi tiina

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Jara yadwonna daa ma ke Gafa teo ne. Filisi tiina bam babea kadwoŋi maa wora o de na ye nɔn-sawɔrɔ. O jeŋa maama déem jege nwa baredo baredo mo. O namimbia de maa ye baredo baredo.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem tɔge o wora, o yere mo Isibi-Benoba. O nwoŋi nɔn-sawaaro dwi dem wone mo. O chichwei dem dunni déem tiini de gaale de dwoi channa kilo tetɔ (

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Zeruya bu Abisayi ma vo David tei o jwoŋi‑o o yage. O ma mage Filisi tu wom o go. Pɛ David nɔɔna bam ma da ko ŋwaane ba gwoni ni ded‑o ba we, “Dé daa bá sɛ se n da debam n vo jara wone. Kokuri to, Isarele tiina bam maama teena daŋe nmo baŋa ne mo. Dé teena yam konto ba jege se ya jei.”

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne, Filisi tiina bam daa ma ke jara de Isarele tiina bam Goba teo ne. Husaa teo nɔɔno Sibekayi ma go nɔn-sawaara dwi tu wodwoŋi, o yere mo Safi.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam daa ta ma kwaare jara de Filisi tiina bam Goba ne. Bɛtelehem tu Jayiri bu Elihanan déem go Giti tu Goliafe choro wodwoŋi. Wonto chichwei dem daga de dwoi gare-yi sɔɔna da-kwolo na mae tei to.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: O maa jege Isarele tiina bam o twea. David zembaaro Samma bu Jonatan ma zaŋe o go‑o.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Filisi tiina bana bam konto déem mo ye nɔn-sawaara dwi dem tiina na nwoŋi Gafa ne to. David de o nɔɔna bam nam mo go-ba.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: O yɔɔre o jwoŋi-ne mo o yage a dona jeŋa ne, kokuri to, balo na chuli-ne to tiini ba dana ba dwoi-ne.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem na yɔɔre o jwoŋi David o yage o dona maama jeŋa ne dedaane Sɔɔl jeŋa ne to, mo David dɛ ko ŋwaane o pane leiŋa kanto se o ma o seini Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: O ma leeni o we: Baŋa Wɛ mo ye amo dam jeiga, de amo jwoŋinu. O nye de peo mo o pa-ne.

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: Amo Tu Wɛ nye de peo gugworo, a na dale da to mo. O maa yeini o kwoli-ne ne jara nantana na kwoli nɔɔna jara wone tei to. O maa jege dam se o ma o vere-ne cham wone. O maa kwori o ye amo dalem jei, de amo vereno. O jwoŋi-ne vuvuga maama wone mo o yaga.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: Amo yeini a bwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ yere mo. O de maa jwoŋi-ne o yage a dona jeŋa ne. Wonto maŋe se nabiina taa tei‑o mo.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Toone déem kekare-ne de vɔ, nenɛɛne na-fɔrɔ na lage ko pu nɔɔno ko ja tei to. Ko nam ya gɛ fee mo se chɔgem yi-ne.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: Ko nye de churu chwoŋa ŋoge ŋone mo ka vɔ amo ka tiŋi. Toone de ma che kalanchogo a chwoŋa ne de cheigi-ne.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Tega baŋa maama maa ziziŋi ye ka yera sae. Peero tem de maa ziziŋi, Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ kom ŋwaane.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: O ma kɔɔre wɛyuu kom nenɛɛne diga ni gɔrɔ to, ye o laam daare o tu tega kam baŋa ne. O na maa tu to, mo kunkwon-lilirru wo o nɛ kuri ne.

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Tigura déem mo wo Judah teo pɛ Asa de Isarele teo pɛ Baasa tetare ne maŋa kalo maama ba na di ba paara yam to. Isarele teo Pɛ Baasa taane

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena yatɔ maŋa ne mo Ahija bu Baasa di Isarele teo paare Tiraza ne. O ma di paare dem bena finlei-yana (

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: O déem ke lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga, ne Pɛ Jeroboam ya na ke tei ye o pa se Isarele tiina de tusi to.

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: “N déem na ye nabwom to, mo a liiri‑m bworu wone se n ji amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam yuu tu. Nmo nam jwoori n kwei Jeroboam totoŋ-naga kam mo n jege keim-balwaaro n toŋa, ye n daare n pa se Isarele tiina de ke wɛleera pa se a bane zaŋe.

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: Nii mo! A lage a chɔge nmo de n dwi dem maama mo, ne a na ke Nebat bu Jeroboam de o dwi dem tei to.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Nmo dwi dem nɔɔno wolo maama na wó te teo kolo wone to wó ji kukuri ni-wodiu mo. Wolo maa na wó te pwola ne to wó taa ye duura ni-wodiu.”

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem mo tɔge o sampwora Jehu baŋa ne o pa o kwora kam konto yi Baasa de o dwi tiina bam, Baasa na tiini o toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga pa se o totoŋa yam chuchugi Wɛ bane dedɛ to ŋwaane. O daa wo daare Jeroboam totoŋ-naga kam. O ta ma kwori o chɔge Jeroboam dwi dem maama nyɔ. Isarele teo Pɛ Ela taane

english_verse: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
translation_verse: Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena finlei-yaredo (

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
translation_verse: Pɛ Ela déem jege o tontoŋeno wolo yere na ye Zimiri ye o nii pɛ sɔŋɔ torokooro tem chichworo baŋa ne to. O ma ke chichuŋu de pɛ wom. Dɛ dedwe mo Ela wo Areza sɔŋɔ ne. Wonto déem nii pɛ sɔŋɔ kom Tiraza ne mo. Ela ma nyɔ sana o wora o buga.

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Zimiri ma zo sɔŋɔ kom o mage Ela o de tega ne o go. Keim dento kea Judah teo pɛ Asa paare dim bena finlei-yarepɛ (

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: O na yɔɔre o jeini paare dem baŋa ne to mo o go Baasa dwi tiina bam maama nyɔ, ye o chorro de o yuudwonna maama bakeira de dedoa de wo daare.

english_verse: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
translation_verse: ) o di paare dem. O dɛ yiga o ke bena yaredo mo Tiraza ne.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Ela déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. Isarele teo Pɛ Zimiri taane

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Omiri déem mo ye jar-keira bam yiga tu. Ba ma ni we Zimiri zaŋe ba pɛ wom baŋa ne o go‑o. Ba ma lɛɛre ba zege ba jara keim jei sem ne ba kuri Omiri se o leiri o ji Isarele teo pɛ dɛ dem konto ne.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Zimiri na nɛ we ba tu ba cheiŋi teo kom to, o ma zo pɛ sɔŋɔ dam jei sem wone, ye o daare o de mini diga kam wone. Mini dem ma zwɛ‑o de go.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Zimiri déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o na zaŋe Ela baŋa ne tei to maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone. Isarele teo Pɛ Omiri taane

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa kam ne kampɔra déem mo zo Isarele tiina bam wone. Ba chichworo mo zege Ginafi bu Tibini kwaga ne se ba tiŋi‑o pɛ. Badaara bam maa zege Omiri kwaga ne.

english_verse: then he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for
translation_verse: Pɛ Omiri déem kwei lu-nyenno dunni na yi kilo fuserepɛ (

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Omiri déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o bembɛɛne dem maama ba popone-te ba tiŋi Isarele Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Pɛ Omiri ma te ye o vo o kwoa tei. Ba ma kwei‑o ba suli Samaria teo ne. O bu Ahab ma leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ. Isarele teo Pɛ Ahab taane

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: O déem paale o kwei Nebat bu Jeroboam totoŋ-naga kam mo. Kolo maa na dwoi to mo ye o kwei Sidon pɛ Efebaal bukɔ Jezebele mo o ma o ji o kaane. O déem tɔge o zuli Baal jwoni dem mo.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: O lɔge diga mo Samaria ne Baal zula ŋwaane o daare o zege kaanem bimbini ka wone.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Ahab ta ma chwi Asera nyenyego daa. O ma tiini o chuchugi Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to bane se ko dwoni pwa balo na dɛ yiga ba ba to.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Pɛ Ahab paare dim maŋa ne to mo Hiyeli na nwoŋi Bɛtel to fɔge o lɔ Jeriko teo. O na bobo o chwi teo kom biri-beira to mo o bu-kwea Abiram tega. O maa na kwaare ko manchwoŋo ni bworru tem to mo o bu Segubi de tega. Ko na ke tei konto to pɛ se Wɛ kwora kalo Nun bu Josua na tage faŋa faŋa to ji chega.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Wɛ sampwora kadwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Elija. O déem nwoŋi Gilead teo Tisibi mo. Dɛ dedwe o ma vo o ta de Pɛ Ahab o we, “Amo toŋe a pa Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to mo. Wonto na ye Ŋwea Tu chekke to, a ná wo jwoori a ta taane, nyɔnɔ daa bá to, doa de nam daa bá ne tega kanto baŋa ne, se ko taa nii bena yalei naa yatɔ wɛɛne.”

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi Elija we,

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: “Zaŋe n yɔɔre wɛ-puli seeni n vo n seigi n tete Kerifi nabara kam na wo Jɔdan buga kam wɛ-puli seeni to ni ne.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Nabara kam konto na mo n jege se n ta‑n nyɔa. A nam pɛ bachangaaro ni se te taa tui te pa‑m wodiu dáane.”

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Bachangaaro tem ma jaane bworobworo de nɔna te tui te pa‑o tetete de dedaan-ni maama. O ma nyɔ nabara kam na bam. Elija de kadeim wodwoŋi taane

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Ko na wora ko wora to, nabara kam ma we, doa daa na ba nena tega kam maama ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Lord told Elijah,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Elija o we,

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: “Zaŋe lela n vo Zarefate na wo Sidon teo kom seeni to n ta‑n zoore da. A nam maŋe a ta de kadeim wodwoŋi se o pa‑m n ni-wodiu.”

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: Elija ma zaŋe o vo Zarefate. O na yi teo kom manchwoŋo ni dem to mo o nɛ kadeim na wora o beeri o da-dwa. O ma bwoŋi kadeim wom o lwoori‑o o we, “Jan ja! Mɔ na n pa-ne se a nyɔ.”

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Kadeim wom na maa vei se o ja na bam o ba o pa‑o to mo Elija daa we, “Jan ja! Kwei bworobworo fee n woli da n ja n ba.”

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Kadeim wom ma leiri o we, “Nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ na ye Ŋwea Tu chekke to, a dugi o yere ŋwaane we, a ba jege bworobworo. Muni fee yerane mo a jega mun-duru wone, a daare a jege nuga de fee kabɔɔ wone. A zege a puuri da-dwa balei se a jwoori sɔŋɔ a ma a saŋe wodiu mo, se a de a bu wom di dé kweeli se dé laam te.”

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Elija ma ta de kadeim wom o we, “Yé ta‑n kɔre foone. Véi sɔŋɔ n ke n na taga tei to. Da yiga n kwei muni delo n na jege to fee n ma n fɔge maase n pa-ne. Se n kwei kolo na daare to n ma n ke wodiu se n de n bu wom di.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: ‘Mun-duru kom bá fɔge ko kwɛ muni. Kabɔɔ kom de maa bá kwɛ nuga se ko taa nii maŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó pa se doa jwoori ka ne tega kam baŋa ne to.’ ”

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Kadeim wom ma seene o jwoori sɔŋɔ o ke kolo maama Elija na taga to. Ko ma seene ko ke we, Elija tete, de kadeim wom, de o bu wom wolowolo wo gɛ wodiu se ba di da dedɛ wone.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Ba déem ná maŋe ba kwoori nuga kam de muni dem tei maama, ko ba tia, ne Baŋa Wɛ na tɔge Elija baŋa o ta we ko wó ke tei to.

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne mo kadeim wom bu-baaro wom weele. Jaweo kom ma tiini ko zo‑o ye o momwɛ ti.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Kadeim wom ma ta de Elija o we, “Wɛ tontoŋeno, bɛ mo ye n ke amo tento? N tu amo tei se n pa a wɛleera lɔre ja, se n daare n pa a bu wom te mo na?”

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Elija ma leiri‑o o we, “Ja n bu wom n ba n pa-ne.” O ma jwoŋi bu wom kaane wom jeŋa ne o ja‑o o di nayuu diga kalo o na zoore da to. O ma tiŋi bu wom o kadwogo baŋa ne.

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: O ma keeri o jare Baŋa Wɛ de kwor-dɛa o we, “A Tu Baŋa Wɛ, bɛ mo ye n pa se lɛɛro tento yi kadeim wom pa se o bu wom te, ye wonto mo jwoŋi-ne o sɔŋɔ ne?”

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: O ma twe o tete bu wom baŋa ne kuni betɔ o keeri o jare Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nam pa se bakeira kam jwoori ka na ŋwea.”

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma sɛ Elija lworo kom ye bu wom jwoori o na ŋwea.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: O na wori to, Elija ma kwei‑o o tu konkɔlɔ kom ne o pa o nu. O maa we, “Nii, n bu wom jwoori o ŋwe.”

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Kadeim wom ma ta de Elija o we, “Leile konto a laam tu a lɔre chekke we n ye Wɛ tontoŋeno. N ma‑n na tage kolo to seene ko ye Baŋa Wɛ kwora chekke mo.”

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: Jezebele déem na wora o goe Baŋa Wɛ sampwori sem to mo Obadia kwei sampwori sem bi o seigi peo bɔɔna yalei wone. O seigi-ba bɔɔna yalei wone, nɔɔna finnu bɔɔne maama wone. O maa jaane wodiu de na o vei o pa-ba.

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Pɛ Ahab tage de Obadia o we, “Véi n beeri buli-yia yam de nabare sem ni maama dé tega kam baŋa ne se dé nii, dé wó na ga-zuru dé pa sisei sem de bona-sisei sem se se di na. Konto wó woli se dé yé go-se.”

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Obadia na wo veiŋa ne konto to mo o jeeri Elija chwoŋa ne. O na lɔre we ko ye Elija to, o ma tiiri o zuli‑o ye o we, “Amo tu Elija, ko ye nmo mo konto na?”

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Obadia ma bwei‑o o we, “A tu, a ke bɛ tete mo a chɔge n yiga pa se n boŋe se a ke keim delo na wó pa Ahab ti a ŋwea to?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: N Tu Baŋa Wɛ na ye Ŋwea Tu chekke to, ko yɔɔre ko ye chega mo we, teo de ko teo tera ye pɛ wom wo toŋe nɔɔna da se ba beeri nmo jeiga. Teo kolo nɔɔna ná we, n tere ba tei ne, Ahab yeini o pa se ba du duuri mo we ba wo nɛ‑m.

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: A ná yage‑m ye a viiri leile konto, a yeiri Baŋa Wɛ Jworo daa na wó kwei‑m o ja o vo mɛ. A nam ná vei a ta a bere Ahab ye o wo nɛ‑m, o laam wó go-ne mo. Ko nam na maŋe ko zege amo biini ne to mo a kɔre Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Elija ma leiri o we, “Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ye Ŋwea Tu mo chekke, ye a toŋe a pa‑o. A nam dugi wonto yere ŋwaane we, a zem wó ja a tete a vo a bere Ahab.”

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Obadia ma seene o jwoori Pɛ Ahab tei o ta o bere‑o we Elija wora. Pɛ wom ma vo o jeeri Elija.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: O na nɛ Elija to mo o we, “Nmo wolo na pae Isarele teo kom na ko lɛɛro to mo konto na?”

english_verse: Call together everyone from Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. Be sure to bring along the
translation_verse: Nam ta n bere Isarele tiina bam maama se ba ba ba jeeri-ne Kamele peo kom yuu ne. Ko ta ná ye Baal sampwori bia yana de finnu (

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Pɛ Ahab ma pa ni yi Isarele tiina bam maama pa se ba de sampwori sem maama jeeri Kamele peo kom yuu ne.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Elija ma fɔɔre o zege ba kɔgɔ kom yiga ne o ta o we, “Á ta wó ta‑á jege boboŋa yalei taa se á vo á maŋe yei ne mo? Nam kuri-na á na wó ke tei. Baŋa Wɛ mo ná seene o ye Wɛ, ta‑á zuli-na wonto. Á nam daa ná we Baal mo ye wɛ chekke, se á ta‑á zuli wonto.” Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maa wo leiri kolokolo.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Ja-na nabɛ selei á ba á pa debam. Baal sampwori sem wó kuri nabɛ sem dedoa se ba ma ba ke kaanem. Ba laam wó go-ka ba cha ka nɔna yam yera yera ba kwei ba daŋe dɛ sem baŋa ne. Ba nam ba jege se ba de mini da. Amo de maa wó cha nabea kadwoŋi kam a daŋe dɛ sem baŋa ne, ye a bá de mini da.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Abam laam wó bwoŋi á wɛ dem yere, se amo de bwoŋi Baŋa Wɛ wom yere. Wɛ delo na wó leiri ye o de mini kaanem dem ne to mo wó seene o taa ye Wɛ chekke.” Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama ma sɛ ye ba we, “N na tage kolo to jege kuri.”

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Elija daa ta ma ta de Baal sampwori sem o we, “Abam kɔgɔ kom na daga to, da-na yiga á kuri nabea dedoa á go se á ti ka nɔna yiga. Á ná ti, se á laam lwoori á wɛ dem se de de mini da, ye ko dae abam mo wó de mini da.”

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Ba ma ja nabea kalo ba na pɛ-ba to ba go ba ti ka nɔna yiga. Ba ma bwoŋi Baal yere dem taa, ko zege tetete se ko yi we-bere maŋa. Ba ma sa ba kaare bimbini delo ba na lɔge to ye ba bage de kwor-dɛa ba we, “Baal, zaŋe n cheigi dé lworo kom!” Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa wo leiri-ba de fenfee de. Ko maa ye yirititi.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: We-bere maŋa ne Elija ma zaŋe o jege Baal sampwori sem o mɔna ye o we, “Tiini á bage de kwor-dɛa, se Baal ye wɛ mo! O ga wo boboŋa wone mo, naa o nwoŋi mo, naa o vei chwoŋa mo. Dɛ delo o tigi o dɔa mo, ye ko maŋe se á pa o zaŋe.”

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: Baal sampwori sem ma tiini ba keeri wɛ-wɛ, ye ba daare ba ma ba fane de se-zɔɔro ba gwoni ba yera pa se ba jana lwo ba ke ba yera ne, ne ba chullu tem na bere se ba ke tei to.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Ba zege wea ne ba bore Baal yiga ne konto mo taa se ko taa nii dedaan-ni kaanem dem maŋa. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno maa wo leiri kolokolo ye ko ye yirititi.

translation_verse: Mikaya laam ma ta o we, “A nɛ Isarele jar-keira bam maama na jage peero tem baŋa ne ye ba beeri yɔɔ yɔɔ nenɛɛne pei selo na ba jege nayero to. Baŋa Wɛ ma ta o we, ‘Nɔɔna banto ba jege yuu tu. Yage-na se ba jwoori sɔŋɔ chemm de yazura.’ ”
