translation_verse: Banto balei na vei ba zege Jɔdan buga kam ni ne to, mo Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kom wo nɔɔna finnu ma tɔge ba vo ba zege dáa ne ye ba nia.

english_verse: When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
translation_verse: Elija ma le o gɔrɔ o kukuli-ko o ma o mage Jɔdan buga na bam. Na bam ma pɔɔre ba peini jazem de jagwia pa se ba balei bam tɔge te-kora baŋa ne ba bɛ.

english_verse: After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?” Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
translation_verse: Ba na bɛ buga kam konto to, mo Elija tage de Elisa o we, “Ta n bere-ne nmo na laga se a ke woŋo kolo a pa‑m to, se Baŋa Wɛ laam ba o ja-ne o viiri.” Elisa ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, a lage se a jwoŋi n dam delo n na jege n toŋe to kuni belei mo.”

english_verse: Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven.
translation_verse: Elija de Elisa na tɔge daane ba via ye ba lara konto to, mo torokooro na jege min-vogo to de te sisein-nɔɔna de na jege mini to pɔpɔ te zaŋe ba baŋa ne kulululu te pwɛ-ba daane. Elija ma da de vo-kekara o kɛ Wɛ telaao.

english_verse: Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River.
translation_verse: O ma kwei Elija gɔrɔ kolo ya na lwei to o jwoori o vo o zege Jɔdan buga kam ni ne.

english_verse: He struck the water with the coat and wondered, “Will the Lord perform miracles for me as he did for Elijah?” As soon as Elisha did this, a dry path opened up through the water, and he walked across.
translation_verse: O ma kwei Elija gɔrɔ kom o mage na bam baŋa ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Elija Wɛ to nam bɛ?” O na mage na bam konto to, ba ma pɔɔre belei ba daare te-kora. O laam ma tɔge da o bɛ Jɔdan buga kam.

english_verse: When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.” They walked over to him, bowed down,
translation_verse: Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kolo déem na nwoŋi Jeriko to ma tole ba na Elisa na ke kolo to, ye ba we, “Elisa mo leiri Elija yuu ne o jege o dam dem.” Ba ma fɔɔre ba yi o tei ye ba tiiri o yiga ne ba zuli‑o.

english_verse: They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him.
translation_verse: Ba ma tiini ba kwoori‑o pa se Elisa ga ba ŋwa. O ma ta-ba o we, “Nam toŋe-na-ba se ba vo.” Ba ma seene ba toŋe nɔɔna finnu ye ba vo ba kwei da yatɔ ba beeri jei maama ye ba wo nɛ Elija.

english_verse: They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.” Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
translation_verse: Elisa déem maŋe Jeriko teo wone mo. Ba na jwoori ba ba o tei to, o ma ta-ba o we, “A ya maŋe a wo tage a bere abam we, á yé vei na?” Elisa na ke wo-kenkagela yalo to

english_verse: One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
translation_verse: Jeriko teo nɔn-bia badwonna déem ma vo Elisa tei ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Debam tu, nii dé teo kom zega na tiini ko lana tei. Ko nam na ye tei to, na bam mo ba lana. Tega kam de maa ba ke wodiiru lanyerane.”

english_verse: He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.” They brought him the bowl of salt,
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta o we, “Kwei-na yɛ á ke zon-doŋa wone á ja á ba á pa-ne.” Ba na ke konto to,

english_verse: and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
translation_verse: o ma kwei yɛ dem o vo o lwo teo kom buli-yi dem ne ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo kwɛ na banto pa ba ji na-ŋona. Wolo ná nyɔge-ba, kotu bá te. Tega kam de nam bá ji kafɛ.”

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Konto na ke to, na bam ma lɛɛre ba ji na-ŋona se ko ba ko yi zem, nenɛɛne Elisa na tage tei to.

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Elisa déem ma zege Jeriko ne o maa vei Bɛtel. O na wo chwoŋa ne konto to, mo bu-donno tedwonna nwoŋi teo kom wone ba ba ba jege‑o ba mɔna ye ba bage‑o ba we, “Yu-kapworo tu, ta‑n kɛa! Lage jei!”

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Elisa ma pipiri o nii ba seeni ye o daare o sɔɔle lwarem o yage ba yuu ne Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane. O na yɔɔre o ta konto to, mo kago-vara balei nwoŋi gaao kom wone ba ja bu-donno tem finna-balei ba tore yera-yera.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Elisa ma zege jeiga kam konto ne o vo Kamele peo kom seeni. Ko kwaga ne o ma jwoori Samaria.

english_verse: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria
translation_verse: Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate paare dim bena fuga-nana bene dem wone mo Ahab bu Joram déem di Isarele teo paare Samaria ne. O ma jeini Samaria ne o di paare dem bena fuga-yalei.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: Joram déem toŋe lwarem mo o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. O lwarem kikia yam nam wo yi o kwo de nu ya na ke yalo to. O wane o chɔge kandwɛ delo o kwo déem na chwi Baal zula ŋwaane to.

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: De konto de, o paale o ke wɛleera dwi delo Nebat bu Jeroboam déem na ke pa se Isarele tiina de da ba ke to mo. O wo sɛ se o yage.

english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Moaba teo pɛ Mesa déem kɔne pei mo. O ma yeini o jege se o ja pipeili morro bi (

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Isarele teo pɛ Ahab nam na tege to mo Moaba teo pɛ ve se o to o pa Isarele teo pɛ wom.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: O ma toŋe ni o pa Judah teo pɛ Jehosafate ye o we, “Moaba pɛ wom ve se o to o pa-ne. Nmo nam wó sɛ se n da de amo se dé vo dé ke jara de Moaba tiina bam na?” Jehosafate ma leiri o we, “A wó sɛ se a woli‑m. Dé ye chorro mo daane. Ta‑n nii debam jar-keira de dé sisein-nɔɔna bam we ba ye nmo tete nyem mo.”

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Isarele pɛ Joram, de Judah pɛ wom, ko woli de Edom pɛ wom ma zaŋe ba kɛ de ba nɔɔna bam. Ba maama ma kwei da yarepɛ ba kaare kagoa kam wone pa se na daa tera se ba de ba vara bam nyɔ.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Pɛ Joram ma laare o we, “Lɛɛro yi debam! Baŋa Wɛ lage o kwei debam pwa batɔ banto mo o ke Moaba tiina bam jeŋa ne se ba di debam!”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Pɛ Jehosafate ma bwei o we, “Baŋa Wɛ sampwora wora ywo-seeni se dé bwei‑o dé lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa na?” Pɛ Joram tontoŋeno wodwoŋi ma leiri o we, “Safate bu Elisa mo wora. Wonto déem mo yeini o bwola de Elija ye o woli‑o.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Pɛ Jehosafate ma ta o we, “Ko ná ye konto, Baŋa Wɛ kwora yeini ka yi wonto mo chekke”. Pwa batɔ bam maama ma zaŋe ba vo Elisa tei.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta de Isarele pɛ Joram o we, “Debam jege bɛ mo se dé ke daane? Véi n bwei n kwo de n nu sampwori sem se ba woli‑m.” Joram ma leiri o we, “Aawo! Ko ye Baŋa Wɛ mo kwei debam pwa batɔ banto o ke daane se o daare o kwei debam o ke Moaba tiina bam jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma leiri o we, “Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o ŋwe ye a ye o tontoŋeno to, amo dugi o yere ŋwaane we, ko ná dae a na nege Judah Pɛ Jehosafate, amo ya ba lage a nii n seeni kɔtaa.

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Nam bwoŋi-na wolo na yei kɔnɔ tam to á pa-ne.” Kokuri to, nɔɔno déem ná yeini o ta kɔnɔ mo Baŋa Wɛ dam dem wó ba Elisa baŋa ne.

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: ‘Ko-na gwonnu á tiŋi nabare-kora kanto ne.

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, amo na wó ke tei to, abam bá na doa, ye vio de bá dole. Ko daare na wó ba ba su bwolo konto se abam de á nɔɔna bam maama de á vara bam taa nyɔa.’

english_verse: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
translation_verse: Keim dento ye mɔle mo Baŋa Wɛ tei ne. O daa ta wó kwei Moaba tiina bam o ke abam jeŋa ne.

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: Abam wó vo á wane ba dam jei sem maama de ba te-fwaaro tem. Á ta wó gwoni ba tei-ŋonno tem á de tega ne ye á daare á se ba buli-yia yam de. Á ta maa wó lwo kandwa á chɔge ba tega kalo maama na lana to.”

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Tega na poore se ko maŋe de zezeŋa kaanem dem to mo na seene ba zege Edom laŋa kam seeni ba ba ba tagele tega kam maama.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Moaba tiina bam na nigi we pwa batɔ bam mo ke ba jar-keira daane ba ba se ba kwaare jara de-ba to, ba ma bwoŋi balo maama na yei jara keim to, nɔn-donno de nɔn-kweero de, pa se ba vo ba laŋa kam siseini ba zege da.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Tega na poore tetete ye Moaba tiina bam zaŋe to, ba ma tole ba na na bam na tigi bwolo kom ne tei to. Wea maa nyeene na bam baŋa ne pa se ko nye de jana mo to.

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: Ba ma laare ba we, “Jana mo tento! Ko wó taa ye pwa bam de ba jar-keira bam mo jaŋe ba go daane. Nam pa-na se dé laam vo dé vere ba wonnu maama dé taa tei.”

english_verse: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
translation_verse: Moaba tiina bam na yɔɔre ba yi Isarele jar-keira bam na tigisi daane mɛ to, mo Isarele jar-keira bam nwoŋi ba kwaare jara de-ba. Ba ma zeili-ba pa se ba duri ba jwoori ba teo. Ba ma pare-ba taa ye ba go Moaba tiina dedɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Ba déem chɔge ba teene dem mo. Isarele nɔɔna bam dedoa dedoa ma dole kandwa ba faare Moaba te-ywoŋa kam maama ba chɔge. Ba ma se ba buli-yia yam maama ba daare ba gwoni ba tei-ŋonno tem maama ba de tega ne. Kiri-Heresi teo kom yerane ya mo daare ko zege puna. Isarele jar-keira laam ma vo ba gilimi-ko ye ba daare ba ma napane ba dole kandwa ba ma ba chɔge-ko.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: O laam ma ja o bu-kwea kalo ya na wó leiri o yuu ne o ji pɛ to o ma o ke zwɛɛm kaanem teo kom kabira kam baŋa ne. Keim dento déem ma tiini de daane Isarele tiina bam pa se ba pipiri ba jwoori ba tete teo ba daare Moaba teo pɛ de o nɔɔna bam.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
translation_verse: Kaane wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o na ye Wɛ sampwori sem dedoa kaane. Dɛ dedwe o ma zaŋe o vo Elisa tei o ŋwane o we, “Amo tu, a baro wom tega ye o ya tɔge nmo kwaga. Nmo maŋe n yei o na yeini o kɔre Baŋa Wɛ tei to. O ya na di jene nɔɔno wolo tei ne to nam mo tu se o jwoŋi a bakeiri sem selei o vo o ma o ji o kabɛ se o ma o yiri jene dem.”

english_verse: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma bwei‑o o we, “Woŋo wora amo na wó wane a ke a woli‑m na? Nam ta n bere-ne, bɛ mo n daare n yage sɔŋɔ ne?” Kadeim wom ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, kolokolo tera ko ná dae kabɔɔ de ka wo nuga fenfee yerane.”

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta de kadeim wom o we, “Tole sane delo na bwola de nmo to se n jene kunkwollu ba tei ne. Pa se te taa daga dedɛ.

english_verse: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
translation_verse: Kwei kunkwollu telo n na nɛ to n zo diga n pe ka ni, se nmo de n bia balei bam taa wora. Nmo ma‑n wó pwori nuga kam n ke kunkwollu tem wone. Kunkwolo kolo ná sua, se n zege-ko dáane.”

english_verse: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
translation_verse: Kadeim wom ma jwoori sɔŋɔ o pe o ni diga wone, o de o bia bam. Ba maa jaane kunkwollu tem ba vei ba pa‑o ye o lɛɛre nuga kam te wone.

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: Kunkwollu tem maama na su to, o ma ta bia bam se ba ja tedwonna ba ba ba pa‑o. Ba dedoa ma leiri o we, “Mo te maama.” O na tage konto to mo kabɔɔ kam wo nuga kam ti.

english_verse: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
translation_verse: Kadeim wom ma vo o ta ko na ke tei to o bere Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa. Elisa ma ta ded‑o o we, “Véi n kwei nuga kam n yeigi n ma n ŋwe jene dem. Sabu ta ná daare, ko wó woli nmo de n bia bam se á na á ni-wodiu.” Sunem tiina kaane wodwoŋi taane

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Elisa déem vei Sunem. Kaane wodwoŋi maa zoore da ye o ye nadum. O ma bwoŋi Elisa o sɔŋɔ ne se o di wodiu. Ko na zege dɛ dem konto ne to, maŋa kalo maama Elisa ná vei Sunem, o yeini o di kaane wom konto sɔŋɔ ne mo.

english_verse: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma ta de o baro o we, “Nii mo. Amo maane we nɔɔno wonto na yeini o tui debam tei to ye Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno mo chekke.

english_verse: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
translation_verse: Nam pa se dé lɔ di-balaŋa nayuu kom ne se dé daare dé zege kadwogo, de tabolo, de yituŋu, de min-zwoŋo da. Konto wó woli Wɛ tontoŋeno wom se, o ná yeini o ba, se o na peiga jei.”

english_verse: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Elisa jwoori Sunem. O ma di o zo nayuu diga kam se o peini.

english_verse: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta de Gehazi se o lwoni o ta kaane wom we, “Nii nmo na pɛ n yera chɛ se n ma‑n woli debam tei! Debam nam wó ke bɛ mo dé ma dé zeini nmo? Dɛ delo amo wó wane a ta n lanyerane a bere pɛ wom naa jar-keira yiga tu wom.” Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “Yé daane n tete, amo na zoore de a sɔŋɔ tiina to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
translation_verse: Elisa laam ma bwei Gehazi o we, “Bɛ nam mo maŋe se a ke a pa kaane wom?” Gehazi ma leiri o we, “Kaane wom ta wo loge bu. O baro de ma tiini o kwe lanyerane.”

english_verse: “Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta de Gehazi o we, “Bwoŋi kaane wom se o jwoori o ba.” Kaane wom ma ba o zege diga kam ni ne.

english_verse: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta de kaane wom o we, “Bene tento wɛɛne nmo wó lo bakeira.” Kaane wom maa wo sɛ ye o we, “Amo tu, yé gane-ne, se n ye Wɛ tontoŋeno mo.”

english_verse: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
translation_verse: Bene na jwoori de yi to, kaane wom ma seene o ja puga o lo bakeira. Ko déem ke ne Elisa na wuuri o ta tei ded‑o to mo.

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Bu wom na ke nɔɔno fee to mo dɛ dedwe o zaŋe o vo o kwo tei kara ne maŋa kalo o kwo wom de tontoŋena badwonna na wora ba zage mena to.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Bu wom ma pɔpɔ o laare bedwe baŋa ne de o kwo o we, “A yuu wɔe ywoo! A yuu wɔe ywoo!” O kwo ma ta de o tontoŋeno wodwoŋi o we, “Ja bu wom n vo o nu tei.”

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom ma teili bu wom o ja o vo o ke o nu wom jeŋa ne. Bu wom ma maŋe o nu nɛ baŋa ne o jeini. Wea na yi yupare baŋa maŋa kalo to mo bu wom tega.

english_verse: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma ja o bu wom o di nayuu kom o zo Elisa diga o tiŋi‑o kadwogo kom baŋa ne. O ma nwoŋi o ja diga kam ni o pe o yage bu wom da.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma bwoŋi o baro o ta ded‑o o we, “Ja, pa se n tontoŋena bam dedoa ja bonaga o ba, se dé da daane dé vo Wɛ tontoŋeno wom tei, se dé jwoori lela.”

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: O baro wom ma ta‑o o we, “Bɛ mo ke ye n lage se n vo zem? Chan-doŋa ta wo nwoŋi. Ko maa dae siu dɛ.” Kaane wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Ko ye yazura mo.”

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma vo o yi Kamele peo kom mɛ Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa na wora to. Elisa ma tole o na‑o yiga yiga ye o ta de o tontoŋeno Gehazi o we, “Nii Sunem tiina kaane wom na maa beene.

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Ke lela n duri n jeeri‑o n bwei‑o n nii, yazura mo o vei na? Bwei‑o n nii o baro de o bu yazura na ye tei to.” Kaane wom ma leiri Gehazi o we, ko ye yazura mo.

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: Kaane wom na yi Elisa tei Kamele peo kom yuu ne to mo o to o yiga ne o ja o naga. Gehazi ma fɔɔre o yi se o vaŋe‑o o yage dáane. Elisa ma ta o we, “Yage o yera! O wo tiini ko chɔge mo ye o ba. Baŋa Wɛ nam wo tage kolo na daane‑o to o bere-ne.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma ŋwane Elisa yiga ne o we, “Amo tu, a wo tage we n pa-ne bu. Konto mo a ya taga a we n yé gane-ne to.”

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta de Gehazi o we, “Fɔge n vɔ n gare-kura kiri-kiri n daare n kwei a nacheiga kam n duri lela n kɛ. Nam yé ware nɔɔn-nɔɔno chwoŋa yuu ne. Nɔɔno ná ware‑m, se n yé leiri‑o. N ná yi da se n kwei a nacheiga kam n daŋe bu wom yibia ne.”

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma ta de Elisa o we, “Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane, de nmo tete ŋwea ŋwaane we, amo bere a bá yage‑m.” Elisa ma zaŋe se ba tɔge daane ba kɛ.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Gehazi ma lwoori yiga o vo o yi da ye o daare o kwei nacheiga kam o daŋe bu wom yibia ne ye bu wom wo gigiri o tete. O ma jwoori o vo Elisa tei o ta ded‑o o we, “Bu wom ta wo zaŋe.”

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Elisa na yi sɔŋɔ kom o zo o diga kam to mo o nɛ bu wom na tege o tigi o kadwogo baŋa ne.

english_verse: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
translation_verse: O ma pe diga kam ni ye o lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o yerane.

english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
translation_verse: Elisa ta ma zaŋe o yi kadwogo kom baŋa, o peini bu wom baŋa ne pa se o ni dem yɔɔre bu wom ni, ye o yia yɔɔre o yia. O ma daare o lware o jea pa ya yɔɔre o jea. O na lware o tete o peini bu wom baŋa ne konto to mo bu wom yera lone.

english_verse: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
translation_verse: Elisa ma zaŋe o kekare diga kam wone ye o daa jwoori o vo o lware o tete o peini bu wom baŋa ne. Bu wom ma te kuni berepɛ ye o daare o puri o yia.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma bwoŋi Gehazi ye o ta ded‑o se o bwoŋi Sunem tiina kaane wom o pa‑o. O na bwoŋi nu wom pa se o yi to, Elisa ma ta ded‑o o we, “Jwoŋi n bu.”

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Kaane wom ma zo o to Elisa nɛ baŋa ne ye o vwi o yibia tega ne. O ma seene o jwoŋi o bu o viiri. Wo-kenkagela yalei taane

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma jwoori o vo Giligal. Da-kore déem maa zege jei sem konto ne. Dɛ dedwe o de Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kom ma jeeri daane se ba zamese. O ma ta de o tontoŋeno wom o we, “Kwei kambi-zaŋa n teini mini ne n saŋe dwoa n pa nɔɔna bam.”

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Ba kɔgɔ kom wo nɔɔno dedoa ma zo gaao se o gwoni dwo-vɔɔro. O ma na kunkwol-chɛɛra o pɛ o su o gɔrɔ ni o jwoori. O ma gwoni te maama o woli dwoa balo na wo kambia kam wone to, ye o wo lɔre te na ye wonnu telo.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Ba laam ma kwei dwoa bam ba maŋe ba pa daane. Nɔɔna bam na yɔɔre ba laŋe wodiu kom to, ba ma laare ba we, “Keitaa! Dé tu, Baŋa Wɛ tontoŋeno, chɔŋɔ mo ba ke wodiu kom wone!” Ba maa wo ware-ko ba di.

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta o we, ba ja muni ba ba ba pa‑o. O ma kwei-de o ke kambia kam wone ye o we, “Jwoori n ke wodiu kom n pa nɔɔna bam se ba di.” Ba ma seene ba di ye ko daa wo bwei-ba.

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno wom déem ma seene o kwei wodiu kom o pa-ba pa ba di ba daare, ne Baŋa Wɛ na maŋe o ta tei to.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Naaman. O maa ye Siria tiina pɛ wom jar-keira yiga tu. O ye dedɛɛro mo ye o kikia su pɛ wom yi lanyerane, Baŋa Wɛ na dɛ o baŋa o woli Siria tiina pa se ba di ba dona jara wone to ŋwaane. Konto to, o ye babea na yei jara keim chekke to mo. De ko de, o déem ye nayɔŋɔ mo.

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Siria tiina pɛ wom ma leiri o we, “Tɔ. Véi se n na nɔɔno wom konto. Amo wó popone tɔnɔ nmo ŋwaane se n ja n vo n pa Isarele teo pɛ wom.” Naaman ma la lu-nyenno kilo bia yatɔ de finna (

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: O ma kwei tɔnɔ kom o vo o pa Isarele teo pɛ wom. Kolo na popone ko wone to mo tento: “Tɔnɔ konto ye se ko bere we amo mo toŋe a tontoŋeno Naaman se o ba nmo tei, se n yɔɔre o naywaane jaweo kom n pa‑o.”

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma toŋe o tontoŋeno se o vo ta de Naaman we, “Nam véi n swɛ n yera kuni berepɛ Jɔdan buga kam wone, se n ya-nɔna yam laam wó kwɛ ye n jaweo kom jei.”

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Isarele teo pɛ wom na gage tɔnɔ kom o ti to, mo o jaane o gɔrɔ o kaare ye o we, “Amo ye Wɛ mo se a wane a pa nɔɔno momwɛ ti, ye a daare a pa wodwoŋi na ŋwea na? Bɛ mo ye Siria teo pɛ toŋe nɔɔno wonto se o ba amo tei se a yɔɔre‑o? Nii-na o na beeri woŋo se o da ko baŋa o ja jara de amo tei!”

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa na nigi kolo na ke ye Isarele tiina pɛ wom kaare o gɔrɔ to, o ma toŋe ni dento o pa‑o ye o we, “Bɛ mo pɛ se n ja n gwaaro n kaare? Toŋe nɔɔno wom se o ba amo tei se a pa o lɔre we, Wɛ sampwora seene o wo Isarele teo ne.”

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Naaman laam ma ja o sisei sem de se torokooro tem o vo o zege Elisa diga ni ne.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Naaman na nigi konto to, o bane ma zaŋe dedɛ. O ma varege ye o we, “Nii mo! A ya boŋe we Elisa tete mo wó nwoŋi o ba o zege amo yiga ne o bwoŋi o Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom yere, se o daare o yeese o jea a ŋɔna yam baŋa ne o yɔɔre amo.

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Abana de Farepa bwi sem na wo Damasika ne to ba gare Isarele bwi sem maama na? A ya wae a swɛ a yera bwi sento wone ye a ya-nɔna kwɛ.”

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Naaman tontoŋena ma fɔɔre ba yi o tei. Ba dedoa ma ta ded‑o o we, “A kwo, sampwora kam ya ná we n toŋe totoŋ-chɛɛre, nmo bá‑n ke na? O nam na tage kolo to dae mɔle ko pa‑m na? O we n swɛ n yera se ya kwɛ. Ko dae konto mo na?”

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Naaman laam ma seene o tu o misi o tete Jɔdan buga kam wone kuni berepɛ, ne Wɛ tontoŋeno wom na taga tei to. O ya-nɔna yam ma jwoori ya kwɛ lanyerane nenɛɛne bakeiri-pwola yera na ye tei to, ye o jaweo kom jei.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Naaman de o nɔɔna bam maama ma jwoori ba vo Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa tei ba zege o yiga ne. Naaman ma ta de Elisa o we, “Amo zem laam tu a lɔre we Isarele tiina Wɛ wom yerane mo ye wɛ chekke logo baŋa maama wone. Jan ja, amo tu! Sɛ se n jwoŋi a pɛɛra yam.”

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Elisa ma leiri o we, “Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora ye a toŋe a pa‑o to, amo dugi wonto yere ŋwaane we, amo bá jwoŋi kolokolo nmo tei ne.” Naaman ta ma lwoori Elisa o ga se o jwoŋi pɛɛra yam o tei ne.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Naaman ma ta o we, “Amo tu, nmo na tage we n bá‑n sɛ se n jwoŋi kolokolo a jeŋa ne to, nam pa-ne chwoŋa se a pɛ teero ywo-seeni se te yi bona-sisei selei na wó wane se zeŋe tei to, se a ja a viiri. Kokuri to, ko zege zem se ko taa via, amo daa bá ke kaanem naa zwɛɛm pɛɛra a pa wɛ dedwoŋi, ko ná dae Baŋa Wɛ yerane.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Amo nam lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o duri a yibwona keim dento ŋwaane: amo ná dɛ de a tu Siria teo pɛ a zo Rimon jwoni diga kam se o zuli-de, ye pɛ wom ná sale a yera ne, ye amo de da a tiiri tega ne ded‑o, se Baŋa Wɛ yage o chɛ-ne.”

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Elisa ma leiri o we, “Nam véi, se Wɛ wó pa‑m yazura.” Naaman ma viiri. Naaman na vei o yi yiga fee to,

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: mo Elisa tontoŋeno Gehazi taga o tete ne we, “Ta‑n nii tei. Amo tu Elisa yage Siria tu wom mo se o viiri konto mɔle mɔle, ye o wo jwoŋi pɛɛra yam o jeŋa ne de fenfee de. Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ na seene o wora to, a dugi wonto yere ŋwaane we amo tete mo wó pare Naaman a jwoŋi woŋo o tei ne.”

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Gehazi ma ke lela se o vo o yi‑o. Naaman na tole o na nɔɔno na duri o beene o tei to, o ma zege o toroko kom baŋa o faŋe o chu tega ne o vo o jeeri‑o. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Yazura mo n vei na?”

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Gehazi ma leiri Naaman o we, “Ko dae wo-lɔŋɔ. Ko ye amo tu Elisa mo toŋe-ne se a ta dede‑m we, Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kom nɔn-donno telei mo zege Efrayim zwonnu laŋa kam ne ba yɔɔre ba yi o sɔŋɔ leile konto. O nam lage se n kwei lu-nyenno kilo fintɔ-tenu (

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Ba na yi peo kom yuu mɛ seeni Elisa na zoore to, Gehazi ma jwoŋi zela yam ba jeŋa ne o seigi o tete diga ne, o daare o bane Naaman tontoŋena balei bam pa se ba jwoori ba viiri.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Gehazi ma zo o zege Elisa tei ne. Elisa ma bwei‑o o we, “Gehazi, nmo ya vei yei ne mo?” Gehazi ma leiri o we, “Amo tu, a wo vei jei jei.”

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta ded‑o o we, “Nmo wo lɔre we maŋa kalo Naaman na zege o toroko kom baŋa ne o chu o jeeri‑m to, amo jworo ya wora mo na? Kanto dae maŋa se n jwoŋi sabu, de gwaaro, de Olivi teeni kare, de Vini teeni kadwi, de pei, de nabɛ, de tontoŋena, de ka-nyaana.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kom taga de Elisa ba we, “Dé tu, jeiga kalo debam na zoore ye n nii dé baŋa ne to daa ba daga ka pae debam.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: Konto to, pa debam chwoŋa se dé vo Jɔdan buga kam ni dé beeri jeiga kadwoŋi se dé taa zoore da. Dáane debam maama wó wane dé gwoni dɛ dé ma dé che jei se ko taa daga.” Elisa ma leiri-ba o we, “Véi-na á ke konto.”

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Sampwori sem wone dedoa ma ta de Elisa o we, “Jan ja, tɔge dé kwaga se dé vo.” Elisa ma leiri o we, “Tɔ. Amo wó tɔge a vo.”

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba yi Jɔdan buga kam ni, ye Elisa de tɔge o wora. Ba ma bobo se ba gwoni teeni dem.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa ma bwei‑o o we, “Ko le ko to yei ne mo?” O ma bere‑o ko na to mɛ to. Elisa ma gwoni tio naga o de buga kam wone. O keim dem konto ma pa se dwooru wom puki na bam baŋa ne.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Elisa ma ta de nɔɔno wom o we, “Laare n kwei-ko.” Nɔɔno wom ma tei o jeŋa o le-ko. Elisa chege Siria jar-keira bam

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Maŋa de maŋa Siria teo pɛ déem yeini o kwaare jara de Isarele tiina bam mo. O ma yeini o bane de o nakwa ye o we, “A laga se dé jeeri-ba ywo naa ywo mo.”

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa de déem ma yeini o toŋe ni o pa Isarele pɛ wom we, “Yé zaŋe n twɛ jeiga kam konto, se Siria jar-keira bam mo vei ba gilimi da.”

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: Siria tiina pɛ wom boboŋa déem vugimi de keim dem konto. O ma bwoŋi o dedɛɛra bam ye o bwei-ba o we, “Abam wone wɔ tete mo nwoŋi a kwaga ne se o woli Isarele tiina pɛ wom?”

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Dedɛɛra bam wone dedoa ma leiri o we, “Dé tu, ko dae debam wolowolo mo ke konto. Ko ye Isarele tu Elisa wolo na ye Wɛ sampwora to mo tɛ woŋo maama o bere Isarele tiina pɛ wom. O bere o yei nmo na tɛ kolo maama n diga ne to de.”

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma ta o we, “Véi-na á beeri Elisa jei se a pa nɔɔna vo ba ja‑o.” Ba ma nii ba na‑o ye ba daare ba ta de pɛ wom we, “Elisa wo Dotan ne mo.”

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma toŋe o jar-keira dedɛ, de ba sisei, de ba torokooro se ba vo jeiga kam konto. Tete ne ba ma vo ba yi Dotan, ye ba kaare teo kom ba pu.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Tega na poore tetete to mo Elisa tontoŋeno wom zaŋe o nwoŋi pwooni o na we jar-keira, de ba sisei, de ba torokooro mo kaare teo kom maama ba pu. O ma vo o ta de Elisa o we, “Woo, amo tu, lɛɛro yi debam! Dé nam wó ke tɛ mo?”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma leiri‑o o we, “Yé ta‑n kɔre foone, se balo na wo debam tei ne to daga ba dwoi balo na wo banto tei ne to.”

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Elisa ma lwoori Wɛ o we, “Baŋa Wɛ, puri a tontoŋeno wom yia se o wane o na amo na tɛ kolo to.” Baŋa Wɛ ma seene o puri nɔn-doŋo wom yia pa o nii o na we, sisei kɔgɔ kɔgɔ de torokooro dedɛ na jege min-vogo to mo faare peo kom maama te gilimi Elisa.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Siria jar-keira bam ma fɔɔre ba yi se ba ja Elisa. Elisa ma lwoori Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A lwoori‑m se n pa nɔɔna banto maama yia dwei.” Baŋa Wɛ ma seene o pa se ba yia dwei, ne Elisa na lwoori‑o tei to.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Elisa ma vo ba tei ye o ta-ba o we, “Abam tusi chwoŋa mo á ba teo konto wone. Tɔge-na amo kwaga se a ja abam a vo a bere wolo á na beeri to.” O ma ja-ba o vo Samaria.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ba na yɔɔre ba yi Samaria ba zo teo kom wo to mo Elisa lwoori Wɛ o we, “Baŋa Wɛ, puri nɔɔna banto yia se ba jwoori ba taa nae.” Baŋa Wɛ ma seene o ke konto pa se ba nae. Ba ma na we ba tu ba wo Samaria teo wone mo.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina pɛ wom na nɛ-ba to, o ma bwei Elisa o we, “Amo tu, chwoŋa wora se a go-ba na?”

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma leiri o we, “Aawo! Yé go-ba. Ko ná maŋe ko ye nɔɔna balo nmo na wane jara wone n ja to, n dae se n go-ba. Nam pa-ba wodiu se ba di se ba daare ba nyɔ na. Ba ná ti, se n pa-ba chwoŋa se ba jwoori ba tu wom tei.”

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma ke wodi-fɔrɔ kuri o pa-ba. Siria jar-keira bam na di ba ti to, o ma pa ba viiri. Ba ma jwoori ba vo ba tete pɛ wom tei. Keim dem konto kwaga ne, Siria tiina bam daa maa wo jwoori ba zo Isarele tiina laŋa kam se ba vere ba wonnu ba ja ba viiri. Siria tiina kwaare jara de Samaria teo

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne mo Siria teo pɛ Ben-Hadadi ke o jar-keira kɔgɔ kom maama o ke daane pa se ba vo Samaria ba kwaare jara de Isarele tiina bam.

english_verse: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
translation_verse: Ba ma vo ba kaare Samaria teo kom taa ba pu. Ko ma pa se kana tiini ka zo teo kom. Bonaga yuu kwora déem ye lu-nyenno sabu-dala funɔnɔ mo. Kunkwon-puura beinnu bɔŋa balaŋa maa ye lu-nyenno sabu-dala yanu.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Isarele tiina pɛ wom déem na tɔge teo kom kabira baŋa o maa kɛ to, mo kaane wodwoŋi laare de kwor-dɛa o we, “Jan ja, amo tu, zeini-ne!”

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma leiri‑o o we, “Baŋa Wɛ yerane ná wo zeini‑m, amo laam ke titigiro mo. A jege mena mo naa a jege sana mo?”

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: O ta ma bwei kaane wom o we, “Bɛ mo daane‑m?” Kaane wom ma leiri o we, “Kaane wodwoŋi ya mo taga de amo se a ja a bu a go se dé maama di, se dɛ dedwoŋi ne o de daa ja o bu o go se dé maama di.

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: A ma seene a go a bu wom a daare a saŋe‑o pa se dé maama di. Tega na poore to, a ma ta ded‑o se o de ja o bu wom o go se dé di. Kaane wom ma ve ye kwei o bu wom o seigi.”

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom na nigi kaane wom taane dem to, o ma vaŋe o gwaaro o kaare wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. O ta na dɔge kabira kam yuu ne o vei to, nɔɔna ma kwoni ba nii ba na o gwaaro tem na kaare mɛ seeni ye o zo gare-nyenyaaro te kuri ne to.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma du duuri o we, “Amo ná wo gwoni Safate bu Elisa yuu zem dɛ dem ne, se Wɛ ti a momwɛ.”

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Elisa déem maa jei o sɔŋɔ ne de Isarele teo nakwa ye ba lara. Pɛ wom ma toŋe o tontoŋeno se o vo o bwoŋi‑o. Tontoŋeno wom ta na wo yi to, Elisa ya maŋe o ta de nakwa bam o we, “Á wo nɛ na? Nɔn-goro wonto mo toŋe nɔɔno se o ba o gwoni a yuu. Nii-na, o tontoŋeno wom ná yia, se á ja bworru tem á pe‑o á yage pwooni yiga ne. Ko nam bá dáane ye pɛ wom tete saŋe o kwaga o ba.”

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: Elisa ni wo to tega ne de tontoŋeno wom na yi o tei. Pɛ wom de ma yi ye o we, “Lɛɛro tento maama na tu de baŋa to ye Baŋa Wɛ yiga mo. Amo nam wó cheigi tento a vo a maŋe yein-seeni mo se Baŋa Wɛ laam ba o zeini debam?”

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma leiri o we, “Nam cheigi Baŋa Wɛ kwora. Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Jwa kanto maŋa ne ba wó taa jege mun-bwei bɔŋa ba yeigi mɔle mɔle sabu-dale dedoa mo Samaria yaga ne. Chaara bwɛ selei de wó yeigi sabu-dale dedoa.”

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wolo na tiini o bwola de pɛ wom to ma ta de Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa o we, “Baŋa Wɛ tete ná maŋe o pore wɛyuu kom se doa tiini ka ne mo de, konto bá wane ko ke.” Elisa ma leiri‑o o we, “Nmo tete yi wó na ko na wó seene ko ke tei to. Nmo nam bá da n laŋe wodiu kom.” Siria jar-keira bam na viiri ye ko daare ko ke tei to

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Baara bana déem mo jei Samaria teo manchwoŋo kom ni ne ba na ye naywanno. Ba ma ta ba bere daane ba we, “Debam wó taa jei ywo-seeni se toone ja debam wo bɛ mo?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Dé ná we, ‘Pa-na se dé zo teo kom wo,’ kana wó go debam dáane. Dé nam ná maŋe ywo, de ta wó te mo. Nam pa-na se dé zaŋe dé vo Siria tiina jar-keira bam tei dé sɛ dé pa-ba. Ba wae ba yage debam se dé taa ŋwe. Ko nam ná dae konto, ba wó go debam ye ko ti.”

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Ba ma ta ba bere daane ba we, “Kolo dé na jege dé ke to ba lana. Zem dɛ dem mo dé jege kwor-ywoŋa se dé tɔɔle dé pa nɔɔna maama, ye dé jege dé jei kafɛ yerane. Dé nam ná chem se tega poore, de wó ná waarem ko ŋwaane. Pa-na se dé ke lela dé vo pɛ sɔŋɔ dé ta kolo na ke to.”

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Ba ma jwoori ba vo ba yi teo kom manchwoŋo ni. Ba ma tɔɔle ba bere teo kom ni-yerena bam ba we, “Debam vei Siria jar-keira bam jei sem dé nii, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera. Kolokolo sɔɔ de nam ba dɔna. Ba sisei sem, de ba bonɛ sem na leigi se zege tei to mo se na zega. Ba vwoa yam de maa na zege tei mo ya na zega.”

english_verse: The guards reported the news to the king's palace.
translation_verse: Teo kom ni-yerena bam ma ja kwora kam ba vo ba ta ba bere pɛ sɔŋɔ ne.

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma zaŋe tete dem konto o ta de o tontoŋena bam o we, “Amo wó ta a bere abam Siria tiina bam na boŋe se ba ke kolo to. Ba na yei we kana lage ka go debam to mo ba yage ba vwoa yam ba daare ba vo ba seigi gaao wone. Ba maa boŋe ba we, debam wó nwoŋi dé beeri wodiu dé di. Debam maa ná ke konto, ba laam wó na chwoŋa ba ja debam ŋweene ba daare ba taa tei dé teo kom.”

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: O dedɛɛra bam dedoa ma leiri o we, “Pa nɔɔna kwei sisei sem ta na daare to senu ba vo ba nii keim dento baŋa ne. Banto ná maŋe ba te ko ŋwaane, ko ta ye bedwe mo de balo maama na maŋe teo kom wone ye ba lage ba te to.”

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Ba ma le nɔɔna de torokooro telei de te sisei. Pɛ wom ma toŋe-ba se ba vo ba nii kolo na ke Siria tiina jar-keira bam to.

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma tɔge Siria tiina bam nɛ taa ba vo ba yi Jɔdan buga kam. Ba ma na Siria tiina bam na duri se ba lu ye ba kwei ba gwaaro de ba zela dedɛ ba de ba yage chwoŋa kam yuu ne tei to. Ba laam ma jwoori ba vo pɛ wom tei ba ta ba bere‑o ko na ke tei to.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔɔna bam ma ke lela ba nwoŋi ba vo Siria tiina vwoa yam jei ba pɛ ba zela de ba wodiiru maama. Ba déem ma seene ba jege mun-bwei bɔŋa ba yeigi sabu-dale dedoa dedoa. Chaara bwɛ selei de yeigi sabu-dale dedoa mo. Ko déem yɔɔre ko ke ne Baŋa Wɛ na maŋe o ta tei to mo.

english_verse: Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa ya maŋe o ta o bere pɛ wom o we, “Jwa kanto maŋa ne ba wó taa jege chaara bwɛ selei ba yeigi sabu-dale dedoa mo Samaria yaga ne. Mun-bwei bɔŋa de wó yeigi sabu-dale dedoa.”

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: Pɛ dedɛɛro wom ya wo sɛ ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ tete ná maŋe o pore wɛyuu kom se doa tiini ka ne mo de, konto bá wane ko ke.” Elisa de ya kaane‑o mo o we, “Nmo tete yi wó na ko na wó seene ko ke tei to. Nmo nam bá da n laŋe wodiu kom.”

english_verse: And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_verse: Konto nam mo yɔɔre ko ke‑o. Nɔɔna mo nɔne‑o manchwoŋo kom ni ne pa se o te.

english_verse: Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there,
translation_verse: Wɛ tontoŋeno Elisa déem ma vo Damasika. Siria tiina pɛ Ben-Hadadi maa ba jege yazura. Pɛ wom na maane we Elisa tu to,

english_verse: Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
translation_verse: Hazayeli ma la zela yalo na wo Damasika ne ye te lana to dedɛ o daŋe kona finna baŋa ne o ja o vo se o pa Elisa. O ma zo o zege Elisa yiga ne ye o we, “Nmo bu Ben-Hadadi na ye Siria teo pɛ to mo toŋe-ne se a bwei a nii, o wó wori na?”

english_verse: “Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.”
translation_verse: Elisa ma leiri‑o o we, “Véi n ta ded‑o we, ‘Chega to, n wó wori.’ Baŋa Wɛ nam maŋe o veere o bere-ne we, o wó te mo.”

english_verse: Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
translation_verse: Elisa ma yɔɔre o nii Hazayeli yibia ne zii pa se chaveera ja‑o. Elisa laam ma to keira ne.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Hazayeli ma bwei‑o o we, “Amo tu, bɛŋwaane mo nmo keera?” Elisa ma leiri o we, “Amo yei lɛɛro telo na wó yi Isarele tiina bam nmo ŋwaane to. Nmo wó pa se mini di ba dam jei sem, n daare n go ba nɔn-donno jara wone. Nmo ta wó yigi ba bu-sese n de tega ne n go, ye n daare n lɔ ba kapwi sem ba pwi seeni n go. Konto ŋwaane mo a keera.”

english_verse: “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.” “Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Hazayeli ma leiri o we, “A ye nabwom mo. Amo nyeene dento wó ke tɛ mo a toŋe totoŋ-kamunnu tento dwoŋi?” Elisa ma leiri o we, “Baŋa Wɛ nam veere o bere-ne we, n lage n di Siria teo paare mo.”

english_verse: But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Tega na yɔɔre ka poore to mo Hazayeli kwei gare-jale o de na wone o ma o peene pɛ Ben-Hadadi momwɛ o go. O na ke konto to, o ma lɛɛre o ji pɛ. Judah teo pɛ Jehoram taane

english_verse: So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes.
translation_verse: Jehoram ma ja o jar-keira de ba torokooro tem maama o vo se o li Zayiri teo. Edom tiina bam ma ba ba gilimi o de o nɔɔna bam ba ke tetare ne. Tete ne mo Jehoram de o dedɛɛra bam wane ba lu ba jeŋa ne. O jar-keira bam de ma pipiri ba duri ba jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king.
translation_verse: Jehoram paare dim maŋa ne mo Edom dwi dem ve se ba taa wo Judah pɛ wom dam kuri ne. Ba ma lɛɛre ba tiŋi ba tete pɛ.

english_verse: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah.
translation_verse: Isarele teo pɛ Ahab bu Joram bena yanu paare dim bene dem wone ye Jehosafate ta ye Judah teo pɛ to mo Jehosafate bu Jehoram bobo se o di paare Judah ne.

english_verse: Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Jehoram déem kwei Isarele pwa bam totoŋ-naga mo, nenɛɛne pɛ Ahab de o dwi dem na ke tei to, kokuri to o di Ahab bukɔ mo. Konto to, o déem toŋe lwarem o chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam wo sɛ se o chɔge Judah dwi dem, bɛŋwaane o maŋe o gwoni ni de o tontoŋeno David we, o diga kam wó taa tei paare dem taa wuu.

english_verse: years old when he became king, and he ruled from Jerusalem for only one year. His mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel.
translation_verse: De zem maama Edom tiina ta ve mo se ba taa wo Judah tiina dam kuri ne. Libina teo tiina de déem ke konto dwoŋi mo.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Jehoram déem na di paare ye o ke wonnu telo maama to, de o totoŋa yam maama, ba popone-te ba tiŋi Judah Teo Pwa Seina tɔnɔ kom wone.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Isarele teo pɛ Ahab bu Joram bena fuga-yalei paare dim bene dem ne mo Jehoram bu Ahazia bobo se o di Judah teo paare.

english_verse: Ahaziah went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Ahazia déem dɛ de pɛ Ahab bu Joram mo pa se ba vo Ramofa-Gilead ba kwaare jara de Siria teo pɛ Hazayeli. Siria tiina bam ma ke Joram zonne jara yam wone.

english_verse: One day, Elisha called for one of the other prophets and said: Take this bottle of olive oil and get ready to go to the town of Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Wɛ sampwori Elisa déem le nɔɔno wodwoŋi Wɛ sampwori kɔgɔ kom wone o ta ded‑o o we, “Fɔge n vɔ n gare-kura kiri-kiri n daare n jwoŋi kabɔɔ konto de ko wo nuga kam n ja n vo Ramofa-Gilead.

english_verse: When you get there, find Jehu son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi. Take him to a place where the two of you can be alone,
translation_verse: Nmo ná yi da, se n beeri Jehu wolo na ye Jehosafate bu de Nimisi naa to jeiga. Nmo ná nɛ‑o, se n le‑o o yuudwonna wone n ja n zo diga wo.

english_verse: then pour olive oil on his head to show that he is the new king. Say to him, “The Lord has chosen you to be king of Israel.” Then leave quickly—don't wait around for anything!
translation_verse: Laam kwei nuga kam n lwo Jehu yuu ne n daare ta ded‑o we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: amo laam mo tiŋi‑m se n ji Isarele teo pɛ.’ Nmo ná ke konto n ti, se n pore diga kam n nwoŋi n yage jeiga kam lela n viiri.”

english_verse: The young prophet left for Ramoth.
translation_verse: Nɔn-doŋo kom na ye Elisa tontoŋeno to ma seene o vo Ramofa-Gilead.

english_verse: So Jehu got up and went inside. The prophet poured olive oil on Jehu's head and told him: The Lord God of Israel has this message for you: “I am the Lord, and I have chosen you to be king of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Banto balei ma zo diga kam wo. Nɔn-doŋo kom ma kwei nuga kam o lwo Jehu yuu ne, ye o daare o ta we, “Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: amo laam mo tiŋi‑m se n ji amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam pɛ.

english_verse: I want you to wipe out the family of Ahab, so Jezebel will be punished for killing the prophets and my other servants.
translation_verse: Nmo nam jege se n chɔge n tu Ahab dwi dem mo. Amo wó da konto baŋa ne a waare Jezebele de o na go a sampwori sem de a tontoŋena bam to.

english_verse: His whole family must be destroyed, just like the families of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah.
translation_verse: Amo lage a pa se o dwi dem yɔɔre de chɔge nenɛɛne a na ke Nebat bu Jeroboam dwi dem, de Ahija bu Baasa dwi dem tei to mo.

english_verse: As for Jezebel, her body will be eaten by dogs in the town of Jezreel. There won't be enough left of her to bury.” Then the young prophet opened the door and ran out.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Jezebele, kukuri mo lage se di‑o Jezerele tega kam baŋa ne, ye nɔɔna bá kwei‑o ba suli.” Nɔn-doŋo kom na yɔɔre o ta konto o ti to, mo o pore diga kam o duri o viiri.

english_verse: Jehu went back to his officers, and one of them asked, “What did that crazy prophet want? Is everything all right?” “You know him and how he talks,” Jehu answered.
translation_verse: Jehu na nwoŋi o jwoori o dwonna yiga tiina bam tei to mo ba dedoa bwei‑o o we, “Yazura mo na? Bɛ mo ke ye chichwoo konto ba nmo tei?” Jehu ma leiri o we, “Ko dae kolokolo. Abam maŋe á yei sampwora kanto dwoŋi na yirisi tei to.”

english_verse: “No, we don't. What did he say?” they asked. “He had a message from the Lord,” Jehu replied. “He said that the Lord has chosen me to be the next king of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri ba we, “N fɔe vwa mo! Ta n bere debam o na taga kolo to chekke.” Jehu ma ta o bere-ba nɔn-doŋo kom na tage kolo de kolo to ye o we, “Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo tiŋi nmo mo se n ji Isarele tiina bam pɛ.”

english_verse: They quickly grabbed their coats and spread them out on the steps where Jehu was standing. Someone blew a trumpet, and everyone shouted, “Jehu is king!” Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
translation_verse: Jehu yuudwonna bam maama ma ke lela ba le ba gare-danno ba lware Jehu nɛ sem seeni. Ba ma daare ba wu nabwanno ye ba tɔɔle we, “Jehu mo ye pɛ.”

english_verse: When the guard in the watchtower at Jezreel saw Jehu and his men riding up, he shouted to the king, “I see a large group of men coming this way.” Joram ordered, “Send someone out to ask them if this is a friendly visit.”
translation_verse: Jehu de o nɔɔna bam na twɛ Jezerele teo kom to mo yereno wodwoŋi zege teo kom vɔŋɔ yuu ne o tole o na ba na maa beene. O ma tɔɔle o ta de Joram o we, “Amo nɛ nɔɔna mo na wurigi sisei ba beene.” Pɛ Joram de ma ta o we, “Pa se nɔɔno kwei siseiŋa o vo o yi o bwei o nii ba veiŋa kam ye yazura veiŋa mo na?”

english_verse: One of the soldiers rode out and said to Jehu, “King Joram wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just stay behind me with the rest of my troops!” About the same time the guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ma seene o di siseiŋa baŋa o vo o jeeri Jehu. O ma ta ded‑o o we, “Pɛ Joram bwei se o lɔre, á beene de yazura mo na?” Jehu ma leiri o we, “Nmo yiga mo ka kɔ? Nam pipiri n zo a kwaga kɔgɔ kom wone.” Teo kom yereno wom na tole o na to, o ma bwoŋi pɛ wom o ta ded‑o we, “Wolo n na toŋe to yi da, ye o nam ba jwoora.”

english_verse: So Joram sent out another rider, who rode up to Jehu and said, “The king wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just get behind me with the rest of my troops!”
