translation_verse: Zekaria chorro telo na tɔge ded‑o to mo tento: Semaya, de Azareli, de Milalayi, de Gilalayi, de Maayi, de Netaneli, de Judah, dedaane Hanani. Banto maama déem zei kwɛɛra zela yalo maama Wɛ tontoŋeno David déem na pɛ ni se ba taa ma-ya ba zuli Wɛ to mo. Wɛ nia zamesem tu Ezera déem ma tɔge kɔgɔ kom maama yiga.

english_verse: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
translation_verse: Ba déem ma vo ba yi Buli-yi Ni dem, ye ba yɔɔre ba vo ba dɔɔle ba di David teo kom ne. Ba ta ma vo ba gaale David sɔ-fɔrɔ kom na zege mɛ to, ye ba laam tole ba vo ba yi teo kom wɛ-puli seeni mɛ kabira kam na vei ka tɔ de Na Ni dem to.

english_verse: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
translation_verse: Lein-leena kɔgɔ kodwoŋi kom ma tɔge kabira kam jagwia seeni ba via. Amo de ma tɔge ba kwaga, dedaane nɔɔna bam chichworo. Dé ma vo dé gaale Jugu di-dedɔrɔ kom dé vo dé yi Kabiri-kayɔlɔ kom seeni.

english_verse: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
translation_verse: Lein-leena popɔre selei sem laam ma vo ba zege Wɛ diga kam wone. Amo dedaane yiga tiina bam chichworo de ma vo dé zege da.

english_verse: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
translation_verse: Kaanem tiina banto de déem nam mo tɔge ba zege de amo, ye ba jege nabwanno ba wui: Eliakim, de Maaseya, de Minamina, de Mikaya, de Elio-enayi, de Zekaria, dedaane Hanania.

english_verse: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne, ba ma ke kaanem dedɛ ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. Nɔɔna bam de ma tiini ba di ywoni se ko gaale, Wɛ na pɛ se ba wo pwoli to ŋwaane. Kaana bam de ba bia maama de ma nwoŋi ba tɔge ba di ywoni dem, pa se de sɔɔ kom zaŋe wɛɛne ko yi yiga yiga. Wɛ tontoŋena bam ni-wodiu taane

english_verse: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne ba déem ma kuri nɔɔna se ba taa nii Wɛ diga zela di sem de se wonnu tem baŋa ne. Ba déem yeini ba kwaleme Wɛ teiri dem, de da-yiga mena yam, de da-yiga tio-bia pɛɛra yam, de pɛɛra yalo maama nɔɔna na pɛ Wɛ diga totoŋa yam ŋwaane to mo. Ba maa wó vo Isarele tiina kare sem na wo ba teene dem maama wone to ba jwoŋi wodiiru telo Wɛ nia yam na pɛ chwoŋa se kaanem tiina de Levi tiina bam jwoŋi to. Judah tiina bam maama wo déem tɔge de kaanem tiina bam de Levi tiina bam kikia mo.

english_verse: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
translation_verse: Kolo ŋwaane, banto déem seene yia mo ba toŋe chullu de kwɛɛm totoŋa yam Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ-ba se ba ke to. Lein-leena bam, de Wɛ diga ni-yerena bam de ma toŋe ba totoŋa se ko tɔge de nia yalo Pɛ David de o bu Solomon na bere-ba se ba taa ke to.

english_verse: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
translation_verse: Ko nam na zege Pɛ David dedaane Asaf maŋa kam ne to, mo ba le nɔɔna se ba yeini ba tɔge lein-leena bam yiga se ba taa leeni ba tei Wɛ, ye ba daare ba ke o lei.

english_verse: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_verse: Ko daa ta na yi Zerubabel maŋa kam ne dedaane Nehemia maŋa kam ne to, Isarele tiina bam maa yeini ba kuri ba wodiiru tem wone ba pae lein-leena bam de Wɛ diga ni-yerena bam dɛ maama se ko woli-ba ba totoŋa baŋa ne. Ba ta maa yeini ba le popɔra kalo na maŋe de Levi tiina badaara bam to mo ba pa-ba. Levi tiina de laam maa yeini ba le popɔra kalo na ye kaanem tiina bam nyem to ba pa-ba.

english_verse: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne mo ba gage Wɛ nia tɔnɔ kom Moses na popone to. Ba na cheigi taane dem to mo ba maane we ko chula se Amon tu, de Moaba tu tɔge ba zo Wɛ nɔɔna kɔgɔ kom wone.

english_verse: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam na nigi Wɛ ni dem konto to, mo ba le nɔn-gongwaaga ba wone, se ba daa yé taa zoore de-ba. Nehemia kwɛ nɔɔna bam de ba totoŋa

english_verse: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
translation_verse: Konto maama de Wɛ kaanem tu Eliasibi déem mo nii Wɛ diga zela di sem baŋa ne. O maa me de Amon tu Tobia.

english_verse: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
translation_verse: O ma da ko ŋwaane o kwei Wɛ diga zela di-kamunu o pa Tobia. Ba nam ya yeini ba kwei wodiu pɛɛra, de talwoŋ-ywoŋa, de Wɛ diga zela yam, de Wɛ teiri delo na ye mena, de sana, de Olivi nuga to mo ba zege da. Pɛɛra yam konto maama ye se ba taa kwei-ya ba pae Levi tiina bam, de Wɛ diga lein-leena dedaane ni-yerena bam mo, ko woli de pɛɛra yalo na ye kaanem tiina bam nyem to.

english_verse: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
translation_verse: Konto maama déem na ke to, dedaane amo daa tere Jerusalem wone. A ya jwoori a vo Babilonia se a lwoni kolo na ke to mo a bere Pɛ Atazeregese. Ko maa ye o paare dim bena fintɔ-yalei bene dem ne mo a via. Ko nam na ke fee to mo a daa lwoori chwoŋa o tei ne,

english_verse: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
translation_verse: se a jwoori a vo Jerusalem. A na yi da to, a nɛ we Eliasibi toŋe wo-balɔrɔ ye o yage chwoŋa o pa Tobia se o taa zoore Wɛ diga di sem dedoa wone.

english_verse: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
translation_verse: Keim dem na tiini de fuli a wo to, mo a zo da a kwaleme Tobia zela yam a dole a yage pwooni ne.

english_verse: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
translation_verse: A ta ma lɔre we ba wo pɛ Levi tiina bam wodiiru tem popɔra kalo na ye ba nyem to. Ko déem pɛ se Wɛ diga lein-leena bam, de Levi tiina badaara bam nwoŋi da Jerusalem teo kom ne, ye ba jwoori ba vo ba wo ba kare totoŋa ne.

english_verse: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
translation_verse: Amo ma bwɛ yiga tiina bam lanyerane ye a bwei-ba a we, “Bɛ mo ye á dole Wɛ diga kam totoŋa yam á yage?” A ma pa se Wɛ diga tontoŋena bam jwoori ba toŋe ba totoŋa yam.

english_verse: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
translation_verse: Judah tiina bam daa ma jwoori ba jaane ba Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra maama ba tui ba zege Wɛ diga wone, ko ná ye ba mena popɔra, de ba sana popɔra, de ba nuga popɔra kam.

english_verse: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
translation_verse: Amo laam ma kwei Wɛ diga zela di sem de se totoŋa yam a ke nɔɔna banto jeŋa ne. Ko maa ye Wɛ kaanem tu Selemia, de Wɛ nia zamesem tu Zadoki, de Levi tu Pedaya. A ta le Zakura bu Hanan mo se o taa woli-ba. Nɔɔna maa pae we nɔɔna bam konto jege chega. Ba totoŋa maa ye se ba taa chɛ wodiiru tem ba pa ba dwonna bam.

english_verse: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
translation_verse: Amo Tu Wɛ, nam guli se n ke-ne lanyerane, a na ke wonnu tento maama to ŋwaane. Yé swei amo na tɔge chega a kwɛ nmo diga kam se ka taa jege zula tei to ni ne.

english_verse: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa ne mo a ta maane we Judah tiina badwonna yeini ba toŋe ba totoŋa Wɛ siu dɛ dem wone. Nɔɔna maa kare ba ŋoke Vini tio-bia nyoa. Badwonna maa zeŋe ba bonɛ de wodiiru zela, de teeni bia dwi dwi ba jaane ba zoore Jerusalem teo wo se ba yeiga. Amo ma kaane-ba se ba yé taa di yaga Wɛ siu dɛ dem ne.

english_verse: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Tura tiina badwonna na tu ba zoore Jerusalem teo ne to de ma jaane ywona dedaane zela dwi dwi ba tui ba yeigi ba pae Judah tiina bam Wɛ siu dɛ dem ne.

english_verse: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
translation_verse: A ma bwɛ Judah yiga tiina bam lanyerane ye a we, “Nii-na á na tiini á toŋe lwarem tei! Abam yɔɔre á chɔge Wɛ siu dɛ dem mo pa se de ye kafɛ.

english_verse: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
translation_verse: Á nabaara bam déem maŋe ba ke konto mo, pa se Wɛ ja chɔgem o ba dé teo konto baŋa ne. Abam daa ta ma‑á yɔɔre á ke kolo na wó pa se Wɛ bane zaŋe debam Isarele tiina baŋa ne de woli da to mo, de á na jege o siu dɛ dem á chɔge to.”

english_verse: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: A ma pa ni we wɛ-zoore maŋa ne se ba yeini ba pe teo kom ni bworru tem, se ko maŋe de siu dɛ dem boboa maŋa. A ma ta-ba se ba yé pore-te ba yage ko ná dae siu dɛ dem na ti maŋa kalo to. A déem ta pɛ se a tontoŋena mo zege teo kom bworru ni ne ba yere, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé ja o zela o ba teo kom Wɛ siu dɛ dem ne se o yeigi.

english_verse: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
translation_verse: A laam ma pa Levi tiina bam ni se ba kwɛ ba tete, se ba daare ba vo ba taa zege ba yere teo bworru tem. A ke konto se ko pa se Wɛ siu dɛ dem seene de taa ye de yera mo. A Tu Wɛ, guli amo gula keim dento de ŋwaane. Tɔge nmo swono kom baŋa n duri amo yibwona.

english_verse: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
translation_verse: Ko ma pa se bia balo ba na loge to chichworo jege Asedodi taane ba ŋɔɔna, ye badwonna jege ta-gɛ ba ŋɔɔna. Ba maa ware se ba ŋɔɔne debam Judah tiina taane dem.

english_verse: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: A ma tiini a bwɛ baara bam konto, ye a daare a sɔɔle lwarem a yage ba yuu ne. A ta mage-ba ye a ja ba yu-ywei mo a vaŋe a vuuri. A ma daare a pa se ba ma Wɛ yere ba du duuri ye a we, “Abam daa yé kwei-na á bukwa á pa dwi-gɛ tiina. Nam yé lage-na dwi-gɛ tiina bukwa á pa á tete naa á bia bam se á di.

english_verse: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
translation_verse: Joyada déem ye Wɛ kaanem yiga tu Eliasibi bu mo, ye wonto de bu dedoa laam vo o di Horon tu Sanbalati bukɔ o ma ke o kaane. Amo déem ma zeili‑o se o daa yé taa zoore Jerusalem teo wone.

english_verse: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_verse: Amo ma pa se nɔɔna jaane dɛ ba tui ba tiŋi Wɛ diga kam wone, nenɛɛne maŋa kam ná yeini ka yi se ba ke konto. A ta ma pa se ba jaane da-yiga wodiiru telo na bege to ba tui ba ke da. Amo Tu Wɛ, nam guli amo gula, se n ke-ne lanyerane.

english_verse: King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled
translation_verse: Ka te-fɔrɔ kom maa ye Susa, pɛ wom na di o paare dem ko dam jei sem ne to.

english_verse: provinces from India to Ethiopia.
translation_verse: ) mo, ka zege India ne se ka yi Etiopia.

english_verse: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
translation_verse: O paare dim bena yatɔ maŋa ne mo Zeregese déem ke kuri-fɔrɔ o pa o nakwa, de o teo kom naduna maama. O ta ma bwoŋi Peresia de Media jar-keira babɛ sem, dedaane dedɛɛra balo na nii o laŋa kam popɔre sem to, se ba maama da ba jeeri kuri dem ne.

english_verse: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne mo Pɛ Zeregese ta kwei da yarepɛ o ke kuri-fɔrɔ o pa nɔɔna balo maama na zoore Susa dam jei sem wone to. O ma bwoŋi naduna de nabwona se ba maama jeeri pɛ sɔŋɔ kapworo kom ne, teeni na wora to.

english_verse: The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
translation_verse: Ba déem kwɛ kapworo kom mo dedaane gare-fefale selo nyenyero na ye napwonnu de nazwon-pupwia to. Ywoa yalo ba na mɛ pe-siswollu ba ke to maa wora. Ba laam ma kwei gare-ŋon-nyenno dwi dwi ba ma vɔ gwaaro tem de lu-nyenno kwana se te lei ywoa yam yera ne. Ba ta ma kwei kandwa-nyenno dwi dwi ba ma kwɛ kapworo kom tega kam, ye ba daare ba kwei sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno ba ma fɔge ba kwɛ yitunnu ba tiŋi jei sem ne se nɔɔna jeini te baŋa ne.

english_verse: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
translation_verse: Ba déem jege sabu-seŋa zwe na ye yera yera to mo ba nyɔ sana se wone. Pɛ wom wo-ywoŋo kom ŋwaane o déem pɛ se sana bam daga ba yi nɔɔna bam maama.

english_verse: and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
translation_verse: O ma pa o tontoŋena bam ni se ba taa pae sana se ko tɔge nɔɔno maama na lage tei to.

english_verse: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
translation_verse: Pɛ Zeregese na ke tei de baara bam konto to, o kaane Vasiti de ya jege kuri mo pɛ sɔŋɔ jei sedwonna ne o ke o pae kaana bam.

english_verse: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
translation_verse: Kuri dem da yarepɛ dim dɛ ne, mo pɛ wom wo tiini ko pwoli de sa-nyɔre. O ma bwoŋi o dedɛɛra barepɛ balo na toŋe ba pa‑o to se ba ba o tei. Banto maa ye: Mehuman, de Bizefa, de Harebona, de Bigeta, de Abagata, de Zetare, ko woli de Kakase.

english_verse: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom tontoŋena bam na vei de o ni dem to, Vasiti ma ve se o vo o tei. Pɛ wom bane ma tiini de zaŋe ye o ware o tete se o ja.

english_verse: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
translation_verse: O déem ma ja taane dem o yi swa tiina balo na tiini ba me ded‑o to. Karesena mo konto, de Sefare, de Ademata, de Tarasisi, de Meresi, de Masena, dedaane Memukan. Nɔɔna barepɛ bam konto déem mo ye naduna Peresia dedaane Media laŋa kam ne ba dwoi nɔɔna maama.

english_verse: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
translation_verse: O ma bwei-ba o we, “Amo toŋe a bwoŋi ka-pɛ Vasiti mo ye o ve se o ba. Dé teo chullu tem nam bere se a ke‑o tetɛ mo?”

english_verse: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
translation_verse: Memukan ma leiri Pɛ wom o we, “Ka-pɛ Vasiti na ke o chɔge tei to, o wo ke o ma o twe Pɛ wom yerane. Ko ye debam balo na ye nmo nakwa bam to mo o gwooni, ko woli de balo maama na zoore nmo paare jei sem ni maama ne to.

english_verse: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
translation_verse: O keim dem ná to kaana bam maama zwa ne, ba de daa bá taa nege ba banna ye ba wó ta de-ba we, ‘Pɛ Zeregese tete toŋe o bwoŋi o kaane Vasiti mo ye o ve se o vo o tei.’

english_verse: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
translation_verse: Zem tento, Peresia tiina dedaane Media tiina nakwa bam kaana nigi Vasiti keim dem ŋwa. Ba maa wó bobo se ba taa leiri ba banna yɔɔ yerane. Banegero maa na wó gaale to, ba banna bam bane wó taa zaŋe de-ba mo.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: Pɛ, nmo wo ná dɛ tento, se n pa ni we n daa‑n ba lage se Vasiti yi n yera maŋa de maŋa, se ba daare ba popone-de ba tiŋi Peresia de Media chullu twanno tem ne, se ko yé taa ye kolo na wó leiri maŋa de maŋa to. N ma‑n ta wó ta se wolo na gare‑o to leiri wonto yuu ne o ji nmo ka-pɛ.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Nmo ni dento ná lwoori yiga de yi nmo paare laŋa kam ni maama, kaane maama laam wó lɔre se o taa nege o baro, de kotu ná ye nadum naa nabwom de.”

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: O ma popone twanno o toŋe o pa teene delo maama na wo wonto dam kuri ne to se te bere o ni we, baaro maama taa jege dam o di o diga tiina baŋa ne. Teo maama tɔnɔ kom popone de ba dwi taane, nenɛɛne ba na yeini ba popone-de tei to.

english_verse: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
translation_verse: Ko na wora ko wora to, Pɛ Zeregese bane ma to. O laam ma yɔɔre o boŋe Vasiti na ke tei, dedaane ni delo o na pɛ we, o daa yé taa ye ka-pɛ to.

english_verse: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom nakwa balo na me ded‑o to ma bwɛ ded‑o ba we, “Nmo ná pɛ chwoŋa, dé wó pa se ba beeri bukɔ-pwoli selo na lana ye ba yeiri baara to.

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: Kuri dedɛɛra n paare dim laŋa kam jei maama ne, se n pa-ba ni we ba ja bukɔ-pwoli sento ba ba Susa ne ywo-seeni. Ba maa wó pa se bukwa bam konto zo pɛ sɔŋɔ di selo ba na jege pɛ kaana ŋwaane to, se ba maŋe da. Nmo dedɛɛro Hegayi wolo na nii n kaana to wó taa nii-ba, ye o pa se ba kwei terale nuga ba kwɛ-ba se ba taa lana.

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: Nmo laam ma‑n wó nii bukɔ-laaro tem konto wone, n le wolo na tiini o su n yi to se o ji ka-pɛ o leiri Vasiti yuu ne.” Pɛ wom na maane we boboŋe dem lana to, o ma sɛ-de.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Juu tu dedoa de déem tɔge o zoore Susa dam jei sem ne. O yere ye Modekayi mo. O maa ye Jayira bu, ye o nwoŋi Benjamin dwi dem wone. Kisi dedaane Simeyi de déem ye o nabaara mo.

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza déem na di Judah teo pɛ Jehoyachin, ye o chwooli o de o nɔɔna o le Jerusalem ne o ja vo o tete teo to, Modekayi de déem tɔge o wo ba wone mo.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ni-doore dem ŋwaane, ba déem ma ja bukwa dedɛ ba vo Susa dam jei sem, ye Ɛseta de déem wo ba wone. Ba déem kwei o de ba ke pɛ sɔŋɔ di selo wone Hegayi na nii ba maama baŋa ne to mo.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Ɛseta kikia ma su Hegayi yi, pa o lage o ni taane. Hegayi ma pa se ba taa mae nuga ba turi Ɛseta yera, ye o daare o pa‑o wodi-laao se o di. Hegayi ta kwei‑o o ke sɔ-fɔrɔ kom mɛ na jege zula chekke to ne mo, ye o daare o kuri pɛ sɔŋɔ ka-nyaana barepɛ se ba taa nii o baŋa ne.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Modekayi nam ya maŋe o ta de Ɛseta se o yé pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre we o ye Juu tu, naa ba lɔre o na nwoŋi sɔŋɔ kolo wone to.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Dɛ maama wone, Modekayi déem yeini o kare pɛ kaana di sem konkɔlɔ ni ne mo o kekara. O nam ke konto se o taa yei ko na ye tei Ɛseta yera ne to, dedaane kolo na wó yi‑o to mo.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Bukwa bam lam kwɛɛm yeini de kwei bene mo. Ba mae Mura nuga mo ba wei ba yera yam chane seredo, se ba daa kwei terale nuga ba turi-ba chane seredo. Konto kwaga ne, ba laam wó ja ka-bwona bam mo dedoa dedoa ba zo Pɛ Zeregese tei.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: Ka-bwom wolo ná ye se o nwoŋi kaana bam di sem ne o vo pɛ tete diga kam, kotu wó wane o taa zoore gwaaro telo maama o na lage to.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: Ba nam jege se ba ja ka-bwom wom konto ba vo ba zo pɛ tei mo dedaan-ni maŋa ne. Tega maa ná poore, ba wó ja‑o ba daa vo di sedwonna sem mɛ pɛ kaana badwonna bam na zoore da to mo. Saasegaza nam mo ye dedɛɛro wolo na nii pɛ ka-bi sem konto to. Pɛ wom ná wo mɛ ka-bwom wolo yere o jwoori o bwoŋi‑o, ko bere we o yi wo su kotu. O maa daa bá jwoori pɛ tei.

english_verse: Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
translation_verse: Ko ye Zeregese paare dim bena yarepɛ bene dem wone chane fuga kam ne, mo ba déem jaane Ɛseta ba zo pɛ-sɔŋɔ kom ne se o zo Pɛ Zeregese tei. Chana kam konto yere ye ‘Tebefa’ chana mo.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom boboŋa maa tɔge Ɛseta se ko dwoni ka-bwona babam bam de o kaana bam maama. Ɛseta keim de ma su pɛ wom yi, ye pɛ wom ke‑o zaane. O ma kwei ka-pɛ yipuga kam mo o pu o yuu ne, se o taa ye ka-pɛ o leiri Vasiti yuu ne.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne mo pɛ wom dɛ Ɛseta ŋwaane o ke kuri-fɔrɔ. O ma bwoŋi o teo nakwa, de o dedɛɛra maama se ba jeeri ba di kuri dem. O ta ma pa ni we de dɛ dem ye kuri siu dɛ mo, ye o daare o kwei pɛɛra na maŋe de pɛ to o pa o nɔɔna bam. Modekayi chege pɛ wom toone

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Ka-bwona bam daa na jeeri daane to, dedaane Modekayi yeini o jei pɛ-sɔŋɔ ni ne o toŋe o pa pɛ wom mo.

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Modekayi déem na wo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ni ne o toŋe o totoŋa to, mo dɛ dedwe Bigetana, de Terese bwɛ se ba go pɛ wom, ba na done‑o to ŋwaane. Ba maa ye pɛ sɔŋɔ dedɛɛra balo na yere o di sem to mo.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Modekayi ma ni ko ŋwa ye o vo o ta de Ɛseta. Wonto de ma pa se pɛ wom lɔre Modekayi na tage kolo o bere‑o to.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Ba ma toŋe nɔɔna se ba yɛ taane dem wone ye ba daare ba maane we ko ye chega mo. Ba ma kuuni nɔɔna balei bam konto de ŋone ba go. Pɛ wom ma pa se ba popone keina yam konto ba tiŋi ba teo pwa yera seina twanno tem wone.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Ko na ke fee to, mo Pɛ Zeregese zeiŋi Haman se o ji wolo na saŋe pɛ kwaga o taa nii teo kom to. Haman nam ye Hamedata bu mo, ye o nwoŋi Agagi dwi dem wone.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma pa o dedɛɛra balo na toŋe o sɔŋɔ kom ne to maama ni se ba tiiri tega ne ba ma zuli Haman. Ba maama ma sɛ ba ke konto, ye Modekayi yerane ve se o tiiri o zuli‑o.

english_verse: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
translation_verse: Pɛ dedɛɛra badwonna bam maa yeini ba bwei‑o ba we, “Bɛŋwaane mo n ve pɛ wom ni dem?”

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: Dɛ maama wone, ba maa jege‑o ba nyenyɔna se o de sɛ o tiiri, ye o ba sɛa. O laam ma ta o bere-ba o we, o ye Juu tu mo, ko nam wo maŋe se o tiiri konto dwoŋi. Ba ma vo ba ta o taane dem de Haman, se ba lɔre wonto wó ja keim dem tetɛ.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Haman na lɔre we Modekayi ve se o tiiri o pa‑o to, mo o bane zaŋe.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: O ta na lɔre we Modekayi ye Juu tu to, o ma jeeli we o ná go Modekayi yerane, ko bá zuri o bane. O ma ke o boboŋa ne se o chɔge Juu tiina balo maama na zoore Pɛ Zeregese paare dim laŋa kam ne to.

english_verse: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
translation_verse: Pɛ Zeregese paare dim bena fuga-yalei bene dem wone, de boboa chana kam, ka yere na ye Nisan to wone mo Haman pɛ se ba ta jɔrɔ se o lɔre chana kalo de dɛ delo chekke o na wó wane o ke o boboŋa yam to. Jɔrɔ kom yere mo ‘Pura’. Ko ma le chane fuga-selei chana kam ka yere na ye Adare to mo.

english_verse: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
translation_verse: Haman na lɔre konto to, o laam ma yi pɛ wom tei ye o we, “Nɔɔna badwonna mo jage ba yi nmo paare dim laŋa kam ni maama. Ba dwi dem zoore kateira maama ne mo. Ba chullu nam ye te yera mo de nɔɔna maama chullu. Ko kwaga ne, ba ba tɔge nia yalo debam na pɛ dé teo nɔɔna bam se ba taa tɔge to. Konto ŋwaane, yé sɛ se debam de-ba taa zoore daane.

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Pɛ, nmo nam ná sɛ a boboŋe dem, se n pa ni we ba jege se ba te mo. Konto ná kea, amo wó kwei lu-nyenno dunni na wó yi kilo morro bia yatɔ de finna (

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma sɛ ye o daare o le o jeŋa jafole delo na bere o dam to, o pa Haman. Wonto maa ye Agagi tu Hamedata bu ye o chuli Juu tiina bam.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: Ko ma pa se Haman bwoŋi pɛ wom tɔn-poponna, ye o pa ba popone twanno pɛ wom yere ŋwaane. O ta pɛ se ba popone o ni dem de teo maama dwi taane, nenɛɛne ba na yeini ba popone-de tei to. O laam ma kwei Pɛ Zeregese jafole dem o nye te baŋa ne, ye o we ba ja-te ba vo o paare laŋa kam ni maama ne ba pa pɛ wom yiga tiina, de kateira yam dedɛɛra, de dwi tiina maama nakwa. Haman déem ke konto boboa chana kam da fuga-yatɔ dɛ dem ne mo.

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Balo na ye se ba pa taane dem jage to ma ja ni dem konto ba vo Pɛ Zeregese paare dim laŋa kateira yam maama ne. Ni dem bere we chwoŋa tiga se chane fuga-selei chana kam, ka yere na ye Adare to, da fuga-yatɔ dɛ ne, se ba chɔge Juu tiina maama ba ti dɛ dedwe wone. Ko ná ye ba nɔn-donno, naa nɔn-kwe, naa kaana, naa bu-somwa de, se ba go ba maama, ye ba daare ba vere ba jejegero ba ja ba viiri.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ni dem ma pa se balo na pae taane dem jage to duri lela ba vo ba yi jei maama. Ba ta ma tɔɔle taane dem Susa dam jei sem wone. Pɛ wom dedaane Haman maa jei ba jege sana ba nyɔa. Susa teo kom nɔɔna maama boboŋa nam vugimi.

english_verse: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
translation_verse: Modekayi na maane kolo maama na ke to, o ma kaare o gwaaro, o wo na chɔge to ŋwaane. O ma zo gare-nyenyaaro, ye o daare o puki o yuu maama dedaane tentwarem. O ma nwoŋi o kare teo kom maama wone o via ye o laare de kwor-dɛa baŋa baŋa.

english_verse: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
translation_verse: O ke konto mo o vo o yi Pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo ni dem, ye o wo zo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wone, ko na chula se nɔɔna zo gare-nyenyaaro ba zo dáane to ŋwaane.

english_verse: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ni dem na yi mɛ de mɛ o paare laŋa kateira yam maama wone to, Juu tiina bam yɔɔre ba laare bugi-bugi mo. Ba maa vɔ ni, ye ba keera, ye ba ta chwoosa. Ba dedɛ ma zo gare-nyenyaaro, ye ba daare ba jei tentwarem wone.

english_verse: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
translation_verse: Ka-nyaana dedaane tontoŋena balo na nii Ɛseta to ma na Modekayi na ke kolo to, ye ba ta ba bere Ɛseta. Ko ma tiini ko daane‑o. O ma toŋe gwaaro o pa Modekayi se o leiri o gare-nyenyaaro tem se o daare o zo-te. O maa wo sɛ.

english_verse: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
translation_verse: Tontoŋena balo pɛ wom na le se ba taa nii Ɛseta to dedoa yere ye Hatake mo. Ɛseta laam ma toŋe‑o Modekayi tei ne se o bwei o lɔre kolo na daane‑o to.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Hatake ma nwoŋi o vo Modekayi tei, ye o wo teo kom kapworo kom ne, ko na jeeri de pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo to.

english_verse: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
translation_verse: Modekayi de ma ta o bere‑o kolo maama na yi‑o to, dedaane Haman na gwoni ni se o tiŋi sabu-fɔrɔ teo kom kwɛɛm ŋwaane, ne o ná nɛ chwoŋa se o pa Juu tiina maama na chɔgem.

english_verse: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
translation_verse: O laam ma daare o kwei tɔnɔ kolo na pɛ nɔɔna ni se ba chɔge Juu tiina bam ye ba tɔɔle ko taane Susa ne to o bere Hatake. O ma kwei ko dwoŋi o pa‑o se o ja o vo o pa Ɛseta. O ta tage‑o mo se o maŋe tɔnɔ kom wo wonnu tem o bere Ɛseta, se o daare o ta‑o we, o véi pɛ wom tei o lwoori‑o se o duri Juu tiina bam yibwona.

english_verse: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
translation_verse: Hatake ma seene o vo Ɛseta tei o bere‑o kolo Modekayi na tage to.

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
translation_verse: ko zege pɛ nakwa ne, se ko yi nɔn-bia bam na wo kateira yam maama wone to, nɔɔno maama yei we chwoŋa tera se nɔɔno zo pɛ wom tei ye o wo bwoŋi‑o. Ba ta yei we wolo ná zo da ye pɛ wo bwoŋi‑o, ba jege se ba go konto tu mo. Debam teo kom wadaa mo konto. Ko nam ye pɛ ná zeiŋi o sabu-seŋa nacheiga kam o jeeri kotu, mo ba bá go‑o. Chana mo tento nam, pɛ na wo toŋe o bwoŋi-ne.”

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Modekayi na nigi Ɛseta kwora kam to,

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: o ma toŋe o ta‑o o we: “Yé ta‑n boŋe we, n na wo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom wone to ŋwaane, nmo yerane wó ta‑n ye Juu tu se n lu.

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: Nmo ná maŋe da chemm maŋa kanto, nam lɔre se wolim wó nwoŋi jei sedwonna ne de ba Juu tiina bam ŋwaane, se ba na verem. Nmo nam wó te, ye n kwo sɔŋɔ kom de ti. Dé nam yeiri dé tia. Dɛ dedwoŋi ne ko zege ko ye maŋa kanto kikia yam ŋwaane mo n tu n ji ka-pɛ!”

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Ɛseta laam ma leiri Modekayi o we:

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: “Véi n la Juu tiina bam maama na wo Susa ne to n ke daane. Vɔ-na ni se á lwoori Wɛ á pa-ne. Yé di-na wodiu, nam yé nyɔ-na na da yatɔ, wea dedaane tete maama. Amo de a ka-nyaana bam de wó ke konto. Dé ná ti, amo laam wó zo pɛ wom tei, de ko na maŋe ko chula to de. Ko ná ye se a te ko ŋwaane, a sɛ se a te!”

english_verse: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
translation_verse: Ɛseta ni-vɔre dem da yatɔ dɛ dem ne, mo o zo o paare gwaaro tem o laam vo o zo pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne o zege da. Jei sem konto jeeri de paare diga kam. Pɛ Zeregese déem jei o paare yituŋu kom baŋa ne mo o nii diga kam ni dem seeni.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: O ma na we Ɛseta zege konkɔlɔ kom ne. O wo ma pwoli ded‑o ye o tei o sabu-seŋa nacheiga kam o jeeri‑o se o ma zaane‑o. O de ma fɔɔre o yi o tei, ye o dwei ka nabili dem seeni.

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma bwei‑o o we, “Ɛseta, bɛ mo daane‑m? Ta n bere-ne kolo n na lage to, se ko ná maŋe ko ye a paare dim laŋa kam chichworo de, amo wó kwei-ka a pa‑m.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Ɛseta ma leiri‑o o we, “Pɛ, laŋa ná daare, se nmo dedaane Haman ba amo tei zem se dé di daane. A lage a vo a ti wodi-fɔrɔ yiga abam ŋwaane mo.”

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma pa ni se ba ke lela ba bwoŋi Haman se ba vo Ɛseta tei ba di, ne o na tage tei to. Ba ma seene ba vo.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ba na di ba ti ye ba nyɔ sana to, pɛ wom ma bwei Ɛseta o we, “Ta n bere-ne n na lage se a ke kolo to, se amo wó ke a pa‑m, ko ná maŋe ko ye a laŋa kam chichworo de.”

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: Nmo yi ná sui a kikia yam ye n wo ná dɛ se n ke kolo a na lage to, se nmo de Haman jwa daa jwoori ywo-seeni. Amo ta wó ke wodi-fɔrɔ se abam ba á di. Kanto maŋa ne, a laam wó ta kolo a na lage to a bere‑m.” Haman bane zaŋe de Modekayi

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne, Haman na nwoŋi ka-pɛ Ɛseta tei ye o maa viiri to, o wo yɔɔre ko tiini ko pwoli mo. Ko daare, o na nwoŋi pɛ sɔŋɔ manchwoŋo kom ni ne o maa kɛ to, mo o nɛ Modekayi. Wonto maa wo zaŋe wɛɛne, o nam wo kɔre foone de Haman. Konto ŋwaane Haman bane tiini de zaŋe o baŋa ne.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: De ko de, o déem peene o bane mo ye o viiri. O na yi sɔŋɔ to, o ma bwoŋi o badwonna se ba ba o sɔŋɔ, ye o bwoŋi o kaane Zerese o woli da.

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: O laam ma ŋɔɔne o bere o tete de o jejegero, de o bu-baara na daga tei, de pɛ na zeiŋi wonto se o saŋe o kwaga pa se teo kom nakwa de naduna maama jege se ba taa kɔre‑o tei to.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Haman laam ma ta o woli da o we, “Kolo na tiini ko dwoi maama to mo ye ka-pɛ Ɛseta na ke wodi-fɔrɔ se pɛ wom ba o di to, amo yerane mo o bwoŋi se a da a vo. O daa ma ta o we dé ta jwoori jwa ne se dé daa di daane.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”

translation_verse: N nam ná twe n jeŋa pa se kolo maama o na jege to ti ko daare‑o, o laam wó yɔɔre o lwɛ nmo jaja.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Setaana pɛ o we, “Tɔ! A kwei o jeŋa woŋo maama a ke nmo dam kuri ne. Nam yé ke o tete yera yam kolokolo.” Setaana pɛ ma yage Baŋa Wɛ tei ye o viiri.

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,

translation_verse: O ta na wora o tɛ taane dem o bere‑o to mo nɔɔno wodwoŋi de yia. O de ma ta de Job o we, “Doa mo nwoŋi wɛyuu ne ka ba ka bage n pei sem de n tontoŋena bam maama ka go. Amo yerane mo wane a lu se a ba a ta kolo na ke to a bere‑m.”

translation_verse: O ta na wora o tɛ taane dem to mo nɔɔno wodwoŋi de yia. O de ma ta de Job o we, “N bia bam ya wo n bu-kwea kam sɔŋɔ ne mo ba di kuri-fɔrɔ, ye ba nyɔ sana.

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Vo-fɔrɔ ma pɔpɔ ko nwoŋi kagoa kam seeni ko ba de dam, ye ko mage sɔŋɔ kom sɛ sem maama pa ko to ko pane ba maama ko go. Amo yerane mo wane a lu se a ba a ta kolo na ke to a bere‑m.”

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Job na nigi konto maama to, o ma zaŋe o zege wɛɛne o ja o gɔrɔ o kaare wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. O ma cheeri o yuu ye o daare o vwi o yibia tega ne o zuli Wɛ.

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: De kolo maama na ke to de, Job wo ke wɛleere. O nam wo poone Wɛ we o tusi.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma bwei Setaana pɛ o we, “Nmo zege yei ne mo n ba ywo?” Setaana pɛ de ma leiri Baŋa Wɛ o we, “A yɔɔre a kare tega kam baŋa ne mo a kekara.”

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ma ta o we, “N nam maane n nii a tontoŋeno Job na ye tei to na? Tega baŋa nɔɔna maama wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na ye nɔn-ŋom ne wonto na ye tei to. english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Setaana pɛ ma leiri o we, “Nɔɔno ya-nɔna jege kuri ya pa‑o! Konto tu wó kwei o woŋo maama o dole o yage se o wane o jwoŋi o ŋwea.

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: N nam ná twe n jeŋa n pa o na zonne o yera yam wone, o laam wó yɔɔre o lwɛ‑m jaja.”

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de Setaana pɛ o we, “Tɔ! A kwei o maama a ke n dam kuri ne. Nam yé le o ŋwea kam.”

english_verse: Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery,
translation_verse: Job maa jei tampuuri teiŋa ne wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. O ma kwei kanchua o jege o zae o yera yam.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: O kaane ma yi o tei ye o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo ta zege de n chega mo na? Nam yɔɔre n lwɛ Wɛ, se n ná wó te se n te.”

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Job ma leiri‑o o we, “Ja n jworim dem n lage jei! Wɛ ná pɛ debam wo-laaro, dé bá tei je selei mo dé jwoŋi-te na? Bɛŋwaane mo o ná toŋe lɛɛro o pa debam, se dé ve?” De Job na zo cham dem maama wone to de, o wo ke wɛleere o ni taane baŋa ne. Job badwonna batɔ bam yera taane

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Job déem jege badwonna batɔ, ba na ye Teman tu Elifaza, de Suuhi tu Bilidad, de Naamatia tu Zofara. Ba ma ni lɛɛro telo na yi Job to ni ne. Ba ma zaŋe ba sam ne ba tɔge daane de ni dedwe se ba vo ba ŋwane ba pa Job, se ba daare ba zuri o bochare.

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Ba ta na vei ba beene o tei ye ba tole ba na‑o to, ba wo lɔre‑o lela. Ba laam ma bobo se ba laare de kwor-dɛa. Ba ma kaare ba gwaaro tem, ye ba daare ba kwei kasolo ba taare ba yuni tem, ba wo na tiini ko chɔge to ŋwaane.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Ba ma fɔɔre ba yi o yera ba jeini tega ne, da yarepɛ wea de tete maama. Ba wolowolo wo wane se o ta taane ded‑o, ba na nɛ o na tiini o yaare to ŋwaane.

english_verse: by saying to God:
translation_verse: O ma ta o we,

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: “A lora dɛ dem ya na jigi kafɛ, ko gara. Tete delo wone ba na tage we ba loge bakeira to, de taa ye kafɛ!

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Yé sɛ se kaane daa ja puga tete dem konto ne. Ko dae se nɔɔna bage wopwolo sɔɔ ko wone.

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: Kokuri to, dɛ dem konto wo pɛ se a nu puga kam kwaale-ne ka yage da. Konto ya wó pa se a yé taa nii a nae cham dento.

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: A ya ná tega a lora maŋa ne mo tento, a zem ya ba tigi churu ne a sii na?

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: Ko déem ná ke ne ba loge-ne ba de bu-too mo, ko gara. Ba ya wó suli-ne tega ne, ne bu-seseŋa kalo na wo nɛ logo pwooni to dwoŋi.

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Churu ne, puseŋ-nyena yeini ba sii de ba lwia yam. Balo yera ya na chɛ to de laam sii mo falalala.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Nɔɔna maama wo dáane mo, nabwona de naduna. Kabɛ de yɔɔre se tei se tete mo jei sem konto ne.

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: Ba ŋwea nam ná tu ka ti pa se ba suli-ba tega kuri ne, ba laam wó di ywoni lanyerane mo.

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: Ko ná ye nɔɔno wolo Wɛ na chege o chwoŋa pa se o yeiri o na wó vo mɛ to, bɛ mo ye Wɛ pa se kotu daa taa jege ŋwea?

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman said:
translation_verse: Teman tu Elifaza ma leiri Job o we:

english_verse: Please be patient and listen to what I have to say. *
translation_verse: “Nɔɔno ná tage taane dede‑m, n bá‑n zuri n yera na? Amo nam daa ware se a taa ye chemm.

english_verse: In my experience, only those who plant seeds of evil harvest trouble,
translation_verse: Amo na maane tei to, balo na dugi lwarem naa cham to wó zage-te mo.

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Wɛ ná sii o yage ba yera ne, ba wó chɔge ba ti mo.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Nywonnu mo yeini te suuri ye te ŋuuri de dam. De ko de, Wɛ mo pae nywon-kamuna yeila gura.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: Ba daane ba waase taane ba bere-ne, pa se a wo nigi-de a ti.

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: Dɔɔne ya tiini de jege-ne tete ne, ye a dwɛ dendwa yalo na daane-ne to.

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Ko ke ne vio mo dole a yibia seeni, pa se waaro da te zo-ne foone ŋwaane.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Ko laam ma zege da chemm. A maa wo lɔre ko na ye woŋo kolo to. Ko nyenyego wo a yiga ne mo, ye a ni kwora na waase ka we:

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: Nabiina nam ye dɔgɔ mo Wɛ mɛ o ke ba yera yam, ye ba kuri nwoŋi teero wone. Banto yɔɔre ba bwona ba dwoi tóa na ye tei to mo.

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Ba maa vaŋe kotu wonnu maama ba le ba daare‑o. O laam ma ba o te ye o wo nɛ yi-poro.’ ”

english_verse: Job, call out for help and see if an angel comes!
translation_verse: “Chwoosi n bwoŋi n nii nɔɔno wó ba na? Malese sem wone wɔ mo wó ba o woli‑m?

english_verse: Envy and jealousy will kill a stupid fool.
translation_verse: Ban-wira goe jworru mo lela, ye kazwe de chɔge nayeiri-nyena.

english_verse: I have seen fools take root. But God sends a curse, suddenly uprooting them
translation_verse: Amo yi nɛ jworru kugu na jaane tega chekke, ye lɛɛro laam yi-ba lela, de ba sɔŋɔ kom maama.

english_verse: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
translation_verse: Wonto mo pa se doa nene tega baŋa ne, se na wane ba bugi pwola ni maama.

english_verse: Darkness is their only companion, hiding their path at noon.
translation_verse: Lim mo kwoli-ba wea tetare ne, ye ba kare we-bere maŋa ne ba taana ne lilwoa to.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Wɛ jwoŋi nabwona mo o yaga de dedɛɛra ta-balwaaro tem na chɔge-ba tei to. O maa vere-ba o jaane o nwoŋa balo na bɛɛse-ba to jeŋa ne.

english_verse: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
translation_verse: Ko maa pae yiniga tiina jege teena, ye balo na kweele chega kam to laam pu ba nia.

translation_verse: Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom na korese wolo to jege yu-ywoŋo. Konto ŋwaane yé gwooni o koresem dem.

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: Kokuri, o yeini o ke zonne nɔɔna yera ne. O nam wó vɔ ba fufwollu tem. O maa ná de cham nɔɔno wolo yera ne, o je sem ta wó yɔɔre kotu.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: Lɛɛro ná yi nmo kuni beredo, Wɛ wó taa kwoli‑m. Cham ná maŋe de ye tei maama de daŋe da-baŋa ne, de bá di‑m.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: Chega to, chɔgem de kana ná yia, nmo wó ta‑n jege-te n gwoona mo. Ko ta ná ye kago-vara de, ko dae se n ta‑n kɔre foone de-ba.

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: Ko na ye tei to, nmo wó ke ni-mɔrɔ dedaane kandwa yalo na tigi n kara kam wone to. Kago-vara de nam bá taa daane‑m.

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Nmo wó lɔre we n bia kɔgɔ lage ko gaale, ye n naaro de puli mo, ne tega baŋa gaaro tem na ye tei to.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Nmo ŋwea maa wó dáane tega baŋa ne. N ta wó ta‑n dana mo se n vo n te, ne mena na yeini ya be ye ba laam zage-ya tei to.

english_verse: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
translation_verse: te ya wó dwoni naneo ni kasolo kom maama na mae tei to. Konto ŋwaane mo nam pɛ se a lɔgere a ŋɔɔne yɔɔ yɔɔ.

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Wodiu kolo na ba jege yɛ to zoore ni na? Chechare napwoŋo jei sem ywoni nam wo yein-seeni mo?

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: Wodiu ná ye konto dwoŋi a ware-ko se a di. Ko yɔɔre ko lwoi a momwa ne mo.

english_verse: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
translation_verse: A dam ti ye a daa ware a tete se a jwoŋi a yage. A ya na teege mɛ maama to kɛ ko daare-ne.

english_verse: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
translation_verse: Nɔɔno teena ná ti, o badwonna ta maŋe se ba ta taa swoi‑o mo, de o ná maŋe o yage Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ kɔrɔ kom de.

english_verse: like streams that swell with melting snow,
translation_verse: Yadɛ ne se maa yeini se su, ye kunu de kwoli-se.

english_verse: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
translation_verse: Nam nii-na! Abam de maŋe á ba sii zore. Á na yɔɔre á na chanɛɛre delo na yi amo to, mo foone tiini de ja abam.

english_verse: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
translation_verse: Nam ta-na á bere-ne mɛ seeni a na tusi to, se a pu a ni ye a daa bá ta taane.

english_verse: The truth is always painful, but your arguments prove nothing.
translation_verse: Chega jei ye ŋɔn-zane mo, se á bwɛa yam nam lage ya woli tetɛ seeni mo?

english_verse: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
translation_verse: Nam pipiri-na á nii amo seeni! Kokuri, amo bá gane abam.

english_verse: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
translation_verse: Vwa mo a jege a fɔe na? Lɛɛro yi-ne ye a wo wane-te a lɔre na?”

english_verse: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
translation_verse: Kabaa yɔɔre o teena se wɛ dem guni ye tega yi. Tontoŋeno de maa jei o teena se o jwoŋi o ŋweero.

english_verse: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
translation_verse: Amo yera maama nwoŋi kanzwa mo, ye ya su de ŋɔna yalo na kuuri to. Mwara de maa nwoŋa.

english_verse: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
translation_verse: Amo ŋwea da yam wora ya ti mo lela, ne gare-yi doleno na dole o gare-yi tei lela lela to. Ya maa wó yi ya kweelim jei ye teena tera ya pa-ne.

english_verse: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
translation_verse: Amo Tu Wɛ, popo guli amo ŋwea kam gula ne ka na lage ka jei lela ne vio tei to. Amo maa da bá fɔge a na ŋwea ywoni.

english_verse: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Chega to, yia yalo zem na nae amo to daa bá na-ne. Nmo tete de wó beeri amo jei n ga mo, a na tera to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
translation_verse: Nmo wolo na yere nabiina to, amo ná maŋe a ke wɛleere mo de, konto lage ko ke‑m bɛ mo? Bɛŋwaane mo n yɔɔre n jeeri amo se n zɔ-ne konto? Amo nam jigi zele-zane delo na daane‑m to mo na?

english_verse: Bildad from Shuah said:
translation_verse: Suuhi tu Bilidad ma leiri o we:

english_verse: and start living right? Then he will decide to rescue and restore you to your place of honor.
translation_verse: Nmo ná ke konto, ye n ná yɔɔre n ke n tɔge chwoŋa, Wɛ wó zaŋe se o jaŋe o pa‑m, ye o pa n sɔŋɔ kom jwoori ko zege de chega.

english_verse: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
translation_verse: Nmo jwa wó ba n duni dedɛ, se ko dwoni n faŋa kam na ye tei to.

english_verse: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
translation_verse: Debam ŋwea ye kukua mo ye dé yeiri kolokolo. Dé ŋwea da yam ba dáane ye ya jia, ne lunluŋu na ye tei to.

english_verse: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
translation_verse: Na ná tera, te wó kwaare lela mo ye te ta wo bege, se ko dwoni ga-lɛɛro na wó kwaare tei to.

english_verse: their life slips away, and other plants grow there.
translation_verse: Gaaro tem konto maa wó ko te te, se gaaro tedwonna de daa puli tega kam konto ne.

english_verse: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
translation_verse: Wɛ bá fɔge o ve chega tu wolo na ba jege tusim to. O nam bá ja nɔn-balɔrɔ jeŋa se o woli‑o.

english_verse: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
translation_verse: O daa wó pa se n ni su de mwanno, se n di ywoni ye n bage wopwolo sɔɔ.

english_verse: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye balo na chuli‑m to, chaveera mo lage ya di-ba. Puseŋ-nyena sam dem de wó to de saare.”

english_verse: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
translation_verse: “Chega ŋwaane to, nmo na tage kolo to ba jege digiru. Nabiinu nam wó ke tetɛ mo se o na chega Wɛ yiga ne?

english_verse: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
translation_verse: Nabiinu ná boŋe se o saŋe Wɛ, Wɛ wó wane o bwei‑o kuni moro mo, se kotu yé wane o leiri‑o kuni dedoa tete de.

english_verse: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
translation_verse: Wonto swa yam mo gaale, ye o dam dem ba tia! Wɔ mo wó wane o dwoni de Wɛ ye o bá to?

english_verse: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
translation_verse: Wɛ yeini o pɔpɔ o guri peero! O ma daare o tɔge o bane baŋa ne o vuvugi-te o dole o yage.

english_verse: God can shake the earth loose from its foundations
translation_verse: O ta wae o ziziŋi tega kam baŋa maama pa ka na chwi mɛ to de bibigi.

english_verse: and set the stars in place— the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the stars in the southern sky.
translation_verse: O ma ke chalechwe sem yera yera o tigisi wɛyuu kom ne. O ta ma pa se tega-kuri seeni chalechwe sem wora.

english_verse: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
translation_verse: Wɛ bane ná zaŋe, de ba gwia. Naneo wo juru Rahaba de ko kwaga kɔgɔ kom maama mo o chochoge o nɛ kuri ne.

english_verse: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
translation_verse: Konto to, amo nam wó wane a leiri Wɛ taane dem na? Amo lage a kuri botare bia tetɛ mo se a leiri‑o?

english_verse: He would strike me with a storm and increase my injuries for no reason at all.
translation_verse: O nam wó kwei vo-fɔrɔ o ma o mage-ne o chochoge, ye o pa se a fufwollu tem de puli kafɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: God is much stronger than I am, and who would call me into court to give me justice?
translation_verse: Ko ná ye dam taane mo dé tɛa, Wɛ dam ba tia. Ko nam ná ye ka-di-bora taane mo, wɔ mo wó wane o saŋe Wɛ?

english_verse: I am not guilty, but I no longer care what happens to me.
translation_verse: Amo seene a wo tusi o yiga ne. A yiga nam tera de kolo na wó yi-ne to. A ŋwea kam ye wo-yɔɔ mo ko pa-ne.

english_verse: When a good person dies a sudden death, God sits back and laughs.
translation_verse: Lɛɛro ná yi nɔɔna pa se ba pɔpɔ ba te, Wɛ jei o nii balo na jege chega to mo ye o mɔne-ba.

english_verse: And who else but God blindfolds the judges, then lets the wicked take over the earth? My Life Is Speeding By
translation_verse: Puseŋ-nyena mo vere tega baŋa ba jege ba tei. Wɛ laam ma yeini o kwoli balo na jege taana ba di to yia pa ba kweele chega kam. Ko ná dae Wɛ mo ke konto, wɔ mo kea?

english_verse: but my sufferings frighten me, because I know that God still considers me guilty.
translation_verse: a yaara yam daa ta pa-ne foone mo, kokuri amo yei we n bá‑n ta we, a jege bora.

english_verse: God would throw me into a pit of stinking slime, leaving me disgusting to my clothes.
translation_verse: n ta wó kwei-ne mo n de gwoŋo kolo na su de digiru to wone. A yera digiru tem wó pa se a tete yera gwaaro tem chɛɛse-ne mo.

english_verse: Then I could speak up without fear of him, but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_verse: Amo ya wó na chwoŋa se a ŋɔɔne jaja ye foone tera. Ko nam na ye tei to, a bá wane konto a ke.”

english_verse: I am sick of life! And from my deep despair, I complain to you, my God.
translation_verse: “Amo chuli ŋwea kalo a na jege a ŋwe to. Konto ŋwaane mo a wó taa poona jaja, ye a yɔɔre a tɛ kolo na daane-ne to.

english_verse: Do you look at things the way we humans do?
translation_verse: N yeini n nii n nae wonnu ne nabiina na nae-te tei to mo na?

english_verse: You know I am innocent, but who can defend me against you?
translation_verse: Nmo nam yei we a jege bora. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera o na wó wane o jwoŋi-ne o yage nmo jeŋa ne.

english_verse: Remember that you molded me like a piece of clay. So don't turn me back into dust once again.
translation_verse: Guli we n naane-ne ne dɔgɔ mo tei. Nmo nam lage n pa se a jwoori a ji teero mo na?

english_verse: Then you tied my bones together with muscles and covered them with flesh and skin.
translation_verse: Nmo laam ma‑n kwei ya-tana de ya-nɔna n daŋe da, ye n pa se ŋwanno de kwi twoŋi daane a yera yam ne.

english_verse: You, the source of my life, showered me with kindness and watched over me. You Have Not Explained
translation_verse: Konto baŋa ne mo n pɛ se a na ŋwea, ye n ta duri a yibwona. N ma‑n yɔɔre n yere-ne se a ŋwea ke dam.

english_verse: but you catch and punish me each time I sin.
translation_verse: Nmo boŋe se n yɔɔre n nii amo, se a ná tusi, se n waare-ne a wɛleera yam ŋwaane.

english_verse: Why did you let me be born? I would rather have died before birth
translation_verse: Bɛŋwaane mo n pɛ chwoŋa se a nu lo-ne? A ya ná tege lela ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo nɛ-ne, konto ya bere ko gara.

english_verse: I have only a few days left. Why don't you leave me alone? Let me find some relief, *
translation_verse: A ŋwea da yam daa ba daga. Ja, yage a yera se a wane a sii fenfee de wopwolo,

english_verse: Zophar from Naamah said:
translation_verse: Naamatia tu Zofara de ma leiri o we:

english_verse: Your words have silenced others and made them ashamed; now it is only right for you to be put to shame.
translation_verse: Job, nmo boŋe we ta-yɔɔro telo n na jege n ŋɔɔne to wó pa dé pu dé nia mo na? Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá zaŋe o bwɛ‑m, de n na jege nɔɔna n mɔna tei to na?

english_verse: You claim to be innocent and argue that your beliefs are acceptable to God.
translation_verse: N tage we, n bera yam lana fase mo, ye n tete de kikia tɔge chwoŋa Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: and let you know that wisdom has many different sides. You would then discover that God has punished you less than you deserve.
translation_verse: O ya wó bere‑m yi-poro kolo na seigi n tei ne to. Kokuri swa yalo na ye chekke to chwei sem ye yera yera mo. Nam lɔre we Wɛ wo waare‑m se ko maŋe de n wɛleera yam ni na mae tei to.

english_verse: They are higher than the heavens and deeper than the grave. So what can you do when you know so little,
translation_verse: Ya diini wɛ-baŋa se ko dwoni wɛyuu kom na ye tei to. Nmo nam wó ke bɛ mo ko wone? Ya ta luuna se ko dwoni churu na luuna tei to. Nmo wó ke tetɛ mo se n lɔre-ya?

english_verse: If God puts you in prison or drags you to court, what can you do?
translation_verse: O nam ná tu se o ja wolo o pe, naa se o saŋe wolo taane dim baŋa ne, wɔ mo wó wane o yiga o che?

english_verse: God has the wisdom to know when someone is worthless and sinful,
translation_verse: O wae o lɔre balo na ye nɔn-yɔɔro to. O ná nɛ lwarem kikia, o bá maane ya ni ne na?

english_verse: but it's easier to tame a wild donkey than to make a fool wise. Surrender Your Heart to God
translation_verse: Kagoa wo bonaga wó wane ka lo nabiinu, ye nɔn-jworo ta wo wane o ja swa.

english_verse: You will rest safe and secure, filled with hope and emptied of worry.
translation_verse: Nmo wó ta‑n jege baare, n teena na wó taa daga to ŋwaane. Kolokolo bá daane‑m. N ma‑n wó sii ye lwia tera.

english_verse: But those who are evil will go blind and lose their way. Their only escape is death!
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye puseŋ-nyena bam, ba yia wó dwei mo ye ba bá na chwoŋa se ba lu. Ba teena maa wó taa wo toone wone se de ja-ba.”

english_verse: Job said to his friends:
translation_verse: Job daa ta ma leiri o we:

english_verse: You think you are so great, with all the answers.
translation_verse: “Abam boŋe we á dwoi nɔɔna maama mo, ye á ná tega, yeino wó tɔge de abam ko te mo!

english_verse: Robbers and other godless people live safely at home and say, “God is in our hands!” If You Want To Learn
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye venverena, ba sam yɔɔre de zega de dam mo. Kolokolo ba yi balo na dwoni de Wɛ to de. Ba nam teena we ba tete dam mo ye ba wɛ.

english_verse: If you want to learn, then go and ask the wild animals and the birds,
translation_verse: Nam bwei-na vara bam, de wɛyuu zuna bam, se ba wó ta chega ba bere abam.

english_verse: Any of them can tell you what the Lord has done.
translation_verse: Wonnu tem konto maama yei we, ko ye Baŋa Wɛ dam dem mo ke konto.

english_verse: We hear with our ears, taste with our tongues,
translation_verse: Nabiina zwa cheigi taana se ba lɔre mo, ne ba dindeilima na yeini ya laŋe wodiiru tei to.

english_verse: and gain some wisdom from those who have lived a long time.
translation_verse: Kokweero pae nɔɔna jaane swa mo. Momwɛ-dɛɛre de jaane yi-poro mo de tui.

english_verse: But God is the real source of wisdom and strength.
translation_verse: Swa dedaane dam ye Wɛ mo tei-te. O maa bere kwea, de yi-poro maama de.

english_verse: puts mighty kings to shame, and takes away their power.
translation_verse: O pae nɔn-yum di ba chaveera mo, ye o vere babɛ dam o daare-ba o zege bwori.

english_verse: God strikes their rulers senseless, then leaves them to roam through barren deserts,
translation_verse: O pae tega baŋa teene dem yuu tiina toŋe jworim mo, o daare o pa ba kare kagoa yuu ne ba beeri yɔɔ yerane.

english_verse: None of you are smarter than I am; there's nothing you know that I don't.
translation_verse: Abam de amo ba gare daane. Abam maa na yei wonnu telo to, amo de yei-te mo.

english_verse: The wisest thing you can do is to keep quiet
translation_verse: Abam ná pugi á nia, ko wó taa gara! Konto ya wó bere we, á jege swa chekke.

english_verse: and not telling the whole truth when you argue his case?
translation_verse: Abam wó sɛ se á zege á pa Wɛ mo, se á jwoŋi o taane saŋa baŋa ne á ŋɔɔne na?

english_verse: If he took you to court, could you fool him, just as you fool others?
translation_verse: O nam ná jwoori o bwei abam, á wó lu taane ne na? Á wó wane Wɛ á gane, ne á na jege nabiina á gane tei to na?

english_verse: If you were secretly unfair, he would correct you,
translation_verse: Chega ná tere abam taane dem wone, á yeiri we o wó bwɛ abam ko ŋwaane na?

english_verse: and his glorious splendor would make you terrified.
translation_verse: O nenɔŋa kam bá fugi abam, pa se o foone taa jege abam na?

english_verse: I will be responsible for what happens to me.
translation_verse: Yage-na se kolo ná wó yi-ne, se ko yi. Amo dole a ŋwea mo a yage.

english_verse: This may be what saves me, because no guilty person would come to his court.
translation_verse: Konto baŋa ne mo Wɛ wó wane o jwoŋi-ne o yage. Kokuri, wolo na ve Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem to bá na chwoŋa se o zege Wɛ yiga ne.

english_verse: I have prepared my case well, and I am certain to win.
translation_verse: Nii-na! A yɔɔre a jeeli taane delo a na wó ta to mo. A nam yei lanyerane we a wó di bora.

english_verse: If you can prove me guilty, I will give up and die. Job Prays I Ask Only Two Things
translation_verse: Wɔ mo wora se o saŋe-ne we a chɔge? A nam ná seene a tusi, amo wó taa chem mo se a laam te.

english_verse: I ask only two things of you, my God, and I will no longer hide from you—
translation_verse: Amo Tu Wɛ, wonnu telei yerane mo a lage a lwoori n tei ne se n ke n pa-ne. Konto ná kea, amo daa bá taa kare a seigi nmo yiga ne.

english_verse: Then speak, and I will reply; or else let me speak, and you reply.
translation_verse: Nam bwoŋi-ne, se a wane a leiri n taane dem, naa pa-ne chwoŋa se a ŋɔɔne, se nmo de leiri a taane dem.

english_verse: Why have you turned your back and count me your enemy?
translation_verse: Bɛŋwaane mo n yiga tere amo wone? Bɛ mo ye n yɔɔre n done-ne?

english_verse: Why do you accuse me of horrible crimes and make me pay for sins I did in my youth?
translation_verse: N nam popone wo-chɛɛro n tiŋi tɔnɔ ne we te ye amo yiga. Ko ta ná ye wɛleera yalo a na ke a nɔn-donne maŋa ne to, n laam ma‑n pa se ya jene wo a yuu ne.

english_verse: Life is short and sorrowful for every living soul.
translation_verse: “Kaane ná loge nabiinu wolo maama, kotu ŋwea ye kukua mo ye ka su de cham yerane.

english_verse: There's no way a human can be completely pure.
translation_verse: Nɔn-diku wó wane o lo nɔn-laao na? Ko bá wane ko ke.

english_verse: Our time on earth is brief; the number of our days is already decided by you.
translation_verse: Nmo wuuri n jeeli nabiina ŋwea da yam mo, pa se ya ba ya kweeli ya maŋa ne. Nɔɔna ware se ba gaale ba maŋa kam chekke.

english_verse: Why don't you leave us alone and let us find some happiness while we toil and labor? When a Tree Is Chopped Down
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane nam yage ba yera, se ba wane ba toŋe ye ba daare ba sii, ne ba na jene nɔɔna balo se ba taa toŋe to.

english_verse: When a tree is chopped down, there is always the hope that it will sprout again.
translation_verse: Ba ná gwoni tio ba de tega ne, teena ta wora we ko wó jwoori ko kwi, se ko nɛ-donno tem daa yé te.

english_verse: but at the touch of water, it sprouts once again.
translation_verse: Se na fenfee ná yɔɔre ba dwei tio kom yera, ko wó jwoori ko kwi nɛ-donno de vɔɔro mo.

english_verse: We are like streams and lakes after the water has gone;
translation_verse: Buga wo ná yeini ba we ba daare-ka, pa se ka tigi te-kora yerane mo,

english_verse: Please hide me, God, deep in the ground— and when you are angry no more, remember to rescue me. Will We Humans Live Again?
translation_verse: Ja! Amo Tu Wɛ, kwei-ne n seigi churu ne, se kolokolo yé yi-ne, ko taa nii dɛ dem n bane na zuri to. Nam kuri dɛ se n laam jwoori n guli amo gula.

english_verse: My Creator, you would want me; you would call out, and I would answer.
translation_verse: Nmo ná bwoŋi a yere, a wó leiri‑m. Nmo boboŋa maa wó taa tigi amo wolo n tete je na mɔɔne to wone.

english_verse: You would take care of me, but not count my sins—
translation_verse: Nmo laam wó ta‑n yere a na-veili maama, ye n nam bá‑n jeeli a wɛleera yam na ye tei to.

english_verse: you would put them in a bag, tie it tight, and toss them away.
translation_verse: Nmo ma‑n wó kwoli a wɛleera yam, ne nɔɔno na seigi wonnu tampɔgɔ wone tei to.

english_verse: We feel no pain but our own, and when we mourn, it's only for ourselves.
translation_verse: Kolo yerane o na yei to mo ye o tete yera na nɛ zonne tei to. O maa wó taa keeri o tete keira.”

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman said: *
translation_verse: Teman tu Elifaza daa ma leiri Job o we:

english_verse: Your words are enough to make others turn from God and lead them to doubt.
translation_verse: Nii mo! N boŋe se n dole Wɛ kɔrɔ n yage mo. N ta ma‑n lage n che se nɔɔna yé taa boŋe Wɛ boboŋa chekke.

english_verse: And your sinful, scheming mind is the source of all you say.
translation_verse: N wɛleere kikia yam de n pipiri totoŋa yam, mo pa se n jege ni se n ŋɔɔne n chɔge Wɛ yere.

english_verse: I am not here as your judge; your own words are witnesses against you.
translation_verse: Ko dae amo mo ŋɔɔne a vane nmo bora. Se n tete ni taane mo le‑m de zege dáa ne.

english_verse: Were you the first human? Are you older than the hills?
translation_verse: Nmo mo puli nabiina maama kuri na? Naa n koe logo baŋa peero tem mo?

english_verse: Have you ever been present when God's council meets? Do you alone have wisdom?
translation_verse: Wɛ kɔgɔ kom ná yeini ba jeeri daane wɛyuu ne, nmo de wó tɔge n gwaane ba wone na? Nmo boŋe we nmo yerane yi mo poore na?

english_verse: We have the benefit of wisdom older than your father.
translation_verse: Balo yuni na peere to mo zege dé kwaga ne. Ba maa ye nɔn-kwe selo na koe nmo kwo to.

english_verse: And you have been offered comforting words from God. Isn't this enough?
translation_verse: Wɛ kwei bochare-zuru taane mo o ta dede‑m. O na zuri o yera de nmo konto to, ko ba jege kuri ko pa‑m na?

english_verse: Your emotions are out of control, making you look fierce;
translation_verse: Bɛŋwaane mo nmo ware n bane se n ja pa se n yibia leiri?

english_verse: that's why you attack God with everything you say.
translation_verse: Nmo nam pɛ se n bane zaŋe de Wɛ, ye ta-yɔɔro yerane tɔge n ni ne ya nwoŋa.

english_verse: and neither are angels— not in the sight of God. If God doesn't trust his angels,
translation_verse: Ko ná maŋe ko ye Wɛ malese-laaro tete de, o ba ke o teena se wone. O maa wo sɛ we wɛyuu baŋa jei sem ye wose o yiga ne.

english_verse: what chance do humans have? We are so terribly evil that we thirst for sin. Just Listen to What I Know
translation_verse: Nabiina laam wó taa ye tetɛ mo o tei ne? Ba boboŋa tiini ya pɔ mo, ye ba toŋe lwarem ne na mo ba jege ba nyɔ to.

english_verse: Those who gained such insights also gained the land, and they were not influenced by foreign teachings.
translation_verse: Banto yerane mo jwoŋi tega kam Wɛ tei ne. Sa-teena maa ba jege chwoŋa se ba gane-ba.

english_verse: But suffering is in store each day for those who sin.
translation_verse: Puseŋ-nyena de nankɔ-nyena wó na yaara mo taa, se ba ŋwea bena yam maama ba ya ti.

english_verse: Even in times of success, they constantly hear the threat of doom.
translation_verse: Ba ni kwori mo ba zwa wone pa se foone zo-ba. Yazura ná yi-ba de, venverena mo beene ba baŋa.

english_verse: They are overcome with despair, like frightened soldiers facing a fearsome king in battle.
translation_verse: Lwia dedɛ jege-ba, pa se ba tiini ba kɔre foone. Foone maa wó wane-ba de di, ne pɛ wolo na kwaare jara de o dona to.

english_verse: They may be rich and fat,
translation_verse: Puseŋ-nyena bam yɔɔre ba nu mo bigila bigila, ye ba yera duna.

english_verse: And God is the one who handed me over to this merciless mob. Everything Was Going Well
translation_verse: Wɛ yɔɔre o kwei amo o ke nɔn-balwaaro jeŋa ne mo, pa a to puseŋ-nyena jeŋa ne.

english_verse: Everything was going well, until God grabbed my neck and shook me to pieces. God set me up as the target
translation_verse: Amo déem jei de bochare-zuru, ye o laam ba o chɔge-ne. O ma sɔ a ba ne ye o daare o dole-ne o de tega ne. Wɛ bole amo mo.

english_verse: for his arrows, and without showing mercy, he slashed my stomach open, spilling out my insides.
