english_verse: Use wisdom and understanding to establish your home;
translation_verse: Swa lɔ sam mo ya zega. Yi-poro pae de fɔge de chwi lanyerane de dam mo.

english_verse: let good sense fill the rooms with priceless treasures. –
translation_verse: Yeino maa pae sam sui de wo-laaro dwi maama.

english_verse: My children, you must respect the Lord and the king, and you must not make friends with anyone who rebels against either of them.
translation_verse: Amo bu, ta‑n kɔre Baŋa Wɛ de pɛ. Nam yé ta‑n ye de balo na ba nege banto to.

english_verse: Battles are won by listening to advice and making a lot of plans. –
translation_verse: Wolo na sɛ bera to mo ke jara o di wɔnɔ, Wolo maa na bwɛ wonnu de nɔɔna dedɛ to bá to jara wone.

english_verse: Who knows what sudden disaster the Lord or a ruler might bring? More Sayings That Make Good Sense
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Wɛ de pɛ jege dam se ba chɔge nɔn-dwoa bam konto mɔle mɔle. Faŋa tu memaŋa yadwonna

english_verse: Wisdom is too much for fools! Their advice is no good. –
translation_verse: Botare dende tiini se dana se dwoi nɔn-jworo jaanem. Nakwa ná jeeri manchwoŋo ni ne, o ba jege ni se o puri.

english_verse: Here are some more sayings that make good sense: When you judge, you must be fair.
translation_verse: Boboŋa tu taana yadwonna mo tento: Ko dae ko chwoŋa ne se n ta‑n kuri nɔɔna da-wone.

english_verse: Everyone hates senseless fools who think up ways to sin. –
translation_verse: Nɔn-jworo jeeli o woŋo maama o vei o guri de wɛleere mo. Nɔɔna maa yɔɔre ba chuli nɔn-lwɛɛno.

english_verse: If you let the guilty go free, people of all nations will hate and curse you.
translation_verse: Wolo ná tage de Agɛbora we, “Nmo jege chega,” nɔɔna wó sɔɔle lwarem ba pa kotu, ye teene maama de ve‑o.

english_verse: Don't give up and be helpless in times of trouble. –
translation_verse: Nmo vɔna ná pare cham maŋa ne mɔle-mɔle, ko nam bere we n tiini n bwona mo lage-lage.

english_verse: But if you punish the guilty, things will go well for you, and you will prosper.
translation_verse: Wolo nam ná waare balo na toŋe vwa to, wonnu maama wó da chwoŋa te pa kotu, ye Wɛ zaane de taa wo o yuu ne.

english_verse: Don't fail to rescue those who are doomed to die.
translation_verse: Ba ná vaŋe wolo ba vei se ba go vwa chwoŋa ne, se n jwoŋi kotu n yage.

english_verse: Don't say, “I didn't know it!” God can read your mind. He watches each of us and knows our thoughts. And God will pay us back for what we do. –
translation_verse: Nmo nam ná we, “Ka wo nɛ amo, a yeiri nɔɔno wom,” nam lɔre we Wɛ yei nɔɔna maama bochara na ye tei to. Wonto mo zei n ŋwea ye o yei n kikia maama ni ne. N boŋe we o bá ŋwe nɔɔno maama ko tɔge de o kikia na?

english_verse: Giving an honest answer is a sign of true friendship.
translation_verse: Wolo na wó ta n yera chega to mo seene o ye n badwoŋi chekke.

english_verse: Wisdom is like honey for your life— if you find it, your future is bright. –
translation_verse: Nam lɔre we yi-poro de ye konto mo ko pa‑m. N ná nɛ-ko, nmo wó ta‑n jege jwa lanyerane, ye n teena yam bá fɔge ya ti.

english_verse: Don't be a cruel person who attacks good people and hurts their families.
translation_verse: Yé ji wolo o teo tiina na mage gulu ba le‑o, pa o beeri nɔn-ŋom de o sɔŋɔ tiina se o de chɔge to.

english_verse: Even if good people fall seven times, they will get back up. But when trouble strikes the wicked, that's the end of them. –
translation_verse: Kokuri, nɔn-ŋom ná to kuni berepɛ de, o ta wó pɛ o zaŋe o zege cheppe. Se ko ná ye puseŋ-nyem, lira tera ka na wó jwoŋi‑o ka yage.

english_verse: Don't accuse anyone who isn't guilty. Don't ever tell a lie
translation_verse: Yé pa maana n chɔge n dwoŋi ye n yeiri chega kam n tia. Nam yé ma n ni n gane nɔɔna.

english_verse: Don't be happy to see your enemies trip and fall down.
translation_verse: Yé ta‑n chaka de n dono na to tega ne to. O na tiri se o to, yé ta‑n jege wopwolo.

english_verse: The Lord will find out and be unhappy. Then he will stop being angry with them. –
translation_verse: Kokuri, Wɛ wó na n kikia se o wo chɔge dede‑m. O laam maa wó pa o bane daa yé zaŋe de n dono wom.

english_verse: I once walked by the field and the vineyard of a lazy fool.
translation_verse: Amo nɛ pwola mo a tɔge jawɔre-nyem kara seeni a kɛ.

english_verse: Sleep a little. Doze a little. Fold your hands and twiddle your thumbs.
translation_verse: Ta‑n swoi dɔɔne, ye n lage se n ta‑n tigi n sia. Vɔ n je daane se n sii n ja n tete,

english_verse: Here are some more of Solomon's proverbs. They were copied by the officials of King Hezekiah of Judah.
translation_verse: Solomon memaŋa yam yadaara mo tento. Judah teo pɛ Hezekia nam mo pɛ ba jwoori ba lwoni-se ba popone ba tiŋi.

english_verse: God is praised for being mysterious; rulers are praised for explaining mysteries.
translation_verse: Wɛ jege dam se o seigi wonnu mo. Pɛ maa jege dam o yɛ wonnu.

english_verse: Who can fully understand the thoughts of a ruler? They reach beyond the sky and go deep in the earth.
translation_verse: Ba ba lɔre pɛ boboŋa ba tia. Ya diini wɛɛne ya dwoni wɛ baŋa kam, ye ya ta tu tega kam kuri kuri.

english_verse: Silver must be purified before it can be used to make something of value.
translation_verse: Lura ná le digiru lu-nyenno yera ne, lu-nyenno tem wó ke wo-kura.

english_verse: Evil people must be removed before anyone can rule with justice.
translation_verse: Pwa ná zeili nakwa-balwaaro ba daare, ba paare wó jeini nɔn-ŋonne baŋa ne.

english_verse: Don't try to seem important in the court of a ruler.
translation_verse: Yé zeiŋi n tete pɛ yiga ne. Nam yé ja n tete n vo n maŋe de nɔn-kamuna.

english_verse: It's better for the ruler to give you a high position than for you to be embarrassed in front of royal officials. Be sure you are right
translation_verse: Pɛ ná tage de nmo o we, “Ba n jeini ywo,” gare o ná gwooni‑m nɔn-yerro yiga ne. Nmo yi ná nɛ n dwoŋi wo-keeru,

english_verse: before you sue someone, or you might lose your case and be embarrassed.
translation_verse: yé wuuri n ja‑o n vo taane dim jei. Kokuri to, ko kwaga ne nmo wó maane we, chave-kukua gare chave-dedɔrɔ.

english_verse: When you and someone else can't get along, don't gossip about it.
translation_verse: Pa nmo de n faro wom jeini á kwɛ daane. Se yé ta‑n jege‑o n chwo n bere nɔɔna.

english_verse: Others will find out, and your reputation will then be ruined.
translation_verse: Ko ná dae konto, nɔɔna wó ta we n ye bebare nyem. Nmo laam ma‑n wó te de n chaveera.

english_verse: The right word at the right time is like precious gold set in silver.
translation_verse: Ta-kuri nye de sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno na gɔgere te ke daane tei to mo.

english_verse: Listening to good advice is worth much more than jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: Yi-pore-nyem ná kwoni‑m o zege de swa taane, ko jege kuri ko dwoi ba ná kwei sabu-seŋa zambili ba de‑m.

english_verse: A messenger you can trust is just as refreshing as cool water in summer.
translation_verse: Wolo ba na toŋe to ná jege chega, o zuri balo na toŋe‑o to bochara mo, ne na-zura na zuri na-nyɔm faao-ni maŋa ne tei to.

english_verse: Patience and gentle talk can convince a ruler and overcome any problem.
translation_verse: N ná peene n bane, dedɛɛro wó cheigi n taane. Wolo ni taane na bwona to wae o kwɛ wonnu.

english_verse: Don't visit friends too often, or they will get tired of it and start hating you.
translation_verse: Yé pa n nɛ taa lona de n faro sɔŋɔ. O fera ná nwoŋi‑m, o laam wó taa lɔŋe‑m mo.

english_verse: Telling lies about friends is like attacking them with clubs and swords and sharp arrows.
translation_verse: Wolo ná fɔge vwa se o ma o chɔge o dwoŋi, kotu nye de o kwei da-lɔŋɔ, naa se-zɔɔ, naa che-tɛɛre delo na sele to mo o chɔge‑o.

english_verse: A friend you can't trust in times of trouble is like having a toothache or a sore foot.
translation_verse: Ne yeili-bɔɔ de nachara na pae nɔɔno yeiri o tete jei to, konto mo nɔn-ŋolo jege o ke de o dwoŋi cham maŋa ne.

english_verse: If your enemies are hungry, give them something to eat. And if they are thirsty, give them something to drink.
translation_verse: Nmo dono kana ná wɔe, pa‑o wodiu se o di. Na-nyɔm ná jege‑o, pa‑o na se o nyɔ.

english_verse: This will be the same as piling burning coals on their heads. And the Lord will reward you.
translation_verse: Kikia yam konto wó pa se chaveera tiini ya ja‑o, ne Wɛ zeiŋi mini mo o yuu ne to. Baŋa Wɛ maa wó zuli‑m ko ŋwaane.

english_verse: As surely as rain blows in from the north, anger is caused by cruel words.
translation_verse: Ne baŋa seeni vio kom na tui de doa tei to, mo ban-zɔŋɔ na tɔge de bebara ko tui tei.

english_verse: It's better to stay outside on the roof of your house than to live inside with a nagging wife.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná beeri gugworo o nayuu ne o tigi da gare o ná zoore de ka-wam.

english_verse: Good news from far away refreshes like cold water when you are thirsty.
translation_verse: Kwor-ywoŋa ná nwoŋi yiga yiga ka ba, ka pae bochara tigi mo, ne na-zura na zuri bochare tei to.

english_verse: When a good person gives in to the wicked, it's like dumping garbage in a stream of clear water.
translation_verse: Vole mo su de weero pa na daa ware se ba bu. Nɔn-ŋom de nam ná sɛ o pa puseŋ-nyem, ko ye konto mo.

english_verse: Losing self-control leaves you as helpless as a city without a wall.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná ware o bane o ja, o nye de teo kolo kabiri na sirimi se to se daare-ko to mo.

english_verse: Expecting snow in summer and rain in the dry season makes more sense than honoring a fool.
translation_verse: Ne doa na ba nena, ye nyɔnɔ de ba toe te-pwoŋa ne tei to, konto mo nɔn-jworo de wo maŋe se n zuli‑o.

english_verse: A curse you don't deserve will take wings and fly away like a sparrow or a swallow.
translation_verse: Ne kawɛbidwoori na ba jege tega jeiŋa tei to, mo sensɔla kalo na wo tɔge chwoŋa to na ye tei. Ka bá jeini n yuu ne.

english_verse: Horses and donkeys must be beaten and bridled— and so must fools.
translation_verse: Fere sisein-nɔɔno de fena, se n de ŋona bonaga ba ne n vaŋe-ka. Ko nam ná ye nɔn-jworo, mage‑o se ko yi.

english_verse: Don't make a fool of yourself by answering a fool.
translation_verse: Nɔn-jworo ná tage taane pa n leiri-de, nmo ded‑o ba gare daane.

english_verse: But if you answer any fools, show how foolish they are, so they won't feel smart.
translation_verse: Leiri nɔn-jworo de o jworim dem. Ko ná dae konto, o wó boŋe we o yɔɔre o yei mo.

english_verse: A fool with words of wisdom is like an athlete with legs that can't move.
translation_verse: Ne gɔrɔ nɛ na ware se vo tei to, konto mo nɔn-jworo de ware o lɔre dende kuri.

english_verse: Are you going to honor a fool? Why not shoot a slingshot with the rock tied tight?
translation_verse: Nmo ná vɔge kandwɛ napana wone se n vuvugi n yage, nye de n na kwaane se n zuli Agɛboŋa tei to.

english_verse: A thornbush waved around in the hand of a drunkard is no worse than a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
translation_verse: Ne sa-nyɔro na yeiri sabara jaanem tei to, konto mo nɔn-jworo de yeiri dende kuri.

english_verse: It's no smarter to shoot arrows at every passerby than it is to hire a bunch of worthless nobodies.
translation_verse: N ná kwei totoŋe n ke Agɛboŋa jeŋa ne, n mage bwogo mo.

english_verse: Dogs return to eat their vomit, just as fools repeat their foolishness.
translation_verse: Ne kukura na jwoori ka di ka tetwanno tei to, nɔn-jworo de kare o toŋe jworim konto mo.

english_verse: There is more hope for a fool than for someone who says, “I'm really smart!”
translation_verse: Nɔn-jworo jege teena se o lɔre, se ko dwoi wolo na pa o yei to.

english_verse: Don't be lazy and keep saying, “There's a lion outside!”
translation_verse: Jawɔre-nyem tigi mo ye o we, “Nywoŋo kare pwooni ne ko beera!”

english_verse: A door turns on its hinges, but a lazy person just turns over in bed.
translation_verse: Ne diga ni bworo na pore ye ko pe tei to, konto mo yezona tu de kare o pipiri o sara ne.

english_verse: Some of us are so lazy that we won't lift a hand to feed ourselves.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna badaara jawɔrɔ ye ko yera. Ba ná tore jeŋa zoŋa ne ba fɔ gole, ba ware ba lu dwoa se ba ja-de ba vo ba ni.

english_verse: A lazy person says, “I am smarter than everyone else.”
translation_verse: Jawɔre-nyem pa o yei o dwoi yi-pore-nyena barepɛ na yeini ba leiri taane de swa tei to mo.

english_verse: It's better to take hold of a mad dog by the ears than to take part in someone else's argument.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná jwoŋi o dwoŋi jara o ja, kotu wó na na-gare chene mo.

english_verse: It's no crazier to shoot sharp and flaming arrows
translation_verse: Ne chichwoo na tae chena yɔɔ yɔɔ tei to,

english_verse: than to cheat someone and say, “I was only fooling!”
translation_verse: mo wolo de na gane o dwoŋi ye o we, “A ke a kwɛɛra mo” de na ye tei.

english_verse: Where there is no fuel a fire goes out; where there is no gossip arguments come to an end.
translation_verse: Dɛ ná ti, mini wó dwei mo. Bebara ná tera, ni-kantɔgɔ jei mo.

english_verse: Troublemakers start trouble, just as sparks and fuel start a fire.
translation_verse: Min-chala nyeeri mini mo, nankɔ-nyem de maa nyeeri jara.

english_verse: There is nothing so delicious as the taste of gossip! It melts in your mouth.
translation_verse: Bebare nyem ni taane nye de wodi-ywoŋo na duri solololo ko tu nabiinu kana ne to mo.

english_verse: Hiding hateful thoughts behind smooth talk is like coating a clay pot with a cheap glaze.
translation_verse: Wolo ná tage taane ye o wo ba tɔge o taane dem, kotu nye de ba na kwei lu-nyenno ba taare dɔgɔ kamɔgɔ tei to mo.

english_verse: The pleasant talk of an enemy hides more evil plans
translation_verse: Pipiri-nyem kwei ni-som mo o seigi o boboŋa. O laam maa tɔge dáane o chɔge nɔɔna.

english_verse: If you dig a pit, you will fall in; if you start a stone rolling, it will roll back on you.
translation_verse: N ná chege kalanchogo, ko wó ja n tete. N nam ná bibili kandwɛ-zane n ja n di peo yuu n yage-de, de wó bibili de to de pane‑m mo.

english_verse: Watch out for anyone who tells lies and flatters— they are out to get you.
translation_verse: Vwa-nyem chuli o dona mo. Ni-som nyem maa jaane chɔgem o tui.

english_verse: Don't brag about yourself— let others praise you.
translation_verse: Yage se nɔn-gɛ tei‑m, se nmo tete yé ta n su n ni.

english_verse: Stones and sand are heavy, but trouble caused by a fool is a much heavier load.
translation_verse: Kandwa-zana dumma, ye kasolo dunni de gaale. Nɔn-jworo nam ná toŋe jworim nmo yera ne, ko cham dem duna de dwoi tento maama.

english_verse: An angry person is dangerous, but a jealous person is even worse.
translation_verse: Ban-lom tu keim chana ye o ware o ja. Wolo kazwe na gaale to nam dwoi kotu.

english_verse: You can trust a friend who corrects you, but kisses from an enemy are nothing but lies.
translation_verse: Nmo badwoŋi ná tage n chega jei, ko jege kuri ko pa‑m. Ko daare n dono mɔne dede‑m mo, se ko dae swono.

english_verse: If you have had enough to eat, honey doesn't taste good, but if you are really hungry, you will eat anything.
translation_verse: N ná di n su, tooro tete lwoi n momwa ne mo. Kana nɔɔno nam yeiri ko chana.

english_verse: When you are far from home, you feel like a bird without a nest.
translation_verse: Wolo na duri o daare o sɔŋɔ to nye de zuŋa kalo na nwoŋi ka daare ka pwogo to mo.

english_verse: The sweet smell of incense can make you feel good, but true friendship is better still.
translation_verse: Terale nuga de talwoŋ-ywoŋa pae nɔɔna wopwolo mo. Badwoŋ-ywoŋo bera nam gare tento.

english_verse: Don't desert an old friend of your family or visit your relatives when you are in trouble. A friend nearby is better than relatives far away.
translation_verse: Ta‑n yei n badwonna de n kwo badwonna ni ne. Cham ná yi‑m, n fara bam konto wó woli‑m ba dwoni n chorro telo na ba bwola to.

english_verse: My child, show good sense! Then I will be happy and able to answer anyone who criticizes me.
translation_verse: Amo bu, kwaane n ja swa se a wo pwoli ko ŋwaane. Konto wó pa-ne chwoŋa se a puri a ni a leiri balo na jege-ne ba lwɛ to.

english_verse: Be cautious and hide when you see danger— don't be stupid and walk right into trouble.
translation_verse: Boboŋa tu duri o seigi cham mo se de yé yi‑o. Nayeiri-nyem nam wó duri o zo de wone mo ye o na yaara.

english_verse: You deserve to lose your coat if you loan it to someone to guarantee payment for the debt of a stranger.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná sɛ se o zege se veiru di jene nmo tei ne, ko maŋe se n jwoŋi kotu gare-bwora mo n woli da.

english_verse: A loud greeting early in the morning is the same as a curse.
translation_verse: Wolo na gwoni tega o tɔɔle o ware o dwonna to nye de o sɔɔle lwarem mo o pa-ba.

english_verse: The steady dripping of rain and the nagging of a wife are one and the same.
translation_verse: Ka-wam wolo na jege nyenyɔna to nye de doa na nene ye na luri n diga ne tei to mo.

english_verse: It's easier to catch the wind or hold olive oil in your hand than to stop a nagging wife.
translation_verse: Wolo ná kwaane se o ja ka-dwi dem konto, kotu wó ke o ga mo. Ko nye de n na zeili vio se n ja-ko, naa n mɔ nuga de n ja-bɔŋɔ tei to mo.

english_verse: Just as iron sharpens iron, friends sharpen the minds of each other.
translation_verse: Seene na kekarege daane se de ja ni tei to, konto mo nabiina de zamese da-tei ne.

english_verse: Take care of a tree, and you will eat its fruit; look after your master, and you will be praised.
translation_verse: Wolo na fɔge o kwɛ teeni to wó di ko bia mo. Wolo de maa na toŋe o pae o tu de chega to wó jwoŋi zula.

english_verse: You see your face in a mirror and your thoughts in the minds of others.
translation_verse: Niu bere nabiinu yibia mo. Ko daare o bochare maa bere o na ye wolo to.

english_verse: Death and the grave are never satisfied, and neither are humans.
translation_verse: Twa ná maŋe ba daga tei, churu ba sui. Nabiina yia de ba nii ya sui.

english_verse: Gold and silver are tested in a red-hot furnace, but we are tested by praise.
translation_verse: Min-vogo pae ba yei lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa lam mo. Ko nam ná ye nabiinu, ba wó lɔre o wo de o na nɛ yere tei to mo.

english_verse: No matter how hard you beat a fool, you can't pound out the foolishness.
translation_verse: Kwei nɔn-jworo n ke kazɔgɔ ne n woli de mena n zɔ n na lage tei. O jworim dem ta bá ti.

english_verse: You should take good care of your sheep and goats,
translation_verse: Ta‑n yei n vara bam ni ne, se n daare n ta‑n nii ba baŋa ne lanyerane.

english_verse: After the hay is cut and the new growth appears and the harvest is over,
translation_verse: Ba ná gaane gaao pa ko jwoori ko kwi, ye ba tigisi ga-korro telo ba na gaane to ba ke daane,

english_verse: From the milk of the goats, you can make enough cheese to feed your family and all your servants.
translation_verse: N ma‑n wó kwei n vara nayela n kɔne n diga kam, de n ka-nyaana bam.

english_verse: Wicked people run away when no one chases them, but those who live right are as brave as lions.
translation_verse: Puseŋ-nyena duri se ba lu mo ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba pare-ba. Nɔn-ŋona nam jege baare mo ne nywoŋo to.

english_verse: In time of civil war there are many leaders, but a sensible leader restores law and order.
translation_verse: Teo ná su de zwabani-nyena, ba leiri balo na nii-ko to yɔɔ yɔɔ mo. Boboŋa tu nam wó kwei yeino mo o ja o teo o dáane.

english_verse: When someone poor takes over and mistreats the poor, it's like a heavy rain destroying the crops.
translation_verse: Yiniga tu ná pɛ ko zo o dwonna yiniga tiina yera, o de do-jworo na chuura ka chɔge wodiiru to ba gare daane.

english_verse: Criminals don't know what justice means, but all who respect the Lord understand it completely.
translation_verse: Nɔn-balwaaro bá wane ba ni chega kam kuri. Ko nam ná ye balo na kɔre Baŋa Wɛ to, ba yɔɔre ba ni ka kuri mo lanyerane.

english_verse: It's better to be poor and live right, than to be rich and dishonest.
translation_verse: Yiniga tu ná jei de o chega gare nadum ná ye nɔn-ŋolo.

english_verse: It makes good sense to obey the Law of God, but you disgrace your parents if you make friends with worthless nobodies.
translation_verse: Wolo na ke o tɔge Wɛ nia yam to bere we o yi poore mo. Wolo nam ná vei de nɔn-kwollu, kotu yaale o kwo mo.

english_verse: If you make money by charging high interest rates, you will lose it all to someone who cares for the poor.
translation_verse: Wolo ná dɔne nyɔɔre dedɛ jena baŋa ne se o ma o duni, kotu wó ga o jejegero, ye wolo na jege yiniga tiina ŋwaŋa to laam na-te.

english_verse: God cannot stand the prayers of anyone who disobeys his Law.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná paale o se o zwa de Wɛ nia yam, o wɛ-lworo tete lwoi mo Wɛ momwa ne.

english_verse: By leading good people to sin, you dig a pit for yourself, but all who live right will have a bright future.
translation_verse: Nmo ná soge nɔn-ŋom n de lwarem ne, n tete wó to n gwoŋo wone mo. Ko nam ná ye balo na ba tusi to, banto jege jwa.

english_verse: The rich think highly of themselves, but anyone poor and sensible sees right through them.
translation_verse: Nadum yeini o boŋe we o yei o ti mo. Yiniga tu wolo yi na poore to nam yɔɔre o yei nadum wo maama mo.

english_verse: When an honest person wins, it's time to celebrate; when crooks are in control, it's best to hide.
translation_verse: Nɔn-ŋona ná diini dam baŋa, nɔɔno maama chake mo. Puseŋ-nyena nam ná jege dam ba di, nɔɔna duri ba seigi mo.

english_verse: If you don't confess your sins, you will be a failure. But God will be merciful if you confess your sins and give them up.
translation_verse: Wolo na jege o wɛleera o seigi to ba vei yiga. Wolo nam ná pɛ ya nwoŋi pwooni ye o chuli-ya, Wɛ wó duri kotu ŋwaŋa.

english_verse: The Lord blesses everyone who is afraid to do evil, but if you are cruel, you will end up in trouble.
translation_verse: Wolo na yɔɔre o kɔre Baŋa Wɛ to jege yu-ywoŋo. Zwabani-nyem nam zoore cham wone mo.

english_verse: A ruler who mistreats the poor is like a roaring lion or a bear hunting for food.
translation_verse: Pɛ ná tɔge puseŋa baŋa o yaare nabwona, o nye de nywoŋo na ŋuuri se ko zi nɔne to mo.

english_verse: A heartless leader is a fool, but anyone who refuses to get rich by cheating others will live a long time.
translation_verse: Pɛ keim ná chamma, o boboŋa mo muri. Wolo nam na chuli kampina to wó dáane.

english_verse: Don't give help to murderers! Make them stay on the run for as long as they live.
translation_verse: Nɔn-goro boboŋa wó daane‑o mo se ko yi o toone maŋa. O dae ba woli.

english_verse: Honesty will keep you safe, but everyone who is crooked will suddenly fall.
translation_verse: Chega tu kikia cho‑o mo. Ko daare nɔn-ŋolo wó pɔpɔ o na chɔgem.

english_verse: Work hard, and you will have a lot of food; waste time, and you will have a lot of trouble.
translation_verse: Wolo na sɛ varem to jeŋa yi o ni. Yini-gwia nam wó ja wolo na kare o toŋe wo-yɔɔro to.

english_verse: God blesses his loyal people, but punishes all who want to get rich quick.
translation_verse: Chega tu wó na Wɛ zaane se ko gaale. Wolo yera nam ná sae se o beeri jejegero, kotu wó yɔɔre o na waarem.

english_verse: It isn't right to be unfair, but some people can be bribed with only a piece of bread.
translation_verse: Ko dae ko chwoŋa ne se n ta‑n kuri nɔɔna da-wone. Dim ŋwaane nam, nɔɔna jege konto mo ba ke.

english_verse: Don't be selfish and eager to get rich— you will end up worse off than you can imagine.
translation_verse: Wo-loŋ-nyem lɔgere mo se o duni. O nam yeiri we yiniga wó yi‑o.

english_verse: If you cheat your parents and don't think it's wrong, you are a common thief.
translation_verse: Wolo ná pini o kwo de o nu ye o boŋe we konto dae kolokolo, kotu de nɔn-goro ba gare daane.

english_verse: Selfish people cause trouble, but you will live a full life if you trust the Lord.
translation_verse: Wo-loŋ-nyem pae nankɔɔre mo zaŋa. Ko daare wolo na ke o wo-dedoa de Baŋa Wɛ to wó di ywoni.

english_verse: Only fools would trust what they alone think, but if you live by wisdom, you will do all right.
translation_verse: Wolo na teege o tete yeino baŋa ne to ye jworo mo. Wolo nam ná ke woŋo maama de swa, kotu wó lu cham wone.

english_verse: Giving to the poor will keep you from poverty, but if you close your eyes to their needs, everyone will curse you.
translation_verse: N ná yei yiniga tiina ni ne, n bá‑n fɔge n ga. N nam ná se n zwa de nabwona keira, ba wó sɔɔle lwarem ba pa‑m mo.

english_verse: When crooks are in control, everyone tries to hide, but when they lose power, good people are everywhere.
translation_verse: Puseŋ-nyena ná jege dam ba di, nɔɔna duri ba seigi mo. Ba dam maa ná ti, nɔn-ŋona daa wó pi ba nwoŋi mo.

english_verse: If you keep being stubborn after many warnings, you will suddenly discover you have gone too far.
translation_verse: Ba ná kaane bere-gɛɔ tu kuni dedɛ baŋa ne ba ga, o wó pɔpɔ o na chɔgem mo ye o bá lu de wone.

english_verse: When justice rules a nation, everyone is glad; when injustice rules, everyone groans.
translation_verse: Nɔn-ŋona ná diini paare baŋa, nɔɔna jege wopwolo. Puseŋ-nyena nam ná jege paare ba di, nɔɔna laare mo.

english_verse: If you love wisdom your parents will be glad, but chasing after bad women will cost you everything.
translation_verse: Wolo na beeri swa to kwo wo pwoli mo. Wolo na tɔge ka-bworru kwaga to ma chɔge o kwo wonnu.

english_verse: An honest ruler makes the nation strong; a ruler who takes bribes will bring it to ruin.
translation_verse: Pɛ ná nii o nɔɔna de chega, teo kom ywomma mo. Kalipera tu yigi teo kom o de tega ne mo.

english_verse: Flattery is nothing less than setting a trap.
translation_verse: Ni-som nyem nye de o chege kalanchogo mo o tiŋi.

english_verse: Your sins will catch you, but everyone who lives right will sing and celebrate.
translation_verse: Nɔn-balɔrɔ wɛleera jigi da-bunnu mo ya gare‑o pa o to. Chega tu lei nam jaana mo ye o wo tiga.

english_verse: The wicked don't care about the rights of the poor, but good people do.
translation_verse: Nɔn-ŋom jege yiniga tiina ŋwaŋa ye o pae-ba ba chega. Konto kolokolo nam dae puseŋ-nyem yiga.

english_verse: Sneering at others is a spark that sets a city on fire; using good sense can put out the flames of anger.
translation_verse: Nɔn-lwɛɛna wiiri jara mo ba yage teo wone. Swa tiina maa lwɛ jara.

english_verse: Be wise and don't sue a fool. You won't get satisfaction, because all the fool will do is sneer and shout.
translation_verse: Swa tu ba saŋe nɔn-jworo pɛ sɔŋɔ ne, kokuri, jworo kom wó da mwanno, de sɔɔ yerane mo pa á bá na taane dem kuri.

english_verse: A murderer hates everyone who is honest and lives right.
translation_verse: Nɔn-goro yɔɔre o chuli chega tu mo, ye o beeri chwoŋa se o ti o momwɛ.

english_verse: Don't be a fool and quickly lose your temper— be sensible and patient.
translation_verse: Nɔn-jworo mo bere o ban-lom jaja. Swa tu maa jaane o bane.

english_verse: A ruler who listens to lies will have corrupt officials.
translation_verse: Pɛ ná mae bebare taana o toŋa, o nakwa maama wó taa ke puseŋa mo.

english_verse: The poor and all who abuse them must each depend on God for light.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ mo pae nabiina maama pwooni pa ba nae, ko ná maŋe ko ye yiniga tu de wolo na bɛɛse‑o to de.

english_verse: Kings who are fair to the poor will rule a long time.
translation_verse: Pɛ ná bore chega o pa yiniga tiina, o paare wó dáane mo.

english_verse: Correct your children, and they will be wise; children out of control disgrace their mothers.
translation_verse: Kafena de bwɛa korese bu pa o jaane swa mo. Bu wolo ba na yage ywori to wó yaale o nu mo.

english_verse: Crime increases when crooks are in power, but law-abiding citizens will see them fall.
translation_verse: Puseŋ-nyena ná jei dam ne, wɛleere puli mo. Ba nam wó to ye nɔn-ŋona zege ba nii mo.

english_verse: If you correct your children, they will bring you peace and happiness.
translation_verse: Korese n bia, se ba wó pa‑m bochare-zuru de wopwolo.

english_verse: Without guidance from God law and order disappear, but God blesses everyone who obeys his Law.
translation_verse: Wɛ kwora ná tera se ka bere nɔɔna, ba ke ba na lage tei mo. Balo maa na sɛ Wɛ nia yam to jege yu-ywoŋo.

english_verse: Even when servants are smart, it takes more than words to make them obey.
translation_verse: Ni taane yerane ba de kabɛ chwoŋa ne. O ná maŋe o yei n na lage se o ke tei to, o bá ke.

english_verse: There is more hope for a fool than for someone who speaks without thinking.
translation_verse: Nɔn-jworo jege teena se o lɔre, se ko dwoi wolo na tɛ taane ye o ba boŋe to.

english_verse: Slaves that you treat kindly from their childhood will cause you sorrow.
translation_verse: Nmo ná maŋe n pa n kabaa ywooli o biini maŋa ne, o jwa wó ba o de‑m jaguli-zane mo.

english_verse: A person with a quick temper stirs up arguments and commits a lot of sins.
translation_verse: Bane tu wiiri kantɔgɔ mo o ke da. Ban-lom tu kikia maa jege daanem.

english_verse: Too much pride brings disgrace; humility leads to honor.
translation_verse: Zeiŋi-n-tete pae nɔɔna toe ba yaale lela mo. Wolo nam na tu o tete to wó na zula.

english_verse: If you take part in a crime you are your worst enemy, because even under oath you can't tell the truth.
translation_verse: Wolo na woli ŋweeno pa o ŋɔ to jege o tete mo o waara. O ná maŋe o chem taane dim baŋa ne, o ta wo sii.

english_verse: Don't fall into the trap of being a coward— trust the Lord, and you will be safe.
translation_verse: N ná kɔre n dwonna nabiina, ko bá woli‑m. N nam ná ke n chega de Baŋa Wɛ, mo n sii.

english_verse: Many try to make friends with a ruler, but justice comes from the Lord.
translation_verse: Wɛ ná pɛ nɔɔno na chega gare o ná lage se pɛ taa yei o ni ne.

english_verse: Good people and criminals can't stand each other.
translation_verse: Chega tiina kɔre nɔn-balwaaro na wo mɛ to mo. Puseŋ-nyena de ma chuli nɔn-ŋona bam jei.

english_verse: These are the sayings and the message of Agur son of Jakeh. Someone cries out to God, “I am completely worn out! How can I last?
translation_verse: Jakɛ bu Aguri memaŋa mo tento. Ya maa ye Wɛ kwora. Nɔɔno maa we, “A yera maama chɛ mo! Wɛ, a yera chɛ mo. A daa bá wane a zege!”

english_verse: I am far too stupid to be considered human.
translation_verse: Amo yeiri kolokolo. A yi maa wo poore nenɛɛne a dwonna nabiina bam tetei.

english_verse: I never was wise, and I don't understand what God is like.”
translation_verse: A maa wo fɔge a zamese swa, ye a yeiri Wo-pwoŋo Tu Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: Has anyone gone up to heaven and come back down? Has anyone grabbed hold of the wind? Has anyone wrapped up the sea or marked out boundaries for the earth? If you know of any who have done such things, then tell me their names and their children's names.
translation_verse: Nabiinu wɔ mo diini Wɛ telaao ye o jwoori o ba? Wɔ mo jaane vio o ke o jaguli ne? Wɔ mo pɛ naneo kom o kukuli o gɔrɔ ne? Wɔ mo lɔge logo kom baŋa maama siseini o tiŋi? Abam yei o de o bu wom yere na? Á ná yei, se á ta á bere-ne.

english_verse: Everything God says is true— and it's a shield for all who come to him for safety.
translation_verse: Wɛ taane dem maama yɔɔre de zege de chega mo. O wae o cho balo na tui ba zoore o woro ne to.

english_verse: Don't change what God has said! He will correct you and show that you are a liar.
translation_verse: Ta‑n yei se n yé woli kolokolo Wɛ taane dem wone, se Wɛ wó bwɛ‑m se ko bere we n ye vwa-fɔro mo.

english_verse: There are two things, Lord, I want you to do for me before I die:
translation_verse: Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, a beeri wonnu telei mo se n ke n pa-ne, se a laam te.

english_verse: Make me absolutely honest and don't let me be too poor or too rich. Give me just what I need.
translation_verse: Yé pa a taa ye vwa-nyem. Ta yé pa zore ja-ne. Nam yé pa-ne dunni dedɛ. Pa-ne kolo yerane na maŋe a jaanem to.

english_verse: If I have too much to eat, I might forget about you; if I don't have enough, I might steal and disgrace your name.
translation_verse: Ko ná dae konto, a ná jege ko gaale, a daa bá teege nmo yera ne, ye a ta we “Wɔ mo ye Baŋa Wɛ?” Yiniga nam ná tiini ka ja-ne, a wae a ŋɔna pa se a yaale amo Tu Wɛ yere.

english_verse: Don't tell a slave owner something bad about one of the slaves. That slave will curse you, and you will be in trouble.
translation_verse: Yé chwo kabaa kwaga ka tu yiga ne, se o laam wó sɔɔle lwarem o ke n yuu ne.

english_verse: others think they are perfect, but they are stained by sin.
translation_verse: Badwonna de maa boŋe we ba kikia yɔɔre ya tɔge chwoŋa mo, ye ba wo laam ye ligi-ligi.

english_verse: Some people are stuck-up and act like snobs;
translation_verse: Badwonna maa bere ba kamunim mo ye ba ta gwooni ba dwonna.

english_verse: others are so greedy that they gobble up the poor and homeless.
translation_verse: Badaara ke wo-goo mo de nɔɔna ye ba ni-yeila nye de se-zɔɔro. Ba maa lage se nabwona yere saare tega baŋa ne.

english_verse: Greed has twins, each named “Give me!” There are three or four things that are never satisfied:
translation_verse: Kasandiu jege bukwa balei mo. Ba maama maa tɛ ba we, “Tei n pa-ne.” Wonnu tetɔ wora te na ba fɔge te sui. Tena mo ba tɛ we “Ko maŋe!”

english_verse: The world of the dead and a childless wife, the thirsty earth and a flaming fire.
translation_verse: Te maa ye: churu chwoŋa, de kadega puga, de tega na ba fɔge ka sui na to, de min-vogo na di bileim-bileim to.

english_verse: Don't make fun of your father or disobey your mother— crows will peck out your eyes, and buzzards will eat the rest of you.
translation_verse: Wolo ná mɔne o kwo, naa o ná ke o nu kachaare, bachangaaro wó zɔge o yia te le, ye duura de di o ya-nɔna yam.

english_verse: There are three or four things I cannot understand:
translation_verse: Wonnu tetɔ wora te na tiini te so-ne. A maa ba ni wonnu tena kuri.

english_verse: How eagles fly so high or snakes crawl on rocks, how ships sail the ocean or people fall in love.
translation_verse: Te maa ye: Maao na jaane tei wɛyuu kom ne, de basankwea na yei ka chwoŋa tei peero yuu ne, de nabworo na yɛ naneo kom wone tei to, de baaro de kaane swono laŋa na ye tei to.

english_verse: An unfaithful wife says, “Sleeping with another man is as natural as eating.”
translation_verse: Ka-tola keim ye de yera. O wó peini de nɔn-gaa ye o ta jwoori o ta we, “Amo wo ke kolokolo a chɔge.”

english_verse: There are three or four things that make the earth tremble and are unbearable:
translation_verse: Wonnu tetɔ mo pae tega baŋa kam ziziŋi. Tena maa dwoi nabiina jaanem.

english_verse: A slave who becomes king, a fool who eats too much,
translation_verse: Te maa ye: Kabaa ná jigi pɛ, de nɔn-jworo ná di ko su,

english_verse: a hateful woman who finds a husband, and a slave who takes the place of the woman who owns her.
translation_verse: de bukɔ wolo yuu na chana to ná pɔpɔ o zo baro, de ka-nyaane ná zeili o tu o daare o vere baro wom o tei.

english_verse: On this earth four things are small but very wise:
translation_verse: Wonnu tena kamɔgɔ mo tiini ko muri tega baŋa ne, ye te yi-poro ba jege dwoŋi.

english_verse: Ants, who seem to be feeble, but store up food all summer long;
translation_verse: Memela tiini ba muri de dam. De ko de, ba lae wodiiru ba tiŋi cham maŋa ŋwaane.

english_verse: badgers, who seem to be weak, but live among the rocks;
translation_verse: Pe-ware dam tiini de muri. De ko de, ya zoore peo gugworru ne mo.

english_verse: lizards, which can be caught in your hand, but sneak into palaces.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wae baleiga o jaane de o jeŋa. Se nam ba kɔre pwa sam, se su da mo.

english_verse: those proud roosters, those mountain goats, and those rulers who have no enemies.
translation_verse: Chebɛɔ na kwoni ko yuu ko keeri to, de bo-bala, de pɛ wolo jar-keira na wo o tei ne to.

english_verse: If you churn milk you get butter; if you pound on your nose, you get blood— and if you stay angry, you get in trouble.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, n ná mage nuga, ka wó peere mo. N ná chugi nɔɔno momwɛ, jana mo wó nwoŋi. N nam ná gware nɔɔno bane, jara mo wó zaŋe.

english_verse: These are the sayings that King Lemuel of Massa was taught by his mother.
translation_verse: Pɛ Lemuweli memaŋa mo tento. Ya maa ye Wɛ kwora kalo o nu na bere‑o to.

english_verse: My son Lemuel, you were born in answer to my prayers, so listen carefully.
translation_verse: Nii mo! Nmo ye amo tete puga bu mo. Nmo lora kam nam tɔge wɛ-lworo baŋa ne mo. Konto to, pore n zwa se n cheigi.

english_verse: Don't waste your life chasing after women! This has ruined many kings.
translation_verse: Yé da kaana ŋwaane n chɔge n dam, se banto dwi yeini ba pa se pwa dedɛ na ba chaveera mo.

english_verse: Kings and leaders should not get drunk or even want to drink.
translation_verse: A bu Lemuweli, pwa dae se ba nyɔ sana. Ba nam dae se ba ke fera de sa-dɛɛra.

english_verse: Drinking makes you forget your responsibilities, and you mistreat the poor.
translation_verse: Sa-nyɔre wó pa ba swei Wɛ nia yam na bere tei mo, ye ba ja chega kam ba ju nabwona yiga ne.

english_verse: Beer and wine are only for the dying or for those who have lost all hope.
translation_verse: Sa-dɛɛra maŋe de balo na jei ba cheigi ba toone to mo, ba teena maama na ti to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Let them drink and forget how poor and miserable they feel.
translation_verse: Ba ná bugi, ba wó swei ba yiniga de ba cham dem ni ne.

english_verse: But you must defend those who are helpless and have no hope.
translation_verse: Jiri nabwona ni se n ŋɔɔne n pa-ba. Pa balo na ba jege nɔɔna se ba nii-ba to na ba chega.

english_verse: Be fair and give justice to the poor and homeless. In Praise of a Good Wife
translation_verse: Zaŋe n ŋɔɔne jaja ye n bore chega bora. Zege nabwona de yiniga tiina kwaga ne se ba na ba chega. Ka-yero taane

english_verse: A truly good wife is the most precious treasure a man can find!
translation_verse: Ka-yero yuu yim chana dedɛ. O dwi jege lonne de dwoi kandwa-nyenno dwi dwi.

english_verse: Her husband depends on her, and she never lets him down.
translation_verse: O baro ba jege lwia de kolokolo. O maa bá ga nyɔɔre de fenfee de.

english_verse: She is good to him every day of her life,
translation_verse: Ka-yero ke o baro lanyerane mo maŋa maama, ye o ba pae o nae zonne.

english_verse: and with her own hands she gladly makes clothes.
translation_verse: O yeini o sɔ gwaaro mo waaro de wulim maŋa ŋwaane, ye o toŋe o totoŋa de wopwolo.

english_verse: She gets up before daylight to prepare food for her family and for her servants.
translation_verse: Tega ba poore‑o sara ne, de o na zaŋe o saŋe wodiu o pa o diga tiina, se o ka-nyaana bam de na ba nyem.

english_verse: She knows when to buy or sell, and she stays busy until late at night.
translation_verse: O yɔɔre o yei pipiu laŋa mo pa o ba toe, ye tega ba poore‑o sara ne.

english_verse: and she helps the poor and the needy.
translation_verse: O ye wo-ywoŋo tu mo, naa ye o yeini o zeini nabwona de yiniga tiina.

english_verse: Her family has warm clothing, and so she doesn't worry when it snows.
translation_verse: Waaro maŋa ne o bá taa lwia o diga tiina ŋwaane, kokuri to, ba maama jege gare-ŋonno se ba ma ba kwoli ba tete.

english_verse: She makes clothes to sell to the shop owners.
translation_verse: O sɔ gare-fefale de se vovwe mo o yeigi o pa pipiu tiina.

english_verse: She is strong and graceful, as well as cheerful about the future.
translation_verse: O ye nɔn-dɛɔ mo ye nɔɔna nege‑o. O maa ba lwia de kolo na wó ke jwa seeni to.

english_verse: She takes good care of her family and is never lazy.
translation_verse: O yɔɔre o chɛ de totoŋa mo, ye o nii o diga tiina baŋa ne lanyerane.

english_verse: Her children praise her, and with great pride her husband says,
translation_verse: O bia wó ke daane ba sɛ we o jege yu-ywoŋo. O baro de maa wó seini‑o o we:

english_verse: “There are many good women, but you are the best!”
translation_verse: “Kaana dedɛ ke wo-kura. Nmo nam mo di yiga ba maama wone.”

english_verse: Charm can be deceiving, and beauty fades away, but a woman who honors the Lord deserves to be praised.
translation_verse: Ya-tega wae ka gana, lam de nam wae de tia. Ko nam ná ye kaane wolo na kɔre Baŋa Wɛ to, kotu maŋe de zula mo.

english_verse: When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
translation_verse: Wolo na ye Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno to kwora mo tento. Wonto mo ye Pɛ David bu, o na di paare Jerusalem teo kom ne to. Dé yeiri wonnu kuri

english_verse: Nothing makes sense! Everything is nonsense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense!
translation_verse: Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno mo we: Dé bá wane dé ni wonnu tento maama kuri. Te kuri nim tiini de chana de gaale se dé lɔre.

english_verse: What is there to show for all of our hard work here on this earth?
translation_verse: Nabiina yaare de totoŋ-chɛɛra mo tega baŋa ne. Bɛ nyɔɔre mo ba nam nae ya baŋa ne?

english_verse: The sun comes up, the sun goes down; it hurries right back to where it started from.
translation_verse: Wɛ dem yeini de puli mo, ye de laam vo de zo. De nam ta wó ke lela mo se de jwoori de tole de veiŋa kam.

english_verse: The wind blows south, the wind blows north; round and round it blows over and over again.
translation_verse: Vio yeini ko dole ko vei kuri seeni, ye ko ta dole ko vei baŋa seeni. Vio kom nam ta vei yiga de kwaga mo ko kare ko vei konto mo taa.

english_verse: All rivers empty into the sea, but it never spills over; one by one the rivers return to their source.
translation_verse: Bu-tole sem maama duri se vei se lwoi se na bam naneo kom wone mo, ye naneo kom ba fɔge ko sui ko wɛɛla. Na bam daa maa yeini ba jwoori mo, ba vei bu-tole sem na buri mɛ to.

english_verse: All of life is far more boring than words could ever say. Our eyes and our ears are never satisfied with what we see and hear.
translation_verse: Woŋo maama yeini ko ke konto dwoŋi mo ye kweelim tera. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o ta ko kuri o ti. Nabiinu yia bá wane woŋo maama ya nii ya su. O zwa de nam bá wane ya cheigi wonnu maama ya su.

english_verse: Someone might say, “Here is something new!” But it happened before, long before we were born.
translation_verse: Woŋo kolo nɔɔna ná tɛ ko taane we, “Nii-na, wo-doŋo mo tento!” konto woŋo kom maŋe ko wora mo faŋa faŋa, ye ba wo loge debam.

english_verse: No one who lived in the past is remembered anymore, and everyone yet to be born will be forgotten too. It Is Senseless To Be Wise
translation_verse: Dé daa ba gula balo ya na wora faŋa kam ne to gula. Ko nam ná ye balo ba jwa na wó lo to, balo na tu banto kwaga ne to wó swei ba de swia. Amo na lɔre chega kalo to

english_verse: I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel.
translation_verse: Amo wolo na ye Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno to déem di Isarele tiina paare Jerusalem ne.

english_verse: If something is crooked, it can't be made straight; if something isn't there, it can't be counted.
translation_verse: Woŋo kolo ná gugwoli, ko tweem chamma mo. Wonnu telo maa na tera to ware se nɔɔno jeeli te ni.

english_verse: I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.”
translation_verse: Amo nam ya tage a tete ne a we, “Nii mo! Amo tiini a jege yi-poro a dwoi balo na maŋe ba di paare Jerusalem ne to maama. A ma jwoŋi swa de yeino dedɛ.”

english_verse: Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Amo seene a yia mo se a lɔre swa, se a ta lɔre jworim de chichwooru na ye tei to. A tu a maane we konto maama de nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja-ko tei to mo.

english_verse: The more you know, the more you hurt; the more you understand, the more you suffer.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno yi-poro na mae tei to, o lwia de mae konto mo. O yeino ná daga tei, o wo-chechɔgɔ de wó taa daga konto dwoŋi mo.

english_verse: Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do?
translation_verse: A ta maane we mwanno ye jworim mo. Kwɛɛra de ba jege nyɔɔre.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
translation_verse: A laam ma zo sa-nyɔre wone se a nyɔ a su a na wopwolo. A maa lage se a tɔge swa ŋwaane a boŋe a nii chwoŋa kɔ mo jege nyɔɔre se nɔɔna taa tɔge-ka ba logo baŋa ŋwea wone.

english_verse: I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards.
translation_verse: Amo déem ke totoŋ-zana yadwonna a pa a tete. A lɔge sam, ye a jeiri Vini teeni de.

english_verse: And I had pools where I could get water for the trees.
translation_verse: A ma ko buli se ba taa mɔɔne na da ba yage teeni dem se de be lanyerane.

english_verse: Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble. Wisdom Comes from God
translation_verse: A laam ma jeini a jeeli a kikia maama, dedaane a totoŋ-chɛɛra na pɛ-ne kolo maama to. A ma na we te ba jege kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo. A totoŋa yam maama ba jege nyɔɔre tega kam baŋa ne. Swa de jworim taane

english_verse: And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
translation_verse: Amo nam tu a maane we swa jege nyɔɔre ya dwoi jworim, se ko maŋe de pwooni na gare lim tei to.

english_verse: Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
translation_verse: Chega to, Swa tu yia wae ya na chwoŋa. Jworo maa wo lim wone o via. De ko maama de, a maane we swa tiina de jworru lage ba guri bedwe mo.

english_verse: Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense.
translation_verse: Amo laam ma ta a tete ne we, “Toone na wó ja jworo to, de lage de ba amo de baŋa mo. Bɛ nyɔɔre mo a nam nɛ a swa yam baŋa ne?” A ma leiri a tete ne we, “Amo bá wane a lɔre ko kuri”.

english_verse: Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
translation_verse: A nam ware se a lɔre konto tu wó taa ye swa tu mo naa jworo mo. O laam maa wó ba o jwoŋi kolo maama a totoŋ-chɛɛra de a swa na jaane te ba te pa-ne to, o taa tei. Ko maama ba jege kuri.

english_verse: I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed.
translation_verse: Amo na jeini a jeeli a totoŋ-chɛɛra yam maama na wó pa-ne nyɔɔre delo to, a wo pɛ ya ŋwaane.

english_verse: When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, dé wó kwei dé swa, de dé yeino, de dé boboŋa maama, dé toŋe taa se dé na wonnu. Bɛ laam nam mo tei se dé yage-te dé pa wolo na wo yaare te ŋwaane to? Ko maama ba jege kuri, se ko ye lɛɛro yerane mo.

english_verse: Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
translation_verse: Dɛ maama wone, dé totoŋa yeini ya ni debam ye lwia daane debam ya ŋwaane. Tete ne de, dé boboŋa maa kare ya beera. Ko maama ba jege kuri.

english_verse: The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us,
translation_verse: Kolo na tiini ko lamma ko pae nɔɔno to mo ye se o taa di wodiu, ye o nyɔa, se o daare o di ywoni o totoŋa yam baŋa ne. Amo nam maane we tento maama nwoŋi Wɛ tei ne mo.

english_verse: and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Wɛ ná wo woli, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware o na wodiu naa ywoni se o di.

english_verse: If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye nɔɔno wolo na ke o sui Wɛ yi to, Wɛ pae kotu swa, de yeino, de wopwolo mo. Ko daare, wɛleere-keira toŋe ba tiŋi se ba laam kwei ba pa balo kikia na sui Wɛ yi to mo. Konto de ba jege kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo.

english_verse: Everything on earth has its own time and its own season.
translation_verse: Woŋo maama logo baŋa ne jege ko maŋa mo. Maŋa tigi mo se dé toŋe totoŋe dwi maama.

english_verse: There is also a time for love and hate, for war and peace. What God Has Given Us To Do
translation_verse: Maŋa ta wora mo se nɔɔna taa swoi daane, ye kadwoŋi de wora se ba taa chuli daane. Jara-keim maŋa maa wora, ye bochare-zuru maŋa de wora.

english_verse: I have seen what difficult things God demands of us.
translation_verse: Amo maane Wɛ na kwei totoŋa yalo o pa nabiina se ba taa toŋe to.

english_verse: God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future.
translation_verse: Wɛ maa pae se wonnu maama ke lanyerane te maŋa ne chekke. O ma kwei boboŋa yalo na vei taa wuu seeni to o ke nabiina yuu ne. Konto maama wone nam, dé bá wane dé lɔre o na jege kolo o ke to maama dé ti.

english_verse: I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life,
translation_verse: Amo ma maane we kolo na lamma ko pae nɔɔna to ye se ba taa jege wopwolo ye ba tɔge chwo-laaro ba ŋwea wone mo.

english_verse: because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do.
translation_verse: Ko maŋe se ba taa di wodiu, ye ba nyɔa, se ba daare ba di ywoni ba totoŋa yam baŋa ne. Konto maama ye Wɛ pɛɛre mo.

english_verse: Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
translation_verse: Amo maane we Wɛ na ke wonnu telo maama to wora mo taa. Dé bá wane dé woli kolokolo o kikia yam wone, naa dé le kolokolo ya wone dé yage. O pɛ se ko taa ye konto mo se dé taa kɔre‑o.

english_verse: Everything that happens has happened before, and all that will be has already been— God does everything over and over again. The Future Is Known Only to God
translation_verse: Kolo zem na wora to maŋe ko ke maŋa kadwoŋi ne. Kolo na lage ko ke jwa ne to de maŋe ko wora mo. Wɛ maa beeri wonnu telo na maŋe te ke te kɛ to se o pa te jwoori te ke. Nabiina de vara ye bedwe mo na?

english_verse: So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good.
translation_verse: Amo ma ta a tete ne we, “Maŋa ná yia, Wɛ wó di nɔn-ŋona dedaane puseŋ-nyena maama taane, o na maŋe o tiŋi dɛ mo se wonnu maama de kikia maama ke te maŋa ne to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, debam nabiina de vara maama guri bedwe mo. Toone yeini de tui de jaane dé maama. Nabiina de vara siu ye bedwe mo. Konto to, nabiina ba gare vara. Chega to, ko maama ba jege kuri.

english_verse: All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth.
translation_verse: Wonnu maama ŋwe ye te guri bedwe mo. Kolo maama na ŋwe to nwoŋi tega kam teero wone mo, ye te maama nam wó jwoori te zo teero wone.

english_verse: Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth?
translation_verse: Wɔ mo wane o lɔre chekke we nabiina ná tega, ba diini wɛɛne mo, ko daare ye vara ná tega ba zoore tega kam kuri ne?”

english_verse: I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful.
translation_verse: Amo daa ta ma maane nabwona na tiini ba nae bɛɛsem logo baŋa jei maama ne tei to. Ba maa keeri bugi-bugi ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na wó wane o woli-ba pa se ba wo to. Balo na jege-ba ba bɛɛse to tiini ba dana lanyerane mo. Konto ŋwaane nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se o pa nabwona bam bochare zuri.

english_verse: I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living.
translation_verse: Amo laam maa boŋe we, balo na tega ye ba daa tera to gare balo ta na ŋwe ye ba yaare to.

english_verse: But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye chega, balo ba ta na wo loge to yuu mo ywomma ba dwoi maama, kolo ŋwaane banto ta wo nɛ lwarem kikia yalo na kare ya ke logo baŋa ne to.

english_verse: Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Amo ta maane we nɔɔna na yeini ba ma dam de yeino ba toŋe tei to maama ye ba dwoni daane mo. Ko maama ba jege kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo.

english_verse: Yet a very little food eaten in peace is better than twice as much earned from overwork and chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ná nɛ o wodiu bɔŋa dedoa ye o bochare zuri, konto gare o ná yaare de totoŋ-chɛɛra se o na bwɛ selei. Konto maama nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo. Badwoŋo taane

english_verse: Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense.
translation_verse: Amo daa ta ma maane woŋo kodwoŋi logo baŋa ne ko na ba jege kuri.

english_verse: For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life! It Is Better To Have a Friend
translation_verse: Amo nɛ we nɔɔno wodwoŋi wora o na ba jege fara, naa chorro, naa bia, ye o laam toŋe taa o ba jeini tega ne. O toŋe mo se o na jejegero ye o yi ba sui-te. Wonto nam jege se o bwei o tete we, “Wɔ mo lage o na nyɔɔre a totoŋ-chɛɛra yam baŋa ne? Amo ba di ywoni ya ŋwaane.” Konto maama de ba jege kuri. Cham yerane mo wora kotu ŋwea wone.

english_verse: You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn.
translation_verse: Balei gare dedoa. Kokuri, ba wó na nyɔɔre da-tei ne ba totoŋa yam baŋa ne.

english_verse: If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble.
translation_verse: Ba wone dedoa ná toa, wodwoŋi wom wó ja‑o se o zaŋe wɛɛne. Se ko ná ye nɔɔno dedoa o yerane ye o to, lɛɛro mo wó yi kotu, o dwoŋi na tera se o woli‑o se o zaŋe to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔno dedoa wae o mage o dwoŋi wolo na zaŋe o baŋa ne to o di. Ko nam ná ye nɔɔna balei mo jaŋe ded‑o, o yerane bá wane o mage-ba o di. Ŋona kalo na ŋoge kuni betɔ to ba kɔe mɔle-mɔle. Swa de paare taane

english_verse: You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice.
translation_verse: Nɔn-doŋo ná ye yiniga tu ye o jege swa, wonto gare pa-dwooru wolo na ve se nɔɔna bere‑o to.

english_verse: Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king.
translation_verse: Nɔn-doŋo kom wae o nwoŋi peena diga ne ye o laam ba o di paare, naa ba loge‑o yiniga wone o paare laŋa kam ne ye o daare o ji pɛ.

english_verse: I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone.
translation_verse: Amo ta ma maane nɔɔna balo maama na ŋwe logo baŋa ne to na kare ba ke tei ye ba pɛ nɔn-doŋo wodwoŋi kwaga ba pu. Wonto lage o ba o jeini pa-dwooru wom jeiŋa jei ne mo.

english_verse: His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Nɔn-kɔgɔ kolo na tɔge wonto kwaga to tiini ko daga ko gaale. Ba kwaga kam nam ná tua, ba wolowolo bá nege‑o. Ko maama de ba jege kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja tei to mo.

english_verse: Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship.
translation_verse: Nmo ná yeini n ma‑n zoore Wɛ diga se n zuli‑o, se n ja n tete. Fɔɔre n yi Wɛ tei se n cheigi o taane, se konto wó taa gare kaanem delo jworru na ke ye ba yeiri we ba tusi to.

english_verse: Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much.
translation_verse: Boŋe n yi se n laam ŋɔɔne n ni taane. Yé gwoni ni de Wɛ yɔɔ yɔɔ ye n wo fɔge n boŋe de wone. Lɔre lanyerane we Wɛ wo telaao ne mo ye nmo zoore tega kam baŋa ne. Konto ŋwaane nam pa se n ni taane dem taa ye fenfee yerane.

english_verse: If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
translation_verse: Boboŋ-fara pae se nɔɔno dwɛ dendwea ye ya daane‑o mo. Konto dwoŋi mo ta-fare dedɛ pae se nɔɔno tɛ wo-jworru.

english_verse: It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it.
translation_verse: Nmo ná wo gwoni ni se n ke woŋo, konto gare n ná tiŋi ni ye n laam kwane-de.

english_verse: Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
translation_verse: Yé pa se n ni taane ja‑m de zo wɛleere wone. Ta‑n cho n tete se n yé ta de Wɛ tontoŋeno we, “Amo wo maane mo ye a ta tento.” Kokuri to, Wɛ bane wae de zaŋe nmo baŋa ne n ŋɔŋa kam ŋwaane ye o daare o saare n totoŋa yam maama.

english_verse: Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
translation_verse: Dendwea dwi dwi wora. Boboŋ-yɔɔro de taana daga dedɛ. Nmo nam jege se n ta‑n kɔre Wɛ mo. Bɛɛsem taane

english_verse: Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do.
translation_verse: Nmo ná nɛ we chega ti teo kolo wone, ye ko dedɛɛra jege nabwona ba bɛɛsa pa se ba ware ba tete se ba jwoŋi, se n yé pa se ko so‑m. Ko nam na ye tei to, dedɛɛro maama jege o yiga tu na nii‑o to. Ko daare ye yiga tu maama de jege o yuu tu.

english_verse: And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
translation_verse: Ko ya maŋe se nɔɔno maama na nyɔɔre tega kam baŋa ne. Pɛ wom tete jege se o nii kare sem baŋa ne. Jejegero taane

english_verse: If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná tiini o lage sabu, kotu yi ba fɔge de sui de o na jege kolo to. Nɔɔno fera ná zo jejegero wone, o ŋweero ba yi‑o. Ko maama ba jege kuri.

english_verse: The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno jejegero na mae tei to, balo na jwoŋi te wone se ba di to de gaale konto mo. Kotu na nɛ nyɔɔre delo o jejegero baŋa ne to mo ye o yi na nɛ-te to yerane.

english_verse: If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
translation_verse: Tontoŋena ná toŋe taa ba ti, ye ba ná di wodi-fɔrɔ naa fenfee yerane, ba laam wae ba dɔ lanyerane tete ne. Ko nam ná ye naduna, ba ba yeini ba dɔ, ba jejegero tem boboŋa na daane-ba to ŋwaane.

english_verse: I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good.
translation_verse: Amo nam ta maane wo-chɛɔ kodwoŋi mo logo baŋa ne. Nadum mo ke o jejegero o ke daane pa se te wae te che‑o cham wone.

english_verse: Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children.
translation_verse: O jejegero tem laam ma jei wo-chɛɔ baŋa ne. O na loge bu wolo to daa ta wo nɛ woŋo se o taa tei.

english_verse: They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work.
translation_verse: Ba ná loge bu wolo maama, kotu nwoŋi o nu wone bwori mo. O ŋwea ná tu ka kweeli, o daa ta wó yage logo baŋa bwori mo. O ná maŋe o toŋe tei maama, o bá ja kolokolo o woli da o kɛ.

english_verse: Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
translation_verse: O ŋwea maama wone, lim dedaane wo-chechɔgɔ mo tɔge‑o. O maa yɔɔre o nae ban-zɔŋɔ, de jaweero, dedaane ni-kantɔgɔ yerane. Ywoni dim taane

english_verse: What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do.
translation_verse: Amo nam maane we ko lamma se dé taa di wodiu, ye dé nyɔa, se dé daare dé di ywoni dé totoŋ-chɛɛra yam dé na ke dé logo baŋa ŋwea kam wone to baŋa ne. Mo nyɔɔre delo Wɛ na pae debam to.

english_verse: Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye Wɛ na pae balo dum de jejegero to, o ta pa-ba pwola se ba di ywoni te baŋa ne, se ba jwoŋi ba ŋweero tem konto ye ba toŋe ba totoŋ-chɛɛra yam de wopwolo. Konto maama ye Wɛ pɛɛre mo.

english_verse: God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam ba jege se o fɔge o jeeli o ŋwea da yam na ye tei to, Wɛ na pae o yɔɔre o na wopwolo o totoŋa yam baŋa ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth.
translation_verse: Amo nam ta maane wo-chɛɔ kodwoŋi mo logo baŋa ne, ye ko daane nabiina jei maama ne.

english_verse: God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
translation_verse: Wɛ wae o pa nɔɔno dum, de jejegero, de zula, pa se kotu jege kolo maama na jege o fera to, ye o wae o vane kotu chwoŋa se o yé di-te. Nɔn-gaa mo wó ba o di te ywoni. Konto maama tiini ko ye wo-chɛɔ. A bá wane a lɔre ko kuri.

english_verse: You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial.
translation_verse: Nenɛɛne nɔɔno ná kwe o ja gaale ye o lo bia bi, kotu ná maŋe o ŋwe taa, ye o ná wo di ywoni o jejegero tem baŋa ne, bu-too wolo ba na loge zem to ta gare‑o.

english_verse: That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you,
translation_verse: Bu wom konto ta wo fɔge o na wea pwooni. O nam wo lɔre ŋwea na ye tei to. De konto de, o ta nɛ siu o dwoni nadum wom konto,

english_verse: even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
translation_verse: ko fɔge ko dae nɔɔno wom ŋwea ná yi bena morro telei ye o wo di ka ywoni. Ba maama kweelim ye bedwe mo. Ko dae konto na?

english_verse: We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied.
translation_verse: Nabiina totoŋa maama yɔɔre ya ye ba ni-wodiu ŋwaane mo. Ba nam ba fɔge ba nae se ko yi-ba.

english_verse: We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right.
translation_verse: Swa tu wó na nyɔɔre o dwoni jworo na? Nabwom de ná yei o na wó taa jaane o tete nɔɔna yia ne tei to, bɛ nyɔɔre mo o jega?

english_verse: It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: “Nɔɔno yi ná su de kolo maama o na jege to, konto gare o ná pɛ se o fera zo wo-gaa wone.” Konto de chana se dé lɔre ko kuri. Ko nye de nɔɔno na duri o zeili vio se o ja-ko tei to mo.

english_verse: Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us.
translation_verse: Kolo maama zem na wora to mo, Wɛ maŋe o tigisi-ko se ko taa jege ko yere. Nabiinu de yei o ŋwea chwoŋa na ye tei to. O bá wane o dwoni de wolo na dana o dwoi‑o to.

english_verse: The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk?
translation_verse: Kolo ŋwaane, nɔɔno ná tiini o ŋɔɔne dedɛ, vuvuga wó tiini ka tɔge da mo. Bɛ nyɔɔre mo o lage o na o ŋɔŋa kam baŋa ne?

english_verse: A good reputation at the time of death is better than loving care at the time of birth.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná beeri yere-ŋom, konto lana ko pa‑o ko gare terale nuga na tiini ka lana to. Nabiinu toone dɛ maa gare o lora dɛ dem.

english_verse: Choose sorrow over laughter because a sad face may hide a happy heart.
translation_verse: Nmo wo ná chɔge, konto gare n ná su de mwanno. Kokuri to, yi-nyɔna wae ya pae n bochare mo fɔge lanyerane.

english_verse: Foolish laughter is stupid. It sounds like thorns crackling in a fire.
translation_verse: Jworo ná puri mwanno, ko nye de sabare na to mini wone ye se parese yɔɔ tei to mo. Konto de ba jege kuri.

english_verse: Something completed is better than something just begun; patience is better than too much pride.
translation_verse: Totoŋe gurim mo gare de pulim jei. Nɔɔno ná wae o jaane o tete bochare, konto gare o ná bere o tete kamunim.

english_verse: It isn't wise to ask, “Why is everything worse than it used to be?”
translation_verse: Yé zaŋe n bwei nenɛɛne, “Bɛ mo ke ye faŋa kam gare leile?” Bwia yam konto nam ba tɔge swa boboŋa!

english_verse: Think of what God has done! If God makes something crooked, can you make it straight?
translation_verse: Nam maane Wɛ na ke tei maama to n nii! Wɛ ná pɛ se woŋo kolo gugwoli, wɔ mo wó wane o twe-ko?

english_verse: When times are good, you should be cheerful; when times are bad, think about what it means. God makes them both to keep us from knowing what will happen next. Some of Life's Questions
translation_verse: Wonnu ná tɔge chwo-laao te pa‑m, se n ta‑n jege wopwolo. Te nam daa ná vei gweeni, se n maane we Wɛ mo pae se lanyerane de cham tui, pa se nabiina yeiri kolo jwa na wó ke ko pa-ba to. Amo bá wane a lɔre wonnu kuri a ti

english_verse: I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper.
translation_verse: Amo maane wonnu dwi dwi dedɛ a ŋwea wone, ye a lɔre te kuri a ga. Nɔn-ŋom wora ye o wuuri o te de o na maŋe o tɔge chega tei to. Nɔn-balɔrɔ de maa wora o na yɔɔre o kwe o ja gaale ye o ta toŋe lwarem.

english_verse: Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool.
translation_verse: Nmo ta yé yɔɔre n ta‑n ke lwarem, naa se n ta‑n toŋe jworim. Nmo boŋe se n wuuri n te mo na?

english_verse: Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
translation_verse: Ko nam lana se n tɔge chwei selei sem konto. Kokuri to, nmo ná kɔre Wɛ n wonnu wó kwɛ mo se maama wone.

english_verse: Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
translation_verse: Swa tu yeini o nae dam o swa ŋwaane, se ko dwoni dedɛɛra fuga na nii ba teo baŋa ne.

english_verse: Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you.
translation_verse: Yé yɔɔre n sɛ kolo maama nɔɔna na wó ta to. N wae n ni we n tontoŋeno mo jege‑m o twea.

english_verse: I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me.
translation_verse: Amo ma kwaane se a tɔge swa ŋwaane a lɔre wonnu tem konto maama na ye tei to. A boboŋa ma ja se a jwoŋi swa. Amo nam maane we ko kuri chana ko dwoi se a lɔre.

english_verse: So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
translation_verse: Amo boboŋa laam ma ja se a zamese yeino ye a buŋi wonnu wone a nii se a ja swa, se a wane a lɔre wonnu na ye tei to. Amo ta maa lage se a lɔre bɛŋwaane mo lwarem kikia ye jworim yerane, ye jworim kikia de jege yiyirim.

english_verse: Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for.
translation_verse: Amo nam ta maane we, kaane wolo na lage o ja‑m ne o ye kalanchogo to mo chana o dwoi toone. O maa kwaane o kukwori‑m ne o na kwei chegero o ma vɔ‑m tei to. Balo nam na ke ba sui Wɛ yi to wó lu o jeŋa ne. O nam wó yɔɔre o ja wɛleere-keira mo.

english_verse: With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together,
translation_verse: Amo wolo na ye Wɛ kwor-tɛɛno to we, “Nii-na amo na buŋi wonnu wone mo fee fee se a laam ba a lɔre wonnu na ye tei to.

english_verse: but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman.
translation_verse: A nam na kwaane a beeri maama to, a gɛ ko ŋwa mo. Amo na beeri baara moro tetare ne to, mo a nɛ baaro dedoa na tɔge chega. Ko daare a wo nɛ kaane banto maama wone, de dedoa de!

english_verse: I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_verse: Woŋo kolo yerane amo na tu a lɔre mo tento: Wɛ ke nabiina pa se ba yɔɔre ba tɔge chwoŋa mo. Ba laam nam mo pɛ se vuvuga tui.”

english_verse: Who is smart enough to explain everything? Wisdom makes you cheerful and gives you a smile. Obey the King
translation_verse: Wɔ mo seene o ye swa tu chekke? Wɔ mo wae wonnu kuri o lɔra? Swa pae se nɔɔno yiga pwoli mo, ye yi-nyɔna daa ba jege‑o.

english_verse: If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise.
translation_verse: Ta‑n yei se n sɛ Pɛ wom ni, nmo na gwoni ni Wɛ yiga ne mo we, n wó ke konto to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?”
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Pɛ wom ni taane tiini de jege dam mo ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware se o bwei‑o we, “Bɛ mo ye n ke konto?”

english_verse: If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it.
translation_verse: Wolo nam ná toŋe o tɔge Pɛ wom ni, konto tu bá zo cham wone. Swa tu yeini o lɔre maŋa kalo na maŋe keim, dedaane chwoŋa kalo keim dem na wó tɔge to mo.

english_verse: Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything,
translation_verse: Kokuri to, woŋo maama jege ko maŋa mo, ye ko de jege ko chwoŋa mo se ko toŋe. Lɛɛro nam yeini te tui nabiina baŋa.

english_verse: We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil.
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware vio se o ja. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware o toone dɛ dem se o che. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware se o le o tete jara keim wone. Nmo ná toŋe lwarem kikia, ya bá wane ya jwoŋi‑m ya yage.

english_verse: I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another? Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
translation_verse: Amo na seene a yia a zamese wonnu tem konto maama to, mo a maane kolo maama na jege ko ke logo baŋa ne to. A ma na we maŋa de maŋa nɔɔno wae o tei o dwonna de dam pa se ba maama yaare. Dé ware dé lɔre Wɛ chwei sem

english_verse: I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense.
translation_verse: A ta nɛ puseŋ-nyena na tege ye ba suli-ba de zula to. Banto ya yeini ba vei Wɛ wara-jei sem, ye nɔɔna tei-ba teo kolo wone ba na ke ba puseŋa kikia da to. Ko maama ba jege kuri.

english_verse: When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna nam ná yeini ba ke lwarem ye ba wo waare-ba lela, konto pa se nabiina yɔɔre ba lage se ba de taa toŋe lwarem kikia mo.

english_verse: They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying: Everyone who lives right and respects God will prosper,
translation_verse: Chega to, wɛleere-keira wó wane ba toŋe lwarem kuni bi mo ye ba ta yɔɔre ba kwe ba ja gaale. Amo nam yei we, “Nmo ná kɔre Wɛ, wonnu wó yɔɔre chwoŋa te pa‑m, nmo na zuli‑o to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
translation_verse: Amo nam wó ta we, dé jege se dé di ywoni mo dé ŋwea kanto wone. Kolokolo daa tera logo baŋa ne ko na lana ko pae nabiina to, ko ná dae dé na wó taa di wodiu, ye dé nyɔa, ye dé di ywoni to yerane. Nɔɔno ná ke konto mo ye o toŋe o totoŋa, ko wó woli‑o o ŋwea wone, ne Wɛ na pɛ se o taa ye tei logo baŋa ne to.

english_verse: I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_verse: Amo laam ma maane Wɛ na ke tei to maama. Nɔɔno ná maŋe o kwaane tei maama se o ni ko kuri, o bá lɔre kolo maama na ke logo baŋa ne to kuri. O ná maŋe o ye swa tu ye o bere we o yei ko kuri, o nam ta yeiri.

english_verse: I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad.
translation_verse: Amo nam seene yia a boŋe wonnu tento maama wone se a lɔre te na ye tei to. A ma lɔre we nɔn-ŋona de swa tiina de ba kikia maama wo Wɛ jeŋa ne mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam yeiri kolo na wo yiga ne to, ne ko ná wó taa jege swono naa ko wó taa jege dono ko pa‑o.

english_verse: But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
translation_verse: Ko wó taa ye bedwe ko pa nɔɔno maama. Nabiina maama lage ba guri bedwe mo, ne ko ná ye nɔn-ŋona de puseŋ-nyena, naa balo na maŋe de Wɛ chullu tem to de balo na wo maŋe to, naa balo na ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ to de balo na ba ke-de to maama. Nɔn-laaro de wɛleere-keira gurim ye bedwe mo, ko ta woli de balo na gwoni ni de Wɛ to, de balo na ve se ba ke konto to.

english_verse: It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die.
translation_verse: Ko na ke tei logo baŋa ne konto to ye wo-chɛɔ mo, de nɔɔna maama gurim na ye bedwe tei to. Nabiina bochara nam ye lwarem yerane mo. Ba ta na ŋwe to, vuvuga mo su ba boboŋa. Ko kwaga ne ba laam ma te.

english_verse: As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
translation_verse: Wolo nam ta ná ŋwe logo baŋa ne, teena wo kotu tei ne mo. “Kukura kalo na ŋwe to gare nywoŋo kolo na tege to.”

english_verse: We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten.
translation_verse: Chega ŋwaane to, balo ta na ŋwe to yei we ba wó ba ba te. Ko nam ná ye twa bam, ba yeiri kolokolo ni ne. Nyɔɔre daa tera se ba jwoŋi, ye nɔɔna maŋe ba swei ba swia mo.

english_verse: Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
translation_verse: Ba na swoi wonnu tei to, de ba na chuli-te tei to, de ba fera na wo wonnu baŋa ne tei to laam jei mo fase. Ba daa ba jege totoŋe logo baŋa ne se ba tɔge ba ke. Ywoni dim taane

english_verse: So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do.
translation_verse: Nam ta‑n jege ywoni n di wodiu, se n daare n nyɔ sa-doora de wopwolo. Kokuri to, Wɛ yi maŋe de su n kikia yam konto.

english_verse: Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best.
translation_verse: Kwɛ n tete se n yeini n zo gare-pwonnu, se n daare n turi n yuu de nuga.

english_verse: Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth.
translation_verse: Ta‑n swoi n kaane se á ta‑á di ywoni daane n ŋwea da yam na ye kukua to maama wone. Mo pɛɛre delo Wɛ na pɛ‑m logo baŋa ne, se n wane n di ywoni n totoŋ-chɛɛra yam baŋa ne to.

english_verse: Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
translation_verse: Totoŋe delo maama n ná jege n toŋa, se n toŋe-de de n dam maama. Kokuri to, churu ne ba ba toŋa, ba nam ba boŋe boboŋa naa ba jege yeino, ye ba ta ba beeri swa dáane. Nmo nam lage n vo dáane mo. N bá‑n wane n che n tete de cham

english_verse: Here is something else I have learned: The fastest runners and the greatest heroes don't always win races and battles. Wisdom, intelligence, and skill don't always make you healthy, rich, or popular. We each have our own share of misfortune.
translation_verse: Amo daa ta tu a maane tento mo logo baŋa ne: Ko dae we balo na duri lela lela to mo wó di yiga durim kayuŋu kom ne. Ko dae we babɛ mo wó di jara yam. Ko nam dae swa tiina mo nae ba ni-wodiu. Ko ta dae yi-pore-nyena mo ye naduna, ye ko dae nɔn-yum mo na yiga-veiŋa. Ko nam na ye tei ko pae ba maama to, keim maama wó ke ko maŋa ne mo.

english_verse: None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap. Better To Be Wise than Foolish
translation_verse: Kokuri to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno yeiri maŋa kalo toone na wó ja‑o to. Ko nye de ba na kwei bora ba ma ja ywona tei to, naa ba na jaane zuna kalanchogo wone tei to mo. Toone de yeini de pɔpɔ de yi nabiina mo maŋa kalo na wo maŋe to wone. Swa gare dam

english_verse: Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me.
translation_verse: Amo ta ma maane woŋo kodwoŋi logo baŋa ne na yɔɔre ko bere-ne swa na ye tei to.

english_verse: It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls.
translation_verse: Te-balaŋa déem mo wora ye ko nɔn-bia ye fenfee yerane. Pa-kamunu ma la o jar-keira o vo se o kwaare jara de-ba. Pɛ wom ma pa se ba kaare teo kom ba pu, se ba daare ba lɔ taara ba sale ko kabiri sem teiŋa se ba wane ba zo ko wone.

english_verse: So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
translation_verse: Konto mo pɛ a lɔre we, swa lana ya gare dam. Nɔɔno nam ná ye yiniga tu ye o jege swa, nɔɔna wó gwooni o swa yam mo. Ba ba yeini ba sɛ kotu ni taane. Swa de jworim taane

english_verse: Words of wisdom spoken softly make much more sense than the shouts of a ruler to a crowd of fools.
