translation_verse: Swa tu ná ŋɔɔne tega tega ye n cheigi o ni taane, konto jege kuri ko gare pɛ ná bage de kwor-dɛa o bere nɔn-jworru.

english_verse: Wisdom is more powerful than weapons, yet one mistake can destroy all the good you have done.
translation_verse: Swa lana ya dwoi jara zela. Wɛleere-keiru dedoa nam wae o chɔge wo-laaro dedɛ na maŋe te tigi to.

english_verse: A few dead flies in perfume make all of it stink, and a little foolishness outweighs a lot of wisdom.
translation_verse: Nanjo-too ná to talwoŋ-ywoŋa nuga ne, ka wó pɔ mo ka lwoi. Konto dwoŋi mo nɔɔno jworim fenfee wó chɔge swa dedɛ.

english_verse: Sensible thoughts lead you to do right; foolish thoughts lead you to do wrong.
translation_verse: Swa tu boboŋa pae o yɔɔre chwoŋa mo. Jworo boboŋa nam pae o toŋe gweeni mo.

english_verse: Fools show their stupidity by the way they live; it's easy to see they have no sense.
translation_verse: O ná kwei chwoŋa o maa via, o bere o tete jaja we o ye jworo mo, o na tiini o ga boboŋa to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Don't give up your job when your boss gets angry. If you stay calm, you'll be forgiven.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom bane ná zaŋe nmo baŋa ne, yé zaŋe n nwoŋi o tei ne. Nmo ná jaane n wo, ko laam wó pa se o ban-lom dem zuri.

english_verse: They honor fools, but dishonor the rich;
translation_verse: Jworru mo yeini te jiri yiga tiina. Naduna de maa wo kwaga kwaga.

english_verse: they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
translation_verse: Amo ta ma na kabɛ na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne tei to, ko daare ye nakwa vei tega ne.

english_verse: If you dig a pit, you might fall in; if you break down a wall, a snake might bite you.
translation_verse: Wolo ná koge gwoŋo, kotu wó wane o jwoori o to ko wone. Wolo nam ná yare kabira o de tega ne, basankwea wó wane ka tɔge dáane ka done‑o.

english_verse: If you don't sharpen your ax, it will be harder to use; if you are wise, you'll know what to do.
translation_verse: Tontoŋeno dwooru ná ba jege ni, ye o ná wo dwori‑o, o totoŋa wó taa chamma mo. Swa nam wó pa nɔɔno totoŋa taa ke lanyerane.

english_verse: The power to charm a snake does you no good if it bites you anyway.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná jege liri se o ma o ja basankwea, ye ka ná wuuri ka done‑o, bɛ nyɔɔre mo liri tu wom wó na ko baŋa ne?

english_verse: If you talk sensibly, you will have friends; if you talk foolishly, you will destroy yourself.
translation_verse: Swa tu ni taane wó pa‑o zula mo. Jworo ni taane nam wó chɔge‑o mo zɔŋ-zɔŋ.

english_verse: Fools begin with nonsense, and their stupid chatter ends with disaster.
translation_verse: Kotu ná puri o ni, jworim yerane mo o ŋɔɔna. O ni taane dem yeini de kweeli de vuvuga yerane.

english_verse: A country is in for trouble when its ruler is childish, and its leaders party all day long.
translation_verse: Lɛɛro wó yi teo kolo pɛ na ye nɔn-doŋo ye o wo lɔre swa, ye ko nakwa yɔɔre ba di wodi-fɔrɔ zezeŋa maama ne to mo.

english_verse: Some people are too lazy to fix a leaky roof— then the house collapses.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno jawɔrɔ mo pae se o diga to ka vwi. O ná wo kwoni o diga lulua, ka wó taa lura mo taa.

english_verse: Share what you have with seven or eight others, because you never know when disaster may strike.
translation_verse: “Pɔɔre n jejegero n pa nɔɔna barepɛ naa nɔɔna nana, se n yeiri cham delo na wó yi‑m logo baŋa ne to.”

english_verse: Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce. Youth and Old Age
translation_verse: Zezeŋa ne se n nwoŋi n vo n bobo duum. Daa ta ta‑n toŋe n kara ne se tega laam ba ka yi. Kokuri to, n bá‑n wane n lɔre totoŋe delo na wó ke lanyerane to. Dɛ delo n totoŋa yam maama wó pa n na nyɔɔre. Ywoni taane

english_verse: Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun.
translation_verse: Tega baŋa pwooni mo jege ywoni. Nɔɔno yia ná nae wea kam pwooni, konto tiini ko lana mo ko pa‑o.

english_verse: Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno ná maŋe o kwe de bena dedɛ, ko maŋe mo se kotu di o ŋwea da yam maama ywoni. O nam yé swei we o lage o taa wo lim wone mo taa. Ko ná ye kolo maama jwa na wó ba ko ke to, dé bá wane dé lɔre ko kuri. Nɔn-donne taane

english_verse: Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
translation_verse: Nmo wolo na ye nɔn-doŋo to, nmo ta ná wo kwe, se n di n ŋwea kam ywoni. Ta‑n jege wopwolo n nɔn-donne maŋa ne. Pa se n boboŋa de n yia taa bere‑m chwoŋa kalo n na wo tɔge to. Nam ta‑n yei we, nmo ná tɔge chwoŋa kalo maama, Wɛ wó di n taane ko baŋa ne.

english_verse: Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_verse: Yé sɛ se lwia zo n boboŋa, se kolokolo de yé pa n yera chɛ. Kokuri to, dé nɔn-donne maŋa kam ba dáane ye ka tia.

english_verse: Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
translation_verse: Ta‑n guli wolo na naane‑m to gula nmo nɔn-donne maŋa ne. Ke konto ye cham maŋa ta wo yi‑m, se n laam ta nenɛɛne, “Amo daa ba ni ŋwea ywoni.”

english_verse: Someday the light of the sun and the moon and the stars will all seem dim to you. Rain clouds will remain over your head.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne wea kam, de chana kam, de chalechwe sem pwooni daa bá taa nae te pa‑m, ye woŋo maama ye lim mo. Do-kunkwonnu de maa wó jwoori te li tega kam.

english_verse: The noisy grinding of grain and the voices of singers will be shut out by your deaf ears, but even the song of a bird will keep you awake.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne, ba wó che manchwoŋo ni dem. Nɔŋɔ kom sɔɔ daa bá taa ni teo wone. Zuŋa dedoa tete ná keeri tete ne, nmo wó zaŋe dɔɔm wone lela. Lenlɛ kwori nam daa bá to n zwa wone.

english_verse: You will be afraid to climb up a hill or walk down a road. Your hair will turn as white as almond blossoms. You will feel lifeless and drag along like an old grasshopper. We each go to our eternal home, and the streets here are filled with those who mourn.
translation_verse: Ka maŋa ne, nmo wó ta‑n kɔre foone de wɛyuu diinim. Lwia maa wó taa jege‑m n veiŋa wone. Alimodi tio kom maa wó kwi punnu na peere to cha. Manchwanno de wó gwane tega ne mɛmɛ. Nmo fera maama wó ti. Kokuri to, ko gɛ fee se n vo n yi n wɛyuu sɔŋɔ kom. Ba laam maa wó taa keeri lua bugi-bugi jei maama ne.

english_verse: The silver cord snaps, the golden bowl breaks; the water pitcher is smashed, and the pulley at the well is shattered.
translation_verse: Nam guli n Keiro wom gula ye lu-nyenno chaponno tem ta wo kɔge, ye sabu-seŋa na-zoŋa kam de wo lɔge. Ke konto ye gwoŋo kom ta wo chɔge vole dem seeni se ko pae ba daa yé wane na ba mɔ.

english_verse: Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
translation_verse: Kwor-tɛɛno wom ma seene o yia o lage botare-bia balo na maŋe to, ye o tɔge chega baŋa o popone taane delo na ye chekke to.

english_verse: Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together.
translation_verse: Swa tu ni taane nye de gwoli mo nayero na jege o yere o vara. Kotu bera yam nye de chena yalo na fɔge ya chwi daa yera ne to mo. Ya maama nwoŋi nayero dedoa tei ne mo.

english_verse: My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these. There is no end to books, and too much study will wear you out.
translation_verse: Amo bu, kolo ta na woli da to mo ye se n ta‑n yei n tete de wonnu tento: nmo ná kwaane n popone swa taana n tiŋi, n totoŋa yam bá ti. Nmo ná tiini n zamese wonnu dedɛ, ko wó bogese‑m mo.

english_verse: Everything you were taught can be put into a few words: Respect and obey God! This is what life is all about.
translation_verse: Dé laam na nigi wonnu maama to, taane dem gurim jei mo tento: Ta‑n kɔre Wɛ, se n daare n ta‑n toŋe n tɔge o nia yam. Konto yerane ŋwaane mo nabiina wora.

english_verse: God will judge everything we do, even what is done in secret, whether good or bad.
translation_verse: Wɛ nam wó di dé taane dé kikia maama baŋa ne, ko ná ye keim-laaro, de keim-balwaaro, de yalo dé na seigi dé ke to de maama.

english_verse: and you smell so sweet. All the young women adore you; the very mention of your name is like spreading perfume. *
translation_verse: Nmo yera terale nuga kam lwom mo tiini ko ywomma. N yere dem ywomma ne ba na lwogi talwoŋ-ywoŋa pa se ka lwom jage jei maama ne tei to. Konto ŋwaane mo bukwa maama wó taa swoi‑m.

english_verse: Hurry, my king! Let's hurry. Take me to your home. The Young Women Speak: We are happy for you! And we praise your love even more than wine. She Speaks: Young women of Jerusalem, it is only right that you should adore him.
translation_verse: Nam ja-ne se dé ke lela dé lage jei dé vo! Pɛ, nam ja-ne n zo n diga kam wone. Jerusalem bukwa bam: Dé wó taa chaka mo de wopwolo nmo ŋwaane. Dé wó tei n swono kom we, ko ywoni lana ko dwoi sana ywoni. Bukɔ wom: Chega ŋwaane to, ko maŋe se bukwa bam taa swoi‑m.

english_verse: My darling, I love you! Where do you feed your sheep and let them rest at noon? Don't let the other shepherds think badly of me. I'm not one of those women who shamelessly follow after shepherds. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Amo bochɔŋɔ, ta n bere-ne mɛ seeni n na yeini n kale n vara bam n vei to, de jei selo nmo na pae ba sii wea tetare ne to. Ko dae se a taa tole a beera nayero de nayero pei-kɔgɔ maama wone. Nɔn-doŋo kom:

english_verse: You move as gracefully as the pony that leads the chariot of the king.
translation_verse: Amo bochɔŋɔ, nmo nye de sisein-nɔɔno wolo ba na kwɛ ka yera se ka vaŋe Ejipti pa-faro wom toroko to mo.

english_verse: Let's make you some jewelry of gold, woven with silver. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nam pa se dé ke sabu-seŋa zwa-kwana mo dé pa‑m, ye dé kwei lu-nyenno dé ma dé gɔgere ya maama. Bukɔ wom:

english_verse: My king, while you were on your couch, my aroma was a magic charm.
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo amo pɛ wom na tigi o jaŋgɔŋɔ kom baŋa ne to, mo talwoŋ-ywoŋa kalo a na ke a yera ne to lwom jage jei maama ne.

english_verse: you are flower blossoms from the gardens of En-Gedi. He Speaks:
translation_verse: O ta nye de ga-pun-laaro telo lwom na ywomma ye ba gwoni-te En-gedi Vini kare sem ne to. Nɔn-doŋo kom:

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— your eyes are those of a dove. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Amo bochɔŋɔ, nii n na tiini n lana tei! N yibia tiini ka lana dedɛ! N yia lam jege fera ne kunkwona mo tei. Bukɔ wom:

english_verse: My love, you are handsome, truly handsome— the fresh green grass will be our wedding bed
translation_verse: A bɔɔlo, nmo yɔɔre n ye lanno mo! Amo bere a ba nii‑m a sui. Dé na tigi ywo-seeni to ga-zuru mo pugi dé vwei dem.

english_verse: I am merely a rose from the land of Sharon, a lily from the valley. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Amo nye de ga-puŋu kolo na puli Saron jei sem ne to mo, de kantɔgele delo na puli bwolo tega ne to. Nɔn-doŋo kom:

english_verse: You led me to your banquet room and showered me with love.
translation_verse: O jaane-ne o zo diga kalo wone ba na di ywoni da to. O ma yɔɔre o kwoli-ne de o swono.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: O ma kwei o jagwia kam o teili a yuu, se o daare o ma o jazem dem o kukwori-ne.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles never to awaken love before it is ready. Winter Is Past She Speaks:
translation_verse: Jerusalem teo bukwa bam, da-na wei dedaane feiri dam ŋwaane á du-na duuri we abam bá gigili debam yia de dé swono kom. Nam pa-na debam chwoŋa se dé toŋe dé fera. Leiŋa

english_verse: I hear the voice of the one I love, as he comes leaping over mountains and hills
translation_verse: Amo nigi a bɔɔlo wom kwora. Nii o na beene tei! O yɔɔre o nɔne peero de zwonnu tem yuu ne mo o faŋe o beene.

english_verse: like a deer or a gazelle. Now he stands outside our wall, looking through the window
translation_verse: A bɔɔlo wom nye de feira naa woŋ-pɔla mo. Nii o na zege bira-kwaga ne, ye o tɔge takworo ne o leesi o nii diga wone tei.

english_verse: and speaking to me. He Speaks: My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: O laam maa ŋɔɔne de amo o we: “Amo bochɔŋɔ, nmo wolo yibia na lana amo yiga ne to, ba se dé tɔge daane dé kɛ.

english_verse: Winter is past, the rain has stopped;
translation_verse: Nii mo! Waaro maŋa kam kɛ, doa kam de maa kɔ nenem.

english_verse: flowers cover the earth, it's time to sing. The cooing of doves is heard in our land.
translation_verse: Ga-punnu laam mo faare tega kam jei maama. Ko laam ye maŋa mo se dé leeni lei. Kunkwona keira laam mo zaŋe dé tega kam jei maama ne.

english_verse: Fig trees are bearing fruit, while blossoms on grapevines fill the air with perfume. My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: Kaporro tem bobo se te taa ke mɔɔro. Vini teeni dem de maa kwi punnu ye te lwom zaŋe jei maama ne. Konto ŋwaane, a bɔɔl-swono, pa dé lage jei dé vo.” Nɔn-doŋo kom:

english_verse: You are my dove hiding among the rocks on the side of a cliff. Let me see how lovely you are! Let me hear the sound of your melodious voice.
translation_verse: Nmo wolo na ye amo kunkwoŋa kam ye n seigi peero gugworru wone to, nam nwoŋi se a na n yibia, se a daare a ni n kwora. Kokuri, nmo yibia kam tiini ka lana mo, ye n kwora kam de ywomma lanyerane. Bukɔ wom:

english_verse: My darling, I am yours, and you are mine, as you feed your sheep among the lilies.
translation_verse: A bɔɔlo wom ye amo nyem mo, ye amo maama de ye wonto nyem. O laam maa yɛ kantɔgela yam wone.

english_verse: While in bed at night, I reached for the one I love with heart and soul. I looked for him, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Tete maama ne mo a tigi a sara ne ye a boŋe a na swoi wolo to boboŋa taa. A maa beeri o jei ye a wo nɛ‑o.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles, never to awaken love before it is ready. The Groom and the Wedding Party Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Jerusalem teo bukwa bam, da-na wei dedaane feiri dam ŋwaane á du-na duuri we, abam bá gigili debam yia de dé swono kom. Nam pa-na debam chwoŋa se dé toŋe dé fera. Leiŋa

english_verse: It is King Solomon carried on a throne, surrounded by sixty of Israel's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Nii mo! Ko ye Pɛ Solomon mo ba zeŋe ba via, ye Isarele jar-keira babɛ sem fuseredo laam gilimi‑o.

english_verse: Its posts are silver, the back is gold, and the seat is covered with purple cloth. You women of Jerusalem have taken great care to furnish the inside.
translation_verse: Ba kwei lu-nyenno mo ba kwoli dɛ selo na teili yituŋu kom to, ye ba ma sabu-seŋa ba ke ko kuri dem seeni. Ko ná ye jeiŋa jei sem tete, ba kwei gare-nasoŋ-pupwia mo ba gɔgere ba kwoli da. Jerusalem teo bukwa mo zuri ba yera ba kwɛ ko wo kom maama.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— as you look through your veil, your eyes are those of a dove. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Nii nmo na tiini n lana tei, amo bochɔŋɔ! Nmo yibia lana dedɛ ka pa-ne! Nmo ná mɛ gare-fefala n kwoli n yibia, n yia yam lana ne kunkwona to mo. Nmo yu-ywei sem zwora lanyerane nenɛɛne bone na zege Gilead peero tem yuu ne de faŋe de maa tu tega tei to mo.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely in every way.
translation_verse: Amo bochɔŋɔ, n yɔɔre n lana mo se ko gaale, ye gɛɛ tera de fenfee de.

english_verse: My bride, together we will leave Lebanon! We will say goodbye to the peaks of Mount Amana, Senir, and Hermon, where lions and leopards live in the caves.
translation_verse: Amo katɔgɔ, pa dé yage Lebanon peero jei sem! Zege dáane yiga yiga n ba amo tei. Zege Amana peo kom yuu ne, de Senira peo kom, de Heremon peo kom yuu ne, n tu n ba. Yage jei sem konto de gugworru tem konto, se nywonnu de gweera mo zoore da.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you have stolen my heart! With one glance from your eyes and the glow of your necklace, you have stolen my heart.
translation_verse: Amo bochɔŋɔ de a katɔgɔ tete, nmo mo yɔɔre n jei a bochare ne. Ko nam ye n na dole n yi bedwe n nii-ne tei to, de n ba zambili dem kandwɛ-nyeno dedoa na nyeene tei to mo n mɛ n gane a bochare n wane.

english_verse: Your arms are vines, covered with delicious fruits and all sorts of spices— henna, nard,
translation_verse: Nmo yera yam nye de teeni dedɛ mo puli da, de na leiri Pomegara tio-bia na ywomma to. Talwoŋ-ywoŋa de pun-laaro telo lwom na ywomma to de maa wora.

english_verse: You are a spring in the garden, a fountain of pure water, and a refreshing stream from Mount Lebanon. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nmo yɔɔre n ye buli-yi delo na tigi gaare wone to mo. Buli-yi dem konto buri bu-dura mo, ye ka na bam nwoŋi Lebanon peero tem seeni ba duri ba tole ba via. Bukɔ wom:

english_verse: Let the north wind blow, the south wind too! Let them spread the aroma of my garden, so the one I love may enter and taste its delicious fruits.
translation_verse: Vio kolo na nwoŋi baŋa seeni to, zaŋe n ta‑n dola! Tega-kuri seeni vio kom de zaŋe ko ba! Pa se ko taa dole amo gaare dem ne, se a gaare dem lwom jage de yi jei maama. Pa se a bɔɔlo wom zo o gaare dem wone, se o di de wo wo-bi-laaro tem maama.

english_verse: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
translation_verse: Amo ya na tigi a dɔ to, a boboŋa ba dɔa. A laam ma ni we a bɔɔlo wom tua ye o dɔne manchwoŋo ni dem! O maa tɛ o we, “Amo bochɔŋɔ, pore diga kam n pa-ne, nmo wolo na ye amo kunkwoŋa ye gɛɛ tera n yera ne to. Amo yu-ywei sem yɔɔre se bugi mo de nyɔnɔ.”

english_verse: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
translation_verse: A bɔɔlo wom twe o jeŋa mo se o pore diga kam ni. Konto maa pae se a bochare yɔɔre de zaga dedɛ.

english_verse: And I yearned for him while he spoke to me, but when I opened the door, my darling had disappeared. I searched and shouted, but I could not find him— there was no answer.
translation_verse: A ma pore diga kam a pa a bɔɔlo wom, de o na pipiri o viiri o daare-ne to de. Amo lage a beiri mo de o na jei to. A ma nwoŋi a beeri o jei a ga. A maa tɔɔle a bwoi o yere. O nam wo leiri-ne.

english_verse: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.
translation_verse: Balo na yere teo kom tete ne to de maa kare ba via. Ba maa na nɛ amo to, ba ma mage-ne ye ba ke-ne zonne. Ba ta ma vere a gare-wogo kom. Ko ye teo kom kabiri yerena bam mo ke konto!

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Jerusalem teo bukwa bam, du-na duuri we, abam ná nɛ a bɔɔlo wom, á wó ta á bere‑o we a lage a beiri mo a fera na wo o swono kom wone to ŋwaane. Á bá sɛ se á ke konto na? Jerusalem teo bukwa bam:

english_verse: Most beautiful of women, why is the one you love more special than others? Why do you ask us to tell him how you feel? She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nmo wolo na lana n dwoi kaana maama to, bɛ mo pɛ se n boŋe we n bɔɔlo wom mo gare nenɔna maama? Bɛ mo pɛ se n pa debam ni se dé kwei dé pa‑o? Bukɔ wom:

english_verse: He is handsome and healthy, the most outstanding among ten thousand.
translation_verse: Amo bɔɔlo yɔɔre o ye lanno mo, ye o yibia nyeena. O ta maa zege mare-mare nɔɔna moro tetare ne.

english_verse: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven.
translation_verse: O yibia lam nye de sabu-seŋa mo chekke. O yu-ywei sem maa bobwale, ye se laam zwora ne badunu na ye tei to.

english_verse: His kisses are sweet. I desire him so much! Young women of Jerusalem, he is my lover and friend.
translation_verse: O ni dem tete mo tiini de sona. A fera maa yɔɔre ya tigi o wone. Jerusalem bukwa bam, amo bɔɔlo wom mo tento. Wonto nam mo ye amo badwoŋ-chɛɔ.

translation_verse: A ma pore diga kam a pa a bɔɔlo wom, de o na pipiri o viiri o daare-ne to de. Amo lage a beiri mo de o na jei to. A ma nwoŋi a beeri o jei a ga. A maa tɔɔle a bwoi o yere. O nam wo leiri-ne.

english_verse: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.
translation_verse: Balo na yere teo kom tete ne to de maa kare ba via. Ba maa na nɛ amo to, ba ma mage-ne ye ba ke-ne zonne. Ba ta ma vere a gare-wogo kom. Ko ye teo kom kabiri yerena bam mo ke konto!

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Jerusalem teo bukwa bam, du-na duuri we, abam ná nɛ a bɔɔlo wom, á wó ta á bere‑o we a lage a beiri mo a fera na wo o swono kom wone to ŋwaane. Á bá sɛ se á ke konto na? Jerusalem teo bukwa bam:

english_verse: Most beautiful of women, why is the one you love more special than others? Why do you ask us to tell him how you feel? She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nmo wolo na lana n dwoi kaana maama to, bɛ mo pɛ se n boŋe we n bɔɔlo wom mo gare nenɔna maama? Bɛ mo pɛ se n pa debam ni se dé kwei dé pa‑o? Bukɔ wom:

english_verse: He is handsome and healthy, the most outstanding among ten thousand.
translation_verse: Amo bɔɔlo yɔɔre o ye lanno mo, ye o yibia nyeena. O ta maa zege mare-mare nɔɔna moro tetare ne.

english_verse: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven.
translation_verse: O yibia lam nye de sabu-seŋa mo chekke. O yu-ywei sem maa bobwale, ye se laam zwora ne badunu na ye tei to.

english_verse: His kisses are sweet. I desire him so much! Young women of Jerusalem, he is my lover and friend.
translation_verse: O ni dem tete mo tiini de sona. A fera maa yɔɔre ya tigi o wone. Jerusalem bukwa bam, amo bɔɔlo wom mo tento. Wonto nam mo ye amo badwoŋ-chɛɔ.

english_verse: My darling has gone down to his garden of spices, where he will feed his sheep and gather lilies.
translation_verse: Amo bɔɔlo wom laam tu o wo o gaare dem wone mo, mɛ ba na dugi dwoa-bia balo lwom na ywomma to. O maa beeri gaare dem wone ye o lae kantɔgela o ke daane.

english_verse: I am his, and he is mine, as he feeds his sheep among the lilies. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Amo maama ye a bɔɔlo wom nyem mo, ye o de yɔɔre o ye amo nyem. O laam maa yɛ kantɔgela yam wone. Leiŋa

english_verse: My dearest, the cities of Tirzah and Jerusalem are not as lovely as you. Your charms are more powerful than all of the stars in the heavens.
translation_verse: Amo bochɔŋɔ, nmo lam dem yɔɔre de nwoŋi mo, ne Tiraza teo na ye tei to. Nmo yibia lana mo, ne Jerusalem teo kom na ye tei to. Nmo yɔɔre n jege nenɔŋa dedɛ, ne chalechwe sem na bere jaja tei to.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: Nmo yeila yam peere cha ne pei kɔgɔ ba na swɛ-se pa se peere tei to mo. Ya maama maŋe daane mo, ye dedoa tete wo sage de chwoŋa.

english_verse: What if I could have sixty queens, eighty wives, and thousands of others!
translation_verse: Pɛ ná maŋe o di kaana fuseredo, dedaane ka-bi funɔnɔ, ye busankan-pwoli moro ná wo o tei ne de,

english_verse: “You are as majestic as the morning sky— glorious as the moon— blinding as the sun! Your charms are more powerful than all the stars above.” She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ba maa we: “Wɔ mo tento na yɔɔre o ye jase ne tega na jege ka poore to? Wonto lam nam nye de chana kam na peere tei, ye o pae pwooni ne wea kam. O ta maa jege nenɔŋa dedɛ, ne chalechwe sem na bere jaja tei to.”

english_verse: But in my imagination I was suddenly riding on a glorious chariot. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Amo boboŋa laam ma vugimi wopwolo ŋwaane. Ko ke-ne nenɛɛne a jei pa-bu saŋa ne mo, ye sisein-nɔɔna vaŋe debam de torokooro se via.

english_verse: Dance! Dance! Beautiful woman from Shulam, let us see you dance! She Speaks: Why do you want to see this woman from Shulam dancing with the others?
translation_verse: Sulam tiina bukɔ, jwoori n ba ywo-seeni! Ba ywo se dé wane dé taa nii nmo! Bukɔ wom: Bɛ mo ye á lage á nii wolo na ba jege gɛɛ to, ne o na tɔge kɔgɔ kuni belei tetare ne o sae to?

english_verse: You are a princess, and your feet are graceful in their sandals. Your thighs are works of art, each one a jewel;
translation_verse: Nmo ye pɛ bukɔ mo chekke. N nɛ sem de se natera jege lam dedɛ. Nmo chwoa yam jege fera ne kandwa-nyenno mo tei. Ya maa nye de gɔgɔ mo mɔɔne-ya.

english_verse: your navel is a wine glass filled to overflowing. Your body is full and slender like a bundle of wheat bound together by lilies.
translation_verse: Nmo wuri dem nye de zoŋa mo na maŋe se ka taa sui de sa-sona maŋa maama! Nmo puga kam nye de men-pwei mo ba tigisi ba tiŋi, ye kantɔgela laam kaare ya maama ya pu.

english_verse: Your breasts are like twins of a deer.
translation_verse: Nmo yela yɔɔre ya maŋe daane mo chekke, nenɛɛne feiri selei na vei daane tei to.

english_verse: Your neck is like ivory, and your eyes sparkle like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-Rabbim. Your nose is beautiful like Mount Lebanon above the city of Damascus.
translation_verse: Nmo ba dem yɔɔre de dɔra nenɛɛne di-dedɔrɔ ba na mɛ tuu yeila ba ke to mo. N yia yam de maa nye de Hesebon chwaro tem na tigi Baf-Rabim ni dem seeni to. N momwɛ dem lam nye de Lebanon di-dedɔrɔ kolo na tole ko nae Damasika teo seeni to mo.

english_verse: I will climb that tree and cling to its branches. I will discover that your breasts are clusters of grapes, and that your breath is the aroma of apples.
translation_verse: Amo laam wó di konkwara kam yuu mo, se a yi ka tio-bia na leigi mɛ to. Ta pa se n yela yam taa nye de tio bi-zwaro telo Vini tio na ke to. Nmo ná sii n yera vio, a swoi se ko lwom taa ywomma ne kaligwoŋo tio-bia lwom na ye tei to mo.

english_verse: My darling, I am yours, and you desire me.
translation_verse: Amo maama ye a bɔɔlo wom nyem mo, ye o de fera yɔɔre ya wo amo wone.

english_verse: At dawn let's slip out and see if grapevines and fruit trees are covered with blossoms. When we are there, I will give you my love.
translation_verse: Dé laam maa wó gwoni tega dé vo dé zo Vini teeni kare sem wone, se dé nii de kwi vɔɔro de punnu na? Dé ta wó daare dé nii Pomegara teeni dem ke punnu na? Dáane mo amo wó kwei a tete a pa‑m se ko bere a swono.

english_verse: Perfume from the magic flower fills the air, my darling. Right at our doorstep I have stored up for you all kinds of tasty fruits.
translation_verse: Mandaraka ga-punnu tem lwom mo jwoŋi jei sem maama. Tio-bia dwi dwi mo tigi dé diga kam ni ne! A bɔɔlo, a kwaleme te maama a tiŋi a pa nmo, se n wane n di te ywoni.

english_verse: If you were my brother, I could kiss you whenever we happen to meet, and no one would say I did wrong.
translation_verse: Ne n ya ná ye a nabɔ wolo na ŋɔge a tete nu yele to, ye dé ná jeeri daane jei selo maama ne, a ya wó mu n ni mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá ta we a ke a chɔge.

english_verse: I could take you to the home of my mother, who taught me all I know. I would give you delicious wine and fruit juice as well.
translation_verse: A ya wó ja‑m se dé tɔge daane dé vo sɔŋɔ, ye dé zo diga kalo wone a nu na kɔne-ne to. A laam wó kwei sa-sona de amo Pomegara tio-bia nyoa bam se n nyɔ n su.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: O ma kwei o jagwia kam o teili a yuu, se o daare o ma o jazem dem o kukwori-ne.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me never to awaken love before it is ready. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Jerusalem teo bukwa bam, du-na duuri we abam bá gigili debam yia de dé swono kom. Nam pa-na debam chwoŋa se dé toŋe dé fera mo. Kweelim taane Jerusalem teo bukwa bam:

english_verse: Who is this young woman coming in from the desert and leaning on the shoulder of the one she loves? She Speaks: I stirred up your passions under the apple tree where you were born.
translation_verse: Busankana kɔ mo tento o zege kagoa seeni o beene, ye o sale o bɔɔlo wom yera ne? Bukɔ wom: Kaligwoŋo tio kom kuri ne, mo a pepage‑m se n zaŋe. Ko ye dáane mo n nu déem jaane n puga. Jei sento ne mo o ta virigi n puga ye o lo‑m.

english_verse: We have a little sister whose breasts are not yet formed. If someone asks to marry her, what should we do?
translation_verse: Dé jege dé nakɔ balaŋa, o ta na wo yi se o mage yela. Ne nɔɔno ná tu o we o lage‑o se o di o ke kaane, dé laam wó ke tɛ mo?

english_verse: She isn't a wall that we can defend behind a silver shield. Neither is she a room that we can protect behind a wooden door. She Speaks:
translation_verse: O ya ná ye kabira, dé wó kwei lu-nyenno mo dé ma dé lɔ dé daŋe o baŋa ne. O nam ya ná ye diga ni bworo, dé wó kwei Sedare da-ŋonno mo dé ma dé kwoli o yera se ya kwɛ. Bukɔ wom:

english_verse: I am a wall around a city, my breasts are towers, and just looking at me brings him great pleasure.
translation_verse: Amo seene a ye kabira mo. A yela yam nam nye de di-dedwaaro na zege choraam to mo. Konto ŋwaane mo a kikia laam su a bɔɔlo wom yi.

english_verse: Solomon has a vineyard at Baal-Hamon, which he rents to others for a thousand pieces of silver each.
translation_verse: Solomon déem jege Vini teeni gaare Baal-hamon ne. O ma kwei-de o jene o pa nɔɔna se ba dedoa dedoa yeini ba taa pa‑o lu-nyenno sabu-dala moro de tio-bia bam ŋwaane.

english_verse: You are in the garden with friends all around. Let me hear your voice! She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nmo wolo na kare n beeri gaare dem wone ye n yuudwonna wo n tei ne ba cheigi nmo kwora to, pa se amo de ni n kwora! Bukɔ wom:

english_verse: I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz. And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah: A Guilty Nation
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem veere wonnu tento na tɛ Judah de Jerusalem taane to o bere Amozi bu Izaya mo. Ko nam ye maŋa kalo Yuzia, de Jotam, de Ahaz, de Hezekia na di Judah teo paare ba saŋe da-kwaga to mo. Baŋa Wɛ vaŋe o nɔɔna bam zwa

english_verse: The Lord has said, “Listen, heaven and earth! The children I raised have turned against me.
translation_verse: Wɛyuu cheigi! Tega baŋa de cheigi! Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Amo kɔne a bia mo, ye a nii ba baŋa ne. Ba nam nwoŋi a kwaga ne.

english_verse: Why be punished more? Why not give up your sin? Your head is badly bruised, and you are weak all over.
translation_verse: Bɛ mo ye á ta yɔɔre á ke zwabania kikia? Á ba kɔre se Wɛ waare abam na? Abam yuni su de fufwollu mo, ye á bochara yam wone de, yazura tera.

english_verse: From your head to your toes there isn't a healthy spot. Bruises, cuts, and open sores go without care or oil to ease the pain. A Country in Ruins
translation_verse: Ko na zege á yuni ne se ko taa tu á napera kuri ne to, yazura tera á yera yam wone. Fufwollu, de kalwanno, de ŋɔn-zana yerane mo wora. Abam nam ba zare á ŋɔna yam, se á vɔ-ya. Á ma á ba ke liri ya wone se ya jei ya pa abam.

english_verse: Zion would have disappeared like Sodom and Gomorrah, if the Lord All-Powerful had not let a few of its people survive. Justice, Not Sacrifices
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ya ná wo daare debam badaara se dé wori, debam de ya wó chɔge dé ti, ne ko déem na ke Sodom teo tiina tei to mo. Dé ya ta maa wó ji ne Gomora teo déem na ye tei to.

english_verse: You are no better than the leaders and people of Sodom and Gomorrah! So listen to the Lord God:
translation_verse: Nam cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ taane dem, abam balo na ba gare Sodom teo dedɛɛra bam to. Abam balo maa na nye de Gomora tiina bam to, cheigi-na Wɛ nia yam!

english_verse: “Who asked you to bring all this when you come to worship me? Stay out of my temple!
translation_verse: Á na yeini á tui á ware-ne to, wɔ mo pɛ se á kare á kekare amo wara-jei sem ne de á vara bam konto?

english_verse: I hate your New Moon Festivals and all others as well. They are a heavy burden I am tired of carrying.
translation_verse: A jworo mo yɔɔre ko nwoŋi á chan-doŋa kura yam, de wodi-fɔrɔ kura yam. A ba veele de-ya mo ne a ga zeŋe zele mo to, ye a yera chɛ ya ŋwaane.

english_verse: and learn to live right. See that justice is done. Defend widows and orphans and help the oppressed.” An Invitation from the Lord
translation_verse: se á laam zamese lanyerane keim! Beeri-na se chega kam taa toŋa, se á daare á che balo na bɛɛse ba dwonna to. Ta pa-na se botara na ba bora, ye á ŋɔɔne á pa kadeina de.”

english_verse: If you willingly obey me, the best crops in the land will be yours.
translation_verse: Abam wo ná dɛa, pa se á jege ni-sɛɛm á pa-ne, mo á wó di tega kam wo-laaro tem á su.

english_verse: But if you turn against me, your enemies will kill you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
translation_verse: Abam nam ná ve, pa se á nwoŋi amo kwaga ne, á dona mo wó go abam jara wone.” Baŋa Wɛ tete ni taane mo konto o taga o tiŋi.

english_verse: Jerusalem, you are like an unfaithful wife. Once your judges were honest and your people lived right; now you are a city full of murderers.
translation_verse: Nii mo! Teo konto déem jege amo chega. Leile, ko laam nam yage-ne mo ne ka-tola tei! Teo kom déem su de chega mo, ye nɔn-ŋona de ya zoore ko wone. Nɔn-gora laam nam mo wora.

english_verse: Your leaders have rejected me to become friends of crooks; your rulers are looking for gifts and bribes. Widows and orphans never get a fair trial.
translation_verse: Abam nakwa bam ye paweero mo, ye ba me de ŋweena. Ba maama swoi kalipera kikia mo, ye ba duri ba tɔge pɛɛra kwaga. Ba yeini ba kweele chega botara tei ne. Ba nam ba di taane ba bore ba pae kadeina.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the mighty ruler of Israel, and I make you a promise: You are now my enemy, and I will show my anger by taking revenge on you.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Dam Tu wom to tage jase o we: “Amo bane wó zaŋe abam balo na jigi a dona to baŋa ne, se á daa yé ja cham á ba á pa-ne.

english_verse: I will punish you terribly and burn away everything that makes you unfit to worship me.
translation_verse: Amo wó pa ko chɛ abam yera ne, se a wane a le á yera digiru tem maama, ne luru na kwɛ lu-nyenno se o le te digiru tei to.

english_verse: Jerusalem, you will be saved by showing justice; Zion's people who turn to me will be saved by doing right.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wó da o chega kam ŋwaane o jwoŋi Jerusalem tiina bam o yage. Balo na pipiri ba jwoori o tei to wó na verem.

english_verse: But those rebellious sinners who turn against me, the Lord, will all disappear.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye wɛleere keira, de balo na ve Baŋa Wɛ to maama, o wó meere-ba mo pa se ba jei.

english_verse: You will be made ashamed of those groves of trees where you worshiped idols.
translation_verse: Chaveera wó ja abam, de á na kwei á teena á daŋe tangwana baŋa ne, ye á daare á zuli jwona liri-mwa tiina kara wone to.

english_verse: You will be like a grove of trees dying in a drought.
translation_verse: Abam wó ji ne tei-zɔŋɔ kolo vɔɔro na kwaare to, de gaare delo na gɛ na se ba ma ba yage-de to mo.

english_verse: Your strongest leaders will be like dry wood set on fire by their idols. No one will be able to help, as they all go up in flames.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛra wó ji ne lɔŋɔ mo tei, ye ba totoŋ-balwaaro de ji ne min-cheŋo de zwɛ-ko, Nɔɔna bam tete de ba kikia maama maa wó chɔge lela ne mini na zwɛ wonnu tei to. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o jwoŋi-ba o yage.

english_verse: This is the message I was given about Judah and Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem na le wonnu telo na tɛ Judah de Jerusalem taane o bere Amozi bu Izaya to mo tento:

english_verse: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills; every nation will rush to it.
translation_verse: Maŋa wó ba ye Baŋa Wɛ diga kam na zege peo kolo yuu ne to na yere ko dwoni logo baŋa jei maama. Ko wó taa zege wɛɛne vili-vili se ko dwoni peero tem maama. Dwi maama tiina wó taa nwoŋi ba teene dem ne ba twoŋi daane taa ba yɔɔre da.

english_verse: People of Israel, let's live by the light of the Lord. Following Sinful Customs
translation_verse: Jakob dwi tiina bam, nam ba-na! Pa-na se dé taa vei pwooni delo Baŋa Wɛ na tiŋi o pa debam to wone. Baŋa Wɛ dɛ-kamunu kom taane

english_verse: Our Lord, you have deserted your people, Israel, because they follow customs of nations from the east. They worship Philistine gods and are close friends of foreigners.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ, nmo yɔɔre n dole n nɔɔna Jakob dwi tiina bam n yage mo. Ba yeini ba tɔge wɛ-puli seeni liri-mwa tiina kikia, ye ba beeri yi-nara ne Filisi tiina bam na ke tei to mo. Ba maa me de dwi-gɛ tiina de ba chullu tem.

english_verse: Everywhere in the country they worship the idols they have made.
translation_verse: Ba tega kam maama su de jwo-yɔɔro mo. Ba maa tiiri ba zuli wonnu telo ba tete je sem na ke to.

english_verse: And so, all of them will be ashamed and disgraced. Don't forgive them! A Day of Judgment
translation_verse: Nɔɔna gwooni ba tete ya yiga ne, ye ba daare ba vwi ba yibia tega ne ba pa-ya. Konto ŋwaane, yé kwei ba wɛleera yam n chɛ-ba.

english_verse: Every one of you, go hide among the rocks and in the ground, because the Lord is fearsome, marvelous, and glorious.
translation_verse: Nam véi-na peero tem gugworru ne, se á seigi tega kam wone. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ kom jege foone mo ye o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom de tiini ko nye.

english_verse: When the Lord comes, everyone who is proud will be made humble, and the Lord alone will be honored.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ná yia, nabiina balo na gwooni ba dwonna to wó to tega ne. Balo na bere ba tete kamunim to de wó jwoori ba ba tega. Baŋa Wɛ yere dem yerane mo wó zaŋe wɛɛne.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has chosen a day when those who are proud and conceited will be put down.
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ le dɛ mo o tiŋi dáa ne, se o waare balo na jege fia ye ba bere we ba fuŋi to. Dɛ dem konto ne banto maama wó to tega ne.

english_verse: The tall and towering cedars of Lebanon will be destroyed. So will the oak trees of Bashan,
translation_verse: O ta wó gwoni Lebanon tei-dedwaaro tem, de tei-zwanno tem na wo Basan laŋa kam ne to o de tega ne.

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone who is proud will be put down. Only the Lord will be honored.
translation_verse: Nabiina kamunim kikia maama wó ti mo pa se ba fia kam ji kafɛ. Baŋa Wɛ yere dem yerane mo wó zaŋe wɛɛne.

english_verse: Idols will be gone for good.
translation_verse: Jwona yam nam lage ya pɔpɔ ya jei mo.

english_verse: You had better hide in caves and holes— the Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna wó duri mo ba vo ba seigi peero gugworru wone, dedaane tega kuri bɔɔna wone, maŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó zaŋe o fugi-ba to. Kokuri to Baŋa Wɛ jege foone o pa-ba, ye o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom de tiini ko nye mo.

english_verse: On that day everyone will throw to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold they made to worship.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto nam ná yia, nɔɔna wó kwei ba jwona yalo ba na mɛ sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno ba mɔ se ba taa zuli to mo ba dole ba yage, se twarro de jenjwaano taa kare te kekare ya baŋa ne.

english_verse: The Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth— they will hide in caves and in the hills.
translation_verse: Ba laam wó vo ba seigi ba tete peero bɔɔna wone, de gugworru wone, se ba wane ba lu Baŋa Wɛ ban-zɔŋɔ de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom. Konto wó ke maŋa kalo Baŋa Wɛ na wó zaŋe o fugi nabiina to mo.

english_verse: Stop trusting the power of humans. They are all going to die, so how can they help?
translation_verse: Yé ta‑á jege-na nabiina chega. Ba yɔɔre ba bwona mo lage-lage ne siu tei. Dam dɔ mo ba jega se á sale ba yera ne?

english_verse: You will each be cruel to friends and neighbors. Young people will insult their elders; no one will show respect to those who deserve it.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna wó da ko ŋwaane se ba taa bɛɛse daane mo. Baaro wó nwoŋi o dwoŋi kwaga ne, ye fara de nwoŋi da-kwaga ne. Bia daa bá taa nege nɔn-kwe. Nɔn-yɔɔro de maa wó dwoni de nɔn-yum.

english_verse: Some of you will grab hold of a relative and say, “You still have a coat. Be our leader and rule this pile of ruins.”
translation_verse: Kanto maŋa ne nɔɔno wó vo o kwo sɔŋɔ o kuri o dwi nɔɔno dedoa ye o ta ded‑o o we, ‘Nmo na jege gɔrɔ n zoore to ŋwaane, ta‑n ye dé yiga tu se n le debam lɛɛro tento wone.’

english_verse: But the answer will be, “I can't do you any good. Don't make me your leader. There's no food or clothing left in my house.”
translation_verse: Konto tu de maa wó leiri o ta jaja we, ‘Amo bá wane abam a jwoŋi a yage. A ba jege wodiu, naa gwaaro a sɔŋɔ ne. Konto ŋwaane, yé le-ne-na se a ji nɔɔna bam yiga tu.’ ”

english_verse: The look on your faces shows that you are sinful as Sodom, and you don't try to hide it. You are in for trouble, and you have brought it all on yourselves. The Wrong Kind of Leaders
translation_verse: Ba yibia maama bere we ba ba lage Baŋa Wɛ ni taane. Ba maa yɔɔre ba ke wɛleera jaja, ne Sodom tiina déem na ke tei to. Lɛɛro mo wó yi-ba! Ko maa wó zege ba tete yera ne.

english_verse: Tell those who obey God, “You're very fortunate— you will be rewarded for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye balo na zege de chega to, ta de-ba we, wonnu wó tɔge chwoŋa te pa-ba. Ba wó na ba totoŋa yam nyɔɔre.

english_verse: Tell those who disobey, “You're in big trouble— what you did to others will come back to you.”
translation_verse: Lɛɛro taa wo puseŋ-nyena bam baŋa ne! Cham mo lage de yi-ba! Ba lage ba na ba totoŋ-balwaaro tem ŋweero mo.

english_verse: Though you are God's people, you are ruled and abused by women and children. You are confused by leaders who guide you down the wrong path.
translation_verse: Busɔ-nyena mo jege a nɔɔna bam ba bɛɛsa. Kaana de maa jege-ba ba nia. Amo nɔɔna bam, á yiga tiina bam mo jaane abam ba ywori. Ba maa pae se á tusi chwoŋa kam.

english_verse: The Lord is ready to accuse and judge all nations.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ tete nam mo tu se o saŋe nɔɔna bam. O jege taane mo de-ba.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says, “You have crushed my people and rubbed in the dirt the faces of the poor.” The Women of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Wɔ mo pɛ abam chwoŋa se á ta‑á yɔɔre á peene a nɔɔna bam? Á ta maa jege yiniga tiina jana á nyɔa.” Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, will cover their heads with sores, and I will uncover their private parts.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, a nam wó pa se ŋɔn-daala jeini ba yuni tem ne, ye a daare-ba a zege de kuri-nɔrɔ yerane.”

english_verse: When that day comes, I will take away from those women all the fine jewelry they wear on their ankles, heads, necks, ears, arms, noses, fingers, and on their clothes. I will remove their veils, their belts, their perfume, their magic charms, their royal robes, and all their fancy dresses, hats, and purses.
translation_verse: de ba niiru tem, de ba gare-fefale sem, de ba yuu gare-yia yam, de ba gare-woru tem, Wɛ wó le wonnu tento maama mo kaana bam tei ne.

english_verse: In place of perfume, there will be a stink; in place of belts, there will be ropes; in place of fancy hairdos, they will have bald heads. Instead of expensive clothes, they will wear sackcloth; instead of beauty, they will have ugly scars.
translation_verse: Ba wó taa teene se lwom na ywona to mo zaŋe, ye ba yera lwom nam mo wó chɛ nɔɔna momwa ne. Ba ya ná teene teiŋa vovwe, ba wó na ŋone yerane mo. Ba ya ná teene se ba yu-ywei taa lana, ba yuni tem wó fe te daare yu-kapwooru mo. Ba ya ná boŋe se ba zo gare-nyenno, ba wó zo gare-nyenyaaro mo. Ba lam dem wó leiri de ji wo-yɔɔro tento dwoŋi mo.

english_verse: When this happens, seven women will grab the same man, and each of them will say, “I'll buy my own food and clothes! Just marry me and take away my disgrace.” The Lord Will Bless His People Who Survive
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia, kaana barepɛ mo lage ba to ba gorege baaro dedoa, ye ba ta ded‑o we, “Dé wó taa jege dé tete ni-wodiu, ye dé daare dé beeri dé tete yera gwaaro. Nam sɛ se dé kwei n yere dé ke dé yera ne, se ba taa mae-de ba bwoi debam, se ba yé ke debam chaveera we dé wo zo banna ŋwaane.” Baŋa Wɛ wó kwɛ teo kom

english_verse: The time is coming when the Lord will make his land fruitful and glorious again, and the people of Israel who survive will take great pride in what the land produces.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se tega kam teeni de gaaro dwi maama puli dedɛ se ka lam de ka nenɔŋa tiini ko gaale. Tega kam wó ke wodiiru dedɛ ka pa Isarele tiina balo ta na daare to, se ba taa jege wopwolo de teera ka ŋwaane.

english_verse: Then the Lord will cover the whole city and its meeting places with a thick cloud each day and with a flaming fire each night. God's own glory will be like a huge tent that covers everything.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam maa wó pa woro ba ko kwoli Zion peo kom de nɔn-kɔgɔ kolo maama na jeeri da to. Wea ne nyoa wó taa nye de kunkwoŋo mo ko kwoli jei sem. Tete ne min-vogo de maa wó taa wora ko nyeena. Ko wó taa ye ne teo kom de ko lam maama wo pwoŋa kuri ne mo.

english_verse: It will provide shade from the heat of the sun and a place of shelter and protection from storms and rain.
translation_verse: Tento maa wó taa kwoli-ba pa se ba na woro wea funyogo maŋa ne, ye ba daare ba na dalem jei vo-dɛɔ de doa maŋa ne.

english_verse: My friend dug the ground, removed the stones, and planted the best vines. He built a watchtower and dug a pit in rocky ground for pressing the grapes. He hoped they would be sweet, but bitter grapes were all it produced.
translation_verse: O ma va tega kam konto maama lanyerane, ye o le kandwa yalo na wo ka wone to. O ta ma jeiri Vini teeni na lana to ka wone. O ma pu vwei se o taa maa yere-ka. O ta ma lu gwoŋo se ba taa ŋoke Vini tio-bia nyoa ko wone. O laam maa jei o cheiga se tio-bia bam be wo-ŋona. De ko de, ba jigi wo-kanywaano mo.

english_verse: Listen, people of Jerusalem and of Judah! You be the judge of me and my vineyard.
translation_verse: “Abam balo nam na zoore Jerusalem teo de Judah kateiri dem maama ne to, Zo-na amo de a kara kam tetare á bore bora.

english_verse: What more could I have done for my vineyard? I hoped for sweet grapes, but bitter grapes were all that grew.
translation_verse: Bɛ mo a ya daa wó ke de a kara kam se ka ke lanyerane, ye a wo ke? A nam ya na beeri wo-ŋona to, bɛŋwaane mo a kara kam leigi wo-kanywaano yerane?

english_verse: Now I will let you know what I am going to do. I will cut down the hedge and tear down the wall. My vineyard will be trampled and left in ruins.
translation_verse: Nam nii a na boŋe se a ke tei de a teeni kara kam to. A lage a le wonnu telo ya na chege-ka to mo, se a daare se kara kam chɔge. A maa wó bwori ka kabira kam a de tega ne, se vara wane ba zo ka wone ba nɔne teeni dem.

english_verse: It will turn into a desert, neither pruned nor hoed; it will be covered with thorns and briars. I will command the clouds not to send rain.
translation_verse: A ta wó pa se gaaro yerane jwoŋi kara kam. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá gwoni teeni dem nɛ se o kwɛ-de, naa o va tega kam. Ga-cheiŋo de sabare mo wó su kara kam maama. Amo laam maa wó pa kunkwonnu tem ni se te yé pa doa ne ka wone.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful! Israel is the vineyard, and Judah is the garden I tended with care. I had hoped for honesty and for justice, but dishonesty and cries for mercy were all I found. Isaiah Condemns Social Injustice
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ teeni kara kam mo ye Isarele dwi dem. Judah dwi tiina bam maa ye gaare delo o yi na su to. O nam ya na beeri se nɔn-ŋonne taa wora to, nɔn-gora yerane mo o nɛa. O maa na lage se chega taa toŋe to, chɔgem mo o nɛa. Lɛɛro de waarem taane

english_verse: You are in for trouble! You take over house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone else in all the land.
translation_verse: Lɛɛro wó yi abam balo na lɔ sam dedɛ á woli da-baŋa ne to. Á ta ma beeri kare á jwoŋa á daŋe da-baŋa ne. Ko ná woli fee, abam daa bá daare jei á tiŋi, ye á yerane laam mo wó ta‑á zoore tega kam ne.

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful has made this promise to me: Those large and beautiful homes will be left empty, with no one to take care of them.
translation_verse: Amo nigi Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage o we: “Abam sɔ-fwaaro tento dedɛ wó ji sɔ-korro mo, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé taa zoore de wone.

english_verse: None of them are tired. They don't sleep or get drowsy, and they run without stumbling. Their belts don't come loose; their sandal straps don't break.
translation_verse: Ba nɔɔna bam wolowolo ba buga. Ba nam ba tiri ba toe tega ne. Dɔɔne ba tui ba wolowolo yibia ne. Ba wolowolo kila wo bwoli o teiŋa ne. Ba natera yam de nam wo bwoli ba nɛ sem ne.

english_verse: You are in for trouble! The lies you tell are like ropes by which you drag along sin and evil.
translation_verse: Lɛɛro wó yi balo na me de ba wɛleera yam ye ba ware-ya ba yage to. Ba maa jaane-ya ba vei jei maama, nenɛɛne nɔɔno na vaŋe toroko de ŋone tei to.

english_verse: You are in for trouble! You get up early to start drinking, and you keep it up late into the night.
translation_verse: Lɛɛro wó yi balo na yeini ba zaŋe tetete ba yɔɔre ba wowole ba beeri sana jei to. Ba maa maŋe sana nyɔɔm ne taa se ko yi tete-koro maŋa, ye sana bam jwoŋi ba boboŋa maama.

english_verse: and so his people know nothing about him. That's why many of you will be dragged off to foreign lands. Your leaders will starve to death, and everyone else will suffer from thirst.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri ba lage ba kale Wɛ nɔɔna bam ba ja vo sa-teo yiga yiga, ba na ba ni o taane kuri to ŋwaane. Kana wó go ba teo nɔn-yum tem mo, ye na-nyɔm de ja ba nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama.

english_verse: The world of the dead has opened its mouth wide and is eagerly waiting for the leaders of Jerusalem and for its noisy crowds, especially for those who take pride in that city.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo churu ke ko fera ko ke daane, pa se ko yale ko tete ko ke da, se ko li nɔɔna bam maama. Toone wó ja teo kom dedɛɛra, de nabwona, de sa-nyɔra balo na ke sɔɔ bɔge-bɔge to.

english_verse: Its citizens have been put down, and its proud people have been brought to shame.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam wó ba tega ne mo. Boyere-nyena de wó di ba chaveera.

english_verse: His people will be like sheep grazing in their own pasture, and they will take off what was left by others.
translation_verse: Pei laam maa wó taa kare se di wodiu teo kom wone, ne ko ye se tete pwola mo to. Veira de wó ba ba zege naduna bam di-dwonnu wone ba taa di ba sui.

english_verse: And you are great at drinking and mixing drinks. But you are in for trouble.
translation_verse: Lɛɛro wó yi balo na ye bembɛ sa-nyɔre baŋa ne, ye ba tiini ba yei sana keim ba dwoi nɔɔna maama to.

english_verse: You accept bribes to let the guilty go free, and you cheat the innocent out of a fair trial.
translation_verse: Taane dim baŋa ne ba swoi se ba taa jwoŋi dim mo ye ba yage balo na gɛ bora to pa ba viiri zɛɛra. Ba ta ma da ko ŋwaane ba vane nɔn-ŋona ba bora.

english_verse: You will go up in flames like straw and hay! You have rejected the teaching of the holy Lord God All-Powerful of Israel. Now your roots will rot, and your blossoms will turn to dust.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, banto kugu jei mo wó ŋɔɔle, ne mini na di ga-korro kula pa se te jei lela tei to. Ba punnu tem de wó jage te jei, ne vio na yeini ko jage fwogo tei to. Kokuri to, ba ve Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele dwi dem Wo-pwoŋo Tu to nia yam mo. Ba ta ma nii o taane dem ba gwooni.

english_verse: You are the Lord's people, but you made him terribly angry, and he struck you with his mighty arm. Mountains shook, and dead bodies covered the streets like garbage. The Lord is still angry, and he is ready to strike you again. Foreign Nations Will Attack
translation_verse: Konto nam mo pɛ se Baŋa Wɛ bane tiini de fuli de o nɔɔna bam. O yɔɔre o zeiŋi o jeŋa mo se o mage-ba o de tega ne. Peero tem wó ziziŋi, ye twa de faare teo kom chwei yuu ne, ne weero tei to. De konto maama de nam, Baŋa Wɛ bane dem ta bá zuri. O ta wó twe o jeŋa kam mo se o waare-ba.

english_verse: The Lord has signaled for the foreign nations to come and attack you. He has already whistled, and they are coming as fast as they can.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wó zeiŋi tuta mo se o pa dwi-gɛ tiina balo na wo yiga yiga to zaŋe ba ba ba kwaare jara de o nɔɔna bam. O ma fwooli o bwoŋi-ba se ba ba. Nii ba na ke lela ba wuuri tei ba beene!

english_verse: Their arrows are sharp, and their bows are ready. The hoofs of their horses are hard as flint; the wheels of their war chariots turn as fast as a whirlwind.
translation_verse: Ba che-tɛɛra yam nia yɔɔre ya di mo bileim-bileim. Ba tɛ sem tete de ma saŋe se ti se se ta. Ba sisein-nɔɔna bam napɔɔna dana ne kandwa na ye tei to mo. Ba torokooro tem nɛ de ye ne vo-kekara na ye tei to mo.

english_verse: In the year that King Uzziah died, I had a vision of the Lord. He was on his throne high above, and his robe filled the temple.
translation_verse: Bene delo wone Pɛ Yuzia na tege to, mo a nɛ a Teiru Wɛ wom. O déem jei paare yituŋu kolo na tiini ko ye wɛ-wɛ to yuu ne mo. O gare-dedɔrɔ kom nabili maa su Wɛ diga kam maama.

english_verse: Flaming creatures with six wings each were flying over him. They covered their faces with two of their wings and their bodies with two more. They used the other two wings for flying,
translation_verse: Serafi tiina déem mo zege o baŋa ne. Ba maama déem jege vɔna yaredo yaredo mo. Ba jege vɔna yalei mo ba maa kwoli ba yibia, yalei de maa kwoli ba nɛ, ye ba daare yalei ba jege ba jaana.

english_verse: As they shouted, the doorposts of the temple shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
translation_verse: Ba kwori sem sɔɔ ma pa se Wɛ diga kam ziziŋi ka yi ka kuri na jaane mɛ to, ye nyoa yɔɔre ka pe ka wo kom maama.

english_verse: Then I cried out, “I'm doomed! Everything I say is sinful, and so are the words of everyone around me. Yet I have seen the King, the Lord All-Powerful.”
translation_verse: A na nɛ konto to, mo a tage a we, “Lɛɛro yi amo! A tege a ti! Kokuri to, a ye wolo ni taane na digiri to mo. A maa zoore de balo ni taane de na digiri to. De ko de, amo ta nɛ Pɛ wom na ye Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ to.”

english_verse: One of the flaming creatures flew over to me with a burning coal that it had taken from the altar with a pair of metal tongs.
translation_verse: Serafi tiina bam dedoa ma jaane o yi a tei, ye o zei min-chale o déem na mɛ tasɔɔne mo o le-de bimbini dem baŋa ne to o ja o ba.

english_verse: It touched my lips with the hot coal and said, “This has touched your lips. Your sins are forgiven, and you are no longer guilty.”
translation_verse: O laam ma kwei-de o dwei a ni, ye o ta de amo o we, “Nii ywo! Min-chale dento na dwei n ni-vɔɔro to, n tusim dem saare de yage, ye n wɛleera yam daa tere n yuu ne.”

english_verse: After this, I heard the Lord ask, “Is there anyone I can send? Will someone speak for us?” “I'll go,” I answered. “Send me!”
translation_verse: Amo laam ma ni a Teiru wom kwora, o na bwei o we, “Wɔ mo amo wó toŋe se o ja debam kwora o vo a nɔɔna bam tei?” Amo de ma leiri a we, “Nii amo da! Toŋe-ne!”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to go and speak this message to the people: “You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.” The Lord also said,
translation_verse: O laam maa we: “Véi n ta de nɔɔna banto we: ‘Abam ná maŋe á cheigi tei maama de, á bá ni wonnu kuri. Abam nam ná kwaane á nii tei maama de, á bá lɔre kolokolo.’

english_verse: If only a tenth of the people are left, even they will be destroyed. But just as stumps remain after trees have been cut down, some of my chosen ones will be left.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna fuga maama wone dedoa tete mo ná daare da, tega kam daa ta wó na chɔgem mo. Ko nam wó taa ye nenɛɛne ba na gwoni tei-zɔŋɔ, ye ko kugu kom ta daare tega kam ne tei to mo. Kugu kom daa wó jwoori ko kwi se Isarele dwi dem taa ye wose.”

english_verse: When news reached the royal palace that Syria had joined forces with Israel, King Ahaz and everyone in Judah were so terrified that they shook like trees in a windstorm.
translation_verse: Kwora ma yi pɛ sɔŋɔ kom tiina we, “Siria tiina sɔge ni de Efrayim dwi tiina mo se ba ke jara de debam!” Taane dem ma pa se Ahaz de o nɔɔna bam yera yɔɔre ya sae, ne vo-fɔrɔ na mage teeni ye de zuuli tei to.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to me: Take your son Shearjashub and go see King Ahaz. You will find him on the road near the cloth makers' shops at the end of the canal that brings water from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ laam ma ta de Izaya o we, “Nwoŋi de n bu Sear-Jasubi se á vo á jeeri Pɛ Ahaz. Abam wó na‑o na-fera kalo na zoore baŋa seeni chɔgɔ kom to ni ne, se ko maŋe de chwoŋa kam mɛ ba na sɔ gwaaro to.

english_verse: Tell Ahaz to stop worrying. There's no need for him to be afraid of King Rezin and King Pekah. They are very angry, but they are nothing more than a dying fire. Ahaz doesn't need to fear
translation_verse: Ta ded‑o we: Ta‑n yei n tete. Pa n bochare taa tiga se n yé ta‑n kɔre foone. Siria teo pɛ Rezin, de o nɔɔna bam, dedaane Remalia bu Peka daa ba jege dam. Banto balei nye ne mini na dwei de daare da-toora yalei tei to mo. Konto ŋwaane, yé pa se n vɔna pare ba bane na zaŋe dede‑m to ŋwaane.

english_verse: to invade and defeat Judah and Jerusalem and to let the son of Tabeel be king in his place.
translation_verse: ‘Dé wó vo dé li Judah teo kom mo dé fugi ko nɔɔna bam ye dé daare dé jwoŋi-ko dé taa tei. Dé laam maa wó tiŋi Tabeeli bu wom se o ji ba pɛ.’

english_verse: Damascus is just the capital of Syria, and King Rezin rules only in Damascus. Samaria is just the capital of Israel, and King Pekah rules only in Samaria. But in less than
translation_verse: Efrayim tiina bam ba dana ba dwoi ba te-fɔrɔ Samaria. Samaria teo kom de nam ba dana ko dwoi Remalia bu Peka. Abam ná wo ke á chega de amo, á bá wane á fɔge á zege de pu-dɛa.’ ”

english_verse: Once again the Lord God spoke to King Ahaz. This time he said,
translation_verse: Izaya na tage Wɛ kwora kam konto o bere Pɛ Ahaz to mo Baŋa Wɛ daa ta tage de pɛ wom o we,

english_verse: “Ask me for proof that my promise will come true. Ask for something to happen deep in the world of the dead or high in the heavens above.”
translation_verse: “Nam lwoori amo wolo na ye n Tu Baŋa Wɛ to, se a wó ke wo-memaŋe a bere‑m, se n lɔre we a tage chega. Amo wó ke wo-memaŋe ne nmo na lage tei to, ko ná maŋe ko ye tega kuri ne naa wɛyuu ne yiga yiga de.”

english_verse: “No, Lord,” Ahaz answered. “I won't test you!”
translation_verse: Ahaz ma leiri o we, “Aawo, amo bá sɛ se a maŋe Baŋa Wɛ a nii.”

english_verse: Then I said: Listen, every one of you in the royal family of David. You have already tried my patience. Now you are trying God's patience by refusing to ask for proof.
translation_verse: Izaya laam ma ta o we, “Cheigi-na, abam balo na nwoŋi Pɛ David dwi dem wone to. Á yeini á daane Wɛ tontoŋena bam mo. Á laam boŋe se á daane Wɛ wolo amo na toŋe a pa‑o to tete mo na?

english_verse: But the Lord will still give you proof. A virgin is pregnant; she will have a son and will name him Immanuel.
translation_verse: Ko nam na ye tei to, Baŋa Wɛ tete mo lage o ke wo-memaŋe o bere abam. Nii-na! Busankan-pwola kam wó ba o ja puga o lo bakeira. O maa wó bwoŋi bu wom yere we ‘Imanuwel’.

english_verse: Even before the boy is old enough to know how to choose between right and wrong, he will eat yogurt and honey, and the countries of the two kings you fear will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, bu wom ta ná wo yi se o pɔɔre lam de lwarem daane, de pwa balei bam nmo zem na kɔre foone de-ba to teene dem jigi di-dwonnu.

english_verse: But the Lord will make more trouble for your people and your kingdom than any of you have known since Israel broke away from Judah. He will even bring the king of Assyria to attack you. The Threat of an Invasion
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam lage o pa ko tiini ko ni nmo, de n nɔɔna bam, de n kwo dwi dem maama mo. Ko zege maŋa kalo Efrayim tiina bam na pwɛ ba tete de Judah teo se ko yi zem to, cham dento dwoŋi wo yi abam. Asiria teo pɛ mo wó ba á baŋa.”

english_verse: They will settle everywhere—in the deep valleys and between the rocks, on every thornbush and all over the pastureland.
translation_verse: Banto wó nwoŋi de kɔgɔ mo ba ba ba faare tega kam maama. Ba wó vo ba jeini bwol-fwaaro ne, de peero gugworru wone, de mɛ na jege sabare to ne, ko woli de vara pwoli sem ne.

english_verse: The Lord will pay the king of Assyria to bring a razor from across the Euphrates River and shave your head and every hair on your body, including your beard.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam ná yia, Baŋa Wɛ wó bwoŋi Asiria teo pɛ se o nwoŋi Yuferata buga kam seeni o ba o chɔge abam pa se á di á chaveera, ne o na kwei fana o ma o cheeri á yu-ywei maama, ye o fane á twana, se o daare o kwooni á yera koro tem maama tei to.

english_verse: Anyone who is able to save only one young cow and two sheep,
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne, valo wae o pɔɔre na-mɔra dedoa de bone delei yerane se o taa jega.

english_verse: will have enough milk to make yogurt. In fact, everyone left in the land will eat yogurt and honey.
translation_verse: De ko de, kotu ta wó na nayela dedɛ se o taa di nayel-pepala. Balo ta na daare tega kam ne to wó di nayel-pepala de tooro mo.

english_verse: You will go there to hunt with your bow and arrows, because the whole country will be covered with thornbushes.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna laam maa wó taa vei dáane ba tɔɔna, ga-cheiŋo de sabare na wó jwoŋi jei sem konto maama to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The hills where you once planted crops will be overgrown with thorns and thistles. You will be afraid to go there, and your cattle, sheep, and goats will be turned loose on those hills.
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá vo zwonnu tem jei sem ne se o va. Kokuri to, ga-cheiŋo de sabare yerane mo wó su jei sem maama. Dáane mo ba nam wó kale naane ba yage da se de di gaao, ye pei de wó taa nɔne jei sem konto ne.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Isaiah, get something to write on. Then write in big clear letters the name, MAHER-SHALAL-HASH-BAZ.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we, “Beeri tɔn-kamunu se n popone botare-bia ko wone se nɔɔna taa wae ba gara jaja. Popone tento: Mahere-Salal-Hasa-Bazi.

english_verse: I will tell Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah to serve as witnesses to this.”
translation_verse: Amo nam wó bwoŋi Wɛ kaanem tu Yuria, de Jeberekia bu Zekaria, se ba ba ba ji maana tiina chekke ba pa-ne.”

english_verse: Sometime later, my wife and I had a son, and the Lord said, “Name him Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz.
translation_verse: Amo déem ma peini de a kaane, ye o ja puga o lo bakeira. Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we, “Bwoŋi o yere we Mahere-Salal-Hasa-Bazi.

english_verse: Because before he can say ‘Mommy’ or ‘Daddy,’ the king of Assyria will attack and take everything of value from Damascus and Samaria.”
translation_verse: Bu wom ta ná wo yi se o taa wae o ni o pura o tɛ we, ‘A nu’ naa ‘A kwo’, Asiria pɛ wom wó ba o vere Damasika jejegero tem, de Samaria wonnu tem maama o ja o viiri.”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me again and said:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta de amo o we:

english_verse: These people have refused the gentle waters of Shiloah and have gladly gone over to the side of King Rezin and King Pekah.
translation_verse: “Judah tiina bam yɔɔre ba ve Siloa bu-nɔgɔ kom na duri mɛmɛ to mo, ye ba sɛ ba pa Rezin, de Remalia bu Peka.

english_verse: Enemy soldiers will cover Judah like a flood reaching up to your neck. But God is with us. He will spread his wings and protect our land.
translation_verse: Na bam ta wó chuuri ba kɛ ba yi Judah laŋa kam ba tagele jei sem, ye ba daare ba lini tega kam de nɔɔna bam maama. Imanuwel, Wɛ nam wó kwoli nmo tega kam maama, ne zuŋa na yarege ka vɔna ka bia baŋa ne tei to.”

english_verse: The Lord took hold of me with his powerful hand and said: I'm warning you! Don't act like these people.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ yɔɔre o tɔge o dam dem baŋa ne mo o kaane-ne se a de yé kwei chwoŋa kalo nɔɔna banto na tɔge da to. O maa we:

english_verse: Don't call something a rebellious plot, just because they do, and don't be afraid of something, just because they are.
translation_verse: “Banto ná jeeli kolo we, ba ke ni se ba baare nɔɔno kwaga, abam yé jeeli-ko konto. Nam yé ta‑á kɔre-na wonnu telo banto na kɔre to. Yé ta‑á fona-na.

english_verse: I am the one you should fear and respect. I am the holy God, the Lord All-Powerful!
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ yerane mo á wó ta‑á nii we o ye wo-pwoŋo tu. Ko maa ye wonto mo á jege se á ta‑á kɔre, ye á fona ded‑o.

english_verse: Run to me for protection. I am a rock that will make both Judah and Israel stumble and break their bones. I am a trap that will catch the people of Jerusalem—they will be captured and dragged away. Isaiah and His Followers
translation_verse: Ba dedɛ mo lage ba tiri ba to ba chochoge ba tete. Ba dona maa wó che-ba de kalanchorro ba ja ba viiri.” Ke n teena Baŋa Wɛ wone

english_verse: My message and my teachings are to be sealed and given to my followers.
translation_verse: Kwei-na nia yalo maama Wɛ na pɛ debam to á ke daane. Fɔge á tiŋi o bera yam, ye á daare á ke-ya amo tɔgena bam jeŋa ne.

english_verse: Someone may say to you, “Go to the fortunetellers who make soft chirping sounds or ask the spirits of the dead. After all, a nation ought to be able to ask its own gods
translation_verse: Nɔɔna nam wó ta de abam se á beeri vora, de yi-nara, de balo na yeini ba seini ba vogo to mo, ye ba we, “Nɔɔna maŋe se ba vo ba wa yam yiga ne ba beeri ba yiga mo. Ba wó bwɛ de twa se ba lɔre kolo ná wó yi balo na ŋwe to.”

english_verse: what it should do.” None of those who talk like that will live to see the light of day!
translation_verse: Nam kwei-na ba taane dem konto á maŋe de Wɛ nia de o bera yam. Ba na tage kolo to bere we, chega seene ka tere ba taane dem wone.

english_verse: They will go around in great pain and will become so hungry that they will angrily curse their king and their gods. And when they try to find help in heaven
translation_verse: Amo nɔɔna bam wó taa kaare tega kam maama wone ba beera, se wo-chechɔgɔ de kana taa jege-ba. Ba bane wó zaŋe ba kana kam ŋwaane. Ba maa wó kwoni ba yuni wɛɛne ba lwɛ ba pɛ wom de ba Wɛ dem.

english_verse: But those who have suffered will no longer be in pain. The territories of Zebulun and Naphtali in Galilee were once hated. But this land of the Gentiles across the Jordan River and along the Mediterranean Sea will be greatly respected. War Is Over
translation_verse: Ko nam na ye tei to, lwia ya na jege nɔɔna balo to wó nwoŋi ba cham dem wone. Faŋa kam to, nɔɔna déem jege Zebulun dwi tiina laŋa kam de Nafitali tiina laŋa kam ba gwoona. Maŋa nam na beene to, Wɛ wó pa jei sem konto na zula lanyerane. Ko maa ye jei selo na wo naneo kom seeni to, de jei selo na wo Jɔdan buga kam bubɛ dedwoŋi dem kwaga ne to, de Galili laŋa kam dwi-gɛ tiina na zoore mɛ to.

english_verse: Those who walked in the dark have seen a bright light. And it shines upon everyone who lives in the land of darkest shadows.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo déem na beeri lim wone to mo pwooni laam yi-ba lanyerane. Balo ya na zoore yibiri jei ne ye toone tei-ba to, wea laam maa nye ba baŋa ne.

english_verse: The boots of marching warriors and the blood-stained uniforms have been fed to flames and eaten by fire. A Child Has Been Born
translation_verse: Ba maa wó kwei ba jara zela yam maama ba ma ba tɔre mini. Bembɛ natere-kogela yam, de gɔrɔ kolo maama na fereme de jana to wo ba te chɔge zɔŋ-zɔŋ.

english_verse: A child has been born for us. We have been given a son who will be our ruler. His names will be Wonderful Advisor and Mighty God, Eternal Father and Prince of Peace.
translation_verse: Ba loge bu ba pa debam. Ba ma pa debam bakeira. Ko nam ye wonto yuu zele mo se o taa tei o nɔɔna. Ba maa wó taa jege‑o ba bwoi we: Swa Bereno na ye kenkagele, de Wɛ-kamunu kom, de Taa Wuu Tu Kwo wom, de Bochare-zuru Tu dedɛɛro wom.

english_verse: and all of them knew it, including everyone in the capital city of Samaria. But they were proud and stubborn and said,
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam maama wó lɔre ko ni ne, ko ná maŋe ko ye Efrayim dwi tiina bam, de balo maama na zoore Samaria teo ne to. Banto yeini ba bere ba tete kamunim ye ba ta de nyɔn-mage ba we,

english_verse: He sent the Arameans from the east and the Philistines from the west, and they swallowed up Israel. But even this did not stop him from being angry, so he kept on punishing them.
translation_verse: Siria tiina bam wó nwoŋi wɛ-puli seeni se Filisi tiina bam de zege wɛ-zoore seeni ba ba. Banto maama laam maa wó kaŋe ba nia ba li Isarele tiina bam.

english_verse: The people of Israel still did not turn back to the Lord All-Powerful and worship him.
translation_verse: De Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na pɛ se ko zo ba yera to maama de, nɔɔna bam ta wo pipiri se ba jwoori o tei.

english_verse: Their rulers and leaders were the head, and the lying prophets were the tail.
translation_verse: Ba nakwa de ba nɔn-yum tem mo ye yuu kom. Ba sampwori selo na kare ba fɔe vwa to maa ye nabili dem.

english_verse: They had led the nation down the wrong path, and the people were confused.
translation_verse: Balo na wo nɔɔna banto yiga ne to mo pae ba tusa. Ko maa pae se balo ba na jege ba bere chwoŋa to na chɔgem.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with his people and kept punishing them, because they had turned against him. They were evil and spoke foolishly. That's why he did not have pity on their young people or on their widows and orphans.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo Baŋa Wɛ yi ba sui ba nɔn-donno tem kikia. O nam ba duri botara bam de kadeina bam de ŋwaŋa. Kokuri to, nɔɔna bam maama ve Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem mo ye ba toŋe puseŋa yerane. Ba nia maa yɔɔre ya ŋɔɔne wo-popwanno. De konto maama de nam, Baŋa Wɛ bane dem ta bá zuri. O ta wó twe o jeŋa kam mo se o waare-ba.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful was angry and used the people as fuel for a fire that scorched the land. They turned against each other
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom dem ŋwaane, tega kam maama wó di mini mo ye ka zwɛ maama. Nɔɔna bam wó ji ne dɛ mo se ba kwei-ba ba ma ba tɔre mini, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá ŋwane o pa o dwoŋi.

english_verse: like wild animals attacking and eating everyone around them, even their own relatives. But still they were not satisfied.
translation_verse: Jazem seeni de jagwia seeni maama ba kare ba beeri wodiu mo se ba di. Ba nam ta ba di ba sui. Ba ma kwaane ba di ba tete dwi dem ya-nɔna.

english_verse: The tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh turned against each other, then joined forces to attack Judah. But the Lord was still angry and ready to punish the nation even more.
translation_verse: Manasɛ dwi tiina ke chichuŋu de Efrayim dwi tiina mo, ye Efrayim dwi tiina bam de ke chichuŋu de Manasɛ dwi tiina bam. Banto balei laam ma ke daane ba ke chichuŋu de Judah dwi tiina bam. De konto maama de nam, Baŋa Wɛ bane dem ta bá zuri. O ta wó twe o jeŋa kam mo se o waare-ba.

english_verse: But what will you do when you are fiercely attacked and punished by foreigners? Where will you run for help? Where will you hide your valuables?
translation_verse: Bora borem dɛ dem nam ná yia, abam lage á ke tetɛ mo? Lɛɛro wó zege yiga yiga ne te ba te to á baŋa ne. Abam laam wó duri á vo bera tei mo se ba woli abam? Á lage á vo á seigi á jejegero tem yei ne mo?

english_verse: to beat down you godless people. I am angry with you, and I will send him to attack you. He will take what he wants and walk on you like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: Amo wó toŋe-ba se ba vo ba ke chichuŋu de dwi tiina balo na ve Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem ye ba chuchugi a bane to. Asiria tiina bam maa wó vere nɔɔna bam konto jejegero ba ja ba viiri. Ba ta wó pa ko yi-ba ne teero mo ba jege ba nɔne to.

english_verse: The king of Assyria says: My army commanders are kings!
translation_verse: O maa tɛ o we, “A dedɛɛra bam maama jege dam ba dwoi pwa!

english_verse: The gods of Jerusalem and Samaria are weaker than the gods of those powerful nations. And I will destroy Jerusalem, together with its gods and idols, just as I did Samaria.
translation_verse: Ne a na maŋe a chɔge Samaria teo kom de ko jwona tei to, mo a ta na wó ke tei de Jerusalem de ko jwona yam.”

english_verse: The Lord will do what he has planned against Jerusalem and Mount Zion. Then he will punish the proud and boastful king of Assyria,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nam ná ke o na lage tei to Zion peo kom de Jerusalem teo kom yera ne, o laam wó waare Asiria teo pɛ wom mo, de o na bere o tete kamunim, ye o ta jege teera to.

english_verse: who says: I did these things by my own power because I am smart and clever. I attacked kings like a wild bull, and I took the land and the treasures of their nations.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, wonto tɛ o we: “Amo tete dam mo pɛ se a ke tento maama. A nam ta ke-ko ko tɔge a swa de a yi-poro baŋa ne mo. A ma gɔ teene dem siseina, ye a daare a vere ba jejegero a jega. A maa jege dam ne nabea tei to pa se a chɔge pwa dam.

english_verse: King of Assyria, can an ax or a saw overpower the one who uses it? Can a wooden pole lift whoever holds it?
translation_verse: Dwooru wó wane o dwoni de wolo na jege‑o o toŋe to na? Seo de wó taa jege kuri ko dwoi wolo na zei-ko to na? Gwoli ba zeiŋi nabiinu. Ko ye nabiinu mo wó zeiŋi gwoli.

english_verse: The holy God, who is the light of Israel, will turn into a fire, and in one day you will go up in flames, just like a thornbush.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ wom na pae Isarele tiina pwooni to laam wó ji mini mo o pa-ba. Ba Wo-pwoŋo Tu Wɛ wom mo wó ji min-vogo, se o zwɛ Asiria pɛ wonnu tem dɛ dedwe wone. O lage o zwɛ-te ne ba na zwɛ sabare de ga-cheiŋo tei to mo.

english_verse: There will be so few trees that even a young child can count them. Only a Few Will Come Back
translation_verse: Goa wone teeni dem wó mɔ mo de daare fee yerane, pa se bu-balaŋa de wó wane de ni o jeeli o ja. Isarele tiina wó jwoori ba tete teo

english_verse: A time is coming when the survivors from Israel and Judah will completely depend on the holy Lord of Israel, instead of the nation that defeated them.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ná yia, balo ta na daare Isarele tiina bam wone to daa bá kwei ba teena ba daŋe wolo ya na bɛɛse-ba to baŋa ne. Ba nam wó kwei ba chega de ba teena maama mo ba ke Jakob dwi tiina Wo-pwoŋo Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom wone.

english_verse: There were as many people as there are grains of sand along the seashore, but only a few will survive to come back to Israel's mighty God. This is because he has threatened to destroy their nation, just as they deserve.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina kɔ-fɔrɔ kom seene ko daga, ne naneo ni kasolo bia na ye tei to mo. De ko de, ba fenfee yerane mo wó jwoori Wɛ tei. Wɛ boboŋa maŋe ya ja ya ti se o chɔge-ba mo. Chɔgem dem nam wó tɔge o chega bora kam baŋa ne mo chekke.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has promised that everyone on this earth will be punished.
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó yɔɔre o ke-ba ne o na tage tei to o ti, pa se tega kam maama na chɔgem mo.

english_verse: Now the Lord God All-Powerful says to his people in Jerusalem: The Assyrians will beat you with sticks and abuse you, just as the Egyptians did. But don't be afraid of them.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam tage tento mo ye o we: “Amo nɔɔna balo na zoore Zion ne to, yé ta‑á kɔre-na foone de Asiria tiina bam, de ba na jege da-lwanno de gwola ba mage abam, ne Ejipti tiina bam de déem na ke abam tei to.

english_verse: I will beat the Assyrians with a whip, as I did the people of Midian near the rock at Oreb. And I will show the same mighty power that I used when I made a path through the sea in Egypt.
translation_verse: Amo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ tete nam wó fere Asiria tiina bam se ko zo ba yera, ne a déem na ke Midian tiina tei Orebi peo kom teiŋa ne to mo. Amo ta wó waare-ba, ne Moses déem na twe o nacheiga kam naneo baŋa ne ye a waare Ejipti tiina bam tei to.

english_verse: Enemy troops have reached the town of Aiath. They have gone through Migron, and they stored their supplies at Michmash,
translation_verse: Á dona bam tu ba li Ayate teo! Ba tɔge Migoron ne mo ba kɛ. Ba ma kwei ba zela ba tiŋi Mikimasa ne.

english_verse: before crossing the valley and spending the night at Geba. The people of Ramah are terrified; everyone in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, has run away.
translation_verse: Ba kwei peero yuu chwoŋa mo ba vei ye ba tɛ we, “Dé wó vo dé yi Geba teo mo dé peini da.” Rama teo nɔɔna bam yera maa sae. Sɔɔl teo Gibea tiina de duri mo se ba lu.

english_verse: Loud crying can be heard in the towns of Gallim, Laishah, and sorrowful Anathoth.
translation_verse: Abam Galim teo tiina bam, tiini á ta‑á chwoosa! Abam de cheigi-na, Layisa teo tiina bam! Anatofe teo tiina bam, lwia jege abam!

english_verse: Like a branch that sprouts from a stump, someone from David's family will someday be king.
translation_verse: Jesse dwi dem da-buŋa kalo ta na daare to wó jwoori ka ta naga. Naga kalo na wó nwoŋi da to mo wó ke bia.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will be with him to give him understanding, wisdom, and insight. He will be powerful, and he will know and honor the Lord.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ Jworo maa wó taa wo kotu baŋa ne. Jworo kom wó pa o taa jege swa de yi-poro, se o taa wae o bere nɔɔna chega. Jworo kom ta wó pa o taa jege dam de yeino, se o taa kɔre Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: The poor and the needy will be treated with fairness and with justice. His word will be law everywhere in the land, and criminals will be put to death.
translation_verse: O nam wó tɔge nɔn-ŋonne baŋa ne mo o di yiniga tiina taane. O maa wó bore chega bora o pa nabwona balo maama na zoore tega kam ne to. O ni-vio kom maa wó taa jege dam tega kam jei maama ne, se ko pa puseŋ-nyena na chɔgem.

english_verse: Leopards will lie down with young goats, and wolves will rest with lambs. Calves and lions will eat together and be cared for by little children.
translation_verse: Wiira de pipeili wó taa zoore daane. Gweera de bebale de maa wó taa tigi jeiga dedoa ne. Na-mɔre de nywon-pɔle wó taa tɔge de na-paala mo se ba me daane. Bu-balwa maa wó taa jege-se ba nia.

english_verse: Cows and bears will share the same pasture; their young will rest side by side. Lions and oxen will both eat straw.
translation_verse: Naane de kago-vara wó zege daane ba di. Ba bia bam de maa wó taa tigi da-tei ne. Nywonnu de wó di ga-korro ne nabɛ na di tei to.

english_verse: Little children will play near snake holes. They will stick their hands into dens of poisonous snakes and never be hurt.
