translation_verse: Abam yeini á ta jei sento taane mo á we, ‘Babilon jar-keira bam tu se ba chɔge tega kam. Ka lage ka ji di-dwonnu yerane, mɛ nabiina de vara na tera ka wone to.’ De ko de, nɔɔna daa wó yeigi tega ywo-seeni.

english_verse: But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Chega to, nɔɔna wó kwei lu-nyenno ba ma yeigi tega jei sento wone. Ba ta wó popone tega kam twanno, ye ba daare ba zi ba je te baŋa ne. Nɔɔna badaara wó maane ba keim dem ye ba de zi ba je ko ŋwaane. Ko nam wó ke konto mo Benjamin kateiri dem ne, de Jerusalem nawuura yam ne, de Judah teene dem ne, ko ta woli de zwonnu laŋa kam seeni, de wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne, de tega-kuri kagoa kam seeni maama. Kokuri to, amo wó jwoori a pa se a nɔɔna bam jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.”

english_verse: I was still being held prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guards when the Lord told me: I am the Lord, and I created the whole world.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ye wolo na naane tega baŋa maama to. O ma fɔge o mɔ-ka o daare o chwi-ka o zege cheppe. Wonto yere mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. O nam tage tento mo o we:

english_verse: Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
translation_verse: “Bwoŋi-na amo yere, se a wó leiri abam. A ta wó bere abam wo-kamunnu telo ya na seigi ye á yeiri te ni ne to.”

english_verse: Many of the houses in Jerusalem and some of the buildings at the royal palace have been torn down to be used in repairing the walls to keep out the Babylonian attackers. Now there are empty spaces where the buildings once stood. But I am furious, and these spaces will be filled with the bodies of the people I kill. The people of Jerusalem will cry out to me for help, but they are evil, and I will ignore their prayers.
translation_verse: Á nam ná ke jara de-ba, á teo kom wó su de twa ye á suli-ba di-dwonnu tem wone. Kokuri to, amo jaane boboŋa se á yɔɔre a chɔge-ba mo, a bane na zaŋe de-ba to ŋwaane. Amo yiga daa bá taa wo teo kom nɔn-bia bam wone, ba lwarem kikia yam ŋwaane.

english_verse: Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace.
translation_verse: Nii-na! Dɛ nam ta wora se amo jwoori a fɔge a kwɛ teo kom. Amo wó yɔɔre a nɔɔna bam pa se ba taa zoore de yazura zurim wone.

english_verse: I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before.
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se Judah tiina bam de Isarele tiina bam jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo, ye a pa ba fɔge ba zege de dam ne ba déem na ye tei to.

english_verse: When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne, Jerusalem teo kom wó pa a na yere logo baŋa teene maama wone. Amo wó na wopwolo, de zula, de nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ mo teo kom konto ŋwaane. Dwi tiina maama wó lɔre wo-laaro telo a na wó kwei a pa a nɔɔna bam to ni ne. Banto ná nɛ a na fɔge teo kom de yazura tei to, ko wó so-ba ye ba yera de taa sae.”

english_verse: Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Abam kare á tɛ we, ‘Teo konto yɔɔre ko ji di-dwonnu yerane mo pa se nabiina de vara maama jei ka wone.’ Chega to, Jerusalem teo chwei sem ne de Judah teene dem maama wone, nabiina de vara seene ba tera. Ko nam na wó taa ye tei to, jei sem konto ne mo abam daa lage á ni

english_verse: happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say: “We praise you, Lord All-Powerful! You are good to us, and your love never fails.” The land will once again be productive.
translation_verse: wopwolo de mwanno sɔɔ na zaŋe. Kadiri ywoni de daa wó taa wora. Ba maa wó ja lei-keim pɛɛra ba ba Baŋa Wɛ ware-jei sem ne, ye ba leeni we: ‘Pa-na se dé ke Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ lei, se Baŋa Wɛ lamma! O swono kom de maa wora taa wuu.’ Kokuri to, amo wó jwoori a pa se tega kanto na yu-ywoŋo, ne ka déem na jege tei to.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord's Wonderful Promise
translation_verse: Ko ná ye zwonnu laŋa kam ne, de wɛ-zoore seeni bwollu tem ne, de tega-kuri seeni kagoa kam ne, de Benjamin laŋa kam ne, dedaane Jerusalem nawuura yam de Judah laŋa kam maama ne, jei sem konto teene maama wone mo vara bam wó puli lanyerane ye nayera bam jeeli ba ni.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: The Lord said: I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta o we: “Maŋa lage ka yi se amo ke a su ni delo a déem na gwoni de Isarele dwi tiina dedaane Judah dwi tiina bam we a wó zeini-ba to.

english_verse: I promise that the time will come when I will appoint a king from the family of David, a king who will be honest and rule with justice.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia, amo wó pa David dwi dem puli naga dedoa ye kotu wó taa ye nɔn-ŋom mo. O ta wó taa tɔge chega de o na ke tei de nɔɔna to mo tega kam maama baŋa ne.

english_verse: In those days, Judah will be safe; Jerusalem will have peace and will be named, “The Lord Gives Justice.”
translation_verse: O paare dim maŋa ne, Judah tiina wó na verem, ye Jerusalem tiina de taa zoore de yazura. Nɔɔna maa wó taa bwoi teo kom yere we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ mo bore debam bora de chega.’

english_verse: and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
translation_verse: Kaanem tiina bam na nwoŋi Levi dwi dem ne to de wó taa wora maŋa maama mo, se ba taa ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de wodiu pɛɛra, de kaanem dwi dwi ba pa-ne.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them,
translation_verse: “Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo gwoni ni de wea kam de tete dem, se tento taa tui dɛ maama te maŋa ne. Abam wó wane á chɔge ni-gwonim dem konto na?

english_verse: and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Á ya ná wane á chɔge-de, á ya wó wane ni-gwonim delo a na ke de a tontoŋeno David to dedaane delo a na ke de Levi tiina bam to á chɔge. Ko nam na ye tei to, maŋa maama nɔɔno wó taa wora o na wó nwoŋi Pɛ David dwi dem wone se o di paare. Levi tiina de wó taa wora se ba taa ye kaanem tiina ba pa-ne.

english_verse: and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye a tontoŋeno David dwi dem, de Levi dwi dem na kaane ba pa-ne to, a lage a pa ba puli mo ne wɛyuu chalechwe sem na daga tei to. Ba ni bá wane de ga de ti, ne naneo ni kasolo bia na ye tei to.”

english_verse: You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
translation_verse: “N wo nɛ na? Nɔɔna badwonna jege a nɔɔna bam ba twe ye ba we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ laam virigi o kwaga o ya dwia yalei yam o ya na kuri to.’ Ba yeini ba ta konto dwoŋi, ye ba boŋe we a nɔɔna bam daa ba jege kuri mo.

english_verse: Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands.
translation_verse: Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Ni-gwonim delo a na ke de wea kam, de tete dem to yɔɔre de zege mo chekke. A ta ma pa se wɛyuu de tega baŋa taa tɔge chwei selo na yɔɔre se maŋe de-te to.

english_verse: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_verse: Ko ta ye bedwe mo, amo bá ve Jakob dwi dem kɔtaa. A bá swei se a kuri nɔɔno a tontoŋeno David dwi tiina bam wone, se kotu di paare a nɔɔna bam baŋa ne. Abaraham, de Izaak, de Jakob dwi tiina bam mo konto. A wó jwoori a pa se a nɔɔna bam taa jege yu-ywoŋo. A maa wó duri ba yibwona.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me
translation_verse: Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza de o jar-keira bam maama déem tu se ba kwaare jara de Jerusalem teo kom, dedaane ko nawuura yam mo. O jar-keira bam konto déem nwoŋi logo baŋa teene delo maama o na di paare de baŋa ne to wone mo. Maŋa kam konto ne Baŋa Wɛ ma kwei kwora kanto o pa Jeremia ye o we:

english_verse: You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Nmo nam bá‑n lu o jeŋa ne. O nɔɔna wó zi‑m ba daare ba ja ba vo o tei. Konto to, nmo wó zege Babilon teo pɛ wom yiga ne se á ŋɔɔne daane. Nmo laam ma‑n jege se n vo Babilon.

english_verse: I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Wɛ sampwora Jeremia déem ma vo Judah teo pɛ Zedekia tei Jerusalem wone, ye o ta wonnu tento maama o bere‑o.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured. The People Break a Promise
translation_verse: Konto maama de Babilon teo pɛ wom jar-keira yɔɔre ba jege Jerusalem teo kom mo ba kwaare jara ko baŋa ne. Ba déem ta wora ba ke jara de Lakisi teo kom, de Azeka teo kom de mo. Judah kateiri teene delo na lɔge de pe to wone, teene delei dem konto yerane mo ta zega. Ba na yiri ba ni kabɛ ŋwaane tei to

english_verse: King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
translation_verse: Teo kom nakwa bam de nɔɔna bam maama ma sɛ pɛ wom ni. Ba ma yage ba kabɛ sem pa ba viiri zɛɛra, baara de kaana maama.

english_verse: That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne Baŋa Wɛ ma da ko ŋwaane o kwei kwora kanto o pa Jeremia ye o we,

english_verse: I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom na tage tei to mo tento: “Amo déem na jaane á nabaara bam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne pa se a jwoŋi-ba ba kabɛɛne wone a yage to, mo a ke ni-gwonim de-ba. A ma ta de-ba a we,

english_verse: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Leile konto abam laam yiri á ni dem konto, pa se á jege amo yere dem á yaala! Abam maama jwoori á kwei á kabɛ selo á ya na yage se ba taa tei ba tete to mo. Á ma fe-ba se ba jwoori ba taa toŋe ba pae abam, baara de kaana de.”

english_verse: You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane Baŋa Wɛ daa na tage tei to mo tento: “Abam wo sɛ amo ni se á yage á dwonna Isarele tiina na ye á kabɛ sem to se ba viiri zɛɛra. Mo kokuri amo de lage a yage abam se á vo á te jara wone, se jaweero de kana de ja á badwonna te go. Abam maa wó ji wo-zɔɔna logo baŋa teene maama yia ne.

english_verse: You asked me to be a witness when you made the agreement to set your slaves free. And as part of the ceremony you cut a calf into two parts, then walked between the parts. But you people of Jerusalem have broken that agreement as well as my agreement with Israel. So I will do to you what you did to that calf.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye nɔɔna balo na chɔge ni-gwonim delo a déem na ke de a nɔɔna bam to, amo de lage a chɔge-ba mo. Ba wo ke ba tɔge ni delo ba na gwoni amo yiga ne to. Ba go na-bala mo ba gwoni-ka kuni belei ye, ba daare ba da ka popɔre selei sem tetare laŋa ne ba kɛ ni-gwonim dem ŋwaane. Amo de wó ke-ba ne ba na ke tei de na-bala kam to.

english_verse: These enemies are King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia and his army. They have stopped attacking Jerusalem, but they want to kill King Zedekiah and his high officials. So I will command them to return and attack again. This time they will conquer the city and burn it down, and they will capture Zedekiah and his officials. I will also let them destroy the towns of Judah, so that no one can live there any longer.
translation_verse: Amo nam lage a pa-ba ni mo se ba jwoori ba ba ywo. A maa wó pa se ba daa kwaare jara de teo konto. Ba lage ba di-ko mo se ba daare ba zwɛ-ko kula! Amo ta wó pa se Judah teene dem taa ye di-dwonnu yerane, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé wane de wone o zo.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei tei to mo konto.

english_verse: “Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
translation_verse: “Zaŋe n vo mɛ Rekabi sɔŋɔ tiina bam na zoore to, se n bwoŋi-ba se á da daane á vo Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem. Ja-ba n zo ko di sem dedoa wone, se n laam pa-ba sana se ba nyɔ.”

english_verse: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
translation_verse: Amo ma seene a vo Jeremia bu Jaazania tei. Wonto ta ye Habazinia naa mo. A ma bwoŋi Jaazania de o chorro tem, de o bia bam maama. Rekabi sɔŋɔ tiina bam maama mo konto.

english_verse: I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
translation_verse: A ma ja-ba a zo Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem wone. Dé déem zo diga kalo ba na pɛ Wɛ tontoŋeno Hanan tɔgena bam to mo. Hanan déem ye Igadalia bu mo. Banto diga kam déem saŋe dedɛɛra bam diga kam mo, ye ka wo Salum bu Maaseya diga kam yuu ne. Maaseya déem ye Wɛ diga kam ni-yerena bam dedoa mo.

english_verse: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
translation_verse: A laam ma kwei kɔɔra de ba wone sana a zege Rekabi sɔŋɔ tiina bam yiga ne. Zwe selo ba na wó nyɔ se wone to de maa wora. A ma ta de-ba a we, “Nyɔ-na á na lage tei to.”

english_verse: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
translation_verse: Ba ma leiri-ne ba we, “Debam chuli sana. Dé nabaaro Rekabi bu Jonadabi maŋe o pa debam ni ye o we, ‘Abam de á bia dae se á nyɔ sana.

english_verse: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
translation_verse: Abam ta ba jege se á lɔ sam, naa se á du wo-dwa tega ne, naa se á jeiri Vini teeni. Yé ke-na wonnu tento kolokolo. Ta‑á zoore-na vwoa wone. Konto mo wó pa se á ta‑á kare á beeri tega kam ne ye á dáane taa.’

english_verse: Our clan has always obeyed Jonadab's command. To this very day, we and our wives and sons and daughters don't drink wine or build houses or plant vineyards or crops. And we have lived in tents,
translation_verse: Dé maa yɔɔre dé zoore vwoa wone mo. Konto to, dé sɛ dé nabaaro Jonadabi ni dem maama.

english_verse: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
translation_verse: Nii-na! Rekabi bu Jonadabi déem pɛ o kwaga kam ni we ba yé nyɔ sana. Ba ma yɔɔre ba sɛ o ni dem mo, pa se de zem maama ba ba nyɔ sana. Amo nam yɔɔre a pae abam ni-kaana mo titwon-twono. De ko de, á ta ba sɛ a ni dem.

english_verse: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
translation_verse: Rekabi dwi tiina bam yɔɔre ba sɛ ba nabaaro wom ni mo chekke. Ko nam ná ye abam, á ba sɛ amo ni kɔtaa!’

english_verse: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: ‘Nii-na! Amo laam lage a pa se lɛɛro yɔɔre ko ba Jerusalem tiina bam de Judah tiina bam maama baŋa ne, ne a na wuuri a ta we a wó ke tei to. Kokuri to, amo yɔɔre a ŋɔɔne de-ba mo, ye ba ba cheiga. A ta ma kwaane a bwoi-ba, ye ba ve se ba leiri-ne.’ ”

english_verse: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Bene delo Josia bu Jehoyakim na di Judah paare o ke bena yana to ne mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ Jeremia ni o we,

english_verse: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
translation_verse: “Beeri tɔnɔ se n popone wonnu telo a na maŋe a ta dede‑m se ko vo Isarele tiina bam, de Judah tiina bam, dedaane dwi-gɛ tiina bam maama seeni to n tiŋi ko wone. Nam popone wonnu telo a na tage a bere‑m ko zege Josia paare dim maŋa ne se ko yi leile to n tiŋi.

english_verse: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
translation_verse: Dɛ delo Judah tiina bam ná lɔre lɛɛro telo maama a na boŋe se a pa te yi-ba to, ba wó leiri ba boboŋa de ba lwarem kikia yam. Amo de maa wó da ko ŋwaane a yage ba wɛleera yam de ba tusim dem a chɛ-ba.”

english_verse: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
translation_verse: Jeremia ma toŋe o bwoŋi Neria bu Baruki. O na tu to, Jeremia ma lwoni kolo maama Baŋa Wɛ ya na pɛ‑o se o ta to, ye Baruki de popone-te o ke tɔnɔ wone.

english_verse: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Jeremia ta ma ta de Baruki o we, “Ba chege amo chwoŋa mo we a daa yé zo Baŋa Wɛ diga kam ne.

english_verse: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
translation_verse: Konto to, nɔɔna bam ni-vɔre dɛ daa ná yia, se n zaŋe n vo Wɛ diga kam. N laam ma‑n wó puri tɔnɔ konto n ga Baŋa Wɛ taane delo o na pɛ-ne, ye a lwoni a pa‑m ye n de popone n tiŋi to n bere nɔɔna bam. Ga-ko se Judah tiina bam na nwoŋi ba teene dem wone ba ba ba jeeri da to maama cheigi.

english_verse: In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud. This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials.
translation_verse: Baruki déem na zo Wɛ diga kam to, o ma vo o zege pɛ sɔŋɔ tɔn-poponno Safan bu Gemaria diga kam seeni. Diga kam konto déem wo Wɛ diga konkɔlɔ kolo na wo baŋa ne to ne mo ye ka bwola de ni delo ba na bwoi we ‘Ni-doore’ ni to. Baruki zege dáane mo o ga taane delo Jeremia na pɛ‑o ye o popone o ke tɔnɔ kom ne to pa nɔɔna bam maama ni.

english_verse: Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Gemaria bu Mikaya ma ni Baŋa Wɛ kwora kalo Baruki na gage to maama.

english_verse: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
translation_verse: O ma tu o vo o zo pɛ sɔŋɔ tɔn-poponno wom diga kam ne. Teo dedɛɛra bam maama maa jei da ba bane wonnu. Banto maa ye: Elisama wolo laam na ye tɔn-poponno to, de Semaya bu Delaya, de Akebora bu Elinatan, de Safan bu Gemaria, de Hanania bu Zedekia, de dedɛɛra badaara bam maama.

english_verse: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
translation_verse: Mikaya ma ta o bere-ba Baruki na gage wonnu telo ye nɔɔna bam maama ni to.

english_verse: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
translation_verse: Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Jeini tega ne, se n ga-ko n bere debam.” Baruki de ma ke ba na we o ke tei to.

english_verse: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
translation_verse: Ba na nigi tɔnɔ kom taane dem maama to, mo ba nii daane ye foone tiini de zo-ba. Ba ma ta de Baruki ba we, “Dé jege se dé pa pɛ wom ni tɔnɔ konto ŋwa mo.”

english_verse: “Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
translation_verse: Baruki ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, Jeremia mo yɔɔre o lwei ta-bu maama o bere-ne, ye amo de popone-ya a tiŋi tɔnɔ kom wone konto jaja.”

english_verse: The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
translation_verse: Dedɛɛra bam ma ta de Baruki ba we, “Nmo de Jeremia jege se á beeri jei mo á seigi da. Yé pa-na se nɔɔn-nɔɔno lɔre abam na wo mɛ to.”

english_verse: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ta ma pa ni se pa-bu Jerameeli, de Azireli bu Seraya, de Abedeli bu Selemia vo ba ja Baruki na ye tɔn-poponno to, de Wɛ sampwora Jeremia ba ba ba pa‑o. Baŋa Wɛ nam ya mo kwei-ba o seigi. Jeremia daa pɛ se Baruki popone tɔnɔ kodwoŋi

english_verse: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
translation_verse: Pɛ wom na zwɛ tɔnɔ kolo Jeremia déem na tɛa ye Baruki popone o tiŋi ko wone to, ye ko ke fee ko woli da to, mo Baŋa Wɛ daa pɛ Jeremia ni o we,

english_verse: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
translation_verse: “Beeri tɔnɔ kodwoŋi se n jwoori n popone taane delo maama ya na wo boboa tɔnɔ kom ne ye Judah pɛ Jehoyakim zwɛ-ko to n ke ko wone.

english_verse: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
translation_verse: Nmo ta wó ta de Pɛ Jehoyakim we, ‘Baŋa Wɛ kwora mo tento: Boboa tɔnɔ kom tɛ ko bere we Babilon teo pɛ wó ba o di teo konto, o daare o chɔge tega kam pa se nabiina de vara maama mo jei ka wone. Nmo nam kwei tɔnɔ kom konto n zwɛ, n na wo sɛ Jeremia na popone kolo to ŋwaane.

english_verse: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwora kalo nam na wora Judah teo pɛ Jehoyakim ŋwaane to mo tento: Nmo bá na dwi se kotu jeini Pɛ David yituŋu kom baŋa ne o di Judah teo paare. Nmo ná tega, ba bá suli n yera tega kam wone. Ya nam wó taa tigi pwola ne mo, se wea de waaro zo-ya lanyerane.

english_verse: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
translation_verse: A nam lage a waare‑m mo, de n bia, de n tontoŋena, á lwarem kikia ŋwaane. A ta lage a tiini a lwo lɛɛro dedɛ mo a yage balo na zoore Jerusalem teo ne de Judah laŋa kam maama ne to yuu ne, ba na wo cheigi a taane dem to ŋwaane. Amo wó waare-ba ne a na pwooli we a wó ke-ba tei to maama mo.’ ”

english_verse: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_verse: Jeremia daa ma kwei tɔnɔ kodwoŋi o pa o tɔn-poponno Baruki na ye Neria bu to. O déem maa tɛa wonnu tem ye Baruki de popone-te o tiŋa. O ma popone kolo maama na wo boboa tɔnɔ kom wone ye pɛ Jehoyakim zwɛ to o ke ko de wone. Jeremia ta ma ta wonnu tedwonna ye Baruki popone-te o woli da.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
translation_verse: Pɛ Nebukadeneza déem tiŋi Josia bu Zedekia mo se o leiri Jehoyakim bu Jehoyachin yuu ne o ji Judah teo pɛ.

english_verse: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Zedekia, de o tontoŋena balo na woli‑o to, de Judah tiina bam maama nam wo sɛ kwora kalo Baŋa Wɛ déem na pɛ o sampwora Jeremia se o ta o bere-ba to.

english_verse: Later, the Babylonian army attacked Jerusalem, but they left after learning that the Egyptian army was headed in this direction. One day, Zedekiah sent Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah to talk with me. At that time, I was free to go wherever I wanted, because I had not yet been put in prison. Jehucal and Zephaniah said, “Jeremiah, please pray to the Lord our God for us.”
translation_verse: Ko ta maŋe de Babilon tiina jar-keira bam ya tu ba kaare Jerusalem teo kom ba pu mo. Ba maa na nigi we Ejipti pa-faro jar-keira bam nwoŋi ba teo kom ne ba beene se ba jeeri-ba de jara to, mo ba tutwoni ba jwoori ba viiri ba daare Jerusalem teo kom.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
translation_verse: “Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom na tage tei to mo tento: Judah teo pɛ Zedekia toŋe nmo mo se n ba n bwei-ne n nii kolo na wó ke to. Nam ta n bere‑o we, Ejipti pa-faro jar-keira bam seene ba nwoŋi ba ba se ba woli abam. Ba nam wó jwoori ba tete teo ba daare abam,

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: se Babilon tiina bam de pipiri ba ba ba kwaare jara teo konto baŋa ne. Ba lage ba di-ko mo, ye ba daare ba zwɛ-ko kula!

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Abam ya ná maŋe á di Babilon jar-keira bam maama mo, pa se balo na nɛ zonne to yerane daare ba tigi ba vwoa wone de, banto mo lage ba nwoŋi ba vwoa yam ne ba zwɛ teo konto maama kula!”

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Babilon teo jar-keira bam déem viiri mo ba daare Jerusalem teo kom, Ejipti pa-faro jar-keira bam na beene to ŋwaane.

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: Jeremia ma ja boboŋa se o nwoŋi Jerusalem teo kom ne o vo Benjamin kateiri dem ne se o jwoŋi tega o sɔŋɔ tiina bam popɔra wone.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: O ma vo o yi teo kom manchwoŋo ni delo ba na bwoi we ‘Benjamin Ni’ to se o nwoŋi o kɛ. O na yi da to, mo jar-keira yiga tu wodwoŋi zege da, o na ye Selemaya bu Irija, de Hanania naa to. O ma zi Jeremia ye o ta ded‑o o we, “Nmo laam lage n gɔ n zo Babilon tiina kɔgɔ kom wone mo na?”

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: Jeremia ma leiri‑o o we, “Ko dae chega. Amo wo lɔge á kwaga ne se a daare a zo Babilon kɔgɔ kom wone.” De ko de, Irija wo sɛ. O ma ja Jeremia o yi dedɛɛra bam tei.

english_verse: They were angry and ordered the soldiers to beat me. Then I was taken to the house that belonged to Jonathan, one of the king's officials. It had been turned into a prison, and I was kept in a basement room. After I had spent a long time there,
translation_verse: Ba ma ja Jeremia ba vo ba pe diga kalo wone ba na lugi tega ne to. Ba ma yage‑o pa o maŋe da o dáane.

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: Pɛ Zedekia ma toŋe pa ba ja‑o ba ba o tei pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne. O ma bwei‑o tega tega o we, “Baŋa Wɛ daa pɛ‑m kwora na?” Jeremia ma leiri‑o o we, “Ɛɛ, kwora wora.” O ta ma ta o we, “Ba seene ba lage ba ja‑m ba vo ba ke Babilon teo pɛ jeŋa ne mo.”

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Jeremia laam ma bwei pɛ wom o we, “A ke bɛ mo a chɔge nmo yiga, de n teo dedɛɛra bam, de nɔɔna bam maama yiga, ye abam yɔɔre á pe-ne á yage peena diga wone?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Nmo tete sampwori sem tage de nmo ba we, ‘Babilon teo pɛ bá ba ywo se o kwaare jara de nmo, naa de tega kanto.’ Banto nam vei yei ne mo?

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: Pɛ Zedekia ma sɛ ye o daare o pa ni se ba ja‑o ba vo ba pe pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom wone. Pɛ wom ta ma pa ni se ba taa pae Jeremia bworobworo dedoa dɛ maama wone, ne bworobworo ná lwoori ko wo teo kom wone. Jeremia déem ma maŋe pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom mɛ ba na pe‑o to wone.

english_verse: that the Lord had said, “If you stay here in Jerusalem, you will die in battle or from disease or hunger, and the Babylonian army will capture the city anyway. But if you surrender to the Babylonians, they will let you live.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we: ‘Babilon teo pɛ jar-keira bam wó seene ba wane teo konto ba di se ba taa tei-ko.’ ”

english_verse: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
translation_verse: Teo kom dedɛɛra bam na nigi Jeremia ni taane dem to, ba ma ta de pɛ wom ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto maŋe se o te mo. O na jege taane delo o ŋɔɔne de jar-keira bam, de nɔɔna bam maama to yɔɔre de bwori ba nɛ mo. O ba lage nɔɔna bam wolim, o beeri ba chɔgem mo.”

english_verse: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
translation_verse: Ba ma kwei Jeremia ba de pa-bu Malekia vole-kore wone. De déem wo pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne mo. Ba ma kwei ŋone ba ba‑o, ye ba daare ba dole‑o ba de vole dem wone. Na déem tere de wone, se bworu yerane mo su da. Jeremia ma moore bworu tem wone.

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: “Pɛ, nɔɔna banto tiini ba chɔge de ba na ke tei Jeremia yera ne to. Ba dole‑o mo ba yage vole dem wone se o yaare de kana o te, wodiu na lage ko jei teo kom ne to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: Ebede-Mɛlɛka ma tɔge de nɔɔna bam ye ba zo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom diga kadwoŋi na wo jejegero tiŋim diga kam kuri ne to. Ba ma na gare-zenzwara yadwonna da, ye ba daare ba kwei-ya ba lei de ŋona. Ba ma vo ba de-ya vole dem wone se ya yi Jeremia na wo mɛ to.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: Ebede-Mɛlɛka ma tɔɔle o ta de Jeremia vole dem ne o we, “Kwei gare-zenzwara yanto n ke n pulugu kuri ne, se ŋona kam yé fuuli‑m. Dé laam wó ma-ka dé le‑m.” Jeremia ma ke konto.

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: Ba ma vaŋe‑o ba le vole dem wone, ye ba daare ba ja‑o ba vo ba pe pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne. O ma lɛɛre o wo dáane. Zedekia bwei Jeremia bwia yadwonna

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe Pɛ Zedekia ma toŋe pa ba ja Jeremia ba ba o tei. Ba ma jeeri daane Baŋa Wɛ wara-jei sem nia yatɔ tu ni dem ne. Ba na nɛ daane to mo pɛ wom tage ded‑o o we, “A lage a bwei‑m bwia mo. Nam yé seigi kolokolo a yiga ne.”

english_verse: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
translation_verse: Pɛ Zedekia ma seigi o gwoni ni de Jeremia ye o we, “A dugi duuri Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane, o na ye wolo na pae debam ŋwea to, we amo bá go‑m. A nam bá le‑m a pa balo na beeri‑m se ba go to.”

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Jeremia ma ta de Zedekia o we, “Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: ‘Nmo ná to n pa Babilon teo pɛ dedɛɛra bam, ba bá go‑m. Ba nam bá zwɛ dé teo kom. Nmo de n diga tiina de wó jwoŋi á tete á yage.

english_verse: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
translation_verse: Ko daare, nmo ná wo sɛ n pa Babilon teo pɛ dedɛɛra bam, lɔre we teo konto lage ko zo Babilon tiina bam je ne mo se ba zwɛ-ko kula. Nmo de n diga tiina bam de nam bá lu ba jeŋa ne.’ ”

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Pɛ Zedekia ma leiri Jeremia o we, “Ko nam ná ye Judah tiina balo na duri ba yage debam ye ba zo Babilon tiina bam wone to, a kɔre foone de-ba mo. Babilon tiina bam ná kwei-ne ba ke banto je ne, ba wae ba pa ko tiini ko zoore a yera.”

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: Jeremia ma leiri‑o o we, “Ba bá le‑m ba pa-ba. Nmo ná yɔɔre n sɛ Baŋa Wɛ ni dem ne a na bere‑m se n ke tei to, nmo wó jwoŋi n tete n yage. N ŋwea de maa wó ke lanyerane.

english_verse: But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey,
translation_verse: Ko daare, nmo ná ve se n to n pa Babilon tiina bam, nam lɔre we Baŋa Wɛ le wonnu tento mo o bere-ne:

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: Ba lage ba kwei kaana balo maama ta na daare Judah pɛ sɔŋɔ ne to mo ba ja ba vo ba pa Babilon teo pɛ dedɛɛra bam. Kaana bam konto laam maa wó taa tɛ de nmo ba we: ‘Ba gane‑m mo ba de tega ne. Ko nam ye n badwonna balo n na pɛ-ba chega to mo ke konto. N nɛ sem laam na moore bworu wone to, mo ba maama duri ba jei ba daare‑m.’

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: Ba lage ba ja n kaana de n bia bam maama mo ba nwoŋi ba ke Babilon tiina bam jeŋa ne. Nmo tete de nam bá lu ba jeŋa ne. Babilon teo pɛ wó seene o ja‑m. Ba maa wó daare ba zwɛ teo konto kula.”

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Zedekia daa ta ma ta de Jeremia o we, “Yé ta de nɔɔn-nɔɔno n na tage tei de amo tento to. Ko ná dae konto, n wae n toe taane dento ŋwaane.

english_verse: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
translation_verse: Teo kom dedɛɛra bam ná nigi we amo de nmo ŋɔɔne daane, ba wó taa lage se ba lɔre dé na bwɛ kolo to. Ba wae ba fugi‑m ye ba we, ‘N ná seigi kolo n na tage to se dé yé lɔre ko ni ne, dé wó go‑m.’

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: Ko ná ye konto, se n ta de-ba we, ‘A ya lwoori pɛ wom mo se o yé pa a jwoori Jonatan sɔŋɔ kom ne. Kokuri to, a ná jwoori dáane, a wó te mo.’ ”

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom dedɛɛra bam ma seene ba vo Jeremia tei se ba bwei‑o ba lɔre kolo ŋwaane pɛ wom na toŋe o bwoŋi‑o to. O ma ta de-ba kolo maama pɛ wom na bere‑o se o ta to. Ba daa maa wo tage kolokolo ded‑o, kokuri to, nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo nigi kolo Jeremia déem na tage de pɛ wom to.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: Jeremia déem ma lɛɛre o maŋe pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne o zoore da, se ko yi maŋa kalo Babilon tiina bam na di Jerusalem teo kom jara wone to.

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Judah teo Pɛ Zedekia de o jar-keira bam maama na nɛ we Babilon teo dedɛɛra bam zo ba jei teo kom manchwo-peo kom ni ne to, mo ba duri se ba lu tete ne. Ba kwei pɛ gaare chwoŋa kam mo, ba vo ba tɔge ni dem na wo teo kabiri selei sem tetare ne to, ye ba laam ma tu Jɔdan bwolo kom seeni.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: “Zaŋe n vo Kusi tu Ebede-Mɛlɛka tei, se n ta ded‑o we, ‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo laam lage a pa se a na gwoni ni delo teo konto seeni to ji chega mo. Ba lage ba na lɛɛro mo, se ko dae lam. Nmo yia nam wó na kolo maama amo na wó ke to.

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: “Kwaane-na á beeri Jeremia jei se á nii o baŋa ne lanyerane. Yé zaŋe-na á ke‑o zonne. Nam ke-na kolo maama o na lage to á pa‑o.”

english_verse: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
translation_verse: De ko de, Babilon teo jar-keira bam déem pare-ba mo. Ba ma vo ba yi ba ja Zedekia se ko maŋe de Jeriko te-kampare sem seeni. Ba ma zi‑o ba ja ba vo Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza tei. O déem wo Ribila teo ne mo, Hamafa kateiri dem ne. Nebukadeneza ma di taane o vane Zedekia dáane.

english_verse: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.
translation_verse: O ma pa ba go Zedekia bia bam, ye o zege da o nia. O ta ma pa ba go Judah teo dedɛɛra bam maama.

english_verse: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne o ta pɛ se ba kokɔrege Zedekia yia yam mo ba le, ye ba daare ba kwei channa chegero ba ma ba vɔ‑o ba vaŋe ba jege ba maa kɛ Babilon.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Babilon tiina bam déem zwɛ pɛ sɔ-fɔrɔ kom, de nɔɔna bam sam dem mo, ye ba daare ba yigi Jerusalem teo kabiri sem ba de tega ne.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan déem mo ye Babilon babɛ sem yiga tu. O ma kale nɔɔna balo ya ta na daare teo kom wone to, de balo na duri ba zo Babilon tiina kɔgɔ kom wone to o ja o vo Babilon teo kom.

english_verse: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye yiniga tiina balo na ba jege kolokolo to, Nebuzaradan ma yage-ba Judah laŋa kam ne. O ma pa-ba tega se ba va, de Vini teeni kare, se ba taa nii se baŋa ne.

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: ba toŋe nɔɔna pa ba vo pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom mɛ ba na pe Jeremia to ba ja‑o ba nwoŋi. Ba ma kwei‑o ba pa Ahikam bu Gedalia se wonto taa nii o baŋa ne. Gedalia déem ye Safan naa mo. O ma ja Jeremia o vo sɔŋɔ. Konto mo tei Jeremia maŋe o tete nɔɔna bam tei ne.

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Maŋa kam ba ta na pe Jeremia pɛ sɔŋɔ konkɔlɔ kom ne to, Baŋa Wɛ ya pɛ‑o kwora kanto mo we:

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Amo wó taa yere n ŋwea kam a pa‑m. Nmo bá‑n te jara wone. N nam wó jwoŋi n tete n yage, n na ke n wo-dedoa de amo to ŋwaane. Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto!’ ”

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Ba déem kale nɔɔna balo maama ta na daare Jerusalem teo kom wone de Judah laŋa kam maama ne to mo ba maa vei Babilon. Ba na yi Rama to, Babilon babɛ sem yiga tu Nebuzaradan ma na Jeremia ba wone de ba vɔge‑o de chegero mo. O laam ma bwoli‑o o yage. Konto kwaga ne mo Baŋa Wɛ pɛ Jeremia ni.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan said: Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan ma ta de Jeremia o we, “Abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom maŋe o ta we lɛɛro tento wó ba á teo kom baŋa.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Amo zem nam lage a bwoli n je chegero tem mo, se a yage‑m se n ta‑n tei n tete. Nmo ná kuri se n tɔge de amo n vo Babilon teo kom, se dé kɛ. Amo wó taa nii n baŋa ne dáane. N nam ná ba lage se n vo da, ko dae fefeo. Ko wo nmo tei ne. Tega kanto na tigi n yiga ne palalala to, n wae n kuri mɛ maama n na lage to, se n vo n jeini da.”

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Jeremia ma vo Ahikam bu Gedalia tei Mizipa ne. O maa zoore de nɔɔna balo fenfee na daare ba wo Judah laŋa kam wone to. Gedalia taane

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Amo tete wó maŋe ywo Mizipa ne, se a yeini a ŋɔɔne a pa abam, ne Babilon tiina bam ná yeini ba ba se ba jeeri debam. Nam jwoori-na teo kolo maama á na di to se á ta‑á zoore ko wone. Abam maa wó gwori Vini tio-bia, de mɔɔro, se á daare á ta‑á ke sana de nuga á zega.”

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo Karea bu Johanan, de jar-keira yiga tiina balo ya na wo sɛ ba pa Babilon teo pɛ wom to tu Gedalia tei Mizipa ne.

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: Ba ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Ta‑n yei we Amon tiina pɛ Baalisi toŋe Netania bu Isameli mo se o ba o go‑m.” Gedalia maa wo sɛ ba taane dem.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Johanan ma vo Mizipa o na Gedalia tega tega ye o we, “Nam pa-ne chwoŋa se a vo a seigi a go Isameli. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá lɔre ko ni ne. Bɛŋwaane mo dé wó taa jei dé nii se o go nmo? Konto ná kea, Judah tiina balo na tu nmo tei tento to maama wó jage mo, pa se balo na daare Judah laŋa kam ne to de jei.”

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Gedalia déem maa wo sɛ ye o ta de Johanan o we, “Yé ke konto! Nmo na tɛ Isameli yera taane tei to dae chega.”

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Bene dem konto chane serepɛ chana kam wone, mo Netania bu Isameli na ye Elisama naa to déem tɔge de nɔɔna fuga pa ba vo Mizipa. Wonto déem ye pa-diga kam wo nɔɔno mo. O ya ye pɛ wom dedɛɛra bam wone dedoa mo. O de o nɔɔna bam ma vo Ahikam bu Gedalia tei, ye ba jei ba di wodiu daane.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Isameli ta ma go Judah tiina balo maama na wo Gedalia tei ne to, dedaane Babilon teo jar-keira balo de na wo Mizipa ne to.

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Tega na poore ye nɔɔna ta wo lɔre we ba go Gedalia to,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Ba na maa beene to, Isameli ma nwoŋi Mizipa ne o vo o jeeri-ba chwoŋa ne. O maa keeri ye o via. O na yi-ba to, mo o tage de-ba o we, “Ba-na se dé tɔge daane dé vo Ahikam bu Gedalia tei.”

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Ba na yɔɔre ba zo teo kom wone to, mo Isameli de o nɔɔna bam go-ba. Ba ma dole ba yera yam ba yage na-keim gwoŋo wone.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam wone fuga nam ya tage de Isameli ba we, “Yé go debam, se dé ya seigi dé mena, de nuga, de tooro gaao kom jei sedwoŋi ne. Dé nam wó ja-te dé ba dé pa‑m.” Isameli ma sɛ ye o wo go-ba ne o na ke tei de nɔɔna badaara bam to.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Isameli na go nɔɔna bam ye o kwei ba yera yam o dole o de gwoŋo kolo wone to, ye kolo Judah teo Pɛ Asa déem na koge to mo. O ya koge gwoŋ-kamunu kom se o ma che Mizipa teo kom se Isarele teo pɛ Baasa yé wane-ko o di mo. Netania bu Isameli déem kwei twa bam konto o suuri ko ni dem maama mo.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo maama ta na daare ye ba wo Mizipa teo kom ne to, mo Isameli déem kale o ja o viiri. Ko maa ye pɛ bukwa bam, de balo maama Babilon babɛ sem yiga tu Nebuzaradan déem na kwei o ke Gedalia jeŋa ne se o taa nii ba baŋa ne to mo konto. Netania bu Isameli kale ba maama ye ba kwei chwoŋa ba maa vei Amon.

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Ba ma ja ba nɔɔna bam maama ba ke ba kwaga ne, ye ba pɛ Isameli de o nɔɔna bam kwaga ba pu. Ba déem vei ba yi-ba Gibeon bu-kayɔlɔ kom ni ne mo.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye Isameli, o de o nɔɔna nana mo lugi Johanan jeŋa ne pa se ba duri ba vo Amon teo.

english_verse: toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar. The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_verse: ba na lage se ba lu Babilon tiina bam jeŋa ne to ŋwaane. Kokuri to, ba kɔre Babilon tiina bam mo. Ba yeiri kolo na wó yi-ba de Isameli na go Gedalia wolo Babilon teo pɛ ya na kuri se o taa nii Judah laŋa kam to.

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: ba vo ba yi Wɛ sampwora Jeremia tei ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Ja! Cheigi dé na jege kolo se dé lwoori n tei ne to. Lwoori nmo Tu Baŋa Wɛ n pa debam balo ta na daare Judah ne to. Dé déem ye kɔgɔ mo. Laam nam nii, dé daare fenfee yerane mo.

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: Nam lwoori Baŋa Wɛ se o bere debam dé na wó vo mɛ, dedaane dé na wó ke tei to.”

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Taane dem konto kwaga ne, da fuga mo kɛ ye Baŋa Wɛ laam pa Jeremia o kwora.

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: O ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam toŋe amo Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom tei ne mo. O nam we tento mo:

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: ‘Abam ná maŋe tega kanto ne á zoora, amo wó fɔge a lɔ abam a zege mo, se a bá vaare abam a de tega ne. A ta wó jeiri abam mo te-ywoŋa jei ne, se a bá vuuri abam a gɔ a yage. Kokuri to, a wo tiini ko chɔge de a na pɛ lɛɛro telo ba abam baŋa ne to.

english_verse: Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him,
translation_verse: Nam daa yé ta‑á kɔre foone de Babilon teo pɛ wom, se amo wo á tei ne se a jwoŋi abam o jeŋa ne a yage.

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Abam nam daa yé ve abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ ni dem se á ta nenɛɛne, ‘Debam bá maŋe teo konto ne’.

english_verse: People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen.
translation_verse: Abam Judah tiina balo nam na daare tega kam ne to, cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ taane dem. Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Abam nam ná kuri se á vo Ejipti teo kom á ta‑á zoora,

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Chega ŋwaane to, ko ná ye balo maama na lage ba duri ba vo Ejipti se ba taa zoore da to, banto wó te jara wone, de kana baŋa ne, de jawe-chɛɛro baŋa ne mo. Ba wolowolo bá lu de lɛɛro telo a na wó kwei a ke ba yera ne to.’

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage tei to mo tento: ‘Á ná yɔɔre á vo á zo Ejipti teo kom ne, amo wó tiini a lwo a ban-lom abam baŋa ne, ne a bane déem na zaŋe de Jerusalem tiina ye a ke-ba tei to. Á wó ji wo-zɔɔna nɔɔna maama yia ne, pa se ba neese abam. Ba wó taa mɔne abam, ye ba daare ba mae á yere ba sɔɔle lwarem ba pa daane. Abam de nam bá jwoori ywo se á na tega kanto.’ ”

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: Jeremia ta ma ta o we, “Abam Judah tiina balo na daare á tega kam ne to, Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o ta de abam o we, ‘Yé zaŋe-na á vo Ejipti teo kom.’ Nam ta‑á yei-na amo zem na kaane abam tei to.

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: Lɔre-na we abam mo ke á sa chwoŋa de á na toŋe-ne á Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom tei ne, ye á ta á we, ‘Lwoori dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom n pa debam, se n daare n ta o na we dé ke tei to, se dé wó sɛ o ni dem konto.’

english_verse: I told the people everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Jeremia déem ma ta de nɔɔna bam kwora kalo maama ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ‑o se o ta to.

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: O na ti to mo Hosaya bu Azaria, de Karea bu Johanan, de boyere nyena badaara bam tage de Jeremia ba we, “N fɔe vwa mo! Dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ bere o wo toŋe‑m debam tei ne se n ta we dé yé vei dé taa zoore Ejipti ne.

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Dé lɔre n lɔra. Ko nam ye Neria bu Baruki mo chuchugi‑m se n ta tento n bere debam. O maa boŋe se Babilon tiina bam mo na dam dé baŋa ne, se ba wane ba go debam, naa ba kale debam ba ja ba viiri.”

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Johanan, de jar-keira yiga tiina bam maama, de nɔɔna bam maama ma ve Baŋa Wɛ ni dem se ba maŋe Judah laŋa kam ne.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Johanan, de jar-keira yiga tiina bam ma la nɔɔna balo maama na nwoŋi ba ya na jage ba wo teene delo maama wone ye ba jwoori Judah laŋa kam se ba taa zoore da to ba ke daane se ba kɛ Ejipti.

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: Ba ta ma ja nɔɔna balo maama Babilon babɛ sem yiga tu Nebuzaradan na yage o pa Ahikam bu Gedalia se o taa nii-ba to ba ja ba kɛ. Baara, de kaana de bia maa wo kɔgɔ kom wone, ko woli de pɛ bukwa bam. Wɛ sampwora Jeremia dedaane Neria bu Baruki de déem tɔge ba wo ba wone.

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam ma yɔɔre ba ve Baŋa Wɛ ni dem, ye ba vo Ejipti. Ba ma vo ba yi Tapanahesi teo kom.

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: “Beeri kandwa-zana n ja n vo Ejipti Pa-faro sɔŋɔ kolo na wo Tapanahesi ne to. Kwei-ya n suli mɛ ba na kwei dɔgɔ ba fɔge manchwo-peena yam to. Nam ke konto se Judah dwi tiina bam taa zege da ba nia.

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: Laam ta de-ba we, ‘Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: Amo lage a toŋe a bwoŋi Babilon teo Pɛ Nebukadeneza mo se o ba ywo. Wonto ye a tontoŋeno mo. Amo laam maa wó chwi o paare yituŋu kom se ko ja tega kandwa yanto a na seigi to baŋa ne. Wonto wó yarege o woro kom se ko yi yanto de.

english_verse: I will let him set Egypt's temples on fire, and he will either burn or carry off their idols. He will destroy the sacred monuments at the temple of the sun-god. Then Nebuchadnezzar will pick the land clean, just like a shepherd picking the lice off his clothes. And he will return safely home.
translation_verse: O yɔɔre o lage o zo diga kalo Ejipti tiina na zuli wea jwoni dem ka wone to mo. O ta wó yigi kandwa yalo ba na chwi ba jwoni dem konto ŋwaane to o de tega ne. O laam maa wó zwɛ Ejipti tiina jwona yam di sem maama.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem daa ma pa Jeremia kwora kanto se o pa Judah tiina balo na tu ba zoore Ejipti ne to. Balo na zoore Migidola ne, de Tapanahesi ne, de Memfisi ne, dedaane Ejipti teo tega-kuri seeni to mo konto.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: “Abam yi nɛ lɛɛro telo a na pɛ ko yi Jerusalem teo kom, de Judah teene dem maama to. Jei sem konto zem tigi di-dwonnu yerane mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba zoore de wone.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: A ma yeini a toŋe a sampwori sem á tei ne titwon-twono. Ba de maa tɛ ba we, ‘Yé ta‑á ke wo-zɔɔna yanto amo na tiini a chuli to!’

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri, a lwogi a ban-lom Judah teene dem baŋa ne, de Jerusalem teo chwei sem baŋa ne, pa se teene dem konto tiini de chɔge de tigi di-dwonnu yerane, de zem maama.”

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Á na tu á zoore Ejipti teo ywo-seeni ye á je de ke wonnu telo to de á na zuli wa-yɔɔro tei to mo chuchugi a bane. Á boŋe se á da ko ŋwaane á chɔge á tete mo na? Dwi tiina maama wó yaale abam mo ye ba daare ba taa mae á yere ba sɔɔle lwarem ba pa daane.

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: De zem maama de, abam wo bere we á wo chɔge de á kikia yam. Á ma‑á ba nege-ne de. Abam bere á wo sɛ se á tɔge nia yalo a déem na kwei a pa abam de á nabaara bam to.”

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Judah tiina balo maama ya na daare ye ba vo Ejipti teo ba zoore da to wolowolo bá lu cham dem konto wone. Ba daa bá jwoori Judah teo kom, se ba taa zoore da, de ba na maŋe ba jege teena se ba jwoori tei to de. Se ba wone nɔɔna fenfee yerane mo lage ba jwoori ba tete teo kom ne.”

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Jeremia na tage konto to, baara balo maama na yei we ba kaana yeini ba zwɛ wonnu ba ma ke kaanem ba pae wa yadwonna to, de kaana balo maama na zege da to ma leiri o taane dem. Ba déem ye Judah tiina balo maama na tu ba zoore Ejipti teo kom baŋa de kuri seeni to mo.

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: Ba maa we, “Dé bá sɛ taane delo n na tɔge Baŋa Wɛ yere ŋwaane n ta n bere debam to.

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Dé wó ke dé boboŋa na jaane se dé ke tei maama to mo. Debam lage dé zwɛ wonnu mo dé ke kaanem de pa dé Telaao Pa-kana jwoni dem mo, ye dé daare dé lwo sana dé pa-de. Dé wó yɔɔre dé ke nenɛɛne debam, de dé kwoa, de dé pwa, de dé nakwa déem na ke tei Jerusalem teo kom wone de Judah teene dem maama wone to mo. Kokuri to, maŋa kam konto ne, dé déem jege wodiiru dé di dé sui, ye lɛɛro ba yi debam.

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Nam nii! Dé daa na ba zwɛ wonnu dé pae ‘Telaao Pa-kana kam’, ye dé daare dé lwoi sana dé pa‑o to, dé bere dé ba nae ywoni. Dé nɔɔna bam yɔɔre ba to jara wone mo, ye kana de goe ba badwonna.”

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Kaana bam de ma ta ba we, “Debam déem na jege wonnu dé zwɛ dé pae Telaao Pa-kana kam, ye dé ta lwoi sana dé pa‑o to, dé banna yeiri ko ni ne na? Banto nam mo yeini ba zege dé kwaga ne ye dé fɔge maasa na lwoni jwo-kana kam konto nyenyego.”

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: “Ko ná ye wonnu telo abam, de á kwoa bam, de á pwa, de á nakwa, de teo kom nɔɔna maama déem na zwɛ ba ma ba ke kaanem ba pa wa yadwonna Jerusalem teo kom wone de Judah teene dem maama wone to, abam boŋe we á kikia yam konto wo zo Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa ne mo na? O nam wo swei ya swia.

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ yera déem yɔɔre ya chɛ de á puseŋa kikia, de á totoŋ-vɛɛsa yam mo. Mo kokuri o pɛ se á tega kam ji di-dwonnu yerane ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba zoore ka wone. Nɔɔna maa yeini ba mae ka yere ba sɔɔle lwarem ba pa daane.

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: Amo yɔɔre a zege a nii-ba se a ja lɛɛro mo a ba ba baŋa, se ko dae lam. Judah tu wolo maama na wo Ejipti ne to wó te mo. Ba lage ba te jara wone mo, naa kana mo wó go-ba, se ba maama jei.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Ko nam na ye tei to, ba fenfee wó lu jara wone de ba ŋwea, se ba nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne ba jwoori ba jeini Judah laŋa kam ne. Konto to, Judah tiina balo maama na daare to wó lɔre wolo taane na jigi chega to, ko ná ye amo nyem dem, naa banto nyem dem mo.

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: A lage kwei Ejipti teo Pa-faro Hofera a ke o dona balo na beeri‑o se ba go to jeŋa ne mo. Ko wó ke ne a déem na kwei Judah teo pɛ Zedekia a ke o dono Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza jeŋa ne tei to mo. Nebukadeneza de nam ya beeri‑o mo se o go.”

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: “Isarele tiina Baŋa Wɛ wom na tage kolo de nmo Baruki to mo tento:

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: Nmo kare n tɛ mo n we, ‘Lɛɛro wo a yuu ne! Baŋa Wɛ fɔge o kwei wo-chechɔgɔ mo o woli a zonne dem wone. Amo yera laam chɛ mo de vuvunim, ye siu tera a tei ne.’ ”

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, nmo ná beeri kamunim se n pa n tete, yé ke konto. Kokuri to, amo lage a pa lɛɛro mo yi nabiina maama. Ko daare nmo, amo wó pa se, n ná ma‑n vei mɛ maama, se n jwoŋi n tete n yage. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.”

english_verse: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ o sampwora Jeremia kwora kalo dwi-gɛ tiina seeni to mo tento:

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: Ejipti teo taane mo tento. Judah teo pɛ Josia bu Jehoyakim paare dim bena yana bene dem ne mo Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza déem wane Ejipti Pa-faro Neko jara wone. Jara yam déem ke Karekemisi laŋa ne mo ye ko bwola de Yuferata buga kam. Ejipti Pa-faro jar-keira bam taane mo tento:

english_verse: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
translation_verse: “Tigisi-na á zege de á jara zela se á vo á ke jara!

english_verse: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
translation_verse: Kwɛ-na á sisein-nɔɔna bam se á daare á di-se. Chichei á zege jara zega ye á yu-gwonnu wo á yuni ne. Dwori-na á chichwoa yam, se á fɔge á vɔ á jara zela yam.”

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Bembɛ selo na wara to bá lu, ba ná maŋe ba duri lela tei de. Ba ná duri ba yi tega kam baŋa seeni, ba lage ba to ba te Yuferata buga kam ni ne mo.

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: Wɔ mo zaŋe wɛɛne tento, ne Naili buga kam na yeini ka su ka pɛɛle tei to?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: Ejipti teo mo konto. Ko yɔɔre ko zaŋe mo ne Naili buga na ke tei to. Ko yɔɔre ko zaŋe mo fugi-fugi. Ejipti tiina maa tɛ ba we, ‘Dé wó zaŋe dé faare logo baŋa jei maama mo. Dé laam maa wó chɔge teene dem, dedaane de nɔn-bia.’

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Fe-na á sisein-nɔɔna bam se se vo jara wone! Duri-na á torokooro tem de fora! Abam bembɛ sem, nwoŋi-na se á kwaare jara. Kusi tiina, de Puti tiina, ja-na á jara tankwallo á nwoŋi. Ludi tiina, saŋe-na á tɛ sem.

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam mo tei dɛ dento. De ye jena ŋweem dɛ mo, dɛ delo ne o na wó ŋwe jene o dona baŋa ne to. O se-zɔɔ kom wó go ba maama ko ti. Ko ta wó nyɔ ba jana ko su, se ko laam yage ba chɔgem. Kokuri to, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na ye Dam-fɔrɔ Tu to lage o ma o dona o ke kaanem mo Yuferata buga kam ni ne.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Logo baŋa dwi tiina wó ni chaveera na jaane abam tei to. Á keira kam de wó jage ka yi tega baŋa jei maama ne. Abam teo babɛ sem wó gare daane mo, ye ba maama laam tiri ba to da-baŋa ne.” Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza taane

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: “Tɔɔle taane dento se de jage de yi Ejipti teene dem maama. Pa se Migidola tiina ni-de, se Memfisi tiina, de Tapanahesi tiina de ni-de. ‘Ke-na á tete daane se á ke jara! Kokuri to, nɔɔna balo na gilimi abam to wora ba to jara wone mo.’

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ nam ye Pɛ mo chekke. Wonto mo we, “Amo yɔɔre a ye Ŋwea Tu Baŋa Wɛ mo. Babea wó ba o jeeri abam o na ye kamunu ne Tabora peo kom na dwoi peero maama tei to. Kotu wó taa zege wɛɛne chwolololo, ne Kamele peo na zege wɛɛne tei naneo kom ni ne to.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Abam balo na zoore Ejipti wone to, lu-na á zela á ke daane, se ba lage ba kale abam mo ba ja ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga. Kokuri to, Memfisi teo wó ba ko chɔge, pa se ko ji di-dwonnu mo ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba zoore da.

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: Ejipti teo nye de na-chwɛ mo na lana chekke to. De ko de, zɔɔ nam mo wó nwoŋi baŋa seeni ko ba ko done-ko.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Ejipti tiina bam wó di chaveera, baŋa seeni nɔɔna bam na wó di-ba jara wone to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to tage tento mo o we: “Nii-na! A ti a yiga mo se a waare Tebesi teo jwoni Amon, de Ejipti jwona yadwonna yam. A nam ta wó waare Ejipti Pa-faro wom, de ko pwa badwonna bam, de ko nɔn-bia bam, ko ta woli de balo maama na kwei ba chega ba daŋe Ejipti Pa-faro wom baŋa ne to.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: A yɔɔre a lage a kwei-ba mo a ke balo na beeri-ba se ba go to jeŋa ne. Ko maa ye Babilon teo Pɛ Nebukadeneza de o dedɛɛra bam mo konto. Kwaga seeni, a nam wó pa se ba daa jwoori ba taa zoore Ejipti wone ne faŋa kam to.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto. Baŋa Wɛ wó jwoŋi o nɔɔna o yage

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ o sampwora Jeremia kwora kalo Filisi tiina bam ŋwaane, ye Ejipti Pa-faro wom ya ta wo kwaare jara de Gaza teo to mo tento:

english_verse: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam wó ni sisein-nɔɔna napɔɔna na dɔna. Ba dona jara-keim torokooro tem de maa ke sɔɔ, te nɛ sem na dɔne to ŋwaane. Nɔɔna wó duri ba daare ba bia, foone na jege-ba ye ba vɔna pare to ŋwaane.

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, dɛ delo Wɛ na wó chɔge Filisi tiina bam maama to yia. Maŋa yia se balo ta na daare ye ba woli Tura de Sidon tiina to jei. Baŋa Wɛ ti o yiga mo se o chɔge Filisi tiina balo ta na daare to. Banto ya nwoŋi Kiriti naneo ni dem ne mo.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Gaza tiina wó cheeri ba yuni wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. Asekelon tiina de wó ke chemm. Abam balo ta na daare te-kampare laŋa kam ne to, á ta wó taa gwe á yera yam wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane na?

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: Abam maa laara ye á tɛ á we: ‘Se-zɔɔ kolo na wo Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ne to, nmo wo ta wo to de n na gwoni debam tei to na? Jwoori n zo n pwolo kom wone, se n ta‑n tigi da n sia!’

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Moaba teo taane mo tento. Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: “Lɛɛro mo wo Nebo teo yuu ne, ko na lage ko chɔge to ŋwaane. Kariafayim de wó yaale ba na di-ko jara wone to ŋwaane. Ba lage ba yigi ko dam jei sem ba de tega ne mo, pa se teo kom nɔn-bia bam na ba chaveera.

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Cheigi-na se á ni nɔɔna na keeri tei Horon wone, vuvuga de cham na to ba wone to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Moaba teo lage ko chɔge maama mo. Ko bia bam wó laare dedɛ.

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Ba kwei Luhifi chwoŋa kam mo ba maa kɛa. Ba na maa diini to mo ba yɔɔre ba keeri taa. Ba ta kwei Horon chwoŋa kam mo ba maa tua, ye ba laare we ba teo kom chɔge.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Ba maa we, ‘Duri-na se á lu de á ŋwea! Véi á zo-na kagoa kam wone ne bonaga tei.’

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Abam Moaba tiina kwei á chega á daŋe á totoŋa de á jejegero baŋa ne mo. Á dona nam wó wane abam ba di. Ba wó kale á jwoni Chemosi de ba ja ba vo sa-teo, ko ta woli de de kaanem tiina de balo na toŋe ba pa-de to.

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: Ko-na yibeeli se á suli Moaba de wone, ko na wó taa tigi mo yɔɔ yerane to ŋwaane. Moaba teene dem maama wó ji di-dwonnu mo, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa yé taa zoore de wone.”

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Moaba tiina jwoni Chemosi wó pa ba di chaveera, ne Isarele tiina déem na pɛ ba jwoni dem chega Bɛtel ne pa se ba di chaveera tei to.

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Moaba dona bam nam wó kaare ba teene dem ba pu, ye ba daare ba chɔge de maama! Ko ná ye Moaba nɔn-donno telo na jege jwa to, ba lage ba go ba maama mo. Pɛ wolo yere na ye Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ to mo tage konto.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: Moaba tiina cham maŋa kam yi ka ti. Lɛɛro mo wó ke lela te ba ba baŋa.

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
