translation_verse: Abam teene delo maama na gilimi Moaba ye á yei o yere déem na zaŋe tei to, keeri-na á pa‑o. Ta‑á tɛ-na we, ‘O paare nacheiga kam laam bwori! Moaba daa ba jege dam!’

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: Abam balo na zoore Dibon ne to, yage-na á kamunim dem, se á tu á tete á ta‑á jei fwogo wone. Moaba dona bam beene abam baŋa, se ba yɔɔre ba chɔge á dam jei sem mo.

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ba laam wó leiri abam we, ‘Moaba tiina mo nɛ ba chaveera, ba dona na di-ba to ŋwaane! Ta‑á chwoosa, ye á daare á keeri-na á pa-ba. Zege-na Arowa buga kam ni ne á tɔɔle de kwor-dɛa we, Moaba teo kom chɔge mo zɔŋ-zɔŋ!’

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: Teene delo na chwi te-kampare sem ne to waarem maŋa yia. Ko nam ye Holon, de Jaza, de Mefaafa,

english_verse: Dibon, Nebo, Beth-Diblathaim,
translation_verse: de Dibon, de Nebo, de Bɛte-Dibilafayim,

english_verse: Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
translation_verse: de Kiriafayim, de Bɛte-Gamuli, de Bɛte-Meon,

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Moaba teo de ko jar-keira dam dem maama ti mo.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: “Moaba teo dwoni de amo Baŋa Wɛ mo. Nam pa-na se ba nyɔ sana ba bugi. Ba wó taa tigi ba tete tetwanno wone mo ba bibila, se nɔɔna taa jege-ba ba ke ba mɔna.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: Abam Sibima tiina bam, a wó keeri a pa abam mo, se ko dwoni a na ke tei a pa Jazera teo tiina to. Abam nye de Vini tio, ko nɛ sem na tage se yi naneo kom ni to mo. Se ma tole taa se yi Jazera teo kom. Abam dona nam tu á baŋa, ye ba chɔge á mɔɔro de á Vini tio-bia bam.

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna tiini ba chwoosi Hesebon de Elealɛ ne. Ba keira kam zaŋe ka yi Jahaza seeni. Ka ta zege Zoara ne mo ka yi Horon de Egalate-Selisiya. Nimirim bu-nɔgɔ kom tete koge mo.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye balo na kare ba kaane jwona zwonnu yuu ne ye ba daare ba zwɛ wonnu ba ma ba zuli ba wa to, amo lage a pa ba jei Moaba laŋa kam ne mo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: A yi-na mo yɔɔre ba chwi a wone Moaba teo ŋwaane. Ko nye de nɔɔno na jege gungwoŋa o mage ye ba mɔɔne luseim tei to mo. Amo wo chɔge Kiri-Heresi tiina de ŋwaane. Kokuri to, ba jejegero maama jei ba jeŋa ne mo.

english_verse: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
translation_verse: Moaba teo sam dem nayuni ne, de ba yɛ sem maama ne keira yerane mo yɔɔre ka zaŋa. Kokuri to, amo lage a ja Moaba teo a chochoge, ne nɔɔno na vae kambia ye o chochoge-ka tei to mo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: Nii-na Moaba teo na chɔge ko tigi tei! Cheigi-na se á ni ko nɔn-bia bam na chwoosi tei to! Ba ma pipiri ba jwoori de chaveera. Moaba tiina bam wó ji wo-zɔɔna teene delo na gilimi-ba to yiga ne. Nɔɔna wó taa jege-ba ba mɔne mo.”

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Moaba teo lage ko chɔge mo se ba yere saare, ba na dwoni de Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Wolo maama ná duri se o lu lɛɛro tem wone, kotu wó vo o to gwoŋo wone mo. O nam ná bɛ o gwoŋo kom wone, kotu wó vo o to kalanchogo wone mo. Kokuri to, maŋa kam ná yia, amo wó yɔɔre a waare Moaba tiina bam mo.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna ná kwaane ba duri ba vo ba yi Hesebon, ba teena wó ti mo ye ba daa ware yiga se ba vo. Kokuri to, min-fɔrɔ mo nwoŋi Pɛ Sihon teo Hesebon wone ko dɔɔle ko yi Moaba tiina bam, ba na swoi vuvuga kikia to ŋwaane.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Moaba tiina bam, lɛɛro wo á yuu ne! Abam balo na zuli á jwoni Chemosi to wó na chɔgem. Ba maa wó kale á bia bam ba ja ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga, bakeiri de busankane maama.

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Amon tiina bam taane mo tento. Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: “Isarele dwi dem daa ba jege baara se ba taa tei ba tega kam mo na? Ko ye konto ŋwaane mo balo na kaane Moleka jwoni to tua ba jwoŋi Gad dwi dem laŋa kam ba tei, pa se ba zoore ka teene dem wone na?

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Maŋa nam lage ka yi se amo Baŋa Wɛ bage tiguri-kaasa, se jara ba Amon tiina teo Raba baŋa ne. Ko wó ji di-dwonnu na tigi zwoŋo yuu ne to mo. Mini wó zwɛ ko nawuura yam de di maama. Isarele tiina laam maa wó zeili Amon tiina balo déem na tu ba zeili-ba to se ba viiri.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: “Hesebon tiina, keeri-na Ayi teo kom na chɔge to ŋwaane. Abam Raba tiina, á de ta‑á chwoosa! Kwei-na gare-nyenyaaro á zo se á ta‑á keera. Ta‑á duri-na teo kom wone á lɛɛna, ba na lage ba zeŋe á jwoni Moleka ba ja ba viiri to ŋwaane. Ba ta wó kale de kaanem tiina de balo na toŋe ba pa-de to, ba ja ba woli da ba vo sa-teo.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: Amo Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wó pa se foone tiini de ja abam, teene delo na gilimi abam to ŋwaane. Ba lage ba zeili á maama mo pa á duri á jage da-yiga ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá wane balo na duri to se o jwoori o la o ke daane.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne nam, amo wó pa Amon tiina bam jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto. Edom tiina taane

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Abam balo na zoore Dedan ne to, pipiri-na á duri, se á vo á seigi peero bɔɔna wone! Kokuri to, maŋa yia se a waare Esawu dwi tiina bam. A nam lage a pa lɛɛro ba ba baŋa ne mo.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna ná tu abam tei se ba gwori Vini tio-bia, ba bá gwori ba daare tio-bia bam badaara na? Ŋweena nam ná tu se ba ŋɔ abam tete ne, ba yeini ba ŋɔne kolo ba na beeri to yerane mo.

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Esawu dwi tiina bam, amo lage a vere ba wonnu maama mo a daare-ba kiliŋi. A maa wó pa se ba seigim jei sem taa tigi jase, se ba daa yé wane ba seigi ba dona yiga ne. Ba bia, de ba chorro maama wó na chɔgem mo. Ba dwi dem wó jei tega baŋa ne.

english_verse: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
translation_verse: Nam yage-na á botara, se amo mo taa nii ba baŋa ne. Á kadeina dé wó wane ba sale amo yera ne.”

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Balo ya na wo maŋe se ba na waarem to nam jege se ba nyɔ a ban-zɔŋɔ na-zoŋa kam wo na mo. Bɛ mo ye á boŋe se á lu waarem dem wone? Amo bá yage abam! Á jege se á nyɔ ka wo na mo!

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Amo Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Baŋa Wɛ dugi de a tete mo we amo wó chɔge Bozera teo pa se ko ji wo-zɔɔne nɔɔna yiga ne. Nɔɔna wó taa mɔne-ko, ye ba daare ba ma ko yere ba sɔɔle lwarem ba pa daane. Laŋa kam teene dem maama wó ji di-dwonnu mo taa wuu.”

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: Abam bere á tete kamunim mo, ye á boŋe we nɔɔna kɔre foone de abam. Abam nam gane á tete mo. Á zoore peero bɔɔna wone, ye á wo peero tem yuu ne wɛ-wɛ. Abam ná maŋe á zoore baŋa baŋa, se ko maŋe de maao na sɔge ko pwogo wɛ-wɛ tei to de, amo nam ta wó vaare abam a de tega ne.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: “Amo lage a pi a nwoŋi Edom tiina baŋa ne se a zeili-ba ba tega kam wone bedwe baŋa ne mo, Ko wó taa nye de nywoŋo na nwoŋi punnu na li mɛ Jɔdan buga kam ni ne tei, ye ko zaŋe vara dim jei sem ne ko zi-ba to mo. Amo laam wó kuri yiga tu se o taa nii teo kom baŋa ne. Wɔ nam mo nye de amo, se kotu wane o bwei-ne? Yiga tu tera o na wó wane o dwoni de amo.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
translation_verse: Edom teo kom ná toa, tega kam baŋa maama wó ziziŋi. Ba keira kam wó zaŋe ka yi Nane-soŋo kom.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Nii-na! Maao mo lage ko taa yaare wɛɛne, se ko foore ko tu ko ba tega kam seeni. Ko nam lage ko yarege ko vɔna yam Bozera baŋa ne mo. Maŋa kam ná yia, foone wó ja Edom babɛ sem, ne kaane na wowole se o lo ye o fona tei to.” Damasika tiina taane

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na tage Damasika tiina bam taane tei to mo tento: “Lwia mo wó ja Hamafa de Arapade tiina, ba na nigi kwor-balɔrɔ to ŋwaane. Ba wo de maa wó leeri, ye ba ware ba sii, foone na jege-ba to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Ko ná ye á teo kolo yere déem na zaŋe ye wopwolo tiini ko wo ko wone to, nɔɔna wó viiri ba daare-ko.

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Chega ŋwaane, ba lage ba go teo kom nɔn-donno tem ko pempala yuu ne mo. Maŋa kam ná yia, ba jar-keira bam de wó te.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: Amo mo lage a zwɛ Damasika kabiri sem, se mini di Ben-Hadadi dam jei sem maama.” Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto. Kedare tiina de Hazora tiina taane

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Kedare dwi tiina, de Hazora dwi tiina balo Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza na di jara wone to, banto taane mo tento. Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: “Zaŋe-na se á nwoŋi á kwaare jara de Kedare tiina bam, se á chɔge nɔɔna bam konto na zoore wɛ-puli seeni to.

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we: “Zaŋe-na á nwoŋi se á kwaare jara de teo kom konto. Lwia ba jege-ba ye ba ba kɔre nɔɔn-nɔɔno. Ba wo pe ba teo kom nia de bworru naa luuru. Teene dedwonna ba bwola de-ba.

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Vere-na ba kona de ba vare-kɔgɔ kom maama á ta‑á tei. Ko ná ye balo na cheeri ba yuni ye ba zoore kagoa yuu ne to a lage a jage-ba a yage vio wone, ye a daare a pa lɛɛro nwoŋi jei maama ne te ba te yi-ba,” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: “Hazora wó ji kagoa yerane taa wuu, mɛ nywoŋ-kuri na kare se vei to mo. Nɔɔna daa bá taa zoore jei sem konto ne.” Elam tiina taane

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Nii ywo! A lage a ja Elam che-tara bam mo a chɔge. Banto mo ye babɛ ba dwoi jar-keira bam maama.

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Amo lage a chɔge ba pɛ de o nakwa bam mo, se a daare a chwi a paare yituŋu ba teo kom wone.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: “Maŋa nam daa wó ba se amo pa Elam tiina jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Kwora kalo Baŋa Wɛ na pɛ o sampwora Jeremia Babilon teo de ko nɔn-bia bam ŋwaane to mo tento:

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: Teo kodwoŋi jar-keira wó zege baŋa seeni ba nwoŋi ba ba Babilon baŋa. Ba wó chɔge tega kam maama pa se ka ji kagoa ka tiga. Nabiina de vara maama wó duri ba jei. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá taa zoore ka wone.”

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: “Maŋa kam konto ná yia, Isarele dwi tiina de Judah dwi tiina wó tɔge daane ba vo ba beeri ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom, ye ba ka yi-na ba via.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Balo maama ná nɛ-ba, ba yeini ba kwaare jara de-ba mo se ba di-ba. Ba dona de maa tɛ ba we, ‘Dé wo ke dé tusi. Banto mo tusi ba chɔge Baŋa Wɛ yiga. Wonto maa ye ba woro chekke. Ba nabaara teena déem nam daŋe Baŋa Wɛ baŋa ne mo.’

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: Amo nɔɔna bam, nwoŋi-na Babilon teo kom wone. Duri-na á nwoŋi á daare Babilon tiina bam. Nam tɔge-na kɔgɔ kom yiga á viiri.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ba lage ba vere Babilon tiina jejegero mo. Balo na beene ba baŋa to wó chwooli ba zela maama.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: “Abam Babilon tiina bam tiini á chake de wopwolo mo, á déem na di amo nɔɔna bam ye á vere ba wonnu to ŋwaane. Á laam ma kare á kekara ne na-mɔra na jege ga-lɛɛro ka di tei to. Abam ta ke ne sisein-nɔɔna na keeri tei to mo.

english_verse: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
translation_verse: Abam tete teo kom nam wó na ko chaveera. Teo kolo na ye á kugu jei to wó yaale. Ko wó taa ye teo kolo na muri teene maama wone to. Ko ta wó ji kagoa kalo na ye te-kora yerane to mo.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá taa zoore jei sem konto ne, Baŋa Wɛ bane na zaŋe de-ba to ŋwaane. Ko yɔɔre ko lage ko ji di-dwonnu yerane mo. Balo maama ná tɔge ko jei ne ba kɛ, ko wó ke-ba yaau pa se ba yaale-ko ko chanɛɛre dem ŋwaane.

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: “Isarele dwi dem nye ne pei-kɔgɔ nywoŋo na zo se tetare ne ye ko jage-se ko yage tei to mo. Asiria teo pɛ mo dɛ yiga o ja-ba o di. Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza ma saŋe o kwaga o de ja ba kwi sem o chochoge maama.”

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: “Amo wó waare Babilon teo pɛ wom de o tega kam, ne a déem na waare Asiria teo pɛ tei to.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ko daare se a ja Isarele dwi tiina a jwoori ba tete te-ywoŋa kam wone. Ba laam wó taa zoore Kamele, de Basan ne, ba taa di ba boboŋa na lage tei. Ba maa wó maŋe Efrayim, de Gilead zwonnu tem yuu ne, ba di ba su ba fera.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we: “Nwoŋi-na á vo á kwaare jara de Meratayim teo de balo na zoore Pekoda ne to. Pare-ba-na á ja se á go se ba dwi ti. Ke-na kolo maama amo na pɛ abam ni se á ke to.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Jara-keim sɔɔ mo zaŋe tega baŋa jei maama ne. Wonnu maama mo lage te chɔge!

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Babilon déem chɔge logo baŋa jei maama, ne swoli mo ba jege ba mage wonnu tei. Nii-na! Babilon teo tete laam chochoge mo ko ji mura-mura! Ko yɔɔre ko ji wo-zɔɔne logo baŋa teene dem maama yiga ne mo.

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Babilon tiina bam, amo chege kalanchogo mo á ŋwaane. Á nam wo lɔre ko ni ne pa ko ja abam. Abam na to ko wone to ye á na dwoni de amo Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane mo.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Zege-na yiga yiga á nwoŋi á ba se á kwaare jara de Babilon teo kom. Puri-na ba tuli sem se á le mena yam. Chwooli-na ba sam se de ji tampuuri. Yɔɔre á chɔge-na teo kom se kolokolo daa yé daare.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Go-na ba babɛ sem maama! Yɔɔre á gwoni-se á tiŋi! Lɛɛro wo ba yuu ne! Ba maŋa kam yia mo konto se ba na ba waarem.”

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo Babilon nɔn-donno tem wó to ba taa tigi teo kom chwei sem ne. Ba jar-keira bam maama wó te dɛ dedwe.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta o we: “Babilon ye boyere nyem mo! Amo nam nwoŋi á kwaga ne. Dɛ dem amo na le se a waare abam to laam yia.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Á teo kom boyerem ŋwaane, á lage á tiri á to tega ne mo. Nɔɔno bá taa wora se kotu ja abam se á zaŋe wɛɛne. A maa wó pa se mini zwɛ á teene dem maama. De ta wó di woŋo kolo maama na bwola da to.”

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Ba teo kom yi-nara bam de wó na chɔgem. Ba jworim kikia wó ba ya lɔre jaja. Ba teo babɛ sem de wó to, ye foone tiini de ja-ba.

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Ba sisein-nɔɔna de se jara-keim torokooro de wó chɔge. Jar-keira balo na ye veira ba wone to de lage ba to mo! Banto wó taa bwona mo ne kaana tei to. Ba jejegero de wó ba te chɔge jara yam ŋwaane. Ba dona wó vere-te ba ja ba viiri.

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Da-kore wó zege ba teo kom wone pa se ba bwi sem maama ko. Jara wó ba ba baŋa ne, ba teo kom na su de jwona yerane to ŋwaane. Yanto yeini ya fugi nɔɔna bam pa se ba boboŋa jei foone ŋwaane mo.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ko wó yɔɔre ko ke Babilon teo ne ko déem na ke Sodom, de Gomora, de teene delo na bwola da to tei to mo. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá taa zoore jei sem konto ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam bá maŋe dáane.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: “Kwoni á nii-na baŋa seeni! Te-fɔrɔ jar-keira dedaane pwa dedɛ mo maa beene abam baŋa. Ba ti yiga mo se ba nwoŋi yiga yiga ba ba ba jeeri abam de jara.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Ba zei ba tɛ dedaane ba chichwoa mo ba beena. Ba nam tiini ba jege puseŋa mo, ye ba ba kɔre nɔɔna yibwona kɔtaa! Ba wurigi ba sisein-nɔɔna ne naneo na-ŋona na wuuri tei to mo. Ba ke ba tete ba ke daane se ba kwaare jara de abam Babilon tiina bam mo.

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: Babilon teo pɛ nigi nɔɔna bam konto ŋwa, pa se o vɔna pare. Ko yɔɔre ko jege‑o ko ni mo ye o fona, nenɛɛne kaane na virigi puga se o lo ye ko ni‑o tei to.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Amo lage a pi a nwoŋi Babilon tiina baŋa ne se a zeili-ba ba tega kam wone bedwe baŋa ne. Ko wó taa nye de nywoŋo na nwoŋi punnu na li mɛ Jɔdan buga kam ni ne tei, ye ko zaŋe vara dim jei sem ne ko zi-ba to mo. Amo laam wó kuri yiga tu se o taa nii teo kom baŋa ne. Wɔ nam mo nye de amo, se o wane o bwei-ne? Yiga tu tera o na wó wane o dwoni de amo.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Babilon teo kom ná toa, tega baŋa maama wó ziziŋi. Ba keira kam wó zaŋe ka jage ka yi logo baŋa teene dem maama.”

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Yé pa-na ba che-tara bam chwoŋa se ba saŋe ba tɛ, naa se ba vɔ ba jara zela yam. Yé yage-na ba nɔn-donno tem tete se ba taa ŋwe. Nam yɔɔre á chɔge-na ba jar-keira bam maama.

english_verse: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
translation_verse: Pa-na se ba na zonne ye ba daare ba te ba taa tigi Babilon teo chwei sem ne.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: Duri á nwoŋi-na Babilon teo kom wone! Duri-na se á lu ye á ta ŋwe! Yé tɔge-na de Babilon tiina bam á te ba wɛleera yam ŋwaane. Maŋa yia se Baŋa Wɛ jwoori o ŋwe jene ba baŋa ne. O lage o pa Babilon tiina jwoŋi ba kikia yam ŋweero mo.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Babilon déem nye ne sabu-seŋa na-zoŋa mo Baŋa Wɛ jeŋa ne. Wonto ma kwei ka wo sana bam o pa logo baŋa dwi maama pa ba nyɔ ba su ba bugi. Ba maama na nyɔge ka wo sana bam to, ba yɔɔre ba yirisi mo.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Babilon nam lage ko pɔpɔ ko to mo ko chochoge. Tiini á keeri-na ko ŋwaane! Beeri-na nuga se á ma á lɛ ko zonne dem, se dɛ delo ko wó jwoori ko na yazura. Veira balo na zoore Babilon ne to maa we:

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: ‘Dé ya ná wae, dé ya wó pa Babilon na yazura. Ko nam ware, o bá na yɔɔrem. Pa-na se dé viiri dé daare teo kom, se nɔɔno maama jwoori o tete teo. Wɛ na lage o waare-ba tei to wó kɛ jeŋa, se ko yi wɛyuu kom tete. Ko nam ye se ba yɔɔre ba na chɔgem mo.’ Judah dwi tiina bam de maa we:

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Abam balo na zoore Babilon bu-tole sem ni ne to, á ye naduna mo pipiu ŋwaane. Maŋa nam yi se á teo kom to ko saare se abam de te.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ dugi o tete ne mo o we: Amo lage a pa se á dona tiini ba yo mo á baŋa ne ne kayere dwoŋi. Ba laam maa wó bage sɔɔ ba yage we ba wane abam ba di.”

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ya ba jege kuri. Ya maŋe se nɔɔna taa jege-ya ba mɔna mo. Ya waarem maŋa ná yia, ya maama wó chɔge mo fase.

english_verse: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo tento: “Babilon, nmo nye de pe-zɔŋɔ kolo na jege logo baŋa maama ko chɔge to mo. Amo Baŋa Wɛ nam mo nwoŋi nmo kwaga ne. Amo wó ma a dam mo a waare‑m. A lage a dole‑m a de tega ne mo, se a daare a zwɛ n sam dem se de ji tentwarem.

english_verse: Your stone blocks won't be reused for cornerstones or foundations, and I promise that forever you will be a desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Nations Will Attack Babylon The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá beeri weero telo na daare to wone se o na kandwɛ o ma o chwi kabiri-beira kadwoŋi. Kokuri to, abam teo kom yɔɔre ko chɔge mo wuu.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.
translation_verse: Tega kam maama ziziŋi mo, ye ka yera sae. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa jaane ya ti se o chɔge Babilon laŋa kam. O maa lage se o yɔɔre o chɔge-ka se nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa yé taa zoore da.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
translation_verse: Nii-na! Babilon babɛ sem yage jara yam keim. Ba ma lɛɛre ba maŋe ba dam jei sem ne. Ba dam maama ti mo. Ba laam bwona ne kaana dwoŋi mo. Mini mo zwɛ teo kom sam. Ko manchwo-nia da-gare sem laam ma bwori.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom na ye Isarele tiina Wɛ to na tage kolo to mo tento: “Babilon teo kom nye de tega kalo nɔɔna na fɔge ba kwɛ-ka se ba ma ba mage mena to mo. Ko bere we wodiu zagem maŋa yia. Ba dona laam wó ba ba zage-ba ba de tega ne.” Jerusalem tiina bam daa ma ta ba we:

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem say, “King Nebuchadnezzar made us panic. That monster stuffed himself with us and our treasures, leaving us empty— he gobbled up what he wanted and spit out the rest.
translation_verse: Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza mo di debam. O ma pa se vuvuga dedɛ to debam tetare ne. O ma kwoori teo kom se kolokolo daa yé daare ko wone. O ma li debam kula, ne o ye juru mo tei to. O na done dé wo-laaro tem o su o puga to mo o tɔne debam o yage.

english_verse: My people, I am on your side, and I will take revenge on Babylon. I will cut off its water supply, and its stream will dry up.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri, Baŋa Wɛ tage tento: “Amo wó zege abam kwaga ne se a ŋɔɔne a pa abam. A ta wó jwoori a ŋwe jene Babilon tiina baŋa ne. A nam wó pa se ba bwi sem we, se ba buli-yi de yé buri na.

english_verse: Babylon will be a pile of rubble where only jackals live, and everyone will be afraid to walk among the ruins.
translation_verse: Babilon teo kom wó ji di-dwoŋ-koro, mɛ nywoŋ-kuri na kare se vei to mo. Teo kom wó di chaveera, se nɔɔna taa mɔne-ko, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá taa zoore ko wone.

english_verse: Babylon's enemies will rise like ocean waves and flood the city.
translation_verse: Naneo kom lage ko zaŋe mo ko yi Babilon teo kom. Na-fwaaro tem mo wó chuuri te kwoli teo kom maama.

english_verse: Horrible destruction will strike the nearby towns. The land will become a barren desert, where no one can live or even travel.
translation_verse: Babilon teene maama wó ji di-dwonnu yerane mo. Tega kam wó taa ye kago-kora mo, mɛ nɔɔn-nɔɔno na bá taa zoore ka wone to. Nabiina bere ba bá taa tɔge ka wone ba kɛa.

english_verse: I will punish Marduk, the god of Babylon, and make him vomit out everything he gobbled up. Then nations will no longer bring him gifts, and Babylon's walls will crumble. The Lord Offers Hope to His People
translation_verse: Ko ná ye Babilon tiina jwoni Bel, a lage a waare-de mo. A ta wó pa de tɔne wo-laaro telo de na ligi to de yage. Logo baŋa dwi tiina daa bá taa vei se ba zuli-de. Chega to, Babilon teo kabiri sem lage se to mo!

english_verse: Get out of Babylon, my people, and run for your lives, before I strike the city in my anger!
translation_verse: Amo nɔɔna bam, nwoŋi-na Babilon teo kom wone! Duri-na á lu ye á ta ŋwe! Duri-na se á wane á lu Baŋa Wɛ ban-lom dem.

english_verse: The time will come when I will punish Babylon's false gods. Everyone there will die, and the whole nation will be disgraced,
translation_verse: Kokuri to, maŋa lage ka yi se amo yɔɔre a waare Babilon teo jwona yam. Ba teo kom maama wó di chaveera. Ko nɔn-bia bam wó te, ye ba yera taa tigi ko jei maama ne.

english_verse: Babylon must be overthrown, because it slaughtered the people of Israel and of many other nations.
translation_verse: “Babilon tiina bam yɔɔre ba go logo baŋa teene maama nɔɔna mo. Babilon teo kom laam jege se ko to, ba na go Isarele tiina bam tei to ŋwaane.

english_verse: My people, you escaped death when Jerusalem fell. Now you live far from home, but you should trust me and think about Jerusalem. Leave Babylon! Don't stay!
translation_verse: Abam Isarele tiina balo na lugi toone to, ke-na lela á viiri se á yé ta‑á zege á dáana ywo! Nam guli-na Baŋa Wɛ wom gula, de á na wo sa-teo ne yiga yiga tei to de. Daa ta‑á boŋe-na Jerusalem teo kom boboŋa.

english_verse: Although Babylon's walls reach to the sky, the army I send will destroy that city. I, the Lord, have spoken. Babylon Will Be Destroyed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Babilon teo kom ná maŋe ko lɔ ko di wɛ-wɛ tei, ye ko daare ko fɔge dam jei sem wɛyuu ne tei de, amo ta wó toŋe jar-keira mo se ba ba ko baŋa.” Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: Listen to the cries for help coming from Babylon. Everywhere in the country the sounds of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Cheigi-na se á ni keira na zaŋe Babilon teo ne tei! Ko nam ye teo kom chɔgem sɔɔ mo ye ko nwoŋi Babilon teo jei maama ne.

english_verse: An enemy will attack and destroy Babylon. Its soldiers will be captured and their weapons broken, because I am a God who takes revenge against nations for what they do.
translation_verse: Teo kodwoŋi jar-keira mo lage ba ba ba chɔge Babilon teo kom. Ba wó ja Babilon babɛ sem, ye ba jwoŋi ba tɛ sem ba bwori ba yage. Kokuri to, Baŋa Wɛ yeini o waare balo na tusi to mo. O lage o jwoori o ŋwe jene maama mo.

english_verse: The thick walls of that city will be torn down, and its huge gates burned. Everything that nation worked so hard to gain will go up in smoke. Jeremiah Gives Seraiah a Scroll
translation_verse: Paŋwa Tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: “Babilon teo kabiri sem ná lira tei maama de, ba lage ba yigi-se ba de tega ne mo buri-buri. Mini wó zwɛ teo kom manchwo-nia yam. Logo baŋa nɔɔna bam yaare ba tete kafɛ ŋwaane mo. Kokuri to, ba na toŋe tei maama to wó ja mini.” Jeremia toŋe kwora se ka vo Babilon

english_verse: Before they left, I wrote on a scroll all the terrible things that would happen to Babylon.
translation_verse: O déem ya popone Babilon teo kom na wó na lɛɛro telo maama to mo o ke tɔnɔ wone. Babilon wonnu maama mo popone te tiŋi tɔnɔ kom wone.

english_verse: I gave the scroll to Seraiah and said: When you get to Babylon, read this scroll aloud,
translation_verse: O ma ta de Seraya o we, “Nmo ná vei n yi Babilon, se n ga taane dento maama baŋa baŋa se nɔɔna bam ni-de.

english_verse: then pray, “Our Lord, you promised to destroy this place and make it into a desert where no people or animals will ever live.”
translation_verse: Ta ta n woli da we, ‘Amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo mo taga we n lage n chɔge teo konto kula, se nabiina, de vara daa yé wane ko wone ba zo, se ko lage ko ji di-dwonnu yerane mo se ko taa vei wuu.’

english_verse: When you finish praying, tie the scroll to a rock and throw it in the Euphrates River. Then say,
translation_verse: N ná gage tɔnɔ konto n ti, se n kwei-ko n vɔ de kandwɛ, ye n laam vo n dole-ko n de Yuferata buga kam wone,

english_verse: “This is how Babylon will sink when the Lord destroys it. Everyone in the city will die, and it won't have the strength to rise again.” The End of Jeremiah's Writing Jeremiah's writing ends here.
translation_verse: se n daare n ta we, ‘Mo Babilon teo na lage ko tu ko lini tei to. Ko nam daa bá zaŋe wɛɛne, amo na yɔɔre a lage a ja lɛɛro dedɛ a ba ko baŋa ne to ŋwaane. Ko nɔn-bia bam maama wó to.’ ” Jeremia kwori sem maama kweeli ywo mo.

english_verse: Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan déem ta jaane Wɛ kaanem nakwe tu Seraya, de o kwaga-saŋeno Zefania, de Wɛ diga kam ni-yerena batɔ bam mo o ja o viiri.

english_verse: After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month,
translation_verse: Ko na yi bene dem konto chane sena chana kam da nogo dɛ dem to, kana déem tiini ka chɛ mo pa se Jerusalem nɔn-bia bam daa ba jege wodiu se ba taa di.

english_verse: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the Jordan River valley,
translation_verse: Babilon tiina bam ma bwori teo kom kabiri sem ba de tega ne, ye ba tɔge pwoli sem ne ba zo ko wo. Zedekia de o jar-keira bam maama déem duri se ba lu tete ne mo. Ba ma kwei pɛ gaare chwoŋa kam, ba vo ba tɔge ni dem na wo teo kabiri selei sem tetare ne to, ye ba laam duri ba tu Jɔdan bwolo kom seeni.

english_verse: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
translation_verse: Ba ma zi Zedekia ba ja ba vo Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza tei. O déem wo Ribila teo ne mo, Hamafa kateiri dem ne. Nebukadeneza ma di taane o vane Zedekia dáane.

english_verse: Jerusalem was captured during Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king of Babylonia. About a month later, Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guards arrived in Jerusalem. His name was Nebuzaradan,
translation_verse: Nebukadeneza déem na di Babilon teo paare o ke bena fuga-nogo bene delo ne to, chane senu chana kam da fuga dɛ dem ne mo o kwaga-saŋeno Nebuzaradan zo Jerusalem teo kom wone. Wonto maa ye Babilon teo babɛ sem yiga tu.

english_verse: and he burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses.
translation_verse: O déem ma pa ba zwɛ Baŋa Wɛ diga kam, de pɛ sɔŋɔ kom, de Jerusalem sam dem maama. Ba déem zwɛ sɔ-laao dwi maama mo Jerusalem teo wone.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan ma pa ni pa o jar-keira bam yɔɔre ba yigi Jerusalem teo kabiri sem maama ba de tega ne.

english_verse: He led away the people left in the city, including everyone who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar, the rest of the skilled workers, and even some of the poor people of Judah.
translation_verse: O ma kale yiniga tiina badwonna, de balo ta na daare teo kom wone to, ko ta woli de gwaro ta na daare to, de balo na duri ba zo Babilon tiina kɔgɔ kom wone to o ja o vo Babilon.

english_verse: people from Judah to Babylonia. Jehoiachin Is Set Free (
translation_verse: ) mo. Ba pore Jehoyachin ba yage

english_verse: Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: O ma ke Pɛ Jehoyachin lanyerane, ye o pa‑o jeiŋa jei na tiini se jege zula se dwoi jei selo pwa babam bam na wo Babilon ne na nɛ to.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: Jehoyachin ma lɔɔre o peena diga gwaaro tem o tiŋi. O ŋwea kam dɛ maama wone o ma lɛɛre o di wodiu Babilon teo pɛ tei ne.

english_verse: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Babilon teo pɛ ta ma kwei kolo maama Jehoyachin na wó ke o yera ne to o pa‑o dɛ maama, se ko vo ko yi o toone maŋa.

english_verse: Jerusalem, once so crowded, lies deserted and lonely. This city that was known all over the world is now like a widow. This queen of the nations has been made a slave.
translation_verse: Nii teo konto laam na tigi tei ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tere ko wone. Ko déem nam su de nɔɔna mo! Ko déem ye te-fɔrɔ mo logo baŋa teene dem wone. Nii ko laam na ye ne kadeim tei! Ko ya ye teene dem maama dedɛɛro mo, ye ko laam to kabɛɛne wone.

english_verse: Each night, bitter tears flood her cheeks. None of her former lovers are there to offer comfort; her friends have betrayed her and are now her enemies.
translation_verse: Teo kom nye de kaane wolo na yɔɔre o keeri mo. Yi-na ma bɔɔre o keila yam tete dem maama wone. O bɔɔla bam wolowolo nam tera se kotu zuri o bochare. O badwonna maama de ma baare o kwaga ne, ye banto ji o dona.

english_verse: The roads to Zion mourn because no one travels there to celebrate the festivals. The city gates are deserted; priests are weeping. Young women are raped; Zion is in sorrow!
translation_verse: Nɔɔna daa ba tui ba zoore teo kom wone se ba di kura Wɛ diga kam wone. Konto ŋwaane chwei selo na vei se zoore Zion wone to de keeri mo. Teo kom ni maama wone nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera. Wɛ kaanem tiina yɔɔre ba vuvuni mo. Ko bukwa bam wo ma chɔge, kokuri to, teo kom cham dem kɛ jeŋa mo.

english_verse: Zion's glory has disappeared. Her leaders are like deer that cannot find pasture; they are hunted down till their strength is gone.
translation_verse: Zion nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom maama laam ti mo. Teo kom dedɛɛra tiini ba bwona ne wei na beeri gaao se ga se se di tei to. Ba ma kwaane se ba duri ba dona yiga ne, ye ba ware.

english_verse: Her people recall the good life that once was theirs; now they suffer and are scattered. No one was there to protect them from their enemies who sneered when their city was taken.
translation_verse: Jerusalem na wo cham wone ye o kare o beeri maŋa kalo to, mo o guli o déem na jege ywoni delo o di to. Ko ye o dendéem gula mo o guli. O laam nam to o dona jeŋa ne mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se kotu woli‑o. O dona bam maa nii, ye ba jege‑o ba mɔna de o na nɛ chɔgem to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Jerusalem's horrible sins have made the city a joke. Those who once admired her now hate her instead— she has been disgraced; she groans and turns away.
translation_verse: Jerusalem yɔɔre o ke o tusi dedɛ mo, pa se o ji wo-zɔɔne nɔɔna yiga ne. Balo déem na nege‑o to laam gwooni‑o mo, ba na nɛ o kuri to ŋwaane. Wonto tete de laam yɔɔre o vuvuni mo, ye o daare o jege o yibia o seiga chaveera na jege‑o to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Her sins had made her filthy, but she wasn't worried about what could happen. And when Jerusalem fell, it was so tragic. No one gave her comfort when she cried out, “Help! I'm in trouble, Lord! The enemy has won.”
translation_verse: O chɔge o tete mo de wo-zɔɔna kikia. O nam wo boŋe se o lɔre ko jwa na wó ke‑o tei to. O laam na to tei to mo tiini ko jege lɛɛro. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera se kotu zuri o bochare. O maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ, nii ko na zoore a yera tei! A dona bam mo di dam a baŋa ne!”

english_verse: Everyone in the city groans while searching for food; they trade their valuables for barely enough scraps to stay alive. Jerusalem Speaks: Jerusalem shouts to the Lord, “Please look and see how miserable I am!”
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔn-bia bam maama yɔɔre ba vuvuni mo ye ba beeri wodiu se ba di. Ba laam ma kwei ba jejegero ba yeigi, se tento leiri wodiu yuu ne se ba ma wori. Ba maa we, “Baŋa Wɛ, nii dé seeni, se ba tiini ba gwooni debam dedɛ.”

english_verse: From heaven you sent a fire that burned in my bones; you set a trap for my feet and made me turn back. All day long you leave me in shock from constant pain.
translation_verse: O pɛ se mini mo nwoŋi wɛyuu ne de ba amo baŋa. De ma zo a yera ne, ye de zwɛ a kwi sem. O chege kalanchogo mo se ko ja-ne, pa se a pipiri a jwoori kwaga. O yage amo a yerane mo, pa se a yera chɛ dɛ dem maama wone.

english_verse: You have tied my sins around my neck, and they weigh so heavily that my strength is gone. You have put me in the power of enemies too strong for me.
translation_verse: Ko nye de o kwei a wɛleera yam mo o ke daane, ne nɔɔno na vɔge ŋone daane tei to. O ta kwei-ya o lei a ba ne pa se a dam maama jei mo. Baŋa Wɛ na kwei-ne o ke a dona jeŋa ne to, a ware se a zege de-ba.

english_verse: You, Lord, have turned back my warriors and crushed my young heroes. Judah was a woman untouched, but you let her be trampled like grapes in a wine pit.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ tete mo maŋe o ve a na teere de babɛ selo to. O ma bwoŋi nɔn-kɔgɔ se ba ba amo baŋa, ye ba daare ba meere a nɔn-donno tem. Wɛ tete mo nɔne Judah dwi tiina bam o le, ne nɔɔno na nɔne sɛɛro o le swa wone tei to.

english_verse: Because of this, I mourn, and tears flood my eyes. No one is here to comfort or to encourage me; we have lost the war— my people are suffering. The Prophet Speaks:
translation_verse: Wonnu tento ŋwaane nam mo pa se a yɔɔre a keera. A yia yi-na de maa chuuri bare-bare. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera se kotu zuri a bochare. Nɔɔno tera se o woli-ne se a jwoori a tete ne. Amo bia bam daa ba jege jwa, kokuri to, dé dona bam wane debam mo.”

english_verse: Zion reaches out her hands, but no one offers comfort. The Lord has turned the neighboring nations against Jacob's descendants. Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag to her neighbors. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Jerusalem yɔɔre o lwoori wolim mo nɔɔna tei ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera se kotu zi o bochare. Baŋa Wɛ maŋe o ta Jakob dwi tiina yera taane o we, ba fara wó ji ba dona. Jerusalem seene o ji wo-zɔɔne mo banto yiga ne, pa se ba chuli‑o.

english_verse: Won't you look and see how upset I am, our Lord? My stomach is in knots, and my heart is broken because I betrayed you. In the streets and at home, my people are slaughtered.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ, nii ko na tiini ko yi-ne tei! Ko jege-ne mo ko ni. A wo kom tete de ma di, a na nwoŋi n ni dem kwaga ne to ŋwaane. Teo kom chwei sem ne, nɔɔna toa jara wone mo. Sɔŋɔ ne de, toone ta maa wora.

english_verse: Don't let their evil deeds escape your sight. Punish them as much as you have punished me because of my sins. I never stop groaning— I've lost all hope!
translation_verse: Pa se ba lwarem kikia maama taa tigi n yiga ne, se n pa ko zo ba de yera, ne n na pɛ ko zo amo yera tei a wɛleera yam maama ŋwaane to. A tiini a vuvuni dedɛ. A wo de ma jei.”

english_verse: The Lord was angry! So he disgraced Zion though it was Israel's pride and his own place of rest. In his anger he threw Zion down from heaven to earth.
translation_verse: Nii Baŋa Wɛ bane na zaŋe Zion teo kom baŋa ne tei! O ban-lom li-ba mo ne kunkwon-liliru tei. Wɛ ma pa se Isarele tiina bam lonne jejegero ji kafɛ. O ma zege wɛyuu ne o de-te tega ne. Maŋa kalo o bane na zaŋe de Jerusalem to, o daa maŋe o wo sɛ se o wara-jei sem taa wora.

english_verse: The Lord had no mercy! He destroyed the homes of Jacob's descendants. In his anger he tore down every walled city in Judah; he toppled the nation together with its leaders, leaving them in shame.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ chɔge teene delo maama Jakob dwi tiina na zoore de wone to mo. O wo kom na fuli to ŋwaane, o vaŋe Judah tiina dam jei sem maama o de tega ne mo. O ma chɔge ba teene dem de ba pwa bam de, pa se ba zula maama ti.

english_verse: The Lord was so furiously angry that he wiped out the whole army of Israel by not supporting them when the enemy attacked. He was like a raging fire that swallowed up the descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: O ma pa se Isarele jar-keira bam maama dam ti o ban-lom dem ŋwaane. Ba dona na beene ba baŋa ne to, o ma dɔne o jeŋa o daare-ba. Wonto tete jigi ne min-vogo na ye tei to mo, ye o yɔɔre o zwɛ Jakob dwi tiina bam kula!

english_verse: The Lord was like an enemy! He left Israel in ruins with its palaces and fortresses destroyed, and with everyone in Judah moaning and weeping.
translation_verse: Chega to, Baŋa Wɛ jigi Isarele tiina bam dono mo. O ma yɔɔre o chɔge-ba. O mage ba sɔ-fwaaro tem pa te ji di-dwonnu mo. O nam ta chɔge ba dam jei sem de. O ma pa se Judah tiina keira kam puli dedɛ, ye ka ba tia.

english_verse: He shattered his temple like a hut in a garden; he completely wiped out his meeting place, and did away with festivals and Sabbaths in the city of Zion. In his fierce anger he rejected our king and priests.
translation_verse: Wɛ ta yigi o diga kam o de tega ne, ne ka ga ye kara wo vwei mo. O ma pa se o nɔɔna bam de swei se ba yeini ba di kura yam, ye ba ta swei o siu dɛ dem swia. Ko ná ye pɛ wom de kaanem tiina bam maama, Wɛ nwoŋi ba kwaga ne o ban-lom dem ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Lord had decided to tear down the walls of Zion stone by stone. So he started destroying and did not stop until walls and fortresses mourned and trembled.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ jaane o boboŋa mo se o yigi Zion kabiri sem o de tega ne. O ma maŋe se dedɔrem baŋa chekke, ye o daare o chɔge se maama fase. Kabiri selo ya na kaare teo kom se che to maama laam maa tigi tega ne buri-buri.

english_verse: Zion's gates have fallen facedown on the ground; the bars that locked the gates are smashed to pieces. Her king and royal family are prisoners in foreign lands. Her priests don't teach, and her prophets don't have a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Jerusalem teo ni-bworru tem moore tega ne mo. Wɛ ma yɔɔre o bwori te luuru tem. Ko ná ye teo kom pɛ de pa-bia bam, o kale-ba o ja o vo o de teene dedwonna wone mo. Nɔɔna daa ba mae Wɛ bera yam ba toŋa. Wɛ sampwori sem daa ware se ba lɔre Baŋa Wɛ kwora na ye tei to.

english_verse: Zion's leaders are silent. They just sit on the ground, tossing dirt on their heads and wearing sackcloth. Her young women can do nothing but stare at the ground.
translation_verse: Zion nakwa bam laam jei tega ne mo chemm. Ba wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane mo ba taare ba yuni de kasolo, ye ba ta yɔɔre ba zo gare-nyenyaaro ba jei. Jerusalem teo bukwa bam de gwoori ba tira tega ne mo de chaveera.

english_verse: My eyes are red from crying, my stomach is in knots, and I feel sick all over. My people are being wiped out, and children lie helpless in the streets of the city.
translation_verse: A keeri a yia yi-na maama a ti. A wo kom de ma yɔɔre ko pɛ. Amo jworo nye de ko lwogi mo ko tigi tega ne, kokuri to, ba jege a nɔɔna bam ba chɔge mo. Bia de bu-sese yɔɔre ba tigi teo kom chwei sem ne mo.

english_verse: A child begs its mother for food and drink, then blacks out like a wounded soldier lying in the street. The child slowly dies in its mother's arms.
translation_verse: Bia bam maa tɛ de ba niina ba we “Dé lage wodiu mo se dé di.” Ba ma to teo kom chwei sem ne, ne ko na tiini ko zo babɛ tei jara-keim ne to. Ba ŋwea ma ti ba niina bam ja-kukworru wone.

english_verse: Those who pass by shake their heads and sneer as they make fun and shout, “What a lovely city you were, the happiest on earth, but look at you now!”
translation_verse: Balo maama na tɔge abam seeni ba kɛ to laam jege abam mo ba yeera. Ba ta chweese mo, ye ba daare ba dole ba yuni, Jerusalem teo kom na nɛ chɔgem to ŋwaane. Ba maa mɔna ye ba tɛ ba we, “Teo kolo na lana ko gaale to mo tento na? Nabiina maama daa jege wopwolo de-ko na?”

english_verse: Zion, your enemies curse you and snarl like wild animals, while shouting, “This is the day we've waited for! At last, we've got you!”
translation_verse: Abam dona maama jege abam mo ba twea. Ba maa chweese abam. Ba maa nyɔne ba yibia de abam ye ba we, “Dé laam wane-ba dé chɔge dé yage. Dé ya jei dé cheigi dɛ dento mo, dé yi nam nɛ-de!”

english_verse: Zion, deep in your heart you cried out to the Lord. Now let your tears overflow your walls day and night. Don't ever lose hope or let your tears stop.
translation_verse: Zion teo kom, keeri-na de kwor-dɛa á lwoori Baŋa Wɛ. Pa-na á yi-na taa chuuri bare-bare wea de tete maama ne. Yé sɛ-na se á sii. Á yia de nam yé kɔ keira.

english_verse: Get up and pray for help all through the night. Pour out your feelings to the Lord, as you would pour water out of a jug. Beg him to save your people, who are starving to death at every street crossing. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Zaŋe-na dɔɔm ne se á keeri á jare Baŋa Wɛ. Lwoori-o-na titwon-twono tete dem maama wone. Lwo-na á wo-chechɔgɔ kom maama á tiŋi Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, ne nɔɔna na lwogi na ba tiŋi tega ne tei to. Zeiŋi-na á je Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se á lwoori‑o, se o duri á bia bam ŋwaŋa se ba yé te. Kokuri to, kana wora ka go-ba teo kom chwei sem maama ne.

english_verse: Think about it, Lord! Have you ever been this cruel to anyone before? Is it right for mothers to eat their children, or for priests and prophets to be killed in your temple?
translation_verse: “Baŋa Wɛ, nii debam seeni, se n duri dé ŋwaŋa. Ko ye n tete nɔɔna mo n jege n yaara! N lage se kaana kwei ba tete bia balo ba na jege ba kɔne to mo ba di na? N ta lage se ba go n kaanem tiina bam de n sampwori sem n tete diga kam ne mo na?

english_verse: My people, both young and old, lie dead in the streets. Because you were angry, my young men and women were brutally slaughtered.
translation_verse: Nɔn-donno de nɔn-kwe maama mo tega ba tigi teo kom chwei sem ne. Nɔn-donno de bukɔ-pwoli de ma yɔɔre ba te jara wone. Nmo bane na zaŋe de-ba to pɛ se n go-ba. N yɔɔre n gwoni-ba n tiŋi mo ye n wo jaane ba ŋwaŋa.

english_verse: He chased me into a dark place, where no light could enter.
translation_verse: O yɔɔre o kale-ne mo se a taa vei lim wone, ye pwooni daa tera kɔtaa!

english_verse: I am the only one he punishes over and over again, without ever stopping.
translation_verse: O nam yɔɔre o jege-ne o maga mo taa. O ma dole o jaguli-zane a yera ne dɛ maama wone.

english_verse: God caused my skin and flesh to waste away, and he crushed my bones.
translation_verse: O ma pa a ya-nɔna yam kwe lela, ye o daare o ja a kwi sem o bwori.

english_verse: he forced me to sit in the dark like someone long dead.
translation_verse: O ma zeili-ne pa se a jei yibiri wone, ne balo na tege ba dáane to.

english_verse: God built a fence around me that I cannot climb over, and he chained me down.
translation_verse: Ko nye de o pe-ne mo o yage diga ne, ye o ta vɔ-ne de chegero se a yé lu.

english_verse: Even when I shouted and prayed for help, he refused to listen.
translation_verse: Amo ná maŋe a keeri a jare‑o tei maama de, o yeini o ve se o cheigi-ne mo.

english_verse: God put big rocks in my way and made me follow a crooked path.
translation_verse: O mɛ kandwa mo o lɔ kabiri o che a chwoŋa. Chwoŋa daa tera se a wane a tɔge da a kɛ.

english_verse: God was like a bear or a lion waiting in ambush for me;
translation_verse: O seigi jei ne mo o tiga, ne kago-varem tei. O maa lage se o zi-ne, ne nywoŋo na ke tei to.

english_verse: God took careful aim and shot his arrows
translation_verse: O yɔɔre o saŋe o taŋa mo, ye o laam jege-ne o tae de chena.

english_verse: I am a joke to everyone— no one ever stops making fun of me.
translation_verse: Amo nɔɔna bam laam jege-ne mo ba mɔna. Dɛ maama ba leeni lei mo ba ma twe-ne.

english_verse: I cannot find peace or remember happiness.
translation_verse: Yazura daa tera amo tei ne. Amo swei wopwolo na ye tei to.

english_verse: I tell myself, “I am finished! I can't count on the Lord to do anything for me.”
translation_verse: Amo laam ma ta a we, “A dam dem jei. Teena yalo amo ya na jege Baŋa Wɛ tei ne to de ti.”

english_verse: Just thinking of my troubles and my lonely wandering makes me miserable.
translation_verse: A guli a chanɛɛre dem, de a na kare a beeri yɔɔ yerane tei to gula. A ŋwea yɔɔre ka su de wo-chɛɛro mo.

english_verse: That's all I ever think about, and I am depressed.
translation_verse: A maa ná yeini a guli konto maama, a wo wó chɔge mo.

english_verse: The Lord's kindness never fails! If he had not been merciful, we would have been destroyed.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ na yɔɔre o jege o swono tei to bá fɔge ko ti. O na yeini o duri debam yibwona tei to de nam ba tia.

english_verse: The Lord can always be trusted to show mercy each morning.
translation_verse: Tega ná poore dɛ maama, tento yeini te jwoori te wora mo. Chega to, nmo zaane dem tiini de daga.

english_verse: Deep in my heart I say, “The Lord is all I need; I can depend on him!”
translation_verse: Amo wó ta a tete ne mo we, “Baŋa Wɛ wo amo tei ne. O nam maŋe amo. Wonto yera ne mo a teena maama tiga.”

english_verse: The Lord is kind to everyone who trusts and obeys him.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ lana mo o pa balo na sale‑o to. O maa zeini balo na tui o tei to.

english_verse: It is good to wait patiently for the Lord to save us.
translation_verse: Ko lana mo se nɔɔna taa cheigi chemm ba nii se Baŋa Wɛ jwoŋi-ba o yage.

english_verse: When we are young, it is good to struggle hard
translation_verse: Nɔn-donno ná lɔre se ba peene ba tete, ko wó taa lana ko pa-ba.

english_verse: and to sit silently alone, if this is what the Lord intends.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ná korese nɔɔno wolo, ko maŋe se kotu zuri o yera mo o pa‑o.

english_verse: Being rubbed in the dirt can teach us a lesson;
translation_verse: O nam ná tu o tete konto dwoŋi teena daa wó jwoori ya ba o tei ne.

english_verse: He causes a lot of suffering, but he also has pity because of his great love.
translation_verse: O ná maŋe o chɔge ba wo tei de, o ta wó duri ba ŋwaŋa, o swono kom na tiini ko daga to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Lord doesn't enjoy sending grief or pain.
translation_verse: Wonto ba swoi se o ja yaara naa cham o ba o de nabiina baŋa ne.

english_verse: or cheat anyone out of what is rightfully theirs. God Most High sees everything,
translation_verse: Kotu ná ve Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom ni, ye o che nɔɔna de ba chega, ko lana na?

english_verse: and he knows when you refuse to give someone a fair trial.
translation_verse: Kotu ná ve nɔɔno bora taane dim baŋa ne, Baŋa Wɛ ba nae ko maama na?

english_verse: Good and bad each happen at the command of God Most High.
translation_verse: Ko ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom kwora mo pae se cham de ywoni tui nabiina baŋa.

english_verse: We're still alive! We shouldn't complain when we are being punished for our sins.
translation_verse: Wɛ nam ná waare nabiina ba wɛleera ŋwaane, ba wolo ná poone ko baŋa ne, ko jege kuri na?

english_verse: Instead, we should think about the way we are living, and turn back to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nam pa-na se dé fɔge dé maane dé ŋwea na ye tei to, se dé laam daare dé jwoori Baŋa Wɛ tei.

english_verse: When we lift our hands in prayer to God in heaven, we should offer him our hearts and say,
translation_verse: Pa-na se dé pore dé bochara, ye dé zeiŋi dé je wɛɛne dé jeeri Baŋa Wɛ se dé ta we:

english_verse: “We've sinned! We've rebelled against you, and you haven't forgiven us!
translation_verse: “Baŋa Wɛ, debam tusi ye dé ta nwoŋi n kwaga ne. Nmo wo yage dé wɛleera n chɛ debam.

english_verse: Anger is written all over you, as you pursue and slaughter us without showing pity.
translation_verse: Nmo mɛ n bane dem mo n pɛ debam kwaga n pu. N ma‑n daare n go debam, ye n wo duri dé ŋwaŋa.

english_verse: You are behind a wall of clouds that blocks out our prayers.
translation_verse: Nmo yɔɔre n kwei kunkwoŋo mo n che n tete, pa wɛ-lworo tera dé na wó ke se ko yi‑m.

english_verse: We are terrified and trapped, caught and crushed.”
translation_verse: Cham de chɔgem dedɛ mo tu debam baŋa. Foone maa jege debam.”

english_verse: until the Lord looks down from heaven and helps.
translation_verse: se ko yi Baŋa Wɛ ná zege wɛyuu ne, ye o tiiri o nii o na-ne.

english_verse: I am horrified when I see what enemies have done to the young women of our city.
translation_verse: A wo tiini ko chɔge, a yia na nae wonnu telo to ŋwaane, de a na nɛ a teo kom bukwa bam na yaare tei to.

english_verse: No one had reason to hate me, but I was hunted down like a bird.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye balo na chuli-ne ba tete boboŋa ŋwaane to, ba jege-ne ba para ne nɔɔno na zeili zuŋa se o ja tei to mo.

english_verse: Then they tried to kill me by tossing me into a pit and throwing stones at me.
translation_verse: Ba ma ja-ne ba vo ba dole ba yage gwoŋ-chanluŋu wone, ye ba daare ba dole-ne de kandwa se ba go.

english_verse: Water covered my head— I thought I was gone.
translation_verse: Na ma bibili a baŋa ne ba kɛa. A ma boŋe we a ŋwea ti mo.

english_verse: From the bottom of the pit, I prayed to you, Lord.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ, amo de ma zege gwoŋo kom wone a bwoŋi n yere se n ba n zeini-ne.

english_verse: I begged you to listen. “Help!” I shouted. “Save me!” You answered my prayer
translation_verse: Nmo ma‑n cheigi a na lwoori‑m tei a we, “Yé se n zwa. Nam cheigi a wɛ-lworo kom.”

english_verse: and came when I was in need. You told me, “Don't worry!”
translation_verse: Amo na bwoŋi‑m konto to mo n fɔɔre n yi a tei. N ma‑n ta de amo n we, “Yé ta‑n fona.”

english_verse: No matter what they are doing, they keep on mocking me.
translation_verse: Nii-ba mo! Ba kikia maama wone, ba jege-ne mo ba mɔne de ba lei sem.

english_verse: Pay them back for everything they have done, Lord!
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ, yiri jene ba baŋa ne, se ko maŋe de kolo maama ba na ke to.

english_verse: Get angry and go after them until not a trace is left under the heavens.
translation_verse: Tɔge n ban-lom dem baŋa n zeili-ba n ja, se n daare n ti-ba se ba yere saare tega baŋa ne.

english_verse: The purest gold is ruined and has lost its shine; jewels from the temple lie scattered in the streets.
translation_verse: Nii sabu-seŋa kam na gɛ ka lam dem tei! Sabu-seŋ-laao kom daa ba jege yuu. Kandwa-nyenno tem laam jage, pa te tigi teo kom chwei sem maama ne.

english_verse: These are Zion's people, worth more than purest gold; yet they are counted worthless like dishes of clay.
translation_verse: Zion teo nɔɔna bam déem tiini ba jege dunni, ne sabu-seŋa na ye tei to mo. Leile konto ba laam nam nye de kambi selo kamɔ-mɔro na mɔɔne to mo.

english_verse: Babies are so thirsty that their tongues are stuck to the roof of the mouth. Children go begging for food, but no one gives them any.
translation_verse: Na-nyɔm mo lage de go bia bam. Ba nia de ma ko ya peere. Ba yɔɔre ba lwoori wodiu mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba sɛ o ke o pa-ba.

english_verse: All who ate expensive foods lie starving in the streets; those who grew up in luxury now sit on trash heaps.
translation_verse: Balo déem na jege wodi-laaro ba di ne pwa tei to, kana laam wora ka go-ba teo kom chwei sem ne mo. Balo nam ya na jege ywoni ba di to, laam mo tigi tampuura baŋa ne.

english_verse: My nation was punished worse than the people of Sodom, whose city was destroyed in a flash without the help of human hands.
translation_verse: A nɔɔna bam na nɛ waarem delo to daga de dwoi delo Sodom tiina na nɛ to. Banto déem nɛ chɔgem bedwe baŋa ne mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se o woli-ba.

english_verse: The leaders of Jerusalem were purer than snow and whiter than milk; their bodies were healthy and glowed like jewels.
translation_verse: Jerusalem dedɛɛra bam déem tiini ba lana dedɛ. Ba maa ye nɔn-pwonnu. Ba ta ma kwɛ ba yera pa se ya nyeena ne kandwa-nyenno tei. Ba maa jege dam de yazura lanyerane.

english_verse: Now they are blacker than tar, and no one recognizes them; their skin clings to their bones and is drier than firewood.
translation_verse: Ba yibia laam ye ligi-ligi ka dwoi sambinnu mo. Ba ná nwoŋi pwooni, nɔɔna ware se ba lɔre-ba. Ba yera yam ma kwaare ya tane ba kwi ne. Ba ya-nɔna yam ma ko, ne dɛ na koge tei to.

english_verse: Life in the city is so bad that loving mothers have boiled and eaten their own children.
translation_verse: Kaana balo na ye pu-bwon-nyena to mo mɛ ba tete je ba go ba bia ba di. Ba saŋe ba bia mo ba di, se ba wori teo kom chɔgem baŋa ne.

english_verse: Not a king on this earth or the people of any nation believed enemies could break through her gates.
translation_verse: Logo baŋa pwa bam de nabiina jei maama ne ya ba boŋe we, debam dona wó na chwoŋa se ba zo Jerusalem wone ba chɔge teo kom.

english_verse: Jerusalem was punished because her prophets and her priests had sinned and caused the death of innocent victims.
translation_verse: Konto nam seene ko ke. Ko maa ye teo kom sampwori de ba kaanem tiina wɛleera yam ŋwaane mo. Kokuri to, banto jege nɔn-ŋona mo teo kom wone ba goe kafɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: Instead, everyone shouted, “Go away! Don't touch us! You're filthy and unfit to belong to God's people!” So they had to leave and become refugees. But foreign nations told them, “You can't stay here!”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna tɔɔle ba de ba zwa ne mo ba we, “Lage-na jei dé tei ne, se á biini á tete dedɛ! Yé dwei-na debam!” Ba nam na kare teene dedwonna ne ba beeri jeiŋa jei to, dwi-gɛ tiina tɛ ba taane ba we, “Dé bá sɛ se ba taa zoore debam tetare ne.”

english_verse: The Lord is the one who sent them scattering, and he has forgotten them. No respect or kindness will be shown to the priests or leaders.
translation_verse: Ko nam ye Baŋa Wɛ tete mo jage-ba o yage. O yiga daa tera de-ba. Nɔɔna daa ba nege kaanem tiina bam. Nakwa bam de maa ba nae zula nɔɔna tei ne.

english_verse: They swooped down faster than eagles from the sky. They hunted for us in the hills and set traps to catch us out in the desert.
translation_verse: Balo na zeili debam se ba ja to nye de maaro na nwoŋi wɛyuu ne te tu te zi wonnu tei to mo. Dé na duri dé di peero yuu to, mo ba pɛ debam kwaga ba pu. Dé na yɔɔre dé zo kagoa kam wone to, ba ta li debam da.

english_verse: The Lord's chosen leader was our hope for survival! We thought he would keep us safe somewhere among the nations, but even he was caught in one of their traps.
translation_verse: Ba ma che kalanchorro ba ja Baŋa Wɛ na tiŋi pɛ wolo o pa debam to, ye wonto ya mo pɛ debam pempanno. Dé nam ya teene we, dé na zoore o woro kom wone to, teene delo na gilimi debam to bá wane debam de di.

english_verse: The people of Zion have paid for their sins, and the Lord will soon let them return home. But, people of Edom, you will be punished, and your sins exposed.
translation_verse: Abam Zion tiina bam, waarem delo á na nɛ á tusim ŋwaane to wó kɛ. Wɛ bá yage abam sa-teo ne yiga yiga se ko dáane. Ko daare, ko ná ye abam Edom tiina bam, o lage o waare abam mo á wɛleera ŋwaane, se nɔɔna lɔre we á puseŋa kikia gaale.

english_verse: Our Lord, don't forget how we have suffered and been disgraced.
translation_verse: Dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ, guli kolo na yi debam to. Nii n na dé yuu na tiini ko yaale tei to!

english_verse: Foreigners and strangers have taken our land and our homes.
translation_verse: Veira laam mo jwoŋi debam tega kam ba tei. Dé sam dem laam ma ji sa-teena nyem.

english_verse: We are like children whose mothers are widows.
translation_verse: Dé kwoa daa tera ye ba daare debam botara. Dé niina de laam ma ji kadeina.

english_verse: We are terribly mistreated; we are worn out and can find no rest.
translation_verse: Dé dona mo pɛ dé kwaga ba pu. Dé yɔɔre dé bugi mo, ye siu tera ko pae debam.

english_verse: We had to surrender to Egypt and Assyria because we were hungry.
translation_verse: Dé laam to dé pa Ejipti de Asiria tiina mo, se ba pa debam wodiu se dé ma dé wori.

english_verse: Our ancestors sinned, but they are dead, and we are left to pay for their sins.
translation_verse: Dé kwoa mo tusi, ba nam daa tera. Wɛ ma waare debam banto wɛleera ŋwaane.

english_verse: Slaves are now our rulers, and there is no one to set us free.
translation_verse: Dé dona bam kabɛ laam mo tei debam. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam tera se o jwoŋi debam ba jeŋa ne o yage.

english_verse: We are in danger from brutal desert tribes; we must risk our lives just to bring in our crops.
translation_verse: Dé yeini dé dole dé ŋwea mo dé yage se dé na wodiu. Kokuri to, nɔn-gora mo kare ba zi nɔɔna kagoa kam ne.

english_verse: Our skin is scorched from fever and hunger.
translation_verse: Dé yera yam maama maa lone bakke. Dé kana kam laam jigi paa ka daane debam.

english_verse: On Zion and everywhere in Judah our wives and daughters are being raped.
translation_verse: Baara yeini ba zi dé kaana bam Zion teo kom ne. Ba maa fe dé busankan-pwoli sem Judah teene dem maama ne ba laga.

english_verse: Our rulers are strung up by their arms, and our nation's advisors are treated shamefully.
translation_verse: Ba jaane dé teo kom dedɛɛra mo ba kuuni de ŋone ba go. Ba maa wo nege dé nakwa bam kɔtaa!

english_verse: Young men are forced to do the work of slaves; boys must carry heavy loads of wood.
translation_verse: Ba jege dé nɔn-donno tem mo ba cho muni. Bakeiri bia de jege se ba zeŋe dɛ selo na duna se dwoi-ba to mo.

english_verse: Our leaders are not allowed to decide cases in court, and young people no longer play music.
translation_verse: Dé teo kom nakwa daa ware teo kom manchwoŋo ni ne se ba jeini. Nɔn-donno tem maa ba mage gungwei.

english_verse: Our hearts are sad; instead of dancing, we mourn.
translation_verse: Wopwolo kikia maama jei debam tei ne. Dé jɔŋɔ magem maama laam leiri ko ji keira mo.

english_verse: Zion's glory has disappeared! And we are doomed because of our sins.
translation_verse: Dé nenɔŋa kam maama jei. Lɛɛro ma yi debam, dé wɛleera yam ŋwaane.

english_verse: We feel sick all over and can't even see straight;
translation_verse: Mo kokuri dé wo maama jei. Dé daa ba nae chekke, dé yia na suli de yi-na to ŋwaane.

english_verse: You will rule forever, Lord! You are King for all time.
translation_verse: Dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo ye pɛ mo taa wuu. N paare dem bá taa jege kweelim se ko taa vei wuu.

english_verse: I am Ezekiel—a priest and the son of Buzi. Five years after King Jehoiachin of Judah had been led away as a prisoner to Babylonia, I was living near the Chebar River among those who had been taken there with him. Then on the fifth day of the fourth month of the thirtieth year, the heavens suddenly opened. The Lord placed his hand upon me and showed me some visions.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwora déem yi amo ye a zege Chebara buga kam ni ne mo Babilon teo wone. A ma maane we Baŋa Wɛ dam dem tu amo wolo na ye Buzi bu Ezekeli ye a ye Wɛ kaanem tu to baŋa.

english_verse: I saw a windstorm blowing in from the north. Lightning flashed from a huge cloud and lit up the whole sky with a dazzling brightness. The fiery center of the cloud was as shiny as polished metal,
translation_verse: Amo déem kwoni a yuu a nii a na vo-dɛɔ na nwoŋi baŋa seeni ko foore ko beena. Kunkwoŋ-zɔŋɔ ma da ko baŋa ko ba ye ko pepele jei maama de dam. Pwooni delo na tiini de pera to maa gilimi ko maama. Kunkwoŋo kom tetare mini dem yɔɔre de seene mo ne channa na tiini ka nyeene tei to.

english_verse: and in that center I saw what looked like four living creatures. They were somewhat like humans,
translation_verse: A ma nii a na wo-kenkagela yana na ŋwe to mini dem tetare ne. Ya déem nye de nabiina mo,

english_verse: except that each one had four faces and four wings.
translation_verse: ye wo-kenkagele maama laam jege yibi sena, de vɔna yana se de taa maa jaana.

english_verse: Their legs were straight, but their feet looked like the hoofs of calves and sparkled like bronze.
translation_verse: Ya nɛ sem nam yɔɔre se twe mo, ye ya napera seeni maa nye de na-mɔra napɔɔna yalo na nyeene ne channa na nyeene tei to.

english_verse: The four creatures were standing back to back with the tips of their wings touching. They moved together in every direction, without turning their bodies.
translation_verse: Ya ma kwei ya vɔna ya dwei daane. Wo-kenkagele maama yɔɔre de vei de yiga na jeeri mɛ to mo, pa se de vei ye de ba pipira.

english_verse: Each creature had the face of a human in front, the face of a lion on the right side, the face of a bull on the left, and the face of an eagle in back.
translation_verse: Ya maama jege yibi sena sena mo na ye se yera: Dedoa maama jege nabiinu yibia de yiga seeni. Nywoŋo yibia maa wo de jazem seeni. Nabea yibia maa wo de jagwia seeni. Maao yibia de maa wo de kwaga kam seeni.

english_verse: Two wings of each creature were spread out and touched the wings of the creatures on either side. The other two wings of each creature were folded against its body.
translation_verse: Wo-kenkagele maama vɔna zeiŋi wɛɛne mo, ye ya yalei yarege ya dwei wo-kenkagela yalo na zege ya yeiri de yera ne to vɔna yam jazem de jagwia seeni. Ko na daare vɔna yalei yadwonna yam to, de laam ma kwei yanto de kwoli de yera yam.

english_verse: The four living creatures went wherever the Spirit led them, and they moved together without turning their bodies, because each creature faced straight ahead.
translation_verse: Wo-kenkagele maama mo yɔɔre de vei yiga ye de ba pipira. Ya maa vei ya jworo kom na bere se ya vo mɛ to.

english_verse: The creatures were glowing like hot coals, and I saw something like a flaming torch moving back and forth among them. Lightning flashed from the torch every time its flame blazed up.
translation_verse: Wo-kenkagela yam nye de min-mɔɔla naa min-zwonnu mo wo ya tetare ne. Mini dem maa zaŋa ya tetare ne ye de vei yiga de kwaga. De tiini de nyeene dedɛ mo ye de pepela.

english_verse: The creatures themselves moved as quickly as sparks jumping from a fire.
translation_verse: Wo-kenkagela yam tete maa yɔɔre ya vei yiga de kwaga lela ne doa pepelem to.

english_verse: I then noticed that on the ground beside each of the four living creatures was a wheel,
translation_verse: A na zege da a nii wo-kenkagela yam konto to, mo a nɛ wo-gigilu na tigi tega ne ya maama dedoa dedoa teiŋa ne.

english_verse: shining like chrysolite. Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it,
translation_verse: Wo-gigillu tena tem nye daane mo, ye te nyeena ne kandwa-nyenno. Wo-gigilu maama maa nye de ko jege wo-gigilu kodwoŋi na wo ko wone ko gare-ko to.

english_verse: The rims of the wheels were large and frightening, and they had eyes all the way around them.
translation_verse: Wo-gigillu tem nia déem dɔra mo ye ya tiini ya jege foone. Yia mo yɔɔre ya faare nia yam jei maama.

english_verse: The creatures controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the four creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels were beside them.
translation_verse: Ko na ye tei to, wo-kenkagela yam ná yeini ya via, wo-gigillu tem de tɔge de-ya te vei mo. Ya nam ná maŋe mɛ ya zege, wo-gigillu tem de wó taa zege mo. Ya daa ná zaŋe ya jaane wɛɛne, wo-gigillu tem de maa tɔge-ya te jaana. Kokuri to, wo-kenkagela yam jworo wo wo-gigillu tem wone mo.

english_verse: Above the living creatures, I saw something that was sparkling like ice, and it reminded me of a dome. Each creature had two of its wings stretched out toward the creatures on either side, with the other two wings folded against its body.
translation_verse: Pwola kam kuri seeni, wo-kenkagele maama yarege de vɔna mo pa ya dwei dedwoŋi vɔna. Wo-kenkagele maama ta ma kwei vɔna yalei de ma kwoli de yera yam.

english_verse: Whenever the creatures flew, their wings roared like an ocean or a large army or even the voice of God All-Powerful. And whenever the creatures stopped, they folded their wings against their bodies.
translation_verse: Wo-kenkagela yam ná yeini ya jaana, a ni ya vɔna yam na wuuri tei to mo. Ya sɔɔ kom nye de na-fwaaro na chuuri tei to mo. Ko ta maa nye de Dam-fɔrɔ Tu Wɛ wom tete kwora, naa jar-keira kɔgɔ sɔɔ na ye tei to. Ko daare ya ná jaane ya ti, ya yeini ya yage ya vɔna yam mo.

english_verse: When the creatures stopped flapping their wings, I heard a sound coming from above the dome.
translation_verse: Wo-kenkagela yam na zege da konto ye ya vɔna yam wo tega ne to, a ma ni kwora na nwoŋi pwola kalo na wo ya yuni tem baŋa seeni to.

english_verse: I then saw what looked like a throne made of sapphire, and sitting on the throne was a figure in the shape of a human.
translation_verse: Pwola kam wɛyuu baŋa seeni woŋo maa wora, ko na nye de paare yituŋu, ye Safira mo ba mɛ ba ke-ko. Woŋo kodwoŋi de maa wo wɛyuu baŋa seeni, ko na jei yituŋu kom baŋa ne ye ko nye de nabiinu na ye tei to.

english_verse: From the waist up, it was glowing like metal in a hot furnace, and from the waist down it looked like the flames of a fire. The figure was surrounded by a bright light,
translation_verse: A ma nii a na nenɛɛne ko na zege ko teiŋa seeni se ko taa diini to, ko yɔɔre ko nyeene ne channa na wo mini wone tei to mo. Ko ta na zege ko teiŋa ne se ko taa tua to, ko nye de ko ye mini mo. Pwooni delo na tiini de pera to de ma gilimi ko maama.

english_verse: as colorful as a rainbow that appears after a storm. I realized I was seeing the brightness of the Lord's glory! So I bowed with my face to the ground, and just then I heard a voice speaking to me.
translation_verse: Ko lam dem ye nenɛɛne doa ná nege ka waare ye manlaataŋa yeini ka gare wɛɛne tei to mo. Nyenyego kom konto bere-ne Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom na ye tei to mo. A na nɛ konto to, mo a vwi a yibia tega ne, ye a ni nɔɔno kwora na ŋɔɔne de amo.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, I want you to stand up and listen.”
translation_verse: O ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu, zaŋe n zege wɛɛne se a ŋɔɔne dede‑m.”

english_verse: After he said this, his Spirit took control of me and lifted me to my feet. Then the Lord said:
translation_verse: O na yɔɔre o wora o ŋɔɔne konto to, mo vio fuli ko zo-ne, ye ko gɔ-ne ko zege wɛɛne. Amo ma cheigi o na ŋɔɔne kolo de amo to.

english_verse: Ezekiel, I am sending you to the people of Israel. They are just like their ancestors who rebelled against me and refused to stop.
translation_verse: O ma ta o we, “Nabiinu, a lage a toŋe‑m Isarele tiina bam tei ne mo. Ba nam ye dwi delo nankɔɔre na daga to mo. Ba de ba nabaara bam nwoŋi amo kwaga ne, ye ba ta ve-ne de zem maama.

english_verse: They are stubborn and hardheaded. But I, the Lord God, have chosen you to tell them what I say.
translation_verse: Amo na toŋe‑m balo tei ne to yi dana ye ba zwa de ba ni taane. Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Taane dento ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage-de!’

english_verse: Those rebels may not even listen, but at least they will know that a prophet has come to them.
