translation_verse: Nmo déem seene n zo ba natera yam mo ye n lwoni ba wo-zɔɔna kikia yam. Nmo laam nam wo dáane ye n ke n dwoni banto na ke tei to!

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, the people of Sodom and its nearby villages were never as sinful as you.
translation_verse: Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we n nyaane Sodom de o bukwa bam wo-lwanno kikia wo yi nmo de n bukwa bam na ke tei to.

english_verse: They thought they were better than everyone else, and they did things I hate. And so I destroyed them.
translation_verse: Ba déem ta bere ba tete kamunim mo, ye ba swoi se ba taa ke wo-zɔɔna yalo amo na chuli to. Mo kokuri, a chɔge-ba, ne a na nɛ ba na ke tei to.

english_verse: You people of Jerusalem have sinned twice as much as the people of Samaria. In fact, your evil ways have made both Sodom and Samaria look innocent.
translation_verse: Samaria maa wo ke nmo wɛleera yam chichworo de. Nmo nam ke wo-zɔɔna n dwoni banto na ke tei to. Nmo na tiini n ke wo-zɔɔna konto to pɛ n zembaaro de n nyaane bere we ba jege bora ba dwoi‑m.

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you.
translation_verse: Konto baŋa ne mo n wó kwei tetɔ-goro n pu n yuu ne se chaveera ja‑m de n na ke kolo maama n ke dam n chorro tem kuri ne to.

english_verse: But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks.
translation_verse: Maŋa kalo nmo déem na bere n tete kamunim ye n puseŋa kikia yam ta wo nwoŋi pwooni to, n yiga tera n nyaane Sodom wone. Teene delo na gilimi‑m to laam nam jege‑m ba gwoona mo. Aram tiina, de Filisi tiina, de teene delo maama na bwola da to mo yaale‑m konto.

english_verse: You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nmo na yɔɔre n toŋe kabwoŋa de wo-zɔɔna to, wɛleera yam konto maama jene wó taa wo n yuu ne. Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.

english_verse: But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever.
translation_verse: De ko de, amo ta wó guli ni delo amo na gwoni de nmo ye n ta ye nɔn-doŋo to. A maa wó pa ni-gwonim dem konto taa wora taa wuu.

english_verse: When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement.
translation_verse: Nmo de maa wó guli wo-lwanno telo n ya na ke to pa se chaveera ja‑m. Kokuri to, a laam wó kwei n zembaaro Samaria de n nyaane Sodom a pa‑m se ba ji nmo tete bukwa, de banto ya na wo tɔge ba woli dé ni-gwonim dem wone to de.

english_verse: I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Amo laam maa wó pa se a na gwoni ni delo de nmo to zege, se abam wane á lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Amo nam wó yage wɛleera yalo maama n na ke to a ma a chɛ‑m. Konto baŋa ne n wó guli n na ke n chɔge tei to pa se chaveera ja‑m ye n bá wane n ni se n puri. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story,
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, véi n sɔɔle sensɔla n bere Isarele dwi tiina bam, se n ta memaŋe dento n bere-ba.

english_verse: so they will understand what I am saying to them: A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree,
translation_verse: Ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Maao mo jaane ko vo ko chu Lebanon laŋa kam ne. Ko déem tiini ko daga, ye ko vɔna yala. Ko koro de maa dɔra ye te ta tiini te lana de nyenyero dwi dwi. Ko laam ma vo ko ja Sedare tio na-gela kadwoŋi na wo tio kom yuu ne to.

english_verse: then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities.
translation_verse: Ko ma bwori naga kam ye ko daare ko ja-ka ko vo pipim-piina teo mɛ ko nɔn-bia bam na ke pipiu to ko jeiri da.

english_verse: The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream.
translation_verse: Maao kom daa ma kwei tio bu Isarele tega kam ne, ye ko vo ko jeiri-ko te-ywoŋa jeiga kadwoŋi ne. Jeiga kam wo bu-zaŋa teiŋa ne pa se tio kom be lela ne buga ni tio na ke tei to.

english_verse: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
translation_verse: Ko ma nwoŋi pa ko ji Vini tio na tage ko nɛ ko lware jei maama. Ko nɛ sem ma lware se tete se jeeri maao kom na wo mɛ to. Ko kuru tem nam sɔɔne tega ne mɛ ko na zege to mo. Ko na ye Vini tio konto to, ko ma ta nɛ dedɛ de vɔɔro tigi-tigi.

english_verse: But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
translation_verse: Ko nam maŋe ko zege te-ywoŋa ne mo, mɛ na na daga da se ko wane nɛ ko taa tae, ye ko daare ko ke bia, se ko taa yɔɔre ko ye tei-ŋoŋo to mo.’

english_verse: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
translation_verse: Nam ta ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Vini tio konto wó be lanyerane na? Boboa maao kom bá gɔ-ko o yage, ye o daare o poore ko bia bam, pa se ko vɔ-lɛɛro tem maama kwaare na? O nam wó yɔɔre o gɔ tio kom mɔle mɔle ye nɔn-kɔgɔ wo woli‑o.

english_verse: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
translation_verse: Nii-na ba na fɔge ba jeiri-ko tei to. Ko nam wó be lanyerane na? Vio ná zaŋe wɛ-puli seeni ko dole ko mage-ko, ko bá yɔɔre ko maŋe jeiga kalo ko na nwoŋi da to mo ko kwaare na?’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
translation_verse: “Ta de nɔɔna banto na ye zwabani-nyena to we, ‘Abam nam wo nigi memaŋe dem konto kuri na?’ Nam ta n bere-ba we, ‘Babilon teo pɛ mo vei Jerusalem, ye o kale teo kom konto pɛ de o dedɛɛra bam o ja o jwoori o tete teo Babilon.

english_verse: He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens,
translation_verse: O ma le pa-diga wone nɔɔno dedoa, pa o de kotu ke ni-sɛɛm daane. O ma pa kotu du duuri we, o wó taa jege chega o pa‑o. O nam ya kale teo kom nɔn-yum tem mo o ja o viiri,

english_verse: so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
translation_verse: se ko pa teo kom taa wo o dam kuri ne, se ba daa yé wane ba zeiŋi ba tete wɛɛne. O déem pɛ se ba dam zege ni-sɛɛm delo o na ke de-ba to wone.

english_verse: But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
translation_verse: O na le Judah teo pɛ wolo to nam nwoŋi ba ni-sɛɛm dem kwaga ne mo. O ma toŋe nɔɔna Ejipti teo ne se ba ja jar-keira de sisein-nɔɔna dedɛ ba ba ba pa‑o. Nɔɔno wonto nam wó wane o lu Babilon teo pɛ wom jeŋa ne na? O na lɔge ba ni-gwonim dem kwaga ne to, o wó jwoŋi o tete o yage na?

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king.
translation_verse: Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we kotu lage o te Babilon teo ne mo, se o bá lu. Ko ye Babilon teo pɛ mo tiŋi‑o paare, ye o nam chɔge duuri delo o na dugi to pa se o nwoŋi ni-sɛɛm delo ba na ke daane to kwaga ne. Babilon teo kom wone mo o lage o te!

english_verse: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Ne amo na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a lage a waare‑o mo. Ko ye amo yere ŋwaane mo o dugi duuri ye o ta ve-de. O na chɔge ni-gwonim delo to de maa ye amo nyem. O keina yam konto jene wó taa wo o yuu ne.

english_verse: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
translation_verse: A lage a che kalanchogo mo se ko ja‑o. A laam wó ja‑o a vo Babilon, ye a di o taane dáane, o na nwoŋi a kwaga ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: O jar-keira babɛ sem maama wó te jara wone. A ta wó jage balo na wó daare to a yage tega baŋa jei maama ne. Konto baŋa ne mo á wó lɔre we ko ye amo Baŋa Wɛ mo pɛ kwora kam konto.

english_verse: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo tete mo lage a ja Sedare tei-dedɔrɔ kodwoŋi na-gela, ye a daare a bwori na-bobɔla dedoa na wo ko yuu ne to. Amo tete laam wó ja-ka á vo a jeiri peo kodwoŋi yuu ne wɛ-wɛ.

english_verse: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
translation_verse: Isarele peero tem yuu ne mo a lage a jeiri-ka. Tio kom wó be lanyerane ye ko ta nɛ, ko daare ko ke bia. Ko maa wó ji Sedare tei-laao. Zuna dwi dwi wó ba da ba sɔ ba pworu ko nɛ sem ne, ye ba sii ko woro kom ne.

english_verse: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
translation_verse: Teeni dem maama na wo goa wone to wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. A maa wae a pa se tei-dedwaaro toe, ye a daare a pa teeni delo na wo tega ne to zaŋe wɛɛne. A ta wae a pa se teeni delo na jege vɔ-lɛɛro to kwaara, ye a daare a pa delo na kwaare to yera zuri. Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto. A nam wó seene a ke kolo a na tage to.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Bɛ mo ye abam jege memaŋe dento na vei Isarele tega kam seeni to ye á tɛ á we: ‘Kwoa mo ke ba wonnu, pa te zem laam gwori ba bia’?

english_verse: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
translation_verse: Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we abam daa bá maŋe memaŋe dem konto Isarele laŋa kam ne.

english_verse: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
translation_verse: Nii-na! Amo mo jege nabiina maama dam, ne ko ná ye kwo, naa o bu de. Ko ye wolo na ke wɛleera to mo jege se o te.

english_verse: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wolo ná seene o ye nɔn-ŋom chekke, kotu wae o ke totoŋ-ŋona ye o tɔge chwoŋa.

english_verse: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
translation_verse: O maa ba diini peero tem yuu se o di jwona wodiiru, ye o yiga tera de Isarele dwi tiina jwona yam. O ba ke tolo de o dwonna bam kaana. O maa ba peini de kaane wolo na jege o chana zarem o ke to.

english_verse: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
translation_verse: Konto tu ba jene wonnu o pae ye o daŋe nyɔɔre dedɛ jene dem baŋa ne. O maa cho o tete de wo-lwanno kikia ye o bore nɔɔna taane de chega.

english_verse: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
translation_verse: ye o kwo ya wo ke te kolokolo. O kare o di jwona wodiiru peero yuu bimbina yam ne. O ta maa swoi se o taa tigi de o dwoŋi kaane.

english_verse: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
translation_verse: O maa jege nabwona de yiniga tiina o bɛɛsa, ye o kare o vere nɔɔna. O yeini o cheiŋi kolo ba na pɛ‑o ba ma tiŋi daare to. O yiga maa wo jwona wone, ye o daare o tɔge wo-zɔɔna kikia.

english_verse: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
translation_verse: O ta yeini o jene wonnu o pa nɔɔna, ye o beeri nyɔɔre dedɛ mo se o dɔne. Nɔɔno ná ke konto dwoŋi, o wó jwoŋi o ŋwea o yage mo na? Kɔtaa! O bá na o ŋwea! Wo-zɔɔna yalo maama o na ke to ŋwaane, o wó te mo ye ko wó taa ye o tete yiga.

english_verse: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
translation_verse: O ba diini peero tem yuu se o di jwona wodiiru, ye o yiga tera de Isarele dwi tiina jwona yam. O maa ba ke tolo de o dwonna kaana.

english_verse: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
translation_verse: O maa cho o tete de totoŋ-balwaaro, ye o ba beeri nyɔɔre dedɛ se o dɔne jena baŋa ne. O maa toŋe o tɔge a nia yam de a bera yam. Bu wom konto bá te o kwo wɛleera ŋwaane. O wó taa ŋwe mo.

english_verse: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
translation_verse: Abam nam bwei we, ‘Bɛ mo ye bu wom konto bá tɔge o yaare o kwo tusim dem ŋwaane?’ Ko na ye tei to, bu wom na jege chega ye o ke kolo na maŋe to, o daare o toŋe o tɔge a bera yam to ŋwaane, o wó seene o taa ŋwe mo.

english_verse: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
translation_verse: Wolo ná ke wɛleere, konto tu mo jege se o te. Nɔɔno kwo wɛleera jene bá taa wo kotu yuu ne. Bu de wɛleera nam bá taa tɔge o kwo. Nɔn-ŋona wó na ba totoŋ-laaro tem nyɔɔre mo, se nɔn-balwaaro na waarem delo na maŋe de ba totoŋ-lwanno tem to.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
translation_verse: Á nam boŋe we puseŋ-nyena toone mo pae amo wo pwoli na? Ko nam na ye tei to, puseŋ-nyena ná pipiri ba yage ba chwei sem, se ko pa ba na ŋwea, konto wó pa a wo pwoli. Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Nɔn-ŋom ná pipiri o yage totoŋ-ŋona keim, ye o lɛɛre o ke wɛleera, o jege se o te mo o wɛleera kikia ŋwaane.

english_verse: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Kolo na wó jwoŋi‑o to ye o na jeeli o totoŋ-lwanno tem ni o ja, ye o daare o pipiri o yage-te to. O daa bá te, o wó taa ŋwe mo.

english_verse: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
translation_verse: Dole-na wɛleera yalo maama á na yeini á ke to á yage, se á daare á beeri bochare-doore de boboŋ-doora á pa á tete. Isarele dwi tiina bam, bɛ mo ye á beeri toone á pa á tete?

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno toone nam ba pae a wo pwola. Konto ŋwaane, pipiri-na á yage wɛleera kikia se á daare á na ŋwea. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
translation_verse: “Mɔ luseim leiŋa n pa Isarele teo dedɛɛra bam

english_verse: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Dwi-gɛ tiina laam ma ni ko ŋwa, ye ba daare ba ko gwoŋo ko ŋwaane pa ko to da. Ba ma kwei gwoli ba lei ko ba ne ye ba ja-ko ba vo Ejipti teo.

english_verse: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
translation_verse: Nywoŋ-kana kam na maane we ka teena yam wo ke, ye ka boboŋa yam de wo toŋe to, ka daa ma le ka bia bam wone dedoa ka korese-ko pa ko de ji nywoŋo na dana to.

english_verse: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
translation_verse: Teene delo maama na gilimi da to maa ba ba ke ni daane se ba ja-ko. Ba ma tiŋi ŋwe-choa se ba ja-ko, ye ko to ba gwoŋo wone.

english_verse: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma kwei gwoli ba lei ko ba ne, ye ba vaŋe-ko ba vo ba ke chefeɔ wone. Ba ma ja-ko ba vo ba pa Babilon teo pɛ wom. Ba ma pe nywoŋo kom konto, pa se ko ŋuurim dem daa yé taa ni Isarele peero tem yuni ne.

english_verse: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
translation_verse: Abam nu wom nam ya ta nye de Vini tio kolo ba na jeiri á Vini kara ne to mo pa ko wo buga teiŋa ne. Ko ma leiri bia dedɛ, ye ko nɛ sem de ke zwase, na na daga ko jeiga kam ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
translation_verse: Ba nam dɛ bane baŋa ne mo ba vaŋe-ko ba vuuri, ye ba daare ba dole-ko ba de tega ne. Vio ma zaŋe wɛ-puli seeni ko dole ko mage-ko, pa se ko tio-bia bam ko. Ko na-dɛɛro tem de ma bwori pa se te kwaare ye mini di-te.

english_verse: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_verse: Mini ma zege ko teiŋa ne de jage de yi ko nɛ sem de ko bia bam maama ko di kula. Na-dɛa daa wo daare se ka maŋe de pɛ nacheiga se o taa zeera.’ Leiŋa kanto mo ye luseim leiŋa, ye ba jege se ba taa jege-ka ba mɔɔne luseim mo.”

english_verse: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Bena yarepɛ bene dem chane senu chana kam da fuga dɛ dem ne, mo Isarele teo nakwa bam badwonna tu amo tei se ba bwei ba lɔre Baŋa Wɛ boboŋa na ye tei to. Ba ma ba ba jeini a yiga ne.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord God said:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, ŋɔɔne de Isarele teo nakwa bam se n ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam tu se á lɔre amo boboŋa na ye tei to mo na? Ne amo na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a bá pa abam chwoŋa se á lɔre a boboŋa. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.’

english_verse: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Nabiinu, nmo nam bá bore taane n vane-ba na? Tole ba kwoa bam wo-zɔɔna kikia yam taane se ba taa yei ya ni ne.

english_verse: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
translation_verse: Ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Maŋa kalo a déem na kuri Isarele tiina bam se ba taa ye a nyem to, a tu a veere a tete de Jakob dwi tiina bam Ejipti teo ne. A ma daare a du yi-seena duuri de-ba a we, “Amo mo ye abam Teiru Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
translation_verse: Amo ta ma du duuri maŋa kam konto ne a ta de-ba we, a wó ja-ba a nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne a vo tega kalo a ya na kuri a pa-ba to. Tega kam konto nam ye te-ŋoŋa kalo na lana ka dwoi jei maama, ye ka ywomma de varem de kɔnɔ to.

english_verse: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
translation_verse: A ma ta de-ba a we, “Abam maama nam dole-na wo-zɔɔna nyenyero telo á na zuli to á yage, se á daa yé ta‑á biini á tete de Ejipti tiina jwo-yɔɔro tem kaanem. Amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ba nam lɔge amo kwaga ne mo, pa ba ve se ba cheigi a taane dem. Ba wolowolo wo dole wo-zɔɔna yalo ba na zuli to de Ejipti tiina jwona yam ba yage. Konto ŋwaane amo boboŋa ma ja se a lwo a ban-lom dem ba baŋa ne, se a pa ba yaare Ejipti teo kom wone.

english_verse: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo a seene a ja-ba a nwoŋi Ejipti ne, ye a ja-ba a zo kagoa kam wo.

english_verse: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
translation_verse: A ma kwei a bera yam de a nia yam a pa-ba. Kokuri to, nɔɔno wolo ná toŋe o tɔge-ya, kotu wó na ŋwea ya baŋa ne.

english_verse: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
translation_verse: A ta ma tiŋi a siu da yam a pa-ba, se ya taa ye maana na tigi amo de banto tetare ne we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo kuri-ba se ba taa ye amo nyem.

english_verse: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Amo nam ba lage se dwi-gɛ tiina bam taa jege amo yere ba yaala, de banto na nii ye a ja Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi dáane to.

english_verse: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
translation_verse: Amo déem vane-ba konto, ba na ve a nia yam de a bera yam, ye ba ta yaale a siu da yam to ŋwaane mo. Ba fera nam tiini ya wo ba jwona kaanem wone mo.

english_verse: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
translation_verse: De ko de a duri ba ŋwaŋa mo, pa se a wo yɔɔre a chɔge-ba kagoa kam wone.

english_verse: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
translation_verse: A déem ma kaane ba bia bam kagoa yuu ne a we, “Abam de daa yé tɔge-na á kwoa bam chwei sem de ba chullu tem. Nam yé biini-na á tete de ba jwona yam kaanem.

english_verse: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Amo mo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom. Ta‑á sɛ-na amo bera yam, se á daare á ta‑á ke á tɔge a nia yam.

english_verse: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ta‑á jege-na a siu da yam se ya taa ye ya yera, se yanto taa ye maana amo de abam tetare ne. Konto mo abam wó lɔre we amo ye abam Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: De ko de, a yɔɔre a ja a bane dem mo, se dwi-gɛ tiina bam yé taa jege amo yere ba yaala, de banto na nii ye a ja Isarele tiina bam a nwoŋi Ejipti ne to.

english_verse: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Ko nam ye ba na wo sɛ ba tɔge amo nia yam, ye ba ve a bera yam to ŋwaane mo a ke-ba konto. Ba ta ma yaale amo siu da yam, ye ba daare ba pa ba fera zo ba kwoa jwona yam ne.

english_verse: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
translation_verse: A ma pa ba biini ba tete de pɛɛra yalo ba na kwei ba pa-ne to. Ba bere ba yeini ba kwei ba bu-kwe sem maama mo ba ke kaanem. A ke konto maama ba yera ne se foone mo zo-ba, ye ba daare ba lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.’

english_verse: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
translation_verse: Amo déem bwei-ba a we, “Jeiga kɔ mo á yeini á diini wɛ-wɛ se á ke kaanem da to?” ’ Mo kokuri ba bwoi jei sem yere we ‘Wɛ-wɛ Jeiga’ de zem maama.

english_verse: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Abam maa tɛ we, “Debam nam lage se dé taa nye de dwi-gɛ tiina bam na zoore logo baŋa teene dedwonna dem ne ye ba zuli wa yalo ba na mɛ dɛ de kandwa ba ke to mo.” Abam boboŋe dem nam bá fɔge de jeini.

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
translation_verse: Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we, amo wó taa ye abam pɛ, pa se a kwei a je-dɛa, de a dam maama, de a ban-lom dem a taa nii abam baŋa ne.

english_verse: and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered
translation_verse: A maa wó ja abam a nwoŋi teene delo maama a ya na jage abam a yage de wone to de je-dɛa, de dam, dedaane a ban-lom dem.

english_verse: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
translation_verse: Amo laam wó ja abam mo a vo a zege kagoa kam wone mɛ dwi-gɛ tiina na gilimi to. Dáane mo a wó jeeri abam yibia de yibia, ye a di á taane se á to.

english_verse: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: A ta wó korese abam pa se á ke ne dé ni-gwonim dem na bere se á ke tei to.

english_verse: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: A maa wó le zwabani-nyena balo na wo á wone to, de balo maama na ve-ne to. A nam wó ja-ba a nwoŋi sa-teene delo ba na zoore de wone to. Ba nam bá na chwoŋa se ba tɔge ba zo Isarele tega kam wone. Konto baŋa ne abam de wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
translation_verse: Amo ná jaane abam a nwoŋi sa-teene delo ne a na jage abam pa á zo dwi-gɛ tiina bam wone to, a laam wó sɛ a jwoŋi abam nenɛɛne á ye talwoŋ-ywoŋa mo ba zwɛ ba pa-ne. A ta ná wo abam tetare ne, a wó bere jaja we a ye wose mo, se dwi-gɛ tiina bam taa zege ba nia.

english_verse: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
translation_verse: Amo laam maa ná jaane abam a ja a jwoori Isarele tega kalo a déem na dugi duuri we a wó kwei-ka a pa á kwoa bam to, á wó seene á lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne, abam wó guli wo-zɔɔna kikia yalo á ya na ke pa se á biini á tete to. Konto wó pa á yaale á tete de wo-lwanno telo a ya na ke to.

english_verse: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
translation_verse: Isarele dwi tiina bam, abam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom, ne a ná tɔge a yere dem ŋwaane a duri abam ŋwaŋa, ye a wo waare abam se ko maŋe de á totoŋ-lwanno tem de á wo-zɔɔna kikia yam na ye tei to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ” Tega-kuri seeni taane

english_verse: Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna maama wó lɔre we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tɔre mini dem konto, ye de nam bá di de dwei kɔtaa.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pipiri n yibia n jeeri Jerusalem teo kom. Tɔɔle kwora n chɔge ko wara-jei sem, se n daare n pworisi taane n chɔge Isarele tega kam.

english_verse: that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil.
translation_verse: Ta de-ba we: ‘Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a vaŋe a se-zɔɔ mo a le ko pwolo kom ne, se a ma-ko a go nɔn-ŋona de puseŋ-nyena de.

english_verse: Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, nabiinu, ta‑n vuvuna wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. Pa se nɔɔna bam na nmo wo na pɛ ye n tiini n vuvuni tei to.

english_verse: When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise! A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ba nam ná bwei‑m se ba lɔre kolo ŋwaane n na vuvuni to, se n ta de-ba we, ‘Kwora kalo na beene se ka pa nɔɔna dedɛ nagwola te to ŋwaane mo amo vuvuna. Ba nadwoona wó taa mage daane mo de foone, ye ba vɔna de pare.’ Wonnu tento nam lage te seene te ke mo. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem: I have sharpened my sword to slaughter you; it is shiny and will flash like lightning! Don't celebrate— punishment is coming, because everyone has ignored my warnings.
translation_verse: Ko ni tiini ko dwori ko ti se ko gwoni ko de tega ne. Ko nam ta liligi jei maama ne mo ne doa na pepele tei to! Dé wó taa chaka Judah paare dem ŋwaane na? Se-zɔɔ kom yiga nam tera paare maama wone!

english_verse: Ezekiel, warn my people, then celebrate my victory by clapping your hands. My vicious sword will attack again and again, killing my people with every stroke.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, nabiinu, pworisi taane se n daare n mage n jea. Pa se-zɔɔ kom zage kuni belei naa betɔ. Kokuri to, ko ye se-zɔɔ kolo na goe to mo. Ko nam wó kaare nɔɔna bam ko pu se ko yɔɔre ko go-ba.

english_verse: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
translation_verse: Amo de maa wó mage a jea daane ye a bane de laam zuri. Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, bei bibeiri selei se se bere chwei selo Babilon teo pɛ se-zɔɔ kom na wó tɔge da ko ba to. Chwei sem nam wó nwoŋi teo kodoo ne mo se ba. Laam chwi daa mɛ seeni chwei sem na wó pwɛ to, se ka bere chwoŋa maama yiga na yɔɔre teo kolo seeni to.

english_verse: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
translation_verse: Ta pa se se-zɔɔ kom tɔge chwoŋa dedoa ko vo Amon tiina te-fɔrɔ Raba seeni, se chwoŋa kadwoŋi kam de vo Jerusalem teo na wo Judah laŋa kam ne to seeni.

english_verse: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Babilon teo pɛ wom lage o vo o zege chwei sem na pwɛ belei mɛ to, ye o daare o tɔge yi-nɛɛre baŋa se o lɔre chwoŋa kalo o na wó tɔge to. O maa zuzugi taŋa chena, o daare o bwei chwoŋa o teo jwona tei ne, ye o kwei chulu varem chwɛ o nii, se o lɔre o na wó ke tei to.

english_verse: His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people.
translation_verse: O jazem ne mo o wó taa zei chene delo baŋa ne ba na popone Jerusalem teo yere to. O maa wó vo da o tiŋi da-kwollu telo ba na wó kwei ba mage teo kom ni-bworru tem ba bwori, se o laam pa o jar-keira bam ni se ba go ko nɔn-bia bam. Ba maa wó bage tiguri-kaasa, ye ba lɔ taara ba sale teo kom kabira kam teiŋa ne ba ja di ka yuu.

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
translation_verse: Jerusalem tiina bam nam bá sɛ we Babilon teo pɛ yi-nɛɛre dem wó ji chega, ba na maŋe ba du duuri ba pa‑o to ŋwaane. Pɛ wom nam wó guli-ba ba tusim dem na ye tei to, ye o daare o ja-ba.

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying: Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ tage tento mo o we: ‘Abam pɛ se á tusim dem nwoŋi pwooni, ye á wɛleera yam maa yɔɔre ya nae jaja. Á kikia yam maama maa bere we á ba jege chega. Konto ŋwaane mo á dona wó ba ba ja abam de dam.

english_verse: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye nmo Isarele tiina yiga tu wom, n lwarem kikia de n puseŋa gaale. Maŋa kam yi ka ti se n yɔɔre n na waarem.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Dɔne n yuu gare-yi dem, de n paare yipuga kam n yuu ne. Ko daa bá taa ye ne ko ya na ye tei faŋa to. Nabwona jege se ba zaŋe de zula, se balo ya na jege paare ba di to ga ba paare.

english_verse: I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city. Judgment against Ammon
translation_verse: Chɔgem beena! Chɔgem beena! Teo kom paare dem wó ti! Konto nam bá ke, ye ko dae we wolo a na kuri se o waare teo kom to tua. A laam maa wó kwei-ko a ke o jeŋa ne.’

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying: A sword is drawn, ready to slaughter; it is polished and prepared to kill as fast as lightning.
translation_verse: Nabiinu, ko nam ná ye nmo, pworisi taane we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei Amon tiina bam de ba toro tem seeni to mo tento: Nii-na se-zɔɔ! Ba laam zei-ko mo se ba ma ba go nɔɔna. Ba kwɛ-ko pa ko liligi mo ne doa na pepele tei to, se ko yɔɔre ko taa chɔge nɔɔna.

english_verse: Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth.
translation_verse: Laam nam kwei se-zɔɔ kom n jwoori n ke ko pwolo wone. Jwoori n vo jei selo ba na naane‑m to. Kokuri to, amo wó di n taane teo kolo na ye n kugu jei to ne.

english_verse: My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing.
translation_verse: A yɔɔre a lage a lwo a ban-lom dem mo n baŋa ne, se n lɔre we a wo tiini ko fuli dede‑m. A ta wó kwei‑m a ke nankɔ-nyena balo na me de nɔn-gora kikia to jeŋa ne.

english_verse: You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nmo wó ji ne da-kora kalo ba na kwei ba de mini wone to. N tete teo kom wone mo n jana wó lwo tega ne. N yere dem laam maa wó saare logo baŋa ne. Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.’ ”

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins
translation_verse: “Ko ta ná ye nmo, nabiinu, n nam bá bore taane n vane teo konto nɔn-bia bam, de ba na swoi nɔn-gora kikia tei to na? Tole ba wo-zɔɔna kikia yam taane se ba taa yei ya ni ne.

english_verse: None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows.
translation_verse: Nmo nɔn-bia bam yɔɔre ba gwooni ba kwoa de ba niina mo. Ba ta maa jege veira, de botara, dedaane kadeina ba bɛɛsa.

english_verse: You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day.
translation_verse: Ba bere ba ba nege wonnu telo na ye wose te pa amo to, ye ba daare ba jege amo siu da yam ba yaala.

english_verse: Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things.
translation_verse: Nmo wone nɔɔna kare ba ba bebara se ba wane ba dwonna ba go mo. Nɔɔna badwonna de maa diini peero tem yuu ba di jwona wodiiru, ye badaara de swoi kabwoŋa kikia.

english_verse: Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period
translation_verse: Nmo wone baara badwonna de maa tigi de ba kwoa kaana, ye babam de fe mo se ba peini de kaana balo na jege ba chana zarem ba ke to.

english_verse: Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
translation_verse: Nmo wone de, nɔɔna jwoŋi dim mo se ba wane ba go ba dwonna. Badwonna de maa jene wonnu ba pae ye ba dɔne nyɔɔre dedɛ jene dem baŋa ne. Ba laam maa tɔge kampina baŋa ne ba duni. Nmo nɔn-bia bam maa swei amo swia. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind.
translation_verse: Amo nam ná tu a toŋe de abam ne ko na maŋe tei to, á ta wó ta‑á jege baare na? Á ta wó ta‑á dana maŋa kam konto ne na? Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto. A nam wó seene a ke kolo a na tage to.

english_verse: I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways.
translation_verse: A lage a jage abam mo pa á vo yiga yiga se á ta‑á zoore logo baŋa teene dem jei maama wone. Konto to, a laam wó le á digiru tem maama a yage.

english_verse: You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. Jerusalem Must Be Purified
translation_verse: Abam ná pɛ se dwi-gɛ tiina bam jege abam ba yaala, á laam wó ba á lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, amo nii a nae Isarele dwi tiina bam we ba ye weeru mo. Ko nye de luru na kwɛ lu-nyenno mini wone se o le channa, de luuru tedwonna o daare lu-nyenno chekke to mo. Banto nam nye de weeru tem konto mo amo yiga ne.

english_verse: I will be like a metalworker who collects that metal from the furnace and melts it down. I will collect the Israelites and blow on them with my fiery anger. They will melt inside the city of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Chega ŋwaane to, a lage a la abam a ke daane teo kom wone mo, se a laam fuli a ban-lom dem a yage á yera ne.

english_verse: like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger. Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
translation_verse: Ne lu-nyenno na nyeene tei min-vogo wone to, konto mo abam de lage á yaare teo kom wone. Abam laam maa wó lɔre we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo lwogi a ban-lom dem a yage á baŋa ne.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious!
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, ta de Isarele tiina tega kam we, ‘Nmo ye tega kalo doa na ba nena n baŋa ne se ka kwɛ to mo, a bane na zaŋe n baŋa ne to ŋwaane.’

english_verse: Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.
translation_verse: Teo kom yiga tiina bam ke ni daane mo ne nywonnu na laare tei se te ja nɔna te kaare to. Ba maa kare ba goe nɔɔna, ye ba daare ba vere ba jejegero de ba lonne wonnu tem, pa se ba daare kadeina dedɛ ba yage teo kom wone.

english_verse: The priests of Israel ignore my Law! Not only do they refuse to respect any of my sacred things, but they don't even teach the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary or between what is clean and what is unclean. They treat my Sabbath like any other day, and so my own people no longer honor me.
translation_verse: Teo kom kaanem tiina bam yiga tere amo nia yam wone. Ba maa yaale wonnu telo na ye wose te pae amo to. Ba nam ba pɔɔre wonnu telo na ye wose amo ŋwaane to, de telo na wora dɛ dɛ totoŋa yam ŋwaane to daane. Ba maa bere we wonnu telo na maŋe de Wɛ chullu tem to, de telo na jege digiru chullu tem seeni to maama ye bedwe mo. Ko ta ná ye amo siu da yam, ba yiga tere ya wone. Ba na ke tei konto to maa pae se nɔɔna jege amo yere dem ba yaala.

english_verse: Israel's officials are like ferocious wolves, ripping their victims apart. They make a dishonest living by injuring and killing people.
translation_verse: Teo kom nakwa bam nye de wiira mo na nɛ vara se ba zi ba kaare to. Ba maa ke nɔɔna zonne ye ba jege-ba ba goe se ba tete ma ba duni.

english_verse: And then the prophets in Israel cover up these sins by giving false visions. I have never spoken to them, but they lie and say they have a message from me.
translation_verse: Teo kom sampwori sem de ye ja chɔge. Ba yɔɔre ba peeri nɔɔna bam kikia mo, de ba veera yam na gane nɔɔna, ye ba yi-nɛɛre taana ye vwa tei to. Ba maa tɛ ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ tage o we tento mo,’ ye Baŋa Wɛ nam bere o wo puri o ni de-ba de.

english_verse: I looked for someone to defend the city and to protect it from my anger, as well as to stop me from destroying it. But I found no one.
translation_verse: A nam beeri se a na nɔɔno mo ba wone, se kotu fɔge o lɔ teo kom kabira kam o zege. Kotu ya wó zege o che se lulua kalo na tigi amo de teo kom laŋa ne to kwoni, se a daa yé chɔge teo kom. A ma beeri a ga.

english_verse: So in my fierce anger, I will punish the Israelites for what they have done, and they will know that I am furious. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo a nam lage a yɔɔre a lwo a ban-lom dem ba baŋa ne, se a zwɛ-ba kula, a wo na tiini ko fuli de-ba to ŋwaane. A maa wó jwoori a ŋwe ba keim-lwanno tem maama jene. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, listen to this story about two sisters.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, kaana balei déem mo wora, ba na ye nu dedoa.

english_verse: The older one was named Oholah, which stands for Samaria; the younger one was Oholibah, which stands for Jerusalem. They became my wives and gave birth to my children.
translation_verse: Zembaaro wom yere mo ye Ohola. O nyaane wom yere maa ye Oholiba. Ba ma ji amo kaana, ye ba lo bakeiri de bukwa ba pa-ne. Ohola mo ye Samaria teo. Oholiba maa ye Jerusalem teo kom.

english_verse: So I gave Oholah to the Assyrian lovers she wanted so badly.
translation_verse: Amo nam yɔɔre a yage‑o mo a pa o bɔɔla Asiria tiina bam. Kokuri to, o fera maŋe ya wo ba wone.

english_verse: Oholibah saw all this, but she was more sinful and wanted sex more than her sister Oholah ever did.
translation_verse: O nyaane Oholiba déem nɛ tento maama, ye wonto nam ta ke o chɔge se ko dwoni o zembaaro wom kabworim totoŋa, o na ware o fera yam o ja to ŋwaane.

english_verse: But Oholibah behaved worse than her sister. Oholibah saw images of Babylonian men carved into walls and painted red.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Oholiba, wonto ke kabworim se ko dwoni o zembaaro wom kikia yam. O déem nɛ ba na gɔgere Babilon tiina nyenyero telo ba yage kabira yera ne pa te lana nason-sonno tei to.

english_verse: They had belts around their waists and large turbans on their heads, and they reminded her of Babylonian cavalry officers.
translation_verse: Ba maa jege vovwe selo na bage ba teiŋa ne to, dedaane yuu gare-yia yalo na vɔge ba yuni ne to. Nyenyero tem maama maa yɔɔre te nye de Babilon teo dedɛɛra balo na nwoŋi Chaladea to.

english_verse: As soon as she looked at them, she wanted to have sex with them. And so, she sent messengers to bring them to her.
translation_verse: O na bobo o na ba nyenyero tem konto to, mo o fera zo ba wone, pa o toŋe nɔɔna ba teo kom ne se ba bwoŋi-ba ba pa‑o.

english_verse: Men from Babylonia came and had sex with her so many times that she got disgusted with them.
translation_verse: Babilon tiina bam de ma ba o tei ba peini ded‑o. Ba ma tiini ba chɔge‑o de ba sare-peiga kikia, pa se o yera ba ya chɛ ye o ma o kwaga o ya-ba.

english_verse: She let everyone see her naked body and didn't care if they knew she was a prostitute. That's why I turned my back on her, just as I had done with her older sister.
translation_verse: O yɔɔre o ja o kabworim kikia yam o nwoŋi pwooni mo pa nɔɔna maama na o kuri. A laam ma ma a kwaga a ya‑o, ne a déem na yage o zembaaro tei to.

english_verse: She eagerly wanted to go to bed with Egyptian men, who were famous for their sexual powers.
translation_verse: O ta yɔɔre o swoi se o taa tigi de o bɔɔla bam mo, ba na dana de sare-peiga ne bonɛ de sisein-nɔɔna na ye tei to ŋwaane.

english_verse: And she longed for the days when she was a young prostitute, when men enjoyed caressing her body. The Lord Will Punish Oholibah
translation_verse: Oholiba, nmo na guli n na ke wo-zɔɔna yalo n nɔn-donne maŋa ne ye Ejipti baara bam peeri n pwoa ye ba teiŋi n yela to, n ta lage se n ta‑n ye konto mo.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Oholibah, though you no longer want to be around your lovers, they will surround you like enemies, when I turn them against you.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane Oholiba, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Ko ná ye n bɔɔla balo n na mɛ n kwaga n ya-ba to, a lage a pa ba zaŋe jei maama ne ba ke chichuŋu de nmo mo.

english_verse: I will gather all the handsome young officials and the high-ranking cavalry officers from Babylonia and Assyria, as well as from the Chaldean tribes of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa.
translation_verse: A nam wó la nɔn-donno telo na jege lam ye ba nwoŋi Babilon, de Chaladea, de Pekoda, de Soa, de Koa to, ko ta woli de Asiria tiina bam maama a ke daane. Ba ye ba teo dedɛɛra, de ba yiga tiina, de jar-keira, de babɛ, ye ba maama dɔge sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne mo.

english_verse: I am angry with you, so I will let them be very cruel. They will cut off your nose and ears; they will kill your children and burn alive anyone in your family who survives.
translation_verse: A lage a da a ban-lom dem baŋa ne mo a pa se ba seene ba yia ba waare‑m. Ba maa wó dɔɔre n momwɛ de n zwa ba yage. Balo ta na wó daare n wone to wó te jara wone. Ko ta ná ye n bia bam de, ba lage ba ja-ba mo, ye ba daare ba zwɛ n nɔn-bia balo na daare to mini wone.

english_verse: Your clothes and jewelry will be torn off.
translation_verse: Ba ta wó lɔɔre n gwaaro tem maama, de n wo-nyenno zela yam.

english_verse: I will stop your wickedness and the prostitution you started back in Egypt. You will never want to think about those days again.
translation_verse: Amo nam wó pa se wo-zɔɔna de kabworim kikia yalo nmo déem na bobo n ke Ejipti ne to ti. Nmo daa bá‑n ta‑n jege kikia yanto dwoŋi fera, naa n guli Ejipti teo gula kɔtaa!

english_verse: I, the Lord God, am ready to hand you over to those hateful enemies that you find so disgusting.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Oholiba, a lage a kwei‑m a ke balo n na chuli to jeŋa ne mo. Ko ye banto mo n déem mɛ n kwaga n ya-ba.

english_verse: have led to this. You were the one determined to have sex with men from other nations and to worship their idols.
translation_verse: pɛ se daanem dento ba n baŋa, n na kare n lage dwi-gɛ tiina bam ye n biini n tete ba jwona yam kaanem baŋa ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: You have turned out no better than your older sister, and now you must drink from the cup filled with my anger.
translation_verse: Nmo yɔɔre n kwei n zembaaro totoŋ-naga kam mo. Konto ŋwaane, amo de wó kwei na-zoŋa kalo a na pɛ‑o pa o nyɔ ka wo cham to mo a pa‑m se n de nyɔ.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, gave your sister a large, deep cup filled with my anger. And when you drink from that cup, you will be mocked and insulted.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Nmo de lage n nyɔ n zembaaro wom na-zoŋa kam wone mo. Ka wo nam tiini ko luuna. Nɔɔna wó taa jege‑m ba mɔna ye ba ta yaale‑m, na-zoŋa kam konto na jege n yera wonnu dedɛ ka wone to ŋwaane.

english_verse: But you must drink every drop! Then smash the cup and chew on its broken pieces. Use them to cut your breasts in sorrow. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nmo nam wó nyɔ ka wo wonnu tem mo n ti maama nyɔ! Nmo laam ma‑n wó feiri-ka tega ne n lɔ muga-muga, ye n daare n bɛ bɛ n yela wo-chechɔgɔ ŋwaane. Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.

english_verse: You have completely rejected me, and so I promise that you will be punished for the disgusting things you did as a prostitute. The Two Sisters Are Condemned
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Nmo na swei amo swia ye n ta-ne n yage kwaga kwaga to, nmo nam jege se n na waarem mo se ko maŋe de n wo-zɔɔna de n tolo kikia yam.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, it's time for you to tell Oholah and Oholibah that they are guilty. Remind them of their evil ways!
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta de amo o we: “Nabiinu, nmo nam bá bore taane n vane Ohola de Oholiba na? Tole ba totoŋ-vɛɛsa yam taane se ba taa yei ya ni ne.

english_verse: They came into my temple that same day, and that made it unfit as a place to worship me. They have even stopped respecting the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Dɛ delo wone ba na kwei ba bia bam ba ke kaanem ba pa ba jwona yam to, mo ba zo amo wara-jei sem wone pa se ba chɔge se chullu tem. Ba seene ba ke konto dwoŋi mo amo tete diga kam wone.

english_verse: They sent messengers to attract men from far away. When those men arrived, the two sisters bathed themselves and put on eye shadow and jewelry.
translation_verse: Ba maa yeini ba toŋe se ba vo yiga yiga ba bwoŋi nɔɔna se ba ba. Nɔɔna bam konto maa ná nwoŋi sa-teene wone ba yi, nmo Oholiba wó swɛ n yera mo, n daare n kwɛ n yibia ye n fɔge n yera de wo-nyenno dwi dwi.

english_verse: They sat on a fancy couch, and in front of them was a table for the olive oil and incense that had belonged to me.
translation_verse: Nmo laam ma‑n wó vo n jeini jaŋgɔŋɔ kolo na jege nenɔŋa to baŋa ne, ye n pa ba kwei yituŋu ba zege n yiga ne. N ma‑n wó kwei talwoŋ-ywoŋa, de nuga kalo ya na ye amo zula ŋwaane to n tiŋi ko baŋa ne.

english_verse: and I noticed that the men were eager to have sex with these women, though they were exhausted from being prostitutes.
translation_verse: A laam ma ta kaane wolo yera na chɛ de kabwoŋa kikia to yera taane a we, ‘Ba ta wó taa tigi ded‑o mo ne ba na ke tei de ka-tole to.’

english_verse: In fact, the men had sex over and over with Oholah and Oholibah, the two sinful sisters.
translation_verse: Ba ma seene ba ke sare-peiga ded‑o, ne nɔɔna na tigi de ka-bworru tei to. Ba ke totoŋ-vɛɛsa konto dwoŋi mo de Ohola dedaane Oholiba, ba na ye ka-tole to ŋwaane.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters: I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Pa se jar-keira kɔgɔ ba ba ke chichuŋu de-ba, pa se lɛɛro de foone yi-ba.

english_verse: They will stone you to death and cut you to pieces; they will kill your children and burn down your houses.
translation_verse: Kɔ-fɔrɔ kom konto wó dole-ba de kandwa mo, ye ba daare ba kwei ba se-zɔɔro ba gwoni-ba ba de tega ne. Ba ta wó go ba bu-baara de ba bukwa, ye ba daare ba zwɛ ba sam dem.

english_verse: I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have.
translation_verse: Amo wó tɔge konto baŋa ne mo a pa se wo-zɔɔna kikia yanto dwoŋi ti tega kam jei maama ne. Kaana bam maama wó na ko na ke banto tei to pa se ba daa bá lwoni ba kikia yam.

english_verse: Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Bena nogo bene dem chane fuga chana kam da fuga dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora tu ka yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, popone dɛ dento n tiŋi tɔnɔ wone, kokuri, ko ye dɛ dem konto ne nɔɔ mo Babilon teo pɛ tu o kaare Jerusalem teo kom o pu.

english_verse: Then tell my rebellious people: “Pour water in a cooking pot and set it over a fire. *
translation_verse: Véi zwabani-nyena banto tei n maŋe memaŋe de-ba we: ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Kwei kambia n teini mini ne, se n daare n lwo na ka wone.

english_verse: These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Lɛɛro wo teo konto na su de nɔn-gora to yuu ne! Ko yɔɔre ko nye de kambi-dwoŋa mo na tiini ka digiri ye ka ba zare ka gɔe to. Nam ta le ka wo nɔna yam dedoa dedoa ye á wo kuri ya wone á daare.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground.
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔn-bia bam kare ba go nɔɔna pa se ba jana bam taare tega kam maama mo. Ba ma lwo jana bam pelwaaro baŋa ne jaja, ye ko dae tega ne mɛ fwogo na wó kwoli-ba to.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood,
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Lɛɛro wo teo konto na su de nɔn-gora to yuu ne! Amo tete mo wó tigisi da-dwa a dogele da-baŋa ne.

english_verse: so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, dogele dɛ sem se se di baŋa, se n daare n dwei mini se kuri ne. Saŋe nɔna yam se ya be lanyerane, se n woli diira ya wone. Nam ta pa se kwi sem fuli.

english_verse: Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it.
translation_verse: Abam nam biini á tete de á wo-zɔɔna kikia yam mo. Amo yɔɔre a kwɛ abam a ga mo. Á wo sɛ se a le á digiru tem. Abam nam daa bá wane á kwɛ á digiru tem, ko ná dae we amo lwogi a ban-lom dem á baŋa ne mo a ti pa se a wo laam zuri.

english_verse: That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Ezekiel's Wife Dies
translation_verse: Amo Baŋa Wɛ wom mo tage konto maama. Maŋa kam yi se a ke tei a na tage to. A bá yiri a ni dem konto. A bá leiri a boboŋa, ye a ta bá duri á yibwona. Amo nam lage a waare abam mo se ko maŋe de á totoŋa yam na ye tei to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ” Ezekeli kaane wom na tege tei to

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, amo lage a pɔpɔ a ke keim mo na wó zwɛ‑m lanyerane. A wó jwoŋi wolo na tiini o tigi n bochare ne to a daare‑m. De ko de, yé keeri o ŋwaane. Yé kane yi-na naa n pa n yiga nyɔne.

english_verse: Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
translation_verse: N jege chwoŋa se n suuri fenfee n wone. Nam yé pa n kwora zaŋe. Yé keeri o lua kam. Kwei n yuu vovoa n ba n yuu ne, se n daare n zo n natera yam. Yé kwoli n yibia ne balo na keeri ba twa na ke tei to, naa se n di wodiu kolo lua tiina na jege ba di to.”

english_verse: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto tetete mo a ŋɔɔne de nɔɔna bam. Ko na yi dedaan-ni maŋa to, mo a kaane wom tega. Tega na poore to, amo de ma ke ne Wɛ na pɛ-ne ni se a ke tei to.

english_verse: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
translation_verse: Konto maama nam ná kea, abam de wó ke ne amo na ke tei to mo. Abam bá kwoli á yibia ne balo na keeri ba twa na ke tei to, naa á di wodiu kolo lua tiina na jege ba di to.

english_verse: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
translation_verse: Ezekeli nam ye memaŋe mo o pa abam se á lɔre ko na wó taa ye tei to á yera ne. Abam de wó ke tei wonto na ke to mo. Konto maama ná yi abam, á wó lɔre we amo mo ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.’

english_verse: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne mo nɔɔno wó duri o lu jara wone o ja kwora o ba o pa‑m se n lɔre kolo na ke to.

english_verse: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne mo chwoŋa wó pore ka pa‑m se n ni puri se n ŋɔɔne ded‑o. Nmo daa bá ta‑n ye chemm. Konto baŋa ne mo nmo lage n ji memaŋe n pa-ba, se ba de wane ba lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pipiri n yibia se ka jeeri Amon tiina bam se n pworisi taane n chɔge-ba.

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, ta‑á yei-na we a lage a ja abam a ke dwia yalo na zoore wɛ-puli seeni to jeŋa ne mo. Ba wó ba ba chwi ba vwoa se ba taa zoore abam tetare ne. Ba maa wó jwoŋi á tio-bia bam ba di, ye ba ta vere á nayela de ba nyɔ ba daare abam.

english_verse: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Amo ta wó pa se Raba pipiri ko ji mɛ kona na vei ya di gaao to, se Amon de taa ye jei selo ba na kɔne pei da to. Abam laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: Mo kokuri nam lɔre-na we amo de lage a twi a jeŋa mo á baŋa ne, se a kwei abam a ke dwia yadwonna jeŋa ne se ba vere á wonnu tem. Amo lage a le abam mo dwi-gɛ tiina bam wone, se a daare a saare abam se á daa yé gwaane logo baŋa teene dem wone. A ná yɔɔre a gwoni abam a de tega ne konto dwoŋi, mo á wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ” Moaba teo taane

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
translation_verse: “Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Moaba teo de Seyira teo déem tage ba we, ‘Judah dwi tiina bam de laam yɔɔre ba nye de dwia yadwonna yam mo.’

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: A laam maa wó waare Moaba tiina bam se ba lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.” Edom teo taane

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: A maa wó tɔge a tete nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa a yiri jene Edom teo kom baŋa ne. A wó pa-ba chwoŋa se ba waare Edom tiina bam ne a ban-lom dem na lage se ba ke tei to. Konto baŋa ne mo ba wó lɔre a ban-zɔŋɔ kom na ye tei to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.” Filisi teo taane

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Amo wó tɔge a ban-lom dem ŋwaane a yiri jene ba baŋa ne. A maa ná yiri jene ba baŋa ne ye a waare-ba a ti, ba de wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Bena fuga-dedoa bene dem chana kam boboa dɛ dem wone, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, Tura tiina bam ya yɔɔre ba chake mo de Jerusalem totoore dem ye ba we, ‘Jerusalem teo laam to ywoo! Ko laam nam jigi di-dwonnu mo ko tiga. Chwoŋa laam pore se dé tɔge da dé ke pipiu de teene dedwonna. Debam mo wó leiri ba yuu ne dé duni.’

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam Tura teo tiina bam, amo dwoni de abam mo. A lage a pa dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ mo ba ba ke chichuŋu de abam, ne naneo na-ŋone sem na zaŋe wɛɛne tei to.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Banto nam lage ba vaare teo kom kabiri de ko dalem jei sem mo ba de tega ne. A ta wó pa ba chwooli ko teero tem maama ba ja jei, se kolo yerane na wó daare da to taa ye peo ko tiga.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ba maa wó yɔɔre ba go Tura tiina balo na zoore naneo ni te-kampare sem ne to. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Kokuri, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a pa Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza mo zege baŋa seeni o ba o jeeri Tura teo kom de jara. Wonto ye pa-faro mo pwa maama wone. O maa jege sisein-nɔɔna de jara torokooro dedɛ. O ta jege balo na dɔge sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne to, de jar-keira kɔ-fɔrɔ na daga to.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: O lage o yɔɔre o chɔge á teene delo maama na wo naneo ni te-kampare sem ne to mo jara-keim baŋa ne. O jar-keira bam maa wó kaare á teo kamunu kom ba pu. Ba wó lɔ taara ye ba dogele teero ba sale á kabira kam teiŋa ne ba ja di ka yuu, ye ba daare ba geene jara-keim nantane ba ma jeeri abam de jara.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: O ta wó pa ba kwei da-kwollu ba ma mage á kabiri sem ba bwori, ye ba daare ba ma ba luuru ba bwori á dalem jei sem ba de tega ne.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: O sisein-nɔɔna bam fwogo wó pe á teo kom, se na daga to ŋwaane. O sisei sem ná guri tega, ye o jara torokooro tem de duri te kɛa, á teo kom kabiri wó taa ziziŋi mo. Ba maa wó tɔge á teo kom manchwo-peena yam ba zo ko wo, ne nɔɔna na mage teo kabira ba yare se ba zo tei to.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Ba sisein-nɔɔna napɔɔna wó taa dɔna á teo kom chwei sem maama ne mo. Ba maa wó taa jege ba se-zɔɔro ba yɔɔre ba goe nɔɔna. Ywoa yalo á na chwi ye ya dana to maa wó to tega ne buru-tu-tu.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: Jar-keira bam wó vere á jejegero tem, de á pipiu zela maama mo. Ba maa wó yigi á kabiri sem ba de tega ne, ye ba daare ba chɔge á sɔ-ŋonno tem. Ko ná ye á sam dem kandwa yam, de dɛ sem, dedaane teero telo na daare to, ba wó dole tento maama ba yage naneo kom wone mo.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: Amo nam lage a pa se á teo kom ji peo kolo ywon-jara na wó yeini ba jare ba ŋwe da to mo. Ba daa bá jwoori ba lɔ teo kom ba zege. Kokuri, amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Naneo ni teene dem pwa laam wó zaŋe ba daare ba paare yitunnu ye ba le ba paare nenɔŋa gwaaro, ba daare ba lɔɔre ba gare-nyenno tem. Foone wó yɔɔre de ja-ba pa ba jeini tega ne, ye ba yera sɔɔre de kolo na yi á teo kom to.

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dem nmo nam na lage n to konto to, naneo ni teene dem maama yera wó sɔɔre mo, de nmo dam dem na ti tei to.’

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: a laam wó pa se nmo de n nɔn-bia bam tu á zo churu, pa se á woli de faŋa faŋa nɔɔna balo na vei da to. Nmo laam wó ta‑n zoore tega kuri ne mɛ faŋa faŋa di-dwonnu na maŋe te tigi to. Ko laam maa wó pa se n maŋe dáane taa wuu, ye n daa bá‑n ta‑n ye teo kolo nɔn-ŋwena na zoore ko wone to.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se lɛɛro ba n baŋa ye n laam guri. Nɔɔna wó beeri n jei ye ba daa bá na‑m. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, mɔ luseim leiŋa n pa Tura teo kom.

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: Tura teo kom lɔge ko zege naneo kom ni ne, ye ko nɔn-bia bam ke pipiu de naneo ni teene dedɛ. Nam ta de teo kom konto we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Tura teo, nmo bere n tete we, “Amo jege lam mo chekke.”

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: N siseina yam yɔɔre ya wo naneo kom tetare ne mo. N lɔra bam ma pa se n lam dem nwoŋi chekke.

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Nmo nye de nabworo kolo da-kwollu na ye Senira tei-dedwaaro mo ba gwoni ba ma ke to. Ba ta ma kwei Sedare tio na nwoŋi Lebanon ne to ba ma ba ke n tetare beiŋa kam.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Basan tei-zwanno mo ba kwei ba ma ba sare n yuŋina bam naywi sem. Ko ta ná ye n wo kom tega kam seeni, ba mɛ Koperese dɛ selo na nwoŋi Kitim ne to mo ba ke-ko, ye ba ma tuu yeila ba gɔgere dɛ sem konto.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Sidon tiina, de Aravadi tiina mo ye n yuŋina bam. Nmo tete Tura nɔɔna balo na jege yi-poro to nam mo nii nabworo yuŋim baŋa ne.

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: Peresia tiina, de Ludi tiina, de Puti tiina de tɔge ba ye nmo jar-keira mo. Ba ma kwei ba jara nantane de ba jara yu-gwonnu ba pale n kabiri sem yera ne, pa se ko ja nenɔŋa ko ba ko pa‑m.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Aravadi tiina, de Heleki tiina mo zege n kabiri sem baŋa ne ba yere jei sem maama. Gamade tiina de maa wo n di-dedwaaro tem ne. Banto de kwei ba jara nantane sem ba pale n kabiri sem maama yera ne. Konto ma pa se n lam dem tiini de nwoŋi.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: Rodan tiina de maa yeini ba ke pipiu dede‑m. Teene delo na wo naneo ni ne to nɔɔna dedɛ mo tu se á ke pipiu daane. Ba ma kwei tuu yeila de kakɔnɔ dɛ ba maa yeigi n zela yam.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Judah de Isarele dwi tiina de pipi de nmo mo. Ba kwei banina kalo na nwoŋi Minifa to, de mɔɔro, de tooro, de nuga, de terale nuga mo ba leiri n wo-yeillo tem.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: Damasika tiina ke pipiu dede‑m, n na jege zela dedɛ de jejegero dwi dwi to ŋwaane. Ba ma ja sana balo na nwoŋi Helebon to, de pei koro telo na nwoŋi Zahara to,

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Seba de Raama tiina bam de ke pipiu de nmo mo. Ba kwei dwoa-bia, de kandwa-nyenno, de sabu-seŋa mo ba ma leiri n zela yam.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: N ta ke pipiu de Haran tiina, de Kanɛ tiina, de Eden tiina, ko ta woli de Seba, de Asuri, de Chilamada pipim-piina bam.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: Tarasisi nabwooru tem mo yeini te zeŋe n zela yam te ja vo jei sedwonna pipiu ŋwaane. Tura teo, nmo déem nye de nabworo kolo zela na duna ye ko wo naneo kom tetare ne ko vei to mo.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: Naneo ni buburi-bɛ maama wó ziziŋi mo, de n nɔɔna bam na tiini ba laare tei to.

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: Ba maa wó laare baŋa baŋa de wo-chechɔgɔ nmo ŋwaane. Ba ta maa wó kwei kasolo ba taare ba yuni ye ba ta bibili tentwarem wone.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: Ba ná laare konto dwoŋi á ŋwaane, ba wó taa leeni luseim lei ba we: “Tura teo jege dwoŋi mo na? Ko ni nam tu de meeri ye naneo kom yɔɔre ko li-ko kula!”

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo maama na zoore naneo ni teene dem ne to yera sɔɔre de kolo na yi nmo to. Ba pwa yera sae mo de foone, ye ba yiga tiini ka nyɔne.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Balo na ke pipiu logo baŋa teene dem wone to pwɛ ba tete de nmo mo. Lɛɛro telo na yi nmo to kɛ jeŋa, pa se n dwi ti taa wuu.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwora ma yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, ta de Tura teo yuu tu wom we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Nmo yeini n bere n tete kamunim mo ye n tɛ n tete ne we, “Amo ye wɛ mo. Tura teo kom ne mo a jei a di paare, ne wɛ dedwoŋi na di paare naneo kom tetare ne tei to.” Nmo nam ye nabiinu mo se n dae wɛ, de nmo na boŋe we n jege wɛ boboŋa to de.

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: Nmo kwei swa mo, de yi-poro, ye n tɔge tento baŋa ne n beeri jejegero n pa n tete. N ma‑n la sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno dedɛ n tiŋi n di sem wone.

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: Nmo tiini n yei pipiu laŋa ye n tɔge ko baŋa ne n tiini n duni. Nmo jejegero tem ŋwaane, n laam ma n bere n tete.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Nmo dona bam konto wó pa se n te dam toone mo, pa se n maŋe tega kuri ne, mɛ na ye naneo kom tetare to.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Nmo nam ná zege balo na lage ba go‑m to yiga ne, n laam wó ta we, n ye wɛ mo na? Ne n ná to n gora bam jeŋa ne, n laam wó lɔre we n ye nabiinu mo, se n dae wɛ.

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Nɔn-yɔɔro mo lage ba go‑m, se n te balo na yeiri Wɛ to toone. Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, yɔɔre n mɔ luseim leiŋa n pa Tura teo pɛ wom ye n ta ded‑o we: ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Nmo déem ye nɔɔno mo chekke. N swa gaale ye n ta ye nenɔm.

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
translation_verse: Wɛ na ke kara kalo Eden jei sem ne to nmo ya n zoora. N ma‑n kwei kandwa-nyenno dwi maama n ma n fɔge n yera. Te maa ye: Rubi, de Topazi, de Emeraleda, de Kirisola, de Onika, de Jasipa, de Safira, de Tukwazi, de Berili. Ba ta ma gɔgere sabu-seŋa wonnu ba tiŋi, se te cheigi dɛ delo ne ba na wó lo nmo to.

english_verse: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
translation_verse: Amo ma le cherubi yuu tu se o taa yere‑m. N déem wo amo Wɛ peo kolo na ye wose to baŋa ne mo. N ma‑n beeri kandwa yalo na di de mini to tetare ne.

english_verse: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
translation_verse: Nmo totoŋa maama déem ba jege tusim ko zege dɛ delo ne ba na naane‑m to. Ko laam ma yi yiga ye n bobo se n ta‑n ke lwarem.

english_verse: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
translation_verse: Nmo na tiini n ke pipiu tei to mo pɛ se n nankɔɔre kikia de n wɛleera laam gaale. Amo de ma zeili‑m pa se n yage Wɛ peo kom de n chaveera. Cherubi tu wolo ya na yere‑m to de laam ma le‑m kandwa yalo na di de mini to tetare ne.

english_verse: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
translation_verse: N déem bere n tete kamunim mo n na ye nenɔm to ŋwaane. N nenɔŋa kam ma li n swa yam. Konto ŋwaane mo a vuvugi‑m a dole a de tega ne, pa se n ji wo-mɔnɔ pwa badwonna yiga ne.

english_verse: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
translation_verse: N tiini n tusi dedɛ, ye n daare n pini nɔɔna pipiu baŋa ne. Ko ma pa se n chɔge wara-jei selo n ya na zuli-ne da to. A ma da ko ŋwaane a pa se mini to n teo kom ne, se de zwɛ ko maama kula! Teo kom laam jigi tentwarem mo, ye balo maama na nɛ nmo to zege ba nia.

english_verse: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
translation_verse: Ko ná ye dwi tiina balo ya na yei n na ye wolo to, ba nia laam yɛ mo de kolo na yi‑m to. Lɛɛro telo na yi nmo to kɛ jeŋa, pa se n dwi ti taa wuu.’ ” Sidon teo taane
