english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pa n yibia jeeri Sidon teo kom seeni se n daare n pworisi taane n chɔge-ko.

english_verse: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se jawe-chɛɛro to ba teo kom ne ko go ba dedɛ. A ta wó pa se jar-keira zaŋe jei maama ne ba kwaare jara de teo kom pa se twa faare ko wo maama. Ba laam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam daa bá taa jege dona balo na nye de sabare de sabare-mangwoli to se ba taa jege-ba ba zɔa ye ba yaale-ba. Ba maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo ná lage Isarele tiina bam a ja a nwoŋi teene delo a ya na yage-ba de wone to, a laam wó pa dwi-gɛ tiina bam lɔre we amo mo ye wo-pwoŋo tu de a na ke a nɔɔna bam tei to. Isarele tiina bam laam maa wó jwoori ba vo ba taa zoore ba tete tega kalo a déem na kwei a pa a tontoŋeno Jakob to wone.

english_verse: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ba maa wó taa zoore da de yazura ye ba lɔ sane ba daare ba jeiri Vini teeni. Kolokolo daa bá daane-ba, amo na wó waare ba dona balo ya na jege-ba ba yaale to ŋwaane. Konto mo ba wó lɔre we amo mo ye ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ”

english_verse: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Bena fuga bene dem chane fuga chana kam da fuga-yalei dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pipiri n jeeri Ejipti teo kom seeni, se n pworisi taane n chɔge ba pa-faro wom, de o teo kom maama.

english_verse: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
translation_verse: Ta o yera taane we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Ejipti teo pɛ, amo dwoni de nmo mo. Nmo nye de naneo wo juru kolo na tigi n teo kom bwi sem ne to mo. Nmo ma‑n bere n tete we, “Amo mo tei Naili buga kam. A nam ke-ka se a pa a tete mo.”

english_verse: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
translation_verse: A nam lage a kwei gwoli mo a ja‑m n peyaa seeni. A ta wó pa se ywona yalo na su n bwi sem to meeli n yera yam. A nam lage a vaŋe‑m mo a ja a nwoŋi n bwi sem ne, ye ywona yam maama ta yɔɔre ya meeli n yera yam.

english_verse: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
translation_verse: A nam lage a dole nmo tete de n bwi sem wo ywona yam mo a yage kagoa yuu ne. Abam laam wó taa tigi pwola ne mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá wane o la abam o ke daane. A lage a pa se á ji wodiu mo á pa tega baŋa vara bam, de wɛyuu zuna bam.

english_verse: Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord. You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick.
translation_verse: Balo maama na zoore Ejipti teo wone to laam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ. Nmo déem nye de kasogo kolo Isarele dwi tiina bam na kwei ba ji ba nacheiga to mo.

english_verse: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
translation_verse: Ba na twe ba je se ba zii nmo ba zaŋe to, n seere mo pa se ba vɔna kaare. Ba maa na sale nmo yera ne to, mo n bwori n daare-ba pa ba nɛ sem te.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a pa se jara mo to n teo kom wone, se nabiina de ba vara bam maama te.

english_verse: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
translation_verse: Ejipti teo kom wó ji di-dwonnu yerane, se ba laam lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom. Kokuri to, nmo tage n we, “Amo mo tei Naili buga kam. Amo mo ke-ka.”

english_verse: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane amo dwoni de nmo, de n bwi sem maama mo. Amo wó pa se Ejipti teo kom chɔge, ye ko ji di-dwonnu yerane, se ko zege Migidola ne ko vo ko yi Sayene se ko kɛ ko yi Kusi siseini dem seeni.

english_verse: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
translation_verse: Nabiina de vara daa bá de ba nɛ tega kam konto ne se ba tɔge da ba kɛ. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno de nam bá taa zoore ka wone se ko yi bena finna.

english_verse: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
translation_verse: Ejipti daa bá taa ye teo kolo Isarele dwi tiina bam na ke ba teena ko wone to. Ba nam wó guli ba na tusi ye ba beeri wolim ko wone to mo. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ”

english_verse: Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Bena finlei-yarepɛ bene dem boboa chana kam boboa dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza déem pɛ o jar-keira bam tiini ba kwaare jara de Tura teo kom. O ma fe-ba jara yam ŋwaane pa ba yuni fe, ye ba vɔna de dɔre ŋɔna. Nebukadeneza de o jar-keira bam nam wo wane Tura teo kom se ba di nyɔɔre ko baŋa ne, de ba na toŋe tei maama de to.

english_verse: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: A nam kwei Ejipti teo kom a pa‑o se ko taa ye o totoŋa yam ŋweero mo, o de o jar-keira bam na ke kolo maama ba pa amo to ŋwaane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ná yia, amo wó pa Isarele dwi tiina bam jwoori ba na dam. Ko daare nmo Ezekeli, a maa wó pa n ni puri se n ŋɔɔne de-ba. Ba maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pworisi se n ta we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Chwoosi-na se á ta we, “Lɛɛro naa!”

english_verse: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
translation_verse: Kokuri to, dɛ dem yi de ti. Baŋa Wɛ dɛ-kamunu kom mo konto. Kunkwon-lilirru wó kwoli tega kam ye lɛɛro yi logo baŋa teene dem maŋa kam konto ne.

english_verse: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
translation_verse: Jara mo lage ya to Ejipti teo wone. Cham de maa wó yi Kusi tiina bam. Ejipti tiina dedɛ wó te jara wone. Ba dona wó zeŋe ba jejegero tem ba ja ba viiri, ba daare ba chɔge teo kom se ko taa zege di-dwonnu yerane.

english_verse: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
translation_verse: Ba jei sem wó yɔɔre se ji kagoa teene delo maama na chɔge to wone. Ba teene dem wó taa ye di-dwonnu yerane mo, ye di-dwonnu de gilimi-de.

english_verse: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom, ne a na wó pa se Ejipti teo kom ja mini, ye a daare a nɔne ko fara maama a meere to.

english_verse: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ná yia, a ta lage a toŋe nɔɔna nabwooru wone se ba ja a kwora ba vo ba pa Kusi teo tiina, de ba na jei de yazura tei to de. Lwia nam wó pɔpɔ ya ja-ba Ejipti teo chɔgem maŋa kam ne, ko na wó seene ko ke to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a tɔge Babilon teo pɛ Nebukadeneza baŋa ne mo se a chɔge Ejipti jar-keira bam dam.

english_verse: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se Naili buga kam we, ye a kwei ba tega kam a pa nɔn-balwaaro. A yɔɔre a lage a tɔge veira baŋa ne mo a chɔge ba tega kam de kolo maama na wo ka wone to. Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.

english_verse: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ ta na tage tei to mo tento: A lage a chɔge ba jwona yam mo, ye a pa se ya nyenyero telo na wo Memfisi ne to jei. Ejipti teo kom daa bá taa jege pwa. A maa wó pa foone zo ko nɔɔna bam maama.

english_verse: The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed!
translation_verse: Amo wó pa se Paforosi taa ye yɔɔ yerane, ye a pa se mini zwɛ Zoan teo kom. A nam ta wó waare Tebesi de.

english_verse: The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
translation_verse: A yɔɔre a lage a lwo a ban-lom dem Pelusi baŋa ne mo, ko na ye Ejipti dam jei sem to ŋwaane. A ta wó go Tebesi jar-keira bam maama.

english_verse: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
translation_verse: A lage a pa mini mo ja Ejipti teo kom, ye Pelusi tiina bam wó taa wowole de cham. Tebesi teo kabiri sem lage se chɔge mo. Foone maa wó tiini de ja Memfisi tiina dɛ maama wone.

english_verse: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
translation_verse: Ona, de Pi-besefa nɔn-donno maama wó te jara wone. Ba maa wó ja teene dem konto nɔɔna bam ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga.

english_verse: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
translation_verse: Wea maŋa ne Tapanahesi teo kom wó ji lim yerane, ne a ná jaane Ejipti teo dam dem a ja a chɔge a yage. Ba ya maa na teere kolo baŋa ne to maama wó ti. Kunkwon-lilirru mo wó kwoli ba tega kam. Ko ta ná ye Ejipti teene dem maama, ba lage ba ja de nɔn-bia bam ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga mo.

english_verse: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
translation_verse: Amo laam maa ná waare Ejipti teo kom a ti, ba wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.’ ”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Bena fuga-dedoa bene dem boboa chana kam da yarepɛ dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, amo jaane Ejipti pa-faro wom jeŋa mo a bwori. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno nam wo vɔge gare-zɔŋɔ se o kwei-ka o de ko wone. Ko laam ma pa se o jeŋa kam wo twoŋi se ka taa dana se ka wane se-zɔɔ ka zeeri.

english_verse: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Amo dwoni de Ejipti teo pa-faro wom mo. A yɔɔre a lage a bwori o je sem maama mo, ne ko ná ye o je-laao kom de je-bubwora kam maama. Konto to, o se-zɔɔ kom wó lwei ko to tega ne.

english_verse: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Chega to, a wó pa Babilon teo pɛ je sem na dam. Se ko ná ye Ejipti pa-faro wom, o vɔna lage ya to tega ne mo vareba. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, ne a ná kwei a se-zɔɔ kom a ke Babilon pɛ wom jeŋa ne, se o de kwei-ko o ma o fugi Ejipti tiina bam.

english_verse: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_verse: A nam wó seene a jage Ejipti tiina bam pa ba vo yiga yiga se a yage-ba logo baŋa teene dem maama wone. Konto baŋa ne ba wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
translation_verse: Bena fuga-dedoa bene dem chane setɔ chana kam boboa dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, ta n bere Ejipti pa-faro wom de o nɔn-kɔgɔ kom we: ‘Wɔ kamunni mo ma de nmo?

english_verse: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
translation_verse: Ko ye amo mo pɛ ko lana konto pa ko jege nɛ selo na tiini se daga to, ye Eden wo teeni dem maama déem tiini de jege kazwe de di de tio kom konto.

english_verse: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Tio kom tiini ko ke dedɔrɔ ko kɛ ko di wɛyuu kom, pa se ko bere ko tete.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri, a kwei-ko a ke pɛ wolo na jege dam logo baŋa teene dem baŋa ne to jeŋa ne. Wonto laam ma yɔɔre o waare-ko se ko maŋe de ko keim-lwanno na mae tei to. Amo mo dole-ko a yage dáa ne.

english_verse: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
translation_verse: Konto ma pa se dwi-gɛ tiina balo na tiini ba ye nankɔ-nyena to ba ba gwoni-ko ba de tega ne, ba daare ba yage-ko pa ko tiga ko na to mɛ seeni to. Ko nɛ sem to mo se tigi peero yuni ne, de bwollu maama tega ne. Ko da-dwa de ma bwori ye se tigi tega kam gugworru maama wone. Teene delo nɔɔna ya na tigi ko woro kuri ne to ma duri ba daare-ko.

english_verse: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
translation_verse: Zuna bam laam ma ba ba jeini tio kom da-buŋa kalo na daare ka tigi to baŋa ne. Ga-vara bam de ma ba ba nɔne ko nɛ selo na to tega ne to baŋa ne.

english_verse: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Dɛ delo ne tio kom konto na to ko te ye ko tu ko zo churu to, amo ma pa buli-yia yam ni se ya keeri tio kom lua. A ma che bwi sem pa se na-fwaaro tem daa ba dura. A ma pa Lebanon tega kam maama ye lim, tio kom na to to ŋwaane. Teeni dem maama de ma kwaare de zega.

english_verse: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
translation_verse: Tio kom na to buru-tu-tu ye dwi-gɛ tiina bam ni to, a ma pa se ba yera sae, ko na tɔge de balo na vei tega kuri ne ko vo ko zo churu to ŋwaane. Eden kara kam wo teeni dem maama, de Lebanon tei-laaro tem, ko woli de teeni delo maama na na yi-de chekke to maama wo laam ma zuri.

english_verse: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
translation_verse: Logo baŋa dwi tiina balo maama ya na yeini ba jei tei-zɔŋɔ kom woro ne ye ba ye ko fara to de ma tɔge de-ko ba zo churu, ba woli de balo na maŋe ba te jara wone to.

english_verse: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Eden kara wo teeni dem maama wone, tio kɔ kamunni de ko nenɔŋa mo ma de nmo? De ko de, ba lage ba gwoni nmo ba de tega ne, se nmo de woli Eden kara wo teeni dem mo n zo tega kuri. Dáane mo n lage n ta‑n tigi de balo na yeiri Wɛ to, dedaane balo maama na tega jara wone to. Memaŋe dento bere ko na wó ke Ejipti teo pa-faro wom de o nɔn-kɔgɔ kom tei to mo. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ”

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
translation_verse: Bena fuga-yalei bene dem chane fuga-selei chana kam boboa dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora tu ka yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying: You act like a lion roaming the earth; but you are nothing more than a crocodile in a river, churning up muddy water with your feet.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, mɔ luseim leiŋa n pa Ejipti teo pa-faro wom n ta ded‑o we: ‘Nmo ya bere n tete we n ye nywoŋo mo ye n jege dam logo baŋa teene dem maama wone. Ko nam na ye tei to, n yɔɔre n ye naneo wo juru mo. Nmo ma‑n tigi n teo kom bwi sem ne n jege na bam n pɔgele de n nɛ, pa se na bam maama ji bworu yerane.

english_verse: King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Amo wó la nɔn-kɔgɔ dedɛ mo ye a daare a dole a bora se a ma a ja‑m. Nɔɔna bam laam maa wó vaŋe‑m ba ja ba nwoŋi buga kam ne.

english_verse: and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams.
translation_verse: N jana wó duri ba taa tole tega kam jei maama ne mo ba kɛ ba yi peero jei sem, ye ba su gugworru tem de.

english_verse: I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining.
translation_verse: Amo ná yɔɔre a chɔge‑m a ti, a lage a li wɛyuu kom mo se chalechwe sem yé ta se nwoŋi. A ta wó pa se kunkwoŋo mo kwoli wea kam. Chana kam de daa bá nye ka pwooni dem.

english_verse: The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Wɛyuu pwooni dwi maama wó ji lim ko pa‑m, pa se n teo kom jei maama taa ye lim yerane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
translation_verse: A ta wó pa se nɔɔna dedɛ yera sɔɔre nmo ŋwaane. Ba pwa bam wó fom mo ye ba yera taa sae, a na wó kwei a se-zɔɔ kom a liligi ba yiga ne to ŋwaane. Nmo totoore dɛ dem ne mo foone wó ja ba maama, ye lwia taa jege-ba maŋa maama de ba ŋwea na lage ka ti tei to.

english_verse: Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Amo wó seene a pa Ejipti teo kom ji di-dwonnu yerane, se kolokolo daa yé daare tega kam baŋa ne. A ta wó mage balo maama na zoore ko wone to pa ba to tega ne. Maŋa kam konto ne mo ba laam wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.’

english_verse: This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. A Sad Ending for Egypt
translation_verse: Luseim leiŋa kanto mo ba lage ba leeni ba pa‑o. Ko nam ye dwi-gɛ tiina bam bukwa mo lage ba mɔ luseim leiŋa kam konto ba pa Ejipti teo de ko nɔn-bia bam maama. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Bena fuga-yalei bene dem chane fuga-selei chana kam da fuga-yanu dɛ dem ne, mo Baŋa Wɛ kwora yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, yɔɔre n ta‑n keeri Ejipti teo nɔn-bia bam ŋwaane. Banto jege se ba tɔge de te-kamunnu dedwonna nɔɔna mo se ba maama te ba daare ba tu tega kuri jei sem ne.

english_verse: Say to them: You may be more beautiful than the people of other nations, but you will also die and join the godless in the world below.
translation_verse: Ta de-ba we, ‘Abam boŋe we á jege lam á dwoi dwia yadwonna mo na? Á nam jege se á tu tega kuri ne á ta‑á tigi de balo na yeiri Wɛ to mo.’

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Ba déem na ŋwe tega baŋa ne to, ba tiini ba fugi nɔɔna dedɛ. Ba maama ma te jara wone, ye ba yibeela yam wo tega kuri gwoŋo kom gugworru wone.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
translation_verse: Ba ma kwɛ jeiga ba pa Elam teo churu ne se ko taa tigi o jar-keira bam maama tetare ne. Banto maama yeiri Wɛ ye ba laam ba ba te jara wone. Ba ma tɔge de balo maama na zoore churu wone to ba na ba chaveera, ba ya ta na ŋwe ye ba fugi nɔɔna dedɛ to ŋwaane. Ba laam maa tigi balo na tege jara wone to tetare ne.

english_verse: They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
translation_verse: Ba nam wo suli-ba de zula ne ba na ke tei de faŋa faŋa bembɛ selo na tege jara wone to mo. Banto déem zo churu wone ye ba jege ba se-zɔɔro ba ma ba yeiri ba yuni, ba daare ba jege ba jara nantane ba kwoli ba yera. Bembɛ sem konto ya ta na ŋwe to, ba ya tiini ba fugi nɔɔna dedɛ.

english_verse: You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
translation_verse: Ejipti teo pɛ, ko nam ná ye nmo, nmo de lage n te mo, se n tɔge n taa wo balo na yeiri Wɛ ye ba go-ba jara ne to wone.

english_verse: The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: Edom teo, de ko pwa, de ko dedɛɛra bam de maa tɔge ba wo churu wone. Ba tu ba tɔge de balo na tege jara wone to, de ba na maŋe ba jege dam tei maama to de. Ba laam maa tigi de balo ya na yeiri Wɛ ye ba zo tega kuri gwoŋo kom wone to.

english_verse: The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: Baŋa seeni teene dem dedɛɛra dedaane Sidon teo tiina bam maama maa wora. Ba ma tɔge de balo na tege jara wone to ba na ba chaveera ye ba te, de ba ya na maŋe ba da ba dam-fɔrɔ ŋwaane ba fugi nɔɔna tei to de. Ba laam maa tigi ba yibeela wone ye ba ta yeiri Wɛ. Ba de di ba chaveera ne balo maama na zo tega kuri gwoŋo kom wone to mo.

english_verse: I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Amo ya mo seene a pa‑o dam se o fugi tega baŋa nabiina bam. Wonto de o nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama nam tɔge de balo maama na tege jara wone to mo ba tigi balo na yeiri Wɛ to tetare ne. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_verse: and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming.
translation_verse: kotu ná nɛ we jar-keira mo beene teo kom baŋa pa o wu nabɔnɔ se o ma o kaane teo kom nɔɔna,

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
translation_verse: Ba na kale debam ba vo sa-teo yiga yiga ye bena fuga-yalei kɛ to, bene dem konto chane fuga kam da yanu dɛ dem ne mo nɔɔno wodwoŋi nwoŋi Jerusalem teo kom ne o duri o lu, ye o ba o ta de amo o we, “Jerusalem teo kom yɔɔre ko to mo jara baŋa ne!”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying: Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, ta de nmo dwi tiina bam we: ‘Amo ná pɛ chwoŋa se jara ba teo kodwoŋi baŋa, ye ko nɔɔna bam kuri ba wone dedoa se o taa yere ba teo kom,

english_verse: If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
translation_verse: Kokuri, kotu nigi nabɔnɔ kom kwori mo ye o ke ne o yiga tera pa o te. O ya ná ke o tɔge nabɔnɔ kom kwori na bere tei to, o ya wó jwoŋi o ŋwea. O toone tɔge de o tete mo.

english_verse: But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Ko daare, wolo na zege o yere teo kom to ná nɛ we jar-keira mo maa beene se ba jeeri-ba de jara, ye o ná ve se o wu nabɔnɔ kom o kaane nɔɔna bam pa ba badwonna te jara yam baŋa ne, ko ye ba nɛ waarem ba tusim kikia ŋwaane mo. Amo nam wó bwei nɔɔna bam konto jana bam jene wolo na zege o yere teo kom to tei ne mo.’

english_verse: Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
translation_verse: Nabiinu, a kuri nmo mo se n ji wolo na zege n yere Isarele dwi tiina bam to. Nmo totoŋe mo ye se n cheigi taane delo a na tɛ to, se n laam vo n kaane-ba n pa-ne.

english_verse: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Amo ná tage puseŋ-nyeno yera taane we o jege se o te mo, ye nmo ná ve se n ŋɔɔne jaja n kaane‑o se o yage o keim-balwaaro tem, puseŋ-nyeno wom konto wó seene o te o tusim kikia yam ŋwaane. A nam wó bwei kotu jana bam jene nmo tei ne mo.

english_verse: If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent. The Lord Is Always Fair (Ezekiel
translation_verse: Ko daare, nmo ná kaane puseŋ-nyeno wom se o yage o keim-balwaaro tem ye o ná ve n ni-kaana yam, o wó seene o te o tusim kikia ŋwaane, ye nmo nam wó jwoŋi n tete n yage.

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Nɔn-ŋom ná pipiri o yage o nɔn-ŋonne kikia, ye o bobo se o taa toŋe lwarem, o wó te mo ko ŋwaane.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.”
translation_verse: Ko daare nmo nabiinu, nmo dwi tiina bam yeini ba jeeri daane mo á teo kabiri sem teiŋa ne, de ba sam manchwo-nia ne, ba waase ba bere daane ba we, ‘Pa-na se dé vo Ezekeli tei, se dé ni Baŋa Wɛ kwora kam o na jege se o pa debam to.’

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me.
translation_verse: Nabiinu, ta de Isarele dwi tiina bam we, ‘Abam na kare á tɛ tei to mo tento: Cham delo debam na nɛ dé zwabania kikia dedaane dé wɛleera yam ŋwaane to tiini de daga de dwoi dé jaanem. Dé wora dé bugi dé jia ya ŋwaane. Debam wó ke tetɛ mo se dé jwoŋi dé ŋwea?’

english_verse: Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
translation_verse: Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we, puseŋ-nyeno toone bá pwoli amo wo. A nam swoi se puseŋ-nyena pipiri ba yage ba totoŋ-nɛ sem, se ba daare ba na ŋwea mo. Isarele dwi tiina bam, nam pipiri-na á yage á lwarem kikia yam. Á wó kuri toone se bɛ mo?’

english_verse: Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
translation_verse: Nabiinu, nam ta de n dwi tiina bam we, ‘Nɔn-ŋom ná tusi o chwoŋa, o nɔn-ŋonne kikia bá jwoŋi‑o ya yage. Puseŋ-nyeno nam ná yage o puseŋa kikia yam, o de bá to o puseŋa kikia yalo o ya na ke to ŋwaane. Nɔn-ŋom ná bobo se o taa ke wɛleera, o faŋa nɔn-ŋonne dem bá wane‑o de jwoŋi de yage se o na ŋwea.’

english_verse: Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Amo nam ná tage de nɔn-ŋom we o wó na ŋwea, pa se o laam kwei o teena o daŋe o nɔn-ŋonne dem baŋa ne se de jwoŋi‑o de yage, ye o bobo se o taa ke totoŋ-lwanno, amo daa bá jeeli wo-laaro telo o ya na ke to de dedoa de. O nam wó te mo o lwarem kikia yam ŋwaane.

english_verse: Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right.
translation_verse: A nam ná tage de puseŋ-nyeno a we, ‘N jege se n te mo,’ ye kotu ná pipiri o yage o wɛleera yam, ye o daare o toŋe chega kam, de kikia yalo na maŋe to, o wó jwoŋi o tete.

english_verse: For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live.
translation_verse: Puseŋ-nyeno ná kwei wonnu telo nɔɔna na pɛ‑o ba ma tiŋi daare to, de wonnu telo o na vere nɔɔna tei ne to o jwoori o pa-ba, ye o ná ke o tɔge a bera yam na pae ŋwea to, ye o daa ba ke wo-lwanno, kotu wó na ŋwea ye o daa bá te.

english_verse: And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Puseŋ-nyeno nam ná yage o puseŋa kikia yam, ye o bobo se o taa ke chega kam de kolo na maŋe to, o wó na ŋwea mo o keina yam baŋa ne.

english_verse: But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done. The News of Jerusalem's Fall
translation_verse: De ko de, Isarele dwi tiina bam, abam ta kare á tɛ mo á we, ‘Chega tera Baŋa Wɛ na ke tei to wone.’ Amo nam wó bore abam dedoa dedoa taane se ko maŋe de o kikia na ye tei to mo.” Jerusalem teo totoore dem taane

english_verse: The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak. What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
translation_verse: Dɛ delo tega na wó poore se nɔɔno wom laam ja kwora kam o ba o pa-ne to, dedaan-ni maŋa ne mo Baŋa Wɛ dam yɔɔre de ba amo baŋa. O ma pa se a ni puri pa a wae a ŋɔɔna se ko lwoori nɔɔno wom tutuuri dem.

english_verse: Then the Lord said:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwora laam ma yi amo we:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, nɔɔna balo ta na maŋe Isarele teo kom di-dwonnu wone to yeini ba tɛ ba we, ‘Abaraham déem ye o yerane dedoa mo, ye o wane tega kam maama o jwoŋi. Debam nam ye kɔgɔ mo. Dé jege se dé jwoŋi tega kanto mo se ka taa ye debam nyem.’

english_verse: So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying: How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder
translation_verse: Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam ta swoi se á ta‑á di nɔna yalo yera jana na wo ya wone to mo, ye á daare á kaane jwona, ye á goe nɔɔna. Konto to, ko maŋe se á ta‑á tei tega kam na?

english_verse: and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
translation_verse: Abam teege á se-zɔɔro tem baŋa ne mo, ye á kare á ke wo-zɔɔna dwi maama. Nɔɔno maama maa beeri chwoŋa se kotu chɔge o dwoŋi kaane. Abam boŋe we konto maama kwaga ne ko maŋe se á ta‑á tei tega kam mo na?’

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases.
translation_verse: Nam ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: ne amo na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we balo na daare ba zoore di-dwonnu tem wone to wó te jara wone mo. Ko ta ná ye balo de na wo pwola ne to, a lage a pa kago-vara mo go-ba. Ko nam ná ye balo na vei ba dale dam jei de gugworru wone to, jawe-chɛɛro mo wó go-ba.

english_verse: I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them.
translation_verse: Amo nam wó pa se ba teo kom maama taa tigi di-dwonnu yerane, se ba dam dem ba na teere de baŋa ne to ji kafɛ. Isarele teo peero jei sem wó ji kagoa ka taa tiga, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o tɔge dáane o kɛ.

english_verse: I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord. The People Listen, but Don't Change The Lord said:
translation_verse: Konto baŋa ne ba wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom, ne a ná pɛ se ba teo kom ji di-dwonnu, wo-zɔɔna yalo ba na jege ba ke to ŋwaane.’

english_verse: So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money.
translation_verse: Ba maa yeini ba tui nmo tei de kɔgɔ, ye ba cheigi n taane dem, ne ko na maŋe de a nɔɔna bam na ke tei to. Ba nam ba lage se ba toŋe ba tɔge a taane dem na bere tei to. Swono taane wo ba nia ne. Ba fera nam wo wonnu telo na wó pa ba duni to wone mo.

english_verse: Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_verse: Wonnu telo a na tage to nam wó seene te ke. Maŋa kam konto ne mo ba wó lɔre we Wɛ sampwora ya wo ba tetare ne.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them: I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pworisi taane n chɔge Isarele teo yiga tiina balo na nii a nɔɔna bam baŋa ne to. Nam ta de-ba we: ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Lɛɛro taa wo á baŋa ne! Nayera jege se ba taa nii ba pei sem baŋa ne mo. Ko dae konto na? Abam nam nii á tete baŋa ne mo.

english_verse: You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock!
translation_verse: Á swoi se á ta-á di á pei lara kam, ye á kwei se koro tem á sɔ gwaaro á ma á kwoli á tete. Á ma daare á kuri vare-laaro tem á go á pa á tete, ye á yiga laam tere pei sem wone.

english_verse: You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep.
translation_verse: Á wo nii ko baŋa ne se á ta‑á cho pei selo na bwona to se se na dam. Á ta maa wo yɔɔre vare-jaweena bam, se á daare á vɔ balo na nɛ zonne to ŋɔna yam. Abam chem mo ye á pei sem ywori se maa jia. Selo maa na jei to, á wo beeri-se se á ja á jwoori. Abam nam bɛɛse pei-kɔgɔ kom de je-chɛa mo.

english_verse: They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Ko maa pa se se jage jei maama, se na ba jege nayero se kotu taa nii se baŋa ne to ŋwaane. Se na jage konto to, se laam ma ji kago-vara dwi maama ni-wodiu.

english_verse: So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
translation_verse: Amo pei sem yɔɔre se jage mo se yi tega baŋa ni maama. Se maa kare zwonnu de peero maama yuni ne se kekara, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno wo ke o yiga se wone se kotu beeri se jei.

english_verse: Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep.
translation_verse: Ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a dwoni de abam mo. Kokuri to, a pei-kɔgɔ kom gɛ nayero pa kago-vara jege-se ba tore ba di. A nayera bam nam wo beeri amo pei selo na tusi chwoŋa to jei, ye ba yɔɔre ba nii ba tete mo, pa ba yiga tere amo pei sem wone.

english_verse: So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo dwoni de nayera bam mo. A maa wó bwei-ba de ba na ke a pei sem tei to. Amo wó jwoŋi a pei sem a daare-ba se ba daa yé taa nii-se. Nayera bam daa bá na chwoŋa se ba kɔne pei sem, naa se ba taa kɔne ba tete pei sem baŋa ne. Ba daa bá done pei sem nɔna.

english_verse: The Lord God then said: I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself,
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo tete mo lage a nwoŋi a beeri a pei sem jei se a taa nii se baŋa ne.

english_verse: just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them
translation_verse: Ne nayero na beeri o pei selo na jage pwola ne tei to, konto mo amo de wó taa nii a pei sem baŋa ne. Amo pei sem déem yɔɔre se jage mo dɛ delo ne kunkwon-lilirru na tu te li tega kam maama to. A nam wó beeri se jei ye a jwoŋi-se a yage.

english_verse: and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields.
translation_verse: Amo wó ja-ba a nwoŋi teene dedwonna dem ne se a la-ba a ke daane, ye a pa ba jwoori ba tete tega kam ne. Amo laam maa wó kale-se se se na gaaro se di Isarele peero jei sem ne, de bwollu tem ne, de jei selo maama nɔɔna na zoore da to.

english_verse: to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right. Judgment on the Strong Sheep
translation_verse: Amo ta wó beeri pei selo na jei to mo, se a daare a kale selo na ywori chwoŋa to a ja a jwoori. A maa wó vɔ pei selo na nɛ fufwollu to ŋwana se ya jei, se a daare a taa cho selo na bwona to se se na dam. Ko daare, ko ná ye pei selo na nugi bigila bigila ye se dana to, a lage a go-se mo. Amo wó taa kɔne a pei sem ko chwoŋa kam ne mo.

english_verse: The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel: I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye abam na ye amo pei sem to, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Ta‑á yei-na we amo lage a bore taane pia de ka dwoŋi tetare ne, ye a daare a pɔɔre pi-bale de bo-bale daane mo.

english_verse: Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy.
translation_verse: Abam na nɛ ga-zuru se á ta‑á di to, ko ta wo maŋe ko pa abam na? Bɛŋwaane mo á yɔɔre á titirigi gaao kom ne, ye á jege-ko á nɔne á chɔga? Abam wo ba tigi de na-zura balo á na jege á nyɔ to mo pa se á jege na bam á pɔgele na?

english_verse: but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane amo wó jwoŋi a pei sem a yage, se se daa yé na bɛɛsem. A ta wó bore pia de ka dwoŋi taane.

english_verse: After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you.
translation_verse: A laam maa wó le nɔɔno dedoa se wonto ji a nɔɔna bam maama nayero. A tontoŋeno David mo konto. O maa wó kɔne-ba ye o ta nii ba baŋa ne.

english_verse: He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Amo Baŋa Wɛ tete wó taa ye ba Tu Wɛ wom. A tontoŋeno David maa wó taa ye ba maama dedɛɛro. Amo Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.

english_verse: The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid.
translation_verse: Amo wó gwoni ni de-ba bochare-zuru ŋwaane, ye a daare a zeili kago-vara dwi maama ba tega kam ne. Konto maa wó pa-ba pwola se ba taa zoore gaao ne, naa ba peini goa wone, ye foone bá taa jege-ba.

english_verse: to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Konto mo wó pa ba teeni dem lei bia lanyerane, ye tega kam de ke wodiiru dedɛ ka pa-ba. Nɔɔna bam maama wó taa jei ba teo kom ne ye kolokolo ba daane-ba. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ, ne a ná jaane nabɛ yɔgese delo ba dona na de ba ba ne to a bwori a yage pa ba nwoŋi ba kabɛɛne ne.

english_verse: Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear.
translation_verse: Dwi-gɛ tiina daa bá ba ba vere-ba. Kago-vara de nam daa bá ja-ba ba tore ba di. Ba wó taa jei ba teo ne de yazura mo, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá fugi-ba.

english_verse: I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners.
translation_verse: A maa wó pa-ba te-ywoŋa se ba jeini ka baŋa ne ba va. Konto wó pa se kana daa yé ja-ba, se dwi-gɛ tiina bam taa jege-ba ba yaala.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pipiri n yibia n jeeri Seyira peo kom se n pworisi n chɔge-ko

english_verse: and say to them: I, the Lord God, am now your enemy! And I will turn your nation into an empty wasteland,
translation_verse: n ta we, ‘Seyira peo, amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ dwoni dede‑m mo. A nam wó twe a jeŋa a jeeri‑m se n ji kagoa n ta‑n tiga.

english_verse: leaving your towns in ruins. Your land will be a desert, and then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: A lage a pa se nmo teene dem maama mo ji di-dwonnu de taa zega, se n laŋa kam ji kagoa. Nmo laam ma‑n wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins.
translation_verse: Ko zege faŋa kam ne mo abam jege sebaŋa á ke de Isarele tiina bam. Á ma da ko ŋwaane á dole-ba á yage se ba te jara wone, maŋa kalo ne lɛɛro na tiini te yi-ba ye ba yɔɔre ba na waarem ba ti to.

english_verse: And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, ne amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na jege ŋwea tei to, ko ye chega mo we a lage a pa chwoŋa mo se nɔɔna yɔɔre ba go abam. Abam bá lu de á ŋwea, á na maŋe á swoi nɔn-gora kikia to ŋwaane.

english_verse: and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: A lage a pa á teo kom ji kagoa mo se ko taa vei wuu. Nɔɔna daa bá taa zoore á teene dem wone. Abam laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God,
translation_verse: Abam nam tage á tete ne we, “Debam mo wó jwoŋi Judah teo de Isarele teo, de ba tega kam maama dé taa tei.” Á tage konto dwoŋi ye amo Baŋa Wɛ nam wo ba tei ne.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pworisi taane n pa Isarele teo peero tem se n ta we, ‘Abam Isarele teo peero tem, cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ kwora.

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, am saying: Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam dona bam laam chake abam ŋwaane mo ye ba tɛ ba we, “Faŋa faŋa peero tem laam jigi debam nyem mo.” ’

english_verse: I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes.
translation_verse: Amo yiga wo abam wone, se a woli abam. Nɔɔna wó va tega kam ye ba du wodiiru ka baŋa ne.

english_verse: Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: A ta wó pa se nabiina de vara puli de kɔgɔ dedɛ á tega kam baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba lo bia. Nɔɔna dedɛ wó taa zoore á teene dem wone mo ne faŋa kam na ye tei to, ye á tiini á na yu-ywoŋo se ko dwoni faŋa kam. Abam laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve.
translation_verse: A maa wó pa se a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam jwoori ba taa zoore á tega kam baŋa ne. Á tega kam wó taa ye ba nyem mo ye ba tei-ka. Te-ywoŋa kam konto nam daa bá pa se ba dwi ti.

english_verse: It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Nɔɔna kare ba tɛ abam taane ba we, “Á tega kam jege nabiina mo ka lira, pa se á teo kom ga ko bia.”

english_verse: But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord Will Be Honored
translation_verse: Amo daa bá pa se á ni dwi-gɛ tiina bam na jege abam ba mɔna tei to. Nɔɔna daa bá taa jege abam ba yaala se á ni ko zonne. Á teo kom de nam daa bá jwoori kwaga abam ŋwaane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean.
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, maŋa kalo Isarele tiina bam ya na zoore ba tete tega kam baŋa ne to, mo ba digiri-ka de ba totoŋ-zɔɔna kikia yam. Amo nii a na ba kikia yam pa ya nye de kaane na wora o ke o chana zarem ye ko ye tei to mo.

english_verse: They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people
translation_verse: Amo ma yɔɔre a lwo a ban-lom ba baŋa ne a ma a waare-ba, ba na chɔge tega kam de ba nɔn-gora de ba jwona kaanem kikia yam to ŋwaane.

english_verse: so tell the Israelites that I am saying: You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, ta de Isarele dwi tiina bam we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo na lage a jwoŋi abam a yage to dae abam totoŋa ŋwaane. Ko nam ye amo na laga se a tete yere dem na zula to ŋwaane mo. Kokuri, abam tiini á pa se dwi-gɛ tiina balo á na zoore ba tetare ne to yaale-de mo.

english_verse: I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols.
translation_verse: A laam maa wó lwo na-ŋona á yera ne a ma a kwɛ abam de á wo-zɔɔna de á jwona kaanem kikia yam.

english_verse: I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts,
translation_verse: A ta wó pa á ta‑á jege bochare-doore de boboŋ-doora se á ma á zuli-ne. A maa wó pa se á wo daa yé ke dam, ye a daare a pa á yi taa bwona.

english_verse: because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: A nam lage a kwei a Jworo mo a ke á bochara ne. Konto maa wó pa á fera taa wo a nia yam de a bera yam tɔgem wone.

english_verse: You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Abam daa maa wó ta‑á zoore tega kam a na kwei a pa á nabaara bam to, se á ta‑á ye amo nɔɔna, se amo de taa ye abam Wɛ.

english_verse: I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve.
translation_verse: A nam wó vere abam a ja a nwoŋi á wo-zɔɔna kikia yam ne. A maa wó pa se á tega kam ke wodiiru dedɛ, se kana daa yé ja abam.

english_verse: Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food.
translation_verse: Á teeni dem wó taa ke bia dedɛ de pa abam, ye á kare wodiiru de puli lanyerane, se ko pa dwi-gɛ tiina daa yé taa jege abam ba yaale we, kana jege abam ka goe.

english_verse: People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Isarele dwi tiina bam, nam lɔre-na we ko dae abam totoŋ-laaro ŋwaane mo a lage a ke tento maama a pa abam. Abam yuni nam maŋe se de tiiri tega ne mo de chaveera á kikia yam ŋwaane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: Your land will be plowed again, and nobody will be able to see that it was once barren.
translation_verse: Abam daa wó ta‑á vare á tega kalo ya na tigi kafɛ to baŋa ne, se nɔɔna daa yé taa nii-ka ne ka ga ye kagoa mo.

english_verse: Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people.
translation_verse: Ba maa wó taa tɛ we, “Tega kanto ya na tigi kafɛ to laam nye de Eden te-laao kom déem na ye tei to mo. Nii-na! Teene delo ya na chɔge ye de sam ji di-dwonnu to laam fɔge de lɔ de pe de dam, ye nɔɔna dedɛ zoore de wone!”

english_verse: I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo daa wó pa Isarele dwi tiina bam chwoŋa se ba lwoori wolim amo tei ne. A maa wó leiri ba wɛ-lworo kom ye a pa se ba kɔgɔ kom puli ne vare-kɔgɔ na daga tei to.

english_verse: The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ba nɔn-kɔgɔ kom wó taa daga lanyerane, ne vara dedɛ déem na yeini ba su Jerusalem teo kom kura dim maŋa ne se ba kwei-ba ba ma ke kaanem tei to mo. Konto mo nɔɔna wó yɔɔre ba su teene delo ya na zege di-dwonnu yerane to. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.”

english_verse: Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ dam dem déem tu amo baŋa, pa se o tɔge o Jworo baŋa o kwei-ne o vo o zege bwolo kodwoŋi tetare ne. Kwi dedɛ jage se yɔɔre se faare bwolo kom jei maama.

english_verse: He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?” I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
translation_verse: O ma bwei-ne o we, “Nabiinu, nmo na nɛ kwi sento to, n boŋe we se wó jwoori se na ŋwea na?” Amo de ma leiri‑o a we, “Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ, nmo yerane mo wó wane taane dento n ta.”

english_verse: He then told me to say: Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you,
translation_verse: O laam ma ta de amo o we, “Pworisi n ta taane de kwi sento we, ‘Abam kwi-kore, cheigi-na Baŋa Wɛ kwora kalo o na jege se o ta de abam to!

english_verse: “I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei de kwi sento to mo tento: Amo lage a pa siu mo zo abam wone, se á ta‑á jege ŋwea.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu, pworisi n ta de vio kom we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Vio, zaŋe n nwoŋi logo baŋa sapɛ sena sem maama ne n ba n dole siu n yage nɔɔna banto ba ya na go to wone se ba laam na ŋwea.’ ”

english_verse: As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
translation_verse: Amo de ma pworisi ne o na pɛ-ne ni se a ke tei to. Siu ma seene ko zo twa bam wone. Ba ma pɛ ba zaŋe ba zege ba nɛ baŋa ne ye ba ŋwe. Ba yɔɔre ba ye jar-keira kɔ-fɔrɔ mo.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ daa ta ma ta de amo o we: “Nabiinu, kwi sento bere Isarele dwi tiina bam maama na nye tei to mo. Ba kare ba tɛ we, ‘Debam kwi sem koge se peere mo, ye dé teena maama ti. Debam teo kom daa ba jege jwa.’

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.”
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, beeri daa se n popone ka baŋa ne we, ‘Judah, de Isarele tiina balo na ye o yera nɔɔna to nyem.’ Ta beeri daa kadwoŋi se n popone kanto baŋa ne we, ‘Josɛf bu Efrayim nyem, de Isarele tiina balo na ye wonto de yera nɔɔna to nyem.’

english_verse: Hold these two sticks end to end, so they look like one stick.
translation_verse: Laam ja se nia yam n ba n twoŋi daane se ya taa ye daa dedoa nmo jeŋa ne.

english_verse: And when your people ask you what this means,
translation_verse: Nmo dwi tiina bam ná bwei se ba lɔre n keim dem kuri,

english_verse: tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
translation_verse: se n ta de-ba we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo lage a kwei Josɛf daa kam na wo Efrayim jeŋa ne to mo, se a pa ka twoŋi de Judah daa kam, se banto maama ji daa dedoa. Ba laam maa wó taa ye dedoa amo jeŋa wone.’

english_verse: Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone
translation_verse: Nam ta‑n zei dɛ selei sem konto n jeŋa ne se nɔɔna bam maama na.

english_verse: I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations.
translation_verse: Ba ná jwoori ba tega kam ne konto, a lage a pa ba maama ji teo dedoa ye ba zoore Isarele peero jei sem ne. Pɛ dedoa mo wó taa nii ba maama baŋa ne. Ba daa bá fɔge ba pɔɔre ba tete se ba ji teene delei.

english_verse: They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Ba nam daa bá biini ba tete de ba jwo-yɔɔro tem, de ba wo-zɔɔna de zwabania kikia yam. Amo tete mo lage a jwoŋi-ba a yage de ba na ywori a chwoŋa kam ne ba tusi tei to. Ba maa wó taa ye amo nɔɔna se amo de taa ye ba Wɛ wom.

english_verse: Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Ba wó taa zoore tega kalo a déem na kwei a pa a tontoŋeno Jakob to wone, mɛ seeni á nabaara de déem na zoore da to. Ba de ba dwi delo na saŋe ba kwaga to laam maa wó taa zoore tega kam konto ne se ko taa vei wuu, ye amo tontoŋeno David de taa ye ba dedɛɛro taa wuu.

english_verse: I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time,
translation_verse: Amo nam wó gwoni ni mo de a nɔɔna bam bochare-zuru ŋwaane. Ni-gwonim dem konto wó taa zega se ko taa vei wuu. Amo lage a jeini-ba ba tega kam ne mo se ba taa wora chɔpe, ye ba puli de kɔgɔ. A maa wó pa se a wara-jei sem taa wo ba tetare ne se ko taa vei wuu.

english_verse: and I will live among my people and be their God.
translation_verse: Amo maa wó taa zoore ba tei ne se a taa ye ba Wɛ, ye ba de ye amo tete nɔɔna.

english_verse: Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
translation_verse: Logo baŋa teene dem maa wó lɔre we amo Baŋa Wɛ mo kuri Isarele tiina bam se ba taa ye amo tete nyem, ne a wara-jei sem ná wo ba tetare ne se ko taa vei wuu.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pipiri n yibia n jeeri Magoga teo pɛ Goga na tei Meseka de Tubal to. Pworisi taane n chɔge‑o,

english_verse: and I will make you powerless! I will put a hook in your jaw and drag away both you and your large army. You command cavalry troops that wear heavy armor and carry shields and swords.
translation_verse: Amo lage a pa se n za n kikia yam mo. A maa wó kwei gwoli a ja‑m n peyaa seeni, ye a daare a vaŋe nmo de n jar-keira bam maama, de á sisein-nɔɔna de balo na diini-se to. Banto maama vɔge jara-keim zela mo ba zege diŋ-diŋ. Ba maa ye kɔ-fɔrɔ zanzam, ye ba zei se-zɔɔro de jara nantane.

english_verse: because in a few years, I will command you to invade Israel, a country that was ruined by war. It was deserted for a long time, but its people have returned from the foreign nations where they once lived. The Israelites now live in peace in the mountains of their own land.
translation_verse: Ko ná tu ko dáane fee, ba wó bwoŋi abam se á ti á yiga jara ŋwaane. Bena yam ná yi ya ti, á laam wó vo á kwaare jara de Isarele tiina bam, de ba ya na nwoŋi jara wone ye ba ba ba sii to de. Ba ma nwoŋi sa-teene dedɛ ne mo ba jwoori sɔŋɔ, ye ba laam zoore ba tete teo peero jei sem ne mɛ ya na tigi kafɛ to de bochare-zuru.

english_verse: to take advantage of Israel, that weak and peaceful country where people live safely inside towns that have no walls or gates or locks.
translation_verse: Nmo wó ta n tete ne we, “A lage a vo a ke chichuŋu de nɔɔna bam konto ye ba zoore chemm mo. Ba teene dem tiini de bwona lage-lage, ye kabiri wo chege-de. Bworru de nam tera se ba taa pe-de.

english_verse: You will rob the people in towns that were once a pile of rubble. These people lived as prisoners in foreign nations, but they have returned to Israel, the most important place in the world, and they own livestock and property.
translation_verse: A nam wó vo a chɔge jei selo ya na ye di-dwonnu ye nɔɔna laam fɔge ba kwɛ-te to. A maa wó vere nɔɔna bam wonnu tem. Ba déem ye peena mo sa-teene wone, ye ba jwoori ba tete teo ba zoora tega kalo na wo logo baŋa tetare ne to wone. Ba maa jege vara de jejegero dedɛ.”

english_verse: The people of Sheba and Dedan, along with merchants from villages in southern Spain, will be your allies. They will want some of the silver and gold, as well as the livestock and property that your army takes from Israel.
translation_verse: Nmo ná nwoŋi se n kwaare jara, Seba tiina, de Dedan tiina, de pipim-piina balo na nwoŋi Tarasisi de ko nawuura yam seeni to wó bwei ba we, “Nmo tu se n vere debam mo na? N lage n jar-keira bam mo n ke daane se á ba á vere debam lu-nyenno, de sabu-seŋa, dedaane dé vara, de dé jejegero, se á zeŋe wonnu dedɛ á ja á viiri na?” ’

english_verse: You will attack my people like a storm-cloud that covers their land. I will let you invade my country Israel, so that every nation on earth will know that I, the Lord, am holy. Judgment on Gog
translation_verse: Á wó vo á zaŋe amo nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam baŋa ne mo ne kunkwoŋo na li tega kam baŋa maama tei to. Goga, da yam ná yi ya ti, amo lage a pa se n vo n kwaare jara de a tete teo kom, se dwi-gɛ tiina bam lɔre amo na ye wolo to, ne a ná tɔge nmo baŋa ne a bere jaja we a ye wose mo ye ba na.

english_verse: The Lord said to Gog: Long ago, I ordered my prophets to warn the people of Israel that someday I would send an enemy to attack them. You, Gog, are that enemy, and that day is coming.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Ko dae nmo taane mo a déem ŋɔɔne ko tɔge Isarele sampwori sem na ye a tontoŋena to baŋa ne na? Ba déem kwei bena dedɛ mo ba pworisi we, amo lage a pa nmo ke chichuŋu de-ba.

english_verse: Every living thing on earth will tremble in fear of me—every fish and bird, every wild animal and reptile, and every human. Mountains will crumble, cliffs will fall, and cities will collapse.
translation_verse: Ko maa wó pa se naneo wo ywona, de zuna balo na kare ba jaane wɛɛne to, de kago-vara, de tega-veila, de logo baŋa nabiina maama wó fom amo yiga ne. Peero tem de te gugworru maama wó sirimi, ye kabiri maama de to buri-buri.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will make the mountains of Israel turn against you. Your troops will be so terrified that they will attack each other.
translation_verse: A maa wó pa se jara ba ya jeeri Goga amo tete peero tem maama yuu ne. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. Nɔɔno maama wó kwei o se-zɔɔ o beeri o dwoŋi se o go.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog and tell him: You are the ruler of Meshech and Tubal, but I, the Lord, am your enemy!
translation_verse: “Nabiinu, pworisi taane n chɔge Goga se n ta we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Goga, amo dwoni de nmo, nmo wolo na ye Meseka, de Tubal yuu tu to.

english_verse: of your dead bodies left lying in open fields. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nmo yera yam wó yɔɔre ya taa tigi pwola ne mo pare-pare. Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ mo tage konto.

english_verse: I will set fire to the land of Magog and to those nations along the seacoast that think they are so secure, and they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Amo lage a tɔrege mini mo a de Magoga de balo na zoore chemm naneo kom ni ne to wone. Ba laam maa wó lɔre we amo mo ye Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: When that day comes, the people in the towns of Israel will collect the weapons of their dead enemies. They will use these shields, bows and arrows, spears, and clubs as firewood, and there will be enough to last for seven years.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto nam ná yia, Isarele tiina bam wó nwoŋi ba sam dem ne ba vo ba pɛ jara zela yalo jar-keira bam na tega ba daare to, se ba kwei-ya ba ma dwei mini. Ba maa wó kwei ba jara nantane sem, de ba tɛ sem, de ba chena yam, de ba jara-keim gwola yam, de ba chichwoa yam, se ba taa jege-te ba dwei mini bena yarepɛ.

english_verse: They will burn these weapons instead of gathering sticks or chopping down trees. That's how the Israelites will take revenge on those who robbed and abused them. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Burial of Gog The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ba daa bá vo gaao se ba puuri da-dwa, naa ba zo goa wone se ba gwoni dɛ, ba na wó taa jege jara zela yam ba ma ba dwei mini to ŋwaane. Konto to, Isarele tiina bam wó yiri ba jene balo déem na vere-ba to baŋa ne, de ba na vere banto de wonnu to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: After Gog has been destroyed, I will bury him and his army in Israel, in Travelers' Valley, east of the Dead Sea. That graveyard will be so large that it will block the way of anyone who tries to walk through the valley, which will then be known as “The Valley of Gog's Army.”
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne, amo wó kwei tega Isarele laŋa kam ne a pa Goga, se ba suli o de o jar-keira bam da. Ka maa wó taa ye chwo-veila bwolo kom ne, nɔɔna na tɔge mɛ ba vei naneo kom wɛ-puli seeni to mo. Ba yibeela yam nam wó che chwoŋa kam mo se nɔɔna daa yé wane ba tɔge da ba kɛ, ba na wó suli Goga de o kɔ-fɔrɔ kom maama da to ŋwaane. Konto ŋwaane ba wó taa bwoi jei sem we, “Goga nɔn-kɔgɔ bwolo” mo.

english_verse: The Israelites will spend seven months burying dead bodies and cleaning up their land.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina bam wó kwei chane serepɛ mo ba suli twa bam ba ti, se ba wane ba kwɛ tega kam.

english_verse: Everyone will help with the burial, and they will be honored for this on the day the brightness of my glory is seen.
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔn-bia bam maama nam mo wó suli twa bam. Ko maa wó pa ba jwoŋi yere dɛ delo ne amo na wó bere a nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom jaja to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: After those seven months, the people will appoint a group of men to look for any dead bodies left unburied. This must be done for seven months to make sure that the land is no longer unclean.
translation_verse: Ba maa wó kuri nɔɔna se ba taa kare tega kam ni maama ba beera, se ba nii ba na twa balo ta na tigi pwola ne to. Ba maa ná nɛ-ba, nɔɔna badaara wó suli-ba mo se ko kwɛ tega kam. Ba wó taa ke konto mo chane serepɛ.

english_verse: Whenever they find a human bone, they will set up a marker next to it. Then the gravediggers will bury it in “The Valley of Gog's Army”
translation_verse: Ba ná kare tega kam ne ba via, ye ba dedoa ná nɛ nabiinu kua, kotu wó ke maana mo o tiŋi ka yera ne. Bayɛ maa wó ba ba kwei kua kam ba vo ba suli Goga nɔn-kɔgɔ bwolo kom ne.

english_verse: near the town of “Gog's Army.” After that, the land will be pure again.
translation_verse: Ba wó tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo ba kwɛ tega kam. Teo kodwoŋi nam wó taa wo jei sem konto ne, ko yere na ye Hamona.’

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to hold a feast on Israel's mountains and offer sacrifices there. So invite all the birds and wild animals to come from every direction and eat the meat of sacrifices and drink the blood. The birds and animals
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye nmo, nabiinu, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei de nmo to mo tento: Bwoŋi zuna dwi maama, de kago-vara bam se n ta we, ‘Nwoŋi-na jei maama á ba á jeeri daane Isarele peero tem yuu ne, se á di kaanem kuri delo a na ke se a pa abam to. Ko ye kuri-fɔrɔ mo a ke dáane, se a pa abam di nɔna, ye á daare á nyɔ jana á su.

english_verse: They will come to my table and stuff themselves with the flesh of horses and warriors of every kind. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Israel Will Be Restored The Lord said:
translation_verse: Wodiu kolo amo na wó pa abam se á di to, abam wó kuri sisein-nɔɔna de balo ya na diini-se to nɔna mo á di á boboŋa.’ Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: The people of Israel will know from then on that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ko maa na wó zege maŋa kam konto ne se ko taa vei to, Isarele dwi tiina bam wó lɔre we amo mo ye ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom.

english_verse: Foreign nations will realize that the Israelites were forced to leave their own land because they sinned against me. I turned my back on my people and let enemies attack and kill them.
translation_verse: Dwi-gɛ tiina bam de maa wó lɔre we Isarele tiina bam na ke wɛleera ye ba nwoŋi amo kwaga ne to ŋwaane mo amo déem dole-ba a yage sa-teo ne yiga yiga. A laam ma le a yiga ba wone, ye a ke-ba ba dona jeŋa ne, pa se ba maama te jara wone.

english_verse: Now I will show mercy to the people of Israel and bring them back from the nations where they are living. They are Jacob's descendants, so I will bless them and show that I am holy.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Amo wó pa se Jakob dwi dem jwoori ba taa jege yu-ywoŋo, ye a duri Isarele tiina bam maama ŋwaŋa. A maa wó seene a yia se a zeiŋi a yere dem na ye wose to wɛɛne.

english_verse: They will live safely in their own land, but will be ashamed when they remember their evil ways and how they disgraced me.
translation_verse: Ba ná tu ba jeini ba tete tega kam wone ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa ba fugi-ba, ba laam wó swei chaveera yalo maama ba ya na nɛ to, de zwabania kikia yalo ba na ke ba chɔge amo yiga to ni ne.

english_verse: Foreign nations will watch as I take the Israelites from enemy lands and bring them back home, and those nations will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: Amo wó le-ba a ja a nwoŋi teene delo ba ya na zoore de wone to, se a jwoŋi-ba ba dona jeŋa ne. A maa wó tɔge ba baŋa ne a bere jaja we a ye wose, se dwi-gɛ tiina dedɛ taa zege ba nia.

english_verse: Never again will I turn my back on the people of Israel, and my Spirit will live in them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Amo daa bá le a yiga ba wone. A nam lage a lwo a Jworo mo a yage Isarele dwi tiina bam baŋa ne. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_verse: He measured the entrance room at the far end of the passageway, and it was ten meters wide.
translation_verse: O laam ma jeeli napɔrɔ kom wɛ-baŋa maŋem dem. Ko maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuseredo. Napɔrɔ kom déem jeeri konkɔlɔ kolo na wo ko sɛ setɔ sem ne to mo.

english_verse: In my vision the Lord took me closer, and I saw a man who was sparkling like polished bronze. He was standing near one of the gates and was holding a tape measure in one hand and a measuring stick in the other.
translation_verse: O na jaane-ne pa a fɔɔre a yi da to, mo a nɛ nɔɔno na zega, ye o nyeena ne channa na ye tei to. Kotu yɔɔre o zege manchwo-peo kom ni ne mo, ye o zei ŋona de kasogo o jeŋa ne, ne ba na ma-te ba maŋe wonnu tei to.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay close attention to everything I'm going to show you—that's why you've been brought here. Listen carefully, because you must tell the people of Israel what you see.” The East Gate
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom laam ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu, fɔge n puri n yia se n nii, n daare n pore n zwa se n cheigi kolo maama a na lage a bere‑m to. Kokuri, konto ŋwaane mo ba jaane‑m ba ba ywo-seeni. Tole kolo maama n na nɛ to n bere Isarele tiina bam.” Wɛ diga konkɔlɔ wɛ-puli seeni ni dem

english_verse: Then he went to the east gate, where he walked up steps that led to a long passageway. On each side of this passageway were three guardrooms, which were three meters square, and they were separated by walls two and a half meters thick. The man measured the distance between the opening of the gate and the first guardroom, and it was three meters, the thickness of the outer wall. At the far end of this passageway, I saw an entrance room that faced the courtyard of the temple itself. There was also a distance of three meters between the last guardroom and the entrance room
translation_verse: Gugworru teredo déem mo zege te geene tetare chwoŋa kam ka sɛ selei sem ne. Te dedɔrem baŋa maŋem ye kasogo dedoa mo. Te kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem de maa ye kasogo dedoa. Kabira kalo na chege ka pɔɔre gugworru tem maama daane to maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu. Napɔrɔ kolo na jeeri Wɛ diga kam to manchwo-ni maŋem de maa ye kasogo dedoa.

english_verse: at the end of the passageway. The man measured this room: It was four meters from the doorway to the opposite wall, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one meter.
translation_verse: Ko wo kom maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni nana, ye ko taara yam maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem belei. Napɔrɔ kom ni dem déem jeeri Wɛ diga kam tete mo.

english_verse: The three guardrooms on each side of the passageway were the same size, and the walls that separated them were the same thickness.
translation_verse: Gugworru tetɔ tetɔ maa wo tetare chwoŋa kam sɛ selei sem maama ne. Te maama mae daane mo, ye taala yalo na wora to de maa mae daane.

english_verse: Next, the man measured the width of the passageway, and it was six and a half meters, but the two doors of the gate were only five meters wide.
translation_verse: O ta ma maŋe chwoŋa kalo na tɔge ni dem seeni to. Ka na yala tei to maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga. Ka dedɔrem baŋa maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni fuga-betɔ.

english_verse: The man measured the distance from the back wall of one of these rooms to the same spot in the room directly across the passageway, and it was twelve and a half meters.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom daa ma zege gugworo dedoa kwaga kabira kam seeni, o tɔge tetare chwoŋa kam seeni o maŋe o zo gugworo kodwoŋi kwaga kabira kam. Ko maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finlei-benu.

english_verse: Finally, he measured the total length of the passageway, from the outer wall to the entrance room, and it was
translation_verse: Pwola kalo ba na tɔge da ba kɛ, ko zege pwooni yiga ni dem ne se ko yi napɔrɔ kom ni dem to maŋem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem finnu.

english_verse: The three walls in the guardrooms had small windows in them, just like the ones in the entrance room. The walls along the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. The Outer Courtyard
translation_verse: Gugworru tem de te taala yam déem jege takworru mo te kabiri sem yera maama ne. Napɔrɔ kom de maa jege takworru konto dwoŋi. Konkwara nyenyero mo gɔgere te tigi taala yam maama yera ne. Da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom

english_verse: In fact, everything along the passageway was also the same size, including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, the entrance room at the far end, and the windows. This gate, like the others, was
translation_verse: Tetare konkɔlɔ kom saŋa maama jege ka napɔrɔ mo. Te maama ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finlei-benu mo dedɔrem baŋa ne. Te ta ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu mo kayɔlɔ baŋa ne.

english_verse: I saw the gates that led to the inner courtyard of the temple and noticed that they were higher than those leading to the outer courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gates, and it was
translation_verse: O ma maŋe pwola kalo na tigi konkɔlɔ kom nia yalei yam tetare laŋa ne to. Ko na zege wɛ-puli seeni ni dem se ko taa vei baŋa seeni ni dem to, ko maŋem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni bi mo. Baŋa seeni ni dem

english_verse: Next, the man measured the north gate that led to the outer courtyard.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom daa ma maŋe ni delo na jeeri baŋa seeni ye de tole de vei da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom to.

english_verse: This gate also had three guardrooms on each side of a passageway. The measurements of these rooms, the walls between them, and the entrance room at the far end of the passageway were exactly the same as those of the east gate. The north gate was also
translation_verse: Gugworru tetɔ tetɔ na wo tetare chwoŋa kam sɛ sem ne to, de te taala yam, ko woli de napɔrɔ kom maama maŋem ye bedwe mo de wɛ-puli seeni ni dem na ye tei to. Ni dem diga kam ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finnu mo dedɔrem baŋa ne. De taa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem finlei-benu ko kayɔlɔ baŋa ne.

english_verse: and the windows, the entrance room, and the carvings of palm trees were just like those in the east gate. The entrance room also faced the courtyard of the temple and had seven steps leading up to it.
translation_verse: Ka takworru tem, de napɔrɔ kom, dedaane konkwara nyenyero telo na gɔgere te tigi ka kabiri sem yera ne to maama yɔɔre te ye bedwe mo de wɛ-puli seeni ni dem na ye tei to. Ka maa jege nateina yarepɛ na diini ya vei ka wone. Nɔɔna ná diini ba yi da, ka napɔrɔ kom wó taa wo ba yiga ne mo.
