english_verse: Directly across the outer courtyard was a gate that led to the inner courtyard, just as there was for the east gate. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was
translation_verse: Ni dedwoŋi de maa wora de na vei de zoore tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone, ye de jeeri baŋa seeni ni dem. Ni dedwoŋi de maa wo konkɔlɔ kom wɛ-puli seeni. Nɔɔno wom ma maŋe pwola kalo na tigi ni dedwe ne, se ko yi ni dedwoŋi dem ne to. Ko maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni bi. Tega-kuri seeni ni dem

english_verse: The man then took me to the south gate. He measured the walls and the entrance room of this gate, and the measurements were exactly the same as those of the other two gates.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom laam ma tɔge a yiga pa dé vo konkɔlɔ kom tega-kuri dem seeni. Amo ma nii a na ni delo na jeeri tega-kuri seeni to. O ma maŋe de taala yam, de de napɔrɔ kom. Te maama maŋem dem yɔɔre de ye bedwe de nia yadwonna yam na ye tei to mo.

english_verse: Seven steps led up to the gate; the entrance room was at the far end of the passageway and faced the courtyard of the temple. Carvings of palm trees decorated the walls along the passageway.
translation_verse: Ka maa jege nateina yarepɛ na diini ya vei ka wone. Nɔɔna ná diini ba yi da, ka napɔrɔ kom wó taa wo ba yiga ne mo. Ka taala yam maa jege konkwara nyenyero na gɔgere te tigi ya yera ne to, konkwara dedoa saŋa maama ne.

english_verse: And directly across the outer courtyard was a gate on the south side of the inner courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was also
translation_verse: Wɛ diga kam tetare konkɔlɔ kom de maa jege ni delo na jeeri tega-kuri seeni to. Nɔɔno wom ma maŋe pwola kalo na tigi tega-kuri seeni nia yalei yam tetare laŋa ne to. Ko maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni bi. Nia yalo na vei ya zoore tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone to

english_verse: We then went into the inner courtyard, through the gate on the south side of the temple. The man measured the gate, and it was the same size as the gates in the outer wall.
translation_verse: O daa ma tɔge tega-kuri ni dem seeni o ja-ne pa dé zo Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone. O ma maŋe tega-kuri seeni ni dem, ye dento de nia yadwonna yam maŋem ye bedwe.

english_verse: The entrance room of this gate faced the outer courtyard, and carvings of palm trees decorated the walls of the passageway. Eight steps led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Napɔrɔ kom nam jeeri da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom mo. Konkwara nyenyero déem gɔgere mo te tigi kabiri sem yera ne. Nateina nana de maa tole ya diini ni dem konto ne.

english_verse: Next, we went through the east gate to the inner courtyard. The man measured this gate, and it was the same size as the others.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom daa ma ja-ne o vo o yi tetare konkɔlɔ kom wɛ-puli seeni saŋa kam. O ma maŋe ka ni dem. De de maŋem yɔɔre de ye ne yadwonna yam maŋem na ye tei to mo.

english_verse: The guardrooms, the walls separating them, and its entrance room had the same measurements as the other gates. The guardrooms and the entrance room had windows, and the gate was
translation_verse: De gugworru tem, de taala yam, de napɔrɔ kom maama maŋem ye bedwe de nia yadwonna yam mo. Ni dem diga kam, de napɔrɔ kom kabiri maama maa jege takworru se yera ne. Ka maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni finnu dedɔrem baŋa ne. Ka ta ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem finlei-benu mo kayɔlɔ baŋa ne.

english_verse: The entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and the walls in the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Napɔrɔ kom jeeri da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom mo. Konkwara nyenyero déem maa gɔgere te tigi kabiri sem yera ne. Nateina nana de maa tole ya diini ni dem konto ne.

english_verse: Then the man took me to the north gate. He measured it, and it was the same size as the others,
translation_verse: O daa ma ja-ne pa dé yi baŋa seeni ni dem, ye o maŋe-de. Dento de maŋem ye bedwe de nia yadwonna yam na mae tei to,

english_verse: and like the other inner gates, its entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and its walls were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate. The Rooms for Sacrificing Animals
translation_verse: Napɔrɔ kom jeeri da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom mo. Konkwara nyenyero déem mo gɔgere te tigi ko kabiri sem yera ne. Nateina nana de maa tole ya diini ni dem konto ne. Kaanem vara kwɛɛm diga

english_verse: Inside the entrance room of the north gate, I saw four tables, two on each side of the room, where the animals to be sacrificed were killed. Just outside this room was a small building used for washing the animals before they were offered as sacrifices to please the Lord or sacrifices for sin or sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Tabollo tena mo zege napɔrɔ kom ne. Te telei mo zege diga kam saŋa dedoa seeni, ye telei de zege saŋa kadwoŋi kam ne. Te baŋa ne mo ba nam goe vara balo ba na wó ma ba ke zwɛɛm kaanem, de wɛleere saarem kaanem, de wɛleere jene kaanem to.

english_verse: Four more tables were in the outer courtyard, two on each side of the steps leading into the entrance room.
translation_verse: Tabollo tena ta mo wo napɔrɔ kom pwooni yiga ne, mɛ nɔɔna na diini ba tɔge baŋa seeni ni dem to. Telei maa wo ni dem saŋa dedoa seeni, ye telei de wo saŋa kakam kam ne.

english_verse: and where the meat was placed until it was sacrificed on the altar. Next to the tables in the entrance room were four stone tables
translation_verse: Gwoli de maa meeli diga kam wo kabira yera maama ne. Se ye da-yiga noa maŋem mo. Tabollo tem nam wora se ba ná go vara bam, se ba kwei nɔna yam mo ba daŋe te baŋa ne. Kaanem tiina bam di sem

english_verse: The man then took me to the inner courtyard, where I saw two buildings, one beside the inner gate on the north and the other beside the inner gate on the south.
translation_verse: Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone di selei maa wora, se na wo konkɔlɔ ni dem pwooni yiga ne to. Se dedoa yeiri ni delo na wo baŋa seeni to mo ye ka jeeri tega-kuri seeni. Diga kadwoŋi kam de maa yeiri ni delo na wo tega-kuri seeni to, ye ka jeeri baŋa seeni.

english_verse: He said, “The building beside the north gate belongs to the priests who serve in the temple,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom laam ma ta de amo o we, “Diga kalo na jeeri tega-kuri seeni to ye kaanem tiina balo na nii Wɛ diga kam baŋa ne to nyem mo.

english_verse: and the building beside the south gate belongs to those who serve at the altar. All of them are descendants of Zadok and are the only Levites allowed to serve as the Lord's priests.” The Inner Courtyard and the Temple
translation_verse: Ko daare kalo na jeeri baŋa seeni to maa ye kaanem tiina balo na nii kaanem bimbini dem baŋa ne to de nyem. Banto nam ye Zadoki diga kam tiina mo. Levi dwi dem maama wone nɔɔna banto yerane mo jege chwoŋa se ba fɔɔre ba twɛ Baŋa Wɛ tei se ba taa toŋa ba pa‑o.”

english_verse: We walked to the porch of the temple, and the man measured the doorway of the porch: It was seven meters long, two and a half meters wide, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one and a half meters.
translation_verse: O laam ma ja-ne o vo o yi Wɛ diga kam tete napɔrɔ kom. O ma maŋe ko taala yalei yam na wo ni dem sɛ selei sem ne to. Ya na lira tei to ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni benu mo. Napɔrɔ kom ni dem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem fuga-bena kayɔlɔ baŋa ne. Ka sɛ kabiri sem ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem betɔ betɔ saŋa maama baŋa ne mo.

english_verse: Next we went into the main room of the temple. The man measured the doorway of this room: It was
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom laam ma ja-ne o zo di-yuu kom. O ma maŋe taala yalei yam na wo ka ni dem sɛ selei sem ne to. Ya dedoa na lira tei to ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem beredo mo.

english_verse: with carvings of winged creatures and had a carving of a palm tree between the creatures. Each winged creature had two faces: A human face looking at the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face looking at the palm tree on the other side. These designs were carved into the paneling all the way around the two rooms.
translation_verse: Ko na zege tega ne se ko ja ko di jeiga kalo na wo ni dem baŋa seeni to, ba yɔɔre ba gɔgere cherubi, de konkwara nyenyero mo Wɛ di-yuu kom kabiri sem yera ne.

english_verse: Then the man walked to the far end of the temple's main room and said, “Beyond this doorway is the most holy place.” He first measured the doorway: It was one meter wide,
translation_verse: O laam ma maŋe di-yun-gala kam tete, de ka na lɛɛne ka yi di-yuu kom to. Ko maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem finlei dedɔrem baŋa ne. Ko ta ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem finlei mo kayɔlɔ baŋa ne. O ma ta de amo o we, “Diga kanto mo tiini ka ye wose Wɛ ŋwaane.”

english_verse: The walls of the temple were thicker at the bottom than at the top, which meant that the storage rooms on the top level were wider than those on the bottom level. Steps led from the bottom level, through the middle level, and into the top level.
translation_verse: Di selo na lɔge se daŋe baŋa gene sem ne to yala se dwoi selo na wo kuri dem ne to, se ko tɔge Wɛ diga kabira kam na ye tei ko zege tega kam seeni ko taa diini baŋa seeni to. Nateina mo zege kuri gene sem ne ya dɔɔle ya tɔge tetare gene sem seeni, ya kɛ ya di baŋa seeni gene di sem.

english_verse: The outside walls of the storage rooms were two and a half meters thick; there was nothing between these walls
translation_verse: Di-balwa bam kabiri sem liliru maŋem ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni benu mo. Ko daare, pwola kalo na tigi Wɛ diga kam di-balwa bam,

english_verse: One door led into the storage rooms on the north side of the temple, and another door led to those on the south side. The stone base extended two and a half meters beyond the outside wall of the storage rooms. The West Building and the Measurements of the Temple
translation_verse: Nia mo wora ya na tɔge ya zoore di-balwa bam wone, ne nɔɔno ná zege pwola kam ne o beene da. Ni dedoa zege Wɛ diga kam baŋa seeni mo, ye dedwoŋi dem zege ka tega-kuri seeni. Pwola kalo na daare to kayɔlɔ baŋa maŋem dem laam maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem benu ko kaare Wɛ diga kam maama.

english_verse: The distance across the front of the temple, including the open space on either side, was also
translation_verse: Wɛ diga konkɔlɔ pwola kalo na wo ka wɛ-puli seeni to, de ka yiga kam seeni de maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem bi kayɔlɔ baŋa ne.

english_verse: were paneled with wood all the way from the floor to the windows, while the doorways, the small windows, and the three side rooms were trimmed in wood.
translation_verse: ba kwei da-pelwaro mo ba kwoli di setɔ sem maama wo kabira kam, ko zege ka tega kam seeni se ko yi takworru tem na wo mɛ to. Di sem nia yam, de se takworru tem, dedaane se gugworru tem maama mo ba fɔge ba kwɛ konto dwoŋi ba zege.

english_verse: The doorframe to the temple's main room was in the shape of a rectangle. The Wooden Altar In front of the doorway to the most holy place was something that looked like
translation_verse: Ni delo na zoore di-yuu kom to sɛ sena sem mae daane mo. Delo dem maa na zoore di-yun-gala kam wo to de ye konto dwoŋi.

english_verse: a wooden altar. It was one and a half meters high and one meter square, and its corners, its base, and its sides were made of wood. The man said, “This is a reminder that the Lord is constantly watching over his temple.” The Doors in the Temple
translation_verse: Kaanem bimbini delo ba na mɛ daa ba ke to maa zege da. De maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem kuni betɔ wɛ-baŋa ne. De dedɔrem dem baŋa seeni de de kayɔlɔ baŋa seeni de maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem belei belei. Bimbini dem nyea yam, de de kuri dem seeni, dedaane de sɛ sem maama ye dɛ mo ba mɛ ba ke. Nɔɔno wom ma ta de amo o we, “Tabolo konto mo ye kolo na zege Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne to.”

english_verse: Both the doorway to the main room of the temple and the doorway to the most holy place had two doors,
translation_verse: Ni delo na zoore di-yuu kom to, de delo na zoore di-yun-gala kam to maama jege bworru telei telei mo.

english_verse: and each door had two sections that could fold open.
translation_verse: Bworo maama jege vɔna yalei mo pa ko wae ko piri ko tete ko ke daane.

english_verse: The doors to the main room were decorated with carvings of winged creatures and palm trees just like those on the walls, and there was a wooden covering over the porch just outside these doors.
translation_verse: Ba ta ma gɔgere cherubi de konkwara nyenyero di-yuu kom ni-bworru tem yera ne, ne ba na ke tei kabiri sem yera ne to. Ba mɛ dɛ mo ba tei pwoŋa Wɛ diga napɔrɔ kom pwooni yiga ne.

english_verse: The walls on each side of this porch had small windows and were also decorated with carvings of palm trees.
translation_verse: Takworru maa wo napɔrɔ kom ni sɛ selei sem ne, ye ba gɔgere konkwara nyenyero ba ke da. Wɛ diga di-balwa bam de se pwei sem de déem kwɛ konto dwoŋi mo.

english_verse: After the man and I left the temple and walked back to the outer courtyard, he showed me a set of rooms on the north side of the west building. This set of rooms was
translation_verse: Diga kam ni déem wo baŋa seeni mo. Ka maŋem dem maa ye jatwogo de noa ni kuni bi dedɔrem baŋa ne. Ka ta ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem finnu mo kayɔlɔ baŋa ne.

english_verse: and at the east end of this wall was the door leading from the courtyard to these rooms. There was also a set of rooms on the south side of the west building.
translation_verse: Ni dem konto maa wo konkɔlɔ kabira kam na bobo mɛ to ne. Di sedwonna maa wo Wɛ diga da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom tega-kuri seeni, ye se yɔɔre se jeeri diga kadwoŋi kam.

english_verse: The rooms on the top level were narrower than those on the middle level, and the rooms on the middle level were narrower than those on the bottom level.
translation_verse: Di sem na lɔge tei to, selo na wo baŋa seeni to muri selo na wo tetare dem seeni to mo. Selo de maa na wo tetare ne to de daa maa muri selo na wo kuri dem seeni to.

english_verse: The rooms on the bottom level supported those on the two upper levels, and so these rooms did not have columns like other buildings in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Di sem na lɔge gene setɔ da-baŋa ne konto to, ba wo chwi ywoa yalo na wó teili-se to, ne konkwallo tem di sedwonna na jege tei to. Ko ma pa di selo na lɔge se zege baŋa ne to muri selo na wo kuri dem ne to.

english_verse: The door to these rooms was at the east end of the wall that stood in front of them.
translation_verse: Tega-kuri di sem maa jege ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni se ko maŋe de kabira kam na bobo mɛ seeni ka lɔ ka zege to.

english_verse: The man then said to me: These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom laam ma ta de amo o we, “Di sento na wo Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom baŋa seeni, de selo na wo ko tega-kuri seeni to ye wose mo. Dáane mo Baŋa Wɛ kaanem tiina balo na bwola ded‑o to wó yeini ba di kaanem wodiu kolo na tiini ko ye wose to. Ba maa wó tiŋi wonnu telo na ye wose to di sem konto wone, ne ko ná ye wodiu kaanem ŋwaane, de wɛleera saarem kaanem, de wɛleera jene kaanem ŋwaane. Kokuri to, di sem ye wose mo Wɛ ŋwaane.

english_verse: When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people. The Size of the Temple Area
translation_verse: Kaanem tiina bam ná yeini ba zo Wɛ diga kam tete, ba daa bá wane ba nwoŋi ka jei sem ne, se ba zo da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom, ye ba wo lɔɔre ba kaanem gwaaro tem ba tiŋi di sem konto wone. Ba maa wó yeini ba kwei gwaaro tedwonna ba zo, se ba laam wane ba yi nɔɔna bam na wo mɛ seeni to.”

english_verse: After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area.
translation_verse: O na maŋe woŋo kolo dwi maama na wo Wɛ diga jei sem ne o ti to, mo o jaane-ne pa dé tɔge wɛ-puli seeni ni dem dé nwoŋi pwooni. O laam ma maŋe pwola kalo na kaare dáane maama to.

english_verse: Then he measured the north side, the south side, and the west side of the wall, and they were each
translation_verse: O ma pipiri o vo o maŋe wɛ-zoore seeni saŋa kam. Ka de maa ye jatwogo de noa ni maŋem bia yanu.

english_verse: The man took me back to the east gate of the temple,
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma ja-ne pa dé vo Wɛ diga kam ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to.

english_verse: meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side. The Dedication of the Altar
translation_verse: A ma nii a na we Isarele tiina Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom zege wɛ-puli seeni mo ko maa beena. Wɛ na dɔne o kwori tei to, ko nye de naneo na-fwaaro na chuuri ye te wuuri tei to mo. Tega baŋa jei maama déem ma li de o nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom pwooni.

english_verse: This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River. I immediately bowed with my face to the ground,
translation_verse: Wɛ na le wonnu telo o bere-ne to yɔɔre te nye de veera yalo a ya na nɛ ye o ba se o chɔge Jerusalem teo kom to mo. Te maa nye de yalo a ya na nɛ Chebara buga kam ni ne to. Amo ma to a vwi a yibia tega ne.

english_verse: and the Lord's glory came through the east gate and into the temple.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom ma tɔge ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to ne ko zo Wɛ diga kam wone.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
translation_verse: Vio laam ma fuli ko gɔ-ne ko zege wɛɛne. Ko ma ja-ne ko ja zo Wɛ diga kam tetare konkɔlɔ kom ne, ye amo de na we Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom mo yɔɔre ko su Wɛ diga kam ni maama.

english_verse: But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
translation_verse: Ba nam jege se ba yage jwo-yɔɔro kaanem, se ba daare ba yage ba pwa yibeela yam zula. Ba ná ke konto, amo laam wó taa zoore ba tetare ne taa wuu.

english_verse: The people of Israel must suffer shame for sinning against me, so tell them about my holy temple. Let them think about it,
translation_verse: Nabiinu, fɔge n maŋe Wɛ diga kam yera seina na ye tei to n bere Isarele tiina bam. Ko maa wó pa se chaveera ja-ba ba tusim kikia ŋwaane. Pa se ba na ka zega kam maŋem na ye tei to.

english_verse: then if they are truly sorry, describe for them the design and shape of the temple, the gates, the measurements, and how the buildings are arranged. Explain the regulations about worshiping there, then write down these things, so they can study and obey them.
translation_verse: Chaveera maa ná jaane-ba ba kikia yam maama ŋwaane, se n pa ba lɔre Wɛ diga kam na zega tei, de ka nia yam, de ka maŋem dem maama na ye tei to. Ta pa ba lɔre ka di sem na tigisi se lɔ tei to, se n daare n ta de-ba ka chullu tem na bere kolo to. Nam popone wonnu tem konto maama n tiŋi se ba maane Wɛ diga kam nyenyego na ye tei to, ye ba daare ba taa tɔge ka chullu tem.

english_verse: Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Kwei da yarepɛ se dɛ maama ne, n ja bo-bala n ba n ma n ke wɛleere saarem kaanem. Nmo ta wó beeri na-bala de pi-bala mo se n ma tento de n ke kaanem dem. Te nam ba jege se te taa jege gɛɛ te yera yam ne.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do:
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu, Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Ba ná lɔge kaanem bimbini dem, chullu telo ba na wó tɔge se ba zwɛ vara, ba daare ba kwei ba jana bam ba miisi bimbini dem yera ne to mo tento:

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Nmo wó kwei na-bala n pa kaanem tiina bam se ba ma ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem. Banto ye Zadoki diga kam tiina mo na jege chwoŋa se ba fɔɔre ba twɛ amo tei se ba taa toŋa ba pa-ne to. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: Nmo laam ma‑n wó pwori jana bam wone se n kwei-ba n taare bimbini dem nyea yana yam ne, dedaane de tetare seeni nia yana yam ne, de fera kalo na kaare bimbini dem maama to ne. Nmo wó tɔge chwoŋa kam konto mo se n fɔge n kwɛ bimbini dem kaanem totoŋa yam ŋwaane.

english_verse: The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
translation_verse: Tega ná poore, n ta wó ja bo-bala kalo na ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to mo n ba se n kwei-ka n ke wɛleere saarem kaanem. Ke konto n ma n fɔge n kwɛ bimbini dem Wɛ ŋwaane, ne n na ke tei de na-bala kam to.

english_verse: Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them,
translation_verse: Nmo ná kwɛ-de n ti, n laam wó le na-bala de pi-bala mo n vara bam wone, te na ba jege gɛɛ te yera ne to.

english_verse: and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Nmo wó kwei-te n kaane Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne mo. Wɛ kaanem tiina bam de wó kwei yɛ ba zezage vara bam nɔna yam baŋa ne, ye ba daare ba zwɛ-ya ba pa Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use.
translation_verse: Ba nam wó kwei da yarepɛ mo ba ma ba kwɛ bimbini dem Wɛ ŋwaane. Ba maa wó tɔge chwoŋa kam konto ba pɔɔre-de ba zege dáa ne kaanem totoŋa yam ŋwaane.

english_verse: From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Da yam konto ná lage ya ti, pa da nana dɛ dem yi se ko taa via, kaanem tiina bam jege se ba kwei abam zwɛɛm pɛɛra yam, de á nu-biu pɛɛra yam ba ma ke kaanem ba pa-ne bimbini dem baŋa ne. Amo laam maa wó sɛ se á ta‑á ye a nɔɔna bam. Amo Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom daa ma ja-ne pa dé vo dé yi Wɛ diga kam konkɔlɔ ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to. De nam ya pe mo.

english_verse: The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate. People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
translation_verse: Isarele teo dedɛɛro wom yerane mo jege chwoŋa se o vo o jeini ni dem diga dedoa ne o di wodiu amo Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne. O nam jege se o tɔge ni dem napɔrɔ kom ne mo o zo da, ye o daare o tɔge chwoŋa kam konto o nwoŋi.”

english_verse: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma ja-ne pa dé tɔge baŋa seeni ni dem ne dé vo dé zaŋe Wɛ diga kam yiga ne. Amo ma nii a na Baŋa Wɛ nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom na su Wɛ diga kam ni maama tei to. A ma to a vwi a yibia tega ne.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ta ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu, fɔge n nii lanyerane, se n cheigi kolo maama a na lage a bere‑m Baŋa Wɛ diga kam chullu tem seeni to se n kwei-te n ke n yuu ne. Ta maane ka nia yam na ye tei to de balo na jege chwoŋa se ba taa tɔge-ya ba zoore wara-jei sem ba daare ba nwoŋi to.

english_verse: Tell those rebellious people of Israel: I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways!
translation_verse: Nam ta de Isarele dwi zwabani-nyena bam we, ‘Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam Isarele dwi tiina bam, yage-na á totoŋ-vɛɛsa yam!

english_verse: Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye pɛɛra yalo na ye wose amo ŋwaane to, abam wo fɔge á nii ya baŋa ne. Á nam kwei sa-teena mo á pa ba jege amo wara-jei sem totoŋa ba toŋa ba pa abam.

english_verse: And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel. The Levites Are Punished The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Sa-teena balo na yeiri amo to ba jege chwoŋa se ba zo amo wara-jei sem ne, de balo na zoore Isarele tiina bam tetare ne to de.

english_verse: Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished!
translation_verse: Levi dwi tiina bam badwonna déem yage amo. Ba ma gwaane Isarele tiina badaara bam wone pa ba ywori chwoŋa ba daare amo ye ba zuli jwona. Ba wɛleera yam konto wó taa wo ba yuu ne se ba na waarem.

english_verse: But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning,
translation_verse: Ba nam na toŋe ba pa Isarele dwi tiina bam jwona kaanem baŋa ne mo ye ba pa ba tusi to ŋwaane, amo nam dugi de a tete yere we a wó waare-ba ba wɛleera yam ŋwaane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins.
translation_verse: A nam bá pa-ba chwoŋa se ba fɔɔre ba twɛ amo se ba taa toŋa kaanem tiina totoŋa ba pa-ne. Ba ta yé twɛ wonnu telo a na pɔɔre-te se te taa ye wose amo ŋwaane to. Ba nam wó di ba chaveera mo totoŋ-zɔɔna yalo ba na ke to ŋwaane.

english_verse: They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple. Rules for Priests The Lord said:
translation_verse: De ko de, a lage a kwei Wɛ diga kam totoŋa dwi maama mo a ke banto jeŋa ne se ba taa nii ya baŋa ne.

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ko daare Levi dwi tiina balo na ye kaanem tiina ye ba nwoŋi Zadoki diga kam ne to, banto mo yɔɔre ba nii amo wara-jei sem totoŋa baŋa ne ba pa-ne maŋa kalo Isarele tiina badaara bam na ywori ba chwoŋa ne to. Banto mo wó fɔɔre ba twɛ amo se ba taa toŋe a kaanem totoŋa yam, ye ba yeini ba kwei vara lara, de jana ba ke kaanem ba pa-ne. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
translation_verse: Banto ta wó wane ba zo amo diga kam wone, se ba ke kaanem amo bimbini dem baŋa ne, ye ba toŋe ba pa-ne. Banto nam mo wó ke amo boboŋa yam na lage tei to.

english_verse: When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple.
translation_verse: Ba ná yeini ba zo Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone, ba jege se ba kwei gare-fefale mo ba zo. Ko dae se ba zo pei koro gwaaro se ba ma-te ba toŋe wara-jei konkɔlɔ kom wone, naa Wɛ diga kam tete wone.

english_verse: And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
translation_verse: Ba nam ná nwoŋi wara-jei sem ne se ba vo ba yi da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom mɛ nɔɔna bam na gilimi to, ba wó lɔɔre gwaaro telo ba na zo ba maa toŋe Wɛ diga kam totoŋa to mo ba tiŋi di selo na pɔɔre Wɛ ŋwaane to wone, se ba laam jwoori ba kwei gwaaro tedwonna ba zo. Ba ná ke konto, nɔɔna bam bá wane ba dwei ba gwaaro tem se ko pa ba de ji wose.

english_verse: Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long.
translation_verse: Wɛ kaanem tiina bam nam dae se ba cheeri ba yuni, naa se ba yage ba yu-ywei se se ke dedwaaro. Ba nam wó wane ba dɔɔre ba yu-ywei sem ba yage.

english_verse: They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Ba wolowolo nam yé nyɔ sana ye o daare o zo Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone.

english_verse: A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
translation_verse: Ba dae se ba di kadeina ba ma ke ba kaana, naa kaana balo de ba banna na yage daane to. Banto nam jege se ba di Isarele tiina bukwa balo na yeiri baara to yerane mo, naa kaanem tiina badwonna kadeina.

english_verse: Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu dae se o twɛ too yera, kokuri, o ná dwei too yera, ko wó pa o digiri o tete chullu tem seeni mo. Ko nam ná ye o kwo naa o nu mo tega, naa o bia wone dedoa, naa o zembaaro, naa o nyaane, naa o nakɔ ta na wo zo baro mo ná tega, o jege chwoŋa se o dwei kotu yera yam.

english_verse: If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later,
translation_verse: O nam ná dwei too yera, o laam wó kwɛ o tete se o jwoori o maŋe de chullu tem. O ná ke konto o ti, se o daare o pa da yarepɛ kɛ.

english_verse: he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: O laam jege chwoŋa se o zo Wɛ diga kam tetare konkɔlɔ kom wone se o toŋe wara-jei sem ne. Dɛ dem konto ne o wó ke wɛleera saarem kaanem o tete ŋwaane. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own.
translation_verse: Yé pɔɔre-na Isarele tega kam wone á pa kaanem tiina bam. Amo Baŋa Wɛ tete yerane mo wó taa ye ba nyɔn-mage nyem. Amo tete mo yɔɔre a maŋe a pa-ba.

english_verse: Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Ko na ye tei to, wodiu pɛɛra, de wɛleere saarem pɛɛra, de wɛleere jene pɛɛra, de wonnu telo maama Isarele tiina bam na jaane ba tui ba ke amo jeŋa ne to ye banto nyem mo.

english_verse: The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
translation_verse: Abam wodiiru telo na lwoori yiga te ke ye te lamma to, dedaane á Wɛ-teiri pɛɛra dwi dwi wó taa ye kaanem tiina bam nyem mo. Á ta wó kwei mun-bwei delo á na bobo á pɔɔre se á ma á fɔge bworobworo to á pa kaanem tiina bam, se Wɛ swolim taa wo á sam dem baŋa ne.

english_verse: Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_verse: Kaanem tiina ba jege chwoŋa se ba di woŋo kolo na tege ko tete toone, naa vara na jaane-ko ba tore to. Ko ná maŋe ko ye zuŋa mo, naa varem mo de, ba yé di-te.

english_verse: So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures.
translation_verse: Abam ná lage á maŋe wonnu á pa daane, se á kwei bwɛ selo na ye chekke to á maŋe-te.

english_verse: The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná ye kuri delo na bobo chane serepɛ chana kam da fuga-yanu dɛ dem ne to, kuri dento da yarepɛ yam dɛ maama wone o daa wó beeri pɛɛra mo se ba ma-ya ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem, de zwɛɛm pɛɛre kaanem, de wodiu pɛɛre kaanem, se nuga de woli te wone.

english_verse: kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem. Land for Israel's Ruler The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ta pɔɔre-na pwola kalo na ye ka yera to belei, se á maŋe naba-laara

english_verse: The Lord God said: You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Abam Isarele teo dedɛɛra bam, á tiini á pini amo nɔɔna bam, ye á daare á bɛɛse-ba se ko dáane. Nam yage-na vuvuga totoŋa, se á daare á toŋe kolo na ye chega ye ko tɔge chwoŋa to. Á daa yé vere tega amo nɔɔna bam tei ne se á daare-ba á zege bwori. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
translation_verse: Kuriwɛ selo á na wó ta‑á mae á maŋe wonnu to jege se se taa ye chekke mo, ne ko ná ye muni mo á jege á maŋa, naa ko ná ye na mo de. Kuriwaa bia fuga mo wó yi homaa dedoa.

english_verse: The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
translation_verse: Ko ta ná yeini ko yi chana kam da yarepɛ dɛ dem, nmo nam ta wó ke konto dwoŋi mo se n ma n kwɛ wolo maama na tusi ye o wo paale o ke wɛleere, naa o wo lɔre ko ni ne to. Konto maa wó pa se n fɔge n kwɛ Wɛ diga kam chullu tem seeni.

english_verse: Leaders of Israel, the people must bring you one sixtieth of their grain harvests as offerings to me.
translation_verse: Pɛɛra yalo á na jege se á kwei á pa Wɛ to mo tento: Maŋe-na á mena bwɛ fuseredo maama wone se á le dedoa.

english_verse: They will also bring one percent of their olive oil. These things will be measured according to the bath, and ten baths is the same as one homer or one cor.
translation_verse: Á ta wó ma kuriwaa mo á maŋe á nuga kam, se á le bwɛ selei kuriwaa bia fuga maama wone. Kuriwaa bia fuga ye bedwe mo de homaa dedoa

english_verse: But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people. The Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom nam jege se o beeri vara balo ba na wó kwei ba ke zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de wodiu pɛɛra, de wo-nyɔɔro pɛɛra, ne nɔɔna bam ná lage ba di ba kura dwi dwi. Ko ná ye ba chan-doŋa kura, de ba siu da yam, dedaane kura yalo maama Isarele dwi tiina bam na jege se ba di to, wonto mo wó beeri wɛleere saarem kaanem vara bam, de wodiu pɛɛra yam, de pɛɛra yalo ba na wó zwɛ ba pa Wɛ to, de nu-biu pɛɛra yam se ba kwei ba maa ke kaanem ba pa Wɛ se ba le nɔɔna bam lwarem o yiga ne.

english_verse: Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Da yarepɛ yam dɛ maama wone o nam ta wó beeri na-bale serepɛ, de pi-bɛ serepɛ, te maama na ba jege gɛɛ te yera ne to mo, se ba kwei-te ba ke zwɛɛm kaanem ba pa Baŋa Wɛ. O ta maa wó beeri bo-bala se ba kwei-ka ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem.

english_verse: The Lord God said: On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Boboa chana kam boboa dɛ dem ne, se á kwei na-bala kalo na ba jege gɛɛ ka yera ne to á ma á kwɛ wara-jei sem.

english_verse: The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Kaanem tu wom maa wó pwori wɛleere saarem kaanem varem wom jana wone o ja o vo o taare Wɛ diga kam manchwo-nia sɛ sem ne. O ta wó kwei-ba o ke bimbini dem tetare seeni nia yana yam ne, de Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom ni-kaywallo tem ne.

english_verse: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Boboa chana kam da fuga-yana dɛ dem ne, se á di Atɔgebabaŋa kuri dem. Kwei-na da yarepɛ á di-de, se da yam konto ne á ta‑á di bworobworo kolo na ba jege sabɔle ko wone to.

english_verse: On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people.
translation_verse: Kuri dem boboa dɛ dem ne, á teo dedɛɛro wom wó beeri na-bala mo se ba kwei-ka ba ma ba ke wɛleere saarem kaanem o tete ŋwaane, de teo kom nɔɔna bam maama ŋwaane.

english_verse: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo tento: Wɛ diga tetare konkɔlɔ kom ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to ye se á pe-de mo á totoŋa da yaredo maama wone. Ko maa ná yi siu dɛ dem, dedaane chan-doŋa dɛ dem ne, se á laam pore-de á yage.

english_verse: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
translation_verse: Teo kom dedɛɛro wom maa wó zege da-yiga konkɔlɔ kom ne o vo o zo ni dem konto napɔrɔ kom wone se o taa zege manchwoŋo ni dem ne. Kaanem tiina bam maa wó kwei o zwɛɛm pɛɛra, de o yazura pɛɛra ba ma ba ke kaanem. Dedɛɛro wom ta ná zege manchwoŋo ni dem ne, o wó chɔɔle o yibia tega ne se o zuli-ne, ye o daare o nwoŋi da o viiri. Ba nam bá pe ni dem, se tega ná tu ka yi, se ba laam pe-de.

english_verse: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
translation_verse: Siu da yam de chan-doŋa da yam maama ne, teo kom nɔɔna bam nam jege se ba gilimi daane ni dem konto yiga ne mo, se ba zuli Baŋa Wɛ.

english_verse: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom na jege se o ja zwɛɛm pɛɛre delo siu dɛ maama ne o ba o ke o pa Baŋa Wɛ to nam wó taa ye pi-bale seredo, de pi-bea dedoa mo. Tento maama nam bá taa jege gɛɛ te yera ne.

english_verse: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Wodiu pɛɛre delo o na woli pi-bea kam wone se o ma o ke kaanem dem to wó taa ye kuriwaa bu dedoa mo. Muni delo o na wó kwei o woli pi-bale sem ne to nam wó maŋe de o na lage tei to mo. O nam wó woli nuga bwɛ sena mo muni kuriwaa maama ŋwaane.

english_verse: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Chan-doŋa dɛ dem ne dedɛɛro wom ta wó kwei na-bala dedoa, de pi-bale seredo, de pi-bea dedoa se o ma o ke kaanem, te maama na ba jege gɛɛ te yera ne to.

english_verse: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: O ta wó ja wodiu pɛɛre kuriwaa bu dedoa na-bala kam ŋwaane, de wodiu pɛɛre kuriwaa bu dedoa pi-bea kam ŋwaane. Ko nam ná ye pi-bale sem, o wó woli wodiu pɛɛre se ko maŋe de o na lage tei to mo. O ta wó woli nuga bwɛ sena mo kuriwaa maama ŋwaane.

english_verse: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔɔna ná yeini ba jeeri Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne se ba di ba kura yam, se ba na tɔge ni delo ba zo to, ba da ni dedwoŋi ne ba nwoŋi wara-jei sem wone. Ba wolo ná dɛ baŋa seeni ni dem o zo, kotu wó tɔge tega-kuri seeni ni dem ne mo o nwoŋi. Wolo nam na tɔge tega-kuri seeni ni dem o zo, kotu de wó da baŋa seeni ni dem ne mo o nwoŋi.

english_verse: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
translation_verse: Ba ná yeini ba zo da, dedɛɛro wom de maa wó gwaane ba wone, ye o ta tɔge de-ba o nwoŋi.

english_verse: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Ba ná yeini ba jege ba kura yam dwi maama ba di, wodiu pɛɛre dem wó taa ye muni kuriwaa bu dedoa mo na-bala maama ŋwaane, de kuriwaa bu dedoa pi-bea maama ŋwaane. Ko daare ko ná ye pi-bale sem, wodiu pɛɛre dem na woli da to wó maŋe de nɔɔno boboŋa na lage tei to mo. Ba ta wó woli nuga bwɛ sena mo kuriwaa maama ŋwaane.

english_verse: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom ná boŋe se o ke wo-ywoŋo pɛɛre o pa Baŋa Wɛ, ne ko ná ye zwɛɛm pɛɛre naa nu-biu pɛɛre mo, se ba pore ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to ba pa‑o. O maa wó ke o zwɛɛm pɛɛre dem, naa o nu-biu pɛɛre dem, ne ko na maŋe ko ke tei siu dɛ dem ne to mo. Ko kwaga seeni o ná nwoŋi se o viiri, ba laam wó wane ni dem ba pe.

english_verse: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
translation_verse: Zezeŋa maama se n yeini n ke wodiu pɛɛre n woli da. Pɛɛre dem n na wó ke n pa Baŋa Wɛ to ye muni bwɛ setɔ mo, ye n guuri nuga bɔŋa dedoa de wone. Ni dento ba jege se de leiri maŋa de maŋa.

english_verse: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
translation_verse: Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ nam na tage tei to mo tento: Teo dedɛɛro wom ná pɔɔre ba dwi tega kam wone se ko ji pɛɛre ko pa o bu, ka laam wó lɛɛre ka taa ye bu wom de o de kwaga nyem mo.

english_verse: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
translation_verse: Ko daare, o ná kwei-ka o ji pɛɛre mo o pa o tontoŋeno wolo, o tontoŋeno wom wó taa jege-ka o toŋe mo se ko taa nii wonnu yirim bene dem. Maŋa kam konto ná yia, se o tontoŋeno wom jwoori o kwei tega kam o pa dedɛɛro wom, dedɛɛro wom dwi dem mo na tei tega kam to ŋwaane. Ko ye wonto bia yerane mo jege chwoŋa se ba taa tei o tega se ka ji ba nyem.

english_verse: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom daa ma ja-ne pa dé tɔge Wɛ diga konkɔlɔ manchwo-ni dem dé vo dé yi di selo na pɔɔre se zega Wɛ kaanem tiina bam ŋwaane ye se jeeri baŋa seeni to. O ma bere-ne jei selo na yeiri di sem konto wɛ-zoore seeni to.

english_verse: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
translation_verse: Ba déem kwei kandwa mo ba lɔ taara ba kaare konkwallo tem konto, ye ba lɔ mini kura kabiri sem tega kuri seeni.

english_verse: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_verse: O ma ta de amo o we, “Kaligwonnu tento wone mo balo na yeini ba toŋe Wɛ diga kam totoŋa to wó taa saŋe nɔna yalo nɔɔna bam na yeini ba ja ba ba se ba maa ke kaanem to.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom daa ma ja-ne o jwoori Wɛ diga kam ni seeni. A ma nii a na na na bura ni dem kuri ne ba dura ba vei wɛ-puli seeni ba kɛa. Wɛ diga kam yiga déem jeeri wɛ-puli seeni mo. Na bam nwoŋi Wɛ diga kam manchwo-peo tega-kuri seeni mo, ye ba duri ba tɔge kaanem bimbini dem tega-kuri seeni.

english_verse: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
translation_verse: O ta ma pa dé tɔge baŋa seeni ni dem ne, dé bebare dé da pwooni yiga dé vo dé yi ni delo na jeeri wɛ-puli seeni to. A ma na we na bam maa tae fenfee ba nwoŋi ni dem tega-kuri seeni ba duri ba kɛa.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
translation_verse: O ma bwei amo o we, “Nabiinu, nmo nɛ konto na?” O ma pa dé jwoori buga kam buburi-bɛ dem ne.

english_verse: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma ta de amo o we, “Bu-tola kanto duri ka yɔɔre wɛ-puli seeni mo, se ka tɔge bwolo kolo na tigi Jɔdan buga kam seeni to, ye ka laam vo ka kweeli Yɛ naneo kom wone. Ka na bam ná zo dáane, naneo kom na bam wó ji na-ŋona mo.

english_verse: Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Bu-tola kanto maa ná duri ka yi mɛ maama, wonnu dwi dwi, de ywona dedɛ mo wó taa wora. Kokuri, naneo kom wo na bam laam kwɛ ba ji na-doora mo ye ba pae ŋwea.

english_verse: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ywon-jara wó yeini ba zege naneo kom ni ne ba taa jaane ywona. Ko na zege En-gedi ne, se ko yi En-egalayim to, ba wó taa zege naneo kom ni ne mo ba dole ba chworu tem. Ba maa wó taa jaane ywona dwi maama, se ko maŋe de yalo na wo Mediterania naneo kom ne tei to.

english_verse: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye chwaro de bwollu telo na bwola de naneo kom ni to, te na bam bá yɔɔre ba ji na-doora. Nɔɔna ta wó taa nae yɛ te wone.

english_verse: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
translation_verse: Teeni delo na ke bia se nɔɔna taa di to dwi maama de wó nwoŋi de taa zege bu-tola kam bubɛ maama ne. Teeni dem vɔɔro bá kwaare, ye de bá lei bia de ga. Teeni dem wó taa ke bia mo chana maama wone. Kokuri to, na balo na nwoŋi Wɛ diga kam ne to mo duri ba yi-de pa de nyɔ-ba de sui. De bia bam wó taa ye wodiu mo te pae nɔɔna, ye de vɔɔro tem de pa-ba zurim.” Tega kam siseini na maŋe mɛ to

english_verse: The Lord God said to the people of Israel: When the land is divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, the Joseph tribe will receive two shares. Divide the land equally, because I promised your ancestors that this land would someday belong to their descendants. These are the borders of the land:
translation_verse: Pɔɔre-na tega kam á pa á dwia yam maama se ko taa mae daane. Kokuri, amo déem dugi duuri we a lage a kwei-ka a pa á nabaara bam mo. Tega kam nam wó taa ye abam nyem mo se á ta‑á tei-ka.

english_verse: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
translation_verse: de Berota, de Siberayim. Jei sem konto wo Damasika de Hamafa tetare laŋa ne mo. Siseini dem ta wó kɛ de yi Hazera Hatikon, de na wo Hawuran siseini dem ne to.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
translation_verse: Wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem wó taa tigi Hawuran de Damasika tetare laŋa ne mo. De wó tole Jɔdan buga kam, ye de wo Gilead de Isarele tega kam tetare ne to. Ka maa wó vo ka yi Yɛ naneo kom, Tamara teo na zege mɛ to. Tega kam wɛ-puli seeni siseini dem na wó taa ye tei to mo konto.

english_verse: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Tega-kuri seeni siseini dem wó zege Tamara ne mo de tole de yi Meriba-kadese buli-yi dem seeni. De daa ta wó tɔge Ejipti nabara kam ne de tole de vo de kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ni ne. Tega kam tega-kuri seeni siseini dem na wó taa ye tei to mo konto.

english_verse: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Nam pɔɔre-na tega kam á pa daane se Isarele dwia yam maama wane ba na ba de nyem ka wone.

english_verse: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
translation_verse: Abam nam ná lage á pɔɔre tega kam, á wó kwei-ka á pa á tete dedaane veira balo na tu ba zoore de abam ye ba jege bia to. Abam na wó ke tei á pa Isarele tembia to, se á ke konto de veira bam de. Ba de jege chwoŋa se ba tɔge de Isarele dwi tiina bam ba jwoŋi ba tega.

english_verse: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Isarele tiina dwi delo wone veiru ná zoore da, kotu wó jwoŋi tega dáane mo se o taa tei.” Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto.

english_verse: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
translation_verse: Nam pɔɔre-na tega kalo na wó taa ye ka yera to. Tega kam konto wó lɔ siseini de Judah dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko kɛ ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni. Maŋe-na jei sem konto se ko taa ye naba-laara kuni

english_verse: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
translation_verse: Tega kam konto wó taa ye ka yera ka pae kaanem tiina bam mo. Ka baŋa seeni siseini maŋem wó taa ye naba-laara

english_verse: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
translation_verse: Ka wó taa ye Zadoki tiina bam na ye kaanem tiina to nyem mo. Banto yɔɔre ba nii amo totoŋa baŋa ne mo ye ba wo yage. Ba wo sɛ se ba tɔge de Isarele tiina bam ba ywori ba chwoŋa, ne Levi dwi tiina badaara bam na ke tei to.

english_verse: I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide,
translation_verse: Ko na yeiri kaanem tiina bam tega kam konto to, Levi dwi tiina bam wó taa jege ba de popɔra. Ka wó taa ye naba-laara

english_verse: and they must never sell or trade any of this land—it is the best land and belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ko dae se ba kwei tega kam ba yeigi ba pa nɔɔn-nɔɔno, naa se ba kwei-ka ba ma ba leiri woŋo kodwoŋi, ka na ye wose ka pa Baŋa Wɛ to ŋwaane.

english_verse: The city will be a square: Each side will be two kilometers long,
translation_verse: Ko sɛ sena sem maama wó taa mae daane mo: naba-laara

english_verse: The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Tega kalo ta na daare ye ka yeiri pwola kalo na ye wose to ne mo ba wae ba kwei-ka ba du wodiu se Jerusalem teo nɔn-bia bam taa di. Tega kam kadwoŋi wó yi naba-laara

english_verse: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔn-bia balo na nwoŋi Isarele dwia yam maama wone to mo wó taa vare tega kam konto.

english_verse: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
translation_verse: Ko na ye tei to, tega kalo maama na pɔɔre se ka taa ye ka yera to sɛ sem maama mae daane mo. Ka maŋem dem maa ye naba-laara

english_verse: The regions east and west of this square of land will belong to the ruler of Israel. His property will run east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea. In the very center of his property will be my sacred land, as well as the temple,
translation_verse: Tega kalo ta na daare pwola kam konto wɛ-puli seeni dedaane ka wɛ-zoore seeni to wó taa ye teo dedɛɛro wom nyem mo. Ka kayɔlɔ maŋem maa wó taa ye naba-laara

english_verse: together with the share belonging to the Levites and the city of Jerusalem. The northern border of the ruler's property will be the land that belongs to Judah, and the southern border will be the land that belongs to Benjamin. The Division of Land among Tribes in the South The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Konto to, Levi dwi tiina tega kam, de kalo na wora teo kom ŋwaane to maama wó taa tigi dedɛɛro wom te selei sem tetare laŋa ne mo. O tega kam de maa wó lɔ siseini de Judah dwi tega kam na wo baŋa seeni to. Ka ta wó lɔ siseini de Benjamin dwi tega kam na wo tega-kuri seeni to.

english_verse: South of this special section will be the land that belongs to the rest of Israel's tribes. Each tribe will receive a section of land that runs from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. The tribes will receive their share of land in the following order, from north to south: Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad.
translation_verse: Gad dwi dem de wó na popɔra dedoa mo. Ba tega kam wó lɔ siseini de Zebulun dwi dem mo, ko zege wɛ-puli seeni se ko yi ka wɛ-zoore seeni.

english_verse: Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Gad dwi dem tega-kuri seeni siseini maa wó zege Tamara ne mo de tole de taa vei de yi Meriba-kadese buli-yia yam ne. De daa ta wó tɔge Ejipti nabara kam ne de tole de vo de kweeli Mediterania naneo kom ni ne.

english_verse: That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Gates of Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Tega kam konto mo nmo wó pɔɔre n pa Isarele dwia yam maama se ba taa tei. Dwi de dwi maama popɔra na wó taa ye tei to mo konto. Yuu-tu Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo to mo konto. Teo kom manchwo-peo nia taane

english_verse: and so the total length of the wall will be ten kilometers. The new name of the city will be “The-Lord-Is-Here!”
translation_verse: Konto to, laŋa kalo na tigi ka kaare teo kom sɛ sena sem maama to ye naba-laara

english_verse: In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Judah teo Pɛ Jehoyakim paare dim bena yatɔ bene dem ne mo Babilon teo Pɛ Nebukadeneza vei Jerusalem se o ke jara de-ba, ye o kaare teo kom maama o pu.

english_verse: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim and take away some of the things used in God's temple. And when the king returned to Babylonia, he put these things in the temple of his own god.
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ déem ma yage chwoŋa se o di Pɛ Jehoyakim. Pɛ Nebukadeneza ma pɛ Wɛ diga kam zela yadwonna o ja o viiri. O na jwoori o tete teo Babilon to mo o jaane Wɛ diga zela yam o zo o teo jwoni zula diga kam o tiŋi da.

english_verse: One day the king ordered Ashpenaz, his highest palace official, to choose some young men from the royal family of Judah and from other leading Jewish families.
translation_verse: Pɛ Nebukadeneza déem jege nɔɔno dedoa na nii o nakwa maama baŋa ne. O yere maa ye Asepenaza. Pɛ wom ma pa‑o ni se o beeri Isarele tiina bam tetare ne balo ya na nwoŋi Judah teo pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne, naa Judah tiina naduna badwonna wone to o pa‑o.

english_verse: Four of the young Jews chosen were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, all from the tribe of Judah.
translation_verse: Judah teo nɔɔna balo ba déem na kuri to badwonna mo tento: Danyeli, de Hanania, de Misayeli, de Azaria.

english_verse: But the king's chief official gave them Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abednego.
translation_verse: Nebukadeneza nakwa yiga tu wom déem ma jwoori o pa-ba yere-doora. O déem page Danyeli yere we, Bɛletesaza. Hanania yere maa ye Saderake. Misayeli maa ye Mesake, ye Azaria yere leiri de ji Abedenego.

english_verse: Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace.
translation_verse: Danyeli ma ke o boboŋa ne se o yé biini o tete de pɛ wom wodi-laaro telo ba na pɛ‑o se o taa di to. O ma lwoori chwoŋa Pɛ nakwa yiga tu wom tei ne se o taa di wodi-gaa.

english_verse: God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem ma pa Asepenaza lage Danyeli ni taane pa se o duri o ŋwaŋa.

english_verse: But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”
translation_verse: De konto maama de, nɔɔno wom ta kɔre foone de pɛ wom mo. O ma ta de Danyeli we, “Amo tu Pɛ wom mo pɛ ni abam na wó ta‑á di wodiiru telo, de á na wó ta‑á nyɔ sana balo to. Abam ná lage á ta‑á di wodiiru tedwonna, ye ba ba ba maane we á yera ba zura ne á yuudwonna bam, Pɛ wom wó wane o chigili amo ba o de tega ne ko ŋwaane.”

english_verse: The king's official had put a guard in charge of Daniel and his three friends. So Daniel said to the guard,
translation_verse: Asepenaza nam ya le nɔɔno mo se o taa nii Danyeli, de Hanania, de Misayeli, de Azaria baŋa ne. Danyeli ma yi o tei o ta ded‑o o we,

english_verse: “For the next ten days, let us have only vegetables and water at mealtime.
translation_verse: “Pa se dé maane dé nii da fuga laŋa ne se n ta‑n pae debam dwo-vɔɔro yerane se dé taa di, de na-gaa se dé taa nyɔa.

english_verse: The guard agreed to do what Daniel had asked.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma sɛ se o maane-ba da fuga baŋa ne o nii.

english_verse: Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace.
translation_verse: Da fuga kam na yi to, ba ma nii ba na we Danyeli de o yuudwonna bam déem mo nugi lanyerane ye ba jege lam ba dwoi nɔn-donno telo na di pɛ wom wodiiru tem to.

english_verse: God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem ma pa nɔn-donno tena tento yi-poro de yeino, se ba wane ba zamese twanno de swa dwi maama. Ko woli da, Wɛ déem pɛ Danyeli boboŋa mo se o taa wae o maŋe veera de dendwa kuri chekke.

english_verse: At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him.
translation_verse: Bena yatɔ yalo Pɛ Nebukadeneza na pɛ se ba ma ba bere nɔn-donno tem to ma yi. Asepenaza ma ja ba maama o ja o jeeri Pɛ wom yiga ne.

english_verse: The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma ŋɔɔne de-ba dedoa dedoa, ye o daare o bwei-ba bwia. O ma maane we nɔn-donno tem maama wone, Danyeli, de Hanania, de Misayeli, dedaane Azaria mo ke lanyerane ba dwoni wuu. O ma pa ni se ba taa bwola ded‑o ba taa toŋe ba pa‑o.

english_verse: From then on, whenever the king asked for advice, he found their wisdom was ten times better than that of any of his other advisors and magicians.
translation_verse: Ba déem na wora to, pɛ wom ná lage se ba woli‑o de swa, o yeini o maane we nɔn-donno tem konto swa de ba yiyiu kɛ o yi-nara bam de o liri-keira bam maama swa mo kuni fuga laŋa ne.

english_verse: During the second year that Nebuchadnezzar was king, he had such horrible nightmares that he could not sleep.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe Pɛ Nebukadeneza paare dim bena yalei bene dem wone mo o dwɛ dendwɛ dedwoŋi. Dendwɛ dem ma pa se o boboŋa tiini ya daane‑o, ye o ga se o dɔ de ŋwaane.

english_verse: and said, “I am disturbed by a dream that I don't understand, and I want you to explain it.”
translation_verse: o ma ta de-ba o we, “Amo dwɛ dendwɛ mo ye de jege-ne de daana. A nam yɔɔre a lage se a lɔre de kuri mo.”

english_verse: They answered in Aramaic, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever! We are your servants. Please tell us your dream, and we will explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Yi-nara bam ma leiri pɛ wom de Aram tiina taane ba we, “Pɛ, Wɛ wó pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre. Nam ta n dendwɛ dem n bere debam se dé maŋe de kuri dé bere‑m.”

english_verse: But the king replied, “No! I have made up my mind. If you don't tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be chopped to pieces and your houses will be torn down.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma leiri o we, “A boboŋa maŋe ya ja mo de taane dento. Abam mo jege se á ta a dendwɛ dem na ye tei to. Ko kwaga ne, á wó maŋe de kuri á bere-ne. Abam ná wo ke konto maama, a lage a pa ba gwoni abam mo muga-muga se á sam dem de ji di-dwonnu.

english_verse: However, if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be greatly rewarded and highly honored. Now tell me the dream and explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Se á ná tage dendwɛ dem na ye tei ye á ta maŋe de kuri á bere-ne, amo wó pa abam ŋweero de pɛɛra dedɛ ko ŋwaane ye a daare a pa á tiini á na zula. Konto ŋwaane nam, yɔɔre á ta dendwɛ dem se á daare á maŋe de kuri á bere-ne.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
translation_verse: Ba de daa ma leiri‑o ba we, “Pɛ, ko ye nmo ná lwoni n dendwɛ dem n bere debam yerane mo dé laam wó wane dé maŋe de kuri dé bere‑m.”

english_verse: because you know what's going to happen if you don't come up with the answer. You've decided to make up a bunch of lies, hoping I might change my mind. Now tell me the dream, and that will prove that you can interpret it.”
translation_verse: Abam nam na yei we á ná wo tage dendwɛ dem kuri á bere-ne, á maama wó te to ŋwaane, mo á jege vwa á fɔe se á ma‑á gane-ne. Abam boŋe we a lage a leiri a wo mo na? Ta-na dendwɛ dem á bere-ne, se ko pa a lɔre we á wó wane á maŋe de kuri chekke á bere-ne.”

english_verse: His advisors explained, “Your Majesty, you are demanding the impossible! No king, not even the most famous and powerful, has ever ordered his advisors, magicians, or wise men to do such a thing.
translation_verse: Yi-nara bam ma leiri pɛ wom ba we, “Pɛ, nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera tega baŋa ne se kotu wane o ke n na lage se debam ke kolo to. Dé nam ta wo nɛ pɛ wolo na tage o yi-nara, naa o liri-keira, naa o yi-pore-nyena se ba ke nmo na tage tei to, ne o ná maŋe o ye pa-faro tei maama de.

english_verse: This made the king so angry that he gave orders for every wise man in Babylonia to be put to death, including Daniel and his three friends. God Tells Nebuchadnezzar's Dream to Daniel
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ni dem ŋwaane, ba toŋe nɔɔna se ba vo ba go swa tiina bam maama mo. Nɔɔna ma vo ba beeri Danyeli de o yuudwonna bam se ba go ba de ba woli da.

english_verse: Arioch was the king's official in charge of putting the wise men to death. He was on his way to have it done, when Daniel very wisely went to him
translation_verse: Nebukadeneza babɛ sem yiga tu wom yere mo ye Arioki. O na vei se o go Babilon teo swa tiina bam to mo Danyeli yi o yera o lwoori‑o de swa se o lɔre kolo na ke to.

english_verse: Daniel rushed off and said to the king, “If you will just give me some time, I'll explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Danyeli na nigi konto to, mo o yɔɔre pɛ wom tei o vo o lwoori maŋa fenfee se o jwoori o tei o ta dendwɛ dem kuri o bere‑o.

english_verse: Then he said, “Pray that the God who rules from heaven will be merciful and explain this mystery, so that we and the others won't be put to death.”
translation_verse: O déem ma ta de-ba o we, “Pa-na se dé lwoori Telaao Tu Wɛ wom se o duri debam yibwona se o le wo-siseigo konto kuri o bere debam. Konto ná kea, debam bá tɔge de Babilon teo swa tiina badaara bam dé te.”

english_verse: In a vision one night, Daniel was shown the dream and its meaning. Then he praised the God who rules from heaven:
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne mo Wɛ seene o veere wo-siseigo kom de ko kuri dem o bere Danyeli. Danyeli maa tei Telaao Tu Wɛ wom ye o we,

english_verse: “Our God, your name will be praised forever and forever. You are all-powerful, and you know everything.
translation_verse: “Tei-na Wɛ yere dem se ko taa vei wuu! Kokuri, wonto mo ye yeino tu, ye o dam gaale.

english_verse: You are the God who was worshiped by my ancestors. Now I thank you and praise you for making me wise and telling me the king's dream, together with its meaning.” Daniel Interprets the Dream
translation_verse: Wɛ wolo a nabaara déem na zuli to, a tei‑m mo ye a ke n lei. Ko ye nmo mo pɛ-ne swa de dam. Nmo ma‑n bere-ne kolo dé na lwoori‑m se n le to kuri, de n na bere debam pɛ wom dendwɛ dem na ye tei to.” Dendwɛ dem kuri

english_verse: Daniel went back to Arioch, the official in charge of executing the wise men. Daniel said, “Don't kill those men! Take me to the king, and I will explain the meaning of his dream.”
translation_verse: Danyeli ma vo Arioki tei. Pɛ Nebukadeneza ya pɛ wonto ni mo se o go Babilon teo swa tiina bam maama. Danyeli ma ta ded‑o o we, “Yé go ba wolowolo. Nam tɔge a yiga se dé vo pɛ wom tei, se a laam maŋe o dendwɛ dem kuri a bere‑o.”

english_verse: Arioch rushed Daniel to the king and announced, “Your Majesty, I have found out that one of the men brought here from Judah can explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Arioki de ma seene o ja Danyeli o vo pɛ Nebukadeneza tei, ye o ta de pɛ wom o we, “Nɔɔna balo dé na kale dé ja dé nwoŋi Judah ne dé ba ywo-seeni to wone mo a nɛ nɔɔno dedoa se o wane o ta nmo dendwɛ dem kuri o bere‑m.”

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, not even the smartest person in all the world can do what you are demanding.
translation_verse: Danyeli ma leiri‑o o we, “Swa tu tera, naa yi-naro, naa liri-mwa tu, naa yi-pore-nyem tera, se kotu wane o lɔre wo-siseigo kolo nmo na tage to kuri o bere‑m.

english_verse: But the God who rules from heaven can explain mysteries. And while you were sleeping, he showed you what will happen in the future.
translation_verse: Pɛ, nmo na tigi n dɔa konto to mo wonnu telo na wó ke jwa seeni to jaane n boboŋa. Wolo wom na veere wonnu telo ya na seigi to mo pɛ se n lɔre kolo na lage ko ke to.

english_verse: However, you must realize that these mysteries weren't explained to me because I am smarter than everyone else. Instead, it was done so that you would understand what you have seen.
translation_verse: Nam lɔre lanyerane we a na lɔre n dendwɛ dem ya na seigi to, ko dae we amo jege swa a dwoi nɔɔna maama mo. Pɛ, ko ye Wɛ nam mo lage se n lɔre wonnu telo na kare te beeri n boboŋa ne ye te daane‑m to kuri.

english_verse: Your Majesty, what you saw standing in front of you was a huge and terrifying statue, shining brightly.
translation_verse: Pɛ, nmo na dwɛ to, n nii n na nabiinu nyenyego na zege n yiga ne. Nyenyego kom maa tiini ko daga! Ko ta tiini ko nyeena, ye ko laam jege foone dedɛ.

english_verse: Its head was made of gold, its chest and arms were silver, and from its waist down to its knees, it was bronze.
translation_verse: Ba kwei sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to mo ba ma ba mɔ nyenyego kom yuu. Ko nyɔɔne dem, de ko vɔna maama ye lu-nyenno mo ba mɛ ba ke tento. Ko puga kam de ko chwa yam de ye channa mo ba mɛ ba ke-te.

english_verse: From there to its ankles it was iron, and its feet were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: Ko nachere sem maama ye luuru mo ba mɛ ba ke-se. Ko napera yam maa ye luuru de dɔgɔ mo ba gwaane daane ba laam ma ba ke-te.

english_verse: As you watched, a stone was cut from a mountain—but not by human hands. The stone struck the feet, completely shattering the iron and clay.
translation_verse: Nmo na zege n nii nyenyego kom konto to, mo n daa‑n nɛ kandwɛ-zane na fɔge de nwoŋi peo yuu ne, ye nabiinu wo mɛ o jeŋa o sare-de. Kandwɛ dem tete mo tua de mage nyenyego kom ko napera yam seeni de mumugi-ya, luu de dɔgɔ kom maama.

english_verse: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed and blown away without a trace, like husks of wheat at threshing time. But the stone became a tremendous mountain that covered the entire earth.
translation_verse: Ko laam ma pa se nyenyego kom luuru tem, de dɔgɔ kom, de channa kam, de lu-nyenno tem, de sabu-seŋa kam maama mumugi mura-mura bedwe baŋa ne. Vio de ma ba ko kale tento maama ko ja jei ne te ye swanno yerane mo tei, ye kolokolo daa wo daare. Nmo laam ma‑n na we kandwɛ dem na mage nyenyego kom de chɔge to jigi peo-kamunu mo. Peo kom konto laam ma jwoŋi tega kam baŋa jei maama.

english_verse: That was the dream, and now I'll tell you what it means.
translation_verse: Nmo dendwɛ dem mo konto. A laam nam wó ta de kuri a bere‑m.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you are the greatest of kings, and God has highly honored you with power
translation_verse: Pɛ, nmo ye pa-faro mo pwa maama wone. Telaao Tu Wɛ wom nam mo kwei dam dedaane nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ o pa‑m, pa se n paare dem gaale.

english_verse: After you are gone, another kingdom will rule, but it won't be as strong. Then it will be followed by a kingdom of bronze that will rule the whole world.
translation_verse: Nmo paare dem nam wó kɛ, se paare dedwoŋi de leiri. Paare dem konto nam bá taa dana ne nmo paare dem na ye tei to. De de maa wó di de kɛ se paare batɔ tu laam ba. Dento mo wó taa ye channa paare dem. Paare dem konto wó jage de yi tega kam jei maama.

english_verse: This fourth kingdom will be divided—it will be both strong and brittle, just as you saw that the feet and toes were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: Paare dem nam lage de gwaane daane mo, mɛ na bwona to de mɛ na dana to maama.

english_verse: During the time of those kings, the God who rules from heaven will set up an eternal kingdom that will never fall. It will be like the stone that was cut from the mountain, but not by human hands—the stone that crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. Your Majesty, in your dream the great God has told you what is going to happen, and you can trust this interpretation. Daniel Is Promoted
translation_verse: Ko nye de nmo na nɛ kandwɛ-zane delo na fɔge de nwoŋi peo yuu ne ye nabiinu wo mɛ o jeŋa o lɔ-de to. N nɛ we kandwɛ dem konto tu de mage nyenyego kom luuru tem, de channa kam, de dɔgɔ kom, de lu-nyenno tem, de sabu-seŋa kam, ye de chɔge-te mura-mura mo. Wɛ-kamunu kom mo lage se o bere‑m kolo na wó ke jwa seeni to. Pɛ, nmo dendwɛ dem wó seene de ji chega, ye amo de na tage tei a bere‑m to ye ko yuu ne mo.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar bowed low to the ground and worshiped Daniel. Then he gave orders for incense to be burned and a sacrifice of grain to be offered in honor of Daniel.
translation_verse: Pɛ Nebukadeneza na nigi konto to, o ma vwi o yibia tega ne o jɔɔne Danyeli. O ma pa ni se ba kwei wodiu pɛɛra ba ma ke kaanem ba pa Danyeli, se ba ta zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa ba pa‑o.

english_verse: The king then presented Daniel with a lot of gifts; he promoted him to governor of Babylon Province and put him in charge of the other wise men.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom déem ma pa Danyeli na zula lanyerane, ye o daa ta pa‑o pɛɛra dedɛ na tiini ya lamma to. O ta ma kwei Babilon teo maama o ke o jeŋa ne, ye o daare o pa o ji o swa tiina bam maama yiga tu.

english_verse: At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high positions in Babylon Province, and he let Daniel stay on as a palace official.
translation_verse: Danyeli ma lwoori chwoŋa Pɛ wom tei ne, ye ba kwei Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego pa se ba nii Babilon laŋa kam ni maama baŋa ne ba pa‑o. Danyeli tete déem ma maŋe pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne.

english_verse: So all of them came and stood in front of it.
translation_verse: Nɔn-kamuna bam konto maama de dedɛɛra bam maama laam ma jeeri daane ba zege sabu-seŋa nyenyego kom yiga ne se ba zuli-ko.

english_verse: Then an official stood up and announced: People of every nation and race, now listen to the king's command!
translation_verse: Kwor-tɔɔlo ma bage baŋa baŋa o we, “Abam balo na nwoŋi dwi maama ne, de teo kolo maama ne, ye á ŋɔɔne taane delo maama to, fɔge á cheigi-na ni delo dé pɛ wom na pɛ to!

english_verse: Trumpets, flutes, harps, and all other kinds of musical instruments will soon start playing. When you hear the music, you must bow down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
translation_verse: Á wó ni nɔɔna na wó wu nabwanno, de wi, de namunnu. Badwonna de maa wó ta kwanno ye badaara de jege gullu ba maga. Abam nam ná nigi sɔɔ konto dwoŋi, se á ke lela á vwi á yibi tega ne á zuli sabu-seŋa nyenyego kom Pɛ Nebukadeneza na chwi to.

english_verse: Some Babylonians used this as a chance to accuse the Jews to King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Babilon teo swa tiina badwonna ma tɔge keim dem baŋa ne ba vo ba ba Juu tiina bam bebara de pɛ Wom.

english_verse: They said, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Ba déem ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Pɛ, Wɛ wó pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre!

english_verse: And you said that anyone who did not bow down and worship it would be thrown into a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: N ni dem ta bere we wolo nam ná ve se o tiiri o jɔɔne nyenyego kom, se ba dole kotu ba de min-vogo wone.’

english_verse: Sir, you appointed three men to high positions in Babylon Province, but they have disobeyed you. Those Jews, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, refuse to worship your gods and the statue you have set up.”
translation_verse: Juu tiina badwonna nam ba nege‑m kɔtaa. Banto maa ye balo nmo na kuri ye n pa-ba dam se ba taa nii Babilon teo kateira yam maama baŋa ne to mo. Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego mo konto. Ba ba zuli nmo teo wa yam. Ba ta ba sɛ se ba tiiri ba zuli nyenyego kom n na ke n zege to.”

english_verse: Now I am going to give you one more chance. If you bow down and worship the statue when you hear the music, everything will be all right. But if you don't, you will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace. No god can save you from me.”
translation_verse: Tɔ! Boŋe-na á nii á na wó ke tei. Abam daa ná nigi wi sem wum, de kwanno tem tam, de sɔɔ dwi maama, se á vwi á yibi tega ne á jɔɔne sabu-seŋa nyenyego kom. Á nam ná yɔɔre á ve se á jɔɔne-ko, ba laam wó dole abam mo ba de min-vogo kom wone. Á boŋe we wɛ dedwoŋi wora o na wó wane o jwoŋi abam amo jeŋa ne o yage na?”

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's face twisted with anger at the three men. And he ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than usual.
translation_verse: Ba taane dem ma gɔ Nebukadeneza de feiri. O bane ma tiini de zaŋe Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego baŋa ne, pa se o luluŋ-bea chiiri ko ŋwaane. O ma pa ni se ba pa mini dem taa dana kuni berepɛ.

english_verse: Next, he commanded some of his strongest soldiers to tie up the men and throw them into the flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom laam ma ta o jar-keira nɔn-wagela bam badwonna se ba ja Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego ba vɔ se ba dole-ba ba yage min-vogo kom wone.

english_verse: The king wanted it done at that very moment. So the soldiers tied up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and threw them into the flaming furnace with all of their clothes still on, including their turbans. The fire was so hot that flames leaped out and killed the soldiers.
translation_verse: Se ko ná ye nɔɔna batɔ bam konto, ba yɔɔre ba to min-vogo kom na tiini ko di to tetare ne ye ba yera ta vɔge de ŋone mo.

english_verse: “But I see four men walking around in the fire,” the king replied. “None of them is tied up or harmed, and the fourth one looks like a god.”
translation_verse: O daa maa we, “Ko nam ke tɛ mo ye a na nɔɔna bana na kare mini dem wone ba via? Ba yera yam daa wo vɔge, ye kolokolo ba daane-ba.” O ta ma ta o woli da we, “Nɔɔno wolo na ke bana tu to nam nye de o ye wɛ dedwoŋi mo!”

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar went closer to the flaming furnace and said to the three young men, “You servants of the Most High God, come out at once!” They came out,
