translation_verse: Pɛ Nebukadeneza ma fɔɔre o yi min-vogo gwoŋo kom ni dem seeni, ye o bage de kwor-dɛa o we, “Abam balo na ye Yuu-tu Wɛ wom tontoŋena bam to, Saderake, de Mesake, dedaane Abedenego, nwoŋi-na á ba ywo-seeni!” Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego ma seene ba nwoŋi mini dem wone ba yi o tei.

english_verse: And I won't allow people of any nation or race to say anything against their God. Anyone who does will be chopped up and their houses will be torn down, because no other god has such great power to save.
translation_verse: Amo zem mo nam pɛ ni we, nɔɔno ná nwoŋi teo kolo maama ne, naa dwi delo maama ne, ye o ná ŋɔɔne taane delo maama, kotu ná ŋɔɔne Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego Wɛ dem o ja o chɔge, se ba cha kotu mura-mura. O sɔŋɔ de nam wó ji di-dwoŋo mo. Kokuri to, wɛ dedwoŋi daa tera, ye de wó wane de jwoŋi de nɔɔna de yage nenɛɛne banto Wɛ dem na ke tei tento to.”

english_verse: After this happened, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to even higher positions in Babylon Province.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom daa ma jwoori o zeiŋi Saderake, de Mesake, de Abedenego se ba taa tiini ba jege dam ba nii Babilon laŋa kam ni maama baŋa ne.

english_verse: I am glad to tell about the wonderful miracles God Most High has done for me.
translation_verse: A wo pwoli de chwoŋa na tigi ka pa-ne se a ta wo-kamunnu de wo-kenkagela yalo Yuu-tu Wɛ wom na ke o pa amo to.

english_verse: I was enjoying a time of peace and prosperity,
translation_verse: Amo Pɛ Nebukadeneza déem jei a sɔŋɔ ne mo de yazura, ye a wo tigi lanyerane.

english_verse: Then I commanded every wise man in Babylonia to appear in my court, so they could explain the meaning of my dream.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri amo ma pa ni se ba bwoŋi swa tiina balo maama na wo Babilon ne to, se ba lɔre a dendwɛ dem kuri ba bere-ne.

english_verse: After they arrived, I told them my dream, but they were not able to say what it meant.
translation_verse: A teo kom liri-mwa tiina, de ko yi-nara, de ko vora, de yi-pore-nyena na tua amo tei to, a ma ta a dendwɛ dem a bere-ba. Ba nam wo wane de kuri ba ta ba bere-ne.

english_verse: Finally, a young man named Daniel came in, and I told him the dream. The holy gods had given him special powers, and I had renamed him Belteshazzar after my own god.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga seeni mo Danyeli tu a tei ne, ye a ta a dendwɛ dem a bere o de. Amo déem nam kwei a jwoni yere mo a pa‑o se ba taa bwoi‑o we Bɛletesaza. Wa yalo na ye ya yera to jworo maa tɔge‑o lanyerane.

english_verse: I said, “Belteshazzar, not only are you the wisest of all advisors and counselors, but the holy gods have given you special powers to solve the most difficult mysteries. So listen to what I dreamed and tell me what it means:
translation_verse: A ma ta ded‑o a we, “Bɛletesaza, n na ye swa tiina bam maama yiga tu to, a maane we wa yalo na ye ya yera to jworo mo wo n tei ne. Konto ma pa se wo-siseigo tera nmo na yeiri ko kuri. A lage a maŋe a dendwɛ mo se n cheigi se n laam ta de kuri n bere-ne.

english_verse: It was covered with leaves and heavy with fruit— enough for all nations. Wild animals enjoyed its shade, birds nested in its branches, and all creatures on earth lived on its fruit.
translation_verse: Ko vɔɔro tiini te lana, ye ko yɔɔre ko leiri bia dedɛ se tega baŋa nɔɔna maama taa di ba sui. Ga-vara maa tigi tio kom woro ne, ye zuna de sɔ pworu ko nɛ sem yera ne. Wonnu telo maama na ŋwe to de yɔɔre te nae wodiiru tio kom yera ne mo te di.

english_verse: and shouted: ‘Chop down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Make the animals leave its shade and send the birds flying from its branches.
translation_verse: Ka bage de kwor-dɛa ka we, ‘Gwoni-na tei-zɔŋɔ konto á de tega ne. Ta sare-na ko nɛ sem maama á yage, ye á daare á poore ko vɔɔro tem. Jage-na ko bia balo na leigi to jei maama ne. Ta daare á chiŋi-na vara bam se ba yé taa tigi ko kuri ne, se zuna bam de zaŋe ko nɛ sem ne ba viiri.

english_verse: Give him the mind of a wild animal for seven long years.
translation_verse: O daa bá taa jege nabiinu boboŋa, se varem boboŋa mo o wó taa jega se bena yarepɛ kɛ ya daare.

english_verse: This punishment is given at the command of the holy angels. It will show to all who live that God Most High controls all kingdoms and chooses for their rulers persons of humble birth.’
translation_verse: Ni dento nwoŋi wɛyuu malese selo na nii logo baŋa to tei ne mo. Ko lage ko ke konto mo se nabiina maama lɔre we Yuu-tu Wɛ wom mo jege dam nabiina paare maama baŋa ne. O nam yeini o kwei dam o pae balo o na kuri se o pa ba di paare to mo, de nabwona de.’

english_verse: “Daniel, that was the dream that none of the wise men in my kingdom were able to understand. But I am sure that you will understand what it means, because the holy gods have given you some special powers.”
translation_verse: Tɔ. Bɛletesaza, amo Pɛ Nebukadeneza na dwɛ dendwɛ delo to mo konto. A teo kom swa tiina bam wolowolo nam tera se kotu wane o ta de kuri o bere-ne. A nam yei we nmo wó wane n ta de kuri n bere-ne, wa yalo na ye ya yera to jworo na wo n tei ne to ŋwaane.” Danyeli tage dendwɛ dem kuri

english_verse: For a while, Daniel was terribly confused and worried by what he was thinking. But I said, “Don't be bothered either by the dream or by what it means.” Daniel replied: Your Majesty, I wish the dream had been against your enemies.
translation_verse: Pɛ Nebukadeneza taane dem baŋa ne, Danyeli, o yere dedwoŋi na ye Bɛletesaza to, boboŋa jei mo ye ko tiini ko daane‑o. Pɛ wom na maane konto to, mo o tage ded‑o o we, “Bɛletesaza, yé pa dendwɛ dem, de de kuri na ye tei to taa jege‑m ko daana.” Bɛletesaza de ma leiri o we, “Pɛ, ko ya ná ke se dendwɛ dem toŋe n dona baŋa ne, konto ya mo wó taa lana.

english_verse: You saw a tree that grew so big and strong that it reached up to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Nmo nɛ tio kolo na yalese mo ye ko jege dam to. Ko ta yɔɔre ko dɔra mo pa se ko yi wɛyuu kom. Nɔɔna balo na zege tega kam baŋa jei maama ne to wae ba na-ko.

english_verse: Its leaves were beautiful, and it produced enough fruit for all living creatures; animals lived in its shade, and birds nested in its branches.
translation_verse: Ko vɔɔro tiini te lana, ye ko yɔɔre ko leiri bia dedɛ se tega baŋa nɔɔna maama taa di ba sui. Ga-vara maa yeini ba sii tio kom kuri ne, ye zuna de sɔ pworu ko nɛ sem yera ne.

english_verse: Your Majesty, that tree is you. Your glorious reputation has reached heaven, and your kingdom covers the earth.
translation_verse: Pɛ, nmo tete mo ye tio kom konto. Nmo yere dem tiini de zaŋe de yi wɛyuu. N paare dem dam de jage mo de yi tega kam baŋa jei maama ne.

english_verse: Then you saw a holy angel come down from heaven and say, “Chop down the tree and destroy it! But leave its stump and roots in the ground, fastened there by a chain of iron and bronze. Let it stay for seven years out in the field with the wild animals, unprotected from the dew.”
translation_verse: Nmo ma‑n na Wɛ maleka na ye ka yera to na nwoŋi Wɛ telaao ne ka tu ka ta we, ‘Gwoni-na tio kom á de tega ne, se á daare á chɔge-ko. Nam yage-na ko kugu tega kam ne se á kwei luuru de channa á vɔ ko yera ne. Pa-na se ko maŋe da ye ga-zuru de gilimi-ko. Ko na ye tei to, nyɔnɔ mo wó to kotu baŋa ne, ye o de vara mo wó taa zoore daane goa kam wone ba di gaaro se bena yarepɛ kɛ ya daare.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, God Most High has sent you this message, and it means
translation_verse: Pɛ, cheigi n dendwɛ dem kuri. De nam ye Yuu-tu Wɛ wom na boŋe se o ke tei de nmo to mo o le o bere‑m.

english_verse: that you will be forced to live with the wild animals, far away from humans. You will eat grass like a wild animal and live outdoors for seven years, until you learn that God Most High controls all earthly kingdoms and chooses their rulers.
translation_verse: Ko bere we ba lage ba le‑m nabiina tetare ne mo, se n zo gaao ye nmo de kago-vara ta‑á zoore daane. Nmo de laam wó ta‑n done gaao, ne n ye nabea mo tei. Nyɔnɔ wó to n yera ne se bena yarepɛ kɛ ya daare. Nmo laam wó ba n lɔre we Yuu-tu Wɛ wom mo jege dam nabiina paare maama baŋa ne ye wonto nam mo yeini o pae balo o na kuri to di paare.

english_verse: But he gave orders not to disturb the stump and roots. This is to show that you will be king once again, after you learn that the God who rules from heaven is in control.
translation_verse: Ba na pɛ ni se tio kom kugu de ko tega nɛ sem taa maŋe tega kam ne to, ko bere we n ná tu n maane we Telaao Tu Wɛ wom mo seene o ye pɛ nabiina baŋa ne, ba laam wó jwoori ba kwei n paare dem ba pa‑m se n daa‑n ta‑n jege n di.

english_verse: Your Majesty, please be willing to do what I say. Turn from your sins and start living right; have mercy on those who are mistreated. Then all will go well with you for a long time. The Rest of Nebuchadnezzar's Letter about His Second Dream
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, Pɛ, a lwoori‑m se n ke tei a na wó bere‑m to. Yage tusim kikia, se n daare n ta‑n ke kolo na tɔge chwoŋa to. Nam yé ta‑n jege puseŋa n ke de nɔɔna, se n daare n ta‑n jege nabwona yibwona. Kokuri to, konto mo wó wane ko pa se n na yiga-veiŋa n dáane.” Dendwɛ dem jigi chega

english_verse: About twelve months later, I was walking on the flat roof of my royal palace and admiring the beautiful city of Babylon, when these things started happening to me. I was saying to myself, “Just look at this wonderful capital city that I have built by my own power and for my own glory!”
translation_verse: O ma ta o we, “Nii Babilon teo kom na ye teo kamunu, ye amo tete dam-fɔrɔ mo a mɛ a lɔ-ko se ko taa jege lam tei! A nam lɔge-ko se a di a paare ko wone se ko bere a nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ kom na ye tei to mo.”

english_verse: But before I could finish speaking, a voice from heaven interrupted: King Nebuchadnezzar, this kingdom is no longer yours.
translation_verse: O ni dem ta wo to tega ne de kwora na nwoŋi Wɛ telaao ne ka ta ded‑o ka we, “Pɛ Nebukadeneza, cheigi amo taane dento: Zem dɛ dem ne mo nmo paare dem ti!

english_verse: You will be forced to live with the wild animals, away from people. For seven years you will eat grass, as though you were an ox, until you learn that God Most High is in control of all earthly kingdoms and that he is the one who chooses their rulers.
translation_verse: Ba lage ba le‑m nabiina tetare ne mo, se n zo gaao ye nmo de kago-vara wó taa zoore daane. Nmo de laam wó ta‑n done gaao, ne n ye nabea mo tei. Nmo wó ta‑n ye konto se bena yarepɛ kɛ ya daare. Nmo laam wó ba n lɔre we Yuu-tu Wɛ wom mo jege dam nabiina paare maama baŋa ne ye wonto nam mo yeini o pae balo o na kuri to di paare.”

english_verse: This was no sooner said than done—I was forced to live like a wild animal; I ate grass and was unprotected from the dew. As time went by, my hair grew longer than eagle feathers, and my fingernails looked like the claws of a bird.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne nɔɔ, taane delo maama Wɛ na tage se ko vo Nebukadeneza seeni to jigi chega. Ba déem le‑o nabiina tetare ne mo se o vo o done gaao ne o ye nabea mo tei. Nyɔnɔ maa yeini ko to o baŋa ne pa se o ye-daa kam bugi. O yu-ywei sem de déem nwoŋi mo gee ne maao koro to. O ja-fwa de jigi nenɛɛne zuŋa ja-fwa dwoŋi mo.

english_verse: To him the nations are far less than nothing; God controls the stars in the sky and everyone on this earth. When God does something, we cannot change it or even ask why.”
translation_verse: Tega baŋa nabiina maama dae kolokolo yiga da o tei ne. O maa yeini o ke o na lage tei to de wɛyuu malese sem maama, ko ta woli de tega baŋa nabiina de. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno ware‑o se o cheiŋi, naa se o bwei‑o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo n ke tento?”

english_verse: At that time my mind was healed, and once again I became the ruler of my glorious kingdom. My advisors and officials returned to me, and I had greater power than ever before.
translation_verse: A swa yam na tu a tete ne maŋa kalo to, mo a jwoori a na a paare dem a jege a di, pa se a dam de a nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ jwoori a tei ne. A teo kom nakwa de dedɛɛra bam de ma jeeri-ne lanyerane. Amo déem laam nɛ dam dedɛ a paare dim seeni ye a yere dem tiini de zaŋe jei maama ne.

english_verse: One evening, King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his highest officials, and he drank wine with them.
translation_verse: Maŋa kadwoŋi ne mo, Pɛ Bɛlesaza déem bwoŋi o teo kom dedɛɛra moro, se ba jeeri ba di wodi-fɔrɔ ded‑o. Pɛ wom maa tɔge de-ba o nyɔ sana dedɛ.

english_verse: He got drunk and ordered his servants to bring in the gold and silver cups his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. Belshazzar wanted the cups, so that he and all his wives and officials could drink from them.
translation_verse: Sana bam na tu o yia ne to, mo Pɛ wom pɛ ni se ba kwei sabu-seŋa de lu-nyenno zwe selo o kwo Nebukadeneza déem na jaane o nwoŋi Jerusalem Wɛ diga kam ne to ba ba. Pɛ wom ma kuri se o dedɛɛra, de o kaana, de o bɔɔla bam kwei-se, se ba nyɔ sana se wone.

english_verse: When the gold cups were brought in, everyone at the banquet drank from them and praised their idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
translation_verse: Ba jege sana bam ba nyɔ konto mo, ye ba daare ba seini ba wa yalo ba na mɛ sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de channa, de luuru, de dɛ, de kandwa ba ma ke-ya to.

english_verse: Suddenly a human hand was seen writing on the plaster wall of the palace. The hand was just behind the lampstand, and the king could see it writing.
translation_verse: Ba na jei da ba di ywoni pɛ sɔŋɔ kom ne konto to, mo nɔɔno jeŋa pɔpɔ ka pi diga kam kabira yera ne, ka wora ka popone ka tete ne. Pɛ wom ma yɔɔre o na jeŋa kam na wora ka popone to, min-zwoŋo mo na zege da ko pae pwooni to ŋwaane.

english_verse: He was so frightened that his face turned pale, his knees started shaking, and his legs became weak.
translation_verse: Bedwe baŋa ne pɛ wom ma ko de foone, ye o yibia da ka leiri. O nadwoona ma bobo se ya taa mage daane ye o yera maama da ya te.

english_verse: The king called in his advisors, who claimed they could talk with the spirits of the dead and understand the meanings found in the stars. He told them, “The man who can read this writing and tell me what it means will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. He will wear robes of royal purple and a gold chain around his neck.”
translation_verse: O ma pa ni se ba bwoŋi o yi-nara bam, de o liri-mwa tiina, de o yi-pore-nyena bam ba pa‑o. Pɛ wom ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam wolo ná wane o ga poponem dento, ye o maŋe de kuri o bere-ne, amo wó pa kotu na zula lanyerane ye a zo‑o nenɔŋa paare gwaaro. A ta wó kwei sabu-seŋa zambili a de o ba ne ye a daare a pa o ji dedɛɛra batɔ tu a teo kom dam seeni.”

english_verse: All of King Belshazzar's highest officials came in, but not one of them could read the writing or tell what it meant,
translation_verse: Pɛ wom swa tiina bam maama déem ma ba o tei, ye ba wolowolo ware poponem dem se o ga. Ba maa yeiri de kuri de, se ba ta ba bere pɛ wom.

english_verse: and they were completely puzzled. Now the king was more afraid than ever before, and his face turned white as a ghost.
translation_verse: Ko ma pa se Pɛ Bɛlesaza boboŋa maama jei, ye o yibia da ka leiri. O dedɛɛra bam de yu-punnu maama ma vugimi.

english_verse: When the queen heard the king and his officials talking, she came in and said: Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! Don't be afraid or look so pale.
translation_verse: Ka-pɛ-dwooro wom ma ni pɛ wom de o teo dedɛɛra bam sɔɔ kom na zaŋe tei to. O ma zo ba tei ye o ta de pɛ wom o we, “Pɛ, Wɛ wó pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre. Nam yé pa n boboŋa jei, naa n yibia de leiri.

english_verse: In your kingdom there is a man who has been given special powers by the holy gods. When your father Nebuchadnezzar was king, this man was known to be as smart, intelligent, and wise as the gods themselves. Your father put him in charge of all who claimed they could talk with the spirits or understand the meanings in the stars or tell about the future.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno dedoa wo nmo paare laŋa kanto ne, ye wa yalo na ye ya yera to jworo tɔge‑o lanyerane. Nmo kwo Nebukadeneza déem na ye pɛ to, o lɔre we nɔɔno wom konto tiini o jege yi-poro, de yeino, de swa, ne wa yam tete swa na ye tei to. Nmo kwo ma kwei‑o o zege o yi-nara, de o liri-mwa tiina, de o swa tiina, de o yi-pore-nyena bam maama yiga ne.

english_verse: He also changed the man's name from Daniel to Belteshazzar. Not only is he wise and intelligent, but he can explain dreams and riddles and solve difficult problems. Send for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom yere mo ye Danyeli. Nmo kwo déem ma leiri o yere se de taa ye Bɛletesaza. O jege boboŋa lanyerane pa se o yeino de o swa gaale. O maa yei se o lɔre dendwa kuri, de dende kuri, se o daare o maŋe wo-siseigiru kuri jaja. Nam toŋe se ba bwoŋi‑o se o ba ywo-seeni, se o wó wane o maŋe keim dento kuri maama o bere‑m.”

english_verse: I was told that the gods have given you special powers and that you are intelligent and very wise.
translation_verse: Amo nigi we dé wa yam jworo mo tɔge‑m lanyerane pa se n jege yi-poro, de yeino, de swa dedɛ.

english_verse: Neither my advisors nor the men who talk with the spirits of the dead could read this writing or tell me what it means.
translation_verse: Amo nam ya tage a teo swa tiina de yi-nara bam se ba ga poponem dento, ba daare ba ta de kuri ba bere-ne. Ba wolowolo nam ware poponem dem kuri se o ta o bere-ne.

english_verse: But I have been told that you understand everything and that you can solve difficult problems. Now then, if you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. You will wear royal purple robes and have a gold chain around your neck.
translation_verse: A nam nigi we nmo wae n lɔre wonnu telo na seigi to kuri, se wo-chɛɔ dwi maama bugi. Nmo nam ná gage poponem dento n bere-ne, ye n daare n ta de kuri, amo wó pa se n na zula lanyerane ye n zo nenɔŋa paare gwaaro mo. A ta wó kwei sabu-seŋa zambili a de n ba ne ye a daare a pa n ji dedɛɛra batɔ tu a teo kom dam seeni.”

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, I will read the writing and tell you what it means. But you may keep your gifts or give them to someone else.
translation_verse: Danyeli ma leiri pɛ wom o we, “Amo wó seene a ga poponem dem, ye a daare a ta de kuri a bere‑m. Se ko ná ye pɛɛra yalo n na boŋe se n pa-ne to, a ke nmo lei ya ŋwaane. De ko de, Pɛ, ta‑n jege-ya, naa n kwei n pa nɔn-gaa.

english_verse: Sir, the Most High God made your father a great and powerful man and brought him much honor and glory.
translation_verse: Pɛ, Yuu-tu Wɛ wom déem kwei paare, de kamunni, de zula, de nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ mo o pa nmo kwo Nebukadeneza.

english_verse: His mind became like that of an animal, and he was forced to stay away from people and live with wild donkeys. Your father ate grass like an ox, and he slept outside where his body was soaked with dew. He was forced to do this until he learned that the Most High God rules all kingdoms on earth and chooses their kings.
translation_verse: Ba ta ma zeili‑o pa o nwoŋi nabiina tetare ne ye o boboŋa ji ne kago-vara boboŋa. O ma vo o zoore de gaao wo bonɛ sem. Nmo kwo déem jege gaao o done ne nabea na ke tei to mo. Nyɔnɔ de ma to o yera ne se o laam ba o lɔre we Yuu-tu Wɛ wom mo jege dam nabiina paare maama baŋa ne ye wonto mo yeini o pae balo o na kuri to di paare.

english_verse: King Belshazzar, you knew all of this, but you still refused to honor the Lord who rules from heaven.
translation_verse: Ko daare nmo Bɛlesaza, nmo ye wonto bu mo ye n yei wonnu tento maama ni ne. De ko de, nmo wo sɛ se n tu n tete n kɔre Wɛ.

english_verse: Instead, you turned against him and ordered the cups from his temple to be brought here, so that you and your wives and officials could drink wine from them. You praised idols made of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, even though they cannot see or hear or think. You refused to worship the God who gives you breath and controls everything you do.
translation_verse: Nmo nam zeiŋi n tete se n dwoni de Wɛ delo na ye telaao Tu to mo. N ma‑n pa ba ja Wɛ dem konto tete diga zwe sem ba ba ba pa‑m. Nmo de n dedɛɛra, de n kaana, dedaane n bɔɔla bam laam ma nyɔ sana se wone. Á ma daare á seini wa yalo ba na mɛ sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de channa, de luuru, de dɛ, de kandwa ba ke-ya to. Wa yam konto nam ba ni taane. Ya maa ba nae ye ya ta ba jege boboŋa. Ko nam ná ye Wɛ delo na jege dam n ŋwea kam baŋa ne, ye o tiŋi chwei selo n na wó tɔge to, nmo ve se n zuli wonto.

english_verse: That's why he sent the hand to write this message on the wall.
translation_verse: Jeŋa kanto nam nwoŋi wonto tei ne mo ye ka ba ka popone botare sento kabira kam yera ne.

english_verse: Belshazzar gave a command for Daniel to be made the third most powerful man in his kingdom and to be given a purple robe and a gold chain.
translation_verse: Bɛlesaza na nigi konto to, o ma pa ni se ba kwei nenɔŋa paare gwaaro ba zo Danyeli, se ba daare ba kwei sabu-seŋa zambili ba de o ba ne. Ba ta ma tɔɔle we Danyeli laam mo ye dedɛɛro batɔ tu Babilon teo kom dam seeni.

english_verse: That same night, the king was killed.
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne nɔɔ mo ba déem go Babilon teo pɛ Bɛlesaza.

english_verse: In order to make sure that his government was run properly, Darius put three other officials in charge of the governors. One of these officials was Daniel.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom na lage se woŋo maama kwei chwoŋa lanyerane te pa‑o to ŋwaane, o déem kuri nɔn-kamuna batɔ mo se ba taa nii dedɛɛra bi de finlei bam maama baŋa ne. Danyeli déem maa wo nɔɔna batɔ bam konto wone.

english_verse: The other men tried to find something wrong with the way Daniel did his work for the king. But they could not accuse him of anything wrong, because he was honest and faithful and did everything he was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Nɔn-kamuna bam de dedɛɛra bam maama ma kare ba beeri tusim delo Danyeli na wó ke o totoŋa yam wone to. De ko maama de, ba wo nɛ woŋo kolo ba na wó tɔge ko baŋa ne se ba bwɛ‑o pɛ wom yiga ne to. Kokuri to, Danyeli déem yɔɔre o tɔge chwoŋa mo de totoŋa yalo maama o na ke o pa pɛ wom to ye tusim tera.

english_verse: Finally, they said to one another, “We will never be able to bring any charge against Daniel, unless it has to do with his religion.”
translation_verse: Ba ma bwɛ da-tei ne ba we, “Dé ná beeri chwoŋa se Danyeli tɔge da o tusi ye dé bwɛ‑o pɛ wom yiga ne, dé bá na-ka kolokolo baŋa ne, ko ná dae o Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgem seeni.”

english_verse: They all went to the king and said: “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Ba ma zaŋe de ba boboŋe dem konto ba yi pɛ wom tei ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Pɛ Darusi, Wɛ wó pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre.

english_verse: Order this to be written and then sign it, so it cannot be changed, just as no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed.”
translation_verse: Pɛ, nam pa ba popone ni dem konto se n daare n zi n jeŋa tɔnɔ kom baŋa ne, se de taa toŋa, ye de ba gɔe maŋa de maŋa, ne Medea tiina de Peresia tiina nia yam na ye tei ye ya ba leira to.”

english_verse: So King Darius made the law and had it written down.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom ma sɛ pa ba ke ni dem tɔnɔ ne ye o daare o zi o jeŋa ko baŋa ne.

english_verse: Daniel heard about the law, but when he returned home, he went upstairs and prayed in front of the window that faced Jerusalem. In the same way that he had always done, he knelt down in prayer three times a day, giving thanks to God.
translation_verse: Danyeli na nigi we ni dem popone de tigi tɔnɔ baŋa ne to, mo o jwoori o tete sɔŋɔ ne. O ma di o nayuu diga o pore o takworo kolo ni na jeeri Jerusalem teo to o yage jaja. O laam maa kuni o nadwoona ye o lwoori Wɛ, ne o na yeini o ke tei to. Dɛ maama wone, Danyeli déem yeini o kuni nadwoon-kunkuna mo o ware Wɛ kuni betɔ.

english_verse: The men who had spoken to the king watched Daniel and saw him praying to his God for help.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛra bam ma ke ni daane ye ba da ba vo ba jeeri Danyeli sɔŋɔ ne. Ba ma na we o wora o ke wɛ-lworo mo o pae o Wɛ dem.

english_verse: The men then told the king, “That Jew named Daniel, who was brought here as a captive, refuses to obey you or the law that you ordered to be written. And he still prays to his god three times a day.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam laam ma leiri pɛ wom ba we, “Pɛ, ko ná ye Danyeli wolo ba déem na jaane ba nwoŋi Judah teo kom ne ba ba ywo-seeni to, wonto nam wo sɛ nmo ni dem, de n na maŋe n popone-de tɔnɔ ne to de. O ta yeini o ke wɛ-lworo mo kuni betɔ dɛ maama wone.”

english_verse: The king was really upset to hear about this, and for the rest of the day he tried to think how he could save Daniel.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom na nigi konto to, ko ma tiini ko daane‑o. O ma kwei dɛ dem maama ko vo ko yi wɛ-zoore maŋa o kwaane se o beeri chwoŋa o jwoŋi Danyeli o yage.

english_verse: At sunset the men returned and said, “Your Majesty, remember that no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed, not even by the king.”
translation_verse: Dedɛɛra bam daa ma ke daane ba jeeri pɛ tei ne ye ba ta ded‑o ba we, “Pɛ, guli we Medea tiina dedaane Peresia tiina tei ne, pɛ wom ná zi o jeŋa o ni dem baŋa ne, o ni dem konto bá wane de kwane.”

english_verse: So Darius ordered Daniel to be brought out and thrown into a pit of lions. But he said to Daniel, “You have been faithful to your God, and I pray that he will rescue you.”
translation_verse: Pɛ wom laam ma pa ni se ba ja Danyeli ba vo ba dole ba de nywonnu bɔɔne dem wone. Ba na seene ba ke konto to, pɛ wom ma ta de Danyeli o we, “Wɛ dem n na seene yia n zuli-de maŋa maama to mo wó jwoŋi‑m de yage.”

english_verse: A stone was rolled over the pit, and it was sealed. Then Darius and his officials stamped the seal to show that no one should let Daniel out.
translation_verse: Ba déem ma kwei pelɔrɔ-kamunu ba kwoli bɔɔne dem ni. Pɛ wom ta ma pa se ba tiini ba kwoni ni dem, ye o daare o kwei o jafole dem o zi de baŋa ne. O dedɛɛra bam de ke konto ba woli da, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé wane o jwoŋi Danyeli o yage.

english_verse: All night long the king could not sleep. He did not eat anything, and he would not let anyone come in to entertain him.
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne, pɛ wom na jwoori sɔŋɔ to, o vɔge ni mo, o wo na tiini ko chɔge to ŋwaane. O wo sɛ se ba ke kwɛɛra ba ma gane‑o, ye o ware o dɔ tete dem maama wone.

english_verse: At daybreak the king got up and ran to the pit.
translation_verse: Tega na jege ka poore to, pɛ wom gwoni tega mo o vo nywonnu bɔɔne dem ni.

english_verse: Daniel answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Danyeli de ma leiri pɛ wom o we, “Pɛ, Wɛ wó pa‑m momwɛ-dɛɛre!

english_verse: My God knew that I was innocent, and he sent an angel to keep the lions from eating me. Your Majesty, I have never done anything to hurt you.”
translation_verse: Wɛ mo toŋe o maleka se ka ba ka pu nywonnu tem nia. Ko maa pa te wo ke-ne zonne. Kokuri to, Wɛ yei we amo jege bora de yiga ne. A nam wo ke kolokolo a chɔge nmo de yiga.”

english_verse: The king was relieved to hear Daniel's voice, and he gave orders for him to be taken out of the pit. Daniel's faith in his God had kept him from being harmed.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom wo ma tiini ko pwoli de o na nigi Danyeli kwora to. O ma pa ni se ba vaŋe‑o ba le nywonnu bɔɔne dem wone. O na nwoŋi pwooni to, mo ba maane we fufwollu fenfee tete de tere o yera yam ne. Kokuri to, Danyeli déem yɔɔre o ke o wo-dedoa mo de Wɛ delo o na zuli to.

english_verse: He rescues people and sets them free by working great miracles. Daniel's God has rescued him from the power of the lions.”
translation_verse: Wonto mo jwoŋi nɔɔna o yaga, ye o ta pa ba na verem. O yeini o toŋe wo-kenkagela de wo-kamunnu mo, te na toŋe wɛyuu kom wone, dedaane tega kam baŋa ne to. O ma vere Danyeli nywonnu tem jeŋa ne o yage.”

english_verse: All went well for Daniel while Darius was king, and even when Cyrus the Persian ruled.
translation_verse: Konto maama na ke to, wonnu ke lanyerane te pa Danyeli, maŋa kalo maama Darusi na di paare to, se ko yi Peresia tu Sarusi de paare dim maŋa.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: In the first year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had some dreams and visions while I was asleep one night, and I wrote them down. The four winds were stirring up the mighty sea,
translation_verse: Danyeli ma ta o we: “A na tigi a dɔa tete dedwoŋi ne to, mo a déem nɛ veera we vo-dɛɔ tiini ko zaŋe jei maama ne ko dole nane-fɔrɔ na bam ko pɔgele-ba.

english_verse: when suddenly four powerful beasts came out of the sea. Each beast was different.
translation_verse: Jurru kamunnu tena ma zege na bam wone te nwoŋi pwooni ne. Juru maama nam yɔɔre ko ye ko yera mo dedaane tedwonna tem.

english_verse: The first was like a lion with the wings of an eagle. As I watched, its wings were pulled off. Then it was lifted to an upright position and made to stand on two feet, just like a human, and it was given a human mind.
translation_verse: Boboa juru kom nye ne nywoŋo mo, ye ko jege maao vɔna. Amo na zege a nii-ko maŋa kalo to, mo ko vɔna yam gwori ya to. Ba laam ma ja juru kom ba pa ko zege ko nɛ selei baŋa ne, ne nabiinu zega na ye tei to. Ba ma daare ba kwei nabiinu boboŋa ba ke ko yuu ne.

english_verse: The second beast looked like a bear standing on its hind legs. It held three ribs in its teeth, and it was told, “Attack! Eat all the flesh you want.”
translation_verse: A ma nii a na juru telei tu wom na nye de faao na ye tei to. Ko déem gwoori ko zega ko saŋa dedoa baŋa ne mo. Ko maa jege saŋa-kwi setɔ ye se gare ko ni ne. Ba ma pa-ko ni ba we, ‘Nam zaŋe n done nɔna dedɛ ne n na lage tei to.’

english_verse: The fourth beast was stronger and more terrifying than the others. Its huge teeth were made of iron, and what it didn't grind with its teeth, it smashed with its feet. It was different from the others, and it had horns on its head—ten of them.
translation_verse: Tete dem konto ne a na nɛ veera yam konto to, mo a ta nɛ juru tena tu wom ko de na nwoŋi. Konto keim yɔɔre de tiini de chamma mo ye ko dam gaale pa se ko jege foone dedɛ. Ko ta jege yeili kamuna na ye luuru to mo, ye ko jege-ya ko yare wonnu ko dona. Ko maa nɔne telo maama na daare to. Juru kom konto déem ye ko yera de tedwonna tem mo, kokuri to, ko jege nyea fuga mo ko yuu ne.

english_verse: Just as I was thinking about these horns, a smaller horn appeared, and three of the other horns were pulled up by the roots to make room for it. This horn had the eyes of a human and a mouth that spoke with great arrogance. Judgment Daniel wrote:
translation_verse: Amo na zege da ye a nii nyea yam to, mo a nɛ nyeŋ-balaŋa kadwoŋi na tage ka nwoŋi ka wo ya tetare ne. Nye sedwonna sem setɔ ma gɔ se kuri dem seeni, se kanto leiri ka zege sento ya na wo mɛ to. Nyeŋa kam konto déem jege yia mo na nye de nabiinu yia, ye ka ta jege ni se ka taa ma ka ŋɔɔne ni-wɛɛle taane.

english_verse: and flames were dashing out from all around him. Countless thousands were standing there to serve him. The time of judgment began, and the books were opened.
translation_verse: Mini mo yɔɔre de zege o tei ne de foore de nwoŋi. Nɔɔna morro dedɛ maa zege se ba ke o na lage tei to. Kɔgɔ kuni morro fuga laŋa ne de maa wo o yiga ne. Bora borem maŋa kam déem ma yi, ye ba laam puri twanno se ba nii.

english_verse: I watched closely to see what would happen to this smaller horn because of the arrogant things it was saying. Then before my very eyes, the fourth beast was killed and its body destroyed by fire.
translation_verse: Amo déem ta zege a nii mo, nyeŋ-balaŋa kam ta na kare ka ŋɔɔne ni-wɛɛle taane to ŋwaane. A na zege a nii konto to, mo ba jaane juru tena tu wom ba go, ye ba daare ba dole ko yera yam ba yage mini wone se ya chɔge.

english_verse: The other three beasts had their authority taken from them, but they were allowed to live a while longer.
translation_verse: Ba déem nam jwoŋi jurru tetɔ tedwonna tem dam dem mo ba daare-te. De ko de, ba pɛ-te chwoŋa se te ta taa wo ŋwea wone se te maŋa kam ba yi.

english_verse: As I continued to watch the vision that night, I saw what looked like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven, and he was presented to the Eternal God.
translation_verse: Amo ta na nɛ kolo tete dem veera yam wone to mo tento: A nii a na nɔɔno na nye ne nabiinu bu to. O tɔge de wɛyuu kunkwonnu tem mo o vei o beene. O ma vo o yi wolo na maŋe o wora faŋa faŋa to tei, ye ba ja‑o ba vo ba zege wonto yiga ne.

english_verse: He was crowned king and given power and glory, so that all people of every nation and race would serve him. He will rule forever, and his kingdom is eternal, never to be destroyed. The Meaning of Daniel's Vision
translation_verse: Ba ma kwei dam, de nenɔŋ-fɔrɔ, de paare ba pa‑o, se nɔɔna maama sɛ ba pa‑o, ba ná nwoŋi dwi delo maama ne, de teo kolo maama ne, ye ba ná ŋɔɔne taane delo maama de. O maa jege dam se o taa tei nɔɔna taa wuu. O paare dem maa wó taa wora taa de daa bá chɔge!” Danyeli veera yam kuri na ye tei to

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I was terrified by these visions, and I didn't know what to think.
translation_verse: “Amo Danyeli na nɛ veera yalo to yɔɔre ya so-ne mo, pa se a boboŋa vugimi.

english_verse: But God Most High will give his kingdom to his chosen ones, and it will be theirs forever and ever.”
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Yuu-tu Wɛ wom nɔn-laaro tem, banto wó jwoŋi o paare dem ba taa tei se ko taa vei wuu.’

english_verse: I wanted to know more about the fourth beast, because it was so different and much more terrifying than the others. What was the meaning of its iron teeth and bronze claws and of its feet that smashed what the teeth and claws had not ground and crushed?
translation_verse: Amo nam yɔɔre a lage se a fɔge a lɔre juru tena tu wom laŋa kam mo chekke, konto na ye ko yera de tetem tem to ŋwaane. Ko tiini ko jege foone mo. Ko yeila ye luuru. Ko ja-fwe sem de maa ye channa. Ko maa yare woŋo maama ko done ko chɔga, ko daare ko jege ko nɛ ko nɔne wonnu telo ta na daare to.

english_verse: I also wanted to know more about all ten of those horns on its head. I especially wanted to know more about the one that took the place of three of the others—the horn that had eyes and spoke with arrogance and seemed greater than the others.
translation_verse: A ta lage se a lɔre juru kom yuu nyea fuga kam kuri, dedaane nyeŋa kalo na saŋe ya kwaga ka ba to kuri de na ye tei to mo. Kanto kam pɛ se nyea yadwonna yam yatɔ gɔ se kuri dem seeni, se kanto leiri ka zege ya jei sem ne. Nyeŋ-balaŋa kam konto déem jege yia mo, ye ka ta jege ni ka tiini ka ŋɔɔne ni-wɛɛle taane. Ka maa nye de ka jege dam ka dwoi nyea yadwonna yam.

english_verse: While I was looking, this horn attacked God's chosen ones and was winning the battle.
translation_verse: A na zege a nii to mo a nɛ nyeŋ-balaŋa kam na bobo se ka kwaare jara de Wɛ nɔɔna bam, ye ka wane-ba.

english_verse: Then God Most High, the Eternal God, came and judged in favor of his chosen ones, because the time had arrived for them to be given the kingdom.
translation_verse: Wolo na maŋe o wora faŋa faŋa to mo laam tu o bore bora o pa Yuu-tu Wɛ wom nɔɔna bam, ye maŋa laam yi ka pa-ba se ba jwoŋi paare dem ba taa jege ba di.

english_verse: Then I was told by the one standing there: “The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom to appear on earth. It will be different from all the others— it will trample the earth and crush it to pieces.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom ma ta o bere ne we ko kuri dem mo tento: ‘Juru tena tu wom bere we teo wó saŋe ko ke tena ko ba ko taa wo logo baŋa ne. Paare dem konto nam wó taa ye de yera de paara yadwonna yam. Dento dem lage de yare tega kam baŋa maama mo ko done ko chɔge, ye ko daare ko nɔne wonnu maama ko se tega ne.

english_verse: All ten of those horns are kings who will come from this kingdom, and one more will follow. This horn will be different from the others, and it will conquer three other kings.
translation_verse: Nyea fuga yam nam zege ya pae pwa fuga mo na wó nwoŋi paare dem konto wone. Pwa bam konto kwaga ne, pɛ wodwoŋi de wó ba, o na ye o yera de pwa badwonna bam. O wó di dam pwa batɔ bam baŋa ne.

english_verse: “This king will speak evil of God Most High, and he will be cruel to God's chosen ones. He will try to change God's Law and the sacred seasons. And he will be able to do this for a time, two times, and half a time.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom konto wó ŋɔɔne ni-wɛɛle taane o ma o lwɛ Yuu-tu Wɛ wom, ye o daare o bɛɛse Wɛ tete nɔɔna bam. O ta wó kwaane se o leiri kura dim da yam se o daare o pipiri Wɛ nia yam de. Wɛ nɔɔna bam wó taa wo o dam kuri ne, maŋa kadwoŋi laŋa ne, de maŋa kuni belei laŋa ne, ko woli de maŋa chichworo laŋa ne.

english_verse: “Then the greatest kingdom of all will be given to the chosen ones of God Most High. His kingdom will be eternal, and all others will serve and obey him.”
translation_verse: Ba laam maa wó kwei teene delo maama na wo tega kam baŋa ne to paare, dedaane de dam, de de kamunni maama ba pa nɔn-ŋona bam na ye Yuu-tu Wɛ wom nɔɔna bam to. Banto de maa wó di paare taa wuu. Teene maama wó sɛ ba pa-ba ye ba daare ba taa tɔge ba ni.’

english_verse: Daniel wrote: In the third year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had a second vision
translation_verse: Pɛ Bɛlesaza paare dim bena yatɔ maŋa ne mo amo Danyeli daa nɛ veera yadwonna na saŋe boboa veera yam kwaga ne to.

english_verse: when I looked up and saw a ram standing there with two horns on its head—both of them were long, but the second one was longer than the first.
translation_verse: Amo na kwoni a yuu se a nii to, a nɛ pi-bala mo na zege buga kam ni ne de ka yuu nyea yalei na dɔra. Nyeŋa dedoa maa dɔra ka dwoi kadwoŋi kam ye ka saŋe kadwoŋi kam ka nwoŋi.

english_verse: The ram went charging toward the west, the north, and the south. No other animals were strong enough to oppose him, and nothing could save them from his power. So he did as he pleased and became even more powerful.
translation_verse: Pi-bala kam ma yɔɔre wɛ-zoore seeni, de baŋa seeni, de tega-kuri seeni ka duri de dam ka chu vara babam bam maama. Ba wolowolo maa ware pi-bala kam yiga se o che. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na wae o jwoŋi nɔɔna o yaga ka jeŋa ne. Ka yɔɔre ka ke ka na lage tei maama to mo, pa se ka bere ka tete kamunim.

english_verse: I kept on watching and saw a goat come from the west and charge across the entire earth, without even touching the ground. Between his eyes was a powerful horn,
translation_verse: A ta na zege a maane keim dem to, mo a nɛ bo-bala de na pi ka nwoŋi wɛ-zoore seeni ka beena. Ka yɔɔre ka wurigi de baare mo. Ka wurigim dem ke ne ka nɛ sem ba yi se dwei tega mo. Bo-bala kam maa jege nyeŋa dedoa na dana ye ka jeini bo-bala kam yia yam tetare ne.

english_verse: and with tremendous anger the goat started toward the ram that I had seen beside the river.
translation_verse: Bo-bala kam ma vo ka jeeri pi-bala kam a ya na nɛ buga kam ni ne to. Ka yɔɔre pi-bala kam mo de ban-lom, dedaane ka dam maama.

english_verse: The goat was so fierce that its attack broke both horns of the ram, leaving him powerless. Then the goat trampled on the ram, and no one could do anything to help.
translation_verse: A nɛ we bo-bala kam bane dem tiini de zaŋe dedɛ. Ka ma yɔɔre ka dole pi-bala kam ka de tega ne, pa se ka nyea yalei yam bwori. Ka ta ma nɔne pi-bala kam pa ko tiini ko zo ka yera. Pi-bala kam ma ware ka tete se ka jwoŋi ka yage, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno de ware-ka se o jwoŋi o yage.

english_verse: After this, the goat became even more powerful. But at the peak of his power, his mighty horn was broken, and four other mighty horns took its place—one pointing to the north and one to the east, one to the south and one to the west.
translation_verse: Amo ta nɛ we bo-bala kam laam tiini ka bere ka tete kamunim. Maŋa kalo ka dam dem na tiini de gaale konto to, mo ka nyeŋa kam bwori. Nye sena na dana to ma leiri nyeŋa kam konto yuu ne se nwoŋi. Se dedoa dedoa ma jeeri tega baŋa sapɛ sena sem.

english_verse: A little horn came from one of these, and its power reached to the south, the east, and even to the holy land.
translation_verse: Nyeŋ-balaŋa de daa ma zege nye sena sem dedoa yera ne ka nwoŋi. Nyeŋa kam konto ma tiini ka ji kamunu. Ka dam dem vei de yi tega-kuri seeni mo, dedaane wɛ-puli seeni. De ta ma vo de yi te-ŋoŋa kam tete.

english_verse: It became so strong that it attacked the stars in the sky, which were heaven's army. Then it threw some of them down to the earth and trampled on them.
translation_verse: Nyeŋa kam dam dem yɔɔre de gaale mo de vo de yi wɛyuu kom seeni pa se ka kwaare jara de wɛyuu kɔgɔ kom jar-keira. Ka déem ma wane banto badwonna, de chalechwe sedwonna ka dole ka de tega ne, ye ka daare ka nɔne ba baŋa ne.

english_verse: It humiliated heaven's army and dishonored its leader by keeping him from offering the daily sacrifices. In fact, it was so terrible that it even disgraced the temple and wiped out true worship. It also did everything else it wanted to do.
translation_verse: Wɛ nɔɔna bam maa wo ka jeŋa ne pa se Wɛ kaanem daa tera dɛ de dɛ wone, ba na nwoŋi Wɛ kwaga ne to ŋwaane. Ka ma kweele chega ye ka daare ka ke tei maama ka na lage to.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I was trying to figure out the meaning of the vision, when someone suddenly appeared there beside me.
translation_verse: Amo Danyeli na nɛ veera yam to mo a kwaane se a lɔre ya kuri. Wolo na nye de nabiinu to laam ma pɔpɔ o nwoŋi o zege a yiga ne.

english_verse: And from beside the Ulai River, a voice like that of a human said, “Gabriel, help him understand the vision.”
translation_verse: A daa ta ma ni nabiinu kwora na nwoŋi Yulayi buga kam ni ne ka ta we, “Gabireli, pa nɔɔno wonto lɔre veera yalo o na nɛ to kuri.”

english_verse: Gabriel came over, and I fell to the ground in fear. Then he said, “You are merely a human, but you need to understand that this vision is about the end of time.”
translation_verse: Gabireli ma ba o zege amo tei ne. Foone ma tiini de ja-ne ye a to a vwi a yibia tega ne. O ma ta de amo o we, “Nabiinu bu, lɔre lanyerane we veera yanto wora kweelim maŋa kam ŋwaane mo.”

english_verse: and said: Listen, and I will tell you what will happen at the end of time, when God has chosen to show his anger.
translation_verse: O ma ta o we: “A lage a pa se n lɔre Wɛ bane na wó ba de zaŋe se ko taa ye tei kwaga ne to mo. Kokuri to, veera yam n na nɛ to lage ya ke kweelim maŋa ne mo.

english_verse: The two horns of the ram are the kings of Media and Persia,
translation_verse: Pi-bala kam nmo na nɛ de ka nyea yalei to zege ka pae Media teo kom, de Peresia teo kom pwa mo.

english_verse: the goat is the kingdom of Greece, and the powerful horn between his eyes is the first of its kings.
translation_verse: Bo-bala kam n na nɛ to, zege ka pae Girisi teo kom mo. Nyeŋa kalo na dana ye ka wo bo-bala kam yia yam tetare ne to, maa zege ka pae teo kom konto boboa pɛ wom.

english_verse: When these rulers have become as evil as possible, their power will end, and then a king who is dangerous and cannot be trusted will appear.
translation_verse: Pwa bam konto paare dim ná gɛ fee se de ti ye ba tusim kikia ná puli ya su, pɛ wolo keim na chana ye o jege nia yalei to wó ba.

english_verse: His deceitful lies will make him so successful, that he will think he is really great. Suddenly he will kill many people, and he will even attack God, the Supreme Ruler. But God will crush him!
translation_verse: Pɛ wom konto wó ke swa pa se vwa taa daga dedɛ o tei ne. O wó bere o tete kamunim, ye o pɔpɔ o chɔge nɔɔna dedɛ. O ta wó dwoni de Pɛ wolo na dwoi pwa maama to. O nam wó na chɔgem, ye ko dae nabiinu dam ŋwaane.

english_verse: This vision about the evenings and mornings is true, but these things won't happen for a long time, so don't tell it to others.
translation_verse: Veera yalo na tɛ dedaan-ni maŋa kaanem, de tetete maŋa kaanem taane to seene ya ye chega mo. Ko nam wó dáane dedɛ se wonnu tento maama laam ke. Konto ŋwaane, seigi veera yam, se nɔɔn-nɔɔno yé ni ya ŋwa.”

english_verse: After this, I was so worn out and weak that it was several days before I could get out of bed and go about my duties for the king. I was disturbed by this vision that made no sense to me.
translation_verse: Amo Danyeli déem yɔɔre a male mo de a na nɛ wonnu telo maama to, pa se a weele da dedɛ wone. Ko kwaga ne mo a zaŋe wɛɛne a daa vo a toŋe totoŋa yalo pɛ wom na pɛ-ne se a ke to. A na nɛ veera yalo to tiini ya daane-ne dedɛ, a na wo wane se a lɔre ya kuri to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: Some years later, Darius the Mede, who was the son of Xerxes, had become king of Babylonia. And during his first year as king, I found out from studying the writings of the prophets that the Lord had said to Jeremiah, “Jerusalem will lie in ruins for
translation_verse: O paare dim boboa bene dem wone, amo Danyeli maa wora a zamese twanno telo Wɛ tontoŋena na popone ba tiŋi to. A na zamese to, mo a nɛ Baŋa Wɛ na tage kolo de o sampwora Jeremia se ko vo Jerusalem teo kom chɔgem seeni to. A déem maane we Jerusalem teo kom wó taa tigi di-dwonnu yerane bena fuserepɛ laŋa ne.

english_verse: Then, to show my sorrow, I went without eating and dressed in sackcloth and sat in ashes. I confessed my sins and earnestly prayed to the Lord my God: Our Lord, you are a great and fearsome God, and you faithfully keep your agreement with those who love and obey you.
translation_verse: A déem lwoori amo Tu Baŋa Wɛ Isarele tiina bam wɛleera ŋwaane ye a we: “Dé Teiru Wɛ, nmo ye kamunu mo, ye dé tiini dé kɔre‑m. N zege de chega mo n swono kom baŋa ne n swoi balo na swoi‑m ye ba tɔge n nia yam to, ne n na gwoni ni se n ke n pa-ba tei to.

english_verse: Lord God, you are merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against you
translation_verse: Dé Teiru Baŋa Wɛ, nmo nam ye ŋwaŋa tu mo, ye n kwei nɔɔna wɛleera n ma n chɛ-ba. Debam nam lɔge nmo kwaga ne.

english_verse: You warned us and our leaders that Jerusalem would suffer the worst disaster in human history, and you did exactly as you had threatened.
translation_verse: Nmo déem na tage we n wó pa kolo yi debam de dé yiga tiina to mo yi debam tento. Tega baŋa maama ne, teo kodwoŋi tera ko na nɛ Jerusalem teo lɛɛro tem dwi.

english_verse: We have not escaped any of the terrible curses written by Moses, and yet we have refused to beg you for mercy and to remind ourselves of how faithful you have always been.
translation_verse: Lɛɛro tento maama mo tu dé baŋa, ne ko na popone ko tiŋi Moses nia yam wone tei to. De ko de, dé ta wo jaane boboŋa se dé yage wɛleera keim, se dé daare dé lwoori dé Tu Baŋa Wɛ se o ke debam zaane. Dé maa ta wo sɛ se nmo chega kam pa debam yi-poro.

english_verse: And when you finally punished us with this horrible disaster, that was also the right thing to do, because we deserved it so much.
translation_verse: Mo kokuri nmo Baŋa Wɛ laam ti n yiga se n pa chɔgem dento yi debam. N yɔɔre n wo n chega wone mo de n na yeini n ke kolo maama to. Ko seene ko maŋe se dé na waarem mo de wɛleera yam ŋwaane.

english_verse: Our Lord God, with your own mighty arm you rescued us from Egypt and made yourself famous to this very day, but we have sinned terribly.
translation_verse: Dé Teiru Wɛ, nmo tete mo kwei n dam-fɔrɔ kom n vere n nɔɔna bam n ja n nwoŋi Ejipti teo ne. Ko ma pa se n na yere dedɛ se ko ba ko yi zem. Chega to, debam mo ke wɛleera, ye dé yɔɔre dé toŋe lwarem.

english_verse: In the past, you treated us with such kindness, that we now beg you to stop being so terribly angry with Jerusalem. After all, it is your chosen city built on your holy mountain, even though it has suffered public disgrace because of our sins and those of our ancestors.
translation_verse: Dé Teiru Wɛ, n yeini n zege n chega wone de n na ke kolo maama to. Konto ŋwaane dé lwoori‑m se n zuri n ban-lom n na jege de n teo Jerusalem na ye n tete peo kolo na ye wose to. Debam tete de dé nabaara bam wɛleera ŋwaane, dwi-gɛ tiina balo na gilimi debam to laam tiini ba gwooni Jerusalem mo, ye ba ta jege n nɔɔna bam ba lwɛa.

english_verse: I am your servant, Lord God, and I beg you to answer my prayers and bring honor to yourself by having pity on your temple that lies in ruins.
translation_verse: Debam Tu Wɛ, nam cheigi n tontoŋeno wɛ-lworo konto a na jege a ke to. Sɛ a na ŋwane n yiga ne tei to. Dé Teiru, nmo tete yere ŋwaane, pa n yiga jwoori ka taa wo n wara-jei sem ne, se na jigi di-dwonnu to ŋwaane.

english_verse: I was still confessing my sins and those of all Israel to the Lord my God, and I was praying for the good of his holy mountain,
translation_verse: Amo maa yɔɔre a tɛ amo tete de a nɔɔna Isarele tiina bam wɛleera a bere Wɛ, ye a ta lwoori‑o ya ŋwaane. A ta maa ŋwana a Tu Baŋa Wɛ yiga ne, se o jwoori o pa o wara-jei sem na wo o tete peo yuu ne to fɔge se kwɛ.

english_verse: when Gabriel suddenly came flying in at the time of the evening sacrifice. This was the same Gabriel I had seen in my vision,
translation_verse: A ta na wo wɛ-lworo kom wone konto to, mo Gabireli foore de baare o tu o yi amo tei maŋa kalo ba na yeini ba ke dedaan-ni kaanem dem to. A nam ya maŋe a na wonto mo a boboa veera yam wone.

english_verse: For one week this foreigner will make a firm agreement with many people, and halfway through this week, he will end all sacrifices and offerings. Then the “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction will be put there. And it will stay there until the time God has decided to destroy this one who destroys.
translation_verse: Pa-dedɛɛro wom konto wó kwei da yarepɛ mo se o de nɔɔna dedɛ fɔge ba ke ni-sɛɛm daane. Ko nam ná maŋe de da yarepɛ yam chichworo, o wó che se ba yé ke kaanem de wodiu pɛɛra ba pa Wɛ. Ba laam maa wó kwei wo-zɔɔne delo na chɔge Wɛ yere to ba zo Wɛ wara-jei sem wone ba zege da jaja. Ko de maa wó taa wora taa, se ko yi maŋa kalo na maŋe se ba chɔge chɔgeno wom tete to, ne Wɛ boboŋa na jaane se ko ke tei to.”

english_verse: In the third year of Cyrus the king of Persia, a message came to Daniel from God, and it was explained in a vision. The message was about a dreadful war, and it was true.
translation_verse: Bene delo wone Peresia teo pɛ Sarusi na di paare o ke bena yatɔ to, mo Danyeli déem nɛ veera yadwonna. Danyeli yere dedwoŋi maa ye Bɛletesaza. Veera yam bere taane delo na ye chega ye de vei tigura na tiini ka chana to seeni mo. Danyeli na nɛ veera yam konto to, o ma lɔre taane dem kuri lanyerane.

english_verse: I ate no fancy food or meat, I drank no wine, and I put no olive oil on my face or hair.
translation_verse: Da yam konto maama wone, a yɔɔre a ve wodi-ywoŋo dim, de nɔna donem mo, ye a ta ve se a nyɔ sana. A wo mɛ nuga a kwɛ a ya-goa kam.

english_verse: Then, on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing on the banks of the great Tigris River,
translation_verse: Boboa chana kam da finlei-yana dɛ dem ne, a déem maa zege Tigirisi bu-fara kam bubɛ baŋa ne.

english_verse: when I looked up and saw someone dressed in linen and wearing a solid gold belt.
translation_verse: Amo na kwoni a yuu se a nii to, mo a nɛ nɔɔno na zo gare-fefale, ye sabu-seŋa na ye chekke to kila vɔ o teiŋa ne.

english_verse: Although the people who were with me did not see the vision, they became so frightened that they scattered and hid.
translation_verse: Amo Danyeli yerane déem mo nɛ veera yam. Ko ná ye balo maama ya na zege amo tei ne to, ba wo nɛ kolokolo. Veera yam sisiri ma tiini ya pa foone zo-ba, ye ba duri ba seigi.

english_verse: and at the sound of his voice, I fell facedown in a deep sleep.
translation_verse: Amo ma ni o kwora. A na nigi to mo a to tega ne, ye a yibia jeeri tega kam. Amo ma maŋe da a dɔ a beiri.

english_verse: I will tell you what is written in The Book of Truth. But first, you must realize that no one except Michael, the guardian angel of Israel, is on my side.
translation_verse: Nam ta‑n ye konto chemm, se a ta kolo maama na popone ko tiŋi chega tɔnɔ kom wone to a bere‑m. Nam lɔre lanyerane we nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera se o woli-ne jara keim baŋa ne, ko ná dae Mikayeli yerane mo. Wonto nam mo ye maleka kalo na nii á nɔɔna bam baŋa ne to.

english_verse: Now I have come here to give you another vision about what will happen to your people in the future.
translation_verse: Amo nam tu se a pa n lɔre kolo na wó yi nmo nɔɔna bam jwa seeni to mo. Kokuri to, veera yam na wó ji chega maŋa kalo to ta wo yi.”

english_verse: Then he appeared in human form and touched my lips. I said, “Sir, this vision has brought me great pain and has drained my strength.
translation_verse: Wolo na nye de nabiinu to laam ma dwei amo ni pa se de puri. A ma ta ded‑o a we, “Amo Tu, veera yam mo tiini ya pa foone zo-ne, ye a yera maama de te.

english_verse: I am merely your servant. How can I possibly speak with someone so powerful, when I am almost too weak to get my breath?”
translation_verse: A ye nmo tontoŋeno mo. A nam wó ke tetɛ mo se a wane a ŋɔɔne de nmo wolo na ye a teiru to? Nii amo dam dem maama na ti, ye a siu vaŋe ko kɔe tei!”

english_verse: The angel touched me a second time and said, “Don't be frightened! God thinks highly of you, and he intends this for your good, so be brave and strong.” At this, I regained my strength and replied, “Please speak! You have already made me feel much better.”
translation_verse: O laam ma ta de amo o we, “Yé ta‑n kɔre foone, n na tiini n jege kuri n pa Wɛ to ŋwaane. Yazura ta wo n tei ne! Ke n tete n ke daane se n na baare.” O taane dem ma pa-ne dam, ye a ta ded‑o a we, “Amo tu, nam ta kolo na wora to, se n taane dem pɛ a dam jwoori.”

english_verse: Then the angel said: Now do you understand why I have come? Soon I must leave to fight against the guardian angel of Persia. Then after I have defeated him, the guardian angel of Greece will attack me.
translation_verse: O ma leiri o we, “Nmo laam lɔre kolo ŋwaane a na tu n tei ne to na? Ko ná ke fee, amo wó jwoori a vo a kwaare jara de Peresia teo dedɛɛro wom. A nam ná wane‑o a ti, Girisi teo dedɛɛro wom de wó nwoŋi o ba.

english_verse: You also need to know that I protected and helped Darius the Mede in his first year as king. The Angel's Message to Daniel Part One: The Four Kings and Their Successors
translation_verse: Bene dem Medea tu Darusi bobo se o di paare to, mo amo déem kuri se a zege Mikayeli kwaga ne se a pa o na dam.” Teene delei pwa bam jege daane Maleka kam ta ma ta ka we:

english_verse: What I am going to tell you is certain to happen. Four kings will rule Persia, one after the other, but the fourth one will become much richer than the others. In fact, his wealth will make him so powerful that he will turn everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
translation_verse: “Amo laam wó pa se n lɔre kolo na ye chega to. Pwa batɔ daa ta wó zaŋe ba di Peresia paare dem. Banto paare dim maŋa kam ná kɛ, bana tu wom wó ba o jwoŋi paare. O wó tiini o taa ye nadum o dwoi o dwonna bam. O nam ná mɛ o jejegero tem o na dam o ti, o wó chiŋi nɔɔna maama se ba ke jara de Girisi paare laŋa kam.

english_verse: Then a mighty king will come to power and will be able to do whatever he pleases.
translation_verse: Pa-dedɛɛro laam maa wó zaŋe ye o jege paare o di de dam-fɔrɔ. O nam wó taa ke tei maama o na lage to mo.

english_verse: But suddenly his kingdom will be crushed and scattered to the four corners of the earth, where four more kingdoms will rise. But these won't be ruled by his descendants or be as powerful as his kingdom.
translation_verse: O paare dem ná yɔɔre de jeini, de wó pɔpɔ de ti mo. Ba maa wó pɔɔre o paare dem kuni bena mo se de jage de yi tega baŋa sapɛ sena sem maama ne. O bia nam bá di ba kwo paare dem, se de lage de gɔ mo pa se nɔn-gɛ di-de. Paare dem ná pɔɔre konto, de nam daa bá taa jege boboa dam dem dwoŋi.

english_verse: The king of the south will grow powerful. Then one of his generals will rebel and will rule an even larger kingdom.
translation_verse: Tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom maa wó tiini o na dam. O jar-keira yiga tiina bam dedoa de daa wó taa dana o dwoi‑o, pa se o vo o jwoŋi o tete paare o taa di de dam-fɔrɔ.

english_verse: Years later the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom will make a treaty, and the daughter of the king of the south will marry the king of the north. But she will lose her power. Then she, her husband, their child, and the servants who came with her will all be killed. After this,
translation_verse: Bena yalei nam ná kɛ ya ke da, pwa balei bam wó ke ni-sɛɛm daane. Tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom bukɔ wó zo baŋa seeni pɛ wom, se ko pa ba ni-sɛɛm dem kwaare chekke. Bukɔ wom dam nam bá dáane, ye o baro de paare dam ti. Ba maa wó go bukɔ wom, de balo na woli‑o to, de o baro wom, de o bu wom de.

english_verse: Then he will carry their idols to Egypt, together with their precious treasures of silver and gold, but it will be a long time before he attacks the northern kingdom again. Some years later
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne, o wó vere baŋa seeni pɛ wom teo jwona, de ba sabu-seŋa zela, de lu-nyenno zela o ja o vo o tiŋi o tete teo Ejipti ne. Ko maa wó ke bena dedɛ se o daa boŋe se o ke jara de baŋa seeni pɛ wom.

english_verse: the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom, but he will be forced back to his own country.
translation_verse: Konto kwaga ne, baŋa seeni pɛ wom de wó zaŋe o vo o kwaare jara de tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom. Ba nam wó fe‑o se o pipiri o jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: The sons of the king of the north will gather a huge army that will sweep down like a roaring flood, reaching all the way to the fortress of the southern kingdom.
translation_verse: Baŋa seeni pɛ wom bu-baara laam wó ke ba tete ba ke daane ba la jar-keira kɔgɔ dedɛ, se ba ke jara de kuri seeni pɛ wom. Ba kɔgɔ kom wó yɔɔre ba mage jara taa ba vo ba yi tega-kuri seeni teo dam jei sem.

english_verse: But this will make the king of the south angry, and he will defeat this large army from the north.
translation_verse: Tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom wó nwoŋi de bane se o ke jara de baŋa seeni pɛ wom de o kɔ-fɔrɔ kom. O maa wó wane-ba o di.

english_verse: The king of the south will feel proud because of the many thousands he has killed. But his victories won't last long,
translation_verse: Tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom ná nɛ wɔnɔ konto, o laam wó tiini o bere o tete. O wó go o dona morro dedɛ, ye o dam nam bá dáane.

english_verse: because the king of the north will gather a larger and more powerful army than ever before. Then in a few years, he will start invading other countries.
translation_verse: Baŋa seeni pɛ wom wó jwoori o la jar-keira kɔgɔ na daga ko dwoi boboa kɔgɔ kom o ke daane mo. Ko ná wora ko wora, o wó pa o kɔ-fɔrɔ kom konto nwoŋi de ba jara zela dedɛ, pa se ba yɔɔre yiga ba taa mage jara ba via.

english_verse: At this time many of your own people will try to make this vision come true by rebelling against the king of the south, but their rebellion will fail.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam konto ne, nɔɔna dedɛ wó nwoŋi tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom kwaga ne. Nmo tete nɔɔna bam wone nankɔ-nyena de wó kwaane se ba dwoni ded‑o, ba na lage ba pa se veera yam ji chega to ŋwaane. Ba nam wó ga ko ŋwa.

english_verse: Then the army from the north will surround and capture a fortress in the south, and not even the most experienced troops of the southern kingdom will be able to make them retreat.
translation_verse: Baŋa seeni pɛ wom de o jar-keira kɔgɔ kom laam wó ba ba kaare teo kom dam jei sedwonna ba pu, ye ba daare ba wane-ko ba di. Tega-kuri seeni jar-keira bam daa bá wane-ba ba zeili, ba ná maŋe ba ye babɛ tei de.

english_verse: The king who invaded from the north will do as he pleases, and he will even capture and destroy the holy land.
translation_verse: Baŋa seeni pɛ wom wó taa toŋe o fera mo, ye ba bá wane‑o ba che. O ta wó vo o yi te-ŋoŋa kam ye dam wo o jeŋa ne se o chɔge-ka.

english_verse: In fact, he will decide to invade the south with his entire army. Then he will attempt to make peace by giving the king of the south a bride from the northern kingdom, but this won't be successful.
translation_verse: O boboŋa wó ja se o tɔge de o jar-keira bam maama o ba o ke ni-sɛɛm de tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom. O bere o wó kwei o bukɔ o pa pɛ wom konto, se o wane o na chwoŋa o tɔge da o chɔge tega-kuri seeni paare laŋa kam. O boboŋa nam bá seene ya maŋe daane.

english_verse: Afterwards, this proud king of the north will invade and conquer many of the nations along the coast, but a military leader will defeat him and make him lose his pride.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne, baŋa seeni pɛ wom wó vo o kwaare jara de dwi tiina balo na zoore naneo ni ne to mo. O maa wó wane ba dedɛ o di. Dwi-gɛ dedɛɛro wodwoŋi nam mo lage o zaŋe o baŋa ne o pa o teera yam jei, se chaveera jwoori ya ja‑o.

english_verse: He will retreat to his fortresses in his own country, but on the way he will be defeated and never again be seen.
translation_verse: O laam maa wó pipiri se o jwoori o vo o tete teo kom o seigi o dam jei sem ne. O ná via, o wó chɔɔle o to tega ne o jei, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno daa bá ni o ŋwa.

english_verse: The next king of the north will try to collect taxes for the glory of his kingdom. However, he will come to a sudden end in some mysterious way, instead of in battle or because of someone's anger. Part Two: The Evil King from the North
translation_verse: Wolo na wó saŋe o kwaga o ji baŋa seeni teo kom pɛ to de laam wó toŋe lampwoo-jwoŋinu se o fe nɔɔna o la sabu, se o paare taa jege nenɔŋa lanyerane. O de nam bá dáane. O wó ba o te lela mo, ye ko dae jara wone naa vuvuga baŋa ne.

english_verse: The successor of this king of the north will be a worthless nobody, who doesn't even come from a royal family. He will suddenly appear and gain control of the kingdom by treachery.
translation_verse: Nɔn-yɔɔ wolo kuri na dae paare dwi to mo laam wó ji baŋa seeni teo kom pɛ se o leiri wodwoŋi wom yuu ne. Wonto wó kwei swa de ni-som mo o pɔpɔ o ba o vere paare dem o pa o tete.

english_verse: Then he will destroy armies and remove God's chosen high priest.
translation_verse: O nam wó yɔɔre o chɔge jar-keira balo maama na wó dwoni ded‑o to mo, de Wɛ kaanem yiga tu wom de.

english_verse: He will make a treaty, but he will be deceitful and break it, even though he has only a few followers.
translation_verse: O ta wó ke ni-sɛɛm de teene dedwonna, ye ko ye swa mo o ke se o ma o gane-ba. O dam dem wó fɔge de taa daga, ye balo na wo o kwaga ne to de ye fenfee yerane.

english_verse: He will gather a large and powerful army, and with great courage he will attack the king of the south. The king of the south will meet him with a much stronger army, but he will lose the battle, because he will be betrayed
translation_verse: Pɛ wom wó tiini o na baare se o la kɔgɔ dedɛ o ke daane se ba vo ba ke jara de tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom. Wonto de nam wó la jar-keira kɔgɔ kolo na tiini ko dana ko gaale to. De ko de, tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom bá wane o dono wom, nɔɔna na wó baare o kwaga ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: by members of the royal court. He will be ruined, and most of his army will be slaughtered.
translation_verse: Ko nam ye o tete sɔŋɔ tiina mo lage ba de‑o tega ne. O jar-keira bam dedɛ wó te jara wone, ye o kɔgɔ kom maama ba ko jei.

english_verse: The two kings will meet around a table and tell evil lies to each other. But their plans will fail, because God has already decided what will happen.
translation_verse: Pwa balei banto wó jeini daane se ba taa lara. Ba nam bá taa jege boboŋ-laaro ba pae daane. Ba wó taa jege daane ba fɔ vwa se lwarem laam ba. Ba kikia yam nam bá ja kuri, kokuri to, ba kweelim maŋa kam jege se ka yi mo.

english_verse: At the time God has decided, the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom again, but this time, things will be different.
translation_verse: Maŋa kam ná yi ka ti, baŋa seeni pɛ wom wó jwoori o vo se o ke jara de tega-kuri seeni teo kom. Wonnu nam daa bá ke lanyerane te pa‑o ne boboa jara yam na ke tei to.

english_verse: Ships from the west will come to attack him, and he will be discouraged. Then he will start back to his own country and take out his anger on the religion of God's faithful people, while showing kindness to those who are unfaithful.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna wó zege wɛ-zoore seeni ba tɔge naneo kom baŋa de nabwooru ba ba se ba ke jara ded‑o. Konto wó pa se o fom, ye o tutwoni se o jwoori sɔŋɔ. O ta ná wo chwoŋa ne o vei to, o laam wó kwei o ban-zɔŋɔ kom o daŋe Wɛ nɔɔna bam yuu ne mo, se o pa ko chɛ ba yera ne. Ko daare balo na ve se ba tɔge Wɛ chwoŋa kam to mo o yiga wó taa wo ba wone.

english_verse: He will send troops to pollute the temple and the fortress, and he will stop the daily sacrifices. Then he will set up that “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction.
translation_verse: O jar-keira bam wó zaŋe ba zo Wɛ diga kam de ka dam jei sem se ba chɔge-ka. Ba wó che nɔɔna se ba daa yé taa ke dɛ maama kaanem dem da, ye ba daare ba kwei wo-zɔɔne delo na chɔge Wɛ yere to ba zege Wɛ wara-jei sem ne.

english_verse: The king will use deceit to win followers from those who are unfaithful to God, but those who remain faithful will do everything possible to oppose him.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom wó kwei ni-som mo o soge balo na nwoŋi Wɛ kwaga ne to o ke o yera ne. Ko nam ná ye balo na ke ba chega de ba Wɛ to, ba bá sɛ ba pa‑o.

english_verse: Wise leaders will instruct many of the people. But for a while, some of these leaders will either be killed with swords or burned alive, or else robbed of their possessions and thrown into prison.
translation_verse: Yi-pore-nyena bam wó taa bere nɔɔna dedɛ se ba lɔre yeino chwoŋa. Ko nam ná yi yiga, ba wó pa ko chɛ banto yera ne. Ba badwonna wó te jara wone, ye ba zwɛ ba badaara de mini. Ba ta wó zi ba badwonna ba vɔ, ye ba vere badwonna jejegero ba daare-ba.

english_verse: They will receive only a little help in their time of trouble, and many of their followers will be treacherous.
translation_verse: Wɛ nɔɔna bam ná zo cham dem konto wone, ba wó na wolim fenfee yerane mo. Balo na wó ba se ba woli ba wone to nam wó taa jege ni-zɛ ni-zɛ.

english_verse: Some of those who are wise will suffer, so that God will make them pure and acceptable until the end, which will still come at the time he has decided.
translation_verse: Yi-pore-nyena bam badwonna wó to ba yaara yam ŋwaane. Wɛ nam wó tɔge ko baŋa ne o fɔge o kwɛ o nɔɔna bam se ba taa lana jase se ko vo ko yi kweelim maŋa kam. Kokuri to, kweelim maŋa kam ta lage ka yi mo.

english_verse: and worship only the so-called god of fortresses, who was unknown to his ancestors. And he will honor it with gold, silver, precious stones, and other costly gifts.
translation_verse: O nam wó yage wa yanto yam, ye o leiri o kwei wɛ delo na nii dam jei to mo o taa zula. O nabaara déem nam yeiri wɛ dem konto. O maa wó kwei sabu-seŋa, de lu-nyenno, de kandwa-nyenno, de pɛɛra yalo na tiini ya ke sabu to o pa-de.

english_verse: With the help of this foreign god, he will capture the strongest fortresses. Everyone who worships this god will be put in a position of power and rewarded with wealth and land. Part Three: The Time of the End
translation_verse: Dwi-gɛ tiina wɛ dento wó woli‑o se o ke jara o vere o dona dam jei sem. Balo maama ná sɛ ba pa‑o, o wó zuli banto lanyerane. O ta wó pa ba taa nii nɔɔna dedɛ baŋa ne, ye o daare o kwei tega kalo o na vere o dona tei ne to o pɔɔre o pa-ba.

english_verse: At the time of the end, the king of the south will attack the kingdom of the north. But its king will rush out like a storm with war chariots, cavalry, and many ships. Indeed, his forces will flood one country after another,
translation_verse: Kweelim maŋa ná yia, tega-kuri seeni pɛ wom wó nwoŋi o ke jara ded‑o. Baŋa seeni pɛ wom maa wó ja jar-keira kɔgɔ dedɛ se o vo o jeeri‑o de dam. Ba badwonna wó taa dɔge sisein-nɔɔna baŋa ne, ye badwonna wo sisei-torokooro yuu ne, ko daare badwonna yɛ nabwooru ba via. O laam wó vo o kwaare jara teene dedɛ baŋa ne, pa se o chwooli-ba ne na-fɔrɔ na chwooli wonnu tei to.

english_verse: and when they reach the holy land, tens of thousands will be killed. But the countries of Edom and Moab and the ruler of Ammon will escape.
translation_verse: O ta wó ja jara o vo o yi te-ŋoŋa kam, ye o daare o pa se nɔɔna morro dedɛ to jara yam wone. Se ko ná ye Edom, de Moaba, de Amon kateiri delo ta na daare to, teene dem konto wó lu o jeŋa ne.

english_verse: The king of the north will invade many countries, including Egypt,
translation_verse: O dam dem wó jage de yi teene dedɛ mo, ye Ejipti teo kom tete de bá lu o jeŋa ne.

english_verse: But he will be alarmed by news from the east and the north, and he will become furious and cause great destruction.
translation_verse: Kwora nam wó nwoŋi wɛ-puli seeni de baŋa seeni ka ba pa se o fom ka ŋwaane. O maa wó kwei o ban-lom dem o zaŋe o nwoŋi mo se o taa chɔge nɔɔna dedɛ fase.

english_verse: After this, he will set up camp between the Mediterranean Sea and Mount Zion. Then he will be destroyed, and no one will be able to save him.
translation_verse: Ko kwaga ne, o wó vo o chwi o paare nenɔŋa vwoa yam nane-fɔrɔ kom de Wɛ tete peo kolo na ye wose to tetare laŋa ne mo. Ko nam na ye tei to, toone wó ba de yi‑o, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na wó wane o woli‑o.”

english_verse: Many of those who lie dead in the ground will rise from death. Some of them will be given eternal life, and others will receive nothing but eternal shame and disgrace.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo na tege ba tigi tega kuri ne to dedɛ wó jwoori ba bi. Ba badwonna wó bi ba na ŋwea kalo na ba jege kweelim to, ye badaara de bi ba na chaveera de yaalem se ko taa vei wuu.

english_verse: Everyone who has been wise will shine as bright as the sky above, and everyone who has led others to please God will shine forever like the stars.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo na fɔge ba jege Wɛ swa yam to wó taa nye de pwooni mo ne wɛyuu pwooni na ye tei to. Balo na woli nɔɔna se ba taa tɔge chega chwoŋa to maa wó taa nyeena ne wɛyuu pwooni na ye tei to taa wuu.

english_verse: Daniel, I now command you to keep the message of this book secret until the end of time, even though many people will go everywhere, searching for the knowledge to be found in it. The End of Time
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye nmo Danyeli, nmo jege se n seigi taane dento na wo tɔnɔ kom wone to mo, se ko taa nii kweelim maŋa kam. Nɔɔna dedɛ wó taa kare ba vei yiga de kwaga, se ba kwaane ba lɔre wonnu tento kuri.”

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I looked around and saw two other people—one on this side of the river and one on the other side.
translation_verse: Amo Danyeli laam ma kwoni a yuu se a nii, ye a na nɔɔna balei mo na zega ba woli da. Ba dedoa zege buga kam bubɛ dedoa ne mo, ye wodwoŋi wom de zege dedwoŋi dem ne.

english_verse: The angel who had spoken to me was dressed in linen and was standing upstream from them. So one of the two beside the river asked him, “How long before these amazing things happen?”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balei bam dedoa ma bwei wolo na zo gare-fefale ye o yaara o tete nabara kam baŋa ne to o we, “Ko lage ko dáane tetɛ mo se wo-kenkagela yanto maama ke ya ti?”

english_verse: The angel then raised both hands toward heaven and said, “In the name of the God who lives forever, I solemnly promise that it will be a time, two times, and half a time. Everything will be over, when the suffering of God's holy people comes to an end.”
translation_verse: Wolo na zo gare-fefale ye o yaara o tete nabara kam baŋa ne to ma zeiŋi o je selei wɛɛne, ye o du duuri Taa-wuu Wɛ wom yere ŋwaane o we, “Wonnu tento maama lage te dáane nenɛɛne maŋa kadwoŋi laŋa ne, de maŋa kuni belei laŋa ne, ko woli de maŋa chichworo laŋa ne mo. Wɛ nɔn-laaro tem yaara yam ná ke te ti, mo wonnu tento maama kweelim de wó yi.”

english_verse: I heard what the angel said, but I didn't understand. So I asked, “Sir, how will it all end?” The angel in my vision then replied:
translation_verse: Amo na nigi o taane dem to, a déem wo lɔre de kuri. A maa bwei‑o a we, “Amo tu, kweelim maŋa kam lage ka guri tetɛ mo?”

english_verse: Daniel, go about your business, because the meaning of this message will remain secret until the end of time.
translation_verse: O de ma leiri-ne o we: “Danyeli, pa dé tiŋi taane dem, kokuri to, taane dento laam kwoli mo pa se de seigi se ko taa nii kweelim maŋa kam.

english_verse: Many people will have their hearts and lives made pure and clean, but those who are evil will keep on being evil and never understand. Only the wise will understand.
translation_verse: Cham maŋa kam wó pa se nɔɔna dedɛ fɔge ba kwɛ mo se ba taa lana jase. Puseŋ-nyena maa wó taa vei yiga ba ke ba kikia, ye ba bá ni wonnu tento kuri. Balo na jege Wɛ swa yam to yerane mo wó ni te kuri.

english_verse: So, Daniel, be faithful until the end! You will rest, and at the end of time, you will rise from death to receive your reward.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye nmo Danyeli, yɔɔre n ta‑n vei de yazura se ko yi n kweelim maŋa. N momwɛ wó ba de ti. Nmo nam ta wó jwoori n bi kweelim maŋa kam ne se n jwoŋi ŋweero telo na tigi te cheigi‑m to.”

english_verse: I am Hosea son of Beeri. When Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah, and when Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel, the Lord spoke this message to me. Hosea's Family
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ kwora kalo o na pɛ Beeri bu Hosea to mo tento. Ko maa ye maŋa kalo Yuzia, de Jotam, de Ahaz, de Hezekia déem na saŋe daane ba di Judah teo paare to mo. Maŋa kam konto ne Jehoasa bu Jeroboam de déem di paare Isarele teo kom ne. Hosea kaane de o bia taane

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Hosea, name your son Jezreel, because I will soon punish the descendants of King Jehu of Israel for the murders he committed in Jezreel Valley. I will destroy his kingdom,
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Hosea o we, “Pa bu wom yere we ‘Jezerele’. Kokuri to, ko bá dáane a lage a pa cham yɔɔre de yi Jehu dwi dem de wonto déem na tiini o toŋe nɔn-gora totoŋa Jezerele teo kom ne tei to ŋwaane. Konto baŋa ne amo wó pa se o dwi dem paare ti Isarele teo kom ne.

english_verse: and in Jezreel Valley I will break the power of Israel.”
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne a lage a chɔge Isarele jar-keira bam mo de ba dam maama Jezerele bwolo kom ne.”

english_verse: Later, Gomer had a daughter, and the Lord said, “Name her Lo-Ruhamah, because I will no longer have mercy and forgive Israel.
translation_verse: Gomera daa ma ja puga ye o lo bukɔ. Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Hosea o we, “Pa bu wom yere we ‘Lo-Ruhama’. Kokuri to, amo daa bá taa jege Isarele dwi tiina bam swono. A daa bá yage ba wɛleera a ma chɛ-ba.

english_verse: But I am the Lord God of Judah, and I will have mercy and save Judah by my own power—not by wars and arrows or swords and cavalry.”
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Judah dwi tiina bam, amo wó taa jege ba swono ye a jwoŋi-ba a yage ba cham wone. Amo wolo na ye ba Tu Baŋa Wɛ wom to mo wó jwoŋi-ba, ye ko dae ba jara zela ŋwaane, naa ba sisein-nɔɔna ŋwaane, naa balo na yei jara keim chekke to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: After Gomer had stopped nursing Lo-Ruhamah, she had another son.
translation_verse: Gomera bukɔ wom na waare o tu tega to, o daa ma kwei puga o lo bakeira kadwoŋi.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Name him Lo-Ammi, because these people are not mine, and I am not their God.” Hope for Israel
translation_verse: Baŋa Wɛ ma ta de Hosea o we, “Pa bu wom yere we ‘Lo-Ammi’. Kokuri to, abam daa seene á dae amo nɔɔna. Amo de maa dae abam de Wɛ.” Isarele tiina wó jwoori ba na verem

english_verse: Someday it will be impossible to count the people of Israel, because there will be as many of them as there are grains of sand along the seashore. They are now called “Not My People,” but in the future they will be called “Children of the Living God.”
translation_verse: Ko jwa na wó taa ye tei to, Isarele tiina bam wó puli ba taa daga dedɛ ne naneo ni kasolo bia na daga tei to, ye nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o ga o lɔre ba ni na mae tei. Ko ná ye jeiga kalo Wɛ ya na tage de-ba we, ba dae o nɔɔna to, jeiga kam konto ne nɔɔ, o wó ta de-ba we, “Abam ye Ŋwea Tu Wɛ wom bia mo.”

english_verse: Israel and Judah will unite and choose one leader. Then they will take back their land, and this will be a great day for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto ne, Judah tiina bam de Isarele tiina bam wó jwoori ba ke daane, kɔgɔ dedoa. Ba wó kuri yuu tu dedoa ba wone se o taa nii-ba. Ba wó taa tei ba tega kam de yazura. Chega to, Jezerele dɛ dem konto wó taa ye dɛ-kamunu.

english_verse: So let your brothers be called “My People” and your sisters be called “Shown Mercy.” The Lord Promises To Punish Israel
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane, á wó bwoŋi á chorro Isarele tiina bam we, ‘A nɔɔna’, de ‘A bu-swonnu’. Isarele tiina na ke ba chɔge tei to

english_verse: Accuse! Accuse your mother! She is no longer my wife, and now I, the Lord, am not her husband. Beg her to give up prostitution and stop being unfaithful,
translation_verse: A bia bam, bwɛ-na á nu wom! Taane wora debam laŋa ne. O daa dae amo kaane wom chekke. Amo de daa dae o baro wom. Kwoori-o-na se o yage o kabwoŋa kikia yam, se o daa yé taa kare o chɔge o tete de baara.

english_verse: or I will strip her naked like the day she was born. I will make her barren like a desert, and she will die of thirst.
translation_verse: O ná wo sɛ se o ke konto, a wó choore o yera zela a daare‑o, ne o nu de o kwo na loge‑o tei to. A ta wó pa o ŋwea taa ye kafɛ, ne te-kora na tigi ye na tera tei to mo. Konto baŋa ne mo na-nyɔm wó go‑o.

english_verse: You children are the result of her unfaithfulness, and I'll show you no pity.
translation_verse: Amo bá taa jege o bia bam ŋwaŋa, o na tole o lo-ba to ŋwaane.

english_verse: Your mother was unfaithful. She was disgraceful and said, “I'll run after my lovers. Everything comes from them— my food and drink, my linen and wool, my olive oil and wine.”
translation_verse: Ba nu wom ywori o baro wom kwaga ne. O ma lo o bia bam de chaveera. O maa we, “A wó nwoŋi a vo a bɔɔla bam tei. Ko ná ye wodiu, de na, de gwaaro, de nuga, de sana de, banto wó ke ba pa-ne.”

english_verse: She didn't know that her grain, wine, and olive oil were gifts from me, as were the gold and silver she used in worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: O nam wo ke o boboŋa ne we ko ye amo mo pɛ‑o mena yam, de sa-doora bam, de nuga kam. A ta ma pa‑o lu-nyenno de sabu-seŋa dedɛ, ye o kwei-te o ma zuli Baal jwona yam.

english_verse: Then I'll strip her naked in the sight of her lovers. No one can rescue her.
translation_verse: A ta wó choore o teiŋa zela a daare‑o, pa se o di o chaveera o bɔɔla bam yiga ne. Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o jwoŋi‑o amo jeŋa ne o yage.

english_verse: She said, “My lovers gave me vineyards and fig trees as payment for sex.” Now I, the Lord, will ruin her vineyards and fig trees; they will become clumps of weeds eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye Vini teeni dem, dedaane kaporro tem o bɔɔla bam na pɛ‑o to, a lage a chɔge-te mo. O tage o we, te ye ŋweero telo o na jwoŋi o baara bam tei ne kabwoŋa ŋwaane to mo. Amo nam wó pa se o kare sem konto ji goa. Kago-vara wó taa tui ba di teeni dem.

english_verse: I'll punish her for the days she worshiped Baal and burned incense to him. I'll punish her for the times she forgot about me and wore jewelry and rings to attract her lovers. I, the Lord, have spoken! The Lord Will Help Israel
translation_verse: A wó waare‑o de o na zwɛ talwoŋ-ywoŋa o ke kaanem o pa Baal jwona yam ya zula da yam ne to ŋwaane. O maa yeini o kwɛ o tete de zambila, de jafola se o ma tɔge o bɔɔla bam kwaga. O na ke tei maama to, o yɔɔre o swei amo swia mo. Baŋa Wɛ na tage tei to mo konto.

english_verse: Israel, I, the Lord, will lure you into the desert and speak gently to you.
