translation_verse: Ba ma tɔge naneo kom wo ba vo ba yi Efesia. Pɔɔl ma yage Pirisila de Akwila dáane. O ma vo o zo Juu tiina jeerim diga kam o ŋɔɔne de-ba.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Ba badwonna ma lwoori‑o se o maŋe ba tei ne se ko dáane fee. O maa wo sɛ.

english_verse: He told them goodbye and said, “If God lets me, I will come back.”
translation_verse: O ma bane-ba ye o ta o we, “Wɛ ná sɛ, amo wó jwoori a ba a na abam.” O daa ma zo nabworo Efesia ne o kɛ.

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: O ma dáane da da fenfee ye o laam zaŋe o kɛ. O ma vo o tole Galatia de Firijia teene dem wone, ye o pa se Yezu tɔgena bam maama fɔge ba zege de dam.

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Juu tu wodwoŋi déem mo wora, o yere mo Apolo. Ba loge‑o Alɛzandaria ne mo. Pɔɔl na kɛ to, wonto ma ba Efesia. O déem ye wolo na wae taane o ŋɔɔne pore-pore mo. O maa kwori o yei Wɛ tɔnɔ kom wonnu tem maama lanyerane.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna déem maŋe ba bere‑o dé Teiru wom chega kam na ye tei to. O maa wora o bere nɔɔna de o wo maama se o pa ba lɔre Yezu wonnu maama chekke. Ko nam ná ye nɔɔna na jwoŋi sɛɛm Wɛ ŋwaane tei to, o lɔre Jɔn yerane sɛɛm dem dwi mo.

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: O ma bobo se o taa ŋɔɔne Wɛ chega kam de baare Juu tiina jeerim diga kam ne. Pirisila de Akwila ma ba ba lɔre o berem dem na ye tei to. Ba ma pa o tɔge o zoore de-ba, ye ba fɔge ba maŋe Wɛ chwoŋa na ye tei to chekke ba bere‑o.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Apolo laam ma boŋe se o nwoŋi Efesia ne o kɛ o vo Akaya. Yezu nɔɔna bam ma pu o boboŋa yam kwaga. Ba ma popone tɔnɔ se ba pa Yezu tɔgena balo na wo Akaya ne to ba ta-ba se ba fɔge ba jeeri‑o lanyerane. O ma seene o zaŋe o kɛ. O na yi Akaya to, o ma tiini o woli balo na dɛ Wɛ zaane dem ŋwaane ba ke ba wo-dedoa de Yezu to.

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: O ma kwaane o ŋɔɔne de Juu tiina bam nɔɔna maama yiga ne, ye o mage ni-kantɔgɔ o wane-ba, de o na mɛ Wɛ tɔnɔ kom o bere-ba we Yezu seene o ye Wɛ Dam Tu wom to.

english_verse: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Apolo déem ta na wo Korinti ne to, Pɔɔl ma zaŋe o beeri o tɔge teene dem tetare o vo o yi Efesia. O na yi da to, o ma na Wɛ chwoŋa tɔgena badwonna,

english_verse: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: ye o bwei-ba o we, “Abam na tu á sɛ Wɛ to, á jwoŋi Wɛ Sin-laao kom na?” Ba ma leiri‑o ba we, “Aawo, dé ta wo maŋe dé lɔre we Wɛ Sin-laao wora.”

english_verse: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl laam ma ta o we, “Ko ná ye Jɔn nyem dem, wonto déem bere nɔɔna se ba leiri ba wo de ba keim-balwaaro tem, se ba daare ba jwoŋi sɛɛm Wɛ ŋwaane mo. O ma ta de nɔɔna bam se ba ke ba wo-dedoa de wolo wom na wó saŋe o kwaga o ba to. Yezu mo konto.”

english_verse: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na nigi konto to, ba ma jwoŋi sɛɛm dé Teiru Yezu yere ŋwaane.

english_verse: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma zi zi o jea ba baŋa ne. Wɛ Sin-laao kom laam ma ba ba tei. Ba ma ŋɔɔne ta-gɛ dwi dwi ye ba daare ba pworisi Wɛ kwora kam.

english_verse: There were about twelve men in this group.
translation_verse: Ba maama ye nenɛɛne baara fuga-balei mo.

english_verse: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
translation_verse: Pɔɔl déem ma ke chane setɔ Efesia ne. O maa yeini o vei o zoore Juu tiina jeerim diga kam o ŋɔɔne de baare o bere-ba. O ma kwaane o mage ni-kantɔgɔ de-ba se o pa ba lɔre Wɛ paare dem na ye tei to.

english_verse: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam badwonna ma se ba zwa, ye ba ve se ba sɛ o taane dem. Ba maa jege dé Teiru wom chwoŋa kam tɔgem ba yaala nɔɔna bam maama yiga ne. Pɔɔl ma viiri o daare-ba. O ma pwɛ balo na sɛ ba tɔge Yezu to o yage o tei ne. Dɛ maama o maa yeini o ŋɔɔne o bere nɔɔna Tiranus zamesem diga kam ne.

english_verse: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
translation_verse: Ko ma ke konto dwoŋi taa, bena yalei. Ko ma pa se nɔɔna balo maama na zoore Asia teene dem ne to ba ba ni dé Teiru wom taane dem, Juu tiina de dwi-gɛ tiina de.

english_verse: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
translation_verse: Wɛ déem tɔge Pɔɔl jeŋa mo o ma ke wo-kenkagela yalo dwoŋi na maŋe ya tera to.

english_verse: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
translation_verse: Ko déem na ke tei to, nɔɔna wó kwei gare-bia naa totoŋa gwaaro telo Pɔɔl tete na zo o daare to ba ja vo ba pa jaweena pa ba na yazura, ye chichiri de yage-ba.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Juu tiina badwonna de maa wora ba na yeini ba beeri ba zeili chichiri nɔɔna tei ne. Banto de déem ma kwaane se ba tɔge dé Teiru Yezu yere ŋwaane mo ba ke konto. Ba maa yeini ba tɛ de chichiri sem we, “Yezu wolo Pɔɔl na bere o taane to yere ŋwaane mo amo tɛ abam se á viiri.”

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Chichira kadwoŋi laam ma ta de-ba ka we, “Amo maŋe a yei Yezu. Amo yei Pɔɔl de ni ne. Se abam ye bera mo?”

english_verse: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wom chichira kam na tɔge‑o to laam ma zaŋe o puuri-ba. O ma wane-ba pa ba maama duri ba nwoŋi o sɔŋɔ kom ne de kuri-nɔrɔ, ye ba yera jege fufwollu.

english_verse: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo maama na zoore Efesia ne to ma lɔre konto na ke to, Juu tiina de dwi-gɛ tiina maama. Foone ma zo-ba dedɛ. Ko ma pa se dé Teiru Yezu yere tiini de zaŋe de zula.

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo na tu ba sɛ Yezu to dedɛ ma zaŋe ba zege nɔɔna yiga ne ba ta ba bere jaja ba na ke ba chɔge tei to.

english_verse: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
translation_verse: Dé Teiru wom na bere o dam konto dwoŋi to ma pa se o taane dem fɔge de jage jei maama ye nɔɔna sɛ-de.

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Wonnu tento déem na ke te kɛ to, Pɔɔl boboŋa ma ja se o beeri o tɔge Makedonia de Akaya wo se o laam kɛ o vo Jerusalem. O ma boŋe o we, “Amo ná vei a wo Jerusalem ne, a jege se a daare a vo Rom mo de.”

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: O ma toŋe nɔɔna balei se ba da yiga ba vo Makedonia. Banto maa ye Timoti de Erasitu, ba na tɔge ba toŋe ba pa‑o to. O tete ma maŋe Asia ne se ko dáane fee.

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: Da yam konto ne mo lɛɛro dedɛ tua dé Teiru Yezu chwoŋa kam ŋwaane.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wodwoŋi déem mo wo Efesia ne, o yere mo Demetiru. O ye gɔgɔ mo ye o mae lu-nyenno o mɔɔne kamwaro pa te nye de diga kalo ba na zuli ba wɛ Atamisa ka wone to. O totoŋa yam maa jaane nyɔɔre dedɛ ya pae o gɔ-bia bam.

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Abam nam nɛa ye á kwori á ni nɔɔno wonto Pɔɔl na ke tei to. O yeini o tɛ we nabiina na mɛ ba jea ba ke wonnu telo to bá wane te taa ye wa chekke. O ke konto mo o soge nɔɔna dedɛ pa se ba sɛ o taane dem, ye ko dae Efesia yerane wone mo o ke konto, ko maŋe ko daare fee mo se ko taa ye Asia jei sem maama.

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: Konto maama wae ko pa se nɔɔna ŋɔɔne ba chɔge debam totoŋe dem. Ko ta woli da, ba laam wó yaale debam wɛ-kamunu Atamisa diga kam ye ba pa ka taa ye kafɛ. Kolo na daare to mo ye se o tete yere dem na chɔgem nɔɔna tei ne, ye wonto ye wɛ delo nɔɔna maama na zuli Asia jei sem ne de logo baŋa maama wone to.”

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam na nigi konto to, ba bane ma tiini de zaŋe dedɛ ye ba bage ba we, “Debam Efesia tiina wɛ Atamisa mo jege dam!”

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: Sɔɔ laam ma tiini ko ke teo kom maama wone bɔge-bɔge. Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom ma vo ba zi Gayus de Arisaka ye ba ke lela ba vaŋe-ba ba ja vo teo kom jeerim jei sem. Nɔɔna banto balei ya tɔge de Pɔɔl mo ba nwoŋi Makedonia ba ba.

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma boŋe se o vo o zege kɔgɔ kom yiga ne o ŋɔɔne de-ba. Yezu tɔgena bam maa wo sɛ ba pa‑o chwoŋa.

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: Teo kom dedɛɛra badwonna ya di badwoŋo de Pɔɔl. Ba ma toŋe ni ba lwoori‑o se o yé zaŋe o vo jeerim jei sem.

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Jeerim jei sem ne ko maama maa ye sɔɔ yerane bɔge-bɔge. Nɔɔno maama maa tiini o ŋɔɔne o boboŋa taane de kwor-dɛa. Nɔɔna bam dedɛ maa maŋe ba yeiri woŋo kolo ŋwaane ba na lage daane to.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Juu tiina bam ma le Alezanda se o nwoŋi o zege kɔgɔ kom yiga ne o ŋɔɔne. Kɔgɔ kom nɔɔna badwonna ma kwaane ba bere‑o o na wó ke tei. O ma zeiŋi o jeŋa ba baŋa ne, ye o bobo se o tole kolo na ke to o bere nɔn-kɔgɔ kom.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Ba nam na lɔre we o ye Juu tu to, ba maama ma tɔge daane ba tiini ba bage bedwe ba we, “Debam Efesia tiina wɛ Atamisa jege dam!” Ba ke konto mo taa, se ko maŋe de awa balei.

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Teo kom takadaa kam laam ma kwaane o pa se kɔgɔ kom bochara peini tega ne. O ma ta de-ba o we, “Amo dwonna Efesia tiina bam, nɔɔn-nɔɔno tera o na yeiri we debam wɛ-kamunu Atamisa diga kam zege Efesia wone ywoba seeni, ye debam mo nii ka baŋa ne. Dé ta kwori dé jege o kamɔgɔ kolo na nwoŋi wɛyuu ne ko to tega ne to dé nia.

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Nɔɔn-nɔɔno bá wane o ta we konto ye vwa. Konto ŋwaane ko maŋe se á pa á bochara peini tega ne, se á yé gare á ke kolokolo.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Nii-na abam na jaane nɔɔna banto balei á ba ywo, ye ba wo ŋɔge debam wɛ-di sem wonnu naa ba ŋɔɔne ba yaale debam wɛ dem.

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye Demetiru de o nɔɔna bam, ba ná jege nɔɔno taane, chwoŋa wora se ba vo kɔɔte ba saŋe‑o dedɛɛra bam yiga ne. Mo ba na jege se ba ke tei.

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: O na tage konto o ti to, o ma ta de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom pa se ba viiri.

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: O ma tole jei sem konto ne o ŋɔɔne wonnu dedɛ o bere nɔɔna bam pa se ba bochara ke dam. O daa ma kɛ o vo o yi Girisi.

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: O ma ke chane setɔ dáane. O laam ma ti o yiga se o zo nabworo o vo Siria. O ma ba o lɔre we Juu tiina bam ke ni daane se ba kwaane ba chɔge‑o. Konto ŋwaane o ma leiri o boboŋa, ye o laam ja se o vo tega ne o tɔge Makedonia wo o jwoori o kɛ.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Balo na zaŋe se ba tɔge ded‑o to mo tento: Sopata, wolo na ye Pirus bu ye o nwoŋi Berea to. Arisaka de Sɛkundu, ba nwoŋi Tɛsaloni mo. Gayus, wolo na nwoŋi Dɛɛbe to. Timoti. Tichika de Torofima, ba na ye Asia tiina to.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Banto mo dɛ yiga ba lwoori ba vo Torase ba cheigi debam da.

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: Debam tete laam ma maŋe Filipi ne ye dé tɔge dé di Bworobworo-memene kuri dem. Kuri dem na ti to, dé laam ma zo nabworo dé tɔge naneo kom wo dé ke da yanu dé vo dé yi Torase. Dé ma jeeri dé dwonna bam da ye dé ke da yarepɛ teo kom ne.

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Bakwɛ boboa dɛ ne debam maama ma la daane se dé di wodiu, ne Yezu ya na fɔge bworobworo o pa o kwaga tɔgena bam pa ba di tei to. Pɔɔl ma tiini o ŋɔɔne o bere nɔɔna bam taa, se ko yi tete kokoro, kolo ŋwaane tega ná poore o lage o viiri.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: Dé ya lage daane wɛyuu diga kalo na ke betɔ to wone mo. Ba déem tɔre min-zwonnu dedɛ ba zege da.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Nɔn-doŋo maa tɔge o wora, o yere mo Yutiku. O maa jei takworo ni ne. Pɔɔl na tiini o ŋɔɔne o dáane konto to, nɔn-doŋo kom maa jei o dɔa o veela. O laam ma ba o dɔ fase o kɛ. O ma tɔge takworo kom o to tega ne. Ba ma tu ba kwei‑o de o tega.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl tete ma tu o vo o peini nɔn-doŋo kom baŋa ne o kukwori‑o de o jea. O maa we, “Á yé pa se á yera sɔɔre. O ta ŋwe mo.”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma jwoori o di wɛyuu diga kam. O ma fɔ bworobworo kom o di. O daa ta ma lare de-ba taa, ye tega ba ka poore. O laam ma viiri.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: O na viiri to, nɔɔna bam ma ja nɔn-doŋo kom ba ja vo sɔŋɔ de yazura. Ba bochara ma peini tega ne ye ba jege wopwolo.

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Debam ma yage Pɔɔl ye dé vo dé zo nabworo kom se dé tɔge yiga dé da naneo kom wo dé vo Asosa. Dé ya ke ni daane se dé jeeri Pɔɔl Asosa ne, o na boŋe se o vo tega ne to ŋwaane.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: Dé na nɛ daane Asosa ne to, Pɔɔl laam ma zo nabworo kom ye dé maama tɔge daane dé vo dé yi Mitulini.

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: Dé ma zege dáane dé tɔge naneo kom wo dé kɛ. Tega ma poore ye dé vo dé tɔge Chiosa buburu kom dé kɛ. Tega daa ma poore. Dé ma vo dé bɛ dé yi Samos. Tega daa ta na poore to, dé ma vo dé yi Militus.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Pɔɔl déem ya boŋe se o da Efesia mo o kɛ se o yé zege da. O ya ba lage se o dáane dedɛ Asia ne, kolo ŋwaane o lage lela mo se o ná wae, se o vo o yi Jerusalem ye Pɛntekɔse kuri dem ta wo yi.

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Debam déem na wo Militus ne to, Pɔɔl ma toŋe ni o pa Yezu kɔgɔ kom nakwa bam Efesia ne o we, ba ba.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Ba na tu to, o ma ta de-ba o we, “Abam maŋe á yei amo déem na zoore abam tei ne ye a ke tei maŋa maama, ko zege dɛ delo a na bobo a ba Asia to.

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: Amo toŋe a pa dé Teiru wom mo. Amo ma gwooni a tete, ye a yi-na nwoŋi. A ma na yaara dedɛ de Juu tiina bam na ke ni daane se ba chɔge amo tei to.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: Abam ta yei we, amo wo yage se a ta woŋo kolo maama na wó wane ko woli abam to mo a bere abam. Amo ma kwaane a bere abam Wɛ chega kam pwooni yiga ne, de á tete sam ne.

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Amo ma tiini a kaane Juu tiina de dwi-gɛ tiina maama se ba leiri ba wo Wɛ ŋwaane, se ba daare ba ke ba wo-dedoa de dé Teiru Yezu.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: Leile konto amo laam maa vei Jerusalem. Ko nam ye Wɛ Sin-laao kom mo gwori-ne pa se a maa vei da, ye a yeiri kolo na wó yi amo da to.

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amo na yei kolo to mo ye Wɛ Sin-laao kom yeini ko kaane amo teo maama ne we, nɔɔna wó ja-ne ba vɔ ye ba kwori ba bɛɛse-ne.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Amo nam na boŋe tei to, a ba pae se a ŋwea taa jege nyɔɔre ka pa-ne. Kolo na ye wo-chɛɔ to mo ye se a toŋe totoŋa yalo dé Teiru Yezu na ke a jeŋa ne to a ti. Totoŋa yam konto mo ye se a kwaane a bere nɔɔna Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam de o na yɔɔre o ke nɔɔna zaane tei to.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Amo nam yei we abam wolowolo daa bá na amo, ye á ye balo amo na beeri á wone a bere abam Wɛ paare dem chega kam.

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: Kolo ŋwaane amo tɔɔle chega kalo maama na tɔge Wɛ boboŋa to a bere abam ye a wo yage kolokolo.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: Amo laam lage a ke abam Wɛ jeŋa ne. Wɛ wó pa á tɔge chega kalo na tɔge o zaane dem ŋwaane to. Chega kam konto wó wane ka fɔge abam lanyerane, se á laam ba á tɔge de balo maama na ye Wɛ nyem to á na ywoni o tei ne.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: Amo nam wo kwaane se a jwoŋi sabia na gwaaro abam wolowolo tei ne.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: Abam tete yei lanyerane we amo mɛ a tete jea mo a toŋe, se amo de a dwonna bam wane dé na dé ni-wodiu.

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl na tage konto o ti to, ba maama ma kuni dwoona ye o lwoori Wɛ.

english_verse: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ba ma zaŋe ye ba maama keeri dedɛ. Ba ma tiini ba kukwori‑o lanyerane.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Ba wo ma tiini ko chɔge de o na tage taane delo o bere-ba we, ba daa bá fɔge ba na‑o to. Ba ma zaŋe ba tɔge ded‑o ba vo nabworo kom na wo mɛ to se ba yage‑o.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Dé laam ma bane-ba ye dé daare dé viiri. Dé ma kwei dé yiga dé yɔɔre naneo kom wo dé vo dé yi Kos. Tega ma poore. Dé daa ma yi Rodizi. Dé ma zege dáane dé vo Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Dé na yi dáane to, dé ma na nabworo kodwoŋi ko na lage ko vo Fonikia to. Dé ma vo dé zo ko wo ye dé tɔge dé kɛ.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Dé na maa vei to, dé ma tole dé na Kupirus buburu kom. Dé ma yage-ko dé jagwia seeni ye dé daare dé kɛ. Dé ma vo dé yi Siria. Dé na yi da to, dé vo dé bɛ dé zege Tura ne. Ko ye dáane mo ba jege se ba le nabworo kom zela yam.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Debam maŋa kam na kɛ to, dé ma zaŋe dé kwei dé chwoŋa se dé viiri. Yezu nɔɔna bam, de ba kaana, de ba bia maama ma ja debam ba nwoŋi teo kom wone ba vo se ba yage. Dé na vei dé yi naneo kom ni to, debam maama ma kuni dwoona tega ne dé ware Wɛ.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Dé na ware Wɛ dé ti to, dé ma bane daane ye dé zo nabworo kom. Banto ma jwoori sɔŋɔ.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, dé ma zaŋe dé vo dé yi Kazaria. Dé ma vo dé peini Filipi ba sɔŋɔ ne. Wonto mo bere nɔɔna Wɛ kwor-ywoŋa kam ye o tɔge o ye nɔɔna barepɛ balo ba na le Jerusalem ne to wo dedoa.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Dé na ke da fenfee dáane konto to, Wɛ ni-jwoŋinu wodwoŋi ma nwoŋi Judea o ba debam tei. O yere mo Agabu.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: O na tu debam tei konto to, o ma le Pɔɔl kila o teiŋa ne o ma vɔ o tete nɛ de o jea o ke daane. O laam ma ta o we, “Mo Wɛ Sin-laao kom na tɛ kolo: Juu tiina balo na zoore Jerusalem ne to wó ja kila kanto tu ba vɔ tento dwoŋi, ye ba daare ba ke‑o dwi-gɛ tiina jeŋa ne.”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Dé na nigi konto to, debam balo maama na wora to ma kwaane dé lwoori Pɔɔl se o daa yé vo Jerusalem.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: O ma leiri o we, “Bɛŋwaane mo abam laara ye á boŋe se á pa amo wo chɔge? Amo ba jege keim se a ke, ba ná lage ba vɔ-ne Jerusalem ne naa ba ná lage ba go-ne de. Amo wó sɛ se a te dé Teiru Yezu yere ŋwaane.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Dé na lwoori‑o taa dé ga to, dé ma yage ye dé ta we, “Wɛ wó ke o boboŋa na lage kolo to.”

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Yezu tɔgena badaara ma zaŋe Kazaria ne ba tɔge debam. Ba ma ja debam ba vo nɔɔno wolo sɔŋɔ dé na lage dé peini da to. O yere mo Manason. O maa ye Kupirus tu ye o maŋe o sɛ Yezu faŋa faŋa. Pɔɔl na wo Jerusalem ne ye ko ke‑o tei to

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Dé na yi Jerusalem to, dé nu-bia bam ma jeeri debam lanyerane.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, Pɔɔl ma zaŋe o tɔge dedaane debam se dé vo dé na Jemsi. Yezu kɔgɔ kom nakwa bam de maama maa wora.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma jɔɔne-ba. O ma tole kolo maama Wɛ na tɔge omo totoŋa yam baŋa ne o ke dwi-gɛ tiina tei ne to o bere-ba.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ba na nigi kolo maama o na tage to, ba ma ke Wɛ lei ko ŋwaane. Ba laam ma ta de Pɔɔl ba we, “Debam nu-bu, n nɛ ko na ye tei. Juu tiina morro kɔgɔ kɔgɔ laam mo tu ba sɛ Yezu, ye ba ta tɔge Wɛ ni-dwoora yam de ba wo maama.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Ba nigi we nmo yeini n bere Juu tiina balo na zoore dwi-gɛ tiina wone to se ba yage Wɛ nia yalo o na ke Moses jeŋa ne to. Ba nigi we n tɛ nɔɔna bam konto se ba daa yé taa gwoni ba bia peina, se ba ta yé taa tɔge debam Juu tiina kikia na ye tei to.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Dé nam wó ke tɛ mo? Juu tiina balo na wo ywo-seeni to jege se ba lɔre we nmo tua.

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Tɔ. Dé wó bere‑m nmo na wó ke tei. Nɔɔna bana wo debam tei ne ba na tiŋi ba ni de Wɛ.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ba ná lage ba vo Wɛ diga kam se ba kwɛ ba tete de Wɛ, nmo jege se n tɔge n vo mo, se n daare n ŋwe ba na ke kolo to jene. Konto wó pa-ba chwoŋa se ba fane ba yuni. N ná ke konto, nɔɔno maama wae o lɔre we, ba na tɛ kolo ba pa nmo to dae chega. Ba nam wó lɔre we nmo tete tɔge Wɛ nia yam na bere tei to mo.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Ko daare dwi-gɛ tiina balo na tu ba sɛ Yezu to, debam maŋe dé popone tɔnɔ dé pa-ba ye dé ta kolo dé na boŋe to we, ba yé zaŋe ba di wodiu kolo nɔɔna na mɛ ba kaane jwona to, naa ba di woŋo kolo na jege jana to, naa ba di varem wolo ba na jujugi ba go to. Dé daa ta ma ta-ba se ba fɔge ba ja ba tete de kabwoŋa kikia maama.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma sɛ ba taane dem. Tega na poore to, o ma ja nɔɔna bam o vo se o tɔge o kwɛ o tete de Wɛ. O ma daare o zo Wɛ diga kam se o ta o bere ka yiga tiina bam da yalo ni ta na daare se nɔɔna bam kwɛ ba tete de Wɛ ba ti, ye ba dedoa dedoa laam go ba wonnu ba kaane Wɛ to.

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Da yarepɛ yam ni na daare fee se ya ti to, Juu tiina badaara ma na Pɔɔl Wɛ diga kam wone. Banto nwoŋi Asia teo kodwoŋi mo. Ba ma pa se nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maama na wora to bane zaŋe de Pɔɔl pa se ba zi‑o.

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Ba déem tage konto dwoŋi kolo ŋwaane ba ya nɛ Torofima de Pɔɔl na tɔge daane teo kom wone ye o ye dwi-gɛ tu na nwoŋi Efesia to. Ba déem boŋe we nɔɔno wom konto mo Pɔɔl jaane o zo Wɛ diga kam.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Teo kom nɔɔna bam maama ma tiini ba chiŋi. Ba ma duri ba vo jeiga kam. Ba laam ma zi Pɔɔl ba tuuri ba ja nwoŋi Wɛ diga kam wone ye ba daare ba pe ka nia yam maama.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Nɔn-kɔgɔ kom maa kwaana se ba go Pɔɔl. Rom soja tiina dedɛɛro wom ma ni we bobɔga to Jerusalem teo kom maama wone mo.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: O na nigi konto to, o ma ja soja tiina de ba yiga tiina badaara, ye ba duri lela ba vo ba yi kɔgɔ kom na wo mɛ to. Nɔɔna bam na nɛ‑o de o soja tiina bam konto to, ba ma yage Pɔɔl magem.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom ma vo Pɔɔl tei o ja‑o. O ma pa ba kwei chaponno telei ba ma vɔ‑o. O ma daare o bwei se o lɔre nɔɔno wom na ye wolo to de o na ke kolo to.

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: O na bwei konto to, nɔɔna badaara kɔgɔ kom wone ma laare ba ta n ni n ni. Sɔɔ kom na ye tei to ma pa se dedɛɛro wom ware se o lɔre kolo na ke chekke to. Konto ŋwaane o ma pa o nɔɔna bam ni se ba ja Pɔɔl ba vo ba dam jei sem.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Ba na jaane‑o ba yi nateina yam diinim jei to, soja tiina bam déem jege se ba kwei‑o mo ba zeŋe, kolo ŋwaane nɔn-kɔgɔ kom yia tiini ya seene o baŋa ne.

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: Nɔɔna bam maama ma pɛ ba pu o kwaga ye ba laare ba tɛ ba we, “Pa-na dé go‑o!”

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Aawo. Amo ye Juu tu mo. Ba loge amo Kilikia teo Tasusi ne mo. Amo ye teo kamunu kom konto nɔn-bu mo. A lwoori‑m se n pa-ne chwoŋa se a ŋɔɔne de nɔn-kɔgɔ kom.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom ma sɛ. Pɔɔl ma zaŋe o zege nateina yam baŋa ne. O ma zeiŋi o jeŋa kɔgɔ kom baŋa ne. Ba maama ma cheigi sɔɔ. O ma ŋɔɔne de-ba de ba tete Juu tiina taane dem.

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Ba na lɔre we o ŋɔɔne ba tete taane dem to, ba ma fɔge ba tiini ba cheigi sɔɔ.

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: O laam ma ta-ba o we: “Amo ye Juu tu mo. Ba loge-ne Kilikia teo Tasusi ne. Amo ma daare a ke nɔɔno teo konto wone. A ma zamese Gamaleli tei ne ye a lɔre debam nabaara chwei sem na ye tei to chekke. Amo déem chɛ lanyerane a kwei a tete a pa Wɛ, nenɛɛne abam zem de na ke tei to mo.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: Amo déem yeini a bɛɛse balo na sɛ ba tɔge Wɛ chwo-doŋa kam to se ko yi ba toone. A maa yeini a jaane nɔɔna a ke peena diga ne, baara de kaana maama.

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: Debam kaanem yuu tu wom dedaane dé nakwa kɔgɔ kom maama wó wane ba zege amo chega kam kwaga ne. Maŋa kadwoŋi ne a yeini a vei ba tei mo a jwoŋi twanno telo a na wó kwei a bere Juu tiina balo na wo Damasika ne to. A ma vo da se a ja balo na tɔge Yezu chwoŋa kam to, se a vɔ-ba a ja a ba Jerusalem se ba na waarem.

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: Amo na maa vei to, a ma daare fee se a yi Damasika. Ko na maŋe de wea tetare to, pwooni ma pɔpɔ de nwoŋi wɛyuu ne de ba de pepele de kekare-ne.

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: Amo ma to tega ne ye a ni kwora na bwoŋi-ne ka we, ‘Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl! Bɛ mo ye n bɛɛse-ne konto?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Amo ma bwei a we, ‘Amo tu, n ye wɔ mo?’ O ma leiri o we, ‘Amo ye Yezu mo, Nazarete tu wolo nmo na bɛɛse to.’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo na tɔge de amo to ma na pwooni dem ye ba wo nigi wolo kwora na ŋɔɔne de amo to.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: A laam ma bwei a we, ‘Amo tu, bɛ mo a nam wó ke?’ Dé Teiru wom ma leiri-ne o we, ‘Zaŋe n vo n zo Damasika teo wo, se dáane mo ba laam wó bere‑m kolo maama Wɛ na boŋe se n ke to.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Amo ma zaŋe wɛɛne, ye a yia daa ba nae, pwooni dem na tiini de pepele-ya to ŋwaane. Konto ma pa se a dwonna bam ja amo jeŋa ba vaŋe-ne ba ja vo teo kom wo.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno wodwoŋi maa wora, o yere mo Anania. O maa kɔre Wɛ lanyerane, ye o tɔge debam Juu tiina chwei sem. Juu tiina balo maama na zoore Damasika ne to maa tiini ba pa‑o zula.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: O ma ta o we, ‘Debam nabaara Baŋa Wɛ mo le nmo se n lɔre o boboŋa na lage kolo to, se n daare n na Wo-pwoŋo Tu wom, ye n daare n ni o na ŋɔɔne de o kwora.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Nmo nam ba jege se n daa‑n dáane. Zaŋe se ba pa n jwoŋi sɛɛm, se n pa n wɛleera yam saare de n na lwoori Wɛ dé Teiru wom yere ŋwaane to.’

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: Amo nɛ dé Teiru wom na ŋɔɔne de amo ye o we, ‘Zaŋe n ke lela n duri n nwoŋi Jerusalem ne, kolo ŋwaane teo kom nɔɔna bam bá sɛ kolo nmo na wó ta amo ŋwaane to.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: A ma leiri a we, ‘Amo tu, nɔɔna bam yei lanyerane we amo tole Juu tiina jeerim di sem mo se a ja nɔɔna balo na sɛ nmo to, se ba pe-ba se ba daare ba mage-ba.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Ko daare maŋa kalo ba na go Stiiven wolo na zege nmo chega kam kwaga ne to, amo tete wora ye a sɛ se ba go‑o. A maa zege a nii ba gwaaro tem ba na le se ba daare ba dole‑o ba go to.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Dé Teiru wom laam ma ta de amo we, a nam véi, se omo wó toŋe-ne yiga yiga se a vo dwi-gɛ tiina bam tei.”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Ba maa nana ye ba vuvuga ba gwaaro wɛɛne ye ba ta mɔɔne fwogo ba chaara.

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Soja tiina dedɛɛro wom na nɛ kolo na ke to, o ma pa o nɔɔna bam ni se ba ja Pɔɔl ba zo ba dam jei sem. O ma ta-ba se ba fere‑o se ba daare ba lɔre o na ke kolo ye Juu tiina bam nane o baŋa ne to.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Ba na vɔge‑o ba ti se ba daare ba fere‑o to, Pɔɔl ma ta de soja yiga tu wolo na zege da to o we, “Abam jege chwoŋa se á ja Rom teo jeŋa nɔɔno á fere ye ba ta wo bwei ba nii amo na chɔge kolo to na?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Soja yiga tu wom na nigi konto to, o ma vo o ta de o dedɛɛro wom o we, “Nmo boŋe se n ke bɛ mo? Nɔɔno wom ye Rom teo jeŋa nɔɔno mo.”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom ma vo Pɔɔl tei o bwei‑o o we, “Nmo seene n ye Rom teo jeŋa nɔɔno mo na?” Pɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Ɛɛ, a ye konto mo.”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom ma ta o we, omo ŋwe sabu-fɔrɔ mo ye o daare o ji Rom teo jeŋa nɔɔno. Pɔɔl ma leiri‑o we, “Ba nam loge amo pa se a maŋe a ye ko jeŋa nɔɔno mo.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo ya na zege se ba bwei‑o taane to na nigi konto to, ba ma kwei o yera ba yage lela. Dedɛɛro wom de na lɔre we Pɔɔl ye Rom teo jeŋa nɔɔno to, foone ma ja‑o de o na pɛ ba vɔ‑o de chaponno to. Pɔɔl zege nakwa bam yiga ne

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom déem maa lage se o lɔre kolo na kea ye Juu tiina bam saŋe Pɔɔl to. Tega na poore to, o ma pa ba le Pɔɔl ba yage. O ma daare o toŋe ni o pa Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam de ba teo kom nakwa kɔgɔ kom maama se ba jeeri daane. O laam ma ja Pɔɔl o vo o pa se o zege ba yiga ne.

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Juu tiina kaanem yuu tu wom, o yere na ye Anania to, na nigi Pɔɔl na tage kolo to, o ma ta balo na zege Pɔɔl tei ne to se ba fere o ni.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma leiri Anania o we, “Wɛ tete mo wó seene o mage nmo. Nmo nye de kabira kalo nɔɔna na fɔge to mo. Nmo ye wolo na jei se n di amo taane se ko tɔge Juu tiina nia yam mo, ye nmo tete mo chɔge-ya de n na pɛ ni we ba mage amo to.”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Nɔɔna balo na zege Pɔɔl tei ne to ma ta ded‑o ba we, “Nmo jege debam kaanem yuu tu wom n twea!”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma leiri-ba o we, “A dwonna bam, amo maŋe a yeiri we o seene o ye kaanem yuu tu wom mo. Ko popone Wɛ tɔnɔ kom ne ko we, n yé zaŋe n ŋɔɔne n chɔge wolo na ye yuu tu n dwonna wone to yiga.”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl na lɔre we kɔgɔ kom nɔɔna badaara ye Saduka tiina, ye badaara de ye Farisi tiina to, o laam ma ŋɔɔne baŋa baŋa de kwor-dɛa ba kɔgɔ kom wone o we, “A dwonna bam, amo ye Farisi tu ye a kwori a ye Farisi tiina bu. Ba zem saŋe amo se ba di amo taane de a na jege teena we twa wó jwoori ba bi toone wone to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: O na tage konto o ti to, Farisi tiina bam de Saduka tiina bam ma bobo se ba mage ni-kantɔgɔ daane. Ba kɔgɔ kom maama ma pɔɔre belei.

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: Kokuri to Saduka tiina bam bere we twa biim tera, ye ba tɛ we malese tera, chira de nam tera. Ko daare Farisi tiina bam maa bere we tento maama ye chega mo.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Ba maama ma ke sɔɔ se ko tiini ko gaale. Wɛ nia zamesem tiina badaara na nwoŋi Farisi tiina kɔgɔ kom wone to ma zaŋe wɛɛne ba tɔne de dam ba we, “Debam wo nɛ kolo nɔɔno wonto na ke o chɔge to. Ko nam wó wane ko taa ye chega we chiru naa maleka mo ŋɔɔne ded‑o.”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Ba ni-kantɔgɔ kom maa fɔge ko pula. Ko ma pa se foone zo soja tiina dedɛɛro wom we ba ga wó ja Pɔɔl ba vaŋe ba tore mo. O ma pa ni se o soja tiina bam zo kɔgɔ kom wo ba ja Pɔɔl ba wone ba ja nwoŋi, se ba daare ba ja‑o ba jwoori ba vo ba dam jei sem.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Dɛ dem konto tete ne dé Teiru wom ma ba o zege Pɔɔl tei ne ye o we, “Ta‑n jege baare. Nmo maŋe n zege amo chega kam kwaga ne n bere Jerusalem tiina. Nmo nam jege se n daa‑n ke konto mo Rom teo ne de.” Ba kwaane se ba go Pɔɔl

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma zaŋe ba vo ba kaanem yiga tiina bam de ba teo kom nakwa bam tei ba ta ba we, “Debam maama ke ni daane mo dé tiini dé du de Wɛ we, dé daa bá di kolokolo se ko taa nii dé ná go Pɔɔl.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Ko laam daare se abam de á kɔgɔ kom maama mo toŋe ni soja tiina dedɛɛro wom tei ne se ba ja Pɔɔl ba nwoŋi ba ba ba pa abam. Abam wó ke se ko taa ye nenɛɛne á lage se á faŋe á nii o ni taane mo. Ko daare debam wó vo dé ke siri se dé go‑o chwoŋa ne ye o ta wo yi abam tei.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nakɔ bu déem maa wora. O ma ni keim dem konto ŋwa. O ma zaŋe o vo o zo soja tiina dam jei sem o ta o bere Pɔɔl.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl na nigi konto to, o ma bwoŋi soja tiina yiga tu dedoa se o ba. O ma ta ded‑o o we, “Ja nɔn-doŋo konto n vo n dedɛɛro wom tei, se o jege taane mo se o ta ded‑o.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Yiga tu wom ma tɔge o yiga o ja‑o o vo dedɛɛro wom tei. O ma ta o we, “Pɔɔl na ye peeno to mo bwoŋi amo o ta se a ja nɔn-doŋo konto a ba nmo tei, o na jege taane se o ta de nmo to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom ma ja o jeŋa o vaŋe‑o o ja nwoŋi dáa. O ma bwei‑o o we, “Nmo jege bɛ mo se n ta n bere-ne?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: O ma ta o we, “Juu tiina kɔgɔ kom mo ke ni daane ba sɛ se ba jwa toŋe ni nmo tei ne se n ja Pɔɔl n vo ba kɔgɔ kom wo se ko taa ye nenɛɛne ba lage se ba faŋe ba nii o ni taane mo.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom na nigi konto to, o ma ta ded‑o o we, o yé ta o bere nɔɔn-nɔɔno we o tu o ta keim dem o bere‑o. O ma daare o pa se nɔn-doŋo kom viiri.

english_verse: The commander called in two of his officers and told them, “By nine o'clock tonight have
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom laam ma bwoŋi o yiga tiina balei o ta de-ba o we, “Pa-na se soja tiina bia yalei (

english_verse: men on horseback and
translation_verse: ) de chichwoa dolena bia yalei (

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Le-na sisei á pa Pɔɔl se o di, se o de wane o vo o yi gɔmena tu Feliki tei de yazura.”

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Dedɛɛro wom laam ma popone tɔnɔ tento:

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Juu tiina badwonna mo jaane nɔɔno wonto ye ba kwaane se ba go‑o. Amo nam lɔre we o ye Rom teo jeŋa nɔɔno mo. Konto ŋwaane amo de a nɔɔna bam ma vo dé jwoŋi‑o dé yage.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: A ya lage se a lɔre woŋo kolo ŋwaane ba na jaane‑o ba saŋe to mo. Mo kokuri a jaane‑o a vo a zege ba nakwa kɔgɔ kom yiga ne.

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: A ma lɔre we ba saŋe‑o ba tete chullu tem ŋwaane mo. Kolokolo nam tera ko na maŋe se ba go‑o naa ba pe‑o.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Nɔɔno nam mo tage o bere-ne we Juu tiina badaara mo ke ni daane se ba chɔge nɔɔno wom. Konto ŋwaane mo amo boŋe ye a toŋe‑o nmo tei ne. Amo ma ta de balo na saŋe‑o to we, ba ba nmo tei ba ta kolo na ke to.”

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Soja tiina bam laam ma zaŋe ba ja Pɔɔl ba nwoŋi, ne ba na pɛ-ba ni se ba ke tei to. Ba ma ja‑o tete dem konto ba vo ba yi Antipatera.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Tega na poore to, soja tiina balo na vei tega ne to ma zege dáane ba jwoori ba vo ba dam jei sem. Ba ma daare sisei dira bam yerane mo se ba tɔge de Pɔɔl ba vo.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Ba ma ja‑o ba vo ba yi Kazaria. Ba na yi da to, ba ma kwei tɔnɔ kom ba pa gɔmena tu wom ye ba ke Pɔɔl o jeŋa ne.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: O ma ga tɔnɔ kom ye o daare o bwei Pɔɔl o we, teo kɔ mo o nwoŋi? O na lɔre we o nwoŋi Kilikia to,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: o ma ta o we, “Nmo saŋena bam ná tua, amo wó bwei nmo taane dem a nii.” O ma daare o pa ni we ba ja Pɔɔl ba vo sɔŋɔ kolo Pɛ Herodi déem na lɔge to se ba pe‑o da ye ba taa yere‑o.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Da yanu na kɛ to, Juu tiina kaanem yuu tu Anania laam ma ba, o dedaane nakwa badaara. Lɔya tu wodwoŋi de tɔge o wo ba tei ne, o yere mo Tɛtulus. Ba ma vo ba jeini gɔmena tu wom yiga ne se ba tole kolo Pɔɔl na ke to ba bere‑o.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Ba ma bwoŋi Pɔɔl se o ba. Lɔya tu Tɛtulus laam ma bobo se o ŋɔɔne taane dem. O ma tole o we, “Debam yuu tu Feliki, debam maama yei we, nmo kwaane n pa se debam logo kom jege ywoni se ko dáane. Nmo na jege debam tei to mo pɛ se n fɔge dé teo kom ye ko kɛ yiga.

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Nmo na ke kolo maama maŋa de maŋa naa jei de jei to, dé ke nmo lei ko ŋwaane kamunu kamunu.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Amo nam ba lage se a ŋɔɔne dedɛ se ko daane nmo. Amo nam lwoori‑m se n cheigi debam na jege kolo fenfee se dé ta to.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: Debam maane we nɔɔno wonto jege nankɔɔre dedɛ. Logo baŋa ni maama ne o yeini o pa se bobɔga taa tui Juu tiina maama tetare ne. O maa kwori o ye yiga tu Nazarete tiina kɔgɔ kom wone.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: O ma pa ni we balo na saŋe Pɔɔl to ba nmo tei.] Nmo nam ná bwei‑o taane, nmo wó wane n lɔre o na ke kolo ye debam saŋe‑o to.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Tɛtulus na tage konto to, Juu tiina bam ma pu o kwaga we, o na tage kolo maama to ye chega mo.

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Gɔmena tu wom laam ma yeese o jeŋa Pɔɔl baŋa ne se o de daa tole o kwora. Pɔɔl ma ta o we, “Amo yei we nmo tei dé teo kom n nii ko baŋa ne se ko tiini ko dáane nenɛɛne bena dedɛ. Konto ŋwaane amo jege wopwolo se a zege nmo yiga ne a ŋɔɔne a jwoŋi a tete.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Nmo tete nam wó lɔre we amo na vei Jerusalem se a zuli Wɛ to, ko ta wo dwoni da fuga-yalei zem dɛ dem ne.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Wonnu telo maama ba na we a ke to, ba nam bá wane ba bere we te ye chega.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Amo nam na wó sɛ a ta kolo de nmo to mo konto: Amo zuli Wɛ wolo na ye debam nabaara Wɛ to mo, ye a tɔge Wɛ chwo-doŋa kalo nɔɔna banto na tɛ ba we ka ye vwa to. Amo nam sɛ a tɔge wonnu telo maama na popone Wɛ nia yam tɔnɔ kom ne, de faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem twanno tem wone to.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: Amo nam jege teena Wɛ tei ne, ne nɔɔna banto de na jege teena tei we, twa maama wó jwoori ba bi toone wone, nɔn-ŋona de nɔn-balwaaro maama.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane amo nam kwaane a ke kokeiri mo se a ke kolo maama na lana Wɛ de nabiina tei ne to, ye foone tera a bochare ne.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: A na wora a ke konto to, Juu tiina bam ma ba ba na amo Wɛ diga kam wone. Ba na nɛ-ne konto to, de amo maŋe a kwɛ a tete de Wɛ a ti. Nɔn-kɔgɔ de maa tere a tei ne. Bobɔga de nam tera.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Ko daare Juu tiina badaara na nwoŋi Asia teene dem wone to mo tɔge ba wora. Banto ya ná jege woŋo de amo, ko nam ya maŋe se banto mo ba ba zege nmo yiga ne, se ba ta kolo amo na ke a chɔge to.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Amo na zege Juu tiina nakwa kɔgɔ kom yiga ne a ŋɔɔne to, nam pa se nɔɔna banto na zege ywo-seeni to ta ba na nɛ kolo amo na ke a chɔge to,

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: ko ná dae woŋo dedoa yerane mo a taga. Amo na zege ba wone to, a ya ŋɔɔne de a kwora maama mo a we, ‘Abam zem nam di amo taane kolo ŋwaane a na sɛ we twa wó jwoori ba bi toone wone to.’ ”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl na tage konto o ti to, Feliki ma pa se ba tiŋi taane dem. O déem maŋe o yei Wɛ chwo-doŋa kam na ye tei to chekke. O ma ta o we, “Soja tiina dedɛɛro Lusia ná tua, amo laam wó di abam taane dem a ti.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: O ma pa soja tiina yiga tu wom ni se o ja Pɔɔl o vo o taa yere‑o, se o daare o pa‑o pwola se o badwonna wae ba zeini‑o de kolo o na lage to.

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Da fenfee na kɛ to, Feliki ma tɔge de o kaane Durusila o ba. Wonto ye Juu tu mo. Feliki ma pa se ba bwoŋi Pɔɔl se o ba. Ba ma cheigi Pɔɔl na wora o tɛ ko na ye tei ye nɔɔna ke ba wo-dedoa de Yezu Krista to.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma daare o wora o tɛ keim-laaro tɔgem taane, de nɔɔna na wae ba tete ba jaana tei to. O ta ma ta o bere-ba Wɛ na wó ba o bore nɔɔna bora tei to. Pɔɔl na wora o tɛ konto dwoŋi to, foone ma zo Feliki. O ma ta o we, “Ko maŋe. Nam véi, se maŋa de maŋa, a ná lage‑m, a laam wó bwoŋi‑m.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: O ya maŋe o boŋe we Pɔɔl wó kwei sabu mo o ma lwoori‑o. Konto ŋwaane mo o déem yeini o bwoŋi‑o maŋa maama o ŋɔɔne ded‑o.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Bena yalei ma ba ya yi. Nɔɔno wodwoŋi ma ba o leiri Feliki yuu ne se o taa ye logo kom yiga tu. Wonto yere mo Pɔkia Fɛsitu. Feliki déem na lage se o pa Juu tiina bam wo pwoli to, o ma yage Pɔɔl peena diga kam ne se o taa wora.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Fɛsitu déem na tu o ji logo kom tu wom ye da yatɔ kɛ to, o ma zaŋe Kazaria ne o vo Jerusalem.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: O na vei o wora konto to, Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam de ba yiga tiina ma vo o tei ba saŋe Pɔɔl.

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: Ba ma tiini ba lwoori‑o se o woli-ba o pa Pɔɔl ba Jerusalem. Ko ye ba na ke ni daane se ba go Pɔɔl chwoŋa ne to ŋwaane mo ba lwoori Fɛsitu se o ke konto.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: O ma leiri-ba o we, “Pɔɔl wo Kazaria ne ye ba jege‑o ba yera. Ko nam bá dáane ye amo tete jwoori a vo da.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Ko nam ná ye o ke woŋo mo o chɔge, á pa se á yiga tiina bam tɔge de amo ba vo se á laam saŋe‑o dáane.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Fɛsitu na ke nenɛɛne da nana naa da fuga ba teo kom ne to, o laam ma zaŋe o jwoori Kazaria. O na yi da ye tega poore to, o ma nwoŋi o jeini se o di taane dem. O ma pa ni se ba ja Pɔɔl ba ba.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl na tu o ba o yi ba tei to, Juu tiina balo na nwoŋi Jerusalem ba ba to maa zege ba gilimi‑o. Ba ma bobo se ba taa tɛ wo-kamunnu dedɛ ba pa‑o. Ba nam ware ba ta kolokolo ye ba bere we ko ye chega.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma ŋɔɔne o jwoŋi o tete ye o we, “Amo wo ke kolokolo na wó wane ko chɔge Juu tiina nia yam, de Wɛ diga kam chullu tem to. A nam wo ŋɔɔne kolo na wó chɔge Rom Pa-faro wom yuu to.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Fɛsitu déem maa lage se o pa Juu tiina bam wo pwoli. Konto ŋwaane o ma bwei Pɔɔl o we, “Nmo wó sɛ se n vo Jerusalem se a di nmo taane dáane na?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma leiri‑o we, “Amo nam maŋe a zege nɔɔno wolo Rom Pa-faro wom na pɛ‑o ni se o di amo taane to yiga ne mo. Ywo-seeni mo maŋe se á di amo taane dem. Ko ná ye Juu tiina bam, amo wo chɔge ba kolokolo. Nmo tete nam maŋe n yei we konto ye chega.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Amo nam ná ke a tusi ye a ke kolo na maŋe se a te to, amo sɛ toone. Wonnu telo Juu tiina bam nam na ŋɔɔne ba pa amo to ná ba jege chega, nɔɔn-nɔɔno ba jege chwoŋa se o ja amo o ke ba jeŋa ne. Konto ŋwaane amo laam ke a tete Rom Pa-faro wom jeŋa ne mo se o di a taane.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Fɛsitu na nigi konto to, o ma ŋɔɔne de o kwaga nɔɔna bam, ye o laam daare o ta de Pɔɔl o we, “Nmo na ke n tete dé Pa-faro wom jeŋa ne to, n nam wó vo dáane mo.”

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Ba na wora da yam konto ne to, Fɛsitu ma ta taane delo na wo Pɔɔl yuu ne to o bere pɛ wom. O maa we, “Nɔɔno mo wo ywo-seeni Feliki na jaane‑o o ke peena diga ne ye o yage‑o da.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: Amo nam vei Jerusalem ye Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam de ba teo kom nakwa bam ta o taane ba bere amo. Ba ma ta ba we, ko maŋe se a di o taane a vane‑o mo.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: Amo ma ta-ba a we, debam Rom tiina ba jaane nɔɔno dé ke nɔɔna jeŋa ne ye o ta wo zege balo na saŋe‑o to yiga ne se o ŋɔɔne o jwoŋi o tete de ba na saŋe‑o kolo ŋwaane to.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Ba laam ma tɔge de amo ba ba ywo-seeni. Amo maa wo pɛ se taane dem dim dáane. Tega na poore to, a ma zaŋe a nwoŋi se a di taane dem. A ma pa ni se ba ja nɔɔno wom ba ba.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Balo na saŋe‑o to ma zaŋe se ba ŋɔɔne. Amo ya maa boŋe we ba lage ba ŋɔɔne wo-kamunnu ba pa‑o, ye ba nam wo ke konto.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: Ba na zaŋe ba ŋɔɔne kolo to ye ni-kantɔgɔ botare mo ba tete Wɛ chwoŋa kam wone. Ko ma woli de nɔɔno wodwoŋi na tega, o yere mo Yezu, ye Pɔɔl maa pae se o ŋwe.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Amo boboŋa vugimi de a na wó ke tei a bwei ba taane dem to. Konto ŋwaane amo ma bwei Pɔɔl, se o ná wó sɛ o vo Jerusalem se a di o taane dem dáane.

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma lwoori se dé daa taa nii‑o mo ye dé yage taane dem se dé Pa-faro wom tete laam wane o di o taane. Konto ŋwaane a ma pa ni se ba taa yere‑o se ko taa nii maŋa kam a na wó wane a pa se o vo Pa-faro wom tei to.”

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Fɛsitu na tage konto o ti to, Agiripa laam ma ta o we, omo tete wó taa laga se o ni nɔɔno wom tete ni taane. Fɛsitu ma leiri‑o we, “Jwa ne mo nmo wó ni.”

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Tega daa na poore to, Agiripa de Bɛnisi ma zaŋe ba kwɛ nenɔŋa lanyerane ba nwoŋi. Soja tiina dedɛɛra dedaane teo kom yiga tiina ma tɔge ba kwaga ye ba vo ba zo taane dim jei sem. Fɛsitu laam ma pa ni pa se ba ja Pɔɔl ba ba ba zo.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Amo nam wo nɛ kolo o na ke se ko maŋe se ba go‑o to. O nam na ke o tete Pa-faro wom jeŋa ne to, amo nam boŋe se a pa o vo dáane mo.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Ko daare amo nam ba jege o woŋo kolo na jege kuri to se a popone a pa amo tu Pa-faro wom. Konto ŋwaane mo amo pɛ se o ba o zege abam yiga ne se á nii, ko fɔge ko dae nmo Pɛ Agiripa. Dé nam ná bwei‑o dé ti, ko wae ko pae se a nae o woŋo kolo a na wó popone a pa Pa-faro wom to.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Amo boŋe we, ko bá taa jege kuri se a toŋe peeno se o vo Pa-faro wom tei, ye a wo tage o na jege taane woŋo kolo ŋwaane to.”

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: O maa we: “Pɛ Agiripa, amo zem jege wopwolo de a na zege nmo yiga ne se a ŋɔɔne a jwoŋi a tete de Juu tiina bam na saŋe-ne wonnu telo maama ŋwaane to.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: Amo seene a jege wopwolo, nmo na tiini n yei Juu tiina chullu tem de ba ni-kantɔgɔ na ye tei to ŋwaane. Mo kokuri a lwoori‑m se n kwaane n cheigi a taane dem.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Ba maa maŋe ba yei we ko ye boboa ne mo amo maŋe a tɔge a wo Farisi tiina kɔgɔ kom wone ye a tɔge a sɛ ba chullu tem na tiini te damma te dwoi debam Wɛ chullu tem maama to. Ba ná laga, ba ya wó wane ba ta we konto ye chega mo.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Debam Isarele dwia fuga-yalei maama tiini dé zuli Wɛ wea de tete maama ye dé jege teena se dé na Wɛ na gwoni o ni se o ke wonnu tento dwoŋi to. Pɛ, amo na jege o teena yam konto to mo pɛ se Juu tiina bam jege-ne ba saŋa.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Wɛ nam bá wane o bi twa toone wone na? Bɛŋwaane mo abam ware se á sɛ konto?

english_verse: I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth.
translation_verse: Ko ná ye amo tete de, a déem boŋe we, a ná wae kolo maama a ke se ko chɔge Yezu na ye Nazarete tu to yere.

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: Amo ke tento maama Jerusalem ne. Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam déem mo pɛ-ne chwoŋa se a taa jaane Wɛ tete nɔɔna a ke peena diga ne. Ba ta ná yeini ba go-ba, amo wó pu balo na go-ba to kwaga.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: Kuni dedɛ amo maa yeini a kare a vei Juu tiina jeerim di sem maama ye a jaane-ba a pa ba na waarem. A maa kwaane a fe-ba se ba twe ba Teiru wom yere. A bane na tiini de zaŋe de-ba to, a yeini a tɔge ba nɛ a vei teene yiga yiga ye a jege-ba a bɛɛsa.

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: Dɛ dedwe mo a zaŋe a maa vei Damasika se a zeili Yezu nɔɔna konto dwoŋi. Juu tiina kaanem yiga tiina bam ya pɛ-ne chwoŋa de dam se a vo da a yaare-ba.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Debam maama ma to tega ne. Amo ma ni kwora na ŋɔɔne de Juu tiina taane ka we, ‘Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, bɛ mo ye n jege-ne n bɛɛsa konto? Nmo ke nenɛɛne nabea ná kwaane se ka ta wolo na jege-ka o pa to mo. Nmo wó jwoori n chɔge n tete mo.’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: A ma bwei a we, ‘Amo tu, n ye wɔ mo?’ Dé Teiru wom ma ta o we, ‘Amo ye Yezu wolo nmo na jege n bɛɛsa to mo.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Nam zaŋe n zege wɛɛne. Amo veere a tete a pa nmo se a wane a le‑m se n ta‑n ye a tontoŋeno mo, se n daare n pa se nɔɔna lɔre nmo zem na nɛ kolo amo tei ne, de kolo amo na wó bere nmo to.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: Amo wó jwoŋi nmo Juu tiina bam jeŋa ne a yage, de dwi-gɛ tiina bam jeŋa ne. Amo laam nam wó toŋe‑m se n vo dwi-gɛ tiina bam tei,

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: se n pa ba yia puri n daare n le-ba lim wone n yage pwooni yiga ne. Nmo wó le-ba setaana pɛ dam wone n daare n ke-ba Wɛ jeŋa ne. Konto to, Wɛ wó yage ba wɛleera o ma chɛ-ba pa se ba na jeiŋa jei o tete nɔɔna bam wone, ba na ke ba wo-dedoa de amo to ŋwaane.’

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: Amo bobo a ta Wɛ kwora a bere nɔɔna Damasika ne mo, de Jerusalem ne, ko woli de Judea teene dem maama ne, de dwi-gɛ tiina bam de tei ne. A bere-ba se ba leiri ba wo se ba daare ba pipiri ba taa tɔge Wɛ, se ba taa tɔge kikia yalo na wó bere we ba seene ba leiri ba wo to mo.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Konto ŋwaane mo Juu tiina bam jaane-ne maŋa kalo a na wo Wɛ diga kam ne to. Ba ma kwaane se ba go-ne.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Wɛ nam mo woli-ne se ko ba ko yi zem. Konto ŋwaane mo a zege ywo se a ta chega a bere nɔɔna maama, ko ná ye nɔn-kamuna naa nɔɔno de nɔɔno de. Amo na yeini a tɛ kolo to ye bedwe mo de faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem de Moses tete déem na tage we ko wó ke to.

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Konto mo ye we Wɛ Dam Tu Krista jege se o na yaara ye o ji wolo na wó da yiga o bi toone wone o vo Wɛ tei. O maa wó pa Juu tiina bam de dwi-gɛ tiina bam de na pwooni se Wɛ jwoŋi-ba.”

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl na wora o ŋɔɔne o pa o tete konto dwoŋi to, Fɛsitu ma zaŋe o ta de kwor-dɛa o we, “Pɔɔl, nmo yirisi mo! Nmo na zamese tɔnɔ dedɛ to mo pɛ n boboŋa tera konto.”

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ma leiri o we, “Debam tu Fɛsitu, ko dae we a yirisi. Amo na zege a tɛ kolo to ye chega mo ye ko jege swa lanyerane.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: Pɛ Agiripa maŋe o yei wonnu tem konto ni ne. Amo wó wane a ŋɔɔne a taane ded‑o jaja. Amo yei we a na ŋɔɔne kolo maama to dae wo-doŋo o tei ne, kolo ŋwaane keim dem konto wo seigi de ke gugworo ne.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Pɛ Agiripa, nmo sɛ faŋa faŋa Wɛ sampwori sem na bere kolo to na? A yei we n sɛ.”

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Agiripa ma ta de Pɔɔl o we, “Nmo boŋe se n ke lela n pa se amo tɔge a ji Krista bu mo na?”

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Pɛ wom, de gɔmena tu Fɛsitu, de Bɛnisi, de balo maama na wora to laam ma zaŋe ba nwoŋi.

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: Ba na nwoŋi to, ba maa ŋɔɔne daane ye ba we, “Nɔɔno wonto kikia wo maŋe se o na toone naa se ba ke‑o peena diga ne.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Agiripa ma ta de Fɛsitu o we, “Dé ya wó wane dé le nɔɔno wonto dé yage, ko ná dae o na ke o tete Pa-faro wom jeŋa ne to ŋwaane.”

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Ba déem laam na boŋe se ba pa dé zo nabworo dé vo Yitalia to, ba ma ja Pɔɔl de peena badwonna ba ke soja yiga tu wodwoŋi jeŋa ne, o yere na ye Juliu to. O nwoŋi Pa-faro wom tete soja tiina kɔgɔ kom wone mo.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Dé ma na nabworo, ko nwoŋi Adaramuta ye ko lage ko vo teene delo na wo Asia naneo kom ni ne to. Dé ma vo dé zo ko wo dé tɔge dé kɛ. Arisaka de ma tɔge debam o kɛ. Wonto nwoŋi Makedonia teo kodwoŋi ko yere na ye Tɛsaloni to mo.
